In a Drake child's story, a hero's sword slays a Mothbear, a Wyvern and a horde of undead.
Hunters must make sure bears they hunt are not Mothbears.
A herd of wild boars is led by an alpha through the snow and forages for food in winter.
Boars are weak individually, but together their tusks and explosive power can gore all but the deadliest enemies.
A grey wolf pack that is not Carn Wolves circles Erin Solstice when she sings, and she fights it with [Minotaur Punch].
A faceless leathery monster with long talons and barbed forearms is killed on the plains.
A huge slime rears twelve feet tall with colored swirling sections and engulfs a Hob whole.
A slime repairs damage from spells with purple gathering at the wounds.
A Goblin tribe fights a slime for thirty minutes and loses many.
A colony of Metalbite Slimes waits at the bottom of a fifty-foot pit trap in the dungeon.
A magic healing slime can mend wounds, and eats dead Crelers.
Skinner's body is layered dead skin, a slug-like bloated torso with two massive arms that drag it along, no legs, and two ruby eyes in a sunken face.
Skinner builds his body from entire skinned bodies, including the faces of the adventurers he kills.
The sight of Skinner leaves Ceria Springwalker unable to move or lift her wand.
Skinner leads hundreds of dead out of the Ruins of Liscor in an invasion directed by a single creature.
Something invisible touches the guards manning Liscor's gates and they throw down their weapons and run screaming, after which Skinner's eyes shift away from the gates.
Skinner commands the flow of the battle like a general.
The skin body is a puppet, and inside is a dark red, eyeless, segmented worm with two antennae and two whip-like tendrils that serve as hands.
Crypt Worms rampage through Antinium tunnels in the Hive and reanimate the Hive's dead.
The Wyvern Lord kills a Garuda [Lieutenant] and crushes a Dullahan [Soldier] when it dives onto Pallass's wall.
A lightning combination from Saliss of Lights leaves a crater in the Wyvern Lord's side, but it is still standing, swaying and stunned.
The Wyvern Lord survives the fight and returns with a much reduced weyr to reclaim territory in the High Passes.
He has killed six challengers within his weyr.
Bird carries and gnaws at a severed Wyvern wing into the inn.
Liscor's dungeon hosts a huge variety of nasty monsters, including Shield Spiders, Crypt Worms, undead, enchanted suits of armor, Bog Wraiths, Face-Eater Moths, giant infested slugs and the Children.
The Antinium also face large maggots that spit acid in the dungeon tunnels.
A dungeon pit trap hides a mile-deep drop with huge webs and gigantic scuttling spiders, including a Shield Spider the size of a house.
Calruz says four great nests in the dungeon are death to awaken: Face-Eater Moths, Shield Spiders, fungus, and one empty because something killed all that was inside.
The fungus nest is sealed off, and Calruz says that if it had a chance to spread it would be deadly, since half the spores shown to him are toxic and some explode.
Natural springs inside the dungeon provide water for its many monsters.
Reports on the dungeon mention infested monsters possibly derived from ancient Drakes and at least one more boss-class guardian monster.
Fierre's family are local farmers whose livestock, such as the sheep Fluffles the Sixth, tend to wander indoors.
Abebi is a young woman from Nigeria who works as the [Manager] of the Singer of Terandria's band.
Abebi is an Earther travelling with Cara's band, whose members were all found by Cara or came to her after hearing her music.
Abebi is one of the oldest members of the band, together with Thien.
Abebi did not know Cara from the very beginning, only after the star had already risen a fair way on her own.
Abebi keeps a clipboard at concerts and ticks off the Earth songs Cara performs, noting the Bruno Mars number during the Phel's Light show.
A stagehand warns Abebi that the ship she wanted watched is arriving, and she hurries to the side of the stage to reach Cara.
Abebi passes Cara gelato and preserved food in the wagon after the concert, and teases her about bursting out of her dress.
Abebi learns from Cara that Cara lied to Rae about once being fat, because Rae needed the confidence.
Cara tells Abebi, as the person who has known her longest, that her stage persona is a mask worn because the band is not safe.
Abebi knows the band is touring to find the best place to settle, and says so to Cara.
Abebi leads the band north through Pheislant after war breaks out in the south between Ailendamus and the Dawn Concordat, since the band wants no part of it.
Abebi takes the band towards Oztera, which has no personal quarrel in the war.
Abebi has seen real fights, and doubts the band members from Earth have the stomach to kill people.
Abebi orders the caravan forward once the broadcast is back on after a mob disrupts the concert.
Abebi sets up a real wooden stage with a draped background for the broadcast concert.
Abebi directs the shot for the broadcast and holds five amulets, which a [Huntress] discusses with her.
Abebi watches the delayed scrying-orb broadcast, which shows Drassi and Noass, while Cara is already performing.
Admiral Dakelos is the [Admiral] of the warship The Foehammer, part of the Ailendamus fleet blockading trade to the Dawn Concordat.
Dakelos has a poor way with drink.
Dakelos had received several coded [Messages] from Ailendamus telling him to watch for a message or persons on the day the Itorin's Pride arrived.
A man in a [General]'s uniform named Yerzhen boards Dakelos' ship, claiming they met when Dakelos was barely a [Captain].
Dakelos does not remember Yerzhen and is embarrassed. A [Fleet Mage] casts a truth spell on both men, and Yerzhen's statements all prove true.
Yerzhen tells Dakelos the fleet must land in Nadel by nightfall, and Dakelos protests that Nadel is the territory of Lord Belchaus.
Yerzhen claims Lord Belchaus is secretly allowing the landing as part of a plan to flank the Dawn Concordat when war begins in six days.
Dakelos thinks the Itorin's Pride was supposed to be much further north, and is uneasy at how quickly it moves.
Yerzhen promises to call for Dakelos to become [High Admiral] if he is made a [Great General] of Ailendamus.
Dakelos takes a drink with Yerzhen in his cabin and leaves an hour later somewhat intoxicated, and the two give the crew a speech.
Dakelos reaches Nadel's waters after nine hours, drunk on courage and dreams of promotion.
Dakelos shouts a demand for passage through a voice-amplifying spell, using notes Yerzhen gave him, and Lord Belchaus Meron answers that Nadel bows to no nation.
Dakelos orders his [Mages] to throw [Fireballs] at Lord Bel's flagship, aiming to miss.
Lord Belchaus boards The Wrath of Sel, a twin of Dakelos' own warship, and kills its [Captain] and [First Mate].
Dakelos sees that Yerzhen has vanished and the Itorin's Pride has been replaced by a tiny trading boat, and realises he may have been tricked.
The Admiral abducted by the illusion Yerzhen was itself an illusion cast by the Elusive Lot, a group of the Ullsinoi Faction of Wistram.
The fake Yerzhen says he wrote the speech with some help from the Admiral himself.
The disguised mages, watching from their hidden ship, say Dakelos is already surrendering and practically screaming that he was duped.
Miss Agnes is the [Innkeeper] and owner of the Frenzied Hare, an inn in Celum.
Agnes works hard to support her sick husband, and Erin sees her as good to friends and family but no better than that.
Agnes says she has little free time and no coin for books, and that she has a pint when the dinner rush is slow.
Agnes says she closes her inn most of the day on city holidays.
Agnes told Erin she wanted to help Jasi find another job, suggesting that being a [Barmaid] was not for everyone.
Erin realised Agnes was not the person she had thought, merely a woman good to her friends and family.
Erin offered to take over Agnes' inn for a while.
Maran and Safry say Agnes docks pay, cannot cook, and screams at staff over wrong orders.
They say Agnes is better when her husband is well, and that her workers get no tips.
Agnes was away from her inn with her husband, having hired another [Barmaid] and a [Cook] because business was good.
Agnes stormed into Erin's inn and screamed that Erin had stolen her best workers and her business.
Agnes greeted Jasi at the Frenzied Hare, calling her the star of Invrisil.
Agnes says Celum will never be the same after the Bloodfeast Raiders attack, and that she and Jerom could not sleep for weeks.
Agnes says Maran and Safry are at Ulna's, who took them in.
Agnes and Erin had not parted on good terms.
Agratha is a [Witch] and [Teacher], described as a [Witch Teacher] who wears a little red pointed hat.
Agratha is not among the most powerful [Witches] in Riverfarm, but her coven is large.
Agratha leads nearly a dozen [Witches] who were the first to take up the Emperor's bargain.
A [Witch] is killed and Agratha loses her schoolhouse, so Alevica tells Califor that Agratha may not attend.
Califor hopes Agratha can attend a meeting of [Witches].
Hedag calls on Agratha to sweep up spilled honey with a spell, and Agratha asks Hedag not to shout.
Agratha has her apprentices join in sweeping the honey as a test, and she and Hedag marshal the young [Witches] to get it into the jar.
Laken thanks Agratha and Hedag with a pot of honey, and Agratha bows slightly.
Agratha is the first [Teacher] Laken has met in this world.
Agratha's coven appeared first among the covens seeking Riverfarm's protection.
Rebeca says that she, Agratha and Devay are trying to create a school of magic for young [Witches].
Aiko is a young Japanese woman from Earth, who appeared in Gravetender's Fist's company a week before meeting Geneva.
Aiko is a [Nurse] and a [Sketcher] hoping to become an [Artist], and Geneva's assistant in most things.
Aiko is Aiko Nonomura, a young Japanese [Nurse].
Aiko and Ken befriend Luan, who tells them wars are never safe.
Aiko develops a crush on Luan, the older, optimistic South African who takes command.
Aiko, Ken and Luan tell Geneva they appeared last week, and Luan says at least forty people from their world remain.
Geneva offers food and shelter only to people from their world.
Luan, Ken and Aiko leave Gravetender's Fist to go to Geneva.
Aiko asks Geneva to let her help, saying she is not brave but wants to help the hurt, and becomes her surgical assistant.
Aiko threads needles, sharpens scalpels and prepares the healing potion, pouring it with a medieval dropper.
Aiko kills a Dullahan with scalpels in his eye and neck, and stares at her bloody hands.
Aiko confesses her feelings to Luan, who refuses because he is married with a child one year and five months old.
Gravetender's Fist and the other soldiers leave the valley together.
Later, Aiko is the first [Nurse] trampled when a mob of patients rushes in, and her protective glass mask breaks.
Aiko develops a fever and facial cuts, which Geneva treats without healing potions.
Aiko is recovering while Blake falls sick with the Yellow Rivers disease.
Alais is a Silver-rank captain and [Aeromancer] who leads the team Thunder's Solace.
Alais has imprecise control of lightning, so her team wears wood and chitin armour.
Alais tells Ksmvr the guilds' bounty on a bandit group was raised by eighty gold, to a hundred gold.
Alais says her team will be the group that takes the bandits out.
Alais warns Ksmvr that too many enchantments on his gear will explode.
Alais explains Stan's caution to Ksmvr, saying he has two kids and a lot saved.
Alais calls Thunder's Solace to her and raises her staff to hold the line against the Crelers.
Alber is a young, stocky, bare-chested fighter in Reizmelt, shorter than Ryoka but well muscled.
Alber takes fights for money, charging silver from normal folk and gold from adventurers, and moves between cities.
Alber is a [Fist Fighter] who is self-taught and not from Ryoka's world, as far as she can tell.
Alber is the only boxer-style fighter Ryoka has seen in this world, which has no boxing tradition in Izril.
Alber calls Ryoka "the Braggart" and guards the stairs against the drunk Madain, offering to shout if he comes up.
Ryoka teaches Alber boxing theory, including the flicker jab and roadwork, and he knocks her flat a few times.
Alber can already fight Silver-rank adventurers barehanded.
Alber has [Fists of Iron] and is levelling since working with Ryoka.
Alber beat a team of six Silver-ranks in a row, though he still cannot knock down a Gold-rank.
Alber uses the Skill [Ten Second Rush] against Ryoka, backing her into the ropes.
Alber asks Ryoka to show him boxing hooks again.
Alevica is a City Runner who is also a [Witch], a young woman in her late twenties with light blue hair and bright pale pink irises.
Alevica wears robes and a hat like a [Mage]'s, and moves like an athlete.
Ryoka feels a strange tugging in her chest, like the wind refusing to obey her, when Alevica walks in.
Alevica is sent by her mentor Oliyaya of the Glokhen Coven, who is busy cleaning up attacks on [Witches].
Alevica holds a Runner's Seal, which she shows Califor.
Califor calls Alevica the most gifted [Witch] of her generation at her age, whose magic is self-destructive, and says such [Witches] often end up in early graves.
Califor says Alevica is a prodigy who took six years to learn to fly.
Alevica is one of the least-trusted Runners though a good one, and Charlay says she opens mail and threatens other Runners.
Alevica will throw away important packages rather than deliver them if a client insults her, and no Courier or local Guildmaster will sponsor her.
Charlay is terrified of Alevica, who calls her "horse-girl", and Charlay tells Ryoka to do as Alevica says.
Alevica takes the Steel-box delivery worth eighteen gold and seven silver, with a double penalty, and counts out gold at once.
Alevica later rides in a hired travel-carriage with three other passengers.
Charlay says Alevica once cut in line at the guild, and that her tail later caught fire on the road, taking four healing potions to stop.
Alevica flies standing on a broom as if it were a skateboard.
Alevica fights from her broom with a crossbow, thrown vials of fire and smoke, and a sword, and raises skeletons from the earth.
Alevica dismisses the skeletons with a sign and they collapse into dust.
Alevica kills the bandit group, and Charlay says she took their money pouches and perhaps their potions.
Alevica dries herself and her clothes by magic after swimming in the river in her undergarments and hat.
Alevica tells Califor and Nanette she has not seen them in two or three years and says she is a City Runner these days.
Califor tells Alevica she knows she killed sixteen [Bandits] and advises burning the bodies next time.
Alevica tells Califor that Agratha may not attend because a [Witch] was killed and she lost her schoolhouse.
Alevica fails to cut the thread sewn through Ryoka's lips with a charmed knife and hurls the knife into the floor.
Mavika removes the thread with Alevica's knife and a Griffin charm, and Alevica tells Ryoka she now owes her a favour.
Alevica says Hedag has a bigger bounty than hers, and that Hedag leaves the dead in villages she passes.

section: The Witch Hunter and the fires
text: Alevica confronts a smiling man who calls himself a scout or hunter, and accuses him of being a [Witch Hunter] who put a [Knight] on Belavierr.

section: The Witch Hunter and the fires
text: Alevica fires a bolt into the man's side, and he stabs her in the stomach with a poisoned spear.

section: The Witch Hunter and the fires
text: Alevica is left poisoned and screaming as he walks away, saying she can hope someone finds her.

section: The Witch Hunter and the fires
text: A man matching the hunter's description paid Fierre to alert the Order of Seasons, according to Fierre's report to Rie.

section: The Witch Hunter and the fires
text: The narration shows a Drake arsonist who set the fires paid the [Bandits] to attack the [Witches] and had spared a [Witch] earlier.

section: The Witch Hunter and the fires
text: Alevica sleeps under Eloise's watchful gaze after being saved.

section: The Witch Hunter and the fires
text: Alevica stumbles up after the ritual with no power left, and Eloise slaps her and tells her flying would get her killed.

section: The Witch Hunter and the fires
text: Alevica thinks Eloise and Hedag are not powerful [Witches] by her standards, and that only Mavika and Califor made her come.
Alime is a [Receptionist] at the Runner's Guild in Reizmelt.
Alime tells Ryoka that someone has told every Runner's Guild north of Invrisil about her, and not in flattering terms.
Alime says she feels she owes Ryoka an apology over rumors that she thinks were wrong.
Alime greets Ryoka cheerfully at the counter of the Reizmelt Runner's Guild one morning.
Alime plans Ryoka a circuit of a bulk-letter delivery to Nonsfru, two deliveries in Ingli and a pickup at Enam.
Alime estimates the circuit takes six hours, or eight with longer breaks.
Alime warns that the deliveries are safe and non-priority and pay only six silver coins and eight bronze for the lot.
Alime says bigger guilds sometimes take contracts from further away, so Reizmelt sometimes loses contracts to Invrisil.
Alime says Reizmelt's guild loses funding when contracts go to Invrisil, so it needs its Wind Runner to stay.
Alime asked Celum's Guild for a dossier on Ryoka, and says Ryoka is different now from what it described.
Alonna Swiftwing is a Drake [Mage] and the Guildmistress of Liscor's Mage's Guild.
Alonna is new to her position as Guildmistress and did not inherit anything that put her in the Mage's Guild's leadership.
Lism Swifttail marches through Liscor promoting Alonna and Senior Guardsman Jeiss as his candidates for the Council.
Alonna stands at a podium in Dragondance Plaza opposing Raekea, and glares at her during the debate.
Alonna is named among the winners of the election with Lism, Jeiss, Tismel Lischscale and Zalaiss Holmfyre, alongside the Gnolls.
Alonna sits flanked with Jeiss at Lism's side of the Council table and rubs her claws to make a magical spark.
Olesm judges that Alonna, Lism and Jeiss are firmly together as a group on the new Council.
Alonna, addressed by Olesm as Councilmember, demands to know why the agents who attacked powerful nobles were not spotted.
Alonna says Liscor's Mage's Guild is affiliated with Wistram, as every Mage's Guild is, because [Message] spells and information go through a central authority.
Alonna says she is not from Wistram but her guild must distribute information from the academy, including a bounty sheet.
Alonna warns that Wistram could direct other Mage's Guilds to ignore Liscor's guild if she refuses to distribute the bounty.
Alonna explains that this would mean Liscor's [Messages] to guilds elsewhere would be shoved to the bottom of the piles and delivered last.
Alrric Kerrfa is a Gnoll [Administrator], the manager of Wall Lord Ilvriss' company and second to Ilvriss in matters of business.
Ilvriss describes Alrric as his [Gemstone Administrator] and executive director in command of all his affairs.
Alrric is one of only two Gnolls in Salazsar with this kind of power, [Administrator] being a rare class for a Gnoll.
Ilvriss' company, the Gemscale holdings in mining, gem processing and more, employs thousands of Drakes, Gnolls and a few other races in Salazsar.
Alrric wears a proper suit tailored to Gnoll specifications, with short-cut, combed fur unlike most Gnolls, and a deferential but only slightly bowed manner to Ilvriss.
Alrric wears custom-tailored suits, and his fur shows as a matte chestnut that his co-workers know him by.
Alrric uses Ilvriss' name without his title, a mutual respect established through a delicate dance years earlier.
Tasilt introduced Alrric to Ilvriss twelve years before Ilvriss' return from Liscor, and it took Ilvriss over a year to agree to hire a Gnoll.
Ilvriss credits Tasilt with persuading him that a non-Drake [Administrator] was better than a Drake after a corruption scandal.
Alrric and Ilvriss have worked together for seven years, coming on eight, and are used to each other's habits.
Ilvriss gives Alrric full control over a development project, saying his claws are off it, and Alrric says that once Ilvriss would never have allowed this.
Alrric proposes selling the rights to the tapped opal shafts to fund investment in a new seam that has already yielded truegold and magicore.
Alrric tells Brilm that Ilvriss is not his master but his employer.
Alrric dislikes the pompous Brilm, and Brilm says the dislike is mutual.
Alrric's wife is Ximenes Kerrfa, and he has a daughter, Sidinel, who is fifteen.
Alrric has an old family friend, Casklal, a Gnoll with a staff who teaches Sidinel.
Alrric started working in the mines at age twelve after lying about his age to get into a crew.
Alrric came to a desk at the top of a tower from the mines, and says he can teach anyone who doubts him a lesson in mining and fighting.
Other Gnolls call Alrric a City Gnoll and a sellout, and in Salazsar they say he does not understand what it is to be a [Miner].
Alrric uses [Earmarked Funds - Recompensation], a monetary Skill that produces project-dependent gold from the company's own profits, which cannot be spent except in certain ways.
Alrric uses the gold from the Skill to buy Ikrr's crews a night out in the city, noting that it cannot increase their pay.
Alrric has the Skills [Quick Recollection] and [Compartmentalized Knowledge], which help him recall and handle large amounts of information.
Alrric gains a black eye in a bar fight with Gnolls who called him a City Gnoll and worse, a pet, and keeps the injury for a day or two as a reminder.
Alrric opens Ilvriss' office door and finds the Wall Lord's chair fallen backwards onto the carpet.
Alrric sees grey in his fur in a hand-mirror, treats it with a vial from his bag of holding and thinks slip-ups could cost him everything.
Alrric goes into the shafts, is hit by beams from Stone Starers and has his ring give out, and runs out while Shriekblade charges them.
Ikrr spots a bit of grey in Alrric's fur, and Alrric says fur dye is a perk of the job and threatens to put Ikrr under Yesh if he tells anyone.
Alrric reapplies the fur dye after returning to his office, and his nervous shakes stop.
Alrric refuses to answer [Gossips] who ask whether Ilvriss is really engaged to a [Princess] of the House of Minos.
Alrric watches a scrying orb three days after meeting a group of Gnolls, and says they replaced two idiots.
Alrric was a Plains Gnoll, a fact that matters greatly to him, though Ikrr and his colleagues think he is a City Gnoll.
Alrric tells Ilvriss he is a City Gnoll when asked about leave for the Meeting of Tribes, and the narration calls the lie casual by now.
Alrric's chestnut fur is dyed, and a dye-removing tonic partly strips it, with Sidinel also dyed and Ximenes needing no dye.
Alrric uses fur dye and scent potions to hide his natural fur and smell when he leaves home with Casklal.
Alrric, Casklal and Sidinel are Doombringers, as are others in the group they meet, and all use dye to hide the common secret.
Ximenes knows the secret and chose to carry it, while Sidinel was born with it.
The retired [Clown] Tom is haunted by a second personality, who appears as the Tom in his bedroom mirror and speaks in his own voice.
The reflection tells Tom that it is not over and that he is insane but not an idiot.

The mirror Tom argues that the Demon soldiers arrived too neatly: they appeared at night and knew where the princesses slept, two for one princess and six for the other, and none were sent for the Blighted King, his Queen or anyone else.
Before the Blighted King and his court, Tom drives a fork through his own other hand to silence the voices in his head, and the narration then continues in a wilder voice that calls Tom stupid.
The alternate holds a dagger to the time mage Nereshal's throat to command the room's attention.
He points at the Fool as the culprit, deducing that the Fool marked the spot in the courtyard for his allies to come through and tried to abduct the princesses beforehand.
He shows that the glowing ward stone is fake, made with a Skill of the Fool.
He kisses the Blighted King on the cheek, and the Blighted Queen backhands him, knocking out a tooth.
The alternate asks the Blighted King for a map, a [Mage] who can cast a few spells for him, knives, healing potions and the King's sword, in order to hunt the Demons.
In the dark, he cuts down Demon warriors, grabs one and vanishes with him, and reappears behind the others with his wounds closed, laughing.
Amerys is an Archmage of Wistram and one of the King of Destruction's Seven.
The students call her the mage of the King of Destruction's Seven, and she belongs to no faction and has never approached one.
She is known as the Calm Flower of the Battlefield, one of the King's generals who conquered a continent and threatened the world.
Ceria thinks of her as a living legend, the equivalent of any Named Adventurer.
Her skin is dark and she is a native Chandrarian.
Her levels came from war, unlike the academic Archmages Viltach and Feor.
Amerys flies by a flight spell, and she can descend from the sky next to Flos.
She stands in the air above the sea and kills a sea serpent with repeated bolts of lightning from her palm.
Ceria hears her laughing in the middle of the fight.
She tells her fellow generals to try not to get in the way of her lightning.
Illphres says Amerys uses lightning and air, prefers rapid all-out assaults and does not think, while Illphres plans every move.
Illphres says Amerys has about six or eight more levels than she does.
Amerys says lightning runs in her body, and that she would have killed Viltach had her cell not been shockproof.
She calls herself the most destructive of the Seven in combat and the most fragile.
Amerys sits among the generals who drink with Flos and Orthenon the night before a battle.
Orthenon asks her to attack the left flank and tie it up so the others can focus on the center and right.
She tells Ceria she will not die until her king returns and says Flos is a king worth being a coward for.
She says she will do all she can to live until the day he calls for her.
In captivity she says she often clashed with Orthenon, while she got on well with Mars and liked Drevish.
She hears that Drevish was killed.
She calls Flos her liege and her king of war.
She says Flos said she often reminded him of a cactus that spat needles, and she liked the compliment.
Verdan Blackwood is another Archmage, and a student says he could have taken down the sea serpent, but Amerys volunteered.
A student reports that she was out hunting when pirates attacked the ship and asks where she is.
Amerys stands for Pisces at the Council against revoking his scholarship.
Amerys stands smiling next to Illphres among a group of mages who watch Ceria.
Illphres says she and Amerys sometimes train together and compete because they are a good match, though they dislike each other.
Illphres says she asked Amerys to join her faction and that Amerys will not join because she is waiting for her King.
Amerys tells Ceria that Illphres asked her to stop Ceria from killing herself if Illphres failed, and that she refused to risk dying.
Amerys says she told Illphres to wait, even for a decade, and to challenge the Golems with ten times their number.
Ceria screams that she is a coward, and Amerys' eyes flash with fury.
Amerys has a cut on her leg through her robe, bound tightly with gauze.
Amerys blasts open a frost-covered door that would not open, thinking of Ceria's master, and comes out holding an ice-blue spellbook.
She orders a student in the crowd to give the spellbook to Ceria Springwalker, threatening to find out if he does not.
Mirin wonders why Amerys has remained in Wistram and suggests she may have turned traitor.
Gazi answers with a heavy "Yes", then says Amerys was loyal, they need her, and if she is an enemy they must know.
Archmage Amerys is Chandrar's lone Archmage and has not been seen since the King of Destruction announced his return.
Rumors spread about why she is missing, and the other Archmages do not speak the truth.
Amerys is shackled and bound in a Wistram cell, protected by wards and an antimagic field.
The Archmages Feor, Naili and Viltach tell her she has refused to eat for a week, and Feor says she bit off the fingers of the mage Teligrain.
Amerys offers Naili to ally Reim with the Revivalists and give her Wistram if Naili sets her free.
Her captivity is a secret in Wistram, and only Archmages may see her.
Later, she is bound in a magical straightjacket, chained and gagged, because she bit the fingers off a mage serving her food.
Cognita conveys Amerys's summons of Aaron because the Council has not formally stripped her of her position as Archmage.
Amerys tells Aaron she could leave at any time if she renounced her lord, turned her back on Reim and swore in blood to serve only the academy.
She says Flos will free her, even if it takes him razing Wistram stone by stone.
She says she clings to sanity because her king is not a patient man.
She says she is the only Archmage in Wistram who tells the new arrivals the truth.
She asks Aaron to set her free, and he cannot because the magical bindings are beyond powerful.
Amerys helped Aaron make magicore batteries, and she refuses to remember his name, calling him boy or bratling.
She says High Mage Telim has a kind heart and is a lazy generalist whose genius lies in small spell details such as speech-quills.
She says Cognita lets her summon only Aaron, and asks what Cognita wants.
Anand is an Antinium Worker and Individual who levels as a [Tactician], and later as a [Strategist].
Anand, Belgrade, Bird, Garry and Pawn are the five Antinium who protected Erin from the undead.
Anand is one of Erin's best chess pupils among the Antinium.
Asked their levels by Pawn, Anand answers fifteen and Belgrade sixteen; both are [Tacticians] playing lightning chess.
Belgrade plays defensively and Anand aggressively, pushing his queen on the left.
Anand and Belgrade coordinate the Hive's defenses in place of Klbkch, with Belgrade favouring static defences.
In the latest skirmish Anand was wounded, leaving him unable to lead, and Belgrade could not command alone.
Anand and Belgrade took over managing the Hive's defenses from the Queen, who no longer needed to command.
Anand commands the day's fighting, using the Skills [Decisive Blows] and [Evasive Tactics].
Anand says the Hive is sadly uniform, which makes it difficult to counter individual threats as other Hives do.
Belgrade doubts why [Strategists] level from chess and suspects an error in how the world levels; Anand frowns.
Anand and Belgrade share a strategy room with maps of the Hive, a chess board and one of Erin's Go boards.
Anand reports that Face-Eater Moths have declined in ferocity after the slaying of their eighth mother-type leader.
Anand was among those consulted on whether Bird could meet Bevussa.
Anand told Pawn that the Painted Soldiers would not hold Liscor, and that Pawn should prepare his unit for combat.
Anand told Klbkch that Pawn eats and tends the Painted Soldiers but is dispirited since the siege.
Anand directed Workers in a Hive war room and allowed a Worker to take the name Bishop after the first Bishop died.
Pawn was angry about the name, but Anand argued the name belongs to both of them.
Later, Anand is a [Strategist] who tells Pawn his leveling has stopped this month, which distresses him.
Anand spoke to Erin and received advice about Klbkch, which he declines to share with Pawn.
Anand asked Klbkch whether he could call him "Father" and hug him, and Klbkch answered no.
Anand now wears a chain vest of altered chainmail that glows faintly purple, and carries a hatchet and a wand.
Anand says Klbkch is still furious at Bird and has not allowed more Antinium than necessary aboveground.
Anand believes he is substandard and that he will be discarded if he fails Klbkch.
Anand says Klbkch is the best of the Antinium.
Anand tells Relc he wanted to call Klbkch father, and Relc hugs him and goes to speak to Klbkch "dad to dad".
Later, Anand is a Level 27 [Strike Strategist].
Anand befriends Sword Prognugators Klberein, Krrechzzeim, Kiskel and others by asking their names.
Anand learned from the Prognugators that the Free Antinium were made in the image of Galuc the Builder.
Galuc died before coming to Izril, and the Shaper Queen Bessachidia saved his form.
Anand built a stone memorial where General Sserys of Liscor fell, with a plaque reading that Sserys stopped the Black Tide.
Liscor's Drakes watched the tribute, and the plaque ends "Drakes do not run."
Anand's memorial for Sserys becomes talk of Liscor, and Maviola El was present.
Anand tapped an aquifer, dug a makeshift sea and floated a small ship while tied to ropes held by Painted Antinium.
Anith is a Jackal Beastkin from the Duskclaw Tribe, with sleek black fur and an elongated, dog-like head.
Anith is a [Mage] and the leader of his adventuring party, carrying a faintly glowing book.
Anith leads the eclectic Silver-rank team Vuliel Drae, which includes Insill, Dasha, Pekona and a Gnoll [Archer], Larr.
Anith introduces himself politely to the masked Toren in the dungeon as the [Mage] and party leader.
Anith casts [Repulsion Barrier], which sends a wave of leeches flying away from him and Larr.
Anith has a [Dangersense] Skill that went off when the stranger Toren thought his party were foes.
Anith believes the masked adventurer is clearly of a higher level than his party.
Anith's party is hired for the first time to guard another adventuring team, Earlia's Gemhammer, in Liscor's dungeon.
Anith agrees to guard Gemhammer out of curiosity and a sense of obligation, and says they are being paid.
Anith assigns Insill and Dasha to watch the entrance, with Larr and Pekona on guard at the other.
Feor is an Archmage of Wistram and an aged half-Elf with a long, silvery-white beard.
Feor has pale blue and silver eyes with unnaturally bright pupils, and is easily twenty times older than Aaron.
Feor is one of the few most powerful spellcasters in the world and calls Aaron by the name Blackmage.
Feor belongs to the Centrist faction of Wistram and keeps a personal group of half-Elf mages he trusts implicitly.
Feor's aide Teura is one of his best [Mages].
Feor is part immortal.
Feor is considered to be Wistram's top chess player.
Feor leads Wistram's circle watching the battle at the inn and recognises the young man who cast the rainfall spell and the half-Elf who cast [Ice Wall].
Feor notes that Falene Skystrall, a Wistram graduate, was also there, and says inquiries should go through her.
Feor wonders aloud what Flos is up to as one of the scrying mirrors shows the King of Destruction.
Feor orders an investigation of Erin's door, an offer to buy it, or else a task for recent graduates.
Feor remembers Perorn Fleethoof as a centaur with a fiery mane who fought beside him on Rhir two decades earlier.
Feor oversees nearly fifty Wistram [Mages] linked in magical circles, who have over four hundred contacts when the feed opens.
Feor orders Teura to send a team to find and retrieve Remi, because Canada is a country from the other world.
Feor tells the team to be ready for conflict, since the Siren of Songs and other rulers are furious at the article.
Archmage Nailihuaile, called Naili, is a slim, smiling Lamia with light white and rose scales and glowing patterns of blue, purple and yellow on her arms and back.
Naili says she is a Star Lamia, and her glowing scales store magic, which helps spellcasting but makes sneaking difficult without illusion spells.
Naili wields the Serkonian Lance, a treasure of the Lizardfolk.
The Serkonian Lance creates a field in which Naili can link spells, change the nature of mana, and fire lances of magic.
Naili specializes in enchantments, best at making scales harder than mithril and casting mass-[Invisibility], and claims to be the best in the world.
Naili says she is one of five Archmages in the world, six if Amerys is counted.
Naili is the most relaxed of the four Archmages in Wistram, lighthearted and joking, unlike the older, stately Feor and Viltach.
Naili is the Archmage of the Revivalist faction.
Naili says she learned in Baleros to prefer quick spells, and dislikes Feor's habit of casting only big spells.
Naili tells Feor she grew up a little Lizardgirl in a swamp village and earned money trapping young Hydras, which is how she became a Lamia.
Naili agrees to protect the Earth people in exchange for access to the Evermote Study.
Naili says the Revivalists have the numbers to resist any faction, including Feor and the Centrists.
Feor suspects Naili knows something he does not, and that someone besides Naili helped Blackmage.
Naili helped Aaron make an artifact, a sealed battery or orb, which impressed her.
Naili hides under Aaron's bed with the Serkonian Lance, telling him she is not there if someone knocks.
Naili shouts at Cognita through the door that she is having sex, and Cognita punches a hole through the door.
Naili tells Cognita that Pisces committed more crimes after leaving Wistram, so Wistram has the right to apprehend him.
Cognita asks Naili to correct the record naming Pisces and Ceria as Wistram graduates, and Naili relents after a tense moment.
When Cognita says she would insist, Naili coils cold and dangerous before laughing that she was kidding.
Cognita tells Naili she is only the academy's protector and test, while the [Mages] control its will.
Naili visits Amerys with Feor and Viltach and says the Earthers have helped her make a shock orb nearly as good as a Level 30 [Lightning Mage].
Naili answers that Cognita does not rule Wistram "Not yet", when Amerys asks.
Naili tries to keep the Earthers under her control and cooperative, and thinks she could dispel Aaron's magic.
Naili suspects Montressa of lying about Erin and Pisces and says Montressa may be expelled too if so.
Naili watches the duel through the Queens' mirrors with Feor and Viltach and ranks the Sword Prognugators high-silver on talent, Gold with artifacts.
Naili wins a public debate against Feor by arguing that enemies should be struck while weak, and Wistram applauds.
Naili says she helped the academy at no cost by capitalizing on information about the enemy.
Naili has helped defeat the King of Destruction, a secret only to idiots.
Naili links her Serkonian Lance with Feor and Viltach to extend the Weatherward about three miles south and save the Emerald Signet.
Archmage Zelkyr is a Drake who ruled Wistram a few centuries ago and held the [Archmage] class.
Calvaron says Zelkyr was the best of the Archmages of his time.
Zelkyr is famous for damaging one of the Walled Cities' walls and more famous for creating Golems.
Zelkyr ordered his Golems to guard the entrances to the upper levels of Wistram so that only he could learn from the mages above.
Zelkyr's order caused a huge battle with the other mages, after which his surviving Truestone Construct Cognita imposed a new order.
Cognita came down from the upper floors and announced that Archmage Zelkyr was dead.
Cognita and the other Golems have maintained Wistram since, still fulfilling his orders, and his order that the upper floors be off limits still stands.
Teriarch grumbles that Zelkyr probably wanted funding for his Golems, and recalls that he made a hundred Truestone Golems.
Teriarch remembers only after ranting that Zelkyr was dead.
The Armored Queen is the largest of the Queens by far, and her Hive is built of stone and metal like an underground castle with a fortress around her.
The Armored Queen cannot move and never leaves her chamber, sitting on no throne.
The Armored Queen birthed more Antinium to create the first Hives than any other living Queen.
The Armored Queen is swollen and in pain because her body cannot sustain her weight, and Workers guide her movements.
The Armored Queen is the most pleasant Queen in that she is willing to speak with Anand.
The Armored Queen directs Sehr and her Prognugators on ore, food and the Free Antinium while talking to Anand.
The Armored Queen recoils on hearing Anand is a Level 27 [Strike Strategist].
The Armored Queen says Sehr is Level 12 in the [Armored Leader] class, and that Tersk, her foremost living Prognugator, is Level 16.
The Armored Queen says Prognugators are made by combining the minds of thousands of Antinium through the sacrifice of personality, intelligence and will.
The Armored Queen keeps a hallway of sandstone statues of nearly forty Centenium, not the full hundred, with the last in progress.
The Armored Queen identifies a statue as Galuc the Builder and tells Anand he was made in Galuc's image.
The Armored Queen says Galuc died before coming to Izril, and Bessachidia saved his form so that Anand and the others could be made.
The hallway includes statues of Rehab, Mellika, Devrkr the Glowing and Mirrex, who might still be alive.
The Armored Queen says each Centenium was made of millions of minds, which is why none have been surpassed.
The Armored Queen grows Steelclad, giant armored Soldiers at least thirteen feet tall, learning from what happened to her.
The Armored Queen says the Steelclad are decoys to draw the enemy's best attacks, with lifespans of weeks at most.
The Armored Queen says the Steelclad can survive underwater for eighteen minutes.
The Armored Queen calls the Steelclad her greatest sin and says she grieves for their existence.
The Armored Queen has Goat fitted with custom steel armor and promises Anand enchanted chainmail.
The Armored Queen has a collection of enchanted gear traded from other Hives or taken from enemies killed in combat.
Athal is a young man of A'ctelios who serves as one of the escorts guiding Trey Atwood through the Carven City.
Athal is tall, pale-eyed and sharp-toothed like the rest of A'ctelios' folk, and is lively and fascinated by outside visitors.
Athal calls Baosar, the ruler of A'ctelios, his father.
Athal shows Trey the Trade Quarter in the head of A'ctelios, where outsiders live and trade temporarily.
Athal tells Trey that A'ctelios sells meat, though few outsiders buy it, and mostly leather and bone.
Athal proudly shows Trey a [Butcher]'s counter where meat of A'ctelios costs four coppers for a family-sized steak dinner.
Baosar scolds Athal for tempting a guest of the Quarass with meat, and Athal bows his head and apologises.
Athal says A'ctelios has crime and quarrels, and uses appointed peacekeepers instead of a City Watch.
Athal has lived in A'ctelios all his life, has no wish to leave, and expects to die there.
Athal is fascinated by Trey's iPhone and compares it to the scrying orbs that merchants have been selling in the city.
Athal keeps children from swarming Trey's iPhone, and warns him that children would pry it away in an instant.
Athal hurries Trey away from a window where a baby is crying, and begs Trey not to tell Baosar he took him there.
Athal explains the baby's strange cry by saying it was born with illness and the shapers will fix it.
Athal tells Trey that outsiders do not travel below the first layer of the city, and that only natives pass the checkpoint of bone-armoured peacekeepers.
Athal eats steak in front of the others at the meeting of the Shield Kingdoms, taunting some of the younger Garuda and Humans.
Athal and other young people from A'ctelios try to press food, wine and water on the guests, which seems to be a game among them.
Athal leads Trey, Gazi and the Quarass to a private room when Baosar asks for them.
After Trey is covered in blood, Athal's cheerfulness drains, and the Quarass sends him off so that he practically runs away.
When a pakeil charges Trey, Athal calls out for Gazi to stop, and Trey recognises that Athal had named the creature a pakeil.
Athal backs away when Gazi points her sword at his face after Trey finds a human backpack in the pakeil's flesh.
Athal tells Baosar the pakeil attacked Trey first, and then says the pakeil are not people but outsiders.
Athal screams that Trey has attacked Baosar, and the peacekeepers draw their weapons until Baosar raises a hand.
During the escape from the Carven City, Athal leaps snarling at Trey and Gazi from above, and Trey blasts him away with three [Light Arrows].
Davi's last recordings show Athal welcoming a group of Earthers into A'ctelios and giving them meat free of charge.
The recording shows Athal picking up Davi's camera after the Earthers transform, eagerly calling it an artifact and saying it could be sold.
Trey later wishes he had killed Athal, as well as Baosar, and burned A'ctelios Salash to ash.
A man describes the Necromancer as a powerful [Necromancer] with pale white hair, white skin and violet eyes, who may use illusions to hide them.
The same man says the Necromancer has an army and a kingdom of the dead.
Some call him Az'kerash, a few remember Perril Chandler, and nobody remembers his forgotten nickname Peril; most call him the Necromancer.
Az'kerash cares about little, and his lack of emotion is a void that grows with each passing year.
Az'kerash appears to Ryoka as an old man with lined face, white hair and albino skin, resembling Teriarch's human form without the physique.
Az'kerash wears black robes woven of rippling shadow and a silver ring that Ryoka senses is not ordinary.
Az'kerash's voice is old and cracked but clear and strong, and distant.
Az'kerash has black corneas with pale ghostly white pupils.
The Gnolls named him Az'kerash, "Slayer of Kerash", after he killed the Gnoll Chieftain Kerash over a century earlier.
A history text calls the Necromancer an outcast of Wistram and a fallen Archmage who had plagued Terandria for over a century.
The same text says he led a massive army against the port-Kingdom of Desonis, overwhelmed its army, seized a port and vanished.
Az'kerash tells Pisces that Archmage Chandler was a man from a different era, over a century dead.
Once he was Perril Chandler, and he was once Human.
His other titles included Lord Chandler, Duke Chandler and Sir Chandler, from estates awarded to him, and he kept the common-born name Chandler.
Az'kerash was also known as the Gravewarden of Therras and the Undying Shield of Calanfer, and was an honorary Knight of the Autumn.
Az'kerash was a friend of the Order of Seasons and a paragon of the defunct Order of Felgeist.
Few remember who he was, among them perhaps a Dragon, a few [Historians] and some Terandrian nobility.
Perril Chandler once stood alone on Calanfer's borders as four armies advanced, and the dead rose and halted four kingdoms.
That day he earned the title of Archmage of Wistram and was called the Undying Shield of Calanfer.
Later, Az'kerash recalls having fought Demons and defended his homeland as the Undying Shield of Calanfer, an Archmage and hero of Terandria.
The kingdom he once served is ash by his hand, and his rage over his betrayal lingers.
Archmage Feor or Az'kerash could tell stories about an uppity half-Elf student, but neither is inclined to reminisce.
Az'kerash says he has walked Rhir and seen terrible things brought to life by the blight, the Demon King and his Deathless.
Az'kerash expects to face such opponents at the end, one way or another.
Az'kerash calls Zelkyr his friend and says neither of them ever finished the secret of creating life.
Az'kerash says Zelkyr made creations to love him and later forsook love for something greater than Truestone.
Az'kerash says he loved a woman like no other, and she died about a century ago.
Ceria says the Necromancer attacked the continent with his legions ten years before, and that even in Wistram she heard of the devastation he wrought.
Gerial says no one found the Necromancer's body, so he is probably still around, though he has not been seen since.
Az'kerash tells Venitra to observe armies near his castle, mark where the dead fall, and kill any who enter.
Az'kerash is creating something no species has ever dreamt of overhead in his chamber while Venitra attends him.
Az'kerash binds the intruding Ryoka in webs with the spell [Sticky Webbing].
Az'kerash tells Venitra she has failed and orders her to lower her sword and leave.
Az'kerash casts [Silent Sickle] at Ryoka, and it cuts her hair and shoulder.
Az'kerash reads Teriarch's letter and ring as a gift marking his two hundredth year of existence.
Az'kerash says the ring is enchanted with warding and movement spells and calls the gift predictable.
Az'kerash describes his relationship with Teriarch as strained.
Az'kerash says the ring from Teriarch might be useful but was of no significance.
Az'kerash finishes a huge undead of flesh and bone, saying his army nears completion and the Walled Cities will tremble.
Az'kerash says he needs more corpses and plans to send Bea, whose plague touch can harvest whole pods.
Az'kerash tells Venitra to take one of the Chosen, Ijvani or Oom, and track down the Human girl Ryoka.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash appears by projection to his apprentice the Goblin Lord, ordering him to go past Liscor and reclaim the Goblins in the mountain.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash tells the Goblin Lord to wreak havoc in Human lands and become the Goblin King if he is able, or die.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Osthia perceives that Az'kerash treats his apprentice like a disinterested owner giving instructions to a dog.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash says he has trusted servants in Liscor gathering information.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: The Goblin Lord tells Az'kerash his servants never reached Liscor; Az'kerash says he must reprimand them.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash orders the Goblin Lord to burn weak cities, leave strong ones, and kill the Drake Osthia.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash speaks to Ryoka through Venitra disguised as Regrika Blackpaw, saying he is watching through her eyes.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash says his creations were sent to learn whether Ryoka had told anyone of his existence, not to kill her.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash heals Ryoka's broken pinkie from afar by rearranging its bones.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash puts a [Word of Death] on Ryoka so that speaking part of his name or mentioning necromancy kills her.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash says he does not want his presence known and will guarantee Ryoka's safety for now.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash orders Venitra and Ijvani to observe, hide their identities, not harm Ryoka and learn about her ties to the Antinium and Drakes.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash tells them to inquire about the inn, its magical door and Erin Solstice, whose enchantment he senses does not belong.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash believes Winter Sprites are powerful but harmless elementals who use no force unless threatened.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash orders Venitra and Ijvani to bring back Ryoka's head undamaged, frozen or in stasis.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash plans to teleport Oom to reveal himself as the murderer of Ryoka and a Gnoll.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash scries for Ryoka with Ijvani and Bea in his castle, with Kerash and Oom present.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash tells Ijvani she did little wrong against Zel Shivertail and a Lord of the Wall.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash decides to remove Zel Shivertail as a thorn and sends Bea, Kerash, Oom and Ijvani to Liscor with scrolls of [Greater Teleportation].

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash tells his servants Zel's death matters above all, to kill all witnesses, and that none of them may die.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash says the scrolls of [Greater Teleportation] are limited and that even he cannot acquire more.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Teriarch forces a truce on Az'kerash, who says he will leave Ryoka and her associates alone.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash casts [Wall of the Damned] to shield himself from Teriarch's fire.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Teriarch tells Az'kerash he may send someone to collect what is left of Venitra.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash asks why Teriarch protects a single City Runner and says he did not know the Dragon cared for Humans.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash warns that his secrets must not be given away, and Teriarch calls him Chandler.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash tells Venitra she has lost his favor and is no longer first among his servants.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash tells Ijvani she has failed him likewise and gives Kerash his authority.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash considers adding a new servant to his number.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash hopes Ryoka survives because she is Teriarch's weakness and is far less well protected than Magnolia Reinhart.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash says Dragons have hides stronger than diamond and hearts softer than snow.

section: The Goblin Lord and the hunt for Ryoka (Book 5)
text: Az'kerash says a different sort of plague, the Goblins, now falls upon the Humans and Drakes.
The Necromancer's army of Draugr, wraiths, Crypt Lords, wights and Bone Giants marched south toward Liscor, despoiling Human lands.
The author of the history says the Necromancer clashed once with the Goblin King's forces and the battle ended in a stalemate.
The Necromancer's army besieged Liscor and cut the continent in two.
During the siege the Necromancer inflicted plagues and launched rotting corpses over the walls, and Liscor held on for four weeks.
On three successive days Az'kerash slew Generals Hekiss, Vusso and Misa.
Az'kerash destroyed every army he met except the Goblin King's, including an Antinium army sent north.
Az'kerash could not kill Zel Shivertail, who refused to retreat despite repeated assaults.
Zel Shivertail tore Az'kerash in two with his claws at Liscor, and the undead began to fall.
Zel later says he cannot believe Az'kerash survived being ripped apart.
A Drake war council later reckons Az'kerash could field at least four hundred thousand undead in a single army.

section: Zel Shivertail and the Goblin Lord (Book 6)
text: Az'kerash is shaken by news that Zel Shivertail commands Magnolia's army, then decides it is an opportunity to seize.

section: Zel Shivertail and the Goblin Lord (Book 6)
text: Az'kerash speaks to his apprentice by spell, and the Goblin Lord then says they attack Invrisil to slay Zel.

section: Zel Shivertail and the Goblin Lord (Book 6)
text: A dome of bone rises around Zel and the Goblin Lord, which Magnolia attributes to Az'kerash.

section: Zel Shivertail and the Goblin Lord (Book 6)
text: Venitra, Ijvani, Bea, Oom and Kerash teleport into the dome as five undead.

section: Zel Shivertail and the Goblin Lord (Book 6)
text: Az'kerash says through the Chosen that his apprentice was the crux of the trap without knowing it.

section: Zel Shivertail and the Goblin Lord (Book 6)
text: Az'kerash calls the Chosen his children and says Zel gave him the idea for them after his defeat in the last war.

section: Zel Shivertail and the Goblin Lord (Book 6)
text: Az'kerash approvingly calls Kerash the first of his Chosen after Kerash speaks.

section: Zel Shivertail and the Goblin Lord (Book 6)
text: Az'kerash tells Zel he wages war on species as a whole and that the living are his enemy.

section: Zel Shivertail and the Goblin Lord (Book 6)
text: Az'kerash asks Zel who told him he was alive.

section: Zel Shivertail and the Goblin Lord (Book 6)
text: Az'kerash arrives himself using a Scroll of Greater Teleport, leaving him four of the eleven the Goblin Lord thought he had.

section: Zel Shivertail and the Goblin Lord (Book 6)
text: Az'kerash hits Zel with [Diamondshard Spray] and [Stone Lance], then four [Deathblast] spells.

section: Zel Shivertail and the Goblin Lord (Book 6)
text: Zel loses his left eye to a diamond shard and part of his head.

section: Zel Shivertail and the Goblin Lord (Book 6)
text: Az'kerash tells Zel he will be the finest of his servants in death.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Reiss says Az'kerash has informants all over the continent and Drake allies in power.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Reiss says Az'kerash aids a Human conspiracy that does not know it is him, and that his servants can cheat [Detect Truth].

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash speaks through Reiss's body and tells Osthia he remembers ordering her slain.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash calls Rags nothing like the previous Goblin King.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash through Reiss tells him to study the Tome of Greir Rot's undead enhancement section next.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash says [Necromancers] struggle against small groups of high-level foes, a weakness he has long sought to address.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash tells Reiss he is disappointed that he failed to preserve Zel's body and lost his undead army.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash suggests Reiss let the Humans use him against the Drakes.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash promises to raise every soul that falls at Liscor and offers his Chosen Bea and Venitra, not Kerash.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash tells Reiss to take the walls and hold the city thirty minutes so his force can teleport in.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash's Chosen Venitra, Kerash and Bea wait to be teleported with ranks of undead.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash takes over Reiss's body and conjures a [Bone Rapier] with [Bloodcaller's Curse], which stops wounds healing.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash fights the five Redfangs using [Flash Step], and his skill comes from centuries of experience.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash uses [Mass Silent Sickle] before taking the body.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash uses [Sightless Winds] and kills Headscratcher with a thrust just below the heart.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash casts [Mass Stone Lances], killing Yellow Splatters, who shielded Pawn.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Garen severs Reiss's arm, Az'kerash screams in his castle, and the link breaks.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash calms after half a day of fury and dismisses the losses at Liscor except Zel's death.

section: Reiss and the siege of Liscor (Book 9)
text: Az'kerash tells Kerash to prepare materials and bring mana potions, Drake scales and chitin for new work.
Ilvriss's investigators link Regrika Blackpaw to Az'kerash and become certain he is alive.
Osthia's investigation lists the cities the merchant Perril Chandler visited and eight Drake persons of interest present at the same times.
The Drakes consider Az'kerash responsible for killing Zel Shivertail and Periss.
A Drake says Reiss thought Az'kerash was over Level 70 and maybe over Level 80.
Az'kerash stands in his workroom in a black-stone castle west of the Bloodfields, hidden in a forest against the High Passes.
The forest around the castle is an enchanted maze of illusions, and an army of undead waits in front of it.
Az'kerash uses three rooms: a workroom, personal chambers and a war room.
Az'kerash does not sleep and sometimes does not move, and he can stand unmoving for months.
Az'kerash remodels a whale into an undead and has not moved his leg for two months.
Az'kerash can split his attention to hold conversations, give orders and work on creations at once.
Az'kerash controls the puppets Sir Salin, Hexilt and a Human merchant at Chandrar auction houses through scrying devices.
Az'kerash decides Hexilt will suffer an accident from a jealous lover, ending in suicide in six years.
Az'kerash calls the mental upkeep on Hexilt tiresome because Chandrar is too far to maintain the spell.
Az'kerash lectures Kerash about auction customs and Drake spectacle, with Kerash replying obsequiously.
Az'kerash cannot control hundreds of puppets because each has to be managed.
Az'kerash tells Venitra she will not be sent out because she remains in disgrace.
Az'kerash may send Kerash as a Gnoll wanderer for the Meeting of Tribes, and says Bea kills too easily.
Az'kerash tells Bea her flaw is an asset because she was made to kill.
Az'kerash speaks to Pisces through an undead rat and addresses him as young Necromancer.
Az'kerash forbids Pisces to call him Archmage Chandler and says to address him by the name the world has given him.
Az'kerash gave Pisces the book Perfecting Facets of Undeath by Credeth, and had taught him designs two months earlier.
After Venitra failed to catch Ryoka, Az'kerash offered Pisces instruction in return for silence about Regrika Blackpaw.
Az'kerash bound Pisces by magic to keep his promises, and considers Pisces a possible replacement for the dead Reiss.
Az'kerash casts [Absorb Recollections] on the rat and sees three months of Pisces's life in Erin's inn.
Az'kerash recognizes Erin and is irritated that she once defeated him at chess.
Az'kerash is surprised to realize he is annoyed at being questioned by a young [Necromancer] less than half his level.
Pisces shows Az'kerash a skeleton whose chest fires a bone bolt, which the Necromancer had thought impossible.
Az'kerash laughs for the first time in a long while at Pisces and the Horns sliding across the inn floor.
Az'kerash cooks a deep dish pizza in his dusty kitchen with his Chosen, who cannot tell flour from sugar or eggs from potatoes.
Az'kerash says the pizza is crude, and recalls a boy who might have loved it.
Az'kerash casts [Ice Floor] in his ballroom and skates on it, having done so before.
Az'kerash conjures an illusion of a Terandrian court that turns on him and falls to dust.
Az'kerash tells Bea he has failed a hundred thousand times to create life, which he and Zelkyr never completed.
Az'kerash promises Bea he will keep trying to find the secret of life.
Az'kerash animates a Bone Behemoth folded into Pisces's room and has the rat engrave a death spell on its skull.
Az'kerash treats the Behemoth as homework like he once gave students.
Az'kerash hears that Ijvani is walking back on foot for lack of Great Teleport scrolls.

section: The bounty on Pisces and the Creler nest (Books 13-14)
text: Az'kerash intercepts Wistram's bounty on Pisces with [Message] interception and [Scribe Thoughts].

section: The bounty on Pisces and the Creler nest (Books 13-14)
text: Az'kerash tells Bea to masquerade as Elden Veis to inquire through the Mage's Guild about Liscor.

section: The bounty on Pisces and the Creler nest (Books 13-14)
text: Az'kerash says Nekhret's bones would be useful.

section: The bounty on Pisces and the Creler nest (Books 13-14)
text: Az'kerash says Pisces is not his apprentice and aiding him is inexpedient.

section: The bounty on Pisces and the Creler nest (Books 13-14)
text: Az'kerash reads Pisces's earlier speech to the Council and laughs.

section: The bounty on Pisces and the Creler nest (Books 13-14)
text: Az'kerash identifies Illphres as a peer of the Siren of Savere.

section: The bounty on Pisces and the Creler nest (Books 13-14)
text: Az'kerash watches Montressa and the Horns through Ijvani while scribing a black spell scroll.

section: The bounty on Pisces and the Creler nest (Books 13-14)
text: Az'kerash tells Ijvani the mission against Pisces will be rescinded.

section: The bounty on Pisces and the Creler nest (Books 13-14)
text: During the Creler battle Az'kerash tells Ijvani to wait for Pisces to retreat and then cover him with barrier spells.

section: The bounty on Pisces and the Creler nest (Books 13-14)
text: Az'kerash predicts the adventurers will betray each other and abandon Pisces.

section: The bounty on Pisces and the Creler nest (Books 13-14)
text: Az'kerash calls the battle an amusing distraction and tells Ijvani to let Pisces be.

section: The bounty on Pisces and the Creler nest (Books 13-14)
text: Az'kerash calls Bird the Prognugator of the Free Antinium a new Centenium.
Az'kerash lives in a hidden castle at the foot of the High Passes on southern Izril, behind his army, and the world thinks him dead.
Az'kerash ranks at the top of the world's villains, even in presumed death.
Az'kerash considers taking a century to research and wait.
Az'kerash thinks Magnolia Reinhart, the Dragon and perhaps Ryoka know of him.
Az'kerash thinks the Wailing Pit's Flesh Worms overrode his command over awakened undead.
Az'kerash tells Kerash that Flesh Worms could never command the greater undead.
Az'kerash rages in his lab and castle, blasting it and setting the forest on fire before putting it out with rain.
Az'kerash discovers Toren holds the key to leveling undead and laughs at its blank space.
Az'kerash says that unless Zelkyr lives in secret in Wistram, only one being still holds the Truestone knowledge.
Az'kerash builds Toren a new magical skeleton body, and Ijvani webs Toren after he attacks.
Toren is later held in a cage of power while Az'kerash studies him.
Az'kerash has the castle walls sing an old hymn from the palace of Silvaria.
Az'kerash says he will make at least ten Chosen and give the four existing ones the ability to level.
Az'kerash decides Ijvani will be the second leveling undead.
Az'kerash says he may conquer the world before the turn of the century.
Kerash is a Level 8 [Warrior] after being granted the ability to level.
Az'kerash teaches Bea to be a [Lady] and calls her the first of the true undead.
Az'kerash has removed Ijvani's spells so that she must earn them by leveling.
Az'kerash has given his four existing Chosen the ability to level, and all are below Level 10.
Az'kerash owes the key to leveling creations to an apprentice less than half his levels.
Az'kerash promised Belavierr one of his new undead for her help.
The world thinks Az'kerash dead, and he can sustain about fourteen simultaneous thoughts by fragmenting his mind.
Archmage Chandler used the same [Parallel Thoughts] Skill.
Badarrow is a Redfang Hobgoblin archer who never wastes an arrow.
Badarrow leads a faction of Redfang archers who hunt, the smallest of the Redfangs' groups.
Badarrow spends his time on the quest for the perfect arrow, fletching and shooting at targets night and day.
Badarrow shot zombies from a watch ledge, one arrow each, grinning at the Horror.
He killed two Goblin [Shamans] with his two best arrows at Esthelm.
Three arrows hit Badarrow, but the one aimed at his chest was badly made, with its glue broken.
Badarrow learned [Farshot Mastery] after sniping the Goblin [Shaman] at Esthelm.
He shot Bird with arrows in three-at-a-time volleys from range.
Badarrow stood by the door of Erin's inn, grumpy but interested in the Humans.
Badarrow hung upside down held by Shorthilt and Headscratcher to shoot Raskghar from the cliff.
He used the Skill [Shattershot], but the arrow was stopped by a wicker shield.
Raskghar arrows struck Badarrow in the back and shoulder as he climbed out.
Headscratcher carried the wounded Badarrow through deep water toward the surface, both nearly drowning.
Badarrow rang a bronze and blue metal bell once, and it made a vast hollow sound that bled his nose, ears and eyes.
Badarrow became a Level 25 [Archer], changed to a [Sniper], and gained [Doubled Range].
His [Keen Eyes] Skill changed to [Eagle Eyes].
Five Redfang Hobs including Badarrow held off the Raskghar while leading Cave Goblins and Gnolls.
Badarrow throws a pitch that drops under Wesle's bat, with Shorthilt catching, in Erin's baseball game.
He stabbed Greydath's shoulder with an arrow held in his hand, and Greydath struck him unconscious.
Headscratcher concluded Greydath could be hurt because Badarrow had hurt him.
Badarrow and the other four Hobs challenged Garen and were beaten bloody.
Badarrow sat with the Hobs who spoke of being Redfangs while Garen was gone.
Rabbiteater and Badarrow report to Rags that Headscratcher, Shorthilt and Numbtongue are dead.
Badarrow is a [Bow Sniper] with [Farshot Mastery], [Doubled Range], [Eagle Eyes] and [Two Mile Shot].
Badarrow uses a [Blinding Arrow] against Eater Goats.
Badarrow was granted an enchanted longbow with a magical string and limbs.
Badarrow and Snapjaw met when both wept for fallen friends, and are in a sexual relationship.
Calescent walked in on Badarrow and Snapjaw, and then on Redscar and Leapwolf demonstrating for Rags.
Badarrow and Calescent's squad drove adventurers from Goblinhome with an exploding enchanted arrow, shouted insults and rocks.
They also used glowing fake Creler egg nests, spread excrement, and launched wasp nests.
Bamer is an elderly Vampire of the Drakle clan who sits in the rafters of the keep with the family when Ryoka is brought there.
Bamer stares down at Ryoka with a frown but says nothing when Himilt asks whether the family disagrees.
Bamer has coughed all his life, according to Fierre.
Bamer thinks that the Vampires' frequent sickness is a curse.
Bamer says Vampires once preyed on people and controlled much of Izril until they were nearly wiped out.
Bamer thinks the Byres family cursed the Vampires centuries ago, after they went into hiding.
Bamer told Fierre stories of the Vampires of old, who used blood magic and shape shifting.
Himilt says Bamer could tell more of the Vampires' history but likes to exaggerate.
Bamer says there were Vampire Lords, royalty with powers such as turning into mist, and even Skills.
Fierre says Bamer is dying, and counts him among the sick Vampires.
Bamer was born with the signs of the Vampires' malady, as were Rivel and Fierre.
Bamer arrives with Rivel when Colfa confronts Ryoka about Fierre's collapse.
Bamer remembers, with Himilt, when House Byres' plan was put forward, so some places to live are instantly off the table for Vampires.
Bastam is a Drake [Mage] of Wistram Academy and one of the five allies of Illphres.
Bastam is the oldest of Illphres' group of five mages, in his sixties, although he does not look it.
Bastam is an Isolationist, like Jurix and Illphres.
Bastam has a tail that wags faster when he is tense, even when he otherwise appears calm.
Jurix says he will message Bastam and Ophelia so the group can teleport to the fight, which will take several leaps.
Bastam arrives with Jurix and Ophelia in the air above the sea, and lands on the choppy water as if it were solid ground.
Bastam stands on the ocean waves with Ophelia and hurls [Fireball] and [Lightning Bolt] spells hundreds of meters at a pirate ship.
Bastam angrily asks Illphres why she has not told her apprentice Ceria what the group is about to do.
Bastam is named by Jurix as one of five mages who will challenge Cognita at the end of the year.
Bastam trains on the rocks by the ocean at dawn with Jurix, Ophelia and Qum, while Illphres trains separately with Ceria.
Bastam took three tries to work out that one of the Golems was a Flesh Golem enchanted to look like a Shadow Golem.
Bastam warns Jurix not to eat too much before the challenge, as the mages will probably be moving around a lot.
Bastam eats sparingly from a bowl of oats and honey on the morning of the challenge.
Bastam tells Ceria before the challenge that her exam showed courage and daring, which older mages have forgotten.
Bastam dies in the challenge, and his remains are laid out in the catacomb room with those of Illphres, Jurix, Ophelia and Qum.
A Golem reaches down for Bastam's face in the catacomb room as Pisces hesitates over what to do.
Ceria later cites Bastam, with Illphres and Jurix, as having shown the courage of true mages.
Bastion-General Quiteil commands the 4th Wall of Rhir and is the person in charge of the entire 4th Wall.
Quiteil has a secretary's build, spectacles, ink-stained fingers and blue eyes, and Cirille found him looking like a [Scribe] rather than a war hero.
Quiteil has a luminescent white patch of skin that covers his wrist and moves up his arm.
Quiteil asks his officers many questions and sends them repeated priority messages that need authentication; he makes no small talk and does not look up while giving orders.
Quiteil told Cirille that he has no time to explain himself to every officer who questions his command.
Cirille's contacts said he runs a tight ship, requires subordinates to know how many arrows they hold, and loves reorganizing units.
Quiteil assigned two thousand one hundred and three Gnolls under Chief Warrior Merish to Cirille's command, and kept the arrangement in force when objections were raised.
Quiteil defended the use of Rhirian [Necromancers], saying necromancy has never been outlawed in Rhir and that he would gladly take ten thousand more like Mage-Captain Hetarria.
A [Huntress] said he came closest to panicking when someone shouted "Deathless" for fun, and that he had the Lizardperson arrested and shipped back to Baleros.
During the serpent-titan attack, Quiteil opened a Tier 7 scroll box from the capital with the [Mage-General] and teleported the scroll to Zavarial.
Quiteil is a [Logistics General], in fact a [Peerless Logistics General], promoted by virtue of his calculating nature rather than as a combat expert.
Quiteil is called Bastion-General of 4th Wall for the same reason, and the narration says he would never lead a battle even from the rear.
Quiteil places his bedroom next to his office, which is a secretary's office with more space for maps, communication devices and documents.
Quiteil picks at the corruption on his right arm as he keys speaking stones.
Quiteil wakes many times a week on instinct and trusts his gut.
Quiteil uses [Eighteen Minutes of the Secretary] to freeze the world for eighteen minutes while enchantments are dead, and spends the time writing memos to his commanders.
Quiteil uses [Unstoppable Command] to authorise the Tier 7 spell [The Thousand Gateways of Orlaey] from 4th Wall.
Quiteil calculates Silvenia's coordinates exactly and notes that it has always bugged him that the wall is 80.3 feet high.
Quiteil tells the Blighted King that Deathslayer Arrows are ready and portal-spells are prepared to cover the retreat.
Quiteil counts 89 spells cast to bring down one serpent-titan, estimating Tier 3-5, by watching the projection on the battle-map.
Quiteil mutes the Blighted King's speaking stone while he works, and asks how many ballistae are mounted on 1st Wall.
Quiteil feels a tremor and drinks cold tea after the Arrow of Winter strikes.
Quiteil tells Cirille that synergies are known to Rhir's forces and that other nations lack experience of them.
Quiteil congratulates Cirille and says he looks forward to her second tour, which a [Scrier] explains is an offer to stay another four years.
Quiteil wakes on instinct, checks the codes of each wall, and finds Zavarial's code good but remains uneasy.
Quiteil speaks to a voice mimicking Cirille on the speaking stone, asks about her arrow stockpile, and realises something is wrong.
Quiteil asked Cirille about arrows the other day, which makes him suspect the Cirille on the stone is not her.
Quiteil confirms through the Blighted King that the enemy is Silvenia, the Traitor, and tells her Lord Hayvon is liberating 5th Wall.
Quiteil tells Silvenia he funded the book she has read, as did Lord Hayvon, and warns her not to trust everything in books.
Bastion-General Zavarial commands 5th Wall in Rhir, and Cirille's division was placed under him.
Zavarial is a half-Elf and was a champion of [Archers].
Zavarial reports to the Blighted King and his [Strategists] by speaking stone during battle.
Zavarial was reluctant to send out units that had not drilled together, and he held irregular divisions on patrol duty until he pronounced them fit.
When serpent-titan copies breached 5th Wall, Zavarial held the wall and asked for Lord Hayvon to hunt raiding parties.
Zavarial requested the Arrow of Winter Scroll, opened a Tier 7 Scroll on the wall and told the area to be cleared.
Zavarial authorised a few support units that use death magic, and a necromancer said he would need Zavarial's permission before taking on a new task.
Zavarial asked for volunteers to try a blood transfusion tactic against poison.
Zavarial has scales running up his forearm to the elbow, a heritage of Lizardfolk blood along with his half-Elf ancestry.
Zavarial rose from [Archer] to [Ranger], [Veteran Ranger] and [Blightwarden], and in the ranks from [Soldier] to [Captain], skipping [Lieutenant].
Zavarial became a [Blightranger General], an expert in hit-and-away missions in Demon territory, and then Bastion-General.
Zavarial's wide-reaching powers come from 5th Wall's enchantments rather than a [General] class like Quiteil's.
Zavarial carries six rings given by the Blighted Kingdom's treasury and a bow made from the bones of a long-dead animal.
Quiteil taught Zavarial to always make plans, and Zavarial carries a backup single-use speaking stone.
Zavarial reports that enemy titans are creating breaches and that Demons are flooding behind 5th Wall.
Zavarial notices the lead titan feeding as smaller snakes devour the dead to regain its mass.
Zavarial requests the Arrow of Winter scroll, and the Blighted King grants it.
Zavarial fires [Arrow of Winter: Glacius Pillar] after announcing he is opening a Tier 7 Scroll, and a pillar of ice forms hundreds of feet up and shakes the world when it fires.
The Tier 7 spell turns about a mile of the field to ice and kills the titan collective and the copies.
Cirille tells Zavarial that she has consolidated her classes into a [Combined-Arms Commander].
Zavarial gives the code Shelten-Khelt-[Brigand]-Dirt to Quiteil at midnight.
Zavarial raises his bow in the darkness and fires [Arrow of Greater Dispel] to break the spell, then dives for the stairs.
Zavarial is lifted into the air, and reports a hundred thousand attackers at 5th Wall to Quiteil before his backup stone falls.
Zavarial fires a Deathslayer Arrow at a laughing half-Elf in the clouds, who makes it vanish.
Zavarial dies in an explosion that consumes him and the tower.
Silvenia tells Quiteil that she killed his friend.
Cirille later notes that Bastion-General Zavarial is dead and the gates at their location are broken.
Bea is one of Az'kerash's undead servants, a rotting woman who stands with Venitra and Kerash in his castle.
