Bea is one of Az'kerash's chosen and a spellcaster, the other besides Ijvani.
Bea's body is rotting and putrefying, though she looks much like a normal Human woman.
Bea was not designed personally by Az'kerash as Venitra was, but was either reanimated from the dead or self-forming.
After Az'kerash lets Ryoka go, voices identifiable as Venitra, Kerash and Bea say his decision may be in error, and agree to hold her.
Bea holds an image of Ryoka running through the snow and tells Az'kerash where she is.
Bea touches Zel Shivertail's arm, giving him a magical plague that a healing potion then spreads.
Zel's claw takes off Bea's arm as she retreats, and she picks it up.
Az'kerash praises Bea for the touch, and Bea mockingly names the plague.
Zel cuts Bea in two and stomps on her, after Venitra lands on her and breaks her body.
Bea asks Az'kerash about the particulars of intercourse, which he tries to forget, and Venitra later asks him about it.
Bearclaw is a large scarred Gnoll woman with dark brown fur mixed with red and patches where fur never regrew.
Bearclaw is called Bearclaw because of the metal claws she fights with, and Mrsha notes it is not a Gnoll name.
Bearclaw is a Plains Gnoll who says she came to Liscor for business after leaving the tribes.
Bearclaw smells of old blood, like the Wanderers the Stone Spears Tribe warns children about.
Bearclaw keeps steel in the pockets of her leather vest.
Klbkch estimates Bearclaw's level at anywhere from Level 20 to Level 30 and quite dangerous.
Bearclaw opens a door to Klbkch in Greas Street, with steel-clawed knuckles on one paw, meeting Mister Soot.
Klbkch orders her to remove the knuckles, says she is not under arrest, and withdraws when it would be a risky fight for the junior guards.
Klbkch reports to Beilmark a possible career criminal known as Bearclaw.
Bearclaw meets Mrsha and the other cubs in the street, walking with two Gnolls and a Drake.
Bearclaw hears there is a white Gnoll in the city and recognizes Mrsha, and a companion says Soot said nothing about her being white.
Bearclaw cuffs the Gnoll who calls the white fur a Doomed One's sign, calling it superstition.
Bearclaw tells Krshia she has heard of her, and Krshia answers politely while backing away.
Klbkch and Relc tell Bearclaw to move along, and she leaves as Relc calls for her to tell Soot hello.
Bearclaw arrives from the south on foot, not through the magic door, to take the bounties on a white Gnoll alive, an [Innkeeper], the magic door and the Heartflame Breastplate.
Bearclaw tortures and breaks two Senior Guards of the Watch in Soot's safe room, one of them a Gnoll woman, and a hooded figure carries them off.
Bearclaw tells Soot that she knows how this works and that the Guard will not die.
Bearclaw scorns Soot's warnings about the Brother of Serendipitous Meetings and the Elusive Lot claims on the inn, saying her gang does not answer to [Mages].
Bearclaw leads a gang of Liscor's most violent criminals, whom she taught a new level of violence, and kills two Senior Guardsmen in a week.
Bearclaw's mission is to abduct Mrsha, kill or kidnap Erin Solstice, and steal the magic door.
Bearclaw snarls about who the Gentlemen Callers are and why they guard the inn.
Bearclaw decides to take the bounty on Relc for fun, saying she remembers him and the Ant-monster who challenged her.
Bearclaw keeps Soot in place with a paw on his shoulder so that they fail or succeed together.
The Raskghar Nokha has Bearclaw held down while she screams and begs, intending to make her a pack-sister.
Nokha asks that Bearclaw's skin and skull be saved for her.
Zevara says Liscor owes thanks for dispatching Bearclaw's gang, that Soot is dead, and that Bearclaw will be found, and she has posted a thousand-gold bounty on her.
'Bearclaw' grins in the crowd during the day of delegations and slips away.
Beatica is a [Councilwoman] from Lancrel in her early forties, well dressed, and wearing one large, expensive ring.
Beatica was a [Councilwoman] for over two decades and did not give up her class when she left her city.
Beatica has a charismatic presence like a torch, which makes the room turn to listen to her.
Beatica uses a Skill that silences Rie mid-sentence, and Rie asks her not to use Skills on her.
Beatica tells Rie that Lancrel's officials deserve a chance to use their classes, and proposes that she and Mayor Rodivek take over tasks.
Beatica says she considers herself in charge of her people though they have lost their home.
Rodivek, a former [Mayor] of Hewlat, argues alongside Beatica that Lancrel's people have no say in how Riverfarm is developed.
Beatica objects to Prost on behalf of her Councilman, asking whether the truth stone is valid and whether Elmmet was wrongly accused.
Beatica argues that a [Thief]'s [Master of Faces] Skill could have been used to impersonate Elmmet.
Beatica's [Uninterrupted Monologue] Skill silences Prost while she argues.
Beatica stumbles back, looking wounded, when Helm shouts at her and the crowd erupts.
Later, Beatica is a [Councilwoman] from Lancrel who jumped into Rie's camp after the drama in the spring.
Rie calls Beatica a reliable snake who is better managed than left wandering, and Laken distrusts her duplicity.
Rie tells Beatica to excavate only twenty feet down, and Beatica hurries to do so.
Beatrice is a dark-skinned Dullahan student at Wistram whose head and armor are not attached.
She is quiet, and at her first meal with Ceria and Pisces she says only about three things beyond greetings.
She eats pudding with a spoon into her head while it sits on the table.
Beatrice is allergic to mushrooms, and she offers to have them taken away if they bother anyone.
Calvaron describes Beatrice as a Revivalist, in the faction that wants to throw open Wistram's doors and usher in a new era of magic.
She is a [Runeshaper] with symbols etched into her armor, and Calvaron says she and he have little clout.
She wants Calvaron to join the Revivalists, and they quarrel about his future.
A student reports that Beatrice and Calvaron have put money on both Ceria and Pisces passing the exams.
She holds the body of Calvaron after the shades kill him in the banquet hall.
She tells Ceria it is her fault and that the cause was Pisces.
Beatrice later attacks Ceria for defending Pisces, and Montressa saves Ceria.
Beatrice silently watches Charles de Trevalier after he drops Illphres' spellbook into the sea, and says nothing.
Beatrice passes her final test and becomes an official mage of Wistram, a [Runeshaper] and one of the secret brokers of the academy.
She inherited Calvaron's network of connections after he passed, but not his easygoing air.
People still come to her because she has a lot of influence, not because she is easy to work with.
Montressa du Valeros is her friend, a full student on the verge of being recognized as a [Mage].
Later, Beatrice is a Dullahan [Runemistress] who is escorting Aaron to Archmage Nailihuaile.
Beatrice backs up as Cognita stops them and says another Archmage, Amerys, requests Aaron's presence.
She calls Amerys a traitor to the academy, and Cognita dismisses the opinion.
Beatrice relays that Cognita insists on the visit when guards of Amerys's cell hesitate to let Aaron speak with her.
Beilmark is a Gnoll Senior Guardswoman of the Liscor Watch.
Beilmark is paired with the Senior Guardsman Jeiss on the walls and bets with him on chases.
Beilmark's patrol catches Rabbiteater, and she reports to Olesm that the Hobs did not draw steel but a fifth Hob escaped.
Beilmark bets five silver that the little bee escapes the pursuit, and welcomes a junior [Guardsman] to the Watch with Jeiss.
Beilmark takes reports at the desk, and swears at news that Soot has the criminal Bearclaw, lamenting Relc is not Klbkch's partner.
Beilmark says she will alert the patrols and take the report to Captain Zevara, who will be displeased at a Wistram visit.
Beilmark calls Antinium "big kids" but doubts they are really children.
Bekia is a Gnoll [Maid] who has been in Magnolia Reinhart's service for years.
Bekia serves a plate of food to the young [Assassin] Theofore, whom Magnolia shelters because his own guild has marked him for death.
Bekia is a former [Chieftain] of a Gnoll tribe, informal unlike the other servants in the household.
Bekia says she got in trouble and was kicked out, and now finds being a [Maid] fun and relaxing, though she misses fighting.
Bekia carries a battleaxe and her own bag of holding, and swings the axe close to Ryoka.
Belavierr is a seven-foot [Witch] with black hair to her waist, a hat wide enough to shade her whole body, and eyes with multiple orange irises ringed in black.
Belavierr rides a huge black stallion and names herself Great Witch of Terandria when seeking sanctuary in Riverfarm.
Belavierr is Wiskeria's mother and tips her hat to Wiskeria, calling her daughter.
Belavierr is called the Spider, Temptress, the Eater of Threads, the Witch of Calamity and Mistress of Strands.
Belavierr says her craft is stitching, sewing, connection and binding.
Belavierr stitches with a pale needle and flesh-coloured thread, with hands too fast for Ryoka to follow.
Belavierr's wind-silencing presence makes Ryoka's wind vanish, and she thanks Ryoka as "friend of winds" before staring at her for minutes.
Belavierr wears robes of stitched cloth that are as hard as steel, and says she once made Seven League Boots.
Belavierr says her great work, the Helpful Servants, was undone while she slept, nibbled away by strange mice that defiled her soul and craft.
Belavierr says her death walks the world again and that it burns.
Belavierr has many magics shattered, with broken strands trailing behind her, after losing her magic in Noelictus.
Belavierr says it will take aeons to rebuild, and that she begins thread by thread.
Belavierr says what ate her magic was the mice, whose identity matters little.
Belavierr layered her immortality by binding her soul, eating the heart of the last Phoenix, buying a [Necromancer]'s secret and sending her death to a hundred or a thousand women.
Belavierr mends the tapestry of her soul, which mice ate holes in while she slept, lonely for her daughter.
After losing her protections Belavierr says she can be killed with age or blade, and feels more alive and aware.
Belavierr says she has lost all but a few years of stored time and needs more power to rebuild the workings that hid her heart.
Belavierr says she has survived her death but foresees a second by fire, and stays only until the deal with the Emperor is struck.
Belavierr speaks like a person, remembers names and faces, and blinks at the sun after her protections burn away.
Belavierr tells Ryoka she gained [Immortal Moment] when she last levelled up recently.
Belavierr later has the lines of her immortality knitting slowly again, though many rings are broken.
Belavierr says she has waxed and waned with the world and has not been so exposed in thousands of years, being close to mortality.
Later, Belavierr is mortal, learning insight from mortality, and is no kinder for it.
A list of Belavierr's alleged crimes includes destruction of a city, murder of a [Prince], murder of a child, summoning of an Old One and mass deaths by it.
Belavierr's threads and garments strangle those who inform on her, and three people died trying to inform the Order of Seasons.
One of those informants was strangled by her collar and another pulled in front of a wagon, according to Fierre's knowledge.
Wiskeria knows that Belavierr never lies, and Belavierr says she promised to give up only her magic, not her craft of bargains.
Belavierr says that when the Order sends [Knights] by tens of thousands, they were never enough.
Belavierr arrives in Riverfarm walking down the main street as Prost, Rie, Durene and Wiskeria confront her.
Wiskeria banishes Belavierr three times and shoves her back several steps with unseen force.
Belavierr says she is wounded, has declared one woman her foe and is pursued by another deathsworn to end her life.
Belavierr whispers a bargain to Rehanna Salesmith, who turns white and flees, and Belavierr then stands still for nearly an hour until she says "I see".
Belavierr tells Ryoka the first thinking Cloth Golems, the String-people, were made by [Golem Artificers], [Weavers], [High Mages] and [Witches].
Belavierr sniffs Ryoka and says she vaguely smells like her nemesis and the mice she has sworn to kill.
Belavierr agrees to stop stitch-magic for two hundred years at Wiskeria's request, but refuses to stop making bargains such as Rehanna's.
Belavierr claims she does not remember Ostevien, then recalls a boy when Wiskeria names him.
Belavierr tells Alevica to take eyes and make a necklace of fingers if she wants to be feared and strong.
Belavierr unravels every stitch within three hundred feet when Beatica confronts her, and then sews Ryoka's lips shut with thread that cannot be cut.
Belavierr tells the crow-witch Mavika that Mavika knows better than to earn her grudge.

section: Hunted by the Order of Seasons
text: Belavierr's ward needle snaps, and she says death is hunting her by flame.

section: Hunted by the Order of Seasons
text: Belavierr stands against Ser Raim and six [Witch Hunters] who ordain her death, and asks whether she knows him.

section: Hunted by the Order of Seasons
text: Belavierr dismounts and returns to protect Wiskeria after Raim swears she lives if Belavierr returns.

section: Hunted by the Order of Seasons
text: Belavierr fights Ser Raim as his flames consume them both and she burns, in front of the village.

section: Hunted by the Order of Seasons
text: Belavierr flees on a bare horse, and the half-Elf Sylind's Skill lets the [Witch Hunters] track her.

section: Hunted by the Order of Seasons
text: Belavierr vows to break the Order of Seasons' stronghold and slay their families generation by generation if her daughter is killed.

section: Hunted by the Order of Seasons
text: Belavierr says she has never considered the Order of Seasons her enemy, but offers war if they wish it.
Belavierr draws the leftover puppet cloth into her dress, leaving only the metal weapons on the field.
Belavierr restitches the dissolving cloud and calls down a storm, while Califor, Eloise, Hedag and Mavika deflect lightning, comets and a [Flamestrike].
A dying spark of the [Flamestrike] seeks Belavierr and ignites her, and every flame afterward homes in on her.
Mavika says Belavierr is marked for death by flame, with a dead man's vengeance in each spark, and that Belavierr's wards will take weeks or months to mend.
Belavierr proposes to take Wiskeria out of the fire, saying she cannot halt it any more than her own death.
Belavierr believes Wiskeria's justice is a poor choice of craft, but that taking it from the villagers made her a [Witch] for a new era of law.
Belavierr tells Ryoka that Wiskeria is a bright colour on dark cloth who matters to her tapestry.
Belavierr says she cut apart and rewove the Griffin Prince years ago, giving him protection against blades.
Belavierr claims she found a way to live and save Wiskeria by trading Nanette's ribbon, a life for a life.
Belavierr severs the coven's friendship, shrugs off their attacks, and tells Wiskeria she will remember the day she found her craft.
Belavierr says she swore to let Califor's daughter live in exchange for one great deed, nothing else.
Belavierr kisses Wiskeria's forehead and says she will watch her grow until the day she dies.
Belavierr stops Ryoka on a forest road and says Perril Chandler owes her a favour.
Belavierr offers Ryoka a way to see Ivolethe again for a small price, saying she wants no life.
Belavierr is the Stitch Witch of whom Laken sometimes dreams, lurking at the edges of his lands.
Belavierr receives a threaded [Message] in an empty village from the Necromancer and sews back "I agree. Later."
Belavierr knits something for her daughter and thinks that if she must be hated, the world should scream her name.
Belavierr waits in a lonely village near Invrisil and answers an adventurer's questions with "Yes", reversing spells and arrows.
Belavierr unweaves the magic of Todi's team and Griffon Hunt and flings Briganda through a wall.
Belavierr is shot twice by Halrac's fletchless arrows and says the bow is powerful, then sews the wounds shut.
Belavierr answers Halrac's question of why she did this with "Evil", and leaves the adventurers alive as witnesses.
Belavierr's name spreads through Invrisil after the night, and the legend of the Spider is rekindled.
Belavierr strings a living red sinew thread through a village and signs "BELAVIERR" in a web over the rooftops.
Belavierr says she cannot be killed with magicless shears and that the world has forgotten how to kill her.
Belavierr wants hunters sent so that her daughter will have strong foes.
Belavierr believes the era cares about those shown on scrying orbs and resolves to attack the Couriers.
Belavierr tells Magnolia that her thread is mixed and that Belavierr remembers when her family first stepped onto the land.
Belavierr tempts the Ladies with power and is encircled by hundreds of them, led by Maviola El and Magnolia Reinhart.
Zanthia and the Ladies name her Spider, Threadstealer, Stitch Witch and Temptress, and say she offers immortality for a soul.
The united Ladies cast Belavierr out with the word "Begone", and she walks away from Izril's north.
Belavierr arrives at Az'kerash's castle after being hunted, her protections mostly gone, and says she has come at his invitation.
Belavierr agrees to stay awhile at Az'kerash's castle after he offers an alliance and hospitality, saying they may strike a bargain.
Belavierr tells Az'kerash that she has a daughter already and addresses him as Peril Chandler.
Belavierr says the Stringfolk idea is not new, since she liberated sentient things that killed their masters.
Belavierr beats the Chosen Venitra with a black rope noose, and tears the Gnoll Kerash's arm off with binding spells.
Belavierr tells Az'kerash that he gave his Chosen arrogance, and that the skeleton is smarter than all the others.
Belavierr tells Az'kerash that she knows what creation she wants and will name it when the moment is right.
Belavierr tells Az'kerash "Wait. Wait to strike" when he asks about slaying great Kings.
Belavierr makes a perfect cloth Gnoll puppet Golem without a Golem's Heart, saying she wishes for a puppet and not a mind.
Belavierr says she would make a second child only if it were greater than she and Az'kerash combined.
Belavierr tells Az'kerash that the world is changing again and that she will weave a grander web with finer thread.
Mavika says Belavierr betrayed her kind by slaying Califor unprovoked.
Belgrade is an Antinium Worker and Individual, one of the five Antinium who survived protecting Erin from undead at her inn.
Belgrade is a [Tactician] who was a Worker, and has four arms like other Antinium.
Belgrade is a stickler for tactics and the openings Erin taught the Antinium, and plays chess defensively and cautiously.
Belgrade favours fixed formations and chokepoints, whereas Anand prefers roving strike forces, and Anand is considered the better player and [Tactician].
After the battle with Skinner, Belgrade is still too injured to move.
Belgrade and Anand give their levels to Pawn as fifteen and sixteen in answer to his question, and Belgrade admits he dislikes Klbkch's requirements of Pawn.
Belgrade wants to learn Go from Erin so as to beat Anand, because he feels Anand is a better player.
Belgrade says Anand was chosen to remain at Esthelm for his decisive and bold reactions, while he can only memorise patterns and repeat them.
Erin encourages Belgrade to study every chess move until he can adapt, and Zel Shivertail watches him closely.
Belgrade holds the Hive's tunnels against monsters from the dungeon, using his [Battlefield Eye] Skill and sending Workers by tunnel code such as L4A and R98.
Belgrade's front is made of countless tunnels, and he wishes he had a clear chess board to fight on instead.
Belgrade faces Crypt Worms and Shield Spiders, and two suits of enchanted armor that fell into the tunnel with his Soldiers.
A Worker turns Aberration beside Belgrade, kills another Worker and cuts off one of Belgrade's antennae in the struggle.
A monster takes both of Belgrade's left arms in the fighting, and he feels no pain.
Xrn stops Belgrade's bleeding with a warm touch that closes his injuries, and then leads him on while pushing monsters back.
Belgrade and Anand coordinate the Hive's defence in place of Klbkch and the Queen.
Belgrade reports that his static defences were overwhelmed in the lowest southeastern breach, but Anand had already redirected Pawn's division.
Belgrade supervises Workers who dismantle tunnels and bring blocks of stone, an unusual material for the Hive, to reshape the area near the dungeon.
At Level 20, Belgrade gains the Skills [Simple Trap Construction] and [Basic Fortification Construction], which suit static defence.
Belgrade credits Erin's lesson that practice can defeat talent, and says preparation wins battles in advance of reactionary tactics.
Belgrade and Anand share a strategy room with a chess board, an improvised Go board and Hive maps.
Belgrade nearly drowned two years ago when water burst through the Hive, and survived by holding his breath, as Antinium cannot swim.
Belgrade and Anand take over management of the Hive's defences from the Queen, freeing her mental space.
Klbkch, Pawn, Belgrade and Anand were consulted on whether Bird could meet Bevussa.
Belgrade says he has built six miles of traps from the Hive to the dungeon, which can eliminate most monster types.
Belgrade breaks down, telling Pawn that he has lost six thousand seven hundred and twenty-three Workers in engagements under his command.
Belgrade says Facestealer killed four hundred Workers whom he sent into a tunnel, and left their heads lined up.
Belgrade asks Pawn what he is now, his stoic demeanour gone, and Pawn takes him to Erin's inn to comfort him.
Belgrade leads Workers and Soldiers to rebuild the inn, ordering earthworks and signalling for a wall to come down.
Belgrade's team takes apart the inn's wall and begins reconstruction while guests are still present.
Belgrade arrives at the inn twenty minutes late after winning a chess game three times out of five against Anand for the right to visit.
Belgrade says he still does not like Dekass.
Lyonette had Belgrade design parts of the inn, and he went overboard with arrow slits and murder holes in the entryway.
Belgrade wanted a trapdoor, a pit of blades or water and a collapsible section in the inn, and Lyonette told him not to build them.
Belgrade has a new class, [Trapsetter Tactician], which he is very proud of.
Belgrade wants a floor trap in the new building at the inn, and Erin, Lyonette and Octavia tell him no traps.
Belgrade tells Octavia that in his breach scenario she is already dead.
Belgrade believes that sex can lead to pregnancy and fears all Antinium could become pregnant, so he goes to Garry for help with Anand and Yellow Splatters.
Belgrade says Chesacre and Thaina have informed him they are female, though he considers them names only.
Belgrade and the others offer a Drake coins for a demonstration of sex and he runs away shouting for the Watch.
Belgrade tells Erin he wants to try sexual intercourse because most Antinium never live past four years.
Erin promises Belgrade that he will live a long time and experience many things.
As a [Trapsetter Tactician], Belgrade directs Painted Soldiers and examines fortifications copied from adventurer tactics.
Xrn enchants Belgrade's barricades and authorises personal artifacts such as his bag of holding.
Belgrade bought a pickaxe from Gemhammer, moved a freezing trap rune out of the dungeon into a tunnel, and extracts enchanted spikes from a pit trap.
Most magic traps need mana and lose power outside the dungeon, and Lyonette will not let Belgrade install them in the hallway.
Beniar is a [Rider] who leads the Windfrozen Riders, one of two Silver-rank adventurer groups Laken hired to escort him and protect the village.
Laken finds Beniar a chatterbox and is glad to be rid of his company.
Beniar is a solid adventurer and Laken's cavalry leader who sometimes gives good advice, counted among Laken's advisors.
Later, Beniar is a [Cataphract] and [Captain] in the service of Laken Godart, wearing heavy mail with a scale-barded horse.
Beniar is a former Silver-rank adventurer who is now a [Captain] and [Cataphract].
Beniar wears full-body plate armor as a symbol of his class, and his steed wears mail too.
Beniar returns to Riverfarm half-dead with a poisoned arrow in his stomach, and healing potions only work partly.
Wiskeria tells Beniar's party to stop giving him healing potion because the poison blocks it and wastes the potion.
Beniar whispers to Laken that Goblins shot him and Fabiel while they were riding, and that Fabiel died at once.
Beniar reports that five Goblins ambushed them, rushed the horses and took Fabiel's mount, while he escaped.
Beniar tells Laken that average Goblins are no threat, but those around Invrisil are nasty because adventurers purge every tribe they find.
Beniar is up and about once the poison is flushed from his system and a healing potion revives him.
Beniar's [Cavalry], [Riders] and a lone [Cataphract] crash into the Goblin flank, killing a Hob with a lance through the armpit.
Beniar leaps from his horse and impales a Goblin [Shaman] with his sword, then hacks at it.
Laken's Skill [Blacksky Riders] lets chosen riders and their mounts see in the dark and dampen light, turning Beniar's mounted warriors into night ambushers.
Beniar's riders kill a bandit camp more than fifteen miles away, with Laken sensing the attack.
Beniar escorts a party of nobles through Laken's lands and says nothing enters the domain without the Emperor's knowledge.
Beniar smiles at the young noblewomen, who blush and fan themselves, and the nobles gather around him.
Beniar, armored, leads riders against Goblins in the night and orders them to pull back to Wiskeria.
Beniar races to Wiskeria to hear Allais's report.
Beniar leads Durene into the war tent, where General Wiskeria is, and is eager to charge the monsters.
Beniar leads his cavalry against the Goblins' unguarded right flank.
Redfang Goblins drop their disguises and surround Beniar's cavalry, forcing him to retreat.
Pyrite cuts down Beniar's horse and crumples his shield, armor and ribs with a battleaxe.
Beniar hugs Durene and leads fifteen riders after a trap on the street, in full plate.
Beniar tells Durene that the riders and militia are all that remain and demands that Wiskeria return.
Beniar says Frostwing tried to savage him when he fed her, and she pecks at his face when he reaches for her.
Beniar rides down the bandit leader Jek with his sword and routs the bandits with the Darksky Riders.
Beniar's riders shepherd five Goblins back toward the edge of their marked territory.
Lady Bethal Walchaís is a noblewoman of Izril who leads her own order of knights, the Knights of the Petal, whom she sometimes calls her Rose Knights.
Bethal is married to Sir Thomast, a [Chevalier], who stays largely silent beside her.
Magnolia Reinhart's letter to Laken calls Bethal a close friend of hers.
Lady Rie describes Bethal as commanding a knighthood whose Knights of the Petal are elite and quite dangerous.
Bethal is the last of her line, as Sir Kerrig says in Reizmelt.
Bethal is tall and thin with short hair, younger than Magnolia, with a spirited, loud and captivating voice.
Bethal wears a slashed yellow and red riding dress when she arrives in Reizmelt on holiday.
Bethal is famous for her temper, while her husband is known for his silence and lack of temper.
Bethal is called the [Lady of Thorns] for her [Aura of Thorns].
Bethal's aura turns spiky, like invisible edged blades, as people around her move away when she is angry.
Bethal casts [Tranquil Skies], which parts the clouds and the falling bolts and arrows in a circle of tranquility around her and her escort.
Bethal's Skill makes the air around her barbed, so anyone touching her against her will cuts themselves on something as sharp as steel.
Bethal's [Aura of Thorns] is powerful but cannot stop a crossbow bolt at close range.
Bethal wears a Ring of Sufferance on one finger.
Bethal's thorny aura turns real when she hisses in fury, cutting Ryoka's legs and Todel's arm until she pulls it back.
Bethal's [Aura of Thorns] only works if someone strikes at her, and it penetrates flesh and blood but not steel.
Laken senses Bethal's aura as a rose or bush covered in thorns that would sting him if he walked into it.
Cimeca says Bethal has a Skill that makes anyone who raises a hand against her suffer, which she learned during the Second Antinium War.
Rumor says Lord Elmha slapped Bethal at a ball six years earlier, tore half the flesh off his hand, and was later cut in the shoulder by Thomast in a duel.
Bethal quickly works out the value of Lupp's corn field in her head as about four gold, seven silver and five copper.
Bethal says that with the right Skills a business venture is hard to fail at, and harder with a husband like Thomast who is good with numbers.

section: Past and the Sacrifice of Roses
text: Bethal fought in the Second Antinium War and stood against Velan the Kind during the Sacrifice of Roses, where the Walchaís line ended in a single hour.

section: Past and the Sacrifice of Roses
text: Bethal says the Walchaís line walked through arrows and flames with pride and never stepped back, and First Landing stood at dawn.

section: Past and the Sacrifice of Roses
text: Bethal remembers losing her mother, Maisy, Lady Alvita, Eruvie and her father at First Landing as the Goblin King's charges broke the banners.

section: Past and the Sacrifice of Roses
text: Bethal remembers hiding among the dead when the Goblin King's hordes attacked First Landing.

section: Past and the Sacrifice of Roses
text: Bethal thinks that Goblins killed her father, her mother and her sisters.

section: Past and the Sacrifice of Roses
text: Bethal says she saw the Goblin King and met one of his Lords, and that Velan the Kind knew no mercy.

section: Past and the Sacrifice of Roses
text: Bethal insists the Goblin Lords all died out after their King fell or led their armies into oblivion.

section: Past and the Sacrifice of Roses
text: Sir Kerrig has known Bethal since she was a child and knows her passion and noble gestures are only half of her.

section: Past and the Sacrifice of Roses
text: Sir Kerrig says Bethal can be caring and compassionate or as uncaring as the sun, and is pragmatic.
Bethal confronts Magnolia over an [Assassin] her guards slew in her gardens two days earlier, and Magnolia denies sending it.
Magnolia drops Bethal and Thomast at Neunham, where the gates are smashed and bodies hang from house roofs after a Goblin raid.
Bethal brings half her Knights of the Petal, just over forty, to a hilltop to kill the Chieftain of the Flooded Waters tribe at Magnolia's personal request.
Bethal says the Goblins must be ended because they are disrupting trade and might join the Goblin Lord.
Bethal has accepted Welca Caveis, a knight-errant in training, into the ranks of her Rose Knights.
Bethal quits the Goblin hunt after two Rose Knights are pinned under a fallen tree, telling Thomast she wants to go home.
Bethal tells Magnolia by earring gem that she will not continue and is going back to her estate, then stomps on the earring.
Bethal complains that Lord Tyrion siphoned off soldiers the army needs before the battle with the Goblin Lord.
Bethal promised Magnolia not to enter the battle if she sees Thomast in trouble, as the condition for observing it.
Bethal reads a book on the Second Antinium Wars in a tent outside Invrisil the night before battle and is upset by its dismissal of the Human [Ladies].
Bethal declined Magnolia's offer of hospitality that night so she could stay with Thomast.
Thomast wants Bethal sent away from the battle so she will not try to save him, and Bethal bristles at being told to obey.
Bethal fell in love with Thomast after reading his open letter defending the Human women of the Sacrifice of Roses.
Bethal deliberately ran into Thomast and dirtied his clothes at a ball at Magnolia's estate to meet him.
Bethal is introduced to Laken with Thomast at his gathering and asks if Bismarck is tamed.
Laken notes that Bethal strikes him as a shark and that her spiky aura is not for show.
Bethal gasps when Ivolethe drinks the poisoned cup, and promises to investigate while assuring Laken that Magnolia was not responsible.
Bethal tells Laken that Magnolia does not use poison and intended the gathering as a test of him.
Bethal and Thomast suspect the poison was meant for her, and Bethal did not tell Magnolia so, to avoid worrying her.
Bethal says the Circle of Thorns has spies everywhere and may have planted the poison, or she may simply have enemies.
Bethal and Thomast were sent by Magnolia to kill Laken in a duel of honor if they found him too dangerous.
Bethal offers four thousand, then eight thousand gold for a trebuchet, dropping the bid when told Magnolia has an interest in them.
Bethal offers to buy ten trebuchets after Magnolia's and to pay in horses, offering a hundred head or six hundred.
Bethal travels with two Knights of the Petal and Thomast and says no brigand has ever troubled her.
Bethal tells Laken she is headed west by way of Yaist, a route she later admits was a lie.
Poisonbite remembers Bethal as the [Lady] who led pink-armored Knights against the Goblins, and Pyrite names her.
Goblins surround Bethal's party, and she sees a small Goblin on a large wolf aim a black crossbow at her heart.
Bethal wonders if Laken asked her direction because he knew of the Goblins, admitting that she and Thomast should not have lied to him.
Bethal agrees to be a prisoner of the Goblins, with Thomast, Sir Nil and Dame Truvia by her side, and learns that Goblins can weep.
Bethal tells Magnolia over the earring that she thinks it hurts differently each time.
Bethal arrives in Reizmelt on holiday escorted by Sir Kerrig and Lady Welca Caveis in rose-pink armor.
Bethal says the black rose once meant something else, but after the Goblin King it became a symbol of cowardice sent to peers who fled.
Bethal says half the nobles who received the black rose after Velan was slain killed themselves from shame.
Bethal believes her peers sent her the black roses to call her a coward for siding with Magnolia and condemning Tyrion Veltras at Liscor.
Bethal bleeds as she grips the rose, and the Runners and the street kneel as she weeps.
Bethal orders Thomast to bring his good sword and her Knights of the Petal to arm and mount, and sends the message "this is war".
Bethal's aura cuts Ryoka and Todel when Bethal hisses at them, and Thomast tells her to pull it back.
Bethal rides a speckled pale grey and white mare, escorted by Sir Kerrig and Welca Caveis.
Bethal thinks someone asked the Runners to send the roses, perhaps the Circle of Thorns and not Tyrion.
Bethal blames Magnolia for pulling her in, but says she agreed to help to avoid war with the Drakes.
Bethal eats an ear of Lupp's corn, calls it the finest she has eaten, and offers to sell his harvest to a [Merchant] who caters to [Chefs].
Bethal says she could get a silver or at least seven copper per ear, then discovers Lupp sells his field for less than five gold.
Bethal gives Lupp an advance in gold, which makes him faint, and promises a Runner and a Merchant's Guild contract in about three days.
Bethal wants a more secure communication method than [Message] spells and plans to ask Magnolia for an artifact or use Knights as couriers.
Bethal sends word to her Grandmaster of the Rose, Sir Nathald, and the Order of the Petal rides to war against her peers over the roses.
Bethal also suffers an unrelated, unknown assassination attempt on the day she receives the black rose.
Bethal reclaims her bareback mare, which Maviola stole, and calls Maviola a thief.
Thomast pickpockets Maviola's money pouch as turnabout for Bethal's mare.
Bethal rides to Liscor with a group of friends and Knights of the Petal, planning to stay the night at Magnolia's and visit a [Seamstress].
Maviola throws a bucket of animal waste at Bethal, and Thomast takes most of it.
Bethal stands furious over Maviola as the [Lady of Thorns].
Bethal and Maviola declare themselves quits after a tense exchange and shake hands.
Bethal laughs when a Fortress Beaver wanders out of the kitchen at Erin's inn.
Bethal says she and Thomast will stay at the Player's Retreat, while Sir Kerrig and the Knights of the Petal guard the inn.
Six Knights of the Petal, including Kerrig, Nil and Welca, guard the inn.
Bevussa Slenderscale is a Garuda adventurer of the Wings of Pallass with spring-green feathers patterned with white and pink down her arms and legs.
Bevussa is adopted: her Garuda people live almost entirely on Chandrar, but Drakes in Pallass took her in after she was abandoned as a chick.
Bevussa says she was born and raised by Drakes, and heard stories of the sky all her life from the library and from Garuda she met.
Bevussa is Gold-rank and the real captain of the Wings of Pallass.
Bevussa's feet are sharp talons, and she kicks with them.
Bevussa has a recall Skill that lets her call her thrown sword back with "Return!".
Bevussa plucks a feather from herself when she has stray ones she expects to lose.
Bevussa notes that alcohol runs through Garuda faster than other races.
Bevussa says she got onto the team because she can fly, and that the other members are Oldblood Drakes.
Bevussa's team members include Issa, Zassil, Kin and others, and Issa admires her greatly.
Issa publicly poses as captain of the Wings of Pallass, since it would not do for a Garuda to lead a team of Oldblood Drakes.
Later, Bevussa introduces herself as only second-in-command of the Wings of Pallass.
Later, it is an open secret that Bevussa is the real captain and Zassil is the official Drake captain, for reasons of Pallass politics.
A Pallassian Drake strokes Bevussa's feathers at a reception, and Bevussa keeps a perfect smile while hating such events.
Bevussa tells Grimalkin she is only a "member" of the Wings, not Captain, outside the room.
Bevussa introduces herself to Erin as an adventurer sent by duty to the dungeon her team had held back from entering.
Bevussa tells Erin the dungeon had been unnaturally quiet, with little action for her team.
Bevussa drops from the ceiling to kick a Stone Starer's eye while Issa and Zassil kill a second Stone Starer.
Bevussa says Halrac is not far from Named Adventurer.
Bevussa says she cannot stand the inn her team stays at, though Keldrass defends the Tailless Thief's food.
Bevussa is jailed for a day for punching people at the Adventurer's Guild over the lottery, with Keldrass in the next cell.
Bevussa negotiates artifact shares with the Halfseekers and complains to Erin that Jelaqua is suddenly calm about gold.
Bevussa trades one plucked feather for all the goose feathers Bird holds, and he says he will treasure it forever.
Bevussa tells Bird she has been known to snack on ants.
Bevussa tells Earlia's team that three horn blasts mean run for the exit as Shield Spiders come in waves, and one long blast means the Facestealer.
Bevussa says the Facestealer rarely strikes, and that Gold-rank teams plan to pin it down and melt it at range.
Bevussa tells Ceria the Wings are sticking with the dungeon, where the real gold is, instead of the Council's new bounties.
Bevussa sets up the door to the purple Bloodfields stone and addresses workers at the edge of the Bloodfields.
Bevussa warns that all the Bloodfields' creatures, even the rabbits, are dangerous, and orders workers to stay two miles from its nearest visible edge.
Bevussa tells Keldrass she has fought Goblins as much as he has, but not all Goblins are bad, so not all [Necromancers] need be.
Bevussa orders civilian fliers to land because flying makes them targets, and leads the Wings against Wyverns.
A Wyvern drops on Bevussa and she falls tangled with it as the other Wings fight a second Wyvern.
Bevussa reports no casualties among the Wings, with Kin's torn wing expected to heal, and says she leveled from the fighting.
Bevussa waits in a comfortable chair in a waiting room to be heard before Pallass's Command.
Beycalt Newman is a woman [Builder] and [Forewoman] who leads a crew of builders working in Riverfarm.
Beycalt says her name is Newman, but that she is without a man.
Beycalt has calluses nearly as tough as Durene's own skin.
Beycalt is a former Street Runner, though that was years ago.
Beycalt raises an eyebrow when Ram says Durene and a few hands can lift a load-bearing beam without ropes, and asks if he is sure.
Beycalt blinks as Durene pushes the heavy beam upright by herself, and then stares at her with amazement and fear.
Beycalt recognises Durene from the army at Lancrel and says she saw her smash at least thirty Goblins before the survivors got away.
Beycalt thanks Durene when Durene apologises for Lancrel.
Beycalt tells Mister Felp that rain does not affect building, and that a house can be raised in an hour with Durene's help.
Beycalt leads builders who came to Riverfarm from Lancrel, and Durene dislikes how quick most of them are to complain about the rain.
Beycalt answers "Death" with a hard voice when Hedag asks what should be done to the one who struck the blow, in the judgment of the [Thief] Elmmet.
Beycalt is among the people Prost calls on to get their folk working when he clears the street.
Beycalt keeps a spear-fishing friend from wandering off to pursue his passion, arguing good-naturedly with him.
Beycalt, Ram and Beniar's [Riders] follow Prost as he confronts the [Witch] Belavierr in the street.
Beycalt drinks and eats with Hedag and other laborers, and brightens at the generous drinks Hedag pours.
Hedag challenges Beycalt to an arm-wrestling competition.
Emperor Laken names Beycalt his [Construction Supervisor] in front of Riverfarm, confirming the authority she already held under Prost.
Beycalt's eyes bulge and she stammers when Laken addresses her by name, saying he has heard good things of her.
Beza is a Minotauress [Spellscribe] and a graduate of Wistram, introducing herself as Bezale of Maweil.
Beza is taller than most species and has an incredible physique for a [Mage], second only to Grimalkin.
Beza specializes in combat scrolls, and scribing is a rarer specialization even in Wistram.
Beza sells [Light] scrolls at about a gold each, and also Tier 4 scrolls, to [Merchants] more than pedestrians.
Beza says that to scribe a higher-Tier spell, a [Mage] generally has to be able to cast two tiers higher.
Beza keeps a small rack of combat scrolls, among them [Stoneskin] and [Haste], watched like a hawk.
Beza came eighth in Grimalkin's lifting contest and calls it disgraceful.
Beza develops a compulsion for working out with Grimalkin's weights.
Beza claims Minotaurs are naturally stronger than any other race and make siege weapons that few understand.
Beza says the House of Minos is a peaceful utopia for those who do not wish to leave its islands.
Beza says honor is the one virtue above all in Minos, and that those above judge those below, but everyone also acts by conscience.
Beza says Minos's King is a title and the King is a female paragon of honor, and that Queen would make others ask about marriage.
Beza says Minotaurs are in an ancient conflict with Goblins, and that Goblin power persists after thousands of years.
Beza lists the paradises of the age as Khelt, the Kingdom of Keys, Heiste the Archmage's Isle, the Silent Dome of the Dullahans and the House of Minos.
Beza left Minos because she lacked the magical ability for the role she wanted, and went to Wistram instead.
Beza says she left to explore the world, show honor, and return to Minos a hero.
Beza says she was carried off the battlefield while the adventurers slew an Adult Creler, and feels she was worse than those who stayed and died.
Beza says that someday she will return to the House of Minos with a story as a gift to her people.
Beza tells Calruz she came to arrest a criminal and see justice done, and claims the right of every Minos to judge another.
Calruz asks whether Beza is an arbiter of the isles, and she hesitates, which answers him.
Beza follows Montressa to hunt Pisces, saying some things cannot be forgiven, despite Palt's plea.
Beza yields to Yvlon in the duel after dropping a scroll with one arm hanging limp.
Beza casts [Stone Skin], [Haste] and [Lion's Strength] from scrolls on the frontline warriors against the Crelers, spending her fortune in scrolls.
Beza says she has orders to watch the inn too, and puts an arm around Montressa, promising not to abandon her.
Beza, Montressa and Palt claim new rooms in the inn, and after the party all three cast [Deafness] on themselves.
Beza overhears Earthers arguing whether the pizza tastes like home, and she suggests grabbing them, but Montressa urges waiting and making an offer.
Beza casts [Calm] on individuals during the riot, grabs Erin, and uses [Iron Skin] and [Haste] to cover Palt and Montressa.
Beza and Montressa decide to build connections by introducing Master Hedault to Erin.
Beza and Montressa act as gatekeepers of the door, brokering businesses between cities, with Cedava of Invrisil as client number six.
Beza and Montressa's first client was Rufelt and Lasica, then Pelt, then Hedault.
Beza brings a scrying orb to Calruz's cell to show the House of Minos going to war, and sits cross-legged beside him.
Beza has visited Calruz twice before.
Bezha is a veiled senior woman of Clan Tannousin, introduced by Silmak under the full name Bezhavil.
Bezhavil is Silmak's aunt second-removed and oversees the womenfolk and manages the Tannousin caravan.
Bezha is the aunt of Hesseif, the caravan's chief guard.
Nawal thinks of Bezhavil as her aunt, and Bezha calls Nawal by the affectionate name Nawali.
Bezha has tattooed hands, as Silmak does.
Bezha is old enough to be lined of face.
Bezha has helped to care for Nawal and her brother since they were children.
Bezha, Silmak and Hesseif have all known Nawal since she was a child, and the clan hoped they could rein her sharp tongue in.
Bezha tells Nawal to mind her tongue before the King of Destruction, and Nawal bristles that she knows she is a woman.
Bezha smacks Nawal on the back of the neck for saying the Tannousin are due respect from the King of Destruction.
Bezha promises Nawal the clan's support, and says she will see to the caravan and find work for its members in Reim if there is any.
Bezha screams at Nawal outside the forge for challenging Master Daiton to a contest, and takes swings at her face.
Bezha studies a puck and bar of Daiton's steel with Silmak and recoils at the soot and grain, which suggests the metal is inferior.
Bezha closes her eyes but does not argue when Silmak and Hesseif ask Nawal whether she can forge a sword that day.
Bezha tells Trey that Tannousin smiths are trained to hold their breath, and that Nawal has learned her forging pattern since she could hold a hammer.
Bezha catches Nawal when she staggers after finishing the forging.
After Nawal faints, Bezha wakes her gently with a stamina potion diluted in water, and tells her the King has mentioned her name.
Bezha gestures Nawal down to her seat as mages walk past in the banquet hall.
Trey, who nearly gets tackled by Hesseif and Bezha when he catches Nawal fainting, thinks Bezha may or may not be Nawal's mother.
Bezhavil is appalled and afraid when Nawal proposes telling Flos the clan has been pretending, since the King of Destruction's wrath is feared.
Bezhavil suggests the clan claim that Nawal's youth and inexperience as a female smith is what delays the Naq-Alrama steel.
Bezhavil kicks the back of Nawal's heels when Nawal babbles a great promise to Lord Venith.
Bird is an Antinium Worker and Individual who lives at The Wandering Inn, where he hunts birds with a bow from a tower on the roof.
Bird is both a [Bird Hunter] and a [Singer], and his voice carries across the Floodplains.
Bird says that he is two years old and will be three sometime in the fall.
Bird says he is named Bird after Henry Edward Bird, a Human chess player who invented Bird's Opening and Bird's Defense.

section: Early life and the battle with Skinner (Books 1-2)
text: A wounded Worker with a missing antenna and two fingers gives Erin her own healing potion during the undead attack, then tells her his name is Bird.

section: Early life and the battle with Skinner (Books 1-2)
text: Bird is one of the four Workers who survive the battle against Skinner and the undead.

section: Early life and the battle with Skinner (Books 1-2)
text: Bird, Belgrade, Anand, Garry and Pawn are the five Antinium who survive after a group of Workers gave their lives to protect Erin from undead.

section: Early life and the battle with Skinner (Books 1-2)
text: Bird becomes the guardian or minder of the Antinium Workers whom Klbkch brings to the inn.
Bird has a short bow and homemade arrows, because Antinium rarely use ranged weapons and he built his own gear.
Bird drinks a mug of five raw eggs, and says that he shoots birds because shooting them is enjoyable.
Bird says he contributes about 261% of the food value of an average Worker, and the Hive considers him a war asset of undetermined value.
Bird is permitted to act autonomously because of his Individual nature, levels and unique class.
Bird says he has no Skills at this point.
Erin offers to cook Bird's birds for free, and Bird is stunned that she would cook birds for him.
Bird's sack holds birds that have been dead for two weeks and are crawling with things, and Erin makes him throw it into the snow.
Bird says his Hive considers freshness irrelevant for birds, but Erin tells him to bring only fresh birds, preserved in ice, to her inn.
Pawn and Bird come through the magic door looking for Erin, with Bird carrying a small pterodactyl-like dead bird and saying his birds are not rotten.
Erin proposes that Bird guard her inn, shoot birds and have his own room, and Bird accepts the duty after Revalantor Klbkch informed him of it.
Bird blurts out that Pawn was to be assigned to combat duty that day and wanted to talk with Erin in case he perished, which silences the room.
Bird introduces himself to Erin's guests as an Antinium who shoots birds, and eats a freshly shot bird raw.
Bird tells Pawn that he wants his tower to be high so that he can shoot birds.
Bird becomes a permanent fixture of the inn, sitting on the roof where the third floor and new wing are being built.
Bird gets a new bow and suggests that a ballista could kill many birds at once.
Bird tells Pawn that social obligations force him to drink with Pawn and Erin, and suspects it is a trap.
Bird shoots an arrow at Regrika that snaps on her forehead, then throws a bucket of outhouse feces over her to irritate her.
Regrika rages and chases Bird out the door, but later returns without his blood on her blade, so he survives.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird's [Eagle Eyes] Skill, based on a bird, lets him spot six Hobgoblins crossing the plains from his tower.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird decides that Erin's sign not to kill Goblins says nothing about Hobgoblins, and shoots with [Long Range Shot] at over eight hundred feet.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird says Halrac taught him how to shoot.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird uses [Homing Shot] against Badarrow, the Goblin archer.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird is struck below the neck by a fifth arrow and tumbles off the tower roof into a long drop.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird recovers with his chest wounds healed by Lyonette's potions, and an arrowhead stays lodged in his carapace without bothering him.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird resumes shooting goats with curving arrows, and tells Erin the Hobgoblins shot him and that Lyonette had healing potions.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird tells Erin to be shush when she interrupts Klbkch's story of the Antinium Wars.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Erin asked Bird to watch for trouble from Drakes, and he has already chased away four Drakes at night.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird has a private room by the tower stairs, but never sleeps in its bed because Antinium shell backs make beds uncomfortable.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Erin made Bird a cubbyhole of blankets, but he is afraid of its luxury and spends most nights with his back against a wall.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird chased off a few Drakes by shooting arrows at their feet when they approached the inn after midnight.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird, sitting in the rain, hopes there are fish birds, and sings a song about being wet.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird forgets to close the tower door, and rainwater floods the inn's third floor.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird tells Erin that he likes high places, and says he will guard against birds and other threats from above while other guards guard the ground.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird calls popcorn bird bait and accepts a bowl from Erin.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird eats a big bowl of scrambled eggs, which he calls bird babies.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: While guarding Mrsha outdoors, Bird kills the eighth bird of the last hour.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird shoots down Face-Eater Moths from the inn's tower and realises there could be too many birds.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: After the moth attack, Bird has been sliced all over, and his bow, tower door and tower are broken.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Badarrow smashes Erin's healing potion over Bird's chest, and Bird fetches his old crude bow as a spare.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird gets a new bow Skill that has a cooldown and works with his old crude bow, and Erin thanks him for a good shot at a tentacled sea creature.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird says the moths broke the lovely bow Erin gave him, and is sorry.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird used the coins he was paid as bird bait because they are shiny, and Erin decides to save up money for his bow.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird learns [Piercing Shot] and keeps watch from his tower, waiting for water birds, with his homemade bow after the other one broke.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Erin tells Bird to come down at least twice a day for food, and he cannot eat bread.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird plays chess to draw a crow on the board, to the confusion of Anand, Belgrade, Garry and Pawn.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird says he refuses when Erin asks him to play chess, though she says he is always weird to play and likes it when he wins.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird tells the Free Queen that he does not want to stay in the Hive and wants to go back to the inn to hunt birds.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird refuses to be fixed, saying that if he were fixed he would not be Bird, and promises to return with a bird to sing for the Queen.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird reaches [Singer] Level 7 and obtains the Skill [Soothing Melody].

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird buys the highest-quality bow in Krshia's cousin's shop with a large budget the Antinium Queen allocated after her interview with him.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird sees Raskghar and Cave Goblins coming from the water toward the inn, raises the alarm and shoots them, including with a [Homing Shot].

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird does not understand why he was shooting at Mister Halrac, and starts rocking and repeating that he is sorry when Erin tells him how bad it was.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird says he shot at Raskghar when he found Lyonette on the ground, and then blames himself over Mrsha's disappearance.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird sets out alone into the dungeon to find Mrsha and Ceria, saying he must do a good thing after doing bad things.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Yvlon finds Bird trapped under a dead Face-Eater Moth, singing about no birds underground, with a crushed left leg.

section: The Goblins, the moths and the flood (Books 6-8)
text: Bird says he killed the monsters around him with his new bow until he ran out of arrows, then with a hunting knife.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird tells a visitor that Klbkch assigned him to the inn for security and a purpose he is not allowed to reveal.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird explains that Workers with names are Individuals, and nameless Workers who do not answer are Aberrations that Klbkch or Soldiers kill.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird believes water birds must exist and has been hoping to see one, but he has not yet.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird insists that Garuda such as Bevussa are birds because they have wings and fly, and that bats and moths are birds too.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird keeps Bevussa's green and blue feather in his room, where he dreams of flying and shooting cloud-sized birds.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird fires arrows from the inn's tower at Greydath during the Redfangs' fight, and none of his arrows can hit the Goblin Lord.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird fires a [Piercing Shot] at Greydath's head, aimed at his left eye.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: The tower collapses, and Bird lies on the grass with both left arms and his left shoulder torn away and green blood pooling.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird tells Erin he is dying, and potions cannot stop the blood pumping from his chest.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird clings to his bow while the Redfangs carry him through Liscor to the Hive.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Klbkch tells Erin that Bird has no chance without his Queen, and orders Soldiers to carry him to her.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Antinium have no arteries or closed circulation, so healing potions cannot stop Bird's bleeding and the Queen can only restore his blood.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird asks permission to cry, and the Free Queen tells him that Antinium cannot cry.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird says "Waah" over and over, and Klbkch realises he has learned to cry.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird survives, badly maimed, and the Free Queen cradles him.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird lies propped on his fortress of fluff, which Erin gave him, with his left side covered in a green substance.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird takes up residence in the Queen's chambers and distracts her with stories and songs.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird asks Garry to promise twice, because Erin told him a double promise is better than a single one.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Garry warns Bird that cake has gluten, which he cannot eat, and the Free Queen allows him one small piece anyway.

section: Bird in the Hive and the Greydath attack (Book 9)
text: Bird tells the Free Queen that he hears laughter from the Soldiers and that she is laughing too.
Bird says Bessachidia's name aloud, having heard it in the Free Queen's thoughts like a distant bird flapping.
The Free Queen says that Bird also heard her and the Soldiers at the battle with the Goblin Lord, and Bird says they were laughing.
The Free Queen calls Bird a True Antinium and one of five true Individuals, and says Bessachidia also sang.
The Free Queen cannot bring herself to kill and dissect Bird, and tells him to grow his legs and arms, return to the inn and stay out of her reach.
The Free Queen says she will take his body and find out what makes him a True Antinium when he dies.
Bird returns whole, with four arms, two legs, a new carapace and a new bow, and shoots Montressa, Isceil and Beza.
Bird tells Erin his tower was exploded by a Goblin with a sword and asks for it back.
Erin hugs Bird, and Bird pats her on the head.
Bird returns home to the inn, sits in a tower of nailed boards he built himself on the unfinished roof, and shoots bats.
Bird sits in a small new tower of nailed planks on top of the inn, which has yet to be rebuilt.
Bird has the Skills [Lure Song] and [Prey Sense], and local [Hunters] now head west because no one catches much near Bird.
Bird shoots with four arms faster than regular [Archers] and misses a bird nearly three hundred feet away, blaming his poor aim.
Bird says that Garry wished to be employed as a [Cook] but the Queen refused.
Bird shoots a Creler off the fleeing Ishkr, raises the alarm, and leaps off the roof.
Bird furiously attacks Ksmvr for bringing the Crelers, shouting that his tower is always broken.
Bird apologises afterwards, and Erin tells him that they can rebuild.
Bird sits in a ramshackle tower on the inn roof, and asks the Workers to build a tower twice as tall as the city.
Bird leaves the inn and walks Pallass's streets shooting Wyverns with [Homing Shot] and [Long-Range Shot].
Unseen arrows repeatedly hit the Wyvern Lord's eye and nostril without piercing, and it flees south with about three hundred Wyverns left.
The world sees Bird standing on a dead Wyvern eating a charred wing, an Antinium in a Walled City.
Bird shouts that he is Prognugator of the Free Antinium and asks Grimalkin if it is war, repeating a lie from Ksmvr.
Watchers conclude that Bird is a new Prognugator built to hunt flyers, and Az'kerash calls him a new Centenium.
Klbkch states that Bird is not a Prognugator and is lying, but no one in the world believes him.
On top of his tower, Bird says life is very sad today because the big birds are gone.
Bird repeats "Is it war?" while standing on the dead Wyvern before Pallass's archers, Grimalkin, Chaldion, Duln and Saliss.
Bird walks into the inn carrying a Wyvern wing he severed and gnaws on it.
Bird now has a bigger room than his old one, and Lyonette helped him remake his Fortress of Fluff.
Bird still has Bevussa's feather after the inn's destruction destroyed some of his others.
Bird has a Level 8 [Tactician] class.
Erin and Lyonette forbid Bird to hunt or eat birds, including eggs, for a week.
Bird throws a tantrum with fake crying, and Erin has to hush him with her aura.
When Erin reminds him of the first time he came to the inn, Bird says "I am Knight".
Bird accepts the punishment after Erin speaks to him seriously, and apologises for causing trouble.
Ilvriss reflects that Bird the Hunter is already being written into security briefings as a new Prognugator.
Numbtongue and Bird secretly eat eggs and chicken with five days of Bird's punishment left, and Erin threatens to extend it.
Bird gives up the plate and begs not to be punished too long.
Bird beats Olesm at chess in a game whose final pieces look like a bird.
Bird stands in a gap in the circle of Worker statues and says "I belong here".
Bird says that Pawn, Anand, Garry and Belgrade should see the statues, as it will make them sad and happy.
Bird goes mining with Numbtongue and Octavia, saying he is going to hit rocks, which Numbtongue assured him is fun.
Bird has memorised every chess opening Erin knows, and can recreate immortal games piece by piece.
Bird lets Mrsha shoot his bow, and goes on little trips with Numbtongue and sometimes Octavia.
Bird asks the Workers finishing the second floor their names and feeds goat's cheese to Archer B12, an Autonomous Worker.
Bird tells Anand that Klbkch is stupid and not his father, after Erin called Klbkch mean and wrong.
Bird leads Pawn, Yellow Splatters, Belgrade, Anand, Garry and the Painted Antinium out of the Hive to the inn, along with Tersk and Dekass.
Bird thanks the Free Queen, saying that she told him she would kill him if he returned.
Bird declares "I am quitting my Hive" and "Klbkch does not rule me".
Bird flies for fourteen seconds later that day after Viceria's Sage's Grass spell.
Bird is unbanned from hunting birds, and eats a bird on the roof, saying he has fulfilled his obsession.
Bird feeds the Archer Workers on the new tower, and tells them that good is a feeling that lasts when happy is gone.
Bird joins Numbtongue and Mrsha's Bee Rescue Team and baits fishing hooks at a pond in the High Passes.
Bird makes birdhouses to cultivate more birds after the Druids' lesson, and asks Lyonette to buy him a ballista.
Bird once took first place at an indoor archery range in Liscor.
Bird stays in his tower at full vigilance with bow and arrows in all four hands, and eats only when Erin feeds him.
Bishop is the name chosen by an Antinium Worker who joins the Workers guarding Erin's inn when the dead are coming.
Bishop declares that he has chosen a name and is individual, the same moment the other Workers announce names such as Vladimir, Calabrian, Emanuel, Garry and Milner-Barry.
Knight tells Erin the Workers have chosen to be individual, and that Pawn was kept in the Hive by the Prognugator.
Pawn says that Bishop named himself in the battle for Liscor and died there.
Anand introduces a Worker named Bishop to Pawn, a Worker who holds a clipboard that is a nail board.
Pawn rejects the new Worker's name and insists that the name Bishop belonged to the Antinium who died in the battle for Liscor.
Anand tells Pawn that he allowed this Worker to take the name Bishop, and that two Antinium may share a name.
Anand tells Pawn that the name belongs to both Bishops and that the earlier Bishop would not have begrudged it.
The new Bishop shudders when Pawn rejects his name, and Pawn's anger subsides when he sees him.
Pawn apologises, and Bishop says he bears no ill will.
Anand says Bishop is the closest of the Autonomous Workers to being truly Individual, because Anand plays chess with him and Bishop helps him.
Bishop tells Pawn he will try his best to become worthy of the name Bishop, and Pawn thanks him.
[BlackMage] is the screen name of the user who sets up the magical phone chat connecting Earth people in the new world.
BlackMage's real name is Aaron Vanwell, but within Wistram Academy he goes by Blackmage and hardly anyone uses his real name.
BlackMage says he thought up the phone connection but that it takes a lot of magical power, and that he used a chat because many voices at once would be too confusing.
BlackMage says he is a Level 11 [Engineer] and a Level 8 [Mage], and that this is how he set up the call.
BlackMage says he got the [Engineer] class by taking apart his iPhone and some of his electronics.
BlackMage relays that some people on his end say no one has gotten the [Hero] class in centuries.
BlackMage tells the chat that a person needs to be activated by another magic-user, because not everyone has the potential to do magic.
BlackMage warns the chat that the mage he is with says first and last names can be used to scry on a person's location and appearance.
Kent Scott deduces that only one group could cast a spell reaching across the world and tells BlackMage he is in Wistram Academy.

A young man with an English accent calls Ryoka Griffin's iPhone, introduces himself as [BlackMage] from the chat and asks if she is [batman], and Ryoka angrily rebukes him for making a call that could reveal locations.
BlackMage tells Ryoka that he and the mages of Wistram are trying to find people across the world and bring them to Wistram, and that they are using magic in secret.
BlackMage says he contacted Ryoka first because she uncovered [Kent Scott] as a fake and warned everyone.
When Laken takes the phone he tells BlackMage to call him "L", says he is from the same world and has just met [batman].
The narration gives his real name as Aaron Vanwell and says that months earlier he opened his college dorm door to get a pizza and found himself standing in a room with Golems.
He was brought to Cognita, who demanded to know how he came there, then summoned four Archmages who debated, cast magic on him and accepted his story, after which he entered Wistram and has not left.
Over eighty mages linked to perform the spell that he and Feor worked on for two weeks, after he tinkered with his phone to call other iPhones in this world.
By the time of the Halloween-style banquet he has reached Level 18 in [Mage].
Feor told Aaron never to use his real name in Wistram's halls once it was discovered that someone was scrying others by their real names.
His [Engineer] class comes from painstakingly taking apart his watch and iPhone and relying on Feor's [Repair] spell to put them back together.
Blackmage pays the Dullahan Beatrice with a secret written on a piece of paper, which she burns after reading, for distracting Teura for about twenty minutes so he can slip away.
Feor decides to cast a lock spell that stops Blackmage from speaking about confidential matters, but Archmage Naili tells him he is now with the Revivalists and has protectors and allies.
Aaron Vanwell is Wistram's first Earther guest and builds a battery combining magicore crystals with the principles of a lead-acid battery.
Archmage Nailihuaile helps Aaron make the orb, and he miniaturizes the battery into a glove painted red and gold.
Aaron puts on the glove and lightning arcs from it along a path he has created.
Aaron counts eighteen Earthers at Wistram so far and nine more on the way, and knows they are prisoners or well-treated guests who cannot leave the island.
Blackmage stands on a table aiming a wand at his own head and threatens to blow his head off to stop Nailihuaile introducing commercials and pay-per-view, and she gives in.
Aaron tells Elena about trying his shock glove, which sends lightning to the nearest metal thing, and they are at the Wistram buffet when every Golem freezes for about a minute before moving again.
Elena, a beautician and member of Feor's Centrist faction, mouths the word "Robots" to Aaron after the Golems freeze.
Naili is unhappy that the cake recipe leaked and suspects the Ullsinoi faction.
Aaron has found a secret room that he told no one about, including Nailihuaile, and which tracking spells cannot follow into.
Aaron hides artifacts under a floor hatch opened by an invisible latch that took him six hours to find, but he says he had been told it was there.
Aaron tells the other Earthers he thinks a ghost of an Archmage named Emerrhain, whom he met during the winter, is hiding in Wistram.
Archmage Amerys helped Aaron with magicore batteries, and he builds a magical sailboat for the [Sailor] Lamont using a Naili wind spell powered by a magicore battery.
Aaron pitches Mage Galei and Mage Taxiela on illusion combat scenarios and videogame-like entertainments, and Telim helps trial an undead scenario in which Aaron is declared out.
Elena says Aaron Vanwell, called Blackmage, was the first Earther at Wistram, has never left it, and is about nineteen, with around forty-one Earthers there, about half of them over eighteen.
The Blighted King wages an eternal war against monster tribes and demons on a continent far to the east across the seas.
His continent has known war for two hundred years, and he fights a daily war that he is losing over the course of years.
Other nations send their own armies to support the Blighted King.
The Blighted King's name is Othius the Fourth.
The Blighted King rules the kingdom of Rhir, and its [King] is known throughout the world.
In Book 18 the Blighted King is named King Othius IV and is shown as an extremely old Human who prolongs his life by magic and other methods.
The Blighted King's hair and eyes are pale grey-silver, and he looks faded.

section: The Fifth Wall and the summoned Heroes
text: The Blighted King greeted the summoned Earthers and told them they would be the heroes who drove the demons out of his kingdom.

section: The Fifth Wall and the summoned Heroes
text: The Blighted King gave the Earthers weapons and sent them out into battle, where they were slaughtered.

section: The Fifth Wall and the summoned Heroes
text: The Blighted King wants to build a Fifth Wall to push back the monsters and Demons, and for that he summoned the Earthers.

section: The Fifth Wall and the summoned Heroes
text: With powerful [Heroes] the Kingdom would have enough power to build another Wall and nearly double its available land.

section: The Fifth Wall and the summoned Heroes
text: The King's magicians summoned a group of children instead of legendary heroes, but all of them held the unknown class [Hero], which the King still pinned hopes on.

section: The Fifth Wall and the summoned Heroes
text: After the Earthers proved unable to fight, the King gave up on them and effectively exiled them from the capital city.
In 5 B.F., news from Rhir said that the Blighted King's armies were shattered in defeat after defeat and every Wall but the one protecting his capital was stormed.
The same history text calls the Blighted King the Demon King and says he was also pushed to the very brink of his territory.
After the Antinium vanished from the continent, news came that the Blighted King was rebuilding and his armies were already retaking his lost kingdom.
The palace of Rhir rises above the capital and is described as taller than any other building of its kind in the world.
The palace was designed by Dwarfs, added to year after year, and made never to be taken.
At the feast, the Blighted King and his Queen sit at one end of the room at a table with an ornate golden chair.
The Blighted King's voice is an old man's voice, tired and not grand.
Tom suspects Nereshal has been keeping the King young, and sees few grey hairs in his beard.
The Blighted Queen is younger than the King and, though not yet thirty by Tom's estimate, her towering height makes her seem older.
The King greeted the Earthers as the heroes of prophecy returned "diminished".
The King said that over sixty Earthers were sent to fight the Demons and now less than a third remain.
The King noted that one Earther has reached Level 30 in three months as a [Knight] sworn against darkness, yet no [Lord] or [Lady] has given him a title.
The King noted that a water [Mage] among the Earthers has taught herself.
The King offered the Earthers a place in his halls, food and his protection so long as they hold back the scourge of darkness.
The King said he had heard of a warrior who slew a Demon raiding party single-handed, and turned his eyes to Tom.
The King's throne room has black and white marble floors and stone beams overhead, on which guards with bows, arrows and wands stand.
The Blighted King's throne is made of twisted ivory, the bones of some ancient monsters carved into a huge seat and enchanted.
The King asked Tom whether [Clowns] are truly entertainers rather than warriors, and whether they fight.
Tom answered that [Clowns] have tricks suited for combat but are not warriors.
The King said the court searches for Skills and classes that might aid its people, and thanked Tom the [Clown].
The King invited Tom to join him in the gardens and said a suitable reward would be deliberated that night.
The King ordered Nereshal to summon the commander of the palace guard, saying failure must be met with appropriate punishment.
The King's young daughter, a Princess, said her father sent the soldiers away, all of them, and she did not like it.
The Fool told Tom that the King decided two days earlier to deploy every soldier to the Fourth Wall for an upcoming battle, except a few foreign regiments and the King's own guard.
The Fool said the decision was a secret known only to the King, his advisors and the Fool himself.
During the attack on the palace, the Blighted King's orders fill defenders of many species with strength so that their flesh is like iron.
The Fool held a knife at the King's throat in the courtyard while a hundred bows and [Mages] were trained on him.
The King stood still and calm and asked the Fool to explain why he betrayed his pledge of loyalty.
The King answered the Fool's accusation about the ritual by saying he does it for his people so that they may live.
Two of the Fool's thrown knives struck the Blighted King in the chest and the shoulder.
After the Fool's defeat, the Blighted King lay on the ground in the courtyard, breathing heavily but alive.
In Book 9 the King, listening to his steward, advisor and personal mage Nereshal, hears that several [Mages] protest the scope of a second ritual.
The King says Rhir's population can sustain ten times the cost of the ritual if needed.
The King decides the ritual must be done, citing the recorded Antinium evolving in strength and Demon spies and traitors in his kingdom.
The King says the summoned chosen ones erred as weak, timid children instead of warriors, but that they grow with guidance and must be raised with care.
The King tells Nereshal that those protesting the ritual will obey or be dealt with.
The King dreams that the Earther children's weapons that rain death from the sky will end the war with the Demons and purify Rhir.
The King sighs at the smell of rot and death on the air, which is the smell of home, and dreams of a day of only spring.
The first ritual sacrificed ten thousand of Rhir's children, in the King's words, for a hundred heroes.
Nereshal later concludes the ten thousand lives produced about a thousand children from Earth who were thrown across the world instead of arriving at their destination.
The King's earlier heirs, including his [Queens] and offspring, all died in battle, treachery or accident.
The Blighted King has a new [Queen] and two daughters, kept as insurance though their levels are too low.
Nereshal the [Chronomancer] is the Blighted King's most trusted confidant.
The King wears the deaths of his family on his face and body, which they have aged to grey.
The King has a hatred of the Demons that has allowed him to live so long and fight the endless war.
The King spat the name of the Fool like a curse, calling him the traitor who nearly ruined the kingdom.
