The King refuses a test of the spell and decides the second ritual will use a hundred thousand lives.
The King dreams of a day when he can walk past the walls and see no Demons and no Blight.
The King's [Mages] say the ritual cannot be altered and that it must use the unborn, after criminals, Demons, animals and slaves failed.
The Blighted Queen is the wife and consort of the Blighted King of Rhir.
The Blighted Queen is very tall, younger than the King, and cannot be more than thirty, though her height makes her seem older.
The Blighted Queen carries a long mace as black as obsidian.
A courtier says the Blighted Queen is at least as skilled a warrior as the champions dueling in the hall, and was known for her mace before marrying the King.
A lord says the Blighted Queen was a famed warrior on the battlefield before becoming Queen, which may be why the King was enamored of her.
The Blighted Queen is full of action and ready to move out when the Demons invade the palace.
The Blighted Queen tells the King that if the Demons are not repelled, all is lost.
The Blighted King refuses to send her with Nereshal to ambush the teleport mage, because losing Nereshal would bring the end closer.
The Blighted Queen volunteers to go and fight the Demons herself, mace in hand.
The Blighted Queen walks out into the courtyard with her mace drenched in gore, beside the King, ignoring Tom's boasts.
The Blighted Queen rushes at the Fool in the courtyard and blocks his thrown daggers with her mace.
The Blighted Queen trips on a juggling ball thrown by the Fool.
The Blighted Queen makes a sound of pain when the Fool's dagger draws blood at the King's throat.
Briganda is a scarred Human [Shield Maiden] in her late thirties, an original member of the Griffon Hunt, with a stocky, muscular build.
Briganda carries an enchanted hatchet and has split more monsters' heads with it than Revi could count.
Briganda has violet mixed into her brown hair, a hereditary trait from magic in her ancestry.
Briganda once would unapologetically kick her teammates out of the way to use the bathroom, and never took more than a minute to decide anything.
Briganda cannot swim.
Briganda has a young son, Cade, about four years old, with dark violet hair deeper than hers and fair skin.
Briganda keeps Cade occupied with a Box of Simulacra that releases a tiny illusionary Dragon with substance, which cost her an arm and a leg.
Briganda cautions Cade that if he breaks the things that come out of the box, he has to wait a long time for them to come back.
Cade expected Laken to wear a crown because Briganda had said he would, and Laken says he will have a circlet made when he has time.
Briganda finds Griffon Hunt after the team disbanded on a bad night, nearly two years since they last saw each other.
Briganda tells Halrac she has heard the survivors of the burned village all went to Riverfarm and joined the Unseen Empire, with some powerful noble, an actual [Emperor].
Griffon Hunt offers Briganda two thousand gold pieces for personal funds, with four thousand of the six thousand going back into the team's pool, as she would be part of the team.
Briganda rejoins Griffon Hunt, answering absolutely when Halrac asks her, and Revi hugs her.
Briganda charges Numbtongue with her axe and buckler when Cade screams about a Goblin, and she slams into the invisible barrier of the Garden of Sanctuary.
Briganda is the only one of the adventurers not used to Numbtongue, and the others try to grab her too late.
Briganda hacks at the invisible door with her enchanted axe, leaving marks, until the others pull her off.
Briganda apologizes to Numbtongue after Halrac tells her to, saying she reacted on hearing Cade scream.
Brilm is a Drake Wall Lord of Salazsar and a friend of Ilvriss, who is described as a childhood friend.
Brilm is a heavier Drake who dresses in a flamboyant red-and-orange outfit and is as energetic as Ilvriss is reserved.
Brilm wears rings on his claws and carries a bag of holding.
Brilm sniffs Balerosian powder from a box and sprinkles it on the carpet.
Later, Brilm is portly and jovial and toasts Ilvriss in Ilvriss' tower after the corruption scandal in the teleportation network is uncovered.
Brilm visits Ilvriss less than a week after Ilvriss returns from Liscor, and mentions a dinner party he is hosting.
Brilm sympathises with Ilvriss over losing Periss, his best subordinate.
Brilm says Zel Shivertail's army cut apart Salazsar's army and that Zel threw the Drakes over for the Humans at the end, and Ilvriss tells him it was not like that.
Brilm complains that Alrric showed him in with no courtesy and used his name, and asks why Ilvriss keeps him around.
Brilm says the magic door would be a treasure, useful for moving miners and trade, and that he and others leaned hard on Pallass over Ilvriss' travel.
Brilm shows Ilvriss a pink-shimmering quartz that holds a recording of a loud song, which Ilvriss finds horrendous.
Brilm plays a second, blue-glowing quartz holding a slow, soulful song that deeply moves Ilvriss.
Brilm says the song is called My Way, originally by Frank Sinatra, performed by the Queen of Pop, who is also called the Baroness of the Beats.
Brilm says the Queen of Pop is a nickname the singer chose for herself and that she is the [Singer] of Terandria.
Brilm notices the groove in Ilvriss' ring finger and asks whether he is getting married, and Ilvriss refuses to answer.
Brilm presses Ilvriss to say how he and Tasilt came to suspect the [Cargomaster], and Ilvriss refuses to say.
Brilm tells Alrric that the other Children of the Walls are wondering what activated Ilvriss' rings and that there are rumours.
Brilm asks Alrric whether Ilvriss has given the ring to a Gnoll, a Human or a Selphid, and says Alrric does not like him and he does not like Alrric.
Brilm says Ilvriss marrying a Gnoll would be bad for his reputation, remarking that old Zail would kill him.
Brilm advises that Ilvriss take a mistress, which would be a scandal but acceptable, and suggests Navine could be the one to marry.
Brunkr is a tall, muscular Gnoll warrior of the Silverfang Tribe, armed with a longsword and a large shield.
Brunkr is Krshia's nephew, and he calls her Aunt.
The narration of Mrsha's viewpoint calls Brunkr Krshia's cousin once, though Krshia calls him nephew in the same scene.
Brunkr ends sentences with "yes?" or "no?" tags when he speaks.
Brunkr is older than Lyonette, though not much older.

section: Arrival and the attack on the inn, Book 2
text: Brunkr arrives in Liscor with his brethren to guard and assist Krshia, his honoured aunt and the Silverfang clan leader's sister.

section: Arrival and the attack on the inn, Book 2
text: Brunkr grabs Erin's hand and calls her an enemy for harbouring the thief, whom he wants to see punished.

section: Arrival and the attack on the inn, Book 2
text: Krshia orders Brunkr to let Erin go and says Erin has made her choice.

section: Arrival and the attack on the inn, Book 2
text: Brunkr leads Gnolls against Erin's inn despite orders not to go after the thief.

section: Arrival and the attack on the inn, Book 2
text: Brunkr takes a [Power Strike] from Erin, gets back up and tells her she cannot do it more than once.

section: Arrival and the attack on the inn, Book 2
text: Brunkr says his aunt wants Erin alive but not unharmed, and he plans to teach her a lesson before dealing with the thief.

section: Arrival and the attack on the inn, Book 2
text: Brunkr tells Zevara that the Silverfang tribe will go to war against Liscor if anything happens to him.

section: Arrival and the attack on the inn, Book 2
text: Krshia seizes Brunkr by the ear, asks if he wants to become Chieftain already, and drags him off.

section: Arrival and the attack on the inn, Book 2
text: Brunkr shrinks in front of Krshia, though he is taller than her.

section: Arrival and the attack on the inn, Book 2
text: Brunkr introduces himself to Ryoka as a warrior of the Silverfang tribe at Krshia's shop.

section: Arrival and the attack on the inn, Book 2
text: Brunkr tells Mrsha that her tribe is gone and never coming back, because she brought disaster and is cursed.

section: Arrival and the attack on the inn, Book 2
text: Mrsha attacks Brunkr in response and bites him.
Krshia calls for Brunkr when Mrsha is in her apartment, and Mrsha goes very still at his name.
Brunkr enters with a foul-smelling bandaged hand, oozing and raw, and introduces himself to Klbkch.
Brunkr blames Mrsha for his hand and calls her Doombringer, Cursed one, Deathbringer and Calamity.
Brunkr says Mrsha took his hand just as she took her tribe, and that she is cursed.
Brunkr tells Erin to take her cursed doombringer away unless she wants to end up as he has.
Brunkr tells Erin that her cursed one bit him.
Brunkr's right forearm is swollen and oozing yellow pus from a bite, and the infection covers a good part of the forearm.
Brunkr asks Krshia whether it is time to cut his hand off.
Brunkr says a [Healer]'s poultice, his tribe's meat and his aunt's stews all did nothing, and he burnt the wound with fire.
Brunkr agrees to try Erin's treatment, saying he has nothing left to lose.
Brunkr keeps a honey-slathered bandage over his arm while Gnolls gather in Krshia's apartment.
Brunkr removes the bandage and holds a sword in his good hand when the Gnolls go out to face armed Drakes.
Octavia's mould, the honey and regular cleaning stop the gash leaking pus and it starts to heal.
Erin checks on Brunkr all week, and he is soon fit and eats half a cow.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr is a [Warrior], and says he is one of the best in his tribe.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr aspires to become a [Knight], but says the class requires something he does not have.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Erin asks Brunkr to train Lyonette, and perhaps Bird, with the sword, and hopes he makes up with Mrsha.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr teaches Lyonette how to hold and swing a sword, outside the inn in the cleared snow.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr is changed by his injury, no longer self-confident but a recovering [Warrior], grateful for his healing arm and quietly guilty.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr and Lyonette have both apologised, and a friendship begins once Brunkr learns Lyonette made his honey salve.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: The narration says Lyonette is the girl Brunkr had tried to kill.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr found a book in his youth about Human [Knights] in shining armour, and trained with sword and shield to be like them.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Lyonette says a [Knight] needs a [Lord] or other nobility to make him one.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr says no Gnoll has the [Knight] class, and he came north to help Krshia and to see if it was possible.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr gains the class [Knight] and says so proudly in front of Ryoka.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr's right arm has completely healed and he no longer wears a bandage.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr says he has his arm and debts to pay, and will be a [Knight] worthy of his class.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Krshia and Brunkr hold a celebration of his new class at Erin's inn.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Erin gives Brunkr a pink-frosted cake with [Knight] written on it.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr tells Erin that she saved his arm and that he misjudged her badly.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr apologises for what he said when Erin first came to him.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr says a life as an adventurer might be worth living after all, but he would not enter the dungeon.

section: Hopes to be a Knight and friendship with Lyonette, Book 5
text: Brunkr says he owes too much to Erin, Krshia and Lyonette to risk his life so easily.
Brunkr walks with a Gnoll he addresses as Regrika, tells her he would help Erin and Lyonette in any way, and she turns into Venitra.
Venitra twists Brunkr's neck and stabs her hand through his chest, killing him in a street.
The next day Brunkr's body is found at the bottom of the crevasse in Liscor's dungeon, with a Silver-rank Gnoll team and Bronze-rank Gnolls who vanished the previous night.
The bodies of the group at the crevasse bear wounds consistent with a monster attack.
Krshia tells Erin that her nephew Brunkr is dead.
Krshia says Brunkr's body and eight others were found at the bottom of the crevasse, torn apart as if by a monster.
Brunkr's body is brought out of the dungeon with magic and ropes, and Mrsha smells it and knows.
Caddin is a Silver-rank adventurer in the Adventurer's Guild, and a member of Alais' team, Thunder's Solace.
Ceria and Yvlon's old teams knew Caddin back in the day.
Caddin is a young man who wears leather armour like the rest of his team.
Caddin halts in shock when Ceria and Yvlon walk up to his team's table in the guild.
Caddin jumps when Ksmvr extends an Antinium hand to shake, and shakes it gingerly, flinching at the exoskeleton.
Caddin asks Ksmvr exactly what he is while Pisces listens to Alais introduce her team.
Caddin snorts at Ceria's proposal to combine teams against a [Bandit] group, and says fourteen of them would face thirty or more [Bandits].
Caddin is angry at Ceria and Yvlon, and refuses to join with them.
Caddin shoves back from the table and confronts Pisces and Ksmvr, asking if they know what Ceria and Yvlon did to their previous teams.
Caddin says that Ceria and Yvlon both lost their teams, and that all the Horns of Hammerad died except Ceria.
Caddin recoils from Pisces as if infected when Stan names him a [Necromancer], and says no one else would partner with Ceria or Yvlon.
Caddin shouts that Ceria hid and Yvlon ran, while Yvlon retorts that everyone ran.
Caddin spits on the ground after Alais says Ceria's and Yvlon's teams were the ones who brought everyone to Liscor.
Caddin tells Ceria she will get no help from his team when she takes the [Bandit] bounty for the Horns alone.
Cade is the young son of Briganda, a [Shield Maiden] of Griffon Hunt, and looks like his mother, with a head of dark violet hair and fair skin.
Cade is about four years old, and talks, which he had not done when Revi last saw him.
Briganda had Cade in the course of being an adventurer, and did not notice she was pregnant until close to delivery.
Briganda has no idea who Cade's father is.
Cade points out that Revi has threads in her face, and asks why she has them in her neck.
Cade keeps himself entertained with a magical box of simulacra that releases an illusory Dragon, which perches on his hand.
Briganda says the toy cost a fortune but is the only thing that keeps Cade's attention while she works.
While travelling with Griffon Hunt, Briganda kept Cade in the care of [Carers] and [Nursemaids], and left him at safer places.
Briganda says Cade has tried to climb off the balcony more than once.
Briganda says she will not leave Cade again, because he nearly forgot she was his mother, and makes taking him along a deal breaker for rejoining Griffon Hunt.
Cade looks confused when Briganda hugs Revi and Typhenous after agreeing to rejoin Griffon Hunt.
Cade's box makes illusory [Knights] that chase Goblins around a table, and he glares at Halrac when Halrac taps the box and makes them vanish.
Cade, apparently forgotten by Briganda, wanders into The Wandering Inn through the door, and Grev asks Mrsha to help find his mother.
Cade cries in the inn until Grev introduces Mrsha, and he stops crying as Mrsha takes him and Grev into the Garden of Sanctuary.
Cade screams when he sees Numbtongue and runs into a burr-bush, and Numbtongue picks him up to pull the burrs off.
Briganda charges Numbtongue with her axe and buckler when she hears Cade screaming, and crashes into the barrier of the Garden of Sanctuary.
Lyonette serves Cade a smiling egg-and-bacon breakfast at The Wandering Inn.
Briganda says she might stay behind at the inn because Cade needs his mother.
Calac is the only son of Venith and Maresar, and a [Lord] trained since childhood to fight and lead soldiers.
Calac is maybe a year younger than Trey and Teres, but taller and muscled like an athlete.
Calac wears plate armor and is known to know how to use a sword.
Calac charges Flos with a spear at Manimar, shouting for the King of Destruction to die, but Flos catches the shaft and unhorses him.
Flos recognises Calac as Venith's son, remembering that Venith wrote the day Calac was born and Flos drank to his health.
Venith slaps Calac across the face with a gauntleted hand, drawing blood, after the attack on Flos.
Venith accuses Calac of disgracing himself in battle the day before, when Calac tried to end things easily by dishonorable means.
Calac admits his dishonorable act was wrong and presses Venith to explain why he lets the Hellios men go.
Calac accuses Venith of hiding behind oaths while Hellios sends an army to kill their people by dishonorable means.
Calac says Venith always told him Flos was a fool, an oathbreaker and a coward, and that he came to see Flos as more honorable than the other rulers.
Calac abandons his father's post and rides with some soldiers to join Flos, saying he never learned what loyalty meant.
Calac rides with Venith to the army four miles from Reim and sees the enemy soldiers, more people than he has ever seen.
Venith orders Calac to stay back and take the foot and archers to his mother, Maresar.
Calac stays in Reim with Orthenon, as Venith did not let him join the Ger posting after his previous failure.
Later, Calac is among the Germinan guests introduced by Teres alongside Nawalishifra, the veiled [Blacksmith] Nawal.
Calac is in disgrace with his father and resents being lumped with the guests in the room.
Trey remembers Calac as headstrong and eager to prove himself, and not at fault for his trouble with Venith.
Calectus is a Selphid who inhabits dead bodies and oversees the Selphids volunteering as Geneva's assistants.
Calectus is the most senior and highest-level of the Selphids with Geneva, a Level 36 [Honor Guard].
Calectus first appears inhabiting a pale, nearly white Lizardman's body and is more at home among Dullahans.
Calectus is troubled by Okasha's possession of Geneva and speaks to her brusquely as a senior to a junior.
Calectus tells Ken to leave the wounded Luan and not make things worse, and tells him the [Doctor] is sleeping.
Calectus says Geneva is valued above Okasha's or his own life, which the Selphids have agreed.
Calectus believes that if any person can save the Selphids from the Wasting, it is Geneva.
Calectus intends to stay with Geneva until she reaches Level 30, then suggest leaving, since both armies grow more savage.
Calectus tells Geneva that Luan, Ken and Aiko are deserters who will be killed if they leave her camp.
Calectus says he can keep the three safe only inside the camp, which Geneva's reputation as the Last Light protects.
Calectus says that no potion could have saved the dying Dullahan War Walker, except those a Named Adventurer would use.
Calectus warns that Geneva, having saved a War Walker and changed the battlefield, is now a powerful ally or a dangerous enemy.
Calectus fights eight Dullahans alone in Geneva's burning camp, wounded and half-burned.
Calectus kicks one armored Dullahan eight feet through the air, leaving an imprint in the iron armor.
A Dullahan shouts that the Selphid is rampaging, and Calectus leaps six feet to crush a Dullahan's helmeted head.
Calectus kills all the Dullahans, cutting the last in half with his halberd.
Calectus is left with arrows in his shoulder and thigh, bloodless cuts and a deformed skull, yet only exhausted.
Calectus lowers his halberd when Luan shouts his name and Ken calls him Calectus-san.
Calectus judges that the Centaurs sent Zalthia and that the Dullahan assassins were experienced soldiers, not hired mercenaries.
Calectus says he has torn this body's muscles and must find another.
Calectus returns from scouting in a female Dullahan's body that he killed himself.
Calectus warns Ken, Luan and Aiko that a Selphid living in a living host is forbidden by every nation and would mean death for Okasha and Geneva.
Calectus gives Okasha a quarter bottle of healing potion for Geneva's torn muscles and tells her to use it sparingly.
Calectus explains that sharing a body between two minds with their own Skills is forbidden because an army of them would be unstoppable.
Quallet makes room around his map for Geneva's group on hearing that Calectus is a Level 36 [Honor Guard].
Calectus arrives in Book 17 leading over two hundred Selphids to Geneva's clinic, wearing a tall Dullahan's body.
Calectus holds a jar containing Okasha after the Selphids pull her out of Geneva's body.
Calectus tells Okasha she has committed the sin for which the Selphids were destroyed and that the Minds will sentence her.
Calectus says the holding-jar will serve as Okasha's prison for now.
Calectus, still an [Honor Guard] in a Dullahan body, tells Geneva that Selphid decisions are for the Minds and that Selphids are not trusted as a species.
The Minds are the governing body of the Selphids, according to Idis.
Califor is a tall, thin [Witch] who dresses in plain black with a worn hat, and her apprentice is Nanette, a round-cheeked twelve-year-old with a fresh dark blue hat.
Califor had never had an apprentice before Nanette, which is famous among witches.
Califor keeps numbered rules for Nanette, and rule eight is that a smart woman looks up now and then.
Wiskeria reports tales that Califor is tougher than nails, and that she is the most powerful [Witch] in generations.
On the road to Riverfarm, a [Bandit Leader]'s axe seems to cleave Califor's skull, but the body is one of his own bandits, and her illusion saves her.
Califor tells Nanette that she survived her first bandits well and that she may trust her teacher but must rely on herself.
Califor says she had heard Riverfarm was safe from [Bandits] of any kind, and Rie replies that the method they use to detect them is not working as usual.
Califor says she is the coven's leader when asked, and she stops a quarrel between Alevica and Mavika by slamming her hand on the table and saying "Enough".
Califor tells Ryoka that she feels like the wind and has an unusual affinity for it, though she is no [Mage].
Califor says her cloak is a flea-market bargain and her staff a gift from a [Shaman], but Durene thinks she sees the staff turn leafy and the cloak swirl like shadow.
Califor loads a pony cart with far more goods than it could hold, and says the cart does not know how much it is carrying.
Prost says Califor may be the woman who broke the Wellfar dam at Lake Roisemead, and Rie confirms that the incident happened eighteen years ago and that Wellfar is still hunting for the culprit.
Prost wonders whether Califor ran Yellats across the north after the 2nd Antinium War, and says that woman had brown hair and nobody called her a Witch.
Califor says she once wore happiness, then passion and great deeds, and that these days much of her craft is Nanette and teaching.
Califor rides down three fake [Hunters], conjures a storm of leaves, and cuts a fireball in half with a knife.
She catches a thrown glass orb filled with bright yellow liquid, binds it with string, and sends it back at one of the fleeing riders, and she makes a tree explode around another.
A third rider is knocked from his horse by a thunderclap of wind, and when Califor finds him he is only ash, which she guesses was suicide to avoid being traced to Noelictus.
Califor stands between the Hunters and Knights and Wiskeria, catches a crossbow bolt bare-handed, and says Belavierr is part of her coven.
Califor buries a [Spring Knight] up to his waist with one blow of her staff that sounds like a gong, while Mavika turns into a giant bird.
Califor tells Nanette that if she had known Belavierr still lived and her crimes in Noelictus were as heinous as suspected, she would have hunted her.
Califor sacrifices her Cloak of Balshadow to hide Riverfarm in shadow from the undead, and the cloak tears away.
Belavierr recognises the hiding of the village as a craft of witches of old.
Califor tosses a glowing thing upward and makes multicoloured rain fall, interrupting Belavierr.
Califor drives her quarterstaff, a relic of an ancient forest, into the ground to burn in the place of the forest, and it erases three wildfires before it crumbles to ash.
Califor shares sake from Drath porcelain with Ryoka and says the secret is being able to do great things, so that one seldom has to.
On Day 70 Califor leaves Riverfarm with Nanette, saying that Nanette comes first and that she is a coward that day.
Two-thirds of the people who tried the river perished, including Mayor Rodivek and many of Lancrel's folk.
Califor's story ended when her thread was cut, and the Stitch Witch had plucked it to trick her own death.
On Day 77 the coven summons her ghost with Nanette's blood and her handkerchief, and Mavika says she was the most powerful in generations.
The ghost calls Nanette Weishart her daughter and curses Belavierr, and says to Nanette that in the end all must walk alone.
The ghost says the other side is empty and that something hungry has devoured the land of death.
She says the nameless one among the dead pursues her and must never return.
The ghost seizes Wiskeria in flame, charges her to keep Nanette safe, and whispers one word into her ear.
Califor is gone, and Wiskeria's arms are marked with raw handprints that no potion or charm removes.
Calirn is the Knight-Commander of the Order of Seasons, who in the Order's stronghold can command even the Grandmasters as a first among equals.
Calirn is a [Winter Knight], one of the small and solitary Season of Winter.
Calirn can turn the cold air around him into a freezing vortex, give his blade a frostbite edge, and form a shield of ice.
Calirn is addressed as a grandmaster-level figure, and the Thronebearer Ser Dalimont bows to him as Knight Commander.
Calirn congratulates Dame Talia on the game and says the Summer's Champion is pleased, while the Fall's Sentinel and Calirn himself have reservations about the outcome.
Calirn says the death of the Fence bears Belavierr's magic, but warns it could be one of her thousand misdirections without confirmation.
Calirn refuses to contact Ser Raim on so little evidence at first.
Calirn confirms to Talia and Dame Wera that Belavierr is the infamous witch who cursed the Griffin Prince Ostevien and destroyed the city of Halen overnight.
The Summer's Champion says he thought Belavierr, once driven from a village, would not be seen for another thousand years.
Frost forms on the walls of the room when Calirn speaks of Belavierr, and melts when the Summer's Champion bursts in.
Calirn orders the Fall's Sentinel to prepare his Season for a grand ritual spell, though he does not know when or if it must be cast.
Calirn tells the Academy of Wistram it may be needed, and tells Ser Raim to return in haste.
Calirn asks the Hunter's Guild to send its highest-level experts with Ser Raim, since the Order cannot muster an army in time.
Calirn declares that Ser Raim has exceeded Level 50, is far above Talia, and has the Skill and will to end the Stitch Witch.
Calirn says Ser Raim injured Belavierr once this winter and she fled his flame.
Calirn orders the grand ritual prepared a second time, and the Fall's Sentinel protests that the cost is too high.
The ritual circle lies in one of the oldest parts of the Order's stronghold, a relic of a half-Elven empire older than the Order.
The Fall's Sentinel, Calirn's old comrade, tells him the ritual cannot move an army, because in it magic is the true weight.
The Fall's Sentinel says only thirty-two Knights can be sent, none with a strong aura or Skills that affect the body, and no Autumn Knights.
Calirn orders the Summer's Champion and the Spring's Warden to choose volunteers who are ready for death.
Calirn sends eight Knights of Summer and eight of Spring, each over Level 30, taking steel and silver only, to reinforce Ser Raim.
Calirn speaks to Raim through a scrying orb after the battle.
When Raim abandons his honor and walks to fight Belavierr, Calirn calls to him not to do it.
Later, after Raim's death and Belavierr's survival, Calirn lowers his head and turns away.
Calirn stands vigil on the docks of Phel's Light, in Pheislant, awaiting the funeral barge that carries Ser Raim's ashes.
Calirn has come personally from the Order's headquarters, which is in Pheislant on the Order's own lands, allied with the Terandrian Kingdom.
Calirn is asked, by Raim and by his love, that they be buried together, and he will honor the request.
Calirn considers Raim by far the highest-levelled Knight to have died here and resolves not to forget Belavierr's added sin.
Calirn bows as the barge enters the harbour and calls on the Knights to let the Season of Summer welcome their fallen brethren.
Calruz is a Minotaur adventurer who introduces himself as "Calruz of the Beriad" and leader of the Horns of Hammerad, an adventuring party in the region.
Calruz is the captain of the Horns of Hammerad, is impatient, and sits at the Adventurer's Guild table bare-chested.
Calruz is only around Level 20 and could have joined a Gold-rank team, but wanted to be in command.
Calruz is a huge Minotaur with a massive steel battleaxe strapped to his back, and wears plate armor.
Ryoka Griffin estimates him at about six foot seven, perhaps a few inches more not counting the horns, with a body of pure Minotaur muscle.
He has goat-like legs with cloven hooves.
Erin Solstice sees three hundred pounds of Minotaur, closer to seven feet than six.
Calruz can eat beef, eats politely and faster than his companions, and dislikes being asked many questions.
Calruz asks Erin not to call him "Bull Guy", saying Minotaurs are not bulls or cattle.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: In the ruins, Calruz hides behind a fallen wall with his human second-in-command, who reports that Terr was hit by a fireball and dragged away by Coblat and Grimsore.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz says Ryoka is no coward like the other Runners, and that she will survive the High Passes, a Human worthy of his admiration and respect.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz says Ryoka reminds him of Minotaur females, fiery ones who would stab any male that offends, and he prefers her to the simpering human women he keeps meeting.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: After Ryoka punches him in the face, Calruz topples down the inn stairs in plate armor and smashes the stairwell.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz runs through the night beside the cart and then sits downwind of the other adventurers, reeking of sweat.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Yvlon and Cervial call Calruz a Levelist of the old-fashioned kind who fights for the experience and does not care what enemies he faces.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz orders the Runner Garia out of her seat, saying the place is for adventurers and that she is no warrior.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz tells Ryoka her fists would do little against most monsters his team faces, and that Humans and women are weaker by birth.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Ceria says Calruz will take every hit Ryoka lands to show he can, which is a Minotaur sign of disrespect and also of courtship.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: When Ryoka knocks Ceria down, Calruz gently scoops her up, says Ryoka tramples Ceria's honor, but refuses her challenge, saying she is not worth the time.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz promises on his honor that he will not attack Erin's guests unless provoked.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: When Erin runs off toward the city, Calruz says the child needs a second for a proper death duel, but finds the city gates closed against him.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz asks Pawn why he did not fight when tortured by his own kind, and calls him a slave after Pawn says the Antinium have no honor and his life is for the Hive.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz recognizes Gazi and gives her room to pass, then tells Erin she looked like someone but it is nothing.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz tells Erin that a female alone should be a warrior, and calls Toren worthless and weak.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz shows his sole skill, [Hammer Blow], by shattering a waist-high boulder with his axe.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz explains that his Skill lets him exceed his hardest strike, and that his kind practice little magic because they are not gifted enough to study spells.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz describes a human woman who fights with her fists as skilled but wild, fighting only at her limit and lacking vision, and says he will make her understand.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz decides to teach Erin to fight for the two days before he goes into the Ruins, saying that "the singer must not be silenced".

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz privately thinks Ryoka is strong but must learn honor, and that Erin's music is unique and should be protected, so he will teach her.

section: Book 1: the Horns, Ryoka and the inn
text: Calruz tells Ceria that Erin overwhelmed a skeleton in a fist fight within hours and unlocked a skill, and calls her gifted at battle.
Calruz proposes luring the undead out with his voice, and Lir casts a spell to amplify it and a [Muffle] spell to shield the others.
Calruz rips one Crypt Lord's head off with his hands and kills another with [Hammer Blow].
Skinner twists off Calruz's arm, leaving a bleeding stump at his shoulder, and a swarm of undead engulfs him.
In Book 6 Olesm notes that the guardsmen never found Calruz's remains or axe, and suspects he escaped through a trap into the dungeon.
Pisces calls it possible, more than likely, that Calruz survived, though he was wounded and the dungeon is dangerous.

An unnamed figure at the dungeon entrance finds a crude drawing of a cow with oversized horns, an old joke known only to the original Horns of Hammerad, picks up a hair from the paint, says "Ceria" and walks back into the dungeon.
Ceria meets a one-armed Minotaur with short dark brown fur and a cow's face in the dungeon and recognizes him as Calruz, who calls her his precious teammate and a Horn of Hammerad.
Calruz commands Raskghar and Cave Goblins in a massive domed chamber with caged Gnolls of Liscor, and a caged white Gnoll, Mrsha.
Calruz tells Ceria the Raskghar are his team, a new tribe he leads and his tools to conquer the dungeon, and that he wants her as his teammate to finish the job.
Ceria concludes that Calruz is completely and utterly insane.
Ceria sees that Calruz has changed: his fur is rough and dirty, matted with dried blood, he stinks of rotten meat, sweat and blood, and his right arm, his dominant one, is missing at the shoulder.
Calruz has fleas and a cracked tooth, but his remaining arm is whole and looks bigger than Ceria remembered.
Calruz says he knew one of his team must be alive, and believes the others are in hiding until Ceria tells him they are all dead and Skinner was killed by the people of Liscor.
When Ceria tells him Erin killed Skinner with acid jars, Calruz laughs and says they should have bought everything she had.

Calruz explains that he misled the Drakes into thinking the Raskghar act only at night, and that a team with artifacts hidden above to seize Gnolls was spotted and retreated, returning with Ceria and a few Gnolls.
Calruz insists the Horns' mission is still on, and that the dungeon is halfway conquered.
Calruz says the Raskghar are his tribe, that he forged the isolated Raskghar camps together, and that they expand under his leadership.
Ceria's dagger tip snaps against Calruz's arm without hurting it; he then beats a Raskghar who hurt her and gently checks her head wound.
Calruz says Raskghar are little more than beasts for most of the month and regain intelligence only when the moon is nearly full.
Calruz swings between fury and humor, which Ceria takes as proof he is not himself.
Calruz limits the ritual to one Gnoll for the day, strikes a female Raskghar who wants more, and puts her in command of Dailre's Fist, and she calls him Chieftain.
Calruz threatens to sacrifice another Gnoll each time Ceria disobeys, and offers to let a few go if she follows his command, perhaps even the white one.
Calruz sleeps in a squalid private chamber on a dirty mattress behind a curtain, and moves the camp nightly between set locations.
Calruz moves most Raskghar out of the way of the adventurer and Antinium invasion and sends kill teams against the Halfseekers.
Calruz claims the dungeon hunts everyone but him and Ceria because he alone has the Skill, and that adventurers will take months to reach him.
Calruz's battleaxe is magical, made of false-gold metal with a bright green edge.
With the axe, Calruz grows a transparent edge three times the size of the axe head and cuts down thirty infested, and uses [Hammer Blow] and [Gore Splash].
Calruz tells Ceria that after losing his arm he fled, fell through a trapped floor into a Raskghar graveyard, was attacked by six Raskghar and killed one, and was captured and caged.
Calruz says he killed two of the largest Raskghar as they slept, one of whom was the Chieftain, and was made Chieftain after a vote; Ceria scoffs at his account.
Calruz says the Raskghar chose him because he was an adventurer with Skills and tactics who was not one of them, and whose intellect does not wane with the moon.
Calruz says he trained the tribe, gave them discipline and organization, conquered the dungeon sector by sector, and sent Raskghar above to acquire Gnolls.
Calruz asks three times whether the other Horns are dead, and Ceria says Gerial saved her, Skinner killed him, and Hunt, Corr and Sostrom died and she buried them.
Calruz insists he invented the name Horns of Hammerad and, in a rage, lifts Ceria by her robes before blinking and dropping her.
Calruz asks whether the families of the fallen were paid, and Ceria says Yvlon took care of it.
Calruz thinks Ceria can see invisible monsters because she is a half-Elf; Ceria replies that half-Elves resist enchantments and do not get magical eyes.
Calruz says the invisible monsters in the dungeon become visible when they are dead.

Calruz concludes there is something in the dungeon's water that blinds drinkers to monsters and stops the monsters fighting each other, notes he has been drinking it, and resolves to drink rationed water.

Calruz shows Ceria a monolith in the city's central plaza, topped with three heads including Skinner's, which warns that the dungeon is protected by the Mother of Graves and served by three guardians of the crypts.
Calruz says that Snatcher killed Stalker and now lurks in the labyrinth, causing paralysis, resisting enchanted arrows and collecting heads on sticks.
Calruz says the dungeon is on the scale of the one Niers Astoragon conquered before founding the Forgotten Wing Company.

Calruz chokes a female Raskghar who speaks as if she were Chieftain until she submits, backhands another so hard it loses a tooth, and says he will spare whichever Gnolls Ceria picks, and the white one.
Calruz agrees to send two Gnolls to Liscor with a list of his demands, with Ceria helping him write the note.
When adventurers attack the camp, Calruz orders the prisoners taken away and strikes Ceria down with the handle of his axe.
Calruz names twenty-one of his elite awakened Raskghar as his vanguard, to bear artifacts, with Nokha leading them.
Calruz beats Ceria for what he calls treachery, then carries her toward his bed with clear sexual intent, claiming it is her duty as his Chieftain, and stops when she says "Ryoka would be so proud".
Calruz says forty-four Gnolls remain and that he will lead the awakened into the city.
Calruz admits sacrificing the Gnolls is wrong but says he must find the heart of the dungeon and win glory for the fallen, saying he has no honor left and will not retreat.
Calruz tells Ceria he now has [Thick Skin].
Calruz agrees to spare the Gnolls with no more sacrifices "for now" in exchange for Ceria's help against the awakened.
Calruz cancels the sacrifices for the night, tells the awakened to prepare to enter the city, and backs down when he sees something poking around the camp entrance.
Calruz and Ceria argue over the word "mute": Calruz says it means unable to make sounds, Ceria that it means unable to speak, which Pisces read in a book.
The awakened Raskghar chafe under Calruz's rule: Nokha withholds the title "Chieftain" and the others eye him calculatingly.
Calruz fights the Horns in Liscor's tunnels, is set aflame by Ksmvr's Flamecoat Dagger, doused by Ceria's snow, and struck between the eyes by an [Ice Spike].
After the fight Calruz thanks Ceria, is shackled, and the Watch takes him to prison.
In Book 9 Calruz sits in a prison cell with his flesh burnt and body bleeding, and a woman says Ceria let him live.
Calruz is held in a runed cell in Liscor's prison, one-armed with his feet shackled, and says to Erin, "You. I know you."
In his magic cell, Calruz barely eats and rarely responds, but says he remembers everything he did and that "Below. She's still there."
Calruz tells Ceria that he went mad and began losing himself, and says death is his only salvation.
Calruz is a Minotaur of six foot seven and about three hundred pounds who lost his right arm to Skinner long ago, and in his cell does one-armed push-ups under the glow of the cell's runes.
Calruz asked for the cell and was given the means to draw maps of the dungeon, which he says need not be trusted but show the general layout.
Calruz expects Drake law to execute him, says he deserves it, and says it is better to die sane than down there like a monster.
Calruz names his lost team as Gerial, Hunt, Terr, Marian, Coblat, Grimsore, Sostrom and Barr, and cannot recall Olesm's name or what happened to him.
Ceria Springwalker calls Calruz mad and a killer of other people, and says he lost an arm and is in jail.
Calruz believes Erin does not visit because she has not forgotten the lives he took.
Zevara tells Calruz that Ceria visits him at least four times a week, and says arranging his execution is complicated since Liscor has no dedicated [Executioner].
Calruz expects the House of Minos would prefer to execute him on Minos publicly, and admits that the pull of the dungeon's treasure still gnaws at him.
Zevara states that the Silver-rank adventurer Calruz has not been executed because the Watch is not certain he controlled himself during his crimes.
Calruz's cell has a magic barrier made to hold Gold-rank prisoners.

Calruz tells Zevara that no magic was found on him, and that he has gained [Peaceful Rest], [Efficient Metabolism] and [Recall Guilt], the last letting him remember half of what he did while the rest was a dream.
Calruz asks for any weapon and an honorable death fighting a friend willing to look him in the eye, and Ceria cannot do it.
A Gnoll [Guardsman] and others argue over Calruz, who lies on the floor after being healed four times, until a white Gnoll cub tackles one man and Zevara arrives and knocks aside a dozen blades.
Calruz keeps two rats in his cell and names them Haldagaz, Vanquisher of Foes, and Rhata, Trident-Guardian of the Harbor of Hammerad.
Bezale of Maweil, a Minotauress [Spellscribe], confronts Calruz in his cell, calls him a disgrace and says she cast [Detect Magic] and found no magic on him.
Bezale tells Calruz to kill himself and promises to smuggle in a knife; Calruz refuses, saying he does not know that he is guilty.
Calruz tells Bezale he won his right to leave Minos by skill at arms and that Ceria would break anyone who touches her; Bezale says the House of Minos will hear of his treachery.
Calruz tells Zevara that the Wistram [Mages] found no spells on him, and Zevara promises an [Enchanter] visit and a legal plan that might help.
Zevara unlocks Calruz's chains and gives him a battleaxe so he can help take the inn, which is full of Crelers, to reach the Horns of Hammerad on the other side.
Calruz charges into the inn alone, shouting "Death before dishonor!".
Calruz survives, gains the class [Honorbound Prisoner] and the Skill [Death Before Dishonor], and Zevara sentences him to hard labor that may mean certain death if the Watch needs it.

In Book 16 Calruz walks through Liscor under guard, scarred and thinner, with his remaining arm secured to his neck by a steel collar and magical shackles on his legs, while crowds throw insults and stones.
The guard detail is a punishment detail for the prisoner, set to cull Shield Spiders and clear Hollowstone Deceivers, which Calruz volunteered for.
Calruz tells Erin that the Watch Captain visits him and Ceria used to, and that he sometimes believes Zevara that he is innocent.
Calruz says it would be justice to execute him and that he would rather have death than confinement.
In Book 17 Calruz sits in his cell with Rhata on his head while Zevara cleans his cuts with a rag dipped in healing potion, after he killed a Face-Eater Moth colony with a rusty axe.
Ryoka visits Calruz in his cell and sees his missing arm, scars and humility.
In Book 19 Calruz plays chess with Zevara at his cell's barrier, after teaching Rhata and Haldagaz to move pieces.
Bezale brings a scrying orb to Calruz's cell, showing the House of Minos marching against the King of Destruction.
Calruz says honor is an ideal to live by, not die for, and that his imprisonment does not match his crimes, so that perhaps this is the greater punishment.
Calruz asks Bezale to carry a letter to someone with the right to judge him, and she agrees.
Calruz warns the Watch that Raskghar can bend iron but not steel, and advises explosives and Tripvine-type weapons ready to throw if they break the cells.
Calvaron is a Centaur and a full student of Wistram, tall and cheerful, who wears only a shirt on his upper half.
He greets Ceria and Pisces after their sea crossing and offers to show them around the academy.
He says the whole academy watched the sea serpent and placed bets on whether Amerys would reach the ship in time.
He is undeclared in Wistram's factions for now and not yet important enough for them to pressure him.
He is a generalist [Mage], and Beatrice is a [Runeshaper].
Calvaron tells new students that rooms in Wistram vary because many people with different styles worked on the castle.
He buys and sells secrets and calls himself just a broker or middle-Centaur.
Ceria notes that his independence lets any faction treat with him without fearing he will trade their secrets.
He tells new students that most magic classes require at least ten levels in [Mage], and many require twenty.
He says the academy gives new students old spellbooks, and older mages sort them so nothing above a Tier 2 spell remains.
Calvaron says the locations of secret libraries and tomes are among the biggest secrets to trade, and he cannot trade for one.
He tells Ceria that all knowledge is useful to someone, and that Pisces' rapier and silver bell are important knowledge.
Calvaron hints that he knows Ceria's sealed origins and that an old Terandrian city warrant lists a small bounty on a half-Elf kid for theft and property damage.
Other students joke that he charges an arm and a horse's leg for the location of the illusion class.
Calvaron owns a truth crystal enchanted to glow red when someone tells the truth, the opposite of most truth spells.
Calvaron carries a very limited bag of holding.
He buys a Sand Tumbler, a drink from Chandrar made with limes and lemons, from a ship captain with a cargo of drinks.
Calvaron tells Ceria and Pisces that Charles de Trevalier got into Illphres' class by having someone else melt her ice wall.
Calvaron says Charles is heavily in Rievan's camp and part of the Libertarian faction.
A student reports that Calvaron and Beatrice have put money on Ceria and Pisces passing the exams.
Calvaron is in his sixth year, with one more to go before he can call himself a mage, and he is terrified of the exam.
He says becoming a mage would embroil him in faction politics, so he wants to stay classless and become an influential broker between all sides.
Beatrice wants him to join the Revivalists, and the two have been fighting about his future.
Calvaron is killed in the banquet hall by the shades called from Archmage Nekhret's spell.
He lies fallen mid-gallop with a wand still gripped in his hand and a desperate, fierce expression.
Beatrice holds his body, and Montressa sits on the ground beside him.
Beatrice later inherits his network of connections.
Cara O'Sullivan is an Irish Earther who is the world's first [Popstar], known as the Queen of Pop and the Singer of Terandria.
Cara has the [Pop Star] class and the second class [Thespian], and her combined Skills give her fame and fortune.
Cara is Level 40, the highest-level of her band, having reached that level the previous month.
Cara's titles include the Baroness of the Beat.
Cara's natural accent is Irish, which comes out when she drops her smile in private.
Elena says that Cara left Earth in 2017.
Jecaina says the Queen of Pop is the greatest [Singer] born in ten thousand years, with many albums, and shows King Raelt a recording crystal of her songs.
The recording crystal plays pop songs with a piano and a beat, which Raelt does not know come from another world.
Jecaina says the Queen of Pop is a famous [Singer] in Terandria who has tons of albums.
Before her band, Cara sang alone with karaoke music on an iPhone, enhanced by a spell for backup.
Cara became a beloved icon sweeping across Terandria, creating a wave of music and a new culture among young folk.
Cara draws the 3rd Prince of Pheislant, Tellsiv, and a Calanfer [Baroness] to her concert at Phel's Light.
Cara keeps a plagiarism log of the Earth songs she plays, to keep her honest and so she can give something back if they get home.
Cara sings everything from modern pop hits to classics such as Sinatra's My Way.
Cara opens a concert with Journey's famed song and later performs Uptown Funk, which is new to the audience.

section: Book 17: the concert in Phel's Light
text: Cara marches her band and audience out of the plaza to the harbor with a marching song as the funeral barge returns Ser Raim.

section: Book 17: the concert in Phel's Light
text: Cara kneels as the Summer Knights kneel to the barge, and her audience follows suit in silence.

section: Book 17: the concert in Phel's Light
text: Cara tells Greg she does not like the [Knights] but respects men who died far from home doing what they thought right.

section: Book 17: the concert in Phel's Light
text: Cara tells the people of Phel's Landing that the next song is for bravery, and sings softly as the [Knights] listen.

section: Book 17: the concert in Phel's Light
text: Cara ends the concert with rock, dyed black hair and a pale look, and the world's second mosh pit begins evolving.
Cara tells her band she is not a [Popstar] but a [Thespian] who is acting, and says she hates the nobility, the monarchy and the [Knights].
Cara admits to Rae that she looked chubby before and lost weight when she gained Skills; her face changed too.
Cara tells Abebi that she lied to Rae, because telling people what they want to hear is her job.
Cara tells Abebi she sings pop only because it is the most accessible music and that she does not necessarily like rock.
Cara tells Abebi that all of this is a mask, and that they tour to earn money to live, buy artifacts and find the best place to settle.
Cara tells Abebi that they are being hunted, that nowhere is safe, and that they need allies.
Cara tells Abebi that her band does not even know her real name.
Cara receives a letter from Elena in Wistram that lacks the agreed passphrases, and concludes it is a trap and that Elena is being held hostage.
Wistram [Mages] follow Cara's tour asking to speak with her and escort the band to Wistram, apparently unaware of the others.
Cara says her fallback is Plan C or Plan G, and blames Blackmage for putting Wistram onto them.
Cara has refused to send more Earthers to Wistram, despite the Archmages pressing Aaron to get her to send them.
Aaron suspects Elena sent a covert message because the [Popstar] of Terandria is staying independent.
Cara is angered at the Drakes' Wistram broadcast, saying it caters to the rich, and wants someone to turn it off.
Cara slams her trailer door on two Wistram [Mages] of the Libertarian faction who come to speak to her.
Cara argues by iPhone with Aaron, whom she calls Blackmage, demanding Elena be put on the line and getting no answer.
Cara says that after one more show she will quit Wistram until they start threatening Elena.
Cara tours with an Earth-born band: Abebi as manager, Thien as [Drummer] and [Historian], Greg as [Guitarist] and Rae as [Bassist].
Cara films the world's first music video, walking through real spells and arrows to Boulevard of Broken Dreams, with a staged battlefield.
Dame Neranthei, a Thronebearer of Calanfer with the crest of the 4th Princess, appears in the first video, and so do Huntress Melitza of Noelictus, a half-Elf and a Dwarf.
Cara's second video has a skull-masked [Necromancer] scrying her, Ailendamus soldiers attacking her, and Wistram mages under a triangle-and-eye symbol helping drive off evil.
Aaron notes the scrying spell fails on Cara's real name, so the name shown in the video is not her real one.
Wistram watchers puzzle over a triangle-and-eye symbol under Wistram's sigil in the video that is not their own, and Nailihuaile eyes it.
Cara tells Drassi she wrote the lyrics just for the scene, which pricks her conscience as the songs are from Earth.
Cara tells Drassi the second video was about Ailendamus's war with the Dawn Concordat, deflecting non-Earthers from the truth.
Ceria Springwalker is a Half-elf mage who meets Ryoka Griffin and Erin Solstice as a member of the Horns of Hammerad.
Ceria later becomes the unhappy Captain of the reformed Horns of Hammerad.
Ceria's right hand was reduced to bone and blackened flesh by magical backlash in the crypt under Liscor, and she casts with it afterwards.
Ceria studied at Wistram Academy with Pisces and was expelled with him, then declared a graduate by the Golem Cognita.
Ceria is an ice mage whose class becomes [Cryomancer] and later [Arctic Cryomancer].
Ceria Springwalker is a Half-Elf mage with slightly pointed ears and pale yellow eyes; her skin and features seem more vivid and real than a human's.
Ceria wears a hat indoors, which Ryoka Griffin first takes for bad manners until Ceria removes it and shows her ears.
In Ryoka's first-person passage after being healed, Ceria's eyes appear to her as gold, like a glimpse of eternity; the same scene calls Ceria a part-immortal with near-supernatural beauty.
Ceria has light hazelnut hair and gives off an unearthly feeling that Ryoka tries not to stare at.
Ceria is not a morning person; she has lived too long among Humans and other species to rise at dawn like the stereotype of a Half-elf, and she does not frolic.
Ceria has lived for forty years.
Ceria says she is a Half-elf, not an Elf, and tells Erin Solstice that no one has seen an Elf for thousands of years because they all died long ago.
Ceria eats meat and says her people are not averse to it; she enjoys properly cooked pork.
Ceria says everyone has some internal mana, supplied by the air and food; she says Half-elves generate a great deal by existing and so make good mages, while Humans have less, with exceptions.
Ceria can drink a lot for her small frame, draining mugs in one go; she says mana potions and alcohol do not mix, so if she gets drunk and drinks one, everything comes back up.

Ceria grew up for part of her life foraging off the land, loves climbing trees to steal eggs from nests, and has eaten earthworms, beetles, bark, birds raw and cooked, mushrooms and roots, having come close to starvation many times.
Ceria says that being a Half-elf does not mean she knows where flowers are, and that most Half-elves do not even like nature much, taking on the culture they are raised in.
Ceria recalls that when she was a child, elders said that long ago faeries were supposed to get along with Elves, though she calls it just a story.
After the battle with the Creler, Ceria's eyes are winter-pale with faint blue and grey and snowflakes fall around her; she tells Yvlon she leveled up.

Ceria's wand is a slender piece of unworked pale white wood tinged with green, with pale blue-white wisps of light flickering at the tip, and she carries it on an armband along her arm inside her sleeve.
Ceria's new dark blue robes, embroidered with glowing golden sigils, are enchanted so that spilled liquid simply runs off the cloth.
Ceria casts the [Light] spell with her wand much faster than Ryoka can, and the orb she makes shows colours deeper and subtler than Ryoka's.
Ceria floats a heap of gold coins in the air with faint green light from her hand and sorts them into four stacks of ten.
Ceria knows [Lesser Resistance to Ice], a basic mage spell of her school, and [Repair], though she says she is no good with movement and telekinetic spells.
Ceria knows one or two flame spells but they are not her proficiency, which is ice; she cannot throw fire far or shoot fireballs without a wand.
Ceria explains that a spell is like a container with a limit to the mana it can hold; a poor spell can be overcharged in theory, but too much mana injures the caster, as it did her hand.

Ceria says wands amplify a mage's magic and hold stored energy that may or may not restore itself, and that artifacts are like wands with recharging mana and deeper reserves, which people will kill for.

Ceria says the highest-tier magic she can cast is Tier 3; [Ice Spike] and [Detect Magic] are Tier 3, a Tier 4 spell would need a spellbook and weeks or months for her, and she is not at the level to learn [Grand Fireball] for years.

Ceria says she cannot cast [Fireball] without a wand, and neither can Pisces; she specialises in cold, having spent winters in snow and ice and liked snowflakes and icicles, so spells like [Ice Spike] make sense to her.
Ceria says Tier 4 spellbooks were beyond her price range even when she was with the Horns.

Ceria discovers that her skeletal hand moves when she channels magic and that she can cast with it more easily than with her good hand; asked by Ryoka whether Half-Elf bones conduct magic more easily, she says it is a secret and asks them to tell no one.
Ceria can cast [Fireball] with a wand but not strongly, and has no more ice spells in Warmage Thresk's spellbook; she says she taught herself [Frozen Armor] in the Raskghar den.
Ceria has the Skills [Weak Frost Resistance], [Ice Magic Affinity] and [Frozen Quickshape].

Ceria's [Glaciersheet Ice] and [Adept Iceform] let her shape her ice, such as spikes growing from an [Ice Wall] or a rough couch, and her wall holds against Tekshia's cane; casting still gives her migraines and Palt has told her no magic.
Ceria says she reached Level 18 in her [Elementalist] class and learned the spell [Fireball] then, which she says would otherwise take a month of study and the right scrolls.
Ceria learns the Tier 4 spell [Ice Wall] at lunch, raising a six-foot sheet of ice in front of her table; she says it is the spell Teriarch showed her and that Illphres had begun to teach her.
Later, Ceria introduces herself as Level 25 [Cryomancer], saying she changed class the day before, which she takes as a sign she was about to learn [Ice Wall].
Ceria, Yvlon and Ksmvr all report levelling up after the night's battle.
Grimalkin guesses that Ceria is a [Cryomancer] below Level 30, perhaps in the upper mid-twenties, with Yvlon in the same range and Pisces above Level 30; he does not know their levels exactly.

Later, Ceria changes class to [Arctic Cryomancer], which she takes as a hint about her specialisation; she gets no powerful new spell but the Skills [Glaciersheet Ice], an upgrade of [Adept Iceform], and [Aura of Rime], which makes snowflakes and cold around her.
Ceria meets Ryoka in an inn, where the vice-captain of the Horns of Hammerad thanks Ryoka for a delivery that let them kill a Lich and recover magical artifacts, including Ceria's new robes.
Ceria tells Calruz that even in Wistram she heard of the devastation the Necromancer wrought with his legions ten years earlier, and says the party would be no match for him even ten levels higher.
Ceria studied with Pisces at Wistram Academy; she calls them acquaintances rather than friends and calls him greedy, arrogant, rude, annoying but not very dangerous.

Ceria personally believes Pisces is delusional and will never achieve his goals, and says the Academy sends a team whenever it learns where he stays, so it is only a matter of time before he is caught.
Ceria suggests necromancy as another way to heal Ryoka when Ryoka is desperate, asking how she feels about it.
Ceria heals Ryoka's leg with a stronger, more expensive red healing potion once the bone has been repaired, and the flesh re-knits within a minute.
Ceria dispels the magic on Ryoka's leg by speaking words that belong to no language Ryoka knows and that make her head ache to hear.
Ceria finds that half of the healing potions she gave Ryoka were in fact mana potions.

Garia says Ceria tried to contact Ryoka several times; Wistram students communicate by touching firefly lights, and Ceria knows no other message spell, so Ryoka, who did not know to touch them, thought she was being hexed.
Calruz says Ceria stayed in Celum to wait for the Runner after mistakenly giving her mana potions instead of healing potions just before the High Passes.
Cervial says Ceria has more adventuring experience than the whole room put together, and calls her the resident Half-Elf whose judgment he trusts about the ruins.
Calruz insists that Ceria does not lead the Horns of Hammerad; he does.
Ceria tells Ryoka to get her first level in the [Mage] class after a nap, hoping it brings a Skill or spell, and then to consider a field of magic to specialise in.
Ceria gives up her seat to Garia and rebukes Calruz, saying a Captain who preaches honor shows little of it.
Ceria covers the downed Ryoka protectively with her own body while shouting at something, as Calruz is held back by ten men trying to rush at her.
Ceria casts [Silence] on Ryoka when she wakes at dusk, then tells her she is furious and is leaving until her anger is gone.

Ceria says the Horns of Hammerad and the other adventurers are heading to the ruins in Liscor and that she will speak with Ryoka again afterwards; she parts with "May we meet in new forests, Ryoka Griffin."
Ceria is working on the [Illumination] spell, an advanced [Light] spell officially Tier-2 but about Tier-3 in complexity, which sheds orbs of light over a hundred meters and suits dungeons.
Ceria complains that as the Wistram mage she is always the one expected to do the hard spell.
Ceria remarks that Erin reminds her a bit of Ryoka.

Ceria is the first out of the inn after Erin, running into the rainy night; she says she has no movement Skills, asks Yvlon to go after Erin, and tells her not to fight Ksmvr, since attacking him is the same as attacking the Hive.
Ceria tells Gerial that the timing of Erin's night departure and the dark stormy night make her feel it is a trap.
Ceria heals Erin's sore throat with pale green light from her fingers, but cannot cure her cold; she knows only basic healing spells and says only [Restoration] cures colds as far as she knows.
Ceria recognises Toren as Pisces' work and considers the intelligent skeleton an improvement that brings him closer to his goal, an undead capable of leveling.
Ceria tells Gerial that the music the night before was probably a Skill she has never heard of, and a rare one.

Ceria is over sixty years old, and has been an adventurer for fourteen years; Gerial has been one for eight, and thinks she should be vice-captain, a role she has always refused to avoid the logistical work.
Ceria says her mastery of [Illumination] is incomplete and she expects to cast it once before needing a mana potion.
Sostrom guesses Pisces has quite a few levels on him, perhaps the same as Ceria; Ceria answers maybe, but calls Pisces an idiot.
Ceria says Pisces was expelled from Wistram for his experiments, was always at the head of his class when he showed up, and left about the time she ran out of funds.
Ceria stands up to Gazi, refusing to answer her questions about Ryoka and shielding herself by channeling mana into her eyes against Gazi's gaze.

Gazi calls herself a Named Adventurer and Ceria Silver-rank; Ceria answers that a former soldier is not a true adventurer, since the Horns of Hammerad got their levels fighting monsters, not killing people.
After Gazi's webbing pins her, Ceria casts [Flashfire] to burn the webbing off and is burned in the process.
Ceria flees the Watch with Gerial and Sostrom into an alleyway after the webbing incident.
Ceria tells Gerial and Sostrom that Gazi was once a soldier who killed many innocent people, and that Gazi wants Ryoka, possibly for the same reason Magnolia is interested in her.
Ceria knows over fifty spells, but her wand holds [Ice Spike], which she can cast faster than anything else, and she uses it against Crypt Lords and zombies.
Ceria casts [Illumination] to light a crypt corridor with orbs of bright light spaced ten feet apart.
Ceria hits a Crypt Lord with a basketball-sized [Fireball] from her wand.
Ceria uses [Flashfire] to set a zombie ablaze that was clawing at Gerial.
Ceria has the spell [Translate] from her time at Wistram; it takes time, needs enough words at once, and gives muddled or nonsensical results at times.
Ceria sees Gerial killed by Skinner in the dungeon; she cannot raise her wand against Skinner out of fear and flees, leaving her friend behind.
Ceria breaks her wand over her good knee to unleash its stored cold magic and fires a giant ice spike that cuts through a Crypt Lord and frees a path for Yvlon and the other adventurers.
The magical backlash nearly knocks Ceria out and freezes the hand she used for the spell, its skin peeling and blackening, after Skinner had already torn open her leg.
Ceria stabs a ghoul with her dagger, then is bitten and torn by it, and closes her eyes believing it is the end.
Ryoka, Erin and Pisces open a sealed stone coffin and find Ceria alive, gaunt from starvation.
Ceria's right hand is ruined: the skin is dead down past the wrist, leaving white bone and sloughed flesh, and where it joins her healthy arm it is blackened like frostbite.
Ceria and Olesm hid in coffins for three or four days in the ruins.
Ceria says she burned up all her remaining mana creating ice for the two of them to suck on while they had no water.
Asked whether her hand was hurt by a frost spell such as [Glacial Spear], Ceria says she simply used up all the magic in her wand.
Ceria thanks Pisces sincerely as "Master Mage"; Pisces replies that Wistram students must stick together.
Ceria tells Erin that Skinner killed Cervial, Gerald and half of their group, then Gerial, Sostrom and Calruz's arm, and that she could not even fight back while he stared at her.

Ceria and Olesm recover in a secluded part of the Liscor Watch building, not under guard but not free to roam, and Ceria explains they are not blamed because they fought and the city took all the treasure as a fine.
Ceria has no wand, spell books or gold after the ruins, and says her ruined hand means she will not go adventuring soon; Yvlon is barely responsive.
Ceria declines Erin's offer of a barmaid job, saying she is not the bar-serving type and does not do well with males.
Ceria and Relc both wonder why their [Dangersense] did not go off near the strange tree fragment.
Ceria remembers the King of Destruction's first rampage, hearing of nations falling and cities sieged, and how he suddenly ended his ambitions; she has never been to Chandrar.
Ceria has lost all her coin, all her magical artifacts except her robes, her friends and her hand, and sometimes forgets it until it hits her again.
Ceria sleeps in the furthest upstairs room of The Wandering Inn from the staircase, having insisted she did not want to take any space.
Ceria wakes screaming from a nightmare in which Skinner finds her in the coffin and opens the lid.
Ceria, half-asleep, points her skeletal hand at Erin and fires a spike of ice that tears out some of Erin's hair and embeds in the wall.

Ceria's skeletal hand moves without her trying to use magic, and she says it must be because she is a Half-elf; she says Half-elves are not immortal, only longer-lived, and their bodies are closer to magic in nature.

Ceria says she lost her hand when the backlash of a badly cast spell froze it: she meant to cast [Glacial Spear], an advanced form of [Ice Spike], but poured all her remaining mana into an oversized [Ice Spike].
Ceria meets Rags and warns her that the Watch is going to wipe out or drive off her tribe within a few days; she says she does it so Erin will not be upset and that she owes Erin a lot.
Ceria tells Rags she remembers the last Goblin King's rampage from the sea, which left fire and destruction across three continents, and that she knows Goblins can be dangerous.
Ceria and Pisces cast [Detect Magic] together, with green and blue fingertips; it shows Ryoka enchanted, and Ceria says it is so powerful she cannot do anything about it.
Pisces guesses the magic on Ryoka is Tier 6 or 7.
Ceria tells Ryoka she likes Olesm "a bit", for more than saving her life, after days alone with only each other to whisper to in the ruins.
Ceria tells Pisces she is reforming the Horns of Hammerad, and strikes him with her skeletal hand to show she can still do magic without a wand, conjuring an [Ice Spike] above it.
Ceria raises her skeletal hand and flexes it in front of Lyonette's face to frighten her, warning her to watch her mouth and obey orders.
Ceria always wakes early and had already left for the city when Erin knocked on Lyonette's door the next morning.
Ceria talks with Erin for a long time over spaghetti and meatballs about foods she has eaten in her sixty-odd years.

Ceria says she planted a tracking spell on Lyonette, a trick learned at Wistram while sneaking around the libraries at night; it shows as a [Light] orb with an arrow pointing northwest and slightly downwards toward the north road.
Ceria tells Erin and Yvlon she is going back to adventuring because it is all she knows and she needs to become stronger; Yvlon says she would be honored to journey with her once she recovers.
Ceria fights the Gnolls with her skeletal hand, using [Snowy Blast] to knock a Gnoll off his feet and [Ray of Frost] against Brunkr's shield.

Ceria is over sixty, which she reckons barely twenty by Human standards; she thinks she will be lucky to live past three hundred, since Half-elves grow about a year for every three of a Human's and the average one dies before a hundred.

Ceria's puberty was long and hard because of her Human side: she reached her adult body in her twenties but spent ten years dealing with hormonal imbalances and uncontrolled magical outbursts, and has had many failed relationships, which she does not want Olesm to become.
Ceria lost her comb in the crypts and has no money to replace it.
Ceria likes Olesm but has her own business to finish and has been putting it off while staying at Erin's inn.
Ceria can still sense the magic moving her skeletal hand when she flexes the bone.
Ceria mourns that Gerial, Calruz and the others are dead and that she has lost everything again, and decides that one Horn of Hammerad still remains.

Ceria says she can cast with her skeletal hand at the same efficiency as before, possibly higher, and as fast, though without a wand's latent boost; she says she can still freeze her skin but that having five digits lets her cast [Icy Shard] on each finger simultaneously.
Ceria says the optimal party size is four and that the reformed Horns need another member who does not rely on magic.
Ceria points out to Erin that she once sold jars of acid to Goblins and built her house from a tree that explodes when anything gets near it.
Ceria raises her skeletal hand and kills a Goblin with an [Ice Spike] during an attack by Goblins, and uses [Icy Floor] to crystallise the snow so a Hob's foot slips.
Ceria demands first choice of any spellbooks from the Horns' loot, and Pisces accepts.
Ceria says she began her career killing over a thousand rats until she could find a better job, and thought she would never have to do it again.
Erin tells Ryoka that Ceria has gone north and gone back to adventuring.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria is the unhappy Captain of the Horns of Hammerad, travelling with Pisces, Ksmvr and Yvlon, and snaps at Pisces to stop his constant complaining.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria idly considers casting [Ice Spike] at point blank range at her own face, finding even horrible mutilation preferable to her situation.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria's skeletal hand no longer hurts but sometimes feels as if it still had flesh; she must let magic flow into it to move it, and touching things is the worst.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria says that a mage of around Level 50 would have many enemies, artifacts and valuables, and that the homes of such mages tend to become miniature gauntlets by the time they die.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria and Yvlon receive a bad reception in Esthelm, where local adventurers treat them with sympathy or contempt and anger, especially Yvlon, because all of them knew someone who died in the crypt.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria remembers her great-grandmother, the last family she had, telling her as a child that Half-elves hold only a drop of Elven blood and are not truly half-Elves; the great-grandmother says a Human and a half-Elf always have a half-Elf child, however many Human ancestors a half-Elf has.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria's great-grandmother died nearly two decades before and is buried in her garden in a village on another continent.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria remembers falling in love at twenty-three with a young half-Elf boy in her village and being caught sneaking off with him.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: In Warmage Thresk's sanctuary, Ceria's half-Elven nature helps her fight off the [Insanity] ward on the wall, but it keeps driving her mad when she looks at the symbol; Ksmvr blindfolds her with a strip cut from her pants, which lets her think.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria improvises a ball of mud from water conjured out of the air and earth materialised as for [Stone Dart], to cover the [Insanity] rune, noting she should have learned [Create Water] and that [Mud Ball] would have been more efficient.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria, still maddened, knocks Yvlon and Pisces back with [Stone Fist], a rock gauntlet over her good hand, and fells Pisces with a blunt-headed [Ice Shard] fired from a finger.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria and Pisces cast [Frozen Wind] together against the fire construct of Warmage Thresk, buying a moment for the Horns to flee the heat.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria's best spell is [Ice Spike], and with her skeletal hand she can fire one shot from all five fingers, drawing on all her reserves.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: The Horns of Hammerad come out almost in front of the door that had sent them into the trap, and Pisces says the door teleported them down as the most efficient use of mana.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria casts a [Light] orb that is azure, and pours a mana potion from her belt, protected by thick glass, over Pisces to restore his mana-drained body.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria tells Pisces that he was caught by the fire construct despite [Flash Step] when as a student he could have danced around it for days; Pisces admits he has grown lax and lost his touch, and Ceria says she admired that part of him.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria walks in a cheering city parade with Pisces, Yvlon and Ksmvr after the Horns conquer a dungeon; she is amazed, never having been cheered for in years of adventuring, and has never seen such a sight in her sixty years.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria proposes sending the artifacts to Invrisil, the City of Adventurers, as the nearest place with people able to dispel their magic and perhaps repair them; she says it is the center of the Human lands and the trip would take weeks, so the Horns would rather hire a trusted Runner.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria tells Ryoka she trusts her to carry the Horns' gear and coin, as does Yvlon, while Pisces is on the fence and Ksmvr does not know her well.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria toasts the old Horns of Hammerad with Ryoka, saying "To the old Horns of Hammerad. We did it."

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria's [Dangersense] goes off when the Maid Ressa stands unconcerned among drawn weapons in The Nobleman's Disgrace.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria keeps the burnt half of a spellbook as her greatest treasure, claiming it as the first spellbook found in exchange for the ring, and refuses to lend it to Pisces.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria cannot read most of the spellbook: like most high-level magical spellbooks it mixes ordinary text and magical formulas, and its descriptive text is in a language she does not know; she judges its spells far above her capabilities.
