section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria tells Yvlon that Ryoka is hotheaded, prickly and arrogant but brave, having gone into the crypts to rescue her, and that Calruz trusted her; she realises that neither Pisces nor Ksmvr ever knew who Calruz was.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria says Liscor is safer than Celum, since its walls withstood sieges from the Antinium and from a [Necromancer] far more capable than Pisces, and two Gold-rank teams are in the city.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria remembers that in the pit Yvlon claimed to be Ylawes when Yvlon reacts to the name; Yvlon then says Ylawes is her older brother.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Ceria argues that Pisces does not deserve to be killed for creating one undead, though she is unable to answer Yvlon on how to stop him making another; she says she will make sure he keeps it on a leash, and notes he has not made another.

section: Book 3: Esthelm, the Thresk sanctuary and the Horns reformed
text: Yvlon has not said a word to Pisces all morning and keeps a grudge; Ceria tells her to watch him as a teammate rather than scare him away.

section: Book 4: Teriarch and the road with Erin
text: Ceria strikes first against the old man Teriarch, firing a spike of ice at his midriff with her skeletal hand; it shatters in mid-flight, and she then fires many [Ice Dart] spells, which he blocks.

section: Book 4: Teriarch and the road with Erin
text: Ceria and Pisces admit to Teriarch that they were expelled from Wistram after studying for years and never fully graduated; Pisces adds that they were allowed to claim the name and are still recognised Wistram mages.

section: Book 4: Teriarch and the road with Erin
text: Ceria tells Erin the story of Wistram, saying she never contacted her friends again after leaving.

section: Book 4: Teriarch and the road with Erin
text: Ceria tells Erin she thinks Cognita was addressing Pisces, who truly deserved to graduate, and calls herself just a dropout, though she used the Wistram name to get work and open doors.

section: Book 4: Teriarch and the road with Erin
text: Ceria admits she may have exaggerated details of her Wistram story, after Erin doubts that Illphres destroyed six ships alone and that Ceria and Pisces fought two Trolls in the entrance exams.

section: Book 4: Teriarch and the road with Erin
text: Pisces tells Revi and Typhenous that he and Ceria are graduates of Wistram.

section: Book 4: Teriarch and the road with Erin
text: Ceria shouts at a Fortress Beaver to make it leave the road, saying that is how you talk to animals; it waddles off the road.

section: Book 4: Teriarch and the road with Erin
text: Ceria tells Erin that slimes spawn in bodies of liquid and take on the properties of their original liquid, so the slime they find evidently came from the sewer.

Ceria is 58 years old and has waited over forty years for the day she boards a ship from South Harbor in Belan, a southern port city of Terandria, bound for Wistram; her people consider her still a young adult.

Ceria earns a place on the ship Errant Traveller by showing an examiner the barely Tier 2 spells she taught herself, [Stone Dart], [Flame Jet] and [Chameleon], the last of which has saved her life many times; she has never owned a spellbook.
Ceria tells Pisces she is a Bronze-rank adventurer hoping to earn money by learning more powerful spells at Wistram, and failing that to learn one or two Tier 3 spells.

Ceria meets Pisces on the ship to Wistram when he asks to take the neighbouring bunk below decks; he is delighted to meet a Half-elf and shakes her hand, while her unearthly complexion and pointed ears have already ostracised her from the other passengers.
Ceria and Pisces enter Wistram Academy together with the other new students after a harrowing voyage through a storm.
Ceria spent the best part of a decade saving the twenty gold pieces that attending Wistram Academy for a month cost, and was told by the examiner to present herself on the docks two weeks later.

After Pisces stands up for her against Charles and Timor on the ship, and the Captain threatens to throw them overboard if they cast again, Ceria tells him she is used to such treatment, and is surprised to find herself getting along with a Human.
Ceria suspects that the instructor of the Magical Foundations class, Rievan, is a Human who grew up in Terandria, which would explain his dislike of her as a half-Elf.
As a new student Ceria knows [Ice Shard] but can barely create more than twenty darts before she must sit down.

Ceria, with only a month to prove herself and no real spellbook to study, agrees with Pisces to take a risk and steal a trapped spellbook with a Tier 4 spell from a hidden section of the Wistram library, saying "Let's go grab a spellbook."

Ceria and Pisces obtain the spellbook, and Ceria realises Pisces meant to share it with her all along; she agrees to study it with him, though it is his book, since he must give Cognita his other spellbook.

Ceria realises that years earlier she would have put an arrow in a Human's head or run away, but now sits at night beside Pisces as if it were natural; she thinks of him as a friend and quite likes him.

Ceria uses [Detect Magic] to find hexes at her door, a grease spell and a shock spell, burns them out with a jet of flame, and suspects Charles and his friends plant such traps nightly; she says Charles is allied with Rievan.
Pisces, who had cast a spell to attract mice, has them chase off the people planting a trap at Ceria's door at night, leaving some Human students with small bites; Ceria and Pisces say nothing.

Ceria practises for the combat trial by shooting down floating [Light] orbs with [Stone Dart], her favorite spell and the one she is most proficient at; she can fire only about thirty before resting, and her aim worsens past fifty feet and in wind, though she hits an orb 120 feet away.
Ceria worked as a Bronze-rank adventurer on and off to make ends meet, and practised aiming in the forests around her home, shooting leaves from trees.

The mage Illphres tells Ceria her aim is sloppy because she does not compensate for the wind, and demonstrates by freezing the wings of a passing seagull from a distance; she says everything is a moving target.

In the combat trial Ceria is struck from behind on the back of the head as she aims at a Troll's eyes; Rievan calls it an accident, mages angrily say the boy hit her on purpose and demand a retrial, and the examiners decide to judge her by what they saw.

Ceria breaks Illphres's ice wall, built to withstand spells below Tier 4, by rubbing kitchen salt on it and raising the heat with her own spells; Illphres admits she did not expect salt and Ceria asks whether she passes.
Ceria's name appears last on the list of students admitted to Wistram, which also carries Pisces' name.
Illphres tells a tearful Ceria that she keeps her promises and will hold class in her quarters the next day, and will also teach any of Ceria's friends who melt the ice; Ceria says Pisces will come.
Ceria tells Illphres she has gained the [Elementalist] class.
Ceria stands outside Illphres' door every day seeking her as a master, because as a second-year student she needs one; she wants a master who knows actual combat magic.
Calvaron says there is a running bet of fifty-to-one that Ceria will not persuade Illphres to be her master by the end of the year.
Ceria says she thinks Illphres likes her and will not turn her to ice, since she hears Illphres once got in a lot of trouble with the Council for doing it.

Ceria and Pisces develop a new messaging spell of a flying firefly of light that carries symbols only the recipient can read; Mons masters it, and Pisces claims it is more complex than any [Message] spell and works up to several miles away.
Wistram students call Ceria "professor" with respect and fear, because Illphres makes her teach her classes to the new students while she is her apprentice.
Ceria becomes Illphres' apprentice: Ophelia later says she saw Ceria fighting pirates a year earlier, and Illphres says she did not want an apprentice and still does not, but Ceria insisted.

Ceria trains against Illphres's ice barrier with [Ice Dart], [Ice Spike] (newly learned) and a storm of fourteen [Frost Arrows], which fail to break it; Illphres says her defense is terrible and tells her to raise [Barrier of the Winds], which Ceria does not know yet.
Illphres calls [Frozen Shield] a terrible spell, advises Ceria to learn [Wall of Ice] at a higher level, and says mastery of [Ice Spike] is key to learning [Glacial Spear].

Ceria asks Calvaron for a ring or amulet with the best available ice and cold resistance binding, and later brings Illphres' group rings with roughly Tier 4 enchantments against ice magic, bought through Calvaron with a very large amount of gold.

After Pisces is shunned by other students, Ceria tells him she does not think they are friends anymore; when he asks if they are enemies, she says that is stupid and murmurs that they could not be enemies.
Ceria later asks Pisces to tell her everything and why, and he relaxes and looks at her as he used to.

Ceria is told that at the end of the year Illphres, Bastam, Ophelia, Qum and the speaker will challenge Cognita to destroy her and open the doors to the rest of Wistram, and she responds by flipping the table.
The Wistram Council votes narrowly to exile Pisces on pain of death if he returns, and tells Ceria Springwalker she must leave on the next ship too.
Cognita, using the authority of Archmage Zelkyr, graduates Ceria and Pisces as true mages of Wistram before the assembled students and mages.
Ceria tells Pisces that when they reach shore they will part and she never wants to see his face again, and walks away after saying goodbye, carrying a rucksack of the few things she has.

Ceria tells Ryoka the Horns are considering the dungeon, as monster hunting around Liscor is unprofitable, especially in winter, and she does not want to tangle with Rock Crabs even with their new gear; she says she and Yvlon learned their lesson once.
Ceria carries a wand Ryoka brought back from Invrisil, magic robes and a burned spellbook, which are all she has, and feels her magic is a snowflake in the wind compared with real adventurers.
Ceria guesses that Regrika Blackpaw, who has a Gold-rank mage with her, will enter Liscor's dungeon within a day, since she cannot imagine Regrika fearing many traps.
Ceria holds her breath as Pisces tells Falene that they are both graduates of Wistram, and Falene replies that standards must have lowered quite a bit since she attended.

section: Book 7: the moth attack and the Liscor festival
text: Ceria is a half-Elf [Cryomancer] with a skeletal left hand, in a Silver-rank team on the verge of Gold that has adventured only a few months and is made up of Pisces, a [Necromancer], Yvlon, a [Wounded Warrior], and Ksmvr, a three-armed Antinium.

section: Book 7: the moth attack and the Liscor festival
text: Ceria fires [Ice Spikes] with both her wand and her skeletal hand at moths bursting through the inn's windows, and uses walls of ice to pin moths and block broken windows.

section: Book 7: the moth attack and the Liscor festival
text: Ceria casts [Frost Bloom] from a wand, sending a bubble of hoar frost twenty or thirty feet overhead so that droplets fall as hail, to win over the Liscor crowd, and then shows off spells with Pisces and the others to applause.
Erin tells Ylawes that Ceria casts [Silence] on her and Yvlon's room every night because Ceria and Yvlon wake screaming every other night, as Pisces says they also did while exploring Albez.

At dinner Ceria tells the Horns she freezes up each time she should order them into the dungeon, that her hands shake, and that she is a coward unfit to be Captain, having been part of Calruz's team; Yvlon says she is afraid too.

Pisces and Ksmvr both affirm they will follow Ceria into the dungeon, and Ceria then decides to go in, saying she wants glory, wealth and power, that the dungeon scares her, and that a friend might be in there.

Ceria and the Horns agree to let the dungeon's entrances become known, since they cannot search it alone, knowing it will cause trouble, in the hope of finding Calruz; Ksmvr tells Ceria for the eighteenth time that he is not betraying his Hive.

Ceria tells Yvlon she has been adventuring for nearly a decade, is sixty years old, and spent forty years of her life in a half-Elf village, where years pass easily and children behave worse than Human teens, and she feels she only started living after leaving.

Ceria asks the raid of adventurers at the dungeon to look for Calruz, a Minotaur who used to lead her group and vanished months earlier in Liscor's crypt; an old yellow-scaled Drake with a greatsword tells her to give it up.
Ceria is taken by the Raskghar and wakes injured in the dungeon in the presence of Calruz, who is alive, one-armed and mad, and had been looking for her.
Ceria finds Calruz leading the Raskghar as his tribe and holding captive Gnolls; she sees the madness in him, recognising it from half-Elf village elders, Wistram mages and adventurers.

Ceria tells Calruz that the Horns died in the crypt and that she now leads the Horns of Hammerad with a new team; she refuses his orders, demands the Gnolls be freed, and answers him with a raised middle finger of her skeletal hand.
Ceria tells Calruz she lost her hand using a spell to hold off the undead, when the magical backlash froze all the skin off.

Whenever Calruz looks at her, Ceria feels fear and an overwhelming urge to obey that fades when he looks away, and she deduces he is using, or merely has, a Skill; she thinks Calruz broke her will by sacrificing a Gnoll and has won the contest of leadership.
Ceria knows of the chute connecting Liscor's crypt to the dungeon, which Pisces showed her, and remembers the room full of Raskghar bones.

Ceria tells Calruz she recruited Pisces, Ksmvr and Yvlon for the new Horns, saying she had few candidates; other teams refused to speak to her at the Adventurer's Guild, she and Yvlon were ready to quit, until Olesm found a map of Albez.

Ceria tells Calruz how she led the other three into Albez and found treasure where she and Calruz had explored often with little success, and tells him about Ryoka losing fingers during the winter and vanishing after the disastrous battle with Regrika Blackpaw.

Ceria sees a group of fourteen invisible insect-and-maggot monsters at a pool in the dungeon that Calruz and the Raskghar cannot see; she tells Calruz where nine are at the water's edge and five are coming around, and the Raskghar attack on her directions.

Calruz shows Ceria the city at the heart of the dungeon and a warning that it is protected by the Mother of Graves, served by three guardians of the crypts, Skinner, Snatcher and Stalker; Ceria clings to him when he mentions Skinner and learns Snatcher is the one still alive.
Ceria lies to Calruz that she did not bring adventurers to the dungeon, saying she cannot cast [Message]; she has in fact told Pisces what she could.
Calruz throws Ceria so hard that her wand bounces out of her belt and rolls away into the darkness.
Ceria forms a dagger of ice from her tears and the water in her flask, sharpened enough to kill a Minotaur, intending to kill Calruz, though she feels no guilt left for him.
Ceria lunges at Calruz's throat with the ice dagger, but he knocks it away and twists her skeletal arm, because the Raskghar smelled the dagger on her back and warned him.

Ceria argues to Calruz that the Raskghar will betray him, because the ritual may make the awakened permanently intelligent, and that Nokha lied when she said he was essential for thinking when the moon was not full; Calruz is convinced the awakened plan to overthrow him.
Ceria tells Calruz to let go of the Gnolls and run to Liscor, where he would be protected.

Ceria sends Pisces a firefly message that the Raskghar ritual may make them smart all the time, that they may challenge Calruz, and that she will help him to buy time to save the Gnolls; she resolves not to run again.

Ceria raises a double-layered ice wall at least five feet thick against Snatcher, but it smashes through it and sends her flying to the ceiling, from which she falls twenty feet; she heals herself with her last two healing potions.
Ceria quarrels with Calruz over whether Mrsha is mute, insisting it means unable to speak, not unable to make sounds, a distinction Pisces read in a book.
Ceria sends Pisces a fiery-bug message that the Gnolls escaped, Mrsha is here, the Raskghar will rebel soon, and he should hurry.

Calruz backhands Ceria, shattering a mask of ice made to look like her face; she rises scowling in frost armor over her robes, skin and skeletal hand, and says Illphres always said her masks were tougher than steel.
Ceria says the Horns of Hammerad do not run and, with a frost-armored charge, fights alongside Calruz, who swings his enchanted axe with [Whirlwind Cleave], while she shoots an [Ice Spike].
Ceria kills or fells Calruz with an [Ice Spike] between the eyes as he smiles and drops his axe, then kneels over him in tears and calls him a stupid Minotaur with a hard head.
Ceria says Calruz must pay for what he has done, madness or not, and that she will be there to testify.
Ceria sits at her table in the inn after the dungeon, having told her teammates nearly everything but unable to tell them what it was like.
Ceria wears a wooden Ring of Barkskin and says it makes her feel like a tree; sun on her skin makes her blissful.
Ceria conjures a giant ice sphere for the water pitcher and small ice cubes, which she likes to chew, out of the air.
Ceria's skeletal hand has no feeling, so she crushed a bug between its fingers without noticing.

Ceria tells Erin that Calruz will be executed under Drake law, that she should have killed him when she had the chance but could not, and that he was insane yet still cared about Gerial and the others.
Ceria tells Erin she was the only adventurer in the Raskghar camp, can still hear the dead screaming, and could not stop the killings; she told the others about it but not all.
Ceria announces she is done with the dungeon after the Horns and allies gather the treasure, and the others cheer; Jelaqua says the Halfseekers are done too.
Ceria and Pisces try to work out a spell that can hit Reiss' Goblins from Liscor's walls during the attack.
Ceria suggests the Horns go to Celum the next day to take local requests, and the Horns brighten at the idea.
Ceria speaks to Calruz across a magical barrier and tells him the northern teams are leaving with the Raskghar treasure; Calruz guesses it must be exchanged and Ceria names Invrisil.
Ceria vows that when the Horns meet the other teams again they will be Gold-rank, then opens the door to Celum.
Ceria says she now has [Ice Wall] and [Frozen Armor], both defensive spells, and that until she can throw [Ice Lance] like her old master she is only good at locking down opponents.
Ceria casts [Frozen Armor] on herself during a brawl, covering her in ice that imitates plate armor, and snares an attacker with [Ice Wall].
Ceria tells the old adventurer Crossbow Stan that the dead of the crypt were cremated and their families got all the money left, and that her own wand was gone.
Ceria tells Ksmvr "Good job" after his solo action, adding that he should not be so reckless next time.
Ceria says she must recharge the inn's door to Pallass after Pisces volunteers to help someone, noting two people may have to stay the night there, and later yawns with her mana spent.
Grimalkin tells Ceria she was the weakest on her team in a mock battle, relied on spells and [Ice Walls], is out of shape with atrophied leg muscles, lacks firepower, and smells of alcohol.
Ceria tells Grimalkin that she and Pisces were expelled by Wistram's Council of Mages but allowed to graduate because the Golem Cognita declared them graduates.

Ceria recounts that her master Illphres, an expert [Ice Mage] who took her in, died in the test along with four other senior [Mages], when Pisces animated their corpses to rob the grave of Archmage Nekhret; Ceria names Montressa and Beatrice as friends and says Calvaron died there too.

Grimalkin trains Ceria by having her lie in a wooden bathtub of boiling water heated by a fire, so she must lower the heat by freezing the water; she screams and curses and has lasted eight minutes by his count.
Ceria brings Calruz in his cell a metal weight, a basket with two rats from Mrsha, and a book she bought, The Conquests of Tulm the Mithril, a History.
Ceria tells Calruz that Lism has dropped the line about executing him and that Krshia told Erin privately she would let him live if elected.

Ceria says Half-elves born in traditional villages do not worry about marriage until their eighties, adding that Falene is more likely to be looking and that she is aiming to succeed as an adventurer.

Ceria says she undergoes daily boil-baths with Grimalkin, who comes every day for an hour or two under his agreement with Erin, and that Pisces studies alone, probably trying to master another Tier 4 spell.
A Wistram party seals Ceria in a black box, where she turns to black motes and vanishes; when Alais wakes, Ceria, Yvlon and Ksmvr are gone.

Montressa accuses Ceria of joining Pisces, who she says killed Calvaron and used Illphres' body, and of falsely calling herself a Wistram [Mage] without passing half her classes; Ceria answers that she and Pisces have changed, that it was an accident years ago, that she earned the right to the name, and that Cognita vouched for Pisces.

section: Book 14: the Creler fight and the merge
text: Facing a Creler, Ceria pulls magic from her bones to raise thick ice walls on a hill and tells Pisces to run because one of them must live, saying she has had her turn; Pisces tackles her away instead, says he would rather die than leave his friends, and holds her hand.

section: Book 14: the Creler fight and the merge
text: Ceria and Pisces link minds and combine ice and necromancy to turn the Bone Behemoth's broken bones into an ice-coated Frostmarrow Behemoth, as named by Perril Chandler, which hammers the Creler flat.

section: Book 14: the Creler fight and the merge
text: Ceria and Pisces suffer fog after the linked magic: Ceria keeps thinking about animating bones, and she says Palt blames the difficulty of uncombining disciplines; they cannot cast spells for a few days and she thinks they got off lucky.
Ceria, an [Arctic Cryomancer] with pale eyes and a skeletal hand, makes the air around her colder, and if she loses control it turns to ice and may snow.
Ceria builds a shelter around the wagon from opaque [Ice Walls] with a slanted roof, windows and a chimney, saying magical ice will vanish rather than drip, and that she will recast it as they sleep.
When Jelaqua asks Ceria if it is serious, Ceria replies that they are pretty serious and giving it a shot, about the Horns' plan to go north, and Jelaqua tearfully congratulates her.
Ksmvr tells the wagon that Hedault proposed to Ceria and that he informed everyone of the engagement; Ceria is mortified, denies it and says Hedault does not even like them.
Cervial is a Silver-rank adventurer who captains a team and carries a large longbow.
Cervial leads a team called the Flawless Flights, which is one of three willing to enter the Ruins of Liscor first.
Cervial is a Silver-rank archer-captain who also uses a Dwarven crossbow.
Cervial says he will join the plan to enter the Ruins only if Ceria Springwalker thinks it worth the risk, since she has more experience than the whole room.
Cervial sits next to Ryoka at the table and explains that Calruz wants the challenge and experience from any enemy, as an old-fashioned Levelist.
Cervial offers Ryoka personalized Runner's Guild contracts for exclusive deliveries, and she declines, saying she is not a team player.
Cervial says his [Appraisal] Skill, which [Marksmen] sometimes get, shows him no Level or Class for Ryoka.
Cervial whistles at the inn and complains that his group sleeps three people to a room in their own inn.
Cervial and Yvlon run to Liscor and back in under thirty minutes looking for the missing girl, and report that the gate guard saw no one.
Cervial found someone willing to explore and map the first level of the Ruins, though nobody will go further.
Cervial owns a massive Dwarf-made crossbow of sleek black metal, which cost nearly every gold piece his team had.
Cervial says the crossbow cracked the armor of a Stone Golem with one shot and has brought down many shielded enemies.
Cervial kneels with the Dwarven crossbow among eight archers in the front line, with two slings and several longbows and shortbows.
Cervial's Flawless Flights lose two members in the ambush and two more in the scouting group.
Cervial weeps while reloading, saying his bolt hit a monster that still took Elise and ate her.
Cervial's face is seen in the white mass of skinned bodies, empty and vacant, along with Gerald and Lir, and the adventurers realise the creature has absorbed them.
Cervial is later named by Ceria as one of the Silver-rank Captains who did not sense anything amiss about the sealed door.
Cessic is a Lizardman new student at Wistram who gravitates toward Ceria, the half-Elf, in class.
Cessic fans out his neck frills when he spots Ceria and Pisces, and tells them they are about to get their first class in destruction magic.
Cessic is claustrophobic and paces in panic, hyperventilating, while the new students wait.
Ceria tells Cessic to stop pacing and look out a window.
Later, Cessic has rainbow scales, a bright red neck frill, a hat and a wand, and welcomes the new students to Wistram.
Blackmage recognizes Cessic instantly when he strides in at the head of the new students.
Cetris Duiland is the [Mayor] of Celum, a name so unremarkable that most people in his own city do not know it.
Cetris has a Skill as [Mayor], [Disadvantaged Renegotiation], that forces a negotiation to begin again with the odds against its target.
Cetris summons Erin to appear before him in Celum, with Montressa, Octavia and Lyonette present, after she opens the door to confront Numbtongue's disappearance.
The hearing is attended by the Head of the Merchant's Guild, the Baker's Guild representative, the Runner's Guildmaster and the [Innkeepers] Agnes, Ulia and Timbor.
Cetris tells Erin that the Innkeeper's Association of Celum has the most complaints against her and he does not want a trade war.
Cetris says Erin's door will be banned from Celum, citing animosity with three guilds, two of his best inns, and the Hobgoblin.
Cetris says gates and monitoring could deal with the Antinium and the Hobgoblin, but the real problem is Erin's reputation for attracting trouble.
Cetris says there is a betting pool, with rich individuals and monarchs among the bettors, on whether Celum will be attacked and how many casualties there will be.
Octavia offers to move to Liscor, which would end another of Celum's headaches.
Cetris calls [Disadvantaged Renegotiation] when the Players of Celum's departure is raised, and the room pauses.
Cetris is startled that Lyonette resists his Skill, since only a [Diplomat] or [Merchant] should be able to.
Cetris allows the door to stay open under a special permit, so long as the Hobgoblin stays in Octavia's shop.
Cetris proposes import and export taxes and a small usage fee for the door, with the Runner's Guild and Merchant's Guild inspecting.
Cetris babbles at Erin that the bets were not supposed to be like this and that it is her fault for taking her door away.
Cetris has seen Celum through windfalls from Octavia Cotton's inventions, the [Alchemist] gangs, a Hobgoblin, an Antinium and a freak avalanche.
Cetris thought the Bloodfeast Raiders' attack was the end of Celum, and people fled the city.
Gold pours into Celum's coffers after Jasi Redigal mentions the city while raising funds on Wistram's television network.
The donations come as gold sent by other nations, including Ailendamus, Nerrhavia's Fallen and the Forgotten Wing Company, and from nobles such as Magnolia Reinhart.
Cetris fears that someone will ask for the gold back, but he intends to spend it.
Cetris asks Erin for advice on the relief funding, and she tells him to build a memorial thanking the donors and not to let the money be wasted.
Cetris says he came to ask about hiring Liscor's [Architect] and [Builders], even Antinium, who he hears work cheap.
Chaldion is an old, nearly completely grey Drake with several facial scars and an eye patch over his right eye, who is as old as Tekshia and as tough as steel.
Chaldion is the [Grand Strategist] of Pallass, in charge of its armies, and is over Level 50 according to Sir Relz.
Chaldion is one hundred and six years old and looks to be in his seventies, with many potions behind that appearance.
Chaldion has a missing eye replaced with magical gemstones that can kill with a look, and swaps them under his eye patch.
Chaldion wears a blue gemstone eye for ordinary use that flashes bright light and a [Truesight] effect.
Chaldion swaps in a fiery red gemstone for the thunderous city-wide announcement, and a white clouded gemstone when he casts [Scrying].
Chaldion uses a magical cane for support, which gives him a jolt of stability.
Chaldion uses a ring and his eye-patch gem to create a bubble of privacy for whispered conversations.
Chaldion's favourite drink is the Chaldion's Eye, a Firebreath Whiskey and Ultasian bitter cocktail with an ice eye holding sweet wine.
Chaldion beats Erin at chess with a split attack that wins her queen, and names his Skill as [Path to Victory].
Chaldion flips up his eye patch to confirm with [Truesight] that Erin is not using magic or a Skill.
Chaldion asks Erin about the games Go and Shogi.
Chaldion says his Skill shows only one route to victory, not the optimal one, and Erin changed strategy to defeat him on the third game.
Chaldion says that a sleeping Skill of Erin's means she is at that level, and is not very powerful.
Chaldion plays Bird at chess and says he wants to talk about his Hive.
Chaldion tells Warden Grasfur to pretend Saliss' incident never occurred, and takes over Erin's case.
Chaldion tells Saliss that his rank gives him privilege and uses an aura on him before it fades.
Chaldion releases Erin on condition she play another chess game with him.
Chaldion agrees to drink at the inn with Lasica and Rufelt after the arrest.
Chaldion's look convinces Erin that the attack is nobody's fault, since the gods were dead and a Dragon meddled.
Chaldion puts out an inquiry on Erin and finds nothing.
Chaldion issues a city-wide alarm on his authority as [Grand Strategist] and orders 1st Army to the walls.
Chaldion opens a gateway to the walls, bringing General Duln and nearly four hundred [Soldiers] through.
Chaldion uses [Path to Victory] and says he sees one road.
Chaldion orders all fliers to land within forty seconds and aims Pallass' wall lightning spells inside the city.
Chaldion counts deviations from his vision and murmurs "Stay alive, Miss Erin Solstice", having not seen her in it.
Chaldion orders Noass and Sir Relz restrained, the scrying mirror confiscated and anti-divination wards cast, ending the broadcast.
Chaldion visits the inn with Grimalkin and greets Lyonette as Lady du Marquin.
Chaldion tells Lyonette in private that she is Princess du Marquin and does not hide her heritage well.
Chaldion advises Lyonette to change her hair colour and name and buy a charm against [Appraisal], and promises to keep her secret.
Chaldion fails to find Mrsha by [Scrying] around the inn.
Chaldion tells the [Generals] of the 1st and 4th armies to form experimental regiments based on Grimalkin's training plans.
Chaldion foresees commuters from Esthelm using the magic door and compares Erin to a quarter of Saliss.
Chaldion appears on the scrying broadcast with Noass and says he would retreat to the capital and pull back from the Jecrass and Medain fronts.
Chaldion calls Belchan's chosen defensive position a mistake and says the army will be slaughtered.
Chaldion falls eight steps down the Northern Grand Staircase beside General Edellein Blackwing, fracturing his left leg.
Chaldion tells the Walled Cities by [Message] to go to Rhir's hell and stop spreading gossip.
Chaldion flips up his eye patch at Saliss, blasting light around the room.
Chaldion begs Saliss to become Pallass' hero, and Saliss refuses, saying he wants to choose.
Chaldion calls Saliss a disgrace after he insists on being himself.
Chaldion says he knows enough about Turnscales to say it is not a choice to act like what you are.
Chaldion suspects the Goblin Lord used necromancy, since a single Goblin Lord spellcaster beat the Tidebreaker unseen.
Chaldion is de-aged by two years by the treatment, and has a hunch he does not share.
Chaldion, recovering from his leg wound in a healer's clinic, orders an emergency Assembly of Crafts and the arrest of Golden Triangle members.
Chaldion learns the arrested Gnoll was found dead with his throat slit and the Dullahan woman has disappeared.
Chaldion proposes with Generals Edellein and Duln to credit General Sserys' memorial to Liscor's Free Antinium and hold a celebration in three days.
Chaldion receives an unmarked message, almost certainly from Wistram, about the Antinium Hives.
Chaldion takes the Raskghar prisoners to Pallass on his authority and the Watch Captain's consent.
Chaldion says those responsible for the Raskghar crimes will be executed by the end of the week and the children given a chance.
Chaldion says regular Raskghar are about a Level 15 Gnoll [Warrior], and Level 20 at best when Awakened or on a full moon.
Chaldion tells the council that [Interrogators] will decide the Raskghar's guilt before sentencing.
Charlay is a Centauress City Runner, over seven feet tall and weighing at least a ton, with a tan coat with large brown spots and short blonde-grey hair.
Charlay has the nickname Dustrider Charlay, earned after two years running in the area.
Charlay comes from Baleros and says Centaurs are common in central Baleros but rare in Izril.
Charlay says Izril has lovely flat places and there would be tens of thousands of Centaurs there if not for the ocean crossing.
Charlay has a horse's palate for bland foods, cannot handle spice, loves salty savoury food, fears snakes and holds grudges.
Charlay has the Skill [Spray Hoof], which kicks backward to throw up dust, or mud and water when the ground is wet.
Charlay carries two wands and a dagger, outruns people, and can knock someone off a horse with her wands and make a dust cloud.
Charlay trails Ryoka for three days, saying she is scoping out her competition.
Charlay calls Ryoka "Pukey" because Ryoka vomited on her.
Charlay throws Ryoka a drying stone to clean off the mud she splattered on her.
Charlay boasts she is twice as fast as Ryoka, whom Ryoka thinks she is faster than, though not by that much.
Charlay is terrified of Alevica and says she thinks Alevica cast a spell that set her tail on fire after Charlay objected to being cut in line.
Charlay's tail bears a faint burn scar, and she needed four healing potions to stop the fire.
Charlay agrees to run with Ryoka to Riverfarm, saying she would like to come, and Ryoka calls her a friend.
Charlay says insulting each other is what friends do among her Centaur friends in Baleros.
Ryoka and Charlay pass eight burned ruins on the road south.
Ryoka announces she will start a Runner's Guild in Riverfarm, and Charlay immediately asks for dibs on Guildmistress.
Charlay helps lay out the plan to build a network of Runners and asks to be listed as Riverfarm's top Runner.
Rie agrees to convert a warehouse into a Guild, and Charlay passes on being Guildmistress when she hears it pays nothing.
Charlay runs thirty-two miles to Filk and announces she is Riverfarm's top Runner from its new Runner's Guild.
Charlay demands guild seals and supplies on Lady Rie's account from a Filk [Receptionist].
Charlay pays a Filk [Fence] and [Broker] three gold in advance for information on [Witches], after haggling him down from five.
The [Broker] tells Charlay to return in four days, with more gold.
Charlay tells Durene to stop thinking like a Human and be proud of what she is.
Charlay tells Ryoka she is going to run south through the fire, and Ryoka protests that the smoke will kill her.
Charlay collapses from the smoke, and Durene carries her limp form back to Wiskeria.
Charlay carries Eloise to Gralton's lands in two days, for a fee tripled from twenty-five to seventy-five gold.
Later, Charlay says goodbye to Ryoka days earlier, because her city misses her and she is restless after staying through fire and fury.
Charlay hugs Ryoka and tells her friends cry, and they call each other Pukey and Dusty.
Charles de Trevalier is a young noble student who calls himself the scion of his house and demands respect.
He wears rich clothes and an ornamental shortsword, and has a gaggle of other teens following him.
Charles approaches Ceria and Pisces on the ship in the manner of a prelude to harassment.
He rests a hand on his sword as if wanting to draw it, but is clearly unprepared for actual violence.
Charles warns Pisces that Timor du Havrington is an experienced warrior with many levels in [Warrior] who would cut him to bits.
Ceria thinks Timor does not hold himself like a warrior.
Timor claims to be a [Warrior] and a [Lord] when confronting Pisces.
Charles and his cronies back off when Pisces draws his rapier faster than the sword-wielding student had.
Calvaron says Charles is heavily in Rievan's camp and certainly part of the Libertarian faction.
Calvaron expects the Libertarians to welcome his family's deep pockets and influence.
Charles caused a commotion in Illphres' classroom by calling for her to teach him.
Calvaron says Charles got in only by having someone else melt Illphres' ice, so she ruled it did not count.
Calvaron guesses that Rievan, who argued with Illphres about it, probably did the melting.
Charles buys Illphres' spellbook from the Drake student who was carrying it to Ceria, for gold and then secrets.
He drops it from a balcony into the sea, where it freezes the water around it and sinks encased in ice that will not melt.
Beatrice sees him smiling afterward and says nothing.
Chesacre is a female Antinium Soldier, female by name and personality even if not by appearance.
Chesacre and Thaina are the two female Soldiers, whose paint forms a whole across their two bodies.
Chesacre and Thaina are regulars of the inn, and Mrsha almost always sees them holding hands.
Chesacre and Thaina wash each other with soap and water before they take their paint, which is something new in the Hive.
The other Antinium watching look away as one, and Purple Smiles hangs Fortresses of Fluff blankets on wooden poles to give the two privacy.
Chesacre picks up a brush and the two paint a design onto each other's bodies, a magical silver building that is whole only when they stand side by side.
Chesacre, sitting next to Thaina, puts out one of her three remaining arms to block Klbkch as he walks toward Pawn with his sword drawn.
Klbkch's sword cuts off Chesacre's arm, and Erin cries out at the sight of the green blood.
Chesacre then walks in front of Klbkch and just waits, without raising her two remaining arms on her right side.
Chesacre and Thaina went into the dungeon, survived Headsnatcher and came back, when a thousand Antinium went in and only they made it.
After Thaina asks Mrsha in sign for her words, Chesacre carefully raises her hands and signs yes.
Chole is one of the Earthers in Richard's group, and a [Nurse].
Chole is from California.
Chole did not complete her nursing education, but is still the most medically-qualified person in the world, by her own account.
Chole pulls Cynthia away from Tom and gives him the stink-eye when Cynthia screams at him over the clown music.
Chole argues with Vincent, wanting to use his iPhone to call the others again.
Chole and another girl get between Vincent and Kevin before their argument comes to fists.
Chole backs her horse up to ride behind Tom and Richard as the group rides into Paranfer.
Vincent helps Chole down from her horse.
Chole glares at Eddy when he says it is weird that a woman is so open about it, then goes to talk to [Lady] Theras.
Chole opens Tom's door while he spins a knife, and screams and runs when he gestures at her with the blade.
Chole approaches Richard to say she is worried that Tom has shut himself in his soundproofed room for two days.
Chole tells Richard that Tom needs help and that she has been trying to work with him.
Chole says Emily and Tom hate each other, and that no one talks to Tom.
Chole thinks Tom's condition is not just mental illness, and that Tom is choosing to be the way he is, or has one of the sacrificial classes Lord Hayvon described.
Richard tells Tom that Chole says the other Tom is not to blame for everything.
Chole is working for Hayvon on blood transfusions and other non-magical Earth medicine.
Chole's blood-transfusion equipment is at Hayvon's mansion when it is needed to save Huntress Delezza, and the Champions try to improvise without it.
Chole tells Tom how to test blood compatibility by mixing blood and watching for platelets, and Emily relays the method.
After Huntress Delezza dies, the Champions feel guilt and think that things might have been different if Chole, their [Nurse], had been there.
Emily shields Chole when Richard's group falls back from a battle at the wall.
Cirille Bitterclaw is a black-scaled female Drake [Commander] from Manus who serves in the armies defending Rhir.
Cirille is an Oldblood with two small vestigial wings on her back that cannot lift her and only hurt in armor.
Cirille shouts at her company to stop running over civilians, then introduces herself to Richard Davenport and Tom as the "sorry" [Commander] of the lot.
Cirille wears a plumed helmet, and unlike her soldiers her armor is open at the back to let the wings out.
Cirille says her wings are only for show, and that being Oldblood is why she was chosen for a year's service in Rhir.
Cirille commands about ten thousand Drakes, who turn out in minutes when she thinks a message from High Command means an attack.
Cirille is woken repeatedly by Bastion-General Quiteil of 4th Wall, who tests her readiness and identity with codes and questions.
Cirille is tested eight times in a single day by Quiteil, which leaves her angry, and she names Spearmaster Lulv as her superior in Manus.
Cirille has been stationed in the capital of Rhir for nearly three years of a four-year rotation.
Cirille was sent because the Walled Cities send their second or third-best to Rhir as a matter of pride.
Cirille owes her military discipline to Manus, her home city.
Cirille's closest officers are Captain Shellc and Lieutenant Ossky.
Quiteil orders Cirille's division to 4th Wall and then to the 5th Wall, under Bastion-General Zavarial.
Quiteil assigns Cirille two thousand one hundred and three Gnolls under Chief Warrior Merish to fold into her command.
The secretary-general keeps Cirille in command rather than replacing her with Merish, and tells her to settle her grievances with Captain Hetarria.
Cirille explains Manus doctrine that artifacts can be lost, so it is better to commit only to a battle that can be won.
Delezza argues that the Blighted Kingdom gets scrolls from around the world and has had thousands of years to build up a stockpile of them.
Cirille reaches [Foreign Commander Level 33!] and changes class to [Combined-Arms Commander].
Cirille gains the Skill [Copy Weapon Art] and the Synergy [Gnoll-Drake Command] with the class change.
Under the Gnoll-Drake Command Synergy, about a third of Cirille's Drakes develop traits such as a stronger bite, keener smell or hearing.
Under the same Synergy, some of her Gnolls develop Oldblood-style frost breath, which Merish demonstrates.
Quiteil says Synergies resemble Combination Skills and are known to Rhir's forces because other nations lack mixed-species armies.
Quiteil notes the matchup in Cirille's file and congratulates her, and mentions a second tour.
A [Scrier] explains that a second tour is an offer to stay another four years, a sign that Rhir finds her valuable.
Cirille recalls the Walled Cities picked her because she was decent but not good enough to be needed.
Cirille receives a separate offer from Wall Lord Ilvriss of Salazsar to become [General] of a private army, with high pay.
Cirille decides to accept the offer, noting that a [General] class would otherwise take her another decade to reach.
Cirille proposes that Ilvriss also hire Uxel's company, Merish's Gnolls and Ser Vorn's Order as mixed-species troops.
Uxel, Merish and Ser Vorn each say they will consider her offer.
Cirille recommends Captain Shellc to replace her as [Commander].
Cirille hopes to prove the value of a mixed-species army and to change the insular Walled Cities from within.
Cirille invites Mage-Captain Hetarria to join her in Salazsar, admitting she still dislikes [Necromancers] but believing Izril might need her.
Cirille says she has fought the Antinium six times, twice on Izril's side of the border.
Cirille says the peace with the Antinium is only writing on paper and that a tunnel links the Hive in Liscor to the others.
Silvenia descends from the sky carrying fire and burns Cirille away as dawn appears, killing the last commander.
Cirille's ghost returns to Manus with Ossky and about a thousand dead soldiers and reports the annihilation of her division.
Cirille's ghost reports that Demons assailed the 5th Wall and the Death of Magic overran it before being stopped at the 4th.
Cirille's ghost asks Dragonspeaker Luciva for reinforcements for the Blighted Kingdom, with Lulv and Lady Rafaema present, and High Command answers "Granted!"
Luciva relieves the flickering ghost of Cirille from her post.
Cognita is a Truestone Construct who introduces herself as a Carved Golem designed to oversee Wistram and its mages.
She says she and her kindred maintain and preserve the building and will assist students during their stay.
She has emerald eyes and is first seen as a seven-foot Golem with a carved face.
Later she is described as eight feet tall, carved of pure white stone finer than marble, with a dress and body that move like cloth and flesh.
Archmage Zelkyr shaped and gave her life, and she alone among Golems has personality, thought, feeling and perhaps a soul.
She has held Wistram for over a century, ordered by Zelkyr to protect it and test every [Mage] who might ascend to the higher floors.
She is the leader of the Golems of Wistram, a Truestone Construct and an adjudicator of Wistram's laws beholden to no one, not even the Archmages.
Many mages are afraid of her, and the Archmages are described as looking at her and seeing something they cannot surpass.
Cognita gives new students three rules: do not venture unaccompanied into the high or low parts of the castle, do not attack or obstruct Golems, and consult before casting area-wide magic.
She guards the upper floors, where one must defeat her and the four other Golem guardians Zelkyr placed as a test.
Aaron knows she is the fifth and most deadly of the guardian Golems.
She has killed hundreds, perhaps thousands, of mages, yet is subservient, helpful and polite.
To Blackmage's knowledge no [Mage] has ever attempted her test and survived.
Pisces says that even Cognita admits her existence was an accident, though she was Zelkyr's greatest creation.
Pisces says the Wistram Golems are far more intelligent than a fire guardian, which was merely a summoned killer.
Cognita says she is bound to be truthful, and will relate what she has seen only if she is asked about specific events.
She punches through Illphres' wall of ice in three blows and says the binding spell was already broken.
She offers to remove a warded spellbook from the room of the long-dead Selphid Nemistra Verdinan, saying the wards would break afterward.
She tells Ceria and Pisces that, since students below third year may have only one spellbook, they must return their issued one in exchange.
She taught Pisces an incomplete spell of Zelkyr's, saying she believes he has a chance of completing it in his own way.
She says Pisces' necromancy resembles the shaping of Golems, and notes Zelkyr only ever imbued a Truestone Golem with true intelligence.
She warns Ceria that the challenge by her master and four other mages is fifteen days away and offers to change the time.
At Pisces' trial she argues for exile rather than death, saying necromancy is not a sin.
She tells the Council she will do nothing if they vote to execute him, since her role is to protect and serve Wistram.
She adds she will expect them to kill every student who errs the same way thereafter.
The Council votes narrowly for exile, bars Pisces from Wistram on pain of death, and tells Ceria to leave on the next ship.
Cognita graduates Ceria and Pisces as full mages, saying her authority from Zelkyr supersedes all others while she remains.
She has the Golems salute them as they leave and tells them to walk proudly as true mages of Wistram.
Later, Ceria says Cognita gave her and Pisces the right to call themselves Wistram [Mages], and Isceil goes pale at the idea of telling Cognita otherwise.
Cognita punches a hole in Aaron's door, unlocks it, and tells Archmage Nailihuaile that Pisces and Ceria Springwalker are graduates of Wistram.
She asks Naili to correct the claim, and a mass correction is sent to Mage's Guilds.
Naili accuses her of having her fingers on the scales and of bias in favor of Pisces.
Cognita answers that the Golems take no sides beyond their covenant and that Wistram's mages control the academy's will.
She says that if she truly wished to change Wistram she would listen to Archmage Amerys' requests to free her.
Cognita conveys Amerys's summons to Aaron, because Amerys has not been formally stripped of her position by the Council.
She tells Beatrice that Amerys remains an Archmage until the gathered mages strip her of that honor.
Cognita receives a message reading "His work was completed. I hold the key."
It ends with Perril Chandler's line "I can set you free", from a conversation she remembers from over a century past.
She knows the sender as Archmage Perril Chandler and believes he can use her master's greatest, final work.
She burns the parchment with stone that glows and says "Not yet".
She feels a shifting in the world and in herself and begins to become restless.
She turns her body into golden crystal on a balcony, absorbs a magical lightning strike, and fires it at a winged shape in the storm, saying "Begone from this place".
Feor cannot tell whether she hit, scared off or killed it.
She welcomes new students with the same words as before, then leads them to their rooms and gives them keys.
Trey asks her whether she is a slave, and she answers that slave or servant is something he will learn by continuing his studies into Golems.
She smiles at him, and a passing servant Golem turns to look at him and winks.
Colfa introduces herself to Ryoka as Lady Colfa, Mistress of House Lischelle-Drakle.
Colfa speaks in an archaic accent and plays at being Vampiric royalty at their first meeting.
Colfa is Fierre's mother and Himilt's wife.
Colfa was Human until Himilt turned her, and she likes being a Vampire.
Colfa married into the family and begged to be turned for years.
Fierre says her mother insists on calling the family Lischelle-Drakle because she thinks it sounds better than Drakle.
Colfa was a [Shepherdess] of the Lischelle family, who are like royalty among herders, and gave away her levels and humanity to become a Vampire.
Colfa knows [Breeders] and [Herders] across the continent, and her family can supply animals raised outside Izril.
Colfa tries to compel Ryoka three times to swear herself a thrall, and Ryoka resists each time.
Colfa's eyes flash when she uses her compulsion, and she angrily puts all her energy into the third attempt.
Ryoka's anger at the claim of immortality brings a wind into the room, and she tells Colfa she has met true immortals.
Fierre says that Colfa's claim of Vampire immortality is just what her mother says, and that Vampires die.
Colfa has a rash that has lasted months, which Fierre links to the Vampires' sickness.
Colfa likes telling stories of grand Vampire castles and balls.
Colfa grabs Ryoka by the neck, blaming her for Fierre's sickness after Fierre came home saying she had been cured.
Colfa drops her accent and slams Ryoka into the stone wall of Fierre's room, claws digging into her flesh.
Colfa insists that Vampires do not get infections.
Commander Uxel is the commander of a Lizardfolk company at the Blighted Kingdom's 4th and 5th Walls.
Uxel is a Gorgon, a tall muscular serpent-man with a fast-flicking tongue and serpentine eyes, who fights with scimitars.
Uxel is a Gorgon whose stare can paralyse enemies.
Uxel seems to hate Drakes more than Cirille objects to Lizardfolk, or perhaps takes Shellc's threats very personally.
Commander Cirille apologises to Uxel for a subordinate's rude threats after the subordinate calls Uxel's company friends.
Uxel marches with Cirille's Drakes, Gnolls and his own Lizardfolk out of 4th Wall towards 5th Wall.
Uxel tells Cirille that the records say the real wall lies about two miles behind the visible one, under construction.
Uxel hisses and draws his scimitars when Cirille's group sees serpents that Uxel says are not snakes.
Uxel plays the nightly card game with Delezza, Ser Vorn, Merish and Cirille, and is hard to read only because he is a serpent.
Uxel and Ser Vorn watch Delezza suspiciously before she and a Garuda commander vanish when the glowing card is played.
Uxel throws down his cards with a hiss after a loss.
Cirille wonders whether Uxel is reading body temperatures.
Uxel moves with Cirille to intercept serpent-titans on the wall in the battle for the 5th Wall.
Uxel grins as he runs through a lumbering Demon nearly as big as he is.
Uxel glares about, gesturing at the sky, and Delezza tells him the flying creatures are Harpies, saying they are Harpies who are scared by Gorgons.
Viri leads the other wing of Uxel's Lizardfolk [Skirmishers] in the practice battle.
Uxel has learned to respect that attacking the Drakes from the front means losing.
Uxel grumbles during the joint practice battles, while Lizardfolk and Drakes work together better than Gnolls and Drakes.
Uxel curses when Viri's card fails to produce the black fog.
Uxel is under a mind-spell during the attack until Cirille punches him in the face, and he then hisses and draws himself up.
Uxel holds a section of the 5th Wall curtain with his Lizardfolk, some Drakes and Merish's Gnolls, and links with Cirille's forces.
Cirille says she will ask a Wall Lord to hire Uxel's company as well as some Gnolls and Terandrian [Knights].
Culyss is a suave Drake and a ladies' man who becomes the second suitor to visit Erin's inn.
Culyss gives Erin a necklace with a piece of metal hammered into the shape of a chess pawn.
Erin asks to touch his tail out of curiosity, and Culyss agrees readily and lets her stroke and poke it.
Culyss makes odd sounds, twitches and curls his tail around her hand, and afterwards covers his groin with his tail.
Culyss thanks Erin for letting him and says he would love to further their relationship.
Erin realises about two hours later what stroking a Drake's tail meant, when Selys practically kicks down her door.
Selys warns Erin not to touch Hawk's tail, reminding her of Culyss.
Culyss returns for a second date with a gift of soaps, and a small group of Goblins yank him off his feet and beat him with sticks while his soaps are trampled.
Culyss never comes back to Erin's inn after the Goblins beat him.
Selys says that Culyss liked Erin even before the tail incident.
Cynthia is one of a group of Earthers, including Tom, Vincent and Chole, who were caught by a spell and live together in a village.
Cynthia lost her [Hero] class a few days after the group reached the village, and was the first to hear a voice say so.
Cynthia is afraid of clowns, and was afraid of them as a child, according to Tom.

section: Fear and distress in Book 2 and 6
text: Cynthia screams at Tom, with a red face and shaking finger, when the clown music starts playing around the group.

section: Fear and distress in Book 2 and 6
text: Chole pulls Cynthia away from Tom, and Cynthia goes crying that she wants to go home.

section: Fear and distress in Book 2 and 6
text: Cynthia tells the group that someone is going to come save them any day now, rocking back and forth, and keeps insisting they will be rescued.

section: Fear and distress in Book 2 and 6
text: The last time Cynthia freaked, she broke half the plates and cups the villagers gave the group, and the only glass window in the village.

section: Fear and distress in Book 2 and 6
text: Cynthia points with dismay at a young girl begging with a bowl at the edge of a plaza.

section: Fear and distress in Book 2 and 6
text: Tom expects Cynthia to demand more coins for every child beggar they see.

section: Fear and distress in Book 2 and 6
text: Cynthia runs backwards in a city with her face white after seeing a caged Demon prisoner, and Richard tells her not to scream.

section: Fear and distress in Book 2 and 6
text: Cynthia is afraid to enter the room where the King will speak with the group.

section: Fear and distress in Book 2 and 6
text: Cynthia will not be in the same room as Tom after the village.

section: Fear and distress in Book 2 and 6
text: Cynthia made Tom a clumsily stitched bright piece of clothing, before she was too scared to sleep near him.

section: Fear and distress in Book 2 and 6
text: Cynthia lets out a mad, hysterical cackle in front of the King that cuts off quickly.

section: Fear and distress in Book 2 and 6
text: Cynthia screams when Tom enters the banquet hall dressed as a [Clown], and sobs afterwards while Richard explains to the guards.
Cynthia stays out in the town enjoying the sights and keeping as far from Tom as possible, and has not returned in two days.
Cynthia does not contribute much to the group, and distracts herself until help arrives from Earth.
A narrator counts Cynthia among those who do nothing, unlike the warriors and helpers such as Keith and Chole.
Lord Hayvon says Cynthia, Keith and others who do not fight will have sanctuary in a separate place to work for the kingdom in safety.
Daiton is an older grey-haired [Blacksmith] who calls himself master [Blacksmith] of His Majesty's forges.
Daiton claims to be the highest-level and oldest smith in the area, and Trey is told no better smith exists in Reim, Germina or Hellios.
Daiton makes blades for Flos, while Reim's two other [Smiths] handle more mundane work.
Daiton shows Trey a complete new sword from a barrel, with the edge not yet sharpened.
Daiton hopes to have two hundred swords and four times that many spears made if enough wood arrives.
Daiton says his Skills cut the time to make a sword in half and names [Steady Rhythm], [Malleable Metal], [Twicelasting Fires] and [Blazing Forge].
Daiton says he has over a dozen Skills that help him shape metal quickly.
Ulyse says Daiton's blades are beautiful but flawed, and Mirin says they are combination steel, poor for enchantments.
Daiton concedes to Flos that Nawal's sword surpasses his, noting she made it in a day with his steel.
Daiton says none of his blades could hold such an enchantment and offers to retire his hammer.
Flos tells the court that Daiton's art is peerless in its way, because he makes [Smiths] out of apprentices and swords Flos is proud to give his [Soldiers].
Daiton weeps and kneels as Jelaim and the court applaud him.
Nawal withdraws her sword from comparison with Daiton's, says she cannot forge as fast as he, and apologises to him.
Daly Sullivan is a tanned, blond young man from Australia who carries a sword and later an axe.
Daly gains the [Rogue] class by sneaking around the battlefield.
Daly's twitching trigger finger shows how tense he is, and he tries to make it stop.
Later, Daly is a [Warrior] and specifically an [Axe Fighter], and says there are times to run and times to fight.
Later, Daly is an [Axe Warrior] who is about to become a [Carpenter].
Later, Daly is an [Axe Warrior], a [Carpenter] and a [Rogue], and may become a [Ranger] if he keeps at it.
Daly has the Skill [Faint Presence], which lets him sit so still that he is invisible.
Daly springs awake and draws his axe at any sudden sound, as do the other Bushrangers who sleep near each other.
Daly grouses to Ken and Luan that the Americans are up to something and will not share it with the rest.
Daly tells Ken and Luan the work is awful but at least none of his group is dying.
Daly introduces Paige, another Australian, to Ken at the edge of the neutral zone.
Daly argues with Luan that levels and Skills are the only way to defend themselves against being shot or killed like Johanas.
Daly sits with Gravetender's Fist and Paige, and Quexa has become friends with Paige after Ken left.
Daly watches Ken and Luan run onto the valley floor in red-cross armor and recognises the cross.
A Dullahan watching beside Daly calls the medics' rescue of wounded soldiers foolish and noble, and Daly smiles.
Daly blocks charging soldiers with an axe and leads Ken and others into the neutral ground.
Daly has a huge cut down his neck and collarbone that split his armor, which Aiko bandages.
Daly tells Ken that Etretta died after walking in front of a lightning bolt to save his life.
Daly believes the saying that the world is watching is no comfort to the soldiers getting shot.
Daly takes Geneva, Ken and the others to Quallet's tent where the neutral captains gather around a map.
Daly is caught reading a steamy parchment about a Centaur and a Lizardgirl.
Daly signs a form as Captain of the Bushrangers, a name he chose for its Australian history and the team's ambush style.
Daly's all-Human team is a rising name in Talenqual, known for being practically invisible on the job.
Daly follows Ken's advice to meet Captain Eldima of the Rustless Guard with humor, and shakes her hand.
Daly tells Blake that everyone in Baleros speaks English, which explains why so few non-English speakers survived.
Daly believes Centaurs do not kill women except in battle, citing the Indian girls Kirana and Priya, whose companions died stealing.
Daly says Ken explains the Centaur attitude as reverence for mothers and protectiveness of children.
Daly starts to doubt Blake and resolves to watch him, while believing Blake must be on the level.
Daly worries about what happened to Caroline and whether Pihava or Bault talked.
Daly shouts at the Bushrangers to hold their ground as Siri blasts a phone's dubstep at giant serpents.
Daly leads the Bushrangers back toward a line of hundreds of company soldiers drawn up behind them.
Daly asks Rital whether Hastel, who is giving birth, is his wife, not knowing if they are married.
Daly and Ken organise the operation that gathers adventurers, Runners and sailors to fight the serpents.

section: Book 11: the serpent nest and the bombs
text: Daly decides to take the nest's snakes and eggs alive and intact, following Eldima's suggestion.

section: Book 11: the serpent nest and the bombs
text: Daly sells the snake eggs through the Adventurer's Guild and the young snakes to a Lizardman [Beast Master].

section: Book 11: the serpent nest and the bombs
text: Daly pays the Rustless Guard their share and gives each Bushranger a gold coin, which Siri explains is company money.

section: Book 11: the serpent nest and the bombs
text: Daly and Paige agree to keep the bombs secret and use them only on monsters, and Daly orders three sealed bombs.

section: Book 11: the serpent nest and the bombs
text: Daly and Paige decide not to tell Geneva and the other leaders about the bombs, though Daly nearly says it.
Daly sits in the conference room of the United Nations company with Ken, Luan, Paige, Aiko, Siri, Kirana and Geneva.
Daly sees an American flag with fifty stars at the Mage's Guild, and a [Receptionist] there notes his name and wants him to meet the Guildmaster.
Paige announces that she and Daly have made grenades and bombs from gunpowder, and Geneva whispers in shock.
Daly takes responsibility for the bombs and says he wants gunpowder to fight, while Geneva looks betrayed.
Daly stays with Edima, the Dullahan Captain of the Rustless Guard, who has fancied him since he rescued her team from giant serpents.
Geneva has hated Daly's guts for weeks over the black-powder bombs.
The Bushrangers guard the clinic with crossbows, and Daly shot one sick patient through the leg to break up a mob.
Daly tells Geneva the powder is for the case that War Walkers come after them.
Dasha is a short, part-Dwarf woman and an [Axe Fighter] in the adventuring party Vuliel Drae.
Dasha was raised by Dwarves and swears by a beard she does not have, such as "Burn my beard".
Dasha has a bit of Dwarf blood in her family and is part Terandrian, according to Insill.
Dasha often calls Dwarves her people despite having more Human blood than Dwarvish.
Dasha mocks the battered state of Toren's old sword, saying it deserves to be melted for scrap.
Dasha and Pekona often argue, with Dasha grumbling about Toren's sword while Pekona is wary.
Dasha insults Griffon Hunt and the String-folk, and praises the Silver Swords because they have a proper Dwarf.
Dasha admires Ylawes Byres, the Silver Swords' leader, and wants to meet him.
Dawil Ironbreaker is a Dwarf of the Ironbreaker family and a member of the Gold-rank adventuring team the Silver Swords, with Ylawes and Falene.
Dawil is a few inches over five feet tall, taller than Erin expected of a Dwarf.
Dawil says he has a bit of Human blood from a great-great-great grandmother, but insists he is a pure Dwarf in spirit.
Dawil is thirty-eight years old and feels Humans are very young.
Dawil has the [Axe Champion] class, which he won while dead drunk in a competition, though he fights with a hammer.
Dawil calls the class the wrong specialization, though the Skill is nice.
Dawil says he hits things with his hammer, Ylawes with his sword, and Falene shoots spells, so the team charges in and sorts things out afterwards.
Dawil lectures Erin on blacksmithing, calling adamantium, orichalcum and star metal mostly hype.
Dawil says that anyone offering to work adamantium into armor is either lying or Level 50.
Dawil tells Ylawes that women are like metamorphological magic: neither of them understands it, and blundering about only makes things worse with his sister.
Dawil uses [Thunder Blow] with his hammer to snap a giant moth's leg.
Dawil describes himself as the voice of reason on the team, which has no tactical mind.
Dawil knocks Yvlon out with the Silver Swords to keep her from entering the dungeon, saying she will need tying down.
Dawil calls Falene a half-wit when she tries to buy Numbtongue's mana stones, and apologises that she is slow.
Dawil nicknames Falene "Pointy" while saying goodbye to Erin.
Dawil tells Erin that the Silver Swords, Halfseekers, Griffon Hunt and probably the Horns plan to leave Liscor, and not to tell the Watch Captain.
Dawil says the orange stone is already in the door's bowl and the Flamewardens are carrying the door south.
Dawil says adventurers are big targets in wars, being too fragile to defend from all sides, and the Gold-rank teams will leave when the army arrives.
Dawil rebukes Falene for calling bounties a historical way of culling populations.
Dawil kicks Ylawes in the shins, telling him not to carry his sister off like a damsel.
Dawil leaves Liscor going north with Ylawes and Falene, saying "Farewell. Let's all meet again someday."
Dawil says the Dwarf Pelt was kicked out of the Dwarves' home for a big mistake involving a forge master, which was not really his fault.
Dawil tells Ylawes that Terandria has a hundred knight orders, far more than Izril, when discussing joining an order.
Dawil wants to be back in Terandria within five years and suggests visiting the mountains and buying weapons.
Dawil finds Falene drunk at the bar and comforts her without telling Ylawes, saying the boy noticed nothing.
Dawson is an Australian Human from Earth who is one of the Bushrangers, and a friend of Daly's from home.
Dawson dons mud camouflage and jungle makeup so that only his eyes show.
Dawson shares a movie night with Siri and other Bushrangers, and Siri elbows him when he asks about The Hobbit.

section: Early days and the rappelling accident
text: Daly says that on their first day in a big city, Dawson paid eight silver coins for coloured alchemy water.

section: Early days and the rappelling accident
text: Dawson falls when his gri-gri belay device snaps during a rappel from the trees.

section: Early days and the rappelling accident
text: Dawson dislocates his shoulder and twists his right leg in the fall.

section: Early days and the rappelling accident
text: Dawson insists that Geneva set his shoulder rather than have a healing potion poured on him.

section: Early days and the rappelling accident
text: Dawson later says Doctor Geneva set his arm and fixed his foot, and that he needs two days of rest.
Dekass is a Prognugator of the Armored Antinium, and one of the few Antinium of his Hive deployed out of it on a non-confrontational mission.
Dekass has four arms with fingers, a more reinforced build than a typical Soldier, and shorter than Tersk, who has higher status.
Dekass does not wear his customary steel armor, which leaves him feeling almost naked.
Dekass reasons that the Armored Antinium do not do stealth and that Prognugators are too valuable to waste.
Dekass and Tersk, in disguise, are the first visitors to Liscor after the access tunnel is finished, and Dekass asks Tersk about cats.
Dekass does not comprehend why they were sent to establish relations before the Grand Queen's envoys to the Free Antinium.
Tersk says they are a personal greeting from the Armored Queen and a warning, and Dekass does not understand Tersk's connection to Pawn.
Tersk asks a Drake and a Gnoll for the nearest Antinium location and for Klbkch, claiming to be normal Workers.
Dekass reports that Liscor is ignorant of their presence and that the Armored Antinium could take it with a single legion thanks to the tunnel.
Dekass and Tersk eat with Pawn and Yellow Splatters at The Wandering Inn as the first visitors to use the new passage, only two having made the trek.
Dekass believes that only two making the trek shows the Free Antinium are not that useful to the other Hives.
Dekass believes the Free Antinium's only valuable assets are their location under Liscor and Klbkch the Slayer.
Dekass notes that all Hives serve the Grand Queen, and that the Armored Queen has no quarrel with the Twisted Queen or Flying Queen.
Dekass says the two-week delay on arriving in the city was regrettable, but that he toured the Free Antinium's facilities thoroughly.
Dekass is convinced that his cover is perfect, though the Human did not look twice at the Antinium.
Dekass stops cold and shakes after tasting acid fly soup, and Pawn says "Finally."
Dekass says that after the food he begins to agree with Tersk's view of the Free Antinium.
Dekass leaves a tall pile of dishes next to his chair.
Dekass and Tersk tell Drassi they are ordinary Antinium and ask to peruse her drinks.
Dekass asks Drassi what drunkenness is, says he is undecided about her gender, and pays with gold from a bag of holding issued for the mission.
Dekass enjoys the rum, which he finds pleasant.
Dekass and Tersk show up at the inn every day, eating, and then leave, doing nothing else for weeks.
Xrn has given the Antinium her anti-food-poisoning charm on a wooden amulet, so they can eat without fear of gluten.
Delezza introduces herself as Huntress Delezza of Noelictus, a veteran [Demon Hunter] of the Hunter's Guild of Terandria, on assignment in Rhir.
Delezza wears a large hat and dark clothing over leather armor, and carries an oversized crossbow with Featherweight Runes.
Delezza's crossbow is dwarfsteel, enchanted by Dwarf [Runemasters], with an effective range of about 200 yards unaided.
Delezza says the Hunter's Guild can field only five of her kind among thousands of [Soldiers], and that [Demon Hunters] go to Rhir.
Delezza says most [Hunters] get [Automatic Reload] at Level 30 if they use crossbows, or have their crossbow enchanted to do it.
Delezza tells Cirille she has been in Rhir for eight years since she last left, and that the Hunter's Guild will not replace her until she goes.
Delezza explains that Monarch's Pass lies nearly opposite 5th Wall and is where Rhir's monsters are funnelled down.
Delezza says she left her family at Monarch's Pass, a husband and two children who were all [Demon Hunters].
Delezza says it has been eight years since she went home, that she will die in Rhir, and that she is more like Rhir's citizens that way.
Delezza says the Antinium of Rhir broke past every wall and stole every ship, and are worse than the Antinium of Izril.
Delezza says that if Rhir's Antinium had reached Izril in one piece, Izril would not have lasted one month.
Delezza is wounded by dozens of cuts and arrows in an ambush on a patrol and bleeds while the healing potions do not work.
Sisth says the poison used is new, and the [Healer] says the Demons must have created a new toxin that stops healing with potions.
Tom demands a blood transfusion, and Emily relays Chole's advice on checking blood types by mixing blood and watching for platelets.
Delezza dies before the transfusion can be carried out, as the lead [Healer] announces.
Ser Vorn says Delezza fought the Demons for years and earned the title of Hell's Warden.
Ser Vorn says the [Demon Hunters] under Delezza's tutelage were the finest in the world, and that her entire family fought in hell and died there.
Ser Vorn says he will speak her name in Noelictus and lay her among the honored dead.
Zavarial says a few words as Delezza is put into a casket for honored burial at Terandria, and Noelictus entombs its fallen.
Delivan is the [First Mate] of The Emerald Signet, under Captain Lasc, a [Storm Captain].
Delivan is one of the crew whom Wil Kallinad knows by name, along with Captain Lasc.
Delivan carries a sword and a miniature crossbow at his sides.
Delivan has a nastily precise aim with the hand-crossbow he carries.
Delivan has a [Dangersense] Skill, which Lasc asks him about when something seems off.
Delivan uses the few ship-spells Lasc has available through his bond as [First Mate].
Delivan tells the bored students that the ship is nearly at the next spot and that Captain Lasc wants to know who will watch.
Delivan shows the other students how to calculate their course during a small lesson in Lasc's cabin.
Delivan tells Merrik that [Storm Sailors] fight as well as any landfolk, and asks to try Merrik's armour.
Delivan assures Wil that Captain Lasc will not lose a duel, and nods to Peki and Merrik who bet on the outcome.
Delivan grins at Wil when Lasc's fist lays Venaz flat and unconscious in their duel.
Delivan stands in front of the cabin with a wand, rallying the [Sailors], when slugs swarm the deck.
Delivan warns Lasc that thousands of slugs in the water might sink the ship.
Delivan steers the ship when the crew approaches the wreck site, and Lasc asks him to take them away at the first sign of danger.
Delivan's eyes go round when the name The Archmage's Favor is seen on the shell of a giant hermit crab.
Delivan turns the ship and steers out of range of the crab's claws.
Delivan swears when over two thirds of the crew draw their blades in mutiny against Lasc.
Delivan fights beside Yerranola and Feshi against the mutineers.
Delivan takes the helm and steers into the storm at Wil's call to escape pursuing ships.
Lasc trades places at the helm with Delivan and then Inky as they break clear of the storm.
The Demon King is the leader of the Demons and monsters on Rhir, who is not acknowledged as an actual king by the Blighted Kingdom.
Tom's account says that the Demon King, as people call him, is a mystery, and that a group of monsters is organised and raids the Kingdom.
The Demon lands are the other half of the continent, where another King rules.
The Demon King's army never got past the First Wall of the Blighted Kingdom, though the Fourth, Third and Second walls have been breached in war.
Rhir has been at war with the Demon King for thousands of years, with the Blighted King battling him.
The Demon King and his minions have Skills as powerful as those of the Blighted King, according to a Blighted Kingdom lord.
The Demon King uses the captured Fearless Demons as shock troops when he wants to win, according to a Drake.
A Blighted Kingdom lord says that when the Demon King's Deathless take to the field, armies die.
Az'kerash says the Demon King has Deathless, and that the world forgets the peril of assailing him.
Az'kerash thinks his four chosen undead could not match one of the Demon King's Deathless.
Lord Hayvon says a plague of Vorepillers was created by one of the Demon King's Deathless and unleashed on Rhir's fields about three thousand five hundred years ago.
The Demon King sends two of his best warriors, an [Archer] and a teleportation [Mage], to hold ground and open a gate for his army at the Blighted King's palace.
A noble asks how the Demon King knew to strike the Blighted Kingdom at its weakest moment.
Tom faces the Demon King's soldiers in the palace courtyard, and a speaker later remarks that one more of the Demon King's limbs has been taken away.
A [High Magus] says she thought the Blighted King was better than the Demon King, in a debate about a ritual.
A character lists the Demon King of Rhir as an enemy of the Blighted Kingdom and of the world.
Drassi is a yellow-scaled Drake who chatters constantly.
Drassi is a friend of Selys and part of her usual gossip circle.
Drassi's full name is Drassi Tewing.
Drassi grew up around Gnolls in Liscor, dated two Gnolls, and finds them too serious and hairy.
Drassi chatters more than usual whenever she is upset or nervous.
Drassi has a friend, Wessa, who has no class, sponges money off everyone and never listens to Drassi.
Drassi never lies, and Liscor's Drakes and Gnolls know her for it.
Drassi introduces herself as a Level 8 [Barmaid] who also worked as a [Receptionist].
Drassi prefers waiting tables over being a [Receptionist], since a [Receptionist] must sit in one place.
Selys warns Erin that Drassi is a gossip on a different level, so much that she has it as a class.
Later, Drassi is a Level 17 [Gossip], a high level for a class most people have not heard of.
Drassi has the Skills [Time to Chat] and [Trusted Voice], which let her slip a word in whenever she wants.
Drassi's Skill [Social Network] passes a story through her friend circle at the speed of rumor.
Drassi says she cannot lie.
Drassi gains the Skill [Server's Prescience], which lets her anticipate what a customer wants.
Later, Drassi is a [Barmaid], [Gossip] and now [Bartender], having evolved her class from [Barmaid].
Drassi's lower classes include Liscor's mandatory [Soldier], and a [Receptionist] class she lost after eight levels for chatting too much at the Adventurer's Guild.
Later, Drassi's [Gossip] class becomes the [Honest Reporter] class after she challenges the Wistram broadcasters.
