Erin hires Drassi, Selys' friend, as part of a new staff with Safry, Maran and the Gnoll Ishkr, to help Lyonette.
Drassi introduces herself to Lyonette with a wall of chatter and says Selys told her Lyonette's expulsion from the city was not that exciting.
Drassi quietly helps Lyonette by pouring mugs while Maran and Safry take their lunch break.
Drassi jokes that they should push Maran and Safry down the outhouse hole, and she calls them fleshbags.
Drassi says she might quit if she must keep hearing Maran and Safry ask which Drake is which.
Drassi leaps forward when Lyonette and Safry are about to fight.
Drassi comes to help Lyonette when Ishkr is unwell.
Drassi throws potions at the Eater Goats with Lyonette and Mrsha, throwing at the same time as Lyonette.
Drassi is terrified of the Goblins in the cellar, saying she does not know if she can work with monsters under the roof.
Drassi chatters constantly while afraid of the Hobgoblins, saying she wishes they would talk.
Drassi drops a stack of plates when Pisces says the Walled Cities are built with Dragon bones.
Drassi asks Erin whether the inn is safe for her, then notes a curfew just past dark for anyone without ten levels in a combat class.
Drassi and Ishkr agree to ask their friends to work at the inn for one silver and two copper per hour for three days.
Drassi admits half her friends slack off, so she will ask only the good half.
Drassi weeps at Erin's speech to the Redfang Goblins and tries to hug Badarrow, who fends her off.
Drassi says she looks at the Goblins differently after Erin's chess comparison.
Drassi serves Dawil an ale and Erin a cup of milk before they ask, using her new Skill.
Drassi works alongside Ishkr and tells Erin that Selys took Pisces to shop for magical items.
Drassi offers to take Mrsha to the climbing playground.
Drassi reports that the Wistram [Mages] are the talk of Liscor and are setting up business, with the Minotauress Bezale organizing it.
Drassi tells Krshia and Elirr that Erin is at Pallass Hunting, sent by Rufelt and Lasica to rest after her inn broke.
Drassi mentions she lost her last boyfriend in a fight two weeks earlier.
Drassi joins Selys's friends in crowding around her for gossip about the armor, and says another [Thief] was caught alive that morning.
Drassi mentions that the Goblins at Erin's inn got artifacts, and defends them as not causing trouble.
Drassi traces a rumor about Erin's inn to Timbor Parithad, who runs the Drunken Swordsman, after a dispute over the two [Barmaids] Erin hired from Agnes' inn.
Drassi shouts down the shopkeeper Lism, telling the crowd she has seen the Goblins at Erin's inn and does not lie.
Drassi says Erin warned Olesm and Zevara of the second Raskghar attack, and that the Hobs helped fight them off.
After the Raskghar are defeated, Drassi wakes Gnoll households before dawn to tell the story, having not slept for over thirty hours.
Drassi tells Rykhai that Raskghar were killed in the lair and the Gnoll prisoners rescued, adding she saw the artifacts brought back.
Drassi thinks she owes Erin a favor and sways public opinion on her behalf.
Drassi and Olesm commentate on the Goblins against the Gnolls in Erin's baseball game, and Drassi sends Olesm away to commentate elsewhere.
Drassi claims to Embria that they played in Liscor's streets as children, though Embria does not remember her.
Relc is unsure whether he remembers Drassi from when Embria first came to Liscor.
Drassi is newly hired as a sports reporter, replacing Sir Relz and Noass for a football game.
Drassi barges onto the Wistram broadcast after someone invokes Grand Strategist Chaldion's order to get her through, and she grabs the microphone.
Drassi challenges Sir Relz and Noass on claims that healing crystals prevent the Yellow Rivers disease, while Grimalkin watches.
Drassi accuses the broadcasters of causing riots by showing mobs, saying she is a [Gossip] but never tells lies.
Drassi fills in as [Commentator] for Sir Relz and Noass, announcing the King of Destruction's battle against the King of Duels.
Drassi's broadcast uses the first news ticker, a sign held by a Gnoll behind her.
Drassi moonlights as announcer for Wistram TV while still working nights as [Bartender].
Drassi covers Grimalkin's new weights project on camera.
Noass and Sir Relz return, because the Wistram News Network wants 24/7 live coverage that Drassi cannot supply alone.
Drassi is made to apologize to High King Perric for her language, then doubles down on air, saying kidnapping is bad.
Drevish is known as the Architect and is one of the King of Destruction's Seven.
Drevish is an [Architect] who sketches landscapes with fortresses in place of grass and stone, using charcoal and a kneaded eraser.
Drevish will not take part in battle, and Flos suspects he would sleep through it or sketch plans for a new fortress.
Drevish scowls at his King in a way Orthenon and Takhatres would never dare, and Flos is used to it.
Flos says Drevish was one of the three of his Seven who knew magic.
Drevish could enchant a gate so the mightiest battering ram could not break it.
Drevish could build a wall overnight with his teams of [Builders], so an enemy army faced a fortified defense.
Drevish did not like war, but Flos says he was essential and asked too much of him.
Drevish worked on Reim and on Flos's palace there, but made only one major improvement.
Drevish disliked remodeling existing architecture and was more interested in Drake construction practices than the Chandrarian style.
Drevish found the sixteen towers of Reim's wall aesthetically disgusting, and the wall resembles a crown.
Drevish told Flos that Reim was an eyesore that ought to be wiped from the face of the earth.
Drevish liked the height of Reim's towers and believed in self-sufficient architecture, buildings capable of protecting themselves.
Drevish worked hard on Reim despite disliking it, but six of its towers have worn away over the decades.
The Quarass says Fetohep commissioned Drevish the Architect to improve his palace last, as each ruler of Khelt does.
A box from the Emperor of Sands arrives by Courier and contains Drevish's head in a block of ice, and Gazi names him.
Drevish had died to a swift chop to the neck, and Flos mourns him as his dear friend and builder of marvels.
Mars grips her sword in tears and rage, Takhatres bows his head in prayer and Orthenon's clenched hand bleeds at the sight.
Flos kept the head in ice by a simple preservation spell, as a reminder of his fallen companion, his failure and a promise.
After Teres and Trey tell him the truth, Flos agrees it is selfish to keep his friend waiting and promises to bury him privately that night.
Later, no head is on Flos's dresser, and Trey wonders if Flos has buried it yet.
Durene is a half-Troll girl who lives near Riverfarm and becomes Laken Godart's [Paladin] and later his consort.
She has a very deep voice that Laken finds soothing.
She is at least a head taller than Laken, who is about 184 cm, and she is heavily built.
Her skin is rough and cracked on the outside of her limbs, while her palm is callused but smoother.
Pyrite sees her as a tall grey-skinned warrior whose skin is like stone with cracks, as if her body were still part earth.
Crossbow bolts fail to puncture her skin in battle.
She eats about four times what Laken does, and she can eat a bowl of stew in under a minute.
She cannot read: she knows her basic letters and numbers but has never owned a book.
Durene tells Laken her mother died when she was four and she never met her father.
Her father was a wandering Troll who met her mother, a woman living alone on a small farm.
She does not know whether her mother liked her father or was attacked, and the villagers only said she was found pregnant and alone, with Troll tracks nearby.
An adventurer came and killed her Troll father, and afterwards wanted to kill Durene too, but her mother would not let him.
Her mother was too weak after the birth because Durene was so big, and never recovered.
After her mother died, the village took her in but she had no real home, sleeping in a barn and eating scraps.
Laken says the villagers cannot accept Durene for who she is.
She calls Drakes "lizard people", has never seen one, and she is excited and overwhelmed by her first glimpse of a city.
Durene lives alone in a large house of wood and rough stone next to a stream in the forest near Riverfarm.
Riverfarm has around sixty people, and the nearest big city, Bells, is over thirty miles away.
Her house has no glass in the windows, and she sleeps on a mattress of soft blankets and pillows.
She raises chickens and pigs and has a large garden, but says she cannot cook well because she has no Skills.
She cannot bring herself to butcher one of her pigs when Laken needs food for Frostwing.
She swiftly snaps the necks of two squirrels.
She says she can kick or push over a small tree, and earns a pittance supplying Riverfarm with firewood.
Later, she lives in a cottage that she built for herself.
Durene tells Laken she is a Level 6 [Farmer] with the Skill [Enhanced Strength].
She lifts Laken with one hand to show her strength.
Laken thinks something about her smells off but keeps the conversation going.
Laken knights her and names her his [Paladin], his foremost champion who will protect and serve him.
The next day she announces that she is a [Paladin].
Durene and Laken become lovers.
Laken calls her the one subject, or consort, of the Emperor of the Unseen.
She was a [Farmer] and is now a [Paladin], and neither knows what that means.
Durene levels five times and gains two Skills.
She is a Level 6 [Paladin] with [Weapon Proficiency: Shield] and [Graceful Step].
Laken says she gained the levels by helping save people and the village, not by slaying monsters.
Later, she is a Level 9 [Paladin] and gains the Skill [Quick Strike].
She uses [Quick Strike] in training to hit Beniar with her club.
Later, she is a Level 14 [Paladin] with the Skills [Radiant Courage] and [Shield of Valor].
[Radiant Courage] makes her glow, blinding Goblins while the soldiers beside her are unaffected.
[Shield of Valor] makes her shield glow and creates a wall holding back Goblins and a Hob.
Laken notes that Trolls are said to be strong and tough but cannot gain classes or level, unlike Durene.
Later, she is a Level 16 [Paladin].
She tells Ryoka she has not trained since the army disbanded, and she has no sparring partners because Beniar's riders need rest.
Later, she reaches Level 17 as a [Paladin] and obtains the Skill [Iron Skin].
A kitchen knife does not cut through the first layer of her skin, and Ryoka comments that [Iron Skin] is a great Skill.
Durene says Laken described a [Knight] as a retainer pledged to a cause, and a [Paladin] as someone who crusades and helps people.
She says she has not leveled for a while and thinks she is missing something.
Durene practices with a club of hammered-together wood and a partially converted door as a shield.
She wears a huge stitched leather jerkin, carries a tower shield made from a door and a club as long as her side.
She has beaten over a dozen Hobs with the club, and she once broke a greatsword in training.
She also uses an old iron greatsword and has killed two Hobs and a score of Goblins with it.
On the road with the Windfrozen Riders, Durene asks Laken if she can punch the cocky adventurer leader who keeps talking.
She says the [Witch] with glasses would turn him into a toad, and Laken doubts the Witch is high enough level.
Durene fights a Mossbear and head-butts it, but the bear claws her on the arm.
She says she thinks the Unseen Empire is a cool name, and that Windrest's people remain Laken's subjects.
While the markers are being set, she races across an open road with the riders to the last marker.
A Goblin arrow strikes a rider's horse, Durene drags the rider and horse away, and the rider cuts the horse's throat to spare it from the Goblins.
Wounded and bleeding, Durene shows her Troll side, roars, kills several Goblins with her club and tears a Goblin's arm from its socket.
She is jealous when Lady Rie flirts with Laken, and he reassures her that he is with her.
Durene insists on joining the army going north, saying she has to fight Goblins as a [Paladin].
She arrives with the main army, and she helps load the first trebuchet.
Pyrite breaks her club with a magical battleaxe that sets the wood aflame, and the axe cuts her chest.
Beniar charges Pyrite to save her.
Durene wakes in a private room of Riverfarm's new hospital, still clutching her chest.
Wiskeria tells her the army lost, Lord Pellmia's cavalry came with Tyrion Veltras, and she had slept for nearly a week.
She has a red scar between her breasts from an enchanted axe.
Durene learns Laken has left Riverfarm without her.
Later, a healing potion closed the chest wound, but infection took root and she had three fevers, each worse than the last.
The healer Pirose says Beniar made her illness worse by pushing more potions into her.
She learns that she has been ill for fifty days and that today is the fifty-first day since the battle.
She snaps a length of firewood in her hands without using her knee and tells Pirose of her Skill [Enhanced Strength].
She reunites with Frostwing and Bismarck and carries Wiskeria and her tent to her cottage.
She lifts a tree stump with roots from the ground with one hand, and tells Beatica that she is in a relationship with Laken.
She houses Ryoka and Charlay in her cottage and sleeps in the kitchen.
She has a thick scar that makes her quieter than the protective Durene Ryoka remembered.
She lifts a loaded wagon out of a pothole, and later pushes a wagon back to Riverfarm into the night.

section: Goblins, Belavierr and the quarrel with Laken
text: Durene tells Ryoka the Goblins attacked Riverfarm and that Laken sensed them attacking another city's army and laid a trap.

section: Goblins, Belavierr and the quarrel with Laken
text: She says the tribe then destroyed Lancrel and its raids burned down half the area around Riverfarm.

section: Goblins, Belavierr and the quarrel with Laken
text: Durene pulls Ser Raim behind her, holds back a cloth giant with a door-shield and a flaming greatsword, and flames do not hurt her.

section: Goblins, Belavierr and the quarrel with Laken
text: She carries Ser Raim to Riverfarm while the Witch Hunters cover her.

section: Goblins, Belavierr and the quarrel with Laken
text: She bars Belavierr's way when Belavierr tries to take Wiskeria, and refuses to move even when Belavierr calls her "Troll's child".

section: Goblins, Belavierr and the quarrel with Laken
text: An arrow from a former Lancrel soldier hits Belavierr's chest, and Belavierr kills him at a distance with a thrown needle.

section: Goblins, Belavierr and the quarrel with Laken
text: Durene argues with Laken over the Goblins, saying they killed her friends and the army.

section: Goblins, Belavierr and the quarrel with Laken
text: Laken says Goblins are people and compares Goblins to Trolls, and she answers that Trolls are not the same.

section: Goblins, Belavierr and the quarrel with Laken
text: She tells him she needs to be a [Paladin] or have him take it away, and that she cannot be half of it.

section: Goblins, Belavierr and the quarrel with Laken
text: She says she thought it would be easier when he came back and that she waited and waited.
Durene drags a wagon thirty miles to build muscle, like the Humans and Drakes.
She declines a set of weights, saying they look light.
She offers to get her shield and club to smash Crelers.
People talk about her more than the Goblins, but no longer in the same terms as before.
Durene patrols Riverfarm by night with the [Witch] Hedag, who took her under her wing.
Earlia is the Captain of Gemhammer, a Silver-rank adventuring team from the north made up of six Humans.
Earlia carries a sledgehammer on her back, and her team carries ropes, crossbows, swords and a net.
Earlia is a former [Miner] who knows gold, and her team of former miners became adventurers after monsters attacked their shaft.
Earlia calls herself a former [Mining Leader] when she asks Numbtongue about mining.
Gemhammer's members have strength Skills and heavy weapons, and Earlia fights with a warhammer.
Earlia says Gemhammer heard rumours of an inn near Liscor with Hobgoblin guards and a magic doorway.
Earlia thought she would have to travel four more days to reach Liscor when the team heard the inn rumours.
Earlia's team is ambushed by Raskghar in the dungeon and a masked woman saves them by slashing the Raskghar.
A Raskghar archer's invisible arrow strikes Earlia through her chainmail and she falls as Goblins appear behind the Raskghar.
Earlia's shoulder is healed but tender, and Gemhammer rests after the ambush.
Earlia says Gemhammer is a dungeon team and is chummy with the Pride of Kelia.
Earlia plans to return to the dungeon at once with proper equipment, since the layout is now known.
Earlia believes the Raskghar have no Skills and can be prepared for, and she wants the armoured Raskghar and the invisible bow.
Earlia wonders how the masked woman survives in the dungeon and suggests bringing her extra supplies.
Earlia wins the scramble for a gold nugget thrown to the adventurers in the inn, ending with a swollen lip and two bruises.
Earlia judges the nugget to be a substantial sum, as she knows gold from her time as a [Miner].
Earlia tells the table of the Golden Goblin, an adventurers' legend from north of Celum, as a myth like seeing a Unicorn.
In Earlia's telling, teams who nearly caught the Golden Goblin saw him drop treasure and flee while they scrambled for it.
In Earlia's telling, the dropped treasure sometimes led to avalanches, pitfalls or a Creler's nest, and the tale popped up in distant places.
Earlia leads Gemhammer in prying enchanted trap blades from de-trapped dungeon rooms, and her team trades with Anith.
Earlia estimates the enchanted trap blades at forty gold pieces each or ten times that if keenly enchanted, then at least six-fifty each after a bone test.
Earlia says her team were [Miners] and that adventuring pays better for about the same danger.
Gemhammer cracks a trap-room wall and harvests fire-elemental magicore, which explains why the room heats up so fast.
Earlia's team and Nailren's Pride of Kelia explore the dungeon together as Silver-rank teams that cannot advance as fast as the Gold-ranks.
Earlia finds a gold ring with a sapphire on a diseased Raskghar corpse, and her team cuts it from the finger.
Gemhammer also finds a bag of cut gemstones and an enchanted-looking knife on the Raskghar.
Earlia suspects the ring is an armour enchantment, since the Raskghar had something like armour made of water.
Both Silver-rank teams meet the Facestealer, which holds severed heads on sticks around a corner, and Nailren orders them to spread out.
Both teams are paralyzed by the Facestealer, and Earlia sobs, until an explosion through the dungeon distracts it.
Earlia asks Numbtongue for good mining spots while Gemhammer is on break from the dungeon, after Fea gets hurt removing a trap.
Earlia offers Numbtongue a fifteen to twenty percent cut of what Gemhammer mines and asks to borrow the door.
Numbtongue points Earlia to a good vein in the cave by the door and warns of what may be acid maggots.
Eater of Spears is a gigantic Hobgoblin and one of the Goblin Lord's lieutenants.
Eater of Spears is a huge Hob with an unusually precise, well-chosen way of speaking.
Eater of Spears is nine feet tall or more and looks like a mass of muscle.
Before he joined Reiss, Eater of Spears led a tribe of fewer than eighty Goblins, almost all Hobs.
That tribe was the Rockbreakers Tribe, which terrorised the cliffs and beat Wyverns to death for food.
Eater of Spears says his tribe fought monsters often and had too little food to build fat.
Eater of Spears says his old tribe fought Stone Starers, which have stone skin, strong arms and little meat.
Eater of Spears says Stone Starer eyes tasted horrible and were partially acidic.
Eater of Spears once went to a small Drake city for healing potions after a fight with Wyverns, and had to scare Drakes off the walls.
Eater of Spears was a [Thrower] before and can hit flying Wyverns with rocks, though he no longer levels the class much.
Eater of Spears carries two weakly enchanted throwing axes that Reiss gave him as a reward.
Eater of Spears carries three healing potions on his belt, a sign of how important he is.
Eater of Spears has a Skill and class for throwing and says the axes are good against [Mages].
Eater of Spears dodges Erin Solstice's thrown [Unerring Throw] bottle, saying the Skill only works if he holds still.
Arrows from Badarrow mostly fail to penetrate Eater of Spears's skin.
Eater of Spears tackles the first War Golem as it charges the Goblin Lord, trading blows despite its burning beam.
Eater of Spears blocks Zel Shivertail's path to the Goblin Lord, telling him "Can try."
Eater of Spears is cut open across the chest by Zel's claws and then breaks down under Zel's attacks, which bounce off his ribs.
Zel Shivertail crushes the last healing potion at Eater of Spears's belt during their fight.
Eater of Spears and Pyrite bond over the importance of food, and Eater admires Pyrite's bulk more than his muscle.
Eater of Spears calls Pyrite's tribe rich and says he himself was a poor Chieftain who only hit things.
Pyrite advises Eater of Spears to grow mushrooms and lichen with dripping water in caves.
Eater of Spears says Reiss is wise and that the Necromancer sees but does not know everything.
Eater of Spears says the Necromancer tells Reiss what he knows about the Humans and their plans.
Eater of Spears leads a group of larger Hobgoblins against Headscratcher and beats him down with punches and a kick.
Eater of Spears fights while Erin Solstice throws a Tripvine Bag that he dodges, saying he had told her he would.
A Cave Goblin throws Pepper Potion into Eater of Spears's nose and eyes, blinding him.
Blinded, Eater of Spears runs through the Flooded Waters tribe and Rags's tribe, splintering pikes and sending Goblins flying.
Ekirra is a Gnoll cub with red fur and a black splotch across one eye, around Mrsha's age, who can talk.
Ekirra is the son of the Gnoll Jeva, and is excitable and a great deal less shy than his friends.
Ekirra has an older sister who brings him places and makes him use utensils at the table.
Ekirra races excitedly into Krshia's room calling Mrsha's name and asking to go to the park to play with her and show his new ball.
Ekirra's new ball is stolen by Visma, who calls it hers; when he demands it back she punches him in the nose and runs off.
Ekirra is stunned and left sitting on the ground, though his nose is not bleeding.
Ekirra has a special ball with stars on it that glow in the dark, a birthday present he waited a long time for.
Ekirra's new ball replaces an old, ratty leather one that his sister had owned.
Ekirra is dismayed when he sees that Mrsha's magical red ball also glows in the dark and can come back on its own.
Ekirra, Mrsha and Visma are about to surprise Erin when they overhear her cursing mildly, and Ekirra repeats "Damn!"
Visma tells Erin that Ekirra learned a bad word and that his mother got mad when he said it.
Ekirra and Visma are Mrsha's best friends, and Erin is trying to make playdates a regular thing.
Ekirra acts as the neutral party and explains to Erin that Mrsha hit Visma for pulling Apista's wings.
Ekirra paces anxiously while Mrsha tries to apologize to Visma, then cries along with his two friends, and the three share chocolate.
Ekirra and Visma come to breakfast at the inn, brought by their older sister and brother, and Ryoka meets them for the first time.
Ekirra puts a crepe on his head, licks syrup off his arm fur and stares at Ryoka as she eats.
Erin introduces Ryoka to Ekirra and Visma as Mrsha's "Aunt".
Elena is a young woman from Earth whose Greek name descends from Helen, and she is a [Beautician] by class.
Elena graduated from a university in Greece in a two-year program, and is older than Aaron by nearly half a decade.
Elena is stunning, and brought a beautician's gift to this world, where her Skills made her one of the most attractive people Aaron had met.
Elena fabricated the first beauty products by herself before Wistram's teams found her.
Elena is a member, or rather an asset, of the Centrists faction under Archmage Feor.
Elena is one of seven young people from Earth in the Centrist faction's grasp, and is especially stubborn.
Elena is better than Aaron at subtly influencing people.
Elena is a friend of Cara, who found and saved her, and Elena was the one the band sent to Wistram.
Elena has a strong throwing arm and a temper almost as bad as Cara's.
Elena has only recently begun to learn magic and has weak command of it, though she can cast [Light].
Elena fills a plate at the Wistram buffet with Aaron, teasing him about his shock glove, when all of Wistram's Golems freeze for about a minute.
Elena keeps her voice light about the freeze, then mouths the word Robots to Aaron, reflecting the Earthers' worries about artificial intelligence.
Aaron and Elena consider Wistram full of idiots who have never heard of a robot uprising.
Elena and some other Earthers think the Golems serving food are effectively slaves.
Archmage Naili suspects the Ullsinoi faction leaked the cake recipe, which had once been a special treat available only among some factions.
Elena lectures a room of Wistram [Mages] that the world is round, using the shadows on the moons, an orange lit by a [Light] spell, shadow lengths and cliff height.
The Wistram [Mages] stay unconvinced and many leave, and Magus Telim says her proofs are circumstantial.
A few [Mages] believe, including a Centaur, a Lizardgirl and some half-Elves of the Centrists, and ask for more proofs.
Elena says that when Cara left Earth it was 2017, while Elena left in 2018.
Elena tells Aaron the Archmages might be nice to the Earthers while useful, but the Earthers are not in control.
Elena says that Cara warned her it might be like this, and that she volunteered.
Elena says she marched with Cara on a village out of hell ruled by an immortal [Witch].
Elena says that powerful people ruling the world and deciding how others live or die is what Cara was afraid of.
Elena, as spokesperson for two thirds of Wistram's young Earthers, demands better journalism from Feor and Viltach, saying the Drake commentators spread misinformation and downplay the disease.
Elena tells Feor to hire a commentator from Baleros with good practices, saying news people should be held to standards.
Viltach dislikes Elena's tone, and when he mutters that the people do not need the truth, Elena looks appalled.
Cara received a letter from Elena that lacked the agreed passphrases, and concluded Elena was being held hostage.
Elena speaks by an illusion phone with Ryoka, who calls herself batman, and warns her that Wistram knows where every device they call is.
Elena says she is a friend of the Singer of Terandria, that Blackmage Aaron says Ryoka dropped out of contact, and that many Earthers are with her.
Elena says that Wistram hunts the world for Earthers and that everyone it gets comes there and cannot leave.
Elena tells Ryoka that Cara is safe, too big for them to get, high-level and with friends.
Elena answers six when asked how confident she is in the call's safety, and Ryoka also rates it six out of ten.
The Elusive Lot, including one named Galei, keep the spell active to listen in on the call.
Elena warns Ryoka never to say anything about Earth before a scrying orb, since Wistram's scrying television may be able to see through them.
Galei tells Ryoka that a mirror enchanted with [Scrying] by Palt cannot be reversed by Wistram to watch the user.
Elena says that most of Wistram do not know what brought the Earthers here, and she is almost positive of it.
Elena reports theories that an interdimensional rift or a huge ritual-level spell brought the Earthers, possibly from Wistram's upper floors.
Elena tells Ryoka that the Death of Magic, a rebel [Archmage] of Wistram who joined the Demons, is at least Level 70 and probably Level 80.
Elena says that Wistram is almost certain the King of Destruction has an Earther.
Elena says someone is buying sulfur from the big markets, and Wistram traced it only as far as Chandrar.
Elena thinks six people know how to make gunpowder, though two might be talking out their asses, and the Earthers are not united about keeping secrets.
Elia Arcsinger is a blonde half-Elf archer and a Named Adventurer.
Elia's team includes a younger half-Elf archer, who is her daughter, and other archers.
Elia was a Silver-rank half-Elf adventurer when she loosed an arrow into the Goblin King's eye, killing him instantly.
Elia used the Skill [Piercing Shot] at nearly point-blank range, as the Goblin King's defences had been stripped by other attacks.
Elia owned an enchanted Arrow of Slaying known for piercing, and her longbow was certified by Gnoll [Bowmakers] to reach four hundred meters.
Many [Strategists] argue that the Goblin King should have dodged the shot, since he had caught and dodged arrows in other battles.
A vocal minority claims Elia used a special Skill or an enchantment she was unaware of.
Killing Velan the Kind earned Elia the title of Kingslayer and the Skill [Line-Ender Shot].
Elia became known as one of the greatest Named Adventurers of her age because of the kill.
Elia arrives above Tremborag's army in Dwarfhalls Rest by [Lesser Teleport], with four archer companions and a silver-glowing bow.
Goblins freeze in dread at the sight of Elia, and Tremborag recognises her face with horror.
The Goblins of Dwarfhalls Rest flee in panic from the adventurer they call Kingslayer.
Elia's Skill affects the whole mountain, terrifying the Goblins there, and Reiss suspects it is more than mere memory.
Elia marches with the great Human army against the Goblin Lord, and Rags's Goblins fear her as Kingslayer.
Elia stands at the head of the Human ranks beside Tyrion Veltras, and the Goblins remember golden hair, a bow and a fallen King.
Elia shoots Tremborag in the back with an arrow, which only wounds him.
Tyrion Veltras's [Mages] then cast a [Siege Fireball] at Tremborag, who dives clear.
Elia is staying in Invrisil as a Named Adventurer, though her contract expired and her team is not Named.
Elia is reclusive, and Typhenous says she is unlikely to drink with Todi.
Halrac and Revi recall that Elia helped rout the Goblins in the Dwarfhalls Rest mountain.
Elia's name makes Goblin tribes flee, and the Greystone Chieftain shudders at it.
The Greystone Chieftain says retaliation from adventuring teams wiped out the Goblin tribes that traded with the Greystones.
Elia leads her team against Goblins in a city street, and the crowd cheers "Kingslayer!".
The Goblins in that fight chant "Arcsinger!" and a Hob raises his shield, remembering her legend.
Elia fires a [Greenbane Arrow] with [Great Enemy: Goblin], which detonates against a Hob's shield and takes his arm.
Elia then readies a [Line-Ender Shot] at a charging Hob.
Elia and her team kill the Hobs in that street fight, and seven smaller Goblins flee because the Named Adventurer is too hard to kill.
Eliasor Melissar is the daughter of Lady Patricia Melissar and is the last of her line, becoming a [Lady] of Izril.
Eliasor's father died in the Sacrifice of Roses before she was born, and her mother Patricia had walked the same trial and survived.
Magnolia Reinhart announces after Lady Patricia's murder that her daughter Eliasor is the new head of the Melissar family and asks the room to welcome her as a peer.
Bethal curtsies to Eliasor first, and Magnolia and the other [Lords] and [Ladies] follow.
Eliasor sees her mother's head and the [Assassin] fall to the [Chevalier] Thomast's blade at the ball.
Magnolia tells Eliasor that she is now a [Lady] of Izril whose line begins and ends with her, and that she must rise.
Eliasor gains her class after her mother's death, though her mother had expected it when she turned ten or later.
Eliasor stops eating after her mother's death, so her servants call for Magnolia Reinhart.
Later, Eliasor becomes a ward of Lady Zanthia, who is sent by Magnolia, and studies with six other young [Ladies].
Eliasor resents Zanthia's strict discipline and has studied under her for two months.
Eliasor was ten years old at the time of the attack on the street.
Eliasor tells Zanthia she does not want to be a [Lady], but Zanthia says she has the class and no right to refuse.
Eliasor stands still when an [Assassin] swings at her in the street, saying a [Lady] faces death without fear.
Zanthia blocks the blade an inch from Eliasor's neck, embraces her, and says she will be as great a [Lady] as her mother.
Zanthia promises Eliasor vengeance for her mother's death, whether by Magnolia's hand, Zanthia's or her own.
Elirr is an old Gnoll of the Silverfang Tribe who runs a pet shop in Liscor, and he is the oldest Gnoll held captive by the Raskghar.
Elirr is a [Beast Trainer], not a [Beast Tamer] or [Beast Master], and his shop is one of five pet stores in Liscor.
Elirr trains dogs, cats and small caged birds, and keeps war dogs, cats, small dogs, birds and a crab in his shop.
Elirr is a Plains Gnoll but less so than Krshia, and had been in Liscor as a retired scout before the Silverfang Clan arrived ten years earlier.
Elirr is a Councilmember of Liscor and finds the new laws and progress make him feel young.
Elirr's level and the Raskghar issue would make him a distinguished speaker at the Meeting of Tribes, according to Krshia.
Elirr is the leader of the Gnoll captives in the Raskghar's cages, and the others defer to him.
Elirr says old legends held that the Raskghar broke away from the Gnolls underground and became beasts that hunted them.
Elirr says the legends were incomplete and that the Raskghar performed rituals that gave them strength.
Elirr says the Book of Levels does not mention such things, and that Gnolls have forbidden blood magic as the worst of deeds.
Elirr is shocked that Mrsha can cast [Mage] magic, because no Gnoll has done so in living memory.
Elirr kicks Nokha, breaks out of his cage and tears open Mrsha's cage bars, then flees carrying her as Nokha and awakened Raskghar chase them.
Elirr tells Zevara that Mrsha howled, bringing the monster down on the Raskghar, and ran back to buy time when the Hobs would fall.
The Raskghar made Elirr eat foul monster parts in the cage, which still haunts him.
Elirr's mastiff war dog is wary of him, because he starved for two days when Elirr was kidnapped just after acquiring him.
Mrsha faces down Elirr's mastiff by eating from its bowl, which cows the dog.
Elirr tells Lyonette that a [Beast Tamer] over Level 40 is exceptionally rare, and that some animals, such as Crelers, cannot be tamed.
Elirr says he could barely tame a Griffin, only to the most basic of social functions.
Elirr says a [Beast Tamer] who tried to train a Creler was found dead in his home, half-devoured.
Elirr believes Skills can make animals only so intelligent, and that a truly intelligent creature would be a person.
Elirr refuses to sell Relc a trained attack sheep and keeps a killer cat named Miss Twekla who is trained to kill pests.
Elirr bans Mrsha and the others from his shop after Mrsha ties two rats together, until they learn to respect animals.
Elirr calls his dogs and cats to kill the rats' basement nest, which none survive.
Elirr is angrier at the two bound rats than at the death of the nest.
Elirr sits with Mrsha at the bar and gets a herbal cream liqueur from Rufelt on the house, and comforts her.
Elirr drinks with Krshia in his pet shop to mark the end of the month of Rerrk.
The Meeting of Tribes was last held ten years ago, and Elirr remembers where he was.
Elirr hears Krshia say Magus Grimalkin is training another Gnoll capable of magic.
Elirr agrees to raise a baby Frost Wyvern found by the army, to muzzle it and get it used to people before handing it to another trainer.
Elirr and Krshia plan to take the Pallass door to the Meeting of Tribes, which saves over a month of travel.
Elirr trains the Frost Wyvern Jekle among his cats and his six-year-old unsold cat Alamaran.
Elirr has liaison duties with Architect Hexel.
Elirr and Hexel, a Lamia, are a new couple, which Mrsha discovers by following Hexel.
Elirr asks Mrsha to tell no one about it, not even Lyonette, Erin or Numbtongue, since it could mean danger.
Elirr says Gnoll tribes do not mind same-sex couples.
Elirr regrets having called Mrsha a Doombringer to her face in the cages.
Elmmet is a Lancrel [Councilman] and one of Lancrel's big leaders, with white hair, who is hardly spry.
Elmmet is a Level 30 [Thief] who probably has [Master of Faces] as a Skill, in the view of a speaker who reports it to Laken's circle.
Elmmet has a face-changing Skill, so that witnesses saw a young man or a woman rather than him.
Beniar chases a hooded [Thief] with his horse, and Durene reaches the pair as the armoured Beniar knocks the man out.
Beniar pulls off the hood and swears when he sees the [Thief] is Master Elmmet.
Lancrel's folk say Elmmet has been set up, and a speaker is disgusted that a [Councilman] was the thief.
Elmmet is held under guard, and a public trial with a truth stone is planned for the next day.
Elmmet is pilloried with head and hands through it while Prost holds a cheap two-setting truth stone, red for false and blue for truth.
Elmmet claims he is innocent and was only caught by Beniar while trying to catch the [Thief] himself.
Elmmet claims the truth stone can be faked and that Prost and his hired adventurers framed him.
Elmmet answers Prost's question about [Master of Faces] by saying the stone would lie if he answered.
Elmmet demands an impartial judge and a proper trial, and Prost replies that this is his one trial.
Elmmet asks that his wife and daughter be asked to vouch for him, and they are pushed forward.
Elmmet's daughter stares at the crowd, and at her father, in terror.
Hedag's axe swings down at the trial, and the crowd shouts that Master Elmmet is dead.
Prost says afterward that he would swing an axe twice if Elmmet stood before him again, and calls the verdict just.
Prost asks Hedag to swear before all present that her Skill revealed Elmmet Patterson's sins and crimes.
Eloise is an old [Witch] who arrives in Riverfarm describing herself as a travelling trader specialising in teas, flowers and herbs.
Eloise carries an heirloom porcelain cup and wears a grey travelling hat, and her teas and biscuits put Rie and others at ease.
Eloise serves tea at a table with a [Carpenter], a Lancrel [Councilwoman] and a mother from one of the towns.
Eloise tells Miss Safey she has a village of her own and no children or relatives who would care for her.
Wiskeria says Eloise is very skilled at herbal magic and tea, lives in one village and generally helps people out.
Wiskeria says Eloise has no secret and is just nice.
Eloise says her talent is tea, sociability and medicines, and that she puts her magic into her tea.
Eloise says that when she sits with people and offers tea and advice, she makes them feel better and takes a little of their good feeling.
Eloise's magic tea made from local roots tastes far better than the identical plain tea.
Eloise says her tea loses its effect within a few days, and neither [Preservation] spells nor bags of holding preserve it.
Eloise prepares a second pot of tea merely by touching it while Nanette struggles to ignite sticks.
Eloise says kindness asks questions and that spreading it is her craft, her reason for existing and the root of her magic, unlike Belavierr's.
Eloise warns the circle that Belavierr offers charms that can be very good, but that no one should accept a deal she seeks out.
Eloise tells Rie that she seeks the same person Belavierr seeks, and asks Rie to convince Rehanna to sit with her.
Eloise sits with the grieving Rehanna, who had a husband, a home and a child before fleeing the Goblins.
Eloise, with Hedag and Mavika, helps take about fifty children and parents out of the fire under fire-resistance charms.
Eloise slaps Alevica and tells her that flying with a spent mana pool would get her killed by the Drake.
Eloise tells Alevica to come with them, since Mavika has agreed to fly with the group.
Eloise trembles with fury and swears by her hat that no [Witch] in the world will give Belavierr shelter or aid after Califor's death.
Eloise is carried by Charlay to Gralton's lands in two days.
Eloise, an old [Tea Witch], judges that the Halrac team is honest because the boy Cade laughs and talks freely.
Eloise notes the strong artifact of an invisible bow on Halrac's back.
Eloise and Hedag represent the [Witches] on Laken's council, having accepted when asked.
Eloise signals Laken by tipping her hat up for a smile and down for a frown, and uses it when giving advice.
Eloise names herself the most suited healer in the region to cure the poisoned Lords, and says she knows of someone as accomplished at poisoning and curing who would not consent.
Eloise says she could cure two poisoned [Lords] in time, but that the journey is too dangerous for her to undertake.
Mavika says protecting Eloise on the journey is not her craft, which is killing, not protecting.
Eloise says she and Mavika spoke no untruths, since it is unwise for [Witches] to lie.
Eloise says she would never risk the trip to House Veltras, even with its army, as it would escalate into open conflict.
Eloise offers to decipher the poison afflicting Lords Hethon and Sammial from Riverfarm, warning that there will be reprisals.
Eloise asks that the Unseen Empire declare itself the beneficiary of [Witches] and that [Witches] receive land in perpetuity, perhaps a small forest.
Laken now regards Eloise as his most knowledgeable and trustworthy advisor.
Eltistiman Verdue is a [Magician] with bright green hair and blue robes decorated with magical symbols, who does illusions.
Eltistiman can cast illusions, is proficient in other spells, and fights fairly well.
Eltistiman appears to Erin as a Dragon, and she punches through the illusion and breaks his nose.
Eltistiman says he hoped to audition for the Players of Celum, and wants to reach Pallass through the door.
Olesm tells Eltistiman the door sends only two people at a time and that Pallass requires a request form.
Eltistiman says a [Lady] with fine taste in horticulture hired him to keep the door at the inn.
Eltistiman takes Typhenous captive at wand-point and has him cuff himself, until a man bursts through the door and beats Eltistiman.
Typhenous says the Smiling Man hired him and that he did it for the favors owed and his team.
Lyonette says Eltistiman vanished the night the door was stolen, and Olesm thinks he is guilty, with a bounty on his head.
Eltistiman shoots magic darts that drop the [Thug Boss] and drive off his Greenblades, saving the Players of Celum.
Eltistiman asks to audition, and Wesle says a flair like his needs none.
Eltistiman joins the Players of Celum.
Eltistiman recognises Typhenous in Invrisil and aims his wand at him before Emme makes him lower it.
Eltistiman and Typhenous agree they are quits over the door, though the Sisters want answers.
Eltistiman says he persuaded the gangs to leave Typhenous alone, woke in the basement and walked out invisible.
Embria Grasstongue is a young Drake [Wing Commander] and the 4th Company Commander of Liscor's army.
Embria has light red scales, later described as crimson, and carries a spear enchanted with lightning.
Embria is younger than Zevara and had last visited Liscor six years before her arrival.
Embria's [Commander] rank gives her autonomy and authority, and [Wing Commander] is roughly equivalent to [Major].
Embria's 4th Company has ninety-seven soldiers in total, all of whom are Drakes and Gnolls.
A Pallass observer states that Embria's main combat class is [Spear Hunter].
Embria is a [Spearmaster] who learned her spear work from Relc, according to Captain Pielt.
Embria uses an Evercut spear that halts regeneration and slows clotting, which she says is not the best but served her for years.
Embria killed her first Wyvern at eighteen, while Relc killed his at twenty-six.
Embria copied Relc's vault trick, which took her a decade to learn, and unlike him she has used it in battle.
Embria is Relc's daughter by a [Major] to whom he was not married, and her mother had pink scales.
Embria grew up travelling with Liscor's army, which Pallass observers assume meant she was raised by both parents.
Relc introduces Embria publicly to Erin as his daughter.
Embria's mother died in service, and Embria says she died a hero.
Embria says Goblins killed her mother, and refuses to make peace with them.
Embria demands that Relc call her by rank while they are on duty.
Embria asks her father why it is so hard to do her job, calling him Dad.
Embria thinks her father is a disappointment and wants him to reenlist, which Relc refuses.
Embria gives Relc her will, which leaves her possessions to him, as is standard practice before a big battle.
Embria tells Relc that his name and a weapon worthy of a commander were awarded to him because he hunted down enemy commanders.
Embria and Relc reconcile while she practises spear forms, and Relc copies her movements in step with her.
Embria holds Relc's hand as they walk to the inn and recalls running away when she was thirteen.
Relc tells Embria he left the army out of fear and unhappiness, and refuses once more to return.
Embria says it is the last time she will ask Relc to return.
Relc agrees to attend morning practice, and Embria says the time has not changed.
Embria ends the day thinking she had always had a father and now has a friend.
Embria and Relc have weekly father-daughter get-togethers at the inn.
Embria brings back her father's spear, saying she found Soot but not Bearclaw.
Embria drinks in the inn in a depressed state after her father is reassigned.
Embria's army was besieging Zeres under contract to Oteslia and was delayed in getting to Liscor.
Embria's orders were to return to Liscor and defend it.
Embria tells the Redfang Hobs that all Walled Cities raised Goblin bounties fivefold after Zel Shivertail's death.
Embria says her army eradicated two small Goblin tribes on the way.
Embria says the Human nobility are mobilising against smaller tribes and that no Goblin will survive near Liscor once the Human with the large army moves.
Embria tells the Redfangs to run while they can, since everyone in the world is hunting them.
Embria asks Selys to put the breastplate in the city's custody, and Selys refuses.
Embria is furious that her command was not informed of the attack on Liscor, and Zevara admits she forgot.
Embria offers to deploy her soldiers to the walls, and Zevara declines, saying it is her city.
Embria says her orders included looking into the Antinium, since the Small Queen was sighted in Liscor and the Hives are acting oddly.
Embria notes that both Xrn and Klbkch visited Erin's inn.
Embria wonders why everyone listens to Erin, noting even Wall Lord Ilvriss and that Zel Shivertail stayed at her inn.
Embria lost two soldiers and has a cut above the shoulder after the battle, and reports to High Command.
Embria clumsily invites Olesm for a drink on her father's advice, and Olesm declines.
Embria claims that with a thousand Level 10 [Soldiers] she could rout an army of two thousand Cave Goblins.
Embria offers to rout the Goblins with Pallass's forces and a thousand Watch, which Olesm warns would cost hundreds of casualties.
Embria tells Relc that High Command gave her classified orders to do her duty.
Embria speaks to High Command by a mana stone, swearing to do her part by the walls.
Embria leads a sortie of about a thousand Drakes and Pallass soldiers out of Liscor's gates to hold the Goblins away.
Embria tells Zevara she has orders to keep Liscor safe, and charges with Skills at the Goblins.
Embria stabs the first Goblin as the walls' enchantments fire behind her.
Errif tells Embria that the Assembly will not act without a vote and that Pallass is not at Liscor's beck and call.
Embria arrives with the 4th Company at Lism's rally and is introduced as the hero of the Battle for Liscor.
Embria speaks against trusting the Antinium with Liscor's walls at the rally.
Embria privately thinks Lism is obnoxious, sycophantic and prejudiced against Gnolls, and wishes she could back Krshia.
Embria's orders from High Command are to support Lism's candidacy.
Embria orders all squads to cull Shield Spider nests, four per squad a day, with a night at Wishdrinks for the winner.
Embria says she has killed Antinium on the neutral Hive border and calls them cold, insectile strangers.
Embria sits mounted and watches her company's nest cull.
Embria tells Vell that Yellow Splatters is more than a Prognugator and a leader, as Zel Shivertail was.
Embria drinks with Relc at the inn when Captain Vell toasts the right candidate winning the election.
Embria hands Zevara a communication stone for High Command.
Embria says her 4th Company has brought down Wyverns before but would advise everyone to shelter if the weyr descended.
Embria smiles widely as her company gets drinks and stories about Relc after he faces the Wyvern Lord.
Embria tells Relc the 4th may stay in Liscor on semi-permanent duty.
Embria tells Zevara that her orders are to let Relc and Klbkch fight.
Embria advises Liscor's Council off the record that Hectval's rudeness is a classic Drake power-move.
Embria suggests answering Hectval with a lavish show of generosity that forces reciprocation.
Embria says Liscor, with Antinium and Human trade, counts as liberal to most Drakes.
Emessa is a Drake [Smith] apprentice who works for the Dwarf Pelt.
Emessa is the longest-serving of Pelt's apprentices, working under him for about a year, longer than the last six apprentices he had over that year.
Pelt calls Emessa only "apprentice", and she wonders whether he knows her name.
Emessa loves being Pelt's apprentice because his corrections let her avoid worrying about the quality of her blade, which ends up as good as Maughin's work.
Emessa is willing to accept near-perfection, since Pelt makes almost no mistakes and only microscopic flaws.
Emessa adores her master and does not understand why other smiths mock him and other apprentices scorn her.
Emessa is a Drake girl too afraid to be her own [Smith].
Emessa is one of three apprentices who follow Pelt out of Deríthal-vel, leaving her home without hesitation.
Emessa walks taller after Pelt lit a spark in her soul.
Emessa tells Pelt that they could make a proper forge to his specifications even in the inn.
Emily is one of the people from Earth summoned to Rhir, a [Hydromancer] who is popular in the group.
Tom calls Emily the idol of the group if anyone can be called that.
Emily is a Level 21 [Hydromancer].
Emily has the highest level in the group besides Richard, and Tom says she is something like the second leader.
Later, Tom calls Emily the group's highest-level [Mage], and by then both Richard and Emily are over Level 30.
Later, Emily is Level 34, which Cirille considers insane for a [Mage] to level so fast.
Cirille thinks Emily has eclipsed Richard and even Tom in level.
Emily is a leader of the group alongside Richard, and Tom calls her beloved.
Emily flirts with Richard at the table, and Tom thinks they are a couple in some sense but not officially.
Tom does not think Emily and Richard have had sex yet, because the news would spread quickly in their tight-knit circle.
Emily stares at Nereshal when he is introduced.
Emily clears the way for Richard's charge at a gap with [Tidal Wave], a wall of water that knocks back the first wave of enemy soldiers and monsters.
Emily then casts [Summon Water Elemental], and a huge water figure lashes about at her command.
Emily stays on the wall, staring, after the fight and says she cannot understand why they need the Earthers.
Emme is the stage manager and later [Director] of the Players of Celum.
Emme is a short, heavy woman with Dwarf blood, shorter than anyone else in her troupe.
Emme is beardless, and says she is relieved not to have the bushy beard some Dwarven descendants grow.
Emme often played the lower half of an animal or a moving prop, since few parts suit her height.
Emme plays Olaf the Snow Golem in a costume during the troupe's performance at the Wandering Inn.
Emme does not rise to the bait when Drakes in the front row cheer against the Players of Celum.
Emme rules that the rewritten scripts are used for most plays and the original text only sparingly.
Emme dreams of having the Players perform for nobility, where they would earn more money.
Emme agrees a restaurant deal at forty-sixty of the takings after the owner's ingredients.
Emme challenges rival Men of Invrisil [Actors] to recite a Hamlet soliloquy, and Kilkran, Yimur and Pralcem each perform part of it.
The Men of Invrisil cannot do the same and retreat while the crowd cheers the Players.
Emme mutters that the riots may smash up the Solstice Theatre, after the Players' performance is cancelled.
The Emperor of Sands rules the largest nation in Chandrar, an empire built in the years after the King of Destruction's fall.
The Emperor of Sands has expanded the empire across the western nations in the last eight years, and the Zeikhal desert has stopped further expansion.
Orthenon believes the Emperor of Sands wants to consolidate the west before expanding, and may conquer north and south rather than cross the desert.
The Emperor of Sands rules from a silver throne, and veiled attendants fill the audience hall.
The Emperor of Sands is a Stitchman who changes bodies, appearing first as a young, impatient man with stitch-marks around his fingers.
Attendants cut the stitches at the Emperor's neck, and the head is sewn onto a new body behind a wall of cloth.
After the swap the Emperor of Sands becomes a tall, elegant woman with a low, soft voice who says she has a new perspective.
The Emperor of Sands is a String-person who can sew and replace any body part, including the head that most String-people cannot replace.
The Emperor of Sands styles herself [Empress] when wearing the female head and [Emperor] when wearing the young man's head, though both are the same being.
The Emperor of Sands has nearly a dozen heads, all String-folk, including a young man who had been a fearsome [Lieutenant].
Another head of the Empress is a grinning, scarred head that makes her a genius but too ambitious, debauched and murderous.
The Empress keeps a female head on a pedestal that she considers the most complete and reasonable, though not the best for combat or war.
The female head the Empress wears was once Emira Saet-rei of Doran, who vanished in a deal with the then-Emperor to protect her defeated folk.
Doran was a small nation subsumed early by the Empire of Sands, and Emira Saet-rei had led its defence well.
The Empress, when wearing Saet-rei's head, loves poor puns, which makes half her other heads groan.
The Empress wears an old [General] head that she will not wear for a long time, regretting that she executed Drevish while wearing it.
The Emperor of Sands has an empire-wide Skill, [Sanctuary of the Desert], that draws water from deep aquifers and springs into dry soil.
The Empress proclaims that a new oasis will begin at a chosen spot within two days, and her people cheer.
The Empress remarks that an [Emperor]'s duties include more than war, though Chandrar thrives on war.
The Emperor of Sands is advised by disembodied voices speaking from the ceiling and walls, who counsel patience against the Garuda.
The voices tell the Emperor that war is not the only tool of empire, and he asks for a different perspective.
The Emperor of Sands sends Flos a box by Courier containing the head of Drevish, one of the King's Seven.
Flos declares war on the Emperor of Sands, vowing not to rest until he is dead.
The Emperor admits he should not have slain "the Architect" and provoked Flos so soon.
The Empress says Flos used [Army of the King] at Reim and would have lost but for a grand enchantment on his city.
The Empress did not know that Drevish had created the grand enchantment on Reim, and regrets executing him.
The Empress believes that to defeat Flos she must have him use [Army of the King] and then slay him before he can use it again.
The Empress resolves that the Empire of Sands will grow while other nations burn themselves against Reim, and she will strike Flos when the time is right.
Erille is the youngest [Princess] of the Blighted Kingdom, a girl in a violet dress who wants to learn backflips from the Fool.
Erille is the half-sister of Princess Isodore.
Erille speaks directly to Tom and says her father claims the Fool has hidden depths.
Erille hides behind the Fool and Tom like any kid her age, and is fond of the Fool.
Erille wears two rings, one of which hides her from Nereshal's scrying, and she evades her guards.
Isodore warns her that her guards are searching in a panic and that Nereshal was about to scry for her.
Erille reluctantly comes out from behind the Fool and returns to the palace with Isodore, who refuses to let the Fool accompany her.
Erille is alive after the Demon attack and kept in a safe place under the highest guard.
Erille thanks Tom in person for saving her life, mumbling her gratitude and then fleeing.
Erille's tears have to be hidden, because as a [Princess] she cannot weep in public.
The Fool cannot look at Erille while he holds a knife to her father's throat.
The dying Fool asks Tom to protect Erille and take her away.
Erille watches as Tom kills her beloved Fool and stares at him afterwards.
Erin Solstice is a young woman from Michigan who arrives in the new world with nothing and becomes an [Innkeeper] by cleaning an abandoned inn.

Erin is introduced as 20 years old, from Michigan, with a casual interest in video games, a deep obsession with strategy games (chess, shogi, go), hobbies of snowboarding and watching Youtube, and a dream of becoming a professional strategy game commentator.
Erin has two first names that could each belong to a girl or a boy, and she thinks Erin sounds more like a boy's name.
Erin tells Pisces that she cannot drink alcohol because she is underage, being only 20.
Ryoka sees Erin as a girl close to her own age, shorter than Ryoka, with fair skin, hazel eyes and only the slightest orange tint to her light brown hair.
Erin is 20 years old, and at Lady Magnolia's house the other girls all seem younger than she is.
The prologue shows an unnamed young woman with burned clothes and many bloody cuts on her arms and legs who finds the empty inn by chance and flees towards it by instinct (read here as Erin).
In the prologue the same unnamed woman sighs that ever since she came to this world everything has gone wrong.
Erin arrives in the world with no smartphone and empty pockets, wholly unprepared for travel.
Erin says she only wanted to go to the bathroom, and instead of the sight of white porcelain she ended up looking down the snout of a dragon.
Erin remembers a dragon in a cave that burned her arms and the Goblins that then chased her.
Erin later describes her arrival as stepping around a corner into what she thought was her bathroom and finding a Dragon larger than a house breathing fire.
Erin remembers the Dragon's swirling blue and violet eyes, and the narration says the overwhelmed sensation then is the same one she feels when she uses the [Immortal Moment] skill.

Erin spends her first evening cleaning the inn: she uses a mildewed grey curtain as a dustrag and cleans the tables, chairs, bar top and barkeep's shelf but leaves the floor, joking that her mother would be happy.
Erin gains the [Innkeeper] class at Level 1 with the skills [Basic Cleaning] and [Basic Cooking].
Erin concludes that the world works like a game, because she levels up and a thought announces her skills.
Erin fights off a Goblin ambush in the common room: she kicks the lead Goblin in the groin, clubs and throws chairs, kicks one in the face, slaps another and takes his knife.
Erin routs the remaining Goblins by raising the knife and shouting "Boo!" at them.
Erin laughs and falls asleep bleeding on the clean floor.
Erin wonders whether levelling in dreams means you level in real life.
Erin gets dehydrated, gulps too much cold stream water until she nearly vomits, and then bathes in the stream.
Erin counts "four levels in innkeeping" as one of her few assets.
Erin slips while skinning a fish and cuts her right palm diagonally; she feels no pain at first, then severe pain, and bandages it with a strip of upstairs curtain.
Erin recites a King's Gambit game aloud through the night to cope with the pain.
Erin takes two seed cores from the blue fruit trees along with her armful of fruit, "just in case".
Erin scrapes a splinter off the glowing runes of a food cupboard, cutting the line of runes in two, and the enchantment on the cupboard fades.
Erin wonders why anyone would leave good food and sharp knives behind in the inn and grows uneasy at the thought.
Erin knocks a Goblin scout senseless and throws him out of the inn door over the heads of the waiting Goblin ambush party, who pick him up and flee.
Erin can read the faded "Closed" sign on the inn even though the writing is not English, and she flips it to "Open".
Erin makes dough and noodles with flour, butter and giant dino-bird eggs, and one cracked egg contains a developing chick, which sickens her.
Erin invents blue fruit juice by peeling and pulping the fruit and adding stream water.
Erin tells Relc and Klbkch that she is from "Michigan", a place they do not know, and suggests a teleportation spell as the explanation.
Erin vomits violently after returning to the inn, and a fish that eats her vomit floats belly-up, so she concludes it was poison.
Erin falls asleep at the bar while waiting for guests.
Erin tells Pisces she did not found the inn but found it and somehow became an [Innkeeper] by cleaning up.
Erin gives Pisces her name.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin's pantry is empty, the flour and butter are gone, salt and sugar are running low, and she keeps her pay on the kitchen counter.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin stops Relc and Klbkch from killing Pisces in her inn, forbids killing, and withdraws her testimony so that they cannot arrest him.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin dares Relc to prove Pisces is a [Necromancer], then raps Pisces on the head with a pot and sends him out as well.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin sleeps at a table in her inn, which the narration describes as lonely but no longer alone.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin's breakfast is three shriveled, rubbery blue fruits, and she reasons that no food means no guests, no money and starvation.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin says she can handle Goblins, rude Necromancers, rock-crabs and giant fish that nibble her while she bathes, but she wants food.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin wonders whether the [Innkeeper] class is changing her.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin's t-shirt is stained blue, ripped and cut at the sleeves and burned on one side, and she has not bathed or brushed her teeth since she arrived.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin carries her coins in the bottom of one pocket and plans to buy clothing, food, soap, a toothbrush and a lamp.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin notes that Relc and Klbkch speak English and wonders whether she can read anything here.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin walks into Liscor for the first time as its only human visitor.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin speaks the same language as Relc and Klbkch but cannot read their writing, which the narration attributes to magic.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin pays a Drake shopkeeper from a mix of silver, bronze and three gold coins, receives a few dented copper coins in change, and buys a large cloth bag.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin has four silver coins left after the bag and the food, and she knows she was ripped off; the narration says she started with two gold coins and a handful of silver and copper.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin lies on the common room floor using the cloth bag as a pillow.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin eats a salty, gristly dried sausage for breakfast.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin vomits and screams at the sight of three Goblin heads, hurls things at Relc to get him out, and then carries the heads outside to find the bodies.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin digs a grave with a wooden spoon and then her bare hands and buries all three Goblins.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin reasons that the Goblin Chieftain hunts her for blood for blood even though she did not kill the three Goblins.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin waits at the table repeating "Checkmate" and asks herself whether it is checkmate or just check, deciding that to survive she must fight and kill.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin plays chess moves in her head while waiting for the Chieftain.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin builds a trap by heating a cast-iron pot of an item from her shopping bag over the kitchen fire.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin batters the Goblin Chieftain with a chair and a rolling pin, breaking his nose.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin grabs the boiling pot by its handles, blistering her hands, and throws the hot oil over the Chieftain's face.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin bandages the wound in her stomach with strips cut from the cloth bag.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin tells Klbkch that Goblins must not be killed because it is wrong, even though she calls them vicious murderers and herself a murderer too; Klbkch agrees but reserves the right to defend himself with lethal force.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin cannot sleep because she keeps seeing the dead Chieftain's eyes and hearing his breathing.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin throws a kitchen knife past Relc's head with [Unerring Throw] when he shouts about killing Goblins, tells him to leave them alone, and says it is her inn and she makes the rules.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin eats blue fruit in the orchard and then vomits, and she judges the pulp inside the seed core to be poison.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin invites four Goblins in, serves them buttered pasta with sausage and onions, tells them the first meal is on the house, and teaches one to eat with a fork.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin laughs for the first time in ages after the Goblin smiles at her.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin recalls her whole purchase list exactly and keeps the shopkeeper's own price paper, which she uses to threaten him with the Watch.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin buys a money pouch with Klbkch's help, then buys goods from Krshia and visits a Liscor bathhouse.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin's only customers for two days are Relc, Klbkch and Pisces, and she has named the inn and painted her sign.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin wears a t-shirt-style top and pants she ordered from a Gnoll tailor whom Krshia introduced her to.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin has never run a business and has only worked as a part-time library assistant and helper in chess tournaments.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin's jobs before arriving also include two weeks as a summer waitress and work as a chess tournament referee.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin rebuilds the floorboards eaten by acid with [Basic Crafting], after Klbkch helped repair them following the Chieftain's attack.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin anchors her acid-fly jars in the stream on Pisces's advice.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin writes a chalkboard menu of pasta with sausage and onions at 3 cp per plate, blue juice at 2 cp per glass, and acid flies at 1 s per plate.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin has eaten nearly half the orchard's blue fruit, catches acid flies in her floating jar traps, and is amused that she can buy pasta from a Gnoll woman instead of making it.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin spends two days failing to make ice cream and ends up with sugary butter.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin sorts her customers into Antinium, Goblins and Pisces, and the Goblins have to wash before they come in.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin never leaves knives or weapons out when Rags is in her inn.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin buys a short sword and a buckler for four gold from a Gnoll shopkeeper as a gift or bribe for Rags.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin gives Rags the sword and buckler on her tab and agrees to sell her acid jars for several bronze coins each.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin has just under ten gold, wants preservation runes, and sleeps in a blanket nest in a corner of the kitchen.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin buys cow's milk and eats cereal with sliced blue fruit for breakfast.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin pours a little acid into the outhouse each morning to cut the smell.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin has fixed up the upstairs, where the mattresses rotted and had to be thrown out but some bed frames only needed a backboard replaced.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin gets paying adventurer guests, the Horns of Hammerad, who pay in advance, and she runs out of food and ale.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin's first guest to return to her inn after the battle with Skinner is Klbkch, who asks to come in.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin sleeps on a bedroll in the kitchen.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin serves "random soup" that she makes by tossing ingredients in a pot and trusting [Basic Cooking].

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin still lists pasta with sausage and onions at 3 cp, blue juice at 2 cp and acid flies at 1 s on her menu.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin sends Toren out to harvest blue fruits and collect water while she naps.

section: Founding the inn and the first customers
text: Erin says half of the inn is still damaged from the battle with the undead two days earlier.
Erin gains the [Innkeeper] class at Level 1 and the skills [Basic Cleaning] and [Basic Cooking].
Later, Erin sleeps and reaches [Innkeeper Level 4], wondering what happened to Levels 2 and 3.
Later, Erin reaches [Innkeeper Level 5] and gains [Skill - Basic Crafting] as she falls asleep.
Later, Erin reaches [Innkeeper Level 6] after her first trip to Liscor.
Later, Erin reaches [Innkeeper Level 9] and gains [Tavern Brawling] and [Unerring Throw] after killing the Goblin Chieftain.
Later, Erin reaches [Innkeeper Level 10] and gains [Alcohol Brewer] and [Dangersense].
Later, Erin reaches [Innkeeper Level 11] and gains [Lesser Strength] and [Immortal Moment] after the emotional last game against Pawn.
Erin says she has gained ten levels in a month and that she is only Level 10, which shocks Selys.
Erin is an [Innkeeper], Level 11, according to an adventurer who questions her.
Later, Erin reaches [Innkeeper Level 12] on waking, then Level 13 and gains [Loud Voice] by the end of the day.
Later, Erin reaches [Innkeeper Level 15] after a night of singing in the inn.
Later, Erin learns [Power Strike], after muttering that being good at hitting is a crappy thing to be good at.
Later, Erin reaches [Innkeeper Level 18] and gains [Skill - Immunity: Alcohol] and [Skill - Quick Recovery] after the battle with Skinner.
Later, Erin becomes a [Warrior] at Level 2 and gains [Lesser Endurance].
Erin tells Selys that she got the [Warrior] class the day before at Level 2, and Selys suggests it came because Erin deliberately went looking for a fight.
Erin tells Selys that she reached Level 18 in [Innkeeper] after the undead attacked.
Later, Erin reaches [Innkeeper Level 19] while sleeping after the inn is rebuilt.

Later, after her rooftop concert, Erin reaches [Innkeeper Level 20] and [Innkeeper Level 21], gains [Advanced Cooking] and [Advanced Crafting], and gains the [Singer] class at Level 6 with [Perfect Recall] and [Control Pitch].
Later, after the faerie feast, Erin reaches [Innkeeper Level 25] and gains [Inn's Aura] and a skill announced as [Magical Cooking].
Erin counts four levels and two skills from the feast, and she names them [Inn's Aura] and [Wondrous Fare], deciding that [Magical Cooking] is not the right name.
Erin tells Calruz that she can fight if she has to, naming [Bar Fighting] and [Lesser Strength] as her skills.
Later, Erin's [Power Strike] is replaced by [Minotaur Punch] after she shouts about the Minotaur who taught her to punch.
Erin says she has two levels in [Warrior].
Lady Magnolia reads Erin's skills with a device and notes that she has [Bar Fighting], [Minotaur Punch], [Immortal Moment] and [Wondrous Fare].
Erin's [Basic Crafting] cannot repair a foundation.
Erin's [Basic Cooking] makes frying hamburgers near-automatic, and her [Advanced Cooking] makes cooking easy and speeds up french fries.
Erin's [Unerring Throw] lets her hurl rocks with the speed of a fastball and never miss.
Erin's throwing skill places a thrown frying pan exactly where she wants it, though she feels she wrenched her shoulder.
Erin uses [Unerring Throw] to hurl pots and pans at zombies during the battle with Skinner's forces.
Erin later calls the skill [Unerring Aim], using it to hit Pisces with a pillow and to throw rocks hard enough to kill zombies.
Erin feels a danger alarm like a tornado siren blasting in her head just before the undead attack.
Erin explains that her [Bar Fighting] only works with objects found in a bar or kitchen, which is why she fights with frying pans.
Erin's [Loud Voice] makes her voice thunderous enough to carry across the hills.
Erin's [Lesser Strength] lets her lift a heavy jar of acid and fight stronger opponents.
Erin's [Immortal Moment] skill makes a single moment seem endless, and she notes she has no idea what it does.
Erin's [Alcohol Brewer] skill is something she thinks she could use to make beer.
Erin's alcohol immunity (announced as [Skill - Immunity: Alcohol] and later called [Alcohol Immunity]) means she does not get drunk or suffer hangovers.
Erin's [Perfect Recall] lets her remember every lyric of any song she has sung, and [Control Pitch] gives her perfect pitch.
Erin's [Perfect Recall] covers songs, play lines and movie quotes but not books.
Erin's [Power Strike] works only once per use, so a second attempt hits with ordinary bruising strength.
Erin's [Minotaur Punch] works twice in a row, unlike [Power Strike].
Erin's [Inn's Aura] makes the air heavy around her inn, which Pisces explains is an aura common among leader classes.
Erin's [Wondrous Fare] skill suggested that the faerie flower drink would work.
Erin does not research her skills when she gets them because she has so much to do.
Erin's first game in Liscor is played quickly and aggressively against Olesm, who opens as White with a pawn from the side.
Erin gives Olesm repeated checks, taking his pieces with a knight depicted as a scaly Drake with a buckler and scimitar.
Erin checkmates Olesm.
Erin says she has played chess for twelve years.
Erin says she has won a chess tournament or two and once played a female Grandmaster, and she also knows shogi, go and card games.
Erin realises she cannot explain Japan or the games from her world to Klbkch and Olesm.
Erin flips the chessboard off the table, says she remembers why she got bored of chess, and says she will make her own rules.
Erin uses chess notation and beats Olesm with the Sicilian Defense against his King's Pawn opening while Klbkch and Olesm confer.
Erin then plays Klbkch and Olesm at once while serving food by relaying each player's moves to the other board, so that each player is in effect playing the other.
Erin draws paper chess boards and teaches the Antinium Workers and Goblins to play, and eight boards are running at once.
Erin stops Rags from stealing a chess pawn and invites her to come back any time.
Erin keeps the base of the broken chess knight in her pocket and plays Pawn on the grass using it.
Erin says she played chess every day as a kid, won her first tournament, learned to play blindfolded before she learned to ride a bike, and quit when the pressure consumed her life.
Erin says she got to just over 2000 points as a child and might be around 2400 now if she had kept playing.
Erin teaches Pawn the Immortal Game and then plays him one last game in tears, beating him.
Erin solves Olesm's five-move chess puzzle at a glance.
Erin sends Olesm a mirror-play challenge that forces checkmate in four moves, and pays him two silver.
Erin solved a similar puzzle in nearly a week in middle school.
Erin greets Ceria in Elvish because she once went to a Lord of the Rings chess tournament where people would not play her without a greeting.
Erin plays Pawn repeatedly through the night with no emotion, using the Queen's Gambit and French Defense lines, and wins every game.
Erin has used DGT electronic chess boards in tournaments and prefers stone pieces.
Erin was one of the child prodigies of chess.
Erin plays chess against herself to hold off Skinner's fear and knocks over the white king, saying she is no king.
Erin tips her own king over and calls herself a queen who is defending her inn.
Erin plays chess on her Android phone and can say check and checkmate in almost every language.
Erin has never lost to Olesm, whom Selys says she beat the first time they met and plays almost every day.
Erin sent out a chess puzzle and receives a plain Afzelia chessboard with no pieces from a Courier from First Landing.
Erin plays a game against a distant opponent while Olesm watches, and for once she concentrates completely, sitting upright and silent.
Erin has played more matches in a year than Olesm has in his life, and Olesm remembers her playing a hundred Workers at once and then an Immortal Game of her own.
Erin loses a queen midway through a game against the distant opponent, then punishes the capturing bishop and wins.
Erin's chess history in her own mind runs from loving chess to hating it to loving it again, and she thinks of the spirit of chess as a god that bestows gifts like curses.
