Erin plays Lady Magnolia, who admits she used [Sense Intention] and cheated, and then wins the second game while Magnolia reads her intentions.
Erin carries a chessboard she calls magical.
Erin hugs Pawn, says she is sorry, and then leaves the inn.
Erin tells Pawn that she was always afraid of losing as a kid and that chess is not scary compared to other things.
Erin tells Queen Klbkch "died free" when the Queen calls him a failure.
Erin offers Gazi a job for food and the upstairs rooms she could fix up, and Gazi declines, advising Erin to invest in defense.
Erin recognises the Workers around her inn as her chess club, though they had never had names.
Erin has woken up screaming and crying every night since Klbkch died.
Erin tells Ryoka the whole story from the Goblins and acid flies to the dragon.
Erin realises Ryoka is from Earth when Ryoka reacts to her mention of an iPhone.
Erin tells Ceria she and Ryoka come from another world.
Erin calls Calruz "bull guy" and other nicknames.
Erin knows Gazi, who was at her inn and helped her when they first met.
Erin says she fed Rags, gave her a sword and shield, and made Pisces teach her magic.
Erin invites Ceria to stay at the inn for free for as long as she likes.
Erin offers Lyonette a job or a coat and five days of food, telling her she gets only one chance.
Erin calls Lyonette "Lyon", and Lyonette demands her full name.
Erin shouts "WAKE UP" in Lyonette's ear to get her out of bed.
Erin asks to see Lyonette's injuries and Lyonette refuses, claiming her noble word is good enough.
Erin punches Lyonette when she attacks, slaps her after she insults Erin, and leaves her sobbing.
Erin cooks spaghetti and meatballs with [Advanced Cooking] and eats two plates with Ceria.
Erin appears to be cut off from Gnoll shops after hiring Lyonette, since several Gnolls on the street give her the stink-eye.
Erin tells Klbkch that making the Workers play chess will not make them individuals, since Pawn chose his name when she asked him.
Erin calls Moore "Hodor", and Moore corrects her.
Erin tells Pawn and Halrac the story of Moses and then of Jesus, explaining heaven and hell as the afterlife and learning that the Antinium cease to be after death.
Erin lends the Horns of Hammerad much of her gold, which they promise to repay.
Erin says Ryoka has no levels or classes, was going south to earn eight hundred gold, and was chased by Frost Faeries.
Erin tells Imani that she ran into a Dragon the first night and then a group of Goblins.
Erin says she has been here three or four months, though it feels like two years.
Erin is unafraid of Ressa's glare because she looked at Skinner.
Erin has stayed in fancy hotels while travelling to chess tournaments, but none had a Van Gogh or a Rodin as Lady Magnolia's home does.
Erin wants to protect her friends, find a way home someday, and live in peace.
Erin stuns the biggest adventurer in the inn with a thrown frying pan.
Erin punches Pisces when he drops his invisibility spell.
Erin hurls a frying pan at a Minotaur with [Unerring Throw].
Erin beats Toren in a spar with Calruz's training and punches his head off the top of the hill.
Erin kicks Calruz in the groin.
Erin sells Gerial an acid jar.
Erin throws a large jar of acid that drenches Skinner.
Erin kills three zombies and one skeleton with her frying pan.
Erin says she killed a Goblin Chieftain with boiling oil, some other Goblins, Shield Spiders and undead.
Erin pokes Gazi in the eye.
Erin touches a Frost Faerie and finds her skin feels like fluid ice and something immortal.
Erin kicks Brunkr in the groin with [Power Strike].
Erin shouts "Everybody stop!" and a heavy aura presses on the hilltop.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin has beaten Olesm at chess and is rumoured to have met the Antinium Queen, so Drakes in Liscor recognise her as that Human girl.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin gets lost in the grasslands and avoids patches of red and white flowers because of a bad feeling that she takes to be [Dangersense].

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin promised Selys that she would stay near the area the Watch patrols.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin's rucksack holds flint and tinder, a long knife from the Adventurer's Guild, a healing potion costing nearly a gold coin, and a hand mirror.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Krshia thinks Erin wants to avenge Klbkch and offered to hunt with her, but Erin refused.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin kills a Shield Spider by throwing acid at it and then stomping it after wrapping her emptied rucksack around her hand; a fellow adventurer says her [Lesser Strength] helped.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin tells the adventurer she has learned she is good at killing, and says she does not want to be a killer or a warrior.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin jumps into the burning spider pit to rescue a baby Shield Spider, then throws it back into the pit when it bites her fingers and weeps.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin earns just over eleven gold from the Shield Spider bounty and the sale of the carcasses.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin returns to find her inn ransacked, with food, her toothbrush, hidden money, one gold coin and three silver coins taken.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin decides to keep the skeleton, and after running through many names ends with "Mike?".

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin tries to force something to happen with her fingertips and cannot, and Pisces tells her there is no more magic left in the air.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin tells Krshia and the others that she lived with her parents in Michigan and arrived by turning a corner and finding a dragon.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin says her world has about eight billion humans and no Gnolls, Drakes or monsters, and no Levels, Classes or Skills.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin did not go to college, preferring to work as a chess tutor and tournament contender to save money first.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin says she wants to go home to her mom and dad and friends, since she never got to say goodbye.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin punches a pile of fish guts in a fit of tears over having no magic.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin's [Basic Cooking] does not cover removing scales from a killer fish.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin dreams of Klbkch bleeding in her arms and saying "I obey my Queen", and of a chess King on a hill.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin says "I don't murder people. Ever." and explains that she kills monsters and has killed in self-defense.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin sits crying on the inn's roof in the rain for at least an hour.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin sings for the inn, including a Lady Gaga song, "Somewhere over the Rainbow", "Hallelujah" and "A Thousand Years", and teaches the room "Here I Am, Lord".

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin has a cold from sitting out in the rain.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin recites a childhood rhyme that the king is smart and uses his head, for if he moves he will soon be dead.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin refuses to keep fighting Toren when she sees the Goblin Chieftain and Klbkch in a flashback, then spars on after Calruz argues a king must defend himself as a last resort.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin tells the Horns of Hammerad she has seen a dragon, and Gerial and the others stop laughing.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin lifts a large jar of acid onto her shoulder and heaves it at Skinner, who is drenched but survives.

section: The Shield Spider hunt and the ransacked inn (Book 1)
text: Erin is told by Bird that she does not want to know where the dead Workers' bodies went, after the Soldier took them away.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin says the first non-European, non-furred, non-scaled face she has seen in this world is Ryoka's.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin whispers that she is not alone before she sleeps.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin thinks the climate might be the equivalent of Florida when she steps outside.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin tells Ryoka she has Dangersense and carries two jars of acid taken from the inn.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin says she has been selling acid to the Goblins and making good money.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: A Ghoul hit by Erin's acid jar dissolves into a glowing green puddle.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin tells Ryoka she is twenty, took a gap year to play chess and earn tuition, and became an [Innkeeper] by tidying a dusty inn until she woke as one.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Frost Faeries speak to Erin and Ryoka as winter arrives, calling someone a half-breed and noting that one human looks different.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin says Pisces told her it would cost eighty gold pieces to enchant some of her cupboards.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Ryoka explains that ice cream is made by heating and stirring milk like custard, and Erin had thought she had to churn milk.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin buys five blankets from Krshia, which may have saved her from freezing.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin tells Toren to find firewood.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin tells Krshia she wants ground beef, cheese, mustard, bread or buns, tomatoes, vinegar and eggs.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin asks that her wrecked inn be rebuilt closer to Liscor, and Klbkch says that should be possible.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin promises the Frost Faeries they will be welcome as guests at the new inn.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin shouts for Toren with [Loud Voice] until Zevara shouts "HUMAN! SHUT UP!" from the wall.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin feels that her rebuilt inn is not finished while Toren is missing.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin plants four wooden arrow signs on hilltops to guide Toren home.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin sells hamburgers from a brazier outside Krshia's stall and estimates perhaps six to eight hundred sold.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin hides her coins under a kitchen floorboard that Pawn installed.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin locks Toren in the inn before going to a tavern with Selys and Krshia.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin says the pickings get slim around the 2,000 Elo level, and recalls an online relationship with "mysterio_Gamer12", who turned out to be a Polish girl.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin begins to admit that she has never actually had sex.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin makes blue fruit juice and sips it afterwards.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin says she made over four hundred hamburgers the day before.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin sings pop songs from the inn roof with Ryoka's iPhone playing, and a crowd of Drakes, Gnolls and humans comes out of Liscor to listen.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Frost Faeries dance above Erin while she sings, and one throws a mug that shatters on Relc's head.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin has jars of coins from the concert night, with Krshia supplying goods during it.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin asks what happened to Toren's eyes and gives Rags a hamburger.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin charges Ceria for her stay, taking her bra as payment, so that she counts as a guest and the faeries leave her alone.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin and Ryoka are scared of the Frost Faeries, and Erin remembers being buried in an avalanche until Toren dug her out and Pisces melted some snow.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin recalls childhood belief in faeries, Santa and magic, and wonders when she stopped.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin asks to touch a Frost Faerie, and the pain of cold stops when she does, leaving a feeling like fluid ice.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin prepares a ritual feast with a cow's first milk, sugar mixed with snow under the moon, hand-churned butter, bread, flowers, mushrooms, Shield Spider venom, rum and mead.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin tells Ceria that she and Ryoka come from another world.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin runs out with a coat to save an exiled thief because no one deserves to die in the cold.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin introduces the exiled girl as her new employee and tells Toren to teach her to clean.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin gives a speech to the falling snow that she cannot let Lyonette die if she can help it, and the snow pauses in the air.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin tells the Gnolls to bring it after kicking Brunkr, who is part of the group attacking the inn.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin gets customers who are not just friends, as Gnolls, Drakes and the odd human come to the inn.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin plucks a faerie flower and says "gold" to turn it into a gold coin that feels real for a day and then turns back into a flower.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin will not spend the flower coins because she thinks it would be stealing.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin offered Ceria a place to live as long as she wants.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin serves hamburgers and pizza and wants maple syrup.

section: Winter, the faeries and the new inn (Book 2)
text: Erin drove off nine Goblins by shouting at them to get lost, and says the inn felt bigger afterwards.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin Solstice reaches [Innkeeper] Level 25 and obtains the [Skill - Inn's Aura].

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin feels her [Dangersense] tingle in the back of her head when Rags's Hobgoblin friend enters the inn, but she ignores it and makes herself smile, reminding herself that Goblins are people.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin tells Relc that the Goblin guests are under her protection and that he will be her enemy if he hurts them.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: While Erin stares Relc down, she feels pressure from a Skill-like force around her and the air in the inn feels solid, as if she were pushing down on the whole inn.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin orders the guardsman Relc to leave her inn because he cannot tolerate her Goblin guests, and tells him he may return later but not that night.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Klbkch backs Erin against Relc, telling him not to use his position as a guardsman, that Erin is within her rights, and that the [Innkeeper]'s word is law in the inn.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin says of Relc that he was the first person she met who did not try to kill her, and she feels awful about throwing him out.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin tells Ryoka that she thinks Lady Magnolia is on their side.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin strikes Ryoka with [Minotaur Punch] without meaning to, sending her flipping over a table, and apologises, calling it a Skill she should not have used.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin cooks crepes with [Advanced Cooking], having worked out pancakes earlier, and fries a stack in under twenty minutes.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin sings the doe-rei-mi song to Mrsha, who sways and relaxes in her lap.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin tells Ryoka she cannot buy anything from any Gnoll shopkeepers because of the Lyonette affair and has not spoken to Krshia since.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin mixes faerie flowers with alcohol into a drink that Halrac says brings back happy memories for a time, and she says it comes from her Skill [Wondrous Fare].

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin has [Advanced Cooking]; Selys says [Basic Cooking] is common among Liscor [Cooks] and [Innkeepers] but [Advanced Cooking] is rarer.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin has [Advanced Crafting], which she uses to plan snow-shoes for herself and Lyonette.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin builds a sledge about six feet long with skis on the bottom, a leather harness for Toren and reins, and rides it behind Toren with Lyonette.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin sledges down the hills outside Liscor with Toren hauling the sledge back up, and onlookers rush back into the city for sleds of their own, so she starts a trend.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin cooks the giant bees for the Antinium; her [Advanced Cooking] applies to them and she does not throw up.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin plays chess against her unseen opponent on the ghostly chessboard, who always answers within the hour.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin reaches [Innkeeper] Level 26.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin wakes on her sledge far from Liscor with no mountains in sight, with Toren gone and only a jar of dead bees, two jars of honey, a pillow, a blanket and a frying pan; a decapitated wolf lies nearby.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin is stranded in the northern snowfields and sings ad-lib songs about being lost because of her skeleton.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin scares an aggressive bear away with an accidental [Loud Voice] and a long scream, and Jerad Riels hears the scream and finds her.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin gives a gold coin to the guard Fuzzylips at Celum's gate, and says the Wandering Inn is partly a joke about her wandering.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin beats three muggers in an alley using [Minotaur Punch], a thumb broken back, and a dead bee thrown with [Unerring Throw]; she is stronger than usual with [Lesser Strength] but not stronger than the third man.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Calruz had taught Erin how to fight armed opponents, and she thinks of fighting Toren at his orders.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: The guard Fuzzylips notes that Erin has no combat classes except two levels in [Warrior].

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin forgives the boy Grev so that he is not whipped, warning that she will not forgive him again.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin reaches Celum alone, pushing her sledge into the city with her jars of honey and bees.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin asks Octavia whether mana potions make food or alcohol magical, and mentions faerie flowers in ale that cause hallucinations.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Ryoka sees Erin alive and chatting with Octavia in Teriarch's scrying image.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin entered Celum with a jar of bees and two jars of honey and offered them to the [Alchemist] Octavia in exchange for help with her own experiments.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin's Corusdeer horn soup uses cold carrots with gelatin, lots of wheat flour and washed Corusdeer horn, with thyme only for taste.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: The Corusdeer soup keeps Ryoka's stomach hot and her body warm, so she walks barefoot on frosted cobblestones.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin has [Advanced Cooking] and [Wondrous Fare], which she says works like [Advanced Cooking] and gives her a sense of how to make food magical, and her [Dangersense] stays quiet over the soup.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin refuses to give Octavia the soup recipe, saying it was not part of the deal for using the lab.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin thinks Toren abandoned her on purpose and says she may have to kill him, or ask Pisces to fix him if he is merely disobeying orders.

section: Book 2: Winter, Relc and the road to Celum (Ch2.19-2.40)
text: Erin cooks hamburgers and fries at the Wandering Inn and punches a man who calls himself one of the Brilliant Swords of Celum.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin bribes the Frost Faeries with a crepe so she and Ryoka can walk away while they fight over it.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin and Ryoka are banned from Celum's Adventurer's Guild, at least for a while, after Erin's "table flip attack".

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin makes Octavia sick with food poisoning by feeding her a dish that did not turn out well.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin and Octavia experiment with cooking and potions in Octavia's kitchen, where Erin has made a mana soup that Octavia says is a more edible mana potion.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin has been in Celum nearly a week, splitting her time between Agnes's inn, the Frenzied Hare, and Octavia's shop, Stitchworks, with Ryoka paying Octavia for her time.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin wants her inn to match higher-level innkeepers and to be unique by selling magical dishes nobody else can copy.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin's alchemical dishes work only when she stirs them with her Skill; Agnes failed to make the Corusdeer soup even when copying Erin exactly.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin creates a blue, thick soup with a skin-hardening effect, using Stonelizard scales, lemon juice and fish, and Octavia's long pin cannot easily pierce her arm after she eats it.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin has also made strength stew and Corusdeer soup, and says soup is easiest and she could make a stir-fry from the same ingredients.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin reaches [Innkeeper] Level 27.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin hires the Drake Jasi as a [Barmaid] at the Frenzied Hare and lets Jasi and Grev stay at the inn.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin doubts afterwards that hiring Jasi was a good choice, because Jasi is a Drake unpopular with the patrons and would have to start at Level 1.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin's crepes, French toast and bacon draw crowds at the Frenzied Hare, and other Celum inns copy her crepes.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin reflects that her hamburgers and music were hits in Liscor mainly because they were new.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin has [Unerring Throw]; Wesle identifies it when she throws a spoon past Grev's nose and says it is rare in an [Innkeeper].

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin is a Level 6 [Singer] with [Perfect Recall], which works on songs and, as she finds, on plays.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: As a child Erin wanted to be an astronaut, then a legendary chess player, then a chess commentator.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin says Ryoka told her a greenhouse could be built next to the inn without glass.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin tells Wesle and Jasi that back home even someone from a faraway village could go to Hollywood and become a celebrity.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin flips a table in anger when Wesle and Jasi do not know plays.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin reaches [Innkeeper] Level 29 and obtains [Skill - Crowd Control].

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin works the kitchen at the Frenzied Hare, making pizza; Agnes and four barmaids staff the inn.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin orders Pisces to cut Toren's supply of mana at once, because Toren killed people because he wanted to and would keep killing.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin grieves after cutting Toren off, regards him as someone who could think, and hopes he may not be dead.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin leads the actors of the Frenzied Hare in Frozen, with Ceria's snow and cold effects.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin asks for the enchanted door as a treasure and the Horns of Hammerad give it to her in return for her help and the gold she lent them.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin owns the door.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin realises that the teleportation stone and a second door could make a portal; Pisces and Ceria tune the stone, Ksmvr leaves it at the Frenzied Hare, and Erin steps through to cook for the wagon driver.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin makes popcorn with butter and salt.

section: Book 3: Celum, Octavia and the portal door (Ch3.03-3.25)
text: Erin leaves Celum on the Horns of Hammerad's wagon to return to Liscor, promising to see more of the world someday.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin remembers a house in Michigan and parents who cannot play chess well, and cooks biscuits and gravy before the others wake.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin wants baking powder, and pays Octavia three gold and eight silver for the experiments after Octavia pushes the price up from two gold.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin promised the Runner's Guild and the Mage's Guild that she would not use her door to carry letters or deliveries, and hinted to Celum that the Horns of Hammerad would be upset if the city took the door for emergencies.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin guesses that Teriarch is Ryoka's "mysterious client", though Ryoka never told her who he was, and Teriarch says he is a mage of significant ability.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin carries a bottle of "blue soup" made from Corusdeer horn that makes Ceria very hot despite her cold protection spells, and Erin expects it to be a huge hit because drinkers will not feel the cold.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin returns to the Wandering Inn through the door, carrying Mrsha, and Lyonette hugs her.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin finds her flower boxes unwatered and tells Lyonette it is her own fault for leaving; she then finds the inn clean and more organised than she left it.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin explains to Klbkch that Macbeth is a play, and offers to teach Olesm and Pawn how to play Go.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Later, Erin reaches [Innkeeper] Level 30, her class changes to [Magical Innkeeper], and she obtains [Skill - Inn: Magical Grounds] and [Skill - Inn: Field of Preservation].

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin tells the others that she is a Level 30 [Magical Innkeeper] whose inn holds a lot of mana, and Typhenous calls it a magical leyline created in her own inn.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin tells Klbkch that friends are made by giving time, trust or a helping hand, with no guarantee of return, and that she cares about strangers because they are people.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin asks the mages how many people the portal door could carry: Pisces estimates sixteen to thirty bodies a day, and Ceria says at least a hundred if every mage used mana potions.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin teaches a [Flautist] and others in Esthelm a version of the song Jingle Bells with a bell.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin rides back to Liscor with the merchant Termin, who asks to be treated to a meal, because a second Goblin army has burnt a town not fifty miles north.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin tells Lyonette and Krshia about Christmas, explaining presents, food and Santa Claus, and plans a party at which each person gives presents to two others.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin tells Krshia that part of Lyonette's pay will go to Krshia's shop.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin pays up front at the Mage's Guild to send Ryoka a message asking her to come back for Christmas and bring Reynold, to tell Magnolia she is a Scrooge, and noting that Ressa is cool.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: A warning like a ringing bell sounds in Erin's head when a Rock Crab attacks, and afterwards she insists that she and Mrsha never leave without seed cores.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin hits Brunkr with [Minotaur Punch] and beats him in a fight, then treats his infected arm with honey.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin tells Brunkr that on Earth there is no healing magic but medicine, and that honey has antibodies and fights infection.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin's cooking Skill signals when food is done like an egg timer in her head.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin asks Octavia to make matches from red phosphorus and sulfur after Ryoka's advice, and demands her magical soups back.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin writes down the idea of healing potion slimes, then finds the Frenzied Hare locked because Agnes is on holiday with her sick husband.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin realises she forgot a Christmas tree.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin's talk of Go sends Olesm off with ideas for his newsletter and Pawn planning to introduce it to the Antinium, and the Wandering Inn fills with visitors who come to play Go.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin assigns Christmas gift-givers in the day before Christmas, and presents pile up in a corner of the inn.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin burns the mistletoe and sings "Silent Night" to the sleeping Lyonette and Mrsha, then blows out the candle.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin cooks sour soup, Drake dumplings, Gnollish kebabs, hamburgers, pizza, popcorn, barbecued ribs, fries and fluffy bread for the Christmas party.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin sings "Jingle Bells" at the party and remembers home.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin breaks down in tears in front of the whole inn, missing her mother and father, and runs out into the snow.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin wakes late in the day on the night after Christmas to find her inn deserted.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin refuses all three gifts offered by three strange men, saying she is just an innkeeper who does not fight battles, and they leave a palm-sized white silvery coin that weighs almost nothing.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin puts the coin in Lyonette's small coin jar and later takes it out and keeps it in her pocket.

section: Book 4: Return to Liscor, Magical Innkeeper and Christmas (Ch3.30-Interlude)
text: Erin wakes to find that all the food in her kitchen is gone, the snow has stopped, and two moons are visible in the sky.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin is a Level 30 [Magical Innkeeper] and the sole proprietress of the Wandering Inn.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin hands out free samples of magical soups, her "defense soup", outside the Liscor Adventurer's Guild, and stabs a black-scaled Drake adventurer in the back and stomach to show that the knife cannot cut a drinker of the soup.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin tells the crowd that her soups last only about a week and that expired ones make people sick, while she keeps food fresh in her inn through a Skill; Mrsha vomited after drinking an expired soup.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin carries a large coin in her belt pouch, and tells Lyonette it is a secret she is trying to figure out herself.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin learns that the going rate for a Bark Potion is seventeen gold coins, and decides she cannot lie about her soups' side effects as Octavia would, even though she charges one gold.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin returns to Liscor with Griffon Hunt, the Halfseekers and the Horns of Hammerad behind her and throws frying pans at Ilvriss; the second one hits his head.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin and Ryoka reunite, Ryoka telling her "Hi Erin. I'm back."

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin says she has just obtained a new Skill when someone complains about raw meat left sitting out.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin and Ryoka cannot talk during the party, and Ryoka sleeps upstairs with Mrsha and Lyonette.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin tells Ryoka that she thinks Lyonette was literally starving while Erin was gone, visited only by Olesm.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin tells Ryoka that she killed Toren, after hearing that he attacked travelers on the road, by telling Pisces to cut his mana.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin tells Ryoka she helped run Agnes's inn, made odd food at Octavia's shop, helped start an acting troupe, and got a magical door; the troupe performs Othello at the Frenzied Hare.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin is angry that Agnes would not help Jasi, and Ryoka replies that Agnes is an ordinary person who will not stick her neck out for others.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin plans to hire help and to talk to Safry and Maran, both [Barmaids], and to ask Klbkch about building a third floor or a second wing because her rooms are sold out.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin says [Field of Preservation] is better than runes a [Mage] offered for her pantry for about forty gold, which would only preserve a shelf or two and not totally.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin wants to meet Laken and Durene, and wonders about hiring Garry.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin met Teriarch in his Human [Mage] form on the road, and taught him Angry Birds; she calls him weird but sort of nice.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin says she taught the troupe Romeo and Juliet first, then Pygmalion, Hamlet and Frozen, and is running out of plays.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin calls her skin-toughening soup "Defense Soup" and says Relc calls it Scale Soup.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin and Ryoka reconcile after their weeks apart and agree to meet again.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin's magical food gives only one effect at a time, wears off in hours, spoils quickly, and can only be made by someone with [Wondrous Fare]; she turns Corusdeer Soup into patties, and her Scale Soup patty contains a Stonelizard scale.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin shows Klbkch a blueprint for a bigger common room, a third floor, a longer second floor and a watchtower for Bird, which she names the Bird's Nest.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin offers Safry and Maran one silver and six copper coins per hour plus bonuses, and Safry says she could start tomorrow.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin speculates that Pisces could power the door with his own mana, so that she could use it to reach Invrisil.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Klbkch quotes Erin three hundred and twenty-eight gold coins to expand the inn, and Erin finds the figure a lot.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin hires the barmaids Safry and Maran, and also Selys's friend Drassi and Ishkr, a Gnoll whom Krshia introduced.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin advertises her magical cooking to the adventurers of Liscor, and cooks days of food in advance on Ryoka's suggestion.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin has [Advanced Crafting] and builds a prototype censer for Pawn from two spaghetti colanders, a basin, string, a coal and ground cinnamon.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin tells Pawn that she talked to Klbkch, and Pawn takes this to mean his Soldiers will not have to fight.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin scolds Maran and Safry in public for refusing to haul water, naming Lyonette as the source, so they glare at Lyonette; Ryoka thinks this was a mistake.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin returns from Celum with a mossy mold grown with mana potions after Octavia's work, which she means to try on Brunkr.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin uses [Crowd Control] by accident and silences the whole inn.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin rules that Lyonette is in charge of the staff, because Lyonette ran the inn while Erin was away, whatever the barmaids' levels.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin fires Safry and Maran, refuses to pay them for the day, and her [Inn's Aura] sends them fleeing into Octavia's shop with a crash of broken glass.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin states that she is a Level 30 [Magical Innkeeper] and refuses to pay Agnes, Maran or Safry or to apologise.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin tells Agnes, Ulia and Timbor to leave, naming Pisces, a [Necromancer] in her basement, and Bird, her security, and they flee through the Celum door.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin says she paid Maran and Safry more than Agnes did and fired them as lazy, cowardly jerks, and that she gave Agnes business by helping the [Actors].

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin resumes the ghostly chess game, moving her king in front of the knight, and her opponent answers grudgingly as if doubting it is her.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin wins the first game against her opponent in six minutes with a trap set about a month earlier, loses the next, and plays the London System.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin explains the Tennison Gambit from the Réti Opening to onlookers.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin plays chess all day and near midnight sends "I'm sorry", and receives the reply "I know. You are forgiven."

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin reaches [Magical Innkeeper] Level 31.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin asks Krshia for a collar and leash for a bee about to hatch, and Krshia mentions a cousin who breeds dogs.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Krshia finds Erin's odd coin ancient, smelling of buried earth, and a good steel knife cannot scratch it; Erin says she got it from a customer.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin takes a load of potions and alchemical items from Octavia for fifteen gold and asks her for a healing slime, over Octavia's protest.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin tells Brunkr she feels uneasy, as if something bad is coming from the northeast, so she is making preparations.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Krshia says Ryoka did her tribe a favor beyond worth, so she charges Erin only for the cost of the bow wood and transport, as friends.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin's newest "cool stuff" for her inn is a bowl of walnuts.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin has pre-cooked lasagna ready for the Gold-rank adventurers returning to the inn.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Lyonette tells Ryoka that she, Typhenous and Octavia helped Erin make a slime from a mana stone and an existing slime, as part of Erin's idea of a healing-potion slime.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin has put up a sign, buried in snow, against killing Goblins, and tells Ryoka it stays.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin and Ryoka fight physically after Ryoka says Erin is awfully good at killing, until Mrsha bites in and Lyonette douses both.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin and Ryoka reconcile after the fight; Ryoka apologises twice and Erin once.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: A Drake officer says Erin's Watch file would attract the attention of any Drake [Leader], listing an unauthorized inn and suspected Antinium ties.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin tests the healing slime on a cut, sees it is afraid when she chases it, and pours it out of the window into the snow.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin decides to send a lodestone to Pallass for Zel Shivertail before Invrisil, and hires the Courier Hawk to deliver it.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin plays chess against Imenet, who is narrated as Az'kerash, wins the first game with a different style, and the match draws Olesm, Typhenous, Pisces and Klbkch.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin feels numb grief and remembers her earlier losses: Klbkch's death, the Horns of Hammerad being pronounced dead, and killing the Goblin Chieftain.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin tells Pisces that Regrika and Imenet say they like her food but hated it, including last night's steak and casserole.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin concludes Brunkr was murdered, because he had promised her he would not enter the dungeon.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin serves Regrika and Imenet a steak made of ground bones, bones soaked in pig's blood and mana potions, marrow glue and strong poison from Octavia; both eat it and praise it.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin tells Regrika that she never mentioned Mrsha's white fur, which every Gnoll knows about, exposing her and Imenet.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Regrika attacks and kills Ulrien after Erin exposes her.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin punches Regrika again and again with [Minotaur Punch] until something crunches in her hands.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin reaches [Magical Innkeeper] Level 32 and obtains [Skill - Inn: Reinforced Structure]; her right hand is bandaged and she has been ordered not to use it.

section: Book 5: Soups, the Redfangs' enemies and chess (Ch4.07-4.31)
text: Erin tells Ryoka to leave and not come back for at least a day.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin tests the glass of her windows with a hammer and [Minotaur Punch] to stress-test her new [Reinforced Structure] Skill, and the window only cracks slightly.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin says anyone with more than twenty levels in a combat class could probably break the glass, and someone like Regrika could still put a hole in her walls.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin says luck saved everyone but Ulrien, that she cannot rely on luck again, and that Ryoka left some of her gold behind.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin throws a knife, a fire vial and Octavia's acid at Eater Goats attacking a village, and a [Minotaur Punch] sends one goat flying.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin bows to five Hobgoblins, thanks them for saving her, and later invites them to the inn for free food.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin asks the Redfang warriors whether they know a Goblin named Rags, and they cannot tell her where Rags is, whether she is well, or where they are going.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin names the five Hobs, Headscratcher, Shorthilt, Badarrow, Rabbiteater and Numbtongue, and shakes Headscratcher's hand when she offers them a place to stay.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin promises the Goblins that no one will kill them while she is there, and has them sleep in the basement; the Horns of Hammerad get second-floor rooms from her finished upgrade.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin tells her guests she believes Goblins are more than monsters because they act like people.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Octavia's door to Celum opened twice and people fled screaming at the sight of the Goblins, so word spreads to both cities.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin digs out and replants her buried sign, making "no killing Goblins" the Wandering Inn's one rule.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin believes that Rags is keeping her head down and being smart.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin welcomes Purple Smile and Yellow Splatters of the Antinium at her door and meets the Goblins and Soldiers with food and hot honey milk.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin tells Lyonette that the Goblins are lost and afraid, and that she wants to help them.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin buys a guitar she cannot play, partly because of the Goblins, who seem to think it is a weapon.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin commands the room to freeze, threatening to break the arm of anyone who moves, and stamps her foot to cause a localised tremor.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin holds Badarrow's hands, tells him she knew he was like her, and tells the Hobs that Mrsha's tribe was killed by Goblins and asks them to forgive her.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin thinks that looking into someone's eyes shows their soul, and that Goblins' shines.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin tells Mrsha that hating Goblins is not wrong, but hating all Goblins or these Goblins is not right either, because people are not the same.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin sings songs from home with the guitar, with Numbtongue on a bowl drum and Headscratcher as chorus; afterwards Numbtongue can sing and takes the guitar.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin uses [Loud Voice] to stop Ilvriss in the street and resists his command Skill, as she once resisted Magnolia's charmed voice.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: The dwarf Dawil tells Erin that the coin a guest gave her is pure mithril or close, and calls it priceless or worthless, since mithril suits alloys more than plate.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin pushes Faerie Flower ale, an ordinary ale with three drops of faerie flower nectar, onto Ilvriss.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin reaches [Magical Innkeeper] Level 33.

section: Book 6: Goblins at the Wandering Inn (Ch4.33-4.47)
text: Erin hosts a story night for the Antinium in the barracks of the Painted Soldiers, with popcorn, hot milk and honey, while Klbkch reads aloud.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin sleeps in her kitchen, waking at dawn from habit, and brushes her teeth with the simple local toothpaste.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin offers a guest a keg's worth of Firebreath Whiskey, which she says is nasty.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin makes pork belly sandwiches with mayonnaise and milkshakes for her guests, and her cooking Skill tells her pork belly needs preparation ahead.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin steps through the door to Pallass after Ilvriss and finds it has no mana left, stranding them until it recharges in about a day.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin floods the door's mana by hopping repeatedly between Liscor and Pallass, then throws a chair that hits two Pallassian senators.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin tells Lyonette that she acted like an idiot in Pallass on purpose, because pretending to be a dumb Human tourist makes angry people less angry, and then she could spring a surprise like a knight to F7.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin has [Alcohol Immunity] or something like it, and drinks milk instead.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin signs the forms that register her doorway as part of her inn, and the Pallass-Liscor crisis over the door ends.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin pays eighteen gold for the twenty-six gold fee for the inn's registration, with both Watch Captains adding four gold.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin and Lyonette have enough coin in the safe for about a week.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin's aura heats the air around her when she is angry.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin tells the Redfang Hobs they are guests, not prisoners, and that they can leave to find Rags if they wish.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin tells Lyonette she has two or three ideas for money, and proposes something to the Antinium Workers Anand and Belgrade.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin sets a deal with Octavia: two coppers per gold coin of Octavia's profits for Erin's ideas, plus free matches for herself; Erin calls the matches her and Ryoka's idea.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin hits on the idea of paying the Redfangs to guard the inn after Venim suggests paying the Halfseekers.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin says that no one can call the Goblins a threat if they are the ones who deal with threats.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin reaches [Magical Innkeeper] Level 34 and obtains [Skill - Inn: Grand Theatre], which makes the common room impossibly large, perhaps three times its size.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin makes a Classic American Breakfast with bread baked with the baking powder from Octavia, and glazed sausages.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin tells her guests that she tells the Hobs apart: Badarrow is bad-tempered and loves bows, and Headscratcher is the cool emotional leader whom the other Hobs listen to.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin calls Shorthilt a snob-Goblin about swords, and Numbtongue the only one who can really talk, with a good memory and probably both plays by heart.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin calls Rabbiteater a hard-working Hufflepuff with no defining feature, and says she herself was a Gryffindor.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin's [Field of Preservation] keeps food she cooked twelve days earlier ready to serve; only soufflés do not last.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin now serves wines from Liscor and Celum as well as ale, mead and whiskey, and calls them by colour.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin shows her guests [Grand Theatre], which she obtained two days earlier, turning her common room into a vast dark hall with a stage.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin shoves Lyonette, Mrsha and Drassi through the door to Octavia's shop during the attack, and stays to fight.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin punches a moth with [Minotaur Punch].

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin opens the door to Pallass to call for help, punches a purple-scaled Drake who doubts her, and drags the whole door across the room so Pallass can see the attack.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin stomps a moth to death.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin becomes a Level 35 [Magical Innkeeper] and gains no new Skills.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin tells Selys that nobody died at the inn, and that Moore and Seborn rushed Jelaqua into the city.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin serves enchiladas from [Field of Preservation] food to the Horns of Hammerad, and worries that dead moths in the preserved room attract unwanted things.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin plans to use her door to link Liscor, Pallass and Celum, and asks Pisces to look at the mana stones Typhenous ordered.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin serves stew to the Painted Soldiers, who eat on the floor of her inn.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin serves slices of vanilla cake decorated with smiling Goblins after a parade that left the Goblins unappreciated; Embria glares.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin pops popcorn in a pot with butter, shaking the pot to keep the kernels from burning.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin pays the Redfang Warriors their first wages, and says she once had an employee she never paid and is not repeating the mistake.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin pulls a ring from her finger and puts it on Headscratcher underwater so he can breathe water, and tells the Hobs to return it to Ksmvr.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the Grand Theatre and the moth attack (Ch5.00-5.15)
text: Erin tells the Redfang Hobs they should be adventurers, Goblin adventurers, as she once urged Selys.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin's [Grand Theatre] Skill is active at almost all times, and the Players of Celum put on multiple plays a day in the giant common room.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin arrives at the Antinium Hive with Klbkch and Anand and kneels beside Pawn, whom she sees is stuck.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin tells Pawn that she loves him like the son she does not plan on having, but that he cannot just sit there while his unit has stopped eating.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin says she knows Lyonette is a [Princess], though she cannot remember who told her, and that Ryoka definitely told her.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin prepares a Quillfish fillet after checking it with her [Dangersense], [Advanced Cooking] and Mrsha's sniff, coating it in flour and breadcrumbs.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin offers adventurers Earlia and Nailren a boat, an escort and a purchasable map to the dungeon, plus free samples of her magic food including Scale Soup.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin has Lyonette write a notice by the magic door offering 50 gold for credible information, under a [Detect Truth] spell, on sightings of the one-armed Minotaur Calruz.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin fights in the inn brawl with [Bar Fighting] and [Minotaur Punch], poking a man in the eyes and punching Ksmvr.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin's Scale Soup acts like a lesser [Barkskin] spell according to Moore, toughening Revi's stitch-flesh enough to resist cuts from an unenchanted dagger.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin and Lyonette suspect that Wall Lord Ilvriss cancelled Erin's aura during the riot with his own aura Skill, as [Lords] have aura Skills.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin rescues Earlia's team, Gemhammer and the Pride of Kelia, from Shield Spiders by dropping ropes from a large boat crewed by Goblins.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin tells Bird that she makes pretzels with cheese sauce for the Antinium, and that she has been practicing with her aura to prevent trouble at the play.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Bird says Erin pays him silver and bronze coins which he can save for a new bow.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin's boycott by the Drakes drags into its fifth day, with Drakes showing up every day to complain rather than avoid the inn.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin has fewer than fifty people in an inn she thinks could hold six or seven times that, and employs ten regular staff and has a contract with the Players of Celum.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin says she can suppress the Drakes' aggression with her aura by concentrating, so they only boo, at the cost of a low-level strain in her head.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin hugs the Redfang Warriors, who risked their lives testing the artifacts, and Headscratcher weeps.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin recasts the play with the Montagues as Drakes and the Capulets as Humans, Relc as Romeo and Lyonette as Juliet; the male Drakes then fight over the part, and she calls the objection sexist.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin yanks open the door to Pallass and shouts for help against the Raskghar attack on Liscor.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin tells the room that werewolves change at each full moon, spread their powers by biting, and are weakened by silver, though it is only a legend where she comes from.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin sells Corusdeer soup and a skin-toughening dish at a discount to adventurers; the dish is now called Scale Salad and tastes more palatable.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin recalls throwing a kitchen knife and a frying pan at the Raskghar to little effect, too afraid to use her aura.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin sketches a bear trap for Rabbiteater and Lyonette, neither of whom understands how it works.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin has [Reinforced Structure] and [Advanced Crafting], and plans to bar the door and shutter the windows herself.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin cancels the play for the night and says she was thinking of Golems, not Toren, for lasting defence.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin tries to stop the Redfangs from killing the captured Cave Goblin Pebblesnatch with her aura, but the text says it was not the aura that stopped them; her plea that they will regret it makes them stop, and she asks for ten minutes.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin plays chess with Headscratcher, opening with Bird's Opening and From's Gambit, and says she uses chess because it is the only thing she knows.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin teaches that life is not chess, spins the board to reverse the sides, and later proposes keeping Pebblesnatch as an ally.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin serves Gambler's Manicotti, a stuffed pasta with a tiny bit of spice in some pieces.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin has shutters built on the ground-floor windows with the Hobs, and learns that adding onto the inn does not trigger [Reinforced Structure]; Bird's tower door has a bar.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin tells Zevara she is keeping the captured Goblins in the basement, and Zevara warns that any Goblin stepping into Liscor will be killed.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin buys three bear traps, the only three in stock, and Numbtongue says they fail against Gargoyles and Eater Goats and only anger Carn Wolves.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin's [Dangersense] rings in her ear before the Raskghar attack; Lyonette says it may miss higher-level or stealthier enemies.

section: Book 8: The boycott, Pawn and the Raskghar (Ch5.24-5.38)
text: Erin realises that the Raskghar are still smart because it is still the full moon, and runs to sound the alarm.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin Solstice tells the Hobs that she knows there was a Plan G but that she is abandoning it because asking them to go into the dungeon is more important.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin storms into the shop of the [Blacksmith] Joiah Kellisman in Celum before opening hours and pushes him back to get inside, demanding to know if he is the best [Blacksmith] in Celum.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin says she would buy only from the best and says she could have gone to Pallass, but her door cannot handle the magic there.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin tells Joiah that Jelaqua needs two flails and that Jelaqua stays at her inn, and she puts a bag of gold on the counter to pay.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Joiah says he has no flails in the shop but could make a pair, and Erin leaves with a bundle of swords; she says next that they need a bow and arrows.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin gives Badarrow a recurve bow that she carries over her shoulder and tells the Redfang Hobs to check the swords she got from the best [Blacksmith] in Celum.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Five Redfang Hobs draw new steel swords; Shorthilt tears up and exchanges his own worn sword for his new one, and the Hobs hug Erin.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin tells the Hobs the swords are her investment and her fee, and asks them as adventurers and as Goblins to find Mrsha and Ceria in the dungeon, since the Raskghar have both.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin amends Plan G so that the Hobs find Mrsha and Ceria first, and she asks them to try not to kill Calruz if they find the camp, while doing what they have to.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin gives the Hobs a crate of Octavia's best healing potions, two for each, along with stamina potions and a Tripvine bag, saying that is all she can afford.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin tells the Hobs to avoid fights if they can, and not to die, and Numbtongue speaks for the Hobs in agreeing to go.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin knocks out a Cave Goblin who lunges at her with a rusty knife, and she is about to throw a [Minotaur Punch] at Pebblesnatch before she sees that Pebblesnatch is offering her a potato.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin realises she has not eaten for at least nine hours and that hunger, tiredness, stress and fear are behind her anger.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin kneels, tells Pebblesnatch she will not hit her, and asks the little Goblin to make a fire, which Pebblesnatch does with flint.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin warns the Cave Goblins that she will hit anyone who tries to stab her and will feed anyone who does not.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin fries potato slices for the Cave Goblins, flicks hot oil at two Goblins who rush her, and tells them never to mess with a chef and hot oil.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin tells the Cave Goblins that she cannot save Mrsha or Ceria or fight the Raskghar, but can feed them, and she starts teaching them to cook a stir-fry.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: The Cave Goblins judge Erin strong, a leader, and begin to follow and watch her cook, perhaps trusting her.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin calls Halrac, Jelaqua and the other adventurers over to the door, and holds up a hand to slow the adventurers with her aura when the Cave Goblins try to flee.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin promises a little Cave Goblin that no one will hurt her if she does not try to hurt them, and the Goblin takes Erin's hand.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin waits awake at night with Lyonette, Apista, Pawn and a group of Painted Soldiers, watching her magic door, which has a white mana stone fixed to it.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin wakes after sleeping in her kitchen to learn that the Gold-rank adventurers have no workable plan to reach the Raskghar.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin thinks that the plan the adventurers made, based on a map of the Raskghar camp drawn by the Cave Goblins, was a good one but that it failed.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin tells Lyonette she is going to talk to the Goblins, because they have to be able to help.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin resumes the chess game with her mysterious opponent, which she had stopped when Mrsha was kidnapped, and plays both sides, moving a pawn and then Knight to F6.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin hears Pisces propose to flood the Raskghar camp through her door and calls it going "Noah's Ark" on them.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin tells Pisces that his plan has too many moving parts, while hers has only one, trust, and she says she knows people and chess.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin tells Pisces to find every Gold-rank he can and stop them entering the dungeon, and says she needs Zevara, Ilvriss and Embria, with Olesm and Venim optional.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin tells Pebblesnatch that she is the only one who can do a task, and that her name was part of how Erin came up with her plan.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin hands Pebblesnatch something from her pocket and tells her to do exactly what she says; Numbtongue understands and approves.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin pushes her way onto the Liscor ramparts despite martial law, pushes Embria's spearhead aside, and tells Relc and Embria that she has a plan and needs Zevara and Klbkch at her inn.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin shouts at Ilvriss's window that she has a plan about the Gnolls, and calls herself the craziest Human he knows, and challenges him to say she cannot save Mrsha, Ceria and the Gnolls.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Erin uses her door with purple, dark brown and black mana stones to open it onto three different sides of the Raskghar camp, sending the Drakes of the 4th Company, Zevara, Ilvriss and then the Antinium through; she notes that the three metal sheets at the entrances were Pebblesnatch's doing.

section: The rescue of Mrsha and Ceria (Book 8)
text: Later, Erin reaches Level 36 as a [Magical Innkeeper] and obtains the Skill [Natural Allies: Goblins] and [Inn - Local Landmark: Liscor].

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin cooks a large spread of hot dishes for Mrsha's first morning back, including goose-egg poached eggs, bacon, pancakes, buns, sausages, spicy Yellets and a fish congee.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin orders from a Celum [Carpenter] a solid one-piece wooden club, six of them within two hours, plus an oversized one and one with a custom grip, and then goes looking for a tanner or leatherworker.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin leads the adventurers north of Celum, about a ten-minute walk, to a wild meadow, where she and Yvlon build a door frame with a wooden backing from boards and open her door onto the inn.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin has the bats and pocket-shaped leather gloves made quickly and at great cost, and she calls the objects "bats" and "gloves".

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin organises a game of baseball outside with hot dogs, popcorn and sausages, because hot dogs are not made in Liscor, and gives Moore an oversized bat that is more of a log.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin says she never liked baseball much back home, since her father took her to a few games but watched only the big ones.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin says the Players are good enough to play her father's neighbourhood team, and later says she still likes chess better.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin tells Ceria that she is "really good at killing people" and that she knew she could find a way to kill the Raskghar, and that she would do it again but does not like it.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin says she feels bad for the Antinium Soldiers, the Watch and Ilvriss's people who died because she asked them to, and she calls the Raskghar monsters who were also people with a home.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin claims that there is a rule making a ball hit beyond a fence a home run and that bases cannot be stolen forever, though she admits she could be wrong.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin proposes a baseball championship with two teams of the best eighteen players, a pitch with bases twice as far apart, and cake and ice cream as the prize.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin has become a minor celebrity in Liscor, and people come up to thank her in the street.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Two young female Gnolls thank Erin for the Raskghar's defeat, say they heard she persuaded the Goblins to betray the Raskghar, and say they had heard she was just a troublemaker called "that crazy Human".

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin says that the Redfangs run the Cave Goblins and teach them things such as fishing, and she buys a great deal of food from Krshia for them, laying gold coins on the table.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
