text: Krshia remarks that [Local Landmark] is a trait buildings can acquire, but says it is the first time she has known someone to have it.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin says that her inn is putting on The Hubris of the Raskghar every night and that The Glass Menagerie will probably be next, because she is running out of plays to give the actors.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin declines a share of the dungeon treasure, saying she was paid and did not fight in the dungeon.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin whispers "Hufflepuff takes the lead" as she watches the Hobs indignant at the Cave Goblins choosing Rabbiteater as their hero.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: The Garuda Bevussa thinks Erin is probably the best [Innkeeper] around Liscor but finds her knowledge of alcohol distressing; Erin asks whether wine goes in kegs.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin uses the Skill [Field of Preservation] on her prepared breakfasts, which depends on whether the food will need reheating.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin keeps mana stones in a wooden bowl by her magic door, where red opens the Redfang cave, green Liscor and blue Celum.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin has the Skill [Immunity: Alcohol] and does not drink, saying she could disable it but fruit juice tastes better.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin has bought Pebblesnatch a chef's hat and apron and finds her stirring a pot at the stove.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin finds the tower of her inn broken off, with the stairs ending in sky, and runs after the Hobs carrying the wounded Bird, pressing the Liscor mana stone to her door.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Olesm tells Erin that as the [Strategist] of Liscor he is confiscating her door under military law and arresting the Redfang Goblins.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin tries to stop the arrest of the Hobs, punching Olesm and kicking him, then using [Minotaur Punch] on a Gnoll [Guardsman] and a female Drake.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Relc blocks two of Erin's [Minotaur Punch] attacks, taps her forehead, knocks her down, and arrests her.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin goes to jail with the Redfang Warriors, and finds Calruz held behind a rune barrier in the furthest cell.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin tells Headscratcher that what other people do is not his fault, only what he does; she later says she wants time to stop so that things stay the same forever.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin sits in her cell, trades her sausage to Headscratcher for his cheese and crackers, and learns that no one has remembered her because of an incident with the magic door.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin spends a night in jail during which she gets the other prisoners to sing, and then mocks Olesm by saying that prison has changed her and she cannot go back.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin refuses to deal with the Goblins unless Zevara and Ilvriss return the Redfangs' gear and release them, threatening to go back to jail instead.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin tells the Drakes that if they refuse, Numbtongue will stay put and will probably join the Goblin Lord once he arrives.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin tells the Hobs she will send a magic doorway with them so they can keep staying at her inn, and says "I'm not leaving. Not yet."

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Garen punches Erin in the jaw, breaking her teeth, and kicks her in the chest.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Pisces cannot fix Erin's broken teeth without more material and does not use a healing potion until they are mended; he offers to cap them with bear teeth.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin has the Skill [Lesser Endurance], which lets her keep going, and wears caps that Pisces made over three of her partly broken teeth.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin sleeps in her kitchen and tells Lyonette that changing rooms is more work than she wants.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin senses that the Goblins are coming and stands on the ruined roof of her inn where Bird's watchtower was to see them.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin makes the wolf Thunderfur sit with her aura, and tells the Goblins that no fighting, no attacking, no bad names and no wolves relieving themselves in her inn is the condition for staying.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Later, Erin reaches Level 37 as a [Magical Innkeeper].

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin hugs Garry on his visit, calling him her favorite Worker, and says she was never much of a cook at home, mostly microwaving food and boiling water.

section: Aftermath, baseball and the Goblin Lord's approach (Book 9)
text: Erin says she has been trying to make ramen without knowing its ingredients, and she is also working on pumpkin pie and on recreating the turducken for Relc.

section: The Goblin Lord's army and the siege (Book 9)
text: Erin tells Garry that she is an [Innkeeper] whose Skills are not focused on cooking, and that she may not be that good a cook, having realised she never was one back home.

section: The Goblin Lord's army and the siege (Book 9)
text: Erin decides that the fight with the Goblin Lord's army cannot go down like this, says "Someone has to try", and fetches a bed sheet to make a white flag.

section: The Goblin Lord's army and the siege (Book 9)
text: Erin wakes on the thirteenth day to her [Dangersense], makes waffles with the last of the Ashfire Bee honey for Lyonette, Mrsha and the adventurers, and says she will lock up after breakfast.

section: The Goblin Lord's army and the siege (Book 9)
text: Erin walks out waving the bed-sheet flag and uses her [Loud Voice] Skill to shout for peace, a truce and a parley at the Goblin Lord's army, while the Humans under Tyrion Veltras watch.

section: The Goblin Lord's army and the siege (Book 9)
text: Erin asks the five Redfang Hobs for a big favour, saying Liscor is her home and its people her friends, and she asks them to help her stop the Goblin Lord and Tyrion Veltras.

section: The Goblin Lord's army and the siege (Book 9)
text: Headscratcher raises his axe in answer on the hilltop and the Goblins roar a single answer, "Yes."

section: The Goblin Lord's army and the siege (Book 9)
text: Erin fights a blinded Hobgoblin with a pepper potion, [Minotaur Punch] and a knife, and kills him, the second Goblin she has killed.

section: The Goblin Lord's army and the siege (Book 9)
text: Erin tells the dying Goblin Lord Reiss that perhaps the Goblins and she are characters in a game, or that this is all a dream.

section: The Goblin Lord's army and the siege (Book 9)
text: Erin lets Reiss's killers have his head but keeps his body, buries him amid the dead where a spell had blown away the dirt, and buries others she finds, sending away those who offer help.

section: The Goblin Lord's army and the siege (Book 9)
text: Erin hears a system message that a Warrior-to-General class change is available and General Level 6 with Skills; she shouts "Shut up!" and the Level Ups are cancelled.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin lies curled up in her room crying and silent for six days after the siege of Liscor, and Octavia and Lyonette cannot reach her.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Lyonette says that Erin barely eats, and only because Mrsha stopped eating when she did.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin walks into Liscor crying openly and refuses Zevara's and Ilvriss's attempts to send her back to her inn, because of what Numbtongue said about hiding her tears.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin hugs Pawn, saying she is sorry and thanking him, and then hugs Halrac, asking why they died; Revi and Krshia also embrace her.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin thinks of herself as twenty and nearly twenty-one, and feels that she asked the Goblins to fight and die for her without counting the cost.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin trusts four people above all others, Lyonette, Mrsha, Numbtongue and Bird, and she excludes even Ceria, Klbkch, Pawn and Ryoka from that group.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin feels that her inn has become too small for her and cannot stay in it, though she still has an [Immortal Moment] in her memory.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin tells Numbtongue, Lyonette and Mrsha that they are more than guests and friends and are family, and that the inn is as much theirs as hers.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin tells Numbtongue, Lyonette and Mrsha that she comes from another world called Earth, where she has a home and parents, and that she wants to go back one day.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin describes Earth to them as having no monsters or other races, paved ground, tall buildings, cars, planes, the internet, and gas used for engines.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin tells them that Goblins exist on Earth only in stories, and that wars there are worse than in this world, with weapons that can kill a million people at once and guns, tanks and machine guns.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin tells them that Ryoka is also from Earth, that Ryoka thinks they should hide who they are, that a BlackMage wants them to gather in Wistram, and that someone is hunting them.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin says she no longer knows whether she agrees with Ryoka about hiding knowledge from Earth, since it might change the world, but she cannot remember how to make anything and says she was just a chess player.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin decides to go to Pallass alone, having avoided her old regulars in Liscor since the battle; she had not spoken to Olesm and was unsure what to say to Relc, who killed Garen Redfang.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin's door cannot carry more than two or three people through before it needs to be recharged.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin feels at that time that she cannot forgive Liscor or Pallass for doing nothing, and hates Zevara, Olesm, Selys and Krshia for it.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Venim tells Erin that if a Goblin enters Pallass the city will kill it as standing Pallassian law, and Erin replies that she will kick his butt if he ever hurts Numbtongue.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Lasica says the Protectorate will not get away this time and asks Erin to come with her and Rufelt to muster troops, and Erin falls into step behind her.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin leaves with two pages of blotched notes from Rufelt and Lasica, and later tells the [Mages] in the room to work out, possibly drunk from having turned off her alcohol immunity.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Rufelt invites Erin to come to Tails and Scales whenever she wishes to leave her inn, with no concern for debts or payment.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin resumes her plays and holds auditions for a new crew of [Actors], and Ilvriss says the quality of acting has dropped.

section: Grief and the decision to leave (Book 10)
text: Erin goes to Pallass on a holiday because her kitchen knife has dulled, changing the door and calling out to Ishkr to tell Lyonette.
Erin does cartwheels with Mrsha, saying she learned them in gym class.
Erin is on break while Lyonette manages the inn, though she still cooks, helps with some tasks, visits Pallass, walks around Celum and plays with Mrsha.

Erin offers to trade her [Alcohol Immunity], [Lesser Endurance] and [Quick Recovery] Skills for Lyonette's [Flawless Attempt], and Lyonette says she would trade for Erin's [Wondrous Fare] Skill alone.
Erin has the [Field of Preservation] Skill, which she expects will keep the inn's orchard fruit through the year.
Erin realises that Rags' tribe must have eaten the blue fruits all the time.
Erin starts selling blue fruit juice, telling Pisces it costs six copper coins per cup.
When Mrsha calls her "Mom" in play, Erin stops and her face goes blank for a moment, and Lyonette notes it.
Erin offers to write down good Go games for Olesm and has a Go board made, and she checks her magical chessboard, which shows no new move from her opponent until a pawn moves experimentally.
Erin watches the culling with a glass of lemonade, sipping through a wooden straw, while Lyonette brings a pitcher.
After Selys tells her that Olesm and Lism's supporters have brawled and turned the momentum against Krshia, Erin says "Oh, it is on."
Erin now sleeps in the first room by the stairs on the second floor of her inn, and her bed in the kitchen is gone.
Erin keeps fish fresh from the rainy season with her [Field of Preservation] Skill and cooks one for Numbtongue's breakfast.
Erin carries a plain, very sharp steel kitchen knife that Maughin gave her after the competition with Pelt, and it cuts through a fish with barely any pressure.
Erin leaves the Market Street debate with Maughin and Grimalkin at her side, and the whole crowd leaves Lism's platform to follow her.

Erin carries her magic door with Relc and Grimalkin up through Pallass, ignoring Guardsman Kel's orders to put it down, to the ninth floor so that Liscor's Gnolls and Drakes can see the forges through it.
Erin sells pizza slices through her door to Pallass at one silver each, and ice cream at four silver a bowl through Lyonette, while Liscor's side laughs that they have eaten pizza for months.
Erin halts a panic in the Pallass crowd with a shout, using [Crowd Control] and telling Venim not to let them run.
Erin tells Krshia, Rufelt and Lasica that Krshia would get Gnoll support in Pallass and Pallass would gain allies in Liscor, and describes her scheme as playing two chess boards at once.
Lasica says she is for the plan and offers to discuss it with Krshia, including the Unitail [Senators].
Later, Erin reaches Level 38 as a [Magical Innkeeper] and obtains the Skill [Inn: Partial Reconstruction].
Erin invites Numbtongue to a dinner with Lyonette and Mrsha on the repaired third floor, and does not believe his answer that he is just going out.
Erin coins the word "nobble" for eating, unaware that it is already slang.
Erin tells Lyonette to give the ice cream meant for Pallass, worth six gold, to the Painted Soldiers, because Numbtongue has made a friend.
Erin is considering selling the Antinium alcohol Rxlvn, which Yellow Splatters says is potent and technically a poison.
Erin brings Relc, Grimalkin, Maughin, Jelaqua, Keldrass and Senator Errif to Celum against the gang that threatened Octavia, and tells Celum's [Mayor] "I am the consequences".
Erin's Skill [Partial Reconstruction] rebuilds broken items, such as a chair, within seconds, and she says she can do about three tables, ten roof tiles and five chairs at once before it stops.
Erin names a price of two hundred and twenty gold pieces for a Faerie Flower and Xif accepts at once.
Chaldion beats Erin at chess with his Skill [Path to Victory], the first time anyone in this world has beaten her face to face, and she tells him all she can do is poison his cookies.
Erin plays Go with Chaldion, who has won three games out of eight, and then, seeing a hot tub, proposes building hot tubs for the inn.
Erin shouts at Krshia on her platform to let Calruz live, and refuses to help unless Zevara decides his fate by law, threatening to slam the door to Pallass.
Erin tells Raekea and Calruz that torturing Calruz would make people no better than the Raskghar, and that Calruz would be a coward to run away from repaying his debts.
Erin asks her inn to protect Mrsha and the Goblins on her next level up, and then reaches Level 39 as a [Magical Innkeeper] in her sleep with no result, saying she wants Level 40 next.

section: The election's end and the Council (Book 13)
text: Erin shouts "We won!" with her [Loud Voice] over Councilwoman Yalla's order to disperse, and Gnolls and Drakes laugh as she tosses Mrsha and does cartwheels.

section: The election's end and the Council (Book 13)
text: Erin turns off her [Immunity: Alcohol] Skill to feel the drink after ordering a Firebreath Whiskey.

section: The election's end and the Council (Book 13)
text: Geillsten tells Erin that the Council has made her inn and her de facto inhabitants of Liscor with the rights of a citizen.

section: The election's end and the Council (Book 13)
text: Geillsten offers a tax discount if Erin aids the [Negotiator] sent to Esthelm, with citizenship for Lyonette and Mrsha and a provisional entry permit for Numbtongue.

section: The election's end and the Council (Book 13)
text: Erin pays the Council's tax in gold the next morning, claiming discounts including one for the Esthelm talks, after the Council argues that the City Watch helped her inn repeatedly.

section: The election's end and the Council (Book 13)
text: Erin's latest invention is the hard-batter ice cream cone.

section: The election's end and the Council (Book 13)
text: Erin has her hair cut by a Gnoll [Barber], and says she signed a deal in Esthelm under which Liscor gets ore and visitors.

section: The election's end and the Council (Book 13)
text: Erin reacts with a pale face to the name Canada on a [Reporter]'s article, pretends it is only a weird name, and asks whether people can send [Messages] to the author.

section: The election's end and the Council (Book 13)
text: Erin stages a fake-blood scare with sauce on her face for Mrsha, who rates it six out of ten.

section: The election's end and the Council (Book 13)
text: Erin tells Rufelt that she created a haunted house because Temile wanted more plays and she has run out of new foods, and that she is avoiding magical foods to keep life calm.

section: The election's end and the Council (Book 13)
text: Erin sells carrot cake for eight silver with frosting four more, says the ingredients cost four to six silver, and accepts an order with a name iced on it.

section: Haunted house, Wistram's mages and the golden flowers (Books 13-14)
text: Erin says that she is not into dating, that she had a boyfriend once back home, and Lyonette, Relc, Ceria, Drassi and Ishkr all turn to look at her.

section: Haunted house, Wistram's mages and the golden flowers (Books 13-14)
text: Erin tells an abbreviated version of a Dr. Seuss story with a message of environmental awareness; some Gnolls nod solemnly, while a Drake in the crowd says to replant the trees.

section: Haunted house, Wistram's mages and the golden flowers (Books 13-14)
text: Erin wants the door to Invrisil because she wants to find Ryoka, who she thinks should come back even if she brings danger.

section: Haunted house, Wistram's mages and the golden flowers (Books 13-14)
text: Erin joins Ceria in doubting that Selys's shopping trip with Pisces is a date, and Drassi then asks her about her boyfriend.

section: Haunted house, Wistram's mages and the golden flowers (Books 13-14)
text: Erin makes a curry with rice obtained through Lasica and Rufelt, using her [Advanced Cooking] Skill to tell her which spices are essential.

section: Haunted house, Wistram's mages and the golden flowers (Books 13-14)
text: Erin asks Montressa whether there are more people from Earth in Wistram and is told about Aaron and the others, but Montressa says Erin called the Gnoll, the staff and the Goblin her family.

section: Haunted house, Wistram's mages and the golden flowers (Books 13-14)
text: Erin asks the Wistram [Mages] whether they know Ceria, Pisces, Yvlon or Ksmvr, says Mrsha smells their blood on them, and slams Isceil's face into his plate of curry.

section: Haunted house, Wistram's mages and the golden flowers (Books 13-14)
text: Erin dumps the curry pot over Isceil, hits Beza with the pot, and later strikes Beza with two [Minotaur Punch] attacks, which Beza dismisses as an imitation and asks who taught her.

section: Haunted house, Wistram's mages and the golden flowers (Books 13-14)
text: Erin says she is unwilling to give Grimalkin too many ideas from home, such as monkey bars and burpees, and plans to thank Seborn and Moore for getting hurt for her, and is banned from the Liscor playground.

section: Haunted house, Wistram's mages and the golden flowers (Books 13-14)
text: Erin shouts at Palt when he stares at the yellow flowers in her window boxes, accuses him of being a stoner, and says that the flowers are dangerous and that one bulb costs two thousand gold pieces.

section: Haunted house, Wistram's mages and the golden flowers (Books 13-14)
text: Erin throws down her basket and punches a laughing adventurer, and the all-male [Warrior] team of the Ensoldier Shields is banned from her inn after their encounter with her.

section: Haunted house, Wistram's mages and the golden flowers (Books 13-14)
text: Erin tells Palt she changed her mind and asks him to talk to his faction, saying she cannot give guns but could work with the Ullsinoi faction if Montressa is called off; Palt promises an answer within two days.

section: Haunted house, Wistram's mages and the golden flowers (Books 13-14)
text: Erin serves saffron rice with eggs and sausage for breakfast, which Ksmvr loves.
Erin falls to her knees at the loudest [Dangersense] she has ever felt, louder than the Face-Eater Moths, shouts at everyone to run, and says it is worse than Skinner.
Erin turns her door to Pallass and sends Drassi through to tell Grimalkin that something is coming, and Kel believes her and orders Venim to be told and the alarm sounded.
Erin turns her door through all its destinations in search of a clue and opens it on the Bloodfields, and Gnolls and Drakes pour in, followed by the Crelers.

Erin focuses her [Inn's Aura] to slow the Crelers while the Antinium strike up from the basement, shakes uncontrollably, and collapses after forty minutes with a burst blood vessel in her nose and eye.

Erin finds the inn wrecked after the Crelers, with her [Grand Theater] Skill no longer working, and her [Partial Reconstruction] can rebuild a chair and table but not the broken floor or sagging ceiling.
Erin imagines a message announcing [Magical Innkeeper Level 40], an [Awesome Innkeeper] class and the Skills [Inn: Unlimited Mana Pool] and [Kamehameha Punch], and then hears nothing.
Erin fights Toren in the wrecked inn with [Minotaur Punch], Pelt's kitchen knife and her fists, and asks him why he killed them.
Erin throws acid jars at Toren, whose bones then regenerate, and she fights on with [Minotaur Punch] and a Relc kick.
Erin's golden ring glows with the letters Salazs, Toren rips it off, and she gets it back and puts it in her pocket.
Erin tells Toren that he is her mistake and that the dead of Esthelm and Numbtongue's friends are all because of him.
Toren strangles Erin, who loses her voice when she tries to use [Loud Voice], until she stops moving; she then inhales with a gasp.
The inn collapses around Erin, who is found kneeling under a beam that caught the weight, weeping.
Later, Erin reaches Level 40 as a [Magical Innkeeper] and obtains the Skills [Inn: Garden of Sanctuary] and [Like Fire, Memory].
Erin tells herself it is time to go back and do things better, forms a small flame with a blue core in her palm, blows it out, and senses home to the north.
Erin camps by a stream with a tent, a fishing rod and a small magic bag, and says she hunted and missed most of the time.
Erin is a [Magical Innkeeper] from Michigan and owner of The Wandering Inn, and she is a myth and legend in Liscor.
Erin uses an Octavia potion to cut down on menstrual cramps and bleeding, and considers it enough reason alone to have come to another world.
Erin has the Skills [Lesser Strength] and [Unerring Aim], but she cannot hit fast rabbits with thrown rocks.
Erin's Skill [Like Fire, Memory] needs a vivid memory to work, and a memory of Toren makes a blue flame with a sapphire core that gives her no heat.
Erin returns a knife to Pelt and apologises; Pelt calls it flawed because of a tiny crack, which Maughin says he removed.
In Pelt's forge, Erin's blue flame grows large from her grief and guilt, and Emessa weeps, as do Maughin and his apprentice Flintel in the forge across, because the flame carries emotion.
Pelt says that the blue flame is cold, and Erin tosses it into his forge, where it turns the flames blue.
Erin realises that the flame is her memory burning, that others feel her emotion in it, and that it lets people see her grief.
Pallass's City Watch arrests Erin for mass mental alteration through her Skill.

Erin is held in Pallass's Watch house on charges of using a mass-effect Skill in public, resisting arrest, public disturbance, nuisance and disruption of industry, with more than four hundred complaints.

Saliss finds that Erin's blue flame sticks to wood, is cold, gives off an emotional aura, can be smothered by stomping, freezes the water used on it, and goes out when poured over with a clear bottle of liquid.
Erin remembers a happy day in the inn and makes a small purple flame fading to pink, which Saliss takes on a torch and runs off with.

section: The Wyvern attack on Pallass and the world's gaze (Book 15)
text: Erin shelters in a stranger's apartment in Pallass with Rufelt and Lasica during the Wyvern attack, armed with two healing potions, a frying pan and Pelt's knife, and shouts at passers-by to go indoors.

section: The Wyvern attack on Pallass and the world's gaze (Book 15)
text: Erin pushes Rufelt and Lasica out of the apartment as a smoking Wyvern collapses the ceiling, and leads them up the stairs to the 5th Floor, where they run to Tails and Scales.

section: The Wyvern attack on Pallass and the world's gaze (Book 15)
text: Erin throws a spare kitchen knife at a Wyvern's eye, which glances off, and then throws Pelt's knife into its neck.

section: The Wyvern attack on Pallass and the world's gaze (Book 15)
text: A Gnoll uses a scroll of [Improved Featherfall] on the diving Wyvern and tells Erin to run inside, and Rufelt bars the door of the enchanted bar behind them.

section: The Wyvern attack on Pallass and the world's gaze (Book 15)
text: Erin asks Rufelt which of his spirits are flammable and has molotov cocktails made from spirits and cooking oil, which she throws until the Wyvern retreats; she says they make Wyverns angry rather than hurt them.

section: The Wyvern attack on Pallass and the world's gaze (Book 15)
text: Erin is seen on the scrying mirrors of the world as she runs to Bird, who sits on a dead Wyvern, and argues with General Duln, Chaldion and Grimalkin that Bird does not know any better.

section: The Wyvern attack on Pallass and the world's gaze (Book 15)
text: Flos Reimarch asks Gazi whether Erin is the girl who poked out her eye, and Gazi says she is and that she comes from another world.

section: The Wyvern attack on Pallass and the world's gaze (Book 15)
text: Niers recognises Erin's name, Az'kerash calls her the chess player, and Venitra says she knows her; Magnolia Reinhart sprays tea at the mirror.

section: The Wyvern attack on Pallass and the world's gaze (Book 15)
text: The mages of Wistram note that Erin said "oh my god", and the Blighted King's [Chronomancer] suspects that the word relates to the summoning spell.

section: The Wyvern attack on Pallass and the world's gaze (Book 15)
text: The Antinium queens watch Erin protect Bird, and Luciva demands to know who the Human is.
A speaker says Erin hates ale and does not drink, and the narration says her idea of bartending is Drassi filling mugs.
Erin comes home to her inn after the war with Pallass is called off.
Erin uses a new aura effect to weigh the room down and quiet Bird, and is fatigued afterwards.
Erin tries her new Skill [Garden of Sanctuary] in the common room, the private dining room, the hallway and upstairs, and nothing happens, though she says she can now make magical fire.
Erin places black Go stones across the board to spell "who r u?" for her unseen opponent.
Erin drinks apple juice at the party for her return, has [Immunity: Alcohol] until she turns it off, and uses her [Partial Restoration] Skill to fix Relc's mug.
Erin's opponent replies "yes" and the board resets for a new game, and Erin proposes six-way chess, Shogi and Tafl by spelling out messages.
Erin paces by her magic door at night, saying that she has had a feeling about it since her holiday, and turns the dial to the setting of the red stone for the Cave Goblin cave without result.
Erin wishes Pebblesnatch safe, and finds she does not feel the hollow pain she expected.
Erin promises Palt plays from Celum and basic information about Earth, and worries about what she can safely give away.
Erin bakes a big vanilla cake with colored frosting making an image of the inn, using baking powder and food dyes from Octavia.
Erin senses where Palt, Montressa and Grimalkin are while they are invisible, then senses that Mrsha is in her inn, saying she could not have done this at Level 20.

Erin finds that her Garden of Sanctuary holds stone statues of her dead, including Brunkr eating cake, a circle of the chess-club Antinium, Zel Shivertail and a group of the Horns of Hammerad with two gaps, and understands the garden as a reflection of her guilt and memory.
Erin is Level 40, and her aura, which Lyonette says lacks finesse, slows two [Pirates] and then weighs them down.
Erin turns on her [Immunity: Alcohol] to keep up with Wailant.
Erin recognises a cacao tree in the garden and shouts "Chocolate."
Erin declares "Let's make chocolate" the next morning, admits she knows how only from shows about it, and relies on her [Advanced Cooking] Skill.
Erin assumes cacao is a bean to be squished and melted, cuts open the pod with her Pelt-made knife, and finds white fruit around the seeds.
Erin's [Field of Preservation] stops the pods from fermenting, so Lasica takes over by hiring a Gnoll [Fermenter] in Liscor.
Erin says she never cooked before coming to this world because food on Earth is often premade.
Erin has been banned from Liscor's playgrounds after rallying the children in a day-long siege against the adults.
Erin uses an inn-sense, like a seventh sense, to locate people in the garden.
Erin tells Lyonette she likes Saliss and wants to be best friends with him.
Erin counts out six hundred gold in stacks of twenty-five to Wailant at the Strongheart farmhouse, and Viceria signs and returns the contract, which Erin tucks in her belt.
Erin says she took the gold from the Halfseekers, as Seborn said they owed it to Numbtongue, and sends Maughin a chocolate cake with a jam heart to give Jelaqua.
Erin shows Mrsha an emergency stash in the arid part of the Garden under an acacia, holding an invisibility potion, a speed potion, healing potions and explosive tripvine bags.
Erin plays Go and chess against her mysterious opponent on two magical boards, and judges that she is a bit better but that the opponent is improving faster.
Erin and her opponent chat by spelling shorthand in Go stones, and agree to speed-chess at five seconds per move, where Erin opens with the Dutch Attack.
Erin wants revenge after the first speed game, which ends in a draw in the second, and she suggests six-sided hexagonal chess.
The opponent tells Erin they were once an adventurer, dislike monsters, have met Crelers, and lost friends to them, adding that elder ones are worse.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin plays her magical chess game with her opponent, whose messages that day read "brd" and "hv mch wrk".

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin times herself crossing from her room through the Garden of Sanctuary door and out of a different door into the kitchen behind Palt in six seconds, knowing where he is, with the kitchen knife that Pelt forged and Lorent refined in her hand.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin listens to Montressa and Beza from the Garden door, which she keeps slightly ajar, and the door has iron bands unlike anything else in the inn; Lyonette catches her, and Erin says she was looking for a dance floor.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin can summon only [Like Fire, Memory] at will: a blue fire of sadness that is cold, stays the same size however sad she is, and flops uselessly when thrown at a tree.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin cannot get a flame from anger or happiness when she tries to, since she lacks enough of either feeling.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin uses her [Advanced Crafting] Skill with Lyonette's [Flawless Attempt] to make a metal-lined lantern that holds the blue flame and gives off cool air, and she freezes water into ice cubes in the oven with the flame.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin tells Selys that her inn is nearly done with the second floor and that she will rent rooms to staff, Temile, some players and actual guests, with a stable for Lyonette.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin offers Palt, Montressa and Beza rooms at her inn for payment with three meals a day, saying that their help against the Crelers matters though it does not balance out their earlier acts.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin has Montressa message Falene Skystrall and Ceria or Pisces that Ryoka is in Reizmelt, north of Invrisil, and to tell Ryoka to come back home; the Silver Swords reply that they will stop by on their way north.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin tells Calruz not to apologise for everything and not to hide, remembering him as Calruz of Hammerad who charged alone into the Crelers, and she makes a flame of glory for him to remember.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin makes a small pink flame of glory, which lengthens the shadows of the inn and which she casts into the fireplaces; Zevara flinches from it and whispers "Skinner."

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin mixes Firebreath Whiskey with faerie flower nectar and Mrsha's faerie flower and burns it with the pink fire, and Relc drinks it and toasts the 4th Company, which roars back that it is the Skywalker's Company.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin turns off her Skill and gets drunk on purpose for what the text calls the first time in a while, finding that it is not so bad.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Later, Erin reaches Level 41 as a [Magical Innkeeper] and obtains the Skill [Inn: Twofold Rest].

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin wakes on the floor with a hangover and rolls into the Garden of Sanctuary and back into her room, and [Twofold Rest] means she will recover with twice the sleep.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin has her period at the inn, has Lyonette fetch her cloth pad, and learns that Lyonette uses potions to stop menstruation, as her whole family does.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin can push the mood in the inn, which Lyonette, Temile and some [Actors] notice.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: The pink flame is kept burning in the same concealed lantern that Erin used for the blue flame of sadness.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin shouts at the inn's patrons with an anger-fueled aura that stills the room, saying Belgrade is not even three and should not know about sex, and then Belgrade asks to speak.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin goes alone into the tropical section of her Garden of Sanctuary, a Level 40 Skill that no one can enter, hangs bed sheets for privacy, and feels she is not enjoying it; she thinks that she had two earlier intimate experiences short of sex and ends up feeling lonely.

section: The Garden, glory and the Wistram mages (Book 16)
text: Erin counts cards and wins a poker pot from Palt, and by the end she has won two birds off of Bird.
Erin plans to brew alcohol, though Lyonette warns that it ferments and so her [Field of Preservation] will interfere, and she then drops the plan to cook for Palt.
Erin tells Xrn that she does not want the Antinium to become a blade and agrees that Pawn and at least a dozen Antinium will stay at the inn, paid in advance.
Erin brings Pelt a very meaty sandwich she calls a "Meat Supreme Sub" as an apology, and Pelt eats it and says she would be welcome in Dwarfhome.
Erin tells Pelt that Liscor has forges and cheap alcohol and that he could get his own forge there, and he stops hammering and seems interested.
Erin opens the door to Invrisil, and Lady Magnolia Reinhart steps through, followed by Lady Pryde and Lady Wuvren.
Erin throws a [Minotaur Punch] at Magnolia, and Ressa catches her in a hold.
Erin tells Magnolia "I hate you", and Magnolia answers that she should not be forgiven.
Erin says she keeps receiving invitations for free week-long stays from Oteslia and Manus, and Grimalkin suspects she is being treated as a [Tourist].
Erin is exhausted and downcast after failing to stop the three [Ladies], and she hugs Ceria and leans on her.
Pisces demands pasta and blue juice from Erin as Miss Innkeeper, and Erin laughs and tells him he had better have money.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin is doused with whiskey by Maviola while glaring at Lyonette, and an invisible black flame of hatred appears around her.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin tells the inn she is going for a walk, steps through her door burning with hatred, and walks into Pallass past Sergeant Kel.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin asks Saliss whether he could make something from flowers if she supplied them, and later uproots a flower from her garden and hands it to him.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin is a Level 41 [Innkeeper] who clashes with Lyonette, a Level 19 [Princess], in aura practice.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin shoves Lady Pryde back with a ripple of her aura without meaning to.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin stares at a destroyed Celum from the first wagon, which carries her door, and gets down.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin's inn pushes against the dragon Eldavin at the Garden of Sanctuary doorway until she invites him in.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Later, Erin reaches Level 43 as a [Magical Innkeeper] and wakes screaming "Who was he!?"

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin warns that the soccer broadcast could tell Wistram about the Earthers, and Palt's advert distracts the mages.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin scribbles a note telling the King of Destruction that he and Gazi are jerks and should stop declaring war, and Flos laughs.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin tells Ryoka that she levelled up twice when Eldavin visited, and keeps in her pocket a mithril coin carrying a word that nearly killed Pelt, showing it to no one.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin scolds Palt for smoking indoors.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin tells Relc that the Golden Triangle scheme is not real and that he may not keep selling it; Relc leaves, saying he will make it right.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin is shocked at the news of Relc and Ryoka's talk of sleeping together and cannot say the words.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin serves the dish Ryoka added to her recipes for a treat.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin does not know how to help Ryoka throw a fae party, but she has a location in mind and wants to raise money.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin tries to make a heat-themed [Wondrous Fare] dish with milk, butter and hot peppers, and it curdles.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin concludes that her cooking Skill needs a theme, and says the dish would have lasted three hours if it had worked.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin decorates the Pallass-side checkpoint room with posters, and Sergeant Kel asks what she is doing.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin says her favourite characters were Snoopy, Linus, Peppermint Patty and Marcie, and that she wanted to be like Marcie.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin stands in front of an armed mob with no lantern and uses only [Loud Voice], asking who they are.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin's golden ring glows and spells out SALAZSAR, which Grimalkin sees.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Later, Erin reaches Level 44 as a [Magical Innkeeper], obtains [Inn: Compartments of Holding], and her Warrior class is consolidated into Bannerlady.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin chats by message under the name Joseph with Geneva, a doctor from Earth who is twenty-five.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin, as Joseph, mentions penicillin to Geneva, who says she needs a cure for the Yellow Rivers disease.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin writes to Ryoka that she has found the second of three people, with complications.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin boils clams that Lord Toldos of House Everight sent to her as thanks, and plans to ask Lasica for fancier clam recipes.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin stuffs tissues in her nose after a nosebleed from Zevara's Skill, and silences a crowd with her aura before shouting at those who attack Rose.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin keeps a list of future ideas, with Golems crossed out as a bad idea.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin tells Selys that she cannot remember how bikes work because she is from Earth, and Selys asks what Earth is.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin has a billiards table made by a [Carpenter], dragged in by Antinium, and says it needs felt.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin sees an [Immortal Moment] of two young women.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin tells Palt that her cooking needs a theme, and that she has tried to make food with a purpose twice.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin asks Palt to cast [Darkness] so she can get in the mood.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin throws the Shadow Loaf at the wall, where it hangs in midair and eats light.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin plans crystalline candies from powdered gemstones, and Numbtongue pushes lightning lollipops.

section: Hatred, the Garden and the Earthers (Books 17-18)
text: Erin's new part of the inn has three rooms with no doors, and only the truest friends can open them.
Erin knows of a pin on a map of the world for Ryoka in Reizmelt, and she keeps a secret about the Emperor.
Erin's shaved-ice slurpies, from her sad-fire freezer or Palt's magic, are a new fad at the inn.
Erin watches a message and says "she's saying something", and later retreats with Kevin and Rose to the secret Earth rooms.
Erin sleeps in the Garden of Sanctuary with a knife, a frying pan and a glowing green acid jar within reach.
Erin tells Palt that the Garden is a great safe-room but cannot support everyone, and that if the inn goes it goes too.
Erin is invisible to [Appraisal] and [Scrying] spells thanks to a ring from Saliss and something else.
Erin cracks two ribs when Palt's horse falls on her, and a healing potion works.
Erin and Maviola find that their fires differ, and Erin says her hate fire is a different color from Maviola's.
Numbtongue tells Erin to kill the adult Raskghar, while Pawn says only those who killed a Gnoll directly should die.
Erin asks Lyonette whether she could forgive Toren or Erin for not knowing what he was doing, and Lyonette says she can forgive Erin.
Erin conjures a flame that is grey, split evenly between white and black, which burns wood slowly and looks like a thousand blades.
Erin has a booth named for her in the Players of Celum theatre that she has not used.
Erin throws Grimalkin out of the inn, removes the yellow mana stone to close the door to Pallass, and says it stays closed until Chaldion talks with her, Zevara and the Council.
Pallass is blocked from Erin's inn for the time being.
Erin plays four tables at once and does not lose any, though Olesm and Belgrade tie her.
Erin says that Chaldion can be beaten even with his Skill, in a way that is not easy but simple.
Erin proposes a Pallass Hunting-style outing, and rejects a beach after Mrsha signs that sand is stupid.
Erin crashes into the fence of magical plants on her first bike ride.
Errif Jealwind is a Gnoll [Merchant] who heads the Merchant's Guild in Pallass.
Errif is one of the Head Speakers of the Assembly of Crafts and wears a skullcap, the first hat Erin has seen on a Gnoll.
Errif tells Erin the Assembly is considering impounding her door for its security risk and economic advantages.
Erin accuses Errif of lying about security and says he just wants her door because it is cool.
Errif tells Embria that the Assembly will not act until a vote is called, and that Pallass is not at Liscor's beck and call.
Errif says the Assembly is on break, and that Pallass's own [Strategists] will review Embria's report.
Erin calls Errif a jerk [Senator], and Lasica says that Pallass backing the non-Gnoll candidate would bother his voters.
Errif is a Gnoll [Senator] of the Assembly of Crafts who joins Pallass's delegation of four [Senators].
Pallass claims custody of the surviving Raskghar, some of whom will go with Senator Errif to the Meeting of Tribes.
Esiela is the Grand Mage of Belchan and head of Belchan's Mage Schools.
Esiela is the highest-level individual on Belchan's side of the battlefield, able to become invisible and levitate.
A professor addressing the class estimates that Esiela is most likely over Level 40, and at the very least in her high thirties.
Esiela's students stare at their headmistress in trepidation but also with trust.
Esiela is dueling the [Mages] of Parasol Stroll when General Fultoolm looks for her.
Esiela is defeated and has her magic suppressed by Parasol Stroll's [Mages], and she imagines a mage collar around her neck.
Ulyse of Parasol Stroll says Esiela is powerful, with six [Mages] killed, and that the Slavers of Roshal's mage-collars would not work on someone of her caliber.
Ulyse offers Esiela six years in Parasol Stroll under a magical blood oath, one year per dead [Mage], or slavery.
Esiela accepts, drawing her own blood and signing the contract, and feels the magic bind her.
Esiela takes a parasol and marches with the [Mages] of Parasol Stroll upon Levrhine, her home.
Later, Esiela is a Grand Mage of Parasol Stroll, bound by blood magic, and casts [Featherweight] on Zamea's axe with the linked spell of the other [Mages].
Esiela casts [Haste] on Zamea, which nearly wipes out her reserves.
Exara is a female Centaur [Captain] who leads the suppression company Rot's Bane in the Baleros war valley.
Exara taps a map and relays a rumour that a skilled [Doctor] treats wounded soldiers of any side in a neutral zone to the north.
Exara reports that a cease-fire is in force around the zone where the rumoured [Doctor] works, which has caught the attention of both companies.
Exara tells Calectus and the newcomers that the first attack killed Ulvial in the first attack on the neutral camp.
Exara takes command of the rest of Ulvial's company together with Quallet after his death.
Exara reports that Xalandrass' camp was also attacked and that the Naga crushed at least six attacking soldiers with his tail.
Exara has joined forces with Xalandrass' group and holds position on the neutral ground with Quallet, hoping to avoid becoming a target.
Ken names Exara of Rot's Bane, Quallet and Xalandrass as neutral parties while addressing the battlefield through an amplifier ring.
Fabiel rides with Beniar of the Windfrozen Riders when a Goblin ambush strikes them.
Fabiel dies instantly from a poisoned Goblin arrow while riding with Beniar, according to Beniar.
Fabiel's horse is lost when the Goblin ambushers rush the horses.
A search party finds the place where Beniar was ambushed but no sign of Fabiel or his horse.
Falene Skystrall is a half-Elf [Battlemage] with light red hair and a dignified bearing, a member of the Silver Swords.
Falene graduated from Wistram three decades ago and remembers the academy fondly.
Falene greets Ceria with ancient half-Elven gestures, and Ceria does not return them.
Falene uses her staff to dry and knock the frosting off Ylawes' armor.
Falene says the standards have lowered at Wistram since she attended.
Falene is a [Battlemage], not an [Enchanter], but as the only fully Wistram-trained [Mage] present offers a free preliminary assessment of the Goblins' artifacts.
Falene receives a note from a Wistram colleague confirming Ceria and Pisces are graduates who left prematurely, and she suspects a cover-up.
Wistram confirms Falene Skystrall is in Liscor, and she refuses to give confidential information on the two expelled students, saying it conflicts with her team's interests.
Falene tells Ceria she was not at Wistram at the time and cannot comment on incidents, but thinks the two are inexperienced for graduates.
Falene says her contacts in Wistram refused to explain unless she did them favors, and that Ceria and Pisces were expelled in their third year.
Falene says several senior [Mages] challenged the academy's higher levels and failed, around the time the two left.
Falene speaks with her old roommate Bashea by a private [Message] variant, and Bashea keeps telling her to come back.
Falene says Wistram gave her a blanket ban on any information regarding this team.
Falene belongs to the Centrist faction, while the Revivalists, led by Archmage Nailihuaile, back Montressa du Valeross' team.
Falene draws on the inn's strong mana to cast [Lightning Shroud], and later casts [Blue Lightning], [Flash Fireball], [Water Arrows], [Sand Spray] and [Aerial Burst].
Falene casts [Grand Fireball] and [Featherfall] against the giant moths.
Falene, Dawil and Ylawes stop Yvlon from entering the dungeon, with Falene arguing she would get herself killed.
Falene pitches a burning fastball that sets Dawil's glove and beard alight, and a swerving ball.
Falene argues that placing bounties has historically culled problematic populations, and Dawil rebukes her.
Falene leaves Liscor north with Dawil and Ylawes, telling Ceria they offered a chance.
Falene transmits what she sees from the walls by scrying, so the entire world watches the battle.
Falene offers to buy Pyrite's blue mana stones from Numbtongue, naming a price that stuns Erin, and Numbtongue refuses.
Falene tells Numbtongue that mana stones are of no use to him, and Dawil calls her a half-wit.
Falene complains of wasting a month rushing to Yvlon's aid, and says Ksmvr and Pisces are rolling in treasure.
Falene waits for Ylawes in a staged room after her bath, nervous and slightly drunk.
Dawil kicks the door open carrying a drunk Ylawes, and Falene covers herself and orders him out.
Falene later drinks alone at the bar, tired of the road and of finding a partner.
Dawil comforts Falene and promises not to tell Ylawes.
Fals is a tall, blonde, tanned senior Runner who wears red clothing of better quality than the other Runners around him and carries two daggers at his belt.
Fals is one of the most influential Runners in all the northern city-states, and the local Guildmasters listen to him.
Fals is twenty-three years old and is nicknamed Fleetfoot Fals.
Garia says Fals can read and has been seen reading books, which most folk cannot do.
Ryoka sees Fals as dirty blonde, handsome and athletic, and thinks he is Garia's type; he has straight, nearly white teeth.
Fals's Skills are geared towards sensing danger and preserving stamina and he has no movement Skills, so he admits Ryoka can beat him in a race even without levels.

section: Book 1 and 2: Celum's Runners and Ryoka
text: Fals tells Ryoka that Magnolia's request is a good delivery and asks her to let other Runners take it next time, since Runners like Magnolia, who tips well and shares her deliveries.

section: Book 1 and 2: Celum's Runners and Ryoka
text: Fals tells Persua not to bother Ryoka again, saying Ryoka broke a few rules but is a good Runner and the Guild needs every Runner it can get.

section: Book 1 and 2: Celum's Runners and Ryoka
text: After Persua's group injures Ryoka, Fals tells Garia he will talk to the Guildmaster, says Persua has gone too far, and offers to call in favours from good [Healers] and a [Cleric] who owes him one so that Ryoka is on her feet by the end of the month.

section: Book 1 and 2: Celum's Runners and Ryoka
text: Fals tells Ryoka that things would be smoother if she suggested that Lady Magnolia open her delivery requests to every Runner.

section: Book 1 and 2: Celum's Runners and Ryoka
text: Fals leads the highest-level City Runners in sprinting to cut Ryoka off, but she blows past him while playing "I Will Not Bow" on her iPhone, leaving him with a stunned face.

section: Book 1 and 2: Celum's Runners and Ryoka
text: Fals apologises to Ryoka on behalf of the Guild and himself after her delivery, offering to let her take any Magnolia request she likes, and warns her that Persua left the Guild with her group that morning and will probably try something.

section: Book 1 and 2: Celum's Runners and Ryoka
text: Ryoka reports that Fals says Runners must band together to survive; Cervial replies that Fals is no coward but represents much of what he dislikes about the Runner's Guild, though he is not wrong.

section: Book 1 and 2: Celum's Runners and Ryoka
text: Fals tells Ryoka that if she never levels up she will never become a Courier, that she is one of the Runners' best but nowhere near fast enough, and that in a year or two even Garia could outrun her.

section: Book 1 and 2: Celum's Runners and Ryoka
text: Fals says the Runner's Guild in Esthelm might have requests going down to Liscor and that he will talk to the Guildmaster there, then asks Ryoka if she would like to get a bite at a pub with a chef who just learned [Advanced Cooking].

section: Book 1 and 2: Celum's Runners and Ryoka
text: Fals tells Garia to listen to Ryoka about buying Octavia's potions, and offers Garia a spare wand with a single cast of [Slow] that should help her get away from bandits.

section: Book 1 and 2: Celum's Runners and Ryoka
text: Fals greets the Courier Valceif Godfrey in Esthelm, saying he has seen only two Couriers before and never so far south.
Fals is absent from the party in Celum, which is conspicuous because Persua follows him about wherever possible.
Fals avoids Celum on purpose because Persua took work from the City Runners after getting the [Double Step] Skill, and he could not make her listen.
Fals tells Ryoka that he has been a [Runner] for about sixteen years and was the best in the area until she showed up, with all his Skills stamina-based and defensive.
Fals is a Human City Runner who works around Celum, with the Skills [Surefoot], [Efficient Run] and [Thousand-Step Sprint].
Fals has been to Erin's inn before and knows the [Innkeeper].

Fals delivers a heavy wrapped package that arrived from the north to Erin Solstice at the inn, getting a seal so that he can swear it was delivered; Erin opens it in her room and finds a Go board that is a twin of her chess board.
After the Bloodfeast Raiders attack, Fals finds Ryoka shot through the shoulder in the ash, gives her a potion that closes the wound, and tells her it is not her fault.
Fals reports that Liscor and Esthelm are sending aid through Wailant's door after word reached Wailant.
Fals fears that Kevin's bicycle will be the end of Runners; Ryoka answers that it will change running but not end it and that Runners will simply become Couriers.
Erin jokes that the bicycle might take Fals' job away.
Farri Sightly is a Human [Merchant] who introduces himself to Selys and has an apprentice [Trader] named Febin.
Farri is a thirty-something [Merchant] who counts Selys as something of a friend.
Farri has the Skill [Evaluation of Wealth], which he notes is handy for a [Merchant] or a [Thief], and reads Selys as having new money.
Farri also has [Prolonged Negotiations], which Selys notices.
Farri says he can pick his clients and plans to stay at the Firehearth inn.
Farri sells Selys a magical vault for eight hundred gold, a bag of holding for six hundred and sixty gold and other items at fair prices.
Farri has a Drake-style full-toothed smile and makes the extra trip to Liscor for Selys, saying one good client makes up for many miles.
Selys praises the cooling charm she bought from Farri, which does not work all night but gets her to sleep.
Farri offers Pisces and Selys credit worth twenty percent of what he thinks they can spend.
Pisces believes Farri painted over the gem on his ring finger so it would shine only towards him.
Farri sells Selys nearly twelve hundred gold's worth of items, to be delivered to her apartment, and adds a tracking charm to her bag of holding.
Farri refuses to place a large order with Bezale of Maweil's scrolls, because of recent events involving his client Selys Shivertail.
Farri describes Selys as new to her money, owner of the Heartflame Breastplate, niece of Zel Shivertail and granddaughter of the Adventurer's Guildmistress.
Femithain is the Magus-Crafter of the Illivere League and leads its army of Golems and Artificers at the siege of Oliphant.
Femithain's spectacles magnify distant sights, letting him see into Oliphant.
Femithain leads a nation comparable to Savere, and technically outranks General Thelican.
Femithain is old enough to have lived through the King of Destruction's first campaign.
Femithain's Illivere League is made of smaller crafter-states that elect their Magus-Crafter periodically.
Femithain is tired of blood and death at Oliphant, Tiqr's capital, and he respects Nsiia's kingdom but thinks she erred by refusing to bow.
Femithain says he has no objection to Nerrhavia sending Golems and elites to seize the Empress of Beasts, but is surprised Queen Yisame wishes her captured.
Femithain explains the Dreamers of Reim to his officers, saying they grow faster and deadlier with their conviction.
Femithain says the Dreamers might number six hundred thousand if the King of Destruction's Skill works on all of them.
Femithain says the Sorcelled Blades are weaker than the Dreamers, but elites whose enchanted blades copy and combine each other's enchantments.
Femithain believes Flos Reimarch is not invincible, because he loses when outflanked or worn down on multiple fronts, so Illivere must hold as an anvil.
Femithain refuses to retreat, saying Illivere is committed and the Dreamers are not invincible.
Femithain orders Armsmaster Dellic to hold and retreat Illivere's army when he falls, and nominates Artificer Antielle d'Elin as his replacement.
Femithain advances with his metal Golems, while Rémi Canada watches from hiding.
Femithain orders Nsiia arrested, her headband and spear taken, and guarded by Stone Golems, eight [Artificers] and sixty of Dellic's best.
Femithain says Illivere claims no land from Tiqr, and he calls Nsiia a political prisoner he will defend before the Head Artificers.
Femithain backs Nerrhavia's claim to Oliphant and most of Tiqr, and proposes a subservient occupied state in place of selling slaves.
Femithain persuades Thelican to give up the Empress of Beasts by pointing out that Oliphant will make him wealthy.
Femithain has stayed in power a long time, keeping everything running smoothly, and drinks stamina-potion on the terrace of his quarters in Delicrel.
Femithain falls asleep on his desk after drafting Golem designs overnight, and financed the paper Chandrar International.
Femithain orders a nude clay Nsiia Golem by Siddin of Veule smashed, since the Watch Captain's comments should treat Nsiia as former Empress.
Femithain says Nsiia abdicated with Tiqr's surrender and that General Vasraf's Tiqr resistance is an unlawful rebellion.
Femithain has Siddin escorted to his family's estates.
Femithain knows of fewer than ten Cognizant-class beings in the world, and met Cognita of Wistram once when she visited Illivere.
Femithain says no one in Illivere can craft Sentient-class Golems, and he intends to visit Wistram once the states vote another Magus-Crafter.
Archmage Feor is a half-Elf of two hundred years and one of the Archmages of Wistram.
Feor used to teach one of the highest-level magic courses for eighth-year students and still advises apprentices and mages.
Feor leads the Centrists, a faction opposed to the Revivalists, and Teura belongs to his personal faction.
Feor is a generalist, according to Naili, who says he wants to be a proper [Archmage] of old but lacks the class.
Naili says Feor prefers big spells in battle and everywhere else.
Feor suspects the Revivalists know something he does not, and that someone besides Naili helped Blackmage.
Feor orders search teams to leave as soon as the first-years begin classes, calling the otherworlders a resource Wistram will collect.
Feor visits Amerys with Naili and Viltach.
Feor watches the duel through the Queens' mirrors with Viltach and Naili, and tells the others to be silent.
Feor debates Naili in public about unity, and Naili's argument for striking enemies while weak wins applause from the audience.
Feor thinks of asking how Naili's view fits Wistram's reputation for opposition without active engagement, but cannot raise it in public.
Feor extends the Weatherward southward with Viltach and Naili so that the Emerald Signet, carrying Trey and Flynn, can reach the isle.
Feor acts to save the ship because it carries two children from another world.
Ferkr is a female Gnoll apprentice of Grimalkin and the only Gnoll apprentice he has ever had.
Ferkr is shorter than Grimalkin and far less muscular, though she has twice Erin's muscle definition.
Ferkr is a Level 6 [Mage], though Grimalkin says she is far too nervous.
Ferkr was born in Pallass and is not a Plains Gnoll.
Grimalkin gives Ferkr a two-hundred-pound weight to carry as she attempts to become a [Mage].
Grimalkin says the rumour that Gnolls cannot become [Mages] is completely false, and that some idiot started it at Wistram.
Ferkr has been studying under Grimalkin for six months.
Ferkr casts a ball of yellow light over her paw as a [Mage] spell.
Grimalkin tells Ferkr she will go to the Meeting of Tribes and show that she can cast magic.
Ferris is a Gnoll agent trained in the City of War, who performs secret duties, and gives the name Ferris Thycarl to Rafaema.
Ferris has no rank or affiliation when he introduces himself, and Rafaema knows what he is.
Ferris is one of Manus's top agents and an expert in covert operations, infiltration and combat.
Ferris can detect truth in three ways: a Skill, an artifact that helps him read people, and training in detecting lies across species.
Ferris is the newest of Rafaema's protectors, and she spots him within a second of meeting him, so his disguise needs work.
Ferris was chosen for Rafaema because he is very good at his job and has the right personality.
Two earlier agents assigned to Rafaema, Kelis and Amessia, fifty and thirty years ago, nearly caused disaster.
Ferris is aware of the war council's decisions in which Rafaema, known only to two Walled Cities, has a respected voice.
Ferris appears at the inn as a Gnoll [Coachman] for the company Izril's Wonders, wanting to add the inn to a tour of the Walled Cities.
Ferris tells Lyonette his company takes people to each Walled City and that he is no [Negotiator], only closest when orders came.
Ferris is revealed as a Manus agent who came to the inn under the guise of Izril's Wonders, a real company with which he actually holds a charter.
Ferris reports by two-way scroll to Rafaema, who is unhappy that he has failed to get Erin to go on the tour.
Erin forgets Ferris's offer and declines the Walled Cities tour, saying she should stay with the inn and will not leave for days.
Ferris has been sent to obtain Erin Solstice, but finds she is too well connected for him to spirit her away.
Ferris concludes that Lyonette, whom he identifies as the 6th Princess of Calanfer, is the real power behind the inn, and that Erin is a mascot.
Ferris changes targets from Erin to Lyonette.
Ferris is not completely right: the text says his conclusion is half-wrong.
Ferris tries to enter the [Garden of Sanctuary] a dozen different ways, and its Skill foils him.
Feshi Weatherfur is a Gnoll of the Weatherfur tribe who, as her tribe's custom, dyes parts of her fur different colours.
Feshi came to the Titan's Academy to become one of the world's best [Strategists], and is better at laying traps than anything else.
Feshi says her tribe colours its fur because it knows where and when to send its large flocks and predicts the weather.
Feshi has the [Shaman] class and boils water by closing her eyes over a pot.
Feshi uses [Bursting Arrow] to detonate arrows in slugs.
Feshi fears her people's hatred of the undead since the Necromancer slew the Great Chieftain Kerash.
Feshi stands at the docks with Wil and aims a wand with a wind spell.
Feshi trades her chance at the prize for a present for the Meeting of Tribes, winning four trading caravans from Talia, each led by at least a Level 40 [Merchant].
Talia first offers two trading caravans from the Kallinad harbours through the Gnoll Plains over six years.
Feshi rallies the citizens of Daquin to fight the Iron Vanguard's soldiers, and thousands answer.
Perorn calls Feshi's ability to rally Daquin exceptional, and says the rest of her performance was not.
Feshi admits she failed to use her best Skill at the end, and Perorn orders her to shadow her on campaign as her second.
Feshi debates breast-feeding with Marian and Umina, arguing warm blood makes sense.
Feshi needs to attend the Meeting of Tribes in Izril, so the trip drops her off.
Feshi tries to stop Merrik diving after Peki and runs to fetch the captain.
Feshi throws a glass sword into the sea as a feint and looses a [Bursting Arrow] to blow up liquor barrels.
Feshi catches the black Sarcophagus Dagger of Devi, and Fetohep says the party may keep the swords until they die.
Feshi sent out a call the moment they arrived, and nearly two thousand mounted Gnolls with fog [Shamans] drive off the seafolk.
Feshi says the Meeting of Tribes approaches ever faster and urges going to Oteslia.
Feshi tells Wil that Yerranola must be saved and puts a paw on his shoulders.
Fetohep is the mummified undead [King] of Khelt, with sunken sockets in which golden flames burn with intelligence and personality.
Fetohep has lost his lips and nose, and his voice comes out of his mouth without a tongue or vocal cords, with a subtle echo.
Fetohep calls himself a Revenant, one of the few undead who kept the will of their life.
Fetohep says he does not level, but keeps all his Skills of old.
Fetohep says Revenants are consumed by grudges and hatred of the living, but he is not, since he swore in life to protect Khelt.
Fetohep was a [Warrior] in life and learned magic only after his death.
Fetohep says he was chosen as ruler because he loved his people, more than being the best warrior.
Fetohep has ruled Khelt for six hundred and fifty-three years and is the nineteenth ruler, after eighteen predecessors.
Fetohep has a chair placed so that in every room of his palace he is never without a throne.
Fetohep drinks a goblet of mana and death essence, and calls a similar draught Ghost's Tears.
Fetohep walked each continent in turn before his death.
Fetohep says his flesh is rotting, and within a century or two the magics that keep him will fail and he will turn to dust.
Fetohep declares that every child, man and woman in Khelt is under his protection, and anyone who harms them will face Khelt.
Fetohep holds that citizens of other nations are free only in illusion, constrained by needs of body and money, whereas Khelt's citizens are fed and sheltered.
Fetohep has lived six hundred years maintaining Khelt's peace, a passionless [King] who is a slave first to his people.
Fetohep says Khelt is neutral about Jecrass and Belchan, though it trades with Reim.
Fetohep says any nation that objects to his will need only cross his borders with an army.
Fetohep's paradise is built on the will of Khelt's rulers and is not a democracy.
Fetohep says his people may travel the breadth of his kingdom at will in undead carriages without cost.
Fetohep says Khelt's rulers have weathered millennia, each ruling for centuries or even a thousand years.
Fetohep greets the Quarass of Germina as "Dragonbane" at the palace steps before kneeling undead and bowing citizens.
Fetohep says the Shield Kingdoms have ever been allies of Khelt, and that Khelt remembers and honors them.
Fetohep tells the Quarass her death troubled him greatly.
Fetohep says he holds Flos of Reim in contempt and demands that Flos swear an oath.
Fetohep says Wistram has declined since Zelkyr's passing, and blames a Drake's vanity for locking Wistram's magics away.
Fetohep says he dislikes Savere and faults Flos for not destroying it, valuing Savere's queen only for summoning water.
Fetohep says Queen Khelta, who founded Khelt, was gifted beyond any who have walked Chandrar's sands.
The Quarass calls Khelta the greatest [Necromancer] she has met, and as great a [Queen].
Fetohep and the Quarass agree a wager of four hundred pounds of Khelt's gold against sixteen assassinations by Germina's [Assassins] of Level 30 or higher.
The wager is that the Antinium will be attacked within six years by the Drakes or some other side.
Fetohep calls Trey Atwood "child" and treats him as a guest.
Fetohep demands an oath sworn in blood that Flos will never attack or imperil Khelt, or Khelt will march on Reim.
Fetohep believes Flos is a man who comes every four hundred years, and his rise and fall are temporary.
The Quarass argues that Flos is a man who comes only every two thousand years at most.
Fetohep says that to give Flos any aid is to court the fate of Empress Nsiia.
Fetohep tests Trey under truth spells before accepting that another world, Earth, exists.
Fetohep laughs at the threat from Earth, saying Khelt will rise or bow, and tells Flos he will have subservience if Flos proves too dangerous.
Fetohep serves the first gelato in Khelt, imported from Terandria, and learns from Trey that it comes from Earth as ice cream.
Fetohep has never heard of chocolate, and has cocoa beans found in his kingdom after Trey describes it.
Fetohep gives Trey a Second Day Potion and has breakfast with him, learning of television and the iPhone.
Fetohep finds escalators hedonistic, and says the mana stones for elevators in Khelt were too expensive.
Fetohep and Trey take the first royal selfie in this world.
Fetohep sees in a picture on a boy's phone something close to immortality.
Fetohep agrees that Khelt will give Flos thirty thousand bushels per month for eight years, in exchange for his oath in blood never to take arms against Khelt.
Fetohep says the Quarass will negotiate the oath terms, and Trey will stay in Khelt for another week.
Fetohep shows Trey marvels and artworks on each visit, and likes to watch him eat magical dishes.
Fetohep discusses Earth history with Trey, including Alexander the Great, Churchill, the Ottomans and Rome.
Fetohep says Trey might gain a history class, but advises him to stay a [Mage].
Fetohep says he dislikes Teres because she reminds him of Flos, and that she challenged his authority by trying to strike him.
Fetohep has Khelt's undead rise to block Reim's [Captain] who demands Trey return, and gives Trey passage.
Fetohep has entertained Trey four times since their first meeting, in a plush private dining room.
Fetohep sends two thousand undead north from Khelt's border to show displeasure at the Quarass.
Fetohep believes the Quarass is so old she weighs only power and the cost in lives, not pain.
Fetohep says that if the A'ctelios vision moves, it must be put back to sleep, since it has happened thrice.
Fetohep says the first vision was followed by tremors felt across Chandrar, and that it must be stopped.
Fetohep tells Trey the war began with Belchan's Prime Minister, a village's prejudice, and the death of Gnolls.
Fetohep says Flos put hundreds to death for his justice, and asks Trey what he says to it.
Fetohep says A'ctelios's flesh was offered as an honorable, optional choice and not a trick.
Fetohep says A'ctelios's mad legions are a weapon kept for Dragons and worse, and that Tombhome was slain by A'ctelios's original heroes.
Fetohep says that a ruler cannot always be moral, and does not know if A'ctelios can be destroyed.
Fetohep addresses Wil Kallinad's ship, calling the discovery of his treasure an interloper's find and offering half of it back for the rest.
Fetohep warns that the curse of Khelt will engulf them until nothing is left if they refuse.
Fetohep appears as a figure made of sand on the Emerald Signet, far from his kingdom, by an ancient curse.
Fetohep offers three of the six Diamond Swords of Serept to Wil for his life, if the other three are brought to Chandrar.
Fetohep says the chest and artifacts are cursed, and only Wil Kallinad has the right to touch his blades.
Merrik has not heard of Khelt, and Fetohep remarks that perhaps legends fade, as young Atwood may have been correct.
Fetohep gives Wil a day to answer.
Fetohep reappears to find the crew drunk, and Wil accepts his terms but asks first to visit one last shipwreck.
Fetohep sighs "Mortals." when Merrik swings the boom and three of Wil's friends go overboard.
Fetohep's sand form is dispersed by the Drowned Crew's [Dispel Magic], but he rises from the chest and uses [The Desiccation of Zeikhal] to turn a Drowned Man to dust.
Fetohep raises a sand whirlwind that engulfs three ships and tells Wil to sail, as the sand will rage for ten minutes.
Merrik concludes the casket goes inert when the chest is far, so the curse's magic is limited.
Fetohep demands the other three swords, but lets the Strategists go after Wil says they cannot spare the trip to Chandrar.
Fetohep says that had they abandoned their friend they would not be worthy of the blades.
Salii says Fetohep lost a wager and gave a condensation stone as a gift, and that he usually bets thousands of gold as a spectator.
Fetohep demands his armaments of the sun at the word Vampires, then sits when Teres says she only asked.
Fetohep says Vampires were a scourge upon Chandrar and devoured the people of Khelt when they claimed their eternal night.
Fetohep says Vampires tried each continent, finding Rhir inhospitable, corrupting Terandria's kings, and infesting Izril.
Fetohep says Dullahans built their bodies of silver, Naga and greater Lizardfolk united, and Selphids drove Vampires from Baleros.
Fetohep wears hollow crystalline armor containing a swirling compressed storm cloud, and at a clap the sun shines from it.
Fetohep tells Teres that no Vampire will gain a foothold while he lives.
Fetohep says the Quarass, after being possessed by Vampire power, was woken by her Champion of Ger and then destroyed the Vampires.
Fetohep says he fears Drakes, whose union with Dragons created the Shield Kingdoms and drove Gnolls underground.
Fetohep says Drakes and Dragons fell only because they fought each other.
Fetohep gives Teres a Potion of Revitalization, which he guesses costs at least eighty gold coins.
Fetohep refuses to give Teres a blade, because a sword doing her fighting would stop her levelling, but offers a [Fashionista] and a wardrobe.
Fetohep says he gave Trey a spell tome, draughts and enchanted clothing as favors.
Fetohep expects the Jecrass war to end soon, as the peace talks will not last long.
Fetohep says Flos has not used his greatest Skill, a single hammer which frightens other nations while it is unused.
Fierre is a thin, pale girl wrapped in layers of clothing who coughs and sniffs, and who has sharp teeth.
Fierre lodges at The Huntress' Haven, Madain's inn in Reizmelt, as does Ryoka.
Fierre has lodged at the same inn in Reizmelt as Ryoka for nearly a year when Ryoka first notices her.
Fierre's irises are slightly red.
Fierre is twenty-five years old but looks about sixteen, and she is a good head shorter than Ryoka.
Fierre's full name is Serafierre val Lischelle-Drakle.
Fierre grew up on her family's farm, then moved to the city to earn a living.
Fierre works as an opener from a small room reached by knocking twice and kicking the door once.
Fierre's workroom has no windows, a locked and barred back door into a [Carpenter]'s shop, and a magical ward that hums in the air.
Fierre opens envelopes and checks their contents without breaking the seal, which makes her a Runner's fence or information broker.
Fierre does not deal on the wrong end of the law enough to worry the local authorities.
Fierre pays Ryoka three silver and six copper for an open-and-check, and offers six gold coins for the information in the letter.
Fierre also grinds Duskwilter stems for the [Alchemist] Kelysta, who scolds her for working without a mask and thick gloves.
