Fierre hauls cargo for a silver coin an hour, and does not sweat while doing it.
Fierre works on foundations as a [Laborer] and spends an hour or two at her brokering job beforehand.
Fierre's [Opener] class is one of only three in Reizmelt. Other cities usually have an [Informant], [Fence] or [Broker] in that role.
Fierre sleeps six hours a night and needs no more.
Fierre is a Vampire, and Ryoka guesses it after noticing her sharp canines.
Fierre panics when Ryoka asks what being a vampire is like, and begs her not to tell anyone.
Fierre's senses are far beyond Human, and she can read a woman's embroidery or a person's heartbeat from a distance.
Fierre wears a hat and cloth wrappings against the sun, whose rays feel unpleasant on her skin even when weak.
Fierre drinks goat's blood as a snack and feels more Vampirish when she has been exerting herself at night.
Fierre has trouble getting drunk.
Fierre is a Vampire, so she gains no levels, and she thinks of Vampires as animal-like or like the sub-races.
Fierre wishes she had a class, because she knows what Skills such people get.
Old Bamer says Vampire Lords had powers such as turning into mist, and even Skills, but Fierre thinks those might be relics.
Fierre casts no reflection, which is why she does not appear in mirrors.
Modern Vampires live on animal blood, but Fierre and her brother Rivel once bribed a girl for human blood and drank it.
Fierre tasted human blood two more times before her parents found out, and finds it far more satisfying than animal blood.
Human blood did not give Fierre the old Vampire powers or cure her cough.
Fierre believes Vampires are all sick, and notes that her father is sick, her mother has a rash and Bamer is dying.
Fierre says Vampires are few and mostly related, and that Humans must be drunk and not notice how cold she is.
Fierre mixes blood with magical liquor in a shot glass for herself and Ryoka.
Fierre has a brother named Rivel who is the only brother still living at home, and one more who moved away.
Fierre once had a lot of brothers, and she says [Knights] hunted down her family.
Fierre's father Himilt dislikes [Knights], especially old noble houses such as the Byres family, and Fierre calls Orders of [Knights] the worst.
Fierre's father is Himilt and her mother is Colfa, and her family includes her brother Rivel and old Bamer.
Fierre's mother Colfa likes to tell stories of grand Vampire castles and balls, while Himilt says it is better to be people in hiding.
Fierre's family lives in a crumbling castle and herds sheep.
Fierre's parents and Bamer warned her to stay wary around Ryoka, whom they regarded as a stranger.
Fierre's father Himilt told Fierre that Ryoka was someone to watch, though he meant it as a warning.
Fierre says Fluffles the Fourth once carried around a toy she hid at home, until her father found it.
Fierre's mother and father saved up to buy her a bag of holding, and she refuses to discard it even after the potion vomit fouls it.
Ryoka tells Fierre she can be a friend, someone to talk to and someone who can order bloody steaks without suspicion.
Fierre hopes she has made a friend in Ryoka, and thinks she can trust her, even though she cannot learn where Ryoka comes from.
Fierre accepts ten gold coins from Ryoka to find Rose, Imani and Joseph, who Ryoka says are under Magnolia Reinhart's protection.
Fierre has heard from Mad Madain about the adventuring team, and thinks he is grateful to Ryoka.
Fierre once threw Ryoka through a tree by accident while they sparred, and she offers to race Ryoka north at night or to learn fighting moves.
Fierre has no leads on the people Ryoka asked about, as Magnolia Reinhart is surrounded by political waves and many want information.
Fierre says Madain likes her and that his drinking friends only stay for free alcohol.
Fierre calls Madain's fits a monthly event in which he smashes things and curses until he passes out.
Fierre tells Ryoka that most of Izril's [Knights] are lacklustre compared to Terandrian ones, and that Clairei Field is a larger order known for speed.

Fierre obtains a public wanted record for the Stitch Witch Belavierr, listing bounties of eighteen thousand gold in Terandria, twenty thousand from the Slavers of Roshal and three thousand from Wistram.
Fierre panics over Belavierr's bounty, threatens a [Mage] not to reveal her location, and sends a priority [Message] for Ryoka to Filk's Runner's Guild.
Fierre has the [Mage] Gailt ask Daufica Longshel, a [Mage] who doubles as a [Fixer], to act for her for eight gold.
Fierre has Daufica send people to beat the Fence called the Ratwhisperer and burn down his office.
The Ratwhisperer's real name is Jenkil Thert, and Fierre reckons he lacks the clout to fight back.
Fierre visits the hideout of Reizmelt's gang, the bar The Blasted Pyromancer, whose [Bartender] William signals the man in the back.
Fierre tells the gang's [Rogue] that she wants her place safe if the Ratwhisperer escalates, and the gang agrees in return for a tenth of the bounty.

Fierre drafts a file on Riverfarm listing visiting witches, Eloise as a former [Lady] of Terandria, Wiskeria as a Silver-rank adventurer of the Celestial Trackers, and Hedag as [Executioner] and [Witch].
Fierre's file also lists Alevica as the Witch Runner and notes Belavierr as the mother of Wiskeria.
Fierre guesses that Belavierr's curse only strikes those who try to betray her location, since Belavierr never confirmed it herself.
Fierre writes Belavierr's name in her notes and trips the curse, and a hail of needles tears through her iron doors and her body.
Fierre survives with needles in her head and throat, her wounds closing, and Watch guards find her office destroyed.
Fierre forces Gailt to send a [Message] to the Order of Seasons to collect the bounty, saying she has tripped the curse.
The curse burns out once Gailt sends the report, and Terandria replies with a confirmation.
Fierre pulls a needle out of the side of her head and collapses.
Fierre sends word of the dead Ratwhisperer through Nesor to Ryoka in Riverfarm.
Later, Fierre works in a new office with a twice-as-thick enchanted door, since needles destroyed the old one.
Fierre owns her new room, and is fairly rich thanks to her payout from the Order of Seasons.
Fierre sells a regular nondescript client three months of world news and Runner reports.
Fierre talks up Ryoka's exploits to the client, as a way to repay Ryoka.
Fierre's new office lies in a less upstanding part of Reizmelt behind thick, warded stone walls.
Fierre spent over half her gold on a network of three file cabinets, maps, bounty lists, a scrying mirror and a list of favors.
Fierre makes Ryoka give a password before she opens the door when Ryoka returns.
Fierre reports Ogre raids about eighty miles southeast, crossing into Lady Pryde's domain, and Magnolia Reinhart's trade war.
Fierre also reports a [Knight] called the Goblin Slayer who has killed multiple Goblin tribes, though she calls it only a rumor.
Fierre says a team of Wistram [Mages] got beaten near Liscor and that Wistram sent a mass correction of a bounty.
Fierre locates the group Ryoka asked her to find, about eight people, at a city thirty miles south of Reizmelt.
Fierre watches Wistram's broadcast of the siege of Belchan in Reizmelt's Mage's Guild and says the odds are one to eighty-six that Belchan survives.
Fierre says Lord Bel and the Savellian [Knights] are famous for dancing and fight in perfect formations.
Fierre has no scrying orb because most of her money went to rebuilding her shop and getting more contacts.
Fierre says the children Ryoka knew are probably dead from rabbit ambushes south of Reizmelt.
Fierre keeps Teriarch's panacea in her office, afraid it might not be real, and thinks of her family.
Ryoka warns Fierre that other causes may be making Vampires sick, as the panacea only cures symptoms.
Fierre decides to go with Ryoka in the Unmarked Coach, saying she has had enough of being left behind.
Fierre drinks the panacea in the carriage and freezes, and the flash of light knocks Ryoka against the coach walls.
The Unmarked Coach's driver is a bound Djinn whose hands and eyes crackle with fury, and who roars about her chains.
The Djinn driver refuses to let Fierre clean her vomit-soaked bag of holding inside the coach.
Fierre vomits black bile into her bag of holding for about five minutes after drinking Teriarch's cure.
Fierre feels cured, with luminous red eyes, sharper canines, a fluid grace and faster speed, and claims she could break a boulder.
Fierre's face burns like a lobster in a beam of weak sunlight, though the sunburn fades as Ryoka watches.
Fierre wakes screaming from garlic chips, which burn her like pepper spray, and the Brother of Serendipitous Meetings hurls the bag out.
Fierre crosses the ocean to the island by boat and is only seasick, as the water does not stop her.
Fierre and Ryoka spend three days in the Unmarked Coach before reaching the island.
Fierre runs a hundred metres in about six and a half seconds, roughly forty miles an hour, and Ryoka rates her Gold-rank in strength and speed.
Fierre throws Ryoka into the surf, but Ryoka says Fierre is not stronger than Grimalkin or Relc by much.
Fierre says she never levelled and that Vampires do not get Skills.
Fierre carries blood, healing potions, a backup wand firing [Steel-Barb Dart], an enchanted dagger and her notes on Izril.
Fierre judges that the spell she survived was Tier 4, saying Tier 5 can vaporize a person.
Fierre has no reflection, so the mirror-copy trap in the mansion fails to copy her.
Fierre goes insane in the Chamber of Insanity, bites Ryoka's neck and throws her into a wall, and the familiars capture both.
Fierre helps loot gear from the dead intruders, and checks it for traps with Salamani.
Fierre, Ryoka and Salamani decide the trap is a bad delivery and leave, then drunkenly cast spells at the mansion until Valeterisa appears.
Fierre goes home, falls ill within hours of being cured, and ends up feverish, barely breathing and screaming for Ryoka.
Fierre has a high fever, a rash and vomiting, and her family insists Vampires do not get infections.
Fierre has ingested silver, washed in it and recovers through Ryoka's treatment, regaining consciousness.
Himilt says several thousand Vampires live in Izril, in scattered families, settlements and towns.
Himilt says the family cleaned its well with silver and will try charcoal pills, and that it bought breeding pairs from overseas.
Fierre travels with Ryoka and Salamani to Invrisil to see Lady Ieka, after Ryoka's necklace blocks Salamani's [Haste].
Fierre arrives at The Wandering Inn and keeps away from sunbeams, while Erin blocks light for her.
Fierre calls The Wandering Inn far nicer than the inn where she stays in Reizmelt.
Fierre has heard of Erin through her work as an Opener and information broker.
Fierre glances at Lyonette's neck for a second when they meet.
Fierre says two hundred pounds doesn't sound like much, and Ryoka drags her away.
Fierre takes notes constantly and tells Erin she is an Opener and broker.
Fierre sees Montressa and Bezale as rivals through Wistram's secrets, and fears Montressa could put her out of work.
Fierre heard that Maviola El drank a Potion of Youth and rode off a month ago.
Fierre drank Ryoka's blood on the way to Invrisil, so that she could check her own blood was not tainted.
Fierre thinks river-fed animal blood matters less, and says Ryoka's blood tasted fresh.
Fierre feels intense blood hunger around Lyonette, Erin, Salamani and the Callers, which began at her farm.
Flora is a young woman from Texas and a [Gunslinger], a class the narration calls the first of its kind.
Flora has short garnet hair with a hint of copper, and wears denim jeans and a long shirt.
Flora carries a compact revolver with .357 Magnum rounds, five of them, which her father gave her as a birthday present for self-defense.
Flora uses a fast-loader, a device holding bullets ready to insert into the cylinder so she can reload in a heartbeat.
Flora has been told by people who know war that her gun is novel and not all-consuming, since there is only one.
Flora demonstrates her revolver to the last Giants of Rhir, who find it small and loud, and she explains it will change everything.
Flora calls the oldest and tallest Giant Callidaz, after the first part of a name so long she gave up pronouncing it.
Flora is afraid to shoot the gun in war, though she has shot an Adult Creler and watched the bullets ricochet off its armor.
Flora has been found by people who look like her but are called Demons, and she asks the Giants whether she is on the right side.
Flora does not think the Demons who found her are evil, though they have wrath, some conjure hellfire, and they are called Demons.
Flora's guardian and friend is Bazeth, a [Champion of Blades] who carries a glaive.
Silvenia invites Flora to walk with her and see why they call the Demons that name, and Flora nods and walks with the gun in its holster.
Flora shoots Uxel and Ser Vorn from behind a rank of Demons, with shots that dent Ser Vorn's enchanted armor.
Flora uses [Double Tap] to fire two bullets from a single pull at the charging [Knight], and hits his helmet.
Flora uses [A Bullet A Day: Armor Piercing Round] after dropping her fast-loader, and fires a shot at the [Knight].
Cirille sees Ser Vorn fall after the shot, and Flora and Bazeth fall back with the Demons.

The King of Destruction is a warlord whom Ryoka reads about as having conquered a whole continent before his empire suddenly collapsed; the books she read did not say why, and he was neither killed nor apparently harmed.
Ryoka's book says the King of Destruction abandoned his dreams of world conquest and now sits in his crumbling kingdom while other countries pick apart his empire: "The King of Destruction sleeps."
Pisces tells Ryoka that Flos was a king once poised to rule nearly half of the civilized world, who abandoned his kingdom and, he says, has slumbered for ten years in his decaying capital.

Pisces tells Ryoka that the Wistram mages feared him even inactive: a gathering of the greatest living mages listed him as the eighth likeliest disaster to destroy civilization, with a 30% chance that he conquers the world, depending on factors.
An Izril speaker tells Erin that Flos conquered nearly all of Chandrar and that his armies were crossing the sea and landing on Izril's southern shores before he vanished.
Flos is entirely Human, with red-gold hair, a strong nose and a grin, and is a huge man of muscle without fat, apparently over forty but looking in his prime.

Flos is one of the highest-levelled [Kings] in the world, perhaps the highest; his true level is a closely guarded secret and his Skills are all geared to war, making his kingdom prosperous in strife and impoverished otherwise.
Flos likes simple food and eats Yellats stew, a poor man's staple of Chandrar that he grew up enjoying; his servants object to it.
In the Interlude of Book 1, a King awakens a ruined city and its countryside with a roar and the shout that the King of Destruction, Flos, has returned.
Speaking through a stolen chat account, Flos tells Wistram's mages and a thief that he sleeps no longer, that he has returned, and that he will break their towers and unmask those who hide.
Gazi sees Flos, six years older than when she last saw him, still vivid, with golden-red hair faded slightly by age and a body that did not go to fat or decay despite his long slumber.
Gazi recalls a decade in which she and Flos fought together and a decade in which he lay quiet.
Flos roars the Ozymandias lines about king of kings and looks on his works, laughs at them, and wishes to meet the poet.
Flos tells Gazi that when one creates what has never been before, one learns the Skill automatically.
Told that the Emperor of Sands slew Drevish, Flos swears to take the Emperor's head and calls his Seven to war.
Flos wakes in the bed he has slept in for twenty years and rises at dawn from habit.
Remembering what has gone, Flos weeps for six minutes, then dresses and strides out as a King.
Flos likes eating while walking and the bacon rolls the twins introduced, which became a permanent part of the castle's food.
Flos admits to Trey and Teres that he hesitates because he fears war and perhaps lacks the stomach for it after all these years.
Flos tells the twins that he slept twenty years, that not all [Kings] are alike, and that he is a King whose nature pursues war, though he fears its cost.
Flos owns a brooch from Mars that disguises him as an ordinary, slightly shorter man with hazel eyes, grey in dark hair and some flab; it lasts several hours and he toggles it by tapping the gem.
Flos says Orthenon would detect the illusion, and Gazi could see through it, perhaps even without her main eye.
Flos carries five heavy sacks at once in his disguise, with the twins hauling one each.
Flos admits he has left logistics to Orthenon, his [Steward], simply saying 'Orthenon, take care of it' without please.
Flos tells the twins he is a King who must act and cannot hide behind petty tasks.
Sparring with Trey using an unenchanted sword, Flos strikes so hard that the blow knocks Trey flat even though his shield holds.
Flos says he struck Trey harder than he should have, wanting to change the gossip about the twins by having them seen blocking a King's blow.
Flos's own healing potion is clear blue, while the one given to the twins is yellow.
Flos escapes the palace by throwing Trey and then Teres off his balcony and catching them, and takes them by horse though neither can ride.
Flos claims the village of Manimar by torchlight; the villagers recognise him as the King of Destruction, and he asks them to follow him one last time, which they pledge.
Flos's banner is a black flag stitched with gold, bearing a flame of gold, silver, white and purple.
Flos duels Lord Venith with an unenchanted steel sword that bends under the blows and breaks against Venith's shield, then punches, kicks and headbutts him down.

Flos tells the twins he was once a low-level [Prince] of a tiny kingdom, that his father had little time for him, and that only his mother had faith in him; she was disappointed when he took up the sword.
When Orthenon scolds him for the reckless trip, Flos tells him 'Take care of it', then adds 'Please'.

In Venith's flashback of the year before, a young Flos tells him that he cannot be killed by [Assassins] because a vassal would guard him, and that his dream as large as all of Chandrar makes him unbeatable.
In the same flashback, Flos leads a few hundred peasant recruits against the Black Judgment after learning a child's name, Merisa.
In Venith's flashback, Flos says he is done after Queravia and Tottenval are found dead, declaring that the King of Destruction is no more.
Flos recites to Trey a simple poem about the forges roaring one last time and the King awake, and says he made such rhymes for his mother and has only a small gift for rhyming.
Flos asked Teres and Trey to refuse any class offered until they were sure; he thinks Teres suits [Warrior] better than Trey because of attitude.
Flos deliberately separates the twins, telling Mars he wanted them apart from each other more.

Flos has Orthenon, Mars, Gazi and Maresar drill his army; he says his veterans carry arms from Mars but his numbers are too few and his newest recruits very low level, and he makes Maresar lead the archers.
Flos has the twins describe Earth over daily snacks the cooks try to imitate, such as Yorkshire pudding and black pudding, and banned servants who glared at the twins for calling him by name.

Flos tells the twins that the world has an edge where the sea pours into blackness, that only one or two living sailors may have seen it, and that islanders nearest it say things sometimes come from there.
Flos dismisses Alexander the Great as a King who failed his dream and King Arthur as of little weight, and loses interest in Churchill.
Flos is excited by Gandhi's nonviolent tale, but says Gandhi would not succeed against his kingdom.
Flos calls Hitler a great leader but not worthy to be called a man, and says he rejects his ideals.
Flos dislikes guns, since one killed Gandhi, and says he could defeat an army of them in two easy ways.
Flos tells the twins that the more classes one has, the lower the level one will reach, and that a [King] stands above all classes with the strongest Skills.
Flos says the gods are dead and finds the title Son of God arrogant.
Flos tells the twins that lands fade when their [King] abandons them, and that he would declare war for a child or to avenge a fallen comrade but never for land, coin or treasure.
Teres says Flos uses the Skill [Rapid March], which lets an army move twice as fast, and has used it since they left Reim; Flos says they have marched four hours.
Flos leads thousands around the walls of Rast shouting his name every fourth step, asks whose King he is, and the people inside open the gates; he later calls it perhaps a metaphor.
Flos tells Prince Siyal that King Treland was a fool and a monster who treated subjects like animals, and that he went to war for the thousands who died, not for land.
Flos says Calliope has seen war once and knows he would not ransom her son.
Orthenon reports that Reim has 6,256 soldiers, perhaps two thousand more from refugees, while each enemy nation has sent around ten thousand.
Flos names his Seven as Mars, Gazi, Takhatres, Drevish, Amerys, Tottenval and Queravia; Tottenval and Queravia died in the war, and Queravia led his armies rather than Orthenon.
Flos says the largest army he has seen mustered was over four hundred thousand, and that a Goblin King's army is a million Goblins or more.
Seeing slaughtered refugees, Flos orders his horse, tells Mars to hold the city, and rides out with Trey and Teres after Mars cannot disobey his order.
Flos kills a dozen mounted raiders with his sword and tells the twins, 'This is my world. See it with your own two eyes.'
Flos forms the refugees, mostly old retired warriors, into a [Royal Vanguard] charge of about sixty riders.
Flos says he has one Skill he could use if this were an army, but it is not, and he has few activated Skills.
After the battle Flos orders a [Message] to Roshal and the Traders for supplies; Gazi calls the Traders slavers.
Flos sells the battle's captives to the Traders of Roshal, saying slavery is part of Chandrar and comparing it to Earth's imprisonment; Trey objects.
Flos asks about the Tidebreaker General Shivertail, wishes he had met the Goblin King, and has Orthenon told to teach Trey and Teres about that battle.
Flos rides across the sands with the twins and Gazi to a mining town to have a new sword made.
Later, Trey recalls that Flos slumbered for over a decade until two Humans from Earth appeared in his throne room, then woke and recalled his vassals, including the Seven.
After defeating the coalition at Reim, Flos led his army north and conquered Germina and Hellios in under two weeks before winter, leaving Orthenon to manage the conquered kingdoms.
Trey recalls Flos beheading the Quarass in her throne room after she had sent a [Mage] to kill him.
Flos gave away his sword, armor, helmet, lance and rings, including a [Ring of Health] taken from Armil's treasury, when he went into his slumber, and now regrets it.
Flos carries ten thousand gold pieces in a black-and-ruby bag of holding taken from the Quarass's treasury.
Flos explains that Dwarves failed to deliver paid-for arms and instead sent the set of armor and sword that Gazi wears, which proved worth far more than he paid.
Flos addresses the world through a scrying orb, claiming the Empire of Sands as his foe and demanding Wistram return Amerys, while offering not to attack nations that do not attack him.
Flos defeated the coalition with a working of Drevish at Reim, ransomed many soldiers, sold the unbought as slaves to a Trader of Roshal, and then took Germina and Hellios.
In Ger, Flos drops his disguise before the crowd and swears by his Seven and crown to protect the child Quarass, and claims Germina for forty years.
Flos offers the Quarass an alliance; she accepts by Ger's waters and agrees to stop child [Assassins] but keeps her adult ones.
Flos has the Skill [The Choice of the Conquered], which makes those who would never accept him flee; he tells Maresar to hunt them down, preferring captives.
Flos rides to Hellios's capital, Blalevault, in a day using his Skill.
Flos tells Teres that people in his world know the gods to be dead and that Earth's belief may only prove it once had gods.
Flos tells Teres he has devised plans against Earth's weapons, such as a [Pyromancer] disabling combustion, an army of Stitch-People in kevlar, and a request for surrender first.
Flos wants to secure Hellios, notes the Republic of Belchan and Jecrass to the north, and says Takhatres harasses the Empire of Sands.
Flos says he has killed sixteen rulers or, counting some, twenty-three.
Flos returns at sundown with about eight wagons of gold and artifacts, and Nawal sees the legends are true.
Flos inspects Daiton's fine but ordinary pattern-welded sword and smashes Nawal's enchanted blade with a sledgehammer onto a ten-brick bridge, leaving it unharmed.
Flos says his old sword was enchanted, while a Naq-Alrama blade is a mage-killer; he wants a spear for Orthenon, blades for Takhatres and a sword for himself.
Flos tells Trey the Seven also included Drevish, Queravia and Tottenval, and that Tottenval, a Beastkin [Gardener] from Baleros who made Reim bloom, died saving his life.
Flos admits he and Queravia were close; his cup dents in his hand at the mention.
Flos says Wistram is surely holding Amerys, perhaps with three Archmages, that she has not answered, and that he still trusts her.

Flos has three edicts, only one of which can be active: [Edict of Bloom] revitalises land and births at a cost, [Edict of Silversky] makes lies difficult and calms weather, and [Edict of the Blooded] speeds levelling for fighters.
Flos decides to issue the [Edict of Bloom] the next day.

Flos says monarchs gain Skills such as [Blessing of Rains], which guaranteed rain, of which one can be active; he also says units like [Driftwind Riders] need conditions, such as about a hundred enchanted blades for the weakest of his units.
Flos took gold and artifacts from the treasuries of the Quarass and Hellios for his officers.
Flos says he intends a world-wide declaration of peace; the scroll is an 'or else' warning delivered by Runners to rulers.
Flos shows Trey a map of nations that threaten Reim, including Khelt, Belchan, Jecrass, Tiqr, Nerrhavia's Fall, Pomle, Savere, Illivere, Medain and the Claiven Earth.
Flos stands at a window remembering a girl who rode a little elephant decades past.
Flos explains how levels affect Skills, using [Deft Hand] and [Power Strike]; he has promised not to wage war without cause and so cannot aid Tiqr.
Flos burned every picture of Queravia because they could not capture her, as Gazi tells Trey.
Flos orders Mars to return from the southern front and Gazi to join her to intercept an army before holding the western border with Khelt.
Nsiia says Flos told her to wait and live until the day he returns Tiqr to itself.
Flos agrees to let the Quarass tell Fetohep what she will, in exchange for his reasons, planning to tell her anyway.
Flos guesses that Fetohep wants a blood-sworn vow of non-interference and senses Reim's weakness.
Flos tells the Quarass that Trey and Teres come from another world and are the reason he returned.
Flos swore by the Shield Kingdoms, Germina's soil and Ger's Oasis to shed his blood before the Quarass's.
Flos wears plate armor, uses [Rapid March] to move at nearly double speed, and calls the [Royal Vanguard].
Flos tells the twins he could not help Tiqr, that Nsiia lives as a captive of Illivere, and swears to return Tiqr.
Flos waits at Khelt's border at midday with Gazi and says he sent Trey because Gazi took him as a pupil and he is kind and listens.
Flos says he took four thousand Kheltian volunteers in his first war, and Fetohep resents it.
Flos agrees with Fetohep that Khelt will give thirty thousand bushels of food per month for eight years in exchange for his blood oath never to take arms against Khelt.
Flos watches refugees returning to Reim from his balcony, wanting to ride out and greet them until Orthenon and Gazi persuade him to wait.
Flos wants more vassals, arms and artifacts, and says he received a message of inquiry from a potential ally.
Flos tells Orthenon to ask the Iron Vanguard publicly how much to take Wistram, then holds off after Gazi offers a cheaper idea.
Flos watches the Wistram broadcast of Pallass under attack, tells Archmage Feor to return Amerys or he will break the academy, and summons Trey, Teres and Mars.
A narrator says the [Army of the King] is believed to have been granted to Flos at Level 50 and lets him transform any army into a force able to defeat one many levels above.
Flos proclaimed peace, kept his word as Tiqr fell, and demanded free passage to Reim for anyone claiming loyalty.
Facing Raelt's army, Flos has his army roar his title; Jecrass's army and mounts kneel until Raelt resists with 'Steady'.
Flos has green eyes, red-gold hair with no grey, and wears royal attire adapted to the heat.
Flos asks to hunt bandits, cross Jecrass and buy magical horses, but Raelt refuses; he offers Raelt Hellios to join Reim, which Raelt also refuses.
Flos tells Raelt that his army exists only for his protection and exercise.
Flos says he has sworn eternal war on the Empire of Sands and will behead its [Emperor].
Flos gives Raelt a rubik's cube made by one of his vassals.
Flos has loaned Gazi a magic carpet, and Trey travels on one with the Quarass to visit the other Shield Kingdoms.
Flos greets a caravan of several thousand Gnolls led by Chieftain Nelrra, with Lizardfolk, who claim fealty to him.
Flos's [A Kingdom's Strength] is his Level 30 Skill, and Mars says he is stronger than all his Seven; he holds a fifteen-pound sword with one hand.
Flos says that without artifacts he is only about Gold-rank, hating illusions, wall spells, mental attacks and flying foes; his shield's burst is slow.
Flos grants the Gnolls land from Hellios's stone mountains to Reim and the right to build a city, and says Tottenval, a Beastkin of the Fox Tribe, died at sea saving his life.
Flos beheads a Belchan [Headman], a [Commander] and others on live broadcast, then declares war on Belchan and Prime Minister Lyfelt.
Flos fights at the front with a broadsword and a fire-burning shield and cleaves a [Lineholder] through his tower shield.
Flos swears to kill Prime Minister Lyfelt and demands Belchan's politicians and officers; Teres resolves to stop the slaughter of citizens.
Duelling Raelt, Flos throws weapons including a Returning Javelin, hatchet and sword, throws Raelt thirty feet and breaks his ribs and later his leg.
Flos orders a retreat rather than use his [Army of the King]; afterwards he calls Raelt a worthy foe.
Flos says King Raelt is honorable and brave, but that he sheltered the Prime Minister and is backed by Flos's enemies, so he must be fought.
Flos says Raelt levelled after challenging him, and that he too levelled.
Flos gains the Skill [The King's Architect], which summons a memory of Drevish.
Flos plays football with Mars and Orthenon on the Wistram broadcast and sends Joseph a [Message] asking for the rules.
Flos survives a rapier through the heart by smashing a healing potion into the wound, kills Winta, and runs back into the fight.
Flos tells Teres he hopes Medain will declare war, so he can take it and then deal with the Claiven Earth, and he fears fighting half-Elves in trees.
Flos marches his army by [Rapid March] toward Medain, claiming to demand Princess Jecaina's return.
Flos's navy was nearly destroyed by Minotaurs in the past; Tottenval's sacrifice saved him.
Flos tells Teres the Minotaurs attacked him at sea though he avoided them.
Flos orders Orthenon to flank the Minotaurs and recognises Ozem's armor from the sea battle.
Flos uses [Army of the King] when Teres falls, giving her eight levels as a Level 35 Trained Bladeswoman with temporary Skills.
Flos's Skill [Army of the King] is expected to be unavailable for a crucial month after use.
Flos orders Takhatres recalled from the Empire of Sands to safeguard the borders.
Flos says that the last time so many nations declared war on him was when he unified most of Chandrar.
Flos assigns Mars to give magical blades to Ytol's Sorcelled Blades, to be led by Orthenon.
Flos gives the Nomads of the Sky to Ytol and keeps Esiela under blood-oath near him.
Flos swears to avenge the Gnolls by killing Lyfelt, and says he will offer Raelt's daughter one chance.
Flos orders Mars, Orthenon and the Nomads to take a border city of Medain without killing civilians.
The Flying Queen is an Antinium Queen whose Flying Antinium are designed for aerial superiority.
The Flying Queen's Hive is normally a chaos of Antinium moving around her, with winged attendants buzzing about.
The Flying Queen's creations show originality but lack of focus.

section: Book 15: contact with the Free Queen
text: The Flying Queen contacts the Free Queen by mirror while her Hive is in uproar, and asks whether the Free Queen's Bird is a challenge.

section: Book 15: contact with the Free Queen
text: The Flying Queen worries that ranged Antinium might be an overture to the Armored Antinium, and that the Grand Queen is punishing the Free Queen.

section: Book 15: contact with the Free Queen
text: The Flying Queen asks why the Free Queen's food is so colorful and whether it is a new nutritional mix.

section: Book 15: contact with the Free Queen
text: The Flying Queen calms as the Free Queen explains that Bird is a single Individual and not an attempt to jeopardize her Hive.

section: Book 15: contact with the Free Queen
text: The Flying Queen says the tunnel is completed, as Pivr tells her, and agrees to talk.

section: Book 15: contact with the Free Queen
text: The Flying Queen asks why the Armored Queen sent Prognugators before the Flying Antinium did.
The Flying Queen has yet to get any of her Antinium to fly, but assures Klbkch that she will soon.
The Flying Queen plans to give her Soldiers thorn-projectiles in place of their acidic bile.
The Flying Queen says the Walled Cities will fall if her Hive bypasses their walls with flight.
The Flying Queen says flight will allow the Antinium to return to Rhir, and plans for them to fly across the sea with wings.
Klbkch finds the Flying Queen innovative but disinclined to do more than encourage her to work with the Free Queen.
The Flying Queen shows Klbkch a stuttering Worker from her own Individual experiments, which can say "I" only after several attempts.
The Flying Queen says the stuttering Worker has no name yet, but she believes she will create Individuals in time.
Foliana is a Squirrel Tribe Beastkin known by the title Three-Color Stalker, the leader of the Forgotten Wing Company, Niers's boss and oldest friend.
Foliana is the world-famous assassin Three-Color Stalker and head of the Forgotten Wing Company, one of the Four Great Companies of Baleros.
Three-Color Stalker is a [Rogue] of the highest order, a legend few have ever seen, whose talents make most [Assassins] envious.
Magnolia Reinhart calls Three-Color Stalker one of the most deadly [Rogues] in existence, better at slaying enemy [Commanders] than most conventional [Assassins].
Foliana is a [Rogue] who hides, steals things and has no sense of personal privacy, and she is in charge of the company without managing it, which is Niers's job.
Her pupils are three colours, bright red-pink, deep yellow and clear green, set in a single iris, and the rest of her is so unremarkable that she fades into her chair.
Foliana can turn invisible if she chooses, and Niers explains that this is a Skill mixed with her own talent, not magic, so a [Mage]'s warning devices do not catch it.
Later her fur is greying, with dark stripes of colour down her sides.

She is exceptionally high-level and can vanish at will, and the staff assigned to wait on her and Niers are screened for phobias and heart defects because three earlier staff members died of heart attacks.
Foliana steals compulsively: she took Peclir's seal and Niers's comb, and she takes students' inkpots, lunches and grapes.
Foliana eats muffins, tea bags and candle wax.
She eats Damcli Noodles, a Dullahan favourite that resembles spaghetti with meatballs, and has a third bowl of it.
She dislikes oysters but eats them for days when they are a target's favourite food.
When Three-Color Stalker eats a target's favourite food, it is understood that she is aiming for that person; Niers says she does it to show off and warn her target.
It is rumoured that she has killed thousands and eats her victim's favourite food first.
When she eats the same kind of food for days on end she is marking her prey, and the pattern can run from a single meal to weeks or months.
A blackberry jam biscuit prepares her for a contract.
Foliana snacks on walnuts dipped in honey while watching a broadcast, which is a favourite snack and not a contract.
Magnolia Reinhart sends Foliana letters every month, and she receives a letter and a muffin with blueberries, which she eats despite Niers's fear of poison.
Foliana refused to take the Forgotten Wing Company across the sea to Izril against the Goblin King because she dislikes water, and she reasoned she would die before she scratched him.
She bargained companies into crossing the sea to Izril with an offer of a muffin made of gold, plus a few baskets.
It is Niers's and Foliana's custom to take a very hot bath after a campaign, naked, as water hot enough to scald kills leeches and parasites.
Foliana reads Niers's secret note, finds it obvious and good, and runs off invisible with it to show his students.
Foliana tells Niers he is lonely and afraid to meet someone like himself in case he is disappointed.
Niers says Foliana is a better leader than he is in a way, that no one can predict how the company will jump with her at its head, and that they have known each other for over fifty years.
Asked by Niers whether she wants children or another life, Foliana answers that she does not, because the citadel, the city and the company are all hers.
Foliana says squirrels are born deaf and blind and that she would be a poor mother.
Foliana keeps multiple rooms of her own, including one with magically grown grass and trees that Archmage Nailihuaile was paid to enlarge, where she lies in a hammock.
Foliana sips from Niers' tea cup and says she is on holiday while he works.

Speaking to a crowd, Foliana recounts that the Gambler of Fates, Queravia, landed at Zaland, killed Grandmarshal Sorolat and defeated Three-Color Stalker, and that a Fraerling, the Forgotten Wing's second-in-command, brought the companies together to break her; one survived.
Foliana adds that an army from Rhir broke the Lord of the Skies and his tribes and that a Minotaur fleet humbled the King of Destruction's forces at sea.
Niers describes himself as a former Named Adventurer and second-in-command of one of the Great Companies of Baleros.
Ken says the Forgotten Wing Company is considered fragile because people think it would fall apart if the Titan and Three-Color Stalker died.
In Wil Kallinad's scene, Foliana erases his memory of Niers' answer with an [Erase Memory] scroll, eats the paper he wrote on, and hands him a letter that explains.
Foliana hires a room for seven students at a brothel, the Scaleless Sight, and she and her two companions throw buckets of cold water on guests.
Foliana says peace in her city and company is hers.
At the brothel, a Naga from the Assassin's Guild in Izril, posing as an employee, intends to plant a gauntlet with five glowing orbs; Foliana kills her.
Foliana hides the Naga's corpse in her bag of holding, pours a potion over the blood, and sends a [Message] to Peclir Im about the Dullahan.
Foliana watches the world's broadcast in front of a scrying mirror while Niers goes back to his chess game.
Foliana and Niers wait four days on flying carpets over the battlefield, then drop alchemical weapons that break the Dullahan lines before the Bannermare charges at Tulm the Mithril.
The Fool is the royal [Fool] of the Blighted King, a small man in a colorful costume who entertains the court and its children.
The Fool says his class is rare and there is scant work for a [Fool] in hungry villages, and he has served the Blighted King for over a decade.
Before coming to Rhir, the Fool was a noted entertainer who travelled across Baleros and Terandria performing grand feats.
Nobles at court think the Fool is high-level.
The Fool juggles seven balls at once, weaving them into a double pattern.
The Fool juggles twelve balls in the garden when Tom is seated with the nobles.
The Fool has a Skill that copies objects, and the copies last a while if handled gently.
The Fool says his copy Skill is good for pranks and trickery, and not for much else.
The Fool has a magic scroll for talking to people, which he rolls up when Tom and the Princess approach.
Tom cannot hear the voice in his head whenever he is near the Fool.
The Fool performs for the Princess and other children, and Erille asks Tom whether he can backflip as the Fool can.
The Fool tells Tom that a plague killed the royal household's other daughter, and that the plague was thought sent by the Demons.
The Fool tells Tom that the royal household once had seven members, and that two sons died in battle.
The Fool tells Tom that assassins killed the last Queen and the one before that.
The Fool tells Tom he was talking to his true love back in the courtyard by scroll.
A Demon slashes the Fool's belly open, the Fool grips the Demon, and the Demon kicks the Fool in the face.
The Fool is taken hostage during the attack, and the nobles say he is regrettably injured.
The Fool says the Demons are not right but are not wrong either, since they fight to live.
The Fool and the Demon teleportation [Mage] stare at one another, and Tom realises the Fool loves her.
Tom holds the Fool at the edge of the battlements as a hostage, and the Fool tells him the Demon mage will not betray her mission for him.
The Fool falls from a tower, lands on his feet, and breaks Nereshal's nose with a thrown juggling ball.
The Fool declares himself the world's greatest [Fool] and says he seeks the Blighted King's life for the king's sins and his own.
The Fool fights the royal guards with daggers, tripping Richard and tripping the Blighted Queen with a thrown juggling ball.
The Fool grabs a fireball and makes it vanish, keeping it hidden in a space of his own.
The Fool catches Nereshal's lightning in his hand, juggles it, and throws it back, knocking Nereshal out.
The Fool holds a knife to the Blighted King's throat and demands the king tell everyone what he did.
The Fool says he could understand the king's war crimes, but never the ritual and its cost.
Tom throws a knife at Erille to distract the Fool, who catches it and throws the daggers back at the king and Tom.
Tom kills the Fool with the Fool's own hidden fireball, after telling him he is a fool and Tom is a clown.
The dying Fool says he turned on the king the day after the ritual, when he learned the cost behind Tom's summoning.
The Fool explains the ladies wear crimson for the lost, because the miscarriages were the price and not a curse.
The Fool says ten thousand unborn souls were sacrificed to summon sixty Americans.
The Fool says the king wants a hundred thousand sacrifices next time, and a million if that fails.
The dying Fool asks Tom to protect Erille and take her away.
The Free Queen is the Queen of the Free Antinium hive beneath Liscor, a massive creature who sits in a dark cavern.
In Book 1 she is a large female Antinium in the darkness whom Klbkch addresses as "my lady" and "my Queen".
She calls Klbkch her Propugnator and champion, and addresses him as "Klbkchhzeim of the Free".
Erin sees the Queen as gargantuan and bloated, so huge she cannot move from her spot, and completely insectile unlike her humanoid-looking subjects, with wide faceted eyes that glow dim orange-red.
Two silent guard Antinium nearly twice Klbkch's size flank the doors, with massive forearms and spiked gauntlet-like arms and no real digits.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: Klbkch asks the Queen to let ten or twenty Workers visit a local inn for several hours, and she asks whether the idea is his own.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: The Queen tells Klbkch the Others are moving, speaking of envoys and an army, and allows the risk: he may take twelve Workers to visit the Solstice child.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: The Queen tells Klbkch she needs success, warns that the Plan has faltered too long and that if the next generations fail more Antinium will fall back into the old ways.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: The Queen asks Klbkch how the acid flies taste, and he promises to bring her a sample.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: Below Liscor the Queen senses the events at the inn, sends her soldiers marching to the surface at her command, and whispers "Klbkchhzeim?".

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: After Klbkch's death, the Queen has Erin brought before her and says she holds Erin accountable for the death.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: The Queen says Klbkch's death in itself means little because individuals die in service to the whole, but that dying to Goblins was wasted, and that Klbkch was more than a match for a hundred Goblins.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: The Queen tells Erin she sees no reason Klbkch would have wasted his life saving her, and says he died a failure.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: The Queen complains that her Workers play games in their rest periods and gain useless levels, and that three have already become Aberration, calling this experiment wasted.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: Hearing what Klbkchhzeim told Erin, the Queen calls him a fool as well as a failure and says the Antinium are not free.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: Far below Liscor, the Queen is busy on a project that needs all her attention, and orders the Antinium reporting to her to deal with the Council while she finishes.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: The Queen tells her Prognugator to investigate the aberration on the surface, and he promises to dispose of any Aberrations he finds.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: Relc says the Queen spoke of "time lost" and needless valuable resources expended when speaking with the Captain, but never about Klbkch.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: Ksmvr tells Zevara that the Queen is in the middle of a critical process, hours or less from completion, and that the Antinium will cooperate in defending the city once she finishes the Rite of Anastases.

section: Book 1: Klbkch, the inn and the Aberrations
text: Later, Ksmvr finds the Soldiers streaming back out of the Hive, the Queen having finished the Rite and returned, and he feels her anger in his mind.

section: Book 2 and the rivalry with the Great Queen
text: In Book 2 Ksmvr reports to the Queen, who is called the Queen of the Free Antinium within Liscor, and who thinks of him as inexperienced and not Klbkch.

section: Book 2 and the rivalry with the Great Queen
text: The Queen says it seems Klbkchhzeim was correct that Erin Solstice is needed for now.

section: Book 2 and the rivalry with the Great Queen
text: She regards Erin as important but not vital, since the Individuals can be replicated, and so the Antinium can continue the experiment.

section: Book 2 and the rivalry with the Great Queen
text: Rivalry exists among the Queens: the Free Queen has endured the ridicule and scorn of her fellow Queens for years and expects the Great Queen to learn of her success.

section: Book 2 and the rivalry with the Great Queen
text: She is in sore need of another assistant but is barred from making another Prognugator or Queen by the Great Queen and the pact made with Liscor.

section: Book 2 and the rivalry with the Great Queen
text: She thinks Pawn has levels in [Tactician], perhaps not as high as her own.

section: Book 2 and the rivalry with the Great Queen
text: Klbkch has argued for years that adventurers should help with the dungeon, thought he had convinced the Queen after Skinner, and finds she wants one Named Adventurer and twice as many Gold-rank ones.

section: Book 2 and the rivalry with the Great Queen
text: Klbkch thinks the Queen is old and might need the Rite of Anastases, which would require bringing her to another Queen.

In Book 4 the Queen receives envoys of four Hives: Prognugator Tersk with three Armored Antinium, Revalantor Pivr of the Flying Antinium with six, two Silent Antinium soldiers, and Xrn of the Centenium, now Prognugator to the Grand Queen.
Xrn tells Klbkch that the Queen has no resources, denied to her by the Hives, and is surprised she managed to alter his form, let alone resurrect him.
Klbkch tells Xrn that the needed reagents can be obtained, with difficulty, by purchasing from [Alchemists].
Klbkch tells the Queen what Xrn told him: that the Grand Queen is not trying to create more Queens, which breaks her faith in the Antinium on Izril.
The Queen drags herself down a tunnel no Antinium but Klbkch enters, past airtight rooms she built for mixing enzymes and reagents.
One room holds corpses and embryos of failed experiments; the Queen rediscovered the Rite of Anastasis there, used it to save Klbkch's life, and created Ksmvr there.
The Queen begins experiments to create a new Queen, using her own eggs, vowing to sacrifice her Hive and body if she must.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: The Queen speaks through Klbkch by a link that works through rock and water, so that when she speaks he speaks and she hears what he hears.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: Through Klbkch, the Queen tells Zevara the Antinium first became aware of the dungeon a few months ago.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: Klbkch states for the Queen that the agreement between Liscor's Council and the Free Antinium exempts the Hive from Liscor's legal restrictions and that the dungeon would not count as Liscorian property.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: She has lived in the Hive for over a decade, can feel thousands of Antinium around her, and she and Klbkch have labored for a decade toward true individuality.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: The Queen considers the Individuals who failed her test incomplete, not true Antinium and not people, only useful tools for Klbkch and herself.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: The Queen is lonely, since only Klbkch keeps her company and only two real Antinium are in the Hive.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: She eats cooked food prepared by Garry, savouring a fried Shield Spider abdomen stuffed with lentils and egg after a decade of eating the Antinium's paste, and likes roast pork.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: She has a sealed, airtight chamber for her experiments, with sacks of fluid on the wall holding failed creations.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: She tells Klbkch she spent four years reconfiguring muscle fibre and two more on balance to build his new form, and will not mass-produce it because it takes too much work and too many resources.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: She calls the Flying Queen's Antinium forms flawed, and says the Silent Queen has improved on her designs.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: She says alchemical goods are too complex to work with without rendering.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: The Queen declares Bird a flawed creation whose mind is broken, assumes an imperfection in the growing stage caused it, and says it was not his fault.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: She lifts Bird in her feelers and tightens them until his carapace cracks, but when he sings she freezes and loosens her grip, having heard no song in the Hive since coming to Izril.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: She tells Bird she finds him worthy and will allow him to live in her chambers and sing for her each day.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: She thinks that Bird may be close to Galuc the Builder, or unique.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: She gives Bird a bag of holding full of gold coins to buy a bow.

section: Book 8: Bird, Garry and the sealed chambers
text: A vessel delivered by the Grand Queen restores contact and the Free Antinium are told they have made adequate progress and will rejoin the larger Hive through this relay.
In Book 9, Drones with six feelers and no arms tend an injured Bird, using gels and a living blood sac designed as a store of organs for the Queen to harvest.
The Queen has learned Garry's name and been kinder to him, and gives him time off to visit the inn on condition that he bring back the choicest morsels.
She eats Garry's pizza, sweet potato hamburgers and cake, saying chemical imbalances were allowed in Galuc's modified form but not in Queens, and tastes concentrated sugar for the first time.
She tells Bird the Antinium will fail on purpose to destroy more than one or two trebuchets, since Klbkch must speak only truths to Drakes who use truth-detection spells.
She says that when the Hive must be defended, Pawn will lead the Painted Soldiers and other Antinium in to move Liscor's citizens into it.
When the Painted Soldiers march to save Erin, the Free Queen denies ordering it, and then pretends she cannot hear the Grand Queen's orders over a malfunctioning vessel and scrying glass.
In Book 11 the Queen tests Bird and Garry a second time on the purpose of the Antinium, and Bird's answer is judged wrong.
She explains that the test is not about the question but about hearing the answer she thinks, which she can send to them through her feelers, while they can only be heard.
The Free Queen states that the purpose of the Antinium is to return to Rhir, destroy the thing in the darkness and avenge the Antinium, in the name of "her".
The Free Queen tells Bird and Garry that she was a barely created Junior Queen on the fleet sent to take Terandria.
The fleet's troops were sealed in stasis aboard ships and died asleep, pursued by Rhir's warships, then attacked by pirates, then storms, and then a Kraken.
Sixteen of the Centenium died there, Klbkchhezeim lost his true form, and fewer than twenty juniors landed on Izril.
Her mentor Bessachidia, a Shaper Queen who could weave forms as well as any but the First Queen, was her teacher and one of the finest Queens ever created.
In Book 14, when Klbkch leads wounded Antinium against Flesh Worms and Ghouls, she takes direct control and speaks "Forwards!" into their minds.
Klbkch tries a Skill he lost in the Rite of Anastases and stumbles; the Free Queen directs each Worker and Soldier individually.
She is at least four decades old, was newly formed when she left Rhir, and learned shaping from Bessachidia alongside the Silent Queen.
She sees through Klbkch's eyes, and the Free Antinium have been in exile for nearly a decade.
The Grand Queen argues that Bird is a Prognugator; the Free Queen replies that the Individual and Autonomous Antinium need no Antinium lives for their formation.
She suspects the Silent Queen thinks she is withholding experimental designs that let Bird hit the Wyverns, and that other Queens misunderstood Bird.
After a decade of neglect, the other Hives now look on the Free Antinium with wariness or approval.
In Book 16, Bird asks the Free Queen if Garry may come with him; she says "Go, little bird".
In Book 18 the Free Queen spends three days in her laboratory while Xrn, Yellow Splatters, Pawn, Belgrade and Purple Smiles run the Hive, and Garry's helpers Pisca and Runel are Flying Antinium.
She feels this is how the Queens of Rhir once lived and that she is being treated like royalty.
Klbkch notes she is still experimenting with creating new Queens, while the Grand Queen says none of the remaining Queens are Shaper Queens and refuses to waste resources on it.
Gaile is a [Witch Hunter] from Terandria who carries an axe and fights in Ser Raim's band against Belavierr.
Gaile was formerly a [Beastslayer] who became a [Witch Hunter] for vengeance, according to Ser Raim.
Gaile says Belavierr is the reason she buried her own daughter.
Ser Raim says he and Gaile sought Belavierr for six years.
Gaile runs at Ryoka and Wiskeria and demands that Belavierr hold or her daughter dies, with a needle buried in her cheek.
Gaile presses her axe into Wiskeria's neck, drawing blood, and tells Ser Raim that nobody there can stop her blade.
Gaile says that she is tired of the chase and that this is the chance to take Belavierr's daughter from her.
Gaile apologises to Wiskeria, who did not choose her mother.
Gaile shoves Wiskeria aside and strikes at Belavierr with a Skill, only lightly parting Belavierr's robes with the axe.
Belavierr crushes Gaile's neck and ribs with her hand, driving her body down, and Gaile dies.
Gaile admits that her threat goes against Ser Raim's pride and honor, and she accepts she will die if she swings.
Ser Raim says afterward that without Gaile's actions Belavierr might have been lost again.
The Order of Seasons carries Gaile's ashes away with those of the other fallen Hunters.
Galina is a young woman from Earth who loves the theatre and is one of the seven Earthers staying at The Wandering Inn.
Galina performed Macbeth twice back in high school.
Galina asks Relc whether the Players know Wicked, Phantom of the Opera, Mean Girls and Chicago, while sitting at the back of the inn.
Galina says she knows many plays and musicals, including Anastasia and To Kill a Mockingbird, though not perfectly, and asks how Erin remembered them.
Galina, too shy to confess her addiction to theatre, bonds with Relc and Temile over the stage.
Galina pitches A Doll's House to Emme, Andel and Temile, arguing Jasi should not be cast as the lead.
Galina wants an older woman who can speak to unhappy married women as the lead, and Emme suggests Yaina.
Galina says she cannot write the script out well because she lacks Erin's memory and hopes Andel can polish it.
Emme and Andel agree to try A Doll's House in the inn, and Emme says hiring Galina was never in doubt.
Galina is hired by the Players, and the narration says she belongs there as her Earther friends split up.
Galina asks Rose to help brainstorm plays to adapt, and says she wants to act rather than just produce.
Galina says some plays, such as Angels in America, do not work because they are too tied to home.
Klbkch tells Pawn that Galuc was one of the Centenium, called the Builder, and that it is Galuc's form that all the Antinium wear.
Klbkch says his own original form was lost when he died at sea, while Galuc's was saved and remains in each Antinium, smaller and weaker.
Klbkch knew Galuc, who felt great emotion and never broke or gave in, even at the end.
The Queens believed in a false version of Galuc and did not think copies of him have morale.
Gamel is a young villager who becomes Laken's follower, and later his [Knight].
Gamel was buried upside down in the snow and dug out by Laken, who told him he was safe.
Gamel did not know the voice that rescued him although he knew everyone in the village.
Gamel's father died in the snow, his neck snapped in the tumble.
Gamel feels ashamed of having thrown things at Durene when she was a child, and part of him is still afraid of her.
Gamel has followed Laken and Durene around since the day of the avalanche and waits outside Durene's cottage.
Laken chose Gamel to accompany him as a helper to Durene, someone who could talk to guards.
Laken and Durene expected to meet Gamel at midday in the plaza, but did not see him early.
Gamel calls Laken "sire" and reports what he sees in the plaza.
Laken had sent Gamel to approach adventurer teams in the plaza and beg for help.
Gamel walks with Laken's caravan and sometimes sits on the wagon, one of Laken's subjects.
Laken believes Gamel knows some fire magic and asks him to request mages to melt the snow.
Gamel was cut across the chest by a Hobgoblin's longsword when he pushed Laken aside.
Gamel survived the night, while those Laken called back from the grave died.
Later, Gamel is Laken's [Knight], and Laken saved his life by ordering him to live.
Laken says Gamel waits outside the gate to attend to him, which Laken tells him not to do.
Gamel announced Laken at the gathering as Protector of Riverfarm and Durene's Cottage.
Gamel was a [Farmer] until a few weeks earlier and is not of noble birth, so some Knights resent him.
Members of the Clairei Fields Order have been teaching Gamel personally.
Gamel is one of three bodyguards of the Emperor, alongside a wand carrier and an archer.
Garen Redfang is a Hobgoblin and Chieftain of the Redfang tribe who rides a rust-red Carn Wolf.
Garen's second name Redfang comes from the enchanted red blade he carries, and Garen is the name he claimed himself.
Garen says he is fourteen years old, which Tremborag calls old for a Goblin and young for anything else.
Garen speaks Human fluently, and he is called a famous legend whose name Goblins know.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: The Red Fang Tribe's Chieftain, a Hob Goblin, leads sixty Goblins riding rust-red giant Carn Wolves and carries a red sword.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: Garen is a tall Goblin, around the height of a normal Human man and not particularly big for a Hob, covered in battle scars, with a gaze like a red beacon.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: Garen's name is Garen, and Rags thinks of him as a legend in his own right.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: Garen's sword is red-forged and far too well made for a Goblin.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: Garen, the Red Fang Chieftain demands in the Goblin tongue that Rags submit to his tribe or die, Rags refuses, and he attacks.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: Garen takes an arrow in the shoulder without blinking, and the arrowhead snaps off, which Rags takes to mean he has some kind of skill.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: As Rags marches her tribe away he strikes it eight more times that day and again on the following days, until over a hundred Goblins are lost and half again as many wounded.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: Garen stops his wolf at the last moment before a gorge where Rags has hidden boom bark and turns away, and he spots every ambush team she sets.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: Garen, the Red Fang Chieftain is warlike but not stupid, and he avoids fighting head-on.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: In the duel both Chieftains hear a scream of a thousand Goblin lives saying that this is Goblin, while Rags also hears the voice of a King telling her "This is not who we are".

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: Rags rolls into a pit, he leaps after her and is struck by a stake, and she breaks a jar of acid over both of them, then heals him with her last potions.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: Garen, the Red Fang Chieftain tells Rags she is Chieftain, that the Red Fang Tribe will submit, and orders both tribes to stop fighting.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: Rags says afterwards that he let her win, and she is certain she should not have won even with a thousand Goblins against his sixty.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: Garen speaks in the Human tongue and says he learned it long ago when he was an adventurer, claiming he became the strongest of a special party that trusted him and then killing them.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: Garen says he came to find a Chieftain to unite the tribes against a great enemy to the south, a bad Goblin, the Goblin Lord.

section: First meeting and the duel with Rags (Book 2)
text: Garen is the leader of his tribe and of several hundred miles of territory north of Liscor, and he calls Rags "Chieftain" the next day despite having part of his face melted off in the fight.
Garen was named by the Shaman of the Old Fire Tribe, and he wandered away from his tribe as soon as he grew older.
Garen levelled quickly as a [Warrior] and became a Hob, terrorising a stretch of land far to the north alone.
A team of adventurers hunted Garen down and nearly killed him, but its leader spared his life and chased him away.
Garen disguised himself in robes and a crude mask and listened to Humans in villages and towns, and learned to speak the Human language.
Garen challenged the adventurers a second time, lost again, and then volunteered to join them, becoming the first Goblin to journey with adventurers.
Garen's team explored dungeons and progressed to Gold-rank status, and Garen got his sword during this time.
Garen met Jelaqua when he killed an Eater Goat that adventurers wanted, while posing as a Bronze-rank adventurer.
Jelaqua invited Garen into the Halfseekers, introducing a team that was a band of misfits, and Garen gave only his name.
Garen had been a Halfseeker for about a year when his memory of Jelaqua asking which way to go takes place.
Garen was the newest member of the Halfseekers and felt out of place, though he often argued over equipment with Seborn.
Jelaqua and Moore recall that Garen was Silver-rank when he hid in a forest with Halassia and attacked a prison with illusion spells.
In Redfang legend, their Chieftain once walked through Human cities masked and hooded, and spoke with Humans.
Garen was Gold-rank for a time and the only Goblin to hold that rank, but he has since lost most of his artifacts in fights.
Garen has no levels in [Chieftain] or [Leader], and his idea of leadership is leading a few handpicked warriors into combat.
Garen is a [Dragoon], a unique class combining [Warrior] and [Rider], and he is also a [Beast Tamer].
Jelaqua says Garen is a [Rider] and [Warrior] who has magical artifacts like any Gold-rank adventurer.
Garen owns a ring against arrows, a ring against poison, and a sword that glows white-hot at a command word.
Garen claims he is more than a match for any single Gold-rank adventurer, even with magical items.
Garen's thick skin turns aside even sharp blades, and Rags judges him Gold-rank in strength.
Garen uses [Deeper Cut] to shear the face off a Shield Spider.
Garen has [Raider] skills that let him appraise targets.
Garen uses [Blur Dodge] and [Frenzy Cuts] against a [Rogue] and Greydath.
Garen carries an enchanted amulet and the sword Redfang.
Redfang glows with white flames and turns transparent, passing through enchanted armor and a carapace.
The transparent blade passes through non-living material but fails against Greydath's greatsword.
Garen rides a Carn Wolf twice as large as any other Carn Wolf.
Garen's Carn Wolf has no name, though it has been his companion for over two years, and Garen has buried four earlier wolves.
Garen's tribe formed because Goblins wandered to his camp like moths to a flame, and he let them stay.
Garen took his tribe by finding the biggest local tribe and challenging its Hob Chieftain, who fled.
Garen later tells Rags that he is stronger than she is but cannot lead like her.
Rags learns that Garen only partly grew his tribe himself.
Garen says level up cannot be without pain and tells Rags she can level by training slowly.
Garen tells Rags to choose one class path rather than level in many.
Garen raids covered wagons rather than Runners, and avoids conflicts with adventurers.
Garen points out a thin City Runner as an easy target and a big slow Runner as strong enough to punch hard.
Garen explains that a Goblin Lord is the enemy to the south and says the Goblin Lord is wrong.
Garen offers Rags an albino wolf pup, and she refuses because a white wolf is a target.
Garen and Rags disguise themselves as travellers and walk to The Wandering Inn.
Garen watches the sledge head north from a hill, and smiles to himself about when Rags will return to her tribes.
Garen wanted to burn the entire city down, calling Rags's approach soft and weak despite her victory.
Garen orders the warriors not to tell Rags, though he was not the Chieftain, and says he would kill himself rather than join the Goblin Lord.
Garen threw his fight with Rags and the Goblins know it.
Rags knows Garen threw the fight, though by Goblin custom she should have taken his tribe and his loyalty.
Garen still gives orders to his tribe while Rags makes sure the warriors are fed.
Garen kills a Hob of Tremborag in a quick duel, and his tribe is angered by the captive women.
Garen answers the grumbling of his tribe with a message that tells them to "Deal with it."
The Redfang Goblins guard the mountain because of their combat prowess.
Garen stays in the mountain and hopes Rags is running far because she could still be useful.
Jelaqua says Garen's Redfang tribe is a Goblin tribe near the High Passes that is a danger to Gold-rank adventurers.
Garen stalks Tremborag's mountain with his red blade, and several fatal duels established his rank there.
Garen hates Tremborag but acknowledges his might, and he says he will never kneel to the Goblin Lord.
Part of the Redfang tribe stayed behind with Garen after the others joined Rags.
Rags took over two thirds of Garen's warriors and many tribes he had gathered when she left the mountain, calling him no true Goblin.
Garen storms at Tremborag when over twenty Hobs and a [Shaman] die in the failed attack on a Human mansion.
Garen forbids further raids on that place, and his faction in the mountain grows.
Garen finds the Valerund mansion deserted and burns it, then destroys a town to the north and robs it of gold from a mine.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen carries a black key like onyx that he took at the bottom of a dungeon, and says it is the key the last Goblin King wanted.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen killed many of his fellow adventurers when they refused to let him have the key.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen says the hiding place of the treasure is death beyond death, too dangerous even for the old Goblin King to reach.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen tells Rags that the adventurers who spared him were half or part Human, different like him.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen touches a little key hidden behind his armor, and Tremborag says he knows what Garen has.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Tremborag and Garen agree to fight together against the Goblin Lord after Garen shows the key.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Tremborag says the Goblin King was Velan the Kind, last King of the Goblins.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen's tiny key lets him remember that Velan the Kind hid a secret.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen senses the Goblin Lord coming like a bonfire growing brighter, and says the Goblin Lord is drawn to the Goblins in the mountain.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Tremborag and Garen agree to bar the gates and wait for the Goblin Lord.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen leads the Redfang Warriors down the slopes in raids, and attacks Reiss's mount in an ambush that fails.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Tremborag takes three [Deathbolt] spells from Reiss.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen leads two or three raids on the Goblin Lord's army without needing Skills before the army entrenches.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen flees with the Redfang Warriors after looting Gold-rank bodies, suspecting the attack is a trap inside a trap.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen is startled at seeing Greydath, whom he thought was dead.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen arrives on a Carn Wolf carrying his famous red blade, and Redscar and the Redfangs in Rags's tribe face their old Chieftain.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen shouts that Reiss is a slave who betrayed Goblinkind.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Reiss publicly says Garen holds the key to the legacy of Velan the Kind, hidden in the High Passes.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen clutches something at his belt and denies it, and all the Goblins agree he is a terrible liar.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen has about eight hundred Goblins wearing the red stripes that mark them as his tribe.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Reiss says Garen refused to accept that the Goblin with magic had a master, and swore to oppose him if they met.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen tells Rags he opposes Reiss because of the undead, and Reiss says Velan the Kind hated undead.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Reiss tells the Goblins that Garen slaughtered half the Halfseekers and fled, and killed them for the key.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen answers that the Halfseekers were never his tribe and never believed he was one of them.

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen keeps a small key at his side, and tells Spiderslicer "Other one missing."

section: The Goblin Lord and Velan's key
text: Garen believes Velan the Kind went to the High Passes to hide a great treasure.
Garen watches the battle, then rides at Rags's fleeing Goblins and shouts for them to join him against the Goblin Lord.
Garen's bid to take Rags's scattered Goblins fails because they run around him, and he sees they have refused him.
Garen realises that Tyrion Veltras is stronger than he is by a bit.
Garen thinks Rags's tribe should have gone to him after Tremborag's death.
Garen's tribe kills three Human commanders and escapes on Carn Wolves with horses.
Garen leaves for the south with his tribe, planning to loop back to the High Passes.
Garen tells Spiderslicer the plan is to go past Liscor, down into Drake lands, and back through the High Passes from the other side.
Garen's tribe has been fully mounted since the split, and Carn Wolves must be won by respect.
The Redfangs call Garen a hero who defines their tribe, the Gold-rank adventurer and brother of the Goblin Lord.
Garen's memories of the Halfseekers grow stronger, and he sees Jelaqua asking him which way to go over a map.
Garen remembers killing four Halfseekers in a private room over loot and the key.
In the flashback, Halassia lies wounded and calls Garen a traitor, and Garen's sword Redfang buries itself in her chest.
In the flashback, Keilam and Thornst are dead, and Ukrina fought hardest, before Garen runs with the key.
Garen insists it wasn't his fault, and that he was betrayed.
Garen freezes on seeing Jelaqua, Moore and Seborn on the road, and the Halfseekers attack.
Garen is attacked by Moore, who knocks him from his Carn Wolf, and Moore's hand grips him.
Seborn fights Garen with acid and frost daggers until Redfang cuts him open.
Garen tells the Halfseekers that Halassia, with a wand, told him the world must never have another Goblin King and demanded the key.
Garen insists his team betrayed him and that he did nothing wrong.
Jelaqua tells Garen that Halassia should not have threatened a teammate, but that killing the Halfseekers is unforgivable.
Garen orders Spiderslicer to kill the Halfseekers, and the Redfangs hesitate.
Headscratcher refuses and says the Halfseekers are Rags's friends and Garen's own former tribe.
Headscratcher tells Garen that only the true Chieftain, Rags, gives orders, and the Cave Goblins stand up in support.
Headscratcher challenges Garen for Chieftain of the Redfang tribe.
Garen loses his tribe's loyalty, backs away and rides north with fewer than a hundred followers.
Garen beheads Jelaqua's Drake body while Moore and Seborn lie wounded, and then rides away.
Garen tells his warriors "I was wrong."
Garen apologises to Rags and offers her a ride, and Pyrite agrees.
Only eight of fewer than a hundred followers remain at the last ride south.
Garen leads the Redfangs against Az'kerash, who is controlling Reiss, and his tribe follows him in a charge.
Garen asks Az'kerash to let his brother go and says "I'll try" to break the link.
Garen's sword cuts off Reiss's arm at the elbow, breaking the link, while the rapier goes through his chest.
Garen calls Reiss "Brother" as he lies wounded, and Reiss asks why he came back.
Garen kills three Drake [Captains] and wounds Embria.
Garen fights Relc and dies when Relc's spear pierces his chest a final time.
Garen dies after freeing Reiss.
Jelaqua burns Garen's body, and the Halfseekers find the key is not on him.
Lady Magnolia doubts that Garen Red Fang will bow so easily to the Goblin Lord.
Garia Strongheart is a City Runner who is shorter than Ryoka Griffin but wider, sturdy without the obvious muscles of a man.
Garia is friendly to Ryoka and greets her cheerfully, slapping her on the shoulder.
Garia is a good-hearted but slow Runner whom Ryoka considers, for her heart, the best Runner of the lot.
Garia visits Ryoka at her table, and cheerfully sits down with her despite Ryoka's cool reception.
Garia admits she cannot read books and can only manage signs and math, and says Fals can read.
When Persua and a gaggle of Street Runners taunt Ryoka, Garia grabs the lunging Ryoka by the shoulder and, one-handed, pins her to her chair while placing herself between Ryoka and Persua.
Garia says she is too slow to run like Ryoka and can only carry very heavy loads instead of fast requests; she says she could not run at all if not for the way the Runner's Guild works.
Garia hugs Ryoka hard enough to threaten a rib, promises to keep the other Runners busy while Ryoka flees, and tells her not to die.
Garia normally takes the heaviest Runner deliveries, saying they are safe because nobody steals raw ore or sugar; the costliest goods she carries are weapons and spices.

Ryoka notes that Garia jogged a pack of roughly thirty to forty kilograms of spices all the way from Wales; Garia says it is not that bad if the weight is distributed properly and that she sometimes walks.
In a brawl, Garia punches the adventurer Arnel, whose feet leave the floor, and knocks him out cold; the blow deforms his chain mail.
Garia tells Ryoka that she was a [Farm Worker] before becoming a [Runner] and reached Level 14 before changing classes.
Garia has the Skill [Enhanced Strength], which she says normally comes to warrior classes around Level 30, so she is much stronger than normal; she barely feels thirty kilograms.
