Garia arrives in Esthelm just before midday with several bags of sugar for a bakery and sees the commotion around Ryoka at the Adventurer's Guild.

Ryoka remembers that Garia was Level 11 when they first met and wonders whether she will get faster as a [Runner]; Ryoka also thinks of her as shorter and stockier than Fals, with terrible running form.
Garia elbows Ryoka in the stomach hard enough that Ryoka had forgotten how strong she is.
Garia says she looked at a tripvine bag for protection, but even that was out of her price range.
Garia carries a horseshoe that appears to keep the faeries away from her.
Garia stumbles into the Runner's Guild with a bloody head wound; she says bandits cut her off from over a hill, some shooting arrows and one with a club, and she tried to outrun them.
Ryoka checks that Garia's skull is not broken and closes the wound with a healing potion that Fals hands her.
Garia has no healing potion and cannot afford one; Ryoka notes she is one of the slowest City Runners, even if she can carry a lot, and earns only a few silver pieces at best, usually coppers.
Garia strides into Erin's inn with a huge smile, greets Ryoka, and asks where Fals is and whether anything is new; Ryoka tells her about Persua.
Garia lowers her voice to warn Ryoka that Persua is going to be a Courier; she does not like violence.
After Persua is hurt in the fight in the Guild, Garia, her nose bleeding, holds Ryoka back.
Fals tells Ryoka that Garia is a good Runner who can haul as much as a horse but is slow.
Fals explains that Garia loses the road in snow because she cannot tell white from grey, so winter is hard for her; Ryoka identifies it as colour blindness.
Fals says Garia has invited him to her parents' farm to thank Ryoka for helping her after her injury, and asks Ryoka to come too.
Garia apologises to Ryoka that she is skipping runs because she sprained her ankle, and says her healing potion was low-quality.
Fals joins Ryoka at the Runner's Guild, mentions Garia told him Ryoka was in a meeting with Erin, and plays along to get food for her guests.
Garia's parents tell the story of two fights at the inn, in which Garia knocked out opponents with one hit each time, including a Bronze-rank adventurer brought by Persua, and fought to defend Ryoka.
Garia's father Wailant says that her [Enhanced Strength] at her age means she could knock out an ox.
Garia refuses to let her parents buy her magical artifacts or things; Wailant says she wanted to fit in, not get ahead, and thought it would be cheating.
Wailant and Viceria say Garia has no talent with a sword, magic, a spear or a bow, and is too clumsy and wrong in temperament to be a warrior.
Garia tells Ryoka, delighted, that she is a [Martial Artist] and has gained the Skill [Basic Footwork].

Garia, now toned and muscular, greets Ceria and the Horns in Celum; Ceria does not recognise her because she was stockier before. She says she lost weight and has a new class, [Martial Artist], and still calls herself a City Runner.

Garia says she has made Celum her home base because it is close to her family's home, she has become much faster and earns more, and she is a regular at The Drunken Swordsman, where the innkeeper is Timbor.
Garia says she is a Level 14 [Martial Artist], has been levelling very fast, and shows a six-pack of abdominal muscle.
Garia says she got the class nearly a month and a half before, and that [Weight Control] was among her first Skills, at Level 6.

Garia says she knocked out her father with a lucky punch to the head during a sparring session after Ryoka left, when he made her practise a hundred of Ryoka's punches; she gained the [Martial Artist] class that night.
Garia confirms she had [Enhanced Strength], and says she was a [Farmer] until she quit.
Garia says she has learned a very fast kick and a dodging Skill, and that she is faster partly from weight loss; she notes almost nobody on Izril has her class.

Garia is researching [Martial Artists] and similar classes among adventurers, consults [Mages] and travellers from Chandrar, and notes that Pomle in Chandrar has [Martial Artists] but no Mage's Guild for a [Message] spell.
Garia says [Martial Artists] also use weapons in some styles, practises daily punches, kicks and a dodging routine, and wants Ryoka to teach her flips.
Garia tells the Horns that she is the best City Runner in the area now, though not as fast as Ryoka.
Pisces says Garia punched a Rockdevil to death; Garia tells how she realised she was a lot better when she killed a monster whose bounty was worth more than her delivery.
Visiting Erin's inn with Fals through the door from Celum, Garia reflexively kicks Numbtongue with [Quick Kick] and knocks him back, mistaking him for a Hobgoblin enemy.

Grimalkin recognises Garia as a [Martial Artist] and a Runner with [Enhanced Strength]; she tells him she wasn't taught by a martial artist and wants to learn more, and he urges her to become a [Mage] instead.
Garia, now a slim [Martial Artist] and City Runner, runs through Celum with Fals searching for Mrsha, and answers Erin's call.
Garia says her parents farm near Celum, that her mother sent a [Message], and that her father fights with a paralysis-poisoned magic cutlass.
Garia says her parents drink like retired [Pirates], which her father is, and the farm grows produce including Sage's Grass.
Garia drags a door tied to her waist with a mana stone on it from Celum to the farm.
Garia explains that Erin took the door from Celum after a trade dispute with the Runner's Guild, and that the Players of Celum are moving to Liscor.
Garia is slim, with full black hair streaked with blue from her mother's side, emerald green eyes shared by all three Stronghearts, and toned abdominal muscles.
Garia says she is a Level 17 [Martial Artist]; she has [Basic Footwork] and [Flash Kick], learned the kick from Grimalkin, and has beaten monsters including a rabid bear.
Garia says she levelled quickly but has slowed despite a thousand punches and kicks per day, and asks Numbtongue to spar.
Garia spars Numbtongue in the barn, and her [Flash Kick] sends him into the wall; he is put to bed with a healing potion.
Garia tells Ryoka she has the [Martial Artist] class and the Skill [Weight Control], and owes it all to her.
Ryoka sees that Garia has become a completely different person, with abs like Numbtongue's and greater confidence.
Fals says Garia now has the nickname Celum's [Martial Artist] after she beat a bandit group and dragged four of them into town for the bounty; Garia says she is not yet Level 20.
Garry is an Antinium Worker who cooks, and his four-armed carapace lets him handle hot and cold objects easily.
Garry carries Erin's ultra-fluffy bread out to the common room of her inn while helping in her kitchen.
Garry is one of five Individual Antinium (with Bird, Belgrade, Anand and Pawn) who survived the Workers' defence of Erin's inn against undead.
Garry helped Erin at the Christmas party, though Erin had hardly had a chance to chat with him.
Garry is the most timid of the five Individual Workers and prefers to work alone in isolation.
Only Anand, Belgrade and Klbkch know Garry's name, apart from Erin.
Garry is a Level 17 [Cook] who has levelled exponentially fast.
Garry is the only [Cook] in the Hive, since what other Antinium do to make their nutritious paste is not cooking.
Garry was assigned to the Queen's chambers to cook for her and has worked and slept ever since.
Garry feels he is slowing down, because he mass-produces what his Queen likes best and has no inspiration and no one to learn from.
Later, Garry is a [Chef] who has learned the Skill [Non-Allergen Cooking], which lets him eat gluten and serve pasta and bread to fellow Antinium.
Later, Garry gains his first apprentices, two Flying Antinium.
Garry teaches his two new Flying Antinium assistants how to mix dough.
Later, Garry's assistants Pisca and Runel are both nearing Level 10 as [Assistant Baker] and [Assistant Cook].
Garry never forgets Knight, Calabrian, Milner-Barry and the other Workers, who had their names for less than an hour before dying against Skinner and the undead.
Garry was as happy the first time he ate Erin's cooking and played chess with her as he is on his day off.
Garry greatly admires Erin, believing she is the best at everything, and hopes to learn from her cooking.
Bird moved into the Queen's chambers and talked about Erin's food, which helped Garry find the nerve to ask for time off.
Garry takes acid flies he bought from Lyonette to the Free Queen, who thanks him and acknowledges him, which she would not have done before.
The Free Queen is growing fond of Garry's attention to the presentation of food before it is eaten.
Garry is granted time off for the first time ever, after Bird's stay with the Queen helps him find the nerve to ask.
Garry wins the Goblins' cooking contest with pan-fried, marinated caterpillar breaded in egg and stale bread, with a garlic-and-fish sauce.
Garry explains that he makes many dishes for his Queen from killed monsters, so he already knew how to cook the caterpillar.
Pebblesnatch hands Garry the big chef's hat after the contest, and the Goblins duplicate his dish.
Garry makes a pizza perfectly after Erin gives him only a verbal lesson on it, chopping onions with several hands at once.
Erin tells Garry he is better than she is and that she would hire him if his Queen would not tear her head off.
Erin proposes that she and Garry cook together instead of her teaching him.
Garry proposes replacing hamburger bread with a bread made from sweet potato, so Antinium can eat hamburgers.
Garry feeds the Free Queen large hand-made noodles boiled in acid-fly broth, which she calls good.
The Free Queen says Queens are not susceptible to products of wheat, which she calls an error in the creation of the Antinium.
Garry spends a third holiday ever in Liscor with money from the Free Queen and eats at a ritzy outdoor café instead of going to the inn.
Garry first calls the café's soured cheese rotten, then retracts his comment after tasting it mixed with the other food and wine.
Garry dislikes spending money on an expensive dish that only one person can eat, feeling it goes against his ideals as a [Chef].
Garry states exactly what funds the Antinium group holds: fifty-six gold, eleven silver and thirty-two copper pieces.
Garry opens Garry's Antinium Edibles on the street leading to the Hive, a location most people avoid.
Garry's shop stocks pies, experimental breads and desserts and is in the red every day for its first four days.
Garry sells everything in his stalls and levels from the sales, even though a pie costs only three copper.
Some customers' feedback cards ask Garry to stop putting centipedes in the pies.
Garry says the Free Queen has given him a large food budget, so his profits carry no expense.
Garry runs his bakery stall himself, right outside the Hive entrance, and it is still running.
Garry sells muffins for a copper and a quiche for a couple of copper, and Erin tells him they are worth far more.
Garry loses money every day since opening, yet clears his entire inventory, including the bug items, and keeps levelling.
Garry tells a customer that bakery bread statistically contains bugs, and that bits of insect in grain add nutritional value.
Garry wants his two Flying Antinium assistants to learn to speak, though their different appendages may stop them signing.
Garusa Weatherfur is a tall female Gnoll [General] of the Longstride Clan, with light brown fur that is almost blonde.
Garusa is one of the lead generals of the Trisstral Alliance, sent as one of its best after Zel Shivertail took leave.
Garusa is a specialist in brutal assaults, a reason she was chosen to face the disorganized Goblin armies.
Garusa rides a large warhorse stallion and fights with a long spear.
Garusa has a clear, deep rumble of a voice.

section: The campaign against the Goblin Lord
text: Garusa is high level, higher than Thrissiam, but she declines to lead the joint army and cedes command to him.

section: The campaign against the Goblin Lord
text: Garusa asks Thrissiam to leave the attacking to her, since his formations suit fighting Goblins.

section: The campaign against the Goblin Lord
text: Garusa says Zel Shivertail warned her a day earlier not to underestimate this Goblin Lord, so she requested extra City Runners and [Scouts] as a reserve.

section: The campaign against the Goblin Lord
text: Garusa recalls that Liscor's fabled army was defeated in the Second Antinium War by a single Goblin Lord's army and not by the King.

section: The campaign against the Goblin Lord
text: Garusa says she has fought against Oldblood Drakes on occasion but never alongside them.

section: The campaign against the Goblin Lord
text: Garusa carries Thrissiam into a bed and shares it for an hour, after which the soldiers all know what happened and joke about it quietly.

section: The campaign against the Goblin Lord
text: Garusa tells Thrissiam a [General] must think of victory and not affection.

section: The campaign against the Goblin Lord
text: Garusa notes that the [Mages] cannot cast [Message], which would require a mage of far greater ability than a Goblin Lord's forces should have.

section: The campaign against the Goblin Lord
text: Garusa says she smells Goblins everywhere but cannot find their scent, and thinks the Goblin Lord retreated to make sure they could not run.

section: The campaign against the Goblin Lord
text: Garusa rescues Osthia from the Goblin ranks by riding in, killing a Hobgoblin and pulling her into the saddle.

section: The campaign against the Goblin Lord
text: Garusa defends Osthia against Thrissiam's anger, saying she might have gone for the Goblin Lord in her place.

section: The campaign against the Goblin Lord
text: Thrissiam and Garusa plan an ambush on Day 66 against the Goblin Lord's alternating forward camps.

section: The campaign against the Goblin Lord
text: A black lance of magic kills Garusa's stallion, and she charges the Goblin Lord and faces him with his black blade in hand.
Garusa is killed by a black bolt from the Goblin Lord, whose body a voice calling his apprentice now speaks through.
Garusa and those the black scythe killed rise as undead, and Thrissiam sees the hole in her chest and the light in her eyes.
Thrissiam realizes Garusa has been raised as a Draugr, a higher undead that only a very high-level [Necromancer] could animate.
Thrissiam kills the undead Garusa with his spear and the [Crescent Arc] Skill.
Hawk later reports that Garusa Weatherfur is dead.

A red-scaled Drake at a table says Garusa and Thrissiam are two of the finest [Generals], dead with over twenty thousand Gnolls and Drakes, and that vital information about undead was not passed to them.
Gazi is a half-Gazer Named Adventurer, called Gazi the Omniscient, who appears in Liscor in Book 1.
Gazi serves a sleeping lord and King, later shown to be Flos, the King of Destruction, as one of his Seven.
Gazi is a [Scout] of Flos' Seven whose central eye has long been blinded, and she says Erin Solstice injured it.
Gazi is a female adventurer with dreadlocks, dark orange-brown armor that only looks rusty from afar, and a large sword at her side, who has learned to see even in sandstorms.

Gazi calls herself part Gazer by ancestry: she has one huge central eye with a yellow pupil, four smaller eyes around it, a mouth of sharp teeth, no nose, reddish-brown soft skin, extra-segmented arms and only four fingers.
Gazi gives Erin Solstice the name Gazi, the name others not of her race use, and says she is an adventurer wandering through these lands.
Selys Shivertail recognises Gazi as a half-Gazer, a rare species made rarer by mixed blood, and her scales pale nearly to gray.
Gazi's main eye can see through objects at close range, and shows her a person's name and nature as well as class and level.
Gazi tells Erin she sees that Erin is an [Innkeeper], Level 11, simply by seeing it.
Gazi's eye can cast [Charm] by gaze; Ceria says it hits anyone who meets her gaze, and that Gazers cast spells as easily as looking, a half-Gazer included.
Gazi's eye makes the yellow pupil widen and glow, so that she becomes terrifying without looking at the person.
Asked by the Quarass for her level and class, Gazi states she is a Level 45 [War Scout], Level 12 [Mage] and Level 18 [Silent Commander].
Gazi walks toward smoke on the wind and comes upon a spider, and later tells Erin she is pleased to meet her; she does not draw her large sword because she has no need of it yet.
Gazi tells Erin that murder is the sin of taking lives that matter, and that those who fight monsters are exterminators, killers perhaps but not murderers.
Gazi gives her name as Gazi of Everst in Liscor, and the crowd falls into awestruck silence.
Selys says Gazi's title is Adventurer Pathseeker, that other continents call her Gazi the Omniscient, and that she is rumored to be over Level 40.
Selys tells Erin that Gazi is the kind of famous adventurer who appears on a list of the top 100 adventurers in the world.
Gazi lent Erin money to hire the wagon that brought the Shield Spiders into the city, after cutting one of them in half.
Gazi says her help in the street fight between Relc and the adventurers would only cause death and that she does not fight with her fists.
Gazi says she was once a soldier but left her position to become an adventurer, as being a soldier is only worth it with a cause to fight for, a leader to follow and a reason not to die.
Gazi tells Erin that she will seek lodgings in the city and that they shall meet again, answering Erin's doubt with "I foresee it."
Gazi says she believes she is more infamous than famous.
Gazi murmurs that Toren is a Level 1 [Skeleton Warrior] and nods in acknowledgement to Pisces, then asks Erin who the [Necromancer] is and calls him talented.
Gazi catches the wrist of a big adventurer who attacks Erin's inn, and with her glowing eye orders him and his two companions never to attack the inn and to leave; they flee.
In her own thoughts Gazi has searched for years for individuals worthy of waking her lord and liege, and believes her King still sleeps and will wait to be woken; she finds Erin and Pisces worthy.

In Gazi's view Erin is unique, unlike any human she has met save one, because she unifies many races and has a skill, [Immortal Moment], Gazi has never seen on anyone else; she reads a thief in the market as only a [Princess], too petty for her ruler's interest.
Gazi decides to wait and learn more about Erin rather than act, and notices two Gnolls shadowing her, probably set by a Gnoll shopkeeper.
A Named adventurer, Gazi the Omniscient, is in Liscor, and a speaker reasons that she has not entered the ruins yet because she is being cautious.

Ksmvr recognises Gazi on sight, crouching and smiling on a distant hill watching Relc and Ksmvr, and Relc says she could eat the Antinium for breakfast; Gazi's eye flicks to Krshia and the hidden Gnolls.

Gazi watches Ceria and Gerial in Liscor while Relc heads for Calruz, with the [Princess] crouching invisible nearby; she judges Gerial an average Level 17 [Warrior] and finds that Ceria and the Horns of Hammerad are the ones she has been looking for.
Gazi Pathseeker greets Gerial, Sostrom and Ceria politely; her high-quality armor and sword mark her as Gold-rank or higher, though she wears no rank armband.
Gazi asks the Horns of Hammerad about Ryoka Griffin, whom she calls a levelless girl who braved the High Passes and survived, and says she is told the Horns are Ryoka's acquaintances.
Gazi calls herself a Named Adventurer and Ceria Silver-rank, and says tradition would have Ceria help her.
When Ceria says Gazi and her mad king can go to hell, Gazi blurs, puts her curved sword to Ceria's throat, says she does not suffer insults to her lord's name, and demands an apology on her knees.
Gazi tells Erin she will be travelling away from Liscor for a while, and asks whether Erin plans to travel because she would enjoy another meal there later.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Gazi the Omniscient tracks Erin's party into the Ruins from a slope several hundred meters away, with her main eye turned back into her head.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Gazi sees the levels of Erin's party: Ksmvr Level 16 [Warrior]; Pisces Level 22 [Necromancer]; the Goblin Rags Level 8 [Warrior], Level 6 [Mage] and Level 10 [Tactician]; Toren Level 11 [Skeleton Warrior] carrying a ruby enchanted with [Terror]; Erin Level 18 [Innkeeper]; and Ryoka level-less.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Gazi waits for the party with a tightly sealed scroll bearing a glowing rune, humming and polishing her sword, since it is finally time to go home.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Gazi stabs Watch Captain Zevara through the stomach with her curved sword after Zevara orders her away, then addresses Ryoka and Erin with a gold-lettered scroll, saying she has been looking for them.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Gazi announces herself as Gazi of Reim, Gazi the Omniscient, and has four small eyes on Erin while her central eye watches the guardsmen.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Gazi says her Lord gave her armor so she could walk through the bloody battlefield, and the guardsmen's arrows do not pierce it.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Gazi reads the Watch aloud as fifteen Drake and five Gnoll [Guardsman] classes, a [Spearmaster] Drake, a [Swordslayer] Antinium and a Human [Assassin].

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Gazi claims she sees the truth in souls and that feints are useless, and calls Krshia Silverfang a liar after seeing the lie on her face.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Gazi fights the guardsmen, Relc and Klbkch defensively, severing arteries and cutting rather than killing, while defending only her head.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Ryoka identifies Gazi's scroll as a teleportation scroll, and Gazi opens a portal with the word "Exus".

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Gazi's portal is a long tunnel ringed by spinning symbols and colors, and its far end shows a patch of grass ringed by runestones.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Gazi holds her sword at Ceria's throat while answering a question about why she waited, saying it would hurt most of all.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Gazi's blood is bright orange-yellow.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: Gazi tells Erin Solstice that one day they shall meet again, then steps through the portal.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: The Antinium Queen recalls that Gazi the Omniscient slew the last group of Silverfang warriors who came to Liscor.

section: Book 2: the Ruins and Erin's inn
text: An account of the Gnolls' spell books says Krshia Silverfang asked her tribe for warriors to transport the books and that Gazi the Omniscient slew the first party sent.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi the Omniscient walks through gates and grins up with her four good eyes at a call from the battlements.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: In Gazi's own view her central eye is her greatest weapon and defense, a gift of Gazers she honed beyond normal; it can see through objects at close range, but her peripheral eyes cannot, and the central eye is now damaged and blind.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi remembers the girl who stood in front of her and injured her eye, and her hand reaches for the sword on her back out of fury.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi has orange-brown skin, no nose and long black dreadlocks, and Trey sees five eyes, with the central one closed and crusted yellow.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi decides she dislikes the human twins because they made her lord laugh and are trusted favorites of her King, and hates them with all her soul.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi reports to her King that Erin has a skill she has never seen in her many years of travel, [Immortal Moment], that Erin befriends Antinium, owns a skeleton servant, forbids slaying Goblins in and around her inn and teaches one chess.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi tells her King that Erin is the one who injured her eye, and that Ryoka Griffin told her he lived while Erin dared to strike the blow.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi is a half-Gazer who calls the enemy camp's mage and cavalry positions out to her side, seeing them from miles away with her central eye in a dream.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi stays behind when Flos' companions rush out and tells them to win victory and glory for their King.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Trey and Teres know Gazi as the Omniscient or Lady Pathseeker, a half-Gazer whose central eye is injured; Trey has heard a girl from his world poked it out.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi says she does not know why Flos has not marched, and that she has waited a long time for her lord to awaken and does not like waiting longer.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: In a flashback seen by Venith, Gazi is a frightened young half-Gazer holding too large a sword who scouts an army of a thousand to fifteen hundred armored Black Judgment soldiers and six mages.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi has no battle scars, like Mars, while Flos and Orthenon do.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi sits beside Trey without a word, and tells him that she and the other seven followed Flos for moments like this, because he was a King.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi kills a girl [Assassin] with raven hair in a corridor with her sword, producing a dagger with a poisoned tip for Flos; she says he knew assassins would come the moment he woke, and he answers that he asks much of her.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi returns after two days of scouting, riding hard and tired, to report a coalition army of sixty-two thousand with fewer mages than hoped, none of the highest level, and siege weapons including a pair of trebuchets.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Trey considers Gazi's smile a mask, a grin devoid of real emotion.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi walks out of the fog at the front humming, cutting down shadows with her sword, her armor dyed crimson with her central eye closed and her four smaller eyes on the soldier Uleth, who recognises her as Gazi the Omniscient.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi staggers to Maresar with black smoke rising from her armor, wounded by a [Mage]'s [Flare Orb].

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: From her tower, Gazi pinpoints enemy [Mages], the enemy [General] and clusters of elite soldiers, and calls down lightning from Flos' crown onto the map, which ends the battle.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi sits on the edge of the balcony over a three-story drop and tells Trey she is the weakest of the Seven, living and dead, always the lowest in level, a [Scout] with a non-specialised class whose arms and armor Flos had forged to make up for her weaknesses.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi says the Traders of Roshal are a nation with their own army and great wealth and artifacts, whose rules are enforced by assassins so that even Named Adventurers must tread carefully.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi says some classes can only be gained by the most terrible deeds, not being real classes, and are born of despair and filth.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi says that she believes in slavery but does not like it, being alone in that opinion, and that she hates slavery, having been a slave once until her King freed her; she confides this to Trey.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi says she was born a slave and that Flos found her as a child, bought her and freed her within a year, since when she has served him.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi tells Trey that a single class is best and that a [King] or other [Ruler] can remove a needless class from those who pledge to him; Flos removed her [Slave] class, Orthenon's [Traitor] and Takhatres' [Cursed Outcast].

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi believes slaves in Flos' kingdom cannot be mistreated and are treated well, and that Flos generally frees any slave he takes an interest in.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi tells Trey that Gazers are highly magical, inclined toward magic like half-Elves, with more chaotic magic than typical [Mages], and offers to teach him spells because he has a [Mage]'s staff he cannot use.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi gives off a smell of spicy cinnamon under her metallic armor scent, laughs with a sound like bells, and says her title came from hatred and fear, her name being whispered among those who spy and wander alone; she says her classic scary smile is an act.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi tells Trey that Flos' fury is directed foremost at Hellios and Germina's Quarass, and that war will come within days.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi Pathseeker is a half-Gazer Named Adventurer and [Scout], feared for spotting any threat, deception or spell from miles away, who returned from Liscor blinded, her central eye damaged by an encounter with a certain [Innkeeper].

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi wears brown scale armor and carries a greatsword at her hip when riding; Flos says neither is enchanted but a masterwork of the truest experts, perhaps Dwarves.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi's four smaller eyes move independently and see through walls and her own head; she trains Trey with a rock target, and he finds her a friend who understands his view of slavery because she was a slave.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi says that without her main eye she would be considered a high Gold-rank adventurer, not Named, and that her closed middle eye leaked pus when she first returned.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi, in an illusory form with blue hair and starry eyes, holds her greatsword at a [Slaver] and [Merchant] to defend Nawal from an illegal slave contract, and kills no one.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi teaches Trey [Farsight]; she shows him four eyes smiling with the main eye shut and a claymore tied to her back.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi catches the falling Trey with [Featherfall] cast from a wand after he is thrown from the tower.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi and Orthenon were once a couple, are professionally courteous but not always on the same page, and Gazi taps her main eye, always closed and still healing or damaged by whoever poked it out.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi studies Flos' phone image, can see the pixels and the screen's refresh flicker, and finds the picture hurts her eyes unless she unfocuses.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi jumps four stories from Trey's window and lands in a crouch before sprinting off.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi teaches Trey magic as his teacher; Trey has never seen her main eye open, and apparently it was damaged in a fight before she returned to Reim, by someone else from Earth.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi tells Flos that Wyverns are native to Izril, larger than Griffins, scaled and stronger, and that Orthenon would know more of Fissival's Drake riders.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi Pathseeker has four-fingered segmented hands, five eyes whose four small ones move independently, a smooth face with no nose, and pointy teeth; Trey knows her as one of the King of Destruction's Seven.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi's closed eyelid hides an eye she says was injured by Erin Solstice.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi says the Dwarves gave Flos her brown scale armor and silver claymore in exchange for an order gone wrong, and that Dwarves would only say there had been an error.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: The Quarass says Gazi's armor was made by a true master and that her level is lower than the other Seven because her Dwarven armor and blade are a crutch; she says it blocks Gazi's spellcasting from other than her eyes, and Gazi nods.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Later, Gazi's central eye is whole again after a Sainath of A'ctelios treats it, and she opens it in battle, loosing a beam of bright light at the dwellers of the Tombhome.

section: Gazi in the service of Flos (Books 2-17)
text: Gazi returns to the battlefield a few days after finishing a mission from A'ctelios, her eye still closed, and Flos says she may soon need to quit the battlefield.
General Duln is a Dullahan and the 1st [General] of Pallass, who arrives with a huge red-hot glowing mace and a tower shield.
General Duln is remarkable for being a non-Drake on Pallass's inner war council.
General Duln arrives apologizing for the delay, saying he was giving orders and equipping a strike force, and his [Soldiers] form up on the walls.
General Duln uses [Volley Fire] on the Wyvern Lord and then [Phantom Volley], whose copied arrows blast the Wyverns overhead to pieces.
General Duln uses [Shieldwall Formation] and [Rapid Advance], and his Skill makes the soldiers' shields repel the Wyverns' frost.
General Duln proposes putting the young Raskghar through military training once their numbers replenish, to see how they react to discipline.
General Duln says the Walled Cities clashed with the tribes often before the Antinium wars and have used unorthodox methods before.
Chaldion cuts General Duln off, which shows his remark was a slip of the tongue, and calls the matter classified.
General Lael is the high commander of the armies of Jecrass, known for emphasis on cavalry and speed, and guards the wide, open realm.
Lael is a Level 27 [General], one of the highest-leveled assets of Jecrass, and young, in her early thirties.
Lael was hired from the Republic of Belchan, a democracy known for its mage-schools and gold mines.
Raelt promoted Lael after his daughter Jecaina suggested her, and hired her from the nation next door.

Lael served with distinction in Belchan as a [Commander] until she was disciplined for striking a [Politician] over what she claimed was a bribery attempt, and she was demoted until Raelt contacted her.
Raelt hired Lael for loyalty over levels, and she has proven incorruptible, at least to the River Wardens.
Lael tells Raelt's court she cannot fathom a scenario where Jecrass's armies would triumph over Reim's, even at three times their size.
Lael says that all things being equal, she would negotiate with the King of Destruction for a favorable surrender of Jecrass's forces.
Lael finds Nerrhavia's chariots retreating without her signal and Medain's adventurers already gone, as the battle against Reim goes badly.
Lael orders the [Archers] safeguarded and a fall back, with Warden Emile's van to hold the line and then retreat.
Jecrass's soldiers die rather than the foreign reinforcements, as in the last two battles, and Lael has a terrible taste in her mouth.
Lael thinks that this is not the foreign forces' war and that Jecrass could have won if they had held and brought down Zamea.
General Sserys is a Drake and the hero of the First Antinium War, and he is called [Spear of the Drakes].
Sserys tells Zel Shivertail that Magnolia Reinhart, a child at the time with vomit dripping off her chin, offered him her hand and proposed that together they could end the war and save the world.
Sserys confesses to Zel that he was afraid of her peace and of what she saw, and he says he would never admit it to anyone else.
Sserys's account says that other Human [Lords] interrupted him before he could answer her.
A diary of General Sserys of Liscor records the army of Liscor, one of the strongest forces on the continent, meeting the Antinium on a guard mission.
At Shivering Falls Pass he alone refuses to retreat, gathers coalition armies, and personally leads fifteen charges against the Antinium.
In Liscor, 4th Company soldiers watching Antinium march in a parade ask what happened to pride and to General Sserys.
Zel recalls that Sserys once ordered a set of magical armor made for him, which Zel refused.
Sserys coined the saying "Drakes do not run".
Selys describes Sserys as Liscor's greatest hero, who died long ago, and his grave has a grand tombstone with his name.
Selys believes that Zel and Sserys were lovers, since Zel's will asks to be buried with his love; she scatters Zel's ashes beside Sserys's coffin.
Sserys's diary records that his Liscorian Army had been subjugating a local Goblin Lord's forces around the city of Ussls before meeting the Antinium.
The army of Liscor is renowned as one of the strongest on the continent and sells its services to any nation that will hire it.
Only a few people of note knew of the Antinium early, including young Magnolia Reinhart, Lord Tyron Veltras and General Sserys.
Sserys writes that a patrol of twenty Drakes and Gnolls met fifteen black individuals harvesting trees in a forest, and six of his soldiers died.
Sserys is deeply troubled that equal losses were taken against a numerically inferior foe.
Sserys forms heavy ranks with defensive classes and assigns [Tacticians] and [Strategists] along each column.
Sserys collapses tunnels that appear behind his lines, and his relentless advance leaves the Antinium no time to dig under his forces.
Sserys sends kill-teams of high-level warriors to devastate Antinium lines and retreat with few or no casualties.
Sserys writes "We will not retreat" and "Drakes do not run", and the next day the First Coalition Army of Liscor counterattacks the besieging Antinium.
Sserys unifies every standing Drake city, forges a non-aggression pact with the Gnoll Tribes, and is named High General of the war.
Sserys personally leads a mounted elite group to rescue Geir's survivors, retrieving over forty Drakes and Gnolls above Level 30.
Sserys pushes to the southern entrance of Liscor, where the Black Tide encircles his back and traps him.
Sserys bans the water-flooding tactic except as a last resort, because mages warn of its effect on the weather.
Sserys's last diary entry says a new breed of Antinium is destroying his army from the tunnels, and that Zel must be told.
Sserys's last entry ends "To Liscor, and the world, fight on," and he says he will die as he lived, a soldier.
Sserys dies at the Antinium Grand Hive, and his journal and corpse are found in the First Unified Army's camp twenty-four days later.
Sserys's body lies fully armored in his command tent, sword in hand, killed by a single strike through armor and bone to the heart.
No other soldier of the First Unified Army is found.
Zel calls Sserys his mentor and friend, and tells Xrn he has not forgotten that the Antinium killed him.
Sserys tells Zel that young Magnolia seems like a god, or the opposite of one, comparing her to a Demon from Rhir.
Geneva Scala is a young woman from Earth who becomes a [Doctor] in Baleros, the only true doctor on that continent.
Soldiers and later the wider public call her the Last Light of Baleros, a title she dislikes.
She refuses to take sides in wars and treats any patient regardless of species or army.
Geneva was born in Wisconsin and is Italian by heritage, and she had often visited Italy.
Geneva is twenty-four, going on twenty-five, when she joins the Raverian Fighters.
She wanted to be a doctor after trying to hold a dying friend together in the garden of her house.
Her aunt died when Geneva was twelve, and she had dreamed of saving even people who had to be buried in pieces.
Geneva was a third-year medical student and had not graduated when she came to this world.
She left a lecture to go to the bathroom and never came back.
Geneva walked down a school hallway, turned, and found green foliage and dirt where sterile tiles had been.
On Earth she studied as a general surgeon, cut up corpses and was a good student, but her experience was almost all theoretical.
Geneva carries a personal oath modelled on the Declaration of Geneva, which she adopted because it is her namesake.
She is a pacifist who has sworn an oath not to harm, though she does not count animals or stinging insects.
Geneva was recruited in a Baleros city by Sergeant Thriss of the 4th Battalion of the Raverian Fighters, who hired her when she called herself a [Doctor].
Thriss accepted her claim because no one in the company can verify classes, and he judged it an odd sort who would lie about it.
Geneva marched in Thriss's 6th Squad.
She gained [Doctor] Level 1 and [Skill - Lesser Resistance: Disease] on the night she made her oath.
Geneva suspected that Thriss staged the dislocated-shoulder training injury, with the healing potion ready, to build a recruit's confidence and test her.
Thriss trusted Geneva with the iron key to the healing potion chest after her first operation, warning that missing potions would bring hell.
The scene that opens the chapter shows a soldier dying under her hands, the fifth person she had seen die.
Geneva reached [Doctor] Level 4 and gained [Skill - Hygienic Hands] and [Skill - Lesser Resistance: Infection] after removing an arrowhead from Clara.
Later, she reached [Doctor] Level 11 and gained [Skill - Injury Sense] and [Skill - Sterile Equipment].
Later, in one night she gained six levels and four Skills: [Numbing Touch], [Flawless Cut], [Speed Stitching] and [Enhanced Thread].
Okasha told her gaining six levels at once was practically unheard of.
With [Speed Stitching] and [Enhanced Thread] she could suture three times as fast and close damaged organs.
The following night she gained [Lesser Stamina], which let her keep working after dark.
Later, Geneva is a Level 26 [Doctor].
Later, her leveling gave her the Skill [Sterile Field], an upgrade over [Sterile Equipment], that keeps the area around her free of unsanitary conditions.
She uses the Skills [Flash Hands], [Flawless Cut], [Hemostatic Pause] and [Detect Injury] when treating a wounded War Walker.
[Hemostatic Pause] stops a patient's bleeding, and Geneva says it gives her six minutes and forty seconds.
Her hands stay sterile because of her Skill, and she has learned she can temporarily disable the field that cleanses the area around her.
She uses [Malady's Cessation] on a Yellow Rivers patient to give an hour of relief.
Later, she has [Lesser Endurance], which cuts down on her fatigue, and she is levelling.
She has a Skill giving her resistance to the Yellow Rivers disease, but says she is still at risk.
Later, she reaches [Doctor] Level 34 and obtains [Skill - Disease Detector] while Okasha seizes control of her body.
Geneva wanted penicillin and antibiotics from her first days, but she did not remember how to make penicillin from scratch.
With no antibiotics, she treated a Dullahan's infected wound with boiled water, salt saline and a sparing dose of healing potion.
She asked for tweezers, a digging instrument, and a strong spirit to clean her tools.
Geneva invented triage in the camp, tying white armbands on priority patients and marking lower-priority ones with charcoal.
Her triage meant she left patients she could not save alone, and she told them she prioritises the people she can save.
Geneva flew a red cross flag on white cloth over her tent, and soldiers began waving crosses of their own when bringing wounded.
An enemy [Mage] who was blasting the camp turned away and left after seeing Geneva hold up the flag before the wounded.
Later, she triages with coloured stones: green for the least wounded, yellow for moderate wounds, red for those about to die, and black for the dead or untreated.
She uses healing potion sparingly, working with a scalpel, curved needle and forceps.
Geneva cannot make blood transfusions because she has not been able to build a needle and pump.
She removed an Evercut arrowhead from Luan's stomach lining with forceps and then closed the organs with healing potion.
She saved a War Walker with nineteen Evercut arrows in him and a nearly severed arm, and reconstructed the arm over an hour.
Geneva says she is just a [Doctor] and not fully trained, and wishes for a true heart surgeon, an anesthesiologist, or someone who knows how to make penicillin.
She has no treatment for poison-gas victims, whose effects resemble mustard gas, and told Ken and Luan to stop bringing them.
Geneva carries a primitive wooden stethoscope, a measuring tape, tongue depressors, clean gauze and a surgical kit.
She sketched a condom of waterproofed linen treated with something to neutralise infection, to stop the spread of bacterial infection.
Geneva asked Paige to supply the linen and designed the condoms to be tailored to different species' sizes.
She tried mixing the [Healers]' poultices into new batches to find an antibiotic to replace penicillin.
Geneva was determined to give the United Nations company an antibiotic, and says she would trade her left leg for penicillin.
She performed her first Caesarian section on a Centauress, saying only a [Doctor] can do it.
Delivering the colt made her feel her purpose as a doctor, and she joked she should have trained as an obstetrician.
By the time of Book 11 she has done eight Caesareans, and a mother travelled fifty miles because a [Doctor] was in town.
Aiko says Geneva is reluctant to give many Caesareans on principle.
Geneva designed a protective mask, protective gear and a sealed laboratory for working with Yellow Rivers samples.
Her laboratory has a metal door and is as airtight as she can make it.
Geneva grew cultures of the Yellow Rivers bacteria in glass petri dishes and tested samples Paige brought.
Her protective armour is brown resin-covered leather, with a red cross painted on the back.
Geneva worked up an electrolyte solution to replace fluids lost to Yellow Rivers fever.
Geneva requires patient details such as gender, weight and symptoms written on a clipboard for each case.
A Zeres [Healer] reported that the mould-based penicillin substitute worked on nearly two dozen trial patients.
Geneva noted that Occillium was not a good name but she was already using it, and she wanted to name it after the mould.
Geneva credits Octavia Cotton, the [Alchemist] from Liscor, for the mould and plans to announce a cure exists.
She used the mould cure on only the gravest cases before testing proper dosages, because the cure was finite.
Geneva compared the cure to blood transfusion and penicillin, and says no healing potion could have saved Seve.
Geneva says that a drop of healing potion makes the Yellow Rivers bacteria multiply wildly and turns a small infection into an open sore.
She insisted that healers use a drop test: if a potion has no visible effect on a wound, the patient is infected and must be quarantined.
She told the Talenqual [Healers] that nothing works against the disease except keeping patients hydrated, clean and rested.
Geneva examined and packed a month-old abscess on the [Guard] Ceriche that she says healing potions caused.
She says the abscess needs surgery that cannot use healing potions, because potions accelerate all parts of the body.
Geneva says potions increase the chance that small preventable ailments become medical emergencies, and are not a cure-all.
On the first day of fighting, Geneva told Thriss the gods are dead in this world and asked if he believes in souls.
Thriss answered that he believes in souls even without gods.
Geneva's friendships with Lim, Clara and Fortum cooled because she triaged others before Lim, who had a shallow cut.
Non-humans were the soldiers most willing to talk to her after that, and many Humans thought she betrayed them by treating other species first.
Geneva faced Thriss down when he wanted to take a wounded Centaur, saying she answered to a higher oath.
She told Thriss that if her oath were broken she would no longer be a [Doctor].
Okasha was the Selphid whom Geneva had put into a dead woman's body and who became her assistant.
Geneva carried an azurite voice-recorder rune stone and secretly recorded a conversation between Okasha and Calectus.
She felt they should have asked her but accepted that help was help.
Geneva told Luan she was a medical student from America, and met him as a person from her own world, along with Ken and Aiko.
She told them she wanted to be a surgeon and never graduated, but still believes in the Hippocratic Oath.
The Razorshard Armor company gave Geneva a donation of potions and gold; she accepted the potions but ignored the gold, saying it would not change how she works.
Geneva told a Razorshard emissary that her position was neutral and that her reputation was what kept her camp alive.
In Book 10 she refuses to let Daly and other Earthworlders go back to fighting as a company, diagnosing at least two-thirds of them with PTSD symptoms.
Geneva asked Daly to use condoms and ask partners about infection symptoms, and she planned a second checkup of everyone.
She proposed setting up a clinic with at least one surgery room and offered to be on call for childbirths.
Ken proposed charging patients by what they could pay, and Geneva insisted she would aid anyone who needed it.
Luan told Umina and others that Geneva was a [Doctor] in his company who had saved hundreds of lives.
Luan said he saw her reattach a War Walker's arm when it was nearly gone, after Evercut arrows.
Luan said Geneva could splice tendons and deliver babies, and that a Caesarian section is medicine.
Perorn Sadiluc offered to authorise bringing Geneva to the academy, with a formal invitation and travel costs.
Geneva ran a field hospital that held patients until a convoy took them back to their armies at night.
She felt she was on her third battlefield since coming to this world and could not remember how to smile.
After a Dullahan assassin stabbed her three times in the stomach and cut her throat, she was left for dead.
She survived because Okasha kept her alive and held her organs together until Calectus's potion arrived.
Okasha's presence in Geneva's body was revealed to Ken, Luan and Aiko, whom Calectus ordered not to tell anyone.
Geneva argued the company should not fight, citing Doctors Without Borders and the French idea of Témoignage.
She said neutrality is pointless if there is no one to witness it.
Later, she admitted she was wrong to try to stay neutral on every battlefield, because it painted a target on her back.
She said there is no Geneva Convention in this world, only herself.
Thriss struck Geneva's back with his mace until her spine broke, and she told Okasha she was dying.
Okasha entered Geneva's body, which is forbidden for Selphids, to bridge the gap in her spine and make her move.
Supply wagons carrying new soldiers and potions arrived shortly after.
Geneva would be paralysed from the neck down without Okasha, since she knows no way to cure spinal-cord damage.
Geneva was paralysed by a mace blow months before Book 16, and Okasha lives in her body.
Okasha lets Geneva use her Skills while Okasha uses hers, and can boost Geneva's body past its limits.
Okasha speaks through Geneva's mouth in a friendlier, deeper inflection, which Daly is used to.
Later, Okasha is held by the Selphids and a Selphid named Idis replaces her; Calectus sets the terms.
Idis is a [Blademaster] and [Barbarian] chosen because she is good at killing, as the Minds worried about Geneva's safety.
Calectus ordered Idis not to take over Geneva's body without consent, and threatened to replace her if she upset Geneva.
Geneva misses Okasha and describes herself as a prisoner with a kindlier warden but stricter rules.
Calectus refused to let Geneva speak with Okasha because Okasha may influence her through Skills.
Calectus said the Selphids would fund research for a cure and had Idis help Geneva contact other Selphids.
Geneva told Idis that her experience with Okasha was troubled, and accepted Idis forcing her to sleep.
Geneva named Joseph of Liscor to Seve, after Idis relented, against Selphid rules about secrecy.
Geneva runs a clinic and had treated two Yellow Rivers patients, who wanted fast cures rather than her advice.
Okasha speaks for Geneva in the meeting with Fezimet.
Geneva holds a wax-sealed invitation to demonstrate her techniques at the Titan of Baleros' academy at Elvallian, signed by Peclir Im.
The invitation includes a travel expense fund she can call upon at the Merchant's Guild.
Geneva treats Yellow Rivers disease, a sexually transmitted infection, and by Book 16 she has over a hundred patients.
Geneva says no one except Okasha, herself and the United Nations company is taking Yellow Rivers seriously, and that it has no cure.
She made condoms in all sizes, including Centaur, Dullahan, Human and Lizardman.
Geneva visited the Slippery Tail brothel in Talenqual, run by the Dullahan Miss Dushal, on her manager's request.
She treated the sex workers, though Talenqual's company, the Feathered Brigade, does not regulate the industry much and abuse is common.
Okasha controlled Geneva's body in a two-hour encounter with the Lizardman prostitute Xeppal, and Geneva planned to return in a few days.
Niers Astoragon's report records that Geneva cancelled her visit to his academy at the last minute and refunded the fee.
The reports say the Last Light of Baleros is treating two children with Yellow Rivers disease.
Geneva wore her protective gear and told crowds not to touch her once treatment began.
Geneva and Siri demonstrated to Commander Fezimet of the Featherfolk Brigade that a drop of healing potion makes the bacteria cover a dish.
Fezimet refused a lockdown but ordered the city's [Healers] to take orders from Geneva.
Geneva spoke at a public announcement in Talenqual, warning that the disease spreads through pus and other fluids.
Okasha seized control and put Geneva in a box, and Calectus's Selphids later sealed Okasha in a holding-jar while Idis took her place.
In Book 18 Geneva is 25 and from Madison, Wisconsin, and works in the Talenqual clinic.
She told Joseph in a message chat that there were dozens of Earthlings who came together, some split apart or died.
Geneva has no antibiotic at that point and tells Calectus she needs one.
By Book 19 Geneva runs two clinics in Talenqual: a mass-treatment and isolation facility and an intensive-care clinic.
Umina uses fake names such as Urrexa while helping Geneva.
The Yellow Rivers disease is mutating, and over seventy percent of Dullahans die because they refuse to have armour removed.
Geneva wants everyone treating a young Dullahan patient to wear protective gear because the disease might be airborne.
Geneva told people in Talenqual to stay indoors, and the citizens listened to her.
Gerald is the captain of Kyrial's Pride, a Silver-rank adventuring team.
Gerald is a big man in armor who carries a battleaxe almost as large as Calruz's.
Gerald's team declares itself armed and ready to fight, and he scowls at Olesm for tagging along.
Gerald says his team will not quit until they reach the bottom floor, a change from what he said earlier.
Gerald calls Olesm a coward for running, before another mage explains that Olesm saved them with a skill.
Gerald uses [Whirlwind Cleave] to scythe through three zombies and a ghoul.
Gerald's face is seen in Skinner's mass of skinned bodies, along with Cervial and Lir, which shows he has been killed and absorbed.
Geram Redfist is the brawny captain of Lady Rie Valerund's guard, a man who was an accomplished [Street Brawler] before she met him.
During the Goblin attack he carries no weapons but wears two gauntlets on each hand, and he beat a Hob to death with his bare fists.
Geram tells Rie that the Hobs are breaking the doors bit by bit while a [Shaman] builds something big outside.
Geram is bald and wears armor when he tries to follow Rie to Magnolia Reinhart's meeting.
Reynold, Magnolia Reinhart's [Butler], intercepts Geram and pivots him out of Magnolia's path, and Ressa steps in front of Magnolia.
Gerial is the vice-captain of the Horns of Hammerad, a Silver-rank adventuring group.
Gerial has the skill [Dangersense], which went off when a Goblin pulled out a jar of acid.
Gerial sits with Calruz before the expedition, discussing the plan.
Gerial winces when asked about the sixth captain, and tells that Hendric pulled out at the last moment.
Gerial stares at Erin in confusion after the adventurers attack the inn at night.
Gerial grabs for his belt dagger on seeing the skeleton in the inn, until Ceria stops him.
Gerial, Sostrom and Ceria flee the Watch after the webbing in Celum.
Gerial tells Gazi that Ryoka stays at the Bloody Tankard in Celum, while Ceria steps on his foot and jabs him in the side.
Gerial touches the pommel of his sword while the Horns discuss the Ruins.
Gerial throws a jar of acid at Skinner to buy time for Ceria to flee, but fear makes his arm spasm and it only splashes Skinner's lower half.
Skinner flings Gerial's sword away with one finger, breaking his hand.
Skinner seizes Gerial, who feels tearing and then coldness, and dies before he hits the floor.
Geril is an old [Servant] respected above the disgruntled nobility of Raelt's court, whom Raelt asks to read the King of Destruction's letter.
Geril is Raelt's [Head Servant] and old retainer, who has been at his side for over four decades, from boy to man.
Geril helped raise Raelt as a child.
Geril clears his throat beside the throne to quiet the court.
Geril guesses that the gathering of rulers Raelt mentions is in Pomle.
Raelt asks Geril to contact Minister Lyfelt about condemning Flos' letter.
Geril has Jecaina locked in the palace vaults, guarded by General Lael's [Soldiers], so she cannot escape to the camp.
Geril reports to Raelt that Princess Jecaina started a brawl with Nerrhavia's [Master Charioteers] after they made remarks she objected to.
Geril tells Raelt he wishes Raelt had not gone to Terandria, because Raelt's father sent him to learn fencing to be safe abroad.
Geril adds that Raelt might have joined the King of Destruction's army or stayed in Chandrar and become a great [King].
Geril fights Perric with [Full Power Blow] and [Bellhammer's Impact] to free Jecaina's horse, then holds off the Golden Ranks with [My Life, My King].
Geril tells Jecaina that her father is captured and that Jecrass needs her as its [Queen].
Geril calls Jecaina his lovely child and tells her not to blame herself.
Geril dies covering Jecaina's escape, having been dead the moment the High King swung his sword.
Gershal is a [Lieutenant] and low-level officer from Vaunt, a small city north of Invrisil.
Gershal commands disciplined but fairly low-level [Archers] and [Swordsmen] and has never fought in a war.
Gershal and his men fight monsters, patrol and keep the peace, and had never been levied for the annual battles against Drakes.
Vaunt's [Mayor] panicked when both Magnolia Reinhart and Tyrion Veltras sent levy requests, since the city could not satisfy both.
Vaunt sent four hundred [Soldiers] to Tyrion Veltras, a battle-ready [Lord], and two hundred under Gershal to Lady Magnolia.
Gershal thinks of himself as the sacrificial lamb sent to Magnolia.
Gershal knows Salvia because her city, Nonelmar, lies close to Vaunt.
Vaunt is known for producing some of the best cheeses on the continent, including the spicy, fragrant Peppermort.
Gershal shares his Peppermort cheese with Salvia over cheap wine.
Gershal wraps cheese in wax paper and tucks it into his armor, following a Vaunt superstition that a cheese once stopped an arrow.
Young men and women leaving Vaunt carry cheese into battle, where it also serves as a field ration.
Gershal argues that a local [Commander] is no match for a Goblin Lord and that an offensive would be suicide.
Gershal says Tyrion Veltras is gathering an army twice as large and should deal with the Goblin Lord instead of Magnolia.
Gershal fears that fighting without a true leader or twice as many soldiers would only level up the Goblins and create more undead.
Gershal says Tyrion Veltras called for six thousand horse from the Terland family, at least a quarter of them [Knights].
Gershal dismisses the Knights of the Petal as arrogant hotheads until Salvia warns him of their temper.
Gershal reassesses the two Rose Knights once he hears their armor is Dwarf-made, though they do not ease his concerns.
Gershal regards Magnolia Reinhart as cunning and manipulative from rumour, though never a fool, and hopes today will not prove the rumours wrong.
Gershal is assigned with his unit to the front ranks of Magnolia's army.
Gershal sees his line begin to step back before the Hobgoblins' charge and orders his men to hold.
"Cheese-rotted heads" is a petty childhood insult from Vaunt, and it snaps Gershal's soldiers out of their fear.
Gershal steadies himself by looking at Zel Shivertail, who stands unmoving before the charge.
Zel Shivertail calls [Stonewall Formation] and [Chargebreaker Guard], and Gershal feels his shield warm and his footing firm.
Gershal's iron and wood shield turns aside a gigantic Hob's massive hammer, and he holds his ground against repeated blows.
Gershal wounds the Hob in the thigh with his sword and thrusts the hammer away with one arm.
The Goblin Chieftain is the leader of the Goblin tribe that lives near Erin's inn, and Erin concludes he is out for her blood.
The Goblin Chieftain is nearly as tall as Erin, very big for a Goblin but still small, with a wide muscled body, a rusted helmet and mismatched bits of metal armour.
The Goblin Chieftain blows a horn from a hill near Erin's inn, then fires arrows at Erin from a bow when she tries to run.
The Goblin Chieftain carries a sword and a bow and has levels, which makes him a better fighter than Erin.
The Goblin Chieftain keeps blowing his horn as he walks toward the inn, then batters at the barricaded door until it splinters.
The Goblin Chieftain smashes the door and enters the inn.
The Goblin Chieftain charges Erin, rams a table into her, and tries to tear her clothes off to assault her; she punches him in the groin.
The Goblin Chieftain follows Erin into the kitchen, loses his sword in the wall, and is hit by Erin's rolling pin.
A kitchen knife is driven into Erin's stomach in the kitchen fight; she pulls it out herself, and the Goblin Chieftain then lunges at her with the knife.
Erin throws a pot of boiling oil in the Goblin Chieftain's face, and he sinks to the floor screaming silently from the burns.
The Goblin Chieftain dies slowly of his burns while Erin sits beside him until his breathing stops.
Klbkch finds the Chieftain dead beside Erin and calls him a great threat.
Klbkch disposes of the Chieftain's body but warns that his tribe may seek vengeance.
Klbkch asks Erin what caused the Chieftain to attack her, noting that the tribal leader rarely takes any aggression himself.
Erin answers that the Chieftain attacked because Relc killed three Goblins and beheaded them.
A bounty notice signed by Klbkch awards forty silver coins for the destruction of a Goblin Chieftain within the area of Liscor.
The people of Liscor say that Erin killed the Goblin Chieftain by herself.

Selys tells Erin that Goblin Chieftains are too dangerous to send most adventurers after, since Watch fighters like Relc and Klbkch are probably better fighters but a Chieftain who calls his tribe well would wipe out an average group.
Only Goblin Chieftains can access far-back memories.
Ryoka first sees the Goblin Lord standing in a mass of Goblins in magical armor, only a bit taller than an average Goblin and smaller than the Hobs, with white pupils in black eyes that glow.
With a raised hand he reshapes the Goblin ranks into a shield wall against Zel's charge.
Ryoka concludes that the Goblin army is raising the dead and that the Goblin Lord is another [Necromancer].
The Goblin Lord pursues Zel Shivertail's army south until the Goblins give up the chase, then gathers to grow stronger before sweeping north to subjugate the northern tribes.
Scouts put his army at about the equivalent of a Walled City's standing army, with over a hundred Hobgoblins and at least ten mages or shamans.
Gnolls in Krshia's apartment discuss that an army strong enough to defeat Zel Shivertail has slain the Stone Spears tribe to the last and has over a hundred Hobgoblins.
His army attacks a Human city in black armor, and Rags's coalition crushes one black-armored warband against the walls.
Garen tells Rags that this was only one of the Goblin Lord's warbands and not his army.
A council speaker warns that a Goblin Lord is raising an army just south of the High Passes, and Tyrion says Esthelm fell but its people retook the city after fighting off another of his armies.
Another speaker says a Goblin Lord is one step from a Goblin King and cites rumors of a "Goblin Great Chieftain" who fought alongside the last Goblin King.
Shivertail is told the Goblin Lord has been spotted around the Blood Fields, retreating from two suppression armies each led by a [General] and nearly ten thousand strong.
Thrissiam curses the snow that erases tracks for a Goblin Lord, and Drake and Gnoll scouts sent out alone vanish one by one.

Osthia sees him on a mountain ledge, human-sized and hooded, with black eyes and white pupils, among Hobgoblins, Goblin [Mages] and [Shamans], and he strikes a Drake [Mage] down with a black lance of light.
The Drake [Mages] cannot cast the [Message] spell, which Garusa says would need a specialized mage or one of far greater ability, and Thrissiam says he has blocked every spell sent at him.
A second, cold voice speaks through the Goblin Lord's body, calling him its apprentice, and Thrissiam explains that the Necromancer was controlling him and is not dead.
The Goblin Lord speaks in a second, less educated voice of his own, and the other voice scolds him for failing to use his greatest weapon and tells him to unify the Goblins or perish in despair.
In his own voice he is educated and thoughtful, mentions a Ring of Protection and [Ward of Repulsion], and Osthia fears this most of all.

He tells Osthia the Necromancer "sees when he looks" and does not look now, points to a dead Goblin child his master created and killed as a weapon, and demands that she tell him about the Necromancer.
He tells Az'kerash that the servants Az'kerash sent were lost a week earlier and never found Liscor, and Az'kerash decides to reprimand them.
The Goblin Lord's army, tens of thousands strong in black armor, marches north past Liscor, having crushed two Drake armies.
He sees almost perfectly in darkness, has orders not to attack Liscor, and senses other Goblins that he means to claim by blood or, failing that, take their bodies.
The army that marched past Liscor numbers tens of thousands, not counting the undead army that marched ahead of them.
He is a human-sized Hobgoblin in black robes with midnight eyes and white pupils, and he is a [Mage] rather than a warrior.
His tent was Thrissiam's command tent, and he keeps a yellow wildflower given to him by a child he healed with a potion, "gift for gift".
He uses a small [Message] scroll to contact the Necromancer, whom he calls his master.
He taught himself to read before the Necromancer found him, keeps six books including Thrissiam's copy of The Triumph of Scales, and reads whatever his army loots.
His camp has sentries, patrols, latrines, a smithy and black resin armor, and he copied the color-coded battalions from the Drakes.
He says he can sense other Chieftains and other Goblin Lords far away, that there are none on this continent, and that he is the "brightest" because he calls other Goblins loudly.
He tells his Goblins he has a master who teaches him magic and is a master of death, and that a slave learns and one day he will not be a slave.
He sends eight thousand Goblins under Snapjaw and Eater of Spears against a Human army and rides out himself on a Shield Spider.
In the battle he changes formations to match the Human commander's cavalry and archer tactics, kills the commander with [Arc of Midnight], and wins.
He aims [Deathbolt] at the Human commander's horse before the duel.
His Ring of Protection swerves arrows aimed at him.
He tells Osthia that Goblins need a home and that he will win three battles, against rebel Goblins, against Humans, and defending a home built in the mountains.
He says Goblins take from Drakes, Humans and everyone, and that someday they will be like them and have a home; his last word is "Soon".
After winning outside a Human city his army pillages for supplies, and thousands of zombies and a few ghouls rise.
He argues with his master and then kneels in agony, rises furious, and orders an attack on Invrisil to slay Zel Shivertail, saying "We are ordered. So we will. Or die."
At Invrisil he rides a Shield Spider in robes, and his Goblins chant "Goblin" three times to break Human morale.
His Goblin [Necromancers] and [Shamans] send tens of thousands of zombies, ghouls and a Crypt Lord at the Humans.
Az'kerash's secret weapon, exploding undead Goblin children, destroys Human lines, and the Goblin Lord's own hands bleed as he clenches them while watching.
He casts [Deathbolt], which Reynold calls death magic like the Necromancer's, instantly lethal to anyone below Level 20, killing Rose Knights.
With over a thousand Hobs and his Shield Spider he charges toward Reynold's position.
Dying, Zel suggests the name Reiss to the Goblin Lord, who accepts it and swears the Necromancer will die by his hand.
Observers elsewhere fear that a Goblin Lord so young and mighty who felled a Drake [General] may be another Velan the Kind, or worse a Curulac.
His forces are estimated down to sixty thousand and he is marching toward the so-called Great Chieftain in the mountain.
The Antinium Grand Queen is the ruler of the Antinium Hives, a position that was entirely new to Drake and Human leaders when she first acted during the Antinium Wars.
Klbkch addresses her as "my Queen", and she addresses him as Klbkchhezeim.
She is a massive, bloated Queen who rests on a huge dais in the centre of a stone cavern with many tunnels.
She says she is Grand Queen of the Antinium of Izril, and that her role has been unlike any earlier Grand Queen's.
During the First Antinium War the Grand Queen sent white-flag Worker messengers carrying identical letters to the armies, requesting an immediate peace treaty with the rest of the continent.
The Drake and Human leaders unanimously refused her peace terms, and Sserys' army was given authority to destroy the Antinium in any way it saw fit.
The Drake and Human armies believed the main Hive held most of the Queens and the Grand Queen.
According to Xrn, the Grand Queen saw the Goblins as a threat and gave three separate orders to her Prognugators.
Xrn says Klbkch, Wrymvr and Xrn herself were each ordered to break the Goblin King's might at any cost.
When Klbkch tells her through a black-glass mirror that Zel Shivertail is dead, the Grand Queen goes still and then replies "Good".
She says the Goblins are moving again, the Humans stir for war, the Drakes have lost their shield, and the Antinium will rise.
Klbkch answers her with a single word, "Perhaps", while gripping the hilts of his swords.
She communicates with the Free Queen through a mindless miniature Drone replica of a Queen that carries a hand mirror linked to a twin mirror elsewhere.
She says the vessel was sent for more secure communication and calls the network a series of magical proxies of her own design.
The Grand Queen judges that the Free Antinium have made adequate progress and tells them to rejoin the larger Hive through the relay.
She confirms that Prognugator Xrn has returned to the Hive.
She orders the Free Antinium to keep probing the dungeon and to commit whatever resources are needed to acquire artifacts.
She is irritated that Klbkch's form was altered without permission, and Klbkch answers that it was a necessary side effect of the Rite of Anastases.
Through a vessel and a magic mirror, she questions Klbkch and the Free Queen about an injured Worker and about Drones being present in Liscor's Hive.
She says her Hive forbade the Liscor Hive to experiment with new forms or make Antinium besides new Workers and Soldiers.
Klbkch tells her the Drones were deemed essential for enacting the Rite of Anastases if he fell, which is a lie she does not detect.
She calls Klbkch and the Free Queen to speak with the other five Hives and tells them to abandon the injured Worker.
Her chamber holds an azure Antinium with a staff by her side and Prognugators carrying silvery blades that replicate Klbkch's weapons.
She angrily accuses the Free Queen of disobeying orders, saying no Prognugators were to be made.
She has nearly two dozen Prognugators of her own, whom she styles the Custodium.
The Free Queen thinks each Custodium Prognugator wears copies of Klbkch's long swords made of enhanced chitin, and regards them as a wasteful creation.

section: Klbkch's visit to the Grand Hive
text: The Grand Queen receives Klbkch in a grand antechamber with mirrors showing the other five Queens, including the Free Queen.

section: Klbkch's visit to the Grand Hive
text: She sits on a high dais that serves as a throne, from which she commands the Queens and consults her Prognugators.

section: Klbkch's visit to the Grand Hive
text: She asks Klbkch to act as Xrn's replacement, and the Silent, Armored and Flying Queens each petition for his guidance.

section: Klbkch's visit to the Grand Hive
text: The Twisted Queen does not speak during the audience.

section: Klbkch's visit to the Grand Hive
text: Klbkch respectfully declines her invitation and says he will tour every Hive willing to host him.

section: Klbkch's visit to the Grand Hive
text: In private, the Grand Queen tells Klbkch that the other Hives are fractured and the Queens do not obey her.

section: Klbkch's visit to the Grand Hive
text: She says each Queen pursues her own goals, some more loyal than others, and fears the Antinium are splintering like the primordial Antinium.

section: Klbkch's visit to the Grand Hive
text: She says she sanctions the works of the Armored Queen.

section: Klbkch's visit to the Grand Hive
text: She says she does not lead the Antinium but keeps each Hive from warring with the others, and that conflicts over resources have occurred more than once.

section: Klbkch's visit to the Grand Hive
text: She says the Twisted Queen sends no envoys and wages war against the Walled Cities against her will.

section: Klbkch's visit to the Grand Hive
text: She tells Klbkch the Walled Cities counter-raid Antinium lands with earthquakes, tunnel collapses and floods, increasing since the Pallass incident.

section: Klbkch's visit to the Grand Hive
text: Klbkch's mind confirms she is telling the truth, because the True Antinium cannot lie to each other.
The Grand Queen decides that creating new Queens is a flawed goal and says the Antinium should return to Rhir, hoping Queens remain there with the knowledge to create more.
She says she does not forget the vow to return to Rhir with an army a thousand times larger than what was left.
She argues the Antinium lack ships that can be sailed properly and that returning past the Blighted Kingdom and the Demons would be too risky.
She says she would not risk Klbkch on a sea voyage because he could not be restored by the Rite of Anastases if he died at sea.
Instead she proposes to destroy the Walled Cities and conquer Izril, then send a thousand ships so one reaches Rhir.
She shows Klbkch silos built underground, full of food and kept free of pests by magic.
She says Xrn's magic created more storage areas over nearly a decade, to sustain an army twenty-three times larger than the first war's peak for three months.
Grev is a scrawny, underfed boy in Celum who looks no more than thirteen years old.
He has a charming gap-toothed smile that makes Erin like him at once.
Grev lives with the Drake Jasi in a squalid hut next to Celum's walls.
The hut belonged to their parents, both of whom were dead or had simply left.
Grev offers to guide Erin to an [Alchemist] when she enters Celum to sell her bees.
He leads her down a side street into an alley where three armed men in dark clothes wait.
He takes a few silver coins from one of the men and runs when Erin accuses him of tricking her.
He still tells the men not to hurt her, saying she carries the money in a pouch.
Erin spots him cutting a young woman's purse in a shop queue, and he runs from her in terror.
Erin chases Grev through Celum's poorer streets and catches him by the hand outside a door.
Grev shrinks away with an arm raised as if he fears being hit.
Jasi shields him and begs Erin not to report him, saying he is one crime away from being exiled from the city.
Erin tells Jasi that Grev helped a group of thugs ambush her when she first came into the city.
Grev denies the pickpocketing, but Jasi knows he is lying.

section: Dreams and the Players of Celum
text: Erin feeds Grev to the point of bursting to calm his restlessness, and he can barely finish his last bite of hash browns with cheese.

section: Dreams and the Players of Celum
text: Asked what he would do if he could have any class, Grev says he would be a famous adventurer and a Named Adventurer.

section: Dreams and the Players of Celum
text: He adds that he would carry a flaming sword and slay Dragons, while Jasi asks Erin not to encourage him.

section: Dreams and the Players of Celum
text: Grev joins the staged Romeo and Juliet with faulty lines and overenthusiastic acting.

section: Dreams and the Players of Celum
text: Grev runs around the Players of Celum carrying a rucksack full of props, costume changes and scripts.

section: Dreams and the Players of Celum
text: The bag Grev carries has to be emptied now and then because the actors' cut of the profits fills it.

section: Dreams and the Players of Celum
text: Grev hovers backstage with water and scripts during the rehearsal of My Fair [Lady].

section: Dreams and the Players of Celum
text: Jasi asks Erin to let her buy a gift for Grev in the secret gift exchange.
Later, Grev says he is a [Street Rat] with a Skill that lets him find out street news.
He tells Jasi and Wesle that Greenblade's Boys, a new gang, are the group that attacked Kilkran and Andel.
He explains that flash gangs run in, take what they can and run out, and that Bandits are all flash.
He says builders give back to what they take so the take is bigger, and protect their clients, like the Brothers.
He says rats are never noticed and strike rarely, and viners are gangs as big as the Watch, like the Sisters.
He says Celum's Brothers and Sisters both got wiped out in the bad job with Miss Erin's inn.
