Grev is among the Players of Celum who arrive at The Wandering Inn when riots cancel the evening's play.
Grev Redigal is Jasi's younger brother, a [Street Rat], who once tried to lead Erin Solstice into a mugging.
Grev has left Celum's crime behind and is Emme's left hand, managing and assisting the [Actors], though Emme says he is too weak to be her right hand.
Grev is short and no longer scrawny, well fed and well dressed, and he has not abandoned all his old ways.
Grev marks Jasi and the inn with his [Waypoint] Skill so he can guide her and Rima back through a huge city.
Grev is low-level because he is a child, but puts his few Skills to good use.
Grev tells Halrac's party that the Players are part of Miss Erin's crew and will flip when they see them.
Greydath of Blades is a former Goblin Lord who served Velan the Kind and was named his servant of arms.
Greydath lived among Goblins as an old Hob called Greybeard in Tremborag's tribe, with a long grey beard that no other Goblin has.
Greydath fights with a rusty, notched greatsword that shines and tears the air when he holds it.
Greydath has a long grey beard and is older than any other Goblin Pyrite has met, by far.
Greydath lacks the pull and aura of Goblinkind, so Rags senses nothing from him and he seems like a ghost in the world.
Greydath can raise a power that makes Goblins fall to their knees and cut the air and water with his sword.
Greydath's crimson eyes show sorrow, a burning hatred that has lasted for ages, and something like regret.
Greybeard, an old Goblin, tells Rags that a big tribe like hers can probably remember Chieftain memories.
Greybeard tells Rags and her Goblins he saw the last Goblin King, Velan the Kind, die and remembers the King before that, Curulac of a Hundred Days.
Greybeard compares the Goblin Kings to stars, distant and unreachable.
Pyrite counts Greybeard among Rags's counselors and has already solved part of the mystery of who Greybeard is.
Pyrite thinks Greybeard is important and wonders whether Rags or he will first notice what he really is.
Greybeard says "Something is coming" just before the horn calls announce the Humans.

section: Reveal at the Knights of the Petal fight (Book 6)
text: Greybeard holds off the Rose Knight Sir Kerrig Louis with a greatsword and then six of the Knights of the Petal at once.

section: Reveal at the Knights of the Petal fight (Book 6)
text: Greybeard turns the battle against Lady Bethal's knights, who realize something is wrong.

section: Reveal at the Knights of the Petal fight (Book 6)
text: Thomast duels Greybeard, who multiplies into several images, an afterimage or a Skill, then opens Thomast's chest and stomach with his greatsword.

section: Reveal at the Knights of the Petal fight (Book 6)
text: The old Goblin declares himself Greydath, and Noears falls to his knees at the name.

section: Reveal at the Knights of the Petal fight (Book 6)
text: Greydath says he served Velan the Kind, who named him servant of arms, and announces himself Greydath of Blades, once a Goblin Lord.

section: Reveal at the Knights of the Petal fight (Book 6)
text: Greydath tells Rags that Goblin Lords define themselves by overwhelming talent and must stand above all others.

section: Reveal at the Knights of the Petal fight (Book 6)
text: Greydath judges Rags too young, too small, too weak and not enough, saying she does not crush others with who she is.

section: Reveal at the Knights of the Petal fight (Book 6)
text: Greydath says Tremborag is old, lazy and fat on arrogance, and Garen Redfang is complacent in his strength.

section: Reveal at the Knights of the Petal fight (Book 6)
text: Greydath says he rode with the Goblin King and that the Goblin Lord is not his equal.

section: Reveal at the Knights of the Petal fight (Book 6)
text: Greydath strikes Rags and the Goblins who rush to protect her with a force from his sword, and Pyrite pleads with him to stop.

section: Reveal at the Knights of the Petal fight (Book 6)
text: Greydath tells Rags he is going to see what the Goblin Lord is, and that she is too small yet, but may be something if she grows.

section: Reveal at the Knights of the Petal fight (Book 6)
text: Greydath answers Rags's question why he did not lead his people as they died with "Because I cannot be King".

section: Reveal at the Knights of the Petal fight (Book 6)
text: Greydath tosses Rags aside and walks out of the destroyed camp.
Greybeard stumbles to the Goblin Lord's fire as an old Hob with a long ragged grey beard, a trait no Goblin Osthia has seen before.
Greybeard tells the Goblin Lord he is a humble traveler who once had a tribe but lost it, too old but too tough to die.
Greybeard says Velan hated undead, which makes the Drake Osthia ask how he knows what Velan hated.
Greybeard muses about a coward, a child and a slave who each claim to be true Goblins, and says the Goblin Lord is a slave to a Necromancer.
Greybeard says any of them might be worthy but that Garen Redfang stands out, though Garen is not a true Goblin.
Greybeard says Garen might become a Goblin Lord, but slaughtered his tribe of adventurers and other species for a relic of the King.
Greybeard disappears across the plains, telling Osthia to keep the secret or he will cut off her tail.
The Goblin Lord notes that the old Goblin with a beard was very suspicious and knew too much.
Greydath, in the history book, is threatening to defeat a small Human army on the Plains of Saltes when Niers Astoragon appears and takes command of the Humans.
Greybeard tells Garen that the Goblins called him that here, but decades ago he was Greydath of Blades.
Garen realizes with disbelief that Greydath was supposed to be dead.
Greybeard kills the Gold-rank [Shield Defender], [Pyromancer] and [Swordsman] with a rusty greatsword before Garen arrives.
Greydath beats Garen in a long duel and asks if he killed his old team because they feared him.
Greydath tells Garen he is a poor leader, a not-Goblin and the poorest of Chieftains who betrayed his first tribe.
Greydath calls the Goblin Lord a coward and says the slave and the child are on the run.
Greydath says he is leaving because Elia Arcsinger knows him and something strange lies to the south.
Greydath hurls a dead swordsman's blade at Elia Arcsinger, and she shatters it with an arrow after the younger half-Elf shouts "Mother".
Pyrite reveals that Greybeard, who visited Tremborag's tribe with a rusty greatsword, was Greydath of Blades.
Pyrite says Greybeard cut a Griffon in half, ate, slept, talked and taught him.
Pyrite learned from Greydath names of rocks, edible moss, bugs, how small Goblins are, what it means to be Chieftain, old stories and the story of a key.
Pyrite says Greydath was never clear about classes and leveling.
Tremborag asks why Greydath sat in his mountain so long after the King's death, and claims the true Lords search for a King only to use him.
Tremborag claims the Lords sent only Greydath with Velan, and that the other Lords were lesser.
A grey-bearded Goblin crouches on a distant hilltop and speaks of an army of lost children and five who walk Garen Redfang's path.
Greydath of Blades is the hilltop Goblin who stares at the inn and senses a strangeness in a cave to the north that drew him south.
A tall, lean old Hob with a grey beard and a greatsword offers the five Redfang Hobs a wheel of goat's cheese as a peace offering.
Greydath tells Numbtongue he dreamed of five not-Chieftains, five seeds not grown.
Greydath calls the five incomplete and says their happiness is a trap, because happiness for one Goblin is despair for all.
Greydath claims the Hobs rely on Erin too much and that she is the reason they are holding back.
Greydath fights all five Redfang Hobs at once and beats them easily.
Greydath claims he met and challenged Garen Redfang, who could not best him, and the Redfangs believe him.
Greydath threatens to hurt Erin to make the Hobs grow stronger, and leads them in a chase across seven flooded hills toward the inn.
Greydath dodges an arrow aimed at his eye, howls with grief and rage, and hurls his greatsword into the tower on top of the inn, collapsing it.
Greydath tells the Hobs they must decide whether they are Chieftains or lost Hobs, then dives into the water and swims away.
Greydath answers why it had to be him with "Because we are Goblins".

section: After the Battle of the Floodplains (Book 9)
text: Greydath leaps down to Rags after the battle, and Rags, Redscar, Snapjaw, Rabbiteater and Badarrow recognize him with fury.

section: After the Battle of the Floodplains (Book 9)
text: Greydath admits he saw it all and did nothing, answering Rags's accusation with the question "Should I?".

section: After the Battle of the Floodplains (Book 9)
text: Greydath blocks Snapjaw's sword and tells the Goblins Garen chose to die, calling him a traitor and Reiss a slave.

section: After the Battle of the Floodplains (Book 9)
text: Greydath tells Rags that Goblins die, and that this is why her people died, because they are weak.

section: After the Battle of the Floodplains (Book 9)
text: Greydath tells Rags he waited and watched for whoever came, Rags, Garen, Reiss or Tremborag, and did nothing.

section: After the Battle of the Floodplains (Book 9)
text: Greydath says he did nothing because it is meaningless and had to be so, and that Goblins wait only for a Goblin King.

section: After the Battle of the Floodplains (Book 9)
text: Greydath says he searches the world for Goblins who can rise beyond Lords, tests and goads them, and holds that a true King must rise alone.

section: After the Battle of the Floodplains (Book 9)
text: Greydath tells Rags that Velan chose his death.

section: After the Battle of the Floodplains (Book 9)
text: Greydath tells the Goblins the Goblin King's treasure waits high on the mountain, that two keys unlock it, and that Rags has Garen's key.

section: After the Battle of the Floodplains (Book 9)
text: Greydath leaves his greatsword behind and jumps laughing down the mountain.
A ship of moss-covered Hobgoblins pulls Greydath out of the sea while he is swimming across the ocean.
Greydath asks the [Shaman] for a map because he forgot where a moving island is, and planned to swim to the Isle of Minos and wait.
The Goblins address Greydath as Lord and stand in awe of him, and the ship is heading to Baleros.
Greydath says he will swim from Baleros for practice rather than wait for the ship's return.
Greydath says he is in a bad mood when the warriors want to challenge him, and answers the question what happened on Izril with the words "Goblins died".
Grimalkin is a bulky, muscular Drake of Pallass who teaches what he calls physical magic as his own personal school.
Grimalkin's class is [Sinew Magus], and he is nicknamed the Fist Mage.
Grimalkin is almost pure muscle from head to toe, with arms twice as large as a normal Drake's.
Grimalkin declares himself Pallass' greatest [Mage], and says he has dueled Archmages.
Grimalkin graduated from Fissival, but his unusual beliefs make him a pariah in the magical community.
Grimalkin visited Wistram though he never attended it.
Grimalkin emphasises physical enchantment spells, which let him fight on par with a Gold-ranked [Warrior] but make him neglect other magic.
Grimalkin's motto is that a [Mage] should be able to keep up with [Warriors].
Grimalkin fought in both the First and Second Antinium Wars.
Grimalkin has killed Adult Crelers, and still bears scars from one.
Rufelt introduces Grimalkin to Erin as the master of physical magic, and his apprentices are dying Drakes and a Gnoll girl.
Grimalkin bellows at his apprentices that Erin has more courage than the lot of them, praising her gonads as the proof.
Grimalkin slaps Erin on the shoulder so hard she nearly falls down.
Pisces and Ceria recall that Grimalkin challenged an Archmage to a duel two years after Ceria left Wistram.
Grimalkin lost to Archmage Feor, but landed a hit that nearly shattered Feor's barrier spell and suffered a bit of the impact.
Grimalkin fixes the door of Erin's inn by releasing mana stored in his body, saying a [Mage] can store mana.
Grimalkin lifts a stone block weighing hundreds of pounds above his head to show what a body can do without a spell.
Grimalkin casts [Lion's Strength] to hold the block with one arm, and [Water Colossus' Grasp] to catch it as it falls.
Grimalkin offers one-year courses, saying a student who meets his basic physical tests will learn his repertoire of magics.
Grimalkin says he does not train [Necromancers] or [Mages] he is not personally training.
Grimalkin says [Lion's Strength] is a Tier 4 spell, which could count as Tier 5 because it is an enchantment.
Grimalkin says he would charge at least nine thousand gold pieces to teach [Lion's Strength].
Grimalkin says he and fellow Drakes created a pocket dimension of fifteen feet by fifteen feet in a six-and-a-half foot sphere.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin has made barbells, weight bars and an EZ-bar based on Erin's description, and orders fifty-pound weights of lead.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin plans to have Pallass' [Soldiers] work out with the weights under a regimen he writes.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin says he has established himself as the expert on fitness and training, and has a formal rank.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin works out that Erin arranged the meeting with him, and compares her to a [Senator], Archmage Feor, Terandrian monarchs and Magnolia Reinhart.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin says Rufelt and Lasica do the same thing as Erin, but that their manipulation is up-front and honest.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin demands Erin do it again and give him something he wants, and she offers the idea of resistance bands.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin agrees to one training session for the Horns of Hammerad, and says more can follow on condition of payment in ideas, artifacts or chance encounters.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin says he will check their fitness and aptitude rather than teach spells, since spells would take more time.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin says he has no interest in training the Horns, and calls the arrangement a consult with Erin providing the information he wants.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin finds the Horns by watching the grass move around the inn when Pisces turns invisible.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin passes Yvlon, and says that on potential Ceria is the weakest of the four.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin says a decent Skill at Level 30 would let him certify Yvlon as Gold-rank on the spot.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin says he can certify someone as Gold-rank, having recommended two of his apprentices to the Adventurer's Guild in Pallass.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin offers a scroll of a Tier 3 spell and says he will charge Erin's account.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin says Wistram graduates lack field experience, and that he throws a rock at them from the side when they cast a huge spell.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin says Wistram has lost its true craft to the Golems, and that only Archmage Amerys and Viltach gave him the time of day.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin says Fissival never lost its artifacts or spellbooks, and trains [Mages] who tend to survive longer in battle.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin calls Illphres a fool for leaving Ceria without a spellbook.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin says Cognita, the Truestone Golem, was made by Archmage Zelkyr less than two hundred years ago.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin says Cognita helped crush the Five Families' foothold on Izril and killed two Archmages in battle.

section: Weights and the Horns of Hammerad (Book 12)
text: Grimalkin says even the best six [Mages] he knows would have only a one-in-three chance against her, and he decided not to try.
Grimalkin appears behind the boasting Beza in The Wandering Inn, calls Wistram's standards low and introduces himself as the strongest [Mage] in Pallass.
Beza is left staring at the ceiling, unable to speak, after Grimalkin deals with her.
Grimalkin says he was coming to tutor Ceria when he received the message.
Grimalkin notes that Erin sounds like a Drake from a Walled City at times.
Grimalkin refuses to help with the Wistram [Mages], saying Wistram can pressure Pallass and he will not entangle himself.
Grimalkin says the Wistram team is legally cleared and that Pisces is a wanted criminal.
Grimalkin says Wistram is a nation in all but landmass, and that Fissival does the same but Wistram does it better.
Grimalkin says Wistram eclipsed Fissival because the Draconae Scholarium is a Drake institution in a Walled City bound to Izril.
Grimalkin says he and Erin are not friends, but that he wants her ideas for treadmills.
Grimalkin refuses at first to be Erin's bodyguard, saying he reacts when called by Pallass and not by an [Innkeeper].
Grimalkin sprints for the door when the Watch reports a Creler nest and an Adult-stage Creler.
Grimalkin and Jelaqua in her Raskghar body race to the door to Liscor, but it is not connected.
Grimalkin leads Jelaqua and six Gold-ranks against the Adult Creler, and kills it only after finding it already dying.
Grimalkin finds the Horns of Hammerad standing among the dead and catches Ceria when she collapses.
Grimalkin incinerates the whole Creler nest and says his spells found all the eggs.
Grimalkin says adults retreat if they think they are in danger, and that Crelers evolve faster with more to eat.
Grimalkin says Oteslia once fought off six Adult Crelers.
Grimalkin says Elder Crelers take at least a century and Adults a decade and a half, and that five Ancient Crelers existed.
Grimalkin runs a harsh course that mixes weights and essays, and certifies students as full [Mages] in one to three years.
Grimalkin accepts any student regardless of species, age or gender, demanding only raw talent in muscle or magic.
Grimalkin's students are certified Silver-rank in the Adventurer's Guilds.
Grimalkin has killed Adult Crelers, slain enemy [Mages] bare-handed, and dueled and lost to Archmage Feor, walking away.
Grimalkin adopts Erin's chess boxing idea, and has his apprentices write essays after exercise.
Grimalkin plans to send sets of weights to Manus and other cities, ordering sixty sets in all.
Grimalkin says Gnolls can be [Mages], and that a Gnoll [Archmage] existed thousands of years ago.
Grimalkin says the white Gnoll Mrsha is also using some nature magic, and he wants to speak to Erin again.
Grimalkin kills a Wyvern at his mansion by throwing fifty-pound weights and punching it.
Grimalkin demands who failed to activate the [Cage of Pallass] spell, then leaps down to the 5th Floor with [Reduce Weight] and [Warlock's Leap].
Grimalkin kills a Wyvern on the 5th Floor with [Lightning Bolt] and by twisting its head until it snaps.
Grimalkin stacks [Gauntlet of Force], [Lion's Strength], [Bound Spell: Impact Shockwave] and [Thunder Step] to kill three Wyverns.
Grimalkin finds Watch Captain Rekhassha frozen on the north wall and crushes a young Wyvern's neck with [Magic Anchor].
Grimalkin shatters a Wyvern mother's leg, and kills another with lightning and [Stone Sphere] boulders.
Grimalkin's right side is frostbitten by the Wyvern Lord, and his [Muscular Restructuring] Skill saves his arm.
Grimalkin is bandaged and thinner the next day, and hundreds line up to be his apprentices after seeing him fight.
Grimalkin says he cannot swear Erin's role is coincidence, and calls her a keystone, a useful ally or unpredictable force multiplier.
Grimalkin says Erin is not Saliss of Lights but might be one day, and the only question is whose.
Grimalkin calls the chaos around Erin the 'Erin-chaos effect' in his personal notes.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin, annoyed that he cannot force open the magic door, stacks [Bound Spell: Siege Fireball], [Salamander's Skin], [Lion's Strength], [Dual Binding: Valmira's Comet], [Haste] and [Thunder Step].

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin punches the door, which vanishes without damaging the wall, and splits and burns the scales of his knuckles and cracks the floorboards.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin tells Erin her door Skill is powerful but localised to her inn, and rates its durability close to perfect.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin guesses Erin is probably Level 40, and says other Skills would suit a capstone level better.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin offers Erin a letter of introduction to Pallass' best [Innkeeper], who runs The Noble's Fancy on the 2nd Floor.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin tells Chaldion that Erin's actions came after her new Skill, and that Mrsha's disappearance bears adding to his data points.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin orders more food from Chef Lasica to build his muscles, including sushi plates, and keeps one sushi piece to stare at.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin sets up a weights room in a private room of The Wandering Inn, with six benches, and has his apprentices run the stations.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin's apprentices Ferkr, Giren and Terreskil set up and load the weights.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin has Ferkr demonstrate a bench press of a hundred and fifty pounds, with two fifty-pound weights and the bar.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin says charging the inn's door was easy because Wailant planted a third of his grass the day before.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin pays most of the attendees to appear, including Pelt, and wants a spread of muscles on display.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin presents 'weight-based training' by scrying to the Walled Cities, including the Dragonspeaker of Manus and Watch Captains.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin forwards the exact cost of a gymnasium to each Walled City.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin advises the guards with strained muscles not to use healing potions, as that would reverse their gains.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin says his digestion cleared the alcohol before he slept, and tells Chaldion Erin's Skills are less efficient than those of better inns.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin notes that the [Law of the Inn] stops even him from casting an offensive spell in The Adventurer's Haven.

section: Erin's door, the gym and the weights (Books 15-16)
text: Grimalkin buys steaks, salad and bullhen eggs into a bag of holding, calling the food junk food.
Grimalkin warns Erin that suggesting Pelt move to Liscor is poaching a high-level individual and a hostile action against Pallass.
Grimalkin warns Erin that a Walled City could blacklist her or take punitive measures, reminding her she was jailed.
Grimalkin says Pallass would like to be strongly connected with The Wandering Inn, and that he has been aiming for that himself.
Grimalkin tells Erin that Magnolia Reinhart's analysis of the Hive shows far more Antinium than any implementation of the treaty allows.
Grimalkin says Magnolia's action was beneficial to Izril and to Liscor.
Grimalkin has listed everyone who could kill him, and has analysed whether he could kill everyone he has met.
Grimalkin reasons that Erin cannot be killed because she is an asset, and wants to know where she comes from first.
Grimalkin compiles Erin's innocuous statements into a visual format as a Fissivilian [Mage], and reaches an extreme conclusion about her origins.
Grimalkin considers and rejects theories such as Erin being a Wall Lord's daughter or a [Princess], and decides she is a time traveller.
Grimalkin thinks Erin is the girl from another era, and wonders whether she comes from before or after now.
Grimalkin casts [Silence] and tells Erin Drake society may seem left behind in time, then probes Kevin the same way.
Grimalkin is deflected by Kevin, who rambles about the nature of time until a distinct scent in the air reaches Grimalkin and Erin.
Grimalkin pays Leon and Troy with a bag of coins for secret information, starting with their reaction to Master Felkhr and flight.
Grimalkin offers Leon and Troy rooms, company and artifacts through Chaldion, and notes the Reinharts are not always allies of the Walled Cities.
Grimalkin carries a magical thousand-page notebook as standard for Fissival [Mages], and has filled two with observations on Erin.
Grimalkin leaps onto a roof with a [Siege Fireball] burning in one claw as Nalthaliarstrelous spins in the fight.
Maviola points out Xrn, Saliss, Eldavin and Grimalkin as the ones who could do that, though Grimalkin might need the Heartflame Breastplate.
Grimalkin is frustrated that Manus, Fissival, Oteslia and Zeres declined to invest in his weights project.
Grimalkin knows Manus is slowly incorporating his weights into its soldier units.
Grimalkin gives Chaldion notes on 'Project Earth', speculating about a future so advanced that only stories of Dragons remain.
Grimalkin realises Lady Pryde's numbers are maximum bench-press weights, and sees one of four hundred and eleven pounds as the product of a Skill.
Lasica tells Grimalkin that Pryde is showing off how fast her group is improving.
Grimalkin copies lifting lists to Erin's gym wall, and other Walled Cities send lists of their own.
Grimalkin describes himself to Ryoka as a consultant to Pallass' standing forces, overseeing his apprentices and Pallass' [Battlemage] divisions.
Grimalkin tells Ryoka he knows she is from Earth, and offers Pallass' protection, residence and information in return.
Grimalkin says a magical prosthesis could be arranged for Ryoka's missing fingers, and that value for value is fair.
Grimalkin slips about Magnolia, which tells Ryoka that one of the Earthers from Magnolia's mansion informed Pallass.
Grimalkin's eyes flicker when Ryoka guesses Leon or Galina, and Ryoka cannot tell whether he is lying.
Grimalkin says that his offer is not a threat 'from Pallass', when Ryoka asks.
Grunter is a large Redfang Hobgoblin who fights at Esthelm and wields an axe.
Grunter asked the Horror if she was an innkeeper and learned she had been a flower-grower, not an innkeeper.
Thirteen Redfang warriors fought twenty-five black-armoured Goblins, and Grunter charged first and threw Goblins into their fellows.
Ylawes broke Grunter's right arm with his shield.
Grunter challenged the Goblin commander, killed a Hobgoblin sent against him, and shouted "Redfang!"
Grunter's axe smashed the commander's Shield Spider, and the commander's halberd then took his hand.
Grunter killed the Goblin commander with his remaining arm, and died covered by the black-armoured Goblins' blades.
Later, Headscratcher and Badarrow mourn Grunter among their fallen.
Halassia Evergleam is a Scorchling, a half-Drake, who was a member of the Gold-rank adventuring team the Halfseekers.
Scorchlings are a kind of Oldblood Drake who are born burnt by the fires within them, so that their scales flake off and cause them pain.
Halassia's scales are blackened as if by soot, many are missing, and burnt flesh shows beneath.
Halassia is an outcast among Drakes, rumoured to be cursed.
Halassia was born in Salazsar, and was shunned by her kin.
Halassia carries a wand and a staff, and is a spellcaster who blocks arrows with a spell.
Moore says Halassia was gentle, and Jelaqua says she always believed in the best of them.
Halassia tells Garen to stay behind the team and let her do the talking, since they are a Gold-rank team.
Halassia and Keilam burn a path through walls of vines for the Halfseekers in the dungeon cave.
Halassia smiles at Garen and tells the team to let him open the chest, since he gave them the lead.
Halassia slaps Keilam's paws away from the chest and sprays him with water from her staff.
Ilvriss recalls Halassia as a Scorchling in the Halfseekers' ranks a few years earlier and thanks them for taking her in when her kin would not.
Jelaqua says Halassia's family did not want her remains, and that the Halfseekers buried her themselves.
Garen says Halassia pointed a wand at his chest and said the world must never have another Goblin King, and demanded the key.
Garen says Ukrina told him to give her the key or bleed, while Halassia insisted.
Garen kills Keilam, Thornst, Ukrina and Halassia in the Halfseekers' private room, and Halassia is the last alive.
Halassia, with a severed hand, curses Garen for having been taken in and calls him a traitor before his sword is buried in her chest.
Seborn says the Halfseekers tried to take the key from Garen, and that Garen struck first.
After hearing Garen, the Halfseekers discuss whether Halassia and Ukrina, as Drakes, provoked him because the Goblin King mattered to them.
The Halfseekers paid funeral money to the families of Thornst, Keilam and Halassia.
Garen remembers the moment he struck at Halassia in his rage and despair as one he can never take back.
Halrac is the lead [Scout] and [Marksman] of the adventuring team Griffon Hunt.
Halrac is a Gold-rank adventurer.
Halrac fought Drakes and Gnolls off and on as a soldier over the years, and he distrusts both.
Halrac distrusts the Antinium and calls them heartless monsters, though he agrees to teach Bird archery later.
Halrac is a former [Soldier].
Later, Halrac is described as a [Veteran Scout], a former soldier and a Gold-rank team captain.
Halrac's unofficial nickname is Halrac the Grim, which Todi started more in jest than as a Named title.
Halrac hates the name Halrac the Grim.
Ceria says Halrac founded Griffon Hunt with Ulrien nearly a decade ago and is famous for never panicking or breaking under stress.
Selys says Halrac is a veteran who has killed Griffons by himself and is probably Liscor's closest adventurer to becoming Named.
Selys had assumed Halrac was staying at Peslas' inn rather than Erin's.
A [Merchant] becomes eager to please when Erin says she knows Halrac, and mentions that Halrac bought a nice amulet from a friend of his last year.
Bevussa has heard of Halrac, and says people call him Halrac the Grim.
Issa wonders aloud whether a man with a title must be a Named Adventurer or nearly one.
A Drake adventurer greets Halrac as Halrac the Grim.
Halrac's team had been the most renowned Griffin-slaying team in northern Izril for a time.
Halrac is a name among the Gold-rank adventurers of northern Izril.
Halrac has a Skill that Ceria guesses tells him when he is being watched.
Halrac's Skills enhance his eyesight, so that his eyes are superior to an owl's in pitch blackness.
Halrac uses a magical compass to look for the dungeon entrance; it has flashed five times over Shield Spider nests.
Halrac begins to call the activated Skill [Pinpoint Shot] when he aims at Relc, before a kick throws off his bow.
Halrac fires an ice-tipped arrow that glows blue and explodes near its target, whether the target dodges or not.
Halrac has the Skill [Dangersense], which tingles when a trap is about to fire.
Halrac's [Dangersense] rings silently in his head when a corridor is too still and may hold an ambush.
Halrac says he uses a reflex bow made from spriggan wood, enchanted for longer range and accuracy.
Halrac calls the reflex bow the best bow for close quarters and for sneaking around.
Halrac's job as a [Scout] is to be both guide and trap finder, analysing threats and leading his group away from ambushes.
Halrac fires a Phoenixflame Arrow, an expensive arrow whose head explodes into flame inside its target like a phoenix.
Halrac keeps Lightningstrike Arrows in his quiver and uses one to follow a [Fireball] from Typhenous.
Halrac uses explosive, poison, frost and fire arrows, and holds five glowing cherry-red arrows for a killing shot.
Halrac has the Skill [Arrow Grab], which lets him snatch an arrow out of the air.
Halrac's bow is invisible, and he can draw transparent arrows out of the air for stealth shots.
Halrac's invisible bow is nicknamed the invisi-bow by Revi, who uses it to annoy him.
Halrac buys only the best steel arrows and charges four copper coins per arrow that breaks or fractures.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: Halrac sits in Erin's inn and stares at Toren, who holds up a menu.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: Halrac drinks Erin's faerie-flower drink on his first try, and the drink shows him his home as it was.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: In the vision Halrac is seventeen again and stands on a hilltop above his hamlet, which in the real world is a burnt wreck.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: Halrac has loved Ariael, the Harvest Maiden, all his life up to the day she died with the others.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: In reality Ariael stood with Telfar on that day, while Halrac watched miserably.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: In the vision Ariael loves Halrac instead, and he sees his father and mother alive.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: Halrac stomps out of an inn in Liscor in a bad mood, thinking the quest for the dungeon's treasure pointless.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: Ceria says it is rare for Halrac to lose his cool.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: Halrac has become a regular at Erin's inn, coming every night, and is a good customer who is silent, throws nothing and tips well.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: Halrac tells Ryoka that Erin's drink is liquid memory, which he has drunk many times.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: Halrac says the drink brings back happy memories for a time.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: Halrac is the one customer who does not fall asleep after the drinking night, and leaves for the city staggering slightly.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: Halrac tracks Erin's trail from the inn to the bee cave and then north for miles, when Ryoka asks him to look for her.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: Ryoka finds Halrac grumpy as ever, and annoyed at being pulled from a digging discussion with Bird.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: Halrac comes by the inn one night while Erin is away and leaves without a word when Lyonette says Erin is not back.

section: Erin's inn and the faerie-flower drink, Book 2-3
text: Lyonette defers to Halrac as a Gold-rank adventurer, though she admits to being a little afraid of him.

section: The Goblin attack on the village, Book 2
text: Halrac tells a Drake messenger he is a Gold-rank adventurer and asks to be led to the village.

section: The Goblin attack on the village, Book 2
text: Halrac shoots from nearly three hundred metres away at the Goblins attacking the village.

section: The Goblin attack on the village, Book 2
text: Halrac kills the majority of the dead Goblins in the village by arrow, and three arrows are in the Goblin leader's helmet.

section: The Goblin attack on the village, Book 2
text: Halrac fires blunt arrows at Relc, then draws an ice-tipped one meant to hit even if Relc dodges.
Halrac smiles when he hears that Erin has returned.
Griffon Hunt returns early from the dungeon because Halrac hears the news about Erin.
Halrac tells Erin the dungeon's rooms change daily, so a trap disarmed one day may be replaced by a new trap or monsters.
Halrac calls the dungeon's traps some of the worst he has seen, though he has seen deadlier ones.
Halrac says the teams are trying to identify all the rooms on rotation, to find the trick behind most of them.
Halrac says there are ways to stop a magical dungeon from changing, and that the crevasse Mrsha found leads into another part of it.
Halrac says that going down the crevasse would mean multiple traps and strong monsters, and he met eight species when they rescued the child.
Erin makes Halrac a special drink with a drop of faerie-flower nectar, enough to take the edge off his day.
Halrac and Ulrien appraise the Horns of Hammerad's extra gear, and Ulrien values a matching set of enchanted plate at ten thousand gold at least.
Halrac values each of the necromancer's wands at least a thousand gold pieces, and estimates twenty-five thousand for the whole lot.
Halrac says it could be half again as much, or half that if the buyer has a haggling Skill.
Halrac passes on word that another adventurer saved a team that took the mace, and describes her as a masked swordswoman.
Halrac says the lone adventurer could resist the mace's effects, slew the monster carrying it and led the team through trap-filled hallways.
Halrac agrees to teach Bird archery after Erin asks him to show Bird tricks, Skills and arrow-making.
Halrac does not like the Antinium much, but Bird's obsession with bows wins him over.
Halrac feels his [Dangersense] tingle as a second set of ghostly blades shoots up from the ground behind a ceiling-spike trap.
Halrac leads a scouting trip with Revi along a tunnel and tells her to be quiet when a corridor feels too still.
Halrac refuses to share dungeon maps with the Silver-rank team Vuliel Drae, saying they will not help Silver-ranks kill themselves.
Halrac says the dungeon will be classified as Gold-rank or higher.
Halrac says that he and his team failed Ulrien, after Revi and Typhenous speak of how Ulrien fell to Regrika Blackpaw.
Halrac stares at the inn on its hilltop beside Liscor and does not walk toward it after admitting the failure.
Halrac, Revi and Typhenous defend Liscor's wall against Face-Eater Moths, and Halrac's arrows tear off part of one moth's face.
Halrac kills the giant Face-Eater Moth with an explosion from the cherry-red arrows, after Typhenous's [Wall of the Winds] lets arrows pass one way.
Halrac has literally one line in Erin's play, and stands like a lone sentinel on the roof.
Halrac shouts that the pit trap is a monster lair and part of the dungeon, and infers the Face-Eater Moths came from a similar trap.
Halrac retreats while loosing arrows at the Shield Spiders that pour out of the pit.
Halrac tells the Horns of Hammerad that Griffon Hunt keeps strict silence, so he moves fifteen paces ahead and uses hand signals.
Halrac's plan for an ambush is for everyone to fall back while Revi summons support and Typhenous buys time.
Halrac insists on having two of Pisces's undead Raskghar walk in front of him, as trap scouts and decoys.
Halrac says the monsters and Raskghar probably pulled back, which means the dungeon is sentient or has a controlling force.
Halrac says flatly that the missing Gnolls are already dead.
Halrac keeps shooting fleeing Cave Goblins from the wall, hitting each target, despite the Redfang Hobs shouting at him to stop.
Shorthilt blocks one of Halrac's arrows with his arm, and Badarrow fires back from the inn's roof at Halrac.
Halrac catches Bird's curving arrow with [Arrow Grab] less than an inch from his chest.
Halrac tells Erin he does not trust Goblins, and would not trust the Hobs with his back, though he will keep eating at her inn.
Halrac says that because Goblins attacked the inn, they will do so again if ordered.
Halrac says he spoke with Bird and thinks he understands him, having met people like him, even adventurers.
Halrac plans to use the Griffin-kill strategy from Screaming Falls against the Raskghar, and asks Erin for her defence food before dawn.
Revi notes that Griffon Hunt was banned after using the Screaming Falls strategy last time.
Halrac dips an arrowhead in a dark substance before the group goes on through the illusory tunnel.
Typhenous says Griffon Hunt attacked three Raskghar groups and let them run, in the hope they carry poison and sickness back.
Typhenous says the contact disease spell takes days to kill the Raskghar.
Halrac says after the failure that the Gold-rank captains are too far in and must pull out.
Halrac says he will not fight Humans if it comes to battle with Ilvriss, but will hold the walls against Goblins.
Halrac fires on Reiss's army from Liscor's walls, with a long-range shot that his invisible bow makes possible.
A stealthed arrow from Halrac streaks past Reiss.
Typhenous casts [Valmira's Comets] from the wall beside Halrac.
Halrac shoots a hawk with an arrow and offers a woman a deal of four copper coins per arrow for two hours of hunting.
Halrac says he is from Windrest, the village next to Riverfarm, near enough to Invrisil and to where Elm is working.
Halrac says there used to be a Troll in that area.
Halrac plans first to settle things up north, then to investigate rumours of Dragons carefully.
Halrac and Revi's group meet Elm, an old Griffon Hunt member who left after the plague incident, to re-establish bonds and make amends.
Halrac puts Elm, a [Ranger], headfirst through a door during their meeting.
Elm refuses the gold Griffon Hunt offers him, and the team is six thousand gold up.
Halrac says Elm can get the gold if he wants it, and that the team owes this to the old team.
Halrac plans to meet Briganda at Invrisil, who is a [Shield Maiden].
Halrac plans to contact Cassielle, the last member of the original team, who is in Terandria and has not replied to a [Message].
Halrac is now the team captain and cannot rely on glares alone.
Halrac shoots the [Raiders] chasing the Courier Lacel the Leaper with his invisible bow, so that he seems unarmed.
Halrac kills one raider with an arrow through the bridge of the nose.
Travellers call Halrac the Invisibow guy and say he has a grumpy face.
Halrac learns from Briganda that Windrest is gone, destroyed during the Goblin Lord's attacks by raids from the mountain.
Halrac was raised in Windrest, which he calls a small village.
Briganda says many Windrest survivors are at Riverfarm, and that rumours say Drakes started the fires.
Halrac accepted the notice to visit a village because it mentioned Goblins and related to his home.
Halrac accepted the notice on a hunch, and his team came with him.
Halrac learns from Master Helm that most Windrest villagers are alive, though Old Kessy died in the Goblin raids.
Halrac's face changes at the mention of Talaya, but he composes himself.
The villagers tease Halrac for being thin and unmarried, and for not sending enough [Messages] despite his Gold-rank.
Halrac stands ready beside Typhenous with a glowing-tipped arrow aimed at a tunnel hole leading to a nest.
Hammera is the nickname of the Hammer of Elbe, the Golem that Crafter Inerta enters in the Testing for the state of Elbe.
Hammera is a titanic Dwarfsteel Golem armed with a huge maul with a spike.
Hammera is a female Golem with a face shaped like a statuesque Garuda in armour, and a breastplate that Crafters gave her.
Hammera can wipe out a lesser Golem in a single blow.
Hammera has a victory routine in which she raises her hammer and struts around the stadium.
The winner of each year's Testing keeps their Golem, so Hammera carries two years of innovations.
Hammera destroys the upper torso of the spitting-Golem from Unst with one blow of her maul.
Crafters say Hammera is faster than last year because of magicore, which gives her a moment of acceleration based on stored mana.
Nsiia judges that the two best Golems are Domehead and Hammera, and that they will meet.
Hammera takes a crushing blow across her shoulder from a careless swing, which is repaired by the next bout but remains a weak point.
Domehead's axe hits Hammera's maul along the haft in their clash, and Hammera stumbles.
Domehead buries his axe in Hammera's chest, which is her weak point, but Hammera rises and the axe head falls out of her chest.
Hammera corners Domehead after his axe breaks, while the referee, who is from Elbe, refuses to stop the bout.
Hammera opens Domehead's metal cavity and destroys many of his magical bindings, though his Golem's Heart remains.
Domehead catches Hammera's hand and punches her in the face, copying moves Nsiia made against Dellic.
Hammera's face is reduced to a mangled bit of steel, but she keeps attacking, leaking magicore from her head.
Hammera is not designed to aim for Domehead's head, where his secondary routines are.
Hammera collapses with her chest dented inwards, and Domehead pounds her against a wall until someone calls the deactivation command.
Hawk is a Rabbit Beastkin of the Long Ear Tribe, with light brown fur marked by dark spots, a pink nose, two long floppy ears and a ripped build.
Hawk is a Courier, a class rarer than City Runners, and says there are fewer than a hundred Couriers on the continent.
Hawk's deliveries cover around a thousand miles, sometimes two thousand on a round trip, and he takes big jobs or none at all.
Hawk is the only Beastkin Runner on the continent, according to the narration of another Courier's visit.
Hawk is the lone Courier living in Liscor, and can do deliveries south of Liscor where City Runners cannot.
Hawk says his parents were from Liscor but did not know what names his species used, so they chose Hawk, though he would have preferred Hakss.
Hawk later says that his original parents left him in Liscor and a Drake couple took him in, and that Liscor is his home.
Hawk is afraid of loud noises and pays for soundproofing spells at home.
Hawk is trying to become a [Chef] as well as a Courier.
Hawk eats little meat and makes carrot dishes, which Selys says bore the Drakes he courts.
Selys says Hawk likes Drakes, not Gnolls or Humans, and that she dated him for only two weeks.
Selys says Hawk killed a Crypt Lord and many undead during the undead attack and carried over a hundred people to safety.
Hawk says Humans seem fleshy to him, and he would rather kiss a Minotaur than a Human.
Hawk offers Erin a Courier discount through the Runner's Guild, especially if she gives him more burgers.
Hawk normally makes Liscor's Courier runs, and Valceif covered one because Hawk was busy with the undead.
Hawk reaches Ryoka and Valceif within seconds of leaving the city gate, and shakes hands with a large paw.
Hawk warns that southern warzones use area spells and shoot at any Human running past, Runner or not.
Hawk says the Necromancer's leftover undead near the Blood Fields include wraiths, ghosts and new types.
Hawk says he ate eight hamburgers at the inn the night before and then went to bed with a Drake.

section: The Goblin Lord and the door (Books 4-8)
text: Hawk sits with Halrac and Ulrien, whom he has met on deliveries, and asks whether a room is free at the inn.

section: The Goblin Lord and the door (Books 4-8)
text: Hawk runs south and back carrying a dead Drake soldier and demands that the Council and Watch Captain Zevara be summoned.

section: The Goblin Lord and the door (Books 4-8)
text: Hawk refuses to try the road to Salazsar because of the Goblin Lord's armies, having seen two Drake armies destroyed.

section: The Goblin Lord and the door (Books 4-8)
text: Hawk delivers a thick sealed letter to Olesm, picked up in Invrisil and probably sent from First Landing on another continent.

section: The Goblin Lord and the door (Books 4-8)
text: Ilvriss orders the Courier of Liscor to carry the door's anchor to Pallass that day, whatever the Goblin threat.

section: The Goblin Lord and the door (Books 4-8)
text: Hawk runs four days to Pallass, sets up the door with a stone Pisces gave him, and tells Erin of his run.

section: The Goblin Lord and the door (Books 4-8)
text: Hawk charges Pallass triple for the job and ignores the Runner's Guild regulations.

section: The Goblin Lord and the door (Books 4-8)
text: Jelaqua reports that Hawk flatly refuses to run near the Goblin Lord's army or wait for an [Enchanter]'s appraisal of artifacts.

section: The Goblin Lord and the door (Books 4-8)
text: Hawk can cross the flooded land by jumping from hill to hill instead of swimming, because some hills are just under the water.

section: The Goblin Lord and the door (Books 4-8)
text: Hawk thinks that Klbkch, whom he has known over a decade, is well liked in Liscor.
Hawk tells Olesm that he took a holiday after a long run to Pallass, and that the Titan reads Olesm's magazine, so copies could be sold at a premium.
Hawk drinks carrot juice seasoned with a shot of rum at Rufelt's.
Hawk catches a plate by outrunning Relc, saying even the Gecko of Liscor cannot beat his legs.
Rufelt says Hawk is a customer at Tails and Scales, and that Lasica cooks carrot dishes for him.
Hawk heads north to Invrisil with deliveries, visits Selys, and says he would like to reconnect when he comes back.
Hawk delivers the Players of Celum's letters and Temile's new roster from Liscor to the Players in Invrisil.
Hawk is happy at the thought of seeing Selys again, now that she is an [Heiress].
Hawk refuses Erin's delivery, saying he is staying in Liscor in case of more riots to protect Selys.
Hawk refuses to chase the thief who mugged Welle, citing the professionalism of his class.
Selys accuses Hawk of doing nothing, and Hawk says she keeps comparing him to Pisces, so she ends their relationship of under a month.
Lord Hayvon Operland is known to some as the fifth most powerful [Lord] in the world, appearing in fifth place on rankings whatever the criteria.
Lord Hayvon is a [Lord] in service to the Blighted King of Rhir and is considered largely boring compared to the other top-ranked [Lords].
Lord Hayvon is very rich, though not as rich as the Emir Yazdil Achakhei of Chandrar.
Lord Hayvon does not care about being ranked fifth and would not blink if told so.
Hayvon Operland is described as the foremost [Lord] of Rhir and of the Blighted King's court.
Lord Hayvon's mansion balcony overlooks wheat fields worked by [Farmers], right beside the home, so close that a hop past the tiny garden lands in wheat.
Lord Hayvon deliberately keeps [Farmers] working next to his mansion because he does not believe in wasting space in Rhir.
Lord Hayvon owns Pegasus boots, made of ancient hide from the animals and decorated with feathers, that let him walk in the air.
Lord Hayvon demonstrates his Pegasus boots by walking an eighteen-step lap through the air from the balcony, over the garden and back to the railing.
Lord Hayvon says flying is simple, as simple as buying the right artifact, while growing wheat is far harder than flying.
Lord Hayvon has a son and a young daughter.
Lord Hayvon says he has ordered tens of thousands of men and women to their deaths with a single word, and has overseen at least a million deaths.
Lord Hayvon's hands are scarred from battle.
Lord Hayvon takes one deer on a hunt to feed his mansion and gives the other six bagged to the public.
Lord Hayvon's mansion is rich but not opulent, and has fewer servants than the nobility of other continents.
Richard reads that Krsysl Wordsmith's treatise ranks Lord Hayvon fifth and Lord Belchaus Meron first among the world's [Lords].
Krsysl Wordsmith's treatise calls Lord Hayvon largely practical and a staunch commander of Humans and the mixed forces sent to Rhir, with levels unknown.
Richard thinks the Drake [Writer]'s rating of Hayvon as average is complete nonsense.
Lord Hayvon says he was something of a [Historian] in his youth and even gained the class, out of a passion for literature.
Lord Hayvon says his father beat him within an inch of his life when he found out he had gained the [Historian] class.
Lord Hayvon says the Blighted King removed his [Historian] class, so he no longer levels in it.
Lord Hayvon says that he now indulges his love of history and understanding the world through his [Lord] class.
Lord Hayvon hosts Sir Richard and his company and Sir Tom as guests at his mansion; Richard's company is waiting for a ride.
Lord Hayvon tells High Magus Laisa that he would use the ritual despite knowing what it entails.
Lord Hayvon insists the ritual is no act of desperation or foolishness but a chance, and calls the Blighted King the finest ruler Rhir has had in centuries.
Lord Hayvon orders his [Mages] to question High Magus Laisa under a truth spell and, if she refuses to answer, to leave her to an [Interrogator] from the capital.
Lord Hayvon offers an old [Farmer] with a scythe, over fifty years in service, retirement in comfort anywhere in the world.
Lord Hayvon promises that, should the old [Farmer] choose to stay, all his estates will break for three days of feasting in the farmer's honor.
Lord Hayvon murmurs as he leaves that someday soon Rhir will know true peace.
Lord Hayvon watches the duel between the King of Destruction and King Raelt of Jecrass in his private quarters, with Richard beside him.
Lord Hayvon predicts that King Raelt will die unless he forfeits the duel, and cannot imagine the King of Destruction losing.
Lord Hayvon calls the duel a waste and a petty conflict while the Demons grow in strength.
Lord Hayvon, after overhearing Richard admire his Pegasus Boots, gives Richard a set of Boots of Flight from his armory.
Lord Hayvon tells Richard straight out that the Earthers cannot leave Rhir, because it is too dangerous.
Lord Hayvon announces that the Blighted King wants to gather the Earthers safely in a place separate from Rhir, such as a Walled City or a nation of Terandria.
Lord Hayvon says those committed to the fight will return to Rhir, while others such as Keith and Cynthia will have sanctuary there.
Lord Hayvon says the King of Destruction still sends aid to Rhir yearly under the Pact of Rhir.
Lord Hayvon says the King of Destruction was once defeated: Minos crippled his ambitions in one battle and the Titan of Baleros dealt the finishing blow.
Lord Hayvon says the Blighted King could slay the Deathless if they were unguarded, but wasting a handful of Skills would risk a stalemate.
Lord Hayvon rides for the walls of Rhir with three thousand elite [Lancers], [Riders] and [Knights] to relieve the besieged 5th Wall.
Lord Hayvon says his Skill cannot activate until his force is at least sixty miles from the wall, after which he could arrive in forty-five minutes.
Bastion-General Quiteil orders Lord Hayvon to hold by order of the Blighted King, and Hayvon turns his cavalry back to 4th Wall.
Lord Hayvon uses [Riders on the Storm], arriving as living lightning that turns into riders, and has his riders sweep the walls clear of Demons.
Lord Hayvon takes as large a force as he can for his Skill: three thousand enchanted [Knights] with Rhir's finest weaponry.
Lord Hayvon urges the Blighted King to let him slay the wounded Silvenia, arguing that the Deathless recovering together would make the coming days far worse.
Lord Hayvon gives Richard a ring from his finger and says he leaves everything to his son before riding at Silvenia.
Lord Hayvon ignores Quiteil's order to retreat and advances at a walk, until the Demon King orders Silvenia to fall back and she vanishes with the Demons.
Lord Hayvon finds the 5th Wall broken by the Death of Magic and says he was too late and a fool to believe there was more time.
Lord Hayvon uses the Skill [The Pride of the Fallen], and the dead of the battle, including Commander Cirille, rise as ghosts to be honored.
The ghosts raised by Hayvon's Skill march home and speak to their loved ones for an hour at most.
Headscratcher is a Redfang Hobgoblin warrior who was the first Goblin to come for the Horror at Esthelm.
Headscratcher is the strongest of the five Hobs, passionate and prone to fury in combat.
Headscratcher is seven years old and had been a warrior for six.
The Horror removed ticks from Headscratcher's head using a hot stick and her nails.
At the inn, Headscratcher mimed asking Lyonette for the leftover eggs and ate food the Antinium refused.
Erin slapped Headscratcher by mistake after he was standing on the ladder listening.
Headscratcher showed he was willing to die with a dagger at his throat if it would help the tribe.
Grief at losing Bugear and the fury of battle made Headscratcher stronger.
Headscratcher carried the wounded Badarrow through deep water and refused to let go.
Headscratcher, Badarrow, Numbtongue, Shorthilt and Rabbiteater all levelled while staying at Erin's inn.
Headscratcher weeps over Grunter, Bugear, Orangepoo and Leftstep, and his grief turns to rage.
Headscratcher reached Warrior Level 20 and changed to the [Berserker] class, gaining [Fury Strength] and [Overpowering Blow].
His new class was born of grief, and he threw a Raskghar across the room.
[Berserker] and Numbtongue's [Bard] are unique classes among Goblins.
Headscratcher was badly wounded in the side by Nokha's sword while holding off the Raskghar.
Headscratcher hit a home run in Erin's baseball game with a roar and glowing red eyes, and Erin gave him a place on a team.
Headscratcher's faction are fighters who train relentlessly and carry an enchanted axe.
Headscratcher won the axe in a brawl among the Hobs and cried with joy.
Headscratcher and others challenged Garen about his order to kill the Innkeeper, and were beaten bloody.
Headscratcher and the four other Hobs effectively took over the Redfang tribe's leadership.
Headscratcher took Erin's white flag and said he was going to leave but then saw it.
Headscratcher carries a golden axe whose jade edge cuts through Goblins' steel shields.
Az'kerash's rapier pierced Headscratcher's chest just below the heart, and he died in Erin's arms.
Healer Demerra is a female Gnoll [Healer], a City-Gnoll born and raised in Pallass, in a leadership that is mostly Drakes.

Demerra runs a personal treatment clinic where Grand Strategist Chaldion is treated, and the text calls her the best [Healer] there, and a Pallass broadcast later presents her as Pallass' own top [Healer].
Demerra tells the crowd of officials that Chaldion is fine for someone of his age falling down the stairs, but needs rest and no visitors.
Demerra says Chaldion is too old for potions to work perfectly and that she told him so last time.
Demerra says Chaldion should have a personal [Healer] or [Bodyguard] with the right specialization on him at all times, a [Minder] at the very least.
Demerra says that, even with her best crystals and recovery Skills, Chaldion must sit on his broken leg for at least two days.
Demerra tells General Edellein that bodies develop resistances to healing potions, and that he recovered faster because he is half Chaldion's age.
Demerra laughs at General Edellein's suggestion of the Healer of Tenbault and says that getting her to visit Pallass would be a miracle.
Demerra insists that Chaldion needs an aide and that someone has to order him to have one.
Demerra tells Edellein that a Ring of Health would help Chaldion but is relic-class, and that he would quickly be dependent on it.
Demerra reminds the officials that Chaldion is one hundred and six years old, then sends them to the waiting room and seals her clinic against intruders.
Demerra's clinic offers expensive treatments such as healing crystals placed around the bed, which naturally boost recovery, and floating trays, though she cannot cure old age.
Demerra allows no pests in her clinic.
Demerra gives Saliss a look of envy and annoyance because she knows, or guesses, what he can do.
Demerra organises the gatherings of a wealthy group that bids on collections, and she has a collection of fine healing crystals that rejuvenate the body.
Demerra is interviewed by Sir Relz on a Pallass broadcast about the Yellow Rivers disease, of which Pallass has reported six cases while Zeres has over a thousand.

Demerra says that her magical crystals have reversed the illness' effects in her patients and that a crystal should enhance the body's natural capabilities and lower the chance of catching the disease.
Demerra says her healing beds have cured three of the sick people, who are completely healthy, and that she is selling the crystals.
Demerra gifts a healing crystal to the broadcasting Drakes, who display it on their desk.
Drassi argues on air that even Demerra admits a full recovery still takes a week in her healing beds, and that Demerra, with six infected people in Pallass, is not on the front lines of the problem.
Demerra is present as Grimalkin and Chaldion read Geneva Scala's correspondence, there at Grimalkin's request and to follow her patient Chaldion, who snuck out of her clinic.
Demerra has two patients with the disease in a room in her clinic.
Demerra protests that her crystals are enough, but Chaldion tells her to treat the patients as the [Doctor] prescribes, and she bows after a moment's hesitation.
Demerra has questions for Geneva Scala about one patient who is doing poorly, and Geneva spends the day helping with the clinic's patients, someone having just broken a leg.
Hedag is a huge woman who is both a [Witch] and an [Executioner], who carries an iron, nicked axe and wears a plain brown hat.
Hedag travels the further villages performing the oldest task where there is no jail, watchman or law in sight but her.
Hedag comes from a line of [Executioners], a family trade that ties into her [Witch] side, and her craft is being the law.
Hedag has a booming laugh and is jovial.
Hedag has eyes in the back of her head, which she describes as a Skill, not magic.
Belavierr says Hedag was a name spread across Izril, borne by village [Executioners], and that this Hedag is the last.
Hedag grins when Belavierr asks about her predecessors, and asks Belavierr how many Hedags she killed.
Hedag uses [Revelation of Sin] to pull a black shadow out of a criminal that replays every crime he has committed, from back to front.
Hedag says her Skill reveals only the truth of criminals and cannot be swayed by magic or lies.
Hedag's Skill shows Elmmet stealing purses, changing faces, robbing a sleeping man, breaking into a house and slapping his wife while drunk.
Hedag's shadow-replay shows Elmmet beating his daughter, whose neck and shoulder bear marks, and then something worse that makes onlookers vomit.
Hedag cuts off Elmmet's hand, grips the stump to stop the bleeding, and punches him, saying that the punch is for a child beaten and the hand for a [Thief].
Hedag says "I see" and beheads Elmmet with her axe.
Hedag says she delivered the justice she had in her axe and swears before the crowd that her Skill revealed Elmmet's sins.
Prost grants Hedag leave to act as judge and arbiter in Riverfarm, but never to execute, and only alone.
Hedag says her axe is a last resort and that she will cut no man or woman down but will not promise to leave those who need her craft unscathed.
Hedag helps build houses in Riverfarm with a hammer and no magic.
Hedag says she will break the arm of a man who strikes a child, and that her craft is justice, not mercy or changing people.
Alevica claims Hedag's bounty is bigger than her own and that Hedag leaves the dead in the villages she passes.
Alevica says Hedag's bounty is only about three hundred gold pieces, because poor folk cannot afford more.
Later, Hedag patrols Riverfarm by night with Durene, whom she has taken under her wing, and answers every child's call for help.
Hedag sweeps spilled honey back into vats with Agratha and four other [Witches], and Laken gives her a pot of honey as thanks.
Hedag, with Eloise and Mavika, agrees to take about fifty children and parents out of the fire under fire-resistance charms, saying it is for the parents to decide.
Hedag holds an infant in her arms with the same terrible light in her eyes as when she swung her axe.
Hedag is among the [Witches] who hesitate when Belavierr warns them off after Califor's death, and Eloise alone swears no [Witch] will aid Belavierr.
Hedag says Hedags seldom go after [Witches], and that covens look away from a [Witch]'s sins unless a [Witch] kills another.
Hedag says a [Witch] who kills another [Witch] is hunted by the others, and that if she meets Belavierr, she owes her a Hedag's justice.
Hedag and Eloise represent the [Witches] on Laken's council, having accepted when asked.
Hedag asks Laken whether he intends to swing at the Circle, saying that if words were deeds there would be no need for the Hedag.
Hedault is an [Enchanter] of Invrisil, barely thirty, with a pale cast to his skin, pale orange hair and a missing left ring finger.
Hedault has a nervous tic of tapping an object twice with his left finger.
Hedault's wards keep all words in his home private, even from powerful mages.
Reynold says Hedault's services are recognized as the best in the city and that he never reveals information given in confidence.
Hedault later has thinning hair, spectacles and a precise manner, and taps his wrist twice.
Hedault specializes in analysis and alteration, figuring out what an enchantment does and repairing or altering it.
Hedault is precise, careful and pedantic and dislikes chaos, and the Horns of Hammerad and the inn have grown on him only as moss grows on a moist surface.
Hedault only sees visitors between dawn and sunset.
Hedault offers to explain the qualities of the Horns of Hammerad's magical items to Ryoka in his work room.
Hedault says some of his artifacts are competent examples of his craft or purchases for study, and he may sell a small selection.
Hedault agrees to Ryoka's deal after Ivolethe says the wand's core is a seed of a tree that stood ten thousand winters, calling it living magic.
Ryoka asks for armor and weapons for four adventurers, wands, a robe, a spellbook, rings and two hundred gold pieces for the wand.
Hedault says he will give what the friends need and write down a debt to Ryoka Griffin that they can call on by message.
Hedault carves an image of Ivolethe in Everfrozen Ice for Ryoka, signing the note as [Enchanter] of Invrisil.
Hedault probably charged Ryoka only a small fortune as a favor.
Hedault blacklists Yvlon and Ksmvr for interrupting him, then relents when they name Ryoka Griffin and the Horns of Hammerad.
Hedault agrees to appraise both the Horns' and Griffon Hunt's dungeon treasure at dawn the next day.
Hedault has a wand of ironwood with which he feels the enchantment in the magic door.
Hedault identifies the magic door as the work of Warmage Thresk of Albez, with a crude alteration to his teleportation trap.
Hedault's first pass through the inn ends up enchanting Numbtongue's guitar, which fascinated him.
Hedault has been trying to limit the draw of the inn's runes on mana with Montressa, setting several basic enchantments.
Hedault arrives forty minutes after a request through Montressa du Valeross and casts [Impact Shield], [Second Skin: Film Weave] and [Invisibility] outside the door.
Hedault says pure metals hold enchantments well and could halve a thirty-pound block of Pelt's pure steel and nearly reduce it to a third.
Hedault will enchant a saddle with a [Cushion] spell and suggests a Ring of Feather Impact.
Hedault says one final test of a true [Enchanter] in most Terandrian academies is making a block of mithril float on his breath alone.
Hedault tells Lism and Krshia that any city has a limit to the enchanted defenses it can maintain, because of mana draw.
Hedault says Liscor's wall enchantments will eventually draw more than ambient mana as it grows, though it is not near that size yet.
Hedault lists four ways to bypass the limit: Sage's Grass, Magicore, magical herds and [Mages].
Hedault says Invrisil is spared by lacking walls, its many mages and its ley line, and that the Walled Cities bypass the limit by means lost to time.
Montressa and Bezale count Hedault among their clients.
Hekra is a Gnoll of the Stone Spears Tribe who carries a bow and hunts in the winter forest.
Hekra moves so unseen that Ryoka's heart skips when she steps out from behind a slim tree.
Hekra greets Ryoka by name and says she is hunting, though not for game, as there is none to be found.
Hekra asks Ryoka whether she was talking with the Winter Sprites.
Hekra fights the Goblins as an archer with three other archers.
Hekra's hand blurs as she shoots, and two Goblins fall with arrows in their chests.
Helm is a [Blacksmith] from Windrest, a village fourteen miles east of Riverfarm by a big prairie.
Helm arrives at Riverfarm frozen and nearly falling from his saddle, brought by the Windfrozen Riders.
Helm weeps when he sees Riverfarm and hears about the avalanche, and hugs Prost.
Helm reports that Windrest is burning.
Helm and Tessia hurry to the larger trebuchet when Laken calls them to demonstrate it to the visiting lords.
Helm is a huge, middle-aged [Blacksmith] who greets Halrac with a hug and is proud of him like a father.
Helm tells Halrac that most Windrest folk survive, though Old Kessy died with an arrow in her during the Goblin raids.
Helm says Eldrim is alive, Turc is now married, and Talaya wrote that she was fine.
Helm says a Goblin Lord nearly overran Riverfarm, but His Majesty dealt with her right quickly.
Helm is now a [Royal Blacksmith] with new Skills, including [Perfect Temperature Control], so his steel never overheats.
Hendric is a Silver-rank adventurer and the captain of the Swordlock Dogs.
The Swordlock Dogs are a Silver-rank team more known up north.
Hendric has a scarred face and talks about how to behead the goats properly.
Hendric pulls out of the expedition into the Ruins of Liscor at the last moment, and Calruz calls him a coward.
Hendric was supposed to be talking to Calruz and the others in Liscor about the expedition.
Hesseif is one of the [Caravan Guards] of Clan Tannousin, who pokes his head in to check on Nawal and then goes back to watching for thieves.
Hesseif is chiefly tasked with the defence of the Tannousin caravan.
Hesseif is a large man with a broad, shaved head, and a proper [Warrior].
Hesseif is rather timid outside of battle, although he and Silmak are technically in charge of the caravan.
Bezha is Hesseif's aunt.
Nawal calls Hesseif the best fighter the clan sent.
Nawal is relieved to feel Hesseif's presence at her back when her clansmen appear to face the [Slaver] who tried to enforce her brother Allaif's sale contract.
Hesseif shifts behind Nawal as she readies for a bloody fight with the [Slaver] and his thugs.
Hesseif bows with Silmak, Bezha and Nawal to greet Orthenon and Gazi when the caravan reaches Reim.
Hesseif has a private room in the palace, as do Silmak, Bezha and Nawal.
Hesseif confirms that Trey is the same foreign boy whom Nawal met earlier.
Hesseif promises to guard the Naq-Alrama metal day and night, letting no one not of the clan's blood enter and no sunlight in.
Hesseif and Silmak inspect the swords and crucible steel in Master Daiton's forge, after Nawal's challenge.
Hesseif and three other men carry a huge stone box into the forge.
Hesseif appears behind Trey and a smith's apprentice during the forging, and shakes his head at a twice-quenched blade that is not perfect.
Hesseif leads a group of men dragging the barrel into the circle where air is not permitted.
Nawal hands Hesseif the finished sword and tells him to guard it until the King of Destruction touches it.
Hesseif nearly tackles Trey when Trey catches Nawal as she faints.
Hesseif stands behind Nawal, with Bezhavil and Silmak, while Nawal lies to Lord Venith and Lady Maresar about the Naq-Alrama steel's progress.
Hesseif agrees with Nawal that the clan can wait for Trey Atwood no longer and should tell the truth.
Hesseif cannot meet Nawal's eyes, in shame, when she storms out after the clan refuses to tell Flos.
Hetarria is a female Drake [Captain] in white armor who leads a group of specialists, and who speaks with Rhir's accent rather than the more sibilant Drake tongue.
Hetarria is a [Necromancer] who holds the rank of [Mage-Captain], and her white armor is made of ivory-like bone.
Hetarria is military, affable and has a white grin with excellent teeth, which Cirille finds likeable despite her class.
Hetarria has one grandparent from Izril, and her parents, [Traders], went back and forth but told her never to visit once she studied [Necromancy].
Hetarria has never visited Izril.
Hetarria's force controls a Bone Behemoth that Cirille realises is shaped like a Drake, with polished white bone armor and a mace of bones.
Cirille calls Hetarria and her Drakes [Necromancers] in horror, and Hetarria says the Bone Behemoth is theirs.
Cirille asks Quiteil not to assign her brigade with the [Necromancers], and he denies the request.
Quiteil says Hetarria has fought for years without issue, her creations never run amok, and he would take ten thousand more like her.
Quiteil says Rhir remembers Archmage Chandler's contribution to the offensive against the Demons a hundred and fifty years ago, and that his legacy is the [Necromancer] corps.
Quiteil says the Bone Behemoth is a war construct that Hetarria's force controls, which does not bleed or die and can be repaired.
Quiteil says he will allow Hetarria time to air grievances with Cirille, though he considers it an imposition on her.
Hetarria leads the [Necromancer] corps in a Bone Behemoth fight against serpent-titans, ordering it to sweep the leg and using [Mend Bone].
Hetarria orders the Bone Behemoth to charge in a frenzy against a titan marked by the Bastion-General.
Hetarria says the Bone Behemoth has nearly forty three years of service and has been ground down and smashed but rebuilt with more [Necromancers].
Hetarria keeps watch at night as Rhir requires undead to be monitored at all times.
Hetarria says Bastion-General Zavarial authorised support units of skeleton archers who climb on the Bone Behemoth and shoot.
Hetarria says the undead are bodies of volunteers from a registry, and that some volunteer for [Golem Artificers] or blood magic.
Hetarria says every [Necromancer] trained in Rhir's schools must study Crypt Lords, Wailing Pits or Dorn Pillars before animating the dead.
Hetarria says Rhir's schools are utilitarian and include experimental practices with captive undead to study the enemy.
Hetarria says Wailing Pits and Dorn Pillars are collections of undead that think, talk and command others, and a Dorn Pillar left underground can wipe out a city.
Hethon is the elder son of Tyrion Veltras and is fourteen years old, described by others as studious, diligent and level-headed.
Hethon is interested in books and does not have his mother's eyes, instead having the eyes of Tyrion's father.
Hethon's mother Salva died four years before the lance practice, and Hethon and Tyrion are strangers to each other.
Hethon excitedly tells Ullim about hitting the hoop on his first try.
Tyrion helps Hethon hit a hoop target on the practice dummy, using one Skill to improve aim while guiding the horse.
Hethon snaps the wooden hoop off the dummy on his first try, and Tyrion tells him it was not luck.
Tyrion tells Hethon that he did very well, may have hidden talent as a lancer, and that it was exemplary work.
Tyrion has the ring kept as a trophy, and Hethon beams at the applause of the Veltras folk.
Tyrion says Hethon hit the target six times out of ten, even without his Skills.
Ullim says Hethon's eyes are excellent and he will have the tutors focus on it in lessons.
Hethon has not seen his friend Eliasor in a few months, whose mother was killed by [Assassins].
Hethon hears Tyrion's account of the battle with the Assassin's Guild and listens agog while Tyrion downplays it.
Hethon falls ill ten minutes before an [Assassin] from the Assassin's Guild arrives, claiming a stomachache, and then does not respond.
Hethon and Sammial remain gravely ill, with Hethon's breathing shallow and laboured, while Tyrion sits with the blood contract.
Hexel Quithail is a male Lamia [Architect] hired to build Liscor, and an anomaly in southern Izril even among Lizardfolk.
Hexel is of average height when upright, with larger scales than a Drake, a long serpentine lower half and two human-like arms.
Hexel has a scar on one cheek that runs down his face.
The narration calls Hexel one of the Naga, a broad term for the higher forms the Lizardpeople of Baleros can become.
Hexel is one of four Lizardfolk living in Liscor at the time of Mrsha's meeting with him.
Hexel and Elirr are around the same age, though a Lamia would live possibly twice as long as a Gnoll.
Hexel lands at Zeres, sails north to Human lands, and is escorted by Lady Reinhart to Invrisil before reaching Liscor.
Hexel arrives at the inn with three nervous Lizardfolk assistants carrying bags, and introduces himself to the Council.
Hexel says he was delighted to be offered the job of building a city like Liscor.
Hexel says he would love to see maps of the Antinium tunnels so he can rework the city to avoid sabotage.
Hexel tells the Council that Drakes slaughtered half his [Assistants] and gave him his scar on his journey north from Zeres.
Hexel demands non-Drake [Bodyguards], Gnolls or Humans preferably, and threatens to return to Baleros without them.
The Council promises Hexel bodyguards, and Lism protests that the attackers were bandits and not Liscor's people.
Hexel says he was forced to kill the rest after the Drake ambush.
Erin sees Hexel naked at his window the morning after he arrives.
Hexel asks Lyonette about entering Liscor from the inn and complains that his bodyguards have not arrived, telling Yemmi not to worry.
Hexel tells the Council he wants multiple bodyguards, one per assistant, and that Baleros' Guild of Builders will hear if they fail.
Hexel insists on Level 20 or higher if the Watch is used as bodyguards.
Hexel uses [Ambition Visualized] to present a first design that expands Liscor with high-occupancy housing, two parks and a larger sewer network.
Hexel's second plan adds a second tier of aerial walkways and streets, and he says it will triple the city's capacity.
Hexel's second plan replaces the walls with fifty-foot sloped walls and doubles the landmass by expanding west and south.
Hexel's second plan places a deep lake in the city centre, nearly three times as deep as Liscor is tall.
Hexel says the lake could be drained and used as a last-resort flood against the Hive.
Hexel says the lake would draw on the Floodplains' groundwater, perhaps raised by a few [Hydromancers].
The Council gasps at the revised budget, which Tismel calls outrageous, and Hexel offers to start only after funding is secured.
Hexel says he devised the plan in one night while drinking with Councilmember Elirr.
Elirr appoints himself liaison to Hexel, and Jeva Silverfang says Hexel is already smoothing out the Floodplains for a football pitch.
Hexel's three Lizardfolk apprentices stay afraid of Drakes and take their breakfast in their room.
Hexel tells Erin he is going to breakfast with Councilman Elirr.
