Hexel tells Mrsha the Council has him working so hard that his tail is raw.
Hexel's team of builders once numbered eighteen of the finest of Baleros, and now he has only three apprentices.
Hexel scolds his Lizardfolk assistants, telling Zekky and Vile to stop cowering when a Drake server approaches.
Hexel packs a wooden bento-style lunch box into a bag of holding for breakfast with Elirr.
Hexel and Elirr are in a secret relationship, and Mrsha, caught sneaking out of the shop by Elirr's cats, sees it.
Hexel coils his lower half around Elirr and later twines his tail around Elirr's foot.
Elirr asks Mrsha to tell no one, including Erin and Numbtongue, because it could mean danger for him and Hexel.
Hexel says some people will not like it, and that he might leave but Elirr has to live in Liscor.
Hexel says Dullahans hate same-sex couples, Naga are not opposed, and Centaurs are very bad, sometimes.
Hexel helps make sure Mrsha understands why she must not tell, and she nods her agreement.
Himilt is Fierre's father and Colfa's husband, and he dresses as a working farmer with muddy clothes and callused hands.
Himilt is a vampire and farmer who keeps sheep and other animals on the old Drakle estate.
Himilt is the most Vampire-like of Fierre's family, though he seems to Ryoka to be pretending to be normal.
Himilt's neck has been swollen since about six years before Ryoka meets him, a symptom Ryoka compares to thyroid cancer.
Himilt casts no shadow.
Himilt argues that Ryoka should not have been abducted, and suggests letting her learn the family's secret.
Himilt shakes Ryoka's hand gently.
Himilt warns Ryoka he will find and kill her if she reveals Fierre's secret or puts her in harm's way.
Himilt shows Ryoka the ruined estate, says the Drakles moved for thousands of years, and stands briefly proud before returning to a farmer's manner.
Himilt tells Fierre that Ryoka is someone to watch, though he means it as a warning.
Himilt holds a hatred of [Knights] who hunted down his family, according to Fierre, especially old houses like the Byres family.
Himilt tells Fierre it is better to be what they are, people in hiding, because Vampires once ruled part of Izril and fell.
Himilt says Vampires once could change forms, cast magic and command lesser beings, and that the greatest feared only dragonfire.
Himilt says a sickness began after a long war, that many powers were lost in the first generations and the affliction stabilised within eight generations.
Himilt says Colfa has a rash because she became a Vampire late in life, and that Bamer, Rivel and Fierre were born with the signs.
Himilt says Vampires committed crimes that made other species recoil in horror, but he would never accept that this is just.
Himilt remembers with Bamer when House Byres' plan was put forward, so some places for Vampires to live are off the table.
Himilt sits by his daughter's bedside while she suffers from fever, rash and pain, holding her hand.
Himilt runs a great distance to bring Fierre packets of meat and blood for lunch and is embarrassed in front of Ryoka.
Himilt says the family boiled water rather than drink from the well, now freshly topped up with silver.
Himilt says he will try charcoal pills first, and refuses to flee since that is what House Byres wants.
Himilt says the family bought breeding pairs from overseas and needs new flocks that were not raised in Izril.
Himilt says there are several thousand Vampires in Izril, in scattered families, settlements, clans and towns.
Himilt says Vampires of Drakes and Gnolls were hunted more bitterly by their own kind, and contact with them was lost.
Holdnose is an elderly Goblin of nearly seven years, from the Flooded Waters tribe, an original Goblin of Liscor.
Holdnose knew Chieftain Rags when she was born, followed her north, and returned to Liscor, only to be captured at the end of the terrible battle.
Holdnose has the class [Rotter], which Pebblesnatch has never encountered before.
Holdnose is a fermentation expert who knows how to turn perfectly good food into a rotten, fermented substance.
Holdnose sets up a stinking camp in a stone cave by the river, with pots, pans and stone vessels full of fish sauce.
Holdnose explains that fish sauce takes a month or two of sealed fermentation, but his Skills let him finish a batch in only one week.
Holdnose trades Pebblesnatch a precious jar of fish sauce for sixteen wrapleaf rolls, and promises more as he experiments with everything.
Holdnose plans to ferment cucumbers in another pot.
The Gnoll [Fermenter] Ushel runs a substantially cleaner and more upscale operation than Holdnose's, though the two would respect each other as fellow craftsmen.
Hunt is one of the most senior members of the Horns of Hammerad, with a mace and a beard.
Hunt has egg in his beard at supper, which Gerial does not mention.
Hunt growls and grips his mace when he sees another group of armed adventurers sitting by a fire.
Hunt is left out of commission but alive after the first ambush.
Later, Erin finds Hunt lying still and dead among the bodies on the Ruins' second floor.
Idis is a Selphid from the Minds, the Selphids' leaders, who takes over sharing Geneva Scala's body in place of Okasha.
Idis tells Geneva she is helping her move because Okasha was trying to take her over, and that the Minds want to meet Geneva.
Idis says she won the honor of the task and the Minds thought she would be best, with other Selphids available if she does not suit.
Idis says she is strong and can be relied on to kill whoever tries to hurt Geneva.
Idis is a Level 32 [Blademaster] and a Level 14 [Barbarian].
Idis says she will help Geneva move and manage her, as Okasha did.
Idis naps while Geneva treats a patient and lectures, then whispers in Geneva's head as Seve speaks of the Carven City.
Idis stops Geneva's mouth when Seve asks for the names of those who made the Occillium, saying the information is important and she must run it by Calectus.
Idis gives in and lets Geneva give a single name, then mutters about breaking the rules.
Lady Ieka Imarris is a [Lady] and [Mage Lady], one of the few nobles able to perform true magic.
Ieka attended Wistram Academy, a rarity for a first-born noble scion.
Rumour says Ieka was expelled from Wistram for unknown reasons after four years.
Ieka believes in magic and has instituted magical reforms in her lands, such as self-drawing wells powered by magic.
Ieka reclines in a chair made of Deguree Rabbit pelts and tails, among the softest substances in the world.
Ieka copies good ideas from her peers, so her [Spellarmor Warriors] copy Lady Bethal's Knights of the Petal.
Ieka's bodyguards are all women [Spellarmor Warriors], led by Captain Kelda, who wears thick ensorcelled plate and carries a mace.
Ieka hired the half-Elf [Aide] Zenna about two decades ago, copying the House of El's use of half-Elven guides.
Ieka and Tyrion Veltras were childhood friends or acquaintances, though it is still poor manners for her to use his name.
The Imarris family is a traditional ally of House Veltras, and Ieka is more allied than most.
Ieka has fought the Goblin King and lost her sister at the Sacrifice of Roses.
Ieka dislikes Magnolia Reinhart, thinking her shallow, manipulative and controlling, and believing Izril does not need her.
Ieka is certain Magnolia and Ressa are in a relationship, though she cannot prove it.
Laken regards Lady Ieka as a noble who makes him nervous.
Ieka is a member of the Circle of Thorns, which asks only loyalty and treats private affairs as meaningless so long as they stay secret.
Hatred of Magnolia Reinhart is one reason Ieka joined the Circle of Thorns.
Ieka believes past Circles fought off invasions from Chandrar and Baleros and humbled Khelt, but that the group mostly waxes and wanes into uselessness.
Ieka has doubts about a Circle that tries to kill without hesitation like the group that slew Suvelta.
Ieka is a higher-ranking Circle member with the power to pull strings for Lady Rie's requests.
Ieka is attracted to women, a secret she keeps from the public.
Ieka has an unhealthy relationship with her [Maids], many of whom are lovers, which is deviant by Izril, Terandrian and Drake standards.
Ieka's fondness for [Maids] comes from Magnolia and Ressa.
Lady Rie tells Ieka that her new [Maid] Sidel is in the employ of Wistram, and Rie's [Gracious Invitation] stops Sidel from fleeing.
Ieka rents a luxury room in an Invrisil inn, though Magnolia owns the city, and resents having no estate there.
Ieka's guards insult Ryoka as a lapdog of Magnolia, and Delanay d'Artien challenges Captain Kelda before Zenna admits them.
Ryoka asks Ieka for a favour, to attend an event at the Summer Solstice, and Ieka thinks the request intriguing.
Ieka's own request is that Ryoka contact a dangerous hermit Archmage, in seclusion on an island for months.
Ieka expects Ryoka may die, like the last three she sent, including one Courier.
Ieka herself tried to reach the Archmage in the third year of her absence, lost three people and fled after the room of mirrors.
A Named Adventurer quit the assignment to wake the Archmage that Ieka hired Salamani for.
Ieka rejoices that Valeterisa is out of seclusion and plans to recommend Ryoka as a Courier.
Ieka plans to arrange the party Ryoka requested in Riverfarm and supply mage-illusions herself.
Ieka receives Ryoka and Salamani, has three hundred gold coins brought for Salamani, and shows Ryoka a pile of gold for show.
The Merchant's Guild will pay Ryoka the full collective bounty for waking the Archmage.
Ieka promises to ensure the Runner's Guild accepts Ryoka's candidacy for Courier.
Ieka promises to attend Ryoka's party and to prevail on the Five Families to join her.
Ieka scowls at the Circle's plan against Tyrion Veltras' children, the largest scowl she has had.
Ieka detects that Ryoka has no levels and that her detection spell was not blocked, and feels she spoke to a ghost.
Ijvani is an undead skeleton [Mage] and one of Az'kerash's Chosen, with black iron bones carved with glowing runes.
Ijvani's golden eyes burn in her skull, and her magic is on par with any Gold-rank adventurer.
Ijvani's bones shine black, and she weighs far more than she should since her body is a kind of armour.
Ijvani says she and Oom are the eldest of Az'kerash's creations and that Venitra is the youngest.
Venitra says she is Az'kerash's favourite, and that she chose Ijvani as her tracker.
Venitra calls Ijvani and Oom their best trackers.
A woman of bone and a shadow, Venitra and Ijvani, walked through snow for three days, sent to find the Courier Ryoka.
Ijvani asked Venitra if they were lost; the narration says they were roughly seventy miles off course.
Venitra and Ijvani killed Goblins of the Goblin Lord's army who ambushed them, then spoke with the Goblin Lord, whose eyes reminded Venitra of her master's.
They set off through the snow to Liscor to find Ryoka Griffin.
Using a map from a corpse they had killed, they mistook Esthelm for Liscor after crossing a mountain.
A dark-purple Drake [Mage] named Imenet walked beside Regrika Blackpaw, a Gold-rank adventurer.
Ijvani cast an eavesdropping barrier, a truth spell and a paralysis on Ryoka.
Ijvani put a listening spell on Ryoka, and Ivolethe warned that the spell cannot detect the fae.
Ijvani carries a staff of bone with a golden gem, and an invisible barrier fractured Ryoka's foot.
Az'kerash spoke through Ijvani's mouth and healed Ryoka's foot.
As Imenet, Ijvani used [Lesser Teleport] to take Zel and Ilvriss away after being hit by Halrac's arrow and Zel's claws.
Imenet created illusions of himself, raised Golems from the flagstones and rained spells on Celum while Zel fought him.
Zel found Imenet hard like armour when cut.
Zel's claws cut through Ijvani's ribs and Ilvriss cut off her leg, which pained her mentally.
After Zel Shivertail's death, Ijvani was left to walk back alone because there were no more teleport scrolls.
Ijvani sits in a pit in the ground, her robes puddled and filthy, for ninety-six days since Az'kerash last contacted her.
Ijvani believes that Az'kerash has forgotten or replaced her, and fears she is like Viltraid.
Ijvani grabbed a healing slime that rolled out of a Shield Spider pit, and the Shield Spiders swarmed her.
Az'kerash sensed that Ijvani was still absent months after Zel Shivertail's death and found her sitting in a cave.
Az'kerash ordered her to stay put and set up a surveillance spell that Grimalkin of Pallass could not detect.
Ijvani put the healing slime inside her ribcage, held by a [Forcewall] spell.
Az'kerash ordered Ijvani to watch Pisces and Montressa, build a teleportation rune usable by two people near the Bloodfields, and prepare for combat.
Ijvani held a [Bound Spell - Blackfire Fireball] in her jaw.
Az'kerash let Ijvani keep the slime.
Ijvani gathered Toren's bones on Az'kerash's order, and later silenced Toren's screaming soul with a smack.
Ijvani had found the healing slime with the Defenders of the Cave, Shield Spiders and Fortress Beavers.
Az'kerash saw that the slime's body uses a minor healing potion as a base.
Az'kerash told Ijvani that she and his other Chosen will be altered to give them the ability to level.
Illphres is an older Human [Cryomancer] at Wistram, described as one of the best [Cryomancers] in the academy and a temperamental teacher.
Calvaron places her with the Isolationists, and he warns Ceria she is angry.
She appears to be in her late thirties, with slightly greying hair and a smooth, wrinkle-free face.
She teaches elemental magic, which she says she was forced to do by the Council even though she has better things to do.
She speaks abruptly with no welcome, and her face seems frozen, neither smiling nor frowning nor blinking.
In the dining hall, Illphres casts the Tier 4 spell [Ice Lance] within seconds, without a wand.
Ceria is impressed by the speed of her casting, though ice is not Ceria's specialty.
She sets her entry test with an [Ice Wall] sealing the classroom door and orders students to melt it without an artifact or another mage.
She says she made the wall impervious to spells below Tier 4, and did not expect anyone to use salt.
She freezes a seagull's wings with a shot of ice to demonstrate aim, and its wings melt as it nears the water.
She says everything is a moving target and that Ceria will never improve by aiming at stationary points.
She explains that a silver bell is given for reaching a certain [Fencer] level or for proving oneself against a master duelist.
Her spellbook has a light blue cover, and she says a spell can only be scribed by someone of equal or higher level than the spell.
She says it would take a Level 40 [Magical Scribe] to write down a spell such as the one in her book.
She says Level 50, let alone Level 60, is the utmost limit mages at Wistram can strive for.
Illphres says Amerys has only six or eight levels on her.
Illphres plans to use [Fortress of the Ice Queen], a famous spell, right away in the battle to shield the others.
Illphres' lower face is blackened with dead, frostbitten skin, hidden beneath a mask of ice.
She reshapes the ice to smile and says she has to alter her face to do so.
She often covers her mouth when she changes her features to a grin.
Jurix knows her secret.
Ceria later realizes Illphres is actually a bit younger than herself, though she feels much older.
After Ceria demands to be taught, Illphres tells her to melt the ice first.
Ceria melts the wall using salt rubbed on it and heat from her own spells.
Pirates attack Wistram's ship, and Illphres skates across the sea on ice, breaking hulls with pillars of ice and killing a mage with an ice spike.
Her mask falls to pieces as she fights the [Storm Captain], and her freezing spell freezes the deck and the captain.
She tells Ceria that this is what the face of a true mage looks like.
She agrees to teach Ceria magic if she truly wants it, and Ceria takes her hand.
Illphres says she and Amerys compete and sometimes train together because they are a good match.
She says Amerys prefers rapid all-out assaults while she uses traps and drawn-out battles, and Amerys will not join her because she is waiting for her King.
Amerys later says she refused Illphres' request to help despite the risk.
Illphres tells Ceria she has prepared for the challenge for over a decade.
She claims that winning will end the Council's rule, so mages will guard the entrance and it will be every mage for themselves.
She reasons that the missing original Golem shows a past group broke the Golems' tandem formation and nearly won.
She tells Ceria she grew up in Wistram and never adventured, and might not be so scared if she had.
Before the doors close she says "This is magic".
Illphres enters the Golems' room with Jurix, Qum, Bastam and Ophelia, and dies in the challenge.
Her body is brought out and raised as a Lich by Pisces, and she hits a Golem with a stone-cracking blow before they flee.
Amerys later blasts open a frost-covered door, comes out with an ice-blue spellbook and orders a student to send it to Ceria.
Charles de Trevalier drops it into the sea, where it freezes the water and sinks.
Later, Ceria recalls Illphres telling her that she could not yet shape her ice, comparing the structure of her [Ice Walls] to an [Architect]'s.
Ceria also recalls Illphres calling the mask an example of ice shaping, and telling her to put an edge on a dagger.
Ilvriss Gemscale is a Drake [Lord] and Wall Lord of the Walled City of Salazsar.
Ilvriss has a sworn duty as a Lord of the Wall to defend his city and Drakes from enemies.
Ilvriss tends to be proud and quick to anger toward Humans and Goblins, but later changes in his dealings with Erin and Liscor.
Ilvriss is a Drake [Lord] known as the Lord of the Wall, in charge of the army that blocks the pass Ryoka is travelling through.
Ilvriss wears pristine red-and-gold armor and is not covered in muck, snow and blood like his soldiers.
Ilvriss's army holds the only viable pass and does not need to move, as the Humans must try to get out elsewhere or attack head-on.
Ilvriss says a [Lord] can detect falsehoods like any other class, and he knows Ryoka speaks the truth, but she is still there.
Ilvriss's aide Berlyrssat tests the stone Ryoka carries with a quartz and finds it a potent artifact of Tier 5 or higher.
Ilvriss, with his subordinate Periss and the elite soldiers behind them, strides toward Zel Shivertail and Ryoka with his sword drawn.
Ilvriss has red eyes and a bad stench in the scene, which keeps his elite soldiers standing back.
An emerald ring on Ilvriss's hand cracks and breaks, and he whispers Periss's name, lowering his sword.
Zel seizes Ilvriss's blade while he stares at the ring, and punches him on the chin so that he collapses.
Zel carries the unconscious Ilvriss away on his shoulder, leaving the broken ring behind, and pretends not to see his tears.
Ilvriss is allowed to keep his armor but not his sword while marching next to Zel as a prisoner.
Ilvriss does not worry about prisoners escaping, as the laws of war and his own sense of honor forbid it.
Ilvriss says he will not speculate about Periss's fate but will investigate it once restored to his city.
Ilvriss and Zel Shivertail walk north through blowing snow toward Liscor with a large retinue that annoys Zel.
Ilvriss tells Zel that unlike Zel, he is a Lord of the Wall whose position forces him to bring attendants.
Ilvriss and Zel dislike each other's presence but tolerate each other out of respect.
Ilvriss and Zel passed the Blood Fields a day ago and are one more day from Liscor.
Ilvriss refuses to stay at the same inn as Zel and chooses the Tailless Thief, which he calls the best inn in the city and whose owner he knows.
Ilvriss and Zel advance down a street in a trance, the memory of the Antinium Wars seizing them, and Ilvriss strikes a guard who grabs at him.
Ilvriss remembers a battle where he coordinated Drakes and Humans against Antinium until Xrn burned the command tent.
Pawn and twenty Soldiers bar Klbkch's way while Zevara and her guardsmen form a wall against Zel and the Wall Lord.
Relc greets Zel, which breaks the memory's hold on Klbkch, and the Antinium withdraw while the Watch and Zel let them go.
Ilvriss argues with Zel at the gate, saying he would rather eat his tail than sit in the same room as an Ant.
Ilvriss stands warm in a heavy fur coat and enchanted clothing while Zel shivers at Liscor's gates.
Ilvriss tells Zel to watch out for the Antinium and Humans, while Zel replies that Liscor's leaders know nothing about why Xrn is there.
Ilvriss is one of the sworn protectors of the Walled Cities, specifically the Wall Lord of Salazsar.
Zel travels with Ilvriss largely for the Wall Lord's network of informants.
Ilvriss has told his contacts to inform him the instant Ryoka Griffin is seen and says he would go north himself if not for the Antinium situation.
Zel tells Ilvriss that he has asked only Drakes, so he should talk to Humans to find a Human.
Ilvriss says Humans lie and that he has more faith in his own kind than in others.
Ilvriss says the Goblin Lord is still the lesser threat, and he wants to know why the Slayer and the Small Queen are meeting.
Ilvriss and Zel use intimidation Skills unconsciously during their argument, which empties the inn around them.
Ilvriss arrives with Zel and about fourteen armed Drakes in fancy clothing, and announces he will speak to Ryoka on a matter of war.
Ilvriss says he will treat everyone who blocks him as his enemy.
Ilvriss uses a Skill that makes him taller with burning eyes and frightens the Gnolls, but Ryoka fights it off.
Ilvriss asks Ryoka how his lieutenant Periss died, and Ryoka answers that she cannot tell him.
Ilvriss is publicly confronting Ryoka over Periss's death in the street in front of the Gnolls and Mrsha.
Welsca Crimsonscale, in service to Wall Lord Ilvriss, tells Erin and Ryoka in their bath that Ilvriss has decided to forgive transgressions against him.
Welsca says Ilvriss would consider it a personal favor and an act of trust if Ryoka spoke with him.
Ilvriss's men tell Ryoka that Ilvriss wants to know only where Captain Periss is and how she died.
Ilvriss concludes that the Goblin Lord will head north and wants nearby villages cleared and his movements tracked.
Ilvriss hopes the Goblin Lord becomes the Humans' problem, though he says they must prepare either way.
Ilvriss demands to know how Periss and the missing soldiers died, and Ryoka answers that the Runner's code forbids her to say.
Ilvriss is in the fight in the streets of Liscor against Regrika and Imenet, where he climbs on a roof and drops to the ground landing as lightly as a cat.
Ilvriss twists a ring on his finger that flashes, summoning bodyguards.
Ilvriss has an amulet with a radius of about ten feet that he uses to search for an enemy.
Ryoka tells Ilvriss that the Necromancer killed Periss and sent Regrika and Imenet to kill her, and warns that he will send them against Ilvriss too.
Ilvriss goes limp and collapses to the ground, shaking, when he hears about the Necromancer.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss, a Lord of the Wall from Salazsar, stays in Liscor because the Goblin Lord's armies make it impossible to return safely to his home city.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss buys rounds for his retinue and fellow Drakes, saying a Lord of the Wall treats his brethren with due respect.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss has already gone out twice and slaughtered a Hollowstone Deceiver and a number of Shield Spider nests while stuck in Liscor.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss is maudlin since the battle with Regrika Blackpaw and Imenet, snapping at people, drinking to excess and falling into melancholy.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss tells a story about his finest subordinate Periss, a warrior and leader beyond repute, and recalls the day he first met her.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss tells Olesm that [Strategists] are Level 30 or lower, or can be lower if a military rank is combined with the [Tactician] class.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss has taken Olesm under his tail, so Olesm has to drink with him and listen to talk of politics and the days before the Antinium.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Hawk the Courier has seen a Wall Lord and General Shivertail suffer defeat at the Goblin Lord's hand, followed by the destruction of two Drake armies.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss turns away and closes his eyes in grief when Zel talks to him, having found out who killed Periss from Ryoka.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss is slumped over and cradling his head, and the disciplined arrogant front the Wall Lord wore at all times is gone.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss tells Zel he would have married Periss if she had not thought it beneath his station.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Zel scolds Ilvriss for drinking again, and Ilvriss says he has not stopped since they last spoke.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss, drunk and hung over, shows Erin two fat rings, one ruby and one topaz, as examples of the magical items a Lord of the Wall carries.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss says one ring sets his scales aflame with magical fire.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss uses a command Skill that freezes Erin's feet and his aides for two seconds, until Erin pushes back against it with her own power.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss calls the Goblins in the inn disgusting, says he could slay however many Hobgoblins infest it, and puts a hand on his sword.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss says it is his sworn duty as a Lord of the Wall to defend his city and Drakes from enemies, Goblins and traitors alike.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss fought to defend the inn with Zel against Regrika despite his hatred of Goblins, after being teleported there.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss apologises to Erin that his weakness let Regrika Blackpaw and the traitor with her escape, and says he is most at fault.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss says Lords of the Wall are nobility whose lineage extends back to the age of Ancestors and Dragons, who built the Walled Cities.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss says he came to Liscor searching for the truth Ryoka hid, which he has now uncovered.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss drinks honeyed milk next to Mrsha, who pats his shoulder, and he tells Erin the story of his forbidden romance with Periss.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss says Periss was glorious, brave and a fine officer, and that he must tell her family in person and arrange a funeral.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss thanks the Halfseekers for their kindness to Halassia, a half-Drake born in Salazsar.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss says he does not believe in ancient curses about half-Drakes, whom he considers worth more than any Human, Gnoll or other species.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss dreams of Periss at a map table of Salazsar's magical map room, after drinking Erin's spiked Faerie Flower ale.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss knows he is dreaming, and sees Periss as his second-in-command and secret lover standing over a map of Izril.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss begs Periss to touch him in the dream, and she slaps him twice and tells him to get hold of himself.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss tells the dream Periss that he fought, but she is gone and he is alone, and he weeps in her arms.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss kisses the dream Periss and asks forgiveness, and she laughs and calls sending her after one Human girl a sound decision.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss swears to protect his home, find the Necromancer and make him pay, and protect his people from the Goblin Lord, without slipping back into grief.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss wakes up at his table, knocking over a nearly empty mug of Faerie Flower ale.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss is sober and in armor at Liscor's council table, and reaches for wine but stops himself and takes water.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss mutters that Periss was right, they cannot keep doing this, while discussing Zel's absence.

section: Book 6: Grief and drinking in Liscor
text: Ilvriss says Zel Shivertail is a hero of the Antinium Wars but may be more popular among Humans than Drakes.
Ilvriss says he is a Lord of the Wall of Salazsar and has no authority over Relc, a former [Soldier] of Liscor, except in dire situations.
Ilvriss says Zel Shivertail was a fine [General], that he regrets letting Zel leave with a Human army, and that Zel will be avenged.
Ilvriss takes one gulp of Erin's milkshake and pushes it aside, saying there is such a thing as too much sweet.
Ilvriss calls himself a connoisseur who appreciates sweet food in moderation and compares the milkshake to a bag of sugar mixed with milk.
Ilvriss calls Erin's mayonnaise acceptable and says he will collect the recipe for his personal [Chef] before he leaves the city.
Ilvriss offers Erin an additional fee if she keeps the mayonnaise secret, so he can surprise his guests in Salazsar.
Ilvriss strides through the door to Pallass, and Erin follows, leaving the door out of mana for a day.
Ilvriss tries hard not to laugh at the blank doorway, and insists on going first in Pallass out of protocol.
In Pallass, Ilvriss bares his blade and cuts down two Drakes through their armor, then three more with three cuts.
Ilvriss leaves over half a dozen [Guardsmen] bleeding on the ground in the melee.
Ilvriss gives his full name and rank as Ilvriss Gemscale, Wall Lord Ilvriss of Salazsar, and his aura makes Drakes flinch and one fall.
Pallass says Ilvriss's intrusion was highly illegal and his noble status does not exempt him, so he is to be fined and returned to Liscor.
Ilvriss tells Pallass it shows how shameless a Walled City can become, being ruled by a democracy.
Ilvriss has been in communication with his Walled City for days, and a political struggle between Pallass and Salazsar has been won by Salazsar.
Ilvriss rallies Liscor's Drakes and Gnolls on the wall with a Skill, shouting for them to push the moths back.
Ilvriss charges down the wall in magic armor with an escort, and his enchanted sword carves into a giant moth.
Ilvriss patrols without sleep for over a day to show Liscor's citizens there is nothing to fear.
Ilvriss orders a dead moth burned, and congratulates Olesm loudly on his Level 30 [Strategist] class.
Ilvriss says most [Tacticians] take another five levels to reach [Strategist] and calls Olesm a prodigy.
Ilvriss has Olesm use [Vigor of Champions] on his escort, and some weary Drakes straighten up.
Ilvriss is already patrolling when Olesm finds dead moth larvae, and he orders the corpses burned.
Ilvriss attends Olesm's celebration with twelve followers through the magic door and orders a table for thirteen next to Olesm's.
Ilvriss returns Embria's salute and asks Erin for water, saying he will pay for one cake for every Drake at his table and for Olesm's bill for the night.
Ilvriss objects to Erin's play at first, calling it a disgrace, until he sees an actor playing Ilvriss rally the Drakes against the moths.
Ilvriss decides the play is not that inaccurate and wants it recorded with his scrying orb, though it is ridiculous that a Human plays him.
Ilvriss arrives at Zel's body at once and looks truly unhappy, despite his animosity with Zel.
Ilvriss tells Selys that someone lurked around the building the night before and a [Burglar] later tried to break in.
Ilvriss offers to buy Zel's breastplate from Selys and says he can pay the price up front and out of pocket.
Embria says the army could use the breastplate and that Selys might give it to someone allied with her interests.
Ilvriss is called arguably the most important Drake in Liscor, and Lyonette serves him first with Firebreath Whiskey.
Ilvriss orders the finest steak, well done and spiced as hot as the kitchen allows, and is pleased to get it within five minutes.
Ilvriss expects to be addressed with respect and served first, and Erin does not give it to him.
Ilvriss leaps up outraged at the Romeo and Juliet play in which a Drake marries a Human, and tries to rush the stage until Hobgoblins stop him.
Ilvriss starts a riot in the inn, decks a Human and grabs a chair, and kicks Pisces over a table after he turns invisible.
Erin punches Ilvriss in the stomach during the riot.
Ilvriss, with his retainers, wins the bar fight by taking out Headscratcher, Badarrow, Pisces and Ylawes with his bare hands, according to Erin.
Moore throws Ilvriss across the room into a wall after he tries to stop Moore from hitting people with a table.
Relc says that because Ilvriss started the fight, the Watch will probably charge him for the damages.
Ilvriss uses a healing potion and has his retainers pick up the unconscious.
Ilvriss demands the play be changed and declares that no self-respecting Drake in Liscor will visit the inn until it is.
Ilvriss walks into the inn with followers, claiming he was not worried, and says he came to see Watch Captain Venim and Olesm.
Ilvriss asks Olesm to fetch Zevara, Embria, Tekshia and Venim because the Goblins may be a source of information of the highest priority.
Ilvriss asks Liscor's Council to instate cooperation bounties on the dungeon, saying the threat goes beyond any one team.
Ilvriss allocates a discretionary budget of forty thousand gold pieces from Salazsar to hire adventurers for Liscor's dungeon.
Ilvriss says Salazsar is the richest of the Walled Cities and he will pay the entire cost himself if need be.
Ilvriss personally puts up a bounty of one thousand gold pieces for each citizen of Liscor brought back alive.
Ilvriss tells Halrac's team to enter the dungeon through the underwater rift and pursue the Raskghar, and Halrac answers that they do not take orders.
Erin makes Ilvriss say Numbtongue's name, and he grudgingly says "Numb. Tongue."
Ilvriss guarantees the Adventurer's Guild's bounties as Wall Lord of Salazsar and says he resides at the Tailless Thief.
Ilvriss says he will not enter the dungeon himself and doubles the reward for returning the missing citizens.
Ilvriss says he is not an adventurer or trap detector, and as a [Lord] his abilities are split between diplomacy, economy and warfare.
Ilvriss warns Erin that going into the dungeon would be a death sentence, then tells his people to keep an eye on her.
Ilvriss speaks into his personal scrying orb to someone in Salazsar, saying Pallass has sent two thirds of its Gold-ranks to Liscor and cannot force its Named Adventurer.
Ilvriss says he is banned from entering Pallass.
Ilvriss tells Salazsar that the Heartflame Breastplate cannot solve the crisis, since its Selphid wearer could fight a hundred Raskghar and there are thousands.
Ilvriss admits that this was a victory for all races working together, naming Dwarf, Human, Drake, Gnoll, Selphid, Drowned Man, Half-Giant and Garuda, and for once with no scorn in his eyes.
Erin adds Goblins to Ilvriss's list, saying the victory was thanks to Goblins and that a Goblin opened the way.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss's bounty of one thousand gold per rescued Gnoll is said to have been doubled, and the sum is to be paid into a pool with the recovered artifacts for the participants to bid on.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss gives a speech to Liscor from a podium during the victory parade, recorded by [Mages] and a scrying orb.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss tells the crowd that Liscor has reclaimed its own and that the dungeon and the Raskghar were no match for the adventurers and the Drake and Gnollish spirit.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss uses Liscor City Hall's council room as an office and war room full of recovered artifacts on cushions and in piles.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss hums when he works on something he enjoys, a habit Periss knew, and he has not hummed or smiled much since her death.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss gives Erin two lesser bags of holding with one thousand two hundred and eleven gold coins as the reward for the use of her magic door and for stamina potions and food.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss tells Erin that it would be politically disastrous for a Lord of the Wall to pay Goblins any sum, and that other adventurers would riot.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss says the Goblins' status as a Bronze-rank team will be certified by Liscor's guild, and that the Council voted on the matter.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss claims to have misplaced the axe recovered from the Minotaur Calruz, so that Erin can take it for the Goblins.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Krshia tells Erin that Ilvriss cannot pay the Goblins because it would embarrass a Wall Lord of Salazsar and admit that monsters did more work than any adventurer.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss argues that the Humans could let the Goblin Lord rampage and claim he got away, since an accord prohibits unprovoked Human assaults on Drake sovereignty.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss predicts that Tyrion Veltras will break open the walls, let the Goblins in, and take the city while pretending it was an accident.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss says Humans need reasons to go to war, even lies, and that such a lie would become truth to those who only hear Tyrion Veltras.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss wears Rabbiteater's blood-red Cloak of Plenty, made of what looks like liquid, while the Cave Goblins have left the dungeon.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss tells Zevara and Olesm that the Cloak of Plenty can replicate mundane liquids such as water, broth or blood, but not magical ones or complex mixtures.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss uses willpower to fix the cloak's property to wine, and had his subordinates and an innkeeper test it.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss reluctantly hands the cloak to Olesm, to give back to the Goblins.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss has not touched alcohol since the drink Erin gave him, and has not given in to despair.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss feels that some days he forgets what Periss's face looked like and the sound of her voice.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss runs through the magic door when he hears of Zevara's plan to take the door back, and proposes that adventurers be allowed to use it to leave Liscor.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss says the door must go to city hall in Liscor because it is a security risk if the inn falls.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss demands that the adventurers stay and fight until the walls fall and the battle is unwinnable before using the door.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss threatens to send a [Message] spell to every city naming any fleeing team as traitors in any place where Drakes draw breath.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss sits in Liscor city hall's war room with Salazsar's head [Strategist] on the other end, as the Goblin Lord's army arrives thirteen days ahead of schedule.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss learns that the Winged Riders of Oteslia might arrive by nightfall but would be half-dead.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss sees from the window of the war room over two thousand Antinium Soldiers on the walls and four thousand more in the streets.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss already knows that the Necromancer Az'kerash is alive, and he silences Osthia Blackwing when she tries to tell him.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss tells Osthia that the secret is their only advantage and that they must trap the Necromancer, and swears they will make him pay.

section: Book 9: Aftermath and the Goblin Lord
text: Ilvriss takes Osthia, a Captain of Pallass's 5th Oldblood Winged Division, onto his horse to hear her information away from others.
Ilvriss reads the official reports from the Walled Cities on the Blood Fields and disgustedly says that the Humans shaved numbers, though Veltras won on numbers.
Ilvriss says the Walled Cities pulled back too many elites when Liscor was not in danger, and sent three [Generals] who were not their best.
Major Asrira Shieldscale, a winged Drake whose lineage is a long-time friend of Ilvriss's family, joins him as an aide in a more combative role than his adjutants.
Asrira is from Salazsar and has served with distinction for over half a decade.
Ilvriss tells Zevara he has stayed far too long in Liscor and plans to leave, but Pallass is still denying him entry.
Ilvriss signs a document on Salazsar-watermarked paper, ahead of Erin, declaring that Numbtongue is a recognised adventurer entitled to the rights of a person.
Ilvriss says a true Drake pays their debts, and a long list of signatories follows his signature.
Ilvriss invites Erin to visit Salazsar and his estates after Pallass, saying the north will wait.
Ilvriss orders his adjutant Welsca Crimsonscale to make copies of Olesm's chess magazine and teaches Olesm to seal letters with flashfire dust and wax.
Ilvriss says the flashfire dust incinerates after two seconds when the envelope is opened, and the wax with his ring seal cannot be removed without destroying the envelope.
Ilvriss tells Olesm that Salazsar has debated arms manufacturing for six years and might poach a few Pallass [Smiths], but not fight in that area.
Ilvriss says he needs to get through Pallass because the Blood Fields are active and the Assembly still will not grant him passage.
Ilvriss activates a bound Tier 5 [Denial] ring against scrying, creating a bubble to hide the room.
Ilvriss learns from an inquiry that Regrika Blackpaw, a fake Named Adventurer, is an undead servant of the Necromancer Az'kerash.
Ilvriss says that only the people in the room and Ryoka Griffin know that Az'kerash is alive.
Ilvriss tells Osthia that every extra person who knows is a liability that may alert Az'kerash, and that would mean war.
Ilvriss plans to approach a list of Drakes, investigate another list, and find artifacts of old Drake legend, saying the Heartflame Breastplate appeared after Zel's death for a reason.
Ilvriss says that if it comes to it he will recruit from other species, but first he must get back to his city.
Ilvriss leaves Liscor three days after announcing it, with no warning to Liscor's Council or anyone else.
Ilvriss appears in Salazsar on the fourth day, and Watch Captain Venim and Pallass's Assembly are very unhappy.
Ilvriss expects Pallass will not work out how he got through for some time, as they have frail imaginations.
Ilvriss tells Olesm that Rissa Inkscale's sketches were merely reproductions of monsters he had heard about and hardly his concern.
Ilvriss hosts a private dinner at his estates for Brilm, Tasilt, Hesalief and about six other Drakes, and the drinking runs into the next morning.
Ilvriss employs a [Chef], [Cleaners], [Waiters] and a [Housekeeper], but no [Servants] or [Butlers], since Drakes believe in military discipline but not servitude.
Ilvriss drinks a hangover potion the morning after, while Wall Lord Tasilt, an old friend, is still happily drunk.
Tasilt's wife is Rhelika, and Tasilt says they have twins, Cecilla and Feldir, of different species who both run on all fours.
Tasilt says Feldir is unruly and stole a Potion of Greater Invisibility from the family vaults, which he used for mischief.
Tasilt's parentage of the twins shows Drakes and Gnolls can have mixed families, as Ilvriss notes of Periss's parents.
Ilvriss meets Wardmistress Geyasa of Fissival, whose team swept his mansion and properties and found nothing of note beyond a few minor spells.
Ilvriss tells Geyasa he disposed of the offending object as soon as he knew it was at fault, and has informed Wall Lord Brilm of his mistake.
Ilvriss lets everyone think Brilm unwittingly brought an object with a spying spell into his home after being duped, though he feels a pang of guilt about it.
Ilvriss has Geyasa check another quartz recording, which she finds to be perfectly fine, and forbears mentioning that she is the second [Mage] he has hired.
Ilvriss listens in his study to a sound crystal that Brilm gave him, with music by the Singer of Terandria, and he does not know what a piano is.
Ilvriss hears the song "My Way" by Frank Sinatra on the crystal, and decides it could not have been made in this era.
Ilvriss feels certain of a connection between the song and Erin Solstice, though the logical leap eludes him.
Ilvriss's father is Wall Lord Zail, who gave him a ring of trust, and Zail pesters Ilvriss about marrying.
Ilvriss tells his father that he gave his ring to someone who did him a great service, who is unique and may need it more, as a gesture of respect.
Ilvriss tells Zail that there was a woman worthy of the line, but that he could not even bury her.
Ilvriss tells Osthia that Regrika Blackpaw was a Named Adventurer and a minion of Az'kerash, whom he fought, and that Zel told him she was sent to silence Ryoka.
Ilvriss believes that someone falsified documents certifying Regrika's rank, and suspects a Guildmaster of the Adventurer's Guild may have helped.
Ilvriss has Regrika's file and lists of names, dates and levels correlating her visits with the deaths of notable Drakes.
Ilvriss tests Osthia with a Mirror of True Seeing and a Diadem of Inner Thoughts, and holds a blade to her neck while she declares her loyalty.
Ilvriss tells Osthia he trusts no one, and then puts on the diadem himself so she can check him.
Ilvriss appoints Osthia head of a private elite force nominally to destroy the Antinium, which is a cover for fighting Az'kerash.
Ilvriss thinks that undead are similar to Antinium and that Az'kerash will slaughter regular [Soldiers], so tactics used against Antinium would serve.
Ilvriss plans to recruit the Named Adventurer Shriekblade of Salazsar, whom money dictates will work for him.
Ilvriss despairs at the scale of his opponent, who is not immortal but only two hundred years old.
Ilvriss's mother is Helessia, and she asks whether he has visited Periss's grave.
Ilvriss learns that his family held a funeral and made a cenotaph for Periss in the Gemscale mausoleum, since her body was never recovered.
Ilvriss visits Periss Veldant's parents, Solicia, a Gnoll, and Elkill, a Drake, and tells them about the events that led to her death.
Ilvriss weeps with Periss's parents before a painting of her, putting aside his vengeance for a while.
Ilvriss tells Alrric that he saw his love die, watched the Tidebreaker die far from any Drake army, met an idiot, and quit drinking.
Ilvriss trusts Alrric and asks about his family, which Alrric has never discussed.
Ilvriss thinks Erin has made the Walled Cities' plans meaningless, as they cannot account for her.
Ilvriss guesses that Manus, Pallass, Zeres, Oteslia and Fissival will each convene their leaders to assess what they saw.
Ilvriss tells the Holders of the Wall that an Antinium claiming to be a Prognugator, Bird the Hunter, is a dedicated anti-air specialist who brings down Wyverns with an unenchanted bow.
Ilvriss argues that if the Antinium can make more such Prognugators, the Drakes' assumption that they can dominate the skies fails.
Ilvriss proposes a secret contribution from each tower to fund a force that recruits elites from other cities and outside Izril.
Ilvriss's sister, Wall Lady Navine, denounces the idea as ridiculous.
The Holders of the Wall pass Ilvriss's motion to fund the force, which he sees as step one completed thanks to Erin Solstice.
Ilvriss has a secret list that only two Drakes in the world know about, and he plans to gather enough people to burn Az'kerash's forest.
Ilvriss's plan is named Project Periss, and it is underway.
Ilvriss and Tasilt, invisible, arrest the [Cargomaster] Dukss for theft and corruption in the teleportation network.
Ilvriss and Tasilt are feted as heroes for uncovering the corruption, and Ilvriss drinks juice while Brilm toasts him.
Ilvriss admits that he was tipped off, but takes public credit and refuses to say who told him.
The scheme was conceived by Ilvriss's Gnoll second Alrric, who is not his spouse.
Ilvriss uses the economic [Lord] Skill [Productivity Spike], which repeats the best day a company has had and lasts four hours.
Ilvriss changed since Liscor: he was once disgusted by pro-Human, pro-peace Salazsar proponents, especially his sister Navine, and a year ago was at dagger-points with her.
Ilvriss tells Alrric that everything in Salazsar feels slow and complacent, and the city needs pressure, innovation and new leaders, Drake or Gnoll.
Ilvriss makes popcorn with a pot and a rune to entertain Brilm, learning it in Liscor.
Ilvriss tells Alrric that he misses Liscor, where the city felt alive, and that he has thought some days of returning.
Ilvriss wants true elite commanders for his task force, and says he would take about a hundred Olesms, or failing that, one Zel Shivertail.
Ilvriss tells Alrric to offer eighty thousand gold pieces for land in Liscor's area of development.
Ilvriss orders a complete discount offer for the Singer of Terandria in return for a percentage of sales, and says he is already marrying a Minotauress.
Ilvriss reads a garbled insulting [Message] signed "Cirille" calling Salazsar cowards and thieves, and suspects someone is playing a joke.
Imani is a young woman from Nigeria who comes to this world from Earth and later works as a [Cook] at The Wandering Inn.
Imani arrived with a different group of people from the airport than Joseph and the others she later travels with.
Imani ran into monsters when she and the others appeared, and Joseph says she was the only one who got away.
Joseph says Imani stayed in a small village until Lady Magnolia found her.
Imani says the monsters were Crelers.
Imani tells Erin that they all died, then cries, and Erin holds her.
Imani says her group appeared right next to Tunnel Crawlers, ran, and made a call for help that no one answered.
Imani says the big rocks stopped the Crelers climbing, but she was the only one that made it.
Imani is standing with Joseph and the other Earthers when they run out of coin in Invrisil.
Joseph sells his sword to rent an inn, while Rose accuses Ryoka of taking their electronics.
Imani's stomach rumbles when Maviola El offers the group a meal.
Imani and the others follow Maviola after a short huddle.
Imani breaks into screaming hysterics at the inn, crying that she wants to go home, and Joseph shouts at her to stop.
Rose explains that Imani was attacked by Crelers, that her group was killed, and that she still has nightmares.
The Earthers have run out of the calming tonic Imani needs.
Erin mouths the word eaten to Lyonette, indicating the Crelers ate Imani's group.
Mrsha takes Imani's hand and leads her into the [Garden of Sanctuary], where she feels safe.
The seven Earthers have been at the inn for roughly a week, but Imani is not among those in the kitchen that morning.
Imani makes fufu, and Palt the Centaur secretly casts [Remove Fear] on her.
Imani practically rules the kitchen when Erin is not using it, and has learned to deal with Mrsha by offering treats.
Imani is one of the inn's two resident [Cooks], with Palt, and is less nervous than usual.
Imani withholds Dekass's fries until he tries her new croissant.
Erin is told Imani can be surprisingly stubborn and has been feeling better of late.
Imani makes bessara, a spiced bean dip, which she says is good for cold weather.
Imani and Palt have taken over the kitchens from Erin.
Imani finds Erin's Shadow Loaf sucking the light out of the kitchen and not going stale on the windowsill.
Erin hides the Shadow Loaf in the [Garden of Sanctuary], and Imani notices.
Imani has the Skill [Minor Accident Prevention], which she got at Level 10.
[Minor Accident Prevention] stops bits of eggshell in food, spilled drinks and a dropped pan.
Imani drinks Dreamleaf water of lemon, Dreamleaf and sugar from Palt to calm herself.
Palt has also given Imani sleeping draughts for her trauma from the Creler attacks.
Imani orders avocados and other vegetables from Earth via Oteslia and the Pallass bazaar.
Imani cooks mandazi with coconut milk, and a breakfast dish of rice, beans, eggs and avocado spread.
Erin tells Fals that Imani survived a bad Creler attack, not the one at the inn, with friends.
Imani takes potions that stop her dreaming altogether to stop the nightmares.
Inky is a short, dark-skinned [Storm Sailor] with two normal arms, one normal leg and an octopus leg.
Inky has a cephalopod's beak, an inner set of jaws, inside her mouth.
Inky has suckers on her hands and the soles of her feet and spits ink, and she climbs the mast using the suckers.
A sailor named Begal says Inky is the daughter of a Drowned Person and a Human, who did not take the Sea's Bargain.
Begal says the Drowned Folk would not take Inky, so she crews with air breathers.
Begal says Inky is good at her job and helps kick the others into shape, though she is only a crew member for the trip and not one of The Emerald Signet's own.
Inky is one of the [Divers] on the ship and has an Amulet of Waterbreathing.
Inky is Second Mate under Captain Lasc, and is a [Storm Sailor].
Inky has an octopus tentacle for a leg and a swaying walk.
Inky screams at Captain Lasc to turn back from the storm, saying they are about to be destroyed, but he ordered full ahead.
Insill is a black-scaled Drake [Rogue] in leather armor with a dagger, thinner and shorter than other male Drakes.
Insill belongs to the party Vuliel Drae, which includes Anith, Dasha, Pekona and the Gnoll Larr.
Insill hides in the dark like a shadow and checks for traps for the group.
Insill introduces his teammates to Toren and the group to her, with Dasha and Pekona as their [Warriors].
A teammate marvels that Toren found a trap in the dungeon that Insill could not.
Insill says Vuliel Drae owes Toren for last time, since the mace she gave them was worth a fortune.
Insill gives masked Toren a cheap steel longsword with a forked rune and a slight enchantment, because her old sword was very old.
Insill teases Dasha for waxing her beard to try to meet Ylawes Byres at the Adventurer's Guild.
Invek is an Ogress and the leader of the Ogre Clan of Tormek Al, in the hills northeast of Invrisil.
Invek is a female Ogre who is not as tall as some, equipped with a large double-sided axe enchanted to return to her hand.
Invek's mate is dead, killed by the [Lady] of House Ulta.
Invek has the best mastery of the common tongue among the Ogres of her clan, and speaks it simply and bluntly.
Rags finds Invek reasonable, unlike some Ogres who look down on the much smaller Goblins.
Invek watches Redscar defeat her clan's champion without Skills, and says that Redscar has an enchanted sword.
Invek declares that Tormek Al makes peace with the Flood Water Tribe, since Redscar proves himself.
Negotiations take six days after an Ogre patrol chances upon Goblinhome and nearly fights the Goblins.
Invek agrees that Tormek Al will come to the High Passes, because Humans keep killing Ogres and her clan wants to leave.
Nearly two hundred Ogres sit in the circle around Invek, and Rags knows her tribe could slaughter ten times its number of Goblins without elites or Hobs.
Invek tells Rags that Tourek was a clan leader of Tormek Al who died, a best warrior who killed Gold-ranked Humans.
Invek shouts that Goblins and Ogres will not fight each other, that they will eat that night, and that gifts will follow the next day.
Rags gives Invek large nuggets of gold and cut gems from Goblinhome's stash, which delights Invek.
Invek gives Rags Goblin-sized steel daggers, armour too small for Ogres, and three full sets of plate armour in return.
Invek stops smiling when the biggest female Ogre announces that she and fifteen others want to join Rags' tribe.
Invek is displeased by the Ogres wanting to join Rags' tribe, and consents to talk about it despite her annoyance.
Invek smirks that Ogre shamans make Ogres superior, and dismisses Snapjaw's [Burning Blade] as not a big fire.
Invek is happy to receive eight Ogres' weight of meat from Rags.
Invek's eyes lock onto Rags' mana potions, and Rags gives her one in a trade for friendship.
Invek smacks a badly bleeding young Ogre who was cut by a Redfang, telling him the Goblins are friends.
Invek touches her fist to Rags' hand when the Goblins leave, agreeing to meet again in the Highest Mountains.
Iratze is a young man from Mexico who is a martial artist from Earth, and leads a small group of Earthers in Chandrar.
Iratze's group consists of a gym's younger members, two aspiring fighters, a girl visiting her father and eight people from outside, one of whom had been in a car.
Nearly twice as many people were teleported from Earth as the group that stuck together and survived.
Iratze speaks a different tongue to his companion, which Orjin cannot place and takes for Drathian.
Iratze watches the Strongest of Pomle fight the Fury of Winds' cult, and notes how superficial the cultists' wounds on Orjin are.
Iratze tells Mendi he studied a different school called MMA, or Mixed Martial Arts, similar to Pomle's fighting, and that he can teach a bit.
Iratze beats the Dullahan Mendi on the ground, holding her in an arm bar until she taps out.
Iratze is better at grappling than Mendi, who is overconfident.
Pomle's warriors surround Iratze to ask about the new move, and Mendi bows to him.
Orjin tells Iratze that if he can teach more like this, there is always a place for him, and Pomle accepts the group.
Iratze says not all of his group can fight, but some hope to at least get something to eat.
Iratze is a new member of Pomle with a mixed-martial-arts background, learning grappling from Master Salthorn alongside a few other Humans.
Iratze asks Salthorn how she would stop a Selphid, and she explains how a Human would break the Selphid's body down.
Iratze has shown Pomle's [Martial Artists] what his world developed, though he has not told Orjin so.
Salii says Iratze helped her come up with Pomle's spectator sparring matches, which already make money from bettors.
Isceil is a Drake [Oldblood Magus] on the Wistram team led by Montressa.
Isceil can exhale combined breath magic, using the team's linked magic to produce a three-element blast.
Isceil tells Liscor's people that Ceria and Pisces are criminals who impersonated real Wistram [Mages], and says the Wistram team may release others later.
Montressa quotes Isceil in saying the team has the right to hunt fugitives from Wistram.
Isceil sneers that Pisces got what he deserved because he was a [Necromancer], before Erin slams his face into a plate of curry.
Isceil shouts to the Watch that Wistram's team has rights, as they are from Wistram.
Isceil describes the dangers of out-of-control dragonbreath of Oldblood Drakes, such as frostbite, burned scales, heart attacks and acid that melts the stomach.
Isceil says he has treated most of the bad cases because anyone who has lived long knows to seek him out, though at his level he cannot fix too much.
Isceil gives Montressa a sealed tonic for Captain Zevara, whose lungs cannot take the smoke of her fire breath.
Isceil says Zevara hates his guts.
Isceil takes the focus of the linked Wistram mages and exhales Frostspark Galebreath, destroying a swarm of insects, then falls with a torn throat.
Isceil and Beza follow Montressa to hunt Pisces, while Palt and Ulinde stay behind.
Isceil says he agrees with Montressa and has a score to settle.
At Palt's call, Isceil fires lightning, fire and air at the Creler, and the Wistram mages add [Valmira's Comets], but the adult Creler is unscathed.
Isceil loses his right arm to a projectile spat by the adult Creler.
Isceil stays to fight, saying Drakes do not run, and he breathes flames at the Crelers.
Later, the adult Creler tears Isceil to pieces as he breathes flames once in defiance.
Palt tells Erin that Isceil is dead.
The Wistram team buries Isceil, and Montressa's team grieves, since it is perhaps their first lost teammate.
Ishkr is a red-brown-furred Gnoll who works at Erin's inn after Krshia introduced him to her.
Ishkr is a Silverfang Gnoll, born around the time some Silverfangs came to Liscor, and he is about nineteen.
Ishkr was born and raised in Liscor and does not know many of his tribe's superstitions.
Ishkr has one sister he grumbles about and two parents he never mentions, who Erin suspects are dead.
Ishkr says he is a Level 16 [Waiter], recommended to work at the inn by Honored Krshia.
Ishkr is physically stronger than Lyonette, even with her [Lesser Strength].
Later, Ishkr is a [Head Waiter] and Lyonette's second-in-command, a position he won over Drassi.
Ishkr runs the kitchen and common room of the inn while Drassi works night shifts as [Bartender].
Ishkr says Honored Krshia assures him Mrsha's white fur is fine, so he does not mind it.
Ishkr drags Lyonette back when she is about to fight Safry.
Ishkr stays away from the inn in mourning after Brunkr's death.
Ishkr returns to work and apologizes, offering to have his pay docked, while Erin hugs him.
Ishkr is described as scared stiff of the Goblins staying at the inn.
Ishkr says he did not believe the rumors of the new guests until he saw them.
Ishkr plays the guitar easily, having played a gittern and earned coins that way before.
Ishkr cannot read Erin's written songs, which say twang twang, and says it is not music.
Ishkr signs off with a hefty overtime bonus, complaining that his claws hurt, but smiling.
Ishkr offers to ask a handful of Gnoll acquaintances to work at the inn without betraying Erin's trust.
Ishkr plays in Erin's baseball game, going for first base after a fly ball.
Ishkr speaks to Numbtongue politely before leaving, which is a small privilege, and does not curse him.
Ishkr works alongside Drassi at the inn.
Ishkr asks for his week's pay in advance, which Erin ties to a family matter.
Erin thinks Ishkr has a secret about money, likely related to his sister, who sends friends to whisper to him.
Ishkr is a model employee who accounts for his own mistakes and never seeks advancement.
Ishkr is one of Erin's two longest current employees, and calls her Miss Erin more respectfully than before.
Ishkr runs the magic door to Esthelm and Liscor, greeting and directing visitors.
Issa is a Drake adventurer and a member of the Gold-rank team Wings of Pallass, led by the Garuda Bevussa Slenderscale.
Issa is publicly presented as the team's captain, while Bevussa is the real leader, because a Garuda would not be accepted leading Oldblood Drakes.
Issa admires Bevussa greatly and is the one tasked with pretending to be captain of the Wings of Pallass in public.
Before Drake investors and influential Drakes in a walled city, Issa is treated as the captain and Bevussa as the pretty Garuda.
Issa and Zassil land on a Stone Starer together and kill it with a spear and a sword.
Issa is hit by one of a Stone Starer's beams, and her armor partly blocks it, so Bevussa has her pull back to be checked.
Issa pulls out a healing potion after the beam strike and protests that she can still fight.
Issa turns bright red and her wings quiver in embarrassment when the mage Typhenous catches her and Bevussa gossiping about his team's past.
Issa gasps at the sight of a bone spider-like monster, and imagines it charging into her team.
Issa and Zassil throw bread pieces at each other while the team sits in Erin Solstice's inn.
Bevussa orders Issa to use a Wand of Lightning when greater undead appear in the dungeon.
Issa uses wands and flashes of [Light] as one of the fliers, alongside Kin's fire spells, against a Wyvern attacking Liscor.
Bevussa calls on Issa to use [Pillar of Earth] during the Wyvern fight, and Issa dives to pull a young child out from under the Wyvern's claw.
Issa shoves the rescued Drake child to Noass and Sir Relz and tells them to get to safety.
Ivolethe is a Frost Faerie who befriends Ryoka Griffin and travels with her through the winter.
Ivolethe says she is a member of the Winter Court and demands respect.
Ivolethe is small and blue, and rides in Ryoka's belt pouch indoors.
Ivolethe says she followed Ryoka with the other faeries, warned her of the armies, led her through the forest, and accepted the second price of her bargain.
Ryoka invites Ivolethe into her room with "Come in", since faeries cannot enter uninvited.
Cold iron saps a faerie's strength and makes her mortal, so Ivolethe cannot use magic indoors.
Ivolethe bites a chunk from a man's finger down to the bone.
Ivolethe refuses to be Erin's friend, saying she has made one friend and needs no other.
Ivolethe says she did not attend Erin's faerie banquet, though her kin spoke of it.
Ivolethe does not know why Ryoka and Erin can see her, and says mortals can see fae under a full moon or after drinking the fae's secret drink.
Ivolethe claims to have witnessed the rise of King Arthur and the deaths of the three kings by Lugaid's spears.
Ivolethe tells Ryoka and Erin the whole story of King Arthur, which Ryoka judges true.
A Runner seizes Ivolethe in the Runner's Guild, and Persua proposes selling her to a [Merchant] or [Alchemist] for thousands of gold coins.
Ivolethe calls to her sisters for retribution before the Runner silences her, which frightens the other Runners.
Ryoka frees Ivolethe by using [Flashbang] and throwing a pepper potion on Persua and her friends.
Ivolethe tells Ryoka that if she had been killed, others of the Winter Court who deal in death would have killed her killer.
Ivolethe offers to teach Ryoka to run like the wind in exchange for friendship, and they shake on it.
Ivolethe says the fey are born knowing magic and cannot teach it, comparing it to teaching a fish to swim.
Ivolethe's glamor leaves Fals seeing only a blur even when she sits.
Ivolethe stays at Ryoka's side day and night after the fight with Persua, usually riding in her belt pouch.
Ivolethe refuses to speak with Ceria, calling her an offspring of whores, and says the fae hate what she has become, not her.
Ivolethe refuses to examine Ryoka's artifacts, saying she can read magic's flow but not mortal systems.
Ivolethe tells Ryoka that in matters of life and death she must not interfere, and that the rule has been broken twice already.
Ivolethe tells Ryoka that Goblin children are marching north in their hundreds, with the Goblin Lord's army below the pass and a smaller fleeing army ahead.
The fae amuse themselves with Erin's antics in Esthelm, where snow has stopped falling, and Ivolethe reluctantly decides to leave and act.
Ivolethe tells Ryoka that Laken bears the mark of command, the old destiny of leaders.
Ivolethe says in German that Ryoka's pronunciation is terrible, and says she has travelled to many lands and learned many tongues.
Ivolethe predicts a blizzard that peaks by nightfall and lasts up to three days.
Ivolethe tells Ryoka that a seed lies sealed inside the wand, a child trapped in a tree's last bloom.
Ivolethe agrees to guide Ryoka to Riverfarm after Laken swears to put up a statue of her.
Other Frost Faeries join as guides and turn many colours, copying Ivolethe.
Ivolethe warns Ryoka that the Winter Solstice is a day of power when spirits and magic mix, and that winter is two thirds over.
Ivolethe warns Ryoka not to refuse gifts, enter uninvited, curse, bargain or lie that day.
Ivolethe says other things take on different aspects on the solstice, though she does not know if magic grows stronger.
Ivolethe says she sees through all glamours and that the strange forest road is not a fae working.
Ivolethe bites Ryoka to break a trance, then is blown away by a gust from the dark figures.
A tall woman with a sword leads Ryoka out of the dark, and Ryoka calls her Ivolethe, who tells her to run.
Ivolethe cannot enter the Guild building because of its cold iron walls and lack of an invitation, and watches Ryoka and Erin through the window.
Ivolethe values Ryoka's friendship, and flies south.
Ivolethe watches two undead among a hundred dead Goblins as the Goblin Lord's larger force approaches.
Ivolethe does not interfere, since meddling on that scale would bring punishment.
Ivolethe tells Ryoka that winter will end soon and that they will part then.
Ivolethe says teaching Ryoka will be entertaining for her.
Ivolethe can speak to whomever she pleases though she seldom does, and she asks Garia for meat left outside without iron in return for a blessing.
A snowball falls on Ryoka from above, followed by distant laughter.
Ivolethe begins teaching Ryoka faerie magic on a hill near the Strongheart farm.
Ivolethe tells Ryoka that the only step is to sense the wind, which she cannot explain because there are no words for it.
Ivolethe says faerie magic is learned not by practice or books but in a moment of grace.
Ivolethe says Ryoka lifted herself on the wind by being natural, not because of any help from her.
Ivolethe weeps, thanks Ryoka for showing her something new, copies Ryoka's corkscrew, and says "Grace".
Ivolethe says she lived with a body like Ryoka's for years.
Frost Faeries cannot tell the future but predict it better than mortals, seeing crossroads where mortals see one road.
Ivolethe believes the gods are dead and had better stay that way.
Ivolethe begins to melt as winter ends, and accepts it with resignation.
Ivolethe tells Ryoka she cannot interfere and that doing so has dire consequences.
Ivolethe tells Ryoka that the wind is a thing that thinks, and that faeries fly by stepping as if to walk into the sky.
Ivolethe says she bent the rules for Ryoka the day before and that tricks on others are not exactly interference.
Ivolethe says the lord of death would cheat in a battle.
Ivolethe sees Ryoka's death on the road if she runs toward Teriarch.
Ivolethe leaves a disguised copy of herself behind as a prank to give Ryoka time to run.
Ivolethe's sisters urge her not to interfere for a mortal, and she agrees at first.
Ivolethe breaks the rules, freezing Venitra and the High Passes, and defies her King, saying she will not let her friend die.
Ivolethe's ice body shatters into melted water in front of Ryoka, and her sisters cry that she broke the rules.
Later, Ivolethe appears blue at Laken's banquet, uninvited but permitted to join her kin, with a silent armoured guardian watching her.
Ivolethe tells Laken they met before, alone in the city, and he recognises her.
Ivolethe says she is forbidden from returning to this world until Ryoka dies, which is her punishment for interfering.
Ivolethe asks Laken to tell Ryoka that she lives and did not die when her form broke.
Ivolethe says the summer court is not like the winter, and Laken was lucky to invite only her kin.
Ivolethe drinks poisoned wine without harm and says few poisons frighten the fae.
Laken tells Ryoka in early spring that Ivolethe is alive, and delivers that Ryoka will never see her in this world.
Ivolethe appears in Ryoka's hallucination in a dungeon, saying the madness is created and Ryoka has no levels.
Ryoka cannot tell if the Ivolethe she sees is really present.
Ivolethe's statue in Riverfarm is finished.
Jackal is a [Ranger] who leads an adventuring team that infiltrates the Goblin mountain, and he carries a shortbow.
Jackal's infiltrators are nearly a dozen strong, in black, dark green or grey, and arrive by magic circle alongside [Mages] and a [Witch].
Jackal's team includes Minerva, who calls him her leader.
Jackal waits with a shortbow beside two Hobs he has shot through the eye, and chides Minerva for being late.
Jackal tells the [Mages] to cancel their light spells, since the arrival must stay a stealth mission.
Jackal says he holds a pass for a personal audience with the Healer of Tenbault, so captured allies who are alive can be made whole.
Jackal leads Minerva and four others deeper into the mountain while the [Mages] cast ward spells.
Jackal is a Gold-rank captain whom Tyrion's messenger orders to shoot the Goblins defending Liscor.
Jackal readies [Farseeker Arrows] and [Double Arrow] against the Hob archer Badarrow, until an enchanted arrow detonates in front of his team.
Jackal recognises Halrac on Liscor's battlements as the archer who shot the enchanted arrow.
Jackal lowers his bow and refuses Tyrion's order, saying Halrac has the angle and uses enchanted arrows.
Jackal tells the messenger to get Tyrion's own [Archers], or the Kingslayer, to do the job.
Jasi is a young female Drake of Celum who works as a [Washer] and later becomes the star actress of the Players of Celum.
Jasi is one of perhaps two or three Drakes in Celum.
Jasi was abandoned as a child and raised by a Human father and mother, and has lived in Celum all her life.
Jasi has never been to Liscor or anywhere with other Drakes.
Jasi and Grev live in a squalid hut by the city walls that belonged to their parents.
Grev is one crime away from being exiled from Celum.
Jasi begged Erin not to hurt Grev, calling him just a child.
Jasi begged on her hands and knees for Erin not to report Grev, who is the only family she has left.
Jasi cannot sew or cook well, and says she would like to learn a craft and start a small business.
Jasi says that if she could, she would travel to Liscor to learn what Drakes are like.
Jasi insisted that Celum is quite a good city to live in.
Jasi and Wesle played Romeo and Juliet in Erin's inn, and their stage kiss looked real to Erin.
On stage they were no longer the low-level [Guardsman] and the impoverished Drake [Washer].
Wesle and Jasi are the highest-level [Actors], who had gained a few Skills.
Wesle and Jasi are the stars of the troupe, and all the cast take a share of the profits.
Grev carries the bag of coins and the props.
The Celum actors rehearsed My Fair Lady, and Jasi asked to buy a gift for Grev.
Jasi said she did not know Drakes to buy for and suggested putting down the handsome Pisces.
Jasi has changed from timid to poised, wears shimmering magical crystal bracelets that radiate chill, and has an inner poise.
Jasi has an actor's mask and plays Zevara in The Battle of Liscor, in which Humans wear fake tails.

section: Skills and the Players of Celum
text: Jasi is a Level 24 [Actress].

section: Skills and the Players of Celum
text: Her Skill [Performance Supplies: 5 Gold] lets her summon five gold pieces' worth of supplies before a performance.

section: Skills and the Players of Celum
text: Her Skill [Eidetic Memory] lets her visualise a script moments after reading it.

section: Skills and the Players of Celum
text: Jasi played Lady Elisial, a Drake who became a [Noblewoman] in Terandria, and used [Audience Charge] to draw energy from the audience.

section: Skills and the Players of Celum
text: The audience went wild at the end of the play.

section: Skills and the Players of Celum
text: Later, Jasi reaches Level 25 as an [Actress] in the final lines of the chapter.

section: Skills and the Players of Celum
text: Jasi guesses that Erin may come from an old village in Terandria where people live cut off.

section: Skills and the Players of Celum
text: The Players of Celum, including Jasi, Wesle, Grev, Emme and Kilkran, cancelled their performance because of the riots.

section: Skills and the Players of Celum
text: Jasi sang "Take on Me" on air with Wesle and a disguised Numbtongue playing lightning from the guitar strings.

section: Skills and the Players of Celum
text: Jasi has a [Perfect Imitation] Skill that lets her act differently.

section: Skills and the Players of Celum
text: Jasi found her old street in Celum gone and was mobbed by people seeking her autograph.

section: Skills and the Players of Celum
text: Numbtongue, in anonymous armour, caught up with Jasi after she fled the crowd and revealed himself.

section: Skills and the Players of Celum
text: Jasi met Agnes at the Frenzied Hare.
Jasi Redigal is a Drake [Actress] and the older sister of Grev Redigal.
Jasi remembers working as a [Washer] to provide for her younger brother Grev, scrubbing until her claws bled.
Jasi became a barmaid for a few days at Erin's inn, and then an [Actress], because of Erin.
Jasi reaches Level 25 as an [Actress], meets the conditions to become a [Lead Actress], and gains [Perfect Imitation] and [Refinement by Accolade].
Later, Jasi is a Level 30 [Famed Lead Actress] with [Refinement by Accolade], [Audience Charge], [Perfect Imitation] and [The Actor's Shadow].
Jasi's [The Actor's Shadow] makes a shadow-Jasi of any species that can perform a second role.
Jasi can produce ten gold coins' worth of make-up for free with every performance.
Princess Jecaina of Jecrass is a young [Fencer] in her twenties, brash, confident, beautiful and long-legged, who dresses for sparring or travel.
Jecaina has hazel-green hair, which some Jecrass bloodlines can turn, inherited from her mother, who is Raelt's half-sister.
Jecaina carries a slim enchanted [Fencer]'s blade and a silver bell that she never goes without.
Jecaina's mother abandoned her after a tryst gone wrong, so Raelt, technically her uncle, raised her as his adopted daughter.
Everyone in Jecrass knows the story, but only Jecaina brings up her heritage.
Jecaina is the sole known heir to the throne of Jecrass.
Jecaina asks Raelt to see the King of Destruction's letter, and Raelt rebukes her mildly for missing breakfast.
Jecaina argues that the King of Destruction could be a powerful ally, since Jecrass never wronged him and several of his Seven are with him.
Raelt, who disagrees, notes her eyes shining as the [Dueling Princess] speaks of Flos.
Jecaina wants to go to Terandria, and she begs to ride to Reim and meet Flos herself.
Jecaina shows Raelt a recording crystal by the Queen of Pop and calls her the greatest [Singer] in ten thousand years.
Geril has Jecaina locked in the palace vaults, guarded by General Lael's [Soldiers], so she cannot escape to join the camp.
Jecaina arrives at Flos' camp demanding an audience and challenges Teres, then Mars the Illusionist, to a duel for entry.
Jecaina asks for one minute of duelling against Mars to earn an audience with Flos.
Jecaina moves quickly enough that Teres barely sees her, and strikes at Mars' shoulder with her foil.
Mars notices Jecaina's silver bell and calls her a [Fencer].
Mars catches Jecaina's lunge barehanded and defeats her with a headbutt, dropping her face-first.
Jecaina rides after Raelt during the march to Levrhine and asks if he will attack it.
