Raelt tells Jecaina the bell is a test: it should not ring when worn by an expert, because a ring means unnecessary movement.
Jecaina learns she earned her bell by defeating a [Fencer], and she goes crimson at Raelt's explanation.
Later, Jecaina brawls with Nerrhavia's [Master Charioteers] after they make remarks she objects to, and she is scraped and bruised.
Later, Jecaina has stopped wearing her silver bell and carries a copy of Raelt's dueling sword.
Raelt, who feels he has failed his adopted daughter, takes her to the practice courts.
Jecaina fights a Gold-rank team from Medain, the Silvereyed Sables, and is dropped by arrows, one in the leg and two sleeping arrows.
Jecaina is kidnapped, hog-tied in a wagon by the adventurers while Raelt's army approaches.
Jecaina kills an enemy [Knight] with [Fencer's Riposte] in a gap between helmet and armour, her first kill of a person.
Jecaina realises she has killed a woman and is grabbed immediately afterwards.
Jecaina is netted by one of Medain's Golden Ranks and dragged before High King Perric.
Perric greets her as Princess Jecaina and says she has inconvenienced him.
Raelt is captured while she escapes, and Geril tells her she must ride because Jecrass needs its [Queen].
Jecaina blames herself for her father's capture, and Geril tells her to go.
Geril dies covering her flight.
Jeiss is a Senior Guardsman of Liscor's Watch, and a Drake who heads the group of guards waiting for Zevara in the barracks.
Jeiss and Senior Guardswoman Beilmark are the Gnoll-Drake pair in charge of oversight of the walls, known throughout the city.
Jeiss is Beilmark's partner and one of the most respected Senior Guardsman pairs.
Jeiss and Beilmark bet silver on whether a small bee escapes a fireball, and Jeiss welcomes the junior guard to the Watch.
Jeiss speaks for the Watch when it asks Zevara about the election and whether she is for Krshia Silverfang.
Jeiss asks Zevara whether she would take a better option if there were one.
Later, Lism advertises Jeiss as a candidate for a seat on Liscor's Council, and Jeiss salutes Zevara awkwardly.
Beilmark says nothing, and Jeiss avoids her gaze, when Lism proclaims him a candidate.
Jeiss and Lism try to persuade Tekshia to congratulate the Horns, but she refuses to give a medal.
Tekshia calls the party a wake after the battle, and says she told the Council not to throw one.
Later, Jeiss is a Councilman of Liscor, sitting on a Council of working-class Gnolls and Drakes.
Jelaim is the leader of the Serpent Hunters, a group of Stitch-folk warriors among the vassals of Flos Reimarch, the King of Destruction.
Jelaim is a Stitch-Man, one of the String People, with golden thread showing at his bare shoulder.
Jelaim says he is a [Serpent Hunter], a class that uses poison in weapons, and that the group was built from it.
Jelaim tells Trey Atwood not to call him Captain, since that is a class term and he has no soldier classes, though he may be a mercenary captain.
Jelaim prefers to be called by his name, or Hunter Jelaim if honorifics are needed.
Jelaim and his warriors carry curved, enchanted blades that are coated in poison in their sheaths.
Jelaim asks Orthenon for more enchanted weapons from the treasury, since steel blades would corrode from the Serpent Hunters' venoms.
Jelaim says the Serpent Hunters have dozens of new recruits learning their tricks, and the king wants them to take in any of the String Folk.
Jelaim teaches only String People, because they can remove a poisoned limb and have a new one woven.
Jelaim loves magical swords and wears scimitars on either hip.
Jelaim tries to swing Flos' sword and cannot manage a proper slash, though his muscles bulge.
Jelaim hurries to Chieftain Nelrra, excited at the idea of an easy new coating for his blades.
Jelaim performs a dueling display on a banquet table with two of his warriors, using real envenomed blades, to honor the King of Destruction.
Jelaim is counted among Flos' vassals, alongside Ulyse, Mars and Orthenon, at the meeting with the Gnolls.
Jelaim throws a knife into a charging Minotauress' unguarded arm, helping the Death Warriors cut her down.
Jelaim's Stitchwarriors use poisoned weapons to support Flos' advance.
Flos orders Jelaim to find the enemy catapults and smash or capture them.
Jelaqua Ivirith is a Selphid, a being who wears dead bodies, and the leader of the Gold-rank adventuring team the Halfseekers.
Jelaqua's skin is deathly white in her first body, and she wears black chainmail and carries a three-headed flail.
Jelaqua's eyes are perfectly black in that body.
Jelaqua's cheeks turn slightly orange when she blushes or is embarrassed, because something inside the dead skin heats up.
Jelaqua's real self sits inside the body, and her blush shows as a faint lattice of orange beneath pale scales.
Jelaqua says she is fifty-one years old and has adventured for about thirty-three years, six more than Typhenous.
Typhenous recalls hearing that Jelaqua came from Baleros as a Silver-rank adventurer, and that the Halfseekers were once one of the best Gold-rank teams, with seven members.
Jelaqua fights with a two-handed flail, and uses it to tear through groups of foes.
Jelaqua says she is a Level 33 [Iron Tempest], a class derived from [Flailmaster], with Skills to fight a pack of foes at once.
Jelaqua Rampages with her arms and body turning into a blur, and shouts for Seborn to get back.
Jelaqua wears Heartflame Armor, a golden-red breastplate that wreathes her body in fire.
The Heartflame Armor deflects Shield Spider bites with its magical flames.
Later, Jelaqua says she is a [Steel Tempest] after upgrading her class from [Iron Tempest].
Jelaqua tells Moore and Seborn that she went first into the corridor because of their rule to always send a Selphid first.
Jelaqua tells Erin that brains have nothing to do with how she controls a body, and she does not need them.
Erin sees that Jelaqua's head is empty inside when its top is cut off.
Jelaqua's real body, a mass of orange, lives inside her vessel and can repair damage such as shattered eardrums.
Jelaqua's dead body cannot heal ear damage with potions as living bodies do, so she must repair it herself.
Jelaqua does not bleed when she is stabbed or shot.
In Book 5, Regrika Blackpaw slices the top of Jelaqua's head off from the eyebrows up.
Jelaqua keeps the cut-off piece of her head stitched on, and it begins to decompose.
Jelaqua says she needs a new body but can manage for a month or two without one.
Jelaqua says Drakes and Gnolls do not like people using bodies, because of the Necromancer.
Jelaqua says finding a body that is not old, diseased and in one piece is very hard.
Jelaqua considers an Antinium body but says she is not familiar with four arms and that Antinium are unwelcome in most places.
Jelaqua tells Erin her body is not doing well, and that no one in Celum or Liscor will sell a body to a Selphid.
Jelaqua says that her body is nearly done for anyway.
Jelaqua is dropped from the air by a giant Face-Eater Moth and her body is broken, so she can only speak.
Part of Jelaqua's face is torn off by the moths.
Seborn says her real form was damaged by the fall too and that there is no saving her body.
Later, Jelaqua wears the body of a Drake with grey scales, supplied by Liscor under its agreement with the Adventurer's Guild.
Jelaqua says the Drake body belonged to a junior city guard who died of blood loss after a moth sliced an artery in her leg.
Jelaqua says the guard's parents agreed to give up the body and were paid a lot, and she hopes not to see them in the crowd.
Later, Jelaqua wears the body of a dead Raskghar, which she calls a good body but too bulky for her tastes.
Jelaqua wants to try a Raskghar body for bragging rights as the first Selphid to do so.
Jelaqua pays Erin to keep dead Raskghar bodies in her basement as spares, to try out or as emergency food.
Later, Jelaqua wears a Human body, which Erin guesses she swapped into so that Mrsha would stop being scared.
Jelaqua wears a female Drake body while travelling, and wakes from a nap on a cart.
Jelaqua appears in a female Raskghar body the morning after a night of drinking.
Jelaqua is a Selphid in a Drake body in Maughin's apartment.
Jelaqua wears a pale scaled body when she orders cookies from Erin.
Jelaqua arrives in a Raskghar body during Ulinde's attack.
Jelaqua carries a flail that Maughin has made for the Raskghar form and is twice as large as her old one.

section: First meeting with Ceria and the Halfseekers, Book 2
text: Jelaqua recognises Halrac and speaks to him easily, telling him it is good to see him again.

section: First meeting with Ceria and the Halfseekers, Book 2
text: Jelaqua introduces herself to Ceria as the leader of the Halfseekers, also known as the Half Freaks.

section: First meeting with Ceria and the Halfseekers, Book 2
text: Jelaqua says the Halfseekers are a Gold-rank team that has lost a few members, and she offers Ceria a place with them.

section: First meeting with Ceria and the Halfseekers, Book 2
text: Jelaqua says they came to explore the new dungeon and to scout for a new member.

section: First meeting with Ceria and the Halfseekers, Book 2
text: Seborn says half-species are rare enough that the Halfseekers knew Ceria's name.

section: First meeting with Ceria and the Halfseekers, Book 2
text: Jelaqua tells Ceria the Halfseekers do not have to hire only Gold-rank adventurers, and would level up a competent person and give them magic items.

section: First meeting with Ceria and the Halfseekers, Book 2
text: Jelaqua offers Numbtongue a place in the Halfseekers, and he declines, saying he belongs at the inn.
Jelaqua insists on going down into the dungeon to find Mrsha, saying she has a soft spot for children and those shunned by others.
Jelaqua is the Selphid that Erin recognises as "that chest-bursting lady" when the Halfseekers arrive at the inn.
Jelaqua shakes Erin's hand, nervous because touching a dead body's hand is not fun for any species.
Jelaqua bursts out that the team that got the mace was already receiving offers for it, and kicks a chair into the air.
Jelaqua apologises to Lyonette, and Moore catches the chair.
Jelaqua grinds her teeth when Halrac mentions a masked swordswoman.
Jelaqua calls the dungeon a vengeance dungeon, because it feels like a huge trap and not just a place to hide treasure.
Jelaqua explains to Revi that future-generations dungeons test those who enter, and vengeance dungeons seal away the best artifacts behind the nastiest traps.
Ulrien says adventurers class dungeons as containment, future generations or vengeance, and that containment dungeons are meant to contain something.
Jelaqua advises young adventurers to write letters to their loved ones, because they will die if they go down.
Halrac tells the same adventurers they will die.
Jelaqua throws her flail across a trapped floor so that Seborn can pull himself over by the chain.
Jelaqua whirls her flail through Ghouls and charges a Flesh Worm.
Regrika stabs Jelaqua through the stomach, after Ulrien is killed, and Typhenous's magic bolts do nothing to Regrika.
Jelaqua charges Regrika from behind with her flail and Regrika backhands her unconscious with a shield, saying only "Selphids".
Jelaqua opens the inn door and sees Headscratcher, and cries out "Garen?".
Headscratcher answers "Redfang?", and Moore throws him across the room.
Jelaqua knocks the Hobgoblin down and says it is not Garen after all.
Jelaqua and the Halfseekers beat the Hobgoblins until Erin's shout shakes the floor.
Jelaqua tells Erin that the Halfseekers will stay at the inn in case she needs them, but will not hang around the Goblins.
Jelaqua says the Redfangs' training looks like copies of Garen, who learned his exercises from the Halfseekers.
Jelaqua and her team are hungover from the party, with Moore sitting on the floor because no chair is large enough.
Jelaqua offers to look after Mrsha for Lyonette.

section: Pallass and the moth attack, Book 7
text: Jelaqua returns to the inn with a barbed arrow in her shoulder from a trap that Seborn missed.

section: Pallass and the moth attack, Book 7
text: Jelaqua joins Relc at Pallass and walks over without armour but with her flail.

section: Pallass and the moth attack, Book 7
text: Jelaqua takes two arrows in the chest and shoulder in Pallass.

section: Pallass and the moth attack, Book 7
text: Pallass's Watch is forced to unshackle Jelaqua and Relc and treat them as guests under Ilvriss's insistence.

section: Pallass and the moth attack, Book 7
text: A Pallass Watch officer says Jelaqua, Relc and Seborn will be kept, with their weapons impounded, to avoid a diplomatic incident.

section: Pallass and the moth attack, Book 7
text: Jelaqua says the Halfseekers do not kill idiots, because they are unpopular enough as it is.
Jelaqua is first into the waves of Shield Spiders, her body wreathed in flame and her flail swinging.
Jelaqua is deaf after the blasts, and Halrac covers her while she repairs her eardrums for a minute.
Jelaqua finds that Typhenous's comet storm has dented her flail's spiked heads and strained its chain.
Jelaqua says she needs an enchanted flail, though she has spares.
Jelaqua agrees that the Halfseekers will team with the Horns of Hammerad while Griffon Hunt works with the Silver Swords.
Jelaqua says the Halfseekers are meeting Halrac, Zevara and Olesm to plan against more monster silos.
Jelaqua strides in with her armour blazing after fighting two groups of Raskghar in the city.
Jelaqua tells the city that dungeon sieges are normal, and that she has seen cities in Baleros fall to a Silver-rank dungeon.
Jelaqua admits she feels like a stomach ulcer for resenting the other teams' competition, but says the people come first.
Jelaqua leads her team in a charge at a Raskghar group after the Halfseekers cut through fourteen corridors.
Jelaqua's flail heads are deformed after hours of fighting, and a spike breaks off one.
Jelaqua is hit by a trap explosion when chasing the armoured Raskghar, and her armour takes the hit.
Seborn stops Jelaqua from chasing the Raskghar and tells her they must fall back, since Moore is wounded.
Jelaqua pours a healing potion into the wound Seborn cuts open on Moore.
Jelaqua leads the charge through the inn's door against the Raskghar.
Jelaqua finally kills the armoured Raskghar.
Seborn says the Halfseekers owe Selys Shivertail a cut of what they get, and discusses trying to claim the magic armour.
Bevussa says Jelaqua is after the armour, and hopes she withdraws her claim on the light-spelled shortsword.
Jelaqua tells a Guardsman that she is a Gold-rank Selphid, and offers to open her chest.
Jelaqua stands and tells the others that the Halfseekers are also done with the dungeon, since they have their gold.
Jelaqua hugs Pisces when the teams decide to be done with the dungeon.
Jelaqua, Moore and Seborn are walking north with a door in the pass when they meet the Redfangs and Garen.
Jelaqua was Garen's Captain in the Halfseekers, and he sees hatred in her face when they meet.
Jelaqua recognises Garen at once, asks Moore to hit her to check she is not dreaming, and gets a dent in her head.
Moore cancels a [Message] before the Halfseekers attack, and Jelaqua greets Garen cheerfully.
Jelaqua runs ahead of the others and fights through Redfang warriors with her flail, even with a spear in her back.
Jelaqua tells Moore and Seborn to go while she covers them.
Jelaqua takes arrows without bleeding, which slows the Redfangs.
Garen runs Jelaqua through three times and the Selphid keeps strangling him.
Jelaqua tells Garen she came back in a new body and found the inn surrounded by Guards, with her dead team inside.
Jelaqua says the innkeeper told them he saw a Goblin run out of their rooms with a bloody sword.
Jelaqua says nothing was cursed, and all the items were there except one small thing.
Jelaqua calls Garen a filthy traitor who killed friends in a moment.
Garen says Halassia threatened him, and Jelaqua says she might have, but that killing them is something she will not forgive.
Jelaqua tells Erin she took hits to her real body in the fight and asks her to tell no one what happened.
Jelaqua says Moore is too weak to eat anything but liquids and that Seborn is angry at himself for letting Garen go.
Jelaqua lies with a smile that it is over and done.
Jelaqua says Garen is a terrible liar who might have exaggerated or twisted what happened, but she can imagine it.
Jelaqua prepares a pyre for Garen's body and tells Moore and Seborn that Selphids prize bodies of warriors over Level 30.
Jelaqua says Selphids leave the bodies of the useless to rot, which is their sign of contempt, and that she will not do so to Garen.
Jelaqua burns Garen's body and finds no key on or in him.
Moore says time stopped for the Halfseekers since that day, and that now they can move on.
Jelaqua proposes one more adventure with the three of them, and the Halfseekers set out with their old motto of searching for a home.
Jelaqua, Moore and Seborn travel by mule cart on a forest road nearly a hundred and fifty miles from Invrisil when Erin opens the door.
Seborn decides for the team, since he is tired of sleeping on carts, to go through to the inn.
Jelaqua wakes next to Maughin after a night of drinking, and Maughin says he enjoyed it and that her Selphid nature does not matter.
Jelaqua cooks for Maughin in his ninth-floor Pallass apartment, which is decorated in the Dullahan style.
Jelaqua and Maughin are a scandal to the Dullahan community, though no one in Pallass calls Maughin out.
Jelaqua tells Bevussa that she is on vacation with Maughin and that her team is on its way to Invrisil a few miles at a time.
Jelaqua says she has met no one she clicked with like Maughin in about eight years.
Jelaqua orders a bag of cookies from Erin for a date with Maughin in Pallass.
Jelaqua says she visited Pallass nine years before, when the Halfseekers worked in the south.
Jelaqua jumps Ulinde, a younger Selphid, rams her host's head into a wall and drags her out as she attacks the inn.
Jelaqua kills a Wyvern with her flail while wearing the Raskghar body.
Jelaqua pays for Erin's field of Sage's Grass with a slip redeemable at the Merchant's Guild in Liscor, saying the Halfseekers owe their fortunes partly to Erin and the Redfangs.
Jelaqua tells Erin the Halfseekers are going to clear a locust swarm.
Jelaqua attends a Dullahan Walking-Waltz of Baleros ball in Pallass in a dress.
Jelov is an extremely old [Carver] from Windrest with contorted hands and back.
Jelov carves wooden toys, hilts and handles, as his hands cannot hold an axe or lift heavy loads.
Jelov begs Laken for work because he has a granddaughter to support.
Jelov carves the wooden markers that Laken uses to claim land around the village, finishing three with one being varnished.
Laken asks Jelov whether the markers are done, and Jelov says they are finished but not polished.
Laken has seven thick, heavy wooden markers bearing his symbol, and uses six of them to claim the land.
Jelov becomes a famous man in the village, with eight apprentices and more work than he can handle, after being a recluse selling small trinkets.
Laken sits on a wooden throne decorated with carved eyes in the meeting hall.
Prost catches Jelov selling miniature totems as good-luck charms while fifteen replacement totems burned by Goblins are still owed after fifty days.
Jelov says his mind wanders on large pieces and that small totems take only minutes.
Prost confiscates Jelov's pouch of bronze and copper coins, since Riverfarm pools its money.
Jerci is a female Gnoll and a native of Liscor who is in her second week as a Junior Guardswoman of the City Watch.
Jerci wears an earring in her right ear and has dyed her fur black in artful slashes down one arm.
Jerci is issued a baton, and as a Junior Guard she is not allowed to patrol outside of squads.
Jerci is uneasy about working with the Antinium Klbkch, and at first refuses even to look at her fellow Gnoll Tkrn.
Jerci confirms the scent of a [Thief] when Klbkch asks her, pointing out the direction when Tkrn scents the air.
Klbkch tells Jerci to observe how he works and to state any thoughts without fear of judgment.
Jerci looks scornful at Tkrn's search routine until Klbkch explains it, after which she blushes and mutters an apology to Tkrn.
Jerci grows nervous when the patrol nearly meets Mister Soot, and Klbkch tells her not to look back over her shoulder.
Jerci tackles the fleeing [Thief] and pins him with a knee on his back, on Klbkch's advice to rush him.
Jerci helps Tkrn cuff the thief, and Klbkch corrects her position when escorting the prisoner.
Klbkch tells Jerci she may ask Tkrn about law enforcement as it pertains to Gnolls.
After the shift Jerci walks with Tkrn, asks him questions in a snappish way, and takes her ear piercing out.
Embria scolds Jerci for grabbing a Creler with her paws during cleanup and tells her to use long-handled tongs.
Jericha is Tyrion Veltras' personal aide and [Mage], and he relays orders and messages through her.
Jericha did not study at Wistram but at the mage's academy in First Landing, which causes tension with Wistram [Mages].
Tyrion considers Jericha one of the best spellcasters he employs.
Jericha is probably higher-level than a visiting [Assassin] in combat and has more expensive artifacts.
Jericha is a nobleman's second-in-command, an elite.
Jericha burns Magnolia Reinhart's [Message] after Tyrion reads it, and Tyrion tells her to send Magnolia his regards.
Jericha stuns Yitton Byres with a spell when he charges Tyrion, on Tyrion's order to take him alive.
Jericha is disturbed when Magnolia's [Message] names her and warns of consequences if it is not delivered.
Jericha insults the poisoning [Assassin], who stabs her in the stomach with a dagger, and Jericha heals herself with a wand.
Jericha hates the [Assassin] who holds Tyrion's sons hostage by poison, as does Ullim.
Johanas is an American from Earth who is stranded in Baleros and is among the Humans at the neutral-zone party.
Johanas is already drunk when he tells Ken that a friend traded a flashlight to a war vendor for a ton of beer.
Johanas tells Ken that casting [Repair] on Earth devices also recharges their batteries.
Johanas points Ken to the war vendors who will sell to anyone for the right price.
Johanas kneels with five girls and two other men, all Americans caught sneaking through the forest, before a Dullahan executioner with an axe.
Dullahans execute Johanas and the seven other American captives before the battle resumes, and Ken remembers Johanas' corpse.
Daly later cites the deaths of Johanas and the others when arguing that the Earthworlders must be able to defend themselves.
Joseph is a young man from Spain on Earth, one of the seven Earthers who travel to Liscor together.
Joseph is not a soldier, having never been in the army, and sees himself as just a kid from Spain.
Joseph is the Earther known as the inventor of soccer in this world, credited with bringing the game here.
The Earthers run out of coin in Invrisil, and Joseph is sober because the group can no longer pay for drink.
Joseph sells a sword for a good price after visiting six shops, saying he is not good with it and would only be killed.
Rose blames Joseph's group and Joseph blames Rose for giving away their money, and both think they are in charge.
Joseph wants to go to Liscor and avoid the Players of Celum, saying it could be a trap and that Ryoka warned them about Wistram.
Maviola El notices the Earthers, treats them to a meal, and they follow her.
Joseph drinks a morning cup of gin and blue fruit juice while Rose tells him to stop because he is sick.
Lyonette says about a week and a few days have passed since the seven Earthers came to The Wandering Inn.
Joseph has the [Drinker] class, which he thinks is nearly useless and which consumes him.
Joseph is a Level 8 [Warrior] but does not feel like one, though he has tried more than Kevin.
Joseph killed an Eater Goat while Magnolia's servants helped keep the Earthers safe, and it refused to die.
Joseph says the Earthers could not kill monsters under Magnolia's care because it was too bloody, like sawing through a corpse.
Joseph feels worthless and says he is no leader, and thinks Rose is not one either.
Joseph hears Ekirra's red ball cost twelve silver and leaves to find the shop, though Drassi wants help playing with Ekirra.
Joseph buys the largest ball the shop sells and asks the [Leatherworker] to charge it to The Wandering Inn.
Joseph teaches Ekirra to kick a ball outside Celum, and Drassi joins in.
Joseph says he played all the time back home, and intercepts Ekirra's kick with his chest.
Joseph plays football with the Gnolls until he cannot move and lies in the grass laughing, not craving a drink.
Joseph gains the [Kicker] class, with the notice showing Level 8.
Joseph goes to bed that night without needing a drink for once.
Ekirra gains the [Kicker] class that same night.
Joseph gains the Skills [Power Kick] and [Sure Footing], and does not realise how powerful his kick has become.
Jeva Silverfang tells Joseph to take responsibility for Ekirra's [Kicker] class and teach him to level up.
Joseph believes Ryoka deleted everything on Kevin's laptop, but Kevin says an automatic backup drive saved the files.
Kevin tells Joseph that he has kicked his habit thanks to soccer.
Palt gives Joseph a wand casting [Stun Spear], Tier 3, with sixty charges.
Palt gives Joseph a bag of gold and a letter written at his master's dictation.
Aaron Vanwell's letter says not to come to Wistram unless Joseph does not want to leave, and that Aaron will send what he can.
Joseph and Kevin teach football and rugby to children and adults, with Councilmember Jeiss asking about the first intercity game with Pallass in three days.
Joseph tells Jeiss that if they practise they will smoke Pallass, citing poor shots and worse teamwork.
Joseph captains Liscor's team in the first inter-city football game against Pallass.
Joseph blocks the kickoff with his chest and passes ahead to Rumerk.
Joseph scores with [Flash Kick], curving the ball past the Dullahan goalkeeper, and Liscor leads 2-0.
Wistram News Network says Joseph Ortega came up with football's rules in conjunction with Wistram Academy, a claim Erin notices.
Jurix is a tall Dullahan mage of Wistram, and a member of the Isolationist faction along with Illphres and Bastam.
Jurix is a powerful mage specializing in combat magic and physical reinforcement magic.
Jurix is cheerful for a Dullahan, and sets his head on the table to eat with floating plates and cups.
Jurix prefers to eat with his head on his shoulders, which is an oddity for a Dullahan.
Jurix knows Illphres' secret, the reason she covers her mouth when she smiles.
Jurix sits at Illphres' table at the banquet and talks with her, ignoring her glare.
Jurix takes one enemy ship while Bastam takes another during the pirate attack on Wistram.
Jurix lands on the enemy ship's deck with impervious armor, striking pirates with [Tremor Impact] and pursuing them with [Flash Step].
Jurix introduces himself at a table with Bastam, Ophelia and Qum, five mages each holding influence within Wistram.
Jurix laughs, puts his head on the table to shake Ceria's hand, and later shouts at her during spell practice.
Jurix gives Ceria a wand to practice with.
Jurix is one of a group of five, with Illphres, Bastam, Ophelia and Qum, who train to challenge Zelkyr's Golems.
Jurix opens the double doors with his own hands as the five mages enter the room of Zelkyr's Golems.
Jurix is one of five mages who were alive less than an hour earlier whose remains Pisces finds in the room where the Golems will disassemble them.
Jurix is remembered as brave, a true mage with courage, in Ceria's angry speech afterward.
Karsaeu-Dequoa is a Djinni, a spirit from Chandrar, who is always the driver of the Unmarked Coach under a different face each time.
Karsaeu appears to Ryoka as a large, irritable woman in a top hat and dark clothes with a scarf over pale skin, driving in rain that never soaks her.
Karsaeu calls herself the slave that has run the Unmarked Coach service for longer than Ryoka and Fierre could know.
Fierre says the coach's owner is a master of the Djinni, whom Fierre does not know.
Fierre warns that Karsaeu may be bound to report anything of value to her master, and Karsaeu laughs that the Vampire is smarter than Ryoka.
Karsaeu says no violence against the coach or its passengers is allowed, by deed or word, and her route is unchangeable.
Karsaeu says she will not answer questions about her bond, her master, or locations and details of other passengers.
Karsaeu says passengers may not request sex from her, a rule that is new by three centuries.
Karsaeu says she is bound to tell the truth, but would lie if Ryoka had found her bottle.
Karsaeu says that if Ryoka had found her vessel, Karsaeu would have been freed and Ryoka dead.
Karsaeu says that if freed she would happily destroy both Ryoka and Fierre, and that sympathy does not make them friends.
Karsaeu says her people died, her little cousins were killed and the rest enslaved, and few of them remain.
Karsaeu declines to say whether she is strong, telling Fierre she may test her if she wishes.
Karsaeu gives only her name, Karsaeu-Dequoa, saying that is enough of her name for Ryoka.
Karsaeu asks Ryoka to tell the visitors of winter that she misses them.
Karsaeu tells Ryoka to warn her other friend to stay away from Chandrar, saying it is the Djinni's land and they will take it back someday.
A Sister of Chell says the coach's food is made from Karsaeu's own magic and that eating too many chips slows her down.
The narration says Djinni create material out of magic, which is the base of their power, so the coach's food is Karsaeu herself.
Karsaeu offers Ryoka, Fierre and Salamani a free ride from her employer back to Reizmelt, with a strained smile.
Ryoka tells Karsaeu that they woke the Archmage of Izril, and Karsaeu relaxes, thanks her and tells them to sleep.
The Unmarked Coach carries the three overnight and they wake at Reizmelt.
Keith is one of the Americans summoned to Rhir, and the narrator describes him as a [Blacksmith] who wants to find out if an [Engineer] class exists.
Keith is into architecture and would have been a freshman at Lehigh University in Pennsylvania, an engineering major.
Keith has lost the [Hero] class, as he did not want to kill.
Keith is an [Inferno Smith], though despite his [Blacksmith] class he has no strength-enhancing Skills.
Keith nervously sits with Cirille between himself and the narrator, and stares at her in worry.
Keith flinches along with Emily and Richard when the group is struck by fear.
Keith charges at Eddy over a dispute and freezes when Eddy puts up his fists, and Richard intervenes.
Keith flips Eddy off from behind after Eddy walks away.
Keith finally figures out how to smelt titanium from their world, which was only powder when given to him.
Keith is confident he can make more of the titanium.
Lord Hayvon promises to prepare a gift for Keith after cutting a chunk off the metal and finding it not magical.
Keith is among the Americans who help in their own ways rather than fight, and is offered sanctuary in the kingdom to work.
Kel is a surly, hot-tempered Drake [Guardsman] of the Pallass City Watch who guards the Pallass end of Erin Solstice's magic door.
Kel carries a spear and resents Erin's repeated unauthorised crossings, which Erin says have happened about eight times.
Kel tells Erin that Watch Captain Venim requires everyone passing from Liscor to Pallass to be authorised.
Kel says one [Guardsman] was judged enough to watch the door despite two unauthorised entries several days earlier.
Kel lets Erin through rather than poke her with his spear, and she believes she is wearing him down.
Kel spars with Erin over members of the Watch having free tea, which he insists is reserved for the Watch.
Kel glares at Erin from the Pallass side after she leaves with Grimalkin and Maughin through the door.
Kel pursues Grimalkin and Relc through the door, until Relc's clawed hand blocks him.
Kel is the one who believes Erin when she warns that something is going to attack the inn, and orders Watch Captain Venim fetched and the alarm sounded.
Later, Kel is promoted to Desk Sergeant two weeks before Erin's arrest, after the Creler attack, and is openly proud of it.
Erin says that Kel was the one who believed her warning to Pallass about the attack.
Kel tells Erin that she was cleared by a truth spell, so he lists her account as completely accurate.
Kel says Watch Captains review cases each evening before nightfall and any of them would agree the incident was an accident.
Kel has Erin placed in the temporary holding area, the punishment cell, rather than the non-magical section.
Kel holds the 8th-floor street in front of his Watch House against a Wyvern, ordering shields and long pikes forward.
Kel uses [Protector's Order] to send a Gnoll family running past his squad's line.
Kel's scales freeze when the Wyvern breathes frost on the squad, though he is nearly but not killed.
A Dullahan [Guardswoman] in the first rank takes the brunt of the frost and dies, her head dropping from her body.
Kel, as Sergeant, commands the Pallass Watch squads posted at the door on the 8th floor, which are the worst posting.
Kel gives new arrivals a serious speech about the Crazy Human of Liscor, and looks sorry for them when they laugh.
Kel tells a new squad that they will collect the food Erin sends through the door, and eats a cookie himself.
Kel says he really hates Erin and tells the squad to file their complaints, while sitting in a comfortable armchair at the door.
Keldrass is the captain of the Flamewardens, a Gold-rank adventuring team, and an Oldblood Drake.
Keldrass cannot control his flames as well as some other Oldblood Drakes, so he speaks in short bursts to avoid immolating people.
Keldrass snorts a plume of fire when angry.
Keldrass served in the army, and Grimalkin believes he taught Keldrass's unit then.
Keldrass grew up when the Necromancer's armies came south and hit Pallass.
Keldrass calls a meeting of adventurer team leaders about working together on the dungeon.
Keldrass heads for Erin's inn to negotiate dungeon artifacts, and tells Bevussa the Flamewardens want the armor.
Bevussa's Wings of Pallass want the invisible bow, a shortsword or a wind staff.
Keldrass defends the Tailless Thief's food, where the adventurers stay.
Keldrass is jailed for a day after a brawl over the lottery at the Adventurer's Guild, in the cell beside Bevussa's.
Keldrass wears armor taken from the Raskghar and carries a mace.
Keldrass argues that Erin undermines the rule of law by after a Goblin and an Antinium Soldier killed two dozen Humans in a Human city.
Keldrass says adventurers who did the same would be arrested, and that he is supporting the system that keeps Drake society running.
Keldrass says Goblins as a whole cannot be reasoned with, and that an earlier Drake was not wrong to be wary since Goblins killed his family.
Numbtongue, speaking as Pyrite, tells Keldrass a story of a mining Goblin and tosses a gold nugget at his feet with the word "fetch".
Keldrass wants the nugget despite his unease, since the gold is gold.
Keldrass snorts dismissively when Earlia mentions the Golden Goblin legend.
Keldrass says he cannot sit across from the Hobgoblin and dislikes that Erin tolerates a [Necromancer].
Keldrass tells Bevussa that Nailren says the Gnolls on his team suspect Mrsha carries a Skill or a curse that attracts bad luck.
Bevussa slaps Keldrass with a wing for arguing the luck theory.
Keldrass tells Ceria that the Horns are the 1268th Silver-rank team to kill an Adult Creler, as Miss Shivertail looked up.
Ken, full name Kenjiro Murata, is a Japanese university student who is twenty one when he arrives in Baleros.
Ken was studying business at university, in the same classes as his lifelong friend Aiko Nonomura.
Ken is polite and deferential, applying the etiquette of his own culture to Baleros, and people tend to like him.
Ken's grandfather died the year Ken entered university, at the age of 88.
Ken's grandfather was fifteen when Japan surrendered and lived through the American bombing raids, which he sometimes described to Ken.
Ken is a Level 1 [Warrior] with the Skill [Lesser Stamina] on his second day in Baleros.
Later, Ken reaches [Warrior] Level 4 and gains the [Negotiator] class at Level 2, plus the Skills [Amateur Linguist] and [Polite Demeanor].
Later, Ken gains the [Medic] class at Level 4 with the Skills [Quick Sprint] and [Sympathetic Ear].
Later, Ken is a Level 18 [Negotiator], after leveling meteorically from his first night of sleep.
Later, Ken is a Level 25 [Negotiator] whose latest Skill, [Moodreader], shows him people's general states of mind.
Ken's Skill [Amateur Linguist] lets him understand written Baleros text and gives him the Japanese meaning of unfamiliar English words.
Ken's narration calls him a [Diplomat] when he makes a budget proposal for the company.
Ken and Aiko befriend Luan on the march with Gravetender's Fist, since Luan is the first person they get to know.
Luan tells a frightened Ken that wars are never safe.
Ken fights a zombie Centaur with Luan, Aiko and two Dullahans, cutting at its side while Luan, who leads their patrol, delivers the final blow.
Ken interrupts Quallet to win a Centaur officer's permission to cross Centaur territory, promising an illuminated company banner and lanterns.
Ken tells Quallet he has only just received the [Negotiator] class, and Quallet answers that it is the same as a [Diplomat].
Quallet makes Ken the company's go-between for both the Centaurs and the Dullahans and promises a bonus for talking them out of trouble.
Ken asks Quallet whether he warned the Dullahans that his friends would try to run away, and Quallet turns away without answering.

section: Leaving for Geneva and the Red Cross Company
text: Luan, Ken and Aiko tell Geneva that they appeared in Baleros only last week and ask whether she is from their world.

section: Leaving for Geneva and the Red Cross Company
text: Geneva offers Luan, Ken and Aiko food and a bed, but only for people from their world, and Luan says at least forty such people remain.

section: Leaving for Geneva and the Red Cross Company
text: Luan declares he cannot be part of the war, and Ken answers that he will go too, hoping the others follow.

section: Leaving for Geneva and the Red Cross Company
text: Ken goes alone through the valley under a white flag to meet the war vendor Xalandrass, escorted by two tall Lizardmen.

section: Leaving for Geneva and the Red Cross Company
text: Ken barters an Evercut arrowhead, taken from a friend, to Xalandrass for red, white and black paint plus some coin.

section: Leaving for Geneva and the Red Cross Company
text: Xalandrass says he once sold Evercut arrows to the Roving Arrow company and hopes Ken will spread word of his fairness.

section: Leaving for Geneva and the Red Cross Company
text: Ken and Luan wear white armor marked with red crosses, plant a flag and carry a shield with the same cross onto the battlefield.

section: Leaving for Geneva and the Red Cross Company
text: Ken and Luan carry wounded soldiers back, making seven trips, and soldiers from both sides hesitate rather than attack them.

section: Leaving for Geneva and the Red Cross Company
text: Ken points to a flying red-cross banner and says the Red Cross is a company, and Geneva later finds a Red Cross Company sign above the camp.

section: Leaving for Geneva and the Red Cross Company
text: Ken leaves a blistered, gassed young Dullahan woman behind to save burn victims he can still help, and feels deep guilt afterwards.

section: Leaving for Geneva and the Red Cross Company
text: Ken and Luan begin acting as [Medics], and are cornered by eight Centaurs six days after starting.

section: Leaving for Geneva and the Red Cross Company
text: Ken thinks Dullahans fight with a Japanese-style ideal of victory at any cost, using suicide attacks, traps and prisoner killing.

section: Leaving for Geneva and the Red Cross Company
text: Ken thinks Centaurs regard ambushes as honorable but abandon honor once they suspect the other side of underhandedness.

section: Neutral ground and the valley exit
text: Ken uses Xalandrass' most powerful amplifier ring to shout across the battlefield that Geneva's group is not an enemy.

section: Neutral ground and the valley exit
text: Ken announces that Geneva Scala, known as the Last Light, had her camp attacked by both sides.

section: Neutral ground and the valley exit
text: Ken names Quallet, Exara and Xalandrass as neutral parties and tells the armies his group is leaving and will fight only if attacked.

section: Neutral ground and the valley exit
text: Ken, Quallet and the other soldiers follow Geneva down into the valley, and the neutral groups leave it together.
Ken has taught his companions how to behave with Baleros races, such as not touching Dullahans and chatting with Lizardfolk.
Ken persuades a Dullahan company, a Gold-rank [Mage] heading the Mage's Guild in Talenqual, the Adventurer's Guildmaster and a ship's crew to fight giant serpents.
Ken and Daly organized the Talenqual operation, gathering adventurers, Runners and sailors rather than inviting just one company.
Ken has no set job in the United Nations company, but visits allies from Hastel to Silver-rank teams and shopkeepers at least weekly with small gifts.
Ken proposes saving for Paige's emergency fund, then giving twenty percent of spare money to repairs, books, beds and tools, and the rest to gear for Daly's team.

This entry gathers two uses of the name: an undead Gnoll commander in Az'kerash's service and a Gnoll Chieftain remembered as the greatest of his people. The texts cited here do not say whether they are the same person.
An undead Gnoll skeleton in armor announces itself as Kerash, Commander of the Endless Legions of Az'Kerash, and raises a battleaxe to attack the living soldiers with the undead Bea.
Kerash, Venitra and Bea stand around Ryoka when she leaves the Necromancer's room.

Venitra, Kerash and Bea discuss that the Master has let Ryoka go, and one says his decision may be in error, though another notes that he does not make mistakes and they agree to hold her until he is finished.
Krshia says Kerash was the greatest of the Gnoll Chieftains and died a century ago.
Sir Kerrig Louis is a Knight of the Petal, sworn to the Walchais family, and an older [Knight].
Sir Kerrig is of the landlord nobility: his claim to aristocracy is a small, worthless inherited plot that once held a village.
Sir Kerrig became a [Knight] despite being a first-born son, and served over three decades, fighting Drakes, Goblins and monsters.
Sir Kerrig carries an enchanted battleaxe that sparks with lightning.

section: Captive of the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 7)
text: Sir Kerrig and Welca Caveis are captured after trees are dropped on them and the armoured [Knights] survive being knocked out.

section: Captive of the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 7)
text: Lady Bethal abandoned the two captured Knights rather than keep fighting in the trapped woods.

section: Captive of the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 7)
text: On their first night as prisoners, Kerrig and Welca overwhelmed a guard, stole a sword, and were flattened by a dozen Hobs.

section: Captive of the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 7)
text: Rags ordered that nobody may take advantage of her prisoners, male or female, and the Redfang warriors back her.

section: Captive of the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 7)
text: Sir Kerrig thanks Pyrite, saying the tribe is unlike what he had been told.

section: Captive of the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 7)
text: Sir Kerrig asks Pyrite to talk honestly, saying he had scarcely believed Goblins could be peaceful after Velan the Kind.

section: Captive of the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 7)
text: As Welca's superior, Sir Kerrig orders her to take no action against the Goblins and not to escape, but to watch and listen.

section: Captive of the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 7)
text: Watching the Goblins argue and care for their children, Sir Kerrig fears he has been blind, and that he may have killed people rather than monsters.

section: Captive of the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 7)
text: Sir Kerrig suggests the Flooded Waters tribe may be to Goblins what Knights are to Humans, hunting those who kill Goblins.

section: Captive of the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 7)
text: Sir Kerrig sends Welca away on a horse to reach Lady Bethal while he stays to influence Pyrite and Rags.

section: Captive of the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 7)
text: Sir Kerrig believes his order alone could not subdue this tribe, which would escape repeatedly and begin to retaliate.

section: Captive of the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 7)
text: Sir Kerrig fights five Hobs and eight Goblins barehanded in a boxer's stance and leaves them all unconscious.

section: Captive of the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 7)
text: Pyrite kicks Sir Kerrig against a cart and knocks him out with a punch for six hours.

section: Release and the Message to Laken (Book 8)
text: Lady Bethal believes Sir Kerrig and Welca perished, until Rags tells her both are prisoners.

section: Release and the Message to Laken (Book 8)
text: Later, the tribe returns Sir Kerrig to Bethal's Knights without ransom, telling her to take the Human and go.

section: Release and the Message to Laken (Book 8)
text: Sir Kerrig tells Bethal he helped Welca escape less than a day before, and describes the poison-gas night attack on the camp.

section: Release and the Message to Laken (Book 8)
text: Sir Kerrig tells Rags that Laken Godart's attacks are preemptive retaliation for Goblin raids, and that Laken cannot tell her tribe from the Goblin Lord's.

section: Release and the Message to Laken (Book 8)
text: Sir Kerrig tends the poisoned Goblins, having them gargle salt water, and watches the wounded with pity and regret.

section: Release and the Message to Laken (Book 8)
text: Sir Kerrig tells the Goblins only that the Unseen Emperor is named Laken Godart, and does not know where he comes from.

section: Release and the Message to Laken (Book 8)
text: Sir Kerrig first refuses to trust Rags or promise to persuade the Emperor of her message.

section: Release and the Message to Laken (Book 8)
text: After Pyrite argues the tribe wants peace, Sir Kerrig agrees to carry Rags' message and try to broker peace with Laken.

section: Release and the Message to Laken (Book 8)
text: Sir Kerrig rides out of the city on a horse supplied by the Goblins.

section: Release and the Message to Laken (Book 8)
text: Tyrion Veltras says he met Sir Kerrig in Riverfarm, where he was well and unharmed.

section: Knights of the Petal and Clairei Fields (Book 11)
text: Sent by Sir Thomast, Sir Kerrig confronts six Knights of the Order of Clairei Fields, including Sir Molte, in an inn.

section: Knights of the Petal and Clairei Fields (Book 11)
text: Sir Kerrig pours his ale over Sir Molte's head and smashes a mug into his face.

section: Knights of the Petal and Clairei Fields (Book 11)
text: Sir Kerrig declares the Clairei Knights enemies of his order until Lady Bethal receives redress, and challenges them to fisticuffs.

section: Knights of the Petal and Clairei Fields (Book 11)
text: Sir Kerrig draws his lightning battleaxe when a Clairei Knight draws a sword, and she sheathes it.

section: Knights of the Petal and Clairei Fields (Book 11)
text: Sir Kerrig throws Sir Molte through a window, smashes another Knight through a wall, and proclaims war.

section: Knights of the Petal and Clairei Fields (Book 11)
text: Sir Kerrig says the Order of the Petal draws no blood unless necessary, as Sir Thomast has proclaimed.
Kevin is a young Earther from California who worked at a bicycle repair shop before coming to this world.
Kevin is one of the seven Earthers who stay at The Wandering Inn for roughly a week after arriving.
Erin thinks of Kevin as the stoner guy, though Joseph knows he is actually very athletic.
Kevin used to do the bookkeeping for the bike shop on his laptop, which is why the laptop carries an automatic backup drive.
Kevin begs for alms in Invrisil with one silver and three coppers, and keeps begging while Rose and Joseph argue.
Kevin begs Maviola El for alms, which leads to her treating the Earthers to a meal.
Kevin says Ryoka took the Earthers' electronics, and Rose and Joseph tell him to shut up when he tells them to chill.
Kevin says he has turned down the last six classes he was offered.
Kevin lists [Layabout], [Beggar] from Invrisil, [Rider] on the horses and [Potter] among the classes he refused.
Kevin thinks he is a Level 4 [Warrior] and says he should probably have gotten rid of the [Warrior] class.
Kevin keeps his laptop's movies on an automatic backup drive after Ryoka deletes the originals.
Kevin shares a spliff with Numbtongue and plays music on his laptop, while Numbtongue copies a song on guitar after hearing it five times.
Kevin and Joseph teach football and rugby to children, and Kevin leads the kids to a newly flattened field.
Kevin teases Joseph by calling him Mr. Soccer when Joseph corrects him to say rugby, and shows Ekirra an American football ball.
Kevin says he once thought about making a bicycle but Magnolia never went for it, and he has some sketches.
Kevin wants to make a bicycle and a skateboard, and names steel, parts, money and the lack of rubber as the problems.
Kevin says his mountain bike weighed about thirty pounds and the average speed of a bike is thirty miles per hour.
Pelt identifies Kevin's metal, aluminum, as Serraleun, one of the metals that goes into Naq-Alrama steel.
Pelt refuses to work Serraleun, saying the process is a pain, he hates the stuff, and it is poison if it gets into the lungs.
Kevin rides a steel skateboard down a Pallass staircase ramp from the 9th Floor, wearing a magical ring from Hedault.
Kevin flips near the 5th Floor ramp, and Hedault's ring stops him a foot above the ground before dropping him.
A [Guard] arrests Kevin after the ride, but a mob of Pallass youth carries him off to ask about the skateboard.
Hedault says the ring is only safe up to a certain weight and the skateboard itself is quite a projectile.
Kevin becomes the new [Tinkerer]-[Boarder], gaining two new classes, and is called the star of Pallass.
Kevin builds the bicycle with Pelt and Hedault, with a budget granted by Lyonette and Selys.
The finished bicycle has a polished wooden frame, metal wheels and a wooden tire, with parts forged by Pelt.
Hedault says the whole device weighs six point eight pounds and can be made lighter.
Hedault says Miss Selys funded the project.
Khalid is a wiry young street boy with a burning courage, who kneels before the new Quarass in the mud-brick court.
Khalid swears to be the Quarass' strength and to do whatever else she asks, naming himself Khalid who has no last name.
Khalid has blood on his skin and clothes from where his arm bled.
Khalid tries to drink from his cup like Vaitsha and declares himself the Quarass' protector and dagger, saying she lives forever.
Khalid calls himself Khalid who has no other name in the Quarass' court.
The Quarass says Khalid is a young boy whose classes are hard to level so young, and he has begun training with the [First Warriors].
The Quarass says she expects Khalid to show her in time which class suits him and to become a champion like no other.
Kilkran is a former [Blacksmith] with a golden voice, a bald head and a full beard, which he shaves when a role demands it.
Kilkran is an [Actor] of the Players of Celum, a troupe over forty strong at the time.
Kilkran wears wigs, which Mrsha finds very adaptable, over his excellent bald head.
Kilkran sighs and drinks while Pralcem argues about the troupe's version of the classic plays.
Wesle laughs at Kilkran's ire over the lesser [Actors] in the troupe.
Kilkran plays King Duncan in Macbeth, and Emme thinks he can emote decently, while Wesle and Jasi have reached another level.
Kilkran and the other Players of Celum enter The Wandering Inn when the riots cancel the evening's play.
Kirana is the [Cook] in charge of feeding the Bushrangers' company, and the second manager of the home front after Paige.
Kirana has pretty much taken over household affairs, so Paige can work on more designs.
Kirana speaks sharply to a younger girl in Hindi, one of the languages of her nation.
Kirana and several of the girls from India joined the company about two months before that scene, and improved the living situation.
Kirana's group makes mint toothpaste that is better than the last batch.
Paige says Kirana is good but mostly bosses around the girls from her country, and suspects she has something on them.
Kirana helps hold the Centaur Hastel down during her birth, and is pale as ice afterwards.
Kirana serves dum aloo with rice and a steak dinner, with muffins Priya has baked.
Kirana turns the meat of giant snakes into something tasty.
Kissilt is a Drake student in Niers' strategy class at Wistram, and is described as surly and grumpy.
Kissilt has mild ice breath and pale white-purple scales.
Kissilt protests mildly when the Centaur Jekilt complains about the arrogance of young Humans and Drakes.
Niers notices Kissilt about to speak and warns him to think before reacting to Olesm Swifttail's idea.
Kissilt mentions that Garen Redfang was slain by the Gecko of Liscor, and Niers asks him to elaborate on Liscor's champion.
Feshi calls Kissilt an example of Drakes who hold a grudge forever.
Kissilt normally does not keep company with Marian and her group, given Umina's presence, and demands that Marian give him his money.
Kissilt bursts out in fury when Jekilt offers a trade of questions, saying he meant to ask a question about classes.
Foliana refuses to lend Kissilt her inkpot, saying he has been rude to her and must amend his ways.
Foliana puts Kissilt's own inkpot back in his bag, and later his inkpot goes missing again at his desk.
Niers places Kissilt on a team as the resident Drake, to partner with Illial and Leondir.
Kissilt enjoys a moment and puts an arm around Wil and Cameral, who edge away.
Klbkch is an Antinium who introduces himself to Erin Solstice as a Senior Guardsman in the employ of the city of Liscor, partner to the Drake Relc.

Klbkch is a giant ant-like being with large black bulbous eyes, a dark brown chitinous body, a pair of swords at his sides, a huge abdomen, two long pincers by his mouth and, in his first body, four arms.
Relc names Klbkch as a [Swordslayer] with some levels in [Guardsman], fewer than in his primary class.
Klbkch is known as "Klbkch of the Free Antinium" and, in the oldest history, as Klbkch the Slayer of the Antinium Wars, one of the Centenium.
Klbkch dies defending Erin from Goblins in Book 1, is reborn in a new two-armed body through the Rite of Anastases, and afterwards rises to the rank of Revalantor of the Free Antinium.
Klbkch has compound eyes, brown and fractal like an ant's, which Erin finds creepy but decides she can trust.
In his first body Klbkch fights with two swords and two small daggers, one in each of his four hands.
Klbkch carries two swords at his waist and draws two daggers with his lower set of hands when he expects a fight.
Klbkch stands still to rest, which Relc calls his "creepy standing hibernation thing"; Klbkch agrees that it is very restful.

Among his own kind Klbkch has no name that can be expressed in words; "Klbkch", and sometimes "Klb", is what members of other species call him and what he calls himself, because he thinks it important to have a name.
Klbkch values doing things properly, keeping good relations with other species and polite posture, and his thoughts repeatedly return to these ideas.
Klbkch's blood is green.
Klbkch's reborn body has only two arms and a slim, graceful build unlike a Worker's or a Soldier's, and he holds two swords.
Klbkch tells Erin the new body is swifter and more mobile, with anatomical changes not incorporated into other Antinium, and calls the older four-arm design inefficient.
Ceria Springwalker notes that she has never seen an Antinium with only two arms and takes it to mean he is a special leader, since the other Workers obey his commands without question.
Klbkch's Queen is still bothered that he has only two hands, but it was something he had requested.
Klbkch keeps his two silver swords at his side even inside the Hive.
Klbkch's office in the Hive is a small dirt room with a table, two chairs and a coatrack that holds only a single scarf.
Klbkch thinks he was made for war and not for kindness, a point Xrn presses on him.
Klbkch's full name is Klbkchhezeim; his Queen uses it when she addresses him.
Pawn refers to "the Revalantor" as the one who instructed the Workers to rebuild Erin's inn.
The Grand Queen and the Free Queen both address Klbkch as Klbkchhezeim.
When he introduces himself in Book 18 the narration lists his titles as Revalantor of the Free Antinium, the Centenium, Senior Guardsman and Klbkch the Slayer.
The Drakes regard Klbkch the Slayer as a known villain among them.
Klbkch is a Senior Guardsman of Liscor's City Watch, and the Watch's Captain sends him and Relc to check on smoke seen from the walls.
Klbkch signs himself out of the duty roster and adds Relc to the log, because Relc never signs out properly.
Klbkch is the fourth-highest-leveled [Guardsman] in Liscor.
Selys Shivertail says Klbkch was the fourth highest-level guardsman in the city and probably second to Relc in strength, ten levels behind him.
As a Senior Guardsman, Klbkch threatens a cheating Drake shopkeeper with an audit of income, unpaid taxes and inventory while Relc trashes the stall.
Klbkch turns in the Goblin Chieftain's head at the Adventurer's Guild; Selys says he told them Erin has no levels in a fighting class.
Klbkch tells Revi, after holding two blades at her throat, that he is a Senior Guardsman in the City Watch of Liscor, and announces that everyone present is under arrest.
Klbkch says the incident was not entirely Erin's fault and orders her inn placed under guard temporarily.
Wearing his [Guardsman]'s armor, Klbkch signs the roster sheets at the Watch barracks and goes on duty.
Zevara trusts Klbkch to check every inch of Liscor's walls before the rainy season.
Liscor has about thirty Senior Guards, a rank just below Watch Captain; Klbkch inclines his head to citizens and is liked for it.
Klbkch tells Gnoll [Guards] Tkrn and Jerci that he has [Detect Guilt] and a few other Skills, but that high-level criminals easily foil it.
Klbkch leads Junior Guardsman Tkrn and Junior Guardswoman Jerci on the patrol to catch the [Thief] who stole Erin's golden flowers.
From Tkrn's viewpoint, Klbkch was until recently the only Antinium who had a name or spoke, and the Watch's rules about Antinium said not to ask their names.
Klbkch arrives late from an incident in the Hives involving Face Stealer and takes charge of the guard line at the inn.
Klbkch tells Beilmark about a meeting between Bearclaw and Mister Soot about arming associates with wands and about Palt's dreamleaf, and advises that Zevara will not wish to fight Wistram over it.
Klbkch and Relc have been partners for nearly seven years on the Watch.
Klbkch proposes placing more Antinium in the City Watch and Zevara grants it; he leads fifteen Watch members into a brawl between Drake and Gnoll Guardsmen.
In Book 16 Klbkch lays his badge on Zevara's desk and takes leave, saying he has a decade's worth of time off saved up.
By Book 17 Klbkch has taken a vacation from the Watch.
After the Queen's Rite of Anastases, Klbkch tells Selys he is Klbkch of the Free Antinium and that he has returned from death.

Klbkch refuses the title of Prognugator, saying he took it only out of necessity during the attack and that Ksmvr resumes it; he says he is second only to the Queen and that a new position will be created.
Klbkch tells Erin he is no longer Prognugator but holds a similar position of command.
Klbkch is described as the newly reincarnated Revalantor of the Free Antinium, technically above the rank of Prognugator, able to ignore even his Queen's instructions given the nature of his duties.
Klbkch still obeys his Queen's orders in normal affairs, and she can question his actions much as he can question hers.
In Klbkch's own thought a Revalantor is a step above a Prognugator, and walks in a bubble of his own within the Hive.
Klbkch has been his Queen's eyes, ears and sword for decades, but as a Revalantor he should now report less and work with Pawn and the Individuals.
An in-world history says Klbkch the Slayer, Wrymvr the Deathless and the Small Queen Xrn were the only three of the six Prognugators sighted after the First Antinium War.
The same history says that, as of its writing, Klbkch is the only Prognugator confirmed still living and resides with the sixth Antinium Hive in Liscor.
Pawn describes Klbkch as the Revalantor who also acts as Prognugator, and says he drove the former Prognugator Ksmvr out of the Hive.
Pawn sees Klbkch seated at a wooden desk as the Revalantor and Prognugator of Liscor's Hive, whom the Queen told Pawn to report to about changes in his level or class.
Pawn knows Klbkch has friends in the Watch and is well liked even by the city's hostile residents, but believes he does not seem to like any of the Workers or Soldiers.
Pawn knows that Klbkch's blades have slain more Workers than any lone monster, because a Prognugator's duty is to lead in battle, oversee the Hive while the Queen is busy and kill Aberrations.

In Book 8 Klbkch stands before Zevara as the Revalantor of the Free Antinium of Liscor, without armor and with only twin silver swords at his waist; Zevara congratulates him on his promotion and he does not explain what the new rank means.

Klbkch's daily briefing as the Free Antinium's Revalantor covers the roles of spymaster, head of security, vice-ruler, steward, strategist, engineer and diplomat; the Free Queen is in charge but listens to him and he can overrule her if need be.
Klbkch has few information sources compared to Ressa, and wishes he had the statistics of the other five Hives, which are all in southern Izril and cut off from the Free Queen.
Klbkch reads numbers on casualties, wounded, income, levels gained by Individuals and tunnels built or collapsed as part of his daily briefing.
Klbkch is part of the Free Antinium but feels the fate of all six remaining Hives concerns him, and he prepares for worst cases.
Klbkch's mental link to the Hive's Soldiers is now faint where he once could read any Worker ten miles away.
Below ground Senior Guardsman Klbkch becomes Revalantor Klbkch, and he works as hard in the Hive as above it.
In Book 16 Klbkch threatens that no one will stop him from purging the Individuals, not even the Queen.
By Book 17 Xrn has changed the Free Antinium: Klbkch, who had been driven to a rage Erin had never seen, is no longer in charge of the Free Antinium.
[Detect Guilt] is a basic skill all guardsmen learn at level 15; Klbkch uses it to tell Pisces flatly "You are lying" and to arrest him.
Klbkch's high levels in [Guardsman] give him [Enhanced Movement], which turns several miles into a blur.
Klbkch tells Erin that [Tavern Brawling] and [Unerring Throw] are unusual for an [Innkeeper] but not unheard of.
Klbkch offers Erin a potion to pour over her wounded hand, and later pours one over her legs and makes her drink the rest.
Klbkch fights Pisces by standing in front of the door with swords drawn, so that he looks like a wall of blades.
Klbkch can use the monthly report to inform Olesm of significant changes concerning Workers outside the Hive, and says he will personally supervise them.
Ksmvr later reports that Klbkch estimated he could hold Relc off for five minutes and wound him seriously before dying, and had an even chance of killing Relc by sneak attack if ordered.

At Level 30, together with gaining [Swordslayer], Klbkch received a skill that deflects blows even from considerable force; he believes he once knocked aside a ballista bolt at point blank range with it.
Klbkch's Level 40 skill was named [Continuous Cut], with which he could strike down enemies so fast that he could eradicate entire battalions over a battle.

Klbkch tells Ryoka that he has reconfirmed the [Assassins] and [Scouts] sent by Lady Magnolia are hidden several miles east and have no listening artifacts or spells, and he senses no one within two hundred meters of the inn.
Klbkch can send silent messages to his Queen across a telepathic link.
Klbkch speaks to the Hive's Soldiers mentally and ordered Pawn to come by mental order.
Klbkch watches Drake tails and can interpret their movements almost as well as a Drake.
Klbkch's voice is amplified by a spell or Skill over a battlefield when he leads Antinium.
As of Book 14 Klbkch has not regained most of his Skills; he says the lost one was lost to him in the Rite of Anastases, and that Yellow Splatters has recovered his.
In Book 16 Klbkch learns [Skill - Recaptured Sublimity] after being beaten down in a fight with Relc, when a voice from within him speaks.
With [Skill - Recaptured Sublimity] Klbkch moves too fast for Relc's [Triple Thrust], beats Relc through the crowd into a wall, and fends off 4th Company when Wikir, Pielt, Vell and Embria join.
In Book 18 Klbkch carries a Ring of Metal, a Ring of Hops, a single-use Amulet of Dispel, backup daggers enchanted with [Ignition] and [Pain], and potions including healing and stamina.
Klbkch's [Recaptured Sublimity] has a twelve-hour cooldown that would kill him if used carelessly.
With the Skill Klbkch hops about six feet, as high as his ring allows, lands and vanishes, cutting off an arm and cracking a chest among the Sword Prognugators.
Klbkch takes a jug of Rxlvn and a pepperoni pizza from his bag of holding as a gift for Wrymvr.
Klbkch is a [Swordslayer] with levels in [Guardsman]; the Guardsman levels are fewer than those in his primary class.
After the Rite of Anastases Klbkch has lost ten levels in every class.
Klbkch is a Level 21 [Swordslayer], a Level 18 [Commander], a Level 11 [Diplomat] and a Level 14 [Assassin].
Klbkch remembers a time before he had [Commander] or [Diplomat] levels, when he was a Level 44 [Swordslayer] and a Level 26 [Assassin], not yet a Prognugator.
Klbkch has already regained five of his ten lost levels by fending off monster attacks on the Hive; he says only that the Hive has suffered monster attacks.
Klbkch tells Ryoka that his current and peak levels are secret information and gives the same numbers.
Klbkch tells Ryoka he loses ten levels from his classes each time his Queen resurrects him, and that he has died many times.
Klbkch says he was named Klbkch the Slayer, slain in battle by General Sserys, and has never regained his former levels.
Klbkch is described as weak after losing his levels, and in Book 5 it is only a dream for him to regain his former strength.
In Book 8 Klbkch says his form is stronger than his old one but that he has still yet to regain the rest of his lost levels.
Klbkch holds the tertiary class [Diplomat] at Level 11, which no one including his Queen knows about, and uses its Level 10 Skill [Reassuring Presence] every day.
Klbkch has used [Reassuring Presence] for ten years, on Erin among others, and thinks it may account for much of his reputation in Liscor.
Klbkch has come to understand that his tertiary classes are inhibiting him from leveling, which he learned in conversation with Ryoka.
In Book 14 Klbkch calls his own leveling slow and mixed, and thinks that his number of classes may be inefficient.
Relc and Klbkch are partners on the Watch and take meals and drinks together.
Klbkch punches the drunk Relc twice after he boasts in a bar about Erin and the Goblin Chieftain, and estimates his own standing in the city and Guard has fallen for it.
Relc says Klbkch was different, had a name, and was the only Antinium he knew with a level above 10.
Klbkch tells Erin he has been Relc's partner for years, that he considers himself Relc's friend, and that he does not understand how he came to be one.
In Book 16 Relc blocks the way as Klbkch storms toward the inn and asks him to come for a drink; Klbkch demands he move aside.
Relc and Jeiss bring Klbkch to Wishdrinks and treat him as if at a wake because Relc believes Klbkch may lack genitalia; Klbkch ends up asking whether he is being fired.
Olesm badgers Relc and Klbkch into helping Krshia roll ale kegs up to the inn.
Klbkch dresses with a goat-hair beard and a belly slap for Relc's Santa scheme and they catch two Drake burglars to a crowd's applause.
Klbkch apologises to Rags for his partner and says Relc fought in the Goblin Wars and thinks of Goblins as enemies.
Klbkch tells Relc not to kill Rags because Erin cares for the Goblins and has been deemed important to the Hive.

Klbkch tells Relc in Book 16 that the Individuals are disobeying his orders and that Antinium do not break rules; Relc offers a pep talk and notes that Zevara has given Klbkch more commendations than anyone.
Relc says that Captain Z told him to write it down if Klbkch ever talked about his Hive, though he had not done so in a decade.
Relc hits Klbkch when he beats Bird, saying he meant to hit harder, and Klbkch tells Relc to stay out of it.

Klbkch deduces that Erin is not from this world, citing her curiosity about levels, her arrival and the unknown nation 'Michigan', and that no human would weep for a Goblin; Erin confirms she is from another world.
Selys and Zevara cannot read Antinium expressions, unlike Erin, Lyonette and Relc, so Klbkch's calm front holds with them.
Klbkch decides the Others must learn of a human named Erin Solstice, because she is unique.
Klbkch leaves forty silver coins as the bounty for destroying a Goblin Chieftain, with a signed note saying he is not fluent in "your script".
Klbkch returns Erin's wager of three gold coins and some copper and silver after the stall dispute.
Klbkch tells Erin she may enforce law inside her own establishment as she chooses.
Klbkch pays Erin for the Antinium meal with a bag of silver and gold and buys a jar of acid flies for a gold coin.
Klbkch beheads the Goblin leader, kills more Goblins and heals Erin with a potion, half drunk and half splashed on her legs.
Klbkch tells his Queen the glass windows are goodwill, saying the Hive needs Erin far more than she needs them.
Klbkch knows Erin is among the best chess players from her world and has told no one, even his Queen; he treats it as his secret.
Klbkch has not told Erin that he lies to his Queen about her origin because of the dangers, and thinks she cannot keep a secret.
Klbkch tells Ryoka that Erin Solstice is "everything" and must survive to help change the Antinium from within.
Klbkch tells Erin the Antinium want "to live", and that other Queens either prepare for war or ally against a "true enemy".
Klbkch notes that Erin is no longer just his friend and the knowledge is slightly painful, as he plays chess with her at a party.
Klbkch tells Xrn that the Individuals all stem from one person, a young human girl named Erin Solstice who comes from another world.

Klbkch quotes Erin 328 gold for a third floor and expansion, notes six silver of every twenty goes to Liscor as a non-negotiable tax, and says a quality new home would cost around two hundred gold and each window about eight.
Klbkch refuses to let Garry work for Erin because the Queen is partial to Garry's cooking, and says the same of Anand, Belgrade and Pawn.
Klbkch says Bird would trade his life for Erin's as a matter of duty and that he would be willing to make the same trade.
Klbkch tells Erin he agreed to take Pawn's unit off combat duty after she visited him.
Klbkch agrees to send a few Workers to rebuild the inn for a fee, noting lumber is an issue.
Klbkch tells Erin and Octavia that Liscorian law requires the city to repay items used in its defence, and that Erin may claim for her inn and magical door.
Klbkch tells Erin he could arrest the Drake hecklers only for tangible interference, and that Zevara would likely refuse a guard detail since Erin lives outside Liscor and pays no taxes.
Klbkch offers Erin a secret squad of Painted Soldiers led by Pawn, plus bow-armed Workers, to guard her inn overnight for free, as an act of friendship and practicality.
Klbkch asks Erin whether Acid Flies are on her menu and eventually tries a pancake despite saying he is allergic to wheat-based products.
Klbkch says he considers Erin his friend but her friends are not his.
Klbkch dodges Erin's punches when she tries to stop him from hitting Bird.
In Book 17 Xrn relays Klbkch's advice to give Erin no vaults of treasure or overt aid and to let Erin be Erin.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch's Queen calls him Klbkchhezeim and they have been a pair for longer than she remembers; she thinks he sometimes irritates her.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: The Queen knows he is keeping a secret about Erin from her but does not mind, because he is loyal.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch believes in his Queen's mission of creating Individuals and wants her to see other species as people, not pawns.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch tells Erin his Queen does not know friendship, not even with him: "What we have is different."

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch says his Queen is the lightest Queen on Izril and the only one able to relocate to Liscor.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch tells the Free Queen that if she orders him to take Liscor, he will, because he is Klbkchhezeim of the Centenium before anything else.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch asks the Free Queen to give Garry a day off, saying it may assist with his leveling; she agrees.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch tells the Free Queen the Hives may soon move.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch tells Xrn that Pawn's walk is not the same as that of the Antinium of old; Xrn says it is exactly the same.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Xrn calls Klbkch a fool, saying she has hit him with her staff many times and that he only understands war.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch and Xrn are both Centenium who knew each other and fought together long before the Wars.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch believed Xrn's visit was to order him back to the Grand Queen.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch agrees to Xrn's plan, saying "We will return", and thinks of Ryoka as one possible ally.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch knows Xrn is the only living Antinium who casts spells.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch tells Xrn to enact the Rite of Anastases if he dies during the Second Antinium War.

section: The Queen, Xrn and the Centenium
text: Klbkch did not weep at Zel's death but reports it flatly to the Grand Queen, who answers "Good".
Klbkch forbids Pawn to speak of Gods, his class or Skills to Workers or Individuals, though Pawn realises Soldiers are not covered.
Klbkch tells Pawn that Erin is safe with Ryoka but cannot return yet because of the Goblins.
Klbkch says Pawn has only a single Skill in the [Tactician] class and is too valuable to risk in battle.
Klbkch has Pawn take twenty Soldiers on patrols to gain trophies and goodwill, raises his stipend, and asks why Pawn paints the Soldiers.
Klbkch tells Bird, Pawn, Belgrade, Garry and Anand that delegations from other Hives arrive that day and that Pawn must not volunteer his [Acolyte] class.
Pawn steps in front of Klbkch with twenty Soldiers at his back; Klbkch's raised sword stops, and Zevara's guards and Relc break up the standoff with Zel.
Klbkch tells Pawn the dungeon is "waking up" and the Hive loses more Antinium than it produces.
Klbkch orders Pawn to select one hundred Soldiers and report to Belgrade at noon the next day.
Klbkch heals himself with a nearly empty healing potion in the Hive with twenty injured Soldiers around him.
Klbkch offers to petition the Queen to perform the Rite of Anastases on Yellow Splatters; Pawn refuses and says "He's free".
Klbkch removes Pawn's budget temporarily.
Klbkch gives Pawn's unit scheduled downtime and orders him to turn it into a fighting force.
Klbkch tells Yellow Splatters that the Free Queen modified his body for improved musculature, that he lost ten levels in resurrection, and that he is unique.
Klbkch allows a rotation of fifty Soldiers aboveground and grants a stipend of four silver and six copper per Soldier or Worker.
Klbkch tells Anand and Yellow Splatters the Free Queen will treat them as Prognugators, trained in the manner of Prognugators of old.
Klbkch refuses Anand's request to call him Father: Anand says Erin told him Klbkch is like a father, and Klbkch simply says "No".
Klbkch tells Anand "Well done" and later repeats it, acknowledging his excellent work.
When Pawn points out Erin was told of Gods, Klbkch answers that Erin is different but Pawn is expendable.
Klbkch strikes Bird twice, cracking his carapace, saying he is a fool who disobeyed orders, and orders the Antinium back to the Hive without Bird, threatening to kill him if he enters Pallass again.
Klbkch is fought by Gazi and knocked down with the pommel of her sword.
Klbkch tells Ryoka that his Queen is not aware that Ryoka and Erin come from another world and that he will lie to her Queen.
Klbkch has never met Magnolia Reinhart in person, though he is aware of her accomplishments.
Magnolia says she met Klbkch the Slayer for one brief moment during the Second Antinium War.
Zel Shivertail treats Klbkch with open hostility and refuses to pretend to like him, but keeps the truce; Klbkch does not wish to engage in hostilities.
Zel Shivertail and Klbkch fought each other right after the victory over Az'kerash; Klbkch says he stabbed Zel in the chest and Zel tore off Klbkch's arm.
Klbkch tells the Hives he will lead one hundred and fifty Soldiers and twice as many Workers to Esthelm; Tersk follows to observe and Xrn goes with him, while Pivr refuses.
Klbkch gives Pivr, called the other Revalantor, a look showing he is not worth the syllables in his name.
Klbkch visits the inn to improve his relationship with Erin, finds Goblins fleeing, and finds Erin barely breathing after the Chieftain's attack.
Klbkch buries the Chieftain's body far from the inn to prevent chance reanimation.
Klbkch delivers the Chieftain's head in a bag made from Erin's shopping bag through Liscor's western gates.
Klbkch bangs his head with a hand after a Designated Worker's request, then goes to make an urgent report to his Queen and leaves the city with the Worker.
Klbkch holds the line for Erin against about forty Goblins, is stabbed from behind, and ends kneeling with nine Goblins circling him.
Klbkch collapses in a pool of green ichor, asks if Erin is safe, says his Queen's soldiers will come, and says "I will die free".
Erin carries the unmoving Klbkch toward Liscor using a fireman's carry.
Relc says Klbkch is dead; he was the only Antinium he had heard of with a level higher than 10.
Ksmvr introduces himself to Erin as Prognugator, not Klbkch, and Erin finds that it is not Klbkch, but it is.
Klbkch returns in a new two-armed body, drives off Skinner with his swords, saves Erin, and says the Antinium never truly die.
