Laken introduces himself as blind and trapped in another world where reality follows the rules of a game.
Laken says he has been in the world only about a month and a half and has gained a form of sight, found someone to love, and found something to fight for.
Laken says he is no hero with a sword, but can be smart and pick his battles, and has friends and a class.
Laken says he came to Invrisil for the people under his protection as an [Emperor].
Laken guesses that a thief robbing him used a Skill to pick out wealthy marks.
Laken answers Ryoka's German question about where he is from with "Aus San Francisco", and is relieved at "I am not alone."
Laken feels forelsket, the Norwegian word, towards Durene every time he touches her.
Laken tells Ryoka that he and Durene are a couple.
Laken says Durene nearly broke Ryoka's fingers when they shook hands and seems protective.
Reynold says Laken's presence felt like standing before Lady Reinhart or Lord Veltras only stronger, making him want to prostrate himself.
Ryoka sees that every eye in the room is drawn to Laken though he does nothing dramatic, and he seems taller than he is.
Laken hires the Celestial Trackers and the Windfrozen Riders at the Merchant's Guild, the only two teams that did not turn Gamel away or laugh at him.
Laken says he wants adventurers who will not look down on the villagers, and compares his test to a story of a [King] who disguised himself.
Laken tells Merec he wants the teams to escort the wagons and guard Riverfarm for at least a month.
Laken tells Merec that liars reveal themselves to him, but privately admits he cannot tell if someone lies and only lets others overthink.
Laken tells Ryoka he is twenty-four, and she remarks that he is part German.
Laken tells Ryoka "Ich bin ein [Kaiser]" to reveal that he is an Emperor, and she drops her iPhone in shock.
Laken tells Ryoka he has met the frost faeries and knighted a few, and that they either caused the avalanche or spared Durene's home.
Ryoka whispers to Laken in German that a God lives, and Laken calls this concerning but says Skills are essential against monsters.
Ryoka tells Laken that someone said a summoning spell in Rhir explains how they came to this world.
Laken takes Ryoka's iPhone and introduces himself to [BlackMage] as "L", from their world, after Ryoka curses the caller out.
BlackMage says the mages of Wistram want to find people from Earth across the world and bring them to Wistram.
Laken tells BlackMage to have Wistram broadcast "come home" in every language and ask Earth-only verification questions.
Laken warns BlackMage that an extremist or criminal from Earth may arrive, so the world will see a target on Wistram.
Laken ends the call, saying it is too risky and that he and Ryoka can only be contacted by chat.
Laken gives Durene her first Christmas present, a clumsily wrapped box that Gamel helped him buy, and she weeps.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken travels in a wagon back to Riverfarm with Durene and Gamel, escorted by the Windfrozen Riders, one of two Silver-rank teams he hired.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: The adventurers believe Laken is rumoured to be some sort of rich [Lord].

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken is a [Beast Tamer] and wonders whether he will command Frostwing once she flies.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken spent about a week in Invrisil buying supplies for Riverfarm and hiring flame mages to clear snow from the roads and two Silver-rank teams.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken says his sense is like a vision in the mind with outlines and expressions but no colour or detail, and calls it sight.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken says he claimed Riverfarm to save the village, and he can sense whatever land he possesses down to the smallest rock.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken's [Emperor] sense does not extend past the village limits, so he goes blind outside them.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken's Skill [Empire: Blessing of the Hearth] makes sleeping pleasant.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken tells Gamel that titles mean nothing to him and he wants to know how people feel about him, though he insists on respect.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken has not told the adventurers Odveig or Beniar that he is an [Emperor], and they react with astonishment when the villagers greet him.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken asks Durene to describe the adventurers' faces and watches Wiskeria's reaction, since he already has plans for her.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken sketches blueprints in dirt with Prost for a rebuilt village with combined fields and more houses.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken proposes building three houses first with the adventurers guarding, living off the supplies he brought from Invrisil.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken names Prost his [Steward], saying he has seen Prost change from refusing a half-Troll to calling him [Emperor].

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken tells Prost he could make him a [Lord], but that would be too many classes at once.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken says he made Durene a [Paladin] and now wants to arm her.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken halts a Mossbear with a shouted "Stop", then opens his eyes and uses [Intimidating Glare] to order it back to the forest.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken realises he did not know the Mossbear was coming, and that he needs to expand his claim over the unowned wilderness.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken invites the Windrest [Blacksmith] Helm to bring his people to Riverfarm, and tells Prost they will need more houses.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken tells the Windrest people they must obey him as their ruler while in his domain, and he promises to protect them.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Later, Laken gains [Emperor Level 10!], [Skill - Empire: Low-born Militias] and [Skill - Rallying Presence].

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken senses below ground and finds a rat tunnel two feet deep, and Prost's farmers and eight terrier dogs hunt the rats.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken reaches [Beast Tamer] Level 5 and then Level 7 with [Skill - Animals: Basic Command] after ordering rats out of the ground.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken finds his command does not work on every rat, and says Durene screamed when one ran up her leg.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken asks Wiskeria to teach magic to villagers with aptitude, and asks Beniar to take Durene personally as a sword student.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Wiskeria notes Durene has [Enhanced Strength] and could face a Hob with a sword.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken orders trainees to run six laps, do push-ups, sit-ups and burpees daily alongside training and their jobs.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken senses someone in his cottage and finds nobody, nothing missing, and Frostwing shrieking.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken takes Durene with a basket of dried fruit and meat to the Mossbear's cave to parley.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Windrest refugees (Book 5)
text: Laken stops the Mossbear with "Stop" at its cave, tells it he is no enemy, and befriends it.
Laken orders Odveig's Trackers to find the Goblins and Prost to build palisades, and bans leaving the village without escort.
Laken says he has worked on a way to see beyond the village that will take a few more days.
Laken touches a dead Goblin, which feels like a dead child to him, and he has never seen colours such as its green skin.
Laken tells doubters that he has known blind painters and singers, and that a blind man climbed the world's highest mountain.
Laken tells Rehanna to "Kneel" while walking away, and is troubled afterwards by his own thought of crushing her.
Laken suspects Wiskeria of sabotage and guesses she serves Lady Magnolia Reinhart, who Ryoka says sent [Assassins] after her.
Odveig tells Laken she is a spy for Lady Magnolia, speaking in an elegant voice unlike her accented one.
Laken calls himself an idiot for panicking and driving Odveig away instead of watching her.
Laken describes three Goblin attacks by Day 69 that left only wounded, with Wiskeria in charge and their relationship strained.
Laken's sixth marker opens his senses over a hexagon around Riverfarm, revealing the forest, the sleeping Mossbear and hidden Goblins.
Laken uses "Stop" on a Goblin archer and a Hobgoblin, but it works only partly and fades as they brace.
Laken tells his council the Goblins are coming and that he tipped them off.
Laken tells Wiskeria he was not born an [Emperor] but became one when he met Durene, inspired by a story of an Emperor without a crown.
Laken names the dying villagers Calop and Fulca as his subjects whom he saved.
Laken commands the mortally wounded Gamel to stand and fight, saying he does not give him permission to die.
Laken rallies the villagers of Riverfarm and Windrest, saying their fates and his burn together.
Laken gains [Emperor Level 15!], [Skill - Empire: Art of the Builder] and [Skill - Undying Loyalty].
Laken offers Wiskeria the post of [General], and she accepts by taking his hand.
Laken tells Wiskeria he can give away only a limited number of positions as an [Emperor].
Laken plans to make Gamel his [Knight] and to have Wiskeria offer Beniar the rank of [Captain].
Laken theorises that [General], [Steward] and [Paladin] are rare classes, stronger than normal because they are more important.
Laken tells Durene that a strange informant he met in Invrisil gave him advice such as Prost as [Steward], Wiskeria as [General], and the markers.
Laken calls himself ruler of Riverfarm and sovereign lord of Windrest, Tunslaven, Kiquel and the surrounding areas, and says some call this the Unseen Empire.
Laken's [Emperor] senses show him Goblins attacking wagons while he is miles away.
Laken rides the docile Mossbear as a mobile throne and feels like a satire of a world leader on it.
Laken is a Level 9 [Beast Tamer] and has [Lesser Bond: Unnamed Mossbear], and Frostwing, a blue bird, lands on his armguard.
Laken has Jelov carve totem markers eight feet tall with the Eye of Providence, and the markers blur if they stand too far apart.
Laken has extended the markers toward Trottvisk and Acran and wants more at Kiquel's fork and a northern pond.
Laken still lives in Durene's cottage, and the villagers approve of his relationship with her and give them space.
Laken has dubbed [Knights] with their consent, including Gamel, and could dub about ten more.
Laken has given away most of his Lord and Lady titles to save his village, including [Baronesses] for the Frost Faeries.
Laken trusts Wiskeria after it was revealed that Odveig was the spy and Wiskeria was loyal.
Laken sends Lady Rie a message spell offering her the gift of swords as a battle looms.
Laken says "Kneel" and "Look this way" to direct the fight, and Beniar kills the Goblin [Shaman].
Laken's side numbers over four hundred soldiers including a levy.
Soldiers and villagers shout "The Emperor of Beasts" at Laken after the battle.
Later, Laken reaches [Emperor Level 19!] and gains [Skill - Imperial Levy] and [Skill - Empire: Darksky Riders].
Laken is confused by news of Zel's alliance until Lady Rie explains the politics of Drakes and Humans.
Laken describes himself as a blind [Emperor] of the Unseen Empire and Protector of Durene's Cottage, sovereign of Riverfarm, Windrest, Tunslaven and Kiquel.
Laken says it feels like only yesterday that he was a normal young man in San Francisco, and he sometimes forgets what his friends' voices sound like.
Laken claimed the land around the village and marked it with totems at the borders of his empire, so he can see the area when he concentrates.
Laken's friend Zoe described the game Age of Empires II to him, and he draws on it for planning his empire.
Laken receives [Lesser Bond: Bismarck] after naming his Mossbear, whom he tamed by feeding him and having him fight beside his people.
Laken uses [Blessing of the Hearth] to give his people a comfortable night's sleep even on the floor.
Laken uses [Imperial Levy] to request soldiers from other towns and cities when large threats appear.
Laken suspects his [King's Bounty] Skill is why Lady Rie's fortune became part of the Unseen Empire, and he worries how to repay her.
Laken has told only Durene that he is from Earth, and considers telling Wiskeria although Ryoka would object.
Laken is training [Engineers], with [Tinkerers] he hopes will level up by building war chariots or an irrigation system.
Laken wants his people to be free to become [Alchemists], [Blacksmiths] or [Scribes], and plans large communal fields so few [Farmers] are needed.
Laken hears Lady Rie say that she is sending Sacra, and corrects his own thought to Odveig.
Laken lies to Lady Rie about his past, saying his blindness explains his ignorance of etiquette, to hide that he is from another world.
Laken finds he cannot judge a fork's quality by touch alone and feels his blindness is a hindrance in hosting.
Laken realises that Lady Magnolia's invitation was a trap forcing him to play the nobles' game, and refuses a helmet for Durene.
Laken has the tables set in a meadow past the new farmland and serves a standing feast with trebuchet test-firings.
Laken has Durene sit at the head table in a suit instead of a dress, over Lady Rie's objections.
Laken orders a notice read on the main roads that anyone abusing another person on his lands will be shot and executed.
Laken asks the nobles to bring food, sweets, pudding and entertainers such as [Jugglers] and [Bards] as their gift instead of money.
Laken sits silent before two feuding builders, Horst and Wellim, then ends their feud within fifteen minutes.
Laken's phone is dead, and he recalls Ryoka saying a [Repair] spell can charge it.
Laken believes his dreamed voices are real memories that become reality as he remembers them.
Laken rides Bismarck to meet the nobles and greets them as "Laken Godart" with no titles.
Laken introduces himself to arriving nobles as Laken Godart, Emperor of Riverfarm, and says Bismarck is not dangerous.
Lady Bevia says Laken is the first [Emperor] to appear on Izril in over a thousand years.
Andres reports that Laken is blind yet sees everything, commands beasts, has a half-Giant bodyguard and a [Witch] for a [General].
Andres repeats a rumour that Laken bought supplies in Invrisil with gems and gold, and some call him an exile from Chandrar.
Laken warns the nobles that the fair folk are neither enemies nor friends and do not answer to him despite their titles.
Laken tells Lady Rie the fae obey bargains and do not lie but twist the truth, hate cold iron, and offer gold that is probably flowers.
Laken perceives colour for the first time through the fae, hearing "green" and later blue, though he has never seen colour.
Laken introduces Durene to Lady Bevia as his consort.
Laken offers to swear on a truth gem to Lady Bevia that he has no intention of taking her lands or any other.
Lady Bethal tells Laken he passed Magnolia's test, and says Magnolia must be sure of her friends and enemies.
Laken has recreated treats from home, including Franzbrötchen and cookies, with his [Cooks] and [Bakers].
Laken notes that the cookies are the first food from home he has recreated, and Durene has never had such a treat.
Laken learns from Lady Rie's map that flags mark cities allied to him and round stones mark cities that boycott him.
Lady Rie says the nobles, including Lord Tourant, may be working through hostile cities to pressure Laken's economy.
Laken learns Rie can contact all larger cities by message spell, though small towns need a capable [Mage].
Laken believes Skills make people rely on instinct, so they never write down knowledge and the world's technology does not advance.
Laken tells Durene to teach math, reading, writing and blueprints so anyone can build trebuchets and gain the [Engineer] class.
Laken asks the nobles to send their surplus people to Riverfarm, and they agree.
Laken senses many presences approaching, swears in German, and calls only Wiskeria and Beniar.
Laken says that someone lied to him and that the plan will not change, as he feels hate for the first time.
Laken tells the nobles that an army of about eight thousand Goblins is camped forty-two miles north of Riverfarm.
Laken tells Lord Tourant that the Goblin Lord sent the army, which destroyed a local army from Filk two days before.
Laken says a mobile force of about six hundred raided the Goblin camp, killing at least a thousand with under a hundred casualties.
Laken tells Durene the nobles are now stuck in Riverfarm and that the cities must also deal with the Goblins.
Laken swears to slaughter the Goblins with traps and poison, whatever he must use.
Laken directs Wiskeria's raids through Nesor's message spells, while Durene marches with the levied main army.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken loses sight of the Goblin-held city, which is not his land, and loses markers to Goblin axes.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken orders guards on the markers and more carved by Jelov to keep a field of vision around the city.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken orders the Goblins surrounded and not allowed to escape, and asks Lady Rie to have Wiskeria keep Durene safe.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken watches Durene help load the first trebuchet as the siege begins.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken senses only the war camp by one marker as the network of totems collapses under Goblin raids.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken orders Wiskeria to keep bombarding and to send Sir Kerrig to Riverfarm with a small escort.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken recalls tipping off a city about a tribe of Goblins and begins to suspect the Filk army was chasing them.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken first hears Rags's voice and is shocked that the Goblin Chieftain is a child.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken tells Rags that a special [Emperor] Skill lets him see.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken tells Rags there will be no peace, because the armies already fought on someone's order.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken says he opens his eyes only briefly because a blind man's stare unsettles others until he cannot help blinking.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken reasons that a fake message spell is easy to send, wishes he had set a password, and recalls a friend's warning about spies.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken sees the pattern of destroyed markers lead to Riverfarm and tells Sir Kerrig he was followed by the Goblins.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken orders the Goblins taken and killed.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Rags's crossbow bolt grazes Laken's left cheek after Gamel knocks him down, and her second bolt kills a [Mage].

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken orders soldiers to chase the escaping Goblin Chieftain, and Lord Tyrion Veltras countermands him.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken says no noble leaves Riverfarm until questioned over who ordered his [General] to attack and who impersonated his mage.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken asks Prost for an axe, saying he might execute the criminal on the spot.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Wiskeria says Laken left Riverfarm two days earlier with an escort, after a deal with Lord Tyrion Veltras.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Wiskeria says Laken left with Gamel, Tessia and over thirty villagers, and would not say what the deal was for.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken is presented to Lady Ieka and others as [Emperor] Laken Godart of Riverfarm.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken says "Heel" to Lord Gralton and pins him with an aura, and Gralton laughs that he is an [Emperor].

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken says he taught his [Engineers] to build trebuchets, of which Riverfarm has thirteen with eight tested.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Tyrion says he has conscripted craftsmen to have at least twenty trebuchets by Liscor, and forty if possible.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken's [Emperor] senses are gone on the march because he owns none of the land, working only in his tent with Jelov's totems.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken reflects that he left Riverfarm to oversee the engineers, which he suspects was Tyrion's political move.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Gamel serves as Laken's bodyguard, manservant and [Knight].

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken tells Gamel that ordering poison gas on the Goblins and Tyrion's hunt place them on the wrong side of history.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken offers to help Yitton rescue his children, and Gralton grins at the idea.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken says Wiskeria's mobile force and Tyrion's march killed Goblins, and he regrets ordering poison gas.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: A volley of trebuchets Laken oversees lands on the back of the Goblin Lord's army, and Laken claims they misfired.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken walks the battlefield by night asking what he has done, with Gamel following him.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken kneels by a dying Goblin, apologises, whispers "Live", and has Gamel leave a healing potion.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken claims a few hundred Goblin prisoners and forbids soldiers, nobles or adventurers from harming them.

section: The Goblin war and Lord Tyrion (Book 8-9)
text: Laken takes the Goblin prisoners north with Yitton and Gralton toward his estates.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Later, someone says Laken went to Liscor with the army, the trebuchets, Tessia and the engineers, and holds hundreds of Goblins.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken tells Durene he loves her, is sending her the only aid he can, and will be back soon.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Durene says Laken used poison gas in surprise attacks, and Ryoka notes he took the trebuchets to attack Liscor.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken rides in the supply wagon, and Gamel, whose fiancee is Tessia, serves as his aide.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken gets a message about Rehanna's cloth changeling, and Yitton says the [Witch] must be at least Level 40.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken orders a message to Riverfarm that no one may strike a deal with Belavierr, with evidence gathered for a trial he will preside over.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken orders that Rehanna be shown every kindness and her baby not taken away.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken says Riverfarm feels hot to him, as if something hot is coming on the wind.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken asks Gralton to ride ahead toward his lands if things get worse.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken praises the [Witch] Hedag's act, which Yitton calls illegal, and says he would change the law to allow it.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken senses a blazing beacon of light from Riverfarm for the first time and sends Gralton to bring his army.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken tells Yitton the Order of Seasons sent someone and Belavierr is in Riverfarm too.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Yitton orders the caravan to push through the night to reach Riverfarm in five days.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken sends word that he could not find the [Witch Hunters] who attacked Ryoka and repeats his orders about Belavierr and Rehanna.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken sends a message that he cannot find the hunter on his lands, but senses a winged Drake [Merchant] with scrolls.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken tells Prost to retreat to the fields as a fire sweeps toward Riverfarm, and says to tell Durene he loves her.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Later, Laken returns to Riverfarm the next day and kisses Durene before the villagers.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Later, Laken reaches [Emperor Level 20!] and gains [Skill - Group: Surge of Inspiration] and [Skill - Empire: Fields of Bounty].

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken tells Councilwoman Beatica of Lancrel that her former station gives her no authority and that Lancrel's people are welcome as citizens.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken introduces Prost as his [Steward], Lady Rie as Prost's counterpart, Gamel as his aide and [Knight], and Durene as his consort and [Paladin].

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken names Mister Ram his [Head Farmer] and Forewoman Beycalt his [Construction Supervisor] as promotions.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken orders deer hunted eight miles north, refugee groups invited in, and fifty-eight burned totems replaced.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken draws a line in the dirt giving the Goblins the land beyond it, with his laws applying on his side.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken leaves the Goblins tools, food for a week and a crate with an iPhone on top.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken tells Ryoka that in early spring he summoned the fae and Ivolethe said to tell Ryoka she is alive.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken tells Ryoka that Ivolethe will never see her in this world, as a punishment.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Laken is blind to the Goblins' territory in Book 15 because he gave away that land.

section: Return to Riverfarm and the Goblin line (Book 12-15)
text: Pebblesnatch sees Laken drag his white cane through the dirt to mark the border and leave supply crates and the iPhone.
An Invrisil speaker recalls that two Silver-rank teams went with Laken to his lands around mid-winter and stayed.
Laken has a request posted seeking a Gold-rank or high Silver-rank team on a long-term contract.
Laken senses the strengths of individual people with what Lady Rie calls an aura-sense.
Laken can sense buried things down to about a hundred feet, at best when standing directly above.
Laken finds a buried structure about eighty feet down, groundwater four hundred paces away, and a cave with ore.
Laken locates clay for [Potters], Rock Mite tunnels and alchemical plants for Wiskeria.
Laken senses a Creler nest about thirty feet down with at least two hundred young, fourteen moving.
Laken's adventurers-wanted notice offers minimal weekly pay, a share of treasure, and free food and lodging.
Laken tells Captain Halrac that no other Gold-rank team has answered his request.
Laken's Mossbear Bismarck, with Frostwing on his back, is still not housebroken.
Laken tells Revi he does not intend to kill the Goblins, because not all Goblins are monsters.
Laken tracks fifteen fleeing Crelers and their eggs with his sense.
Laken is a debtor to Ryoka and prepares Riverfarm for her party's guests.
Laken calls his sense "landsense", which Durene calls [Emperor]-sense; he reads postures but not faces or colours.
Laken rules some Riverfarm streets "scare zones" at night and asks Hedag to speak to Oliyaya.
Laken recognises egg-drop soup from the Goblins' cooking and says he has not heard of rice.
Laken's rule is that a Goblin caught stealing is ransomed at their body weight in ore.
Laken suspects that Rie tried to poison Lady Bethal Walchais and sent Wiskeria against the Goblins, per Ryoka's supposition.
Laken rebukes Rie for not briefing him on a matter among the Five Families and orders that anything of note in Izril be directed to him.
Laken meets the Witches Eloise and Mavika privately, and Mavika asks if he sensed the malice from Lady Rie.
Laken ranks Eloise as his most knowledgeable and trustworthy advisor, above Rie.
Laken agrees to let Eloise decipher the poison on Lord Hethon and Lord Sammial.
Eloise asks the Unseen Empire to declare itself beneficiary of Witches and to grant them land, perhaps a small forest.
Laken promises Mavika that no one will be killed on his lands without him doing everything to stop it.
Laken tests Rie with a story about a ritual while Typhenous tugs his beard to signal her truthfulness.
Laken says he gained Skills after Sacra that help him judge truthfulness.
Laken plans to tell Lord Veltras the cure once found, since the Circle of Thorns should not be made an enemy yet.
Lasc is the [Storm Captain] and captain of the ship The Emerald Signet.
Lasc fights with a shortsword in his right hand and a metal gauntlet on his left.
Lasc says he would rather meet a storm than a monster, and a monster rather than a [Pirate] ship.
Lasc calls the Drowned Folk saltsucking bastards and says he will be grateful if they do not see a Drowned Ship on the errand.
Lasc parries Venaz's thrusts with his shortsword and strikes him across the face twice with his left hand so fast that the Minotaur cannot pull his head back.
Lasc strikes Venaz twenty times before landing from a leap, with a Skill-fast left hand.
Lasc lays Venaz out unconscious with his fist in a duel on the deck, and the sailors and students roar in amazement.
Lasc tells Merrik and Peki that at sea he would dump them in the water, since there is no sense fighting folks who cannot swim in armor or with feathers.
Lasc offers to use a [Storm Captain]'s first and last Skill at Lord Kallinad's order, calling it an act of desperation that could sink them all.
Lasc calls a storm that obeys no one, a terrible [Storm Captain]'s Skill of last resort that can crack a ship like The Emerald Signet in a moment.
A [Storm Sailor] is blown over the sides in the storm and cannot be found.
Lasc stays at the helm, navigating the ship and refusing to budge as the waves shake it.
Begal says old Lasc took Inky on as a crew member for the trip because she is a [Storm Sailor].
Lasc commands his repaired ship while coordinating the loading of cargo and people, with Inky as Second Mate.

Lasc tells Inky that until the ship is re-enchanted and the crew up to snuff, he does not want complaints, and that the alternative is dancing with Lord Seagrass, the Undersea Crews and half the [Pirates] in the sea.
Lasc ties himself to the wheel and fights the storm to reach the Isle of Mages, telling Inky they never had a choice.
Lasica Feltail is a middle-aged female Drake with bright purple scales, and she introduces Rufelt as her husband.
Lasica is a [Chef] who owns the kitchen of Tails and Scales, the Pallass bar that Rufelt runs, in a partnership with him.
Lasica says she and Rufelt both hold rare versions of their classes, the kind a person only gets past Level 30.
Lasica is known for making food that makes people shed weight, or gives them energy all day.
Lasica and Rufelt serve Erin a [Comfort Food] dish and a blue swirling drink that lifts her mood.
Lasica laughs and pats Erin's back as she chokes on the floating Dwarfrain drink.
Lasica advises Erin to stock food for months, and to invest in runes of preservation.
Lasica explains that runes of preservation do not stop insects, so contaminated food can stay preserved.
Lasica advises cultivating friends and not turning down a good opportunity, saying she and Rufelt have a highly-leveled friend in Baleros.
Lasica warns Erin never to mention her [Field of Preservation] again, as people would target her for it.
Lasica says she and Rufelt belong to the Unitail group, which wants to vote out the Protectorate and make Pallass more open.
Lasica says she and Rufelt back [Senators] so that they vote the way the two want.
Lasica objects that the Protectorate does not support free trade, and says they disagreed with how it handled the Siege of Liscor.
Lasica reacts that Pallass tax money funding Liscor would not be popular once it got out.
Lasica tells Erin that she and Rufelt guessed that Erin was steering them, and that Grimalkin's students rank above Wistram graduates.
Lasica says she already knows all of Erin's recipes, even mayonnaise.
Lasica remarks to Rufelt that Erin's circle are all very young, with no couples besides Jelaqua and Maughin.
Lasica and Rufelt dance together to an invisible cello, and the rest of the inn follows with many pairs.
Lasica proposes visiting the bazaar the next day for fertility spells, telling Rufelt it is time.
Lasica tells a hooded Drake she was not aware adoption was an issue, and mentions alchemists and magical items in Pallass.
Lasica tells Erin she recommended Pallass Hunting to keep her out of trouble, and is acerbic when Erin lands in jail.
Lasica is not allowed alcohol and is fussed over by Rufelt, which makes Erin suspect something is up.
Lasica reveals she is only a few weeks into a pregnancy, using charms for interspecies couples.
Lasica carries the baby, and glares at Rufelt for treating her like glass.
Lasica serves Chaldion and Grimalkin sushi, saying Erin calls it that though it is a Dullahan and Drathian dish.
Lasica says Erin has names for everything, and Erin is taking lessons from her.
Lasica agrees to ask a friend in Baleros for the recipe for chocolate after Lyonette's note.
Lasica buys eight jars of fish sauce, and tells Erin that one can hire specialists rather than do it oneself.
Lasica says she is about two months into her pregnancy, using a fertility spell tweaked for cross-species pregnancies, which she bought from Wistram.
Lasica tells Ekirra's mother the pregnancy is her first, and that Rufelt is just being protective.
Lasica is pregnant and the whole floor has heard, with Rufelt overprotective and smacking anyone who brings alcohol near her.
Lasica tells Grimalkin that Lady Pryde's lifting lists are her way of showing off, and says he should take the interest as a compliment.
Leafarmor is a female Hobgoblin and a loyal Redfang warrior, whose name Pebblesnatch learns from another Goblin.
Leafarmor once made armor out of leaves after being separated from her tribe in a bad attack and wounded.
Leafarmor killed her way back to the Redfangs through a dozen Eater Goats, and Garen Redfang gave her the nickname.
Leafarmor had once been an enemy of Raidpear, who defected to the Flooded Waters tribe, before both ended up in the same tribe.
Leafarmor sharpens her spear after Raidpear says a dead Goldstone Chieftain was strong.
Leafarmor throws axes, and sews leaf scale mail from stiff, thick leaves, a skill she calls [Tough Leaves].
Leafarmor shows Pebblesnatch a wrapleaf, which curls around her hand and leaves burrs in her skin, then helps remove them.
Leafarmor explains to Pebblesnatch what Ulvama meant, and grins in a way that is not a smile.
Ulvama paints sigils on Leafarmor's face, and Leafarmor is very impressed.
Leafarmor swings up her axe as the Goblins wait while Humans argue with the Emperor's soldiers.
Leon is a young Earther from Poland who is a big fan of tabletop and miniatures games and also likes Magic the Gathering.
Leon is one of the seven Earthers who stay at The Wandering Inn for about a week after arriving, and is absent from the kitchen scene that morning.
Leon and Troy do their own thing as a team, according to the narration.
Leon doubts Erin has a higher level, asking how she has so much after being in this world only a few months.
Kevin says Leon and Troy wanted a [Gamer] class, but he told them it would only make them better at playing on his laptop.
Leon and Troy note that Joseph has football and Galina has the actors, and wonder what they themselves are good at.
Leon and Troy are given free room and board and paid by the hour for help, at slightly less than Ishkr and Drassi.
Leon says that Imani gets special treatment and that Kevin would survive anywhere.
Leon and Troy discuss making a tabletop or card game, wondering how to design miniatures and whether they could draw cards.
Leon and Troy are touring Pallass with a bag of coins and secretly investigating the city.
Grimalkin notes that Leon and Troy came from Magnolia Reinhart's estates, which suggests they told her something.
Grimalkin gives Leon a bag of coins instead of a bag of holding, and Leon recalls that Magnolia never gave him that much money.
Leon tells Grimalkin that he and Troy are just travellers who are not taking sides.
Leon and Troy agree to talk to Grimalkin for pay, secretly from Erin Solstice, beginning with their reaction to Master Felkhr.
Levil is a [Pyromancer] and the Captain of the adventuring team the Pithfire Hounds.
Levil and his team keep war dogs, including Makki and Dassa, the latter belonging to Bram.
Levil's team includes the [Mage] Ullica, Tally, Keima, Lamont and Bram.
Levil sees Ryoka racing across the grasslands, and throws himself to the ground when she signals him.
Levil's team puts down the Wailer Frogs with fire after the frogs' lungs are filled with dirt, so the Runner who answered their call saved them twice over.
Levil carries a bag of charred Wailer Frog tongues as proof of the kill.
The dog Dassa dies to a frog, and the Pithfire Hounds are most torn up about her.
Levil argues with Tally while the Pithfire Hounds wait at Reizmelt's gates, telling her to aim left and wait for his signal.
Levil conjures an orb of fire while waiting to hit whoever comes out of the city.
Ryoka misses Levil and the Pithfire Hounds when far from home.
Levil hugs Ryoka, beaming, when she brings the team a new dog from Lord Gralton Radivaek's kennels.
Lir is a mage and one of the Silver-rank captains who joins the expedition into the Ruins of Liscor.
Lir is the only mage at the captains' table besides Ceria.
Lir shakes his head when Calruz blusters about commitment, and Yvlon winces.
Lir tells Calruz that the captains agreed to come but are all equals and will go in properly or not at all.
Lir wants to bring in good Silver-rank adventurers from the city and agrees with Cervial that they need time.
Lir raises his staff and casts [Wall of Flames], which burns a curtain of fire across the corridor against the charging undead.
Lir and two more mages raise [Ward of Safety], [Lesser Barrier] and [Sanctuary of Light] at the entrance, all Tier 1 and Tier 2 spells working together.
Lir's head emerges from the folds of Skinner's body of skinned corpses, and he is killed and absorbed like Gerald and Cervial.
Liska is Ishkr's younger sister, two years younger than him, whom Drassi describes as difficult.
Liska is a Gnoll with red-brown fur and a sullen manner, who growls something like hello when Ishkr nudges her.
Ishkr asks Erin about his sister Liska, and Ishkr does not want anyone but himself, or perhaps Erin, to find her.
Drassi says Liska gets in trouble because she is often with female friends, which Drassi explains as Turnscales, and she says Ishkr asked her to keep it secret.
Liska works the morning shift at the inn behind Ishkr, who insists she say hello.
Lyonette says Liska has a bad attitude but follows orders, so she is not unmanageable like Maran and Safry.
Erin suggests work for Liska where she does not have to smile at people, like loading jobs with the Antinium.
Lyonette says Liska might suit writing receipts or secretarial jobs, and that she is rebellious rather than untrustworthy.
Lyonette says Liska works better when Lyonette talks to her than when Ishkr does.
Lism is a Drake [Shopkeeper] who runs a stall on Market Street in Liscor and is known as a vocal anti-Human voice.
Lism is Olesm's uncle.
Lism is Krshia Silverfang's long-standing rival on Market Street, the two being the top salespeople there.

A Drake shopkeeper who sold Erin food and a bag refuses her a refund, pointing to a sign saying the store gives none, and when she produces his own written price list he wagers a chess game instead: if she wins against his chosen player, he repays her money.
Erin identifies this shopkeeper as Lism, and Krshia says Lism gave her the heavy bag of flour on purpose without warning her.
Lism screams at his store and his nephew Olesm after the chess game that Erin wins.
Lism accuses Erin of robbing him of merchandise and of cheating his nephew at chess, after a guardsman says Shopkeeper Lism was the latest victim of petty thefts in the city.
Lism claims that humans have caused only trouble since arriving, that they steal, will take Drake jobs, and attack people on the streets.
Lism ducks back into his stall when Krshia glares at him.
Lism turns around and walks away when he sees Krshia unwrap huge broadhead arrows.

After a fire destroys a stall, Lism blames the Humans for destroying parts of the city twice, first by unleashing the undead; Krshia tells him to be quiet, and Erin tells him he is not a nice person, unlike Olesm.
Lism grins and laughs with friends while eating nuts as the crowd watches the thief girl being exiled.
Lism and his Drake friends plan to bid on all the good meat at an auction, but Krshia outbids him, boasting that he could not tell a prime cut from entrails.
After the second Raskghar attack, Lism stands on his stall on Market Street and tells a crowd the Watch failed them and that Human-lovers are in charge.
Lism accuses Erin of employing undead and letting Goblins work at her inn, and suggests the Goblins told the Raskghar where and when to strike.
Lism says Erin may be a Human spy and that he heard she met Magnolia Reinhart.
Lism shouts from his stall that the inn is a den of criminals when Lyonette walks through Market Street, blaming it for riots and for nearly drowning him.

Krshia says Lism has been angry since someone tried to drown him in the baths, and the Watch warned him twice to be quiet while he argued they favoured others by not investigating; she wears wax earplugs against him.
Lism tells Krshia that Gnolls have lived in Liscor only about a decade and that Drakes built the city and have lived in it for centuries.
Lism objects to Krshia's election plan, saying the Council has led Liscor well and that elections are a power grab, and he rejects her proposal that the Antinium build larger walls.
Lism rushes to the Mage's Guild and demands a highest-priority [Message] to Liscor's High Command, but the receptionists refuse without the Watch Captain's or Council's authorisation.

Lism tells a rally the army defended Liscor and promises three more companies stationed in Liscor permanently, claiming he has spoken with High Command, which has approved funding the walls with army money.
Lism consults supporters including the old [Seamstress] Shazzi and Cellic, a Drake veteran in his mid-thirties with a scarred skull, who is half-asleep at the meeting.
Lism adopts a "Jobs for Liscor" platform of hiring Drakes and Gnolls rather than the Antinium to expand the wall, a path through the hills around the Bloodfields, and funding the Watch.
Lism claims three Walled Cities have each pledged to cover five percent of the wall costs.
Lism presents Senior Guardsman Jeiss and the Mage's Guild head Alonna Swiftwing as candidates alongside himself.
Lism fields three Gnoll candidates in Gnoll-heavy districts and demands that the Antinium swear under a truth spell that the Hive has no plans against Liscor.
Lism calls the Dullahans traditional allies of the Drakes, and Maughin corrects him that the species were great enemies in the time of Dragons.
Lism argues against trusting the Antinium in a debate, while his nephew Olesm whispers to him.
Lism promises to execute the Minotaur Calruz if elected, claiming Calruz's team released the undead from the crypts and that he sent the Raskghar against citizens.
Hooded, Lism visits the inn the night before the election, advises Rufelt and Lasica to consider adopting a child since Liscor has children needing homes, and says he will tax the inn if elected.
Lism tells Rufelt he came to see the inn because his nephew talks about it so much, and says he will do what is right for Liscor but disagrees with Silverfang about what that is.
Lism proposes a surcharge of one silver on every Shield Spider body so Liscor takes a cut of the trade, estimating it adds five thousand gold after the culling.
Lism says a fully-grown, unscratched Shield Spider corpse fetches eleven silver, and that Liscor lacks the industry to process the silk.
Olesm tells the Council the annual cull kills three or four thousand Shield Spiders on average, about double that this year.
Later, Lism settles for demanding that the Merchant's Guild owe Liscor two silver pieces per Shield Spider corpse instead of checking its records.
Lism relaxes at Teliv Witherscale's laugh and agrees that Teliv will be present at the negotiations, first with Klbkch, then the Guildmasters, then Esthelm.
Lism and Jeiss try to persuade Guildmistress Tekshia to congratulate the Horns, but she refuses and takes more cake.

Lism concedes the Council cannot resist Wistram's mages, saying they have been outmanoeuvred like a Level 50 [Merchant] with thugs, but he moves to send Hawk to Fissival's Draconae Scholarium to ask about replacing Wistram's services and to co-sign Zevara's complaint.
Lism sits with Olesm at the inn instead of pestering Drassi about Erin.
Lism started the [Carers] initiative, which pays volunteers to check on vulnerable residents across Liscor and which he has run for years; Krshia helps organise it.
Lism pays about forty people to run the [Carers] project and wants a place for the many children who live on the street.
Lism proposes selling more land to Pallassian [Senators] and Salazsar Wall Lords at a 23% markup and expanding the city a second time to supply it.
Lism offers the Antinium six square miles above ground, with digging limited to ten feet, and Belgrade agrees to relay the offer to the Free Queen and Xrn.
Krshia kisses a distracted Lism in the conference room, revealing her attraction to him, part dislike and part odd infatuation.
Lism tells Krshia the Raskghar are held by Watch Captain Zevara, and when Zevara objects to killing every Raskghar, asks what she proposes; the Council defers to her authority as Watch Captain.
Lism slaps and punches Scalespeaker Yisht of Hectval for slandering the Gnolls, tells him he owes Krshia, Elirr and Raekea an apology, and bans Pallass from Liscor for a week.
Lism puts to a Council vote the end of negotiations with Hectval, and the Council agrees and has the delegation escorted out.
Lord Bein Terland is a [Lord] of the Terland family, one of the Five Families of Izril, though not from the main branch.
The Terland family is known mainly for its trade in magical artifacts, and has fallen on hard times since its days of glory.
Lord Bein's father is Lord Sheldae Terland, whom he persuaded to support his engagement to Lady Dealia, though his mother disliked the concept.
Lord Bein is a [Lordling] who travels with nearly a hundred private Terland guards.
Lord Bein is engaged to Lady Dealia of the Zolde nobility, who count as Chandrarian to many nobles, and the wedding is scheduled for the next month.
Lady Dealia is one of the most beautiful [Ladies] in Izril, ranked fourth on lists of top [Ladies] to marry.
Lord Bein had been secretly seeing the widowed Lady Hetessana Wellfar for about two years, before falling for Dealia.
Lord Bein flees Hetessana's bedroom half-naked as she pursues him, calling him a faithless dog.
Lord Bein tells Hetessana he cannot call off the engagement and that his hand was forced, claiming he tried to talk his father out of it.
Lord Bein puts a ten-thousand-gold bounty on Lady Hetessana's pendant, spread through unofficial channels.
Lord Bein orders his guards to spread out and block the road so no one goes around the Couriers.
Salamani uses [Invisibility] and [Flash Step], Tritel and Ci clear the guards with [Gazelle's Leap], and Hawk runs around them, so the blockade fails.
Clods of dirt thrown up by Ci's landing hit Lord Bein in the head as the Couriers pass him.
Lady Dealia confirms the locket is Bein's, and the Zolde brothers announce the engagement is off, and Qiam calls Bein a filthy Terland rat owing a blood debt.
Noass tells the crowd that Lord Bein is unfaithful and that the Zolde and Terland Houses are at war, though the older Zolde brother says they did not say war.
Lord Bein is outed as a treacherous philanderer, and the Zolde family and the Terland House are at war.
Lord Belchaus Meron is the [Lord] of Terandria known as the Lord of the Dance, who tops the lists for both eligibility and strategic genius.
Lord Belchaus held Terandria against foreign fleets for over a decade, and his presence alone kept the coast where his fleets patrol a safe harbor even in wartime.
Lord Belchaus is unmarried and is called the most eligible bachelor in the world.
The Drake [Writer] Krsysl Wordsmith ranks Lord Belchaus first among the five most important [Lords] in the world, placing Tyrion Veltras second and Hayvon Operland fifth.
Lord Belchaus is announced on a Pallass broadcast as the best [Lord] in the world according to Sir Krsysl Wordsmith, though the broadcaster notes that the list has been disputed.
Fierre says the title of best [Lord] in the world is only what some Drake wrote, but that Lord Bel is one of the best [Lords] in combat and other aspects.

section: Dancing and the Order of Savellia
text: Lord Bel studied dancing from every species and pays to see new dances or to meet people who are really good at it, according to what Fierre has heard.

section: Dancing and the Order of Savellia
text: When he is not defending his lands, Lord Bel entertains challenges like the Order of Savellia's all the time.

section: Dancing and the Order of Savellia
text: The Order of Savellia enters Lord Bel's ballroom, where hundreds of his [Dancers] wait, and Lord Bel stands at the far end posed on the balls of his feet, wearing an old-fashioned Terandrian noble suit in pale blue and rose-red.

section: Dancing and the Order of Savellia
text: Lord Bel refuses to bow to the Order of Savellia and dances against its grandmaster, his style being freer and more energetic than the Order's slower dances.

section: Dancing and the Order of Savellia
text: Lord Bel and the Savellian [Knights] are both famous for their dancing, and Fierre says they fight in perfect formations in battle and that Lord Bel is said to be better than most [Strategists].

section: Dancing and the Order of Savellia
text: Lord Bel catches a young Savellian [Knight] who challenges him in a dance, lifts him as if he were a [Lady], and the two then waltz together.

section: Dancing and the Order of Savellia
text: Ryoka tells Fierre that the Lord of the Dance could be homosexual or else straight and simply open to dancing with men.
Lord Belchaus rules Nadel, a safe-zone near the middle of Terandria's southern coastline, where no fleet except the Lord of the Dance's is welcome.
Lord Belchaus is infamous for keeping his waters free of marauders even in wartime, and his harbors are poor for illicit cargo and [Slaves], so anyone at odds with him steers clear of his waters.
Lord Belchaus has always been neutral, and his harbors were thought practically unassailable.

General Yerzhen tells Admiral Dakelos that Lord Belchaus has agreed, unhappily, to let Ailendamus' ships land at Nadel to flank the Dawn Concordat, and that the fight with the Lord of the Dance is a staged attack.
Lord Belchaus answers the Ailendamus demand for passage by stating that Nadel bows to no other nation and threatening to destroy their fleet.
Lord Bel's flagship rams The Wrath of Sel, and he leaps aboard with a sword and beheads its [Captain], then kills the [First Mate] while his retinue follows.
Admiral Dakelos realises that the Lord of the Dance is not acting.
Lord Erill is a merchant-lord, a noble who built his fortune and amassed enough power and land to be considered true nobility.
He carries no sword and is not a warrior.
Erill and Lady Ieka are protected by enchantments that keep the rain from falling on them as they leave a tent with Gralton and Yitton.
Yitton sees Erill as one of the richer [Lords] and newly come to his nobility.
Tyrion Veltras presents Lady Ieka of House Imarris, Lord Gralton of House Radivaek, Lord Erill of House Fienst and Lord Yitton of House Byres as representatives of the larger gathering of nobility.

Erill gives Lady Ieka a bag of holding with two hundred thousand gold pieces' worth of gold, gems and goods as a donation for the Circle of Thorns, which he says is repayment to Magnolia Reinhart, who is to know nothing of it.
He wants nothing to do with the Circle of Thorns and leaves quickly once his task is done.
Lord Gralton Radivaek is a large, roughly-dressed [Lord] in his early forties with a tattoo of a snarling dog on his cheek, who smells of wet dog.
The nobles call Gralton the [Dog Lord] behind his back in jest, and he raises dogs.
When first seen at Tyrion Veltras' gathering he is introduced as Lord Gralton of Lycit.
Gralton is of House Radivaek.
Gralton is rumoured to be more beast than man, wild and savage compared with many [Lords], though Ryoka finds that rumour twisted fact and exaggerated truth.

Gralton rages in Tyrion Veltras' pavilion that the army has sat idle while Magnolia Reinhart took the fight to the Goblins, and Yitton Byres answers by asking whether he means to assault their field commander, saying he would rather come to blows than suffer mutiny.
Yitton Byres thinks Gralton is an excellent fighter and leader in his own way, a hothead who smells of wet dogs but who can evaluate good strategy.

When Tyrion presents Laken Godart as an [Emperor], Gralton demands to know where he came from, half-rises with a low growl when Laken refuses to answer, and then sits down and laughs when Laken stares him down.
Gralton grins madly at Tyrion's talk of war, with a burning fever in his eyes, and Tyrion tells him that he has a way to open Liscor's walls.
Gralton and Yitton Byres ride with Laken as his companions, and a speaker at Riverfarm is shocked that Gralton is among them.
Laken thinks Gralton is impetuous and thoughtless at times, but higher-level than Yitton or Laken, and that he does not scoff at Laken's dreams or feelings.
Gralton gives advice through stories of his own failures, such as a Creler nest in his lands for which he hired three Gold-rank teams and Baudin the Brass.
Gralton and Yitton pay for the escort, the [Messages] and the food of Laken's caravan, mostly out of Gralton's money.
Laken calls Gralton one of the richer [Lords] in the area and one of his new allies.
Laken asks Gralton to ride ahead toward his lands if things get worse, in case he needs to bring back his army.

When Laken senses danger at Riverfarm, he tells Gralton to ride, and Gralton and his escort race ahead; Yitton says Gralton can muster thousands, and Laken thinks he should have sent Gralton the instant the coven arrived.
Oldblood Drakes attack the nobility's lands, and Gralton races into his kennels to find the dogs sick and poisoned while a Drake spits acid into the water supply.
Laken tells the [Witches] that the Drakes engineered a plague, or perhaps poison, in his friend's lands, and that Gralton's dogs and people lie dying while his [Healers] are stymied.
Laken offers four hundred gold coins to each [Witch] who heals Gralton's sick, and tells Yitton to have Gralton put up the eight hundred pieces.
Many dogs die, and some people too, but Gralton cares more about the dogs.
When Ryoka visits his lands, Gralton is kneeling in his kennels with red, weeping eyes, feeding a wheezing puppy goat's milk.
The kennels, built as a paradise for dogs, could house hundreds, but they are deathly silent and half-empty, since death swept through them.

The Drake came while Gralton was absent and spread plague and poison, getting the wells and the water, and poisoning the air; no one noticed except the dogs, and he says many people died, as well as dogs.
Gralton says he would never have known it was Drakes because the Drake was invisible.
Gralton vows to kill all the Drakes who did this.
Gralton tells Ryoka that the [Witches] already left, saying there was nothing more they could do.
Gralton shows up in Riverfarm with nearly four dozen dogs of many breeds, as a gift for the Unseen Empire.
Gralton says the kennels are filling up and that the dogs will be ratters, herders and guards, and that there would be no dogs to give if Riverfarm had not sent the [Witches].
Gralton introduces a blind dog, Draugmot, named after a Draug that its mother brought down.
The narration calls Gralton surly and even oafish to anyone who walks on two legs, but a friend to four-legged animals everywhere.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Gralton is said to train the fiercest war hounds and the finest trackers in all of Izril.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Gralton's lands are prosperous, in contrast to Yitton Byres' modest holdings.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Laken considers Gralton one of the most powerful and most unpredictable [Lords] in the camp, and had said barely two words to him since the first night.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Gralton enters Laken's tent smelling of dog, and Laken tells him "Heel", which makes Gamel gasp.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Gralton sits on the tent floor and asks Laken whether he is for the attack on Liscor and war with the Drakes.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Gralton joins Laken in discussing ways to rescue Yitton's children, and bares his teeth in a savage grin.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Laken judges that Gralton made his choice of ally faster than Lady Ieka or Lord Erill.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Gralton hunts deer with a dozen warhounds and says a herd or a bear would be more of a challenge.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Laken thinks Gralton is intelligent and merely likes dogs.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Gralton once ran a [Witch] off his lands after villagers complained she was hexing their farms over debts.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Gralton says the village the [Witch] cursed was deserted within two years, either through her curse or lost fields.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Lord Erill's lands are reported beset by flame and Lady Ieka's and House Veltras' by lightning, while Gralton's kennels are reported filled with sick dogs.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Gralton blames Laken and Yitton for pulling him away from his lands and says his dogs killed the invisible Drake.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Gralton says the [Witches], especially the old one with medicines and tea, saved many puppies.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Gralton asks Laken for more [Engineers] and sends six bags of holding by City Runner with dogs.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Laken gives Gralton three [Engineers] and eight [Builders] when Gralton asks for six more.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Gralton tells Laken that Tyrion's sons are poisoned and held hostage by the Circle of Thorns.

section: Additional claims (merged from batch chars_32 seeds for "Gralton")
text: Gralton passes on Tyrion's request that Laken recall House Veltras' goodwill and help find an [Alchemist] or [Healer] for a cure.
Lord Pattin of Vaunt is a young [Lord], the heir to Vaunt, a small city with a few villages that produces cheese and little else.
Lord Pattin ranks lowest among the visiting nobles in wealth and land, and wears worn riding clothes and rides a sad mare.
Vaunt's herds suffered sickness among the cattle six years earlier and have not been replenished, leaving the house in hard times.
Laken's [Lady] Rie reports that Lord Pattin is considered a very intelligent [Lord] and that Vaunt will prosper when he replaces his father.
Lord Pattin corrects Lord Andres that the Valerund family was lost in the First Antinium War, not the Second.
Lord Rael, annoyed at Pattin's lecturing tone, tells him that no one wants his opinion and insults his poor house.
Lord Pattin warns Rael that the fae outrank him and that pursuing them is not seemly, and flushes under the insult.
Laken notes that Pattin interests him more than Rael, who does not strike him as hugely bright.
Lord Pattin tells Lord Andres that a nearby stone is not magic, since he detected nothing from it when it was inspected.
Lord Pattin tells Lord Tourant that the trebuchet resembles Drake siege weapons, though he has only seen sketches.
Lord Pattin answers politely, unworried, when put on the spot, saying the weapons resemble those defending the Walled Cities and the design seems easy to replicate.
Laken's narration singles out Lord Pattin as one of the interesting young nobles.
Lord Tourant is a fiery nobleman and the father of Oswalt.
Tourant punishes Rael, Oswalt and the others when they cause trouble on his lands.
Tourant draws his sword on a fae woman after Oswalt is injured, saying he would cut her down if she were not a woman.
The fae woman grips Tourant's steel blade with her bare hands and says to duel the fae he must bring cold iron and star metal.
Bethal Walchaís steps between Tourant and the fae, saying Emperor Godart had warned him of the perils of following them.
Tourant claims his son was bewitched, and Bethal replies it was passion and that Oswalt lost only part of an ear.
Bethal orders Tourant to sit down in Emperor Godart's presence.
Lady Rie says Magnolia Reinhart might work through fools like Lord Tourant, whose touch is tactless, to pressure Laken's economy.
Rie says Tourant is an old friend of the [Mayor] of Elkhan, and that the boycott by hostile cities could refuse trade caravans carrying Laken's goods.
Tourant shouts that Goblins are not the same as Humans and is told to be silent.
Lorent is a Dullahan [Sharpener] in Pallass who sells knives from a permanent stall built into a building.
Lorent wears a full set of polished iron armor and speaks in a dour, flat voice.
Lorent sells knives crafted by Maughin and says a blade could skin a Wyvern.
Lorent removes his head, puts it in a basket on the counter and lets his body fetch stock from the back of the shop.
Lorent says a knife should fit the hand and offers to have a [Carpenter] sand down the grips for Erin.
Lorent greets Erin as Hello and says business could be better, doubting a Gnoll's claim about good knives.
Lorent splits a wooden block in half by dropping it on an upturned knife in front of a Pallassian and Liscorian crowd.
Lorent is among the Dullahans who put their heads on their shoulders to join the dance after Maughin does.
Luan Khumalo is a tall South African man in his twenties who is transported to Baleros from Earth.
Luan is twenty five, several years older than Ken and Aiko.
Luan speaks four languages: English, Afrikaans, Zulu and Tswana.
Luan was an Olympic rowing contender for South Africa rather than an Olympian, and would have competed in 2020.
Luan aimed at gold in the single scull, having first trained for a coxless pair with his best friend Ben.
Luan was in Australia on a break when he was transported to Baleros.
Luan says Ben will get a chance at the Olympics in his place.
Luan has a wife and a baby son, whose names are later tattooed on his arm.
Luan befriends Ken and Aiko on the march with Gravetender's Fist and tells them wars are never safe.
Luan leads a small patrol of Gravetender's Fist and strikes the final blow on a zombie Centaur with a hammer.
Luan is hit in the chest by an arrow while carrying wounded in the Centaur forest at night.
A healing potion closes the wound, but it tears open again, and a voice calls the arrow shaft enchanted.
Ken, Aiko and Quexa carry the wounded Luan on a stretcher at dawn to the [Doctor] known as the Last Light.
Geneva removes a squirming arrowhead from Luan's body in surgery and saves his life.

section: Geneva's camp and the Red Cross
text: Luan tells Geneva that his group appeared in Baleros last week and asks whether she is from their world.

section: Geneva's camp and the Red Cross
text: Luan tells Geneva that there are still at least forty people from their world besides the three of them.

section: Geneva's camp and the Red Cross
text: Geneva offers food and a bed only to people from Earth, and Luan tells her he will leave his company.

section: Geneva's camp and the Red Cross
text: Luan tells Daly he would rather not fight at all, because he has someone to live for.

section: Geneva's camp and the Red Cross
text: Luan and Ken wear white armor with red crosses, plant a flag in the valley and carry wounded back, making seven trips.

section: Geneva's camp and the Red Cross
text: Luan turns away choking when Ken abandons a gassed young Dullahan woman to save burn victims.

section: Geneva's camp and the Red Cross
text: Ken and Luan act as [Medics] for six days before eight Centaurs corner them.

section: Geneva's camp and the Red Cross
text: Luan customizes a Lizardfolk canoe within an hour and beats Lizardfolk racers in a canoe race.

section: Geneva's camp and the Red Cross
text: Luan leaves the valley with Ken, Quallet and the other neutral groups after Ken's amplified announcement.
Luan teaches Aiko to row and is followed by Lizardfolk who are taken by his skill on the water.
Rumour says Luan is a married man, while Aiko is clearly deeply attached to him.
Luan decides to earn money for the United Nations company by running messages in his canoe.
Luan is an [Expert Rower] at Level 27 after only two months in Baleros.
Luan's Skills include [Boat: Spray Cutter], [Power Strokes], [Greater Endurance], [Lesser Strength], [Enhanced Durability - Oars], [Boat: Lightweight Craft] and [Wave Sense].
Luan also uses the Skill [Second Wind] to feel fully rested while racing.
[Lesser Strength] makes Luan strong enough to lift an extra 20 kilograms with each arm.
Luan feels his levels are unfair because he has not earned them as an athlete.
Luan rows a Lizardfolk canoe with oar riggers made by a [Blacksmith] and a mirror from Paige to watch ahead of him.
Luan marks his boat with a painted letter symbol to show he is a water-based Runner for the Runner's Guild.
Luan has earned fifty-four gold coins from his deliveries by the time he returns to a Runner's Guild.
Luan has his wife's and son's names tattooed in gold on his arm after Venaz hires him, and thanks Aiko.
Luan stays away from Talenqual for a long stretch, going from city to village doing deliveries nonstop.
Daly says Luan is simply better at rowing than any Centaur, Dullahan or Lizardfolk and always returns with a lot of gold.
Luan returns from a three-day trip with the names Nandi and Lubanzi tattooed in gold on his arm.
Luan says he pushes himself harder to stop thinking, but no longer forgets.
Luan plans to upgrade his scull with a bag of holding if the company can afford one.
Luan shows the company a borrowed smartphone with pictures and videos of a city festival.
Luan's pictures of a spellbook turn out pure white, and spells also look different or invisible on screen.
Luan tells the company he is committed to Venaz's job and suggests using it to reach a Great Company for Geneva's sake.
The company votes on Luan's plan to mention Geneva to Venaz's contacts, and Geneva relays Okasha's agreement.
Luan sails a scull into Daquin harbour past Dullahan warships using [Power Strokes], and crashes into the pier.
Luan hurries toward the Starlight Requiem inn while Dullahans on the warships do not chase him.
Lizardfolk and Centaurs catch Luan in Daquin and plan to tie him up among other captives.
A Centaur is delighted that Luan slipped past the Iron Vanguard through the harbor.
Luan delivers a bag of holding to Venaz, who is hiding in a septic pit with Marian and Umina.
Luan understands what drives the student [Strategists] because he spent his life chasing victory as an athlete.
Luan tells the students he once served in a suppression company but is mainly good at rowing.
Marian hires Luan for twenty gold coins plus Venaz's fee, saying her [Headhunter] Skill rates him highly.
Luan tells Umina he belongs to the United Nations company based in Talenqual.
Luan fights with a club in the mist, using [Lesser Strength] to knock a Dullahan out of her armor.
Luan pays Lizardfolk, Dullahan and Centaur children coins to climb the War Walker Xol's legs, blocking his way.
Luan tells Xol that a friend who has met War Walkers explained how they prize children.
Luan's scull is wrecked and sunk in the harbor collision, and he must return to Talenqual by cart or canoe.
Luan uses a small glowing artifact over a banquet table so friends in his company can see it, and Marian and Umina notice.
Luan demands his pay from Venaz after the game.
Luan returns from Daquin with a large bag of gold covering the United Nations company's costs, and has met the Titan and Tulm the Mithril.
Xol of the Iron Vanguard puts a fifty-gold bounty on Luan to beat him up and wreck his boat.
Toughs threaten Luan in the street and try to attack his boat at the harbor, though the company keeps the boat locked away.
Kirana chases off one group of attackers carrying knives with a crossbow.
Luan wears a tattoo in gold of his family's names, like Siri's silver tattoo, so he will not forget them.
Luciva Skybreath is the Dragonspeaker of Manus and has ruled Manus for fourteen years.
Luciva is a Drake with pale-sky-blue scales mixed with white and, rarely, yellow, which give her an exotic, un-Lizardperson look.
Luciva has wings and breath, which mark her as a True Oldblood, the rarest of the Oldbloods.
Luciva wears Dragonscale armour, a cold-blue helmet that gives off vapour and boots whose soles never touch the ground.
Luciva carries a glaive crackling with electricity, known to Manus' people as the Fang of Manus, whose old name is Parentkiller.
Luciva's breath gives off bright flashes and an acrid smell, and her furled wings stir when she is moved.
Luciva wears white beneath her armour in mourning.
Luciva loses her daughter Hedica when reinforcements from Manus take part in Tyrion Veltras' battle at the Bloodfields.
Luciva tells Wall Lord Makhir that she takes no offence at his remark and that no one at the table is to blame, though she calls the battle beyond all acceptable cost.
Luciva convenes Manus' Security Council to discuss the Siege of Liscor, the battle at the Bloodfields and the ambitions of Tyrion Veltras.
Luciva asks whether the Human assault on Manus' people was unprovoked, and the Council agrees it was.
Luciva looks to the youngest Drake, Rafaema, for her opinion when the Council is divided on replying.
Luciva decides that the south must answer the Human attack.
Luciva says Manus will take the lead and may request the best fliers from other Walled Cities, since Manus' children need not bear all the risk.
Luciva signs and seals the order for Manus' first plan of ruination with her ring.
Luciva expects only Oteslia to object, and the Cyclops who drew up the plans says nothing.
Luciva tells Aldonss to report on Noelictus, saying the matter concerns a Grade 9 threat, the Witch.
Luciva says no one kills the Witch, and asks Aldonss for a proposal and for news if the Witch is credibly reported arriving on Izril.
Luciva tells Rafaema that a war with the Humans would be disastrous because the Antinium would not be idle.
Luciva asks Rafaema what she means when she says the Wyverns could pool their breath attacks.
Luciva's lips twist at the report of Frost Wyverns attacking Pallass.
Luciva wonders whether Bird is a hunting Prognugator designed for anti-air attacks, and says she must change her plans.
Luciva and Manus' war council know that Rafaema is a Dragon and that she is the hope of Dragons and Drakes.
Luciva is believed in Oteslia to have no idea of the different sort of Dragon, Cire, whom the people of Oteslia protect.
Lupp is an old [Farmer] who works a farm three miles south of a village, with a main cornfield and a smaller field of other crops.
Lupp's corn is ripe in spring, which Ryoka judges a Skill with limited effect because the field is small.
Lupp's corn stalks stand sixteen feet high, with thick, heavy ears of golden kernels.
Lupp keeps one cow, Helli, and dresses like a scarecrow, with straw sticking out of his ragged clothes.
Lupp has a [Dangersense] Skill that screams at him to stay quiet when something rustles outside.
Lupp's daughter is Kamine, who sends him a package from Reizmelt at least every month.
Kamine sends Lupp a whittler's knife because he wrote that his old knife had grown too dull.
Lupp glances back at the farmhouse when he mentions the knife, and Ryoka wonders what happened to Kamine's mother but resolves never to ask.
Kamine is a [Shoemaker] in Reizmelt, and Ryoka delivers milk and corn to her.
Lupp says Kamine is not a high-level [Shoemaker] but might make something of herself with better materials and a bigger shop.
Lupp bars his door and waits with a knife and healing potion on bad nights, sending a [Message] spell by scroll if it gets worse.
Lupp once found pieces of an adventuring team that failed to scare off a monster when he opened his door afterward.
Lupp says he used to drink, gave it up because it made him too miserable, and then devised his own method of coping.
When Lupp starts staring at shadows or stops talking to himself, Lupp leaves the farm, taking corn or bread to the road or going to Reizmelt.
Lupp says a friendly hand, a smile over some corn, or even a cursing match with a drunk [Wagon Driver] helps, though sometimes he needs to be alone.
Lupp tells Ryoka of a hateful [Innkeeper] who brewed the best ale he ever tasted and hanged himself in his own inn using a keg as a stepstool.
Lupp says the villagers found the [Innkeeper] the next day, argued over whether he was murdered, and then drank the ale rather than let it go to waste.
Lupp, disguised as a scarecrow, shoots an [Assassin] through the head just as the man is about to attack Bethal.
Lupp puts a second arrow in the air, and the two remaining [Assassins] flee.
Lupp checks the road and puts an arrow in all four bodies on the ground, which Bethal finds funny and Lupp does not.
Lupp says no one enters his fields, animal or person, without his knowing, and that only six strangers had been about besides Bethal and Thomast.
Lupp says even a Level 40 [Thief] cannot hide on his lands while standing on them.
Lupp says his winter price is a copper for two ears, or one copper for three ears in bulk.
Lupp plants about six hundred stalks and harvests twice a season, sometimes three times if he is quick.
Lupp says he can harvest his whole corn crop in two days, or one if need be.
Lupp accepts Bethal's offer of seven copper pieces for an ear of corn, saying he has his old age to think about.
Lupp suggests the City Runner known as the Wind Runner when Bethal needs speed, though he has only seen her run for a few seconds.
Lupp is paid gold for corn by Lady Bethal Walchaís, and says he never expected a [Lady] to keep her word.
Lupp asks Ryoka to bring him gin, which she delivers along with Bethal's payment and a jar from his daughter.
Lupp has made three harvests of corn and is surprised Lady Walchaís has not tired of it.
Lady Walchaís sends a fast wagon by Lupp's farm each month, and Lupp says the corn is going to a market.
Lupp tells Ryoka she is as miserable as a [Farmer] he once knew and that her only choice is when she goes.
Lupp admits he was close to a darker day when Ryoka first met him than ever before, and says she has been a comfort to him.
Lupp says the miserable [Farmer] became a famous adventurer named Eldert, who fought the Goblins in the Second Antinium War and joined a Named-Rank team.
Lupp says Eldert used to grow beets and probably changed his name to something fancier.
Lyfelt is the elected [Prime Minister] of Belchan, a career [Politician] who consolidated his class into [Minister].
Lyfelt has a pleasant, soothing voice and a charisma that is partly inborn and partly from his class.
Lyfelt has served for six years as [Prime Minister] and is new enough to find power intoxicating.
Raelt and Lyfelt speak through a marble bust and mirror that cost Jecrass 28,413 gold.
The bust lets Raelt and Lyfelt talk instantly without trusting a [Mage] with [Message] spells.
Raelt warns Lyfelt that Flos is no one to play games with, since he knew Flos when he was becoming the King of Destruction.
Lyfelt says Claiven and Medain hate the King of Destruction too much to worry about Belchan except as bulwarks.
Lyfelt says Claiven and Medain keep sending him [Messages] about a defensive pact.
Lyfelt says Perric of Medain knows Lyfelt has a [Court Mage] and that Claiven has also reached out to him.
