Raelt says Lyfelt told him Reim's worries lie south, where rulers are gathering.
Lyfelt is content to let the gathering do whatever it is doing, Raelt says.
Lyfelt tells Raelt that the Manticore hunt serves Belchan, since he had time to consider how to use Flos best.
Lyfelt says he is a [Politician] and that events like this help him and Belchan.
Lyfelt says Flos is clever about goals but is a novice at politics.
Lyfelt says he has allowed refugees through the border but his aid to Flos ends there.
Lyfelt says the refugees are much hated in Belchan and he thinks he can easily win re-election this year.
Lyfelt uses a Skill to calm Raelt in conversation, though it does not work.
Lyfelt claims he did not order the attack on the refugees when Raelt tells him they were slaughtered.
Raelt tells Lyfelt that children were hacked apart and the rest were being sold as slaves.
Lyonette is a young Human woman who is eighteen years old, and a [Princess] of a Terandrian kingdom.
Lyonette thinks of herself as a scion of the Marquin house, one of the Hundred Families of Terandria and Sixth Princess in line to the Eternal Throne of Calanfer.
Lyonette tells Erin she is of a minor Terandrian house, the Clavalettes, and distantly related to the royal family.
Lyonette later claims to be a distant relative of Magnolia Reinhart.
Lyonette thinks of herself as the third daughter of a small kingdom when she despairs, and as heir to one of the kingdoms of Terandria in another thought.
Lyonette is the girl Erin first calls Lyon, and she insists on her full name Lyonette.
Lyonette has had only one small Skill from her [Princess] class in her entire eighteen years.
Lyonette collapses in the snow after being exiled from Liscor, hating the Gnolls and Drakes for stripping her.
Her rings and cloak had been drained of power from overuse and their bindings broken, and the Gnolls and Drakes took the ones that still had power.
Lyonette reacts to Ceria with hostility, calling her a half-breed and a freak, and demands she leave.
Lyonette calls Erin a [Necromancer] for keeping Toren the skeleton, and says she defies her magic.
Lyonette leaves the inn with all of Erin's gold that was not hidden under the floorboards.
Lyonette wakes Erin and Ceria with a scream when Toren catches her trying to filch food.
Halrac, who had helped save the girl, watches her storm into the inn demanding that Erin call her by her name.
Lyonette gains a level in the [Barmaid] class and announces it to Erin as an insult.
Lyonette is a Level 1 [Barmaid] serving adventurers while sulking.
Lyonette refuses to fetch water from the stream, saying the Goblins that attacked the inn may be lurking outside.
Lyonette refuses to go out with Toren, and runs out of the inn crying when his eyes flash.
Lyonette screams and throws things at Reynold the [Butler], who replies that the invitation is extended to Miss Solstice alone.
Erin has Toren restrain Lyonette so she does not follow the coach to Magnolia Reinhart.
Lyonette demands to know when Magnolia Reinhart will send for her, and Erin tells her Magnolia knows she is there.
Lyonette watches Erin and Ryoka from the staircase in silence.
Lyonette introduces herself to Ryoka as Lyonette de Marquin, and Erin calls her an employee.
Lyonette has a [Barmaid] class at Level 3 and the Skill [Lesser Stamina].
Lyonette resents that her royal class has been ruined by a common class.
Lyonette thinks she crossed from Terandria to Izril by booking passage herself, surviving monsters, starvation and the mob that cast her out of Liscor.
Lyonette thinks her father probably sent search parties only as far as the shores of Terandria.
Lyonette knows a light-ball spell even though she does not have the [Mage] class.
Lyonette gains another [Barmaid] level and the Skill [Basic Cooking].
Krshia says Lyonette destroyed something precious her clan had laboured for years to build.
Krshia says the damage Lyonette caused is equivalent to fifty thousand gold coins.
Klbkch says Lyonette du Marquin destroyed Krshia's shop with a powerful magical artifact that bypassed the normal protections on the spellbooks stored there.
Lyonette is banned from Liscor as a thief, though she does not have the [Thief] class.
Lyonette thinks she is a failure and will starve in an inn that is not hers.
Lyonette has [Basic Cooking] as a Skill and is ashamed but privately elated about it.
Lyonette's first pasta is watery and bland, and she cannot finish it.
Lyonette serves the Antinium Worker Pawn, who pays her, and she resolves to survive on his custom until Erin returns.
Lyonette fears the Antinium and remembers the stories of their atrocities, but concludes they are a stable source of income.
Lyonette is reluctant to tell the Antinium that she cries in the inn and has only a few copper coins and two silver coins left.
Lyonette cannot feed the Antinium bread or pasta, so she settles on the Ashfire Bees as her one chance for free ingredients.
Lyonette serves a Worker eggs and bacon, who leaves bronze coins and makes her cry again.
Lyonette believes Pawn will come back, and has been too afraid for two nights to try the bee cave.
Lyonette is knocked out by smoke from a dead faerie flower thrown in the fire.
Lyonette uses the smoke of dead faerie flowers in a fire in the bee cave to make the bees fall asleep.
Lyonette cuts out three jars of honey and honeycomb, and fills two jars with sleeping bees, then flees.
Lyonette keeps a grub and royal jelly from the hive.
Lyonette fries two bees per Soldier and serves soup to the Antinium Soldiers.
Lyonette earns a bag of coins selling bees.
Lyonette feels free and happier than she ever felt in the palace, and is glad she is no longer alone with Mrsha there.
The honey brings in a few Drake guests who drink honeyed water and fill jars with honey.
Selys teaches Lyonette to make shepherd's pie.
Later, Lyonette reaches [Barmaid] Level 8 with [Basic Cleaning], gains [Carer] Level 2 with [Calming Touch], and gains [Tactician] Level 1 with [Lesser Intuition].
Lyonette thinks she got [Carer] from taking care of Mrsha and [Tactician] from playing chess.
Lyonette has not levelled in her chosen class for four years.
Later, Lyonette gains [Beast Tamer] Level 1 with the Skill [Healthy Rearing] for looking after a bee grub.
Lyonette wants every class she can get, even if it means she never reaches a high level in her one true class.
Lyonette says her family has many old secrets about classes, which her father insisted she learn.
Lyonette tells Mrsha that some classes are better than others, and that influencing classes like [General] are among the best.
Lyonette says her mother taught her that royal classes can touch entire kingdoms, and that [Emperor] might be better than [King].
Lyonette says royal, rare and merged classes are better than normal ones, and that a [Princess] can give someone a unique class.
Later, Lyonette says she is a Level 3 [Beast Tamer], Level 4 [Carer] and Level 9 [Barmaid], and a Level 5 [Princess] despite being one all her life.
Later, Lyonette is a Level 11 [Barmaid], Level 4 [Beast Tamer], Level 6 [Carer], Level 2 [Tactician] and Level 5 [Princess], with new Skills [Charming Smile] and [Lesser Strength].
Lyonette knows she has far too many classes, and that she should have only one.
Lyonette cooks poorly, fusses about cold and bugs, and has blisters from scrubbing, according to Mrsha.
Lyonette takes care of the inn while Erin and Ryoka are away.
Lyonette hauls water from the stream before sunrise and cooks for the guests, who are Griffon Hunt, the Halfseekers and Zel.
Lyonette counts nine private rooms in the inn, just enough for the adventurers, Zel, herself and Mrsha.
Lyonette thinks the inn needs more than one outhouse, and talks to Pawn about a larger temporary one for Moore.
Lyonette cooks three times as much for Moore, since he is a half-Giant who eats three times as much.
Lyonette tells Erin she has [Basic Cooking] now but is still no good.
Lyonette casts [Light] after the inn shakes and its walls glow, and the orb turns from blue to murky green.
The orb of light Lyonette casts grows far larger than it should, and more orbs rise from the tables and ground.
Lyonette keeps the bee larva in her room and feeds it royal jelly, saying she meant to feed it to Klbkch before she got a [Beast Tamer] class.
Erin calls the larva Mr. Ugly Fat Worm, and leaves it to Lyonette to name once it grows.
Lyonette makes a fry-up of mushrooms and greens with fried beef in a Gnoll sauce as a buffet for the returning travellers.
Lyonette fries bees in oil with melted cheese for the Antinium, and Ksmvr tells her they are good.
Lyonette bakes bread with Erin's baking powder and butters the tops.
Lyonette overhears Erin crying that she wants to go home, and weeps for her.
Lyonette swears an unfinished oath by her name and her blood to Erin's cause, speaking to the sky.
Lyonette uses dried seed cores from blue fruits to scare off Rock Crabs and has done so twice.
Lyonette tells Erin that Maran and Safry refused to fetch water, and that the six barrels Maran bought must have cost at least twelve silver coins.
Lyonette assigns Drassi to wait tables and Ishkr to fetch water and clean the outhouses, and both do their jobs without trouble.
Erin names Lyonette to be in charge of the inn's staff.
Lyonette screams at Erin that Toren was always a monster, who pushed her into Shield Spider nests, made her run for miles, hit her and abandoned her for hours.
Lyonette says Erin never noticed or believed her about Toren and still does not listen or trust her.
Lyonette runs out of the inn after shouting at Erin.
Ryoka tells Lyonette she is not meant to be an innkeeper but is a [Princess], showing that Ryoka knows her secret.
Lyonette tells Pawn her mother's story of a [Queen] who stayed still on a battlefield while her soldiers fought to protect her.
Lyonette tells Pawn that the Queen's soldiers chose to fight, and what mattered was that they believed.
Lyonette teaches Pawn to stand with his head straight and chin up so he can lead bravely and gracefully.
Lyonette tells Erin she played about six games of chess against an unseen player, levelling up, and the player reset the board after the last game.
Lyonette's bee pupa grows to twice the size of an Ashfire bee on royal jelly, moves, and starts to grow hairs.
Lyonette names the bee Apista and says she does not know whether she can control her.
Lyonette whispers the start of an oath, "I, Lyonette du Marquin do solemnly", and Ishkr and Brunkr hear it with their Gnoll ears.
Mrsha stares at Lyonette as she whispers the oath.
Lyonette asks Brunkr to show her how to parry again to cover for what she said.
Lyonette gains [Warrior] Level 1 with [Basic Footwork], and [Princess] Level 6 with the Skill [Royal Tax].
Lyonette realises that knighting Brunkr made her level, and that she knows about [Royal Tax] from the secret book of kings her father showed her.
Lyonette wonders why her mother and father never told her that making a [Knight] would level her.
Lyonette believes no one on the continent knows she is a [Princess] except Magnolia Reinhart, Pawn and Ryoka.
Lyonette fears her identity is dangerous to the people she loves, and so keeps it secret.
Lyonette notices that customers give her small extra tips but give Ishkr none, which she links to [Royal Tax].

section: Mrsha and the Eater Goats, Book 6
text: Lyonette missed her home sometimes and had never seen a dead body before leaving Terandria.

section: Mrsha and the Eater Goats, Book 6
text: Lyonette recalls that as a [Princess] she was too delicate to look on a poisoned uncle's face or go to a funeral.

section: Mrsha and the Eater Goats, Book 6
text: Lyonette has feared and then begun to like Brunkr, and his death hurts her.

section: Mrsha and the Eater Goats, Book 6
text: Lyonette, Drassi and Mrsha throw potions at charging Eater Goats, including lightning, thorn, tripvine, pepper and Silverfrost vials.

section: Mrsha and the Eater Goats, Book 6
text: Lyonette orders Mrsha not to harm the Goblin guests, saying they are Erin's guests and she will have no lunch if she causes trouble.

section: Mrsha and the Eater Goats, Book 6
text: Lyonette spanks Mrsha hard after Mrsha tries to hurt Badarrow with a wand, and stops only when someone grabs her hand.
Krshia tells Lyonette that she knows Lyonette is a [Princess] and that she gave her blessing to make Brunkr a [Knight].
Lyonette says a [Knight] can be made with only a few words, though it is usually a matter of ceremony.
Lyonette says a [Princess] can appoint only a limited number of [Knights] who serve as personal protectors, so she can choose them quickly.
Lyonette says that she can royally appoint a business, bestowing a royal class such as [Royal Gardener] on someone.
Lyonette says a royal appointment is an addition that makes the holder better and does not prevent normal class change.
Lyonette grants Krshia and her business her royal favour in a solemn oath.
Lyonette tells Krshia she ran away and fears her family would send someone after her if they knew where she was.
Lyonette says she is not a First Princess or high-level.
Lyonette helps hold off two Pallass Watch Drakes after the portal door goes dead behind them, and the Drake [Captain] surrenders.
Lyonette keeps a sword hidden under her bed that Mrsha is forbidden to touch, and practises sword forms at night.
Lyonette practises the moves that Brunkr showed her, which hurts her to remember.
Lyonette is a Level 3 [Warrior] who has never actually fought anything.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette reaches [Carer] Level 8 and [Beast Tamer] Level 5, and gains the Skill [Apista: Basic Training].

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette reaches [Barmaid] Level 15 with [Balanced Posture], and [Warrior] Level 4.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Later, Lyonette loses the [Princess] class after "Class Conditions: Princess failed", and loses [Detect Poison] and [Royal Tax].

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette weeps uncontrollably the next morning and lies to Erin that nothing important happened.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette tells Pawn she lost her class because she stopped being a princess, and she says she does not need it.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette says she was only Level 6 in [Princess] and had two Skills that were not useful.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette tells Pawn she is glad to lose the class, and that her name is just Lyonette now.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette suggests crafts, tag and a communal living space to help Pawn keep the Antinium busy.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Pawn buys knitting needles, yarn, balls and clay for the Hive after Lyonette's advice.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Pawn tells Erin that the Hive has expanded its barracks and added crafts.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette shouts at Pawn not to pray for her class or try to change her, after he admits praying every day for its return.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette runs away upstairs in tears after shouting at Pawn in front of the inn.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette teaches Pawn to waltz, drawing on years of court training.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette watches the Workers and Soldiers waltz in pairs after Purple Smile teaches them.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette believes part of her wanted to lose her class so she could be someone else.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Later, Lyonette regains [Princess], [Detect Poison] and [Royal Tax] after "Class Conditions: Princess met".

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Her [Princess] class becomes [Worldly Princess] at Level 11, and [Warrior], [Barmaid], [Beast Tamer], [Tactician] and [Carer] are consolidated into it.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: She gains [Basic Crafting], [Weapon Proficiency: Sword], [Basic Negotiator], [Basic Leadership] and [Flawless Attempt] with the new class.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette and Pawn hold hands the next day and agree to find out whether what they feel is love.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Erin reports that Lyonette's new Skill [Flawless Attempt] makes whatever she does the best she can, and that it needs time to recharge.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Erin says Lyonette made Mrsha an omelette with [Flawless Attempt] that was great but not perfect.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette says Wall Lord Ilvriss may have cancelled Erin's [Inn's Aura] with his own, since Lords have aura Skills.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette says she has some expertise on auras, which are rare, and that Erin's is confined to her inn.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Lyonette meets Erin's gaze while holding Mrsha, and Erin's aura presses on her in vain.

section: Losing and regaining the Princess class, Book 8
text: Erin suggests that Lyonette take Bird as a bodyguard when she goes to Celum with Mrsha.
Lyonette's head is bleeding and her wrist is broken after the Raskghar break through the inn's door and ignore her.
Lyonette finds that Mrsha is gone and Apista has two legs mangled.
Lyonette serves tables dazed while Drake [Barmaids] watch over her.
Lyonette begs the Horns of Hammerad to find Mrsha, saying she would go with them if she could.
Lyonette goes to Liscor with Drassi to buy food for Erin, and refuses to stay at the inn.
Lyonette and Drassi pass a crowd in Liscor where Lism blames Humans, while Krshia stands silent at her stall with her head bowed.
Lyonette parries Nokha's sword, stabs her shoulder, and keeps her at bay with Apista's sting until Moore breaks Nokha's arm.
After the dungeon, Lyonette says she levelled up and Apista has the Skill [Crimson Stinger] through her.
Lyonette uses her aura on Erin to press the argument that Mrsha needs time alone, and Erin pushes it back.
Lyonette's father, a king with a crown, sees her in a scrying pool carrying Mrsha up Liscor's walls, and tells a servant to bring her back.
Lyonette keeps a plain steel sword at her side as a [Barmaid], and draws it when a monster climbs the inn.
Lyonette's hands are cracked and bleeding from soap, and she remembers hand creams from her kingdom's [Court Alchemist].
Lyonette admits to herself that she wants to be a [Princess] again, though she is a [Barmaid] now.
Lyonette tells Erin, Numbtongue and Mrsha that she is a [Princess] of the Eternal Throne of Calanfer.
Lyonette says Calanfer's Eternal Throne is not actually eternal and dates back about six thousand years.
Lyonette builds a wooden wheel with mana stones so the door can switch destinations without a bowl.
Lyonette takes over management of the inn while Erin travels, asking for authority over its money and decisions.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette tells Zevara she agrees with her exile sentence, and thinks that being let back into the city without a fine was the real problem.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette says she knows General Zel Shivertail interceded for her, and she survived her exile thanks to him.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette says she studied Drake law, and knows that a second offence could mean death.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette asks to pay her fine to reclaim the artifacts that Liscor's Watch confiscated, which are mostly drained or locked.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Zevara recalls that Lyonette's artifacts gave her [Invisibility], webs and [Fireballs], and that they were powerful.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Zevara sets Lyonette's fine at forty-seven gold coins, with a claim by Lism and any claim for Krshia's shop ignored.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Zevara says Lyonette's fine beat the previous offender's record, which belonged to Pisces.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette pays eight gold coins toward the fine from her own salary and refuses to ask Erin to pay.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Zevara keeps Lyonette's artifacts impounded until the last coin is paid.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette asks how to train Apista, and does not mention that she consolidated her [Beast Tamer] class into [Worldly Princess].

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette sends Apista with a note to Krshia asking for three dozen eggs, and says Apista will deliver messages in future.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Later, Lyonette reaches [Worldly Princess] Level 17 and gains [Apista: Enhanced Intelligence], [Apista: Agile Flier] and [Imperial Aura].

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette's [Flawless Attempt] lets her do a task once perfectly, and then repeat it again; she cartwheels with it to tease Erin.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette says she would trade [Flawless Attempt] only for Erin's [Wondrous Fare].

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette tells Erin there are two cakes and enough ice cream ingredients for eight guests, and that ice is expensive.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette and Pawn hold hands as she goes up to supervise the construction of the third floor.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette keeps the Liscor and Pallass doors closed until late morning so the staff can rest and restock.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette plans to buy Mrsha clothes so she learns to wear something.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette tells Mrsha she is not allowed outside without a minder, and mentions the Raskghar.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette promises Mrsha a new inn, with her own designs, and says she needs things from Zevara, including her family's cloak.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette declares to the Gnolls in a prison that Mrsha is her daughter, and that she is Mrsha's mother.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: The Liscor Council tells Erin that the inn and its people are de facto inhabitants of Liscor, and offers to put Lyonette and Mrsha in for citizenship.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette orders the inn cleaned with a strong soap-mix from Octavia while Erin is away.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette finds that the floor becomes so slippery that Drassi falls, and says she may not have added enough water.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette uses [Flawless Attempt] to make a nearly perfect veggie burger from Erin's recipe.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette stops Erin from chasing a thief herself and tells her to call the Watch.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette tells Erin she needs an ally in Wistram and should negotiate with Palt, because Calanfer survived thousands of years by making allies.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette tells Erin not to teach Wistram how to make guns.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette asks Erin to let the back wall of the inn be torn down because the Antinium have tripled the hill's size.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Erin asks Lyonette to delay Belgrade by one week.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette goes for her sword when she meets Relc and Mrsha after Mrsha is hurt by a Rock Crab, and bans Relc from the inn for six days.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette says Liscor paid for the inn, with the Creler attack money and Erin's savings, and she hopes more Gold-rank teams will stay.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette silences the inn with her aura, and Zevara adds her own authority at the same time.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Erin can resist both auras because it is her inn.

section: Fine, citizenship and the inn, Books 10-15
text: Lyonette gives her name as Lyon at a meeting with the Mayor of Celum.
Lyonette is the effective day-to-day manager of the inn, and Erin is like a trusted subordinate she sends out.
Lyonette tells Erin that she ran away from home, and that Calanfer can live without half its [Princesses].
Lyonette thinks her family probably has one of her doubles standing in for her.
Lyonette says a [Message] home would just be trouble, and that her sisters are better than her father.
Lyonette says she usually takes a potion against bleeding, as her whole family does, though her bleeding is bad.
Lyonette and Pawn begin a sexual relationship in her room, which they planned for a month against Klbkch's orders.
Lyonette says she is a terrible [Princess] and her parents will have to live with that.
Lyonette reaches Level 19 as a [Worldly Princess] and gains [Magnified Training], a rare consolidation before Level 20.
Lyonette and Pawn keep their relationship secret, and Mrsha knows by scent and sulks.
Lyonette says Erin would go ballistic at the thought of anything improper.
Lyonette explains that better classes level more slowly, and that her father guessed the King of Destruction is only above Level 50.
Lyonette says the Blighted King would be around the King of Destruction's level.
Lyonette says Calanfer keeps a list of rulers above Level 40, with fewer than forty on it in the entire world.
Lyonette asks Krshia to let her learn a spell from the spellbook Krshia keeps, because her Skill [Magnified Training] may help.
Lyonette says Marquin children have natural mana pools larger than most people, and that her parents would call it superior breeding.
Lyonette says Calanfer would trade hundreds of thousands of gold pieces' worth for Krshia's spellbook.
Lyonette chooses to learn the Tier 3 wind spell [Razorwind], and gets a nosebleed from the effort.
Lyonette uses [Flawless Attempt] to focus her mind on [Razorwind], and loses two hours picking up a knife to understand how sharp a blade is.
Lyonette ends up able to move the wind weakly in Krshia's apartment, though she is not a tenth of the way to learning the spell.
Lyonette wants a private bathing room with a hot tub, and has the Antinium divert a stream.
Lyonette calls herself Lyon to Veeid.
Lyonette wakes in Pawn's room, and Mrsha does not like it when she stays the night there.
Lyonette calls Mrsha Mrsha du Marquin and tells Erin she does so deliberately.
Lyonette says she outranks Pryde, and that by shifting her own authority she can stop Pryde from clashing with Erin.
Lyonette uses her aura to stop Magus Grimalkin from interrupting Erin, with a push toward politeness.
Lyonette redirects Pryde to Grimalkin and his weights.
Lyonette collapses after using up her aura, and then gains [Worldly Princess] Level 20.
Lyonette gains the Skill [Boon of the Princess], which she uses on Mrsha to give a glowing sigil and temporary [Barkfur] and [Lesser Strength].
The boon can be given to only one person at a time, and Mrsha's temporary Skills last more than six hours.
Lyonette slaps Ryoka five times when they reunite, the first with [Flawless Attempt], and Ryoka does not dodge.
Erin tells Ryoka that Lyonette and Pawn are dating, and Ryoka promises not to tell anyone.
Lyonette teaches Mrsha etiquette and the Lessons From Home, including one on public disturbances.
Lyonette refuses Selys's offer to invest in the inn for a share of profits, saying the inn is funded on its own income.
Lyonette has Belgrade and Pawn rebuild a stable with two floors as one floor, because horses dislike heights.
Lyonette hires eighteen unpainted Antinium Workers from Bird's crew as labour.
Lyonette has nearly paid off her fine to Zevara from her own income.
Lyonette has used [Boon of the Princess] only on Mrsha and then on Octavia, and gives two temporary Skills and a mark of her royal house.
Lyonette's father, the King of Calanfer, has the Skill [Favor of the King], a more powerful version of her boon.
Lyonette knows Calanfer's Champion of the Dawn benefits from the King's boon.
Lyonette gives the boon to Numbtongue, with the temporary Skills [Directional Sound] and [Soul's Armaments: Mundane].
Lyonette promises to give Bird the boon the next day, saying it is not a Skill she can toss about.
Lyonette hopes to hire eight more staff from thirty-seven applicants, including four Antinium permanently.
Lyonette manages the new hires, including Ishkr's sister Liska.
Lyonette is the sixth [Princess] of Calanfer, which has so many princesses that they have numbers.
Lyonette dreams of the early inn, the first Painted Antinium, and General Zel Shivertail as her first real guest.
Lyonette wakes alone and sour because Mrsha spent the night with Ryoka.
Lyonette's jealousy is a mother's jealousy, since she raised Mrsha when Erin and Ryoka were away and became her mother.
Madain is the owner and [Innkeeper] of The Huntress' Haven in Reizmelt, and people call him Mad Madain behind his back.
Madain is a huge burly man who sets out bowls of last night's soup for breakfast.
Madain is a retired adventurer who was part of a Gold-rank team, though that is not the same as being certified Gold-rank himself.
Madain opened an inn as many retired adventurers do, but has the opposite temperament to a good [Innkeeper].
Madain was a [Javelineer], and his arm is still strong enough for hunting.
Madain wakes his guests at his own hour, sometimes before dawn, then serves food and leaves his inn to go hunting.
Madain calls Ryoka by her nickname because he cannot be bothered to learn her real name.
Madain's inn survives on meat served almost every night and on cheap alcohol.
Madain gets a lot of dining custom, and is in a good mood after a successful hunt.
Fierre says Madain likes her and that his friends drink with him only because he is good for free alcohol.
Madain has a fit at least once a month, smashing things, fighting with friends and cursing until he passes out.
Ryoka worries about Madain's rages, and says she has seen him throw his axes.
Alber calls Madain crazy but strong, and says he faced the inn's owner once.
Madain tells Ryoka that Fierre's old office was destroyed by sewing needles, and guesses Ryoka's [Witch] was responsible.
Madain says Fierre is fine and has some high-level defensive Skill, and may have used healing potions.
Madain does not tell Ryoka that Fierre is fine, and grins when Levil points out he could have.
Magnolia Reinhart is a [Lady] who rules House Reinhart, one of the Five Families, and is called the Deadly Flower Blooming in the North.
Magnolia is a high-level [Lady] who strides gracefully, and is cheerful by design while sharper than she appears.

Magnolia Reinhart receives a delivered enameled bottle of blue liquid distilled from the very poisonous Amentus fruit, and tells the young woman who brought it that she promised to share a glass with friends at brunch after drinking the last glass the day before.
Magnolia has blonde locks curled as stylishly as anything Ryoka remembers from her world.

Magnolia receives a canister of ice cream from Ryoka, who got it from other Runners, after it travelled from the port city of Hazenbrad; Magnolia says it cost seventy gold coins not counting shipping, and that she heard it was invented only a week earlier by a master [Chef] in the northern continent.
Magnolia tells Ryoka that she is a [Lady], that most of her class learn [Sense Intentions] early, and that she is quite high-level in it; she then says "sit," and Ryoka sits without thinking.

Magnolia tells Ryoka that [Ladies] have a few useful tricks in social situations, and she can detect far more than her posture indicates, which also lets her keep her poise even when her stomach hurts.
Ryoka thinks Magnolia is the scariest person she has met in this world and that her cheerful manner hides a sharp and intelligent woman whom she first took for a plump social butterfly.

Magnolia guesses where Ryoka comes from, trying in turn Terandia, the Isles of Minos, the southeastern continent, the frozen archipelago, the wilds of this continent, the Gnoll tribes, Drake settlements, the Antinium Colonies, Wistram and the Dwarves; Ryoka denies each.

Magnolia asks Ryoka whether she comes from any place in this world, then has her head maid Ressa ask the Mage's Guild to cast the expensive long-distance speaking spell on her that night, judging the cost worth the secrecy and privacy.
A Runner's Guild contact says Lady Magnolia has been asking for a delivery for several days and wants only one Runner to do it: Ryoka.
Magnolia, dressed in an expensive pink dress with floral embroidery, visits Ryoka at The Rat's Tail in Celum with head maid Ressa glaring behind her.
Ressa addresses Magnolia in front of Ryoka as a Lady of the Six Houses.
Magnolia says she has a number of skills including [Charming Demeanor], which has no effect on Ryoka, though she has had more effect on stubborn generals and obnoxious Dragons.
Magnolia offers Ryoka healing from a friend who can cast [Restoration] and other spells of the 4th Tier, in exchange for her answering as many questions as Magnolia dares to ask.
Magnolia leaves Ryoka a bronze medallion inlaid with a sapphire, saying that shattering the gem will let her know Ryoka accepts her terms.
A Runner's Guild member tells Ryoka that Lady Magnolia is refusing to take any other requests until Ryoka delivers something in person, which is hurting Runners in every city nearby.
Magnolia knows Ryoka's personality well, from experience and from her Skill, and not predicting Ryoka's unmarked request was a slight oversight that may cost Ryoka her life.

Magnolia is a happy woman almost all the time, deliberately so because people like a happy person and it lowers their guard; she believes generosity combined with an implicit threat opens even more doors.

Magnolia goes to Ryoka's inn at night since Ryoka has avoided her; she has paid the innkeeper to clear the inn, brings a manservant, maids and discreetly hired men and women, uses an umbrella enchanted with [Water Resistance], and has her maids discourage Runners and adventurers lurking at the back door.
Magnolia brings Ressa up to Ryoka's door while [Assassins] and [Maids] wait below, and gets no reply to her knocking or greetings.
Yvlon Byres tells Ryoka that her aunt twice-removed, whom Ryoka realizes is Magnolia Reinhart, told her it was worth seeking Ryoka out and has told all her family to keep an eye out for Ryoka.

Yvlon tells Ryoka that Magnolia has heard she defeated a low-level [Assassin] with her bare hands and fought a Carn Wolf without weapons; Ryoka suspects Magnolia hired the [Assassin] and wonders how she knew about the wolf.
Ryoka thinks Magnolia put a ninja on her rooftop, though she wonders whether he was there to hurt or guard her, and that Magnolia has never directly attempted to hurt her, unlike Persua.
A speaker tells Erin that, of the five families, Lady Magnolia rules the entire House Reinhart and is probably one of the ten most important individuals anywhere.
Magnolia argues in the far north with an invisible Teriarch while studying a map of the northern continent and then the world.
Someone tells Ryoka that Magnolia always travels north for winter, was only in her holdings here for a few months, and is now in Invrisil, the city of adventurers, six hundred miles north.
Magnolia tells Teriarch that Ryoka has no skills, levels or class, and that it is extraordinary she reached his cave without help.
Magnolia tells the Courier Val that Ryoka has gone further south, but declines to hire him to track her, saying Ryoka will come north soon and her answer will be disappointing: nothing.

Magnolia shows Val into her mansion, where bowing servants and priceless artifacts fill the halls, and lets him look at a room of ordinary-looking young people in bright clothes, one holding a flat glowing device that makes sound; Val thinks he has seen something like the device.

Val thinks Magnolia plays games with fates and lives, as anyone with power does in the north, but does her scheming in the open as much as in shadow, with laughter and a willingness to share her fortune.
Reynold tells Erin that Lady Magnolia is quite rich and has many servants with many levels in strange classes, but he is not allowed to say more.
A speaker tells Erin that Lady Magnolia is the heir to the Reinhart family and one of the richest individuals on the continent.
Magnolia receives Erin in a sitting room whose predominant colour is light pink.
Magnolia is in her forties, a larger woman than Ressa but shorter, wearing a shimmering green gown, graceful, refined and serene, with eyes that sweep over Erin like searchlights.

Erin knows Magnolia as the pursuer of Ryoka who pieced together the truth about Erin, a wealthy [Lady], the head of the Reinhart family, the heroine of the First Antinium Wars, and a woman who loves ice cream and blue fruit juice.
Magnolia is friendly, firm of handshake and quick to laugh, and shares citrus tea that tastes of limes, poured by Ressa.
Magnolia tells Erin she learned chess at sixteen and has since played regularly with at least one good opponent.

Magnolia wears a monocle with an obsidian rim and rune-carved sides, made for her by a friend, which lets her read [Skills] and [Levels] unless they are concealed; she says she would love to know what [Immortal Moment] and [Wondrous Fare] do.
Magnolia says she has a skill called [Sense Intention] and uses it to sense which pieces her chess opponent is focusing on, which helped her play well against Erin.

Magnolia tells Erin that at least five people could best her at chess, including an old fool, the world's smallest strategist, a reclusive mage, a miserable king and a dashing and charming lord, one genius on each continent except Chandrar, where she says the young [Emperor] and the King of Destruction's Left Hand are not good enough.
Magnolia says that Teriarch told her this would happen sooner or later, and laments that it happened with her favourite tea pot out.

Magnolia says she tried to persuade Erin into the group of people she saved from being beaten or torn apart, that she tested Erin's chess in the hope she could be useful, but that her main goal was to sequester Erin from the world where she could cause no harm.

Magnolia says she found the Earth-born because they were in danger, two groups having already been slain by monsters before she knew to act, that she saved Imani nearly too late and found Rose and the others more easily, and that she questioned them about their world using [Charm] to persuade them to reveal more.

Magnolia tells Erin that she decided that Erin, Ryoka and anyone else from Earth must not be allowed to talk freely once she saw the difference in technology, naming guns among other things, and says the existence of another world would drive many kings into a frenzy and a war her world would lose.

Magnolia says that none of the Earth-born she found knew exactly how to make such weapons, which changed her beliefs again, and she has a trembling voice as she says that their technologies would ruin this world.

Magnolia says that a few experts and a worldly confidant assure her it will take years and much groundwork to reproduce Earth technology on a large scale, and that she will search the world for traces of such preparation and quash it.

Magnolia tells Erin she is considering sending the Earth-born out with a few guides as Bronze-rank adventurers with a gift of coins and some items, and that she will not let them die, but thinks non-life-threatening injuries and terror would be good for them.

Magnolia tells Erin she will never create guns and other Earth weapons unless someone else has already spread them until they are commonplace, since a thousand reasons include that it would destroy this world; she says Ryoka knows this and has avoided her for fear she would use them.

Magnolia says that tanks, planes, bombs and guns would let even children kill the greatest warriors, that nothing stays secret for long, and that if guns spread, the House of Minos would fall to its ancient enemy and the Antinium would sweep across the continent in less than a decade.

Magnolia refuses to tell Erin where Ryoka is, honoring Ryoka's discretion as a Runner, and calls Ryoka a gamble, saying every person of note on the continent gambles for high stakes except the Antinium Grand Queen, who only takes safe bets.
Magnolia asks Erin how much she knows about Klbkch the Slayer's past.

Magnolia says she has no enemies on this continent, or so it is said, yet considers the Antinium Queens her greatest nemeses, because the Antinium fight under the assumption that all soldiers are equal and do not level.

Magnolia tells Erin that in this world a single hero can win a war because people level, so armies protect or risk their highest-level warriors, and a hundred Level 15 [Soldiers] are not worth the life of a single Level 30 [Vanguard].

Magnolia believes the Antinium Queens once attempted to wipe this continent of every living species, that the Antinium leave no survivors and make no permanent peace, and that they have been waiting since the last Antinium War to fight a final war and slaughter everyone.
Magnolia tells Erin that war is coming, a world war such as Erin's people have spoken of, and that the arrival of Erin's people has ended a torn peace.

Magnolia lists threats from whispers: the Isles of Minos closed to all but their own ships with her spies there gone quiet, a Goblin Lord emerged in the south, Az'kerash building an army of the dead, and Flos going to conquer, whom she calls perhaps the least dangerous; she says all this happens because of Erin's people.

Magnolia calls Lyonette de Marquin a dreadful girl who wrote her several strident letters demanding hospitality, and tells Erin that she chose to let Lyonette die and does not regret it, just as she does not regret confining the Earth-born.
Magnolia tells Erin she is worth two Antinium Soldiers in a battle, while Ryoka with items might defeat a dozen or two dozen, though she doubts it.

Magnolia hopes Erin will persuade Ryoka to visit her, saying Ryoka's cheaper defensive potions and alchemist creations will save lives, but farmers will be hard to convince to grow spicy peppers and bottles are expensive, unless it can be made into a spray as Rose claims.
Magnolia sends Erin home in a carriage stocked with enough food for Erin and Reynold for a week.
Ressa is Magnolia's maid and childhood friend and disapproves of the raspberry tea Magnolia drinks like water, sweetened to be practically poisonous, as much for the caffeine as for the sugar high.

Magnolia tells Ressa that Erin had [Unerring Throw] and is resourceful, and that she expects Erin to cause the Queen in Liscor a lot of trouble while an Antinium delegation makes its way towards the city.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Magnolia tells Ressa that no one pays attention to Goblins until it is too late, and that Teriarch convinced her thoroughly of that point.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Magnolia wants a second hand of equal ability for Zel Shivertail, so that with his services she would have a peerless army with a general to match, and orders fifteen more letters to a certain [Strategist] whose replies to her missives have so far all been ignored.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: A history of the Antinium Wars states that the young Lady Magnolia Reinhart, Lord Tyron Veltras and General Sserys were among the few who knew of the Antinium's arrival early, that it is unknown how Magnolia and Tyron learned of it, and that Magnolia took the news most seriously and began contacting other prominent lords and leaders of the Human city-states.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: The same history credits Lady Magnolia with bringing a Human army of over a hundred and sixty thousand to Liscor in Issiysil's darkest hour, despite the Human city-states being divided.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: The history says that the young Magnolia gathered influence and support, seized power among her family in a swift and bloodless coup, and had every Gold-rank and Named adventurer in the north offered exorbitant sums to act as vanguards and special units.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: The history says that Lady Magnolia was spotted on the battlefield inspiring troops from behind her house's elite personal guard, unusually for nobility, though she did not fight.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: The history says that Magnolia returned north after the battle for Liscor, having lost her taste for war, but remained instrumental as a diplomat who convinced wavering allies to aid embattled armies and campaigned to maintain pressure on the Antinium.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Erin tells Ryoka that Magnolia holds a group of younger people from Earth who want to become adventurers but whom she does not want to leave, since she fears they will tell the secrets of their world, and that Magnolia knows about guns.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Erin tells Ryoka that Magnolia tried to use a Skill on her that did not work, because Magnolia wanted to know whether Erin could be trusted.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Teriarch tells Ryoka that Reinhart has acquired several children from Ryoka's world whom he could question.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Magnolia asks Ressa whether she could use a tablet from the young people while talking by spell, has Theofore the [Assassin] brought before her by two silvery metal Golems, and tells him she wants to send a message to his Guild; two other [Assassins] lie dead and still smoking in a corner of the room.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Magnolia warns Theofore that she did not bring him to be killed nor interrogated, given the magical wards of his Guild that stop him from speaking, and tells him she will ask a few questions; she threatens to have a Golem tear off his arm if he asks another stupid question.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Ceria Springwalker thinks that no one refuses a request from one of the Five Families without good reason.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Ceria thinks that every garrison of every major city in the north would mobilize at Magnolia Reinhart's word if she so ordered.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: A speaker tells the party that Magnolia's estate lies next to the city of Invrisil.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Magnolia offers Ryoka tea, biscuits or a knife to the throat, studies her face as a cat studies a mouse, and says she has a [Sense Intentions] Skill that she is quite adept at using.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Magnolia drinks tea so sweet that Ryoka puts down the cup at once.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Magnolia says the Earth-born are guests as long as her patience allows, and calls them pestilential, inconsiderate brats.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Magnolia takes a monocle from a pocket sewn into her dress, studies Ryoka through it, then tucks it back into her secret pocket.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Magnolia asks Ryoka what she would do if she asked Ryoka to tell her everything she knows, and the words strike Ryoka like pink lightning, opening her mind; Ryoka resists as she did against Teriarch's geas.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Magnolia's dress has ward spells to prevent staining.

section: Antinium Wars, her scheming and Invrisil (Books 2-3)
text: Magnolia tells Ryoka that she is rich enough to buy a Walled City, and says she expects the parfait that the Earth-born describe to earn her tens of thousands of gold coins once one of them figures out how it is made.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia tells Ryoka she only wants ice cream, cake with frosting, whipped cream and cotton candy, which Ryoka reads as the start of Magnolia's wish to monopolize every invention from her world; Magnolia admits Ryoka has figured it out and that she intended to have her teach one of her [Chefs] treats before asking for the rest.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia tells Ryoka that she could destroy an army of ten thousand soldiers with guns, several tanks and aircraft in less than ten minutes, but that a million guns would change the world, because numbers would decide wars and the most numerous races would conquer the others.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia tells Ryoka that she does not want to create guns or let such secrets spread, and that she will prevent this world from seizing such weapons if she can; Ryoka does not know whether she can believe this, since she cannot trust Magnolia with the knowledge of how to make guns.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia says it is inaccurate to call Nemor a Great Mage.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia cannot see Frost Faeries, and Ryoka realizes this when Magnolia asks what she should be staring at.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia tells Ivolethe that the mansion and land around are hers and that Ivolethe is not welcome, and the word "Begone" sends the Frost Faerie screaming out of the courtyard as if set on fire.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia tells Ryoka that from this moment they must be allies, because she must pursue peace with the Antinium and learn what they know, and because Ryoka will not live with her as an enemy.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia makes Ryoka her official guest, saying she will feed her, and says she will allow the Winter Sprite back on her estate if Ryoka can find her, because she would like to talk to her.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia says she is clearly an ally of sorts because she can stop the world from using guns.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia commands "Be silent, Nemor," and he recoils with his hands at his throat, but he shakes off the effect and answers when she asks the [Assassins] who sent them.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia and Ressa teleport away with a turn of one of her rings and reappear in the courtyard no more than a hundred feet away; lightning from a rain cloud over her courtyard kills the attackers, leaving only Nemor and one [Assassin] who flees.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia points at Nemor and a thin line of light from a ring spears through his shield and chest and then expands into a column of fire, leaving only a crater of black ash where he stood.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia tells Ressa that no one reporting anything unusual means their spies are compromised, and says that if her great grandmother's diary is right it will be a nightmare.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia decides to gather her flight of attendants, her allies and anyone who can be trusted, from the Reinhart estate in First Landing, a place she hates, and to leave that night with Reynold's coach.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia declares that no injured servant in her employ will lose their job.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Magnolia says that, as allies, she will arrange for Ryoka to meet the best magical experts in Invrisil the next day about the relics Ryoka's adventurer friends uncovered.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Ryoka notes that Magnolia suggested and will pay for the artifacts from the dungeon to be appraised by the most reputable [Enchanter] in Invrisil, although Ryoka must pay for any repairs.

section: Alliance with Ryoka and the attack on her estate (Books 3-4)
text: Ivolethe sees that the books in a grand library of the mansion are all first-edition and spotless, with spells in their bindings to protect the pages.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia arrives at the Melissar estate in a pink carriage pulled by ghostly horses that use mana to move at extreme speed, accompanied by her tall stern [Maid] Ressa; she wears a long pink-and-green gown, and has standing orders for her carriage drivers to run over any [Bandits] they meet.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia is a high-level [Lady] who strides gracefully, in no mood for formalities, and threatens to kick any servant who bows to her as she hurries in.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia notes that young Eliasor of the Melissar family must be eight, and Bethal corrects that she is nine.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia senses the mood in the room swinging towards an unexpectedly convenient solution to the crisis, which she thinks too convenient; she notes that voting against the resolution without a solid reason would have consequences.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia studies a Minotaur envoy, a trained [Courtier] whom she has never seen in a diplomatic role, and replies that the proposal is probably a trick in the sense that the Minotaurs will honor their word and then demand something else, perhaps the lands that belonged to Flos.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia swears to Eliasor, now head of the Melissar family after her mother Lady Patricia's death, that Patricia was one of her confidants and a trusted friend, that she fears the death was her fault, and that she will find those who ordered it and kill them all.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia calls Ladies Bethal, Pryde, Wuvren and Zanthia to her, tells them to summon their most trusted protectors and soldiers, including Bethal's husband and her Knights of the Petal, says she is reforming her entourage, and announces she will return to the family estate to take an army from her grandfather.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Typhenous's [Message] reaches Magnolia as a scroll that Ressa hands her in her moving carriage, and is relayed to Lord Tyrion Veltras at the same time; Ressa utters words that make the driver swerve, and Magnolia stares silently at the snowy landscape.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia sits in her carriage pulled by spectral horses, eating cookies from a tray, and tells the Mayor of Leadenfurt, Wullst, whom Ressa has brought in, that it is a pleasure to meet him; she throws a plum cookie out of the door and tells Reynold to clean blood off the carriage that she thinks came from a young Wyvern.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia declares before the Reinhart armory that she returns to her ancestral home to claim the right of her blood and asks for relics of the past for war and protection, to protect the family's lands, destroy its enemies and safeguard its legacy.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Regis Reinhart, the specter who keeps the armory, tells Magnolia that she has proven a worthy scion over the decades she has ruled the family and returned more riches to the vault than she took, so she may take what is needed and no more.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia kicks Regis in the shin and says that the motto is to give more than you take and that by rights she should walk out with a quarter of the armory's contents, adding that they do this every time.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Regis tells Magnolia that the Circle of Thorns haunted her grandmother, whom he aided, and that she died with their curse still lingering over the family, which troubles him.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia tells Regis that a Goblin Lord crushed two Drake armies of ten thousand each, led by a Gnoll [General] and a Drake [General] from a Walled City, and that a single [Scout] made it out of the massacre.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia predicts that the Goblin Lord will not attack Liscor but will march past and sack northern cities, trapping himself on the north side by spring, and notes that the Necromancer and the Antinium both failed to bring down Liscor's wall in a month.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Regis taunts Magnolia about the scaled disgrace of a lover she trysted with, and Magnolia, saying she will not be lectured on her private affairs, replies that Teriarch would refuse to help her and that he has told her he could dispel or destroy Regis's enchantments for half the treasury, which she refused.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia demands the Crown of Flowers, a laurel wreath of glowing flowers, one of the three great treasures of the armory, saying its power would end any Goblin threat; Regis refuses because there is no Goblin King, only a Lord.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia tells Regis that a Great Goblin Chieftain that fought for the last Goblin King has been living at Dwarfhalls Rest and seeks to join the Goblin Lord; Regis says he recalls such Goblins, akin to Goblin Lords but lacking the drive to be Kings.

section: War councils and the Reinhart armory (Book 5)
text: Magnolia says she is levying soldiers from every city from there to Invrisil, about forty thousand, to attack the Great Chieftain first and then the Goblin Lord.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia tells Regis that Tyrion Veltras is also raising an army against the Goblin Lord, which makes Regis agree to give her everything she asked for and more, and he calls her an impertinent brat but a good head of the family.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia orders Ressa to have word sent to Lady Bethal to hunt down a Goblin Chieftain waylaying travelers on the road with her Knights of the Petal and Thomast, whom Magnolia thinks could outduel any Chieftain living, and to join Magnolia later at Dwarfhalls Rest.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia tells Ressa that she has assassins to deal with, the Antinium, Az'kerash, and now the issue of otherworlders that Regis does not know about.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia tells Regis that a [Necromancer] may raise only a single army, however strong, which is less dangerous than six Antinium Hives, and that killing one Antinium Queen means the rest will lead her Hive; she says she will kill Az'kerash when she is ready or when he makes a mistake.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia leaves the Reinhart estate with her soldiers and arms ready, and the family flees when she comes out of the stairwell pointing a magical artifact of devastation at them.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia owns two magical carriages, which is more than most kingdoms have; her personal one is maintained at all costs, while the other lacks the resources and [Mages] needed to repair it, and refuses to start.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia shouts in fury on hearing from Sacra that an [Emperor] lives in Riverfarm, learns of Lady Rie, and orders Reynold to drive at once to Lady Rie Valerund's estate.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia strides through the destroyed town past a large group of Silver and Gold-rank adventurers who part before her, and orders that Lady Rie be alive or she will hold every adventurer there accountable.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Sacra, the [Maid] who pretended to be the Silver-rank adventurer Odveig, tells Reynold of her undercover mission to learn who the stranger that Ryoka met was, and that he is an [Emperor].

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia's presence freezes the servants, guards and adventurers in the room, except Reynold, Sacra, Ressa and Rie, when she asks Lady Rie why she is packing to leave; Rie, a low-level [Lady], says she no longer considers her home safe after the Goblin attack and that she would be dead but for the intervention of Laken Godart.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: In a vision of the past, General Sserys tells Zel Shivertail that a human girl younger than seventeen, Magnolia Reinhart, led an army to the Drakes' aid, that she threw up after battle, and that she wanted peace to save the world and looked more than a [Lady] when she smiled.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia tells Zel Shivertail that her one dream is peace, to save the world, that she will do anything for it, and when he agrees to help she says they will begin with the Goblin Lord, then Az'kerash, then the Antinium.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia's servants are like her fingers; many are ordinary [Maids] and [Manservants] who cook and clean, but others are assassins, spies, warriors and mages who resolve her issues across the continent, which gives her the reputation of the Deadly Flower Blooming in the North.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia's right foot jiggles before a sugar rush, her tea is a slurry of sugar, and Ressa takes her cup away and snatches the sugar bowl from her.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia tells Zel that her highest-level Skill is [Aegis of Grace], which extends across her lands and wards off attack from any settlement affiliated with her, such as her mansion and Invrisil, so that casual [Bandits] and monsters are deterred.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia suspects that the Goblins raid other settlements because her [Aegis of Grace] protects hers, and says peace brings prosperity and with enough money she can do a great deal.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia tells Zel that she always intended to kill Az'kerash, sooner rather than later, with a short list of about six individuals of whom only one was a true [Assassin], with her first choice the leader of the Forgotten Wing Company, Three-Color Stalker, whom she calls one of the most deadly [Rogues] in existence.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia says Three-Color Stalker never answered her letters, ate two of her gold-leaf cards, and after the sixteenth letter sent a badly decomposed muffin by City Runner that had been in transit for about six months.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia asks for milk with honey and pigs in the blanket when Zel suggests them, her [Chef] preparing them.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia tells Zel she has hounded him with letters over the years because she wants him, not just to guide her armies but to form an alliance, and that the second person she has contacted most consistently is Niers Astoragon, the Titan.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia says the most powerful army would have a world-famous [General] and an unbeatable [Strategist], Zel and Niers, and that she already has the [Mage], a magic user beyond any other, who would join once she has both.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia says her goal is not an empire but a resolution to the world's issues, beginning with a new army to deal with the Antinium and the Necromancer, like General Sserys's army, and with ending the senseless war between Drakes and Humans.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia says she would open the High Passes and encourage Humans and Drakes to settle in each other's lands.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia lists the world's major issues as the Demons of Rhir, the Emperor of Sands in Chandrar, the King of Destruction, the Terandrians, the state of war in Baleros and the Roshal slavers.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia tells Zel that there was an attempt on the Blighted King's life the previous week, that the King of Destruction stirs from his slumber, and that a new [Emperor] has emerged in Chandrar, the Emperor of Sands, who controls a good sixth of the continent.

section: Zel Shivertail, Riverfarm and the coalition plan (Books 5-6)
text: Magnolia envisions a centralized peacekeeping force of all nations and a governing body beyond [Kings], with the Goblin Lord and the Antinium as the first step, and says she will bring peace to Izril so she can send five, six or eight armies against the King of Destruction.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: Magnolia refuses to let Tyrion Veltras, whom she calls an idiot, shine against the Goblin Lord, and says she does not want a [General] for just a few weeks but wants Zel for the long term.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: Magnolia asks Zel to deal with an [Emperor] who has popped up close to her lands, saying she has a problem with loyalty and hired killers at the moment, dislikes [Emperors] because they have nasty tricks and a [Lady] is disadvantaged against them, and that her charming Skill cannot sway anyone with a powerful class or strong will, as she learned recently.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: Magnolia asks Zel to call her Magnolia and says they are allies and she hopes friends; Zel replies that they are allies, not friends, and he still does not trust her, although she gave him his armor.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: Magnolia orders her two War Golems to blast a hole in a walled hedge maze at her personal estate, causing a battle between Ressa, Zel and an enraged [Druid] gardener.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: Magnolia addresses the gathered leaders of the northern cities, telling them that a Goblin Lord with an army of tens of thousands marches on Invrisil, raises the undead from every city he destroys, and has destroyed two Drake armies, while Tyrion Veltras is gathering his own forces elsewhere.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: Magnolia silences a noisy crowd with a clap of her hands so that no one can speak.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: Magnolia has Ressa record a speech by Zel with a spell on a small crystal, and plans to have her agents sell copies of the recording for perhaps a thousand gold pieces each, wanting to be first to sell the information about Zel.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: A history of the Antinium Wars states that Magnolia led a counterattack from her estate on the Goblin King's forces, appearing two weeks after the Sacrifice of Roses with another army a hundred thousand strong, despite having committed almost all of her family's soldiers to defending First Landing.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: The history says Magnolia summoned the army of plant-based constructs with the artifact known as the Crown of Flowers, whose powers are a well-guarded secret, and that the constructs grew out of the ground around her estate and marched south.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: The history says Magnolia was forced to negotiate with the Assassin's Guild to ensure that neither her life nor the Crown would be targeted for the duration of the war.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: The history says the victory over the Goblin King's army earned Magnolia the title of the Deadly Flower Blooming in the North, since she had shown the Goblin King her thorns.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: Magnolia says she has been preparing ever since the Second Antinium War ended, and her War Golems and magical artifact have been reviewed; she says she cannot easily conscript adventurers outside the defense of Invrisil but will double the reward for Gold-rank adventurers.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: Magnolia says she paid Krsysl Wordsmith, an eager young [Writer], to write the first history of the Antinium Wars shortly after the war ended, but did not fund the second history.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: Magnolia says the magic user she relied on stalled the Goblin King for a few days in the High Passes but excused himself from the war, since the Goblins were not his enemy, much to her displeasure.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: A speaker, apparently Magnolia, warns that Human [Lords] and [Ladies] might leave the Drakes to fight alone or turn help into a dagger in the back if Lord Tyrion marched south of Liscor, and says Tyrion still dreams of conquering Izril.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: Magnolia watches the Goblin Lord's army from the fields beside Sacra, who wears thick metal armor, and eighteen other [Maids] and [Servants] who are former spellcasters and warriors armed with magical artifacts and out of uniform.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: Magnolia orders in the name of the Reinharts that the two War Golems in covered wagons slay the Goblins; the wagons explode and two metal giants, built in the era of Archmage Zelkyr's Golems to slaughter armies by the thousands, run on all fours shrieking and cut down Goblins with razor hands and a red beam.

section: The Goblin Lord campaign and the Antinium Wars histories (Book 6)
text: Magnolia uses the Skill [Deft Hand] to push arrows out of the sky, as Bethal uses her [Tranquil Skies] Skill, and then [Polite Deflection] to make a Goblin charge swerve around her and her escort.

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: Magnolia tells Bethal that Humans do not always act in their people's best interests and that her enemies would let a city of hundreds of thousands burn to hurt her; she adds that Zel Shivertail realized how lackluster a force he was given but chose to lead it, believing he can win.

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: Magnolia uses a Skill to whisper "Look over there" to Zel and his head turns toward the Goblin Lord, then she calls out to the War Golems, which charge toward the Goblin Lord while Bethal's Rose Knights cut into the army.

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: Magnolia takes from Ressa the strange tube her grandfather Regis gave her and activates it with the command Thaurmodenasium; a cone of silence bursts out, then sparks multiply into lightning forming a dragon, ships and warriors, trailing a script that reads "From the armories of the Emperor of Storms: a gift."

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: Magnolia declares to Ressa that she will offer a million gold coins or whatever artifacts she owns, spread among the Assassin's Guilds in every part of the world, to have the Necromancer dead.

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: After Zel's death, news spreads that the power of Magnolia Reinhart was shattered as well, as her army fled the field in disarray, a political blow that would ripple for months.

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: Magnolia commands the defense of Invrisil because no high-level commander is ready and because she is the [Lady] of the land, and she stands on the walls with Ressa behind her holding an enchanted dagger that makes the city's [Mayor] nervous.

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: Over two thirds of Zel's army remains intact, having withdrawn quickly from the Goblin Lord's army without pursuit, though its morale is nearly shattered.

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: Magnolia forbids Gold- and Silver-rank adventurers from fleeing Invrisil, after guards turn back several groups who tried to slip out, threatening an unspecified punishment, and the adventurers stay.

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: Magnolia waits on the walls with her heart pounding and feeling almost entirely fury, and steam rises around her as the cold air heats up, obscuring her spyglass.

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: Magnolia writes a letter to the [Emperor] Laken Godart of Riverfarm, which Lady Rie reads out, professing deep apologies and announcing that she has taken it upon herself to host a gathering of about thirty local nobility, with her close friend Lady Bethal Walchaís, at his estates in Riverfarm a week later; Laken says the apology is a lie.

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: Magnolia says she is willing to enjoy being a cold-hearted tyrannical bitch, as an Earth girl called her, and that if the children from another world are alive they may return to one of her holdings, so long as they behave properly around her servants, who are not slaves.

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: Magnolia tells Ressa that Lady Rie will try to help Laken by being as helpful as possible, which will do more harm than good, and that the real test is whether Laken notices and how he represents himself at the party, so Sacra, Bethal and Thomast will evaluate him.

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: Ressa has grown up around Magnolia all her life; she is good at serving tea, running a household full of servants and cutting throats, whereas Magnolia is a people person.

section: Zel's death and the defence of Invrisil (Books 6-7)
text: Magnolia gives Sacra a ring from her middle finger that can destroy much of a building when twisted and aimed, which Ressa thinks is an open display of power and threat when Magnolia wears it and a declaration of war when Sacra wears it.

Magnolia wonders why Tyrion hesitates to attack when the Goblin Lord is headed straight for Tremborag, the Great Chieftain of the Goblins, whose forces could make the Goblin Lord's army strong enough to destroy major cities.

Magnolia tells Ressa that she is tired of dancing to other people's tunes and that Laken Godart has one chance to prove he is worthy of his class, or she will destroy him and his empire where it stands.

Magnolia sends Sacra to offer Emperor Laken terms: an immediate cessation of hostilities, recognition of his sovereign rights, and support in the form of connections, trade and political support, in exchange for his refusing for four months to sell, gift or share the secrets of his trebuchets and other weapons of war with any other party in Izril.
Magnolia proposes through Sacra a binding contract enforced by magic, authenticated by a third party such as Wistram, as is common among the nobility when trust or a grave matter is at stake.

Magnolia writes in a letter to Laken that she is content to suffer his presence on her continent and foresees benefits from a relationship with his empire, but that her goodwill goes hand in hand with her demands, ending by telling him to keep his trebuchets out of sight.

Bethal speaks to Magnolia by magical earring from outside the Unseen Empire, recalling how they met, when Magnolia slapped her and told her to run or be cut down with her family; Bethal says she is done killing Goblins for a while and wants sixteen Knights of the Petal to meet her, and Magnolia replies that she needs Bethal closer to home because Tyrion is moving.

Magnolia sends a direct [Message] to Lord Tyrion Veltras, which surprises him with its directness, and he answers that he will not be swayed from his course and will counter her attempts to the full extent of his ability.

Magnolia meets her inner circle of Ladies in her parlor, Lady Bethal Walchaís, Lady Zanthia, Lady Pryde and Lady Wuvren, with only Ressa present and husbands and bodyguards barred, to put into action a plan to stop Tyrion even at the cost of throwing the north into chaos.

Magnolia tells her Ladies that she would gladly make enemies of her peers to stop a war, in answer to Wuvren's warning that Tyrion will never forgive her; Zanthia says they may all be dead in a few months but tells Magnolia to strike at the right moment.
