Magnolia tells Bethal that Tyrion's wife and a Drake [Assassin] were found dead together when Sammial, his youngest, was not six, and says she herself told Tyrion that the Walled Cities sent the [Assassin], hired in Zeres and funded by their money, having made sure of it herself.

Magnolia appears by projection before the Veltras estates with Ressa and tells Tyrion to turn back from Liscor with the Goblin Lord's head, or he will have nothing to come back to; she silences Tyrion and Jericha with "Be silent," shows projected images of her allied Ladies close to the kin of other Lords on the battlefield, and Tyrion tells Jericha to cut the connection and then turns away.

Magnolia tells Lady Zanthia and the others that a letter from a noble of one of the Walled Cities leaves the door open to an invitation to a soiree or gathering, which no Human noble has had in a long time; she acknowledges the cost of her decision but believes it correct.
Magnolia tells Bethal that no one wins a war, and that she and the others only stopped it from being a larger one.

Magnolia tells Ressa that she wants to kill the Necromancer without forcing a war, and that she cannot yet take him or the Antinium off the board until she is sure they would win; Ressa notes that the bounty Magnolia placed is not drawing the people she wanted.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia wakes reluctantly each morning, asking Ressa for another hour, and she is called the Deadly Flower Blooming in the North, head of the Reinhart family, and one of the most famed and feared Human women in the world.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia's main pink carriage is pulled by two ghostly horses, its wheels levitate a few inches off the ground, and it can reach insane speeds, over a hundred miles an hour, and even fly.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia's main carriage enchantment is malfunctioning, because the encounter with the Goblin Lord damaged its wards beyond the ability of the [Enchanter] Hedault, who says a [Mage] of Wistram should repair it.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia owns Invrisil, the City of Adventurers, the surrounding demesne, and a few other properties as her main holdings, although the Reinhart family possesses far more land; Talizmet lies on her lands.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia approves of the Bronze-rank team Haresbane skinning a boar for a village without wasting meat and has Ressa add them to her list.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia guarantees a bounty of twelve gold pieces on each Ogre head and thirty for the leader, to bring any Silver-rank team to deal with Ogres raiding a village.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia refuses Ressa's suggestion that she answer insults with assassination or move on the Assassin's Guild after its refusal, because she wants peace, has received an invitation from her Drake counterparts, and does not have the Assassin's Guild at her back.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia tells Ressa that destroying the Assassin's Guild would require killing them all, that she grew tired of killing people and never wanted to be good at it, and that it has taken her decades to foster the idea of peace among the nobility.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia says it is better to be less feared than she was a decade ago, than to have even children checking their plates and cups when she passes, because she missed their smiles.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia refuses to hand the Earth-born magical gear, telling Ressa that they arrived with nothing, half of them stealing from honest people within the first day, and expected magical swords and heroes' treatment; she says they may use magic swords once they prove they can fight without them, that she will give a spellbook to anyone who masters a spell, and sponsor any who excel in a profession.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia believes that the Circle of Thorns sent the [Assassins] that came after the insults from some who joined Tyrion's army, while everyone else assumes she still has a contract with the Guild, and she agrees that at least one noble in Tyrion's camp belongs to the Circle of Thorns.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia declares a [Trade War], bringing her hand down on a coffee table with a Skill that shakes the table, the floor and the mansion, and has Ressa send [Messages] to Invrisil's Merchant's Guild and her other affiliates.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia's Trade War raises the price of barley by four coppers a pound for anyone buying and selling in Vite lands and other estates, and she tells the heads of the Merchant's Guild at her gates that they may sell to her competitors only at one and a quarter times the rate they charge anyone else.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia plans to leak truthful gossip to enraged brides-to-be, writing letters from her little black book, and asks for trustworthy Couriers or City Runners; Ressa thinks of one name that has come up lately but does not say it.

section: Trade War and the Drake alliance (Books 11-14)
text: Magnolia plans to sail by sea to meet Drake Ladies of the Wall of Salazsar, Helessia Gemscale and Navine Gemscale among them, with over a hundred gifts packed, to end the conflict between Humans and Drakes; Ressa worries about the quiet Assassin's Guild and the Circle of Thorns.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia, on the walls of Liscor with Ladies Pryde and Wuvren, asks for a [Scrying] spell to Wistram's new television network and speaks to the world, introducing Liscor's Council members Krshia and Lism and Watch Captain Zevara, while Tyrion Veltras stands on the walls watching her smile at him.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia points out to the broadcast a flood of Antinium marching down Liscor's street, with Xrn the Small Queen striding beside Klbkch and Pivr, Xeu, Tersk and Dekass, including Flying, Silent, Armored and Painted Antinium, and says they must be from other Hives, which shocks Zevara, who had not seen them.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia tells the Antinium that an attack on her would be war and a personal affront, and she says to the audience that she believes in unity, that she is a [Lady] of Izril before politics and species, and that when an enemy comes Izril repels it.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Wuvren blows a kiss at Klbkch that passes through him with no effect.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia hands Chaldion diagrams of an elevator and of moving floors, escalators, as gifts of goodwill for his [Engineers], after giving information on Nalthaliarstrelous, a high-level [Druid].

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Erin remembers that Magnolia led the first defence of Liscor against the Antinium, breaking their siege long ago, and some of the crowd cheer Magnolia's name as they remember that during the First Antinium War she led the defense of Izril.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia invites Chaldion to attend a little party in Oteslia in the near future and says she owes Zel Shivertail this much.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia tells Maviola that the Antinium are still enemies, and that the garden of Izril is infested with insects that the guardians of Izril must prune away.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Erin tells Magnolia that she hates her; Magnolia says she is another on a long list and should not be forgiven, and Ressa agrees that the move was incredibly underhanded but better than war.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia's broadcast exposes the Hive's numbers, fortifications and a tunnel leading south, and Olesm sees that the Antinium are double even the largest estimates, so that they could sack Liscor any time.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia sends Maviola El a Potion of Youth won at auction and tells her she cannot reverse her age, and Maviola replies that the El family lacks the coin to chase immortality.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Maviola wonders aloud whether Regis Reinhart holds the lost Mirror of Eternal Vitality, and Magnolia replies that if he does, he will not share it, and that she will tell Regis that it is like him to cling to life.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia leaves handling of the [Assassins] to the Runner's Guild under Guildmistress Godfrey of First Landing, tells Ressa to send [Messages], and says she hates spiders because an old monster has scuttled into her lands.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia appears in a carriage on the street and greets Lady El, with Ressa behind her, while Maviola, who thinks of Lord Reinhart as dead and Magnolia as owner of the land, looks at her.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia writes to Teriarch that she sent Sacra to check on him and that Sacra could not find his cave, and asks about the incident with the Wyverns.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Teriarch's memory slips so that he thinks of Magnolia as sixteen, pestering him with her carriage and a [Maid]-[Assassin], until his notes correct him that she is forty two.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: A speaker in Liscor says that Magnolia Reinhart's aide has come to the city, promised gold and supplies to rebuild, and thanked the people there.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia beams at the door of her mansion at the respectful [Druid] Grand Mage Eldavin, who is Teriarch, and greets him as old man, inviting him in for tea.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia meets Lady Edere Sanito in private without Lord Alman Sanito's knowledge, takes advantage of sugar being scarce in the Trade War, and says she will not lift the Trade War for another month.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia says that being called a coward in flower-language, the black flower of shame, grates, and that Alman knew what he sent her; she recalls she was at the Sacrifice of Roses and Edere was not.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia agrees to settle with House Sanito for a public renouncement of the insult and a gesture of goodwill, plus the couple attending a little party this summer around the solstice, which she plans to attend and calls a personal favour.

section: The broadcast over Liscor and the Antinium Hives (Books 17-18)
text: Magnolia has a personal contract with Stormlord Seagrass for her sugar, and Teriarch waits outside in the carriage, feeding a dog and trying to teach it to bow.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: Magnolia returns in her pink carriage with Teriarch to find a mob of Invrisil citizens and angry Lords at her gates, led by Todi, the leader of Todi's Elites, demanding reimbursement for the Golden Triangle scheme; sixteen-foot Steel Golems with swords and shields stand at her gates, and the carriage flies over the crowd.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: Magnolia refuses to repay the crowd, saying she did not tell them to invest, it was their own choice, and that she believes in charity but not in covering for others' mistakes; she silences the mob with a stamp and the word "Silence," although higher-level people can still speak.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: Lord Mel slaps Magnolia across the face and she slaps him back with the Skill [Insult to Injury], knocking him unconscious and breaking his fingers, then tells the Lords to bring their armies or an apology, and has the gates closed on the Lords as the crowd turns to stare at them.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: Magnolia tells Teriarch that her threat against Tyrion's sons was a bluff, as she knew Tyrion would not risk his sons.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: In Oteslia, the First Gardener is told that Magnolia Reinhart is prepared to arrive within a month, and that Wall Lady Navine, her mother and nearly thirty dignitaries from Salazsar are coming.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: Magnolia rides in her carriage to First Landing with Ressa, Sacra and two other [Maids], driven by Reynold, at the request of Lady Aerta, who has learned of the meeting in Oteslia and wishes to accompany Magnolia; Teriarch has reinforced the carriage's spells.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: Magnolia fires the crimson beam from the ring that killed Nemor at a [Blademaster] in the ambush, but a Minotauress grabs her hand and twists the beam into the sky; Teriarch's ring, fit for an [Empress], saves her from a wire trap.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: Magnolia vanishes from the ambush site in front of the [Assassins], Ressa and Tyrion, and leaves the north three days later.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: News in Izril reports that Magnolia Reinhart was attacked and saved by Tyrion Veltras, and Ryoka suspects only Teriarch could have teleported her out of danger.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: Magnolia learns that Sacra is dead and her primary carriage was destroyed or taken, with its tracking spells removed, though her backup carriage is fixed and reinforced by Teriarch; she tells him she will be at sea on the Velistrane until she reaches Drake lands.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: Magnolia evacuates her estates and servants from Izril aboard the Reinhart flagship Velistrane, letting the Circle of Thorns think she has run rather than starting a war until one side is destroyed, as her grandmother faced.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: Magnolia notes that Teriarch has not answered since a strange message, and that reports show Eater Goats and Gargoyles growing more active around the High Passes.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: Magnolia judges that the Healer of Tenbault would refuse to help Tyrion, whose cure no one knows how to find, and that Regis Reinhart would not open his vault to House Veltras.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: Magnolia thinks Tyrion Veltras will sign the contract, and that her side will have to break the enchantment through Regis, Teriarch or an allied [Mage], since she cannot fight on Izril; she hopes he will give in and not let pride break him.

section: Mobs, ambush and flight from Izril (Books 18-19)
text: Theofore is the last [Assassin] in Magnolia's direct employ, and he tells her the poison could be any number or mixed dosage and that a master [Healer] or [Alchemist] who knows poisons is needed.
Maran is a [Barmaid] at the Frenzied Hare in Celum who later works at Erin's inn together with her co-worker Safry.
Maran told Erin that she had bought quartz earrings, and mentioned dancing in taverns and looking forward to city festivals.
Maran and Safry say Agnes docks pay for breaks, pays little and gives no tips, so they asked Erin to hire them.
Maran and Safry said Erin's inn is larger and Erin is easier to work with than Agnes.
Maran and Safry cannot tell Drakes from each other, and served the wrong Drake the wrong food.
They served Gold-rank adventurers before the Drake Zel in the hope of tips.
Maran and Safry are uncomfortable around Bird and the Antinium, and Maran says the Antinium in the Horns of Hammerad was one thing.
Maran and Safry flirted with Halrac, Ulrien and Typhenous.
Maran admired Pisces until Lyonette told her he is a [Necromancer].
Maran refused to fetch water from the stream, citing fish with teeth, Rock Crabs and Shield Spiders.
Maran claimed that having water delivered costs a few silver and is how civilized folk do it.
Maran took coins from Erin's money jar and had six huge barrels of water delivered through the Celum door.
Maran and Safry brought about two dozen Human friends from Celum and took a thirty-minute lunch break during the rush.
They claimed the Innkeeper's Guild's policy gives them a break.
Erin fired Maran and Safry and her [Inn's Aura] Skill drove them out through Octavia's shop.
Agnes later claims Maran and Safry are at Ulna's, who took them in.
Maresar is Venith's wife, a tall, dark-skinned woman with short-cropped black hair and a longbow.
Maresar speaks with a slight lisp, or in a deep, slightly slurred voice.
Maresar says little but has a sense of humor, and Trey finds her hard to read.
Maresar is a former [Bandit Lord] of renown who pledged her service to Flos after being defeated.
Maresar says there is no [Bandit Lady] class, as all leaders are called [Bandit Lords] regardless of gender.
Maresar's Skill [Eagle Eyes] enhances her eyesight.
Maresar looses two arrows at Flos from a hilltop during his duel with Venith, and Flos cuts the second from the air.
Maresar says she follows her King, calls Venith a fool, and says he will not die while she lives.
Maresar tells Venith that Flos is her King too, and rides away with half their retainers to serve him.
Maresar slaps Flos for leaving them, kisses his cheek, and says that was for coming back.
Maresar leads her soldiers to Flos, and they kneel, having come to fight for him rather than march against him.
Maresar says Venith will return in time, once he sees Flos is back in spirit as well as body.
Flos asks Maresar to lead the archers in his army, though it was not her role before, and she accepts.
Maresar mounts and fires into the fog, hitting enemy mages at the targets Gazi calls out for her.
Maresar kills one mage and distracts two, forcing the enemy [Mages] to scramble for cover instead of dispelling the fog.
Maresar orders her archers to volley the soldiers on both flanks as the fog lifts.
Maresar returns to Venith's side after he joins Flos, and the two stand together.
Maresar and Venith hold Ger, where her bow can reach half the city.
Maresar declines Venith's monocle and judges a group of armed youths no threat using [Eagle Eyes].
Maresar notes that Venith told Calac no, so she refused him too, when Calac wanted to come to Ger.
Maresar and Orthenon dislike each other, since she was a [Bandit Lord] and he hates criminals of all kinds.
Marian is a Centauress [Strategist], one of Niers Astoragon's students, and the friend of the Lizardgirl Umina.

section: A different Marian: the human mage of the Horns of Hammerad (Book 1)
text: Marian is a human mage in the Horns of Hammerad, and the only other human mage in the group besides Sostrom.

section: A different Marian: the human mage of the Horns of Hammerad (Book 1)
text: Marian is a solid Level 16 [Elementalist], ordinary in both class choice and spell selection, who pulls her weight in the party.

section: A different Marian: the human mage of the Horns of Hammerad (Book 1)
text: Ceria does not consider Marian a true adventurer, because Marian only wants to earn enough money to start a store or an inn.

section: A different Marian: the human mage of the Horns of Hammerad (Book 1)
text: Ceria has not worked out whether Sostrom and Marian are sleeping together.
A Centauress named Marian is one of Niers Astoragon's students; Centaurs dislike small places such as his command tent, as horses do.
Marian guesses that Niers' unbeatable chess opponent must be a Dragon, since only a brilliant mind could repeatedly defeat him.
Niers rejects the guess because his opponent switched to a risky style after losing, which he reads as curiosity, whereas Dragons are touchy and hate losing.
Niers calls Marian's guess a good one, and tells her kindly that she could not have known the opponent's behaviour.
Her full name is Marian Felthof, and a young Centaur laborer in the crowd shouts it to cheer her on.
Marian received a great deal of support from her Centaur clan, whose members all contributed money to fund her studies, and she feels she must repay them.
Marian brings back a huge yellowed fang from a freshly hunted creature as her homework for the Professor.
Marian says her Armorgator was over twenty feet long and could swallow a Mossbear whole, boasting to Venaz about it.
Feshi tells the class there is no rule against teaming up, because the Professor's only rule is not to kill anyone, so the class decides on a truce.
Marian tells the table that she and Umina remain part of the truce but will work together as a team to win.
Marian has a Skill, [Rapid Retreat], which makes her cover a three hundred foot dash in three and a half seconds.
Marian carries Umina on her back through Daquin and scatters a group of Dullahans from the Iron Vanguard by charging at them.
Umina talks Lizardfolk sailors into hiding her and Marian aboard their ship in the harbour, and the crew cheers the Titan's personal class.
Marian is seasick and uneasy aboard the ship, because Centaurs dislike boats, the sea and small spaces, and a Lizardwoman hands her a bucket.
Marian has gold and items in a bag of holding, and she carries a tripvine bag that Umina says will not work on elite soldiers.
Marian leads a charge shooting arrows alongside Sir Kelm, and calls [Unit: Freedom's Gallop] to rally the [Knights] behind her.
Marian uses [Hurricane Arrows] on a last dash across the plaza toward the Professor.
A Dullahan [Mage]'s spell strikes her back left leg and brings her down in the plaza before the Professor's platform.
Marian's leg is badly burned by a Dullahan [Mage]'s fire spell, and she can smell her cooked flesh.
An old Lizardwoman [Healer] identifies it as a Tier 2 magic burn, and first applies a caustic cream that hurts badly so the potion can reach the skin.
The [Healer] then treats the leg with a healing potion, the flesh regrows, and she tells Marian not to gallop for a day.
Perorn angrily tells Tulm the Mithril that his fire spell could have killed Marian or crippled her for life, as it seared her to the bone.
Tulm explains that the fire spell was an error by his panicking [Mage].
Perorn rushes to Marian and offers a higher quality potion, which the [Healer] says she does not need.
Niers tells Marian that the flaw of every [Strategist] is weakness in combat compared to [Warriors], after she admits she fared poorly at close quarters.
Niers' reward for Marian is personal instruction from his weapons masters until she can fend off even a Level 30 [Warrior] with a bow.
Marian hugs Umina but says she is not forgiving her yet, because she lost money and must now duel a [Weapon Master] every morning.
Marian demands details of what Niers' room is like and what he says to Umina as payment.
Marian drinks mug after mug of alcohol and becomes cheerful, in line with the legendary Centaur tolerance for it.
In a good-natured argument, Marian and Feshi insist it is weirder not to have breasts, after Umina calls it unnatural that they nurse their young.
Marian stamps a hoof and denies that Nagas are like Centaurs, insisting Centaurs are not half of anything.
Marian and Umina are in Elvallian, capital of the Forgotten Wing Company, while Umina packs to move into Wil's larger quarters.
Wil invited Marian to go with him on his secret sea trip, but she declined because she cannot swim well.
Marian says she can float but Centaurs are not great swimmers, and she would die in a wooden box for a month.
Marian and Umina are sent by the Professor to Talenqual to watch Geneva, with Umina using the code name Dancing Serpent and calling Marian Fast Hooves.
Marian wants to simply make Geneva an offer, since the other companies and the Professor all want her.
Marian talks to Kissilt over a speaking stone, learning that he and Cameral train as adventurers with Daly's Bushrangers.
Mars is a [Vanguard], a variation of the [Warrior] class, and one of the King of Destruction's Seven.
Orthenon tells Trey that Mars is Level 66, the highest-leveled of Flos's group and the second-highest-level warrior class on the continent.
Mars says she is no [Mage] and can do no magic, although she has several magical items, which is what her name refers to.
Mars is called the Illusionist not because she knows illusion magic, but because she possesses many trinkets.
A [Vanguard] is an advanced type of the [Soldier] class, a powerful warrior class.
Mars is the King's Champion, a [Vanguard] who stands at the head of every battle.
Mars appears as a tall woman with flawless skin pale as a moonbeam, red curling locks, huge breasts and a dancer's grace.
Trey suspects part of Mars's attraction is magical, since she is not called the Illusionist for no reason.
Mars has no battle scars, unlike Flos and Orthenon, as Teres snidely points out.
Teres claims that Mars's breasts are fake.
Mars twists a ring and her illusion vanishes, revealing a shorter figure in plain grey armor who is spattered with blood and grime.
Mars's true appearance is a bit plain, with pale skin from lack of sunlight, faint freckles, brown hair and a snubbed nose.
Mars shows the truth only briefly, and by the time the crowd cheers she stands beside Flos with her illusion restored, waving.
Trey realizes the ring and the brooch Mars gave Flos explain it: Mars is no good at magic, but she has a lot of magic on her.
Flos kisses Mars on the forehead and calls her his beautiful vassal, with pride that has nothing to do with looks.
Gazi flicks sand at Mars and her seductive illusion flickers, revealing a shorter, less enthralling woman.
Gazi tells Mars she needs a new artifact for a bad illusion.
Mars's illusions change: her hair is red, then purple, then short-cropped green, with the green guise looking younger and more like a soldier.
Mars asks Teres if she likes the spell as a new look, and Teres asks if all her illusions have huge breasts.
Mars never leaves her armor, and her illusions let her appear as a beautiful woman, changing appearances as Teres changes clothes.
Mars has a hangover in Reim's camp, and the illusion captures even her haggard look, including red eyes.
Mars carries a round shield on her back and a sword at her hip.
Mars says swords are rarely over five pounds unless used against Minotaurs or specialists, and teaches the twins to grip them.
Mars's armor stops lances, arrows, stone shards and boulders, and Mars swings her shield like a mace.
Mars killed the Quinfer, Germina's champion, in a duel that lasted only a minute, then charged into the army.
Trey thinks Mars could have destroyed Germina's army alone if she had enough time.
Mars wades through arrows and a [Fireball] unscathed at Blalevault, and the defenders give up shooting within forty feet.
Mars uses [Grand Slash] repeatedly in battle with Khelt's undead, destroying hundreds of zombies at a time.
The Quarass says Mars uses [Six-fold Grand Slash], able to use it six times for every time a lesser [Warrior] would.
Mars uses [Call of the Champion] against Belchan's army; if no champion answers, it demoralizes the army and any champion classes lose their class.
At Belchan, Mars wields a sword of living fire twelve feet long, a black shield with a snarling face that bites, and a second moonlight-pale blade from her bag of holding.
Mars has used [Call of the Champion] on Jecrass's armies without being answered.
Mars presents Flos with a black bag with glowing symbols, containing a small armory of weapons, armor and magical items for his army.
The bag includes a curved, double-sided scimitar that glows purple.
Mars, Gazi, Takhatres and Orthenon each want to please Flos best, and Mars's gift is a challenge to the others.
Mars bowed her head blushing when Flos smiled at her, and later reaches for her sword at Gazi's insults.
Mars grips her sword with tears falling and rage in her eyes when Drevish's head arrives.

section: Book 5: The war against the Emperor of Sands
text: Orthenon says Mars is on the way and should arrive by midday, sooner if she is marching as fast as he thinks.

section: Book 5: The war against the Emperor of Sands
text: Trey knows only that Mars is a [Vanguard] nicknamed the Illusionist; she is angry that the world does not yet know Flos has awoken, but Orthenon is unruffled by her ire.

section: Book 5: The war against the Emperor of Sands
text: Mars thinks Flos is waiting until he is ready, since she has not seen him on the training grounds in twenty years.

section: Book 5: The war against the Emperor of Sands
text: Mars slings an arm around Trey's shoulder and says she once took a blow from Flos and could not see straight for two days.

section: Book 5: The war against the Emperor of Sands
text: Mars is not suited to leadership, being a [Soldier] who fights rather than leads, and Flos admits she is lacking at other matters.

section: Book 5: The war against the Emperor of Sands
text: Orthenon orders Mars to stay with Flos to guard the city while the others take the field, and she argues, rages and overturns chairs.

section: Book 5: The war against the Emperor of Sands
text: Mars sulks, doing nothing, while the others work, and Orthenon, Gazi and Flos struggle to explain her use outside battle.

section: Book 5: The war against the Emperor of Sands
text: Mars rides past Lord Venith without a word and kicks him in the back as he gets to his feet.

section: Book 5: The war against the Emperor of Sands
text: Mars arrives alone on a hilltop in silver armor with red hair, bare-headed, and Flos calls her his champion and [Vanguard].

section: Book 5: The war against the Emperor of Sands
text: Mars charges the enemy alone; lancers and arrows break on her, boulders break instead of her, and she runs through the enemy ranks.

section: Book 5: The war against the Emperor of Sands
text: A stone larger than a car crushes the mud where Mars stood, and then she walks out of the air itself and runs the [Geomancer] through.

section: Book 5: The war against the Emperor of Sands
text: Mars says she disobeyed Flos's orders to come because Venith's son Calac sent word that Flos was in danger.
Mars camps with her soldiers outside Blalevault in Hellios, and tells Flos the defenders dare not sally out so long as she is there.
Mars sits with Flos in her tent after Blalevault surrenders, speaking softly about the past.
Mars leads about a thousand of Reim's [Soldiers] across no-man's land from Nerrhavia's border force of at least twelve thousand, with no movement on either side.
Nerrhavia reinforces its lines twice until it has over ten times her number.
Flos rides to the border, tells Mars to ride with him, then turns back without charging, and Mars remains and spits in the dust.
Mars charges left in the battle at Khelt, covering Flos's flank.
Mars is normally spoiling for a fight and laughing, even drinking before battle, but looks intense and checks her armor at the sight of the Minotaurs.
Ytol suggests retreat from the Minotaurs, and Flos orders an advance instead, with Mars glancing at Ytol and nodding.
Mars challenges the House of Minos as Champion of the King of Destruction, using [Call of the Champion] to demand they send a fighter or be forsworn.
Sixteen Minotaurs step forward, and Mars beheads the first, Lewril of Maweil, in one stroke with an elongating sword.
All sixteen Minotaurs die to Mars, and the Minotaurs cheer their names as General Ozem declares the lawbreakers' shame ended and honor upheld.
Maughin is a huge Dullahan smith in Pallass, nearly as broad-shouldered as Moore, who wears light engraved steel plate.
Maughin works the forges of Pallass, and says Dullahans there supply much of the southern continent's armor and weapons.
Maughin is Baleros-born, from Invictel in the north, and spent nearly thirty years there before coming to Pallass.
Maughin has lived in Pallass for over six years at the time he gives his citizenship figure, enough for voting rights.
Maughin says he lived in Pallass for the last decade, after thinking he would not grow competing with smiths from home.
Maughin says the Dwarf Pelt puts out better quality goods than he does.
Maughin says he will support the protest if Erin swears Liscor knew nothing of the fines, and she swears.
Maughin offers to take a commission from Erin.
Maughin goes pale when he meets Numbtongue, and then Ksmvr, at The Wandering Inn.
Maughin shakes Ksmvr's hand mainly to make him go away, and says he is unsure why he is there.
Maughin watched the end of the Daquin game through a friend's scrying orb.
Jelaqua wakes in bed with Maughin after a night of drinking, in a female Raskghar body.
Maughin says he enjoyed the night, and answers 'So?' to Jelaqua's embarrassment over being a Selphid.
Jelaqua says she likes Maughin and has danced off to Pallass every day since meeting him.
Maughin is a Dullahan [Armorer] forging a flail for Jelaqua of the Halfseekers, whom he is dating, which causes scandal in Pallass' Dullahan community.
Maughin keeps his head on his shoulders to dance with Jelaqua instead of mingling, and refuses a carrier twice.
Maughin says metal does not hurry, and neither will they.
Other Dullahans begin to dance whole after another [Smith] and Lorent join in.
Mavika is a strong [Witch] who commands crows and ravens, called a great witch by some and among the strongest of her era.
Mavika can make her crows talk, carry messages or do things for her, which Wiskeria says is not like being a [Beast Tamer].
Mavika is one of the senior [Witches] of Izril, and Wiskeria says there is no formal ranking but she is among the most important.
Mavika leads the Marshlands Coven, which Wiskeria says covers all the [Witches] in about three hundred miles.
Mavika looks hunched and bird-like, in grey rags with a dark pointed hat, yellow teeth and bird's eyes overly large in her face.
Mavika keeps a huge raven on her shoulder, and her raven familiar can turn into her.
Mavika speaks in rhymes and in a sibilant voice.
Mavika's crows call "Wiskeria! COME!" in a blended voice that is neither human nor animal, and attack when Wiskeria refuses.
The crows attack Durene when she intervenes, until Frostwing kills two of them.
Wiskeria drives the flock off by cracking a wet cloth like a whip and stunning two crows, ordering Mavika to send her crows away.
Mavika burns Rehanna's hand with a spell cast on a doorknob, and perches on a roof to claim responsibility to Ram.
Mavika tells the people of Riverfarm that those who scorn a [Witch]'s gift must pay the toll, with discourtesy matched by discourtesy.
Mavika bows to Wiskeria, touches her black hat, and tells her "I am the first".
Prost fines Mavika two gold coins, which Alevica pays, and Rie gives Rehanna eight silver as compensation.
Mavika says she was not present when Tillica summoned the coven, that the Circle committed dark deeds in her absence, and that she repaid blood with blood.
Mavika took the Circle's offer from her sister's dying lips and the screams of fools before they died.
In Califor's view, those who slaughtered the Marshlands Coven died painfully at Mavika's hands.
Mavika says the Circle demanded a curse on Magnolia Reinhart and her kin that would boil her by her own skin.
Belavierr recalls that she and Mavika last spoke when they ordained the Witch of Molten Stone as a [Witch] unquestioned.
Mavika offers Riverfarm's crows' services for one week in return for a field of freshly grown corn a hundred paces square.
Mavika promises her flock will eat no blade or seed, kill the rodents in the fields and devour the insects plaguing them.
Mavika demands that no crow be harmed, or she claims the forfeit and three times as many fields.
Mavika says her flock have the [Eyes of Many] and will find whatever hides.
Mavika sets her raven Sephraic on a four-foot Colony Rat mother with [Ancient Form], and it kills the rat.
Mavika uses [Primal Fear] to drive the rats out of their warrens into the waiting crows.
Mavika diagnoses that Belavierr is marked for death by flame, since a single spark now carries the dead [Knight]'s vengeance.
Mavika says Belavierr could remake any ward but needs time she does not have.
Mavika says each flame saps Belavierr's power and her flame wards will take weeks or perhaps months to mend.
Mavika agrees to fly the children and parents out of the fire with Eloise and Hedag, saying her flock will chase pursuers away.
Mavika tells Eloise she cannot shield them from the flame twister, and leaves when Eloise tells her to go.
Belavierr catches Mavika's hand as the crow-witch begins to grow, and warns her that she has everything to lose.
Mavika tells Laken that Belavierr took the life of a fellow [Witch] without cause, and that she is welcome among neither [Witches] nor men.
Mavika carries the news to Anazurhe's Molten Stone tribe that Belavierr slew Califor unprovoked and should be given no aid.
Mavika refuses gold to cure Gralton's lands but agrees to four gold coins' worth of food for her flock.
Mavika knows Drake poisons and their venom, and the coven cures Gralton's poisoned water and dogs.
Mavika tells the coven that Laken paid his promised price on Day 76 and urges caution.
Later, Mavika calls her crows against the Humans who stoned Nanette, and says a Goblin defended a [Witch] while Humans threw stones.
Laken stops the crows, and Mavika storms into the village to remind the Unseen Empire of its pact.
Mavika refuses a seat on Laken's council, which Laken thinks is for the best.
Mavika says protecting is not her craft, only killing, when Laken asks her to escort Eloise.
Mavika asks whether Laken noticed the malice coming from his [Lady] sworn, Rie.
Mavika says her crow familiar has flown to House Veltras, and that the other [Witch] who could cure any ill would die before reaching the manor.
Mavika agrees with Eloise to help, and tells Laken the pact is struck.
Maviola El is the matriarch of the House of El, one of the Five Families of Izril, and is known by the nickname Lady Firestarter.
Maviola El is over ninety years old, and both she and Lady Gresaria Wellfar are over a century old by another account.
Maviola has a Skill that tells apart little girls who lie to her, even when their parents give them tricks to avoid truth spells.
Maviola has the Skill [Like Fire, Memory], and says she was the first to have it, so Erin's fire is the same as hers.
Maviola can call forth an aura of fire, suited for combat, which she uses as a [Lady].
Maviola has orange eyes and hair that is black mixed with orange or red.
Maviola's old Skill is [Deft Hand], with which she shoves people off a hill.
Maviola El sits in a magical wheelchair, old, with white hair and papery skin, in the study of House El, whose ironwood doors were carved over nineteen thousand years ago.
Maviola controls the distribution of wealth among the El family, so she could cut children's families off from gold if she chose.
A half-Elf aide, Zedalien, serves Maviola, closes the study doors and pushes her chair, and is older than she is.
Maviola says her brother Fulviolo El and the Terland twins Petria and Ulva would have been magnificent leaders, but losing Petria broke Ulva.
Maviola says that too many nobles were lost during the Sacrifice of Roses, and that the Goblin King took a terrible toll.
Maviola says she has a Skill that tells liars apart and tells Zeci El to put her hand in the fire.
Zedalien asks whether Maviola is tormenting children with illusionary fire.
Maviola tells Zedalien that she plans to announce her retirement within the week, sooner if she can do it with one last triumph.
Maviola tells Deilan that he will be the next patriarch of the House of El, with Zedalien as her witness for months.
Zedalien says he will retire with her and will stay with Deilan until his replacement is ready.
Maviola drinks an entire Potion of Youth in front of Magnolia Reinhart and the assembled ladies of Izril and becomes a young woman with ember-orange hair mixed with black.
Maviola says she bought her potions from Saliss of Lights with only her own money, and shows three vials remaining, each lasting a week.
Maviola relinquishes leadership of the House of El to Lord Deilan El, saying she is no longer of the House.
Maviola tells Desinee that all her life she has been Maviola, and that she had the nickname Lady Firestarter as a girl, a name only she remembers the reason for.
Maviola walks out of the field as the [Ladies] kneel, then rides south on Lady Bethal's unsaddled horse, which Bethal notices she stole.
Maviola arrives at Invrisil as a young [Lady] with black-and-red hair, little gold and three vials of priceless worth, on a last adventure.
Maviola introduces herself to the Horns of Hammerad as Maviola Imarris, a distant relation of the House of El and an offshoot of the Imarris family.
Maviola says she has not tasted a good cup of wine in eight years, and cries at her first sip.
Maviola is sore from riding Lady Bethal's horse without a saddle, which she stole because of Bethal's eccentricities.
Maviola walks Invrisil's old street and finds that Seatale's Tavern is gone, remembering that she walked it sixty years before.
Maviola collapses to her knees with a slowing heart, and Magnolia urges her up with the words that fire dies when it stops moving.
Magnolia addresses her as Lady Maviola El, and Maviola says she nearly died, thanks Magnolia and declines a carriage, saying she has a meeting to keep.
Maviola walks into the wall of Erin's inn instead of the door, which no longer works for her.
Maviola curses Lady Bethal and her charming husband when she finds her money pouch is stolen.
Maviola is stuck behind the [Bouncer] Redit until she shouts for Ceria, who pays six silver to let her through.
Maviola befriends Olesm in the inn, challenging him to chess, and calls Check while pressing him about the ideas he has not acted on.
Maviola tells Olesm to do the best job he can and inform his superiors, not wait for orders, and Olesm proposes a newspaper, The Liscorian Gazette.
Maviola tells Olesm that they call her Lady Firestarter, kisses him, and gives him [A Little Bit of Courage].
Two days after they meet, Maviola has moved into Olesm's apartment and The Liscorian Gazette is circulating.
Maviola takes command of the Human officers during the relief, telling a [Commander] she outranks him as a [Lady] of Izril.
Maviola collapses aged after a scuffle with Bethal, drinks a viridian vial and says three weeks.
The narration notes that one person has three weeks left to live, among three Great Houses of Izril.
Maviola cooks badly with a burnt breakfast and lectures Olesm on logistics, including donkeys and birth control potions for mixed-gender armies.
Maviola says she never had children and regrets it, and has lived with Olesm for nearly two weeks.
Maviola shows Erin her memory fire, and says she was once matriarch of the House of El, with brother Fulviolo, and a wild girl before.
Maviola explains to Erin that Saliss of Lights's Potion of Youth restored her for a while, and that she stepped down about two weeks ago.
Maviola and Erin's fires merge into an [Immortal Moment] of Erin meeting Knight and Skinner, and Maviola recoils at Skinner.
Maviola relives a memory of the first Antinium war, where she stood with Fulviolo, Petra, Ulva and Lord Dallien Veltras, and Fulviolo told her to stay with the [Archers].
Maviola says she has two more weeks to go, and calls it a beautiful ending, saying fire should burn out fast and she has something to do, teaching Erin.
Maviola trains Erin and Lyonette's auras by shoving them off a hill and teaching that the trick with auras is to force others to break their rules.
Maviola calls Lyonette a prodigy for developing her powers young, and says she is already more powerful in station.
Maviola sets lessons in logistics and bookkeeping for Erin, Lyonette and Mrsha, drawing up a spreadsheet.
Maviola says that Flos was forceful enough of will as a boy to resist the most cunning [Lords] and [Ladies].
Maviola arranges for Erin to consult the enchanter Master Hedault through the Mage's Guild, using the name House El.
The [Scribe] Setil learns that she is the runaway of House El, for whom the House has a bounty on sightings, and plans to send a [Message].
Maviola tells Erin that her plan was flawed, after she shows how to use an aura to stop a riot.
Maviola has one vial of Potion of Youth left, with about two weeks, and is writing letters to Olesm and Magnolia.
Saliss of Lights recognizes Maviola, since she did not change her name and red hair is rare among Humans, and offers more potions for her flames.
Maviola tells Olesm she is on a time limit and cannot say where she is going, and that she has made arrangements.
Maviola tells Olesm that if he ever meets a dark woman named Belavierr he should give her nothing.
Maviola had resolved to ride upon the Hives to end her life, a week's fast ride from Liscor.
Desinee arrives and calls Maviola grandmother in front of Olesm, who faints, and Maviola is identified as the retired matriarch over a century old.
Maviola tells Gresaria that she has about twelve days left, unless something happens.
Maviola and Lady Gresaria Wellfar, the Duchess of Waves, were enemies, allies and in love, and rivals over a hundred years.

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: Maviola and Selys become the first inductees into Erin's secret Earth clubhouse, and Maviola at last understands that Erin is from another world.

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: Maviola tells Erin there is no wall that cannot be broken, since the Goblin King nearly broke First Landing.

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: Maviola says Deilan is a leader first and a good man second, and recommends Tyrion Veltras for anyone fearing for their life.

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: Maviola recommends Soloun Veltras for less dire danger, and promises to write a letter that House El will honor.

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: Maviola drinks the glowing potion left by Saliss labeled Drink me.

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: A red-haired Human baby crawls through the inn, and Maviola, looking different, winks at Mrsha.

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: Maviola is now a woman in her mid-twenties with a stronger aura than before, and she demonstrates an [Aura of Flame] to Embria.

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: Maviola uses a calm blue-green flame and a red fury flame in front of a Raskghar's cell, tricking her into lunging at the bars.

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: Maviola tells Olesm that the Raskghar prey on his morality and will try something if they think they are in danger.

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: Maviola gets Octavia to unlock her alchemy shop for ingredients at sixteen percent over market value.

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: Maviola sprinkles gold leaf on pizzas and decorates a cake with rhinestones from Numbtongue to make the food noble-quality.

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: Maviola invites the Players of Celum and others to an event at Liscor's City Hall in forty-six minutes, and lures a Gold-rank team from Pallass with talk of Pallassian [Senators].

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: Maviola arranges a fancy event in under an hour with a budget of less than a hundred gold.

section: Book 19: Erin's Earth secret and the Raskghar
text: Ryoka has not talked to Maviola El, who has not come into the inn, but Erin promises it is actually Maviola El and Fierre confirms it.
Mendi is a young Dullahan in her mid-twenties and the apprentice of the Selphid Salthorn, who has taught her for eight months.
Mendi wears a new, well-tended cloth uniform with a badge of a falling giant, Salthorn's symbol, sewn on one arm.
Mendi is new to Pomle and fights as a light-footed warrior in cloth armor.
Mendi is a disciple of Pomle and gets to spar fellow disciples even when she cannot fight outside challengers.
Mendi spars a Stitch-Man Hurricane's Fist, blocking without taking a direct punch and landing two hits in the first minute.
Mendi does not press her opponent, which mystifies the other masters, and she backs away from his pressure-point attacks.
Mendi later blocks punches and two kicks, then hits her opponent sharply and apparently cracks his femur.
Mendi grapples a second Hurricane's Fist, kneeing him in the chest and breaking his ribs with a punch.
Mendi is described as a bit overconfident, or tired of foreigners, when she agrees to spar Iratze.
Iratze beats Mendi on the ground with an arm bar, and Mendi taps out, rises panting and bows to him.
Merec is a [Merchant] who receives Laken in the center of his guild.
Merec has never heard of Riverfarm when Laken names it, though he heard of the avalanche there.
Merec is a ruddy-faced man who turns pale quickly at Laken's revelations.
Laken tells Merec he wants food, supplies, livestock and tools for a village of around a hundred people to last the winter.
Laken asks Merec for twelve wagons and guards, at least two adventuring teams, loaded within an hour.
Merec tries to retake command of the talk, then turns genial and professionally good-humored.
Merec asks Laken to swear an oath on a truth spell, since he cannot be sure where the money came from.
Merec makes a very small sound and shrinks back when Durene towers over him.
Merec offers Laken a frothy fruit drink, with profuse apologies, after the truth is established.
Merec offers Gold-rank teams, but Laken insists on hiring the Celestial Trackers and the Windfrozen Riders.
Laken explains to Merec that those two teams did not laugh at his man begging for help.
Merish is a Plains Gnoll Chief Warrior with light reddish fur, standing over seven feet tall, brawny, with dyed blue and white fur in an intricate pattern.
Merish carries a bone axe, wears only light cloth clothing without armor, and says the Tribes send their own pact-warriors to Rhir.
Merish is a [Shamanic Warrior] of the Plain's Eye tribe, and he describes it as a magic warrior suited to heavy fighting whose fur becomes armor and blades cut steel.
Merish tells Cirille his class is his own business at first and answers only reluctantly when she demands it.
Merish leads sixty warriors of heavy infantry himself and commands Gnoll archers, including two hundred archers.
Merish tells Cirille that the Gnolls obey being placed under her command because a [General] said so, but does not believe they will work together.
Merish shakes Cirille's hand after she promises not to take direct command of his forces.
Merish is the commanding officer of a unit of two thousand one hundred and three Gnolls from the tribes, which Quiteil orders Cirille to fold into her own command.
Merish proposes mixed commands, trading his Gnoll [Hunters] for more Drakes and commanding only the heaviest warriors, so others follow if they see Gnolls running.
Merish and Cirille try the mixed formations against Uxel's forces and win handily, and then go on to defeat six groups of Rhir's forces in skirmishes.
Merish's Gnolls join the archers and heavy infantry, with enchanted-weapon Gnolls best where they must stay in the fighting.
Merish fights at the breach with [Enchantment: Flashfire], which blows a Demon's face off.
Merish uses [Enchantment: Leaden Weight] on his second axe to cave in a metal shield.
Merish survives the battle, covered by Drake and Gnoll bodies, though arrows did not kill him.
Merrik is a Dwarf student of Niers Astoragon, whom Niers calls a fine [War Leader] rather than a formal military class.
Niers says Merrik fought several brisk battles against Trolls in the mountains before coming to the academy.
Merrik introduces himself to Perorn as a fighting maniac from Pomle.
Merrik is from Deríthal-Vel, the Mountain Kingdom of the Dwarves, which most people call Dwarfhome.
Merrik claims Dwarfhome has never been taken by force of arms, saying it has surrendered but never been breached or starved.
Merrik can swim in armour, unlike Peki, and he is a Dwarf [War Leader].
Merrik uses [Body of Stone], and his armour hides steel under his tunic.
Merrik says his real Skill is [Giant's Hammer] and he shouts fake Skill names for fun.
Merrik calls [Battalion of Glory] his big one, making his club shine and his allies glow as they charge the Iron Vanguard.
Merrik laughs off hammering a Dullahan [Sergeant] and says he did not know it was her.
Xol's [Attraction Shield] pins Peki to his shield and slams her down, and Xol lifts Merrik and drops him.
Perorn praises Merrik's leadership but says he wasted his best Skill in an early engagement.
Perorn orders Merrik to accompany her on a patrol across her territories, battling monsters and [Bandits].
Merrik tries to dive into the stormy sea to save Peki and is held back by Yerranola and Feshi.
Merrik says he joined the seminar abroad for the adventure and brought his armour and hammer.
Mihaela Godfrey is a Human [Courier], and later the Guildmistress of First Landing's Runner's Guild.
She is regarded as one of the most famous Couriers to run across Izril.
She is rarely active as a Courier in her later years.
She is the mother of Valceif Godfrey.
In her late fifties, she has white or silver hair, many lines and scars, and the build of a marathon runner.
Her eyes are violet torn by yellow, and Ryoka thinks she could pass for a Dragon if the irises were mismatched.
Two days after the Antinium attacked the city of Geir, Mihaela broke through the Antinium lines from within.
She delivered to General Sserys a message written by a young Drake [Lieutenant] stationed in the city.
She says she got her lung damage on her last run during the First Antinium War, when Wrymvr the Deathless poisoned her.
Wrymvr could not hold her on the Courier's Road, but he still got her.
She tells Tritel, Salamani and Hawk to deliver a package together and doubles the delivery fee to send a message.
She knew Hawk was coming north and insisted he join the delivery.
Tritel says she is in a foul mood and would pull off Hawk's ears and tail if he got within a hundred miles of First Landing.
She comes north to Reizmelt specifically to meet Ryoka Griffin and tells Salamani to get lost.
She says she heard Valceif met a City Runner and that this was how he lost his charm.
She says Ryoka sent her a [Message] saying Valceif's death was Ryoka's fault.
She presses Ryoka to say why Valceif lost the charm that would have kept him alive.
Mihaela punches Ryoka in the jaw, side and back of the head before Ryoka can raise her hands, then tells her to heal up because it is a test.
She hits Ryoka a third time in the ribs after the potion, and Ylawes hears something crack.
She tells Salamani he is starting to annoy her, and warns Ylawes she knows his mother and will remove him.
Ylawes thinks that if Couriers had a Named-rank, Mihaela Godfrey would hold it.
She wins against the Silver Swords, Salamani and the crowd with a wand spell, saying "[Transfer Momentum]. [Lightning Bolt]."
The stored lightning hangs almost without momentum, then grounds itself, and Ryoka's [Forcewall] explodes as Ylawes, Dawil, Falene and Salamani are thrown.
She moves with a passive movement Skill and coughs a deep, wet cough.
She rules that Ryoka lacks anti-[Appraisal] spells and fights only with bare hands, and would fail First Landing's Courier test even if someone else gave it.
She says the Healer of Tenbault can restore flesh but cannot remove the poison in her chest.
She calls herself the greatest Courier of Izril and says she will die of the lung damage.
Minerva is a Human [Rogue] who infiltrates the Goblin mountain and blends into shadows.
Minerva keeps a small white mouse named Keri that scurries up her sleeve and rides in her belt pouch.
Minerva's leader is Jackal, and she reminds herself of her grandfather when she looks at an older half-Elf [Mage].
Minerva uses Keri to lure six Goblin sentries into an alcove and kills them with a black dagger.
Jackal tells Minerva that using her pet mouse again is too slow, and she replies that it gets the job done.
Minerva follows Jackal into the shadows with four others.
Garen Redfang's [Blur Dodge] defeats Minerva's lunge and he cuts her down the chest.
Garen later slashes Minerva's belly open, and she drops clutching her sword.
Mirin is a [Mage] of Parasol Stroll, quiet and soft-spoken, and she is about six years older than Trey Atwood.
Mirin carries a parasol, crimson and indigo in Book 10 and indigo and teal at the banquet.
Mirin is the second-in-command of Parasol Stroll.
Ulyse asks Mirin to take part in the Parasol Stroll performance for the King of Destruction.
Mirin conjures a river from the stone floor and air that rushes up to the ceiling, and the water proves real.
Mirin agrees with Ulyse that Smith Daiton's combination-steel blades are imperfect and poor for enchantments.
Ulyse asks Mirin whether she can feel that a pure blade will hold an enchantment.
Ulyse orders Mirin to take her group and burst acid orbs over the enemy during the battle.
Mirin, Ulyse and Esiela of Parasol Stroll approach Flos as the group's [Mages].
Mirin is told that Roshal's mage-collars will not work on Grand Mage Esiela, so she must be prevented from escaping.
Mirin and Palke escort Trey south through Nerrhavia's Fallen from Reim, teaching him magic on the way.
Mirin casts a cooling spell on Trey and reminds him to remember to use magic.
Mirin watches with Palke as Trey boards the ship.
Flos' commanders ask who leads Parasol Stroll with Ulyse gone, noting that Mirin is with Trey.
Mirn is a Drake with dark, nearly midnight-blue scales, an infectious smile and a scar across both his lips.
Mirn is an old acquaintance of the Named Adventurer Onieva, and owns the pub where they meet at that moment.
Mirn runs a bar, though he is a rude Drake.
Mirn cannot cook and serves Onieva stale sandwiches bought that morning, because his bag of holding is poor at preserving food.
Mirn's pub has clients who mostly bring their own food or drink, and someone plays a music crystal of the Queen of Pop.
Mirn's pub has a secret exit, a hole in the basement leading to the 1st floor, and three reinforced and magically locked doors that he installed.
Mirn herds his clients out of the secret exit when the Watch arrives, since they have done this before.
Mirn holds a blade with two razor-sharp edges in a side pocket, and hesitates before leaving Onieva behind.
Onieva tells Mirn to go and buys him a minute, so Mirn vanishes through the trap door.
The Watch finds no Turnscales and no illegal activities in the pub, only Onieva, whom they fight and she knocks out.

section: Book 18: looking for a safe place
text: Mirn is stalking through the crowd in Pallass with Onieva, who says the Watch is cracking down after the riots.

section: Book 18: looking for a safe place
text: Onieva says that Mirn gravitates towards people he needs to protect, and that he did not think he had anything in common with Selys.

section: Book 18: looking for a safe place
text: Onieva and Mirn have been looking for a safe place to establish his bar, where no [Guard] will kick down the door and arrest everyone.

section: Book 18: looking for a safe place
text: The riots put the Watch on full alert, and they go after criminals and deviants when angry, which makes finding a spot harder.

section: Book 18: looking for a safe place
text: Mirn and Onieva cannot use Saliss's laboratory for safety reasons, and cannot go outside the city.
Miss Hastel is a Centaur [Landlady] in Baleros who owns several properties on the street where the Bushrangers live, and keeps the loveliest home.
Miss Hastel has tan fur with dark black spots around her flanks, dark skin on her upper half and dyed blonde hair.
Miss Hastel's apartment is made of stone and is magically cool inside.
Miss Hastel is heavily pregnant with her first child and hopes to welcome visitors after the birth.
Miss Hastel keeps a Centaur [Midwife], whom she calls the best in the city, on call.
The foal comes out the wrong way with its legs tangled in the birthing cord, and the [Midwives] cannot deliver it.
The [Midwives] push the foal back against the contractions, and Geneva makes up a transfusion from the Centaurs outside and cuts Miss Hastel open to extract it.
Miss Hastel stays awake through the operation, since she could not be put to sleep.
Geneva uses healing potion sparingly, by dropper, while stitching Miss Hastel up.
The foal cries and the Centauress survives, so mother and child live.
The [Midwife] Caleffe Umbalt thanks Geneva, who tells her this was a Caesarian section, which only a [Doctor] can do.
Miss Iglesias Theroben is a female [Innkeeper] who runs the Rose's Retreat, an inn in Walta.
Miss Iglesias is described as accommodating, strict, somewhat portly and very gracious.
Miss Iglesias told Ryoka she wanted her rooms not sullied by impropriety or untoward advances toward her all-female staff.
Miss Iglesias thinks of Lady Bethal Walchaís as a paragon of virtue.
Miss Iglesias serves a breakfast buffet of goat's cheese, sausage and vegetables from her own garden.
Miss Iglesias stands on no customs aside from forbidding hanky-panky and horrifically graphic displays of sex.
Miss Iglesias' inn has no stairs, and she gets oats especially for the Centauress Charlay.
Miss Iglesias shakes Ryoka's hand as she leaves, and steps aside when Charlay clatters into the inn.
Montressa du Valeross is a red-haired Human first-year student at Wistram when she joins Ceria's table.
Montressa's parents are of the lesser Terandrian nobility and made a gift to Wistram for her enrollment.
Montressa has pale saffron and topaz eyes and red hair.
Montressa is an [Aegiscaster], which means she specializes in barriers.
Montressa carries a marble-like staff with a hoop head holding a red gemstone and a copper orb circling it that fires [Lightning Bolt].
Montressa is a secret-broker partnered with Beatrice, fairly high in the Revivalist faction.
Montressa tells Ceria she got into Wistram late without taking the exams and has only studied for a week.
Calvaron pays Pisces four small secrets to tutor Montressa.
Montressa, called Mons by everyone, studies her spellbook as Pisces learns [Invisibility].
A year later Montressa has grown into a young woman, two inches taller, with longer hair and more confidence.
Mons tells Ceria she has a knack for ward spells and has gained the Skill [Layered Ward].
Mons still sees Pisces once or twice a week and says he taught her to use [Flame Arrow] more effectively.
Montressa slips out after Blackmage using an [Invisibility] spell and threatens a [Flame Arrow] if he reaches for his wand.
Montressa knows [Flash Step], and remembers who taught her the beginnings of both spells.
Montressa claims to have studied magic for years and won more duels than he can count.
Montressa dreams of the undead attack on Wistram in her second year, when Calvaron told her to run for help.
In the dream a specter has eaten Chaise's face and wears it, grinning and laughing in Chaise's voice.
Chaise and Calvaron are among the dead of the undead attack on Wistram.
Montressa throws up a [Barrier of Air] taught by Pisces in the dream.
Montressa does not dream the next part, in which Cognita tears the undead apart and the Academy takes comparatively few casualties.
Montressa spent months rocking in a corner afterward with [Light] spells in every corner of her room, ostracized in class for her friendship with Pisces.
Montressa still casts a light spell by her bed each night and wards her rooms in case she dreams of the past.
Montressa says she once thought Pisces was right that magic is magic, and that he taught her to animate rats and other small things.
Montressa says that when Pisces opened Archmage Nekhret's crypt, Calvaron died and she saw what undead were.
Montressa says she was a pariah for nearly a whole year until Beza, Isceil, Palt and Ulinde arrived.
Montressa says she fought her way back into everyone's good graces, rose in her faction and leveled.
Montressa says she thought Pisces had tricked her and that she made it happen, and that Beatrice and Ceria were furious at her.
Beza tells Montressa she wanted to see if the rumors were true and found the most talented [Mage] of her year and a secret-broker.
Montressa pulls back her hood in front of Pisces, a bit younger than him by about a year, and fires [Lightning Bolt] from her orb.
Montressa tells the Horns of Hammerad's friends that Wistram mages have apprehended Pisces for his crimes and that he will stand trial in Wistram.
Montressa says Wistram has decided Ceria owes the academy an explanation for consorting with him, and must come, as a prisoner if she resists.
Montressa tells Ulinde to call her Montressa, not Mons, and says they are within their rights to hunt fugitives from Wistram.
Aaron, whom Beza almost calls "Ea-", helped Montressa make her attack orb, which she says is experimental and contains something she will not reveal.
Montressa guards the Silent Box holding the Horns of Hammerad, tense and refusing to hand it over.
Isceil says Montressa will stop having nightmares now that they have got the murderer, and she glares at him.
Montressa identifies Erin Solstice as from Earth and offers to bring her to Wistram to meet others from Earth and go home.
Montressa reveals that Ulinde is a [Spellslinger], Isceil an [Oldblood Magus], Beza a [Spellscribe], Palt an [Illusionist], and herself an [Aegiscaster].
Montressa tells her team she told Erin about Aaron and the others and the safety of Wistram, and wants Erin to leave the inn.
Montressa did not tell Erin about the Horns of Hammerad and gave Erin the false name Elenope, planning to tell the truth once Erin agrees to come to Wistram.
Montressa says Pisces has always been good at deceiving people and that Erin must not know what he was.
Montressa tells Ceria that Pisces killed Calvaron and used Ceria's master's body to unleash the things that killed their friends.
Montressa says that because of Pisces Calvaron is dead, that she and Beatrice never forgot, and that Ceria has no right to call herself a Wistram [Mage].
Ceria answers that Illphres was her master and that Cognita vouched for Pisces to the Council.
After the merchant Farri refuses Beza, one of the three Wistram mages says their faction wanted to rent the Heartflame Breastplate, whose owner is Zel Shivertail's niece.
Montressa tells Beza and Isceil their orders are to grab Pisces and the magic door and Miss Solstice, and that the Horns of Hammerad are fair game outside Liscor.
Montressa says she has heard the Horns are working a job for Liscor in the Bloodfields, and Beza and Isceil object to going after them there.
Beza fears Grimalkin of Pallass as a deterrent to kidnapping Erin.
Palt warns Erin that Montressa outranks him, has orders to bring her to Wistram and is from the Revivalists, one of the biggest factions.
Montressa orders her team to follow the Horns, saying they will all follow them.
Montressa insists Pisces tricks everyone, and that those who trust him will die or suffer.
Montressa casts [Five-fold Arcane Barrier], blocking nearly fifty feet by herself while her staff's orb spits lightning, in the fight against the Crelers.
Montressa freezes at the sight of a Bone Horror, drops her staff and flees, crying that Pisces is a monster.
Pisces rescues Montressa with [Flash Step], takes her hand for the first time since Wistram, and tells her there are worse monsters than him.
Montressa then grabs her staff and raises her shields again just in time.
Montressa bows silently to Pisces after the Horns of Hammerad slay the death from Rhir.
Montressa returns to the inn with Palt and Beza after two weeks away, getting few friendly looks, and Lyonette wonders whether they took Isceil's body.
Montressa and Beza day-drink at the inn, which is not uncommon in Wistram.
Montressa says she made a mess of things, must report on the inn and the Antinium, and that Beza could split from her.
Beza answers that she has orders to sit and watch too, and will not abandon Montressa.
Montressa offers Erin a conversation with friends from Earth, swearing privacy, and Erin declines.
Montressa believes the creation Pisces made to beat the Adult Creler with Ceria was real magic.
Montressa blames herself for Isceil's death, saying he trusted her.
Montressa tells the Mage's Guild [Scribe] she is a Wistram Mage, gets a slip of paper naming the sender of Erin's message, and swears on a truth spell not to report it.
Montressa, Palt and Beza have claimed rooms in the newly finished second floor and are barely alive the morning after.
All three mages hit themselves with [Deafness] spells and roll over.
Montressa and Beza overhear seven young people debating whether pizza tastes like it did back home, and Montressa thinks of "the Solstice effect", Magus Grimalkin's theory.
Montressa decides they should confirm the guests are Earthers and make them an offer first, rather than start a fight in the inn.
Montressa casts [Mass Calm] and a [Forcewall], and uses a barrier to block a thrown log, as Erin's attempt to calm Liscor's crowd with the depression lantern backfires.
Montressa, Beza and Palt reach the inn with Erin after Maviola's [Fast Fireball] and Pyrite's [Power Strike] hold the mob back.
Montressa and Beza plan to remind Erin of her meeting with Hedault, the best [Enchanter] in the region, and flatter him to build connections.
Montressa and Beza bring Hedault to the inn, hoping he will remember them and that Pallass will want Pelt's work.
Hedault has been trying to limit the draw of the inn's runes on mana together with Montressa.
Hedault arrives precisely forty minutes after a politely worded request through Montressa du Valeross.
Montressa realizes she is done hunting Pisces and done with her grudge, having no team left.
Montressa has no team anymore: Isceil is dead and Ulinde has gone to the Halfseekers.
Montressa and Bezale broker businesses between cities through the magic door, using Wistram's name as credibility.
Cedava of Invrisil is their sixth client, after Rufelt and Lasica, Pelt and Hedault.
Moore is a part-Giant [Mage] of the Gold-rank adventuring team the Halfseekers, who stands eight or perhaps nine feet tall.
Moore wears patched clothing and carries a massive staff crowned by an orb of light.
Jelaqua describes Moore as the team's only spell caster, unless Ceria joins them.
Jelaqua says Moore is a quarter-Giant or eighth-Giant, though he is not sure which, and is used to stares.
Moore speaks politely and gently even in a fight, and sits cross-legged on the floor because no chair is large enough.
The Halfseekers, called the Half Freaks, are a Gold-rank team led by Jelaqua Ivirith, and Moore and Seborn are her companions.
Jelaqua says the team has lost a few members recently and came to the new dungeon to explore it and scout for a recruit.
Lyonette sees Seborn drink like a sailor, a pace only matched by Jelaqua's enthusiasm and Moore's capacity for alcohol.
After a party, Moore, Jelaqua and Seborn are hungover, and Moore offers to look after Mrsha with the other two.
Seborn tells Moore that he is thirty-one, and that Moore, Jelaqua and Halassia were all romantics.
Moore remembers Halassia as an old friend of the team, and he can now talk about the past without the old tension.
Moore argues that the Halfseekers were founded to chase a dream, which is why he defends Jelaqua's romance.
Moore is a [Green Mage] who works with plants and earth.
Moore kicks Typhenous before the older mage can finish casting a binding spell, without raising his staff.
Moore taps his staff so that a line of grass sprouts from the floorboards, as a safe and accurate way to measure mana use.
Moore proposes this grass cantrip because a flame spell would risk Erin's wooden inn.
During the inn fight, Moore thrusts his staff into the ground and raises a wall of earth to block Regrika.
Moore calls vines covered in huge thorns from beneath Erin's floorboards to cover himself, Jelaqua and Seborn.
Moore's spells [Barrier of Thorns] and [Thorn Spray] appear against spiders in the dungeon, and he says he has no Tier 5 spell.
Moore wears a [Thorn Armor] spell of thorns and vines in the dungeon fight against the Raskghar.
Moore fights Garen's tribe in [Armor of Thorns] and his skin resists Garen's cut with [Barkskin].
Moore says [Mass Armor of Thorns] covers himself, Jelaqua and Seborn, cuts what they run into, and does not restrict movement much.
Moore casts [Earthen Spire] to seal a cave of bees in solid stone, a spell four times as thick as Ceria's or Pisces' spells.
Moore says [Earthen Spire] is the first spell he earned after the battle with the Redfang tribe, though he levelled in the dungeon.
Ceria and Pisces judge [Earthen Spire] to be a Tier 4 spell because the stone stays in place.
Ceria gives the reward for sealing the cave to the Halfseekers, because Moore sealed it.
Moore teaches the spell to Mrsha over two days, and Mrsha finds it easier than learning from Krshia's spellbook.
Moore asks whether the door will be used as an involuntary translocation spell or a portal effect, since that affects mana cost.
Typhenous says Moore had the idea of a mechanism to attune the door to each lodestone, creating multiple connections.
Moore recharges the door, and Jelaqua says he has managed to juice it up once already.
Moore says recharging the door takes a lot of mana and he is nearly tapped out, but he could cross using a mana potion.
Pisces works a long time with Moore and Typhenous to let Erin switch the door's portal by tapping a mana stone against it.
Moore charges the door so that he and Seborn travel to Pallass, which tires him out, because Seborn refuses to walk to Invrisil.
Moore breaks his fist punching Regrika after she runs her sword through his abdomen, then escapes through a hole in his own earth wall.
Moore tells Erin that the dungeon is protected against flooding, so water will not enter past a certain point.
Moore warns that the moths are probably hungry, and that something or someone woke them.
A giant moth drives a leg through Moore's stomach and armor of thorns while he carries Jelaqua toward the inn.
Moore's wound closes thanks to healing potions, and he is expected to recover with rest.
In the victory parade, Moore walks with flowers blooming in his footsteps and on his body while Jelaqua throws them to the crowd.
Moore argues that if people make an exception for those they call monsters, the label will soon apply to Selphids and others like his team.
Moore advises Erin to prepare her inn, especially for Mrsha, while the adventurers enter the dungeon.
A barbed stone spear goes through Moore's vine armor into his side, and Seborn cuts the head out.
Jelaqua pours a healing potion into the wound after Seborn cuts it out, and it begins to close.
Moore makes the first hit of the day, the six-hundred-foot shot that Bevussa catches, ending the game at 19-18.
Moore smiles melancholy at Bevussa after the catch and stands at the centre of a crowd that is wise enough not to lift him.
Moore, Jelaqua and Seborn meet the Redfangs in the pass while carrying a wooden door north, and Moore carries it under his arm.
Moore sends a [Message] on Jelaqua's order, then cancels it when they recognise Garen.
Moore asks whether Garen is really here after they looked for so long.
Moore bellows with grief and rage as the trio attacks Garen.
Moore runs through the Redfang lines, knocks Garen from his wolf, and demands to know how Garen could kill their friends.
Garen's sword pierces Moore's palm, but Moore's hand closes around Garen with thorns and vines.
Redfang warriors snare Moore with ropes, but he keeps coming, dragging horses and wolves, with his eyes always on Garen.
After Garen dies, Moore pours oil on the pyre and later hunches over his staff without weeping.
Moore says that time stopped for the team and for Garen, and that with Garen dead their oaths are fulfilled.
Moore asks Jelaqua whether the key might be on the pyre, and she says she checked and Garen did not have it.
Moore agrees to one more adventure after the pyre.
Moore tells Mrsha that he is getting spoiled staying at the inn, while Seborn wants to get on the road.
Moore is called away from Mrsha by Jelaqua, who wants him to talk with Maughin.
Seborn suspects Moore hides envy beneath his support of Jelaqua's romance with Maughin.
Seborn says Moore keeps waiting for someone to fall in love with him, citing a girl in Wales, a woman in Invrisil and a [Mage] from Wistram.
At a dance in Book 19, Moore bumps another partner, apologises, and panics that he is too large to dance.
Maughin tells Moore he is too self-conscious and that the dance was meant for War Walkers to spend time with the smallest of their kindred.
Bevussa promises to be around Moore and says she has his back, and Moore agrees to dance with a female Dullahan he calls Miss Xerca.
Palt casts an illusion as a spell for courage, making all the dancers look as tall as Maughin and Moore.
Moore dances with misty eyes, feeling average among his peers.
Mrsha is a young Gnoll child of the Stone Spear tribe, mute from birth, who is later raised at Erin Solstice's inn.
Mrsha's fur turns from light brown to pure white during the events at the tribe's end, and Gnolls and others treat white fur as an omen.
Mrsha is the only survivor of the Stone Spears, who were killed by Goblins.
Mrsha later becomes a [Druid] with a wand, a growth spell, and a bond with Apista and the Fortress Beavers.
Mrsha speaks through her own sign language, written notes and pre-written cards.

section: Book 2: The Stone Spear tribe and the crevasse
text: Mrsha is a young Gnoll of the Stone Spear tribe who is playful, curious and unafraid of Ryoka Griffin.

section: Book 2: The Stone Spear tribe and the crevasse
text: Urksh says the young Gnolls have the best noses, and that Mrsha smelled Ryoka under the snow while others were gathering food.

section: Book 2: The Stone Spear tribe and the crevasse
text: Mrsha takes Ryoka's bra and wears it, after getting it off Ryoka during the night along with her other clothes.

section: Book 2: The Stone Spear tribe and the crevasse
text: Mrsha yelps and runs when Ryoka demands the bra back, and Ryoka seizes her outside the tent; the child struggles as if expecting a beating.

section: Book 2: The Stone Spear tribe and the crevasse
text: Urksh apologises that Mrsha is young and does not yet know boundaries.

section: Book 2: The Stone Spear tribe and the crevasse
