Niers refuses two more [Mages] to Balegilt's Marsh Troll company until it stops losing them to [Snipers], and orders Peclir to warn him that ties may be severed.
Niers has the 14th Division, skirmishing with local Centaurs, avoid killing if possible while Centaur [Diplomats] are sent in.
Niers does not want a [Scribe] reading confidential reports and keeps to regular written reports.
The Forgotten Wing Company's specialty is training students from around the world as military geniuses, including [Lieutenants], [Commanders] and [Generals], but is best known for [Strategists].
Niers' students call him the Professor, and he spends most of his time on teaching in peace and in war.
Niers has his core students watched, expecting Wil to sense what is coming and Venaz to think it a small event.
Niers' new noble students from Terandria were made to survive three nights in the jungle without supplies, and their parents sent angry [Messages].
Niers' company needs a fallback system so he can leave for a vacation, and he will not leave until he can trust it.
Niers sometimes feels the weight of being the Fraerlings' only hero and wants to go to Liscor, but cannot yet.
Niers meets Xalandrass, a Naga war merchant, who shows him items such as a flashlight and an iPhone and tells him of a company called the United Nations.
Niers connects the flashlight, chess, Go, a new game from a Drake city, a girl waving a white flag and Wistram's scrying orbs.
Niers concludes that there are at least two worlds, since no material in the flashlight or iPhone is known in this one.
Niers keeps outward calm while Xalandrass finishes, tapping his armrest, and tells him to say nothing of this or the company.
Niers pays Xalandrass twelve thousand gold coins for the information, six thousand at once and the rest in business deals.
Niers also buys Xalandrass' silence with a purple-covered object, to reach him and his [Mage] friend hidden in a bundle of wool.
Niers receives word from the Seer of Steel that Tulm the Mithril will be present in three weeks, at the Titan's request.
Niers tells Peclir to contact the Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings in First Landing with a proposition, sending fine wine.
Niers has an illustration at his tent of a girl in mud holding a white flag on a hill with her back turned, and resolves to start with her.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers is half a foot tall and needs a voice-amplifying artifact so that students at the back can hear him.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers introduces himself to new students as the Titan of Baleros and their teacher for as long as they are enrolled in his school.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers promises that anyone under Level 30 will gain five levels in a year of his basic course.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers claims to have raised [Strategists] out of [Farmhands] and made [Generals] out of people with no levels in [Soldier].

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers promises that no one in his advanced class will exit below Level 30, and that talented students may join it regardless of tuition.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers tells Venaz that he would have sent his command forward without going himself, and would have charged the crossbow line with the remaining [Riders].

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers says leading from the front has practicality, but warns Venaz that Minotaur cultural emphasis on bravery makes his tactics predictable.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers uses a tiny wand to draw battle illustrations in the air for his class.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers teaches his best class politics as well as tactics, so that they think of the nation they fight for as a whole.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers says he admires what the Empress of Beasts tried at Pomle and that the King of Destruction is in a bind.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers says Tiqr is at war with all of its neighbors, and suspects the Emperor of Sands orchestrated the situation.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers believes Tiqr's [Empress] tried to take a middling stance at the summit, which backfired.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers says that if the Forgotten Wing Company were based on Chandrar, he would be approaching the King of Destruction for an alliance.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers says Flos was never one to forswear himself, and if he broke his oath Niers could not predict what he would do.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers says the Slavers of Roshal will benefit from the Chandrar conflict more than anyone else.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers says Tiqr is in trouble against Nerrhavia and Illivere, and that Savere will raid constantly if fighting stays away from the coasts.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers sets his best students to command the defense of a nation against eight hostile armies, and gives Venaz a grudging point for a suggestion.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers reminds the class that a decade earlier his company had a pact with Goblin's Lament, the only Goblin-led company in Baleros.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers says Velan the Kind was considered the equal of any company leader until he became a Goblin King, and kept his promises more than any company.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers says he trusted Velan the Kind, spoke to him, and found him sane; he believes Olesm Swifttail's claim of Hobs defending Liscor.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers tells the class that Goblin adventurers have been employed only once in Baleros, while Velan was alive.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers mentions Garen Redfang of the Halfseekers as the only other Goblin adventurer he has heard of, and understands he died at Liscor.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Myth says the Titan lives on excitement and would die of boredom within a week without chaos, which the narration calls patently untrue.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers' game at Daquin is one of the things he uses to entertain himself between campaigns and is a penultimate test for his students.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers tells his former student Tulm to go ahead and crush the students, saying he wants Tulm to try.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers tells Perorn that only Wil in his class seems to have figured out the identity of the mystery guest.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Wil nods to Umina, showing he had known Niers' secret, and she deduces that Niers left hints only Wil caught.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers touches a ring and leaps twelve feet to stand on the helmet of a Dullahan in black armor to talk to Perorn.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers tells Tulm that teamwork nearly won once already and wonders what happens if the other students work together.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: When Umina's reveal ends the game, Niers laughs uncontrollably for about a minute before stopping himself.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers taps a ring that amplifies his voice and declares the game over, and the plaza calms instantly.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers tells Wil it was a masterful move, that he saw the ships at the harbor but lost them after, and that Wil will not repeat the trick because the world knows his name.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers admits to Perorn that he lost track of Wil's ships, since he could not send scouts, and says the reward is deserved.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers offers the city of Daquin hospitality, renting every inn and pub and threatening to expel any student who leaves sober.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers says he will award the dead's families double the standard pension, and reach out to the Seer of Steel and Sir Kelm of the Order of Seasons.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers whispers to Perorn through an anti-listening artifact to have Venaz search for Armor Captain Shailt discreetly.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers leaves Daquin carried off by a trained owl, as he employs [Beast Masters] among his tricks.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers thinks to himself that the game, Tulm, his question and the prize for Umina were all a feint to arrange one meeting.

section: The Titan's School and the Daquin Game (Book 11)
text: Niers admits he nearly started a war to arrange that meeting, and is glad Tulm did not win.
Niers teaches a special class that includes Venaz, Marian, Wil Kallinad, Umina, Cameral, Yerranola, Feshi, Kissilt and the newer student Reniz.
Niers nearly laughs himself off his podium at Wistram's false announcement that Reim had gone to war.
Niers tells the newer student Reniz to always expect the enemy to do what benefits them, and agrees Venaz may be right about Wistram spying.
Niers sets homework to find the best way to defeat the coalition's army with a force like the Dreamers of Reim, and the counter.
Niers is as short as a mouse, and anyone who mocks it to his face, his [Soldiers], Fraerlings or his students will regret it.
Niers' students all agree he wears the boots of the greatest [Strategist] in the world.
Two students, a Lizardgirl and a Human, won the right to ask Niers a question at Daquin about a month earlier.
Niers' academy is in Elvallian, headquarters of the Forgotten Wing Company, one of the Four Great Companies.
Niers sets 87 advanced-class students a test of outfitting his division of fourteen thousand [Soldiers], and sixty two percent of the cases fail, rounded down.
Niers sets the failed students to take part in the real march with actual [Soldiers] the next week, following the soldiers.
Niers says it is no disgrace to fail in his academy, as everyone has failed at least a dozen times, and wants students to learn failure is inevitable.
Niers had set up a whole town of real [Merchants] and [Informants] where students spent real gold on a hypothetical army.
Niers hired expert [War Merchants], criminals versed in trickery, and red-light district workers to tempt his students during the test.
Niers tells the students a quarter of them never even managed to spend all their gold, and says he has records of everything.
Niers holds a one-on-one dinner with the winners of his game as a prize, as a dialogue rather than an examination.
Niers tells Wil and Umina that they are nearing graduation, possibly in a year or two or sooner.
Niers says he has held such dinners countless times with winners of his games since he started offering them.
Niers taught Tulm and talked with him, but not in this room after Tulm won his game.
Niers was furious that Tulm burned down an entire city to win his game, and sent his answer by letter.
Niers says the Forgotten Wing Company is one of the Four Great Companies of Baleros, and counts the still-powerful Jungle Tails as a former Great Company.
Niers says the large companies are held in a stalemate by an unofficial agreement to ally against an aggressor.
Niers says there has been no major battle between the companies with hundreds of thousands of [Soldiers] in over a decade.
Niers dislikes the stalemate and wants the Forgotten Wing to gain more power, but cannot expand abroad because the Iron Vanguard controls the seas.
Niers has tried repeatedly to build his own navies, and Tulm shuts down each attempt.
Niers says the purpose of a secret is to prevent change, and the world stays the same while it is kept.
Niers explains he offers secrets because he is tired of constancy and counts on young [Strategists] to generate excitement for him.
Niers hates cats, which are banned wherever a Fraerling village exists and wherever the Forgotten Wing Company holds power.
Niers says cats kill anything as small as a mouse for fun, and he knows of at least twenty eight people who died to cats.
Niers says a Level 60 Fraerling [Warrior] can kill even a Griffin but still dies if stomped on, so being a [Warrior] is a waste of levels.
Niers grew up in a Fraerling village and dreamed of leaving, so he became a [Strategist].
Niers helped clear a hornet's nest on his first campaign and pushed back a boar herd for his village.
Niers was a higher-level [Strategist] than anyone his age by the time he turned twenty.
Niers spent three years going from adventuring team to team before meeting one that welcomed him, and Foliana was a loner then.
Niers' adventuring team started at Bronze rank, reached Silver within a month and Gold the next year, then became Named Adventurers as a team of thirty.
Niers says many from his original team joined the Forgotten Wing Company, and many died or quit over fifty years.
Niers says that only he and Foliana remain from the adventuring days.
Niers killed Queravia by charging her front, tying up her forces, finding her command and killing her.
Niers feels guilt over Queravia's death, saying she outfought him and he robbed the world of a truly great mind.
Niers says the King of Destruction's dreams fell apart with Queravia's death.
Niers wagers that Wistram used the threat of a Demon King alliance to move the Blighted King to send an army against the King of Destruction.
Niers has warded his scrying orb against Wistram, whose Academy he hates, though he knows they have eyes and ears everywhere.
Niers warns Wil's family that Lady Cassicel is not of pure-blood bloodline, her grandmother being a commoner, so marrying her would invalidate offspring unless she is inducted as a Kallinad.
Niers tells Wil that Lady Cassicel's grandfather was Bedil, a [Lord] with decent Skills to whom he entrusted a command for six years.
Niers says Bedil was running from his family, who came for him with [Bounty Hunters] and mercenaries, and Bedil gave himself up so as not to be pursued.
Niers says Bedil was married to a Lizardwoman, and thinks both their children were Human through fertility spells.
Wil and Niers conclude Lady Cassicel's descent from Bedil's firstborn son means her line shares Lizardperson ancestry and is ineligible unless inducted into the Havrington family.
Niers' answer to Tulm's question, as Umina recalls it, tells him he got a young one, that there are more, that he knows of two on Izril, and to leave them alone.
Niers drunkenly tells his linked chessboard he needs to meet his opponent soon after finding the young Humans, and thinks of the young woman at the inn in Liscor.
Niers writes Wil that a question asked on someone else's behalf is no real question, and that Wil may direct his father's inquiries to Niers.
Niers tells Wil he does not know where infamous wrecks like Laleday's Triumph with the Mooncaller's Quiver lie.
Niers sends Wil a list of sea sites the Forgotten Wing could never explore because of Dullahan sea superiority.
Niers advises Wil in a postscript to pick a trustworthy [Captain], since [Storm Sailors] can be as bad as [Pirates], and to return before summer break ends.
Niers does not cook, since cooking is a challenge for a Fraerling, and has a Garuda [Pictorial Chef de Entremetier] who prepares his breakfasts.
Niers is one of the leaders of the Forgotten Wing Company and strides through the Fraerling-ways to the dining room he shares with Foliana.
Foliana picks up Niers and carries him to the entrance of the Fraerling-ways, where he disappears up a ramp.
Niers gives Foliana a parchment contract to handle that day concerning an amateur with a dangerous artifact.
Niers says the amateur is apparently from Magnolia Reinhart, but he suspects an Izril idiot who wants to stir things up.
Foliana eats the parchment after reading it.
Niers' classes let students reach Level 30 through study, which is slower than fighting but safer, and so draw [Lieutenants], [Generals] and [Commanders].
Niers announces one last four-day project before summer: teams plan practice battles with Selphid volunteers, using no Skills and not witnessing the battle.
Niers allows students to customize practice armies on a twelve thousand point team budget but forbids aiding the armies, and selects the teams himself.
Niers twists a ring on his finger while explaining the project to Marian.
Niers has asked Foliana in different ways over the years whether she wants children or another life, and she answers that the citadel and company are hers.
Niers claims that an incident involving Foliana and Feshi's work was an exercise to test how fast the company reacts to alarms.
The narration describes Foliana as the myth of Three-Color Stalker, a dark shadow cast by the Titan, who claims the citadel and company as hers.
Niers agrees to let Foliana keep a comb after she disrupts his class, provided she stays out of his classroom.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Niers pauses a lunch with Foliana to watch the Wyvern attack on Pallass, saying it is impossible because the city has a Tier 7 city-wide defensive spell.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Niers has nothing to gain or lose from Pallass falling, but hides signs of stress, searching faces in the inn for a woman he does not see.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Niers later estimates casualties from the Wyvern attack at three to eight thousand at most.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Niers' opponent and Erin Solstice converse by spelling shorthand words with go stones, such as "gg" and "gd victry".

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Erin proposes speed-chess at five seconds per move through the go stones, and her opponent accepts.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Niers paces in front of the go board in Foliana's room, and points at a little emoji Erin left on the board.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Niers asks whether his opponent is a woman so he does not make an ass of himself as he did with Lord Belchaus, whose handwriting looked feminine.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Niers complains that the Gentleman Callers are not being cooperative, and that he is overplaying his hand by asking.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Foliana, here named Three-Color Stalker, rolls onto Niers and smooshes him, and Niers survives, since it takes more to kill a Fraerling.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Niers says he is still teaching summer classes while many of his students are at sea.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Niers teaches a class watching Flos Reimarch's invasion of Belchan, and asks Marian to analyse how the King of Destruction advances so fast.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Niers tells his students that Belchan has nearly a hundred and forty thousand [Soldiers], nearly double the King of Destruction's forces.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Niers notes at least three individuals on the field over Level 50, and puts Grand Mage Esiela over Level 40.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Niers points out Orthenon, Mars the Illusionist and the half-Giants on the scrying mirror, and says First Shepherd Zamea of the Nomads of the Sky is twice a War Walker's size.

section: Pallass, Go Stones and the Gentleman Callers (Book 15-17)
text: Niers has merged his special class with advanced students and officers to watch the battle, and says levels are not everything.
Niers is in a good mood because his Go board has arrived and he now regularly plays and communicates with his opponent.
Niers drinks Human-sized cups of tea, being able to eat and drink his body weight like all Fraerlings.
Niers' [Chamberlain] Peclir serves his tea and finds files in his miniature cabinets.
Niers asked Peclir, through Venaz, to arrange for Geneva Scala, the Last Light of Baleros, to lecture at his academy after a chance encounter with a [Rower] named Luan.
Geneva Scala, a [Doctor] and member of the United Nations company, cancelled at the last minute and refunded the lecture fee.
Niers invites a variety of guest speakers to his academy, including [Veterans], [Commanders] and [Mages], so students learn from varied sources.
Niers could march an army on Talenqual to take Geneva but refuses, since he does not want to kill innocents and the other Great Companies watch his moves.
Niers has not confided his secret about Geneva's company to Foliana, finding it too close and too vast.
Niers tells Foliana it is deeper than she thinks and not to pry, that his plans have changed, and that he needs an agent or two.
Niers gave Wil the treasure map, and six students, Venaz, Wil, Feshi, Yerranola, Merrik and Peki, are at sea hunting wrecks though Niers did not choose the group.
Niers judges Venaz competent but arrogant and needing to learn when to run, and says Wil is better than he thinks but too hesitant.
Niers judges Yerranola and Feshi to rely on cunning rather than trust their ability to win a death match, and Merrik and Peki to be fine commanders who need orders.
Niers drinks tea from what is for him a bucket, and keeps a thimble-sized cup for students.
Niers keeps notes on the United Nations Company, which gets attention only because of the Last Light.
Niers supposes the United Nations Company is composed entirely of Humans of a certain age from another world.
Niers tells Marian that people watch his every move, some of his opponents watch [Spies], and he cannot go to the bathroom without alarming Tulm.
Niers fears that sending a company to Talenqual might be taken as an act of war by the Featherfolk Brigade, and Tulm might attack his escort.
Niers sends Marian and Umina to Talenqual as a subtle assignment, then briefs a second pair, Kissilt and Cameral, to investigate Geneva Scala.
Niers has already sent three pairs of students after Geneva Scala, and the fourth pair is meant to make his opponents see just another assignment.
Niers gave all the students stipends and similar-yet-different assignments, expecting one to procure the [Doctor] or learn what he wants.
Niers receives a note on tiny parchment that the Gentlemen Callers are in Liscor awaiting instructions, and his hands shake.
Niers replies to the Gentlemen Callers to investigate the [Innkeeper], using a chess-board code.
Niers is obsessed with the thought that his opponent is her, hoping to meet someone who can keep up with him.
Niers waits in his lonely citadel, held prisoner by his enemies' fear of his might, drinking tea.
Niers loses a chess game to Perorn Fleethoof, copying a style from a tiebreaker match he had seen between his opponent and another player.
Niers tells Perorn that his game with his mysterious opponent was five splendid games, mostly draws, with a final tiebreaker.
Niers is in a good mood, hums and praises students, and Perorn suspects he has worked out that his partner is female.
Perorn knows Niers sent Kissilt, Cameral and Umina to look into Geneva Scala, and asks why a Selphid company is in Talenqual.
Niers did not know the Selphid company was in Talenqual and swears at missing the reports.
Perorn asks why Niers is recalling six senior [Strategists] from their posts, and he says it is to see if their replacements can handle things.
Niers tells Perorn he will soon announce something he has been meaning to do, and then loses two more games.
Niers and Foliana wait four days on flying carpets over the field and wave down at Tulm the Mithril.
Five carpets drop alchemical weapons from bags of holding on the tightly-knit Dullahan lines, and the Bannermare charges through the opening at Tulm.
Niers watches the Minotaur landing against Flos with his class and asks why.
Niers teaches a new summer class, because most of his oldest students are on assignment, including Princess Angelica.
Princess Angelica says her kingdom funded the Minotaurs together with a number of Terandrian kingdoms.
Niers has taught only six other members of royalty and treats Angelica like the others.
Niers adds that the House of Minos was also funded by the Kingdom of Morein, two thirds of Terandria's kingdoms, Izril's nobility, two Walled Cities and Balerosian nations.
Niers says the Minotaurs gave the King of Destruction his first real defeat with a small high-level force and powerful siege weapons.
Niers drills students on the flaws in Flos's army: few mages, no high-level archers and no Garuda in the sky.
Niers says General Ozem would never have landed had there been even a whiff of Garuda in the air.
Niers is restless and enlivened by battle, like the King of Destruction.
Noass is a Drake of Pallass who becomes a [Commentator] with his companion Sir Relz.
Noass and Sir Relz gain a class from their commentary on the attack on Liscor and become minor celebrities.
Noass is less expensively dressed than Sir Relz, and the pair are well fed.
Noass spots Seborn, the Crab-type Drowned Man and [Rogue] of the Halfseekers, while he and Sir Relz comment on the battle at the inn.
Noass and Sir Relz commentate with Eltistiman Verdue, a [Magician] for hire who provides the [Scrying] spell.
Noass reports that Senator Errif is arguing with a Wing Commander from Liscor, and doubts the claim that Liscor will be attacked.
Noass weighs what is best for Pallass if Tyrion Veltras's army with two hundred thousand soldiers drives the Goblin Lord toward Liscor.
Noass and Sir Relz broadcast live from Pallass during the Wyvern attack and take cover from the Wyverns.
Noass says a massive explosion and a chill came before the Wyverns attacked, and that Grand Strategist Chaldion shouted the alarm.
Noass and Sir Relz commentate on the advance of Flos's army, which has been slower than projected.
Viewers send Noass angry [Message] spells when the scrying of the Couriers' run is cut off.
Noass pays Drassi a gold piece for transport through the inn door to Invrisil and goes live as soon as he arrives.
Noass ignores Numbtongue's warning that the riots in Invrisil are dangerous, and says he knows what he is doing.
Noass opens the broadcast from Invrisil by announcing a riot over The Golden Triangle fraud.
Numbtongue calls Noass and Sir Relz idiots through the door, and his voice is broadcast worldwide for a moment.
Noears is a Goblin without ears who acts dimwitted around other Goblins and is shoved forward to cast lightning at attacking Humans.
Noears tells Rags he is a [Spellcaster] to the other Goblins, weak and stupid, but a [Mage] to her, stronger than he seems.
Noears was in Tremborag's tribe and knows Ulvama's ways.
Noears explains his missing ears with the adventurer bounty of two copper coins for Goblin ears.
Noears cannot be excused by Dawil, who says he cannot excuse the ears.
Noears warns Rags not to sit with Tremborag that night and advises her to be humble and small.
Noears detoured while fleeing Tremborag's mountain to steal all the maps from the Goblin war room.
Noears tells Rags that Human [Knights] and [Riders] run down Goblins with lances, that cities have armies and that riding patrols are common.
Noears tells Rags of stronger local tribes: one led by a big Hob with many Hobs, one with a [Witch] who knows fire magic, and one of thieves.
Noears keeps a charged field of air to hold off bugs around his group.
Noears teaches fourteen adults and eight children lightning magic aboard a wagon, saying lightning is built up in the air and hands then shot.
Noears explains that Goblins do not believe in small spells, so he teaches [Lightning Bolt] rather than [Electric Jolt].
Noears emerges unhurt from the darkness after the night ambush, with lightning crackling, followed by the wheezing Poisonbite.
Noears's lightning bolts convince the Humans' camp to keep out of range of the walls.
Noears says he has four potions and can cast many spells, and uses [Lightning Bolt] to crack an incoming boulder on the city wall.
Rags thinks Noears's [Lightning Bolt] can only crack or redirect a boulder and could protect the city for an hour at best.
Noears tells Rags that a bag of holding cannot hold living beings, and later carries the tribe's discarded armor and weapons in it.
Noears's lightning nearly strikes Ulvama in the fight against Tremborag's tribe.
Noears sits at the sit-about with Quietstab and grabs Redscar's shoulder to hold him back when Redscar half-rises.
Noears holds the pike line against Eater of Spears, staggering him with a bolt of lightning and telling Rags to go.
Noears tells Erin in English that he is Noears, and blinks up at her unusually shy.
Erin remarks that Noears's name is very accurate, noting the ragged flesh around both earholes.
Noears stands on the shattered third floor of the inn where Bird's tower had been and calls down lightning bolts minutes apart.
Erin feels that Noears is using all the mana the inn normally spends on the magic door, which is not there.
Poisonbite later recalls that Noears did not flee, was killed by the Humans after calling lightning from the skies, and let more Goblins escape.
Nokha is a female Raskghar, taller and bigger than the others, who keeps her clarity of thought even during the full moon.
Nokha carries a glowing yellow enchanted blade that bites into steel.
Calruz calls Nokha quite intelligent for a Raskghar and a competent warrior who led the raid on Liscor.
Nokha is one of the awakened Raskghar, created in a ritual in which Gnolls were killed on a stone altar and their hearts eaten.
Nokha kills a Gold-rank adventurer, a member of the Reldiev Scalers named Cassa, by slashing his throat with the glowing blade.
Twenty Gnolls die on the altar and twenty-one Raskghar stand changed, with Calruz inspecting them, and Nokha says "We are whole".
The awakened Raskghar gain intelligence through the ritual, and Nokha smiles as she watches each Gnoll sacrificed.
Nokha tells Ceria that the Raskghar need Chieftain Calruz because he is smart and can think when the moons fall.
Ceria sees from Nokha's body language that she is lying about needing Calruz, since Nokha has not learned to control her expressions.
Nokha says the Raskghar need Calruz for knowledge but adds that it is a good thing they have two.
Nokha fights Shorthilt, whose steel blade is nearly knocked out of his grip by her glowing sword.
Nokha licks Ceria's face as a challenge to Calruz, and Calruz forces her to apologise and go back to work.
Ceria believes Nokha licked her to say that the Raskghar needed only one of them for their knowledge, and that Nokha does not fear Calruz.
Calruz says Nokha is growing bolder and that the Raskghar might revolt if he crushed her, and tells Ceria to blast Nokha with magic next time.
Nokha and several awakened Raskghar chase Elirr after he kicks her, breaks out and flees with Mrsha.
Nokha, now sick but the healthiest of her pack, kills Soot and his five Gnoll bodyguards, eating their hearts.
Nokha says potions Soot gave did not cure the Raskghar's sickness, but eating hearts did.
Nokha has Bearclaw held down and says her heart makes two, as she wants a pack-sister.
Nokha says the pack must take no more hearts beyond those, as the city is too watchful.
Nokha says the Raskghar must learn from surface-people, who are too smart and made them sick.
Nokha orders Bearclaw's skin saved so she can wear it and her skull saved to learn how she thinks.
Nsiia is the Empress of Beasts, ruler of Tiqr, who wears no crown but a headband of feathers from birds she has caught.
Nsiia's headband holds a Roc's feather, a magical heirloom of Tiqr, and a bright yellow feather from a sparkling shock-bird.
Nsiia's headband feather lets her use the powers of the bird it came from when she plucks it.
Nsiia carries the Tusk of Tiqr, a spear enchanted as a fairly standard relic-class weapon.
Nsiia grew up alongside Thef, a Grand Elephant she calls her friend and protector.
Nsiia tells the other monarchs at Pomle that as a girl she opened her borders to Flos and joined her armies to his because she believed in his cause.
Nsiia says she no longer calls herself Flos' subject, but will not join a plot to attack him and calls the other monarchs cowards hiding in the dunes.
Nsiia leaves Pomle with her animals roaring and trumpeting, telling Orjin she enjoyed talking with him most.
Nsiia uses [Empire: Wild Riot] as the Wildkeepers prepare a caravan to leave.
Nsiia loses Thef when Alked Fellbow, a Named Adventurer, brings him down.
Wildkeeper Jvaile and the [Druids] tell Nsiia they are leaving because half their circle has died.
Nsiia tells the [Druids] to take her people, the herds, the young and the elephants to the Kilalle Steppes.
Nsiia says Tiqr will not yield and that surrender to Savere or Nerrhavia would mean giving her people to slavery.
Nsiia dons her cracked war-mask, which Fellbow's arrow cracked, and tells her warriors they may leave with her blessing.
Nsiia's honour guard has lost over half its number, and only a few war elephants remain.
Nsiia tells Flos that Thef is dead, slain by an arrow from Alked Fellbow that gave her time to flee.
Nsiia says General Vasraf holds the walls of Oliphant while the coalition's ten armies encircle it.
Nsiia says six hundred thousand citizens remain in Oliphant and its food will last about two more days.
Naili notes Nsiia's headband has one feather left.
Nsiia asks Flos to take Tiqr as his subject, pledging her life by blood and asking to be made one of his Seven.
Nsiia says Flos can revive the Sorcelled Blades from a hundred enchanted weapons.
Nsiia believes her people are no less than the Dreamers who brought nations to ruin and could become unbreakable if turned into Dreamers.
Nsiia sends Femithain a message that makes Viltach say she told him to run.
Nsiia plucks the Roc's feather, the last gift of her father, and grows as tall as one of her Grand Elephants.
Nsiia throws down the Tusk of Tiqr and her headband, shrinks, and surrenders Tiqr unconditionally to the Illivere Federation.
Nsiia tells Femithain she gave Vasraf leave to do as he wished and does not know his plan.
Nsiia says she would have surrendered to Deimos or Nerrhavia, but never to Savere.
Nsiia says she chose Illivere because Femithain tried to warn her and Illivere has few slaves.
Later, Nsiia lives under house arrest in private quarters in Femithain's city, called a prisoner by Savere and Nerrhavia.
Nsiia asks Femithain for help against the war on Reim, and Femithain says Illivere will not declare war on Reim but will not help it either.
Roshal made a bid of eight hundred thousand gold for Nsiia, and Savere offered about a tenth with threats.
Nsiia trains a Largebeaked Marraw named Teska in secret for a month and sends him with a note to find Vasraf.
Nsiia steals enchanted stone and premade control inscriptions from Femithain's private workshop.
Nsiia is a [Golem Maker], Level 14.
Nsiia's [Empress] class is gone, and she has lost [Wild Riot], the Laughing Brigade's Skill and her royal abilities.
Nsiia still has [Cat's Grace] and [Gazelle's Leap] and can still hide like a bat.
Nsiia gained [Wild Riot] with Thef's death, in grief and rage, and she is glad Flos saved her from that dark path.
Nsiia's class is [Animalfriend Exile], an exile rather than a prisoner, and she has gained a [Famous Name] Skill.
Nsiia stabs her arm with a fork each morning as punishment, counting forty-three days.
Nsiia built a clay Golem that broke after three minutes and smashed it, then made a bone Cat Golem from bones dogs brought her.
Nsiia considered and turned down the [Thief] class and believes in [Golem Maker].
Nsiia heals the cat Yinah and breaks the feet of the man whose Golem crippled her.
Nsiia smashes her Cat Golem with [Elephant's Strength] to give its legs to Yinah, saying she values the cat above the Golem.
Femithain has Yinah fitted with Golem legs, and the cat walks happily.
Nsiia gains [Skill - Sentience-class Crafting] after Domehead wins.
Numbtongue is a Hobgoblin of the Redfang tribe, one of the five Redfang Warriors who live at Erin Solstice's inn.
Numbtongue is a [Bard] who plays a guitar and calls lightning with his music.
Numbtongue is the most literate Goblin in the setting: he reads and speaks the common tongue better than Garen Redfang, and may write Human and Drake scripts.
Numbtongue speaks more fluently than any Goblin Pisces has met.
Numbtongue got his name because, as a child, he talked so much that he bit his tongue.
Numbtongue learned to speak as a small Goblin by stealing words, hiding in the sewers of a town far to the north.
Numbtongue listened outside the Mage's Guild and other guilds, thinking that if Humans knew he could talk they would stop hunting Goblins.
Numbtongue was swept out of the sewers, was hunted when he spoke and pleaded, and survived, and then he met Garen Redfang.
Numbtongue was one of thirteen Redfangs sent by Garen to kill an innkeeper, but the group got lost.
Numbtongue fought at Esthelm, where thirteen Goblins fought and only six walked away.
Numbtongue recites the names of Redfangs fallen before the battle of Liscor, including Grunter, Orangepoo, Rocksoup, Leftstep, Bitefly, Patchhelm and Justrust.
Numbtongue tells Garen the group met the innkeeper Erin Solstice, who was nice and has a name, and that Garen's orders to kill her were bad orders.
Numbtongue is surly, speaks little, and is afraid no one will listen to him when he talks.
Numbtongue wants only a quiet chat with Erin at night around a table.
Numbtongue has defined abs and keeps in good shape.
Numbtongue eats toothpaste because it tastes good, and Erin scolds him to rinse and spit.
Numbtongue would rather play the guitar than sing, and Erin keeps encouraging him to sing songs from her world.
Numbtongue refuses to sing when asked while covering songs from Erin's world.
Numbtongue refuses to go anywhere without a sword or guitar nearby.
Numbtongue helped Mrsha learn to quick-release her wand and make a grass garrote.
Numbtongue hides a hand crossbow and bolts in a small box by the windowsill, and wants acid jars hidden around the inn.
Numbtongue likes the Liscorian Gazette and drinks Blue Tea, which turns the tongue blue for about a day.
Numbtongue thinks Redfang ambushes against [Mages] should use pit traps, archers behind cover, boulders, Carn Wolf riders, Tripvine bags and beehives.
Numbtongue says a Goblin alone dies a slow, lonely, wandering death to monsters and adventurers.
Numbtongue says that when you kill something, you kill it fast.
Numbtongue snaps a rat's neck in the inn to make the point about killing quickly.
Numbtongue does not believe in wishing "good luck".

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue studies the inn's menu carefully while Shorthilt stares blankly, and he asks about the black things on spaghetti by calling them acid flies or blue fruit.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: The black things on the spaghetti are olives.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Goblins identify potions by their appearance because most cannot read.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue says that everyone in the world hunting the Goblins is nothing new.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue and the other Hobs feel five Hobs are as useful as thirteen regular Goblin warriors, but cannot hope to fight an army.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue memorised every line Vuliel Drae spoke and chooses the correct turn in the dungeon.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue remembers every word of Erin's songs and the plays he has heard.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue answers for the Redfangs when Lyonette asks about the artifacts that they do not need appraisal.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue steals the guitar Erin bought and teaches himself notes in the basement, hiding there each night.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue bursts from the basement trapdoor, smashes his wooden guitar into a Raskghar's face, and chants "Redfang" and "Goblin" to rouse Headscratcher.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue repairs the broken guitar enough to play a riff and says "Music", which foreshadows a Goblin [Bard].

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue spits on the blood cloak and turns it into a saliva cloak, and Rabbiteater throws it back at him.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue refuses to talk until Ilvriss says his name, and Ilvriss grudgingly says "Numb. Tongue."

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue explains to Erin that the Redfangs planned to kill a Raskghar captive because she would tell the Raskghar their plans.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue and Rabbiteater agree to find Mrsha and Ceria after Erin begs, abandoning Erin's Plan G.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue's mended guitar throws lightning from the strings, and he calls the ability [Electric Chords].

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue sings a Redfang song as he strides into the room with his crackling guitar.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue's claws strike lightning on the guitar as the Hobs spread out against the Raskghar.

section: Early Days at the Inn, Books 6-8
text: Numbtongue stands with Headscratcher, Rabbiteater, Shorthilt and Badarrow, who lead about forty Cave Goblins and meet the fleeing Gnolls.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue becomes a Level 25 [Bard], learning the Skills [Electric Chords] and [Lightning Melody].

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue leads the Cave Goblins' musical ensemble in the cave, and they try to copy the guitar with rocks and crude instruments.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue feels protective of the Cave Goblins, who follow him as small Goblins look at a hero.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue calls down lightning that strikes near Badarrow, and Badarrow is knocked off his perch.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue learns I See Fire by Ed Sheeran, a song Erin taught him.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue receives a memory of Velan's death, with Elia Arcsinger's [Piercing Shot] through the left eye.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue and the other Hobs escape arrest, and Numbtongue runs shouting about a Raskghar attack and jumps off Liscor's battlements.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Thirty Cave Goblins, including Pebblesnatch, go with the Redfangs to Erin's inn after the Hobs bang heads and throw the rest back.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue plays the guitar from a rock as a bolt of lightning blows up the thieves' boat, and the Cave Goblins ambush the Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue fights the last Brother of Serendipitous Meetings, who salutes him and compliments the song.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue recovers Erin's magic door from the undamaged boat.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue walks out of the cave at the head of the Cave Goblins, after seeing the bright star over Liscor.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue leads at least twenty-four thousand Cave Goblins to the foot of Liscor's walls, and Olesm sees him with a guitar and a sword.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue stands before Liscor shouting "Redfang!" and the Cave Goblins join in.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue tells Erin the Goblins will go south, then west to the High Passes, once the Hobs are released.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue says the Goblin Lord is his tribe's enemy and he does not know if his Chieftain is alive.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue and the other four Hobs challenge Garen, who beats them bloody, and say Garen's orders to kill Erin were bad since Rags is true Chieftain.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue lifts his lightning guitar against Garen, who recoils before kicking him in the chin.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue says he played music and was welcomed, which is part of why the Hobs will not obey Garen.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue, Headscratcher and the other Hobs take over the leadership of the Redfang tribe after Garen leaves.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue leads a Cave Goblin band in the inn, and the Painted Soldiers waltz while Erin dances Gangnam Style.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue and the other four Hobs return to take Erin's flag, saying "Somebody" told them she would stay and fight.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Numbtongue calls lightning down on the Goblin Lord's army from a hilltop while Cave Goblins play with him.

section: Cave Goblins and the Redfangs, Book 9
text: Noears pours his mana into the lightning and Numbtongue shapes it.
Numbtongue survived a spear through the chest, which left a red scar, and half his body is paler from the lightning.
Numbtongue wakes in Erin's basement alone and silent, with Pyrite and the music gone.
Numbtongue dreams the Goblins walking off a hill into the sky, with Garen, Reiss, Headscratcher, Spiderslicer, Noears and Shorthilt leaving, and last Pyrite.
Numbtongue tells Erin the Goblins chose to stay and fight and die, and that hiding is wrong since they did nothing wrong.
Numbtongue asks Selys what the Adventurer's Guild pays for Goblin ears, and wants a bounty for the army the Redfangs killed.
Selys says the guild cannot pay for the Goblins the Redfangs killed, and Numbtongue leaves, asking if they were adventurers or pets.
Numbtongue takes a glowing blue gemstone from Pyrite's mouth and cracks two teeth biting it.
Numbtongue obtains the [Miner] class at Level 1 and the Skill [Durable Picks].
Numbtongue carries Pyrite's memories, which include mining, gemstone lore and over a decade of mining techniques.
Numbtongue also holds Pyrite's sword technique from Greydath and the secret of two keys, one of which Garen has.
Numbtongue holds Pyrite's memory of a dungeon lost to all but Goblins, too dangerous to enter.
Numbtongue gave the Raskghar's fortune to adventurers and carries Pyrite's sack of gold and gems, which he gives to Erin.
Numbtongue believes Rabbiteater and Badarrow may be alive because they were missing from his dream, and perhaps Rags.
Numbtongue turns down an offer to leave with the Halfseekers and says he belongs at the inn.
Numbtongue sings his first Goblin song at the inn, with a rhyming account of the dungeon and the Raskghar, to applause.
Numbtongue reaches [Bard] Level 27 and gains the Skill [Song of Rejuvenation].
Numbtongue goes mining in the mountains with a purple mana stone as a door stone.
Numbtongue replies verbally more, and tells Mrsha her two-fist sign is a Goblin sign meaning he is better than you.
Numbtongue carries a plain steel sword, a repaired guitar and a pickaxe, and a rolled wooden-slat door frame.
Numbtongue uses a lit purple mana stone in the dark to prospect for magical deposits in a Rockmite cave.
Pyrite's memories overwhelm Numbtongue whenever he touches the blue stone.
Numbtongue's guitar crackles with [Electric Chords], but the blue stone does not react to guitar music alone.
Numbtongue bottles electrified mana sludge in a jar with gloves and a spade.
Numbtongue sings a Goblin song of peace to the Rockmites and walks past them unharmed.
Numbtongue crunches a blue mana stone before Falene and Erin, and viridian gas pours from it as he spits liquid into a jar.
Numbtongue throws the jar of mixed liquid towards the Floodplains.
Falene offers to buy Pyrite's blue mana stones, but Numbtongue refuses.
Numbtongue reaches [Miner] Level 6 and [Bard] Level 29, gaining [Grinder Teeth], [Lightcaller Harmony] and [Peaceful Melody].
Numbtongue calls down lightning to defend the orchard, and Lyonette suggests he use his emergency door stone.
Numbtongue has newly healed Rockmite bites on his legs.
Numbtongue says Gnoll smiths probably have fire-resistance Skills, which Goblins in Garen's tribe prize for trap-laying.
Erin leads Numbtongue by the hand past Pallass' crowd to meet Rufelt, and Liscor's citizens defend him against a Dullahan's jab.
Numbtongue uses [Peaceful Melody] with a light-making Skill while walking through Rockmite caves.
Numbtongue steals a nugget from a gold-plated Rockmite nest, and the bugs follow him until the sunlight.
Numbtongue finds that he calls lightning faster under clouds and when the air is already crackling.
Numbtongue remembers his sewer childhood and Pyrite's dream of seeing cities.
Numbtongue realises the inn feels like a cage and hates his cycle of joy and exclusion.
Numbtongue bonds with Yellow Splatters as last survivors, and offers to help him clear Shield Spiders.
Numbtongue eats mac and cheese with Acid Flies and finds it crunchy but lacking taste.
Numbtongue and Yellow Splatters both enjoy Acid Flies in cheese sauce and on ice cream.
A drunk Drake whose sister and friend were killed by Goblins confronts Numbtongue in the inn, and Relc drags him towards the door.
Numbtongue answers that Humans killed his parents, Relc killed his Chieftain, and Embria killed thousands of his people.
Numbtongue says the Redfangs and the Flooded Waters tribe fought for Erin and so Liscor would not forget, not for Liscor.
Numbtongue draws Redfang ambush tactics for Yellow Splatters, who says the Antinium use no potions except stores Klbkch reserves.
Numbtongue takes an iron sword from a Human [Warrior] in Celum and cuts a man's hand off as Pyrite's memories guide him.
Numbtongue beats a woman in a fist fight, and he breaks six of a [Ruffian]'s teeth as a threat to Alchemist Quelm.
Numbtongue tells the Watch Captain that he is a Bronze-rank adventurer and shows a signed paper proving he is a person.
Yellow Splatters bluffs the Watch Captain by claiming to be the Prognugator of the Free Antinium's Hive.
Numbtongue sings The Ballad of the Redfangs in the inn, naming the thirteen sent to kill an innkeeper, Esthelm where six survived, and Bugear's death.
Numbtongue changes class from [Bard] to [Goblin Soulbard] at Level 30, gaining the Memory of Pyrite, Flooded Waters Tribe, and Skills [A Minute, Reborn] and [Ballad of Bravery].
Numbtongue thinks about the new class the next morning, calling [A Minute, Reborn] a Skill with serious limitations that lets Pyrite act for a minute.
Numbtongue needs about eight hours between uses of his Skill to bring Pyrite back.
Numbtongue refuses Xif's offer for his services, quoting a price of one million gold.
Numbtongue wants to learn alchemy from Octavia and trades mana stones, an emerald and silver for potions and lessons.
Numbtongue carries Shorthilt's steel sword and his guitar.
Numbtongue becomes Octavia's paid guard and sleeps at Stitchworks.
Numbtongue keeps night watch at Stitchworks, and a bolt of lightning strikes a [Blackguard] while a [Nightstalker] Sister of Chell flees.
A man humming a children's song tips his hat to Numbtongue outside Stitchworks and walks on.
Numbtongue now reads fluently and can become Pyrite for a minute, a power limited to a few uses per day.
Numbtongue fights Beza, and Pyrite takes over his body for a minute and smashes bottles over her face.
When Pyrite's minute runs out, Numbtongue is struck and nearly strangled, until Erin stabs Beza with a kitchen knife.
Numbtongue has lunches with Octavia and learns alchemy with her, and Octavia calls him a semi-regular guest.
Numbtongue drinks Octavia's fire-breathing potion and gets flaming saliva, then sets her toilet alight.
Numbtongue pulls Crelers from his legs and is gutted at the inn, and Pyrite takes his body and throws it out a window.
Relc is bitten with Creler poison that Erin's potion does not cure, and Seborn and Moore are badly hurt.
Numbtongue recovers on liquids in Krshia's apartment, where he cannot be in Liscor officially and Krshia disguises his scent.
Numbtongue sneaks Bird a Wyvern wing and Firebreath Whiskey, and the two become friends.
Numbtongue and Bird eat eggs and fried chicken despite Bird's punishment, and Numbtongue acts like a rebellious teen.
Numbtongue calls on Pyrite's memory when Mrsha vanishes, and Pyrite deduces from the door's dial that Mrsha went to Celum.
Numbtongue rejects Reiss's ghostly offer of help to find Mrsha.
Numbtongue describes fighting thousands of Crelers at the inn.
Mrsha leads Numbtongue to the hilltop of the dead Goblins, where he kneels to Garen Redfang and finds Reiss at the stone table.
Numbtongue learns that Rabbiteater and Badarrow are absent from the hill.
Numbtongue, Bird and Octavia go mining for gems and opals, with potions, a guitar, a sword and Pyrite.
Numbtongue plays an acoustic guitar that sounds like a cross between acoustic and electric, and covers Don't Stop Believin' by Journey.
Numbtongue's [Lightning Chords] send lightning bolts through the Garden of Sanctuary's dome, and Saliss bottles one for free.
Numbtongue plays in the Sage's Grass meadow, and the lightning becomes a barrage fed by the Sage's Grass mana.
Numbtongue feels the grass-charged mana first and acts as a conduit for it.
Numbtongue reaches [Goblin Soulbard Level 32!] and obtains the Song [Harmony of Mana].
Numbtongue trips Erin into the pond when Mrsha signals him.
Octavia leaves Numbtongue six potions: Barkskin, Quickened Body, Vanish for fourteen seconds, Bat's Ear, Jumping and a Blast Vial.
Octavia is now an apprentice to Saliss of Lights, and her new shop is built into the inn.
Numbtongue sits with Pyrite's and Reiss's ghosts on the garden hill and refuses Reiss's offer to merge for now.
Reiss tells Numbtongue that [Ladies] work through formality and indirect power rather than direct harm.
Numbtongue plays Halo CE on Kevin's laptop, having learned the password.
Numbtongue shows Erin that he can use the laptop, and she finds Peanuts comics on it.
Numbtongue tells Erin she is sometimes a jerk when she asks, and later tells her she did good things.
Numbtongue carries Pyrite's memories, while Reiss's voice still offers help that Numbtongue declines.
Numbtongue gains temporary Skills [Directional Sound] and [Soul's Armaments: Mundane].
Numbtongue summons a transparent pickaxe that lasts three minutes, and can also call Pyrite's unenchanted battleaxe.
Numbtongue takes Mrsha and Bird fishing at a pond in the High Passes with Apista, as the Bee Rescue Team.
Numbtongue refuses to train Mrsha, Visma and Ekirra as [Warrior]s and hits them until they give up.
Numbtongue takes up gambling in the inn's rec room, and adds ore or silver to pots to make people friendlier.
Numbtongue tells the Goblin Nolocks to run north, tears off his armor, then kicks him out of the air when he lunges at Mrsha.
Numbtongue throws Nolocks through the door to the High Passes, and Arcsinger's Bows kill him after he attacks them.
Numbtongue gains the [Gambler] class at Level 4, with Skills [Sense Trickery] and [Weak Lucky Draw], and [Goblin Soulbard Level 34!].
Numbtongue obtains the Memory of Shorthilt, Redfang Tribe.
Numbtongue plays lightning guitar in disguised armor, painted with red eyes and a frowny face, as Jasi covers "Take on Me" on air.
Numbtongue shows Kilkran a Dragonblood crystal sword, to Kilkran's amazement.
Numbtongue practices sword exercises at dawn, though he got in trouble for cutting down a tree.
Numbtongue finds Fierre's red eyes and pointed teeth fine Goblin features, and is fascinated.
Octavia Cotton is a young dark-skinned [Alchemist] who owns the shop Stitchworks in Celum.
Octavia is a String Person, a Stitch-Girl whose body is cloth held together by string, and she can remove and reattach limbs.
Octavia has a braided ponytail or dreadlocks, stitch marks around her shoulders and neck, and a muscular build.
Octavia is a String-Girl of the Cotton folk, which is where her surname comes from.
Octavia says she is from Chandrar, and specifically from Nerrhavia Fallen.
Octavia has not returned to Nerrhavia in nearly five years, but she still receives [Messages] with gossip from there.
Octavia feels sensations, burns easily, and would die if cut apart, and she cannot throw her arm like a Dullahan.
Octavia can take her arm off, and the cloth is unharmed by the effect of a potion, which still works after she reattaches it.
Octavia has Skills that protect her against acid, burns and poison.
Octavia is a Level 21 [Alchemist], just at the point where she could take on an apprentice.
Octavia has the Skills [Magic-Water Solvent] and [Mineral Distillation].
Octavia removes her stitched hand to doodle on a table, and her cotton eyes can pop out of their sockets.

section: Early Celum shop and Ryoka's potions (Book 2)
text: Octavia sells Ryoka a stamina potion that tastes awful, and offers twelve for fourteen gold.

section: Early Celum shop and Ryoka's potions (Book 2)
text: Octavia says she could make stamina potions, but not invisibility or regeneration potions, which would need fifty more levels.

section: Early Celum shop and Ryoka's potions (Book 2)
text: Stamina potions give a burst of energy and a crash and do not heal.

section: Early Celum shop and Ryoka's potions (Book 2)
text: Ryoka asks Octavia for a potion that chases away everything that might hurt her, and the stench is so strong that it clears a block when brewed.

section: Early Celum shop and Ryoka's potions (Book 2)
text: Octavia charges eight gold for the testing and delivery of Ryoka's custom potions.

section: Early Celum shop and Ryoka's potions (Book 2)
text: Octavia tests the pepper potion on herself, and her cotton eyes pop out.

section: Early Celum shop and Ryoka's potions (Book 2)
text: Octavia finishes the pepper potion and hands over two cloth bags and two bottles of enchanted glass that weaken when uncorked.

section: Early Celum shop and Ryoka's potions (Book 2)
text: Octavia gives Garia a yellow healing potion free and promises discounts to any Runner who wants a healing potion.

section: Early Celum shop and Ryoka's potions (Book 2)
text: Ryoka's potions, including pepper spray, are all based on things from her world and were made by Octavia.

section: Early Celum shop and Ryoka's potions (Book 2)
text: Octavia sells stamina, pepper and blur potions, smoke bags, and tries to sell Erin potions, but Erin is only selling bees.

section: Early Celum shop and Ryoka's potions (Book 2)
text: The Watch has banned Octavia from using her stink potion anywhere in the city.

section: Early Celum shop and Ryoka's potions (Book 2)
text: Octavia stops her sales patter when Erin says she is an [Innkeeper].
Ryoka pays Octavia twenty gold to keep hosting Erin.
Erin and Octavia experiment in Octavia's kitchen, bickering over a stew in which Erin used Octavia's potions.
Octavia wants to buy the recipes Erin has come up with, and says she has benefited from them.
When Erin leaves, Octavia is relieved, says she nearly died several times, and claims Erin owes her extra fees.
Octavia is known as one of three [Alchemists] in Celum who makes potions cheaply, and is thrifty with ingredients.
Octavia charges customers for lingering in her store.
Octavia comes through the door and hands Revi a free mana potion to pitch her wares to the Gold-rank adventurers.
A wagon convoy knocked down the front wall of Octavia's shop and she patched it with planks, and she was reimbursed too little to fix it.
Erin pays Octavia thirty-six gold for her door and for hiring her, and Octavia cheerfully forgets about the hole in her wall.
Erin apologises to Octavia for not being a good friend to her, and Octavia lets the matter go because of the pay.
Krshia negotiates with Octavia to sell her potions, and gets a better cut on the strength of her levels as a [Shopkeeper].
Octavia makes workable matches by blending a little Corusdeer horn with sulfur, after staying up all night making prototypes.
Octavia hopes to sell matches for silver coins, and Erin teases her about her cut.
Octavia walks through the door from her Celum shop to the inn without having been told about it.
Octavia stumbles into the inn red-eyed from lack of sleep.
Octavia has sold matches to merchants, and levelled up three times from them, and also from the penicillin mold.
Octavia shows Erin more penicillin-type mold as her match sales go through the roof.
Octavia dips wooden sticks in a red liquid to make matches, and can finish up to fifty boxes a day.
Octavia's match formula uses powdered Corusdeer horn and Fire Beetle shells, not phosphorus.
Octavia leaves her potions and matches at the inn for Krshia to sell in Liscor, and Krshia gets a cut.
Octavia has installed Erin's magic door in her shop, and her front wall is not yet repaired.
Erin says the matches were her and Ryoka's idea, and asks for two coppers per gold coin of sales plus free matches.
Octavia tells Erin she cannot make an anti-gravity potion, and that the penicillin molds are hard to figure out.
Octavia undercuts Pallass potions by manufacturing cheaply from local ingredients.
During the Face-Eater Moth attack, Erin pulls crates of potions from Octavia's shop through the door.
Over thirty members of Celum's Watch stand behind the inn's windows with crates of potions at their feet.
The adventurers used forty-one healing potions, thirty-five mana potions and over six crates of stamina potions from Octavia's stock.
Octavia plans to buy up supplies and sell through Liscor to beat Pallass in a trade war.
Erin tells Lyonette that Octavia has no recipe for exploding potions.
Octavia protests when Erin carries the door away, saying she thought they were partners, and follows the procession.
Octavia is eating mouldy bread when Erin asks if it is the penicillin mold she wanted her to cultivate.
Octavia is one of four [Alchemists] in Celum.
Quelm copies Octavia's match formula and improves it with a spark-dust igniter, and she retaliates by throwing a burning brick.
Octavia has a sample of a high-grade haste potion glowing yellow streaked with pink, shown to her by Ryoka.
Octavia is growing molds on bread and cheese to look for the blue-green mold Ryoka described.
Octavia pesters Lyonette to stay and chat while Lyonette is passing through.
Octavia asks Erin and the adventurers for guards for her shop, and Erin refuses.
Octavia asks Krshia for bulky Gnolls for a job she says is probably not underhanded, and Krshia refuses.
Hooded thugs sent by Quelm smash the front of Octavia's shop with bricks, and Ksmvr buys potions but does not help.
Octavia is forced to pay Quelm twelve silver every day.
A [Thug] seizes her potions and says everything must be sold through Quelm's store.
Octavia accuses the Captain of the Guard of taking money from Quelm, exposing that the Watch is bought and has let thugs burn her shop.
Octavia is subdued and says she has learned her lesson.
Octavia tries to ask Xif to teach her but he refuses, noting her gang trouble.
Octavia says that only Mabel is left among Celum's other [Alchemists] now that Jeffil is out, and that her name is mud with the Watch.
Octavia calls herself a fraud and says Numbtongue should buy good potions from Xif.
Octavia is thrilled when Numbtongue gives her a glowing pink-red mana stone.
Octavia sells baking soda at eight silver a packet, and the Bakers of Celum object.
Octavia says she will move to Liscor, and the Mayor later lets the door stay open.
Octavia goes mining with Numbtongue and Bird.
Octavia wants a shop at the inn with bigger display shelves, barricades, quarantine areas and a sign.
Octavia asks Saliss to take her as an apprentice, offering to clean his shop, and he refuses because the last apprentices died horribly.
Octavia trades her Potion of Haste to Saliss for his invisibility recipe notes, which use ruby dust.
Saliss tells Octavia he can show her some things and she runs after him.
Octavia is apprenticed to Saliss, and regulars joke she is sleeping with him.
Octavia makes penicillin and Ryoka tells her to sell it cheaply without revealing how she found it.
Octavia sells the penicillin-like paste and looks for buyers among [Healers].
Erin sends all the penicillin she can by sea to Geneva, and tells Octavia to put her name on every jar and make more.
Grimalkin promises that Pallass will pay for the penicillin, and Octavia agrees to put her name on jars as a logo.
Octavia is thinking of naming the mold Octavia's Mold, or Octalius.
Octavia has an apprenticeship with Master Saliss, and is closed most of the time.
Lyonette cancels Octavia's boon, and Octavia begs to keep it because she cannot do her fungoid research without it.
Lyonette has not told Octavia that she is a [Princess].
Octavia is working for Saliss of Lights, who has been using little yellow flowers and wears a glass-lensed helmet with a Jar of Air.
Wispel of the Assembly of Crafts offers Octavia the Alchemium Scholaris place, a laboratory and home in Pallass with a grant of 3,200 gold per year.
Octavia asks whether the offer is a mage-contract and recognises it as a way to make her sell through Pallass.
Octavia declines for now, saying the offer is generous but she has a shop and room at The Wandering Inn.
Erin says that Octavia made the Yellow Rivers cure, and that she hired Tritel to carry it from the inn.
Okasha is a Selphid who first appears as a [Rogue], Level 23, of the Burning March 6th Division, living in a dead woman's body with a useless right side.
Okasha offers to help the [Doctor] Geneva, who had put her into that body, and becomes her assistant.
Okasha has lived in Dullahan and Lizardfolk bodies before.
In a dead body, Okasha breathes and blinks much less than normal people.
After Thriss broke Geneva's spine, Okasha entered Geneva's living body to bridge the gap, an act forbidden to Selphids.
Okasha stabbed Thriss through the chest as he raised his mace over Geneva.
Okasha controls Geneva's right arm and speaks inaudibly inside her head.
Okasha hums to Geneva by projecting sound directly into her inner ear.
Okasha is a Level 23 [Rogue] and a Level 15 [Medical Assistant].
Okasha puts Geneva to sleep by triggering her brain to secrete drowsiness chemicals, which Geneva calls melatonin.
Okasha wonders whether Selphids' predecessors worked with their hosts rather than just controlling them.
Okasha takes full control of Geneva only when she is asleep or in dire need, and is uncomfortable with that.
Okasha urged Geneva to leave the battlefield camp for four days, but Geneva refused to take sides.
Okasha says the Centaurs paid Zalthia to attack Geneva's camp.
After Geneva was stabbed, Okasha spoke with her voice, pumped her stopped heart manually and held her internal wounds closed until Calectus's potion arrived.
Geneva's spine is broken, with a neck bone crushed by a soldier's hit, so she cannot move without Okasha bridging the connection.
Okasha leapt from tree to tree in Geneva's body to scout, and warned the leaps would tear Geneva's muscles.
Selphids can exceed a body's limits for a brief period at the cost of damage.
Okasha secretes a pain-relieving agent and told Geneva to use a healing potion for torn muscle.
Geneva describes Okasha in Book 10 as the Selphid who lives in her body since Thriss paralysed her, bridging her nerves and helping her move.
Okasha can release hormones into Geneva's brain to change her mood, which Geneva objects to.
Okasha is gullible about biology and believes Geneva when she claims to know everything about her body.
Okasha can force Geneva's muscles to exercise, and gave her more muscular strength and fine control in her hands.
Okasha speaks through Geneva's mouth in a higher, more cheerful voice.
Okasha speaks for Geneva in the meeting with Fezimet, acting enough like her to nearly fool Daly.
Okasha complains of feeling like a prisoner and demands sex, saying she cannot control the body unless Geneva sleeps.
Okasha calms Geneva's adrenaline spike with endorphins and makes her pinky-swear to find someone that night.
Later, Okasha is a Level 11 [Inner Friend], and Geneva says Okasha was Level 4 earlier.
Okasha has the Skill [Host: The Thinking Room], gained at Level 10, which separates Geneva's mind from her body.
Okasha is the first Selphid in current memory to gain a class like this.
Okasha's Skill [Physical Enhancement: Flexibility] lets her bend Geneva's arm nearly a hundred and eighty degrees.
Another Skill lets Geneva move even when Okasha is not awake.
After the Xeppal incident, Okasha got three days a week of six hours each to pilot Geneva's body, with sex with others off limits.
Okasha claims "our body" and says Geneva is sick from overwork and her image.
Okasha seizes control of Geneva's body and puts her in the box.
Later, six Selphids led by Calectus take Okasha out of Geneva and seal her in a holding-jar.
Calectus says Okasha committed the sin for which the Selphids were destroyed, and the Minds will sentence her.
Idis is introduced as Okasha's replacement and takes Geneva's body.
In Book 18 Geneva misses Okasha, and Calectus says she is being held and cannot be spoken with.
Olesm Swifttail is a young Drake of Liscor, thinner than his uncle but taller than Erin, who plays chess and is the city's [Tactician].
Later, Olesm is Liscor's [Strategist].
Olesm is meticulous and careful, unusual among the Drakes Erin has met.
Olesm has blue eyes patterned like falling raindrops.
Olesm has light blue scales.
Olesm is Lism's nephew, whom Lism helped raise.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm plays Erin at chess on his uncle Lism's wager, urging her not to bet against him and saying he has played over a hundred games and won over two thirds.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Relc tells Erin that her opponent is a [Tactician], the highest-leveled one in the city, and someone says all [Tacticians] sense when they are being led into a trap.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Klbkch tells Erin that Olesm is a Level 22 [Tactician] and that no higher-level [Tactician] exists even in the Liscorian army.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm visits Erin with a chess set and says he is the [Tactician] who liaises with the council, other guilds and the guard, so he knows about the Workers within the Antinium.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm says the Antinium entered Liscor eight years ago and that Klbkch was the first and only Antinium accepted into the Watch.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm receives Erin's chess puzzle, sent out to all the known [Tacticians] and chess players on the continent, and excitedly shows it to Erin.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm solves Erin's chess puzzle after nearly a week of locking himself away and levels twice.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm objects when Erin accepts a skeleton, saying one skeleton is not worth the food she has fed Pisces.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm is a Level 24 [Tactician] when he asks the Horns of Hammerad to let him join their ruins expedition; Yvlon refuses because he looks like a civilian.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm is a [Tactician] the adventurers hired the day before the ruins expedition, and the ruins are his first dungeon.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm uses [Rapid Retreat], a [Tactician] Skill that many [Thieves] also know, and later [Attack Formation], which he can use once a day at his level and which makes the adventurers' weapons lighter and revitalises mages.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm has the [Dangersense] Skill, and says he cannot read the old tongue, that Drakes cremate their dead, and that a [Necromancer] attacked Liscor when he was a child ten years earlier.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm is found alive, very thin and dusty, with light blue scales, in another coffin in the crypt.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm and Ceria hid in the coffins for three or four days.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm drags Ceria into a coffin when a ghoul appears, stabs the ghoul from behind, and uses a healing potion on her, which Ceria says saved her life.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Zevara calls Olesm "our" [Tactician] and says she would have sent help had she known he was down there.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm and Ceria recover in the Watch barracks, and the city takes the treasure from the ruins as their fine.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm reports that the Liscor archives yielded a map of the ruins and other underground buildings; the ruins were a tomb that Skinner was assigned to guard.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm says the old list gives Skinner the title Flesh Worm, Lesser Guardian of the Crypts.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm says the map and texts were found while the city was looking for what species Skinner was.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Later, Olesm has gained a few levels, but they do not help him beat Erin at chess.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm staggers out of Ceria's room at the inn in the morning, sees the others, and backs in to shut the door.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm loses three games in a row to Erin's mystery opponent on the magical chessboard.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm tells Erin there is no class for gamers, with [Gambler], [Layabout] or [Idler] and [Tactician] the nearest.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm writes up Erin's games in notation, and Ryoka recognises it as a newsletter or magazine.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm guesses that the mystery chess player must be a [Strategist], a class change like [Spearmaster] that comes at a certain level.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm plays chess in the Hive with Pawn and Bird.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm asks to join Ceria's adventuring group as a [Tactician]; Pisces, Yvlon and Ceria vote against him and he storms out.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm has avoided Erin since her game with the unseen player, but Erin tells him to keep playing her anyway.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm teaches chess to Antinium Workers for pay, and says he is no longer in Ceria and Erin's league in terms of levels.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Klbkch calls Olesm the highest-level [Tactician] in Liscor.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm brings news by mage spell that a Goblin Lord in the south has raised an army and that Zel Shivertail clashed with him and retreated.

section: Chess and the first dungeon, Books 1-2
text: Olesm gives Erin's group the map of Albez, which Pisces identifies.
Olesm delivers supplies to the inn while Erin is away and tells Lyonette that Zevara has put the dungeon entrance on permanent watch; he asks if she plays chess.

Olesm sends Erin's chess games, puzzles and notation to major cities; replies are misaddressed to "Oresm" after he misspells his name, and a Walled City [Strategist] tells him the puzzle helped him level.
Olesm promises to visit the inn after lunch to play chess and learn Go.

Olesm runs a chess newsletter with over twenty readers, built on Erin's puzzles and annotated games; Erin suggests logos, a "Tactician of the Week", a crossword and selling it through Runner's Guilds, and Pawn suggests sending it to Niers Astoragon.
Olesm fears sending his work to Niers Astoragon, said to be chess's inventor, before more people read it.
Olesm tells Erin a famous [Strategist] of a Walled City wants to come play her at chess.
In a council meeting Olesm asks about the Antinium's role in a siege; Ilvriss and Zel are reluctant to answer.
Zel says Liscor's [Strategists], including young Olesm, judge that the Goblin Lord will not take Esthelm.
Olesm is a Level 27 [Tactician], up from Level 22 a few months earlier, and Liscor's dedicated [Tactician]; Ilvriss calls him a prodigy and says he will soon be a [Strategist].
Olesm feels guilty for having told Regrika about Ryoka, which led to Brunkr's death and Ryoka's disappearance.
Olesm thinks the Antinium are the real enemy, though he is unsure all of them are.

Olesm and Pisces quarrel: Pisces jabs at him for loving adventuring yet not being an adventurer, and Olesm retorts that he was brave enough to go with them the first time and asks why Pisces rejected Ceria's invitation.
Olesm receives a letter and a brass ring with an eye insignia and a tiny diamond from Niers Astoragon, and puts the ring on.
Pisces tells Olesm that Niers cared about Erin's games rather than his newsletter, and that Olesm deserves praise as a [Scribe] rather than a [Tactician].
Olesm and Pisces reconcile after the argument, apologise to each other and bond over politics, Drake nobility and resentment of seniority.
Olesm thinks Ilvriss's praise is exaggerated and thinks of himself as barely smart.
Olesm reaches [Tactician Level 28] and gains the Skill [Rallying Presence].
Ilvriss tells Zel that Olesm reached Level 28 the day before and that he intends to recommend him in Salazsar.

Olesm gets word from an informant in Invrisil that Zel Shivertail has allied with Magnolia Reinhart, calls an emergency council meeting, and briefs it while Ilvriss reports to a scrying-orb council of about sixty Drake nobles in Salazsar.
Olesm downs a second giant moth with lightning.
Olesm becomes Liscor's [Strategist].
Olesm tells Ilvriss he gained two levels, is now a Level 30 [Strategist], and has the army Skill [Vigor of Champions].
Olesm offers the Hive a war gratuity for the fallen Soldiers, but Pawn says the Antinium have no such practice.
