Olesm hugs Erin and tells her the Antinium killed fourteen giant moths and never leave the Hive during the flood season.
Olesm ends a clash on the wall by shouting [Rapid Retreat] so the Soldiers clear the area.
Olesm submitted a proposal to station Pisces's undead in the sewers, which Tekshia refuses until Zevara threatens to overrule her; Selys must supervise Pisces.
Olesm and Pisces find a third entrance, a shaft from the crypt toward a Raskghar burial chamber.
Olesm explains to Embria that "horde style" vengeance dungeons are built to eradicate trespassers rather than test them, the most malignant dungeon type.
Olesm arrives at the inn after the Raskghar attack, hugs Erin, and Lyonette feeds the Gnolls and Guardsmen hamburgers.
Olesm argues the captured Cave Goblin is worth more alive, and Ilvriss realises the Redfang Hobs can translate and sends for Zevara, Embria, Tekshia and Venim.
Olesm says Erin killed Skinner, is the best chess player in this world, better than Niers Astoragon, and saved him from the crypt.
Olesm and Drassi commentate and umpire a ball game at the inn, quarrelling over the speaking crystal.
Olesm is a [Strategist] who fought in the dungeon with Ilvriss and the Watch and slew a Raskghar; he writes the official account of Liscor's victory.
Olesm delivers a report from Zeres and other strategists that Tyrion Veltras is pushing the Goblins into Drake lands.
Olesm estimates Tyrion's army is four days from Liscor and relays Tekshia's view that the rains follow a pattern.
Olesm realises from an unsigned fan letter's underlined sentence "He has trebuchets" that the walls can be breached.
Olesm calls a city-wide alarm, confiscates Erin's door under military law, and arrests the five Redfang Hobs.
Olesm loses his temper on stage, shames the Gnoll [Senator] Errif before scrying orbs across the world, and demands reinforcements; Drake cities respond with troops.
Olesm notes the water has fallen, hindering trebuchets and tunnelling.
Olesm sees about twenty-four thousand Cave Goblins camp outside Liscor and chant "Redfang".
Olesm reads the second Goblin force as dissidents from a tribal dispute, and Ilvriss expects Erin to be what draws them.
Olesm uses a scroll to fire a nova at Reiss' army from the walls, calling it a tactical shot, and Zevara tells him to stop.
Olesm is now a full [Strategist], paid an extra gold and six silver per week, and publishes a chess and Go magazine, with a twelve-silver print job at Miss Rissa's shop.
Olesm sends his magazine to Niers Astoragon by sealed Courier.

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: Olesm's newsletter analysing the Siege of Liscor suggests Goblins may be allies, which students at Wistram's academy read.

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: Olesm's newsletter proposes using Goblins as an irregular adventuring force and cancelling the ear bounty, which a listener in a command meeting dismisses as idiotic.

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: Olesm's newsletter provokes furious letters, some with poison, feces, hexes and bugs.

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: Olesm decides to write a clarification newsletter, with Raskghar notes and a Go tutorial, and goes to Pallass through Erin's door with Pisces to find books.

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: Olesm snaps "Shut up" at his table when Erin's friends cheer beating Lism and wish he had drowned, then leaves with Zevara.

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: Olesm tells Zevara that he does not know Klbkch the Slayer and that, to him, "we are all dust".

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: Olesm warns Zevara that each expansion of Liscor adds two Workers or Soldiers per new resident and that the Hive could overwhelm Liscor.

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: Olesm tells his uncle he disagrees with much of what he says but will help on the Antinium, and begins dictating a plan to him.

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: Olesm publishes a second newsletter apologising for his Goblin claims, adding an election analysis and a Guild report on the Raskghar.

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: Olesm stands behind Lism's platform and Selys realises Olesm is behind Lism's truth-spell challenge to Klbkch.

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: Olesm briefs the new Council, reporting that Manus's [Infiltrators] and [Saboteurs] attacked the lands of nobles who sieged Liscor.

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: Olesm argues the Antinium hoped to claim the dungeon for themselves and expand their Hive into it.

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: Olesm tells the Council that the Wistram [Mage] Palt said Pisces had been allowed to go free until he started committing crimes again.

section: The Goblin newsletter and election, Book 11-13
text: During the Wyvern attack on Pallass, Olesm takes command of Desk Sergeant Kel's sector as Liscor's [Strategist], using [Rapid Retreat] and [Attack Formation] while Relc uses [Triple Thrust].

section: After the break with Erin, Books 17-19
text: Olesm sides against Erin in the election and no longer feels welcome in her inn.

section: After the break with Erin, Books 17-19
text: Montressa and Bezale do not recognise Olesm and he introduces himself as a new guest.

section: After the break with Erin, Books 17-19
text: Olesm believes he is a fraud who rode Erin's coattails.

section: After the break with Erin, Books 17-19
text: Olesm has lost his spark after the break with Erin and still wears Niers's Ring of Sight; his chess magazines have stopped.

section: After the break with Erin, Books 17-19
text: Olesm vetoes action against the Free Antinium as Liscor's [Strategist], arguing that Liscor was left underfunded on purpose and demanding full funding; the Council and Zevara back him.

section: After the break with Erin, Books 17-19
text: Olesm submits that the Walled Cities may have deliberately left Liscor weak as a sacrifice, since Liscor's fall would draw Human intervention.

section: After the break with Erin, Books 17-19
text: Ilvriss grants Liscor the proposed budget with oversight.

section: After the break with Erin, Books 17-19
text: Olesm has his salary doubled and reaches [Strategist Level 33], gaining [Instantaneous Barrage (Phantom Arrows)].

section: After the break with Erin, Books 17-19
text: Olesm and Maviola become intimate after his speech; she reaches Level 49 as a [Lady Firestarter].

section: After the break with Erin, Books 17-19
text: Two days later, Maviola has moved into Olesm's apartment, and his Liscorian Gazette circulates the city.

section: After the break with Erin, Books 17-19
text: Olesm offers to take Maviola to the Healer of Tenbault or Saliss of Lights; she laughs and says she will not go today or tomorrow.

section: After the break with Erin, Books 17-19
text: Olesm is convinced the Raskghar surrender is a trick, since Calruz counted thousands of them.

section: After the break with Erin, Books 17-19
text: Olesm interrogates a captive Raskghar under three truth stones, learning that Nokha left many moons ago, taking the strong with her, a sword and magic, and told them to surrender when both moons were full.
Oom is an Acid Slime created by Az'kerash, with a mana stone as its heart.
Oom is one of the Chosen, undead who can think and grow, though not by levels; Az'kerash had five of them.
Zel Shivertail finds the core of Oom's slime body, a mana stone as large as his fist, and crushes it while Bea begs him not to.
Oom's slime body burned Zel and tried to infiltrate his body before the stone broke.
Ijvani considers Oom destroyed beyond repair, gone rather than merely broken, and fears she could be gone too.
Az'kerash thinks of Oom, an Acid Slime that perished fighting Zel Shivertail, for the first time while speaking with Bea.
Az'kerash names Oom's destruction by Zel Shivertail as the reason the gathering of his remaining Chosen is reduced.
Orjin is the Strongest of Pomle, a [Martial Artist] who has trained in Pomle all his life, since before he could walk.
Orjin trains by balancing on his toes on gravel and broken stones, without using his arms.
Orjin knows eight different weapons well enough to use them in combat.
Orjin's Skills include a tremor stomp, [Spear Dance: Crashing Rapids] and [Aeriform Shockwave].
Salii acts as Orjin's [Secretary].
Orjin stomps and uses a Skill that sends a tremor through the ground, silencing the gathered rulers' argument.
Orjin charges Nerrhavia's chariots with [Spear Dance: Crashing Rapids], severing Stitch-warriors' limbs, which turn to cloth.
Orjin leaps at the rampaging Grand Elephant Mezha and punches it once in the skull, and it sits down.
Orjin punches a jet of water aimed at Nsiia, and the blast of air knocks the Siren of Savere onto her rear.
Orjin throws his spear into a Golem's face and fights the steel Golem with fists, leaving imprints in the steel.
Orjin stops the fight and tells the rulers that any who bare a weapon again lose the peace of Pomle.
Nsiia tells Orjin he was the most enjoyable person to talk to at the gathering.
Orjin reads the Emperor of Sands' letter that Salii copied, then rips it up, saying it explains what is about to happen.
Orjin stands at Pomle's ring of coloured stones facing a Nerrhavian force of about six thousand and a Savere force of about two thousand pursuing Tiqr's refugees.
Orjin thinks the armies want the refugees as slaves.
Orjin tells the two armies that Pomle claimed this land thirty years ago, and the refugees are guests under Pomle's peace.
Orjin tells the armies to leave, warning that stepping across the line will remind them why Pomle is free.
Orjin has barely a hundred [Martial Artists] and [Warriors] with him, on the high ground with stone spears.
Both armies withdraw, and Salii leads the refugees to temporary camps.
That night Orjin helps kill a raiding party of Savere rogues, kicking one off the canyon.
Salii tells Orjin the latest group of refugees is a thousand two hundred and eighteen strong, and Pomle may run out of food.
Orjin says it is not Pomle's duty to feed the refugees, but lets Salii try to handle it.
Salii tells Orjin that Pomle has taken in over sixty thousand of Tiqr's citizens during the war.
Orjin smells blood on the wind and knows Tiqr's end is near.
Orjin has allowed many outsiders, refugees fleeing the war in Tiqr, to settle in Pomle, and some have built a small settlement.
Salii warns Orjin that the Windcaller's Wrath, a foreign martial arts group, is a cult.
Orjin beats the Fury of Skies by clinching, throwing him and punching him in the face.
Orjin mounts the Fury of Skies, locks down his arms and punches until he stops moving, stopping at the jaw and teeth.
Orjin wonders how he would kill a Kraken, or a foe that attacks from beyond the clouds like the Death of Magic.
Orjin imagines the Death of Magic killing him.
Orjin fought and beat a Grand Elephant in his youth, killed Crelers bare-handed and fought sand worms.
Orjin's [Aeriform Shockwave] reaches about three hundred feet at best, far short of the clouds.
Lacten of Pomle was weaker than Orjin and died without killing a single foe, fighting illusions.
Orjin tells Xil he beat the Fury of Skies but the Fury would do better against an aerial opponent, as Orjin cannot fly.
Salthorn tells Orjin he cannot help him fight the Death of Magic and that flying is the only reason a [Mage] would survive him.
Orthenon is the steward of King Flos, a tall, gaunt man who walks with unnatural grace and bows to his king perfunctorily when summoned.
Gazi sees Orthenon as tall, serious and once gaunt but now filled out, with a long mustache, dark somber clothing with an edge of faded gold, and a stern, unwavering, formal manner.
Orthenon and those who stayed kept the palace better maintained than the rest of the ruined city.
Orthenon says his role differs from the others' because he is the King's steward and can hardly leave his side.
Orthenon warns the twins to stay away from Gazi, who is the most feared and perhaps the most possessive of their King.
Orthenon is not one of the Seven but is second only to Flos, and is called the Left Hand of the King of Destruction.
Orthenon was raised in the Drath Archipelago, believes in formality, and will not call Flos by name alone though Flos sees him as friend as much as vassal.
Orthenon dresses for war in form-fitting enchanted leather with a single-edged sword at his belt, unlike Flos's plate or Gazi's scale armor.
Orthenon nearly ran Trey through with a sword when the twins first met Flos, before Flos stopped him.
Orthenon reports that he has found two more vassals in mercenary companies, one in Baleros, and sends encoded [Message] spells from other cities, which may be intercepted.
Orthenon says word of Flos waking is probably known to the powerful leaders of nations and perhaps Wistram's mages or Roshal's Traders, but not the world, since he has kept a lock on it.
Orthenon advises Flos to strike nearby nations first to recover strength before fighting the Empire of Sands.
Orthenon tells the twins that caution may be what holds Flos back from marching.

Flos says Orthenon learned his swordsmanship from a foreigner and studied it, so he cannot be copied by Mars or Gazi; Flos says he is not Mars's match, but expects him to be a good teacher for Teres because their tempers are similar.
Flos says he has never known Orthenon to unsheathe his sword without wrath, and Mars says Orthenon once knocked Venith off his horse in one blow.
Orthenon arrives at Manimar with about four hundred mounted warriors and knocks Venith from his saddle with a winged spear.
Orthenon scolds Flos for the reckless trip and then receives the order 'Take care of it. Please.'
Orthenon reports that three more villages of Venith's lands have declared for Flos, and that messengers to Rast, Belevadim and Chalm have had no reply.
Orthenon says Mars is competent in battle but best used at present sitting still, though her presence may inspire others.
Orthenon organises the realm for war, sending riders with news, readying walls, gear and recruits; Flos notes a formal declaration gives time because an army will not arrive for days.

Orthenon estimates the coalition army at probably 50,000 to 80,000 although one claim says seventy thousand, and thinks it led by Duke Balimar Wulten, who earned his [Duke] title in battle and is a [General].
Orthenon led Flos's armies to victory with Queravia.
Orthenon, using the Skills [Sword Art: The Tide Breaks] and [Sword Art: Scattering Petals on the Wind], cuts down pursuing lancers in battle.
Orthenon, as the King's [Steward], rides with a spear in the rescue of refugees.
Orthenon manages the conquered Hellios and Germina, quelling unrest, while Venith and Maresar guard Reim.
Orthenon greets Silmak and Clan Tannousin at Reim, offering sanctuary, and tells Nawalishifra that Flos accepted her pledge to forge a blade without equal.
Orthenon says he prepares to ride north that day despite Reim's affairs, and that he will relieve Venith and Maresar.
Orthenon tells Flos he will leave as soon as they finish speaking for Germina, send back Venith and Maresar, then Mars on reaching Hellios.
Orthenon reports that Takhatres says the Empire of Sands has pulled back armies and [Mage] battalions, and that it may be half as large as Nerrhavia's Fallen by summer's end.
Flos calls Orthenon his glorious left hand, his [Ruinbringer Steward]; Orthenon uses the Skill [Vanguard of the King, the Phantom Storm].
Orthenon leads about a hundred elite riders and knocks out the third Wistram [Mage] covering the battle in Belchan with the butt of his spear.
Orthenon circles with nearly ten thousand [Riders] to Belchan's rear and breaks its cavalry with [Sword Art: The Tide Breaks].
During Flos's duel with Raelt, Orthenon holds his sword to Geril's throat and tells General Lael the duel will not be interrupted.
Orthenon sets out Flos's terms to Raelt: Jecrass cedes nearly a quarter of its lands, becomes a vassal by magical contract, cannot declare war, and sends tribute and troops to Reim for fifteen years.
Orthenon says Lyfelt and the officials responsible for the refugees must die; Raelt wins that their families be spared and held under his charge.
Orthenon charges the Minotaur lines with [Vanguard of the King, the Phantom Storm] and [Steelflesh Charge], and falls back after veteran [Lineholders] using [The Line Holds] stop him.
Rasea severs Orthenon's forefinger and middle finger of his right hand.
Later, a Rustängmarder [Death Keeper] reattaches the two severed fingers, and tells Orthenon to watch for pain or stiffness.
Ossky is a Lieutenant and an Oldblood Drake with wings under Commander Cirille.
Ossky is a rare descendant of Dragons who breathes light, in contrast to Oldbloods who breathe fire, lightning, acid or darkness.
Ossky is useful for blinding the enemy, so long as she does not turn her head and cough.
Ossky flashes light when she speaks, and her tells show light from her nasal cavities or ears when she gets excited.
Ossky is yellow-scaled.
Cirille tells Ossky to keep her mouth shut at night, since she would otherwise snore with light, and Ossky apologizes.
Ossky is Cirille's only flight group, and her wing keeps up aerial pressure as the only fliers.
Cirille describes Ossky as an expert at Oldblood formations, where one breathes and fights.
Ossky commands the [Archers] and blinds the Demons by flying up and breathing light.
Cirille calls for a covering flash from Ossky, and the Demons are blinded while the Gnolls fall back.
Ossky nearly has her scales frozen when Chief Warrior Merish exhales a plume of frost.
Osthia Blackwing is a Drake [Soldier] and [Captain] who leads the Ancestor Guard (Oldblood) company assigned to General Thrissiam.
Osthia's wings are dark yellowish-green, her scales are bright yellow, and the spines on her head crest are dyed bright blue.
Osthia has wings, which most Drakes do not, because of the old blood in her veins.
Osthia is a graduate of Pallass' military academy with high marks.
Osthia is Thrissiam's niece, technically, though only about ten years younger and a very distant cousin.
Osthia has liked Thrissiam since meeting him as a hatchling, never told him, and tried to be assigned to his command.
Osthia does not breathe fire but spits a corrosive greenish acid from glands in her mouth.
Osthia's wings and breath attack work without the problems that afflict some Oldblood Drakes.
Osthia cannot fly long, becoming very tired after about ten minutes of flight.
Osthia drinks a foul-tasting mana potion to fly longer, and can do so only four times before she throws up.
Osthia can melt a Ghoul's face with her acid, and her own body is immune to it.
Osthia sees Garusa carry Thrissiam into a tent and not emerge, and the thought hurts her.
Osthia dives at the Goblin ranks spitting acid, goes for the Goblin Lord, and is shot down through the wings.
Osthia is rescued by Garusa, which makes her respect Garusa as a [General] while resenting her.
Osthia wishes Garusa had not taken her dream away, and cannot bring herself to say that was why she charged.
Thrissiam slaps Osthia, then forgives her and tells her to do nothing that is not ordered.
Thrissiam orders Osthia to fly away and tell the cities that the Necromancer is behind the Goblin Lord, and she flees east.
Osthia is captured by the Goblin Lord's forces ten minutes after she leaves Thrissiam, muzzled and beaten.
Osthia wakes shackled in Thrissiam's former tent and overhears the Goblin Lord being scolded by the voice of his master.
Osthia spits acid in the Goblin Lord's face, but a Ring of Protection and a [Ward of Repulsion] stop it, and he proposes that they share an enemy.
Az'kerash appears as a projection before the kneeling Goblin Lord in his tent, noting that Osthia is Oldblood but a useless corpse.
The Goblin Lord keeps Osthia as a spy who tells him information about his master.
Osthia becomes convinced there is no greater threat on the continent than the Goblin Lord's master.
Osthia's wings are bound in black metal restraints, and her hands are restrained.
The Goblin Lord forbids a muzzle on Osthia but threatens to cut out her tongue and claws if she melts anyone with acid.
Osthia thinks someone must live to warn everyone that the Goblin Lord is a pawn of Az'kerash the Necromancer.
Osthia remembers Thrissiam ordering her off the field and killing Garusa before falling to the undead.
Osthia stares at the undead each night, looking for her uncle among the Drake zombies and ghouls.
Osthia thinks each Goblin Lord is equal to a high-level [General].
Osthia privately laughs at the Goblin Lord's box formation as evidence of his inexperience.
Osthia is in the Goblin Lord's tent as Goblins read the history of the Second Antinium Wars.
Osthia is chained and muzzled beside the Goblin Lord's personal guard and used to gauge enemy tactics.
Osthia warns Zel Shivertail that the battle is a trap, spraying acid at a Hob before another clubs her down.
Osthia is the sole prisoner in Reiss's camp, with her wings manacled and her armor lost.
Osthia advises Reiss that the mountain's passages must be surrounded, and he agrees.
Osthia tried to kill Reiss after Zel Shivertail fell, knowing the Necromancer killed him, and finds she cannot hate Reiss for leaving Zel's body for the Humans.
Reiss promised to free Osthia if he made his kingdom a reality.
Osthia is introduced to Rags as a captive Drake kept alive by Reiss against his master's order for her knowledge of the Necromancer.
Osthia says Reiss kept her alive to defy the Necromancer, and that she will kill him if she can get away safely.
Reiss says that Osthia refuses to teach him chess.
Az'kerash, speaking through Reiss's body, kills Osthia with [Deathbolt], and she lies with a clenched claw wearing a black ring.
Later, Snapjaw finds Osthia's body on a wagon, and Osthia revives after half a day under the [False Death] spell.
Reiss's black ring held the spell for Osthia because he worried she might be killed, and its charge is exhausted.
Snapjaw head-butts Osthia unconscious as Reiss ordered and has her chained, saying Reiss is sorry.
Osthia escapes Reiss with her wings still bound after his lines break, and crawls through the mud to avoid the Antinium and Humans.
Wall Lord Ilvriss meets Osthia running toward Liscor and she tells him that Az'kerash is alive.
Osthia identifies herself as [Captain] of Pallass' 5th Oldblood Winged Division.
Osthia's scales are dyed blue and she is given a fake name, Osthmissa Shieldscale, which Ilvriss gave to Olesm.
Osthia says Reiss was sure his master could cast at least Tier 7 spells, probably Tier 8.
Osthia now sits in military posture, her shackles gone and her muscles recovered.
Osthia is disguised as Captain Asrira Shieldscale in Salazsar, with yellow scales under the dye.
Osthia saw Az'kerash take over his minion, the Goblin Lord Reiss.
Ilvriss persuaded Osthia to stay silent and return to Salazsar with him instead of warning the Walled Cities.
Later, Osthia is promoted to head of Ilvriss' private armed forces, and people speculate about her relationship with him.
Paige is an Australian young woman from Earth whom Daly introduces to Ken at the edge of the neutral zone.
Paige studied aerodynamics, not the engineering of workshops, and had planned to go into engineering.
Paige is the appointed treasurer of the United Nations company, under pressure to save coins.
Paige relays a rumour that a soldier near Untimely Demise's work area was shot rather than killed by undead.
Paige says she heard that the Captain was asking about the shooting but not whether he got an answer.
Paige becomes friends with Quexa after Ken, Luan and Aiko leave Gravetender's Fist.
Paige screams when the Dullahans execute the American captives.
Paige photographs a crossbow on sale in the market with her smartphone and works out how its parts fit together.
Paige plans an almost all-wood crossbow that is cheap to make, with Daly asking his boss for wood cut to her measurements.
Quexa values Paige's wooden crossbow at about two gold coins, saying it looks poor next to a metal one.
Paige adds a wooden stirrup to her crossbow so Daly can span it.
Paige gains the Skills [Reinforced Frame], [Quick Assembly] and [Advanced Crafting], and levels up quickly.
Paige has banned weapons in the house, but treats the Bushrangers as a special case.
Paige hands Kirana four gold and three silver coins as the weekly food budget and pays the month's rent through Daly.
Paige tells the group she can now make gunpowder from charcoal and saltpeter, and that volcanoes supply plenty of materials.
Paige decides to skip guns, since a [Blacksmith] would expose her work and others would steal them.
Paige plans an emergency weapon and grenades, which would be non-magical pots filled with shrapnel.
Paige builds a papier-mache grenade the size of Daly's hand, and an iron-shelled shrapnel bomb a bit smaller than a basketball.
Paige took three days of experiments to find the gunpowder ratio, and less than a week to make the bomb.
Paige fears what would happen if Quallet or a larger company got the bomb.
Paige and Daly agree the bombs stay secret and are used only on monsters, and Paige agrees to make three.
Paige cannot build ballistae because she does not know how torsional force works, which Blake thinks involved skeins of rope.
Paige and Daly decide not to tell Geneva and the other leaders about the bombs.
Paige consolidates her classes into [Blackpowder Engineer] and can make a small mound of black powder from her palm daily.
Paige tells the leaders that she and Daly have created grenades and bombs, and Geneva looks deeply betrayed.
Paige keeps producing black powder every day, agreeing with Daly though she thinks they should have told Geneva.
Paige shows Siri a steel hand-crossbow with spring steel limbs, with improved range and punching power.
Paige says the Greek Earthworlders helped her make torsion crossbows, and that she may mount a mini-ballista on a wagon.
Quallet has bought three dozen of Paige's crossbows, and Gravetender's Fist won a battle with crossbow fire at range.
Palt is a Centaur [Illusionist] and a [Mage] of Wistram on Montressa's team.
Palt is a [Fairday Illusionist], and good times are his specialty.
Palt is also a [Smoker], whose class reflects that his life revolves around smoking.
Palt can exhale a cloud of smoke with a Skill so that everyone within fifteen feet shares his vibe.
Palt says his smoke strengthens calming spells.
Palt is an amateur [Cook] with only six levels.
Palt is a member of Wistram's small Ullsinoi faction, led by the Elusive Lot, of under a hundred members.
Palt says the Ullsinoi faction is secretive and made almost entirely of the illusion school, and its members use nicknames or classes for master [Illusionists].
Palt's superior is a master named [Phantasmal Trickster].
Palt smokes cigars, dreamleaf, and a blue cigar of Mela's Kiss, a sea plant that gives off almost no smoke.
Palt can chew a nicotine gum and make a chewable dreamleaf toffee.
Palt says Centaurs are nervous, spooked by thunderstorms, and that Centaurs, Lizardfolk and Dullahans leave mountains alone.
Palt can name four holders worldwide of the Inheritance Skill [Garden of Sanctuary], including Erin.
Palt casts [Mind Blank] on Selys, [Glitterdust Storm] to reveal Pisces, and an illusion that stops Pisces from escaping down the street.
Palt tells Zevara that Pisces is responsible for deaths and offers to use a [Calm] spell on Selys.
Palt casts a calming spell over the Watch house to lower Selys's scream.
Palt tells his superiors that the Revivalists should not have put Montressa, who is too young and too focused on Pisces, in charge.
Palt's faction bails him out, since Wistram does not abandon its own, but there are consequences.
Palt introduces himself to Erin as an [Illusionist] whose team was sent to escort her to Wistram.
Palt offers Erin dreamleaf as a gift, and when she says tell me about Montressa, he does.
Erin says she heard from Palt that Montressa has nightmares almost every night.
Palt is loyal to the Ullsinoi faction, which wants an Earther, and hopes bringing Erin would be a feather in his cap.
Palt sells dreamleaf at eight silver per leaf, one leaf lasting a week, and gives free samples to the poor, since he was poor once.
Palt gives Erin saffron, cinnamon, Nali-sticks and turmeric, saying he disagrees with Montressa going after Pisces without alerting the Watch.
Erin lets Palt sit in her inn, but he must leave if the Horns, Selys, Seborn or Moore come in.
Erin tells Palt that he is the only [Mage] of his team she will talk to.
Palt cooks saffron rice with baked vegetables in the inn's kitchen and teaches Lyonette and Mrsha.
Palt says rice is to Baleros what bread is to Terandria and Izril, grown in water.
Palt memorizes Lyonette's pizza recipe to send to the Ullsinoi faction, and thinks Wistram's big factions monopolize knowledge of Earth.
Palt tells Erin that Wistram has sent his team to rescue anyone from Earth, because the world is dangerous.
Palt tells Erin he is low on the hierarchy and cannot control Montressa, who has orders to bring her to Wistram.
Palt joins the linked Wistram mages in the battle with insects, linking with Ulinde, and adds his magic to Montressa's [Valmira's Comets].
Palt says that abducting Erin would be too costly politically and that she would not leave of her own volition.
The Ullsinoi faction persuades the Revivalists not to interfere with the inn for a few concessions, after a night of debate by the Elusive Lot.
Palt gasps for Beza not to follow Montressa, and later begs Ksmvr to let him stop their team, but Ksmvr aims a bow at Palt and Ulinde.
Palt shouts at Isceil to use his breath on the Creler.
Palt tells Erin that Isceil is dead after they held as long as they could.
Palt shakes Pisces' hand and asks forgiveness, saying he misjudged him.
Palt, Montressa and Beza return after two weeks away, and Lyonette wonders if they took Isceil's body.
Palt says they brought Isceil's remains within range of Fissival's teleportation network, where the body was taken, and the family did not speak to them.
Palt asks permission to write sigils by Erin's door so that Ullsinoi allies get free passage.
Palt says the Ullsinoi faction does not deal with criminals, and compensates Erin for help she gives.
Palt tells Erin that Montressa and Beza have a vested interest in her door and want to negotiate for their factions.
Chaldion says Palt offered him a cigar, and that Wistram has its tentacles in the inn.
Palt volunteers to dry cocoa beans with magic when Erin makes chocolate.
Palt, Montressa and Beza claim new second-floor rooms and are dead to the world on the morning after the party.
Palt tells Erin that the Elusive Lot want her information on weight training, and she agrees to share it in exchange for favors.
Palt says Montressa and Beza are in the inn for orders from their factions, and the Ullsinoi faction has Erin claimed in a non-possessive way.
Palt tries a charm spell on Erin which fails, and Montressa and Beza laugh at him.
Palt says charm spells and love potions are banned hard in Baleros.
Palt casts an advert reading "Presented by the Ullsinoi of Wistram" in the air over the broadcast, which the Ullsinoi call the world's first advert.
Palt gives Lyonette and Pawn dreamleaf, including a chewable toffee, and Pawn becomes high.
Palt, Montressa and Beza try to calm the Liscor crowd with [Mass Calm], [Calm] and [Calming Winds] while Erin uses her lantern.
Palt casts [Fog of Apathy], and a Gnoll notices the spells and says they are using spells on them, making the crowd furious.
Palt covers the retreat with [Volcanic Smokescreen], and a brick hits him in the chest at the inn's door.
Maviola's [Fast Fireball] and Pyrite save the group.
Palt copies images from Kevin's laptop into an illusion of a bicycle for Pelt and Hedault.
Palt gives Montressa and Bezale the skateboard plans as part of his sharing agreement.
Palt tells Ryoka and the other Earthers they are under the protection of the Elusive Lot and the Ullsinoi faction, and that Erin has asked him to be their formal contact.
The Elusive Lot's sign is a U with a twist at the ends that looks like a horseshoe.
Pawn is an Antinium Worker who took his own name after Erin Solstice told him he was an individual.
Pawn plays chess with Erin and has a [Tactician] class from the game, and later becomes the Hive's only [Acolyte], then a [Priest] who leads the Painted Antinium in prayer.
Pawn is a Worker who, when Erin Solstice tells him he is an individual and could be one, says that this one has become "I".
Selys tells Erin that Antinium Workers have no names and must never be asked for them.
Pawn is distressed at being an individual and calls himself an Aberration, saying that when the many become one it is Aberration.
Pawn tells Erin that he is sad and sorry for the deaths of Klbkch and the Worker, after she says she is simply sad.
Pawn asks Erin for a name, will not ask his Queen, and chooses the name "Pawn" for himself.
Pawn plays chess with Erin, and she says she was the one who gave him his name.
Pawn tells Erin that among the Workers all is unchanged, but that they sense the Queen below doing something unknown and that another Prognugator now guards the Hive and walks above.
Pawn tells Erin that the Workers level quickly, that it is rare for Workers to level, and that they owe her a debt.
Ksmvr comes to Erin's inn to ascertain the state of the Worker "Pawn", orders him to stand, and takes him back into the city to be questioned.
Workers at the inn tell Erin that Pawn will be interrogated to determine whether he is an Aberration, and that he will be executed if he is.
Pawn is returned to the inn helped by two Workers, missing an antenna, three arms and part of a leg and trailing green blood.
Pawn says he is an individual and Antinium, that he was questioned and tested and passed, and that the Prognugator let him go.
Erin bandages Pawn's stumps; the adventurers' healing potions have stopped the bleeding, but lost limbs cannot be restored.
Pawn tells Calruz that he had no right to resist the Prognugator, who judges other Antinium and may use their lives, and that the Antinium have no honor.
Pawn tells the adventurers that the Queen is occupied with the Process of Anastases.
Pawn tells the adventurers that the Antinium came ten years earlier, that a single Hive was sent to Liscor and paid gold for a place among those not of the Hive, to make a new kind of Antinium.
Pawn declines Erin's offer to stay and says he belongs in his Hive.
Pawn knows his Queen would never order him to die and lies when he agrees that the Antinium would reclaim him, to protect Erin.
Pawn returns to the Hive, accompanied by Ceria and Gerial.
Pawn walks to Erin's inn with four other Antinium, saying they have no tasks because they are waiting for the Queen, who will finish tomorrow.
Erin thinks Pawn plays chess aggressively and takes chances, as if he had a confidence boost, perhaps from what happened with Ksmvr.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn tells Ksmvr that Klbkch's motives are unclear and supposes he will no longer be a worker, after Klbkch says Pawn stays under his authority rather than Ksmvr's.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn tells Ksmvr that he hates him, because Ksmvr cut off his arms and leg, though he serves the Hive and is loyal to the Queen.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn asks Ksmvr whether he knows how to play chess.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn comes to the inn with one good hand, helped by another Worker, and Erin hugs him.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn tells Erin that the Hive has substances that regenerate Antinium limbs and that he expects to regain mobility within the month.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn tells Erin that the Revalantor has instructed the Antinium to rebuild her inn and that they should finish by midnight; Pawn directs the other Workers in the repairs.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Ksmvr reports to the Queen that the Workers are being tested as Pawn suggested, and that Pawn and Bird brought together the Workers who had visited the inn to recreate the conditions for individuality.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Ksmvr reports that of the five Individuals Pawn, the first, is the most independent and assumes a position of command among them while staying receptive to Klbkch's orders.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: The Queen summons Pawn and the other four Individuals and questions them about their nature and what they might achieve.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn tells Erin the Queen asked what being an individual means, what classes they can take, and whether he would lead Soldiers to battle.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn tells Erin he has a [Tactician] class gained from chess and is the highest-level Antinium besides Klbkch, but that he has stopped leveling and cannot lead armies.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn tells Erin he is lost, since he cannot go back to being a Worker and not even his Queen knows what the Individuals are.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn tells Erin that he alone, not the Queen, Ksmvr or Klbkch, suggested that the Workers go to defend her and die.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn names the dead Workers Magnus, Rook, Calabrian, Vladimir and Emmanuel, and the living Individuals Bird, Garry, Belgrade and Anand, saying only they remember the fallen.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn listens to Erin's stories of God, a son who died on a cross, redemption and Heaven, and on the walk back to the city he believes for a moment.

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn receives [Acolyte Class Obtained!], [Acolyte Level 1!] and [Skill - Prayer Obtained!].

section: Book 2: Recovery, the Queen's questions and faith
text: Pawn is said to be occupied within the Hive and unable to visit the inn.

section: Book 3: The Hive, the [Acolyte] and the Soldiers
text: Pawn sleeps sitting upright with the other Antinium, eats the same brown-grey paste as the Workers and has regrown all but a few digits, with his severed limbs nearly regenerated.

section: Book 3: The Hive, the [Acolyte] and the Soldiers
text: Pawn is one of five original Individuals, with Bird, Belgrade, Anand and Garry; over a hundred newer Individuals chose names and play chess in a room of the Hive, but still obey orders and show no personality.

section: Book 3: The Hive, the [Acolyte] and the Soldiers
text: Pawn has the [Tactician] class but has stagnated and stopped leveling, like Erin.

section: Book 3: The Hive, the [Acolyte] and the Soldiers
text: Pawn doubts what it means to be an [Acolyte], having believed that night and gained a Skill, [Prayer].

section: Book 3: The Hive, the [Acolyte] and the Soldiers
text: Pawn tells Lyonette he cannot digest gluten, is served eggs and bacon, pays with coins Klbkch gave him, and decides to ask Klbkch about his class because Erin is gone.

section: Book 3: The Hive, the [Acolyte] and the Soldiers
text: Pawn recalls being afraid only when Ksmvr questioned him and when he heard the undead were attacking Liscor and feared for Erin; he dislikes both Ksmvr and Klbkch and is afraid of Klbkch.

section: Book 3: The Hive, the [Acolyte] and the Soldiers
text: Pawn counts Relc and Erin among his friends.

section: Book 3: The Hive, the [Acolyte] and the Soldiers
text: The Queen told Pawn to report any change in his level or class to Klbkch, who monitors the new Individuals.

section: Book 3: The Hive, the [Acolyte] and the Soldiers
text: Pawn gives his food bowl to a Soldier in the Soldiers' mess whose own bowl was spilled.

section: Book 3: The Hive, the [Acolyte] and the Soldiers
text: Pawn tells the Soldiers Erin's account of God, creation, sin and a God who cares for everyone, and the Soldiers gather close to listen.

section: Book 3: The Hive, the [Acolyte] and the Soldiers
text: Pawn returns the next day to tell the Soldiers of a man who died on a cross and a prophet who parted seas, and believes the Soldiers believe.

section: Book 3: The Hive, the [Acolyte] and the Soldiers
text: Pawn tells the Soldiers about Heaven, a place God made where there is no suffering, they need not fight and no one orders them about.
After Pawn's talk of Heaven, hundreds of the Soldiers fight and kill one another in what Pawn realises is mass suicide, and Klbkch strikes Pawn with a sword pommel for it.
Pawn tries to pray to God during the Soldiers' slaughter, calling on his [Prayer] Skill, but hears no answer.
Pawn reasons that Antinium Soldiers cannot be called sinful because they were born without any choice and to disobey was to die.
Pawn stops the slaughter by shouting; he says there is no god for the Antinium and no Heaven yet, but that the Antinium must build one themselves and must live.
Klbkch tells Pawn that the form all Antinium wear is that of Galuc, the Builder, one of the Centenium, whose form was saved after Klbkch's own was lost when he died at sea.
Klbkch says he will tell Pawn more about Gods if Pawn can turn the surviving Soldiers into something more; Pawn then sits among the dead Soldiers and prays.
Afterward Pawn is a Level 6 [Acolyte] with the Skill [Humble Presence], and Klbkch has given him command of the remaining Soldiers; hundreds had died.
Pawn's [Humble Presence] makes him ordinary-looking unless he does something that stands out or is alone, and Klbkch says it may have uses in battle.
Pawn tells his Soldiers they will not fight that day and to rest in barracks, which displaces the shift system until Klbkch reassigns them to protective details.
Pawn brings twenty Soldiers to Erin's inn, where Lyonette offers them food.
Pawn notes that Soldiers have formless gouging digits, reinforced carapaces and larger mandibles, unlike his Worker hands.
Pawn gave a Soldier the name Robert, but unlike Workers the Soldiers neither became Individual nor Aberration; Pawn realises they have no voices to speak a name.
Pawn tells Selys the official line from Klbkch that the Hive's Soldier patrol exists to eliminate monsters and improve citizens' morale, and he accepts that it is a promotion.
Pawn stops a Soldier from smashing a nest of eggs, calling them innocent.
Pawn realises that paint paw prints on a Soldier mark him with an identity better than a name, and he buys all of Lyonette's paint.
Pawn buys all of Krshia's paint except brown and black, and about twenty brushes; her stall is smaller and poorer than before.
Pawn concludes that paint, needing no voice, turns identical faceless Soldiers into people.

Pawn tells Klbkch that painting is a way of naming Soldiers without words; he would not try it on Soldiers outside his command, who might become Aberration, and Klbkch has the experiment monitored before expanding it.
Klbkch tells Pawn that the patrol has won goodwill in the city, orders him to take twenty Soldiers and retrieve trophies from the monsters they slay, and allows a second patrol at his discretion.
Pawn orders cheese from Krshia enough to feed roughly two hundred and forty individuals, trusting her because Erin does.
Krshia tells Pawn her rebuilt stall will take a year or more to reopen with pride, and Pawn thinks the stall is smaller and poorer than before.
Pawn gets a large jar of honey from Lyonette for Krshia, with the message "I am very sorry", and tells Krshia it is the beginning of an apology.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Pawn is put in charge of the Antinium sent to help rebuild Esthelm, a group of over a hundred Soldiers and three hundred Workers, because Klbkch has to deal with Antinium from other Hives.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Pawn assigns Belgrade and Anand, his sub-leaders, to repair a wall, and the two [Tacticians] command the Soldiers without spoken orders; Bird goes off to hunt birds with a bow.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Pawn asks General Zel Shivertail what to say to a dying soldier under his command, and Zel tells him to say what they need to hear, or sometimes nothing, and to hold their claw.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Pawn plays Zel at chess, and Zel bows out when Pawn proves the far better player.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Bird, Belgrade, Anand, Garry and Pawn were the only survivors of the first Individuals.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Pawn and Bird come into Erin's inn from the snow, Pawn asking Lyonette if Erin is there and Bird carrying a dead bird.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Pawn is an [Acolyte], the first of his kind, and commands hundreds of Soldiers; he has no god but believes in heaven, and that faith gave him his class and Skills.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Pawn let his Soldiers paint themselves with thick, water-resistant paint bought from Krshia, so each can be told apart.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Belgrade, overwhelmed by Shield Spiders and armored monsters, shakes in the chess room; Pawn tells him that on Klbkch's order he will fight with his Soldiers, who are of higher level than the others.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Belgrade makes Pawn promise to stay behind his Soldiers, saying he would not know how to speak to Erin if Pawn died.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Pawn tells Prognugator Tersk that paint is only a marking the Soldiers chose themselves, and compares him to Ksmvr for not understanding what it means to be Individual; Tersk replies that Ksmvr was expelled from the Hive for incompetence.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Pawn is unmarked after the battle, sheltered behind his Soldiers, and holds a dying Soldier who has no body below the chest while Xrn clears the passage.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Pawn loses twenty five Soldiers, exactly a quarter of his command, and the dead Soldier is taken to be processed for food.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Pawn paints a green star on the barracks wall to remember the dead Soldier who bore it, and the other Soldiers paint marks for their fallen.

section: Book 4-5: Esthelm and the Hive battle
text: Pawn heard Belgrade report to Klbkch that over two hundred Workers and about half as many Soldiers died in the fighting.
Pawn believes Aberrations arise when a Worker cannot make sense of the death and emptiness of Hive life, and he feels he came close to that once.
Pawn is reunited with Erin, who hugs him tightly enough to stop his shaking.
Pawn tells Ryoka Griffin that he is a Level 6 [Acolyte], a class received after he prayed and Erin told him of religion and heaven.
Klbkch tried to kill Pawn for knowing about gods and told him not to speak of gods to anyone.
Pawn tells Ryoka he believes in Jesus Christ as a God but not as his own, since the Antinium created themselves and God did not create them.
Pawn says he believes in the Antinium, in Heaven, in an afterlife and miracles, and that Gods exist but the Antinium have none.
Pawn asks Ryoka how to make unleavened bread, plans a communion of bread and honey for the Antinium, and wants to hear of every human religion because the Antinium copy what is glorious.
Pawn asks for a censer, valued for its physical presence, possibly on a chain, which Erin notes is properly called a thurible.
Pawn trusts Lyonette fully because she fed his Soldiers and himself, gave them honey and shelter, and helped paint the Soldiers.
Pawn gains [Acolyte Level 8] and the Skill [Mass Prayer], then wakes in the Wandering Inn's basement under a blanket, still holding the thurible.
Later, Pawn tells a unit of Soldiers that he cannot command, then promotes the yellow-splattered Soldier to [Sergeant] as the unit's leader.
Pawn asks Klbkch to be assigned to combat duty with his entire unit of Soldiers.
Pawn walks the Hive tunnels humming and swinging the thurible, followed by painted Soldiers clicking their mandibles in unison; Belgrade names the feeling "Faith".
Pawn sits outside the inn with over a hundred Soldiers, eats bee soup, and tells Prognugator Tersk that praying only takes faith in "us".
Pawn tells Erin that Belgrade and Anand would love to see her game, and the two come wounded and covered in orange slime.
Pawn brings painted Soldiers and a score of Workers to expand Erin's inn, starting with scaffolding and a foundation.

section: Book 5-6: Inn expansion and the Painted Soldiers
text: Pawn tells Erin that Tersk says the Armored Antinium use crossbows, and that Pawn's Hive has a limited supply of bows and arrows used mainly against aerial foes.

section: Book 5-6: Inn expansion and the Painted Soldiers
text: Pawn tells Erin he placed the new watch tower at the back of her inn in case she later wants another tower, a fourth floor or a ballista; he is not aware of how to build enchanted lightning-throwing towers.

section: Book 5-6: Inn expansion and the Painted Soldiers
text: Pawn, censer in hand, tends the wounded Soldiers during fighting in the Hive tunnels, and Sergeant Yellow Splatters leads forty of his Soldiers.

section: Book 5-6: Inn expansion and the Painted Soldiers
text: Belgrade and Anand never contradict Pawn except on strategy, and Yellow Splatters regards the sole [Acolyte] and first Worker to become Individual as deeply respected, though not a leader.

section: Book 5-6: Inn expansion and the Painted Soldiers
text: Pawn adds a pile of picture books to the barracks, which the Soldiers leave untouched.

section: Book 5-6: Inn expansion and the Painted Soldiers
text: Pawn lays his hands on the Aberration Twin Stripes, Purple Smile and Yellow Splatters and says "Hope", using [Benediction of Hope]; Twin Stripes calms and is freed.

section: Book 5-6: Inn expansion and the Painted Soldiers
text: Pawn explains that he can use [Benediction of Hope] three times per day, which he thinks calms thoughts and gives hope and understanding of being Individual.

Pawn walks the walls of Liscor during the Face-Eater Moth attack with an incense censer, naming the fallen painted Soldiers (Blue Circles, Jilted Lines, Leaves of Trees) while the Soldiers answer with clicks of their mandibles.
Pawn says that after the attack he has been busy flood-proofing the Hive and has expanded his unit to many more Workers and Soldiers.
Pawn asks Erin for entertainment for his unit that cannot be done outdoors, since rain stops patrols and books go only so far.

Pawn leads a weekly sermon of about twenty minutes in a converted barracks, telling his congregation that there is no god for them, that he believes in heaven and in them, and that they will build heaven themselves.
Pawn hands out flatbread wafers after the sermon, an innovation he persuaded Klbkch to add to his budget.

Pawn's congregation grew in the weeks after he gained [Benediction of Hope]; his unit now includes Individual Workers made by his chess experiments, who are not Aberrations but are less distinct than Pawn, Belgrade and the others.
Not all of Pawn's Individuals pray: Belgrade will not, Anand might, Garry has no time and Bird prefers his tower.
Lyonette has told Pawn her secret that she is a [Princess], which he keeps, having come to know her while Erin was away from the inn.
When Lyonette says she has lost her class, Pawn promises to pray for it to return and later says he prays for it every day.
Pawn visits the inn every day, asking Lyonette whether she is well, and Yellow Splatters comes to think something is wrong with him.
Pawn curls up in the barracks, refusing to move or eat, after believing that his prayers angered Lyonette.
Klbkch kicks Pawn and cracks his carapace, draws his swords and places the tip on his neck, then withdraws and calls him a disgrace.
Erin rolls, sits on and tries to tickle the curled-up Pawn without success, then tells him his Soldiers and Workers are on hunger strike, and he uncurls.
Erin tells Pawn she loves him like the son she does not plan to have.
Pawn tells his unit that Erin is not their friend but is to Workers what the sun is to grass, "the sky", and that Lyonette is the only friend he has.
Pawn hollows out and decorates a barracks as a ball for Lyonette as an apology, with a yellow dress on a stand that Krshia helped him pick out, so she could dance and be happy.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: Pawn tells Lyonette that on Krshia's advice, not Erin's, he came to tell her how he feels, and that when Krshia asked how much he likes her he said he likes her more than Erin.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: Lyonette realises that Pawn's liking for her is romantic; he had not understood this himself, and thought romance was only for Drakes, Humans and Gnolls.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: Pawn tells Lyonette that he is an [Acolyte] who believes in things that may never exist, and that she is a [Princess] who must have her class back.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: Pawn tells Lyonette that Klbkch says a third of the disputes he settles are rooted in romantic conflict, and fears he might start attacking her.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: The next day Pawn takes Lyonette's hand in the inn, does not want to let go, and agrees to find out whether what they feel is love.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: Pawn greets Bird in the barracks after Bird follows the flow of Antinium in the tunnel.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: When Bird breaks down before Halrac, Pawn asks to apologise alongside Bird, saying he has known Bird as long as he has been alive, and the Antinium leave promising to return the next night.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: Pawn prays for good fortune for the Antinium baseball team, telling Erin that prayer is not a limited resource.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: Erin, Klbkch, Pawn, Belgrade and Anand were consulted about whether Bird could meet Bevussa.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: Pawn says he is jealous of the Goblins, since Erin seems to spend more time with them than with the Antinium, and in her inn makes peace with Numbtongue as Yellow Splatters shares his soup.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: Pawn leads the Painted Soldiers to Erin's hill with a glowing censer; Ceria sees no magic in it, and Erin calls it faith made manifest.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: During the Goblin Lord's march, Klbkch lets Pawn leave the Hive only to scout the inn and Erin's condition, and Pawn leaves by the hidden auxiliary tunnel near the inn.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: Pawn begs Sergeant Yellow Splatters and the Painted Soldiers to defy the Queen and save Erin, saying she made him who he is and told him of faith.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: Pawn insists on going with the Soldiers, saying they will need his prayers, and leads the march with his censer, telling them to pray only to survive and believe in each other.

section: Book 8-9: Lyonette, the Raskghar and the war for Erin
text: Pawn kneels before the bodies of a hundred and one dead Painted Soldiers, and Lyonette tells him they were heroes he will never forget.

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Pawn sits among hundreds of Workers and Soldiers in a room covered with colorful symbols for the fallen, which Erin finds moving because the Antinium vow the dead will not be forgotten.

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Pawn kneels in the Hive and prays for his people to stop suffering and for peace and Heaven, which he and the Painted Soldiers will build if none exists.

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Pawn offers a morning and a night prayer to the Painted Soldiers in their barracks, swinging a cinnamon-scented censer on a stick.

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Pawn heals a Shield Soldier's open leg wound by pressing two hands to it, on a hill during Erin's party.

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Klbkch tells Pawn and Yellow Splatters that Pawn can heal a smaller wound in moments six times in an hour, which is unprecedented but less useful than any quality healing potion.

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Yellow Splatters, who returned after dying, tells Pawn that Heaven is real and small and fragile, and that it must be guarded and grown by the Painted Antinium; he tells Pawn "We forgive you".

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Pawn kneels as Yellow Splatters returns and is told of Heaven, and gains [Acolyte Level 18!] and [Miracle - Heal Minor Wounds obtained!].

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Archer B19 thanks Erin for soup and chess, and Pawn stands beside Lyonette, then she holds his hand as they go to "supervise" the third-floor construction.

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Pawn creates loaves of bread with [Create Bread], a Skill gained at Level 20 along with his ability to conjure light, and breaks them into tiny pieces for the Workers and Soldiers.

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Pawn says a crust of his bread, four days old, has not vanished, and Anand finds the bread real and tasting like Erin's.

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Pawn uses [Benediction of Hope] three times and [Heal Minor Wounds], healing barely twelve Antinium before fatigue stops him.

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Pawn hugs two Soldiers, Chesacre and Thaina, who named themselves from an alphabet in the room; they are [Acolytes] who watch the others when Pawn leaves.

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Pawn uses [Holy Radiance], which makes his body glow a soft blue to the Antinium and blinds only his enemies.

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Anand reports to Klbkch that Pawn is now a Level 23 [Priest], a low increase in levels but enough to change his class.

section: Book 10-14: Priest of the Painted Antinium
text: Anand reports that Pawn can heal one moderate wound, or repeat the Skill on a larger wound inefficiently, up to twelve times, and becomes extremely fatigued afterwards.
Dekass of the Armored Antinium sees Pawn as a smaller Worker who now and then stops to poke himself in the head, which Dekass takes for a defect.

Pawn and Lyonette have sex for the first time in her room, against Klbkch's orders, after planning it for a month, using a harness Pawn bought from Krshia's shop; Pawn casts [Heal Minor Wounds] by accident.
Pawn reaches Level 24 as a [Priest] and gains a new power that is not a Skill, over which Lyonette is excited.
Mrsha knows that Pawn and Lyonette had sex the night before, and Pawn tells her he is very fond of Lyonette before Lyonette covers his mandibles.
Pawn and Lyonette keep their relationship secret from everyone except Mrsha and plan to use another bedroom.
Klbkch, in a murderous state, tells Pawn in the Hive that the Rite of Anastases is not for him; Pawn refuses to flee, saying some things are worth dying for.

Pawn raises his censer and a [Miracle - Holy Barrier] stops Klbkch's sword; Klbkch screams at the sight, strikes at it with a sword saying he will slay God, and drives the blade through Pawn's stomach.
Pawn is stabbed and bleeding green blood, and is saved when Xrn points her staff and magic halts the bleeding.

Pawn leads a service in a new wing of the inn funded by Xrn and conceived by Erin and Pawn, a copy of a Hive room, where wounded Workers paint themselves after the riot; the Painted Antinium click their mandibles.
Pawn blesses the first Worker with [Benediction of Hope] and prays for the Workers who died.
Lyonette goes after Pawn into his rooms and holds his hand, crying, as he says he could not bring the dead back and one died.
Pawn is now a [Priest] and leader of the Painted Antinium along with Yellow Splatters, while Garry is a [Cook] and Bird is Bird.
Xrn stress-tests Pawn's [Holy Barrier] with a Tier 4 spell, [Siege Fireball], which holds for a moment before the barrier winks out and Pawn runs away screaming.

Pawn announces that he is writing a sacred text, a guide to finding Heaven for the Antinium, with its first entry just added, and plans to hire an [Illustrator] to add the sky and a flower to each copy.
Pawn's text states that the gods, if they existed, were not gods for the Antinium, who were not born but made, and it admits the gaps in what he knows.
Pebblesnatch is a small Cave Goblin whose name Numbtongue gives to Erin.
Pebblesnatch is a scrawny, young Cave Goblin with grey skin who wears a big white chef's hat.
Pebblesnatch has crimson eyes.
Pebblesnatch keeps a worn white cloth as her pillow and a glowing crimson mana stone she shows no one.
Pebblesnatch remembers Erin's inn as the one time in her life she felt safe.
A captive Cave Goblin, Pebblesnatch bites at Erin's extended hand and the Redfangs cuff her.
Pebblesnatch wets herself on the Hobs carrying her to the bathroom.
Pebblesnatch obeys the Redfangs because they are Hobs, which Numbtongue explains to Erin as Hobs being natural leaders.
Pebblesnatch sleeps in Badarrow's room, locked in, with a Hob watching her all night.
Pebblesnatch places a purple mana stone on a crude metal door the Cave Goblins built and opens it onto Erin's inn, in front of the Raskghar.
Pebblesnatch receives a giant cookie from Erin and reluctantly gives out fingernail-sized pieces to other Goblins.
Erin appoints Pebblesnatch to marshal the cooks of three tribes, and she wears the chef's hat and shouts "Cook!"
Pebblesnatch's harsh critiques of the cooks anger the hungry Goblins, since her standards come from Erin's inn.
Pebblesnatch has the Skill [Quick Boiling], while other contestants use [Glove Grip] and other Skills.
Pebblesnatch kills a Rock Crab with the Goblins and cooks soup in its upturned shell.
The judges rank Pebblesnatch's soup the worst entry because of blood taste, uneven cooking and dull extras.
Pebblesnatch loses to Garry's dish, is humbled, then decides her soup was not that bad.
Pebblesnatch got the hat back after it ended up on Garry's head, and hides in Erin's kitchen afraid.
Pebblesnatch returns to the old dungeon cave for the red mana stone from the door, and hides as Reiss' and Tyrion's armies pass.
Pebblesnatch is trapped in the cave and held there afraid, with the stone clutched in her claws.
Pebblesnatch is among the Goblin prisoners, crying as Ulvama strokes her head.
Pebblesnatch is carried north in a cage in a wagon after the Humans dragged her from her hiding place.
Pebblesnatch has nightmares of the dungeon, the Raskghar and the Facestealer, and dreams of the inn that wake her in the cage.
Pebblesnatch is a [Grabber], [Cook] and [Hider] with over thirteen levels, high for a Cave Goblin.
Pebblesnatch steals a pan and ladle, bites Ulvama and flees to hide in a tree trunk.
Pebblesnatch puts on her chef's hat and orders two Cave Goblins to fetch eggs, and the other Goblins let her pass.
Pebblesnatch credits Erin and Garry for her cooking, having learned from Garry the night of the cooking competition.
Pebblesnatch fries meat scraps and eggs into a Wildegg Pocket and wins over Raidpear with it.
Pebblesnatch reaches Cook Level 6 and gains [Ingredients Sense (Minor)].
Pebblesnatch reaches Cook Level 10 and becomes a [Forager Cook], with Grabber removed, gaining [Natural Oils] and [One More Portion].
Pebblesnatch's [Natural Oils] distills cooking oil from the animals the Redfangs bring in.
[One More Portion] always leaves Pebblesnatch a bit more food than expected, and even Ulvama praises it.
Pebblesnatch charges alone at the Human army with a ladle, climbs Durene and is held in the air.
Mavika and the [Witches] step between the forces, and Mavika declares the Goblins not at fault, ending the battle.
At the Goblin wall, Pebblesnatch recognises Griffon Hunt and waves, and the Gold-rank team decides to stay a while.
Pebblesnatch has a new Skill, [Remove Food Poisoning], as a [Forager Cook].
Pebblesnatch cooks Dropped Eggs Soup for Griffon Hunt, using chicken stock, flour, garlic powder and ginger.
Peclir Im is a Human [Chamberlain], an experienced high-level servant who works under Foliana.
Peclir is a [Chamberlain] because [Stewards] are rare and require royalty to appoint them.
Peclir has worked for four years and notes his anniversary is that month.
Peclir fears dying of a heart attack like his predecessor, whom people still discuss as the previous [Majordomo].
Peclir cleans Niers's dishes and offers to poison rats in the Fraerling passages.
Peclir is the [Chamberlain] of the Forgotten Wing company who keeps much of Niers's citadel academy and home running.
Peclir brings Niers a purple cloth-covered item on a pillow when Niers summons him.
Peki is a Garuda [Martial Artist] with bright purple-and-green feathers, and a Lieutenant and student at Niers Astoragon's academy.
Peki tells Xol that Pomle's Strongest taught her to fight.
Orjin recalls Peki, a Garuda he used to train, who challenged him each time and promised to return when she met the Titan.
Peki cannot swim, because she is a Garuda and flies.
Peki says she came to see the Walled Cities before going home to Pomle, and to find treasure.
Peki uses [Aerial Dance: Waterfall Strikes] to strike down Xol's armour from the air.
Peki has trained to fight in the air and dodges pirates' spells and arrows.
Peki uses a [Galewinds] scroll to blast a pirate ship's sail around.
Xol's [Attraction Shield] pins Peki to his shield and slams her into the street, leaving her unconscious.
Perorn says Peki has outstanding fighting Skills but a subpar choice of opponents, and orders her to duel Perorn's officers.
Peki thrashes in stormy water, and Wil swims to her and is pulled aboard by a rope.
Peki lies to Bloodtear Pirates that Drowned Folk attacked her, then kicks the wheel so their ship's boom crashes into another ship.
Peki drops explosive alchemical flasks on pursuing ships, while the other [Strategists] throw a glass sword and barrels of liquor as feints.
Peki asks if she can fight the undead.
Peki follows Venaz to stall pursuers until Feshi's Gnoll reinforcements arrive.
Pekona is a young Human woman and a [Blade Dancer] in the party Vuliel Drae, carrying a wide, double-edged curved sword.
Pekona says [Blade Dancer] is a class from where she is from, with unique footwork and sword techniques, not copyable by just copying the moves.
Pekona's people live on the Drath Archipelago and speak a language different from the rest of the world.
Pekona is a silent woman, as her command of the common tongue is weaker than her teammates'.
Pekona demonstrates her sword style, and Toren memorizes it in minutes without blinking or forgetting.
Pekona stares at Toren with admiration and fear after Toren copies her moves with the same timing.
Pekona takes charge of the group as they leave Liscor for the dungeon.
Pekona produces the longsword with the forked rune that Insill gives to masked Toren.
Pekona guards the dungeon entrance with Larr while Vuliel Drae protects Gemhammer.
Lord Pellmia is a [Lord] of Izril, broader in the shoulder and gut than Tyrion, with a mustache, and rides a white stallion.
Pellmia is probably fifteen years older than Tyrion, close to sixty, but looks like a young man in the evening light.
Pellmia has lived over sixty years, survived both Antinium Wars and fought Goblins on his land.
Pellmia has the Skills [Second Wind] and [Far Riders], which restore vigor and let slow horses outdistance horses without Skills.
Pellmia has a son, Gilam, and an old companion named Kilmet.
Pellmia leads a second cavalry force in a wedge charge on the Goblin army, using [Second Wind], with Welca Caveis at his side.
Pellmia reports that his charge scattered the Goblins around Pyrite's city on the first attack.
Pellmia says he did not assault the city because of the Goblins' many pikes and crossbows, and he has been rationing healing potions to the wounded.
Pellmia carries out Tyrion's orders while guessing at what Tyrion has planned.
Pellmia leads over five thousand mounted Humans sent by Tyrion who pursued Rags' tribe for three days.
Rags judges Pellmia a Lord whose Skills revitalize his forces and make them move faster than normal.
Pellmia has promised Tyrion that he will reach the meeting spot by the sixth day.
Pellmia wonders why Tyrion spent so much effort on a tribe of under ten thousand, and guesses Tyrion cares more about the [Emperor].
Pellmia has his men dismount and run beside their horses, restoring them with [Second Wind], and runs too after putting his armor in his bag of holding.
Pellmia is burned in a forest fire the Goblins set, and a [Healer] applies poultice to his skin and warns he needs it reapplied.
Pellmia refuses Gilam's demand for a hundred [Knights] to retrieve his stolen horse Olli, since the Goblins spared him.
Pellmia puts Gilam under Kilmet's authority in the vanguard and says the duty to Tyrion changes nothing.
The spared Gilam makes Pellmia doubt his certainty about Goblins, and he thinks of the small Chieftain's size.
Pellmia resigns his command to Tyrion, saying the Chieftain could have killed Gilam and did not.
Pellmia tells Tyrion that his legacy is more uncertain than he hoped, since Gilam is not the man he wanted.
Later, Pellmia accepts Tyrion's request to command the infantry instead, with Gilam kept safe in the rear.
Pelt is a short, bearded Dwarf [Smith] who works a forge beside Maughin's in Pallass.
Pelt is a master blacksmith who can work mithril and other metals beyond steel.
Pelt is a Dwarf from Deríthal-Vel, which he calls Dwarfhome, and he travelled far from it.
Pelt is a miserable, grumpy drunk who stumbles into his forge late in the morning, badly hung over.
Pelt rests in a sling chair of crossed legs and stretched canvas that his apprentice relocates with every move.
Pelt has given nearly a century to his craft and says it took him eighty years to reach his level.
Pelt is strong enough to curl a two-hundred pound dumbbell effortlessly and out-lift Relc.
Pelt is as strong as Maughin despite his size.
Pelt finishes a breastplate in a morning and leaves the engraving and inlays to apprentices, calling them adornment.
Pelt tells Lasica he does not care who is voted into the seats, so long as the walls do not come crashing down.
Pelt inspects each steel bar before heating it, and refuses to use Pallass' steel, forging his own with his apprentice.
Pelt forges a knife in under an hour with an iron-and-steel sandwich, an edge of steel between softer iron, quenched with clay.
Pelt finds a hairline crack near the edge on grinding the knife, calls it a flaw in his metal, and flees.
Pelt makes a basket-hilt blade from a mithril alloy he forged while drunk, using three-layer forge-welding.
Pelt realises the alloy holds truegold and a ghost slayer, and says it will be a fancy magic mithril blade.
Pelt wonders whether the alloy holds Dwarfsteel or wolfram, and Emessa notes Dwarfsteel is an alloy that Pelt refuses to talk about.
Pelt calls the finished blade done and tells Emessa to triple the price.
Pelt tells Erin he felt her magical fire in his forge all day, and that it would ruin truegold forging.
Pelt grabs Erin's arm and crushes it, saying the kitchen knife he made in the competition is flawed and he has to erase it.
Maughin, Emessa and other smiths pull Pelt off, and Erin drinks a healing potion.
Pelt calls the flaw in the knife his sin and says it must be broken.
Pelt forges a bardiche head from Grasgil, a metal that melts at room temperature, using Everfrozen Ice powder and Erin's cold blue flame.
Pelt says Grasgil gives one chance and falls apart if reheated, and the cold from the flames makes his forge freeze.
Pelt says Maughin's people invented the way to smith Grasgil, and that levels do not define a smith.
Pelt says he once led a team of Dwarven smiths, and left his home in disgrace over impure steel, never to go back.
Pelt thanks Erin for her art, and asks her to take the flame away.
Pelt knows Dawil of the Silver Swords, but tells Drassi he does not care about another Dwarf.
Pelt gives Mrsha his complimentary peanuts to make her go away.
Pelt has hired more apprentices, including the Drake Emessa, so that they do the hammering while he finishes.
Pelt runs a forge with a glowing circle of powdered gemstone for Dwarfsteel and higher metals.
Pelt sold the Grasgil axe, which was then enchanted into a low Gold-rank weapon.
Pelt says he was banished from home, not forbidden, and is working on a euphonium for Wistram.
Pelt examines Erin's white mithril coin and says it is monetary and very old.
Pelt guesses the coin is so old that Humans lived on Izril in few numbers when it was made.
Pelt says mithril should not wear like that, and seems to recognise the coin before keeping it to restore.
Erin finds Pelt choking on the floor behind the anvil, having restored the coin.
The coin's restored inscription reads that Tamaroth leads, and ends 'Protect Us in Our Weakness', with a word scratched out.
Pelt starts breathing once Erin removes the coin, and says it was just an accident at the forge.
Pelt says he remembers nothing of the coin, and chokes again when he thinks of it.
Pelt announces he is leaving Pallass, and Senator Errif offers triple pay and five years.
Pelt says he left because of the Golden Triangle protests, and not because of Erin.
Pelt tells Maughin he was only the second greatest smith of those who left Deríthal-Vel, and to surpass him.
Pelt takes three apprentices, including Emessa, with him.
Pelt tricks everyone by changing the door's dial so that it opens on Esthelm.
Pelt forges a one-edged sword in about an hour in Esthelm, with a Dragonblood Crystal and Truegold edge.
Pelt gives the blade to Erin for Numbtongue, saying he does not forget his debts.
Pelt arrives six minutes late and drinks wine, giving Erin until the wine runs out to pitch.
Pelt says the Grasgil ring he sent Hedault had a slight impurity, and he would have trashed it.
Periss is a Drake [Commander] who captures Ryoka Griffin and serves as second-in-command to Ilvriss.
Ryoka thinks Periss seems to worship the ground Ilvriss stands on.

section: Book 2: The march on the Necromancer's castle
text: Periss leads elite Drake and Gnoll soldiers who take Ryoka toward the home of the Necromancer Az'kerash.

section: Book 2: The march on the Necromancer's castle
text: Periss goes nearly white and orders a retreat when she learns the castle belongs to the Necromancer Az'kerash.

section: Book 2: The march on the Necromancer's castle
text: Periss seizes Ryoka and demands how to leave the maze, and Ryoka says she knows only a stone that points toward the Necromancer.

section: Book 2: The march on the Necromancer's castle
text: Periss tells her soldiers that it has been an honor, and invites them to say their last words.

section: Book 2: The march on the Necromancer's castle
text: Periss tells Ryoka that she has always loved her Lord and wishes she had had the courage to tell him.

section: Book 2: The march on the Necromancer's castle
text: Periss tells Ryoka that Drakes do not run and orders her to go while the soldiers charge.

section: Book 2: The march on the Necromancer's castle
text: Periss and her soldiers, sixteen against a horde, die fighting the undead, and Ryoka hears Periss scream as she runs into the castle.
In a dream after Erin spikes his drink, Ilvriss sees Periss, his second-in-command and secret lover, standing over a map of Izril.
Periss in the dream has light blue scales near the spines on her head, which she brushes with a claw when she studies the map.
Periss in the dream says that the Goblin Lord has been destroying villages while avoiding every city, even those he could take.
Periss in the dream thinks the Goblin Lord is conserving his forces to move fast, and wonders whether he fears a Drake army from the rear.
Periss in the dream says that the key is what General Shivertail knows and why he disappeared.
Periss in the dream slaps Ilvriss twice and tells him she has been dead less than a month and he is no longer the leader she fell in love with.
Periss never liked Ilvriss to say her name, and was strict about rank and about flirting before a battle ended.
Periss in the dream tells Ilvriss that he must stand up because his people and she need him.
Periss in the dream calls sending her after a lone Human girl a sound decision, though sending all the elites with her was a mistake.
Periss in the dream says she will always be there in the map of Izril, and that Ilvriss should focus on all of Izril and on the inn.
Perorn Sadiluc, called Fleethoof, is a [Galewinds Strategist].
Her right hind leg was hamstrung, and healing potions did not fully restore it; she kept some mobility, but the pain and her aging body make her old feats of speed a distant memory.
Perorn Fleethoof is a famed [Strategist] in her own right, and she beats Niers in a game, which he takes well.
Perorn is a Centauress [Strategist] known as Fleethoof, and one of the foremost [Strategists] and commanders in the Forgotten Wing Company, one of the Four Great Companies of Baleros.
Perorn is a famous [Strategist], almost as famous as Niers Astoragon, who teaches joint classes and speaks in a crisp, no-nonsense tone.
Niers calls her one of his first winners and says she sat in a chair in the class years earlier.
Perorn says Tulm was the one who took away her leg, and asks Niers why he brought her.
Tulm hamstrung her back right leg in a past battle, and when Niers introduces her to him she says a single word, "Mithril", laden with over a decade of feeling.
Perorn authorizes bringing Geneva to the academy, with a formal invitation and the cost of travel expenses.
She gallops out of Daquin at great speed, filled with hope, even though her leg hurts.
Perric is the [King] of Medain, a powerful ruler of a powerful nation whose army includes former adventurers.
Medain is called the Kingdom of Adventurers, and its army relies on adventurers, many of them Gold-rank.
Perric styles himself a [High King], and says four nations fall under his aegis.
Perric was a [Prince] and a Gold-rank adventurer in his youth, who levelled in another class abroad.
Ulyse of Parasol Stroll says that Perric's title High King is given because he rules a defacto smaller kingdom, one of his coastal holdings.
