Perric collects at least one member of each species in his harem, except Selphids, most half-breeds and every Beastkin tribe.
Perric believes that a wife should be loyal if he ever finds one worthy of ruling beside him.
Perric considers that his artifacts and levels as a [King] put him at the rank of Named Adventurer.
Perric wears a record twelve artifacts, each balanced so that the magical leakage stays at the threshold.
The Adventurer's Guilds outside Medain refuse to grant Perric the Named Adventurer title, which eternally infuriates him.
Perric wields the enchanted sword Wavebreaker of Medain, a heirloom of his house.
Perric wears a Ring of Ironskin, the Greater Arrowguard Ring and an Amulet of Solidity that resists both aura and spell.
Perric's boots are [Haste]-capable for two minutes.
Perric demands that Wistram broadcast his parade, and is angry that the Academy has not answered his summons.
Perric silences a Wistram [Mage] with one look when she says she is not privy to the Archmages' thoughts.
Wistram says its single channel can support only one event at a time, and that it will not show any one nation until a fair order is set out.
Perric sits down slowly, his wrath paused, when the half-Elf [Mage] gives her answer.
Perric condemns the atrocities of Reim and Belchan in equal measure in a measured tone, but his armies march on Belchan.
Perric covertly hints to Raelt that some of Medain's adventurers might enlist in Jecrass's armies as outsiders.
Flos tells Teres that, before this battle, he would have put Perric far above Raelt in levels and strength, but now Raelt may be the better fighter.
Flos plans to insult Perric into declaring war and to kill the High King in one big battle, since Medain's army is not half as mobile as Jecrass's.
Perric thinks Flos is not a better [King] than he is, since Perric is younger and has greater vision.
Perric believes he is the one true [King] among all the half-baked men, and that he will eclipse Flos given more vassals like the Seven.
Perric is incensed by the King of Destruction's decree about his refugees, and by Raelt of Jecrass giving him orders.
Perric sends a [Message] asking for the most mobile Gold-rank team in Jecrass's capital, and orders the Wistram [Mages] to remain in the capital.
Perric sends a [Message] to Queen Yisame and the Speaker of Trees.
Perric faces Raelt with his Gold-ranks cheering their leader, and Raelt challenges him to fight.
The King of Duels is Medain's prisoner, leaving only his daughter to rule Jecrass.
Perric reflects, after a few bracing drinks, that the day went mostly according to his plan.
Persua is a City Runner in Celum with a sallow, shrewish face, brown hair and a strong perfume, who tosses her head often and annoys Ryoka on sight.
Ryoka considers Persua slow, lazy and an idiot who takes few long-distance contracts and only delivers light items like flowers or letters.
Persua has Street Runner friends, mainly new or low-ranking ones, who watch Ryoka for her.
Persua claims a Magnolia request that was to go to Ryoka, saying Ryoka has already done one this week and should switch, and Ryoka takes it instead by saying it is urgent.
Persua, sweaty and tired from running back to the city, insists she can make the run in time, and then stomps her foot and tells Ryoka she will regret it.

About twenty Street Runners surround Ryoka on a run, trip her and drive her onto a small street where a heavy mule-drawn cart and a patch of solid air hit her; Ryoka sees a familiar sallow face grinning.
Persua stands facing Ryoka and Garia with at least eight Street Runners behind her.
Persua tells Ryoka she is terribly sorry she got in the way of a runaway cart and says the other Runners tried to warn her.
Persua says Ryoka does not listen to her fellow Runners.
Persua tells Ryoka she will die in the High Passes alone because she is a fool, saying experienced Runners avoid such requests and work together.
Persua backs the adventurer Arnel against Ryoka, telling her she no longer has a Minotaur and a half-elf to protect her.
Ryoka says she still owes Persua a shattered leg bone and thinks Persua still has it out for her.
Persua hates Ryoka because the popular Runner Fals seems to like her, while Garia likes Fals.
Ryoka is passed on a snowy road by a pale, pinched-faced Runner at a speed she cannot match, and recognises her as Persua.
Persua gains the movement Skill [Double Step] before Level 20, is delivering faster than any Runner, and is leaving Celum for Invrisil or another northern city as a likely Courier.
Ryoka breaks Persua's nose and parts of her face in a fight in the Runner's Guild, and Persua swears she will have Ryoka raped and killed.
Persua is kept overnight by a [Healer] even though potions mended most of her wounds.
Fals expects Persua to run cross-continent deliveries if she becomes a Courier, or to move north if she does not.
Persua has left the Celum Runner's Guild, which Ryoka feels let her act as she did, and her gang revolved around her.
Garia says Persua lost almost all of her clique after she got in trouble, and that Claudeil and Toriska vanished.
Garia says she might be on track to becoming a Courier now if she had trained earlier, rather than Persua.
A young City Runner in Invrisil accuses Ryoka of causing an avalanche in a guild, stealing contracts and being violent, and Ryoka recognises the accusations as Persua's.
Delanay says Persua has won over half the Runners in Invrisil with sob stories of Celum mistreating her.
Ryoka had heard Persua was being considered for Courier status after going north from Fals.
Peslas is the biggest Drake Erin has ever met, apart from possibly Relc, and he is huge rather than muscular.
Peslas is the innkeeper of the Tailless Thief, the most famous and expensive inn in Liscor, on the north side of the city.
Peslas is generous, and sometimes insists a meal is on the house.
Peslas says that he is Level 30, as are some of the innkeepers around his age, and most are Level 20 or higher.
Peslas has the Skill [Intuition], and says it has never been wrong.
Peslas says he has heard that an innkeeper in First Landing is nearing Level 40, and that she is the highest-level innkeeper on the continent.
Selys says Peslas is above Level 30 as an [Innkeeper], and that he levels only about once every couple of years because he is old and takes it easy.
Peslas last levelled up six years before this conversation and threw a huge party, to which Selys and her grandmother were invited.
According to Selys, Peslas was a [Warrior] who reached Level 16 serving in the army, and has a few levels each in [Cook], [Bartender], [Singer] and [Dancer].
Later, Pisces refers to Peslas as the Level 30 Drake [Innkeeper] in Liscor, saying he would keep a large sum on hand.
Peslas welcomes Selys because she is the grandchild of Isshia.
Selys says Peslas is only an acquaintance of her grandmother, whom she talks to every other month, and that he married a girl nearly as young as she is.
Peslas says that a Human once ran Erin's inn, and that he had told the man its location was bad.
Peslas says that before the Necromancer, people travelled north across the Blood Fields, and a small village grew around the Human's inn but was destroyed.
Peslas says that the undead forced everyone to flee the area, after which the Human never got the inn running again.
Peslas tells Erin she needs something special, a hook, and not just her best.
Peslas sells hamburgers in his inn after Erin's success with them.
Pielt is a male Drake [Captain] in 4th Company under Wing Commander Embria.
Pielt commands a squad that is mainly made up of Drakes, including Sergeant Fika.
Wikir says Pielt's squad has to clear Shield Spider nests all by hand and torch.
Pielt boasts that he is as smooth on a tavern floor as he is on the battlefield, and Vell mocks his attempts at flirting.
Pielt tells Wikir to go to hell after Wikir jokes that Pielt's group, lacking a strong [Mage], will be picking baby spiders out of its ears.
Pielt's tail lashes under his table when Embria says Lism is not their man and that she cannot approach Krshia instead.
Pielt's scales turn beet red when Kesa whispers a joke at his expense, and Embria tells him to stop bringing up his failed romances.
Pielt tells Embria her test pick-up line is terrible, and the other officers cannot meet her eyes except Wikir.
Wikir says he went into the pit rather than let Pielt call him a coward.
Pielt tells a crowd of listeners that all of 4th Company heard the stories about Sergeant Relc.
Pielt says Relc was 4th Company's secret weapon who would charge in, cut his way to an enemy officer, and escape again, sometimes against a [Commander]-class opponent.
Pielt says Captain Wikir served with Relc, and that Embria learned [Spearmaster] skills from him.
Pisces is a young Human [Necromancer] and [Mage] who studied at Wistram Academy before being expelled over what he wanted to do with necromancy.
His true name is Pisces Jealnet, and he calls himself a Silver-rank adventurer on the team of the Horns of Hammerad.
Pisces is a pale young man with unkempt brown hair who smells bad, and Erin Solstice first meets him in grimy grey robes that look as if they have never been washed.
When Erin first looks at him closely, his robes hang thin on his frame and he is in rough shape, though he eats with the energy of two men.
The huge skeletal creature wreathed in slime and darkness that frightened Erin was an illusion: struck by her flung pot it vanished, leaving Pisces unconscious on the floor with a bruise forming.

He introduces himself as Pisces, practitioner of magic and student of Wistram Academy, specialised in the Elementalist and Illusionary schools with additional competencies in multiple spell schools; when Erin asks for a hobby, he admits it is Necromancy.

Pisces is wary of the Wistram title system: he insists "mage" is the proper general term and defines wizards as arcane researchers who study the mainstream branches, sorcerers as self-educated casters with little formal education, warlocks as drawing power from sources such as summoning, and witches as practising alchemy along with specialised schools.
Ceria Springwalker says she studied with Pisces at Wistram Academy as an acquaintance rather than a friend, and describes him as greedy, arrogant and rude but not very dangerous, and competent.
Ceria says Pisces is hiding, and that he agreed to meet the party at an inn a few miles southeast of Liscor.
Ceria says Pisces is only around twenty in her years, and that if all his levels in multiple mage classes are added up he has more than she does although she is three times his age.

Ceria says Pisces was kicked out of Wistram Academy, and that Wistram accepts necromancers, so it was because of what he wanted to do with necromancy that he was expelled; she will not give details but says his research violated what few magical laws exist.
Ceria says several cities want Pisces for extortion and troublemaking rather than murder.
In Wistram, Pisces was always at the head of his class whenever he showed up, according to Ceria, and he dropped out about when she ran out of funds.
Gerial recalls that Pisces was expelled for his experiments, and Ceria confirms he is not technically a graduate.
Pisces calls himself among the better chess players of his fellow students at Wistram, and he loses an hour-long game to Erin and has the wager added to his tab.

Pisces spends nearly a month terrorising travellers and lone households and stealing food and money from them as a monster, and by robbing graves and reburying the dead afterwards; Relc tells him there is a bounty on his head.
Relc threatened to stab Pisces if he kept stealing from the locals, so he stopped taking supplies from them.

Pisces tells Erin he is banned from entering Liscor because of his magical inclinations, and Erin adds that he also stole food and money from people by pretending to be a monster; he says he occasionally has to evade the Watch's patrols even this far from the city.
Selys Shivertail tells Pisces that he had a bounty on his head until a week earlier.
Pisces eats soup and other food at Erin's inn without paying, citing a lovely tradition known as a tab, and later he admits he has no coins on him.
Pisces' robes are stained but give off no smell, because he says magic has eliminated the chore of washing them.
Pisces says he wrote a paper on the phenomenon of classes while at Wistram Academy.
Pisces' robes smell of the outdoors because he never washes, which he regards as an advantage against Gnolls who rely on their noses.
Ryoka Griffin first learns that Pisces is the [Necromancer] who fixed her leg and the apparent teacher of one of the Goblins.

Pisces has a criminal record as a thief who went to villages and scared people into giving him food and coin, but he claims he paid three times what he took, and in the eyes of Liscor's law his debt is settled; Selys notes Relc made him repay.
Liscor, an apolitical city of commerce, lets people who committed lesser crimes pay a fine and clear their record, which is why a [Necromancer] like Pisces can walk through its gates.
Pisces says he practises his craft without harm and does not disturb Liscor's graves.

After the Liscor attack Pisces lives in a small den that was once a bear's cave, which he has reinforced at the entrance and warded with a few spells; he hates it as smelly, cramped and exposed, and wants money to improve it.
He decides to become an adventurer because he is short of coin and wants a better place to study magic.

Pisces says that he attended a class at Wistram that looked into adventuring trends, and cites that smaller groups of higher-levelled warriors beat large groups and that most Gold-rank teams have six adventurers or fewer.
Pisces is informed that raising the dead from the bones of Drakes or Gnolls is not allowed while he resides in Liscor or the surrounding area.
Ceria says Pisces survived alone for a long time as an arrogant loner who scared people out of coin, and that he reached Izril and the spot where he lives by himself, past bandits and monsters.
Ceria reports that Pisces killed at least a hundred undead in the battle for Liscor and that Olesm says he downed a Crypt Lord by himself.
Ceria says Pisces does not obey people he does not like and will not follow orders he thinks are stupid.

Ceria says that Pisces is a powerful mage for his level, an excellent duelist back in Wistram whose specialty is one-on-one battles, who has far more spells than she does, and who is a better Silver-rank adventurer than the Horns.

Ceria also says Pisces learned [Invisibility] at Level 18 and levelled twice from learning it, and that it nearly killed him because he studied every night for at least two hours for a month; she calls him a genius, though an arrogant and insufferable one.
Pisces remembers an earlier path in which he knew [Flame Rapier] and [Flashstep] alongside his death magic.
Ceria and Pisces both admit they were expelled from Wistram and never fully graduated, but Pisces says they were allowed to claim the name and are still recognised Wistram mages.
Ceria remembers that Pisces stood unrepentant before the Council of Wistram the day they exiled him, certain he was right.

Pisces says that Wistram had few books on necromancy and no teacher he could study under, that the spells he found were standardised incantations for humanoids only, and that the only other authorities tend to be crazed madmen or cults.
Ceria remembers the Pisces she knew as someone who always hated physical violence, however much he had changed otherwise, and knows he is deadly with a rapier as well as spells.
Pisces tells Griffon Hunt that he and Ceria are graduates of Wistram.

Selys relays that the Guild forbids Pisces from animating the corpses or bones of people: Drakes, Gnolls, Humans, Minotaurs, Centaurs, half-Elves, Dwarves, Drowned people, Stitch People, Dullahan and Gazers, while Lizardfolk bodies are allowed; he may still practise necromancy otherwise.

Pisces tells Olesm that Horns of Hammerad are resting after a mundane task of clearing a roach-infested cave a few miles from Liscor, where about ten thousand cockroaches, some larger variants, swarmed his companions and Ice magic was futile so they burned them.
Adventurers in Liscor's Guild turn their backs on Pisces, and Olesm knows [Necromancers] are unpopular in Liscor and most of the world, with Pisces' attitude making it worse.

Pisces says he kept necromancy hidden at Wistram, learned mostly by trial and error, and after leaving sought other [Necromancers] in his travels, joining the Krythien Sect a year before coming to Liscor and finding them amateurs who only know how to animate a body, not how it works.
Zevara tells Lyonette that the [Necromancer] Pisces was the previous record-holder for Liscor fines.

Pisces seals his room with [Muffle] and [Sealed Space] with six ash-drawn runes, keeps it organised with an undead rat skeleton on the dresser, and works from two identical spellbooks, one made to look the same to hide a new spellbook.
Ceria says Pisces has studied alone in his room for days since his scream, muttering about puzzles, possibly attempting another Tier 4 spell.
Wistram posts a two thousand coin bounty on Pisces, which Jeiss calls high for an adventurer but not for Gold-ranks.

A Wistram report lists Pisces' crimes as extortion, burglary, blackmail and the usual [Necromancer] crimes, and alleges he was responsible for the deaths of over sixty [Mages] in a case of rampant necromancy, for which he was expelled; Liscor's Watch did not consider him a threat after he passed their tests.
Ceria tells Montressa that Wistram will reduce Pisces' bounty from two thousand coins to two hundred and rescind the order to bring him in.
Typhenous tells Pisces that his lower bounty is still common knowledge.
In a flashback of Ceria's first days at Wistram, Pisces is a nervous young man with a shock of brown hair and a polite smile who is delighted to meet a half-Elf for the first time.
As a new Wistram student he says he is only a Level 14 [Mage], with a focus on basic elemental magic and some minor reinforcement magic, and wants to study every field.
In the same flashback he carries a rapier, claims levels in [Fencer], rings a silver duelist's bell that marks a level of skill recognised among duelists, and says he cannot swim.
As a student he knows no Tier 2 combat spell yet and practises [Electric Jolt], and says a local [Hedge Mage] in his village agreed to teach him.
At the Wistram flashback he is a Level 14 [Mage] with [Fencer] levels.

Pisces tells Ceria he overheard the older students' conversation about a spellbook they do not have, hidden in a secret section of the library and warded to kill anyone who tries to take it, and says he also overheard where the section is and how to get in.
Pisces will not say how he overheard the students, answering only that it was a spell.
A dead mouse climbs onto Pisces' dresser, and he calls it to him and tucks it into his robe pocket, a sign that he animates the dead.
Ceria and Pisces agree to take the risk of stealing the warded spellbook, with Ceria saying they only have about three weeks.
Pisces tells Ceria that Wistram's restrictions are probably meant to test how students react, and that rules can be broken if the students are not caught.

Pisces sends Cognita a note by a method he will not disclose and asks her to help him retrieve a warded book to advance his grasp of spellcraft; he reasons that because she broke Illphres' enchantments she can break the trap on the book and the Golems are bound to help students.
Pisces and Ceria obtain the spellbook, and Ceria realises he meant to share it with her from the start; she agrees they will study it together.

Pisces learns the Tier 3 spell [Flash Step] in under three weeks, which Ceria thinks no other new student could do, and then moves with it in a dance-like pattern with his rapier without ever hitting a wall.

In the exam, Pisces carries the unconscious Ceria on one shoulder and kills a Troll with his rapier, using [Flash Step] superbly; the watching mages note he needs no [Warrior] class because of his silver bell and consider accepting him as a [Swordmage].
Pisces' name appears on the exam pass list without a last name, and Ceria's name appears at the end.
Calvaron says Pisces finished his first-year exams by killing a Troll, was passed unanimously by all the mages, was paid by Wistram to stay, and is the best second-year student at dueling and debate.
Calvaron says that Pisces was one of only six students to have passed the Ice Demon's class the year before.
Pisces manages to turn himself transparent, which Montressa notes is far from true [Invisibility].

Pisces wins duels for money, beating the third-year Ramon, and says it is his eighth duel in a week and that he won six gold pieces and ten silver; he came to the academy poor but is rich in coin and secrets.

Pisces and Ceria develop a ranged messaging spell, the firefly of light, and Montressa masters it; Pisces says it is many times more complex than any [Message] spell, no one has deciphered it, and it works up to several miles away.
On the pirate ship, Pisces' zombies grab the tattooed pirate and Pisces runs him through, saying the duel is only a duel to him; when pirates shout "Necromancer", he says there is no hiding it now.
Ceria sees the undead Pisces has created on the deck, throws up, and backs away as he says he wanted to tell her.

Pisces stands alone before the Council of Wistram accused of being a [Necromancer], and argues that necromancy is a force for good or evil and that Az'kerash, the most powerful [Necromancer] of the millennium, once studied at Wistram before being slain on Izril.
After the trial, Beatrice leaves rather than speak to him and Calvaron, Montressa and Ceria look at him as if he were changed.
Pisces offers his rapier to Calvaron to pay for the academy's fees, and Calvaron takes it, with the silver bell chiming once as it is offered.

The whole academy knows there is a necromancer studying there and turns its back on him, with Selphid students possibly sympathetic but silent; Beatrice nearly attacks him, Calvaron cannot look him in the eye, and only Montressa stays by his side.
About a month later, Pisces has lost his rapier and silver bell, which now belong to Timor du Havrington, and his smile and neat appearance, and his robes are dirty.

Pisces argues in a verbal duel that Archmage Nekhret, a true [Archmage] over a thousand years ago whose bones lie in the catacombs below the academy, should not be condemned for being tainted by necromancy, and cites the executed Burning Killer Calico of Chandrar to argue that a group should not be condemned for a few.
Ceria tells Pisces she does not think they are friends anymore; he asks if they are enemies, and she says it would be stupid.
Pisces lives in a messy room with a pile of mouse bones and has the newly mastered [Flame Rapier] to show Ceria.
Pisces learns the spell [Flame Rapier].
Pisces builds a deformed, unanimated clay Golem under the tutoring of Cognita, who he says is one of the only beings in the academy who will give him the time of day.
Ceria agrees to hear everything and Pisces relaxes and speaks to her as he used to.

Pisces tells Ceria he asked every mage he knew to take him as an apprentice, even promising to swear off necromancy, and none were willing, so with no coin and no one to speak for him he must leave Wistram.

Pisces proposes creating an undead that can level, weaving the spells in at a deeper level closer to how a Golem is created, and says Cognita taught him the formula for embodying Golems with sentience; Ceria calls the idea stupid and impossible.
Pisces argues that Golems need high-grade materials such as mana stones and flawless rock, and that the same should apply to undead made from superior body parts.

Invisible, Pisces watches five lesser Golems carry the dead mages Illphres, Bastam, Jurix, Ophelia and Qum to a room with an empty Selphid body; he raises all six bodies as undead, then flees through a locked gate using [Flash Step] to evade a Golem.
In the Wistram catacombs, Pisces and his four remaining undead slide off the lid of Archmage Nekhret's tomb, and he takes the bones using a bag of holding stolen from the Golems.
The Council exiles Pisces and tells him he may never return to Wistram under penalty of death and that no true mage of Wistram shall treat with him; Ceria is told to leave on the next ship.
Cognita uses the authority of Archmage Zelkyr to graduate Ceria and Pisces, saying both showed the qualities of a true mage of Wistram.
Pisces can turn invisible, and mumbling and touching his belt makes him vanish with a booming echo.
Pisces escapes the guards by an illusion double: Relc's spear passes through him and Relc concludes he cast an illusion spell and walked off while they chatted.

Spells Pisces shows in his first fight with Relc and Klbkch include gathering shadows around his hands like a cloak, pushing the air to throw Relc off him, setting a leather cord on fire, a small explosion of lightning that blasts Klbkch into a wall, and a flickering barrier of wind in front of Relc.
In the acid fly crisis Pisces casts [Gust] to blow the swarm into a funnel, then [Frozen Wind], which freezes the flies so they fall and burst, leaving smoking dirt and frozen grass.
Pisces calls [Frozen Wind] a beginner's spell downplayed by his instructors and not suitable for most combat, but says all magic is worth using, and that he specialises in Wind Elementalist magic.

Pisces says the acid flies have few predators and are nearly limitless in number; the specimens in jars are only males, whose purpose is to gather food and absorb nutrition for the substantially larger females.
Pisces knows [Invisibility], which he calls a 3rd Tier spell acquired after much practice and study, and one of his fortes.
Later, from his own point of view, [Invisibility] is Tier-4 magic that took a year of study to master, and he casts it before entering the inn.

Pisces tells Erin that most mages use [Farsight] and [Scrying] to watch anyone they like, that upper-class dwellings and bath houses are warded against them, and that no other human mages are in the area.
Pisces starts a lesson for Erin on the "Mage's Test" in exchange for forgiving his tab and buying alcohol, tracing glowing blue-white light in the air with his finger.
Ceria says Pisces can control bones, while Pisces insists necromancy is a misnomer and that reanimation is only one component of raising the dead.
Pisces repairs Ryoka Griffin's shattered leg bones in seconds with no written spell, by sensing where the bones are and reassembling them, which Ceria says no normal mage could do.
Ceria says Pisces is a genius with an intimate knowledge of human bodies, and that he does not know healing spells but can reinforce and repair bone.
Pisces haggles his fee for the repair from sixty to forty gold coins, noting a [Cleric] would charge two hundred for a [Restoration] spell.
Pisces creates a skeleton attuned to Erin that obeys all her commands, guards her and her possessions, and has very limited thought for now; he gives it to her to pay off his tab.
Pisces says he has made several improvements over traditional undead animation spells.
Pisces says he could create a stronger undead than that skeleton, but not a higher-level one.
Pisces snaps zombies' and ghouls' spines at range by pointing at them, with purple energy in his hands, which he says takes ample mana reserve.
During the first undead attack he has killed over half of the fallen dead on the street and Relc the other half.
Pisces re-knits the shattered bodies of six zombies, three skeletons and four ghouls, and orders them to go to the inn, protect Erin and kill anyone who would harm her.
As a [Necromancer], Pisces can sense how many dead are in the city and outside it, a fact he carefully neglected to mention to the Watch.
Pisces keeps a hiding place in a dirt cave on the plains where he stockpiles bodies saved from the purging flames, including the dead Crypt Lord.
Pisces breaks Erin's locked door with lightning and says "They're alive" after receiving a glowing message spell in the form of a firefly of colours and shapes.
The message says Ceria is alive and needs help somewhere deep in the Ruins, and it read only: Ruins, second floor, inside, which Pisces thinks was all Ceria had mana for.
Pisces, Ryoka and Rags each cast [Light] together in the Ruins.
Pisces can sense undead as they draw near to him.
Pisces snaps ghouls' spines with the word "Decease" and a crooked finger, felling several Ghouls in a row.
Pisces says he can deal with most forms of undead quite easily, but that Crypt Lords pose a considerable threat to him.
Pisces explains that a Lich is simply the undead version of a spellcaster, dangerous but hardly immortal, and that he never saw one in the attack on Liscor.
Pisces says necromancers use dead bodies because bones are ideal vessels for storing magical energy and spell bindings, whereas chitin decays too rapidly to sustain a long-form spell.

Pisces sees the iPhone's chat spell and speculates that a high-level mage or several of them used [Far Speaking] with a location spell, which would require a [Message] spell per recipient and an insane amount of mana.
Ceria says Pisces cannot take control of a living body part or one attached to a living body.
Pisces animates a spider as undead, calling himself perhaps the first [Necromancer] in years to master animating a species without bone; he says he learned a new Skill and levelled.
Pisces cannot sense Toren's aura or location, though he says he would know if Toren had been uncreated, and suspects something is interfering with the aura.
Pisces says he needs food to cast magic.
Pisces and Ceria cast [Detect Magic] at the same moment, which lights the inn with magical auras and shows an enchantment on Ryoka; Pisces guesses it is Tier 6 or 7 magic.
Pisces casts [Repair] on Ryoka's iPhone, restoring its battery to 100 percent, and [Amplify Sound], which Ceria says she could learn in less than a day.
Pisces says he copied the [Message] spell from Ryoka's phone conversation, recreating it with difficulty, and brags about it as the Horns leave the Ruins.
Pisces flicks an orb of fire that curves around Brunkr's shield and strikes the Gnoll's chest.
Pisces believes Toren absorbed some of the magic of the gemstone stored in his head.
Pisces uses [Frozen Wind], then the Tier 3 spell [Shock Volt], then [Animate Dead] against Hobs and a group of dead Goblins.
Pisces explains that an aura skill lets a leader class control an area, that powerful monsters resist most of it, and that Erin's [Inn's Aura] seems good at deflecting low-level enemies.
Pisces says he layered the reanimation spell on each individual bone of Toren and tied it together so that it cannot be replicated.
Pisces casts [Raise Skeleton], which he finds the most cost-effective, and summoning the dead is a crime up north unless there is an agreement with the local cities.

Under the [Insanity] runes Pisces speaks and fights as a cruel father, threatening Ceria with a shard of bone and calling her "boy", and later uses [Flash Step] to dodge a fiery construct with a very large distance kept.

Pisces builds a bone staircase from the bones of the pit's dead and has skeletons dig upward, saying he can conjure as many skeletons as he needs from that supply; he admits using quite a bit of mana.
Pisces raises skeletons to hold down the delirious Yvlon Byres, who calls him a Necromancer and demands his death.
Pisces says he is a better [Necromancer] than he is a [Mage] by far, and Ceria says he reanimated over thirty skeletons in ten minutes.
Pisces casts [Frozen Wind] to push back a crowd, and then admits by his manner that he was less unsteady than he pretended.
Pisces says Toren's creation was the culmination of years of work, with groundwork and materials in his animation that were exceedingly rare, practically unique.

Pisces says that creating another Toren is theoretically possible, but the result would either be mindless or develop sentience again, because the theorems Cognita passed on to him were incomplete and sentience is a byproduct of the spell matrices animating Golems.
Pisces fills the pit with yellow smoke and descends by bone staircase to recover the teleportation door's anchor stone.

The door in the pit carries a potent teleportation spell and cannot be destroyed; Pisces says a small stone anchors the other half of the spell, and the one in the pit is a palm-sized stone embedded in the floor that he blasts with fire so Ksmvr can crack it.
Pisces isolates the location aspect of the door's spell, learns to trigger it independently of the detection trap, and tells Erin the enchantment replenishes itself by absorbing natural mana.

Pisces warns that connecting a door to multiple points risks entanglement and says he would hesitate to create more than four focal points; he suggests linking to two more cities and giving the Horns one anchoring point.

Pisces confirms he used four of Archmage Nekhret's bones in Toren, carving the spell into them to restore the form he gave Toren however badly he is broken, but the bones consume too much mana for him to survive without a source.
Pisces practises [Flash Step] by stepping to keep pace with Erin's wagon, learning to appear precisely at its back, and adds rapier lunges to the exercise.
Ceria says [Flash Step] is one of Pisces' specialties, a good movement spell but hard to use, where one bad step can break a foot.
Pisces eavesdrops on Typhenous with [Invisibility] and uses the light-fly code to tell Ceria "Tell you later. Much is afoot."
Pisces can read lips as a learned art rather than a Skill, which proved useful at Wistram once his eavesdropping with undead creations was discovered.
The Shield Spider was the first non-mammalian creature Pisces animated, an extraordinary feat in necromancy that no one appreciated.

Pisces measures the door's remaining mana with [Lightning Jolt] cast from ambient mana, marking the reach of the bolt twelve feet away with a cup and estimating it falls two to three inches per cast after Ryoka teleports.

Pisces raises two bears with a rhyming chant to fight a Creler, and then fires a bolt from a ring that fragments into magical needles inside the Creler's underbelly after Yvlon breaks its armor with a mordhau strike.

Pisces explains that a [Mage] who transcends into a unique class such as [Necromancer] or [Cryomancer] becomes focused in that class, and must begin again with the [Mage] class from Level 1 to pursue other types of magic.

Pisces says he could not practically fool a truth spell, nor could Ceria or Typhenous or probably a Named Adventurer, but the Archmages of Wistram could in theory, and simpler versions can be deceived.

Pisces fights Venitra: his flaming rapier and spells do not hurt her, but he blinks about with [Flash Step], resists her mist of madness because he has already experienced his own insane delusions once, and breaks her arm with [Bone Fracture].

Pisces builds a Bone Horror he calls the Scythe Crawler: a tall, thin ivory bone creature with a headless torso, a single burning green eye, a spider-like lower half on four legs, a cylindrical waist, and long arms ending in bone scythes with barbs.
Pisces says the Scythe Crawler is quick and attacks from many angles because its waist rotates freely.

Pisces tells Olesm that the earlier bears were the Bone Horror in its earlier form, reworked by carving and rearranging their bones, and that the ability to create such a being correlates directly to his current level.
Pisces prefers Bone Horrors to Draugr, because a Draugr needs a body and relies on the strength of the deceased, while a Bone Horror can be reanimated at will and kept in a bag of holding.
Pisces works for a long time with Moore and Typhenous to make Erin's door switchable by tapping a mana stone against it.

Pisces animates a scaled-down Bone Horror variant that looks like a dog, cat and rat; he says it follows his instructions precisely, and it hunts down rat nests, climbs into the dens and excavates blockages; Selys kicks it into the water to show she is not afraid.

Pisces knows the armor's history: last in the possession of General Ironscales of Oteslia, lost in a clash north of Liscor between her command and the Reinhart and El families, over a trade dispute from Chandrar.
Pisces keeps [Invisibility] up to pass through the door into Pallass with Selys, then drops it; physical contact breaks it, and Selys's elbow nearly broke it at the Archive.

Pisces sits with a spellbook, then sends an undead Shield Spider to follow Lyonette and Purple Smile to the Hive entrance while he senses it and controls it directly, and he also senses his rat-hunter Bone Horrors in Liscor's sewers.
Pisces prefers unarmed spellcasting because fingers aim faster than a wand and are more flexible, and a young Gnoll holds his wand.

Pisces says a [Necromancer] has extreme difficulty working with living bodies: he can crack an unled skeleton at fifty paces but needs skin-to-skin contact to manipulate a living person's bone, and only if they do not resist; he says he cannot repair Yvlon's arms at his level.

Pisces says his first prototype Bone Horror with whip arms was inefficient, as Miss Shivertail told him, and that he has used the bones of three bears for the Bone Horrors for Liscor's sewers, with about one bear's worth intact.
Pisces offers to research a [Hardening] spell or other reinforcement magic for the metal in Yvlon's arms.

Pisces taught himself some Goblin by listening to Rags and her retinue at the inn, keeping a small dictionary; he tells Selys the Cave Goblin keeps saying "not Goblin" to the Redfang Hobs, a potent insult.
Pisces says he stayed up designing new combat Bone Horror forms, including an almost indestructible armor form, a quick spider form, and deadly rat-hunting horrors.
Pisces says he does not know [Dispel Magic].
Pisces reasons that Erin's inn has charged ambient mana because the door is not teleporting people to Celum or Pallass every night, so it is drawing less mana.

Pisces keeps a bear Bone Horror at the inn to guard it, and says his undead cannot function long without consuming a great deal of mana and are limited in number, and that breaking the bones of undead stops them only briefly.
Pisces says he lost all but the components for one Bone Horror after the last one was incinerated and needs new bones.
In the Guild fight Pisces uses [Flash Step], [Shock Volt], [Lightning Jolt], [Barrier of Air] and [Flying Bone Club].

Pisces' rat-shaped Bone Horrors have killed a number of nests in Liscor's sewers, though they ran into trouble with Acid Fly nests; he has solidified the designs, finds the Warbear form the most effective, and experiments with a skeleton soldier build.
Pisces plans a Bone Behemoth, two or three times as large as his Warbear Bone Horror, and decides to learn [Acid Orb] from the scrolls Grimalkin gave him because his team lacks a hammer.
Pisces wears a true Arrowguard ring that can deflect multiple arrows and recharges in a day, and says it has saved his life.
Pisces says that with a source of mana he could animate at least a hundred undead but realistically about two dozen working in small groups he directs personally.
Pisces' [Invisibility] does not work on Maviola El.
Pisces states his levels as fifteen in [Elementalist], eight in [Alchemist], six in [Enchanter] and ten in the general [Mage] class, while calling Necromancy a passion.
Ceria says that as a student Pisces was about Level 22.
Pisces says anyone with even a single level in the necromancer class is killed on sight in that part of the world.
Ceria says Pisces has the most levels in [Necromancer], and knows a good many [Elementalist] spells.
Zevara doubts a [Necromancer] of his level could reanimate more than five bodies, let alone a horde.
Pisces calls himself an accredited [Mage] in front of the adventurers.
Ceria says Pisces knows one Tier 4 spell, [Invisibility], and learned it at Level 18.
Ceria describes Pisces as an excellent duelist who knows a Tier 4 spell and can conjure a small army of minions.
Pisces says he is a higher level than when he first built Toren.

Pisces regards a true [Mage] as specialising in as many classes as possible, naming [Pyromancer], [Seer], [Alchemist], [Sword Mage], [Warlock] and [Druid], while he is a [Necromancer] and also a [Mage] who specialised in one field and then studied every other.
Pisces says he is a Level 29 [Necromancer] and a Level 18 [Mage].

Pisces says he reached Level 30 just the other day and kept it secret; his Level 30 Skill is a greater mastery of bone shaping, though he notes the ability to create Draugr would have been another common Skill at that level.
Grimalkin judges Pisces to be a [Necromancer] of Level 30 plus, with Ceria a [Cryomancer] below Level 30.

Pisces says he gained two [Necromancer] levels for summoning both behemoths, his [Mage] class reached Level 20 for a second time, and he gained the Skill [Mana Well] (Ashen), which lets him charge his reserves with ambient death-grade mana.
Pisces and Ceria Springwalker know each other from Wistram; at the inn they greet each other by name.
Pisces eats at Erin's inn constantly and Erin treats him as a nuisance but feeds him, kicking him when he bothers customers.
Selys Shivertail is horrified when she learns Pisces created the skeleton, and tells him to leave Erin alone.
Pisces proposes alternate forms of payment for his tab after his funds are confiscated.
Pisces agrees to teach Rags every other day in return for free food, though he has never considered an apprentice and doubts Goblins have the potential.
Gazi greets Pisces as "Necromancer" on arriving at the inn, and he nearly chokes in surprise.
Pisces and Ceria Springwalker were Wistram students together and were once friends, and he says he felt the world would be poorer for her absence.
Pisces greets Ceria as "Springwalker" when she and a Drake arrive at the inn.
Pisces says he gave Toren to Erin because he owed her a small debt for meals and had observed her work with the Antinium, such as Pawn, and thought she would appreciate a fine worker.
Pisces, Ceria, Yvlon and Ksmvr divide the Ruins treasure as teammates, and Ceria and Pisces stare at each other over the deflection ring before he takes it.
Yvlon does not speak to Pisces all morning after Toren; Ceria persuades her to keep watching him as a teammate.
Ksmvr calls him comrade Pisces and asks after him.
The crowd cheers Pisces, Yvlon, Ksmvr and Ceria as heroes; Pisces finds the goodwill unfamiliar and more enchanting than any spell.
Pisces ties a knot in a cherry stem and uses mint leaves for fresh breath, and Ceria says he is not bad at kissing and had plenty of practice in Wistram.

Pisces and Olesm Swifttail quarrel: Pisces jabs that Olesm is not an adventurer after one rejection, and Olesm retorts that Pisces came crawling to Ceria after rejecting her once, and that Ceria had asked him.
After a snowball quarrel, Pisces helps Olesm up, and they apologise to each other and agree to bygones.

Pisces and Olesm bond as young, thoughtful, strategy-loving peers who resent seniority and the gated access to power, and Olesm is stunned that Pisces understands Drake politics, including the Germina-Reim incident and the Hellios conflict.

Pisces tells Olesm that he too once had a relationship with Ceria and then says he misspoke, saying it never truly came to be because she learned the truth about who he is before he could explain; he asks Olesm not to repeat it to her.
Selys Shivertail tells Pisces she is not afraid of the undead, just does not like them, and hears from other [Receptionists] that they are terrified of him.
Pisces tells Selys that they are both pariahs in Liscor with inverse fortunes, and that she was cursed with a conscience and affection, since she cared about her uncle's passing more than the armor.
Ceria tells Pisces he is rich now and can afford the drinks.
Ceria, Yvlon, Ksmvr and Pisces reconcile and pledge to stay together; Pisces offers to leave because Wistram will keep hunting him, and Yvlon and Ceria refuse.
Pisces tries to pay Erin for the scare with bronze coins, then silver, then a gold coin; Erin takes only the silver and bronze.
Pisces offers to be ransomed, claiming Wistram would pay thirty gold coins for his return after a fight with Relc and Klbkch.

During the Goblin attack aftermath, Pisces runs into the inn with sparks at his fingertips wanting to kill or curse Goblins; Erin gives him a dried sausage and says she will kill him if he kills a Goblin.
Pisces stands before the inn on its hill in dirty white robes when Ryoka's party arrives, and says the owner is elsewhere.
Pisces creates the skeleton to settle his tab; Erin is angry.
After the sighting at the Ruins, Pisces appears out of the air beside Selys and Zevara, says he did not raise the horde, and mocks Selys.
Zevara believes him because witnesses saw the dead emerge from the ruins.
Pisces tells Erin that she cannot use magic, as Erin tells Ceria.
Gazi knocks Pisces unconscious with one punch.
Pisces refers to the Winter Sprites and Cold Folk, and orders the Cold Folk to leave the inn.
Pisces gets beaten up by Gnolls, and Brunkr drops him on seeing the skeleton.
Ceria knocks him out of his chair and chokes him after he admits Toren could level, and Yvlon and Ksmvr restrain her.
Pisces cuts the thread of mana from Erin to Toren by laying his hands on Erin's head; he says no undead can live without mana.
Pisces proposes hiring a horse or wagon to visit Albez and retrieve the door left behind from the expedition, and says he is adept at [Invisibility].
Pisces lip-reads Ilvriss telling Zel Shivertail "Ask her", and sees a Drake hand Zel something small.

Pisces sends a reanimated Shield Spiderling with listening and vision spells to eavesdrop on Zel and Ryoka, and Mrsha smashes it; Ceria afterwards advises him to enchant it next time to be faster, more durable or smell bad.
Pisces offers Erin his sympathies and an apology in the kitchen, saying he knows he is not the person she would turn to.

After breaking her arm, Pisces says to Venitra "You are no Gnoll", asks what she is and who made her, and Venitra decides he must die; an unseen voice she takes to be her master tells her to leave him, and Pisces asks who is speaking to him.
Pisces and Olesm both receive the brass ring bearing an eye with a tiny diamond from the envelope, and the two scream and dance wildly in disbelief.
Pisces offered Selys to resolve the giant rats in Liscor's sewers with an undead construct; Selys refused, and Pisces blames her grandmother's distrust of necromancy.

Olesm calls the sewer plan a good idea and, as the city's lone [Tactician], authorises a permit for a single undead under Pisces' supervision, offering ten gold pieces and a bounty of one copper piece per ten rats killed.
Pisces tells the Horns "Calruz is alive", then admits it is only probable and that he may have jumped to conclusions on partial evidence, and the shouting starts after five seconds.
Pisces uses [Flash Step] to leave the roach cave before the swarm reached him.

At night Pisces reads a book aloud to the inn's guests, the Horns of Hammerad, the Halfseekers, Mrsha, Drassi and Lyonette and five Redfang Warriors, with Erin away, and tells the tale with shadows and sparks, which Ceria asks him to stop.
Pisces and Ksmvr hold the inn's second floor against moths, backed by three giant bear skeletons and deformed bone horrors, and Pisces impales a moth on his rapier.

Pisces asks Erin to let him use the inn's mana for a spell, needing Falene's, Moore's and Ceria's help and cover from the moths; he forms a linked casting with Falene and Moore, having never studied the theory at Wistram, and Falene mocks him for it.
The linked spell brings the rain that ends the moth attack, and Erin sees that Pisces saved them all.
Zevara considers trusting Pisces despite his previous crimes of extortion, remembering Olesm's report on having him clean Liscor's sewers with an undead.
For Erin's play, Pisces animates dead moth bodies as monsters, since fake or illusory ones are not much fun to fight, and plays himself in a hammy Deus ex machina ending with a monologue.
Pisces offers Selys a delay to the sewer errand, showing tact, and uses a muttered word and a breeze to remove the sewer stench.
In Pallass's Archive Pisces is admitted invisibly alongside Selys, who is allowed in because the librarian recognised her from General Shivertail's funeral.

When eight Drake thugs in Pallass threaten Selys, Pisces appears and stabs one with his rapier, then uses [Stone Spray], [Flame Jet], a bolt from his ring and a shot of lightning, and says he is a Silver-rank adventurer.
Pisces' Bone Horror kills several of the Drakes in Pallass, and Pisces tells the last, who grabs Selys with a club, to let her go in a cold voice.

Pisces slips into Selys' apartment behind her before the guard check, saying Zevara's guard missed the window as she opened the door, and gives her wine, spaghetti and meatballs, and salad from his bag of holding, which Erin made at his request because Selys is under a form of house arrest.
Pisces asks Selys the one question that matters, whether she wants the Heartflame Breastplate.

Pisces and Selys spend about two hours trying over a hundred mage-sounds and phrases such as "Drakes do not run" on the armor, with no effect; Pisces says Sserys' line postdates the armor's creation by at least six hundred years.
Pisces suggests more command phrases ("Ia curim law", "Drakes rule") and says any phrase could work, probably the most nonsensical to avoid guessing.
Pisces runs the bidding for the Heartflame Breastplate by [Message] spell, having taught himself the spell, and tells Ilvriss his bid is among the highest while keeping other bidders confidential.
Pisces relays that Pallass offers Selys a modest sum if she agrees not to lend, lease or otherwise give the armor to Wall Lord Ilvriss.
Pisces and Olesm find a third entrance, a shaft down from the crypt, and Pisces says it leads to a Raskghar burial chamber that he scouted with a Shield Spider.
Pisces plans to reanimate at least eight skeletons in the burial chamber as an advance guard and to fashion a Bone Horror.

Pisces plans to sell the Antinium-entrance secret by [Message] spell to the Walled Cities, perhaps except Oteslia, and a list of northern Izril nobles he bought, and predicts more adventurers will flood into Liscor.
Pisces pours bones from his bag of holding to raise three skeletal Raskghar, then fights behind Yvlon and Ksmvr throwing fire while Ceria casts [Ice Spike].
Pisces interrogates the Cave Goblin with an illusion that turns his face into a rotting mask and makes him a booming fleshy monster.

In his room at the inn, Pisces rearranges a pile of bones and receives a coded butterfly from Ceria, the spell they devised at Wistram that not even Calvaron could crack, saying she and Mrsha and the Gnolls are alive in the dungeon with the Raskghar, and then that Calruz is the enemy and Chieftain.
Pisces tells Yvlon and Ksmvr that Ceria contacted him twice by coded message, describing a large domed room, saying she is a captive, and that Calruz killed a Gnoll and is leading the Raskghar.

Pisces raises an eight-foot armored bear Bone Horror with a flame in its eye socket and a giant barbed bone spider, and the rat-hunting Bone Horrors climb out of Liscor's sewers, all heading for the dungeon rift while Pisces says he has mana potions.
After Revi punches him, Pisces loses control of his Bone Horrors and collapses out of mana, and Yvlon catches him.
Pisces is the last to walk through the door; he plucks off the white mana stone and stomps on it.
Pisces assembles another Bone Horror from yellowed bones beside Ceria, and uses [Flash Step] to snatch the ball in the game.
Pisces recites a short poem about the night at the inn, with Antinium dancing and Goblins playing.

Pisces' two-headed Bone Horror, which weighs over two hundred pounds without flesh and is solidified bone, is burned to pieces by the bees; Pisces loses his connection to it, and the bees melt Ceria's ice wall and bulge Falene's force wall before it holds.
Pisces gives Ksmvr his ring enchanted with [Shatterbolt] and his bag of holding with all his bones, warning that another skeleton in it must not be lost.

Ksmvr says he lied in the jail out of concern because Pisces had told him execution sentences are common for menial crimes and that [Necromancers] are unduly hated; Yvlon replies that this is a half truth and that such a sentence is only likely in a Drake city.
Pisces remotely animates three zombies from fallen bandits and a dead Face-Eater Moth to distract bandits attacking Ksmvr, who thanks him as Comrade Pisces.
Pisces attacks Grimalkin with [Flash Step] and a flaming rapier, and Grimalkin deduces his level from observation as "Level 30 plus".
Grimalkin offers Pisces a choice of a scroll of [Fireball], [Lightning Bolt], [Acid Orb] or [Stone Spear], noting the [Necromancer] equivalent [Deathbolt] is a poorer spell.
Pisces says Ksmvr acquired a number of bandit bodies, and describes skeleton soldiers with ribs that shoot out as traps; Selys calls this lazy and a gimmick that works once.
Pisces wakes the inn with a scream one morning, calls it a happy accident, reads a scroll of news he bought from the Mage's Guild for nine copper pieces, and has a huge bone project filling his room.

In the fight with the Wistram mages, Pisces slashes with a [Bone Shiv], uses [Flash Step], a bone rapier from his bag of holding, [Stone Dart], [Barrier of Air] and lightning, and a [Shatterbolt] from his ring destroys Isceil's buckler.
Pisces' ring is still recharging when he tries a second [Shatterbolt], which gives the Wistram mages an opening.
Montressa du Valeross captures Pisces in a Silent Box.

Pisces is found unconscious with a swollen bloody face and broken bones, and Grimalkin and a [Healer] stabilise him, noting the Silent Box preserved the fresh injuries and that his captors left him alive on purpose.
Pisces challenges Isceil, and then Beza, to a duel to the death, demanding satisfaction after being attacked and kidnapped in Liscor, and offers to remove his magical items.
Zevara says duels are old but traditional in Liscor and allows it, and Ceria challenges any one of them too.

Pisces casts an undead illusion on Montressa, which Zevara rules legal because illusions are permitted if not unduly disruptive; Montressa screams, a pyramid-shaped barrier springs up around her as her personal emergency spell, and she weeps until the illusion ends.
Pisces tells the Horns that he does not regret what he said about Calvaron and wishes the curse had killed all of Wistram, and Ceria punches him in the face.

Pisces tells Montressa he made a terrible mistake that killed people, never intended it, wanted to prove there was a place for him at Wistram, and will not surrender to Wistram; he apologises and asks her not to forgive him.

At Yvlon's urging Pisces shows adventurers a skeleton, then six and eight carrying stones for Master Reikhle's road, and Reikhle accepts the offer after asking if they can use a pickaxe; Pisces also offers to animate horses.
Pisces gives an impassioned speech that he is a [Necromancer], human, [Mage] and person who practises necromancy because he is good at it and loves it, and that he is hunted unfairly.
Pisces draws his rapier and challenges Montressa to a duel to end their old mistake, and she accepts.

Pisces carries Montressa away from the Crelers to the foothills, then returns after seeing Ceria's eyes on him, drinks mana potions and raises a Bone Behemoth that fights an adult Creler until it is torn apart, leaving him bleeding from the eyes and nose.
Ceria and Pisces combine their magic in thought so ice coats the Behemoth's broken bones, creating a Frostmarrow Behemoth, as Perril Chandler names it, that hammers the Creler flat.
After the linked magic, Ceria says she and Pisces have trouble uncombining their disciplines and cannot cast for a few days, according to Palt.
Pisces cooks cheesy potatoes on the road with a levitated cast-iron pot.
Pisces says no one is worthy of his help because they judge him in ignorance and fear.
Pisces claims classes are earned only by what a person pursues seriously, so Erin does not level as a [Tactician] because she thinks of chess as a game.
Pisces claims his gold came from a complex bit of magic for which he received remuneration.
Pisces claims Goblins' innate capabilities are too low to support true spellcasting.
Pisces theorises the the skin-taking creature takes skin to sustain itself, uses the dead as fodder, and that Crypt Lords are a byproduct of many dead gathered together for long.
Pisces tells Zevara that Erin probably does not matter to the creature.
Pisces says the Winter Sprites brought the snow.
Pisces believes the chat spell must come from Wistram because of its magnitude and says only they would be this moronic.
Pisces thinks everyone able to retrieve the chat log would be alarmed and that word is spreading by spell and letter.
Pisces names the Krythien Sect, the Magnus Corpsus, Az'kerash and The Putrid One as necromancers who could command a horde.
Pisces insists Toren will return in time whatever Erin orders.
Pisces speculates Toren outgrew Erin's commands and may have developed the capacity for thought.
Pisces says Cognita has no moral compass and functions well enough without one; Ceria calls her a monster who has killed more [Mages] than any other being.
Pisces says Erin's decision to cut the mana link was the most correct choice she could have made.
Pisces tells himself he has no side, has always been alone, and expects friendship to be fleeting and alliances to precede betrayal, yet admits he likes the Horns of Hammerad, even Yvlon.

Pisces tells Yvlon that necromancers lack direct attack spells, that the strength of death magic lies in minions and sapping spells, that necromancy is the mastery of preparation, and that he wants to live among people without their disdain.
Pisces says Regrika and Imenet frighten him terribly although he can sense nothing magical about them, only instinct.

Pisces believes in quality over quantity of undead, with custom designs and specialisation superior to mass-animated armies, and calls himself the only [Necromancer] who believes in the total assurance of quality over quantity.
Pisces regards people as largely predictable, and considers only Niers Astoragon, Erin Solstice and Olesm Swifttail as worth his respect and attention.

Pisces tells the story that the Walled Cities are built with the bones of Dragons, ancestors of the Drakes, and that this is why the Necromancer marched south; he admits he cannot verify it because the cities' secrets are jealously guarded.
Pisces urges Ceria to forgive the people who made a terrible mistake that killed hundreds, reminding her that she once forgave a fool who unleashed wrath on the innocent.

Pisces advises Selys not to sell or give away the Heartflame Breastplate to the wrong faction: he reasons that Salazsar and Pallass are at odds, and that gifting the armor to Liscor's army for a small sum would offend the fewest parties.
Pisces reasons that the fiery ward protecting the user's back came from the Heartflame Breastplate, because of its motif and name and the enchantment learned in Pallass' library.
Pisces declares the necklace cursed, citing the suspicious enchantment and the gripping spell that keeps it from being removed.

Pisces tells Ilvriss, Zevara and Embria that the Antinium secretly want the dungeon's treasure, citing their failure to disclose it, the open pathway into their Hive and a kill box built to last, and calls it speculation.

Pisces theorises the blood cloak takes on the properties of base liquids and is meant as a portable well of blood for a [Bloodmage]; he says he would not use blood magic because necromancy can work on a cadaver or animal's corpse without harming the living, whereas blood magic demands sacrifice.
Pisces surmises at least one moon is full and possibly both.
Pisces scorns an emotional spell cast on Liscor as crude, reliant on a visual component, no better than a hot meal and warm bath, and begins to criticise shamanic magic.
Pisces suggests Numbtongue offer the stone to Octavia to brew into a potion, and Falene dismisses alchemists.
Pisces tells Caddin that the crypt deaths were a tragic dungeon accident that was not Ceria's or Yvlon's fault.
Pisces says the cores of blue fruit are a deadly poison that could kill even with a healing potion, and that no one dying yet is a statistical anomaly.
Pisces defends Olesm's right to say what he chooses, arguing that deriding an opinion is the mark of a weak position.
Pisces predicts Elirr and Raekea will win their Gnoll-heavy districts, citing his discreet survey of the streets, which Selys calls invisible.
Pisces says he is content alone, having chosen to be true to himself as a [Necromancer], and that anyone he found would have to accept what he is, though he is not seeking it.
Pisces predicts news of Tiqr's fall within a day or two and finds it interesting that the King of Destruction never intervened.

Pisces advises Selys to buy single-use items rather than rings: an invisibility or stone skin potion, a Scroll of Lesser Teleport bound to her home, a Wand of [Forcewalls] or [Lightning Bolts], a tracking spell, and a few of Erin's acid jars in her bag of holding in case of Skinner.

The Watch's report says Ceria swore under a truth spell that the deaths were an accident and not homicide, and Zevara says that since Pisces paid off his Liscor crimes the city's laws protect him; Ceria insists to Montressa that it was an accident.
Pisces says Montressa's [Five-Fold Arcane Barrier] shows Wistram's linked spells and formal training are more advanced than his and Ceria's, though he calls it Tier 5.
Ceria says the accident at Wistram killed people but was an accident, and that the necrophilia charge against Pisces is not true.
Pisces says the King of Destruction would kill Raelt, the fencer [King] of Jecrass, and advises the Horns to run if they had to fight Flos Reimarch.
Pisces admits that he gave an undead the ability to level; Ceria attacks him, and he calls Toren an experimental prototype meant to repay Erin and guard the inn, saying he never expected sentience.

Ceria explains that Pisces did not devise leveling undead alone: a Golem, a Truestone Construct, taught him an incomplete formula for creating beings capable of leveling, and he completed it; Pisces says he was taught a theoretical piece of magic and was not certain Toren would level.
Pisces says he did not give Toren a conscience because he does not know how and no one does, and he made Toren to fight and protect with only golem-style problem solving.
Pisces explains that Toren is fed by Erin's natural mana, however far away she is, and that cutting it would make him cease to live.
Pisces says Toren could be stopped and made harmless, but at danger.

Pisces thinks of the secrets pressing at his lips as he looks at Ceria: he ran away from home, his father thinks him a disappointment, he is working on a new undead creation, his [Fencer] class does not exist because he never wanted to level it, he sometimes misses what could have been between them, and he apprenticed himself to an ancient monster for knowledge and power.

Among those same unspoken secrets, Pisces knows that Erin and Ryoka are from a different world and that there are more like them, ate Ceria's extra lasagna and let her blame Ksmvr, and reached Level 30 yesterday.

Pisces tells the Gold-rank adventurers that the ritual makes the Raskghar stronger, then shows a flaming butterfly with Ceria's message that she is alive but says they ruined everything, that the Raskghar escaped, that Calruz suspects treachery, and that he ordered a ritual with twenty more Gnoll captives.
Pisces tells Lyonette that Mrsha is safe for now.
Pisces has considered the problem before, appealed to his new master for help, and been flatly rejected; his Bone Horrors are too weak and inefficient.
Stan calls Pisces a filthy [Necromancer] in front of the Guild, the room turns hostile and eight adventurers stand up, and Pisces acknowledges the truth of the accusation.

Ceria and Pisces tell Grimalkin that Wistram's Council of Mages expelled them but that Cognita declared them graduates; Pisces says it was his fault, that he was revealed as a [Necromancer], and Ceria names Illphres, Montressa, Beatrice and Calvaron as people who died.
Nobody on the Horns knows Pisces' last name, nation, or past before Wistram.

Pisces tells the Horns his true name is Pisces Jealnet, a commoner's name, born in the Kingdom of Ailendamus in Terandria and raised in House Dultel, where his father, Padurn Jealnet, was a [Fencer] employed by the [Lord]; his mother is Enica, and both were alive when he left.

Pisces says he ran away from home because he was a [Necromancer] and stole and used magic and sleight of hand to earn enough gold for Wistram's admission, and that he had always hinted at an aristocratic past that was not true.

Pisces says he once wanted to be a [Fencer] or [Spellsword], learned fencing from his father, and met a beautiful [Necromancer] around the age he was about to level, who showed him a creature of bone; he spoke to her in the month before she died.

Pisces describes the rebellion against his father and attracting the Dultel [Lord]'s approval as a [Mage], being found out, defeating his father and fleeing into crime, learning to read lips and pickpocket, and a fascination with Az'kerash.

Pisces tells of meeting Ceria at Wistram, becoming an outcast once she found out who he was, and trying to rob Nekhret's tomb using the corpses of Ceria's master and the others, unleashing death on Wistram.
Az'kerash regards Pisces Jealnet as his new student and the only recent one whose name he knows, and recalls he himself once owned a golden bell and learned the rapier.
Az'kerash observes Pisces' hand-carved spell inside Toren's bones, which Pisces wrote with a sewing needle on the bones of Archmage Nekhret, and concludes Cognita gave Pisces the knowledge.
Az'kerash recalls that Pisces learned to create a Bone Behemoth in under a month and battled an adult Creler, and witnessed the Frostmarrow Behemoth made with Ceria.

Pisces tells the Horns that in Terandria, before leaving for Wistram, he belonged to a cabal of [Necromancers] who taught him necromancy and ran a commune with a farm tilled by a few hundred undead, emulating Khelt and Az'kerash; it failed because wild dogs attacked the skeletons for bones and undead wandered off or cut down trees.
Pivr is a Revalantor of the Flying Antinium who introduces himself to Klbkch by that title.
Pivr has jade-colored wings, four sets of eyes, a hunched body, twin daggers at his side and poisonous spit.
Pivr produces acidic bile from his mandibles when upset, a trait he was engineered to have.
Pivr has a higher-pitched voice than other Antinium and fans his wings restlessly when he stands still.
The Free Antinium Queen regards Pivr and the Flying Queen's winged soldiers as half-baked copies of the true winged soldiers she saw long ago.
Pivr asks Klbkch whether his Queen has been creating variations of the Worker and Soldier form without authorization.
Pivr brings six warriors of his Queen: five regular warriors and one larger heavy-combat variant with huge wings and a beetle-like horn.
Pivr says the Flying Antinium came to see what Klbkch's Hive has wrought.
Pivr announces that his orders were to obey Prognugator Xrn only until the Antinium reached Liscor, and that the Flying Antinium will enter the city by the main gates.
Pivr tells Xrn her input was not required and that she has no authority over his Queen's orders.
Pivr promises the Flying Antinium will not fight even if provoked, but will maintain a show of force, and invites Klbkch to join them.
Pivr and his six warriors spread their wings and skip across the snow toward Liscor, too fast for Klbkch to follow on foot.

section: Visit to the Free Antinium Hive (Books 4-5)
text: Pivr tells the Free Antinium Queen's chamber that he has surveyed the Hive and found only four Individuals with formal designations and no significant levels, Skills or classes.

section: Visit to the Free Antinium Hive (Books 4-5)
text: Pivr asks, on behalf of his Queen, what formal plan the Free Queen would put before the Hives for converting a whole Hive to Individuals.

section: Visit to the Free Antinium Hive (Books 4-5)
text: Pivr ignores the Free Queen's questions about how many Prognugators and Individuals his own Hive has produced.

section: Visit to the Free Antinium Hive (Books 4-5)
text: Pivr refuses Klbkch's offer to join an expedition and says he will stay to observe the Hive and the dungeon.

section: Visit to the Free Antinium Hive (Books 4-5)
text: The Free Antinium Queen privately considers arranging for a monster to break through and slaughter Pivr by accident, noting that Flesh Worms are quite lethal.

section: Visit to the Free Antinium Hive (Books 4-5)
text: Tersk reports that Pivr fought in the dungeon and was wounded, that three of his five accompanying warriors died, and that his heavy-combat variant was badly damaged.

section: Visit to the Free Antinium Hive (Books 4-5)
text: Tersk considers Pivr a failure of the Prognugator class who does not deserve the title of Revalantor, lacking Klbkch's presence and battle experience.
Pivr stares at Tersk as Tersk holds a history book describing an entire Antinium army destroyed by a Goblin.
Pivr protests to Xrn that the Antinium cannot be defeated so easily and notes that the book says she led the first army.
Pivr's wings fan wide and acidic bile leaks from his mandibles when Xrn confirms the book's account; Tersk snatches the book away before acid lands on it.
Pivr asks Xrn how the Antinium fought and won against Goblin Lords, since the Antinium do not retreat.
Xrn thinks that for all his faults Pivr is brave, and answers his question truthfully.
Pivr flexes his wings with his four Prognugators as Xrn addresses fourteen Prognugators and one Revalantor of the Flying, Silent and Armored Hives.
The narration calls Pivr the Flying Antinium's Prognugator and shows him accompanying Xrn, fluttering his wings in a slight challenge at Xeu.
Pivr notes his own inefficient motion compared with the perfectly hexapodal Xeu of the Silent Antinium.
Pivr follows Belgrade around for three hours asking why he does things and calling them inefficient.
Pivr's constant refrain to Belgrade is to ask whether Prognugator Xrn gave him orders to do something, and if not why he does it.
Pivr is always mystified when Belgrade answers that he chose to act on his own because it seemed useful.
Poisonbite is a female Goblin warrior known by her nickname for the two poisoned daggers she wields.
Poisonbite is a typical Goblin warrior who likes fighting but not practicing fighting.
Poisonbite wears chainmail at all times as proof of her rank, which has saved her life eight times and has only three holes.
Poisonbite is a [Venom Warrior] who is a Hob in the making, growing by the day and eating a massive amount of food.
Poisonbite likes female Goblins.
Rags puts Poisonbite in command of a group of warriors after Redscar takes the Redfang vanguard.
Poisonbite objects to Rags's training plan, saying Goblins do not train, and asks whether it is Goblin.
Poisonbite tells Rags that Goblins must be strong, and answers Rags that training is not Goblin.
Poisonbite recalls Lady Bethal's attack that killed hundreds of Goblins, and says Greydath's identity reveal helped save them.
Poisonbite leads an all-female unit of Goblin raiders, who were good within Tremborag's mountain.
Poisonbite unhorses Snapjaw by killing her mount with poisoned daggers, and the two face off with their warriors behind them.
Poisonbite's female warriors engage Reiss's warriors from the pikes with poisoned blades, but are useless against undead, which are immune to poison.
Poisonbite follows Redscar toward Liscor and the inn with Noears.
Poisonbite tells Erin in English that she is Poisonbite and draws her coated daggers when Erin jokes about her bite.
Erin tells Poisonbite to keep her daggers sheathed and to follow the inn's rules.
Poisonbite insists instantly that Rags, called Chieftain, is alive.
Poisonbite tells Erin that Rags rebelled from Tremborag, fought the [Emperor], defeated the pink-death [Knights] and spoke to Greybeard.
Poisonbite survives the battle by hiding and being overlooked by the Humans, then climbs the mountain toward Rags.
Poisonbite watched Noears die after he called lightning from the sky, and he stayed so more Goblins could escape.
Poisonbite breaks up with Shineshield in her own mind, but Shineshield, a Redfang [Shield Maiden] who survived Garen's last charge, had decided she had enough.
Poisonbite hops mad around Shineshield until her warriors drag her off, and Snapjaw says Shineshield likes one Goblin at a time while Poisonbite likes many.

In Book 1 a filthy blonde girl with pale skin, hiding behind a shopkeeper's stall, rushes into the street when her [Invisibility] spell fails, and fires a web-shooting emerald ring that pins Gerial and Sostrom and cocoons Ceria.
Gazi severs the web with her sword, and the girl has already fled down an alleyway.
In Book 2 a starving [Princess] steals from market stalls in Liscor's winter chill, using a few remaining charges of [Invisibility] and spells to open locks.
The [Princess] believes richness is her birthright and that she deserves everything she takes.
A Gnoll, Krshia, catches her, noting that invisibility is not enough against the Gnolls' sense of smell.
Her invisibility breaks, and in fear she fires a ring and screams "Ignis!", whose fireball destroys a stall and engulfs the Gnoll.
Gnolls seize the [Princess] from behind, capturing her hand and ring.
Prost is a [Farmer] of Riverfarm whom Durene helped with his broken wagon before Laken arrived.
Prost is married to Yesel, who gives Laken a basket of goods for Durene's home.
Prost's son Finnon fetches Durene when the family wagon loses a wheel, and the family's old plow horse is Evera.
Prost shakes Laken's hand first when Durene brings him into the village.
Prost tells Durene she does not belong with the villagers and says they took her in and fed her at risk to themselves.
Durene answers that the village only took her in because her mother asked, gave her scraps, and made her sleep in the barn.
Laken says Prost called Durene a monster, a freak and inhuman.
Laken greets Prost coldly because he remembers their last meeting, and asks after Yesel and the children.
Laken offers Prost one gold coin for dried meat and eggs, then two if the village adds to it.
Laken infers that Prost later apologised to Durene, though more briefly than he would have liked.
After the avalanche, Prost stands humble before Laken and calls him "Emperor".
Laken swears to Prost, as an [Emperor], that he will return to Riverfarm.
Laken says Prost lost his youngest boy in the avalanche, though his attitude toward Laken and Durene has since improved.
Prost reports that Ryoka brought food a week before Laken's return, and that the village is rationing it.
Prost helps Laken sketch plans for a rebuilt Riverfarm, doubting at first that it can be done.
Laken asks Prost to be his [Steward], though Prost says he is not worthy of the class.
Laken says he saw Prost change from refusing a half-Troll to calling him [Emperor].
Later, Prost gains the class [Steward] overnight and loses all his earlier levels.
Prost had been a Level 20 [Farmer], plus a few levels in other classes, before becoming a Level 8 [Steward].
Prost has the Skills [Talent Finder] and [Eye of Need], which help him find the people best suited for tasks.
Prost's wife and two surviving daughters regard his loss of levels as terrible but made up for by a superior class.
Prost shouts "Kneel before Emperor Laken, the Protector of Riverfarm!" to the Windrest refugees until Laken elbows him quiet.
Prost organises the Windrest refugees by class, with Carpenters and Woodcutters going straight to work.
Prost leads Laken to ground covered in sawdust and plans stone work from the quarry.
Laken sees that Prost's wife is the one who lost her leg in the Goblin attack, though his children are alive.
Prost tells Laken that his people are sworn to him and bound to him by more than class or Skill.
Prost tells Laken that Rehanna had likely been prompted, and that only the adventurers brought alcohol.
Prost coughs gently to stop Laken when he is being foolish, a system they have developed.
Prost reports that three villagers became [Tinkerers], and Tessia learned [Detect Flaw].
Laken says Prost is now his right-hand man who oversees construction, settles disputes and coordinates food and housing.
Prost tells Laken that families fear nobles attending the banquet will seduce or carry off their daughters.
Laken suspects Prost nudged him to intervene in the builders' feud because the two men would not heed a new [Steward].
Prost tells Laken that [Emperors] do not make mistakes, because they know what they are doing.

section: Prost in the Goblin war and after (Book 12)
text: Prost pools villagers' coins, charges no rent, and makes everyone work for their food.

section: Prost in the Goblin war and after (Book 12)
text: Prost says he would obey Laken without question, because Laken found his daughter in snow ten feet deep.

section: Prost in the Goblin war and after (Book 12)
text: Prost admits to Durene that he never apologised after the avalanche.

section: Prost in the Goblin war and after (Book 12)
text: Durene tells Prost she was terrified when she beat a thief four years ago, and cried for three days afterward.

section: Prost in the Goblin war and after (Book 12)
text: Prost tells the village that Laken is about two weeks away with the [Engineer] teams, escorted by two [Lords].

section: Prost in the Goblin war and after (Book 12)
text: Prost uses [Crowd Control] to silence the crowd.

section: Prost in the Goblin war and after (Book 12)
text: Prost declares an execution just, makes Hedag swear on a truth stone, and says his authority rules until Laken returns.

section: Prost in the Goblin war and after (Book 12)
text: Prost agrees to send wagons, Beniar and bows to help, and strides out before Rie can object.

section: Prost in the Goblin war and after (Book 12)
text: Prost orders Belavierr in Laken's name not to bargain with anyone, and she walks past him without a word.

section: Prost in the Goblin war and after (Book 12)
text: Eloise promises Prost that the coven will remind Belavierr of Laken's request.

section: Prost in the Goblin war and after (Book 12)
text: Prost lost children in the Riverfarm avalanche, and Belavierr shows him a picture of a boy waving at him.

section: Prost in the Goblin war and after (Book 12)
text: Prost sees his living children Finnon and Margery run toward him in the street, led by Califor.
Lady Pryde Ulta is the [Lady] of House Ulta, a close friend of Magnolia Reinhart who considers herself no one's inferior.
Pryde is a tall woman with black hair, high cheekbones and an imperious posture and voice.
Pryde has orange pupils that flash when she is furious.
Ultase is the largest city of the Ulta lands and was founded by Pryde's ancestors.
