The people of Ulta share Pryde's belief that pride is a virtue above all others, and the Ulta region includes a population of nudists.
Pryde once imported a Griffin in the hope of riding it around, and always seeks an edge to establish her superiority over her fellow nobles.
Later, Pryde wears a stylised bob cut with blonde hair that has dusky threads, having consented to an Earth-style haircut.
Pryde crushes a pinned [Assassin] with the Skill [Ego is Weight], which doubles the gravity on him until his crossbow snaps.
Pryde uses [Pride is Weight] to crush an Ogre Chieftain with gravity that grows stronger the closer he gets to her.
Pryde survives three blows from an Ogre Chieftain's hammer with [Pride is Unbreakable], and the Ogres' morale breaks.
Pryde's ego, spent in battle, returns as she is cheered after the Ogre fight.
Pryde's [Pride is Weight] drags Grimalkin's reaching hand down, and Grimalkin identifies it as a gravity Skill.
Pryde has the Skill [Compressed Muscle], which Grimalkin calls a [Lady]'s Skill that he has not seen in years.
Pryde says [Compressed Muscle] was a gift from her mother and that House Ulta has always been in high physical shape.
Pryde says she keeps fit without magic or an aura, and that she has ensured House Ulta's retainers follow a strict training regimen.
Pryde lifts a weights bar with over two hundred pounds on it and does two squats in front of Grimalkin.
Pryde, in the middle of her city, is attacked by four [Assassins] who leap from a rolling wagon but are pinned by her aura.
Pryde angrily demands to know how many [Assassins] were sent to Magnolia, Zanthia, Wuvren and Bethal, and tells the Guildmaster to take the contract himself.
The citizens of Pryde's city descend on the four immobilised [Assassins], and Pryde afterwards touches her subjects' hands and brows.
Pryde dismounts and faces an Ogre Chieftain who threatens her lands, telling him he deserves death for what he has done.
Pryde mocks the Chieftain's lewd threats, saying he is too unsightly to be a consort, and he is killed after his Ogres begin to fall to her [Archers].
Pryde's dress is shredded across the chest when the Chieftain's first blow lands, and she mocks him with "Too much woman to handle, Ogre?"
Pryde rides home to Ultase with a cloak covering her, then wears the cloak over her shoulders and refuses to have her dress repaired.
Pryde tells her retainer Beshard that shame is not something she feels for her body, and says a [Lady] is a [Lady] naked or clothed.
Pryde admits she briefly considered making the Ogres her vassals, and says Wuvren claims to have charmed a Troll once.
Beshard, a Chandrarian Stitch-man, has served Pryde for eight years and still finds her people's attitude to nudity disconcerting.
Pryde slaps Belavierr across the face and tells her to begone, breaking one of the rules the [Ladies] had agreed to.
Pryde holds a grudge against most of the assembled [Ladies], and the narration describes her as still a girl and defined by her pride.
Belavierr tells Pryde that pride is fleeting and that she does not know how small she is, then strikes her down while she is still invoking her greatest Skill, which is cut off mid-name.
Pryde lies in the earth with her head lolling, alive but with her ego extinguished, and Wuvren and Zanthia lift her up.
Pryde arrives at the Wandering Inn in an Earth-style yellow satin tracksuit, with Wuvren and Magnolia in similarly modern dress.
Pryde has a clash with Grimalkin, who uses half a dozen spells to push her back a step, and she says he is not bad.
Pryde offers eighty thousand gold pieces for the inn's magic door and says she has other objects she wishes to buy.
Pryde's aura gathers around her, brushes off Erin's aura and begins to overpower the [Innkeeper], and Lyonette notes that someone has taught her.
Pryde's aura immobilises Yvlon, Ksmvr, Pisces and Ceria, and an observer says she has control, potency and manifestation.
Pryde stumbles back a few steps when Erin manifests her aura, and then answers with a locked contest of auras.
Pryde has experience, a more powerful class and a more distinguished aura than Erin, but Erin is fighting in her own inn.
Pryde and Erin advance on one another as Pryde activates [Pride is Unbreakable], until Lyonette pushes Erin aside and sends her after Rose's group.
Pryde fails to squash Lyonette, who curtsies as the inn's [Manager] and [Head Barmaid], and Pryde remarks that Lyonette has politeness and a spine.
Pryde places an order for multiple weight sets while Grimalkin cleans blood off his scales.
Pryde was one of the few people to actually order Grimalkin's weight sets, and House Ulta later sends him lists of bench-press numbers.
Pryde has nearly sixty people on her lists by the end of the week, with the top entry four hundred and eleven.
Grimalkin copies the numbers into a master list and posts it at Erin's weight-room, and the next day Pryde sends a list topped by Human, male, 500.
Pryde does not cede anything to Drakes, and Grimalkin posts her list, which brings an immediate demand for proof.
Pryde declares that it is possible to break one thousand pounds without magic and aims for a Human-only record.
Purple Smile is an Antinium Soldier of the Painted Soldiers who has painted a purple ring around both eyes and a smile across his mandibles and lower face.
Purple Smile leads the Soldiers who patrol above ground, and two other Soldiers copy his painted markings.
Purple Smile is relaxed and calm, in contrast to Yellow Splatters, who stands at straight attention.
Pawn tells Yellow Splatters he is considering Purple Smile as the next [Sergeant].
Yellow Splatters thinks the smile looks ridiculous, but Purple Smile enjoys the activity.
Purple Smile leads ten Painted Soldiers against zombies, but retreats when two Crypt Lords lurch toward them, to Yellow Splatters' outrage.
Purple Smile and his Soldiers then flank the Crypt Lords from behind.
Anand praises Purple Smile's efficiency in combat, saying his lateral thinking is impressive though he is less powerful than Yellow Splatters.
Yellow Splatters doubts Purple Smile is fit to be a [Sergeant], since he does not spar and wanders the barracks playing with a rolled-up ball.
Pawn congratulates Purple Smile as a [Sergeant], and Purple Smile hugs Yellow Splatters and Twin Stripes.
Purple Smile touches Twin Stripes' chest as Pawn's blessing restores him from Aberration.
Purple Smile and Yellow Splatters are both [Sergeants] under Pawn, a new concept to both.
Purple Smile mimes a plan with his four hands, which Pawn interprets as a suggestion to talk to a woman.
Pawn tells the Queen that Yellow Splatters and Purple Smile show great promise.
Purple Smile dances and shows other Workers and Soldiers how to do it, while Yellow Splatters reads a book.
Pyrite is a fat Hobgoblin who was the Chieftain of a small mining tribe, the Gold Stone (Goldstone) tribe, and later calls himself Rags's second.
Before he is called Pyrite the Gold Stone Chieftain has no name, because his tribe had no [Shaman].
In Garen's first attack the Gold Stone Chieftain steps in front of Rags and takes a one-handed sword slash meant for her, which breaks his shield and cuts through his armor.
The Gold Stone Chieftain knows more Goblin history than Rags does.
Rags sees the Gold Stone Chieftain as a classical Hob, fat and trusting his body mass to shield him, fairly good with an axe and shield, and chewing pine needles.
The Gold Stone Chieftain refuses Rags's order to go and be nice to the strongest Redfang Hob in order to gain his trust, saying "Not Goblin".
The Gold Stone Chieftain tells Rags that he once lived in Tremborag's mountain long ago.
The Gold Stone Chieftain says he is strong but not smart, that he cannot be a Lord and does not want to be.
The Gold Stone Chieftain attacks Tremborag's Goblins with the Hobs Rags sent him.
Pyrite has deep slashes on his belly and arm, chews a stick and spits out pieces of wood, and says chewing rocks keeps his teeth sharp.
Pyrite drags Rags to safety miles from the village and tells her that fewer than a hundred Goblins died.
Pyrite eats soap, smooth stones from the lake bed and slabs of bark.
Pyrite stays awake at night while Rags sleeps, so that he is there in case something goes wrong.
To Pyrite smells are like colors, and he cannot write.
Pyrite's first memory of a Human is being stabbed by a farmer with a pitchfork on a raid.
Pyrite wonders why the last Goblin King, Velan, was called Velan the Kind, and how Tremborag took on the giant form he used to slaughter Gold-rank adventurers.
Pyrite wonders what the key-like thing Garen Redfang showed Tremborag unlocks, since it convinced the Great Chieftain to ally with Rags's tribe.
To lift morale Pyrite throws Goblins into the lake for fun, then throws Rags herself in, and she swims out quickly.
Pyrite is sure the nearby Human town sent the adventurers who killed the Undercrawler tribe, though there is no proof.

Pyrite composes verses in his head, including lines beginning "The wretched few gather" and "We are not monsters yet", and dreams of Goblins living freely at peace with other races and of Rags becoming a Goblin Lord and someday a King.
Pyrite tells the grumbling Goblins that Rags is aimless and young but "Will grow", while he crunches a giant Barkeater Beetle.
Pyrite drowns a Rose Knight in the lake, fights on with his axe broken, and is stabbed in the side by a frost dagger.
Pyrite tells the Goblins that Greydath taught him some old things and stories, that he left the mountain long ago and made his own tribe, and he punches a Hob who suggests he could be Chieftain.
Rags regards Pyrite as a big, classically fat Hob who is deceptively placid and sometimes quite sharp, and he is respected by all factions of her tribe.
Pyrite says Greydath was an old Goblin who liked to talk but was very secretive and that he knew little, then passes gas and walks off.
Pyrite beats six Hobs and about nine smaller Goblins from Tremborag's mountain who are attacking Welca, together with Sir Kerrig.
After Pyrite offers the older Knight a muddy dandelion, Sir Kerrig thanks him and asks to talk honestly, saying he had scarcely believed Goblins could be peaceful after Velan the Kind.
Pyrite tells the Knights that Goblins want only to live.
Pyrite says his tribe attacked caravans and one settlement, took only from caravans, did not kill, and was not like the Mountain City tribe.
Pyrite says a Human town killed Goblin adults and children, and that the Goblins then killed the same number of Humans because they counted.
Pyrite tells Welca that he does not kidnap or rape.
Pyrite says he was the Chieftain of the Goldstone Tribe, which never fought Humans and gathered gold stones for fun.
Pyrite carries an old hemp sack of pyrite nuggets and gems, and he treats a real gold nugget as worthless and trades it to a Goblin child for tadpoles.
Pyrite tells the Knights that his tribe threw gems at attacking armies as "Human bait" to make them stop and fight each other.
Pyrite gives Welca a polished, cut sapphire the size of an egg that he made himself, and gives Sir Kerrig a piece of turquoise.
Pyrite asks the Knights how magic works and what it wants.
Pyrite says he wants to be a [Mage] rather than a [Shaman] because [Mages] cast spells easily, and because Humans kill Goblin [Mages] first.
Pyrite crunches a topaz, says "Sink", and turns the soft ground to mud so that he and Welca sink into the earth.
In the battle Pyrite cuts a Human [Captain] down with his fiery battleaxe and orders his Hobs not to chase the fleeing Humans because the Chieftain said so.
At a crossroads Pyrite tells Rags that the Human Knight who stayed wants to learn and thinks Goblins are like people, and Rags orders them to watch him.
Pyrite carries an enchanted battleaxe that sets a tree alight, and takes arrows in his fat.
Pyrite calls himself second and orders Redscar to obey, and Redscar does.
Pyrite tells Bethal "Tears are a waste of water" and that his tribe is not the Goblin Lord's army and does not raid Goblins.
While Rags lies unconscious, Pyrite fights off the Unseen Empire's raids for three days, keeping the tribe marching, and takes five arrows in the chest.
Pyrite refuses to use a healing potion on himself so that potions are conserved for the wounded.
Pyrite works out that the totems are the Humans' eyes, and he sends eighty Goblins in pairs with axes and torches to destroy them.
Pyrite tells the Goblins to put their backs to the walls of the shattered city, with rows of twenty-foot pikes and a line of a hundred veteran Hobs behind them.
Pyrite's enchanted battleaxe burns through flesh, sets Humans ablaze and sets the club of Durene alight.
Pyrite reflects that he told Sir Kerrig and Welca that his tribe did not fight Humans, but that this was not true.
Lord Tyrion's army identifies the fat Hob with the enchanted battleaxe as the probable Chieftain, though Welca cannot be sure.
Pyrite says he killed forty-three Humans in battle before other Humans came, out of anger.
Pyrite lifts his battleaxe and says "Small" to the Goblin Lord, who does not get the joke.
Pyrite tells Tremborag that Greydath of Blades taught him, and Tremborag is stunned.
Pyrite lived happily as a [Mining Chieftain] with the Goldstone Tribe, learned Skills to find, cut and polish gemstones, and has a second class, [Blademaster], at Level 3.
Pyrite finds a nest of burrowing rats with his gem-finding ability, roasts them and shares them with Eater of Spears and the other Goblins.
Pyrite charges the Eater Goats with a Hob charge, cutting through them with his flaming battleaxe despite being bitten, and then tells Redscar he did it to show the Mountain City Hobs.
Pyrite tells Eater of Spears that he can see when and where someone is going to hit by reading muscles, which he learned from Greydath and which is not a Skill.
Pyrite privately doubts Greydath's secrets about Goblin Kings, which drove him from Tremborag's mountain.
When Reiss's army turns on Rags, Pyrite throws Eater of Spears' axes and cuts off Reiss's hand, saying "Told you".
Pyrite fights through Reiss's army with his enchanted battleaxe, blocks [Deathbolt] with the metal, and cuts a charred line across Reiss's chest.
Seemingly killed by [Deathbolts], Pyrite is found alive by Rags chewing on gemstones, and tells her he ate the magic gemstones to absorb the magic.
Pyrite tells Rags his class is now [Magestone Chieftain] and makes an emerald glow with a trail of magic.
Pyrite says he left Tremborag's mountain at about age five after a fight with Greydath, founded the Mountain Fierce Warriors Tribe, saw it destroyed by Humans, and gave up on becoming a Goblin Lord.
At the mountain slope Pyrite blocks the Humans, hurls Tyrion Veltras down the mountain, and kills Humans with his battleaxe.
Pyrite dies sitting on the slope after being run through by Tyrion and struck by magic and steel, reaching for a snack, with Rags far above him.
Numbtongue finds Pyrite's body lying on its back with a smile on his face, takes a glowing blue gemstone from his mouth, and buries the head on a hill across from the inn.
Pyrite had guessed that if one could remember a scene, one could pass on a sword technique or spell, and he tested it on Numbtongue in his last moments.
Pyrite sent Numbtongue knowledge he deemed important, including the secret of the two keys, one of which Garen has.
Pyrite consolidated his [Mining Chieftain] class into a [Magestone Chieftain] one, and his memories include carving an emerald marble for the Goblin Stickhair.
Through the Skill [A Minute, Reborn], Pyrite wakes in Numbtongue's body for about a minute and scratches questions into the floorboards, ending with "Find the others if they remain. Find our King."
In Numbtongue's body Pyrite carves a smoky quartz marble with [Rock Polishing] and [Miner's Claws] and rolls it to Mrsha, thanking her for the good food.
Pyrite again speaks through Numbtongue to Mrsha, and uses a knife on a chair leg to hollow a hidden compartment to test how much an [Innkeeper] Skill enlarges it.
The Greystone Chieftain is told that the Goldstone Chieftain is dead, killed by being impaled, "Sacrifice death".
Qissa is a Drake Watch Captain in Pallass who carries an enchanted spear.
Watch Captain Qissa tries to hold a dozen Wyverns that have occupied the 4th Floor, while her [Mages] fail to hurt them even with a [Fireball].
Qissa asks where 1st Army and General Duln are, and a Senior Guard answers that they are fighting below and working their way up.
All twelve Wyverns breathe at once, shattering a magical barrier, and Frost Resistance potions fail to protect Qissa's [Guards].
Qissa orders her [Guards] to keep the Wyverns pinned until reinforcements arrive and decides to charge in herself despite attempts to restrain her.
A thrown jar of red oil bursts on a Wyvern, and the oil-covered Wyverns go berserk and attack their fellows, saving Qissa and her [Guards].
Qissa recognizes Saliss's voice and turns to find the naked Drake alchemist standing in the street.
Qissa survives the battle and is later seen working in a window of the Watch House.
Quallet Marshhand is a Human Level 32 [Mercenary Captain] who commands the suppression company Gravetender's Fist.
Quallet has the Skill [Talent Seeker], which lets him find the best recruits in any group.
Quallet uses [Commanding Presence] to stare down a challenging recruit.
Quallet has light skin tanned from days in the sun, and later bears several scars.
Quallet reflects that only Niers Astoragon or Valka Cerethrian could win every recruit, and the Four Great Companies' leaders never recruit in such grounds.
Quallet signs over eighty recruits in one night, doubling the size of Gravetender's Fist.
Gravetender's Fist keeps expensive bags of holding and a single wagon instead of many supply wagons.
Quallet has the Dullahan Xor unload the bags of holding, while Raeh oversees soldiers eating preserved food.
Quallet punches a recruit who drops his sword in drills and threatens to leave shirkers in the forest to rot.
Quallet kills a Ghoul with his axe at blinding speed during a night patrol in the valley.
Quallet carries the company flag, a fist shooting out of soil on glowing cloth, so neither army treats suppression companies as enemies.
Quallet pulls the whole company back within range of the banner and orders them to move together after losing soldiers.
Quallet thanks Geneva for saving one of his soldiers and offers silver and copper coins, and she refuses fees.
Quallet is not offended by Geneva's interruption and notes that the soldier she saved is a good one.
Ken's negotiation after the Centaurs' demand wins Quallet's praise, and Quallet makes Ken the company's go-between for Centaurs and Dullahans.
Quallet stares at Ken and turns away without answering when asked whether he warned the Dullahans about the deserters.
Quallet holds the neutral ground with other surviving neutral parties around a map of the valley.
Quallet and Exara take over the surviving soldiers of Ulvial's company after the first attack kills Ulvial.
Ken names Quallet as a neutral [Captain] of Gravetender's Fist when addressing the battlefield.
Quallet rents an inn and listens as Geneva briefs him on sexually transmitted diseases.
Quallet asks for at least four hundred condoms for his company, which Geneva and Paige plan to have stitched by hired Lizardfolk.
Quallet tells the Earthworlders that a company that does not fight dies.
Quallet leads the search for the missing Caroline with Daly and Paige and never finds her.
Quallet says he is done with suppression-company work and wants a real fighting company at his back.
Quallet agrees to split from the United Nations company, expects most of his men to follow, and will look for work that day.
Quallet shares out the remaining funds generously with Ken and promises to keep ties with Ken's group.
The Quarass of Germina is the ruler of Germina, protector of Ger, and a Dragonslayer, one of the rulers of Chandrar's four Shield Kingdoms.
The Quarass dies and is found again as a new young girl, while her memories pass on to the next incarnation.
The current Quarass has a child's body of perhaps nine to thirteen, pale yellow eyes and black hair with a widow's peak.
The Quarass's eyes look as old as forever, and her voice carries adult intelligence through a child's voice.
The Quarass has lived eighty-seven lifetimes, some brief and some long.
The Quarass says she chooses to be Quarass and give herself for Germina, though she could flee.
The Quarass remembers lifetimes upon lifetimes and can compare the best [Strategists] and builders of all ages.
The Quarass remembers Reim's castle being built about fifteen hundred years ago, first as a keep.
The Quarass ranks Drevish the [Architect] in her top twenty, probably the top ten, though the previous Quarass disliked his personality.
The Quarass remembers her previous death, a woman who feared the King of Destruction, with red-gold hair and a sword.
The Quarass says she was once a [Carpet Racer], a [Skyrider of Ger], and that she died at age thirty-eight flying a carpet into a Dragon's maw.
Fetohep says that when the world rose against Vampires, the Quarass was possessed by their power and her Champion of Ger sacrificed his life to wake her.
Fetohep says she drank poison, poisoned the Vampires' bloodwells with her own ichor, and fought for hours until she died.
Fetohep says the reborn Quarass led an army that staked every remaining Vampire and burned the rest from the toes up in molten stone.
The Quarass says the current girl's only notable event was killing a viper with her father's dagger, and the viper bit her four times.
The Quarass arrives at Reim with about forty Germina citizens, who were enemies of Flos months ago, and she greets Flos as the King of Destruction.
The Quarass travels with sacred protectors, including a street-tough boy and a noblewoman, and her private entourage includes hidden [Assassins].
Trey Atwood is a friend of the Quarass, who tolerates him on her trip.
The Quarass flies a carpet with Trey and Gazi, and says most carpet riders die within a month.
The Quarass walks into Jecrass's palace sworn to peace by Ger and is besieged by servants seeking her advice.
The Quarass tells King Raelt she comes in peace, not at the King of Destruction's command, and only seeks to rest an hour or two.
The Quarass tells Raelt she would have sent twenty thousand riders to raid and burn villages that did not declare against Flos.
The Quarass advises Raelt to choose whichever answer he can live with.
The Quarass spots the adventurers' wagon from Medain, and her bodyguards kill the [Mage] and capture another adventurer.
The Quarass cannot cast lightning magic in her current body.
The Quarass orders a [Message] sent to Jecrass that their [Princess] has been kidnapped.
Yisame is a [Queen] of Nerrhavia, who sees the truth of battle for the first time while watching Flos's attack on Belchan.
Yisame's horror at the scene is genuine, which earns her appreciation for her sincerity.
Yisame, pale, declares war again on Belchan.
Yisame covertly tells Raelt that she has sent a small gift and that at least forty thousand Nerrhavian mercenaries may head north.
Yisame says the mercenaries require payment, hence the gift, which the Merchant's Guildmaster estimates at about three hundred thousand gold pieces.
Raelt has also just received money from the Empress of Sands.
Quelm is an [Alchemist] in Celum, one of four [Alchemists] in the city, and a competitor of Octavia.
Quelm is level 20 to 25 and moderately successful.
Quelm is less thuggish than Jeffil or Mabel, but he holds a grudge.
Quelm figures out Octavia's match formula and improves it, selling more reliably ignited matches for less.
Quelm chases Octavia after she delivers a message to him, and his neighbors do not call the Watch.
Quelm bought out the muscle Octavia approached, according to Octavia.
Quelm's matches are said to be the best in the city and the only ones sold, with his designs stolen.
Quelm is the backer of a new gang that has created a monopoly on matches through low-level racketeering.
Quelm's [Thug] seizes Octavia's potions and tells her she will sell through Quelm's store for two-thirds, with Quelm getting a third.
Quelm's [Thug] says Quelm is concerned and sent him to help Octavia sell.
Octavia calls the seizure robbery and threatens to go to the City Watch.
A thug, shaken by Numbtongue, answers that Alchemist Quelm sent and hired them.
Queravia was one of the King of Destruction's Seven and the strategist who led his armies.
Queravia won the fiercest battles in Flos's name by directing soldiers while his other vassals fought on the front lines.
Queravia was a [Gambler Strategist] who bet against luck itself.
Before she died, Queravia advanced to [Gambler of Fates].
Queravia and Tottenval died in the war, and Flos did not see her end but heard of it.
Queravia lost her last bet in Baleros.
Flos had thought it impossible that Queravia would ever die.
In a flashback, Gazi and Flos tell Venith that Queravia and Tottenval are dead, whereupon Flos declares himself finished as King.
Niers fought a famous battle against Queravia, the Gambler of Fates, the King of Destruction's [Strategist].
Niers thinks Queravia had a sixty percent chance in any scenario left to the odds, so she won six of ten even matchups.
Niers says her tactics sometimes worked against impossible odds, creating a huge difference over time.
Quexa is a blue-scaled Lizardgirl with deep red neck frills, bordering on purple, who serves in Gravetender's Fist.
Quexa is a [Sorcerer], and says [Sorcerers] cast by thinking hard and do not study as [Mages] do.
Quexa says Lizardfolk are the biggest species in Baleros and resemble Drakes without being related to them.
Quexa shouts at the Centaurs that Gravetender's Fist are not enemies when Luan is shot.
Quexa helps carry Luan to Geneva's camp on a stretcher.
Quexa spots Ken and Luan running onto the battlefield in red-cross armor and leaps up in fear.
Quexa becomes friends with Paige after Ken, Luan and Aiko leave.
Quexa loses a leg to a Centaur with an axe, and also part of her tail.
Quexa tries to smile and chatters as if the loss were nothing when she greets Ken.
Quexa uses a simple prosthetic leg that Geneva helped design and Daly carved.
Quexa uses a pegleg that Geneva helped make, and Geneva hopes to improve it with modern technology.
Quexa tells Daly she likes him but is not sure they should be together as she leaves to be a mercenary.
Quexa leaves the Earthworlders with Quallet's company because she wanted to be a mercenary.
Quexa limps on her pegleg and keeps up with Quallet's revitalized Gravetender's Fist.
Quexa is the first person Daly shows the crossbow to, and he hopes to impress Quallet with it.
Quexa values Paige and Daly's all-wood crossbow at two gold coins, calling crossbows poor against armor or monster hides.
Quietstab is a Hob of Rags' tribe who wields a huge stave or cudgel.
Quietstab followed Rags from Tremborag's mountain and misses some of the luxuries Humans enjoy, such as alcohol.
Quietstab knocks Lord Pellmia's son Gilam from his saddle with the stave during the forest ambush.
Quietstab ignores Gilam, yanks down his white mare and mounts it, riding it off.
Drunk and happy after the celebration, Quietstab goes to the latrines outside Rags' camp.
Tremborag greets Quietstab as "traitor", twists his head and tosses him into the latrine.
Quietstab dies, his neck snapped by Tremborag.
Goblins find Quietstab's body in the latrine ditch, and Rags recognises his terrified face.
Rabbiteater is a Redfang Hobgoblin, one of the five Hobs who stay at Erin Solstice's inn.
Rabbiteater earned his name by catching rabbits and is an expert at running fast.
Rabbiteater was as close to a [Scout] as the Redfang Warriors had, but Garen promoted him because he was a better warrior.
Rabbiteater learned to hunt rabbits in the grass and became the stealthiest of the five Hobs by honing his skills.
Rabbiteater is the only Goblin of the five with [Dangersense].
Rabbiteater is the jack-of-all-trades among the five Hobs, and later teaches his followers about traps, foraging, nets and beds.
Rabbiteater frightens Octavia when he comes down the stairs, and she flees screaming while brandishing a potion at him.
Rabbiteater's [Dangersense] makes him freeze and warn the others at the Pallass door, and he hears breathing on the other side.
Rabbiteater holds up four fingers to signal that four watchers are posted outside the Pallass door.
The five Hobs judge themselves worth thirteen regular Goblin warriors but unable to defeat an army.
Rabbiteater takes point in the dungeon, following monsters' tracks on the floor to avoid traps.
Rabbiteater wraps a white cloak around himself and pretends to writhe in agony, a joke that earns him a beating from the others.
The white cloak turns to water when Rabbiteater rolls into a puddle, and blades pass through it but are slowed as if underwater.
The cloak turns blood red when Shorthilt's sword cuts Rabbiteater, and it turns clear again when water is poured on it.
Rabbiteater charges a Raskghar, and the water cloak wraps over its head until it drowns.
Erin hugs Rabbiteater in thanks with one arm, and the Hobgoblin freezes.
Rabbiteater mimes putting shutters on the outside of the inn's windows, which Erin praises as genius.
Rabbiteater and Lyonette agree to shutter only the ground-floor windows.
Erin begs Rabbiteater and Numbtongue to find Mrsha and Ceria, abandoning her Plan G, and Numbtongue promises they will.
Rabbiteater fixes a doorknob and a red mana stone to a plank to mimic a magic door, which only shows the cave wall.
Rabbiteater swirls his water cloak to catch Headscratcher's punch.
Rabbiteater hears [Warrior Level 19!] but gets no class change and sags in disappointment.
The five Redfang Hobs lead about forty Cave Goblins and meet the fleeing Gnolls, and then hold off the Raskghar.
Rabbiteater wears a red cloak that looks like liquid and smells of blood, and Nokha's blade hisses and steams against it.
Rabbiteater reaches [Level 20 Warrior!] and changes to the [Champion] class.
Rabbiteater gains the Skills [Champion's Gear], [Grand Slash] and [Valor of Champions] with the class change.
Rabbiteater's cape is magical, shifting between water, mud and blood, though it is usually blood.
Rabbiteater is learning to cook from Erin, and the Cave Goblins who saw him lead the charge consider him their leader.
The largest faction of Goblins at the inn follows Rabbiteater, and they cook rather than focus on Redfang training.
Rabbiteater's group is envied and scorned by the other four factions, though no one complains at mealtime.
The five Hobs tell Garen they did not kill Erin because she was nice, and Rabbiteater says she is very good.
Rabbiteater explains that Erin left Liscor and the Redfangs could not track her over many days of walking.
The five Hobs tell Garen that his orders were bad and that Rags was the true Chieftain.
Rabbiteater tells the Redfangs he is called [Champion] now.
Rabbiteater trades blows with Garen despite being struck repeatedly, and Garen breaks his ribs.
Rabbiteater, bruised from Garen's kick, gets back up with the others each time they are struck down.
Rabbiteater climbs the hill to Erin wearing shining chainmail and a wine-red cloak, saying he saw the flag.
Rabbiteater helps Erin up and lifts her white flag with the other four Hobs.
Rabbiteater credits Pebblesnatch, while Numbtongue says "Somebody", as the source of their news that Erin was staying.
Rabbiteater tells Erin simply "We like you" as the reason they returned.
Rabbiteater is among the five brothers who run ahead against the Goblin Lord.
Rabbiteater tells Rags the names of his missing friends and weeps.
Rabbiteater sobs and embraces Badarrow when Redscar arrives carrying Garen's blade, Redfang.
Badarrow reports that Headscratcher, Numbtongue and Shorthilt are all dead.
Rabbiteater wears a helmet and poses as a Goblin hunter known as the Goblin Slayer, which the Goblins recognise as the name of an adventurer who leaves none alive.
Rabbiteater removes his helmet before the Rolling Rocks tribe, who scream at the sight of a Hobgoblin.
Rabbiteater apologises to the Rolling Rocks in their own tongue, since the Ogres enslaving them are dead.
Rabbiteater points the Rolling Rocks tribe south and west toward the High Passes, and the tribe vanishes that night.
Rabbiteater shows the villagers Goblin ears from a bag of holding, and no one asks how old the ears are.
Rabbiteater tells the Order of Seasons he has vowed never to take off his helmet in a Human town, which is partly true.
Rabbiteater thinks of Numbtongue, Shorthilt and Headscratcher, all gone for months, and never forgets.
Rabbiteater lies that enchanted weapons are dangerous for hunting Goblins, and the Knights read it as bravery.
Rabbiteater keeps hundreds of Goblin ears, many from dead Goblins of Rags's tribe, and the coppers sold for them buy the Flooded Water tribe supplies.
Badarrow tells Rabbiteater that Rags says "good work" and that he may come back if he wants, but Rabbiteater refuses.
Rabbiteater tells Badarrow and Snapjaw he will go north with the Knights, pretending to be the Goblin Slayer, and will not return.
Rabbiteater says he is not strong enough to go back to the inn, and that Greydath was right.
Badarrow and Snapjaw give Rabbiteater a crimson cloak of blood tied to Shorthilt, and Snapjaw gives him a funnel for his arm.
Rabbiteater wears the blood cloak while riding north with the Knights and says it came from a friend.
Rabbiteater asks the Order of Seasons to call him Solstice, and they name him Ser Solstice.
Rabbiteater reaches [Champion Level 28!], gains [Steelcut Sunder], and obtains the [Knight] class at level 2 with [Reinforced Armor (Steel)].
Rabbiteater, as Ser Solstice, has sworn an oath never to reveal his face and to wage a crusade against Goblins.
Rabbiteater dives into the sea in armor to kill a Quillfish because he was hungry, remembering Erin once serving him the fish.
Rabbiteater travels with Talia Kallinad by ship to Pheislant without knowing where they are going.
Rabbiteater tells Talia that nothing is left for him, then that there is nothing he can protect, not yet.
Talia promises Rabbiteater a stay as guest at House Kallinad in Terandria.
Rabbiteater deflects an arrow from an Ailendamus ship with a wooden practice axe on the transport ship.
A Knight of the Spring announces that Ailendamus has crossed Kaliv's border, a month earlier than Grandmaster Calirn predicted.
Ailendamus declares war on the Dawn Concordat and its ships begin to blockade nations such as Pheislant.
Raekea is a Gnoll [Armorer] in Liscor, married to the best Drake [Blacksmith] in the city, and her arms are patterned with burns.
Raekea is a Plains Gnoll of the Silverfang Tribe, and her husband is the Drake Jekss.
Raekea is called the best [Armorer] in Liscor.
Maughin is attracted to Raekea at the forges until Erin whispers that Raekea is married.
Raekea takes Mrsha to the city, saying she will be an honored guest of the Silverfang Tribe at the Meeting of the Tribes.
Raekea says Gnolls thought magic was a curse and hopes Mrsha and another Gnoll [Mage] may weaken that belief.
Raekea says Krshia might ask the Chieftain, her sister, to name Mrsha a Silverfang.
The Council votes 6-0 to authorise Raekea to offer the Dwarf smith Pelt a forge in Liscor.
Raekea says Liscor gets most of its ore cheaply from Esthelm, and that Pelt is interested.
Raekea posts a 272 lb lift on Erin's gym list, claiming one of the higher numbers.
Raelt Leysars is the King of the Realm of Jecrass, a small country north of Hellios and Germina, and is regarded as a decent but unremarkable [King].
Raelt is unmarried, with no title beyond his own name, and raises Jecaina as his daughter.
Raelt dislikes his court, oranges, horses, bells, his River Wardens and war, though Jecrass breeds horses.
Raelt eats a half-rotten orange slice that Geril peeled, because his daughter loves oranges.
Raelt is exactly forty and not young any more, and he exercises in private.
Raelt's father, King Meriden Leysars, was a good, popular [King] who pledged Jecrass as a vassal to Flos and died of heart failure a few years after Flos' slumber.
Raelt's mother passed within a year of Meriden.
Raelt was a young [Prince] enjoying peace in Terandria when his father died, and he took the throne with a new class.
Raelt's half-sister abandoned her royal class for a love-marriage and left her baby, Jecaina, in the palace.
Raelt fought with his father under Flos' banners twice, according to Flos.
Raelt is a Level 26 [King], average and low-level, with higher levels in another class.
Raelt carries an enchanted cup rapier with cutting enchantments and a parrying dagger enchanted with a five-pound [Weight] spell.
Raelt fights as a traditional [Fencer] and taught his daughter to fence.
Raelt wears light, enchanted, flexible leather armour in preference to royal mail.
Raelt's [Duelist] class reaches Level 35 and [Quick Step] changes to [Flash Step] while he is knocked senseless, and he gains [King Level 28].
Raelt gains [Skill - Aura of the Lion] after a thirty-foot fall, at [King Level 28].
Raelt reaches [King Level 30], becomes a [King of Challenges] with [Duelist] removed, and gains [Skill - Army: Flicker Charge] and [Skill - Royal Arms].
Raelt's army glows with [Aura of the Lion] when he leads it.
The world calls Raelt the King of Duels or the Duelist King after his duel with Flos.
Raelt has Geril read the King of Destruction's letter to his court.
Raelt warns Lyfelt that he knew Flos when he was becoming the King of Destruction and says Flos was never one to break his oaths lightly.
Raelt tells Geril that Lyfelt says Reim's worries lie in Pomle's gathering and not in the north.
Raelt stands up to Flos' aura at the parley, pushing back the pressure on Jecrass' forces, and Flos nods to him as one monarch to another.
Raelt tells Flos he is exactly forty.
Afterwards the River Wardens, servants and soldiers look at Raelt with respect and use his full title.
Many young people, mostly men, try to cross Jecrass' borders to join Flos' army.
Raelt watches Wistram rebroadcast Flos killing Manticores in Belchan.
Raelt senses the Empress of Sands' call is more than ordinary, since she gives no titles or name.
Raelt takes the capital of Belchan, whose people open their gates, and tells Orthenon the lands are now formally part of Jecrass.
Raelt tells Orthenon that Jecrass declared war on Belchan because it could not let the slaughter of innocent citizens pass.
Raelt tells Lyfelt his plan is to take Levrhine before it is destroyed, and says he does not intend to fight Flos but to give him what he wants.
Lyfelt begs Raelt, saying Flos will kill him, then weeps.
Raelt tells Geril and General Lael that an army with morale would hurt Flos' army even in defeat, since his strength comes from a few elites.
Raelt tells Flos he will give up Lyfelt to justice but no more, and asks whether Flos will declare war on Jecrass.
Flos invokes ancient custom, as in Hellios when King Treland made war, and Raelt agrees to the duel.
Raelt takes a [Stone Wall] scroll but refuses the [Fireball] scroll, poison and a wand of [Lightning Bolts], saying this is a duel.
Raelt tells Warden Dulfe he is better served without his illusion spells.
Raelt ties a golden bell to his rapier before the duel, which rings as he circles Flos.
Jecaina learns the golden bell belongs to a Level 30 [Duelist] and that her father had earned it.
Raelt rallies Jecrass' cavalry, spears a Rustängmarder through the throat and charges at Flos.
Raelt uses [Flurry Blades] against Orthenon and takes a mortal wound that healing potions save.
Raelt uses [Flash Step] to run up Zamea's axe haft and stabs her in the cheek.
Mars sets Raelt and his horse on fire, and he keeps riding and heals with a potion.
Raelt kills a half-Giant who put up her sword after being surrounded, and it leaves about one twentieth of Reim's fighters dead.
Raelt receives letters from Yisame, Perric and Claiven Earth, and Yisame hires mercenaries, most of whom refuse to fight.
Raelt has over eighty thousand soldiers against a little more than half that for Flos.
Raelt uses [Flicker Charge], [Trick Riders] and [Step of Light] to leap past the Rustängmarder wall with [Flash Step].
Raelt tells Flos he is aware he is alone and would like to finish this, and Flos laughs.
Raelt stabs Flos through the heart, but Flos heals the wound with a potion and survives.
Raelt thinks poison on the rapier would have killed Flos.
Raelt pulls his armies back, cedes the south and west, and asks Flos for his terms of surrender, pausing the war.
Raelt asked Queen Yisame for the rain, and four Scrolls of Weatherchange were used to awe Reim's armies.
Raelt demands a magical war contract from Perric, Yisame and the Speaker of the Trees.
Raelt rebukes Yisame, and she promises Jecrass will not stand alone and then agrees to a treaty.
Raelt tells Yisame, Perric and the Speaker of the Trees that he will sign Reim's contract, and he cuts Perric off.
Raelt says Flos is not a man he loathes, though he hated his strength and tried to kill him twice.
Raelt rides after Perric's adventurers, and stabs the scrying mirror when Perric says Jecaina is across the border.
Raelt challenges Perric to a duel, then frees Jecaina with [Fencer's Lunge], [Royal Arms], [Triple Slash], [Flurry Blades] and [Wind Cutter].
Raelt stays behind and is captured and chained by Perric, leaving Jecaina to rule.
Rafaema is a Wall Lady of Manus, a young-looking Drake with teal scales that shine and flow like water, wings and yellow neck spines.
Rafaema has wings and breathes lightning, and people say her Oldblood manifestation is the strongest in living memory.
Rafaema looks younger than any other Drake at the Manus Security Council by at least a decade, which no one remarks on.
Rafaema has heterochromia, with two differently coloured pupils.
Rafaema is courted by half of Manus' eligible males and swats suitors away each week.
Rafaema says Lady Coloseuvia is a last name she barely remembers.
Rafaema is believed by most people to be a gifted young Drake who is politically kept from the front lines due to a complicated family dynamic.
People in Manus think Rafaema arrived from abroad at about sixteen, with certified ancestry from the original founders of Manus.
Rafaema sits on Manus' Security Council as the youngest member, and the Dragonspeaker asks for her thoughts on whether to reply to the Humans' attack.
Rafaema says that if the Humans attack, Manus should attack back, and this sways the High Command, except Lulv and General Milka.
Rafaema asks whether the first plan of ruination will go forward and then says she forgets which plan that is.
Rafaema recalls that the Witch has not caused major trouble since before she was born, when Luciva raises a Grade 9 threat.
Rafaema tells Luciva that Humans have always been Humans and that the Antinium bother her more because they are new.
Rafaema says that if Manus did not reply, the Humans would get away with it, and asks why Manus would ever allow that.
Rafaema offers condolences to Luciva about Hedica before leaving the room.
Rafaema tells the council that Wyverns and Oldblood Drakes can pool their breath attacks, and that a Manus flying wing used the tactic eighty years ago.
Rafaema says she has read older accounts, and that a Drake riding a Wyvern can combine his attack with the Wyvern's, even with different elements.
Rafaema is secretly a Dragon, a fact known only to a few people such as Manus' inner war council.
Only the Dragonspeaker and a handful of others know of the vault holding the document that says there are only two Dragons left in all of Izril, one of them Rafaema.
The Manus war council knows who Rafaema is and respects her voice, and she is part of their discussions along with Dragonspeaker Luciva.
Rafaema keeps a Drake form through transformation magic, with wings but without concealing her shadow, and has the size of a Drake.
The narration says the Drake cover would continue until Rafaema 'died' or had an accident in her forties, when a new young Drake with different features and backstory would appear.
Rafaema asks her minder Ferris how old she is, and he says she is a hundred and twenty-three.
Rafaema cannot level, which the narration says is just as well, since Dragons able to level would have ruled the world forever.
Rafaema keeps her Dragon's strength, speed and toughness and could throw Ferris a long way.
Rafaema can cast spells as well as many [Mages] and mastered [Detect Lies] long ago.
Rafaema asks Ferris if his books mention Dragonspeaker Telimer, then says it took her four decades to understand why they kept putting her back to sleep.
Rafaema remembers sleeping for seventeen years once and nine years at another time, and her latest slumbers have grown shorter.
Rafaema last napped twenty-seven years ago.
Rafaema did not step outside the keep until she was fifty years old, and then an entire army was set to watch her.
Rafaema threw the worst adolescent tantrum in Manus' history at age eighty, according to the narration.
Rafaema's Dragonspeakers had dealt with her in different ways, and her wrath on finding she had been deceived is written in the history books.
Two earlier minders, Kelis and Amessia, assigned to Rafaema fifty and thirty years ago, nearly caused disaster.
Rafaema spots her new minder, the Gnoll Ferris Thycarl, disguised as a suitor within a second and asks him to speak with her.
Rafaema tells Ferris that the war council plans to seek joint funding from other Walled Cities for operations against the Hives and to investigate Liscor.
Rafaema declares that she wants authority and that she wants the Human Erin Solstice brought to Manus so she can appraise her.
Rafaema tells Ferris that Manus will send Erin an invitation and that he should offer gold, not kidnap her.
Rafaema threatens that her old minder would be sent flying, burnt by lightning, if Ferris refuses, and says she knows where he lives.
Later, Cire is revealed to be a younger Dragon whom Rafaema is thirty years older than.
Cire says he will tell Rafaema something at their next meeting, in two months at Manus, and calls her uptight these days.
Rags is a small Goblin whom Erin Solstice meets at her inn; she is the smallest of the Goblins playing chess there and has already beaten two Antinium Workers back to back.
Rags is the Chieftain of the Flooded Waters Tribe of Goblins who live and die in the area around Liscor.
Rags is a young female Goblin with dark green skin that camouflages her in long grass.
Rags has crimson eyes, as Goblins naturally do.
Rags is short and attractive and just past four years of age, which by Goblin standards makes her about twenty, at least developmentally.
Rags is not a Hob and has not undergone the growth spurt Hobs do, though by Book 7 she has levelled as high as many Hobs.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags answers Erin's offer of a game with an obvious challenge, opening with her knight, which Erin calls the Baltic Opening.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags is one of four Goblins left out of nine who watch from the grass while forty other Goblins surround the inn.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags is nursing bruises and cracked bones from a beating the night before, and holds a dagger as the other Goblins surround Erin's inn.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags and her three Goblins strike the other Goblins from behind, with two holding one down while Rags stabs him in the face.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags and her companions then flank the remaining Goblins, stab one in the back, and retreat until the inn is at their backs.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: After Erin throws a knife into one Goblin and knocks down others, Rags and her Goblins chase the two survivors, and Rags stabs the last held-down Goblin repeatedly in the chest.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags visits Erin's inn often with a small group of Goblins who are almost always injured, and Erin concludes Rags is in command although not in charge of her tribe.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags pays for her followers' meals and her own, eats in silence, plays occasional chess, and watches Erin.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags leads the smaller breakaway faction of her splintered tribe, which does not believe all humans should be eaten on sight, after the Chieftain is killed and the tribe falls into a power struggle.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags knows the Floodplains and is sure that guarding Erin's inn would be a death sentence, so she tries to refuse Erin's offer of weapons and food in exchange for guarding.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags tries speaking Goblin and then Erin's language to Erin without success, and Erin and Rags end up communicating by gesture and sign.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Erin and Rags settle on a deal by which Rags and her Goblins pay several bronze coins per jar of acid.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags sparks a small flame on her fingertip and Pisces identifies it as the very beginning of the [Firefly] spell rather than tribal magic.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags topples a Worker's king with one finger, and plays unusual and daring strategies that Erin admires compared with Pawn's solid, memorised games.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags checkmates Toren effortlessly; asked how many games they played she holds up fingers and Erin reads eighteen, and Rags's grin when asked how many he won implies none.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags arrives at the inn with thirty-odd Goblins following her, leaves five outside as an escort, and has scouts check first that the inn is empty apart from the skeleton and Erin.

section: Chess and first meetings with Erin (Book 1)
text: Rags winces over a huge bruise on her side, judges it not worth a valuable healing potion, and wears cuts on her face and a glowing orange-pink potion on her belt that was probably looted from travellers.

section: Skinner and the fall of Liscor (Book 1)
text: When Liscor is attacked, Rags and her followers flatten themselves in the grass on a hilltop to hide from Skinner's gaze.

section: Skinner and the fall of Liscor (Book 1)
text: Rags decides not to move from the hilltop and watches Liscor fall, calculating.

section: Skinner and the fall of Liscor (Book 1)
text: Rags counts the odds and does not order her tribe down to help the Workers, because the undead are too numerous and Goblins are poor at fighting the dead.

section: Skinner and the fall of Liscor (Book 1)
text: Rags feels a small part of herself hurt over the choice, and a Goblin who wants to descend stops when she glares at him, as she is Chieftain and has decided.

section: Skinner and the fall of Liscor (Book 1)
text: Rags's cold, learned [Tactician] self tells her that the battle is unwinnable, while the frightened Goblin part of her tells her to run.

section: Skinner and the fall of Liscor (Book 1)
text: Rags's Goblins later swarm down a hill and help kill Skinner, with acid jars and fire.

section: Skinner and the fall of Liscor (Book 1)
text: Rags controls a flame spell that burns Skinner, stabs him in the head with a bronze sword that shines like gold, and tosses a jar of acid into his mouth as he dies.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags plays chess with Pawn at the inn and later with Ryoka.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Erin dangles Rags upside down by the ankles and shakes her until she agrees to help rescue Erin's friends, and Rags then vomits in the grass.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Erin reminds Rags that she has fed her, given her a sword and shield, and had Pisces teach her magic.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Pisces, Ryoka and Rags each cast [Light] at the same time.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags stabs a Ghoul in the back of the head during the fight in the ruins.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags takes a broken black crossbow from the ruins and keeps dragging the splinted weapon around.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags throws a jar of acid at Gazi, and an armored foot kicks her off her feet, after which she does not move.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags leads sixty Goblins against a Rock Crab for food in winter, and afterwards has closer to forty, possibly forty-five, Goblins left.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags carries a new, bright, polished bronze shortsword and a small buckler, while her warriors have rusty swords, a dagger, a club and a hatchet.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags knows only three spells, one of which is [Firefly], and uses it from afar while her Goblins keep bears away with arrows and rocks.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags loves chess, has played hundreds of games, gained the [Tactician] class from it, and expects to beat Erin one day.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags remembers Klbkch's death, in which he and a Worker carved through the Goblins who set out to avenge their Chieftain, and finds his revived body unchanged in smell and manner, which terrifies her.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags pulls a small jar of acid from her belt as a warning to Ceria, and has no intention of actually using it.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags remembers that the highest-level [Warrior] Goblin she knew was the old Chief, a Level 18 Hob, and that Goblins older than three years are only Level 9 [Scavenger].

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: At this time Rags has eight levels in [Warrior], the highest in her tribe, a [Mage] class that is almost unique among Goblins, and the [Tactician] class at Level 11.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags has not grown into a Hob despite her levels, and the tribe's single Hob, its former Chief, was killed by Erin.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags relives a memory of the Scale Slayer Tribe fighting a huge slime for thirty minutes in a crack in a mountain in Red Fang territory, which the Goblins call the place of death beyond death.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags has slings adapted from the Red Fang tribe, has six small jars of acid left, and several potions taken from travellers whose effects she does not know.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags obtains the [Leader] class at Level 2 with the Skill [Aura of Command], and the [Tinkerer] class at Level 1 with the Skill [Basic Repair].

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags uses her new Skill to organise her Goblins and move them more quickly, and tests boom bark by throwing a roll of it into a fire, burying the rest as a trap.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags has fourteen crossbows besides her own, and distributes slings and bows among the rest of her tribe.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags does not know how babies are made until Erin explains it during a game, and backs away in horror.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags believes that, unlike other Goblins, she will never die.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags's memories of the Goblin King come only as fragments because her tribe is not large enough to let her focus on them.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags plans to make her tribe's home near the dungeon, partly because the Watch will not patrol that far.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags plays chess against an unseen player on a magical board, loses every game quickly, and sees the pieces form a face with an upside-down smile that she reads as disappointment.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags remembers Relc killing the three Goblins who raised her while she hid in the grass as a child.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags draws her sword on Relc and refuses to be small again, until a Winter Sprite hovering over Relc freezes him and drives him out of the inn.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags attacks the Jawbreaker Tribe, a small tribe that pays tribute to the Red Fang Tribe, and shoots their Hob Chief Rockgaw with a crossbow bolt.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags resolves to build a tribe large enough to kill Relc, oppose the Watch, beat the unknown chess player and finally beat Erin.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Within a week Rags's tribe overruns the Jawbreaker, Sword Taker and Bloody Hand Tribes, then the Gold Stone Tribe, and absorbs their Goblins.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags ambushes the Gold Stone Tribe with hidden Goblins, archers, clay-pellet crossbows and eight Hobs behind her, and an order to her Hob archers wounds their Chieftain with a black crossbow bolt.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags uses horn calls to signal her warriors, heals the Gold Stone Chieftain with a potion, separates children and pregnant females from her new Goblins, and adds archers to her ranks.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags now leads over eight hundred Goblins and twelve Hobs and has levelled several times as [Leader], [Tactician] and [Mage], while her [Warrior] level has not risen.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags carries the bronze shortsword and shield Erin gave her, which are shiny, though she now also has better weapons and armor from conquered tribes.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags rules her tribe by superior intelligence and her black crossbow.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags uses the gem of [Terror] against the Red Fang riders' Carn Wolves, but the Red Fang Chieftain roars and the wolves charge anyway.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: In a few days of fighting the Red Fang Chieftain and sixty riders Rags loses over a hundred Goblins with half again as many wounded, and Goblins, mostly from the Gold Stone Tribe, start deserting.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: A Sword Taker Hob challenges Rags, and she rolls clear and kills him with her crossbow.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags and the Red Fang Chieftain both hear a voice of a thousand lives saying this is Goblin, but Rags also hears a younger King's voice saying this is not who we are, which makes her falter.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags breaks a jar of acid over herself and the Chieftain, heals herself with potions, then pours her last potion over him and says she won.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags becomes leader of the Red Fang Tribe and of all the tribes allied with or subservient to Garen.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags ordered her tribe to kill the Carn Wolf mounts first, so that of the fifty-odd Goblins Garen took to harass her only a little over twenty survived.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags's tribe nears a thousand Goblins and she leads the Flooded Waters Tribe.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags casts [Firefly] at Garen, and he bursts it with a branch and tells her spells can be broken.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags invents stone crossbows that fire clay pellets, which Garen calls too weak, though she values them as weapons for children and noncombatants.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags finds herself looking south more often, missing Erin's inn and the dungeon, and wants Erin's help in making Goblins stronger.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags and Garen disguise themselves as hooded travellers and walk to Erin's inn.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags arrives at the inn with a hooded Hobgoblin, looking a little taller and without fear, and Erin welcomes her and the Hob as guests who will not be attacked.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags is banned from the inn and sits on a hill sulking and adjusting her crossbow.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags leads the burning of Esthelm from the back of a huge Carn Wolf, orders that fleeing Humans be left untouched while those with weapons die, and cannot smile at it.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags was barred from the inn, and she had seen a reflection of herself in the child Mrsha, which confused her.

section: Winter and the Flooded Waters Tribe (Book 2)
text: Rags concludes that Goblins stand alone and orders the Goblins to go north.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: In the snow Ryoka sees a small Goblin riding a wolf among Hobgoblin elites, raising a black crossbow that nearly matches her own size, and recognises Rags.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags's bolt shatters on the magically reinforced carriage but ends the spell hiding it, and Rags's eyes widen as she meets Ryoka's gaze.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: After nearly two weeks of marching Rags wakes on a Carn Wolf in the centre of the coalition army, still full of the Goblin King's fury from a dream.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: On the march Rags levels as a [Warrior] through Garen's training, gains two levels as a [Tactician] and more than ten as a [Leader], and is told her [Leader] class will become a [Chieftain] class unique to Goblins.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags had conquered four tribes: the Rockjaw (she killed its leader), the Still Grass (led by a young Chieftain), the Fire Bite (Hob Chieftain, least loyal) and the Gold Stone.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags trusts the Gold Stone Chieftain because he took the sword stroke meant for her from Garen.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags can recall past events as visions, and finds it easier now that her tribe has grown, though she cannot look back far.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags realises that Garen has taken effective command of the coalition from her, and that he only pretended to be under her command because it was convenient.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: At the feast Rags climbs on the table and kicks a Hob sitting by Tremborag, saying she is Chieftain and this is her seat.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Only the Gold Stone Chieftain, the Still Grass Chieftain and three Hobs stand for Rags, until Garen declares her his Chieftain, knocks down the Hob, and holds her chair.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags tells the Gold Stone Chieftain privately that the place is not Goblin and Tremborag's people are not Goblin, but she is.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags learned the fundamentals of magic from Pisces, and when Ulvama pokes between her legs and urges her to sleep with Garen and others she slaps her hand away and kicks her in the stomach.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags has no interest in sex and says so, holding a hand on her sword with [Firefly] burning in her hand against Ulvama's magic.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Tremborag greets her as "Fake Name Goblin", at which Goblins around the room laugh.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags sweeps aside Tremborag's plan to attack the town from every side and plans feints on the gates and the west wall while the east is struck by the main force.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags has sent the Gold Stone Chieftain, with others, to attack Tremborag's Goblins as she declares war.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags wonders what she would do if one of the captured women were Erin and then sees Erin's face on each captive.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags names Pyrite after the gold-like stones that Goblins value as an alternative to flint and steel.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags takes her sword, crossbow and dented buckler, which Erin gave her, and walks into the mess hall; the Redfang tribe recognises her as their former Chieftain.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: In Goblin, Rags declares herself Chieftain of the Flooded Water Tribe, says "I am Goblin. This place is not." and calls on Goblins to follow her, a declaration of war.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags's breakout raid takes weapons from Tremborag's armory, frees hundreds of Human women with Pyrite, and takes the Redfang warriors and their wolves, with the Redfangs covering the retreat.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags had planned the breakout herself as a raid to break away from Tremborag, and now leads a bigger tribe than before.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags eats three bowls of porridge with cinnamon, butter and sugar from stolen stores.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags still has the gem of [Terror], which is ineffective against Goblins.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags lets the freed women go at a Human city and tells their adventurer leader that Tremborag fought alongside the Goblin King and that the Goblin Lord lies south.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags lets the Humans conclude that Tremborag and the Goblin Lord will join forces.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags names the scarred Redfang elite Redscar and the old Goblin Whitebeard, later renamed Greybeard.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags relives a Biting Blade Hob Chieftain's memory of facing the silver-armored [Knight] Yaltes Byres, and concludes that the lance makes mounted warriors deadly.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags has her carpenters make twenty-foot pikes, each carried by two to four Goblins.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: In a mock battle the pike wall routs sixty Redfang elites on foot, but the Redfang wolf riders win by charging the side, so Rags aims to train multiple pike groups.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags expects that pikes can be countered by shooting the pike holders, using magic against them, or sending infantry at them.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags becomes a [Chieftain] at Level 15, her [Tactician] reaches Level 16, [Scavenger] and [Tinkerer] are consolidated away, and she gains [Skill - Tribe: Fleet Foot] and [Skill - Lesser Tinkering].

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: The Flooded Waters tribe celebrates her level-up, which Rags considers more special than a birthday.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags finds that only five of her captured weapons are truly powerful: an unbreakable flower shield, a shocking sword, a fire-throwing sword, a sledgehammer-weight mace and a chest plate that fractures non-magical weapons.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags gives the shocking sword and chest plate to Redscar, the shield to Pyrite, who declined the mace and sword, and a mace to one of her Hobs, and withholds the fire sword.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags blames herself for the Goblins who died after she wanted to prove herself a warrior, and resolves that a Chieftain must also be strong.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags ambushes a thirty-wagon caravan bound for Ostegrast, tells the guards to leave their wagons and run, and kills only five Humans who resisted.

section: The march north and the mountain (Books 3-4)
text: Rags decides to head south to fight the Goblin Lord and make a base near Liscor, and wants to talk to the innkeeper.
Rags has brought organisation and systems to her tribe, including daily work rosters and rotating duty, and taught Goblins to make crossbows and use twenty-foot pikes.
Goblins in Rags's tribe are growing smarter by copying her, since a Goblin tribe is moulded after its Chieftain.
Pyrite does not know Rags's age, and wonders why she has not become a Hob, since Hobs can match average Silver-rank adventurers.
Rags's common tongue is far better than before, though she still pronounces words with difficulty.
Rags uses her [Fleet Foot] Skill to shorten marches, and carries a huge black crossbow of Dwarf-made quality that other Goblins can only copy.
Rags has a soft spot for Humans, has freed those held in Tremborag's mountain, and is rumored to have met a strange Human near Liscor who fed Goblins and Rags.
Rags sets fire to a tree trunk carved with words about what happens to Goblins by glowing her hand against it.
After the Undercrawler Tribe's massacre by adventurers, Rags decides to attack a nearby Human town, breaking her policy of non-violence toward Humans.
Rags's tribe takes the town with crossbows, a pike wall, a battering ram built at her order and Noears's lightning.
Rags has the dead Humans hanged from the rooftops, lets the Goblins loot for an hour, spares all living townsfolk, and forbids the Goblins to touch them.
Rags has the Goblins build a fort of four twenty-foot wooden walls, orders them not to run, and has trees pre-sawn so they can be toppled on the Rose Knights.
Greydath reveals himself as a Goblin Lord of past years, and when Rags asks if she is worthy he answers No, telling her she is too young, small and weak, and most of all not enough.
Rags says "Not yet" bitterly, and none of the other Goblins can look her in the eye save Pyrite.
Rags leads about forty Goblins, nearly a third of them Hobs, in flight from a thousand Humans, using [Firefly] and [Fire Arrow] to stall them and a black crossbow to shoot a rider's mount.
Rags is Level 19 [Chieftain], Level 13 [Mage], Level 18 [Tactician] and Level 11 [Warrior], having started as a Level 2 [Backstabber] and Level 5 [Scavenger] hiding in the grass around Liscor.
Rags's Skill [Fleet Foot] affects her whole tribe and lets them cover far more ground.
Rags's tribe is made of separate groups that lack unity, and some of the former Tremborag Goblins, the male ones, still regard rape and torture of Humans as acceptable.
Rags can cast [Firefly] and the [Fire Arrow] that Noears taught her, and fails to produce [Lightning Bolt], finding lightning less intuitive than fire.
Rags asks Pyrite for the ruby from three gems and he gives it to her, and she finds it holds magic.
Rags refuses mercy to the Humans, telling Kerrig and Welca that Humans kill Goblins and do not leave them alone, and that the Humans started it.
At a crossroads Rags and Pyrite decide to go south, since Liscor is not a Human place, and to watch the Human who stayed rather than let him run.
Rags has uneasy memories of Erin's inn, Erin's face on the dead, a voice greeting her in the inn, and fragments of what she wants to say, ending in "Thank you".
Rags reaches Level 20 [Chieftain] and gains [Skill - Tribe: Scavenger Armor].
Rags feels the Goblin Lord nearby, and the hunting Humans, and fears something is coming.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags's new Skill [Scavenger Armor] makes the tribe's [Hammerers] turn out crude armor from bark, cloth, leather and scrap.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags has nightmares about dead Humans, and tells Poisonbite that Goblins are not Humans and can be better.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags rides a large wolf and aims her black crossbow at Bethal, then spares her because her fear recalls Erin's look, and declares Bethal a prisoner.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags casts [Light] to see the smoke drifting through her camp.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: An armored rider cuts Rags across the chest, whispering "So small", and she lies down without reaching for her potion, until Pyrite pours a healing potion down her throat and finds her barely alive.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags wakes in a wagon after three days, and Pyrite stands bloodied and says "Yes, Chieftain".

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags takes Lancrel with Hobs hurling Goblins onto the walls, Noears's lightning, Redscar on the battlements, a ram on the gates, and Pyrite leading the charge in.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags uses her wounded Goblins' crossbows in volleys against the walls to break the enemy riders.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags holds a [Fear] gem that shows Skinner to Wiskeria and breaks the Darksky riders' horses, then shows Redscar that it has stopped working.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags orders the Redfangs to burn the villages, towns and fields with no Humans spared, says "They started it", and shoots fire onto a farm roof herself while screaming.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags leads about forty Redfang warriors in ambushes, uses trip ropes that kill the riders pursuing, and raises the [Fear] gem, which works a bit less each time.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags has under four hundred Redfang riders, and spreads them thin with suicidal diversions.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: When the first boulder breaks part of the wall, Rags announces she has a plan.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags sends Redscar for nails, Quietstab for wood, Poisonbite for stones, and Pyrite to wait for a signal, and sends Hobs out to fell a tree.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags's first copied trebuchet collapses, but a later one fires a stone that lands short of the Human camp.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags offers Kerrig peace, pointing to the Goblins' trebuchets as proof of power and gold from Pyrite's sack, and says the Goblins will keep the know-how to build them.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags demands a truth spell and a talk with the Emperor, even by shouting from far away, and says the Goblins did not start the fight.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags leads sixty Carn Wolf riders towards a village, helped by her Skill [Fleet Foot] to rest her warriors while running.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags spots the Emperor in the crowd, the only one not looking at her, his eyes closed and head turned east.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags offers the Emperor peace if his army leaves the city and she takes hers away, gives no proof, and offers a one-hour standoff while his message goes out.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags spits at Tyrion, and Lord Pellmia's sword flicks the spit away.

section: Lancrel and the war with the Unseen Empire (Book 8)
text: Rags reaches Level 24 [Chieftain] and gains [Skill - Tribe: Rapid Reload], [Skill - Flashfire Spellcraft] and [Spell - Burning Blades].

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Rags's Skill [Rapid Reload] speeds her tribe's crossbows, [Flashfire Spellcraft] lets her shape fire and fire an oversized [Fire Arrow], and [Burning Blades] sets her sword aflame for about three minutes.

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Rags has [Fleet Foot] to move her tribe quickly.

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Rags reaches Level 25 [Chieftain].

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Rags tells Pyrite of meeting Laken Godart, who told her he could not make peace because she had killed his people, and was sad and angry.

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Rags says "They started it", and tries to work out why the words sound wrong.

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Rags holds Gilam under her crossbow, recalls Relc humming while cutting off her family's heads, and lowers it when Pellmia arrives, though no Goblin fires.

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Gilam says the Goblins stole his horse Olli and his gear.

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Rags jumps on a tired Hob's stomach, mocks him until he gives his club to Noears's bag of holding, and has other Hobs do the same, then jogs ahead until the whole tribe follows.

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Rags's tribe has a shared Skill that keeps it ahead of the pursuing Humans at a jog, and other Goblins do not have it.

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Rags senses a fire to the north, which Pyrite feels as bright light and Redscar as a mountain, and sees the Goblin Lord's black-armored army approaching.

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Rags runs at the head of a hundred thousand Goblins, with her tribe at the front of the column.

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Rags forbids even Redfangs to enter her camp, saying they might be spies.

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Rags accuses Tremborag's tribe of kidnapping and raping Human women as not-Goblin, Tremborag laughs and says they are only Humans, and Garen answers "It is Tremborag's tribe. He decides."

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Rags tells Reiss that she is not his or the Necromancer's tool, but agrees that they will talk again since Humans are the danger.

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
text: Redscar shouts "Rags!", the Redfangs and then her whole tribe take up the chant, drowning out Garen's camp.

section: Flight and the Goblin Lord's army (Book 9)
