Rievan seems to have it out for Ceria, who suspects he is a Human from Terandria who dislikes half-Elves.
Rievan snaps at Ceria that her [Ice Shard] mixes the cold and water aspects and that she freezes water instead of forming a shape and solidifying it.
Rievan evaporates Ceria's [Ice Shard] with heat from his hand.
Rievan has taught the whole class [Electric Jolt], but insists anyone who knows a higher-Tier spell practice that instead.
Rievan expects Pisces to make a mistake with his [Electric Jolt], but nods with a hint of respect at the immaculate control.
Rievan tells the class to emulate Pisces's way of diverting the whole spell into his other palm.
Rievan asks Pisces to repeat his statement on the dangers of mana overabundance.
Rievan stares hard as Pisces gives a perfect summary of the previous day's lesson, then grudgingly says "Very good".
Rievan scolds a student named Elkrin for an abysmal [Fire Orb] and tells Ceria to attend to detail.
Rima is one of the Players of Celum, a troupe of [Actors], and is described as dark-skinned and deep-voiced.
Rima left her job to join the Players, as acting stole Wesle, Kilkran, Pralcem, Rima and others from theirs.
Rima is an [Actress] and one of the first [Actors], part of the Players' leadership with Jasi.
Rima was arrested as a [Thief] once.
Temile says he and two of the old crew, Damius and Rima, stayed behind with some new recruits when the Players left for the north.
Rima gives Jasi her view of the new recruits and says they need a week, as they are still a bit raw.
Rima and Jasi walk through a city together, and Rima gawks at buildings that are a precursor to skyscrapers.
Rima envies Jasi's Skill that summons five gold pieces' worth of performance supplies.
Rima frets about competing entertainments, and Kilkran tells her to relax because the Players have done well so far.
Rima appears in the play alongside Wesle, Pralcem, Jasi, Chellise and Medel, the troupe's best.
Rose is an Earther from California who was transported to this world and later stays at The Wandering Inn with six other Earthers.
In the Earthers' group chat, Rose says she is alone in a forest in the middle of nowhere and has seen only monsters.
Rose says she is from California.
Rose says that she has been in this world only one day, and that she is flipping out.
In Invrisil, Rose finds Kevin begging and snaps at the group for gathering instead of looking for jobs, since they have run out of money.
Rose blames herself partly for tipping their [Wagon Driver] and escorts, though she says everyone mismanaged the coin.
One of the group says he sold his sword for a good price.
Rose is told they cannot afford a play, and that Ryoka took their electronics and left them in the city.
Maviola El sees the despairing Earthers and offers to treat them to a meal at an inn.
Seven Earthers have stayed at The Wandering Inn for roughly a week, and Rose is one of them.
A young man from Spain growls at Rose over breakfast while drinking a morning cup of gin and blue fruit juice.
Rose pitches an all-male version of Romeo and Juliet, called Romeo and Romeo, to Temile of the Players of Celum.
A crowd in the inn shouts "Disgusting" at the idea, and a Drake woman angrily accuses Rose of something called Turnscales and punches her.
Rose finds she stands alone against the crowd, and Onieva wants to protect her until Erin stomps her foot.
Rufelt is a City Gnoll with dark, near-black fur streaked a bit with grey, and he works as a [Bartender].
Rufelt introduces himself to Erin as 'City Gnoll', and co-owns the Pallass bar Tails and Scales with his wife Lasica, a Drake who runs the kitchen.
Tails and Scales is a large tavern just off the main stairwell on the fifth floor of Pallass.
Rufelt says that he is reasonably high-level.
Rufelt has an advanced version of the [Bartender] class, and can make drinks with effects.
Rufelt has the Skill [Immunity: Alcohol], though two shots of a black Dwarf spirit still knock him off balance.
Rufelt's Skill [Bar: Selective Admission] can keep anyone below his level from casually walking into his bar.
Rufelt did a few years in Zeres, which allows in Pirates who have paid off their bounty under Drake law.
Rufelt says City Gnolls do not bow to tribe loyalty, and are free rather than born into a family of hundreds.
Rufelt calls the Plains Gnoll view of City Gnolls that of a domesticated fool without tribe or loyalty.
Rufelt cautions Erin not to rush rare ingredients, saying he and Lasica once sold for far too little.
Rufelt tells Erin to cultivate signature dishes, saying he and Lasica boast the widest variety in Pallass thanks to Balerosian ingredients.
Rufelt says an [Innkeeper] is a generalist class and that he can make better alcohol, including drinks that cheer, energise or knock out.
Rufelt tells Erin that he and Lasica could have been affiliated with a large Gnoll tribe if they had not let the chance slip.
Rufelt warns Erin not to mention Skills, saying he and Lasica could have been the wrong couple to tell.
Rufelt serves Erin a drink of floating Dwarfrain liquor, which rises toward her lips.
Rufelt says he and Lasica back the Unitail group and [Senators], and mixes blue fruit juice with rum, chilled with [Chill Paws].
Rufelt serves Pisces an amber drink with a green energy mix, based on a stamina potion recipe he worked out with Xif.
Rufelt and Lasica dance to an invisible cello at The Wandering Inn, and the other guests pair off to follow them.
Rufelt agrees to look at fertility spells and talk about it when Lasica has not had four drinks.
Rufelt takes offence at a hooded Drake who suggests adoption, and later guesses the Drake has a child, because he sounded like a father.
Rufelt knows Hawk as a customer at Tails and Scales, and says Lasica has done carrot dishes for him.
Rufelt thinks Hawk lays off the carrots when he likes someone, to find a Drake date who will eat them.
Rufelt and Lasica bail Erin out of jail with Chaldion and Saliss, and Rufelt is amused.
Rufelt stops making a molotov and presses Lasica down, refusing her alcohol until Erin guesses the reason.
Rufelt provides the drinks at a get-together while Lasica sits with a juice, and blushes when Erin congratulates them.
Erin says Rufelt told her Gnolls have no problem with chocolate, which Mrsha jokes about by pretending to choke.
Rufelt is overprotective of Lasica during her pregnancy, and keeps trying to do her work in the kitchen.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka Griffin is a Runner who runs barefoot, and she says she was born in New York, which she calls the greatest city in the world.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka dislikes her own name and enjoys running more than talking to people; her listed hobbies include not mentioning her name, running, hunting and drinking coffee.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka knows she is in another world and has no way to get back.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka calls herself a girl from Wisconsin and a college freshman, and says she found herself in this world while out on a run, carrying her iPhone, her wallet and her watch.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka says she looks Asian and so stands out in a world where few people have skin darker than tan.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka won a track-and-field scholarship, which she cites as why she outpaces the local Runners.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka has been in the world only about a week and a half, though it feels much longer to her.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka's left ear has been torn at some point in the past; the lower part of the earlobe is missing and the rest healed jaggedly around the gap.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka has Japanese grandparents and describes her heritage as Japanese-American; her grandparents wanted her to appreciate tea, but her American side insists on coffee, which she has not yet found in this world.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka describes her Japanese side as half of her heritage.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka reflects that she was accepted to Columbia University on a Track and Field scholarship for the 400-meter run, with a 3.89 GPA, but never set foot on campus.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka lists among her past interests hunting, sports shooting, reading, Youtube videos and video games, and she has not chosen a major.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka thinks of herself as an unfriendly daughter who does not like her dad, holds a 4th Dan in Muay Thai though she prefers Parkour, refused Mensa membership and was kicked out of two high schools.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka loves running music, favouring rock and disliking pop, techno and opera; her favourite artists include Meatloaf, Imagine Dragons, Fueled by Ramen, Lady Gaga and Five for Fighting.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka's iPhone 4 is black, holds 32 GB that is almost entirely music, and has no password lock, only a few books, saved files and an empty contact list besides.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka listens to "Heathens" by twenty one pilots while running, and notes that Suicide Squad, the film it was written for, came out a month before she came to this world and that she never saw it.

section: Background and arrival in the world
text: Ryoka says that thinking of the world she came from hurts, but like a thorn pulled from her foot long ago.

section: Running for the Runner's Guild in Celum and Wales
text: Ryoka runs barefoot because she is slower in shoes, and Garia, hearing this, asks whether a [Barefoot Runner] class is better than a [Messenger] class.

section: Running for the Runner's Guild in Celum and Wales
text: Ryoka earned over thirty silver in one day as a City Runner, much of it from the Magnolia request, and decides to pay three silver for bed and board at an inn.

section: Running for the Runner's Guild in Celum and Wales
text: Ryoka's first priority is to save enough to buy a good healing potion for emergencies, and she also wants enchanted equipment such as other Runners carry.

section: Running for the Runner's Guild in Celum and Wales
text: Ryoka blocks out the system messages about a [Barefoot Runner] class and a skill each night before sleeping, and hates having to do so.

section: Running for the Runner's Guild in Celum and Wales
text: Ryoka delivers fifteen healing potions and five mana potions to the vice-captain of the Hammers of Hammerad, who pays with a silver and copper seal showing a hammer standing on a mountain.

section: Running for the Runner's Guild in Celum and Wales
text: Garia says Ryoka is the fastest City Runner and that even Fals cannot beat her time.

section: Running for the Runner's Guild in Celum and Wales
text: Ryoka left the city of Wales when she set out on the run that brought her to Magnolia, and she notes it shares its name with a country on Earth.

section: Running for the Runner's Guild in Celum and Wales
text: Ryoka bought a history book in the Celum market; she learns books can cost several gold coins, though some sell for silver, and there is no library in Celum so she must buy what she reads.

section: Running for the Runner's Guild in Celum and Wales
text: Ryoka agrees to carry a fifty-pound delivery with Garia the next day, though she expects Garia to talk throughout.
Ryoka tells Magnolia she has had ice cream before, and that it is common in her home country; Magnolia, who senses lies, judges her to be telling the truth.
Magnolia says the ice cream before them cost seventy gold coins to ship across the sea, while Ryoka compares it with a tub she could buy for three dollars.
Ryoka offers to show Magnolia how to make ice cream.
Ryoka makes ice cream by heating milk, salt and sugar in a large pot into a custard flavoured with the beans of one vanilla stalk, which must then be frozen slowly while stirred.
Magnolia has her maid Yvony ask the Mage's Guild for an [Elementalist] with basic ice magic to do the freezing, and the mage churns the ice cream.
Ryoka concludes that Magnolia is the scariest person she has met in this world, since someone with her class can practically read minds.
Ryoka's leg is injured and a week has passed since her "accident"; she swears vengeance on the Street Runners.
Ryoka hates the inn and the entire world in her pain, and wants to find a way to heal her leg.
Persua says no one helped Ryoka until she dragged herself to the nearest guardhouse after the runaway cart hit her.
Ryoka's right leg is a mass of crushed and splintered bone that cannot reattach by itself, and the healers told her the choice was amputation or a spell she could not afford.
Ryoka keeps the leg on with enchanted bandages, about ten gold coins and more expensive than healing potions, plus a healing potion every few hours; she cannot feel anything below the knee.
Ryoka has three healing potions left, enough for a day or two, and tells Magnolia she has used forty or fifty.
The only thing Ryoka says she really owns from her own world is a dead device with earbuds attached, useless without electricity.
Ryoka bargains with Magnolia over how many questions she will answer for her help, starting at twenty, moving to forty, and refusing unlimited answers.
Ryoka believes Magnolia can read minds or sense untruths, and that unlimited questions would eventually give her the whole truth.
Ryoka fears that answering questions would expose Earth technology such as gunpowder, firearms, germ warfare and nuclear weapons, and that the secret would spread even if she trusted Magnolia.

section: Healed by the Horns of Hammerad
text: Ryoka's bone is made whole after the Horns of Hammerad's help, and instead of lashing out she bows her head to Ceria and thanks her repeatedly.

section: Healed by the Horns of Hammerad
text: Ryoka says she once swore never to perform a dogeza for anyone, and she performs one now only in her mind and soul to thank those who gave her back her legs.

section: Healed by the Horns of Hammerad
text: Ryoka tells Calruz she is grateful, apologises for her earlier rudeness, shakes hands with him and the other Horns, and names honor as what defines them.

section: Healed by the Horns of Hammerad
text: Ryoka introduces herself to the Horns, says she is in their debt, and offers her help whenever they need it.

section: Healed by the Horns of Hammerad
text: Ryoka tests her healed leg with spins, kicks, cartwheels, back handsprings and front flips, and denies having the [Performer] class, saying she simply has skill.

section: Healed by the Horns of Hammerad
text: Ryoka runs back toward Celum, over a hundred miles away, and leaves Calruz behind after ten steps.

section: Healed by the Horns of Hammerad
text: Ryoka runs a record thirty-mile marathon at top speed right after the cure and collapses; the Horns find her with locating spells from Ceria and carry her back on the cart.

section: Healed by the Horns of Hammerad
text: Ryoka rests two days on Ceria's word, and is penniless, living on help from Garia and the Horns.

section: Healed by the Horns of Hammerad
text: A mage repairs Ryoka's iPhone with a [Repair] spell, and the screen shows 100 percent charge.

section: Healed by the Horns of Hammerad
text: Ryoka runs out of Celum to "Sweet Home Alabama" and then, on shuffle, "I Will Not Bow" by Breaking Benjamin, which makes her run faster than before.
Ryoka has bright green eyes and calls herself a barefoot runner who does not care what people think.
Ryoka thinks this is an era of peace, with the great wars, gods and legends long past, and wants to see what wonders remain.
Ryoka takes the High Passes request from the bottom of the board and walks out of the Runner's Guild amid shouts of fury.
Ryoka kills a Goblin with a kick to the head, her first kill, and is shaken because she has never killed a creature before.
Ryoka drinks two potions that are not healing potions and suffers mana poisoning, and an elderly man in a cave tends to her.
Ryoka delivers a package to the cave's occupant with the word "Delivery." and collapses unconscious.
Ryoka believes she could beat most adventurers below Gold-rank in a fight, since they are human or humanoid and martial arts does not exist in this world as far as she knows.
Ryoka tells the pointed-eared mage in the cave that she stopped herself from leveling and has no class, so he cannot see one.

Ryoka says she dislikes being controlled, that she thinks classes and levels are a way for the world or some system to control people, and that levelling feels like cheating; she says she can cancel a level-up by thinking hard enough.
Ryoka stands six foot one, a few inches shorter than the tall mage she faces.
Ryoka tells the mage she was born in Oakland, California, in America, a place he does not recognise.
Ryoka's name is Japanese; her U.S. birth certificate shows the English reading, but the name given to her is written 涼香 in kanji.
The mage tells Ryoka that three Runners have already died trying to reach his home.

The mage pays Ryoka a bag of gold for the delivery and arriving injured, gives her a speed potion, warns her not to drink it all at once, and tells her not to wear a ring or open a letter he hands her or she will suffer.
Ryoka senses that the silver and onyx ring she is given is magic, as it feels warm and shines from within.
The mage tells Ryoka her mana poisoning came from confusing mana potions with health potions, and Ryoka recalls that she thought Ceria had given her the right potions.
Ryoka arrives in Celum, teleported too high above the city, and plummets from roof height; Teriarch watches it in his magical view.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Garia says Ryoka is the only Runner to survive the High Passes in years, and without a scratch.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka brawls with the adventurer Arnel in the inn, using Muay Thai kicks and a sweep, until Garia punches him unconscious.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka tells Garia that Muay Thai is not a Skill but something she learned as a kid, and that Garia could learn it too.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka packs her clothes, money, iPhone and books into her Runner's pack, having sold the books she had read, and leaves her room at night through the window.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka lands a low kick on the leg of the [Assassin] Theofore and escapes across rooftops using parkour, making a rude gesture as she goes.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka runs through the night to the Adventurer's Guild in Esthelm and asks Ceria to teach her magic.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka tells Ceria that magic was not widely practiced where she comes from and that it simply interests her, along with defending herself.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka sees Ceria's wand trace a rune in three dimensions and feels a spell word, then casts [Light] herself, producing an orb that shifts through colors.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka's [Light] spell runs out when she uses all her mana, leaving her light-headed, and Ceria is struck at how quickly she altered a basic [Light] spell.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka eats a hunk of cheese, half a loaf of bread, meat and a stick of butter in sandwiches after her first spell; Ceria says being ravenous is normal for new casters.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka tells Ceria and the Horns that the contact she met in the High Passes was "No one special", and plays the Runner's confidentiality card to avoid more questions.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka privately thinks of the mage as "the mystery possibly-elf archmage Teriarch".

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka is tugged by a spell to deliver the ring and letter she left in her pack in Ceria's room.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka thinks she and Ceria would attract attention anywhere, as she has bare feet, is taller than many men, looks Asian, and Esthelm is a very Anglo-Saxon place.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka says she hates talking to people in groups but is fine with individuals such as Ceria, Garia and Sostrom.

section: Return to Celum, the brawl and Esthelm
text: Ryoka ran over sixty miles the night before to reach Esthelm, and then, tired and cranky, sets out to challenge Yvlon to a spar and Calruz to a fight.

section: The Esthelm spars and the break with the Horns
text: Ryoka tells Yvlon she practises Mixed Martial Arts and Muay Thai, and treats the spar like an MMA fight although she has never been in one herself and only practised in case her parents allowed her to fight in the ring.

section: The Esthelm spars and the break with the Horns
text: Ryoka does a full five minutes of stretches before the spar, from toe touches to hip rotations, while a crowd of adventurers, street vendors and pedestrians gathers and starts betting.

section: The Esthelm spars and the break with the Horns
text: In the spar Ryoka trips Yvlon, throws her again with an elbow over her knee, pins her arm and lands three punches before Yvlon catches the third and calls the fight over.

section: The Esthelm spars and the break with the Horns
text: Ryoka fights Calruz next, landing a spinning back kick and a roundhouse to his face and hammering his legs and stomach until he punches her.

section: The Esthelm spars and the break with the Horns
text: Ryoka tells the Horns that she survived the High Passes without a single level and that they would not whine about unexplored ruins if they had guts.

section: The Esthelm spars and the break with the Horns
text: Yvlon asks whether Ryoka has no levels or classes at all, Ryoka answers "Not one", and Cervial confirms with [Appraisal] that he cannot see her Level or Class, so the adventurers learn she is unleveled.

section: The Esthelm spars and the break with the Horns
text: On impulse Ryoka brushes Ceria's chin with a blow that makes the half-elf stagger and sit down.

section: The Esthelm spars and the break with the Horns
text: Ryoka feels the same snapping inside her that she felt when she was kicked out of school, and tells herself she is a girl who destroys everything and picks fights with friends.

section: The Esthelm spars and the break with the Horns
text: Yvlon's punch lifts Ryoka off her feet and her body shuts down.

section: The Esthelm spars and the break with the Horns
text: Ryoka leaves the Adventurer's Guild running toward Liscor and the Blood Plains without a plan, ignoring a carriage and the [Maids] and [Assassins] who block her way.
Ryoka kicks a Goblin girl's shield hard enough to send her across the ground and escapes with the ring, letter, money and potions strapped to her rucksack.

Ryoka's pack holds three healing potions, a ruby ring, a letter, dry rations, two water flasks, spare clothes, soap, a toothbrush, salt, a small lantern, her iPhone and headphones, a wool blanket and a pouch of gold.
Ryoka reflects that she has been in trouble many times, waiting in rooms for her parents to talk with teachers or police, and that what she did to the Horns was different and wrong.
Ryoka decides it is better to die an idiot than a slave, then admits she has hurt the people who were kind to her and cut herself off from adventurers, Magnolia and the Runner's Guild.
Ryoka thinks of herself as flawed by perfection, with high test scores and martial arts trained from choice rather than need, a hollow person with nothing that defines her.
Ryoka thinks she has been an outsider since birth, since other children could not see past the color of her skin or her top marks.
Ryoka writes out a program-style description of how bullies behave toward a resisting victim and concludes bullying is a group dynamic, which fuels her anger at them.
Ryoka hits shuffle and skips "Centuries" by Fall Out Boy for "Counting Stars" and then "Apologize", feeling the guilt of the last lyric.

Ryoka's dream is to climb the highest mountains, sail ocean storms and see what the world offers, alone and free; she accepts she may eventually die doing so, and says what she wants is "A place to die".
Ryoka realizes what she lacks is a friend, regrets running from Ceria, and kneels to pray for the first time in a long while, begging not to die alone and without a single friend.
Ryoka resists Teriarch's compulsion to turn back and deliver the message, stepping forward through burning runes on her arms until the pain stops and something in her breaks.
Ryoka wakes after four days to the notice [Skill - Indomitable Will Learned.], cancels it as meaningless, and runs north toward Liscor.
On her second day Ryoka finds six Gnoll warriors stripped of their gear and stabbed repeatedly, freshly dead, and runs on without knowing she is watched.
On the night of the second day Ryoka finds eight Gnoll warriors lying dead, each beheaded by a single slash.
On the third day Ryoka meets a smiling adventurer with a large eye and a curved sword who knows her name, says nothing, and wonders if the woman killed the Gnolls.
On the fourth day Ryoka returns to Liscor, asks about Ceria, Calruz, Gerial and Sostrom, and feels the world drop away at what she hears.
Ryoka sits beside Yvlon, whose eyes are blank, and then walks out to the Ruins, where twenty giant ant-men blockade the entrance behind a wall of dirt.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka reaches Erin's inn near Liscor, puts a hand on the door, hesitates because her heart still hurts too much for company, and turns away.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka turns on her iPhone, begins to jog, and answers when it starts ringing.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka uses the chat handle [batman] on the call, posting as a troll claiming to be a [Dark Avenger] of level 999999 and later giving mock instructions to "exit the simulation".

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka admits she played [batman] herself, drawing on Youtube comments to pass as an egotistical thirteen-year-old, though she thinks she gave herself away at the end.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka thinks the caller using the name Kent Scott was not from Earth and was fishing for names, and that Teriarch's teaching told her he was using a [Scrying] spell.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka wonders if the people on the call were summoned as an accidental side effect of a spell for [Hero] classes, and notes a Level 26 [Knight] who arrived a month or two ago had leveled past Calruz at about Level 22.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka returns to the inn about fifteen minutes after nearly leaving it behind, in despair and full of anger.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka has a single spell, [Light], which she casts in the dark inn.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka has been living off water and dry rations for about eight days, and she still has several gold coins in her Runner's pack.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka thinks that Erin, hovering over her, is annoying and that tossing the juice in her face would be easy, yet she describes a thin red line keeping her from madness.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka believes the Horns of Hammerad are dead and that it is not her fault since they died days before she neared Liscor, though it hurts more than anything in years.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka tells Erin she is a City Runner, not a Street Runner, and her left eye twitches at the comparison.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka recalls eating ice cream with Magnolia while comparing it to Erin's juice.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka tells Erin she has dodged spells from a Lich while delivering healing potions to the Horns, among the dumbest things she has done.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka tells Erin she once had her leg shattered, and the scars are now invisible thanks to magic.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka tells Erin that the High Passes are the other gateway to the southern part of the continent.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka laughs at Erin's stories of Calruz, learns the Horns stayed at the inn the night before they died, and feels better for staying.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka decides she must run north to Celum to talk to someone and do something at once.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka has red earbuds for her iPhone.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka tells Erin she comes from Ohio and arrived in the year 2016, around October.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka realizes there must be many more people from Earth in this world than the sixteen on the call, possibly hundreds or thousands.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka imagines Celum overrun by Earth's modern military and colonial powers, a gateway that could open both ways.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka recognises the glowing spell that appears around Pisces' head and sits down on the stairs, drained.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka was taught by her father to look people in the eye, speak clearly and lie through her teeth when needed.

section: The Call and meeting Erin Solstice
text: Ryoka read in a book that Antinium have no names except the Prognugator and the Queens, which puzzles her after she meets two named Antinium.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka tells Krshia that she found a group of dead Gnolls about forty miles from Liscor, killed by something that cut them apart, and that minutes later she met a woman with a large eye named Gazi.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka, Pisces and Rags each cast [Light] at the same moment, producing three orbs.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka freezes and cannot fight a zombie because it is a dead human come back to life, until Erin smashes it with a frying pan.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka says she has taken martial arts lessons since she was eight and has been in countless fights, but could not bring herself to kill that zombie.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka remembers the Goblin she kicked long ago and the way his neck crunched.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka suggests to Pisces that undead bears, spiders, mice or birds could be raised, and could even serve as spies.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka tells Erin her parents were pretty rich and that she was about to start college when she vanished, having taken several gap years from high school.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka tells Erin she had the opportunity to take a class but refused, since leveling and gaining Skills seemed too much like a game.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka sees her iPhone at 24 percent and thinks Sostrom's [Repair] spell restored the failing battery.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka once blew up a chemistry classroom, which she says gets one put on a list for life.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Faced with Gazi's sword over Ceria, Ryoka threatens to bite off her tongue and kill herself, then names Flos, the King of Destruction, as awakened to make Gazi pause.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka recalls the continents Baleros, the Blighted Kingdoms of Rhir, Terandria, Chandrar and Izril, which the Drakes call Issrysil.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka proposes finding a healing mage who knows a restoration or regeneration spell to heal Ceria's hand, says no [Priests] exist in this world, and offers to pay.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka knows someone who thought she could fix Ryoka's shattered leg, and that person knows a famous healer.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka estimates the healing at a thousand gold, or at least a few hundred, and says she knows two ways to earn a lot of money rather than relying on running.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka still holds a good amount of money from the delivery for Teriarch that she never completed, and feels guilty about it.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka tells Erin that she has a trick memory for details she finds interesting, studied history for her AP exams, and got a few 5's.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka warns Erin that a world without copyright means shopkeepers will copy her recipes within days, and that ice cream is costly and hard to store without a fridge, so snow cones may be cheaper.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka advises Erin to repair the inn's walls, cover the windows, enchant the kitchen, and improve Toren, who she says can only clean and haul.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka wears oversized boots from Krshia and is dressed in this world's equivalent of a t-shirt and running leggings in the cold.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka heads back to Celum to start earning, promising to return within about a week with money and news of what the spell might cost.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka reaches Celum with at least eight blisters after nearly two days running in ill-fitting boots.

section: Gazi, the undead and the plan for Ceria
text: Ryoka buys the Runner's Guild rulebook for fifteen silver, paying with a gold piece from those Teriarch gave her.
Ryoka's father counts as a big hitter in both politics and business, so her allowance as a child matched what someone just above the poverty line earns.
Ryoka keeps the potion Teriarch gave her as payment for the delivery, which glows orange and pink and is far more valuable than she first understood.
Ryoka threatens to hurt Octavia unless she gives back the potion, after Octavia refuses to return it and offers samples and gold instead.
Toren senses that Ryoka has four times as much magic in her as Erin, though far less than the bonfires that are Pisces and Ceria, who could each sustain at least ten Torens.
Ryoka has eighty gold pieces and reflects that she never worried about money back home.
Ryoka tells Garia that the Horns of Hammerad are dead, and Garia breaks down crying in the street.
Ryoka wears new shoes in place of the Gnoll boots, and heals her blisters.
Ryoka bargains with Octavia, who will talk for five teaspoons of Ryoka's potion after Ryoka holds out against six.
Ryoka resists Teriarch's compulsion spell by refusing to open her mouth, and tells him it is willpower; he is floored because she has no class.
Ryoka tells Teriarch she could not find the recipient, checked the Blood Fields, and broke the spell on her as well.
Ryoka tells Teriarch she will finish his delivery when she has time, and sprints nearly two miles from the cave before slowing.
Ryoka delivers a huge sprouting potato to Rikku, a blue-haired [Alchemist] covered in blue dust.
Ryoka stays in the north a day after angering Teriarch and taking an eight hundred gold contract, running small deliveries while Octavia prepares equipment for her.
Ryoka treats Teriarch's potion as a last resort because she lacks the skills to beat anything above an ill-equipped bandit or Goblin raiding party.
Ryoka sets herself the goal of becoming a Courier for the respect, access and higher pay it brings, which would also let her support Erin's inn.
Ryoka turned off her iPhone's GPS the day she got it so her parents could not spy on her, and the battery is at about 30 percent.
Ryoka stops ten miles down the road to pull out her snow shoes and a fresh change of clothes to wipe off the snow.
Ryoka starts to suspect that Teriarch, with his Elven looks, odd expressions, cave, treasure and hot flames, may not be a mere mage, and wonders if he did something to her head.
Ryoka runs at her fastest and cannot shake the Courier Valceif, who runs beside her grinning and says her speed is impressive for someone with no Skills or Classes.
Ryoka runs through the night and the next day on willpower and one of Octavia's foul blue stamina potions.

Ryoka finds a massive battered suit of black steel armor with holes and no blood, a broken sword, a muddy swath nearly two miles wide, and a narrow crack in the mountain; she buries the armor in the snow and moves on to catch a Courier.
Ryoka fears that Erin's openness about her chess skill could be dangerous if the sender of the chess board came looking for her.
Ryoka's iPhone holds over ten thousand songs on a 32 GB model with almost every app besides a few essentials uninstalled.
Ryoka throws her bedside dresser down the stairs to stop Erin's singing.
Ryoka was an antisocial outcast on her high school track team despite being its best runner, and her parents had the coach let her train alone.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka tells Valceif about Teriarch's request, saying the price began at forty gold pieces and a potion until she bargained it up to eight hundred gold.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka carries four healing potions and three stamina potions.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka concludes the leveling system was not made by anyone from Earth, noting there is no [Gamer] class, which explains why chess players such as Olesm level while Erin does not.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka wonders whether the sender of the expensive chessboard knew chess could help a person level their class.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka learns to make her [Light] orb brighter by concentrating, which tires her, though she holds back from pushing it further.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka tells Erin and Ceria that faeries cannot be trusted: never go near a mound, thank one, eat their food or tell them of your child; they fear cold iron and cannot enter a place uninvited as far as she knows.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka punches a Frost Faerie out of the air in Erin's inn and gets frostbitten knuckles; the faerie warns "You will regret that, human" and then grins.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka and Erin do not swat the faeries because both are frightened of them, aware they could kill with something like an avalanche.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka arrives among the Stone Spears Gnolls with wasp stings, bruises and cuts, after faeries woke a wasp colony, pelted her with snowballs and cut her with ice.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka tells the Gnolls that she hit a Winter Sprite to make them stop while she was defending a friend.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka follows a stone Teriarch gave her that points south and far west of the Blood Fields, despite the faeries' interference.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka heals her burns from faerie-thrown campfire coals with spare potions, stops using potions afterwards, and finds her clothing stolen and hung in a tall tree one day, which makes her snap.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka deduces that Erin earned a faerie's favor, since the faeries say they owe one, and says Erin's name.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka feels a lifelong emptiness she calls the great beast of not caring, and says she is worthless.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka thinks she can no longer learn new spells, rejects the class system, and cannot help her friends, and sees the limit of her abilities floating by her head.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka thinks a Frost Faerie is far stronger than she can ever be, noting she nearly lost her hand to frostbite when she punched one.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka tells stories from Earth to the faeries and Gnolls for a whole day, beginning with Superman and Batman and going on to Lord of the Rings, and a faerie admits there are still things in her world worth hearing.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka leaves the Stone Spears after three days, healed and carrying a refilled pack, and tells Urksh she owes him a debt.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka runs quickly but without movement-enhancing Skills, so the Drake Venitra guesses she is a Runner, possibly a Courier.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka knows a Tier 0 spell [Noise] taught by Ceria besides [Light], and is able to project [Light] from her hands like a flashlight.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka sees her first corpse, a Drake killed by a thrust through his armor, and then finds the snow hides more.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: From a hilltop, Ryoka watches Drakes and Gnolls fight and die in the snow below.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka buries herself in the snow to hide from soldiers searching for a Human, but their leader's threat was a bluff and Ryoka is caught.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka carries a City Runner Seal, spelled to break if it leaves her for more than five minutes.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka lies to the Drake Captain that she is delivering to Urksh, Chieftain of the Stone Spears, and the Captain accepts her Seal as a non-combatant.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka uses Octavia's stink potion, a pepper spray potion thrown in Ilvriss's eyes, a kick that knocks Periss out, and a smoke bomb bag to escape the Drake camp.

section: Faeries, the Stone Spears and the Wall of Drakes
text: Ryoka is down to one bag, one potion and Teriarch's [Haste] potion.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka alters her [Light] spell with the image of a flashlight, speaks the new word [Flashlight], and her fingertip emits a narrow cone of light.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka digs a large arrow fragment out of her leg with a small knife and pours the last of her healing potion over the wound.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka blinds the Drakes and Gnolls by casting [Flashlight] on high beam, then runs into the enchanted trees where a faerie calls out directions.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka reaches the Necromancer's castle in a cleared stretch of snow, where Periss seizes her at sword point and her soldiers follow.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka tells Periss the castle is the home of the Necromancer Az'kerash, and says the forest is a maze that traps anyone who does not follow its path.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: The delivery Ryoka carries is worth eight hundred gold pieces.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka punches Venitra in the face, bruising her hand, and drinks the whole bottle of Teriarch's orange-pink potion, after which her legs carry her out of the castle against her will.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka runs across the battlefield at blinding speed, shouting too fast for anyone but the Frost Faeries to hear her.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ceria and Yvlon reject Erin's suggestion of Ryoka as a fourth party member, since she has no levels and her fighting skills are not adequate for killing monsters.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: The effect of Teriarch's potion on Ryoka lasts about twenty minutes, in which she thinks she covered over fifty miles.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka spends two days in a cave recovering from torn muscles, with her healing potions all gone.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka uses [Flashlight] on a faerie twice, adjusting the beam's intensity to blind her.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka says she has no classes and no skills, never leveled, and chose not to.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka gives a faerie her first and last names but, because her first name is in kanji and names are dangerous to give faeries, she does not give her middle name.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka strips down to a shirt and trousers with fur wrapped around her feet to run faster than a Gnoll, and gets frostbite.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka and Urksh offer to pay any price for a chance to save a child, and the faerie tells Ryoka only she may follow.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka says her ability is earned rather than given: she has no Skills or classes, but a few spells such as [Flashlight] and [Flashbang] that she shaped from things she understands.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka can make [Light] brighter, reshape it, and toss the orb ahead of her, but cannot control it once thrown.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka finds that casting a single spell tires her.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka thinks the fae love fragments of immortality, eternal stories and children, and that this may be why they help.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka ties a rope harness for Mrsha and climbs out of a crevasse on the rope to pull her up.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka casts [Flashbang] with her thumbs in her ears, carries Mrsha over her shoulder down the slope, and two Goblins fall into the crevasse behind her.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka recalls Erin's remark that she is not a killer and thinks of the Goblin Rags.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka kicks one Goblin, blinds the rest with [Flashlight], beats the first down with his mace, and fires a red flare into the night sky twice.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: A Goblin bites off Ryoka's right pinkie and ring fingers and swallows them.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Surrounded by Goblins, Ryoka begs the faeries for help as Ryoka Dawning Griffen and offers everything, while Urksh also offers everything.

section: The Necromancer's castle and the Haste run
text: Ryoka, filled with magic by the faeries, runs through the Goblin ranks carrying Mrsha, each step feeling like ten, as the faeries lead her to safety.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka vows "Next time I will save them all. Or die trying", then collapses face-first into the snow.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: The system announces [Barefoot Runner Class Obtained!] at Level 8 with [Skill - Flawless Stride], [Skill - Enhanced Movement], [Skill - Dangersense] and [Skill - Final Run], but a faerie tells it Ryoka is different and will learn nothing from it, and the notice [Level Ups Cancelled] follows.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka's iPhone rings for five minutes in her pack beside her unconscious body, while elsewhere mages stop casting and change their target and another phone rings on another continent.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Magnolia is told Theofore reports that two of Ryoka's fingers are missing, that she moves much slower than normal and is not alone, and that she may have rescued a young Gnoll cub.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: A note in the text of an Antinium Wars book records that Ryoka stopped reading it and left it behind to journey to the High Passes, and has not reopened it.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka's two missing right-hand fingers leave stumps that ache, and she is exhausted, hungry and injured.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka stopped hearing the system's notifications after the night of the faerie bargain, having formerly heard and cancelled notices such as [Barefoot Runner Level 1!] and, after her fight with Calruz, [Disciple Level 3!].

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka returns to Erin's inn with Mrsha, greets Erin, and collapses into her arms.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka tells Erin everything since she left the inn, keeping the stories she told in the Gnoll camp private, and says she struck a bargain with the faeries that saved her and Mrsha while the Stone Spears were left to the Goblins.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka knows Magnolia's healer friend can repair damaged parts but cannot restore missing body parts, so her fingers are gone forever.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka breaks down sobbing in Erin's arms, saying she could do nothing.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka insists to Erin that Lyonette must be a runaway princess.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka plans first to collect her reward from Teriarch and then deal with Lady Magnolia.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka has not told Erin that Teriarch is a Dragon.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka tells Krshia that the Stone Spears tribe is gone.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka announces to the listening Gnolls that she will take on Erin's debt and pay it, though the eight hundred gold she is owed is only 1.6 percent of it and she does not have it yet.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka insists that Mrsha stay with Erin instead of Krshia, after seeing how the young Gnoll Brunkr looked at her, and vows to protect her.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: After Ryoka drinks Erin's faerie-flower drink, which Halrac says brings back happy memories, the world dissolves and she sees the Stone Spears camp, with Urksh grinning and Mrsha beside her.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka tells Selys that she has never paid attention to levels, while privately knowing she must learn how levels and classes work.

section: Aftermath: the bargain, Mrsha and Erin's debt
text: Ryoka argues to Klbkch that total levels across all classes, not age, slow leveling, and speculates there is a cap near Level 100.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka calls the Earth-style vehicle at Erin's inn a sledge and says it comes from where she and Erin are from.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka gives Selys and Krshia most of her gold coins, leaves Mrsha with Selys and Lyonette at the inn, and runs north looking for a sledge, a girl or a skeleton, thinking of a Dragon who can scry for people if he knows their names.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka discards her boots, coat and hat while running north through the snow, and shreds her feet bloody.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka tells Teriarch to his face that he is a Dragon, and he denies it badly.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka tells Teriarch she delivered both ring and letter to Perril Chandler, who read the letter and called it an appropriate gift.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka says she broke a memory spell Teriarch cast on her, helped by a Courier's powerful charm, and remembered what he is.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka punches Teriarch in the nose with her left hand because her right is still missing fingers, and he then reveals his Dragon form.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka challenges Teriarch to a game of riddles, offering the secret of her name as her wager, after he threatens to erase her mind.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka learns to cast a fire spell instantly from the tome, since fire needs a source of fuel unlike [Light], and understands basic fire magic.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka plays "Beethoven's 5 Secrets" on her iPhone for Teriarch, and tells him her 32 GB iPhone could store over a hundred thousand books.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka appears two feet above the floor of Octavia's wrecked shop, bangs her head on the ceiling, lands on her feet, and advises Octavia to cool the carrots with something before adding Corusdeer horns, and to use flour.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka sends a message to Krshia saying she has what Krshia wants and that the others should wait for her return.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka keeps her right hand under the table so Garia has not noticed her missing fingers, and says she lost them to overconfidence.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka lost two fingers on her right hand to a Goblin a week ago, leaving three fingers on that hand.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka shows a Seal of her own as proof she is a City Runner, and runs barefoot through snow thanks to Erin's magic soup.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka's prize for the Dragon duel is a bag of holding with gold coins, which holds all her bed covers and two chairs as well.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka is banned from the Adventurer's Guild after Erin's table flip attack.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka learns a basic telekinesis cantrip and a wind trick from Teriarch's tome, and quickly masters one of its spells.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka cannot cast [Water Spray] from the tome, because she cannot believe magic can turn into water without violating physics, and concludes "Education ruined magic".

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka becomes friends with a Frost Faerie who gives her name as Ivolethe.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka stands barefoot on a snow-covered hill in a shirt and loose leggings, kept warm by Corusdeer soup that wears off.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka tells Fals that she traded two fingers for her gift, and he shakes her hand gently.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka is not charged for the destruction of the Runner's Guild because eyewitnesses saw Persua and the other Runners grab Ivolethe, and she is banned from the guild in Celum.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Hearing of the Horns, Ryoka runs from Celum toward Ocre to arrive by tonight, asking Fals to tell Garia and Erin.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka and Ceria toast the old Horns of Hammerad.

section: Teriarch's Dragon duel and Book 3 in Celum
text: Ryoka tells Ceria that Pisces must track down Toren, the skeleton, and Ceria suspects Pisces made one that thinks.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: Ryoka Griffin carries at her side the bag of holding that Teriarch gave her.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: Ryoka stores the Horns' recovered weapons (a buckler, a sword, the blade of a sword and a dagger) in her bag of holding, and Ceria pours several hundred gold coins into it; her pack and a small bag like hers go into the carriage trunk.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: When Ressa comes for her, Ryoka tells Ceria she has no choice and agrees to go, asking where Magnolia is now; Ressa answers that Magnolia is in Invrisil and Ryoka will be taken to her estate next to the city.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: Ryoka's only condition for going with Ressa is fifteen minutes to prepare; Ressa says running will do her no good, and Ryoka answers that she knows.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: Using the fifteen minutes, Ryoka storms into the Runner's Guild, demands every delivery bound for Invrisil, drags the [Receptionist] over the desk when he objects, and leaves with a large bundle of multi-part and other deliveries, which she piles in the carriage beside Ressa.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: Ryoka's family home had gardeners, pool people and personal masseuses, which she grudgingly admits means servants were at her beck and call.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: Ryoka remembers that she ran from Magnolia at first, so long ago that she had nearly forgotten; Magnolia was the first person to work out where Ryoka came from, and she could command her easily.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: Ryoka wonders whether the wine in Magnolia's hamper is spiked to make her more truthful, then notes that Magnolia could simply have her servants pour a truth serum down her throat.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: Watching Ivolethe fly alongside the carriage, Ryoka glimpses a faint, colourless ripple like a heat shimmer trailing in the air ahead of the faerie, but it vanishes when she tries to point it out.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: Ivolethe says Ryoka's glimpse of the trail is the first step.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: Cresting a hill, the carriage drives into a vast Goblin column marching across the snowy valley; Carn Wolf riders at its head turn to cut the carriage off.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: Ressa casts [Invisibility Field] and the carriage runes glow, but the Goblins follow the geysering snow it throws up.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: A small Goblin with a large black crossbow, riding among elite Hobgoblins, fires on the unseen carriage; the bolt shatters against the reinforced side but ends the spell, and Ryoka recognises the archer as Rags.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: A tall Hobgoblin on a Carn Wolf charges the carriage with a crimson sword; Ressa throws blades that he deflects, and the carriage escapes.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: Ryoka thinks the tall Hobgoblin could be the one she saw at the inn, and wonders what the Goblins are doing.

section: Book 3: the summons to Magnolia Reinhart
text: Ryoka has a smoke bag made for her by Octavia.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: Magnolia presses Ryoka in her silken voice to tell her everything; Ryoka recognises the feeling as like Teriarch's geas spell, remembers she has resisted it before, lunges at Magnolia with a fist, and is knocked back onto the sofa by Ressa.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: Asked about guns, Ryoka judges that a prototype gun could be ready in under a month with a kingdom's resources, but a war-ready gun and army would take years, and that a cannon is the easier and more dangerous route.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: Pressed for the ingredients of gunpowder, Ryoka reluctantly says "Sulfur"; Magnolia finds this troubling and, refusing to explain, leaves Ryoka suspecting someone is already moving on sulfur.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: Ryoka tells Magnolia she must convince the Antinium not to go to war, and Magnolia's smile vanishes; Ressa puts Ryoka in an arm-lock at Magnolia's word until Magnolia says Ryoka is not lying.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: Ryoka heals her arm with a potion from her belt and sees that Ressa holds a sharp, magical-looking dagger with a green tint to the edge.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: Ryoka tells Magnolia the Antinium are not her enemy, that their real enemy is a god, and that the Queens fled Rhir because they were fighting something they believed was a god.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: Ryoka names Klbkch, a Prognugator of the Antinium Hive in Liscor, as her source, and Magnolia says she knows Klbkch the Slayer from the Second Antinium War and gives Ryoka her full attention.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: Magnolia gives Ryoka a copy of The Antinium: A Brief History by Krsysl Wordsmith, a book Magnolia funded, and Ryoka puts it in her bag of holding.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: Magnolia releases Ryoka, saying that a chance of avoiding war with the Antinium is invaluable and that from now on the two must be allies, adding that Ryoka will not live with Magnolia as her enemy.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: When the wall of the sitting room explodes, Ryoka is thrown through the air and ends up with a deep fragment of stone in her thigh.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: After the attack, Ryoka presses a dead maid's dress against a stabbed man's stomach to stop the bleeding until a maid brings a potion that heals him.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: Magnolia tells Ryoka that she has become too busy to press her about inventions from her world, lets her go, and says they are allies and Ryoka will meet the best experts in Invrisil tomorrow.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: Ryoka stays that night in the large room Ressa finds for her, still seeing in her mind the lightning and the line of fire that engulfed Nemor.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: Ceria tells the Horns that Ryoka is hotheaded, prickly and arrogant but brave and no coward, that she went into the crypts to rescue Ceria, and that she is a lot like a female Calruz, whom Calruz himself trusted.

section: Book 3: the meeting with Magnolia and the alliance
text: The Horns' remaining coin and valuable artifacts are with Ryoka in the north while the team is broke in the south.

A week after the attack Ryoka has still not left Magnolia's mansion; Magnolia and Ressa left for her northern estates the day after the attack, leaving her with promises of help, subtly dire threats and Reynold as her guide in Invrisil.
Ryoka has skimmed over a hundred books in Magnolia's library in a week, reading from dawn to dusk.
Ryoka wears bulky, ill-fitting magical lenses that translate the many languages in the library's books, though they do not translate bad handwriting.
Ryoka asked about the other people from Earth that Erin met but received no answers, and she feels like the odd one out in the mansion as the only guest not in Magnolia's employ.

Ryoka proposes to run to Invrisil and meet Reynold at the Runner's Guild, but he explains that Invrisil's customs check everyone, Runners included, because of the dangerous artifacts that pass through, while Lady Reinhart's carriage is never stopped; Ryoka agrees to take the carriage and tells him to stop calling her Miss Ryoka.
In Invrisil, Ryoka sees a blind man speak German to a guard lieutenant and realises it is German, a language she does not expect to hear in this world.

Ryoka hesitates over whether to go to the enchanter or follow the blind man, since she can hardly believe she has found someone else from her world; Ivolethe, peering from Ryoka's belt pouch, fixes her eyes on Laken.
Ryoka speaks halting German to Laken Godart, who answers that he is from San Francisco, and they realise they are both from Earth.
Laken, who has believed he was alone in this world, repeats that he is not alone and weeps with relief on meeting Ryoka.
Ryoka gives Laken her name and asks when he came and who he has talked to; Laken says he came a little over a month ago and that Durene, who found him, is his guide and friend.
Ryoka tells Laken his iPhone can be recharged by a mage's [Repair] spell.

Ryoka warns Laken that his iPhone might be used to track him by people in this world who know humans come from another world, tells him not to answer any call on it, and says there are more people from Earth here.
Ryoka promises to meet Laken at the same place in an hour, as she has something to do first.
Ryoka tells Ivolethe she cannot ignore Laken, who could know something important, and that Magnolia knows of the other Earth kids but not of Laken; she wants to keep it that way and warn him.

At the enchanter Hedault's shop, Ryoka tests her bag from Teriarch on a hunch; Hedault's eyes bulge when he examines it, and Ryoka concludes that a Dragon would not own a bag of holding of less than perfect quality.
While Hedault examines the artifacts, Ryoka notices Reynold writing down everything, both the artifacts and what she is carrying, and resolves to have words with him afterwards.
Ryoka tells Laken that Reynold was sent by Magnolia, whom she knows, and warns him in German that Reynold is a friend but a spy and to say nothing; Laken answers "Ja".
Ryoka tells Laken that a few other people from Earth have been pulled to the continent, about five or six kids around their age, and that Magnolia knows about everyone.
Ryoka tells Laken about her friend Erin Solstice, an [Innkeeper] in Liscor, and says she would like him to meet her.

Ryoka warns Laken that Magnolia is friendly-looking but devious, comparing her to an older Daenerys who is smarter and less arrogant than Cersei Lannister and as bold as Catelyn Stark; Laken says he knows Game of Thrones from audiobooks and episodes with visual description.
Ryoka worries she has given Laken away and wants Magnolia's servants to see him as just another person from her world, though she briefly thinks of killing Reynold.
Ryoka tells Laken that Reynold is Magnolia's servant, that Magnolia knows everything, and that her servants have probably been listening in.

At the Mage's Guild, Ryoka has messages sent to Erin Solstice, Krshia Silverfang, Ceria Springwalker and Mrsha saying she is sorry and will return home soon, and dictates to Ceria her summary of the analysed items.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka was a Pokemon fan as a child: the sight of a blue bird sends her back to being ten years old on her balcony with a Gameboy and the game that defined her life then.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Laken recognises the Pokemon theme song playing in Ryoka's earbuds and she admits she was a fan long ago; she says the winged Frostwing reminds her of Articuno, one of the original legendary birds.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka tells Laken she was teleported to this world a few days after she downloaded the Pokemon Go app.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka hands Durene, who is ready to fight her to protect Laken, a pepper potion from her belt (one of several Octavia gave her), explaining that it blinds an opponent when thrown and advising Durene to get magical items and a weapon.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka tells Laken in German "Ein Gott...lebt", says she was assured by someone she believes that a god is alive, and corrects herself to say the god is sleeping, asleep and waking (Schlafen, Aufwachen).

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka tells Laken that the angry ant people she described are scared out of their minds of this one person, and that talking about gods apparently gives them strength.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka wonders whether people lose anything by having a class and offers to be the test subject; she says she is unsure whether the class system and the sleeping god are connected, though it seems so.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka tells Laken that someone said there was a summoning spell in Rhir behind their arrival.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka answers the ringing iPhone call from a caller using the name [BlackMage] and swears at him for calling at all, since the call could be traced and says the man trying to find out locations may be tracing them now.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: [BlackMage], who has a faint English accent, is surprised that [batman] is a girl; he says he and the mages of Wistram are calling people across the world to bring them to Wistram, and that he called Ryoka first because she exposed [Kent Scott] and warned everyone.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka tells [BlackMage] she suspected [Kent Scott] from the start and will not trust anyone who calls unexpectedly; when she asks how to prove the Wistram mages are trustworthy he admits they cannot, and Laken takes the phone and introduces himself as "L", from their world.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka sells the cold, metallic-wooded wand to the enchanter Hedault for enough weapons and armour to outfit four adventurers, two wands, a magical robe, a spellbook, rings and two hundred gold pieces, and Hedault agrees on condition she tells him what is inside it.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ivolethe, speaking in an ancient voice, tells Hedault that the wand holds a seed of an ancient tree, a trapped child that has endured ten thousand years, and Ryoka calls it living magic.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka tells Hedault she will lie to her friends about the sale, because the wand would make them a target of every magic-user on the continent and what the Horns need is gear to become a Gold-rank team; Hedault agrees to record the debt, which the Horns can call on by messaging him.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka runs through a blizzard for about eight hours towards a village, following faerie lights and kept going by the Runner's Guild's stamina potions and a healing potion.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: A Snow Golem rises from the ground and chases the faeries away, and Ryoka sees a hat-like black mass on its head and murmurs "Thanks, Frosty" to it.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka tells herself that the ragged villagers have put blind faith in a false leader, the [Emperor], but cannot face Prost's tears of relief and feels her heart hurt.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka tells the village children that she delivers presents for Santa Claus, a friend of their [Emperor] Laken, giving every child a gift and food.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: A girl named Anabelle tells Ryoka her brother died in the avalanche and she could not find him; Ryoka kneels, tells her it was not her fault, and gives her a doll dressed as a male adventurer with blonde hair, claiming Laken told her to make sure Anabelle got a present.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka sends a Mage's Guild message that she is on an emergency delivery for a village that needs supplies and food and will try to be back for Christmas.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: The day after Christmas, Ryoka says her goodbyes to the villagers, and Prost's wife Yesel gives her a thick hand-knitted dark grey scarf with a blue wave-pattern band that looks unused, which Ryoka senses was not meant for her; she accepts it.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: At a fire in the dark, Ryoka sees that the three people sitting with her are dead things; she calls [Light] and finds she cannot feel her magic, and the old woman says there is no magic there, only the fire.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka refuses the dead things' offer to sit with them, lights a stick in the fire as a torch despite the warning that it will soon go out, and runs into the darkness as it burns.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka escapes the darkness and is found by Ivolethe, who makes a fire; Ryoka finds that part of Yesel's scarf has changed into the impression of a hand and throws the scarf into the fire.

section: Book 4: Laken, Wistram and the Christmas run
text: Ryoka finds two twitching fingers in her pocket and throws them into the fire, crying out and doubling over, clutching at the stumps of her fingers; her right hand burns with pain as she runs back towards Invrisil.

A day's journey from Liscor, near Celum, Ryoka runs down side roads in the snow with a Frost Faerie, tired, cold and hungry; she would have arrived sooner but Reynold ran over a group of bandits and broke the carriage axle.
Ryoka sleeps outside the night before she crests a hill and spots the inn, footsore in boots because the snow is too deep for her to run barefoot.
Ryoka says Reynold told her Magnolia has orders to turn every [Bandit] he spots into road kill.
Ryoka tells Ivolethe she will leave her a stack of gold coins so that Erin feeds her; Ivolethe promises not to bother Ryoka's friends.
Ryoka worries about how to tell Erin about Magnolia, the [Assassins], Laken the [Emperor], Blackmage in Wistram and the night with three strangers at the campfire.
Ryoka lifts Teriarch's feather-light spellbook, as big as Mrsha, out of her bag of holding in front of Krshia and the Gnolls and says it settles the debt.
Ryoka calls the book a first-edition instructional tome of Rihal that contains every spell they knew from Tier 1 to about Tier 4, worth fifty or a hundred lost spellbooks.

Ryoka names Teriarch to Krshia as an incredibly powerful magic user, the equivalent of an [Archmage], whom she has convinced to be a patron of the tribe; she says she gave him something of equal value that she cannot explain, and she hopes his name will cause no problem.
Ryoka decides to give the Gnolls half-truths about the trade because lies come less easily in this world, and swears it was a fair trade.
Ryoka asks only for friendship as payment; Krshia accepts, vowing that Gnolls will remember Ryoka's name and Teriarch's as long as the tribe endures.
Drakes led by Ilvriss and Zel Shivertail confront Ryoka and the Gnolls; Ryoka recognises Ilvriss from a battlefield and tent and remembers how his lieutenant died.

Ryoka's memory shows undead led by an armored Gnoll with a battleaxe, Kerash, and a rotting woman who calls herself Bea; a Drake commander, Periss, tells Ryoka to run and stays with sixteen elite warriors to fight while Ryoka flees.
Ryoka and Erin reunite and Ryoka tells her she is back.
Back at the inn, Ryoka tells Klbkch "I told Magnolia" and he nods, replies and leaves swiftly; Ryoka understands that he got the message that Magnolia knows his intentions.
Ryoka has two missing fingers on her right hand, which makes her grip feel uneasy and lopsided when she lifts anything heavy.

Zel Shivertail puts Ryoka through a lie detector test with a recording truth detector of green gems, finds she told the truth, and promises to tell Ilvriss what she said though he cannot promise Ilvriss will stop coming after her.
Ryoka thanks Zel for helping to save Mrsha once; she feels guilty because she is Mrsha's guardian, the only one the Gnoll has left, and should have been there.
Ryoka remembers that Ivolethe can enter and leave The Wandering Inn freely because the inn is built with copper nails.

Ryoka tells the Horns that she sold one valuable item from the bag to the enchanter Hedault in exchange for the whole set of gear, and that he says he owes the Horns a favour they can call in at any time.

After the party, Lyonette suggests Ryoka sleep upstairs with Mrsha and her; Ryoka and Erin, tired and feeling distant, agree to talk tomorrow, and Lyonette tells Ryoka about Christmas, after which Ryoka knows what she has to do.
Ryoka blocks Olesm from telling Erin his news from a Walled City about chess, since no one will die if it waits and it will still be there tomorrow, and tells Erin she is taking a break.

When Ryoka was a child she hid in a closet for two days to avoid formal events her father made her attend, until the police came to take her parents' statement, thinking she had run away again or been kidnapped.

Ryoka argues that Toren may not be dead, since the monster is not dead until you see the body, and wonders whether he found a mana potion or another master; Erin says she will listen for news of a skeleton.

Ryoka tells Erin that Magnolia spirited her away with threats, interrogation and intrigue and tried to charm her first; she says Ressa is not just a [Maid] but a [Ninja], having seen her throw a star at ambushing Goblins and fight the assassins.
Ryoka tells Erin about the servants killed in the assassins' attack and about Magnolia's death-ray ring.

Ryoka suggests Erin cook food in bulk and reheat it because her Skill keeps food fresh, and that the inn's surplus mana could run a bigger door, reach Invrisil, or power runes for heating, cooling and distilling water from the air.

Ryoka tells Erin of the blizzard, the forest and the three visitors at the campfire, and of throwing her fingers into the fire; Erin shows her an off-silver coin given in exchange for food, not for their gifts, which she received on the Winter Solstice.

Ryoka realises the three visitors' gifts match what Erin was given, including a horn she heard at her own fire; she says she has never heard the name Tamaroth, tells Erin not to show the coin to anyone she does not trust, and will ask Klbkch and Teriarch.

Ryoka says her plan is to stay in Liscor for now, shop for magical items, have Octavia brew potions and be taught something by Ivolethe, perhaps faerie magic or running faster, with the goal of becoming a Courier and reaching First Landing on foot to seek a ship to Wistram.
