Ryoka and Erin dissolve the distance between them, plan to return to the place and part with Erin saying she is glad Ryoka is back.
Ryoka pays a Guild receptionist two gold coins, the 5% Guild fee on a pretend delivery worth forty gold coins from Erin, so that the Guild thinks Erin has given her a delivery.
Ryoka arranges to visit Garia's family farm in a day or two, inviting Fals to come along and offering to bring Mrsha.

Ryoka asks Pisces to help measure the inn's door, asking how much mana each teleport uses, whether weight and distance matter, and how far it could reach; Pisces asks whether she has a link to the [Engineer] class and she says "You could say that".
With Pisces and Typhenous, Ryoka sets up a test of the door using a [Light] spell linked to the door's mana and Pisces' mug as a second anchor, which she carries a mile from the inn.
Ryoka nearly calls Moore "Ha-" by a different name when he hands her the mug.
From Pisces' measurements Ryoka calculates that the door could bring over fifty people to the inn and back before running out, not counting how fast it recharges.
Ryoka feels as sick after teleporting back as after a roller coaster at double speed.
Ryoka offers to pay for the inn's expansion from the Horns' payment for her Invrisil run, which still leaves her over a thousand gold coins for magical items.

Ryoka asks Pawn to stop praying, saying Klbkch and, she thinks, the Queen agree with her; Pawn asks what she would give someone with one day to live, and she realises he means an Antinium Soldier or Worker and concedes "I'm wrong".

Ryoka tells Pawn she thinks there is a god in this world and would refuse to believe in him or her or it, yet cannot say Pawn is wrong to believe and is worried; Pawn infers that she and Klbkch know a god exists because they fear one.

Ryoka offers Pawn instruction in other religions, saying she read the Bible back to front and knows about Buddhism, Sikhism, Shinto and Zoroastrianism, and tells him about Islam, Judaism, Catholic and Protestant differences, Mormons and Quakers, including transubstantiation and consubstantiation.
Ryoka notes that the barmaids Maran and Safry came from Agnes' inn, and that she may "do something about this".

Ryoka tells Erin she spent all day invisible under Pisces' [Invisibility] spell in the inn, and that Maran and Safry, not Lyonette, are the problem: they brought in Humans to avoid serving Drakes and Gnolls, cannot tell non-Humans apart, will not fetch water, take breaks when busy, and were rude to Lyonette.
Ryoka tells Erin that Maran and Safry were a bit like Agnes: good, but not great, nice but not adaptable, flawed.
Ryoka finds Lyonette sitting miserably in the snow five minutes from the inn, tells her Mrsha is back at the inn with Moore levitating her, assures her Erin will not fire her, and gives her her coat.
Ryoka tells Lyonette she is too capable to be a [Barmaid] and should be an [Innkeeper] at least, then says she is a [Princess] and asks her to keep it a secret between them.

Ryoka shows Lyonette a spell she invented herself, [Flashbang], a flash of light with a deafening bang, and advises her to learn it and more spells from Typhenous or Ceria and to pick up a sword, because a princess should know her people's work.
Ryoka tells Lyonette she is taking Mrsha to visit Garia's family that night and will stay a day or two.
Ryoka dreads visiting friends' homes, a fear rooted in her life on Earth, even though she has never actually done it.
Ryoka's nightmares show Goblins slaughtering the Stone Spears tribe and her fingers being bitten off, and she dreads the coming of the Goblin Lord and the [Necromancer].
After Safry and Maran are fired, Ryoka takes Mrsha from the inn to Celum and runs on, carrying her in a Gnoll child basket, to Garia's family farm a few miles west of Celum.
Ryoka says she learned a fighting style back home rather than a Skill, and shows Garia's father Wailant that she fights like a boxer with her hands high, bouncing on her feet.
Ryoka says her punches could not knock down a Carn Wolf or a Minotaur and feels a pang at the thought of Calruz.
Ryoka names Muay Thai Kickboxing and Karate as styles she knows, thinks Karate might suit Garia, and offers to teach her.
Ryoka and Wailant spar after dinner; her kick sobers him up and Ryoka finds herself enjoying the visit and talking with Garia's mother Viceria.
Ryoka's iPhone has run out of power and she must get Pisces to cast [Repair] on it.
Ryoka teaches Garia, Fals and Mrsha warm-ups, punching with controlled breathing, and knee strikes (hiza-geri, from Shotokan Karate), explaining that martial arts work by connecting the whole body.

Ryoka performs handsprings, backflips, a standing front flip and a standing cork (a move from the martial art Tricking), slips on the snow on one landing, and hits Ivolethe with a spinning aerial kick.
Ryoka sees the wind twist around her while attempting a gainer and is carried upward in flips about ten feet before falling and knocking herself out in the snow.
Ivolethe tells Ryoka that in the moment she did not try, did not feel and saw, and the wind saw her.

section: Book 5: the fight with Erin and the Necromancer's agents
text: Ryoka wakes in a bad mood with a beetle on her toothbrush and brushes her teeth with the sage, salt and pepper toothpaste that Octavia sells.

section: Book 5: the fight with Erin and the Necromancer's agents
text: Contrary to what Ryoka fears, Frost Faeries cannot tell the future, though like humans they can predict it.

section: Book 5: the fight with Erin and the Necromancer's agents
text: Ryoka fears that the Frost Faeries can tell the future.

section: Book 5: the fight with Erin and the Necromancer's agents
text: Ryoka tells Erin she is awfully good at killing for someone who does not like it; Erin punches her and they fight until Mrsha bites in and Lyonette hits both with a bucket of water and the bucket.

section: Book 5: the fight with Erin and the Necromancer's agents
text: Ryoka had an anger management class after her second arrest because her father insisted; she received therapy and pills, hated them, and refused to take the pills again after they turned her into someone else.

section: Book 5: the fight with Erin and the Necromancer's agents
text: Ryoka says her father tried to make her take the pills and she stopped him by sneaking Xanax into his drinks, driving a bunch of rich businesspeople insane with a spiked bottle of wine.

section: Book 5: the fight with Erin and the Necromancer's agents
text: Ryoka and Erin make up in the hot tub, Ryoka being terrified of losing one of her few friends; Ryoka apologises twice and Erin once.

section: Book 5: the fight with Erin and the Necromancer's agents
text: Welsca Crimsonscale, in service to Wall Lord Ilvriss, enters the hot tub uninvited and Ryoka kicks her; since she kicked Welsca into someone else's tub, Ryoka is handcuffed in Liscor's guardhouse.

section: Book 5: the fight with Erin and the Necromancer's agents
text: A purple-scaled fake [Guardsman] who is one of Ilvriss' people asks where Captain Periss is and how she died, and threatens that Erin's file could prompt a Wall Lord to act through the Assassin's Guild; Ryoka warns him she will tell Zel Shivertail, then kicks him.

section: Book 5: the fight with Erin and the Necromancer's agents
text: Ryoka tells Krshia and Brunkr that Lyonette is a [Princess], insisting she is certain, and says Brunkr got his [Knight] class when he heard Lyonette knighting him.

section: Book 5: the fight with Erin and the Necromancer's agents
text: Venitra, disguised as Regrika Blackpaw by a ring, reveals herself in an alley, tells Ryoka that Ryoka delivered a letter to the Necromancer a month ago, and lifts her by the throat.

section: Book 5: the fight with Erin and the Necromancer's agents
text: Ryoka tells Az'kerash that the Dragon did not choose her but put up an open request, which she took because it paid well, and she says she would not have done it for all the gold in the world had she known the outcome.

section: Book 5: the fight with Erin and the Necromancer's agents
text: Ryoka writes a note, leaves her belt pouches and bag of holding in the room she shares with Lyonette and Mrsha, and steps through the door and runs.

section: Book 5: the Word of Death and the flight north
text: Ryoka cannot make her legs move when she is about to leave, because she is too afraid.

section: Book 5: the Word of Death and the flight north
text: Ryoka runs barefoot through the snow in shorts and a t-shirt, bleeding, having left her belt pouches and bag of holding behind but taken potion vials; she downs a healing potion and a stamina potion, her eighth and ninth, and vomits twice from the potions.

section: Book 5: the Word of Death and the flight north
text: Ryoka shouts at Teriarch that her friends will all be killed, asking why he did not think of the consequences of a birthday letter and did not protect them.

section: Book 5: the Word of Death and the flight north
text: Az'kerash has put a [Word of Death] spell on Ryoka that kills her if she speaks any part of his name or mentions necromancy.

section: Book 5: the Word of Death and the flight north
text: Ryoka shouts the Necromancer's names at Teriarch, Perril Chandler and Az'kerash, and her heart bursts and she collapses dead.

section: Book 5: the Word of Death and the flight north
text: Later, Teriarch revives Ryoka by dispelling the death magic and rebuilding her heart, then flies her away in his talon; she tells him he brought her back to life and he answers that a death spell destroys very little.

section: Book 5: the Word of Death and the flight north
text: Ryoka tells Erin that her note blamed herself because Regrika and Imenet came for her and killed Brunkr, Ulrien and Ivolethe, over something she saw while on one of her deliveries.

section: Book 5: the Word of Death and the flight north
text: Ryoka says her enemies threatened to kill Erin and everyone else if she told anyone, and that she went for help to a person she will not name, whom she thinks, but cannot be sure, can protect her; Erin guesses Teriarch.

section: Book 5: the Word of Death and the flight north
text: Asked by Zel who might know about the Necromancer without spreading the secret, Ryoka answers at once that it is Magnolia Reinhart, though she is not certain.

section: Book 5: the Word of Death and the flight north
text: Ryoka leaves Liscor on foot northward from Celum, playing "It's Time" by Imagine Dragons on her iPhone, and raises one hand to Erin as she runs out of sight.

section: Book 9: the Wind Runner in Reizmelt
text: Ryoka lives in Reizmelt as a City Runner whose stride is long and who carries deliveries in a bag of holding; a Receptionist recognises her as the girl who made a name for herself on a spice delivery two weeks earlier.

section: Book 9: the Wind Runner in Reizmelt
text: The wind blows at Ryoka's back as she runs, to the grumbling of caravan drivers and guards as it changes back once she has passed.

section: Book 9: the Wind Runner in Reizmelt
text: Ryoka lodges at The Huntress' Haven, an inn for adventurers whose bear-like [Innkeeper] calls her the Wind Runner, and she carries a bowl of stew up to her room as the second to last room along the stairs.

section: Book 9: the Wind Runner in Reizmelt
text: Ryoka gives a beaten [Fist Fighter], who lodges at the same inn, his healing potion bottle that his clumsy gloved hands cannot open.

section: Book 9: the Wind Runner in Reizmelt
text: In her room Ryoka lets the wind blow, and, having heard the news from half a dozen [Criers] about a battle, a rout, Tyrion Veltras challenging the Drakes and Goblins fighting Goblins, concludes that the Goblin Lord is gone while Liscor still stands.

section: Book 9: the Wind Runner in Reizmelt
text: Ryoka says it is a good thing she was not there to make it worse, and she thinks of a white Gnoll, a smiling young [Innkeeper] and shattered ice before whispering that it will be a beautiful spring.
Ryoka has been staying at The Huntress' Haven for two weeks and is one of its three regulars, now called the Wind Runner; she is a City Runner and an otherworlder.
Ryoka always has the wind at her back and it is why people call her the Wind Runner; she treats it as her one triumph and as Ivolethe's last gift.
Ryoka left Liscor, and ran north with Ivolethe dead behind her, because she felt too weak and too destructive to stand up to Az'kerash and Venitra; she found the wind on the way.
Ryoka has been gone from Liscor a month and a half, spending two weeks running barely resting to reach Reizmelt, passing Invrisil on the way.
Ryoka has two missing fingers on her right hand and a [Butler] notices them and her muddy bare feet when he opens a door.
Ryoka's first rule about the wind is that it is not her friend; it has moods and she can only run with it or fight it.
Ryoka cannot control the wind, but it is stronger where she is and inclined to follow her, she can only suggest or push it slightly, and it rages when she rages and calms when she is calm.
Ryoka lies that her wind is a rare Skill called [Runner's Wind] that she cannot control.
Ryoka's iPhone is dead and she trusts no [Mage] to repair it, so she runs without music.
Ryoka keeps an ear out for news around Liscor but refuses to go back until she can be useful and deserves it.
The Reizmelt Runner's Guild sends emergency adventurer requests to Ryoka before any other City Runner or Courier, because she put herself on a list of one.

Against Wailer Frogs, Ryoka empties dirt from her bag of holding and flour and the last of Octavia's smoke bag powder, calls on the wind, and a dust storm chokes the frogs' lungs so that adventurers kill them.
The Runner's Guild pays Ryoka a fee for the rescue, covering the healing potions and other items she used and extra money for rescuing a wounded adventurer.
Ryoka asks to be added to the Courier listings so that she can be asked by name for Courier-level deliveries, clenching a creation of Hedault's in her right hand.
Ryoka takes a gold bar bound for the Mage's Guild in Baepr, on which the Silversmithers have a hundred-gold bounty to stop the delivery.
On the road, Ryoka uses wind and dust from her bag of holding to blind bandits, a charm at her side blocks a [Mage]'s [Sleep] spell, and she scatters caltrops that the dust storm picks up.
Ryoka tells the vampire Fierre vampire stories from Earth, including Dracula, without saying where she is from; Fierre notices that most of them turn out to be fairly accurate.
Ryoka holds the ice figurine of a flying faerie that she commissioned from Hedault, shimmering, enchanted ice caught mid-smile, and her heart beats painfully at the sight.
Ryoka clutches the small icy figurine and feels less sadness, seeing a world of possibilities.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Ryoka dreams that she led Mrsha into the crevasse and lost her fingers there, blaming herself for the deaths of the Horns of Hammerad, Periss and her soldiers, the Stone Spears tribe, Brunkr, Ulrien, Zel Shivertail, Valceif Godfrey and Ivolethe, and for taking Teriarch's request.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Ryoka keeps a small ice figurine on the dresser by her bed, and reaching for it grounds her when she wakes from the nightmare.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Alber, a fist fighter, nicknames Ryoka the Braggart because she claimed to know more of fist fighting than he did, and he has taken to closing his shutters at night because the wind blows harder when she is around.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Madain, called the Madman, addresses Ryoka as Wind Runner.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Alber notices Ryoka's two missing fingers on her right hand and wonders how she lost them.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Ryoka tells Fierre that she and Madain are kindred spirits, with good days and bad days neither can help, and that her bad days are a kind of sickness that is all in the head.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Ryoka tells Fierre she has a bad temper and knows her problems, and she feels bad for Madain because no one told him it is not all his fault.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Ryoka has cemented her reputation as the first person to call when adventurers are in trouble since the Pithfire Hounds rescue, and the Receptionist Alime says Ryoka is first on her list aside from the Couriers.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Ryoka takes ears of corn from the [Farmer] Lupp for free and carries corn and milk to his daughter Kamine in Reizmelt, telling him to dare her to get a pie to her before it is cool.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Ryoka brings corn, bread and tarts to Madain, who tells her to fuck off and slams the door; later he thanks her gruffly for the damn good corn and tells her not to bother again.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Ryoka watches the Titan's game in Daquin through Fierre's mirror, amazed and worried.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: After a low day on which she lashes out at no one, Ryoka counts it a victory that she did not make anyone else's day worse, and she feels better the next day.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Ryoka tells Fierre that a Clairei Knight, Sir Molte, has given her a delivery; any City Runner would do and she thinks it is ceremonial, but she wants to deliver it honestly as her first personally requested delivery ever.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Ryoka feels a prickle down her spine at Lady Bethal Walchaís' command voice, which she thinks is eerily like Magnolia's charm Skill but more direct, and closer to Teriarch's.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Ryoka proves her control of the wind to Lady Bethal by making a breeze touch only Bethal, then a gust around the whole street, and stopping it when asked.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Bethal has Sir Thomast give Ryoka a proof token and a whispered message for Sir Nathald, grandmaster of the Knights of the Petal, and Ryoka says she has it word for word.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Before setting off, Ryoka clutches the ice figurine, addresses Ivolethe, and calls the winds to blow until they push her to run.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Ryoka runs for hours to Walta using stamina and healing potions in turn until she feels more machine than person, outrunning three ambush parties of which the Pithfire Hounds wipe out the first.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: The Walta [Receptionist] tells Ryoka she ran seventy-nine miles in under five and a half hours and has passed the qualifying speed for a Courier.

section: Book 11: the Wind Runner of Reizmelt
text: Ryoka's message from Lady Bethal arrives by Runner, not by spell, delivered by the Wind Runner of Reizmelt.
Ryoka stays at the Rose's Retreat in Walta, run by Miss Iglesias Theroben, resting after her now-famous run from Reizmelt for Lady Bethal and recovering from minor potion-sickness.
Ryoka senses the wind howling angrily and thinks that someone, perhaps a [Weather Mage], is trying to control it, so that it is out of her control that day.
Ryoka accepts the request to go to Riverfarm after thinking it over, knowing Laken Godart is the real sender.
Ryoka feels she has a debt to pay and wants to see the trouble Laken hinted at, though she does not know to whom or how she should pay it.
Ryoka and the Centaur Charlay pass eight burned ruins on the road south, evidence that something has swept through and left only destruction.
Charlay tells Ryoka she has her hooves, two wands and a dagger, and that she can outrun people, knock riders from horses with her wands and make a dust cloud.
Ryoka sees the [Witch] Alevica stand on her broom as on a skateboard and fly, and is shaken, shouting "She can fly!?".
At Riverfarm, Ryoka brings a few low-grade potions that were the only help Laken's side sent in answer to Durene's request, which were mainly there to prompt her arrival.
Prost tells those present that Ryoka ran through one of the worst blizzards to bring Riverfarm food when it was starving, and that he trusts her with any delivery.
Ryoka says Laken's message asked her to come because of trouble, using some German words, and that Laken implied he was worried; she had not known what to expect.
Ryoka suspects a traitor manipulated Laken into attacking the Goblins, which Durene told her about the night before, and she is already trying to work out who it is.
Ryoka steps in front of Prost, bows to the [Witch] Mavika and speaks for the farmers, saying a bargain made in faith deserves an answer in faith.
Mavika calls Ryoka "wind's child" and says Belavierr pointed her out.
When Durene asks if she has ideas from her and Laken's world, Ryoka winces and can only suggest a pesticide of water and soap, saying she does not really know.
Ryoka and Charlay eat omelettes made with meat Charlay gave her that turns out to be rat meat from Frostwing's scraps, and Ryoka spends ten wretched minutes in the outhouse.
Ryoka offers to visit anyone within about twenty miles of Riverfarm with letters free of charge, and makes the villagers wash their hands with her soap when she meets them after the outhouses.
Yesel recalls that Ryoka arrived with Christmas presents for the little ones during the terrible snows.

Ryoka and Charlay propose a Runner's Guild in Riverfarm, so that Runners can provide cheap communication for Laken's would-be empire and Riverfarm can advertise through them; Lady Rie agrees to convert a warehouse and write to the Runner's Guild in Filk.
Ryoka also suggests a commercial district with a Merchant's Guild, Mage's Guild, an inn and shops, to which Rie adds that Riverfarm already has chess boards and carved items to sell.

Next day Ryoka runs letters to the outlying settlements around Riverfarm: a [Fisher] on the marsh edge, who tells her Goblin raiders under the Great Chieftain Tremborag burned the area; and an [Archer] on a watchtower, who warns of a bandit group led by a [Pyromancer].

Ryoka finds a burned house with a message carved on a beam saying the family has gone to Melon's, and then Melon, a [Farmer] with a pitchfork Skill, who has three families under his roof, and who says Kayla's home was burned two weeks earlier and that Kayla died.
Melon says the people hereabouts want the [Emperor] back and would otherwise have to hire a Silver-rank team against the [Bandits].
Ryoka proposes giving food, wood, nails and an escort by Beniar's [Riders] to families outside Riverfarm, free of charge and without any return, and bringing back anyone who wants to come.
Lady Rie refuses, calling the plan charity in which a noble gives away resources, since people level in adversity; Ryoka answers that this is exactly what Magnolia Reinhart would say.

Ryoka tells Durene that she does not make decisions for herself but defers to Laken, Prost and Rie, and that neither she nor Laken can tell Durene what to do; she says she can reach out if Durene is drowning but Durene must learn to swim.

Ryoka argues that Rehanna's trade with Belavierr was her own right, asking whether anyone would give up ten minutes, a year or ten years of their life for happiness; she says she relied on coffee, medication and her parents' money back home.

Wiskeria angrily tells Ryoka not to moralise about her mother, the Witch of Webs, and Ryoka answers that she has not seen Wiskeria speak to her mother; at night Ryoka asks Durene if she would give up parts of her life to be Human, and Durene throws a pillow at her.

Ryoka tells Wiskeria that she dislikes her own mother, a rich trophy wife of her business tycoon father, and that Wiskeria and Belavierr remind her of her mother: someone who does not understand her, whom Ryoka would like to change.
Ryoka tells Belavierr she should change and so should her daughter, and Belavierr hurls her through the air with her clothes into a field where Ram and some farmers are working.
Ryoka wonders whether the Circle of Thorns or Magnolia Reinhart gains if Riverfarm collapses, then pulls back from the idea of Magnolia, thinking she does not kill innocent people.

Ryoka names the smoke cloud over the fire a pyrocumulonimbus and realises the flames come from fires at many points, set by a Drake who can breathe fire, fly and change the wind, so that running is a trap.

Ryoka calls the wind, shouting that she is the Wind Runner, and leads a tornado of fire away from Riverfarm by running ahead of it until it burns out; she can lead the wind but not run with it, and she collapses charred.

Ryoka punches Laken in the stomach for the Goblins and for the siege of Liscor; Laken answers that he did not know they were attacking Liscor, that Tyrion Veltras took the trebuchets from him, and that tens of thousands died.

Ryoka tells Laken that she suspects Lady Rie of being the traitor who ordered the attack on the Goblins at Lancrel and a member of the Circle of Thorns, since a [Detect Truth] spell can be fooled; Laken is rattled.
Belavierr offers Ryoka a deal that would let her see Ivolethe again, and Ryoka thinks of her dearest friend, raises her right hand with its missing fingers and sighs.

section: Book 14: the road south and the electronics
text: Ryoka eats a live bug while running with the dog Mousey, who has been with her nearly a week, and tells her not to say a word.

section: Book 14: the road south and the electronics
text: Ryoka tells Fierre she did not stop the fire tornado but turned it, and that the wind has become easier to ask since seeing it, because she learns by witnessing rather than studying.

section: Book 14: the road south and the electronics
text: Ryoka tells Fierre that Belavierr was a monster, that the Order of Seasons was right to go after her, but also true to herself and loved only her daughter.

section: Book 14: the road south and the electronics
text: Ryoka gives Mousey, an Aldasian warhound from Lord Gralton Radivaek's personal kennels, to the Pithfire Hounds to replace Dassa, then says she cannot keep a dog and mutters "I hate dogs".

section: Book 14: the road south and the electronics
text: Fierre has found the address of a Bronze-rank Human team backed by Magnolia Reinhart, whom Ryoka needs to meet for a personal reason; Ryoka puts the matter off until later.

section: Book 14: the road south and the electronics
text: Ryoka lunches with Fierre at The Huntress' Haven, relaxes and offers to leave when Madain complains; Madain says Alber has gone to another city.

section: Book 14: the road south and the electronics
text: Ryoka runs barefoot south to Laiss as the Wind Runner of Reizmelt, passing Alber, and finds that Magnolia's mansion there is staffed.

section: Book 14: the road south and the electronics
text: Ryoka asks a [Maid] at the mansion for Rose, Joseph, Imani, Galina and Troy, saying she is like them and Lady Magnolia knows her; the [Maid] refuses visitors, but the seven-foot Gnoll [Maid] Bekia lets her in.

section: Book 14: the road south and the electronics
text: Ryoka offers nearly all her gold, keeping twenty coins, to borrow the Earthworlders' tablets, smartphones, computers and MP3 players for two weeks, enough time to reach the High Passes.

section: Book 14: the road south and the electronics
text: Assassins attack Magnolia's mansion in Laiss, and Ryoka knocks out a female [Assassin] with a one-two combination of punches while Alber also fights; she sees Reynold drive the pink carriage through the Assassins.

section: Book 14: the road south and the electronics
text: Ryoka tells the Earthworlders they will be targets under Magnolia's protection, leads them and Alber out through the gates in the confusion, and says Magnolia is at war with the Assassin's Guild and whoever else opposes her.

section: Book 14: the road south and the electronics
text: Ryoka sends the Earthworlders to The Wandering Inn, where Erin can help them, rather than to the Unseen Empire and Laken, and asks Alber to go with them while she finds a wagon and stays to see who wins.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka eats unpopped popcorn kernels from popcorn she made herself in Madain's kitchen, watching the Mage's Guild's scrying with Fierre, and she can still cast normal magic to warm it.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka is ejected from the Mage's Guild after expressing her vexation, and thinks she should send Erin a [Message] and gold and ask about Mrsha.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka believes she brings death and that she left Mrsha with Erin for safety, wondering whether it would be best if Mrsha forgot her.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka dictates a [Message] to Erin apologising for how she left and for letting Mrsha down, warning that people like her are coming to the inn, promising to return changed, and sending gold for Mrsha.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: In Fierre's office Ryoka explains sexuality terms to Fierre, saying that nothing is wrong about any way a person is, while aware of Fierre's attention and her own attraction.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka pushes Fierre away before they go further, saying she is attracted to her but has tried with boys and girls before and that her bad days ruin relationships; she says she left a little kid alone because she would burn everything down.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Rose tells Erin and Mrsha that Ryoka, whom people call the Wind Runner of Reizmelt and who can command the wind, was busy, had a boxer friend who hated them, and hired adventurers to escort them south.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka lives in Reizmelt on summer days and calls up the wind so that children race handcarts with cloth sails and parachutes.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka has stayed around Reizmelt rather than making major runs, boxing with Alber, spending time with Fierre, dining once at the van Lischelle household, and keeping friends in the Pithfire Hounds including the dog Mousey.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka feels the wind blow at her back and has a bit more control over it since visiting Riverfarm, but cannot conjure the tornado of wind and fire she raised there and does not run nearly as fast, relying on stamina potions.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka feels guilty about sending the Earthworlders to Liscor.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka carries a laptop and devices in her bag of holding, which she nearly touches near a [Farmer].

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka tells Lupp that Belavierr met her one last time and offered a deal, with a time limit before summer reaches its zenith, which she turned down, telling the Witch to "eat shit"; she says she has something better than a [Witch] if she can get him on her side.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka tells Lupp that she has gotten her friends killed, people like her and others in Reizmelt such as Fierre and Alber, and that she left her mistakes behind in the south.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka boards the overnight carriage heading south after Alime vouches for her; the [Driver], Olat, says three carriages have been attacked for taking Runners, and when Ryoka asks if the Runner is Alevica the [Witch] she says she hates her guts.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka is thrown into the mud when a [Fireball] hits her carriage, and the masked Bloodfeast Raiders circle her; she thinks it is her fault and not Erin's.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka's bag of holding is loaded with sand and caltrops, and the Bloodfeast Raiders take her iPhone but dismiss her bag of holding as a poor one, missing the electronics in Teriarch's bag.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka runs towards Celum shouting a warning to a merchant caravan, a female [Farmer] and a group of riders; the caravan scatters, but the raiders kill the merchant and burn his wagon with [Fireballs].

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka knocks two raiders from the air with a blast of wind and throws her bag's contents into their faces, but the wind will not kill for her because she is fighting herself, and an arrow passes through her shoulder.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka believes the raiders came to Celum because of her iPhone, and that they would not have come if she had not been there.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka fights the memory loss placed on the raiders' victims and recalls that one raider was flying with wings and was a Drake, so an Oldblood Drake; the Receptionist says only six members have been identified, all Human, and that the Drake Cities deny the possibility.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: For her third wish, Ryoka makes Teriarch watch The Hobbit on Kevin's laptop; he objects to the Dragon's design but tears up at the Halflings, calling them Tamaroth's.

section: Book 16 and 17: Reizmelt and the return to Celum
text: Ryoka returns to Celum and comforts the children she lifts into the wind-driven parachutes, and Erin sees her; Ryoka says sorry for not coming back sooner and Erin hugs her, saying they missed her.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Ryoka returns to The Wandering Inn after running in shame from the deaths she brought to Liscor; she lifts Erin in a tight hug, and Erin refuses to let go, dragging and then carrying her down the street.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Mrsha hugs Ryoka around the neck and cries when Ryoka walks up to her, holding a bit of ice that refuses to melt.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Ryoka runs to Calruz's jail cell, her hair mussed, her face pale, and two fingers missing from her right hand, with the wind blowing the scents of summer into his cell.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Ryoka tells Erin and Mrsha about a Vampire in Reizmelt, Fierre, secret even from others, who has red eyes, pointed teeth and once threw Ryoka like a ragdoll; Ryoka says Vampires burn in the sun and are sick, and that she carries a tiny vial that may help.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Ryoka shows Erin the tiny vial of panacea and says she told Fierre she would return and must go back to Reizmelt.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Ryoka raises a wind in the Garden of Sanctuary that lifts Mrsha under a bedsheet parachute, then realises she has brought aerodynamics to the world when Bird and Felkhr plan to jump off Liscor's walls.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Ryoka tells Teriarch she has an [Emperor] from her world who owes her a favour and has links to the fae, which makes him stare in disbelief.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Teriarch tells Ryoka that the fae came to Laken's gathering of nobles because he set a worthy stage, that they come again if such a gathering is made twice, and that a ball thrown by the [Emperor] at the Summer Solstice would be the third such celebration in recent memory.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Ryoka tells Erin that the Golden Triangle is a Ponzi scheme, more like a pyramid marketing scheme.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Ryoka sits with Relc for hours in his flat, working on his puzzles in silence, and then tells him "You did the right thing" as he leaves for Erin's inn.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Ryoka shared a bed with Relc and tells Erin it was not the first time she had sex since coming to this world, more like the third.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Ryoka leaves a small ice statue of Ivolethe under Mrsha's pillow as a promise to return after the Summer Solstice.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: The Runner's Guild lets Ryoka apply to meet requesters of high-risk Courier-level deliveries for [Lords] and [Ladies], on the strength of Alime's comments on her file.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Ryoka asks Fierre how to approach Ieka and receives the summary: innovative, magical, strongly dislikes Magnolia Reinhart and her circle, fond of pretty faces.

section: Book 17: back at The Wandering Inn
text: Ryoka leaves Invrisil to carry out the first of many requests for the Summer Solstice, hoping to wake an Archmage from seclusion.

Ryoka carries a vial of viridian panacea from Teriarch and wonders what causes Vampires to fall ill; she is returning to Reizmelt to prepare the party for the Archmage of Izril, having promised Mrsha she will return.
When the Silver Swords' Ylawes Byres, Yvlon's older brother, says someone wants to speak to her, Ryoka bolts from the coach and the Silver Swords chase her.
Ryoka sends letters to The Wandering Inn via the Minotauress Bezale and the Mage's Guild, so that those who care about her know where she is.
Ryoka returns to Mad Madain's inn, where Alber, Fierre and she eat bear with the Silver Swords who kidnapped her, and the Silver Swords make the inn their base while hunting Wailer Frogs.
Madain says Ryoka bailed out a team of Silver-ranks attacked by Wailer Frogs.
Ryoka needs a Scroll of Dispel Magic, which Fierre promises will arrive by tomorrow, for her big assignment for Lady Ieka, bringing the Archmage of Izril, unseen for a decade, to the Summer Solstice.

Ryoka tells Fierre that there may be other reasons contributing to her sickness besides being a Vampire, which she knows only as a hint from Teriarch that the panacea cures the symptoms but not the cause.
Ryoka is delivering Lady Ieka's message to the Archmage of Izril's mansion so that she can convene a meeting of the Fae at the Summer's Solstice.
Ryoka carries a jar of garlic and garlic oil mixed in water that she made after Fierre kidnapped her, in case she had to fight off Fierre.
Ryoka plays cards with magical decks in the coach, and Fierre travels under the name Fanni.
Ryoka and Fierre spend three days in the Unmarked Coach before reaching the mansion.
Ryoka has run deliveries before, to the Horns of Hammerad and through the High Passes to the Necromancer, but now puts her life on the line for a delivery in return for Lady Ieka's help.
Ryoka carries a [Detect Magic] amulet, a ring that deflects arrows, caltrops, sand, potions and six jars of Erin's acid, her trump cards being a bundle of cloth in her bag of holding and the acid.

Ryoka can sense the wind without seeing it, though it sometimes fails her when she asks it to blow hard; she needs a teacher, but Teriarch has offered insights and she has learned to call the wind stronger since the fire at Riverfarm.
Ryoka tosses a handkerchief parachute tied to a stick towards the mansion and finds that it flies straight through the mansion's walls, showing the mansion is a fake.
Ryoka wakes in a cell with a glowing barrier across from Fierre and a Courier, Salamani; her neck is healed from where Fierre had bitten her after throwing her into a wall.

Ryoka spends two hours rolling her bag of holding into her cell with wind, only to find the glowing runes of the cell block the bag's useful items, then pushes an enchanted sword half into Salamani's cell so that he can scrape away the barrier runes and free all three.

After freeing the cells, Ryoka, Fierre and Salamani loot the Archmage's holding area for Gold-rank gear, leaving Ryoka with dozens of scrolls, top-grade potions, six wands, three enchanted weapons and armour, noting that bags of holding must not be taken outside the cells.
Ryoka decides that the death trap makes the delivery a bad one and that they should retreat, as even Couriers turn down bad deliveries.

Ryoka, Salamani and Fierre drunkenly cast spells at Archmage Valeterisa's mansion and shout for her to come out until she appears with nearly a hundred shadow familiars, an army of Golems and a giant maw of shadows.
Ryoka jokes that she will have to live as a Vampire from now on.
Ryoka reckons that she has won her reward for the impossible delivery, with only a few more impossible tasks for the Summer Solstice party before she can meet her friend who died.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka Griffin, the Wind Runner of Reizmelt, becomes famous for waking the Archmage Valeterisa, which no one had done in ten years.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Mihaela Godfrey declares that Ryoka failed the Courier's test but is certified as a City Runner, and that she will break the legs of anyone at Celum and Invrisil who keeps barking about her record.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka lists to herself every action Fierre took, including the panacea three days earlier, which made her stronger and faster before making her more allergic to garlic and nearly killing her in the sun.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka breaks Falene's spectacles to make a crude microscope, magnified with a [Farsight] spell, and finds black silver particles in Fierre's dried vomit.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka realises that the silver has been poisoning the Vampires through House Byres' tradition of well seeding, so everything in their water, animals and crops carries it, and that this is why they are sick and short-lived.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka saves Fierre by having her washed with Liscor soap, made to vomit with pure water and fed burned charcoal, and then gives her blood: Fierre bites her neck, which tingles pleasantly, until Himilt stops her; Ryoka passes out after hugging her.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: In the field Ryoka murmurs to an angry wind in the west, and it seizes her; Fierre and Rivel pull her down, and the wind slams all three to the ground, cracking Ryoka's ribs and breaking Rivel's arm; she says someone has angered the wind.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka runs through Reizmelt's gates to cheers of "Wind Runner" and requests for autographs because she woke the Archmage of Izril; she reflects that no one knows of her greater runs, including the Goblin Lord's army, the Necromancer, a Dragon and the Bloodfields.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka wonders whether House Byres had good reasons for poisoning the Vampires.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka plans to visit Invrisil, where Hedault owes her a favour, to see Lady Ieka; Salamani's [Haste] spell fails on her until she removes a looted anti-enchantment necklace.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Over two thirds of the way to Invrisil, Ryoka collects a letter from Mrsha at the Mage's Guild saying the Raskghar have left the dungeon and are prisoners in the city but Nokha is not among them.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka arrives at The Wandering Inn with Fierre and Salamani and hugs Mrsha.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka has [Twofold Rest], arrives exhausted after running into the night, and sits quietly with Mrsha at dawn.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka tells the Pallass Magus Grimalkin that whoever informed Pallass about the Earthers knew nothing of value, and that some Humans are idiots or wrong about basic mathematics and medicine.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka tells Grimalkin that Magnolia Reinhart let the Earthers she helped away because she had no use for useless things, and she refuses to go to Pallass to meet Grand Strategist Chaldion.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka makes her bed in the room she shares with Mrsha and, having once gone through a hair-dye phase, is almost tempted to dye her hair with Octavia's magical dyes before dismissing the idea.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka realises she has missed Mrsha's birthday.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka tells Lady Ieka that she has already been tested for Courier and failed, and Salamani confirms that Mihaela Godfrey herself met her.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka stops insisting that dangerous Earth knowledge be hidden: she tells Erin the bicycle is likely to be big and to patent it, explaining that she once trusted no one, not even herself, but is no longer the sole owner of dangerous knowledge or an absolute authority on morality and the future.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka asks Erin, Rose, Joseph, Kevin, Imani and Galina, but not Leon or Troy, to come into the inn for another talk, leaving a hurt Fierre outside.

section: Book 19: fame, silver and the Earthers
text: Ryoka, introduced as 'batman', takes a call to Elena, whose side includes members of the Elusive Lot, who keep the spell active and listen in; Elena says she is allied with Ullsinoi, and Ryoka rates the security six out of ten and proposes keeping anything extremely important secret.
Sacra is a [Maid] in Lady Magnolia Reinhart's service whose specialty is undercover work.
Sacra wears boots that do not match the rest of her maid outfit.
Sacra fights with a mace, which she prefers in combat.
Reynold and Sacra caught the last assassin as he tried to flee Magnolia's estate, and he is dead.
As Odveig, she is a [Macewoman] and the self-proclaimed leader of the Celestial Trackers, with the [Witch] Wiskeria as her subordinate.
Laken senses that Odveig is paranoid that Wiskeria might take her place as leader.
Odveig has an accent that runs "not a" together as one word, which makes Laken think of Scotland.
Odveig and Wiskeria told Laken the rumour of a Great Goblin Chieftain living on a mountain called Dwarfhalls Rest.
Odveig said women were found outside the gates of Merendia after a Goblin tribe left them there, but she called it rumour and hearsay.
Odveig says the Goblins still in the mountain are angry after a tribe splintered from it.
Odveig found the site where Beniar was attacked, with no sign of Fabiel or his horse, and pulled back feeling watched.
Odveig revealed herself to Laken as a spy, knocked out Durene and Wiskeria with her mace, and gave her real name as Sacra.
Sacra told Laken that Lady Magnolia would be very interested to speak with him after her report, "if you survive."
Sacra then left the cottage and rode out of the village on a horse.
Laken and Durene discuss that Odveig worked for Magnolia Reinhart and posed as a Silver-rank team leader.
Later, Laken refers to Wiskeria as loyal all along after it was revealed that Odveig was the spy.
Reynold knew Sacra as one of Magnolia's special servants, like him, who had trailed Ryoka in Invrisil.
Sacra told Reynold of her undercover mission to learn who Ryoka met, and that the stranger was an [Emperor].
Sacra served as a mace-wielding armoured battle analyst beside Magnolia in the field, since Ressa was absent.
Magnolia regrets that Odveig was outed as a spy but says such is the cost of Sacra's work.
Magnolia asks Sacra for her impression of Laken, whom she met in person.
Sacra visited Wiskeria in her maid uniform and told her that Sacra is her true name.
Sacra says Laken knows she is a spy and has at least three people watching her.
Laken keeps two watchers on Sacra at all times.
Sacra says Magnolia is concerned about Laken because he is an [Emperor].
Sacra and Reynold beat a fleeing [Thug Boss] in Invrisil and left him to the Watch.
The Thug Boss claimed Magnolia is hands-off with Invrisil, and Reynold said that is what people say.
Safry is a Human [Barmaid] who works at Agnes' inn, the Frenzied Hare, alongside Maran, an older [Barmaid] and her friend.
Safry is a Level 21 [Barmaid], according to Maran, while Maran is a Level 22 [Barmaid].
Safry and Maran claim to be the highest-leveled workers at Erin's inn.
Safry says she worked at Agnes' inn for over eight years.
Safry asks Erin to hire her, then calls Maran over, and the two say they do not like working at Agnes' inn.
Safry and Maran say Agnes screams at staff over wrong orders and docks pay for breaks, and that she is tight with her coin.
Safry says Agnes told her she would be fired if she did not work with a terrible cold, though Maran was down with the same illness.
Safry says Agnes is only Level 18 despite nearly a decade at the inn, and that Agnes' husband holds the cooking Skills.
Safry says Agnes is afraid of Erin, a Level 20 [Innkeeper] at least, because her inn earns ten times more since Erin came.
Erin hires Safry and Maran along with Drassi and Ishkr to help Lyonette run the inn.
Safry and Maran treat Lyonette's advice as suggestions and think of themselves as in charge.
Safry serves a Drake the wrong food and cannot tell Drakes apart, saying they all look the same.
Safry serves Gold-rank adventurers first, leaving Zel for last, hoping to be tipped.
Safry says Gold-rank adventurers throw gold around like water and tip a gold coin just for serving their table.
Safry and Maran flirt with Halrac, Ulrien and Typhenous of Griffon Hunt.
Safry and Maran are visibly uncomfortable around Bird and walk wide of him.
Safry pushes Mrsha off a table onto the floor, and Lyonette threatens her until Ishkr drags Lyonette back.
Safry and Maran bring about two dozen Human friends and take a thirty minute lunch break at the height of the rush.
Safry and Maran say the Innkeeper's Guild policy gives them a break, and Erin agreed to it.
Safry quits, saying she deserves better treatment than Lyonette gives, and Maran says she will quit too if Safry does.
Erin fires Safry and Maran for their conduct, saying she believes Ryoka and Lyonette.
Safry and Maran claim Agnes will not take them back and demand pay from Erin.
The inn's [Inn's Aura] Skill terrifies Safry and Maran into fleeing the inn into Octavia's shop.
Salamani is a Human [Mage] and Courier with a trace of Lizardfolk in him, almost completely human but with slitted pupils like a lizard's.
Salamani says his lizard-like eyes are a gift from his Lizardfolk parents.
Salamani has high levels and experience and had prepared well for his run to the Archmage.
Salamani refers to Wistram as home, saying the academy makes Golems up to Autonomous-Combat types.
Lady Ieka Imarris massively inflates her reward to entice Salamani into reaching the Archmage before Ryoka, so Ryoka does not die on a suicide mission.
Salamani does better than projected in Valeterisa's mansion but loses his objects, and his mental charm breaks against the repeated glyphs.
Shadow familiars carry Salamani, babbling, into a holding cell, and he languishes there for about a day.
Salamani meets Ryoka in the cells, having been told of her by Fierre and Ieka, and explains the trap to her.
Salamani says Valceif had a charm that could have beaten the insanity trap but lost it.
Salamani agrees that the trapped hallway means a bad delivery, and he, Ryoka and Fierre leave the mansion.
The three drunk intruders burn the isle with spells and shout for the Archmage, with Salamani casting [Message] and [Fireball].
Salamani drops a scroll when Valeterisa appears with about a hundred shadow familiars, Golems and a giant shadow maw.
Salamani sends Ieka a note that the Archmage is awake, ceding credit for the delivery to Ryoka Griffin and requesting hazard pay.
Salamani says he gave all credit to Lady Ieka for Ryoka, and says he owes Ryoka and Fierre his entire life.
Salamani offers to help Ryoka get a Courier's certification and to give her all the artifacts he took, telling her to call on him.
Salamani casts [Haste] on Ryoka, which fails because of an anti-enchantment artifact, and she must remove her necklace for it to work.
Salamani plans to buy a spellbook with a Tier 6 spell and a Golem, such as a hulking fighting type or a Golem horse.
Salamani says Illivere is by far the best place to commission Golems and Wistram makes up to Autonomous-Combat types.
Salamani says House Terland, further north than Reizmelt, buys all the Golems.
Salamani is bushed from casting [Haste] on all three of them and does not remember meeting Mrsha.
Salamani says he ran a joint delivery with the Moonlight Rider, Tritel, which was a warning to [Assassins], and brought him free drinks.
Salii is a Drake woman who appeared in Pomle one day, found Orjin and began acting as his secretary, and no one stopped her.
Salii carries a clipboard and is a [Secretary]; one scene calls her Pomle's Drake [Receptionist].
Salii is high-level and once blocked a wind-slash with her clipboard.
Salii can copy any object of a secretarial nature once per day, which is how she makes paper and sometimes ink.
Salii says she can copy any material she wants once a day.
Salii has a [Memo] Skill that works like a free [Message], with limited range, and her messages are priority-delivered even to monarchs.
Salii says she comes from Zeres, where she organised everything for its commanders and was the best [Secretary] in Zeres and perhaps Izril.
Salii wants to become the highest-levelled [Secretary] in the history of the world, and says her level is higher than Orjin's.
Salii copies the Emperor of Sands' letter, since their silencing spells cannot stop a [Secretary]'s Skills, and gives it to Orjin.
Salii, clutching her clipboard like a shield, stands behind Orjin when he ends the fight among the rulers.
Salii leads Tiqr's refugees to temporary camps, introducing herself and Orjin.
Salii tells Orjin that Pomle will run out of food if more refugees arrive.
Salii says she can feed the refugees by trading, scavenging and organisation, calling herself the greatest [Secretary] in all the Walled Cities.
Salii tells Orjin that the King of Destruction is speaking to the Empress of Beasts by communication spell on the eve of Tiqr's fall.
Salii calculates that Pomle has taken in over sixty thousand of Tiqr's citizens.
Salii warns Orjin that the Windcaller's Wrath is a cult.
Salii says that if the water runs out Pomle dies, and with the new arrivals it would last 67 days.
Orjin says the water had run low before, and that some of Pomle's warriors would have to leave for a time.
Salii has ordered healing potions from Nerrhavia in bulk with funds from Pomle's treasury, a vault she holds the key to.
Salii pays Trader Melkhit, a Stitch-Man, with a bag of gold for a shipment of hundreds of healing potions.
Salii charged refugees who stayed a fee to buy land around the oasis and to compensate the [Martial Artists] who had to move.
Salii runs a betting arena, with an announcer named Raul reading levels, classes and odds into a scrying mirror.
Salii avoided Wistram for the scrying network and went to Nerrhavia and Khelt instead, because Wistram likes controlling everything.
The arena's scrying network has about three hundred viewers, and the pot for one fight was fifty-nine gold, sixteen silver and two copper.
Salii says Fetohep of Khelt watches and usually bets thousands of gold pieces, and he paid for the condensation stone.
Saliss of Lights is Pallass' resident Named Adventurer, and Lasica says he was arrested in front of Erin on her first visit.
Chaldion introduces Saliss Oliwing as the highest-leveled [Alchemist] in Pallass, perhaps the world, and its only permanent resident Named-rank adventurer.
Chaldion says the Assembly of Crafts has given Saliss immunities, so he does what he pleases even in prison.
Lasica says Saliss is arrested every other week for nudity but is above the law because the city needs him too badly.
Saliss is a Drake with dusky yellow scales and a slim, tall frame, who is usually completely naked.
Saliss says he is arrested at least once a week for stripping whenever clothes go on him.
Saliss says his Skills help him resist effects on his scales, so spilled substances usually ruin only his clothes.
Saliss also calls nakedness an act of expression, a protest against Drake society and its shackles.
Saliss says he wanted to be a [Performer], and he dances very well.
Saliss says he makes poisons.
Pallass' citizens call him a naked bastard, their number one nuisance and an insane [Alchemist], but also treat him as their own.
Grimalkin says Saliss has one of the highest if limited combat potentials in the world and could kill Grimalkin if he caught him off guard.
Grimalkin keeps a list of everyone who could kill him in combat, and Saliss is on it.
During the Wyvern attack on Pallass, Saliss tests three liquids on variant Wyverns and ignites them with [Flash Sparks].
Saliss tells the Watch he missed the alarm because his laboratory is soundproof, and says he hates Chaldion.
Saliss drinks two potions, one of them a Potion of Speed, and runs up the staircases throwing potions from his bag of holding.
Noass announces Saliss as the Named Adventurer rumoured to have the highest attacking power in the world and a pure [Alchemist].
Saliss clears a path up the stairs alone and onto the walls, and the city shouts his name.
Saliss dances naked outside the 4th floor Watch House hoping to be arrested, but no one reacts.
Saliss tosses Watch Captain Qissa a vial for frostbite before he runs off.
In Book 19, Saliss kills over thirty Raskghar in less than a minute, and Erin sees the bodies.
Palt says Saliss is called the most dangerous Named Adventurer for five minutes, and Palt would hate to be on his bad side.
Saliss throws a bottle that catches a lightning bolt, and the glass turns black and opaque.
Saliss makes a Potion of Youth that lasts about a week and says he can succeed one time in ten on a good day.
Saliss says Erin's fire helps cut one of his processes, because its happy warmth works on an alchemical level.
Saliss says his best anti-aging potion gives about two years and is harder to make than the youth potion.
Saliss plans to take the youth potion to the Merchant's Guild to be auctioned and asks Erin not to tell anyone he can make it.
Saliss says Erin's fire burns fuel too fast but works on wood, and he feeds it charcoal or magicore while away.
Saliss says Erin's fire added another 6 percent chance of making the potion instead of it exploding.
Saliss says four [Alchemists] in the world can make Temporary Youth, and he is better than Xif, who thinks they are equals.
Saliss says reverse aging makes people go crazy, so no sane [Alchemist] advertises it.
Saliss lists Talent Potions as rare, says Blademaster Draughts exist, and has heard the best [Alchemists] brew Luck Potions.
Saliss says [Witches] can brew potions that make a drinker literally drink life.
Saliss tests a drop of Ryoka's leftover Haste Potion with a magical condensing test, forming a thumb-sized mana crystal.
Saliss is stunned that the crystal is larger than his Youth Potion's, and Xif, listening through the speaking stone, demands to be let in.
Saliss keeps a cupboard of gemstones sorted by purity and size, bought from Salazsar.
Saliss' hidden laboratory is run-down, with a concealed door and a speaking stone on the counter.
Saliss carries a bag of holding full of potions, including blast potions and poison gas clouds that he calls his arsenal.
Saliss says Xif can make antidotes when a broker pushes him to produce one.
Saliss meets Erin in prison and introduces himself, saying he knows Xif, Rufelt and Lasica and had seen the flower Xif bought.
Saliss says he can see basic facts about Erin but no Skills, and calls her a Level 40 [Magical Innkeeper].
Saliss says Rufelt and Lasica thought Erin was Level 30 and promises not to tell.
Saliss says Erin reached Level 40 before turning thirty, a feat also pulled off by the King of Destruction.
Saliss's cell door is unlocked and the [Guards] defer to him, and he works at a lab bench in his cell.
Saliss says he is still under arrest for general indecency but gets his cell open and equipment because of who he is.
Saliss compares Erin's blue fire to useless sad fire and tells her she is wallowing, then makes her think of other uses for it.
Saliss dances through the prison to cheer Erin up, unlocks her cell with a ring of keys and dances the Cha Cha Slide with her.
Prisoners shout at Saliss to put clothes on while Erin laughs until she cries, and the prisoners riot.
Chaldion says Guardsman Kel put Erin in a cell near Saliss, which is normally considered a kind of punishment.
Saliss enters The Wandering Inn naked and laughs at Erin's "noneya business" line, saying he needs to use it.
Lyonette orders Mrsha to cover her eyes, and Mrsha hides under her bed while Saliss argues with the inn's guests.
Saliss drinks a marked vial and sniffs the cake and Mrsha's room, then says the little Gnoll must be good at hiding.
Saliss says "Nice class" to Numbtongue and is not wary of him.
Saliss, mashing something in a mortar, is shown to have [Eyes of Appraisal], a Skill for an [Alchemist], and reads Erin's level, class and Skills.
Saliss names [Garden of Sanctuary] as the inn's Skill and says he had not worked it out much earlier than Chaldion.
Saliss throws Erin a ring of ruby-coloured metal with a crossed-out eye sigil, saying clothes are dangerous.
Saliss says he gave Erin the ring to bother old Chaldion and Grimalkin.
Rufelt tells Saliss he is not allowed in the inn without at least pants, and Saliss walks into Rufelt's bar naked anyway.
Saliss visits the inn naked, drops gold on the counter for chocolate, and Lyonette asks him to wear a towel.
Saliss pays for food but trades Erin a Potion of Speed and an Invisibility Potion for her chocolate.
Erin senses Saliss might have given her the potions even if she had brought nothing.
Saliss offers four, then eight, then sixteen potions for a faerie flower, and Erin refuses.
Erin thinks she sees an inner-Saliss, a calculating observer watching the outer dancer, which she finds familiar, like an inner-Erin.
Erin believes Saliss shares her odd desire to help people without always getting something in return.
Saliss says Erin gives her fire away for free or too cheap, and that Xif and he both got some.
Saliss arrives naked, finds Erin's box with a label reading "Warning: contains small nuts," and keeps it over his private parts.
Saliss says Chaldion's forces kicked people's teeth in during the riots and that he thinks they beat a few children.
Saliss sees the fiery-haired Maviola at the inn and stabs himself in the mouth with his fork.
Saliss runs into the inn out of chocolates after eating a box of thirty-six pieces in two days.
Saliss introduces himself to Rose, a nervous Human, as her best friend.
Saliss arrives at the inn in exhausted work pants, falls asleep on the floor and then in the garden.
Saliss slips a glowing potion labelled "Drink me" into Maviola's pocket.
Saliss demands every flower Erin can give him and tells her not to give Xif another.
Saliss has used nearly half of Erin's flower supply and sent one flower to Oteslia.
A gardener's letter addressed to Saliss and Xif asks for more flower samples, and Saliss webs Xif with a potion.
Saliss made Maviola a Potion of Youth with Octavia's help, giving it to her for free.
Saliss says he used nearly a hundred of Erin's flowers for a single potion and keeps that from Xif.
Saliss identifies Octavia's baking soda as trona ore and her matches as phosphorus with charcoal by tasting them.
Saliss says the alchemists' guild he never attends will buy Octavia's recipe, since Pallass keeps a registry crediting original inventions.
Saliss warns Octavia that one of her fluffy spore moulds is very toxic and should be kept from kitchens.
Saliss tells Octavia he bets Xif made a mistake by thinking Erin had only one special thing.
Saliss slips and calls Lyonette Octavia's [Princess], then explains it away as a Drake joke about stuck-up Humans.
Saliss teaches Octavia but says he cannot make her an apprentice because he does not do that.
Saliss says they bargained that Octavia will break Level 30 before they are done.
Saliss tells Octavia he will never ask her for anything sexual, illegal or wrong.
Saliss says he studied in Nerrhavia and compares a master and apprentice in bed to sulfur and fire.
Saliss drinks half a Talent Potion marked with a musical note and plays Numbtongue's beat on a string instrument.
Saliss offers the Talent Potion to Octavia and says he cannot make more.
Saliss and Xif teach Octavia a banned orgasm potion at Xif's shop, and Saliss gives Octavia the full dose.
Saliss says the Walled Cities banned such potions because too many ingredients went into them.
Saliss brings Chaldion a mincemeat pie baked by Erin that contains a Potion of Reverse Aging.
Saliss says the potion works best eaten with food, and Chaldion says he will not turn it down.
Saliss says he is up to two years of reversal now, and Chaldion remembers when it was one.
Chaldion is a hundred and six years old and looks about seventy.
Saliss answers Chaldion's question about when he will stop with "When you dance naked with me in the middle of Pallass."
Chaldion trusts Saliss' discretion, the only thing about him he trusts, and Saliss lets himself into Chaldion's home to eat popcorn naked.
Saliss lies on the floor of Erin's hallway, drinks milk with her and beats her in a single hand of poker by bluffing.
Saliss stands up to Xrn when she enters the inn and asks "Is it war? I'm asking for a friend."
Onieva insists she is Saliss and says she is as authentically Saliss as she is Onieva, which means Saliss and Onieva are one person.
Onieva's eyes are pale blue and yellow, her scales deep green, and she is taller than she had been a moment earlier when the Watch finds her.
Onieva calls Chaldion her grandfather and says she is a disappointment to him.
Onieva says Chaldion will not look her in the eye even after all she has done for Pallass.
Onieva says Saliss is the closest she can get to what Chaldion wants and she will not put on pants.
Onieva says she is keeping Chaldion alive until he will look at her.
Onieva believes that after Chaldion dies the Walled Cities will hunt and exile Turnscales.
Onieva confirms to Mirn that Zel Shivertail was a Turnscale and says she thinks he found her out.
Onieva sits at Mirn's bar in Pallass, where Turnscales and other people who do not fit gather as friends.
Onieva tells Chaldion Erin is Level 40 with Skills [Immortal Moment] and [Wondrous Fare], and wonders whether Erin is on their side.
Onieva asks Chaldion who Xrn is, and Chaldion says he will someday find out whether she is ally or foe.
Chaldion promises Onieva to learn it soon when she asks him to make it quick.
Teriarch asks Saliss why she hides her true form and wears an illusion, and Onieva walks away weeping.
Later, Onieva has rose and cobalt scales and is introduced to Selys as the black sheep [Layabout] funded by Saliss and Chaldion.
Onieva and Mirn are looking for a safe place for his bar, because the Watch's crackdown after the riots makes it harder.
Onieva claims to be Saliss' cousin after nearly saying "I'm Saliss of Light."
Onieva thinks Zel Shivertail's secret was an open secret in Izril's high society.
Onieva suspects Selys knows Zel's secret and decides the inn would be a perfect safe place.
Onieva notices Rose speaking about "back home" and leaves for Pallass determined to tell Mirn.
Salthorn is a Selphid [Martial Artist] and one of Pomle's masters, an expert in grappling.
Salthorn is the only Selphid in Pomle, since few Selphids could survive there given how hard it is to find new bodies.
Salthorn's body is old and desiccated, and her Skill lets it move and keep active with minimal wear.
Salthorn wears a carelessly worn uniform on a worn, half-rotten corpse, and her symbol is a falling giant.
Orjin would rather jump into a nest of giant flame ants than let Salthorn get an arm around him.
Salthorn brings a young Dullahan apprentice, Mendi, in her mid-twenties, to Orjin.
Mendi says Master Salthorn has taught her for eight months.
Salthorn pushes forward to find her apprentice on the ground after Iratze beats Mendi.
Salthorn teaches her pupil Mendi, a [Grappler], holds and submissions, including how to subdue a Dullahan by grabbing the head.
Salthorn says that if she touched the Death of Magic and broke her magic shields, she would never let go.
Salthorn teaches Iratze, a new pupil, to stop a Selphid, who a Human would need to break down by tearing muscles.
Salthorn advises Orjin that if he wants to fight enemies like the Death of Magic, he should buy a flying artifact and train with it.
Salthorn tells Orjin she cannot help him fight the Death of Magic, and that flying is the only reason a [Mage] would survive an encounter with him.
Salvia is a [Captain] from the city of Nonelmar and an old acquaintance of Gershal of Vaunt.
Salvia greets Gershal with a clash of gauntleted fists, which is her city's unique greeting.
Salvia is cheerful and teases Gershal about his tone, correcting him sharply when he calls her Lieutenant.
Salvia specifically requested the Invrisil posting so that she would be among the first to fight the Goblin Lord.
Salvia mocks Gershal's soldiers as Level 5 [Farmers] who have barely trained with bows for a month.
Salvia says she has orders not to join assaults on the Goblin Lord unless she can pull her cavalry out safely.
Salvia expects that half the officers in camp will refuse to commit to an assault either.
Salvia warns Gershal not to criticise Magnolia Reinhart where her people can hear.
Salvia kicks Gershal under the table for insulting the Knights of the Petal, who punish insults to their [Lady] or order.
Salvia says the pink-clad Knights of the Petal wear custom Dwarf-made armor enchanted by Wistram mages and carry magical weapons.
Salvia would want those knights charging into the Goblin Lord's ranks.
Salvia mutters to Gershal that someone has to destroy the Goblin Lord.
Captain Salvia leads [Riders] in hit-and-run charges against the Goblin Lord's army, wheeling away before the Goblins can catch them.
Salvia pulls a rider whose horse was shot into her own saddle and carries him back to the Human lines.
Salvia notes that the Goblins' Shield Spider riders are too slow to catch her cavalry.
Salvia waits for orders from General Shivertail or a [Strategist] between charges.
Salvia hopes that Gershal and his cheese-eating soldiers are unharmed while she charges a gap in the Goblin lines.
The Human cavalry in the battle numbers some six thousand horse and strikes Goblin rear lines before pulling away.
When the Goblin Lord's death magic and Goblin riders strike the cavalry, Salvia orders [Scatter Gallop] to break formation.
Salvia's own unit scatters successfully, but the rest of the cavalry, untrained in the technique, are hit by arrows and spells.
Sammial Veltras is the ten-year-old younger son of Tyrion Veltras and already has an aura that influences those around him.
Sammial is described as a Veltras born, fiery like his mother, with the Veltras rage and command, but he has a lot to learn about emotions.
Sammial is very good at most athletic things, and his [Fencer] instructor says he is a natural with a sword.
Sammial has had coughing fits since he was young, and his lungs were always weak, according to Tyrion.
Sammial bites his tongue hard while riding with Jericha, who heals it, and he blames her, saying it was a rock.
Sammial refuses to apologise to Jericha for striking her, and says he hates her.
Sammial spits at Jericha and shouts that she is just a servant, not his mother.
Tyrion spanks Sammial over his knee, and Sammial screams that he hates his father and wishes he had died too.
Sammial has a summer cold, fever and coughing the day after Tyrion rescues Magnolia Reinhart.
Sammial falls into a coma struggling for breath, as his airways close within a day, and the [Healer] cannot explain it.
Sammial worsens overnight and by morning is barely responsive, and a second [Assassin] arrives later that day.
Hethon and Sammial remain gravely ill while Tyrion sits staring at the blood contract left by the [Assassin].
Seborn is the [Rogue] of the Halfseekers, a Gold-rank team of part-humans also called the Half Freaks.
Seborn is a tall, gaunt man covered across half his body in a shell, and he has a crab arm.
Seborn is a Drowned Man, and he says he has been like this since he was a young man.
Seborn explains that Drowned is the name for everyone who suffered the fate of a sea creature latching onto and melding with their body.
Seborn's left side looks merged with a sea crustacean, including his left hand as a crab's claw, his face and his leg.
Seborn has a Human eye on one side of his face.
Seborn seldom laughs and speaks little, though Erin notes he talks more than usual when nervous.
Seborn is of the Sailwinds family and is a Gold-rank adventurer.
Seborn wields enchanted daggers and prefers to wound rather than kill.
Seborn's daggers carry acid and [Frostbite] enchantments, and he says acid, a thousand cuts that grow worse, suits a [Rogue].
Seborn says he hopes to change his other blade to lightning if the team gets a big payout, since lightning paralyses and weakens muscles.
Seborn can slip into shadows and vanish from view even when watched.
Seborn uses the skills [Shadowsteps], [Blur Leap], [Cat's Evasion], [Flurry Blades] and [Rearward Cut] against Garen.
Seborn uses [Blur Leap] again in his brawl with Wailant.
Seborn is a trap expert, in the same role in his party as Halrac in his.
Seborn recognises the dungeon door's pressure mechanism and suggests a Bronze-rank adventurer could use a protected door as a shield.
Seborn explains that an enchanted mace shrieks like a Death Wailer, affects everyone but its wielder, and may also immobilise.
Seborn asks Ceria to consider selling the Horns' dagger when Typhenous and Revi bid for the ring.
Seborn scouts ahead of the Horns of Hammerad in the dungeon and tells them to stay about ten paces behind.
Seborn says he is a retired [Pirate], not a [Sailor], and a member of the Undersea Crews.
Seborn orders a Narwhal's Knife, a double, in the Pallass bar and says it tastes like a port-city bar's, only cleaner.
Seborn lists the worst waters to avoid: the Iron Vanguard's port cities, Wistram, Roshal, the Siren's territories and Zeres.
Seborn says he left the sea because he was sick of it, since land monsters are mild next to ship-eating whales.
Seborn says Crelers are as bad on land as in water.
Seborn says he sailed with The Siren's Depths, a crew of the Undersea Crews.
Wailant Strongheart says he sailed with the Steelsails Armada, whose ships The Siren's Depths sank in the past.
Seborn replies that the Steelsails Armada clashed with some of the Drowned Folk.
Wailant throws his drink into Erin's face and knocks the table over, and Seborn punches him, starting a brawl.
Seborn and Wailant, both [Pirates], agree that people who cast [Clear Skies] are idiots because it delays a storm and makes it worse.
On Noass's show, Seborn recognises the crew of The Passing Shadow and its [Depth Captain] Therrium Sailwinds.
Seborn says Therrium is a lawless [Thief], despised even by other Drowned Folk for breaking his word, and a backstabbing shrimp.
Seborn answers Noass's question about relation with a flat "Relation".
Captain Therrium addresses Seborn as "my boy" when Seborn locks eyes with him through the orb as if he were his father.
On the show, Seborn says he is there to advertise his team and tells viewers to hire the Halfseekers.
Seborn drinks like a sailor, and hungover after a party he jokes that he would shank himself to end the misery.
Ilvriss demands that the Gold-rank adventurers and Relc be unshackled and treated as guests rather than prisoners.
The Watch Captain says the Selphid, Guardsman Relc and the Drowned Man are staying and their weapons are being impounded.
Seborn performs a flip with glowing daggers in the victory parade after Jelaqua nudges him to show a trick.
Seborn tells Erin that Silver-rank teams risk their lives to reach Gold, and Golds become more cautious.
Seborn tells Erin that Named Adventurers are the ones who never stopped diving into the abyss, some heroes and most just insane.
Seborn plays in the Liscor baseball game, throwing the ball surprisingly fast as pitcher after Erin shows him how to pitch.
In the final, Seborn becomes the underrated player of Team B who steals bases and slips away from fielders.
Seborn later gets cornered between Dawil and Ishkr but is called safe because he never left the lines.
Seborn is annoyed that Jelaqua has been distracted for three days by Maughin, and tells Moore they need to get to work.
Seborn tells Moore that his romantic friends Moore, Jelaqua and Halassia need new teammates, and urges Moore to stop waiting for someone to love him.
Moore tells Mrsha that Seborn wants to get on the road.
Seborn refuses to walk to Invrisil while Jelaqua is seeing Maughin, so Moore charges the door for him and Moore to Pallass.
Seborn is in a poor temper since Jelaqua began dating Maughin.
Seborn tells Ulinde that her body is disgusting and that she can borrow one of Jelaqua's bodies.
At the inn, Seborn comes out of a shadow behind the Selphid Ulinde, chokes her with one arm and stabs her chest repeatedly with a flaming dagger.
Ulinde survives and later moves as fast as Seborn when Rampaging, and she cannot lose him as they dodge around the inn.
Seborn joins Jelaqua and Moore walking north with a door when they meet the Redfangs and Garen in the pass.
Seborn utters an oath on seeing Garen and straightens when Jelaqua names him.
Seborn shakes hands with Jelaqua before the team attacks Garen, and reaches for his daggers.
Seborn charges silent as Jelaqua leaps and Moore bellows.
Seborn leaps over the Carn Wolf riders to fight Garen and cuts a horse and a Goblin with both blades.
Seborn is roughly Garen's level but, as a [Rogue], cannot win head-on, yet he fights on without fear.
Garen uses [Frenzy Cuts] and then his transparent Redfang to cut open Seborn's side and carapace.
Seborn shatters a potion across his wounds and goes on fighting, shouting "traitor" at Garen.
A flashback shows Garen arguing with Seborn over an acid dagger, with Seborn the cold voice of reason in the team.
Seborn tells Garen that the old teammates tried to take the key, but Garen struck first and stabbed three of them before they could move.
Seborn agrees that threatening to kill Garen was absolutely justified to stop a Goblin King.
Seborn says Halassia and Ukrina were right about a Goblin King, because one cannot appear again, but that Garen was wrong to attack them.
Seborn says Garen attacked them and that what he remembers was murder.
After Garen dies, Seborn says Garen was a traitor regardless of how he died, and looks away from the body.
Seborn says that Garen's key is gone and that he has debts and obligations, and he is unsure whether to quit.
The Halfseekers burn Garen's body, find no key on him, and Jelaqua proposes one more adventure.
Seborn watches over Moore as he panics dancing, wondering whether to help him apologise or kick him.
Bevussa winks at Seborn during the dance.
