Seborn feels larger when Palt's illusion makes all the dancers look as tall as Maughin and Moore.
The Seer of Steel is the leader of the Iron Vanguard, a company of northern Dullahans.
Ken says the Seer of Steel is a [Juggernaut] whose body is made of the most expensive armor money can buy.
Geneva says the Seer of Steel never goes into battle with his head, but leaves it in his fortress and controls his body through a scrying orb.
Geneva says that way only his body can be hit, so he is practically impossible to kill, or so it is said.
The Seer of Steel speaks through a scrying orb in a booming, rumbling voice, in capital letters.
The Seer of Steel tells Tulm not to regret a defeat, because he quite enjoyed it.
The Seer of Steel tells Tulm to uncover the Titan's answer, saying he will await him in person.
The Seer of Steel says that if the question is worth answering, then it is worth almost any cost, and tells Tulm to pay it.
Selys is a light green female Drake who works as a receptionist at the Adventurer's Guild in Liscor, smaller than Relc and with thinner limbs.
Selys is a close friend of Erin Solstice and one of Erin's earliest Drake contacts in Liscor.
Selys is the niece of Zel Shivertail, whom she calls Uncle Zel, and the granddaughter of Tekshia Shivertail, who is her boss.
Selys is a young Drake just past twenty years old, stubborn and opinionated, who dresses stylishly.
Selys introduces herself to Erin at the Adventurer's Guild counter and tells her humans are rare so far from the coast, since they usually stay in their own cities.
Selys has the Skill [Fast Stitching] from having stitched up adventurers at the Guild.
When Erin asks for thin soft fabric, Selys fetches Guild bandages and suggests washing and reusing the pads rather than throwing them away, then offers to sew them for Erin.

After Klbkch's apparent death, Selys urges the grieving Erin to stay in the city for the night and offers to find her a job as a Guild receptionist, but Erin refuses and insists on going back to her inn.
Selys tells Erin that the Watch keeps the really bad monsters away from the inn and that without it Erin would be in danger.
Selys sits with Erin and tells her the adventurers now arriving from further south ignore the laws more, so the Guild gets many complaints.
Selys works at the packed Guild with three other receptionist Drakes, overworked by the crowd of adventurers.

Selys cowers in front of Toren in Erin's inn, and Pisces recognises her as the Guild receptionist who often talks to Erin; she threatens a twenty-gold bounty on him if he raises undead within twenty miles of the city.
Selys tells the northern adventurers Gerial and Ceria about a persistent Human messenger bothering the city on behalf of Lady Magnolia.
During the undead attack on Liscor, Selys raises a bow against a zombie, which splits the bow in two with one blow.
After the attack, Selys has become a [Warrior] and gained several levels in her [Hunter] class, her first level-up in a month.
Selys is a Level 4 [Warrior].
Selys wakes in a room at The Wandering Inn in the same bed as Krshia, with both their clothes missing; Krshia says nothing happened.
Selys tells Erin that all the best human adventurers went down with the Horns of Hammerad.
Selys tells Erin that the Frost Faeries follow Relc for a week each winter, causing mischief, and that the people of Liscor regard them as a force of nature rather than as creatures.
Selys doubts that the Council or the army will act against the conqueror threatening the north, expecting Chandrar to unite against him instead.

Selys says that if she had trained with a sword when young she might be near Level 12 now, and that reaching Level 20 in a second class would probably take at least a decade; only someone like Ceria has time to level more than one class.
Selys confirms she is Level 4 as a [Warrior].
On her day off Selys takes over Erin's burger table, crosses out Erin's price and doubles it, and keeps raising it; a customer named Hawk pays a silver.
Selys tells Erin she raised the subject of males with Krshia out of curiosity, and when put on the spot says she has just stuck with Drakes since Gnolls have so much fur.

Selys says Relc, a soldier even if retired, might be good for one night before chasing someone else, and privately thinks he is ugly; she finds Olesm good-looking, a [Tactician] with good prospects and many admirers.
Selys bets Krshia fifteen copper that Erin takes a Drake partner before a Gnoll.
Selys and Krshia each give Erin a wooden replica gift, a Drake one from Selys and a larger Gnoll one with a knot from Krshia.
Selys told Erin that Level 20 is not high, since almost everyone reaches it before they die.
Selys secretly gets Pisces to carry a message to Erin about a thief girl abandoned in the snow, promising in return to approve his request as a Bronze-rank Guild member.
Selys is one of the older and most experienced receptionists at the Liscor Guild, and her grandmother is the Guildmaster.
Selys has the [Warrior] class but is no fighter and does not want a brawl inside the Guild.
Yvlon avoids owing further debts to Selys or to the Guildmaster, who is Selys' grandmother.
Selys has not heard of Lady Magnolia Reinhart, as she pays little attention to famous Humans beyond some adventurers and teams; Relc says he knows "The Deadly Flower".
Selys exclaims that Magnolia is a hero who helped beat the Antinium both times.

Selys avoids Relc after he flirted with her on the way to the inn and calls him muscly, arrogant and selfish, preferring better-looking males; she begins to say she is almost the same age as his d- before he interrupts.
Selys stands up beside Erin when she faces down Relc, shaking with nerves, and afterwards tells Erin that Relc once beat up over forty people and that even Watch Captain Zevara is careful with him.
Selys says no one in Liscor has [Expert Cooking] and that it would need a very high-level [Chef], around Level 30 to 40.

Selys laughs at Ryoka's theory that levels slow because of accumulated classes, insisting they slow with age; after Klbkch says Ryoka's theory matches his own stalled main class, she breathes "Dead gods" and agrees to keep it secret.
Selys then worries that her many classes mean she will never reach a high level.
Selys offers to take Mrsha for the day to the playground in the city, since she has a day off.
Selys sends Erin and Ryoka a [Message] saying that Mrsha is with her, Olesm is watching the inn, and she has told Klbkch and Relc.
Selys faints on opening the door of the inn to the Soldier Antinium Pawn.

Selys asks in alarm why Soldiers are above ground and whether it is war, and tries for twenty minutes to drag Mrsha out of the inn before collapsing; she is eventually reconciled to Mrsha staying with Lyonette.
Selys brings toys for Mrsha at the inn, saying Mrsha never wanted to play with them at her apartment.
Selys is delighted when Uncle Zel visits the city, feeling lighter and refreshed at her desk at the Guild.
At the Winter's Solstice party Selys kisses Pisces under the mistletoe for a laugh and the cheering room, then pulls another Drake in for a kiss.
Selys works at the Guild and is Erin's friend; Drassi is her fellow receptionist friend, whom she tells Erin about.
Selys tells the Horns of Hammerad that, after talking with her grandmother the Guildmaster, they are not yet certified Gold-rank and must prove themselves on requests.
Selys refuses Pisces's request to put a creation in the sewers, saying her grandmother is the Guildmistress and dislikes [Necromancers] even more than she does.

Selys's parents died in the Necromancer's siege of Liscor when she was young: her mother, shooting enchanted arrows at Draugr, was killed from behind by a wraith, and her father charged a Carcass Walker with [Ram's Charge] and fell with it; his body was never found.
Selys visits her grandmother Tekshia at least weekly; Tekshia is the Liscor Guildmaster and Selys's boss, and withholds her pay if she does not appear.
Selys tells Tekshia that Pisces saved her and Erin in the undead attack and killed more undead than anyone she saw; Tekshia dislikes having a [Necromancer] in the city and the Guild.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys runs the Adventurer's Guild desk in Liscor and grins at newcomers who do not know the city.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys agrees to do the paperwork for Erin's plan, though she thinks it insane and will never work.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: During the Giant Moth attack Selys distributes potions, herds civilians into the Guild's back rooms, and orders lower-ranked adventurers out to fight; Hawk the Courier kicks apart a group of moths, and she hands him a stamina potion.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys is a Level 18 [Receptionist] and also holds Level 1 [Soldier] from Liscor's mandatory training; she has not levelled in about eight months.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys learned to use a sword and bow at her aunt's insistence, and as a girl of twelve once practised with a sword and begged Zel to teach her claw fighting.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys tells Tekshia that Pisces is a good kisser.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Only two Shivertails live in Liscor, Selys and Tekshia; there were once four, including Selys's father and her mother, who married in.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: At Zel's will reading, Selys is left whatever personal effects were on his corpse, which makes her the heir to the Heartflame Breastplate.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys wakes with the class [Heiress] at Level 4, gaining [Increased Income] and [Lingering Presence].

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys's parents died when the Necromancer attacked the city, and she compares the funeral to her parents'.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Ilvriss states that under Drake law the Heartflame Breastplate is legally Selys's, having passed from Magnolia Reinhart to Zel and then to her by his will.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys tells Pisces his Bone Horror was poorly designed for the sewers and advises armour, ranged bone spikes like a Spiked Stalker, and a larger hunter; she then approves four more undead patrolling the sewers without Tekshia's permission.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys once kissed Pisces and would rather not talk to him.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys is kidnapped in Pallass by thugs and knocked out as she shouts for help.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys breaks free of a captor by jabbing two clawed fingers into his eye and kicking him.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: As a girl Selys tells Zel she will be a more famous Named Adventurer than him; she says her grandmother is teaching her the sword and that she may enter the sewers at fifteen.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys fears that selling the armor to the wrong city would see her treated as a traitor and blacklisted in Pallass.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys and Pisces spend about two hours trying mage sounds and phrases, such as "Drakes do not run", on the armor with no effect.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys's circle of friends, including Drassi, Wuvisa and others, crowd round her for gossip about the armor, and Drassi reports that the Goblins in Erin's inn have artifacts.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys hisses angrily at Pisces and the Heartflame Armor bursts into pale flame; hissing, even subvocalised, turns the flame on and off.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys sees the flames turn slightly purple with a white core.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys decides to keep the armor, saying her uncle gave it to her.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys puts the armor on, finds it a perfect fit, and walks ten minutes to the Adventurer's Guild on fire, with the whole city watching.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys leases the armor to the Halfseekers for a share of whatever they find; Jelaqua counters with thirty percent.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys says her will sends the armor back to Magnolia Reinhart if she dies, a will sealed by Falene that lasts ten years.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: With Pisces, Relc and Klbkch as lookouts, Selys digs up the grave of General Sserys and pours Zel's ashes beside his coffin.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys haggles with Jelaqua in the inn over the percentage for the armor.

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Later that night Selys advances to [Receptionist Level 19] and [Heiress Level 6], gaining [Skill - Legacy Whispers: Heartflame Set].

section: Inheritance of the Heartflame Breastplate, Book 7
text: Selys receives in her mind a rhyme about finding the helm of fire in a village without rest where the Putrid One met his death.
Selys is a Guild receptionist whose grandmother Tekshia approves the Goblins' Bronze-rank paperwork, and she speaks to the Hobs about it.
Selys tells Drassi to keep Erin in the inn after the Council bars all Gnolls except adventurers from leaving the walls.
Selys tells Olesm she has been leasing the Heartflame Breastplate to the Halfseekers for 30% of their earnings.
Selys is tempted to quit her job; Maviss says everyone knows she is loaded after inheriting the Heartflame Breastplate and guesses at the amount.
Selys has a good bit over three thousand gold, perhaps as many as six thousand, from Jelaqua's cut and Ilvriss's rental fee for the Heartflame Breastplate.
Later, Selys becomes a Level 8 [Heiress] with no new Skill.
Selys has known the friends Mica, Warsh and Lellia since childhood; Mica is a Gnoll [Clerk], Warsh a Drake [Receptionist] and Lellia an apprentice [Spinner].
Selys buys three bolts of cloth from the Merchant Humric: blue and red, black-and-gold silk for her grandmother, and yellow cotton for a dress.
Selys realises her friends want her money and shouts at them in the street, telling Mica she will not pay for dresses or parties.
Selys carries her money in a twenty-pound safe and moves to a new apartment near the eastern gates, close to Market Street, after Tekshia steals gold from her.
Selys pledges four hundred gold to Krshia's campaign in return for a bigger Guild twice its size with more staff and money.
Selys offers to lend Zevara the Heartflame Breastplate in exchange for help, and they settle on three weeks, haggled down from four.
Selys realises she does not want to be an adventurer, since she can act indirectly by hiring people, bribing crowds and funding campaigns.
Later in the same chapter Selys becomes Level 11 [Heiress], gaining [Everything Has a Price] and the Inheritance [Shadow of His Name].
Selys, Krshia and Zevara form an alliance to force a Liscor Council election with one Council member per district.
At the election rally Selys sees Olesm holding his notes, punches at him and throws her notes at his face, and a brawl breaks out between Lism's and Krshia's supporters.
Selys has leased the Heartflame Breastplate to Keldrass, and the City Watch stores it in its vaults when it is not being worn.
When Erin leads Maughin and Grimalkin down the street, Selys realises Erin never planned the visit around the election, although the crowd follows and leaves Lism's street nearly empty.
Selys uses the Skill [Everything Has A Price] to ask Xif what Erin's flower is worth; he says two thousand gold pieces.
Selys introduces herself to the bartender Rufelt as a [Receptionist], correcting herself to [Heiress].
Selys scolds Pisces for not helping Krshia's campaign and for helping Olesm write his chess letter.
Selys opposes Pisces's suggestion of excluding Servail Street's four hundred Drake voters, calling it cheating; Pisces calls it strategy.
Selys advises Pisces to give his skeletons armour and crossbows, and Pisces explains that running zombies come from charged zones with high ambient mana.
Selys is now an [Heiress] with a magical vault full of gold; Keldrass still rents the Heartflame Armor from her even after getting Raskghar armor.
Selys has the Skill [Incisive Comment], useful for getting things into thick heads.
Selys, who has never left Liscor, knows about [Pirates] and [Sailors] because she studies classes as part of her job.
Selys tells Pisces she is thinking of telling him about her class and the breastplate, saying that something may be on Izril.
Selys has her memory wiped by [Mind Blank] and is left standing vacant in the street; Palt later says it will wear off in an hour.
Selys is described as niece to the Tidebreaker Zel Shivertail, granddaughter of Tekshia, an [Heiress] and the most eligible bachelorette in Liscor; she bids on a plot in the new city.
Selys has glossy scales, new clothes and a collection of magical artifacts.
Selys says rich Drakes pay about a hundred gold to wear the Heartflame Breastplate for a week and that Keldrass is paying her.
Selys buys land and plans apartments for any species but mainly Humans, with Antinium labour; she housed nearly forty Players of Celum and families in a night and plans them as her first tenants.
Selys plans soundproofed Gnoll apartments and will ask Krshia, Elirr and Raekea about rent.
Selys thinks low rent is solved by building competition.
Selys offers to pay half of Erin's six hundred gold Sage's Grass cost in exchange for free access to Pallass through the door, which she says would be worth three hundred gold.
Selys has bought plots in the new district and is building apartments and warehouses to rent with Antinium Workers.
Selys says she had sex the day before in her apartment with a casual partner; she says nothing happened with Pisces beyond a dare kiss and that she likes him.
Later, Selys tells Erin and Drassi that she and Hawk dated and it is casual.
Selys sits with Drassi at a Cream Tea cafe; she rents the Heartflame Breastplate to Keldrass for about three gold per day and no longer works much at the Guild.
Selys visits Pallass via Erin's door; Sir Relz Hauscale and Watch Captain Venim welcome her and Sir Relz offers to introduce her to society.
Selys is bored by having so much money and wants a purposeful investment; her apartment block, built by Antinium labour for Human tenants, has six floors.
Selys tells Erin she attended Sir Relz's invitation party with an auction, did not back any projects, and felt not that rich.
Selys breaks up with Hawk after they have seen each other for less than a month.
Selys offers to finance the bicycle project and pays down payments to Pelt and Hedault.
Selys and Maviola learn that Erin is from another world, Earth.
Selys sits up sleepless in the Earth rooms watching movies, shaken by the idea of a round world, and Galina says Maviola is fine.
Ser Raim is a [Summer Knight] of the Order of Seasons who has exceeded Level 50 and is one of the finest members of the Order.
Ser Raim is at the edge of his forties or the end of his thirties, in yellow, orange and gold armor.
Ser Raim's gaze burns as though fire flickers in his pupils.
Ser Raim carries the last torch of Paladin Arteis, a flame born of a long-dead Paladin's wrath.
Raim's flame burns magic and steel alike, and its source consumes his life while he lives.
Ser Raim and the Hunter's Guild have been hunting Belavierr, and the Summer's Champion calls it his battle.
Calirn says Raim injured Belavierr once this winter and she fled his flame.
Belavierr killed Raim's fiancee, the Autumn Knight Dame Fale, almost a decade ago, according to the Spring's Warden.
Ser Raim leads six [Witch Hunters] from Terandria on foot toward Belavierr, and declares her death ordained by the Hunter's Guild of Noelictus and the Order of Seasons.
Ser Raim names himself [Summer Knight] of the Order of Seasons and promises to bring Belavierr to justice for the dead.
Ser Raim uses [Aura of Righteous Fire], which melts Belavierr's needles before they touch him and sets a path of fire around him for twenty feet.
Ser Raim offers his own time and life through [Lifeburning Flames], invoking the last torch of Paladin Arteis.
Ser Raim then offers everything with [My Life, be Thou My Fire], and the flames burn the shadows themselves.
Ser Raim's sword sets Belavierr's tapestry alight, and his flames burn her despite her wards of ancient Dragonscale.
Belavierr sees her death coming in Raim for the first time in an age.
Ser Raim cleaves an artifact, stabs Belavierr in the chest, and later stabs her stomach a third time.
The [Hunters] use Raim's aura as a shield, letting him burn weaker puppets by his presence.
After the first clash Raim has aged, with grey hair and a lined face, as though he burned thirty years away in under thirty minutes.
Raim insists he has at least twenty more years to burn and that Belavierr will not escape a second time.
Raim tells Ryoka that Belavierr's Noelictus crimes include renting out Helpful Servants who were prisoners in their own minds, bound by a contract.
Raim tells Ryoka that Belavierr killed scores of people before the Order drove her from Noelictus.
Raim says he was a rather broken man until someone gave him a spark.
Raim abandons his honor and says he is a [Summer Knight] no longer, threatening to slay Belavierr's daughter unless she stands.
Raim tells Talia that if he falls none are to pursue Belavierr, and orders her to return to the Order.
Ser Raim walks to Belavierr as the Order of Seasons salute him, and Riverfarm's people cheer him on.
Ser Raim burns away his life, whispers his love's name, and dies, leaving Belavierr alive but mortal.
Belavierr's eyes no longer glow after Raim's death, and she does not remember her death's name.
Raim's ashes return aboard a black barge to Phel's Light, where Calirn and the Season of Summer receive them.
Raim is buried alongside his love, and is the highest-levelled Knight of those who had died there, by far.
Ser Thornst is a veteran [Spring Knight] who rides in Dame Talia's company hunting Ogres and Goblins.
Ser Thornst reminds the junior Ser Eldein that diplomacy is the other edge of a Knight's sword and that a Dragon should be addressed with words first.
A senior knight orders Dame Talia and Ser Thornst to choose four riders each and scout ahead of the company.
Ser Thornst agrees with Ser Eldein that their steeds cannot manage the rough, rooted foothills and that the knights must continue on foot.
Talia asks Ser Thornst to lead the horses back, saying he has a way with them, and he agrees.
Ser Thornst arrives at the scene after Talia meets the Goblin Slayer and stops on seeing him.
Ser Thornst nods in agreement as a knight remarks on the quality of the Goblin Slayer's light, well-fitted armour.
Ser Thornst frowns and questions the Goblin Slayer's count of fifteen female and ten male dead Goblins.
During the night fight with the Ogres, Ser Thornst is among the senior knights shouting Skills and concentrating their auras.
Ser Thornst eyes a blade and asks the Goblin Slayer why he did not use it before.
Ser Thornst pretends to study a blade while glancing sidelong at the Goblin Slayer, then sobers after the Goblin Slayer's remarks on enchanted weapons.
Ser Vorn is a [Knight] of the Order of the Thirsting Veil, deployed to Rhir to honour ancient pacts.
Ser Vorn is decades older than the other officers at the 5th Wall.
Ser Vorn's Order of the Thirsting Veil does not induct non-Humans.
Ser Vorn is an even-tempered man with a good sense of humour, normally a font of patience.
Ser Vorn introduces himself to Commander Cirille after his knights sing of their homeland, and says the singing has been cleared with Bastion-General Quiteil.
Ser Vorn's knights are held back for heavy engagements, and he hopes to work harmoniously with Cirille's forces.
Chief Warrior Merish asks Ser Vorn not to have his knights sing before morning, and Ser Vorn is visibly taken aback by the request.
Delezza says Ser Vorn is sworn to slay undead, which becomes a point of argument when necromancers join the defence of the 5th Wall.
Ser Vorn joins the officers' card games and has a terrible tell, his fingers dancing on his cards, and half the table folds the moment he smiles at a hand.
Ser Vorn loses three gold coins in one hand and takes it in good humour, and later loses five times as much as Cirille in one night.
Ser Vorn says the 5th Wall must be defended, and calls it a different war from the one he prefers but one he respects.
Ser Vorn's knights are mounted and ready to reinforce any group in trouble at the wall.
Ser Vorn's knights serve as the heavy cavalry that no other species at the wall has.
Ser Vorn is discouraged when the joint Gnoll and Drake skirmish exercises go poorly, saying he cannot understand why the two species fight.
Ser Vorn dodges all the Drake spear formations in one skirmish exercise and carves up their archers.
Ser Vorn rides to complain to Cirille after a clash with Drake [Riders] leaves paint all over his armour.
Ser Vorn declines a night of drinking with Uxel and Merish, citing an aging body.
Ser Vorn assures Cirille that a tall armoured figure among the group approaching the wall is Human, not a half-Giant.
Ser Vorn is astonished when Cirille suggests bringing Lizardfolk to Izril, and says his Order is no stranger to crusades abroad.
Ser Vorn notes that Ailendamus would never send him as a mercenary, though other knights of his Order might be interested.
Ser Vorn leads the Order of the Thirsting Veil and four other Knight Orders in a charge into the Demons' flank.
After nearly two dozen charges, Ser Vorn calls the disengage, as a fifth of his knights have fallen.
Ser Vorn charges a Demon commander on horseback with a spear, and Uxel hurls a scimitar as the Demon's glaive spins towards Ser Vorn.
Ser Vorn is struck by a heavy, fast projectile fired by a young human woman, whom the Demon calls Flora, and Cirille later sees him fall.
Ser Vorn is later counted among the fallen, a casualty of an encounter that only Cirille and Uxel witnessed.
Ser Vorn's ghost walks forward in formation with the other fallen defenders of the 5th Wall, glancing back at his body.
Ser Vorn kneels before his [King], answering frantic questions until he vanishes.
Seve-Alrelious is the Hundredfriends Courier, a dark-skinned Sea Courier from Chandrar who left the sands long ago, and a [Worldtraveller Inkfriend], a class of his own.
Seve comes from A'ctelios Salash, called Tombhome, a Shield Kingdom of Chandrar, which he calls peculiar and dangerous but home.
Seve carries living tattoos on his skin, including six dolphins, an ape and a Nelgaunt, each a friend met at sea and made into ink.
Seve's living tattoos are both Skill and ink, and he says the practice is Drathian, since Drathians turn pictures into magic.
Seve says his tattoos stay with him because feeding so many friends is hard work.
Seve's tiny craft is the World's Pact.
The Nelgaunt Arveil, a friend of ships, comes from Seve's arm, and Seve hastes it with a scroll so it can pull the ship through the waves.
Six large armored dolphins drag Seve's ship ahead in the typhoon.
Seve uses his Steelfriend tattoo, a little waving suit of armor, with [Steelfriend's Pact] to guide him through the storm, and the pact with Seql still shines.
Erek is Seve's Orangutan tattoo, an intelligent ape from the jungles who hid on his boat.
Seve says Erek cannot properly speak but can play chess, sail the boat and use magical artifacts, and is as strong as a Gemlion.
Seve says he is one of the [Fleshchosen], who grew up eating Tombhome's meat and so heals faster, is stronger and lives longer.
Seve says he grows hungrier over time, that food he brings from home never rots, and that he must return at least once every few years.
Seve says that someday the Carven City will call him home and he will say goodbye to his friends and not leave again.
Seve says Tombhome welcomes anyone who is lost or alone, that it is always a choice, and that its [Flesh Shapers] do healing work like Geneva's.
Seve was born in the Carven City, and says its rumors of those who enter and do not leave have some truth.
Seve carries three crates of the cure and has not slept for a day as he heads into the magical typhoon.
Seve says Seql's family and the Great Companies paid him for his delivery, though he would have done it for free.
Seve says he charges no fee when the cause is enough.
Seve asks Geneva for the names of those who made the Occillium, and after Idis interrupts, Geneva gives only the name Joseph from Liscor.
Shailt of Tergim is a Minotaur and the Iron Vanguard's Sixth Armor Captain, as large as Venaz, who challenges him to a fist duel and threatens that running means forfeit of his honor.
Venaz wins the weaponless duel, and her jaw is broken; her Dullahans carry her away and retreat.
Venaz says she is at least a Level 30 [Warrior] and that she would have beaten him if she had kept her weapon.
Venaz says his gauntleted punch shattered her bones because he misjudged his strength.
Shallel Byres is Yvlon's mother, and Yvlon refers to her as Mother.
Shallel is a former [Scribe].
Shallel comes from Terandria, where Yvlon says her mother is from.
Shallel grew up in the big cities of Terandria and knew a few half-Elves, as much as any Terandrian Human.
Shallel says she was the daughter of a very minor noble house and married into money.
Shallel says Terandria has a group of young [Ladies] whose purpose is to earn a large dowry or marry upwards.
Shallel is married to Yitton Byres, who coughs as she tells how she reached Izril.
Shallel pinches the tip of Yvlon's glove and pulls it off, exposing Yvlon's silver-flesh hand in front of a gasping crowd.
Shallel asks Yvlon in a pointed tone to explain, and Yitton looks at his daughter with wide eyes.
Shorthilt is a Redfang Hobgoblin and one of the five Hobs who stay at Erin Solstice's inn.
Shorthilt is a weapon expert, and his iron sword was the only one that did not break against the Face-Eater Moths.
Shorthilt has the Skill [Keener Edge], which lets his iron blade cut flawlessly for the first few blows.
Shorthilt is quiet and loves weapons, studying them as poets study love.
Shorthilt reaches [Warrior Level 24!] and changes to the [Weapon Expert] class, gaining [Sharper Edge] and [Bleed Cuts].
Shorthilt and Badarrow shoot out of their bedrolls on hearing their level-ups and throw up their arms in joy.
Shorthilt's unenchanted sword cuts as if by magic, aimed at the weak points in Goblin armor.

section: At the inn and in the cave
text: The five Redfang Hobs lead at least forty Cave Goblins and stand in a line holding off the Raskghar.

section: At the inn and in the cave
text: Shorthilt is the Hob in front of a mini-tribe of Goblins who seek the sharpest, most effective weapons.

section: At the inn and in the cave
text: Shorthilt's followers are both armorers and weapon smiths, using a small armory of weapons Shorthilt got from Erin.

section: At the inn and in the cave
text: Shorthilt's Goblins shape edges even on wooden axes, with Shorthilt's help.

section: At the inn and in the cave
text: Headscratcher tackles Shorthilt and pounds on him while the others laugh.

section: At the inn and in the cave
text: Shorthilt and the other four Hobs tell Garen that his orders to kill Erin were bad orders.

section: At the inn and in the cave
text: Shorthilt says that every night he sleeps and feels safe, and that Erin gave him his sword.

section: At the inn and in the cave
text: Shorthilt is kicked and beaten by Garen when the five Redfangs challenge him.

section: At the inn and in the cave
text: Shorthilt winks at Erin and says the five were "sneaky Goblins" when they return to the hill with her flag.
Shorthilt cuts through a Hob's club and beheads him in two swings as the Redfangs charge Reiss's Goblins.
Numbtongue's guitar carries electricity, Badarrow's bell arrows cause pain, and Rabbiteater with his [Grand Slash] stands out as a [Champion].
Shorthilt steps forward to face Az'kerash, who is inhabiting Reiss's body, and the other four Redfangs attack alongside him.
Shorthilt knows Az'kerash's dance of blades, even though he is far behind in it.
Shorthilt's sword crosses past Az'kerash's face while Az'kerash is fighting the five Redfangs.
Az'kerash cuts open Shorthilt's stomach after Headscratcher is stabbed, and Rabbiteater drags him away.
Shorthilt tells Rabbiteater to run and gives him his jade axe, because his own beloved sword is broken.
Shorthilt's blood turns Rabbiteater's cloak red as he hands over the axe.
Shorthilt walks back with a chipped sword and cuts down Humans who charge him, then falls.
Rabbiteater later wears a cloak that holds the blood of a dead Goblin, Shorthilt.
Shorthilt appears to Numbtongue as a ghost, asks to see his sword, and takes Numbtongue's hand.
Shriekblade is a Named Adventurer who works for Ilvriss in Salazsar, and money dictates whom she works for.
Shriekblade's real name is Tessa, but she and everyone else prefer not to use it.
Shriekblade is one of two Named Adventurers currently resident in Salazsar, and the more dangerous and unpredictable of the two; the other is the steady Gnoll Akral the Adamantium.
Shriekblade is a female Drake, younger than Alrric, and is called a prodigy of an adventurer.
Shriekblade wears long, tight-clinging black silk, probably enchanted, with no armor, and her grey-green scales are scarred wherever they are exposed.
Many of Shriekblade's scars are self-inflicted, and the split scales do not regrow.
Shriekblade can cling to a ceiling like a gigantic, demented gecko, and lands on a desk as lightly as a cat.
Shriekblade swings abruptly between laughing and looking tired and drawn, and her fits of shuddering include a full-body shake.
Shriekblade fights with a long dagger, drawn so quickly that Alrric only sees a blur.
Alrric judges that she is not a [Rogue] or [Assassin] but a close-quarters combat specialist who has seen more combat than Captain Shieldscale four times over.
Shriekblade has a terrible record of failure and success, and is a good mercenary if the job is killing something.
Shriekblade was imprisoned twice for murder, though both times were counted as self-defense.
Shriekblade depends on potions and calming tonics, including high-quality ones that Ilvriss provides, and says they do not help enough.
Shriekblade says that the Healer of Tenbault makes her feel better for a month, and then it is worse.
Shriekblade has visited the Healer of Tenbault many times, but whatever the Healer does does not stick.
Shriekblade asks Alrric whether Ilvriss has someone for her to kill yet, as casually as asking about weeding a garden, since killing people or monsters is all the same to her.
After drinking three tonics, Shriekblade becomes completely without emotion and reports for duty, asking whether she should kill the [Weapon Master] she is sent to test.
Shriekblade is on retainer to Ilvriss, who hired her despite Alrric's objection.
Ilvriss sends Shriekblade to test a half-Elf [Weapon Master]; later he explains how to fight Antinium while she yawns openly, and Alrric guesses his bruises come from a duel with a Named Adventurer.
Shriekblade charges screaming at the Stone Starers at a barricaded shaft, killing them without tactics, before Ilvriss leads Gold-ranks and [Mercenaries] in behind her.
Killing the monsters does not improve her temper, and she sits in a void of space ignoring the blood and singe marks, as killing just is for her.
The Assassin's Guild sends Shriekblade a contract as black letters tracing themselves on her arm; the Guild normally leaves the Named Adventurer alone, so the target must be big.
Shriekblade is calm after drinking too many potions, and answers the contract with a lodestone, saying "I am working. No."
The Silent Queen is an Antinium Queen with a genius for shaping Antinium forms.
The Silent Queen is described as the smallest and most timid of the Queens in one account, and as second-smallest next to the Free Queen in another.
The Silent Queen's hive lies in the shade of the cliffs, uses darker soil and dim corridors, and has camouflaged attendants.
The Silent Queen is fond of Klbkch and is practically vibrating when he visits.
The Silent Queen says her Hive is not True Antinium.
The Silent Queen, via mirror, directs the Free Queen's surgery on Bird, ordering gel, warmth and splicing of a blood-sac organ with flesh and chitin.
Bird survives the surgery and says he is brave.
The Silent Queen contacts the Free Queen and accuses her of withholding the design of her new Bird-Prognugator.
The Silent Queen offers to trade and to send a Prognugator through the new passageway, misunderstanding the Free Queen's explanations.
The Silent Queen's elite Infiltrator Antinium are six-legged, scythe-armed and shell-camouflaged, with blades able to cut weak enchanted armor.
Each Infiltrator takes two months to create, and the Silent Queen calls her Hive the smallest but with elite soldiers.
The Silent Queen shows Klbkch a light-emitting Antinium built to blind enemies, based on Sii the Glorious.
The strobe Antinium flickers its lights while others attack the blinded foe, though it must rest after a minute.
Sillk is a Lizardman student three years older than Umina, whom Merrik worries about in front of the graduates.
Sillk is a [Rogue], and Niers calls him one of the officers in training.
Sillk tells Merrik that each of them has unique abilities and Sillk has his class.
Sillk and Xelic jump a group of Dullahans and take down their leader.
Niers says he is glad Sillk and Merrik did not team up, since each fought in his own strengths.
Niers praises Sillk for taking out enemy officers but says he was captured the instant Wistram's [Mages] tagged him with a locator spell.
Sillk says he should have gone to ground sooner and hidden after being aggressive.
Niers rewards Sillk with three days of shadowing Foliana, to learn how she disappears.
Niers says the Forgotten Wing does not and never has run an [Assassin] training school, and he is challenged to swear it on a truth spell.
Sir Nil Moxae is one of Lady Bethal Walchaís's Rose Knights, a [Knight] wearing pink armour who carries a sword and shield.
Sir Nil Moxae's companion among the Rose Knights is Dame Truvia Cartiil, who carries a spear.
Sir Nil raises the alarm at movement in the trees as Lady Bethal's party rides through the forest.
Sir Nil and Dame Truvia ride ahead to scout and are stopped after about a hundred yards, when Sir Nil reports two dozen mounted Goblins ahead.
Sir Nil proposes to draw the Goblins off by attacking from the side, and Lady Bethal refuses, saying they break through together or not at all.
Sir Nil turns to face the first Goblin Carn Wolf rider and utters a challenge as mounted Goblins surround the four Humans.
Sir Nil and Dame Truvia shield Lady Bethal with their bodies while over a hundred Goblins aim crossbows at her.
Sir Nil blocks a stray crossbow bolt aimed at Lady Bethal's chest with his shield, shattering it.
Sir Nil rides forward when the Goblins demand that the Humans drop their weapons, and the Goblins back away.
Sir Nil sheathes his sword with Thomast and Truvia when Lady Bethal nods her assent to the Hob's demand.
Dame Truvia suggests that Sir Nil stay on the road with Lady Bethal, but Bethal insists they all go together to find Sir Kerrig.
Sir Nil dismounts to check the churned ground at the ambush site and coughs from the lingering poison.
Sir Nil clasps Sir Kerrig's arm and urges him to mount his stallion.
Sir Nil bows his head at once when Lady Bethal sharply tells him to let Sir Kerrig speak.
Sir Relz is a Drake of Pallass and, with Noass, one of the world's first [Commentators].
Sir Relz wears a monocle on a chain looped around a neck-spine and dresses expensively.
Sir Relz gained a class with Noass from their commentary on the attack on Liscor.
Sir Relz identifies Jelaqua Ivirith as a Gold-rank adventurer who leads the Halfseekers while he and Noass watch the battle at the inn.
The two Drakes say the Halfseekers were once a group of eight on the verge of Named status and are now three Gold-rank adventurers.
The two Drakes identify Moore as an earth-magic specialist using a mass variant of [Armor of Thorns].
Sir Relz joins Noass in broadcasting through Eltistiman Verdue's scrying orb about the warnings of an attack on Liscor.
Sir Relz comments that the Liscorian Wing Commander stormed up to Senator Errif in a huff.
Sir Relz broadcasts live from Pallass during the Wyvern attack, with a portable scrying mirror and [Spectator's Concealment].
Sir Relz is inept at angling the scrying mirror and shows the audience a close-up of his own face.
Sir Relz says the pair's class gives them [Spectator's Concealment], which works so long as they do not interfere.
Sir Relz tells Noass that Flos's army is systematically destroying each group it meets rather than racing.
Sir Relz adjusts his monocle as the pair arrange transport through the inn door to Invrisil.
Siri is a Swedish woman from Earth who joined the Bushrangers in Baleros, and who has no relation to the voice assistant of the same name.
Siri and Tofte are the two Swedes among the Bushrangers.
Siri was picked up by the Bushrangers three weeks before a later scene.
Siri came up with the idea of camouflage, which is how she and Tofte survived after being transported to Baleros.
Siri likes all things Lord of the Rings.
Daly names Siri his backup leader, calling her the best of the Bushrangers and a solid head.
Paige names no leader of her own, though she says Kirana is good but bosses around the girls from her country.
Siri visits the Centaur landlady Miss Hastel with Daly, and asks when her child is due.
Siri sits white-faced on the ground after the birth, having once faced down a serpent with a crossbow and a dagger.
Siri has the names of her family tattooed in silver on the inside of her arm, including her brother.
Siri sometimes forgets she has a brother, and Luan has a matching tattoo in gold.
Tattooing names so as not to forget is a growing trend among some of the company.
Erin Solstice's skeleton stands in a doorway, taller than her, with yellow-white bones and twin burning blue-white flames for eyes.
Erin notices that the skeleton has a human head but its ribs and some other bones are slightly different from the human bones in her biology books.
The system labels it [Unnamed, Level 1 Skeleton Warrior].
Erin orders the skeleton to clean the whole upper floor; it first tosses the rag aside and wipes with its foot, until Erin shows it how to scrub.
The skeleton cleans every upstairs room until the floorboards regain their original lustrous color.
The skeleton struggles to lift both full buckets at once.
The skeleton charges Pawn and two Workers with a wordless rattling shout, and Erin's punch knocks its skull off; its body finds the head and puts it back on.
The [Skeleton Warrior] is now Level 2, though skeletons are not supposed to have free will or to level.
Snapjaw is a female Hobgoblin with an oversized head and teeth fused with steel or something harder.
Snapjaw is shorter than a regular Hob, and her classes are [Eater] and [Rider].
Snapjaw bites through things better than Eater Goats and often does so in combat.
Snapjaw was Reiss's lieutenant, so she is fluent in the common tongue and prefers it.
Snapjaw runs at Zel Shivertail with Eater of Spears, but a Human woman's whispered voice holds her in place for three seconds.
Snapjaw rides a horse beside Reiss at his first meeting with Rags's tribe.
Snapjaw speaks for the first time at the council fire to say that Reiss can make a nation and keep Goblins safe.
Poisonbite kills Snapjaw's horse with poisoned daggers and the two female Goblins face off.
Snapjaw leads at least fifteen thousand mounted Goblins against the Redfangs.
Snapjaw is one of the last two lieutenants Reiss has left, since Zel slew his best officers.
Snapjaw snaps Spiderslicer's sword with her metal teeth and bites a Redfang Hob in half.
Snapjaw screams when Tyrion Veltras's lance strikes Reiss.
Snapjaw sits with Badarrow in his tower whenever she is not working, leaning on him to calm his nerves.
Snapjaw and Badarrow are lovers.
Snapjaw and Badarrow met because both wept for Eater of Spears and other fallen friends.
Badarrow is taciturn while Snapjaw is outgoing, yet they trust each other.
Calescent walks in on Snapjaw and Badarrow mid-act and says he will return with a less spicy dish.
Mister Soot is an ashen-scaled old Drake [Fence] of Liscor, one of the city's more notorious.
Soot is very particular about being called Mister Soot.
Soot's class is [Mastermind], specifically [Gang Mastermind], a step below a [Crime Lord].
Soot operates a significant portion of Liscor's underworld, with a gang that has magical wands, gear and good numbers.
Soot's gang avoids the Watch's dangerous fighters, and Soot is one of the Watch's most wanted.
Soot owns several safe houses where a [Thief] could hide for a price.
Klbkch finds Soot meeting Bearclaw on Greas Street, and Soot says they are just having a civilized meeting.
Soot gives up Saucy's Bar as where the thief is.
Klbkch reports that Soot is arming his associates with wands and handling dreamleaf imported by Palt the Centaur.
Soot relays that the Brother of Serendipitous Meetings and the Elusive Lot both have claims on the inn.
Soot watches Bearclaw break two Senior Guards in his safe room, having lost control the moment he found her there.
Soot no longer visits Bearclaw without at least eight bodyguards.
Soot warns Bearclaw about Relc, then suppresses an inner smile when she takes it as a challenge.
Soot dies, and by the time the Watch finds the safe house only Soot is left.
Zevara states that Soot is dead.
Sostrom Reidez is a human mage of the adventuring team the Horns of Hammerad.
Sostrom is in his early thirties, or very late twenties, and is bald save for his eyebrows.
Sostrom tugs a pointy hat lower on his head and wears his mage's hat whenever possible because he is completely bald.
Of the three mages in the Horns of Hammerad, Sostrom is the second-strongest, according to Gerial.
Sostrom cannot cast [Fireballs], but Gerial has grown to appreciate his ability.
Sostrom repaired Ryoka Griffin's iPhone with the spell [Repair], tapping it with his wand, whose tip flashed green.
Sostrom introduced himself as at Ryoka's service and flushed lightly when she thanked him for the repair.
Ryoka notes there was a flash of magic when Sostrom repaired her phone, unlike the finger-glow of another mage's spell.
Ryoka reminds herself that Sostrom fixed her iPhone and gave her music.
Sostrom is one of the Horns who come out of the inn to watch Ryoka leave for the High Passes.
Sostrom nudges Ryoka and mutters to her in the inn's common room.
Sostrom chokes on his drink when Erin addresses Calruz.

section: Conversation about Lady Magnolia and Gazi (Book 1, Ch1.40)
text: Sostrom says the innkeeper, Miss Solstice, was sick, so the Horns all left the inn without breakfast.

section: Conversation about Lady Magnolia and Gazi (Book 1, Ch1.40)
text: Sostrom is interested in Ryoka's repaired phone, her fist-fighting skill and her lack of levels, and thinks there is something else to her.

section: Conversation about Lady Magnolia and Gazi (Book 1, Ch1.40)
text: Sostrom says Lady Magnolia's name tells you how important she is.

section: Conversation about Lady Magnolia and Gazi (Book 1, Ch1.40)
text: Sostrom immediately offers his seat to Gazi when he recognises her name.

section: Conversation about Lady Magnolia and Gazi (Book 1, Ch1.40)
text: When Gazi's group fires a webbing artifact, Gerial and Sostrom are pinned to the ground, and Sostrom's wand is caught in the webbing.

section: Conversation about Lady Magnolia and Gazi (Book 1, Ch1.40)
text: After Ceria frees them, Sostrom points to an alleyway and the three adventurers run from the Watch.

section: Conversation about Lady Magnolia and Gazi (Book 1, Ch1.40)
text: Sostrom hands Ceria a potion as they walk back toward the inn.
The Horns of Hammerad formed two years earlier and have ten members, including Sostrom and the mage Marian.
Sostrom is described as liking Marian as the only other human mage in the group who does not tease him about his bald spot.
In the first attack of the undead, Sostrom fights back-to-back with Ceria, throwing bolts of fire from his staff.
When a Crypt Lord seized Sostrom, he screamed in agony while Gerial stabbed it.
Calruz axed the Crypt Lord and Sostrom fell to the ground, its severed hand still holding him.
Sostrom casts [Sticky Ground] at Calruz's order, a spell whose webbing would slow the dead down.
Skinner took Sostrom's skin and made it part of his body, killing Sostrom.
Sostrom screamed for help before he died, but Ceria ignored him.
Spiderslicer is a scarred veteran Redfang Goblin who rides a Carn Wolf and wields a thin falchion.
Spiderslicer was Garen's second and had been the third-strongest Redfang in the tribe.
Spiderslicer resents Redscar, who beat him repeatedly and then left the tribe for Rags.
Spiderslicer parries Garen's killing blow on Headscratcher, saying "Redfangs don't fight alone".
Garen calls Spiderslicer a traitor, and Spiderslicer apologises but raises his falchion again.
Garen's blade shears through Spiderslicer's sword, and most of the tribe forms a wall beside the Hobs, with fewer than a hundred staying with Garen.
Spiderslicer and Redscar duel with identical steel swords on a hill near the inn, and both heal after.
Halrac bets two hundred gold on Redscar, and Pisces takes bets from adventurers and Goblins.
Spiderslicer rides in front of Garen to block bone shards and falls limply.
Stan, known as Crossbow Stan, is an older Silver-rank [Crossbowman] in his early forties who wears chainmail and carries a dagger and a small pouch.
Stan leads the Silver-rank team the Boltspitters, and his teammate Lailli has a broken foot.
Stan stays in the Silver ranks because he lacks the punch to go higher.
Stan keeps preloaded crossbows in a bag of holding, six in all, and has spent his coin on better bags.
Stan carries two crossbows at his side and four more in his bag of holding, and he can fire six bolts in a blink.
Alais says Stan has two kids, avoids huge risks and has a lot saved up, and Alais confirms his wife left him.
Stan greets Ceria and Yvlon warmly and says the Boltspitters took some injuries but nothing to speak of.
Stan describes his craft, saying a crossbow can be loaded ahead of time, and he can pull one out aimed at the table.
Stan shouts "dissonance" when Ksmvr's rings, weapons and necklace vibrate, telling him to pull the rings off.
Stan says the enchantments are not active when piled together, and that most adventurers can wear about four items, including a bag of holding.
Stan and Alais tell Ksmvr the Humpbacker Hills bandit contract is now theirs, with the bounty raised by eighty gold to a hundred.
Stan says the bandits are in the Humpbacker Hills, a tall stretch of hills southwest of Celum, just short of the High Passes.
Stan tells Ksmvr that Ceria and Yvlon leaving Liscor and then getting rich in Albez looks suspicious.
Stan commands his Boltspitters to hold the line against the Crelers and fires two crossbows.
Stan orders barriers and staggered lines with enchanted armour and line-holders at the front.
Walt's Ensoldier Shields and Alais' Thunder's Solace join the line.
Sylind is a half-Elf [Archer] and [Hunter] among the Witch Hunters who pursue Belavierr alongside Ser Raim.
Sylind has the Skill [The Eternal Hunt], which lets her mark a quarry she will never lose once marked.
Sylind joins the hunt because she sees Belavierr's crimes as unforgivable, according to Ser Raim.
Sylind fires a Phoenixfire arrow at Belavierr on the order of the Witch Hunters' leader, and is later told to mark Belavierr as she flees.
Sylind says she will never lose Belavierr again because she is marked, and Coroise tells her that her life is as precious as Raim's.
Coroise orders the others to protect Sylind, because if she dies Belavierr escapes.
Ser Raim tells Knight-Commander Calirn that the Skill worked this time because he had weakened Belavierr's protections.
Sylind aims up at a huge shadow as the hunters take their position by the orb.
Sylind argues with Tagil that she and Raim together make a doubly large target, and proposes moving Raim to a warded house in Riverfarm.
Sylind says Belavierr cannot be perfect if her Skills work on the Witch, and that Raim can be warded just as well elsewhere.
Sylind sits upstairs in the slanted house meditating and checking her arrows while five Witch Hunters remain.
Tagil tells Sylind that Belavierr once captured him during the attack on her village and made him an offer.
Tagil says the offer was never for then but for now, and Sylind urges him not to go through with it.
Tagil kills Sylind with a hidden crossbow, shooting her twice despite her protective charms, after she reaches for her bow.
Later, the Order carries Sylind's ashes home with the ashes of the other fallen Witch Hunters.
Tagil is a [Witch Hunter] who introduces himself as the Foreign Hunter leading the Hunters of Noelictus on business of the Crown of Noelictus.
Tagil wields iconic scissor-swords that he commissioned to fight Belavierr.
Tagil has a daughter who is very sick, and even the Healer of Tenbault could not cure her.
Tagil says he was captured by Belavierr during the attack on her village, and she made him an offer.
Tagil says Belavierr saw right through him, and that he had given up hope after a meeting for his daughter failed.
Tagil tells Sylind that the offer was never for then, but for now.
Tagil shoots Sylind with a hidden crossbow, then kills Coroise with his sword, and fires bolts at Faigen and Erashelle, killing all four.
Erashelle calls Tagil a traitor and hopes he suffers forever before she dies.
Tagil walks out of Riverfarm past the Knights, whom he placates with lies, following a thread to Belavierr on a hill.
Tagil tells Belavierr that Raim lives and that he has done his part, and she confirms she has sworn the pact.
Belavierr says she will keep her promise in the hour after his death, whatever happens to Tagil, and does not promise to tell Raim or his daughter.
Tagil curses Belavierr, asks her to save his daughter, and hangs himself from a tree on the hill.
Prost oversees the burial of Tagil, and the villagers bury him where he fell as a traitor in silence.
No one asks for Tagil's remains, while the Order carries away the ashes of the other fallen Hunters.
Takhatres is a Garuda, a bird-man native to Chandrar, with blue and green feathers, a bird's face with a curved beak and clothing mixed with light fabric.
Takhatres has wings for arms, with long feathers and nimble talons at the ends.
Takhatres is called the Lord of the Skies and is one of the King of Destruction's Seven.
Takhatres is a vassal of Flos Reimarch and a sworn enemy of the Empire of Sands.
Takhatres cannot fly, but runs like a man and is called the fastest warrior on the continent.
Takhatres tells Flos he has brought his tribe, which has quadrupled in number since he last led it to war.
Takhatres says his warriors are trained to fight fiercer than before and will blot out the sun on Flos's enemies.
Flos says he would not trade five armies for Takhatres' tribe and expects it to spearhead the war.
Takhatres bows his head, crossing his wings together, and murmurs what sounds like a prayer at the sight of Drevish's head.
Takhatres drinks two cups of wine at most and sips slowly, making his drink last.
Takhatres tells Flos he will lead his kin into the left as Flos attacks, to take out the enemy mages.
Takhatres leaves the very night he promised, to strike the first blow against the Emperor of Sands with his tribe.
Takhatres' army of Garuda drops stones from hundreds of feet overhead, and a ten-pound stone crushes a camel's back.
Takhatres has small blades in his feathered wings and daggers on his claws that cut through steel armor.
Takhatres leads a tribe against an army of eight thousand led by a young Sand commander, whose subordinate Khal fears him.
Takhatres fought two battles against armies sent by the Empress of Sands specialised against Garuda, dealing as much damage as his tribe received, then retreated.
Takhatres becomes a moving force, striking weak targets and rallying enemies of the Empire of Sands against her.
Talia Kallinad is formally Lady-Dame Talia Kallinad, Knight of the Summer, and is called Dame Talia or Talia among friends.
Talia is a [Summer Knight], twenty-eight years old, and a full member of her Order.
Talia is the elder sister of Wil Kallinad, the [Strategist] and pride of House Kallinad, and is potentially heir to the Kallinad family if she marries.
Talia comes from a coastal duchy, and she is used to seafood rather than pickled food.
Talia has her family's colors, gold and orange with hints of white, which she has personalized on her armor.
Talia answers to her Grandmaster, the Summer's Champion, but senior members of other Seasons can also command her at need.
Talia has the [Lady] class and a few Skills gained before she became a [Squire].
Talia's Skill [Mark of Worth] tells her when a person is worth attention, helping her choose worthy retainers though not necessarily trustworthy ones.
Talia says she saw such worthy people in Riverfarm.
Talia's [Aura Blade] heats plain steel from red through orange and yellow to white-hot, and the blade burns flesh and sets weapons aflame.
Talia lacks the ability to become a burning fireball like her season's senior Knights, but her sword is as deadly as many enchanted weapons.
Calirn tells Talia she is over twenty levels below Ser Raim.
Talia has a nearly healed scar on her left leg from an enchanted arrow that went straight through her plain steel armor.
Talia returns from Baleros after the Titan's game at Daquin and is brought home by mocking [Sailors] who tease her with her title.
Talia's younger brother Wil calls her Tal before she leaves Baleros.
Talia is congratulated by Calirn on the game, and he says the Fall's Sentinel and he himself have reservations about its outcome.
Talia is at the stronghold when Belavierr is identified, and she asks Calirn whether it is really the Spider, the enemy of the Order.
Talia takes part in the ancient magical ritual that sends her across the world to fight for Ser Raim.
Talia cries as Raim, before his last charge, touches her shoulder and orders her to return to the Order if he falls.
Talia takes command of the surviving Spring and Summer Knights after each of her seniors has fallen or been too badly wounded to stand.
Talia has auburn hair, and her orders are clear: she walks past Belavierr and bows to Riverfarm's people.
A wounded senior Knight charges Talia with escorting him to a [Healer] and with returning the younger Knights home.
Talia promises that the Order will not forget Raim's sacrifice, and she thanks Durene and Sir Beniar for fighting beside the Knights.
Talia carries Ser Raim's ashes and greatsword away without speaking to Ryoka, with her hands clenched so hard that Ryoka thinks the gauntlets bleed.
Talia leads the survivors, Knights of Spring and Summer, more than half of whom are younger than Ryoka, and the Order's dead.

section: Book 14: Izril and the Goblin Slayer
text: Talia travels across Izril's dirt roads with her company, tormented by the failure to kill Belavierr.

section: Book 14: Izril and the Goblin Slayer
text: Talia argues that Selphids should be allowed into the Order, and cites three Selphid members in its history, with Chalica of Spring holding the gates until the enemy dead piled up.

section: Book 14: Izril and the Goblin Slayer
text: Ser Lorell answers that one in three Selphids proved false, and cites the ruin of the Crowlende Order as a warning against crowding the ranks.

section: Book 14: Izril and the Goblin Slayer
text: Talia and the Order of Seasons fight Ogres and Goblins in a dark clearing, and Talia's blade scorches the enemy.

section: Book 14: Izril and the Goblin Slayer
text: Talia promises Ser Solstice she will be his ally and stand with him so long as his cause is just and his heart unwavering.

section: Book 14: Izril and the Goblin Slayer
text: Ser Solstice says that someday he will ask if she remembers the vow, and Talia answers that she will never break it.
Talia respects Ser Solstice, who has sworn never to reveal his face, and she says her failure at Riverfarm still weighs on her.
Talia thinks of her many levels and fast growth as hollow after Raim's death.
Talia tells Ser Solstice that war is brewing with Ailendamus and that she believes the Grandmaster will order some Knights to war.
Talia and Rabbiteater are aboard a transport ship when Ailendamus ships attack with arrows, and a Knight of Spring shouts that Ailendamus has crossed Kaliv's border.
Talia is startled that war has come a month before Grandmaster Calirn predicted.
Tallis the Stormbreaker is a Goblin Lord and the great [Shaman] of the Goblin King's armies.
Velan the Kind left the southern strategy to Tallis, the mightiest of his Goblin Lords.

section: Role in the Second Antinium War
text: Tallis joined the war between the Antinium and Drakes late, beginning by sacking port cities on the western coast.

section: Role in the Second Antinium War
text: Tallis then moved slowly inland and routed Drake armies with contemptuous ease through his magical might.

section: Role in the Second Antinium War
text: The Antinium were already besieging Pallass and Zeres when Tallis advanced, and Drakes despaired at news of him.

section: Role in the Second Antinium War
text: Tallis's advance brought him close to an Antinium Hive, which sent Xrn the Small Queen against him.

section: Role in the Second Antinium War
text: Tallis annihilated that Antinium army with a single spell within ten minutes of its charge, the Antinium's first great defeat of the war.

section: Role in the Second Antinium War
text: Tallis defeated the first, second and third armies the Antinium sent against him, according to Xrn.
Tallis opened a hole in the sky above the Antinium charge, which widened into a vortex that tore up trees, rocks and earth.
Tallis's spell sucked tens of thousands of Antinium Soldiers and Workers upward, and Xrn could not dispel it.
Even the Flying Antinium were dragged hundreds of miles up and hurled down by the winds.
Tallis laughed with a voice like thunder while other Goblin [Shamans] and [Mages] broke Xrn's spells, and she fled.
Tallis could not cast the grand spell on the second or third army sent against him, but still broke them with magic.
Tallis grew more exhausted with each spell he cast, according to Xrn.
After the three defeats, the Grand Queen ordered Klbkch, Wrymvr and Xrn to break the Goblin King's might at any cost.
Three Archmages of Wistram cornered Tallis's army and fought him in a magical battle lasting two days and two nights.
On the second day Xrn and an Antinium force attacked from his side, and the history thinks her unpredictable magic helped overwhelm him.
Tallis unleashed a storm as he fell that battered Izril for a week with drenching rain and hurricane winds.
Tallis's fall told the world that the Goblin King was on the verge of defeat.
Taxiela is a Lizardgirl [Mage] of the Elusive Lot, a faction of Wistram, who answers Palt's spell.
Taxiela calls Palt her beautiful apprentice and promises him a tome and forwarded lessons as a reward.
The narration says Galei and Taxiela are presumably the same being, and presumably Palt's master and member of the Elusive Lot.
Taxiela's eyes widen when Palt saves the most impressive bit of his request for last, and she says she can do it.
Taxiela agrees to help after Palt explains his request, and says Earthers are known to her but all other attempts have failed.
Taxiela offers Liscor, Invrisil or Pallass the chance to be among the first to experience Wistram's illusion simulations, a collaboration with Aaron.
Taxiela tells Palt to stay ready for a window after an hour or two.
Taxiela materialises before Elena holding a glowing phone that is a very good illusion, and winks as she hands it over.
Galei is a male Centaur of the Elusive Lot, addressed by Palt as Master Galei, who breaks into the call with a friendly male voice.
Galei says that enchanting a mirror with [Scrying] is safe from Wistram reversing the spell if Palt does it.
Galei says the call has about six minutes left and arranges to resume later that night in one of the Elusive Lot's warded rooms.
Galei says half of Wistram's [Mages] could communicate without anyone in Wistram knowing, since they are the Elusive Lot.
Tekshia Shivertail is a very old Drake lady who leads the Adventurer's Guild of Liscor and sits on Liscor's Council.
Tekshia is the grandmother of Selys, the guild's [Receptionist], and holds the title Guildmistress.
Tekshia is the aunt of General Zel Shivertail, which makes Zel Selys's uncle.
Tekshia is a former adventurer who retired and has run Liscor's Adventurer's Guild for over three decades.
Tekshia has dusky purple scales that are greyer and less lustrous than Selys's, yet she is spry and still attractive.
Tekshia lashes her tail irritably when she glares at Selys, and her temper is short.
Tekshia has shrunk with age and is shorter than Selys, but still carries far too much muscle for her years.
Tekshia's scales are faded and patchy, and she likes to say she was a beauty in her youth and still matches Selys.
Tekshia holds old-fashioned views, saying that in her day everything was tougher and Drakes took matters into their own claws.
Tekshia complains of aching bones and a bad back, yet she can still do backflips and outrun Street Runners.
Tekshia's tail gives away nothing when she does not want it to.
Tekshia carries a little wooden cane that occasionally turns out to be a spear.
Tekshia smokes dreamleaf puffers when someone is in the area, and offers one to Ceria.
Tekshia keeps a barbed spear in her office and nearly throws it at Selys when she kicks the door open.
Tekshia says that to reach her age one must be prepared for [Assassins], hired thugs or monsters coming through the door.
Tekshia leans on her barbed spear when she stands on Liscor's walls during the giant moth attack.
Tekshia has a Skill, [Implacable Order], that makes whatever she commands happen, leaving the target only the choice to obey or refuse.
Tekshia is a retired Gold-rank adventurer known as "Tekshia the Spearmaster", though she says it should have been Spearmistress.
Tekshia says she earned her Spearmaster class honestly, and she sneers at Relc for getting his by killing a [Spearmaster] in battle.
Tekshia says she quit adventuring because she was getting older and tired of days spent hunting Trolls in bogs.
Tekshia carries a good bag of holding from her adventuring days.
Tekshia throws her cane like a javelin with a launching Skill, and the impact sends Walt flying backwards.
Tekshia taught Selys to roll when thrown as a hatchling, and Selys remembers visiting Tekshia's apartment then.
Tekshia scolds Selys for not knocking, telling her she could have been thrown at.
Tekshia pinches Selys's cheek at the party and complains she never brings her popcorn.
Tekshia remembers Zel visiting Liscor as a hatchling and later fighting at the front against the Necromancer.
Tekshia stares down at Zel's dead body, and Selys hears her voice shake for the first time.
Tekshia is named in Zel's will as the heir to the spears in his armory and his investments held in Liscor.
Tekshia sits in a chair looking older than Selys can remember while Ilvriss discusses Zel's death and the Heartflame Breastplate.
Tekshia calls Zel's extended family greedy idiots for moving so quickly on legal matters after his death.
Tekshia tells Selys she may have tomorrow off but must be back at noon the day after.
Tekshia praises Selys for poking out an eye in a fight and advises her to duck next time.
Tekshia tells Selys to buy a vault worth at least two thousand gold, probably four thousand, and to trade in the cheap one.
Tekshia tells Selys to rent the Heartflame Breastplate to the Flamewardens and to go to Pallass with Erin Solstice.
Tekshia orders Selys to keep the armor, saying never to offer even a part of it whatever she is offered.
Tekshia says Zel and Selys's parents would be proud that Selys got rich through cleverness, and tells her not to let anyone steal the armor.
Tekshia refuses Selys's wish to quit as [Receptionist], but lets her work day shifts of six hours instead of nine.
Tekshia scoops a handful of Selys's gold into her bag of holding for a night out at Wishdrinks with her old friends.
Tekshia tells Selys not to come to work the next day and says she will make Warsh cover the shift.
Tekshia tells Selys that she will need to earn twenty thousand gold before it would lure a [Mage] to Liscor.
Tekshia tells Selys how her father charged a Carcass Walker on the wall with [Ram's Charge] and fell off the wall with it.
Tekshia says Selys's mother was shooting Draugr with her last enchanted arrows when a wraith killed her from behind.
Tekshia says Drakes have too few [Mages] because they call magic dishonorable and not military.
Tekshia says that with as many [Mages] as [Sergeants] the army would have beaten the Necromancer without help.
Tekshia declares Liscor's Dungeon Gold-rank on the walls, in her authority as Guildmistress, and invites adventurers of legend to challenge it.
Tekshia gives the Redfang Warriors the evil eye throughout the party at Erin's inn.
Tekshia refuses to let a band of monsters roam as a sanctioned adventuring team, calling the idea Erin's insane one.
Tekshia says she will agree if Selys gives her one assurance about the Goblins.
Tekshia suspects an insane group built the dungeon, citing its fixation with flesh and body parts.
Tekshia asks Selys to search for any older Drake nation that focused on necromancy, and says she will write a note to that [Strategist].
Tekshia tells Selys to watch a person under her [Implacable Order], leaving Selys unable to argue.
Tekshia refuses at first to sign the form for a Bronze-rank Goblin team, saying she does not trust them.
Tekshia signs the form after Selys offers to take responsibility and the blame if the Goblins cause trouble.
Tekshia is pleased to finally hear Selys take responsibility for her actions.
Tekshia asks Erin for a bag of her cookies to share with friends.
Tekshia laughs at Selys's belief that she was being groomed as the next Guildmistress, saying she wanted Selys to take responsibility and level up again.
Tekshia tells Selys she can have her post when Tekshia is dead and not a moment before.
Tekshia declines to intervene when Zevara consults the guild about stopping Silver-rank teams from entering the dungeon.
Tekshia throws her spear at Revi and Yvlon inside her office, and later chases Olesm out of the guild with the spear.
Tekshia pokes Relc with her spear and works out that he taught Embria the spear dance, since it cannot be learned by sight alone.
Tekshia breaks up a dispute between Bessr and Walt, and throws her cane to knock Walt flat when he argues.
Tekshia orders the new recruits to report to the guild every morning or go unpaid, and to scout east or west for the Bloodfields road.
Tekshia tells the guild that anyone trying to take the bounty on the [Necromancer] in Liscor gets stabbed.
Tekshia refuses to recognise the group of wand-wielding upstarts hunting that bounty.
Tekshia docks the Horns' pay for a day they rested with broken bones.
Tekshia tells Pisces to kill whoever hexes her granddaughter next time, or stay out of her guild.
Tekshia promotes the Horns to Gold-rank for slaying an Adult Creler, tapping Ceria's ankle with her cane.
Tekshia says the guilds will announce the Horns' promotion that night, so everyone in Izril will know by month's end.
Tekshia says she has not forgiven the Wistram [Mages] but will let it go since they nearly died and one did.
Tekshia was once far richer than Selys is after her armor windfall, and told Selys she lost it all when the Necromancer attacked.
Tekshia admits that her loss story is a lie, and that she spent much of her fortune on parties, drinks, travel and helping friends.
Tekshia donated the rest of her wealth to Liscor's army, then sold much of her gear to pay off debts when the money ran out.
Tekshia distrusts milk because it comes from cows, which she says have parasites and can have Creler burst from them.
Tekshia says she just dislikes [Necromancers] when Selys asks if Pisces's tasks were meant to train her.
Teliv Witherscale is a Drake with black scales spotted with yellow.
Teliv introduces himself to the Council as a part-time [Host] at Wishdrinks, available for dinner parties, birthdays and level-up parties but not funerals.
Teliv later calls himself the [Negotiator] in charge of the Esthelm diplomatic trip, and Liscor's Council authorises him to negotiate for the city.
Teliv attended Manus's academies with Olesm, and he decided being a [Tactician] was not for him.
Teliv says Manus trains [Diplomats] because of threats that come with the class, such as assassination, poisoning, intimidation and blackmail.
Teliv says he has not yet reached the [Diplomat] class, but hopes work from the Council will help him level up.
Teliv has a likeable manner and a perfect handshake, and Erin cannot tell whether it is a Skill or his personality.
Teliv says he has a healthy regard for his life and is allergic to death, trouble and Erin's inn.
Teliv bows to the Council, then pales when he is told the first talks will be with Guardsman Klbkch, saying he does not do Antinium.
Teliv asks Olesm about the new Council and then decides he needs a suit and a protective amulet.
Teliv collects Erin at her inn for the Esthelm trip, giving her a green flower as an academy custom.
Teliv tells Erin to leave the bargaining to him, and that her presence is needed because Esthelm's people feel goodwill toward her.
Teliv says Esthelm is poor and somewhat traumatized after the Goblin Lord's attack, and suggests a gift of dried fish.
Teliv asks Erin not to mention that Liscor is swimming with Gold-rank adventurers.
Teliv says Erin came close to a diplomatic incident four times in Esthelm, and says she encouraged a near riot.
Teliv says Numbtongue sneaked into Esthelm by following the party, and Erin says Esthelm's people were calm, with some knowing Numbtongue.
Erin says she helped get rid of a jerk who charged travel fees like [Bandits], and Ceria and Yvlon think it was a coup.
Erin wears a wreath of flowers given to her in Esthelm.
Teliv visits Erin on official city business to propose that Liscor's Council and Pallass subsidise her magical door upgrade in return for negotiation about its use.
Teliv says the Council wants shipment oversight, a [Guardsman] or two, and can roll any transport fee into her annual taxes.
Teliv says Pallass will check any transport into its city at its checkpoint.
Teliv leverages the Skill [First Reasonable Offer] and uses a third Skill to silence Wailant while presenting a contract.
Erin writes "no thanks" on Teliv's contract in place of a signature, then challenges the offer and the idea of Liscor setting prices.
Erin hands Teliv and Wailant a folded paper of fair terms drawn up with Maviola, and both begin to object.
Teliv, as Liscor's [Negotiator], explains inter-city politics to the Council in a hurried rush, since the Council does not know Drake city politics.
Teliv warns that Pallass's seizure of the Raskghar was not diplomatically wise if Liscor wanted to control their fate.
Teliv admits he is out of his depth, since the [Senators] have Skills like his but out-level and outclass him.
Teliv says Liscor has no real levels on Pallass anyway.
Temile is an [Actor] who has become a low-level [Producer] in charge of the second-string Players of Celum.
Temile whips a new cast of Drakes, Gnolls and Humans into shape during rehearsal.
Temile says the Players who went north are earning more money than they can spend in sold-out shows near Invrisil.
Temile says money from the northern team has let the troupe hire [Builders] and [Carpenters] and lease apartments.
Temile's [Producer] class gave him a few Skills, among them [Eye for Talent], [Pinpoint Discord] and [Revitalizing Touch].
Temile has a stump on his hand, and Jasi observes it, since he fought Crelers.
Teresa Atwood prefers to be called Teres and is the twin sister of Trey Atwood.
Teres and Trey are sixteen, nearly seventeen, and come from England, with moderately dark blonde hair and fair skin.
Teres and Trey are both 5'10 tall, and are fraternal twins rather than identical.
Teres and Trey are close enough that they can usually understand what the other is thinking, and mirror each other's emotions.
Teres is summoned to this world with Trey and is one of Flos's two wards and personal attendants.
Teres and Trey come from another world, which Flos says tells of armies and weapons that would humble the greatest monsters, and it is they who reignited his flame.
Teres and Trey fell into Flos's throne room after stepping off a Tube subway train's ledge expecting to reach the platform.
Flos, sitting alone in a small chair in the empty throne room, was woken by their arrival after twenty years of slumber.
Teres and Trey had been in this world little more than a month by the time of the war with the Emperor of Sands.
Orthenon nearly ran Trey through before Flos stopped his men, and then the twins told the court everything.
Teres and Trey do not hold a servant class; Orthenon tells them to think of themselves as aides, expected to become bodyguards and assistants.
Teres and Trey are required to follow Flos around, mostly watching him attend to the kingdom.
Teres claims that Mars's breasts are fake.
Teres usually starts the twins' fights and is the first to pop her lid when they get angry.
Teres and Trey openly refuse Flos's order, shouting that they are not his subjects and that he is wrong.
Flos laughs ruefully and thanks Teres and Trey for speaking the truth, apologizing for demanding the opposite.
Teres and Trey wake at dawn for training; Teres takes Trey's pillow away to wake him, and stands swaying with her eyes closed.
Teres trains every day away from the courtyard with Orthenon and comes back looking like she ran a marathon.
Teres and Trey fought with Flos and each other over Flos selling the first army he crushed to slavers, and the rift lasted months.
Teres is a Level 18 [Warrior] taught by Orthenon, soon to become a [Swordswoman], and spars with Flos and Mars.
Teres explains television to Flos, who listens with growing interest, and she curses Trey for leaving her behind.
Teres and Trey feel like friends or siblings but not like twins, and Trey cannot tell what Teres is thinking.
Teres gave Trey a full account of what had happened with Flos, the Quarass and Hellios.
Teres tells Trey that Gazi was once a slave whom Flos found and raised, and who became one of his Seven by killing many people.
