Teres is with Flos at Blalevault, where she asks Mars whether all her illusions have huge breasts.
Teres rides with Flos while Trey goes with the Quarass to Khelt, since Flos thinks Trey the better [Diplomat].
Teres's iPhone is recharged by a [Repair] spell cast by Ulyse, leader of the [Mage]-group Parasol Stroll, after both twins' phones had died within two days of arrival.
Teres photographs Flos on the balcony as returning refugees approach, and he stiffens into an old-photograph pose.
Teres urges Flos to smile or point, and he gives his fakest smile, and the flash makes the picture a work of art in the hall of failure.
Teres is one of the King of Destruction's personal servants and befriends a Garuda [Soldier] named Mefaa, who rose from Level 2 to Level 13 in under two weeks.
Flos forbade Teres to fight Manticores, since they are above her level.
Teres likes Orthenon, and Orthenon tells her she is to be Flos's bodyguard rather than a [Commander].
Teres wears a slightly curved sword at her hip and is addressed as Lady Atwood.
Teres was haunted by the people she killed with a sword after the battle at Reim, but she no longer dreams of her kills.
Teres rides a mare she named Frecklehooves, and this was her sixth major engagement, at the border of Jecrass.
Flos was offended at the name Frecklehooves.
Teres arrives freshly bathed in Fetohep's court as the only outsider present, and denies she saw Vampires.
Teres tells Fetohep that Trey is on special business she cannot name, and that Flos told her to take a break and placate him.
Teres says that Flos did not have Trey fight in the war, and that peace talks are under way.
Teres tells Fetohep that Gazi is gone, and that Trey and two of Parasol Stroll's [Mages] are heading to a harbor in Nerrhavia's Fallen.
Teriarch is a Dragon who lives in a cave in the High Passes and first appears to Ryoka as a silver-haired old mage.
In human form Teriarch has silvery-white hair, a statuesque body, and eyes that are blue and violet like nebulas.
Teriarch's human form is nearly six foot six with faintly bronze skin, white hair and pointed ears.
In true form Teriarch is a massive bronze-scaled Dragon with a mane like molten bronze and mismatched eyes.
His bronze scales look golden in the light, and his mismatched eyes are heliotrope and cerulean.
Teriarch is about the size of a passenger airliner in Ryoka's estimation.
Later, the Dragon is called a brass Dragon with a copper-like mane.
Teriarch lives in a cave of marble, art, weapons and treasure that he insists is a collection and not a hoard.
His human illusion still casts a dragon-shaped shadow, which he removes later.
Teriarch swears by "Tamaroth's beard" and "Darkscale's breath".
Teriarch casts spells without speaking them aloud.
Teriarch remembers ten thousand years ago, when four true Dragons flew, and watched one fall in the Creler wars.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch freezes Ryoka in place, forbids magic and violence, and questions her under a truth spell.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch cannot read Ryoka's class or level with appraisal and identification spells.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch wants news after being secluded for years and asks if Magnolia Reinhart still lives.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch asks about a Runner named Ryoka Griffin without knowing she is the girl in front of him.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Ryoka realizes Teriarch cannot scry her because he lacks the kanji spelling of her real name.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch gives Ryoka a scroll and a small silver-and-onyx ring to deliver to Az'kerash, also named Perril Chandler.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch tells Ryoka Az'kerash is a [Necromancer] with white hair and skin and violet eyes who may use illusions.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch says both Az'kerash and himself are shielded from spells of location or communication.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch says the mana Ryoka drank would not have killed her, only caused violent illness over days.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch teleports Ryoka from his home toward Celum and introduces himself by name.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch lectures that the rhetorical question was invented by Dragons.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Ryoka concludes a geas drove her toward the Blood Fields and burned her arms with runes when she turned back.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Ryoka thinks Teriarch implied Az'kerash would be near the Blood Fields, surrounded by the dead.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch speaks with Magnolia over four hundred miles by a spell no mage can eavesdrop on.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch has known Magnolia for thirty or forty years, since she was a girl, and expects to outlive her.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch says he could not teleport Magnolia to him because both homes are heavily warded.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch says he tried to scry Ryoka many times and failed.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch thinks Ryoka's name must hide a trick that defeats his scrying.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Magnolia says the ring is magical and the delivery important.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Ryoka returns to Teriarch, who gives her a stone with a golden arrow that points to Az'kerash's magical signature southwest.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch had earlier paid forty gold to reach him and a single Potion of Haste for the delivery.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch agrees to pay eight hundred gold for the delivery after offering lower sums.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch has ignored Magnolia's messages while sulking, and she gave him an earful about the delivery.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch says Reinhart does not have the power to order him about.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch heals Ryoka's feet with [Mend] and gives her eight hundred gold as agreed.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch watches the High Passes by scrying after waking, but cannot focus on Ryoka because her name will not work.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch considers casting a [Greater Geas] on Ryoka before he smells her fresh blood.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch burns the Frost Faeries accompanying Ryoka with a spit of fire.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch claims to be an [Archmage] and suspects Magnolia's pranks when Ryoka identifies him as a Dragon.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch takes five thousand eight hundred and eleven pears at eight silver each as a sum test, and Ryoka answers forty-six thousand four hundred and eighty-eight silver.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch agrees to scry for Erin Solstice after Ryoka begs, and offers her hospitality while the spell runs.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Ryoka tells Teriarch her original name is in another language, which is why scrying with "Ryoka" failed.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch knew Ryoka was from another world through Lady Magnolia and will not divulge Magnolia's secrets.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch says he can erase only chosen memories.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch says Gnomes and Elves have walked on the twin moons.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch says Gnolls can learn magic and finds Wistram's expulsion of a Gnoll apprentice two hundred years ago puzzling.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch calls the Frost Faeries pests and says their glamour usually defeats even accomplished mages.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch repairs Ryoka's iPhone with [Repair] and duplicates a torn piece with [Reconstruct], keeping the copy.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch refuses to duplicate the iPhone again, since Dragons hate that their possessions can be copied.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch gives Ryoka a spellbook for a price after she refuses ten or twenty thousand gold.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Ryoka tells Teriarch she lost her fingers to a pact with the faeries that cost a Gnoll tribe.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch says the Gods are dead in this world, and the faeries travel between worlds.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch spares Ryoka's memory after she promises to tell no one that he is a Dragon.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch says he does not receive letters, and Magnolia must use a mage spell.

section: Meeting Ryoka and the delivery to Az'kerash (Books 1-2)
text: Teriarch tells Ryoka they will not meet again.
Teriarch speaks to Magnolia by mind link after the assassins' attack, offering to be there in minutes or to fly.
Magnolia answers that there is only so much he can do from his cave.
Teriarch appears at Erin's inn in human form as an old man with a white beard and mismatched cerulean and heliotrope eyes.
Teriarch in human form defeats the Horns of Hammerad and Pisces using basic spells such as [Stone Dart], [Mud Slap], [Call Object] and [Frozen Wind].
Teriarch casts [Tripgrass], [Flash], [Snowball] and [Flame Jet] against them.
Teriarch kicks Pisces unconscious and leaves all of them alive.
Teriarch scolds Ceria and Pisces that Wistram's standards have fallen greatly.
Teriarch asks about Archmage Zelkyr, and Ceria answers that he died over a century or two centuries ago.
Teriarch refuses Pisces's plea to be his apprentice.
Teriarch has played the game 2048 on his copy of Ryoka's iPhone and learned the swipe from Erin.
Teriarch releases the remote spell on his human form and realizes Erin Solstice is "the girl".
Teriarch reaches over five hundred thirty-eight quintillion cookies per second in Cookie Clicker on his iPhone copy and then says he feels empty.
Ryoka bursts into his cave, broken and weeping, and screams that Az'kerash had killed because of his letter.
Teriarch rebuilds Ryoka's heart and dispels the death magic, reviving her.
Teriarch's cave at the High Passes is marked by a yellow flag tied to a rock.
Teriarch calls Venitra "Wretch. Thing.", hurls her into the mountainside and burns her with dragonfire.
Teriarch breaches Az'kerash's [Message] with a fire spelling "Worm" and burns his room.
Az'kerash survives with [Snap Freeze], [Void Room], [Sanctuary of Protection] and [Wall of the Damned].
Teriarch declares Ryoka under his protection and extracts Az'kerash's promise to leave her and her associates alone.
Teriarch tells Az'kerash he may send someone to collect what is left of Venitra.
Teriarch tells Az'kerash that Ryoka delivered a gift for him and calls him Chandler.
Teriarch says a death spell destroys little and that he is a master of magic.
Teriarch flies Ryoka back under an invisibility spell and drops her within sight of Liscor's east wall.
Teriarch says he will not force Ryoka to keep Az'kerash's secret and declines another geas.
Teriarch appears in human form at the inn to say he does not believe Ivolethe is dead.
Teriarch believes Ivolethe was punished by banishment and not killed.
Teriarch says the faerie king has many names, such as the Lord of the Glades, and he has never met him.
Teriarch declines to attack the Goblin Lord or Az'kerash, saying he does not know if he could win.
Teriarch says Az'kerash was not always an enemy of the living and that Teriarch knew his past.
Teriarch says Goblins are as innocent as any race.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch intercepts mages' communications and dismisses Magnolia's [Message] spells asking for a General, a Strategist and him.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch owns a magical copy of Ryoka's iPhone, charged constantly, and listens to podcasts to sleep.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Wyverns attack Teriarch's cave, and he vaporizes one with a ray from a talon and throws glowing meteors.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: He says he bested the Wyvern matriarch two hundred years ago.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch searches for a Baneblade he misplaced and uses an enchanted trident and a quiver of exploding arrows.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch plans to hire Gold-rank adventurers against the pests after he wakes.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch wakes to a recorded iPhone alarm in his own voice saying his hoard is being stolen.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch moved his home less than a year earlier and set up Evielda's Skyshield spells.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch reveals himself to Rags in his cave and freezes her Redfangs with a word.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch tells Rags she holds Velan's key and that he does not have the second key.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch tells Rags he is neither ally nor hindrance and she must not reveal his presence.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch says Garen once challenged him over the key and was removed.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch says Velan climbed the High Passes to hide his treasure for one who was worthy.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch says Curulac of a Hundred Days and Sove the Island Queen each left a legacy.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch says he could tell Rags the Goblin Kings' secret only if she spoke the right words.

section: Reinhart, Zel and the wyvern war (Books 6, 13, 15, 16)
text: Teriarch posts a [Message] bounty to guilds within two hundred miles: 2,000 gold per Wyvern head and 80,000 for the Greater Wyvern.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Magnolia's [Message] spells hover unread around Teriarch's head while he sleeps.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch wakes believing a hundred hunters mean to kill him and roars a challenge, then remembers he hired them for Wyverns.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch keeps a second cave in the High Passes with wards and a Dragonthrone.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch's hoard holds a Concealed Spoonblade forged by Maia Whitforgers and an armoire of holding with a thousand pounds of beef from a long-extinct breed.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch keeps notes on his hoard and affairs, and has fake personae such as Grand Magus Eldavin.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: A creature with Todi's face and overlong arms stands outside his cave, and he orders it away.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch heals Ryoka with a touch and feeds her the extinct beef.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Ryoka brings him a laptop, two smartphones and a tablet owned by the Earthers under Magnolia's protection.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch tells Ryoka that good or evil, effort or not, never matters because all things end.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch remembers meeting the Quarass of Germina in flowering Zeikhal and swearing a pact with her.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch remembers swearing to defend Iltanus under Empress Sheta and being called High Eminence.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch remembers Magnolia as a young woman asking him to join her, and he said he would think about it.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch scores Ryoka's plea fifty-seven out of a hundred and Magnolia's sixty-two, and refuses to act.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch gives Ryoka one starlight vial for Fierre that eases symptoms only.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch says interfering would begin the Nights of Blood again.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch agrees to copy the electronics into his hoard in exchange for one small favor.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch walks into Celum as a mismatched-eyed half-Elf [Mage], following Ryoka's magical trail.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch tells Ryoka his name is Grand Magus Eldavin and their business is unfinished.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: As Eldavin he claims to have been of Wistram's Council of Magi and absent over a hundred years, with the class [Grand Magus].

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch makes Ryoka explain the movie on Kevin's laptop, which shows a farting Ogre, and she makes Erin and Mrsha watch.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch says the Garden of Sanctuary was first created by Empress Sheta of Iltanus.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch says the soonest chance to meet Ivolethe comes in the middle of summer.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch speaks to Magnolia, declines her offer to visit Invrisil or Oteslia, and says he is putting in half-effort.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch tells Erin that safety is an illusion and she should value courage and moments.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch says "Ghosts" to Reiss near Numbtongue, and Reiss answers "Dragon".

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch explains the fae are bound by a compact, and Ivolethe was punished never to see Ryoka again.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch says Ivolethe is close to fae royalty.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch tells Ryoka to throw a ball for the Summer Court on the Summer Solstice, with no iron.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch says she needs a ruler's permission, a hundred nobles, and three of the greatest nobles of Izril.

section: Ryoka's plea and the Summer Court (Book 17)
text: Teriarch says Laken is new to Izril and so no true [Emperor] to the fae.

section: Eldavin at Magnolia's and the sealing (Books 18-19)
text: Teriarch appears as a tall half-Elf with Magnolia in Invrisil, and she grants his odd requests.

section: Eldavin at Magnolia's and the sealing (Books 18-19)
text: Teriarch asks Magnolia how she will deal with the mob, then says he is too tired and will watch.

section: Eldavin at Magnolia's and the sealing (Books 18-19)
text: Teriarch says he has seen every answer to riots and none is perfect.

section: Eldavin at Magnolia's and the sealing (Books 18-19)
text: Ryoka reads Teriarch's half-hearted replies as hints that the vampires' illness is connected.

section: Eldavin at Magnolia's and the sealing (Books 18-19)
text: Eldavin repairs Magnolia's pink magical carriage into a crimson red coach and refuses to scry on assassins.

section: Eldavin at Magnolia's and the sealing (Books 18-19)
text: Eldavin teleports cats off the roof and Sacra into the parlor, and tells her he has stayed three days.

section: Eldavin at Magnolia's and the sealing (Books 18-19)
text: Sacra lures Eldavin to Invrisil by saying Nalthaliarstrelous beat a young man.

section: Eldavin at Magnolia's and the sealing (Books 18-19)
text: Eldavin leaves the inn after sending Magnolia a note and tells Mrsha to write instead of using sign language.

section: Eldavin at Magnolia's and the sealing (Books 18-19)
text: Teriarch gives Magnolia his ring, and he does not answer her when she calls.

section: Eldavin at Magnolia's and the sealing (Books 18-19)
text: Teriarch severs [Messages], teleports Magnolia, Ressa and Reynold to safety, and tells them he reinforced the carriage.

section: Eldavin at Magnolia's and the sealing (Books 18-19)
text: Teriarch seals himself in absolute seclusion with a spell leaving no loopholes, and forgets the Summer Solstice.

section: Eldavin at Magnolia's and the sealing (Books 18-19)
text: Eldavin, a half-Elf body, wakes in a secret laboratory and leaves the cave to travel toward Wistram Academy.
Termin is a [Wagon Driver] who tells Pisces that wagon drivers commonly have Skills like [Continuous Rolling], since around there one moves fast or gets eaten.
Termin drives a cart at the head of a convoy of more than a hundred adventurers, [Guards], [Healers], [Masons] and [Hunters].
Termin says no army the Human cities could assemble would be half as powerful as one led by Zel Shivertail with Gold-rank teams and Antinium Soldiers.
Termin takes the Horns of Hammerad to Esthelm, then heads north as fast as he can, preferring to be closer to Invrisil if a Goblin Lord is coming.
Later, Termin says he levelled up after Ryoka rescued him from Wailer Frogs, and owes her a bit of a debt.
Termin runs a passenger shuttle with goods, with Invrisil as his last stop, pulled by two mules.
Tersk is a Prognugator of the Armored Antinium who greets Klbkch as a fellow Prognugator on the Hive delegation's arrival.
Tersk is a big two-armed Antinium with proper hands who wears steel plate armor and carries a shield and mace.
Tersk has no antennae under his helmet, so he signals his Soldiers by striking his mace against his shield.
Tersk describes the Armored Antinium as the sole Hive to use steel and metal to reinforce their bodies and to fight with weapons in formation.
Tersk is older than Dekass, the other Armored Prognugator who accompanies him in Book 15.

section: Xrn's delegation and the Free Antinium (Books 3-5)
text: Tersk brings three other Armored Antinium to Liscor, all as tall as he is and in armor, armed with swords and a spear.

section: Xrn's delegation and the Free Antinium (Books 3-5)
text: Tersk meets Pawn in the Free Antinium Hive and has two of his Soldiers carrying a greatsword and a spear brought in as examples.

section: Xrn's delegation and the Free Antinium (Books 3-5)
text: Tersk says he did not enter the dungeon himself because his safety matters to his Hive.

section: Xrn's delegation and the Free Antinium (Books 3-5)
text: Tersk considers Pivr a failure of the Prognugator class who does not deserve the title of Revalantor.

section: Xrn's delegation and the Free Antinium (Books 3-5)
text: Tersk reports that his Queen calls Klbkch the most stable and trustworthy of the three remaining Centenium.

section: Xrn's delegation and the Free Antinium (Books 3-5)
text: Tersk says his Queen told him Hives on Rhir sometimes had as many as thirty Prognugators each.

section: Xrn's delegation and the Free Antinium (Books 3-5)
text: Tersk admits that Klbkch and Xrn would know more than he does about the time before the Antinium crossed the ocean.

section: Xrn's delegation and the Free Antinium (Books 3-5)
text: Tersk has not worn his armor for a while, and sits at the Free Antinium table without it, eating bee soup that spills on his bare chest.

section: Xrn's delegation and the Free Antinium (Books 3-5)
text: Tersk confides that the Armored Antinium lack the metal to outfit all their Soldiers and use monster hides and bark for Workers and some Soldiers, a secret his Queen would not want told.

section: Xrn's delegation and the Free Antinium (Books 3-5)
text: Tersk asks for the recipe for Erin's bee soup, believing his Queen will rejoice at it.

section: Xrn's delegation and the Free Antinium (Books 3-5)
text: Tersk tells Pawn he will regret leaving, but must go because his Hive has to know what the Free Antinium have done.
Tersk holds the history book in shock as it describes an entire Antinium army destroyed by a Goblin, and snatches it back from Pivr's acid.
Tersk had not known the history of the Second Antinium War in any great detail.
Tersk stands with three other Prognugators in thick steel armor as Xrn briefs the Antinium army before the attack on Liscor.
Tersk knows why the Antinium want a city, remembering the strange city and what he learned there, while the other Prognugators are confused.
Tersk thinks of Pawn and wonders whether the Worker is as excited as he is.
Tersk and Dekass walk Liscor's streets in disguise without their customary steel armor, being subtle.
Tersk is a little taller than Dekass, as befits his higher status.
Tersk tells Dekass they are a personal greeting from the Armored Queen and a warning, and that his wish to visit Liscor is also personal.
Tersk asks a young Drake for directions to the nearest Antinium location or to Revalantor Klbkch of the Free Antinium, claiming they are normal Workers.
Tersk notes that the access tunnel is done and that he and Dekass are the first visitors to the city, with more to come.
Tersk and Dekass are hosted by the Free Antinium as the first visitors to use the new passage meant to link them to the other Hives.
Two Antinium in disguise tell Lyonette they are ordinary Workers, then ordinary Soldiers, while one whispers "Nearly perfect infiltration" and the other answers "Thank you, Tersk".
Tersk had talked nonstop to Dekass about the food of the inn, which Dekass fears might be poisoned.
Tersk and Dekass say they are ordinary Antinium and ask Drassi to see her supply of liquids.
Tersk tells Dekass the Free Antinium are weak in shell and number, but have morale and an understanding of living that escapes the Armored Antinium.
Tersk and Dekass pay for their drinks in gold from a bag of holding issued for the mission.
Tersk's secret scrying orb is compromised by Wistram's alert just before the Wyvern attack on the inn.
Tersk and Dekass show up at the inn every day, eating and then leaving, and have been doing so for weeks.
Tersk and Dekass are ordered and allowed to frequent the inn, try new foods, watch plays and ask questions.
Xrn gave the Antinium visitors her anti-food-poisoning charm on a wooden amulet.
Tersk looks content and bloated, casually talking with Belgrade, while Erin wonders what he does all day.
Tessia is one of Laken's two [Engineers] and was the first to acquire the class.
Tessia is the higher-leveled of Laken's two [Engineers].
Tessia is a young woman who lived all her life on a farm before finding a vocation making weapons of war.
Tessia pulls the rope on Laken's trebuchets and took to them remarkably well.
Tessia is Gamel's girlfriend.
Tessia, an [Engineer], is in Wiskeria's war tent and looks beside herself as the general speaks to her about the enemy's trebuchets.
Teura is a half-Elf with bright red hair and sable eyes, and Blackmage flushes around her.
Teura is senior to many [Mages], having lived in Wistram for over six decades, and belongs to Archmage Feor's personal faction.
Teura guards and escorts Blackmage through Wistram.
Teura tells Blackmage that the Council deliberated on waiving fees, a Revivalist notion rejected as too drastic.
Feor tells Teura that Wistram is in a race to collect otherworlders.
Teura holds the mists back around herself in the plaza, brightening the air.
Teura is a half-Elf High Mage, a Council member and a Centrist under Archmage Feor.
Teura still holds a grudge against Aaron for giving her the slip when he was under her authority.
Thaina is a female Antinium Soldier, one of the two female Soldiers along with Chesacre.
Thaina's paint forms a whole with Chesacre's across their two bodies.
Thaina and Chesacre wash each other, with Thaina dipping her cloth into a bucket, before they take their paint.
Thaina and Chesacre paint a joint design of a silver building on each other's bodies, in the privacy made by blankets that Purple Smiles hangs.
Thaina sits next to Chesacre when Klbkch walks toward Pawn, and stands up after Chesacre's arm is cut off.
Thaina uses Mrsha's sign language for the first time to say she and this one would like a drink too, pointing instead of using a name.
Thaina is trembling when she signs a request to Mrsha for her words, and Mrsha agrees.
Soldiers could never talk, and their identities came when they painted themselves, but they can have words.
The [Enforcer] is an unnamed, high-level criminal who goes only by his class, [Enforcer], and strolls into Celum unnoticed.
The [Enforcer] is a member of the Brotherhood of Serendipitous Meetings, whose branches turn up in unexpected places and whose members keep standards.
The [Enforcer] wears a cap he treats with care, and brushing something off it relaxes a tense confrontation.
The [Enforcer] has a [Grudgescent Terrier] Skill that lets him see the deaths of his associates on the person responsible.
The [Enforcer] refuses to budge before a [Nightstalker] of the Sisters of Chell, and takes his hat off.
A [Blackguard] with the [Nightstalker] freezes mid-strike when the hatless [Enforcer] looks at him.
The [Enforcer] says it was just a bit of dust on his cap, and the [Nightstalker] realises she misjudged his level and nature.
The [Enforcer] asks Numbtongue about three Humans who wore caps and died during the siege of Liscor.
The [Enforcer] hums a rhyme about slow thieves dying that Numbtongue recognises from the thieves who took Erin's door.
The [Enforcer] asks how Numbtongue crossed paths with his brothers and why he killed them.
The [Enforcer] says his Skill [Grudgescent Terrier] lets him see the deaths of his associates on Numbtongue, and asks him not to lie.
Numbtongue admits he killed the three men.
The [Enforcer] concludes that Numbtongue had no warning of the group's arrival and simply saw the boats and the door.
The [Enforcer] tells the [Nightstalker] that Numbtongue is a tribe Goblin, and she tells him to step off.
The [Enforcer] says Numbtongue answered truthfully or his Skills would have said so.
The [Enforcer] says his association does not as a rule work with Goblins or non-Humans, but has a few such lads in its ranks.

A narrator describes a warlord who conquered a whole continent and was sweeping through the next when his empire suddenly collapsed; the books never say why, and though he was not killed or harmed, he abandoned world conquest.
That king now sits in a crumbling kingdom while other countries pick apart his empire, and he is called the King of Destruction.
In the Interlude, the King is an older man in his forties, with red-gold hair beginning to streak with grey, a muscled physique and emerald eyes.
The King sits in a smaller chair across from the empty golden throne in a cracked, decaying throne room, wearing worn, finely woven gold-embroidered robes over chainmail.
The King tells two young strangers from another world that he knows they are telling the truth, not just because of a Skill.
The King describes his empire as once packed with people of every nation, with goods from afar and armies marching, until he abandoned his dreams of conquest and let the nation he had built collapse.
The King's city below his balcony is crumbling, its people malnourished and its food rotten.
Moved by the twins' news of a greater world, the King takes up his throne, tells his steward Orthenon that he has returned, and calls his kingdom to wake.
Orthenon reports that the kingdom is failing: the treasury is empty, crops have failed, armories are rusted, nearly every decent soldier has fled and foreign armies hold the vassals' lands.
The King orders his vassals to dispose of the foreign forces within two days and rejoin him with warriors and youths of worth.
The King names the twins his personal attendants and bodyguards.
The Interlude ends with the word spreading across the countryside and the world that the King of Destruction, Flos, has returned.
Thelican is a Stitch-person [General] of Nerrhavia, who commands its nearly three hundred thousand strong army at Oliphant.
Thelican reclines on a sofa in a large tent, attended by eight servants, and eats nuts fed by a Garuda [Slave].
Thelican's silk-turned-flesh skin gleams palely.
Thelican's officers are of the Silk-caste, and the Stitch-warriors made of Hemp are sturdier.
Thelican says his Hemp [Soldiers] will take the first wave at the walls, and that he needs only Illivere's Golems.
Thelican pulls Nerrhavia back nearly six hundred paces from Oliphant and fortifies when news comes that the Empress of Beasts sought the King of Destruction's aid.
Thelican tells a [Mage] to tell Yisame he is fortifying and that the armies stay where he says.
Thelican orders General Heic of Deimos to hold the left flank or he will break Heic's army himself.
Alked Fellbow tells Thelican he forfeits his contract if Flos has joined Tiqr.
Thelican says Nerrhavian pride demands Nsiia be taken as its prisoner, on Queen Yisame's insistence.
Thelican, tongue-tied, yields Nsiia to Femithain after weighing the wealth of garrisoning Oliphant.
Theofore is an [Assassin] who looks so ordinary that he is forgettable, which Magnolia suspects is a skill.
Theofore clearly dislikes being addressed by his name.
Theofore is not a high-level member of the Guild, but is competent enough to be assigned to Lady Magnolia on request.
Theofore and his associates guarded Ryoka Griffin for Lady Magnolia but lost her when she accepted a request to the High Passes.
Theofore told Magnolia his group was not equipped to fight monsters, having assumed the job was protection against other humans.
After his team's failure, Theofore said Magnolia would be fully reimbursed, but that the Guild would take no further responsibility.
Theofore was assigned to watch Ryoka at the inn and found her climbing onto the roof over her room.
Ryoka kicked Theofore's right leg just above the knee, numbing it, and then outran him across the rooftops.
Theofore knew Magnolia would be unhappy with his failure and went back to the inn to report.
Theofore uses an unarmed combat skill, [Nerve Strike: Paralysis], and Ryoka swatted his hand down.
Theofore lacks the [Sure Footing] skill, which would have helped him fight on the slanted roof.
In Book 2, a report to Magnolia says Theofore has located Ryoka, who will return in two days.
Magnolia thinks Theofore perhaps understands Ryoka better than the other [Assassins] and [Scouts] who searched.
Theofore reported that two of Ryoka's fingers are missing and that she is not alone.
Theofore believes Ryoka may have rescued a young Gnoll cub.
By Book 11, Theofore is an [Assassin] who stands in Magnolia's entrance hall beside her [Butler] and [Maid], with a bounty put on him by the Guild.
Theofore's fellow [Assassins] thought he was dead, and he answers that life is not so kind.
Theofore draws a throwing dagger and tells three attacking trainees that he is better than all of them.
Theofore urges the trainees to surrender, and they throw down their blades.
Therrium Sailwinds is a half-Eel Drowned Man and a Depth Captain of the Undersea Crews, who commands the Drowned ship The Passing Shadow.
The Passing Shadow is feared above and under the sea.
Therrium has three sons, a ship of his own and a good deal of gold, and is used to risky ventures though he hates it when they fall through.
Before he is named, Therrium appears as the unnamed half-Eel captain of a Drowned ship with a half-starfish [First Mate]; he can walk through lightning and generate it, and his fish-half is rubbery.
Therrium's enchanted sword shocks any enemy [Depth Sailor] whose blade it locks with.
Seborn, a Drowned [Rogue] with a half-Crab body, recognises Therrium on a broadcast and the narration calls Therrium his father.
Seborn describes Captain Therrium as a lawless [Thief], despised even by other Drowned Folk for not honouring his word.

The unnamed half-Eel captain of a Drowned ship follows the Emerald Signet, saying that everyone has heard the rumour of a treasure map and that whether it heads into Seagrass' waters or sails with an armada of storm-ships, they follow.
Therrium's scouts find nothing in the first shipwreck that the landfolk did not find, and he curses the landfolk who plundered it.
A second Drowned ship follows the Emerald Signet along with his own, and its captain is the other [Depth Captain] who is making the same calculation as Therrium.
Therrium watches the jellyfish attack on the Emerald Signet and then the giant crab, and he and the other Drowned captain decide not to take the guarded wrecks, saying "Nope".
Therrium curses on seeing Rasea Zecrew's ships, since he knows her and her ship spells trouble.
Two Drowned ships clash, and Therrium defeats the other [Depth Captain], who surrenders her blade and signs a document placing her under his command for six months.
The quarrel was over whether to attack at once and take the Swords of Serept, and Therrium insists on waiting for the final shipwreck.

Therrium, with the Sinking Light behind him, surrounds the Emerald Signet from beneath, and demands that the students surrender the treasure; he tells Wil that he does not intend to spill landfolk blood.
Therrium has the casket opened with an oar, sees the diamond blades flash, and takes the casket onto his ship.
Therrium tells Wil, after the theft, that it is nothing personal and that the adventure was failed from the start.
Therrium blows off the head of Fetohep's sand form with a wand and orders the chest lashed to the side of his ship, planning to dispel Fetohep's magic underwater.
Therrium advances with his Drowned crew on the deck of Prince Khedal's warship, and tells Wil that it would have been better if he had given over the blades at the beginning.
Therrium places a half-Blowfish [Archer] on the prow of The Passing Shadow, and Lasc warns that one dose from her arrows is deadly.
Therrium gives the Emerald Signet a last chance to stop or die, and raises a hand as the archer sights.
Zeres, a Walled City, fires on the Drowned ship with spells and its Drake navy sails out, and Therrium, in a rage, curses the landfolk and their Walled Cities.

Therrium orders Glisal, a half-Blowfish [Venom Archer], to aim at the [Lord] and kill him, and she spits venom onto an arrow, which the narration calls his one last vengeance, and the ship then sinks under the waves.
Thomast Veniral is the [Chevalier] husband of Lady Bethal Walchaís and is known as Sir Thomast.
Thomast is renowned for his silence and lack of temper, in contrast to his wife's moods.
Thomast has warm black hair, a mustache, yellow-green eyes, a light red coat and a long, cat-like stride.
Thomast carries a long, thin duelist's blade and an enchanted rapier.
Thomast is a [Fencer], signing his open letter with that title.
Thomast fights better on foot than on horseback.
Thomast and Bethal ride without riding Skills, though both have excellent horses.
The Knights of the Petal look to Thomast rather than Bethal for orders in the field.
Thomast uses [Affair of Honor] to force a fleeing [Assassin] to turn and duel him.
Magnolia notes that few can match someone of the [Duelist] class in a one-on-one bout.
Thomast cuts the air with his rapier from a distance, wounding Hobs and testing Greybeard.
Thomast uses [Double Cut] against Greybeard, thrusting with a second silvery blur at the same moment.
Thomast sends wind slashes along his enchanted rapier and uses [Flawless Dodge] and [Lunge] against Assassins.
Thomast uses [Flicker Onslaught] to teleport between spots, striking down daggers, an arrow and an [Assassin] at once.
At Magnolia's ball Thomast kills the [Assassin] who murdered Patricia Melissar after forcing him to duel.
Thomast duels Greybeard but is cut open across the chest and stomach by the old Goblin's greatsword.
Thomast is healed from his wounds by the next day, and Bethal refuses to let him be first into combat.
Thomast recalls the Goblin Lord Greydath of Blades, who could cut the air itself, and says the old Goblin reminded him of him.
In the battle against the Goblin Lord, Thomast kills eight Hobs and rallies the Soldiers around him.
Thomast sidesteps the Goblin Lord's [Deathbolt], which kills the Hob instead, and coolly beckons the Goblin Lord to duel.
Thomast wrote an open letter defending the Human [Ladies] of the Sacrifice of Roses to the Drake [Historian] who questioned their sacrifice.
Thomast says he regrets writing it, as he was young and was challenged to eight duels within the week.
Thomast was at the war, writing that he was there and will never forget the sacrifice.
Thomast and Bethal first met at a ball at Magnolia's estate after Bethal deliberately ran into him.
Thomast and Bethal were sent to kill Laken in a duel of honor if they judged him too dangerous.
Thomast says the fae warrior at Laken's banquet could have killed him in a duel, and that he hated the banquet.
Thomast asks Bethal why she did not tell Magnolia the poison was meant for her.
Ellia Cantras warns Oswalt to keep away from Bethal or her husband will run him through, saying Thomast is ten times better with a rapier than anyone there.
Bethal asks Thomast to bring his good sword as she mounts her Knights of the Petal for war over the black roses.
Thomast makes Bethal swear on the Sacrifice of Roses to wait an hour before acting over the black roses.
Bethal slaps Thomast across the face, and he does not rub the handprint, telling Kerrig and Welca to investigate the Runner's Guild.
Thomast pursues Bethal south out of Reizmelt and catches up when she slows her horse.
Thomast tells the Assassins he has no [Fencer]'s bell because it makes too much noise and his wife despises the sound.
Thomast's silver bell is much worn and scratched, and Kerrig confirms it is genuine and that Thomast would never give it up.
Thomast gives Ryoka his silver bell as proof, whispers a message for Sir Nathald, grandmaster of the Knights of the Petal, and sends her west.
Thomast thinks the Assassins were amateurs, first-tier recruits of the Assassin's Guild, but well armed and paid in advance.
Thomast kills several Assassins protecting Bethal on the road, helped when a scarecrow, the [Farmer] Lupp, shoots one with a bow.
Thomast chases two fleeing Assassins and catches one, saying the other would have taken too long.
Thomast whispers a plan to Bethal for Sir Kerrig and Sir Nathald to move on the Order of Clairei Fields without any deaths or war.
Sir Kerrig says Thomast proclaimed that the Order of the Petal draws no blood unless necessary.
Thomast says he wants a more secure way to communicate than [Message] spells.
Thomast pickpockets Maviola's money pouch, apologizing, and says Bethal wants fair turnabout for the stolen mare.
Thomast says he met Bethal in a similar situation.
Thomast leaps from his horse to shield Bethal from Maviola's thrown bucket and takes most of it.
Thomast introduces himself to Erin as Thomast Veniral, Lady Bethal's husband, apologizing for the misunderstanding.
Thomast and Bethal stay at the Player's Retreat while Knights of the Petal guard Erin's inn.
Warmage Thresk's personal sanctuary is a small narrow room holding a rack of unusual weapons, a bookshelf of a mage's library, gold coins and gems, and a two-part staff topped with an aquamarine.
A guardian voice in the room warns Ceria and Pisces that they are trespassing in the personal sanctuary of Warmage Thresk.
A scholar says that Warmage Thresk of Albez is a [Mage] he has studied from unearthed artifacts, whose secret quarters were recently looted by adventurers.
The scholar says the plain door was the final trap of Thresk's apartments, which teleported unwary robbers into a room full of overlapping [Insanity] spells.
Thriss is a [Sergeant] in the 4th Battalion of the Raverian Fighters' Company, who recruits soldiers from a crowd in a Baleros city.
Thriss has an amazingly loud voice, which Geneva wonders may be a Skill.
Thriss commands 6th Squad, in which Geneva marches.
Thriss carries a huge mace into battle.
Thriss asked if Geneva was a [Warrior] or [Mage] and then hired her when she said she was a [Doctor].
Thriss said the company has no magical items or [Appraise] user able to verify a class, so lying about one would be found out.
Geneva suspected Thriss had the healing potion ready for the dislocation demonstration and expected someone to be hurt.
After Geneva removed an arrowhead from Clara, Thriss promised to get her the equipment she needed and spoke of respect for her.
Thriss gave Geneva the iron key to the healing-potion chest, agreed on by the officers, and warned of hell if any potions went missing.
Thriss held a full healing potion in a water flask at his side, but the battalion's regular soldiers would not receive potions.
Thriss told Geneva the closest force, the Burning March 6th Battalion, refused to give them potions.
Thriss said he believes in souls, even if there are no gods to judge them.
Thriss wanted to take a wounded Centaur from Geneva for interrogation and threatened to have her executed, but looked away first when she held to her oath.
On the last day of the war, Thriss killed a Centaur who had spared Geneva, struck her down with his mace and shouted "Traitor!"
Thriss's blows broke Geneva's spine.
Later, Thriss dies when Okasha stabs a blade through his chest as he raises his mace over Geneva.
Thrissiam Blackwing is a Drake [General] from Pallass, the northernmost of the six Walled Cities.
Thrissiam is a [Lineholder General] whose formations suit fighting Goblins.
Thrissiam is chosen to lead the suppression effort against the Goblins and the Goblin Lord, and he rides a mare.
Thrissiam fights with a spear and has an enchanted spear.
Thrissiam is a relation of Osthia Blackwing, technically her uncle but only about ten years older and a distant cousin.
Thrissiam taught Osthia to use a spear, accepted her into his army and gave her her first promotion.
Thrissiam expects to take seniority against the Goblin Lord, but meets Garusa Weatherfur, a higher-ranking and higher-level Gnoll [General].
Thrissiam bows his head first and accepts overall command when Garusa declines to lead.
Thrissiam sends Osthia's Oldblood company on scouting flights.
Thrissiam sleeps with Garusa during the siege, and Osthia later recalls the Gnoll as someone he loved for a short few days.
Thrissiam tells Garusa he will not risk her, calling her an asset that cannot be replaced.
Thrissiam slaps Osthia after she dives at the Goblin Lord, then forgives her and tells her she is a treasure of their family.
Thrissiam and Garusa plan an ambush of the Goblin Lord's forward camps, having observed his predictable movements.
Thrissiam realizes the Goblin Lord's master is the Necromancer, whom he says is not dead.
Thrissiam orders his Scouts and Runners to flee south to warn the cities, and orders Osthia to fly away.
Thrissiam tells Osthia to tell them the Goblin Lord has a master, the Necromancer, and to bring back Shivertail and the Tidebreaker.
Thrissiam kills the undead Garusa, fights on against the undead and dies holding a Gnoll in his arms.
An hour after his death, Thrissiam's corpse rises as undead and lurches north after the Goblins, not to Liscor.
Osthia fears she will someday see her uncle among the Goblin Lord's undead, and has so far not found him.
A dying Drake soldier reports that Thrissiam ordered both armies to buy time so word could reach the other cities.
A red-scaled Drake at a table says Thrissiam and Garusa died with over twenty thousand Gnolls and Drakes and blames bickering over the size of the force.
Timbor Parithad is a big, bearded, red-haired man who owns the Drunken Swordsman, which he calls one of the finest inns in Celum.
Timbor is a Level 24 [Innkeeper].
Timbor threatens Erin and tells her to make things right, as an experienced [Innkeeper] lecturing an upstart.
Pisces says Timbor holds a particular grudge against Erin Solstice, having been one of the [Innkeepers] who upset her.
Garia protests that Timbor is a great innkeeper who has had her over for years, and wants to speak to Erin.
Timbor worries about the Antinium Ksmvr in the room and asks the Horns of Hammerad for a promise that it will not act up.
Timbor sends a free round of drinks around the room.

section: The loss of the Drunken Swordsman
text: Timbor sits on the ground in tears before the ruins of his inn, which is gone.

section: The loss of the Drunken Swordsman
text: Erin sits with Timbor and hugs him as he breaks down, though they were enemies a day earlier.

section: The loss of the Drunken Swordsman
text: Erin takes Timbor to the magic door and helps him through the line, and Lyonette leads him to a bed.

section: The loss of the Drunken Swordsman
text: Later, Timbor leaves Celum and opens a second Drunken Swordsman in Liscor under the new name The Drunken Gnoll.
Timor du Havrington is a young noble student of Wistram who carries a sword and stands with Charles de Trevalier.
Charles de Trevalier claims Timor is an experienced warrior with many levels in the [Warrior] class who would cut Pisces to bits.
Timor himself claims to be a [Warrior] and a [Lord], but his voice trembles and he does not hold himself like a warrior.
Timor and Charles run a Wistram faction called the Libertarians.
Timor approaches Pisces to invite him to join the Libertarians, offering quite a few incentives.
Timor keeps pestering Pisces after the refusal, wanting him to abandon his friendship with Ceria and add his abilities to Charles.
Pisces refuses the invitation outright.
Tkrn is a Gnoll [Guardsman] of Liscor's City Watch who is assigned to the city gates.
Tkrn carries a sword at his waist and a shield buckled to one arm, and is dangerous even without them.
Tkrn is a junior [Guardsman] who grew up in Liscor and like most city Gnolls is under Krshia's unofficial command.
Tkrn calls Krshia his aunt.
Tkrn has the Skill [Eagle Eyes].
Tkrn is among seven Gnolls who lie hidden in the grass with bows to watch Ksmvr and the Soldiers outside Liscor.
Tkrn is the most junior and most inexperienced of the Gnolls with Krshia, and flattens his ears in embarrassment at a mistake.
During the undead attack on Liscor, Tkrn reports to Captain Zevara that the streets are closed off but larger creatures are out there.
Tkrn reports the Southern Gates are closed with archers shooting at climbing undead, but guards on the north walls have fled.
Tkrn is on duty at the gates when Erin stumbles past.
Tkrn says he saw from the walls with [Eagle Eyes] that Erin's inn was broken.
Tkrn brings Erin a bouquet of smelly orange flowers as the first Gnoll suitor, saying he has heard she seeks a mate.
Tkrn gives Erin a cheap carved wooden ring, believing it is what Humans have before they mate.
Erin suspects Krshia put Tkrn up to courting her.
Erin reports that Krshia said Tkrn was marking her inn so other Gnolls knew he was courting her.
Tkrn herds a distressed girl out of the gates, and his face is blank and impassive.
Zevara, Captain of the Watch, watches Tkrn move the girl farther from the gates.
Tkrn comes to tip Krshia off about an auction of fresh meat from cows put down after injury.
Caught napping on duty, Tkrn tells Krshia the door in Erin's inn was stolen and recovered.
Tkrn says the thieves broke the connection to Pallass, and Olesm told Zevara a mana stone was broken.
Tkrn says Pallass cannot send reinforcements directly without the mana stone and would have to march an army north.
After Liscor's election Tkrn is in disgrace for being party to the torture and attempted murder of Calruz, though he tried to halt it.
Tkrn is the only [Guard] involved who is not fired.
Tkrn tried to stop the torture and execution and protected Mrsha, which is the only reason he still has a job according to Zevara.
Krshia appealed his case, and Tkrn's pay is almost nothing for a month, demoted to the lowest-level [Guardsman] on his last chance.
Tkrn tells the rookie Jerci that the special protocols for the inn are a joke played on rookies.
Tkrn says no one goes to the inn with trouble without a full squad, and usually Relc is sent in.
Tom is the name Thomas prefers to be called, and he is the class clown of his group of people summoned from Earth.
Tom says no one ever laughs at his jokes and that he is not actually that funny.
Tom has clinically diagnosed depression and no medicine in the new world, where the only drugs are different kinds of alcohol.
Tom says depression makes him feel worthless.
Tom wears white face paint with red on his mouth and juggles pins, performing prat falls and bad jokes for children.
Tom is a Level 19 [Clown], who took the class as a sign.
Tom has skills for clownish things like juggling and prat falls, and a [Loud Voice] skill that he thinks is odd for a [Clown].
Tom's main trick is pulling objects seemingly out of nowhere, which works within a 5 ft radius if he has them on him.
Tom has an annoying skill that plays a cheerful carnival tune from him unbidden.
After the village massacre, Tom reaches [Clown Level 24!], gains [Skill - Greater Pain Tolerance] and [Skill - Devil's Luck], and receives the Conditions [Horrific Laughter] and [Lesser Insanity].
Tom then gains [Hero Level 2!] and [Skill - Weapon Proficiency: Knives].
Later, Tom says he is a Level 28 [Clown] who is retired and has lost the [Hero] class by refusing to fight.
Tom says he has levelled four more times since the Demon massacre and has learned [Unerring Throw] and [Flawless Dodge].
[Unerring Throw] lets Tom choose where thrown things land but does not make him a good thrower, so a thrown knife strikes hilt-first.
Tom says the only skill his [Hero] class gave him was [Weapon Proficiency: Knives].
Tom's pocket space is two skills, [Sleight of Hand] and [Trick Space], an invisible space around his body that he pulls objects out of and puts into.
Tom's [Trick Space] holds juggling balls and pins, a dead flower, coins, knives, and a clown costume.
Tom steals a dagger from Nereshal's hand without touching it, and Nereshal says the skill resembles a bag of holding like the Fool's.
Tom levels up as both a [Clown] and a [Hero] after the fight with the Fool.
Chole says Tom is either choosing to be like that or has one of the sacrificial classes Lord Hayvon told them about.
Later, Tom has a new and deadly skill that creates a second identical Tom, used in a stage performance.
When Tom's clown music plays, a spectral audience laughs along, including a voice that is his own.
The other people from Earth remember the music and fear it.
Tom goes back into the village for the children after the group leaves, and Richard gives him a high-quality healing potion.
Tom believes the gods are dead as he holds a dying child, and says he has always been a failure and that his medicine is gone.
Tom says he cannot be a hero, cannot fight, and cannot save even one kid.
Tom concludes that Classes are what people make them and that [Clowns] are hilarious as well as funny.
Tom drinks two healing potions, which burn like fire because they are meant to be applied, not consumed.
Tom kills a Demon archer by pulling his own sword out of his hand with his skill and running him through.
Tom stabs the Demon Lieutenant in the stomach with her own dagger and the soldiers run.
Tom drags the wounded Lieutenant down the street toward a burning stable, telling jokes.
Tom opens the stable so panicked horses stampede past, and laughs even as they break his nose and hand.
By morning the Lieutenant is gone and Tom stands in a ring of dead Demon soldiers, covered in blood.
A dying Demon soldier calls Tom a monster.
Richard leads eighteen [Soldiers] and several townsfolk to find Tom laughing and blood-covered in the ruined village.
The soldiers and townsfolk freeze and recoil, Richard pales, and Emily throws up.
Tom later swears he will never be a [Clown] again, nor fight, after what he remembers.
Tom says he went crazy on the night Wilen died, when a Troll killed the boy.
Tom's inner voice tells him that his smile for everyone is wearing thin and that he lost it the day Wilen died.
Tom has lost at least thirty pounds from not wanting to eat, and he no longer wears face paint or juggles.
Tom calls the voice in his head "Tom" and insists it is only himself.
Keith tells Tom the "same thing over and over" definition of insanity is a myth and not Einstein's, and insanity is a legal term.
Tom's blood runs cold at Keith's correction.
The Blighted King rises at the feast and stares at Tom, and Tom fears the laughter in his head is not his own.
Tom grabs Captain Kirust at a feast and shouts that he is not a warrior and not a hero.
In the palace, Tom kills a Demon soldier with a thrown knife that sinks into his forehead.
Tom takes a second Demon's knife with his skill and kills him in a hand-to-hand fight, stabbed repeatedly in the stomach.
Tom screams that he is in control and that this is his choice while he fights the second Demon.
The Demon says Tom and he are both monsters before dying.
Erille pours a bottle over Tom's chest as he blacks out, and the voice says this was only the beginning.
Tom wakes in a larger room with a private bathroom, which no one else in his group received, and is invited to the gardens.
Tom believes he won the argument with the voice in the mirror, and the voice replies that it left a little present.
At a banquet, Tom discovers he is wearing a yellow clown suit and white face paint without remembering putting them on, and Cynthia screams.
Tom realises at the banquet that he is not in control.
Nereshal teleports Tom, falling from a tower, onto a Demon archer, whom Tom kills with a stab to the head.
Tom throws swords and other artifacts pulled from the air at the Demons, including Blightbane borrowed from the Blighted King.
Tom kicks the Demon [Mage] after knives wound her, and she vanishes with a word that sounds like despair.
Tom tells the Fool that a fool makes people laugh while a clown laughs at the world.
Tom pulls a fireball out of the Fool's own stored space and sets him on fire.
Tom has lost at least sixty pounds, and his kind face has turned cold.
Tom smashes mirrors, and Lord Hayvon allows him seven mirrors a week.
Tom tells Richard that no one is a good guy in this war and that Richard is a prisoner.
Tom shouts at Richard that the Skill, not himself, drives him mad and that it turned him into this.
Tom performs dark stand-up with a speaking stone in a converted bar at 5th Wall, before his Gloomless Troupe.
Tom tells the story of killing his first monster, which turns out to be Lady Emirelle's pet Skeljaw.
Tom stabs his own hand to make a knife vanish in his act.
In a skit, Tom and his clone wound each other for real, and Tom beats the second Tom to death with a stick.
Cirille thinks Emily has even eclipsed Tom, who has not yet used his latest and most horrifying skill.
Tom stabs a [Soldier] in the leg so the pain breaks the mind-haze and tells the soldiers to sound the alarm.
The Gloomless Troupe is unaffected by the haze, which puzzles the onlookers.
Tommie is a human [Warrior] on Walt's all-male [Warrior] team, the Ensoldier Shields.
Tommie's closest teammate is Belt, another [Warrior] who fights beside him.
Tommie grumbles to Walt that the Horns are eating snacks while riding their chariot, while the Ensoldier Shields march on foot.
Tommie and Belt are turned by pollen and walk into the Bloodfields, and Tommie is dragged towards the spore sacs by a root.
A Watchertree spears Tommie's right leg and shoulder with roots as he tries to heal himself with a potion.
Ksmvr leaps in, and Yvlon cuts the roots with her Sword of Weight so that Ksmvr drags Tommie free.
Yvlon lifts Tommie into the Horns' chariot as they flee.
Tommie and Belt look half-dead even after potions, but are later on their feet with holes in their armour.
Tommie says he owes the Horns one and proposes killing the adult Creler by attacking it from the inside.
Tommie uses [Armored Leap] to jump into the adult Creler's mouth, with Belt covering him with [Target Shield].
Tommie is covered by baby Crelers pouring out of the adult's stomach, and his corpse is shaken out of the Creler's mouth.
Later, Terrim of Walt's team remarks that Tommie would have been proud of the jump that took down the adult Creler.
Toren is a skeleton created by the mage Pisces and bound to protect and obey Erin Solstice.
Ceria notes that Toren is quite intelligent for a skeleton, which means Pisces is closer to his goal of an undead that levels.
Toren cannot speak.
Erin names the skeleton Toren, or Tor for short; the name means rook in another language, and Toren does not know what a rook is.
Toren is Level 2 after battling the adventurers, and has gained the skill [Sword Fighting – Basic].
Toren believes that levels are strength, and he can feel a shift in his coordination, strength and endurance when he gains one.
Toren kills several large flat-fish while filling buckets, and brings one back to the inn for Erin as something useful.
The flat-fish have crushing strength and lethally sharp teeth, and Erin says their scales are sharp enough that she nearly sliced her hand off cutting them.
Toren hacks the fish apart with his sword, because they latch onto his arm, and leaves them washed in a neat pile on a cutting board in Erin's kitchen.
Toren the Level 2 skeleton works as part of Erin's inn staff, and wishes he were killing something instead of dusting.
Toren understands vaguely that he cannot gain the [Innkeeper] class because he does not own an inn, and thinks the [Barmaid] class is a misnomer.
Toren blocks Ceria from entering the kitchen so that Erin can sleep, then reluctantly goes to cook for her instead.
Ceria notes that Toren walks with something approaching grace, unlike the many skeletons she has seen or killed.
Ceria recognises Toren as Pisces's work and thinks he is quite intelligent, which means Pisces is closer to his goal.
Toren is a Level 3 [Skeleton Warrior] who has no way to level except through the [Barmaid] class, which he thinks would not be helpful.
Toren feels he failed to guard Erin when he lost to the Antinium a few days earlier.
Toren understands Rags perfectly because the dead speak a universal language.
Toren is fascinated by Rags's comments about the [Strategist] class and chess.
Toren sits down across from Rags without attacking, sets up the chess pieces and moves a pawn, and she begins to play him.
Toren's eyes are fiery blue at this time.
Toren plays chess poorly; Rags checkmates him after about sixteen more moves.
Erin sees Toren's chess improve after her coaching, but he is just an amateur with no spark, unlike the fast-learning Workers and the gifted Rags.
An Antinium Worker seizes Toren halfway down the hill outside the inn, rips his skull off and takes his sword.
Toren leaps onto Skinner's face with a dagger, stabs and tears at the crimson eyes, and is hurled aside with a chunk of flesh.
Toren escapes with something red in his hands, and one of Skinner's eyes is gone.
After the battle Toren is Level 11, eight levels higher, and can think, act and feel more clearly than before.
Toren thinks he gained the levels from wounding Skinner so badly and from slaying countless other skeletons.
Toren can now ask why he obeys, and can think of Erin as a person rather than only a master.
Toren senses that the red gem holds powerful magic, including fear, and feels that something is calling him.
Toren thinks of Pisces as a former master and wonders whether Erin is a master or a mistress.
Toren hides the red gem inside his hollow skull with sticky roofing tar so that Erin will not take it away.
Toren's [Tactician] side suggests hiding the gem, and he is stronger now, able to help Erin wrestle planks into place.
Toren walks into the inn with blue fruits and water, and Zevara and Klbkch draw swords until Erin intervenes and explains.
Toren serves Ryoka a plate and a drink; his eyes burn with twin blue flames.
Toren finds himself a new sword in the dungeon while the group searches for a way out.
Toren clears a large patch of snow around the inn with his bare hands and digs Erin and Pisces out when the faeries' snow packs the inn.
Toren builds a wall of compacted snow nearly eight feet tall around the inn overnight, after Erin casually told him to clear the snow.
The wall blocks the wind but also traps Erin inside her inn.
Toren is a Level 11 [Skeleton Warrior], which he regards as his purpose, his name and his sense of being.
Pisces created Toren and named him; the mage danced and laughed in triumph that Toren was the first creation to succeed.
Pisces's creation orders bind Toren to protect Erin Solstice, obey her words and be used in less-optimal tasks.
Toren remembers only three things: his creation orders, the voice from the south that calls the dead, and music.
Toren feels a call pulling him south but forgets its words.
Toren remembers Pisces's name only because some of his orders concern Pisces, such as not letting him steal kitchen food.
Toren can always get back up after being smashed, unlike other skeletons, because of mana that Erin supplies him.
If Toren ran out of mana he might die for good like other skeletons.
Erin generates mana by living and it goes directly to Toren thanks to Pisces, but the amount is very low.
Toren can vaguely sense the magic of others, and Ryoka has four times as much as Erin.
Toren's bones include human, Drake and Gnoll bones, and his ribcage and bones are thicker than a normal Human's.
Toren has the skill [Lesser Strength] from reaching Level 11, which makes a sword feel much lighter.
Toren can understand every language, including the somewhat comprehensible language of the faeries.
Toren sees the Frost Faeries only as hard-to-see dancing blue shapes.
Erin sits in the snow in front of her destroyed inn, weeping, and tells Toren to go away; he obeys against his wishes.
Toren learns what crying and sadness mean by watching Erin, though he knew the words before.
The music in Toren's mind is the song Erin sang, which tells of a place beyond the rainbow, heard in a man's voice with piano and violins.
Toren cannot stop the music even by hurling himself off the roof or putting his head underwater.
Toren is forbidden to kill Humans, Drakes, Gnolls, Goblins, Antinium and many other things, and wonders about the shadowy human following Ryoka.
Toren decides to become stronger and more useful, thinking of armor, and resolves to go back to Erin for orders.
Toren falls through a hole in the snow into ruins about four hundred feet down, and his bones scatter.
The ruins have runes glowing on the walls and are full of magic and life.
Toren seats Skinner's gem in his skull behind his eye sockets, and his blue eye flames mix with its light to turn deep purple.
Toren bursts from the ruins pursued by a headless suit of enchanted armor with a greatsword; Rags's Goblins flee in terror at his purple eyes.
Toren's purple flame eyes cause fear like the fear that came from Skinner.
Toren dodges a wooden replica that Erin throws at him after he catches her with them while holding a dustrag.
Rags meets Toren, whose eyes are now two purple flames, in her cave.
Toren understands Goblin because the dead speak all tongues, and answers Rags by gesture and drawing.
Rags concludes Toren is smarter than he acts, and wonders if he grew smarter over time.
Toren agrees to show Rags the first few dungeon levels in exchange for her taking him back to the inn.
Toren has a poor sense of direction.
Toren feels resentment for the first time when Erin sends him out of the inn for the night and he has to wait until morning.
Toren was not ordered to follow Ceria's instructions, only to follow her, so he waited within sight of the inn.
Toren questions Erin's orders for the first time, thinking they are not good orders, though he cannot disobey her.
Toren kills a Shield Spider by battering it with a rock and brings venom back, which makes Erin proud of him.
Toren battered the enchanted armor for over an hour, reforming himself until he was low on mana, but could not destroy it.
Rags's tribe destroys the enchanted armor with flying clay and exploding bark, which makes Toren think she would serve Erin better.
Toren resolves to level up because Relc threatened Erin and she signalled him to stand down, which Toren takes to mean she did not think he could beat Relc.
Toren walks off toward the Shield Spider nests, bears and snow creatures to level up before Erin needs him again.
After the fight with the enchanted armor, Toren is a Level 14 [Skeleton Warrior].
Toren has the skills [Weapon Proficiency: Sword], [Lesser Strength] and [Conceal Presence], which he considers his three valuable ones.
Toren received [Lesser Strength] when he hit Level 10 in the [Warrior] class.
Toren can become part of a room like a coatrack by standing still and creeping a few feet every hour or two.
Toren uses [Conceal Presence] to creep up behind Erin and Ceria, then waits until Erin orders him outside.
Toren has long known that standing behind Erin or getting in her way gets him sent outside, and this time he does it deliberately to go hunting.
Toren cannot speak, and he runs across the Floodplains of Liscor and beyond without tiring because death took pain and exhaustion from him.
Toren is slower than Ryoka, Val, Relc and possibly Erin because he carries a sword, but he never stops.
Toren reaches Level 16 as a [Skeleton Warrior] and obtains the skill [Skill – Even Footing].
Toren never sleeps or rests, so level-up notifications appear in his head the instant a battle or chess game ends.
Toren is ordered to supervise the new girl Erin hired and to protect her and show her the ropes.
Toren resents the new girl and secretly mistreats her when Erin is not watching, using fists, feet and pushing, because he enjoys it.
Toren goes out to hunt whenever Erin has finished and the new girl is sniveling or hiding.
Toren runs through ten grey-pelted Goblins coming from the south, who are not part of Rags's tribe, and hacks one down mid-spell.
Toren kills a wolverine that slips on the ice, biting upward at it.
Toren throws a small hatchet taken from dead adventurers in the Ruins to wound a second Corusdeer, then butchers it.
The Corusdeer herd turns snow to steam with its glowing horns and charges, and the heat blackens and ignites Toren's bones.
The Corusdeer flee when Toren uses his gem of [Terror], and he cannot walk again for half a day but still levels up.
Halrac's party meets Toren, and Revi's phantom warrior Kelthor knocks off Toren's arm; Kelthor is Level 25 or so by Halrac's estimate.
Toren stuns Kelthor with his gaze of [Terror], realises the phantom is probably resistant, and lures him toward the Corusdeer herd.
In the Corusdeer steam Toren kills Kelthor's phantom with a sword cut through the gap at the neck, and the phantom leaves behind armor, shield and weapon.
An arrow shatters Toren's skull as he reaches for the dented bronze armor.
Toren becomes a [Skeleton Knight] at Level 20 and gains [Skill – Power Strike], [Skill – Weapon Proficiency: Shield] and, by skill change, [Skill – Mirage Cut].
Toren wonders whether being a [Skeleton Knight] means he holds the [Knight] class or whether that differs from being a skeleton.
Toren dons the dented bronze armor and takes the shield, leaving the mace, and feels tough but slower.
Toren sees Gnolls attacking the inn and charges in with sword and shield because he feels a duty to protect Erin.
Toren stops a Gnoll's blow to Erin with his bronze shield and runs the Gnoll through the stomach with his sword.
Toren, in bronze armor and a helmet, stops swinging at the fallen Gnoll when Erin shouts at him, and an arrow through the back of his helmet shatters his skull.
Fragments of something red spray from Toren's skull when he is shot.
Toren's shattered bone reforms after the arrow, and he pushes himself up again before Ulrien slashes at him.
Erin tells Halrac that a red gem in Toren's head made his eyes purple, and that they stayed purple after the gem broke.
Halrac sees Toren walking around after the battle, and thinks the skeleton's gaze emits fear.
Toren refuses an order from Lyonette ("Thing, I order you to"), punches her in the stomach twice and kicks her to make her pick up the dustrag.
Toren believes only Erin gives him orders.
Because Erin forbade hitting, Toren pokes Lyonette 158 times and then with a knife until she does her chores.
Toren pushes Lyonette into a Shield Spider nest, then scares the spiders off with his gaze of [Terror] because Erin told him not to let Lyonette come to harm.
Toren finds he can switch his gaze of [Terror] on and off, and uses it to chase Lyonette.
Toren's purple eyes flash at Lyonette and she runs out of the inn sobbing.
Pisces says Toren absorbed the magic of the gemstone into his spell matrix, giving a lesser version of the original spell useful for shepherding the girl.
Erin realises that Toren picked up one of Skinner's eyes after the battle, which explains the red gemstone.
Erin finds it troubling how much Toren has changed.
Erin orders Toren to stand still when he grabs his sword at Relc, and he stays frozen until she remembers to release him.
Toren prowls the snowy landscape at night, hunting and killing in order to feel alive.
Toren returns to the inn at dawn in battered bronze armor, with a notched sword and shield and faint blood on the blade.
Toren is harnessed with bells to pull a sledge; his resentment fades when Erin appears, hoping she will give an order to release him.
Toren can pull the sledge only about as fast as Erin can jog, but it spares Erin from walking through the snow.
Toren thinks the magic binding him still prevents him from harming Erin, but that he can misinterpret her orders or act slowly.
Toren snaps the bell in his hands, resolves never to be a slave again, and runs north away from Liscor while Erin sleeps.
A [Skeleton Knight] stabs a pair of travelers to death, takes their coins and heads back toward the dungeon at Liscor to level up.
Wesle reports that no city has seen Toren, and Erin worries that she may have to do something about him when she finds him.
Toren left Erin Solstice behind in the snow, hoping she would get lost or starve, and thereby freed himself from her orders.
Since he became a [Skeleton Knight], new thoughts come to Toren, including leaving Erin so she could not order him about.
Toren's eyes were blue when he was created; after he absorbed Skinner's gem he gained the power to inflict [Fear] and his eye flames turned purple.
Toren can regenerate from separated bones, and even from being crushed by Corusdeer horns.
Skeletons are light enough to run on top of crusted snow, which lets Toren catch fleeing travelers.
Toren kills travelers on a side road and uses their corpses as bait to ambush a score of others, for fun.
Toren makes a kill list that starts with the bees, then Lyonette, then Ryoka because her long shinbones bother him, and finally the bells and the sleigh.
Toren realises for the first time that he can dislike things.
Toren is not sure whether he would kill Erin, or the other guests of her inn.
Toren is haunted by the music he heard at Erin's inn and hits himself in the head, even with his sword, to silence it.
Toren's memory does not fade, so every time he hears the song he is caught in the same moment of awe.
Toren wants to become as strong as Griffon Hunt, especially the [Scout] who shot him through the head.
Toren digs up the battered bronze armor he hid in the snow and sets off south-east toward something that calls to him.
Toren has the skill [Mirage Cut], which he uses to cut a [Fighter]'s arm to the bone.
Toren plans to decide whether he feels like killing Erin Solstice once he has levelled, and intends to kill Lyonette and everyone else who annoyed him.
Toren kills a Goblin [Shaman] but loses an arm to a Goblin Leader's halberd, and dies on a charge into the Goblin army.
The Goblins stomp Toren's bones into the snow, and he waits until they leave to reassemble himself.
Toren is sure these Goblins are not led by Rags.
Toren goes into Esthelm to kill Goblins, undead and Humans for levels, leaving his battered armor behind.
Toren knows he can only reanimate so many times, and plans to ambush in the shadows, since he can see in the dark.
Toren uses the [Fear] effect in his eyes on a screaming naked woman after beating a man to death with his club, but spares her.
Toren stabs the monstrous girl from behind in the street, then beats her on the ground until twelve Goblins led by Headscratcher leap down and attack him.
Toren feels fear for the first time in danger because his mana is running dangerously low from repeated deaths and reassemblies.
Toren fears that if scattered one more time, the animation spell might end for good.
Toren loses his sword in the fight and cannot find it.
A freshly risen Ghoul attacks Toren in the sewers and tears at his ribs until six zombies pull it off and kill it.
Toren does not know why the zombies helped; he wonders whether it was his call for help, his eyes (since Skinner commanded the dead) or a secret of his creation.
Toren gains the [Leader] class at Level 1 and the skill [Skill – Command Lesser Undead], and the six zombies wait for his command.
Toren can only have a zombie move and attack what he wants, not do specific tricks, and wonders if he is too low level.
Toren orders his six zombies simply to run, which makes them fast, and they kill a gang of eight men in an alley.
Three of the six zombies survive the fight with the gang.
Toren plans to get the gang leader's iron short sword and to test whether zombies can wipe out a bigger gang without losing any.
Later, Toren reaches [Leader] Level 4 and gains [Skill – Daring Charge] after killing a Goblin group of over twenty with his zombies.
Toren has eight zombies under his control in that ambush, hidden motionless under the snow behind the Goblins.
Toren's [Fear] enchantment does not work on Goblins, though it can still make a Goblin hesitate.
Toren cannot command a horde of zombies, only herd it like cattle while his personal band strikes.
