Toren stands among a mass of zombies and points his sword, and groups of fourteen zombies sprint to hit Goblin flanks and barricades; Ylawes sees him coordinating them.
The Redfang Goblins tackle Toren, and Headscratcher's sword cleaves his spine in two before they break apart his body.
Toren walks away from Esthelm defeated, with thirteen zombies and a Ghoul, back toward Liscor.
Erin hears from Wesle that a skeleton on the road killed a bunch of travelers and buried them in the snow.
Erin tells Pisces that survivors of Esthelm retook the city and report that a skeleton who fought like a swordsman led the dead.
In Liscor's snow, Toren hunts Mrsha with weak, guttering purple eye flames that burn brighter at the sight of her.
Mrsha sees hatred in Toren's eyes and flees; he corners her at a rift in the earth with his sword drawn.
Toren lowers his sword and stares as Mrsha hangs over the chasm; she lets go and falls just as he reaches out.
Toren feels the mana connection to Erin vanish while approaching Liscor with the undead taken from Esthelm, and realises he is dying.
Toren was plotting revenge on the Goblins, the Knight, the Humans and especially Lyonette when the connection broke.
Toren survives by taking mana from the zombies and ghouls he commands with [Command Lesser Undead], and they fall lifeless.
Toren learns that he can steal mana from things he owns, and thinks of himself as a straw or sponge skeleton.
Toren senses a source of power deep in the earth and makes his way to the dungeon crevasse where he once fell in.
Toren recalls that Mrsha fled from him to the crevasse and tumbled in, and that she let go when he went to pull her out.
Toren climbs down into the dungeon, loses his grip, falls to the bottom and fractures several bones.
The dungeon's ambient mana is enough to fill Toren so that he can reassemble himself a few times.
Toren believes Erin Solstice is dead, because the mana link is gone, and blames himself.
Toren recalls that he deliberately left Erin near a cave with a sleeping bear and threw rocks at a pack of wolves as he walked off.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren realises for the first time that death can be bad, because Erin will never move or speak again.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren considers ending himself in the dungeon or in the snow, but rejects it because he fears the blank look of the dead and wants to live.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren throws a rib over his shoulder and it flies back into place, which no other skeleton he has met does.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren searches with his mind and senses that the mana in his body is stored in four specific bones, the second-lowest left rib, right tibia, left clavicle and fourth rib from the top on the right.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Two of the special ribs and the tibia are slightly shorter than their pairs, which leads Toren to conclude he is multiple skeletons.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren concludes that he is several skeletons put together, and faints at the thought.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren can sense where mana is concentrated without having learned the [Mana Sense] Skill, and concludes one can have a skill that is not a Skill.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren recovers a somewhat dulled iron longsword with a cracked crossguard and dried blood on it.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren lures about two dozen Shield Spiders over a rune trap, where they burst as they cross it.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren makes eight more spiders trigger the trap until it stops working, then senses the dungeon's latent magic slowly replenishing it.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren ignores etched warnings, opens a metal door, comes back out ten seconds later and flees things that burst through the doorway.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren finds twelve dead adventurers and pulls a ragged brown cloak off a woman whose throat is missing.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: The cloak awakens a sense of style in Toren, who finds a smashed mirror in the dead woman's pack and reassembles it to look at himself.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren decides he lacks the clothing to carry the cloak and takes the dead adventurers' clothes, because anything reminding him of Erin hurts but forgetting hurts more.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren dresses for the first time since he was created, padding the loose clothes with torn cloth and putting stiff leather armor under them.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren stuffs rags into a bra he has seen Erin use, to make himself look Human-shaped.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren builds a full-face mask from dead Shield Spider carapaces held with web.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: In the mirror Toren sees a slim female warrior in a cloak and mask, which he thinks looks stylish.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren dims the purple flames in his eyes until they go out, so that nobody can tell who is under the mask, and he still sees normally.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren is referred to as "she" while in the disguise.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren shoves Insill back from a hidden rune trap that only she can see, and points the runes out to Pekona's party.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Anith suggests the trap may have been hidden by magic that nullified Insill's Skill.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren tries to copy Pekona's dancing sword style, cartwheels into a wall and falls.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren walks at the front beside Insill after spotting the trap, and checking corridors together fills her with a happiness she cannot explain.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren uses her own Skill [Daring Charge] in a fight against Goblins and bear-creatures, and it gives her strength and speed rather than physical momentum.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren grows bored of the battle, uses her purple [Fear] flames to freeze a mace-wielding not-Gnoll, and rams her blade into its chest.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Pekona demonstrates her [Blade Dancer] sword style and Toren copies every move; she does not blink or forget, and memorises it within a few minutes.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren lifts the shrieking mace thanks to [Lesser Strength], then hands it back, since coin means nothing to her and she cannot swing it fast.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: The team offers the mace to the masked swordswoman for saving them twice.

section: In the dungeon: the masked swordswoman (Book 5)
text: Toren lets the adventurers live for the first time, because they offered a share and she regards them as an asset, and feels she has acted like Erin.
Toren is a Level 24 [Skeleton Knight], a Level 2 [Barmaid], a Level 4 [Leader], a Level 5 [Tactician] and a Level 3 [Sword Dancer].
Toren lives on the mana in his surroundings and dies if it runs out, so he cannot leave the dungeon, where there is enough mana but outside there is not.
Toren's body consumes more mana than he can absorb from most places above; a master or [Mage] supplying mana would let him go above freely.
Toren sits below the chasm under an invisible barrier that keeps rain out of the dungeon, and the dripping water annoys him.
Toren puts on a mask, and the narration switches to "she" and "her".
Toren has two personalities, a male one who hates the mask and a female one who appears when he wears the mask and the clothes.
The male Toren fights with sword and a wooden buckler and walks rather than glides, while the female one glides gracefully with her sword.
The male Toren blames the [Sword Dancer] class and the clothing on the new personality, and tosses the mask away when he takes control.
The female Toren takes the mask back with his left hand, rearranges her body and replaces her breasts.
Toren cannot take the clothing off every time he changes personality, since she would painstakingly put it back on.
Toren, in either personality, remembers serving Erin and tricking her into being left to die in the snow, and believes Erin is dead.
The male Toren is surprised that Erin's death ended her mana link to him.
The female Toren thinks it fitting that he is trapped and alone, because he let down the master who died.
Toren cannot fight most of the dungeon's denizens, so he runs, hides, ambushes or lures enemies into traps.
Toren plays dead by deliberately disassembling himself, which fools most dungeon monsters, including a patrol of four enchanted suits of armor.
Toren notes that Flesh Worms, Crypt Lords, enchanted armor, Golems, Cave Goblins and even a Minotaur live in the dungeon.
Toren has few corpses to raise with [Command Lesser Undead] in the dungeon, since monsters eat bodies, and he cannot reanimate large bodies or non-living things.
Toren recently reanimated a poisonous-fanged mouse, which bit a Cave Goblin's toes for a minute before being stepped on.
Toren has noticed the monsters organise themselves in the dungeon, leaving some places that they almost never go.
Toren builds a crude inn in a four-entrance circular room with a fountain, using piled stones, wood and Shield Spider web glue.
Toren's inn has a bar, a storage area, doors, and cups and plates hammered from armor remnants.
Toren keeps a barrel of liquefied maggot guts and fungi as food, and suspects the clear water from the fountain is a deadly poison.
The male Toren hates the inn project, which belongs to the female personality.
The female Toren wants a name to separate her from him and tries many, including Torina, Tofu, Lieutenant Bones, Papyrus and Sans.
Toren is named Toren because he was first, so she could be someone else.
Toren thinks the female personality appeared when he put on the clothes, controls his body, argues with him and fights differently.
The masked swordswoman answers Anith by gestures, and does not speak; she gives sorrow as the reason for staying below.
Anith suggests that the swordswoman might be a [Doomseeker], and says it is not for them to ask.
The masked swordswoman drops her old sword, accepts an enchanted blade with small durability and cutting enchantments from Vuliel Drae, and smiles with a line across her mask.
Toren leads the team of Vuliel Drae through the dungeon, planning to keep them alive since they gave her an enchanted sword.
Earlia of Gemhammer sees the masked swordswoman fighting at the dungeon entrance, drags her behind the adventurers, and finds she is light as a feather.
The masked swordswoman does not answer Earlia, and a purple glow in her eye sockets frightens Earlia before it vanishes.
The masked swordswoman's mask looks crude and patchwork, with no breathing holes or mouth.
Toren drags a dead Raskghar beaten to death by Workers and Soldiers back toward his inn, as he is starting a collection of bodies.
After the Raskghar and many monsters die, Toren drags corpses of Humans, animals and Goblins into the dungeon nonstop, since any body can become a zombie or Ghoul.
Toren stacks the dead in an amphitheater beyond a door at the far end of his inn hall, and counts into the thousands.
Toren hopes to harness the power of so many dead, thinking that alone he can only run, but with an army he could fight the dungeon's monsters.
Toren keeps his mask hanging at his side and feels it call to him, but is in charge until adventurers return.
Toren keeps a zombie that he treats as Erin in his crude inn, hears Erin's scolding in his head, and stabs her repeatedly in the head and chest.
The zombie-Erin is just the body of some Human that looked most like Erin, and Toren cannot make it speak or think.
Toren has killed things 20,651 times and is tired of killing for no reason.
Toren admits after months that he wants to go home, but the dungeon is his prison.
Toren lacks a living person supplying him with mana, so he would run out within minutes above, but the dungeon's mana makes him very hard to kill.
Toren blames himself for Erin's death because he left her in the snow far from home.
Toren fills a room with about four thousand and a few hundred bodies of Raskghar, Humans, Goblins, Drakes and Gnolls, which begin to rise.
Eight Crypt Lords and a flesh-pit arise from Toren's room of bodies, five more Crypt Lords than last time, and ignore his orders.
Toren cannot steal undead from the Crypt Lords, who have more authority than he does.
Toren is a Level 27 [Skeleton Knight] and a Level 12 [Undead Leader], with the skills [Command Lesser Undead] and [Raise Corpse].
Toren sees in a Crypt Lord's mind a future of an empty world with only undead, and decides undead are idiots, except for him.
The masked persona is a Level 13 [Sword Dancer] who has fought the Raskghar twenty-three times without success.
The masked persona wanders the dungeon asking the questions the male Toren never does, and is the more proactive of the two.
Half the dungeon's monsters do not attack the masked skeleton because bones are not nutritious, and the other half do not seem to see her.
Flesh Worms cannot control Toren any more than the Goblin [Shaman] could, but she dislikes their attempts to impose their will.
The masked Toren follows a Flesh Worm and its zombie escort into the enchanted armor's inner territory, a part of the dungeon she had never seen.
In the armor's inner territory Toren sees forges repairing battered suits and rows of enchanted armor, and a suit of armor lets her pass when she mimics a zombie.
An armored general on a pedestal at the head of the legion points a sword at Toren, and the legion turns on her, so she runs.
The masked Toren watches the Antinium send an army into the dungeon, fall until only two Soldiers remain, and waltz together in a dark corridor.
Toren, both personalities together, is amazed by the Antinium's battle, and the male Toren revels in the slaughter while she is shown something more.
Toren signals the two Soldiers to flee and charges the approaching Facestealer, who crushes her skull and bones to powder.
Toren later finds the two Soldiers dead two corridors over with their heads missing, and kneels by them for a very long time.
Toren hunts Nokha's Raskghar camp after nine hours of searching, and Nokha, who has a new glowing sword and a cough, stomps her to pieces again.
Toren has played a part in reducing the Raskghar's numbers and camps since the Minotaur led them.
Toren wants Nokha's magic sword and thinks she needs a bow, but weapons are hard to keep because her body gets smashed.
The masked Toren likes people, thinks of the adventurers she met as her team and friends, and keeps the mask on because the male Toren is lonely too.
When Insill is caught by the flesh-pit, the male Toren and the masked persona realise something together and cooperate for the first time to rescue him.
Toren uses [Daring Charge], [Mirage Cut], [Hi-Jump], [Perfect Dodge], [Sharpened Edge] and [Shield Bash] in the rescue, using Nailren's buckler.
Toren faints on hearing Bevussa name The Wandering Inn and Miss Solstice, and wakes wondering if he heard it wrong.
Toren hears Erin Solstice's name for the fourth time that day and smashes his skull into a wall in disbelief.
Toren had not put on the mask for over a week, and had instead been shadowing adventurers and listening for her name.
Toren learns that an [Innkeeper] named Erin Solstice runs The Wandering Inn above, with a Goblin guest, an Antinium and a white Gnoll.
Toren concludes that if Erin is alive, she must have severed the bond and tried to kill him.
Toren's rage flares and then goes out like a spent torch, and a Flesh Worm backs away from him.
A Crypt Lord with many cut marks, formerly disobedient, now stands subservient to Toren, the [Undead Leader].
Toren unlocks and shoves aside the adventurers' barricade and leads the undead to the abyss, where ropes lead up to the surface.
Toren stamps on the mask, shattering it, while the masked persona resists; he catches himself and finds only him left.
Toren feels Erin Solstice is the center of his being and the reason for his creation, and that she gave him nothing, unlike the many others she saved.
Toren decides to go above to find out whether Erin is alive, planning to remake the mask only if she is dead.
Toren thinks of himself as the dark shadow and consequence of Erin's triumph.
Toren ambushes Bevussa's Wings of Pallass, in a crude wooden mask, takes a shortsword in the chest, then removes the mask and uses [Fear] to stab her in the stomach.
Toren lets two dozen Ghouls loose on the Wings of Pallass, and then opens the metal door of his inn so the undead stream through the tunnels.
The Flamewardens of Pallass under Keldrass hold a line of flames against the undead, with Siegespell Armor and a Heartflame Breastplate.
Toren removes the mask and clothing, climbs a rope out of the dungeon as Ghouls and a Crypt Lord hold the entrance, and cuts the anchors of the adventurers' ropes.
Toren bleeds magic as he leaves the dungeon, but has enough in his bones to survive.
Toren stands outside Liscor watching The Wandering Inn as the Watch surrounds it, counting his mana potions.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Toren stands still as a statue in the kitchen doorway of the inn, purple flames burning, and spreads his arms to welcome Erin back.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Toren returns to The Wandering Inn, which he calls home.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Toren had waited a long time, hiding and watching the inn from afar until he ran out of mana potions, and then came into the inn.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: The inn is full of mana now that the door is gone, which fills Toren and lets him live there, though only there.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Toren cannot speak, and Erin cannot hear his thoughts however hard he tries.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Toren recalls his whole history with Erin, from waking and her orders to the song, the exploding inn, the sleigh, Esthelm, the dungeon and hearing her name.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Toren regretted killing Erin, as it took away the pleasure he got from killing and leveling, and he thinks of the Toren of old as a stranger.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Erin greets him cheerfully and suggests he help clean up, which makes Toren hear her old orders and the sleigh bells and see the lie in her wary posture.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Erin punches Toren, calls [Minotaur Punch] and stabs him with Pelt's kitchen knife while he tries to tell her it is him.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Erin throws acid jars from an emergency box at Toren, who is dissolving, and he decides that she hates him.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Toren believes Erin has wanted him dead from the start, not wanted him or needed him.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Toren strangles Erin after her [Loud Voice] comes out silent, until she stops moving, while he waits for someone to stop him.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Erin revives with a gasp after Toren's grip, with a broken windpipe.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Toren makes a heart with his hands, breaks it in two, and tells Erin silently that he is tired and wants to stop feeling pain.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Toren pulls his own skull off his body on the last day of spring, and the purple flames in his eyes go out.

section: Return to the inn and death (Book 14)
text: Ijvani takes Toren's remains on her master's order, and is told to maintain the animation spell and leave a pile of ash infused with death magic in his place.
Erin reflects two weeks later that Toren possessed a soul, attacked her in her inn, and was her first [Barmaid], and she feels guilty for not seeing him as a person.
Erin connects the masked woman in the dungeon and Numbtongue's encounter with a skeleton at Esthelm to Toren's history.
Erin believes Toren killed Numbtongue's friends and stabbed Bevussa, and that he killed dozens, maybe over a hundred people directly and indirectly.
Erin remembers her last sight of Toren as a breaking heart and a skeleton pulling off his head, and holds herself responsible.
Toren is kept as a skull in a unique bag of holding filled with the essence of death, after he would not stop screaming at the black skeleton Ijvani.
Ijvani takes Toren's skull out of the bag, spills the rest of his bones on the floor and makes the skull hover as his purple flames return.
Toren's spell is a diagram of over a hundred thousand tiny lines written inside each of his bones, interconnected into one grand spell.
The spell gives the capacity for thought and growth, creating a soul where none existed, and it has a blank space at its center.
Az'kerash laughs that Pisces Jealnet's answer was blank, and that leaving the center blank was what let magic fill the void.
Toren is appraised as a Level 28 [Skeleton Knight], Level 13 [Sword Dancer], Level 14 [Undead Leader], Level 6 [Tactician] and Level 3 [Barmaid].
Toren is Az'kerash's guest and prisoner, held in a cage made of power and made to watch, because he keeps trying to attack the other Chosen.
Toren is still weak and without a voice in Az'kerash's castle.
Toren tried to kill Az'kerash during his first week in the castle, and Az'kerash imbued him with [Limited Regeneration] saying he has need of the bones.
Toren can throw his arm to fetch a bone and have it return to his body, like a Dullahan's.
Toren makes his own broom and cleans the castle, and Venitra, Ijvani, Bea, Kerash and a Plague Zombie beat him and break his bones out of frustration.
Toren reforms slowly without the Archmage's bones and fears telling Az'kerash about the Chosen's bullying.
Toren once tried to blow up Belavierr with bags of flour, at Az'kerash's request to demonstrate how to fight her.
Toren wishes now to be invisible and to never be found, but no longer to die.
Toren realises the Chosen are like him, and sees that they share the same flaw.
Toren hides Ijvani's neglected Healing Slime, shrunk by half to fake its death, in a closet nest and feeds it ingredients he gathers.
Toren and the slime hug each other and become friends, the first either has really known, though they cannot speak.
Toren thinks he could not love before, and that his feelings for Erin broke him because she was thoughtlessly cruel.
Toren now fears the Chosen and is unhappy, and the Stitch Witch weaves his fear and the slime's bright emotion into her magic.
Tottenval is one of the Seven, the highest-levelled and most trusted vassals of King Flos Reimarch of Reim.
Tottenval is a [Gardener], not a warrior, and not even a magical one.
Tottenval is a Beastkin from Baleros, according to Flos, and nicknamed the Blooming Plague by Mars.
Flos describes Tottenval as a Beastkin of the Fox Tribe with some Gnollish blood, a gentle, merry soul and a prankster.
Tottenval makes Reim bloom and feeds Flos's entire kingdom, which Flos says would bloom eternally had he been there.
Flos found Tottenval good company for talks because he was incurious, answering Flos's grand schemes and enemies with a shrugging "so?".
Flos showered gold on Tottenval for flowers, according to Mars.
Flos says Drevish and Tottenval each had an army of [Builders] and [Farmers], in their way, unlike the other Seven's fighting armies.
Flos tells Venith that Tottenval and Queravia are dead.
Tottenval and Queravia died in the war, before Flos entered his slumber.
Tottenval died at sea saving Flos's life where no one else could.
Flos says he still owes Tottenval's people a debt.
Teres knows that Minotaur navies ambushed Flos's fleet at sea, and that but for Tottenval's sacrifice they might have killed Flos himself.
Flos murmurs during the fighting against Minotaurs that Tottenval was his Gardener and took no lives.
The Trapmaster Assassin is an older [Assassin] and [Trapmaster] of the Assassin's Guild who rides the Unmarked Coach and is a full-timer as a Face.
The Trapmaster Assassin is named Sithorn, the oldest of the [Assassins] in his group.
The Trapmaster Assassin leaves the coach and walks into the forest, vanishing out of sight and mind.
The Trapmaster Assassin finds two other Faces of the Assassin's Guild already camped among the trees, not full-timers but just as good.
Mire asks about the Trapmaster's kids, and her own eldest is having trouble in his woodworking business.
The Trapmaster Assassin says the Unmarked Coach is the way to travel and that he does not know how the other two stand to go on foot.
The Trapmaster Assassin tells Mire he met a Vampire on his ride, new, who had a strong reaction to even a bit of garlic.
The Trapmaster Assassin is the white-haired man that Ryoka and Fierre had met, and is one of five Faces sent by the Assassin's Guild.
The Trapmaster Assassin's wires between posts stop Magnolia Reinhart's pink carriage at full speed and hold, flipping it over.
The Trapmaster Assassin leaves cover with four other Assassins to approach the downed carriage.
The Trapmaster Assassin throws long mithril wires anchoring them in the air and uses [Create Field: The Steelthread Web].
The Trapmaster Assassin gives Mire the wires and a glove for the combination Skill [The Web Closes], which Sithorn and Mire perform together.
A warning is called that Ressa used to be a Face, and the Trapmaster eyes her before withdrawing his wires.
Tremborag is a huge, obscenely fat Hobgoblin with crimson eyes who rules a vast tribe from a stone mountain city.
Tremborag stands as tall as a Minotaur and bigger, and sits on a throne in his hall.
Tremborag speaks the common tongue fluently.
Tremborag's shouted command to kneel carries pressure that must be a Skill, and most visiting Chieftains kneel.
Tremborag calls himself the Great Chieftain of the North.
Tremborag's tribe is called the Mountain City Tribe, though Rags hears it more often called the Great Chieftain's Tribe.
Tremborag is only the sixth Goblin with a name that Rags has ever known.
Tremborag rules his tribe from Dwarfhalls Rest, a mountain he has made his lair.
Rags wonders why Tremborag has not become a Goblin Lord, since his tribe is as vast as the Goblin Lord's but she would feel it if he were one.
Rags sees Tremborag as a Goblin who rules a palace and acts and speaks like a Human, whom she cannot trust.
Tremborag changes in battle into a gargantuan eight-foot form where all his fat becomes muscle and he is powerful and quick.
Tremborag tells Rags there are more things in the world that she does not know than she knows, and that he is one of them.
Afterwards Tremborag is fat and normal again, laughing and eating among his warriors as if the change was an illusion.
In the siege, Tremborag's form grows larger and his fat becomes muscle as he tears the head off a Hob.
Tremborag takes a bestial form with red eyes, yellowed teeth and a body of muscle and fury when he emerges from hiding in a wall.
Tremborag agrees with Garen Redfang that the Goblin Lord is not a true Goblin, then asks again why Garen has come.
Tremborag claims he met the Goblin King Velan the Kind ten years ago, when the King came to Izril and to his tribe with his armies.
Tremborag agrees to fight beside Garen against the Goblin Lord after Garen shows a small key and Tremborag says he knows what Garen has.
Tremborag vows that the Goblin Lord will break his teeth upon the mountain should he come to battle.
Tremborag tells Rags he will not move against the Goblin Lord unless the Lord comes to the mountain, since it is easy to defend.
Tremborag asks which Hob will fight with Rags, and none of the Goblins at his high table moves to give her warriors.
Tremborag finds his armory emptied of magical arms and four guard Hobs dead after Rags's tribe flees the mountain.
Tremborag estimates that between two and six thousand Goblins left, including several hundred of his own warriors and some Hobs, plus food, supplies and Garen's wolves and women.
Tremborag returns to his enraged form and threatens to kill Garen for bringing Rags, but backs down when Garen says he has the key and knows where the other is.
Tremborag says he would take the other key even from the heart of Invrisil, behind a Walled City or at the bottom of the sea, and Garen replies it is in a worse place.
Tremborag vows to take the key all the same, as soon as he hunts down the small Goblin Rags and eats her alive.
Tremborag answers Garen's demand to stop sending raids by calling himself Great Chieftain under the mountain, who will bow to no Lord or King.
Tremborag names two other famed Chieftains, a pyromaniac witch and a brute who loves combat, who refused his request to join against the Goblin Lord.
Tremborag says the witch also refused the Goblin King, as he did, and the brute accepts no master.
Tremborag, eating savagely on his throne, tells Garen that the Goblin Lord wants his strength and will not have it.
Tremborag claims he refused a Goblin Lord who once came to his mountain, and looked the Goblin King in the eye and refused to follow.
Tremborag says Velan told the young, old, pregnant and fearful to hide, took only willing warriors, and came across the sea from Baleros.
Tremborag calls Velan's fight an arrogant waste.
Tremborag says he too dreams of the secret Velan hid and that he will have it; he and Garen agree to decide who gets it after the Goblin Lord.
Tremborag orders his armies summoned, the gates barred and swords sharpened, and Garen agrees to wait for the Goblin Lord.
Tremborag claims to be old, to have lived decades ago when the Goblin King was an unborn seed, and to remember Velan's fall and the King's face.
Tremborag tells Reiss that a slave cannot lead others, that Reiss is a pet and not a Goblin, and that he does not even deserve to be Chieftain.
Tremborag mocks Reiss's small army and says he bows to a master and copies Humans' formations and armor.
Tremborag eats and laughs on his dirty throne during the siege, an act that boosts the morale of his tribe.
Tremborag boasts that his tribe is greater than the Goblin Lord's and that he has been Chieftain for decades while the Lord has held the title perhaps half a year.
Tremborag loses the narrow tunnel entrances to exploding undead, then orders his Goblins to pull back and fight in the open central caverns.
Tremborag reasons that the Goblin Lord must fight or run now as the Humans approach, and that fighting Humans in his own mountain suits him.
Tremborag recognizes Elia Arcsinger, calls her Kingslayer and flees, which causes both Goblin armies to rout.
Tremborag claims Elia Arcsinger shot the arrow that killed Velan the Kind.
A huge green hand drags a [Light Mage] into the wall, and Tremborag charges out of hiding to strike the [Pyromancer] and a [Rogue] among the adventurers.
Tremborag tells Garen to run, says his mountain is lost and his tribe flees, and swears to hunt the adventurers.
Tremborag lumbers through the Goblin ranks, calls Rags a traitor and transforms to attack her.
Tremborag chews a dead cow's haunch at the sit-about and calls Rags the "nameless child" who is better suited to refueling a fire than leading a tribe.
Tremborag remembers Pyrite as always accompanying a decrepit old Hob called Greybeard, and is stunned when Pyrite names him Greydath of Blades.
Tremborag tells Reiss that his master will throw him away when he is done.
Tremborag turns into a muscled beast in front of Reiss and says he will eat him slowly, and Pyrite's fart ends the standoff.
Tremborag declares the sit-about a farce, swears to kill Reiss and Rags and all the traitors, and storms out with his tribe following.
Ulvama protects Tremborag from Rags's crossbow bolts with a haze illusion that makes him a green indistinct blob.
Tremborag is forced to run alone for eight miles by trotting Human cavalry while his tribe flees, and collapses.
Tremborag tells Rags the Goblin Kings are pawns of the Goblin Lords, and that Greydath sat in his mountain pretending to be Greybeard.
Tremborag claims Curulac lived years before his hundred days of war and was betrayed by the Lords who turned him against the Humans.
Tremborag claims the Lords sent only Greydath of Blades with Velan, and that Tallis Stormbreaker was Velan's friend, not a Lord, who told him the truth.
Tremborag claims he begged Velan to reconsider and that the Lords conspired to let him die.
Tremborag lunges and nearly claws Rags once she draws near, calling the exchange a lie of no importance.
Tremborag claims Quietstab told him everything about Rags's tribe before he died.
Tremborag kills a Gold-rank adventurer and several mages and soldiers, then taunts Tyrion Veltras about his fallen wife.
Tremborag rises again after Tyrion's lance leaves a hole in his chest, saying only he decides when it is time to die.
Tremborag keeps fighting while dying, then walks north toward his mountain, sits facing it and dies.
Six Gold-rank adventurers died or were maimed in the battle against Tremborag.
After Tremborag's death, his tribe splits and roughly half the Mountain City Goblins go to Rags, with the rest to Garen and Reiss.
Rags weeps for the Great Chieftain of the Mountain after his death.
Trey Atwood is a sixteen-year-old from England who was summoned to this world and became Flos Reimarch's ward and personal attendant.
Trey is the fraternal twin of Teres, and they are both 5'10 tall with moderately dark blonde hair and fair skin.
Trey is a young man from London.
Trey is afraid and confused by Flos, who shattered everything he believed in, and whose waking Trey can feel as a shock to the spine.
Trey is not by his own estimation cut out to walk with legends.
Trey eats crunchy bacon bits at breakfast and dislikes vegetables even in another world.
Trey and Teres do not hold a servant class; Orthenon tells them they are aides, expected to become bodyguards and assistants.
Orthenon introduces Trey to Clan Tannousin as a companion of the King of Destruction, chosen to follow him.
Trey and Teres fell into Flos's throne room after stepping off the ledge of a Tube subway car, and found Flos sitting alone in a small chair.
Orthenon nearly ran Trey through before Flos stopped his men.
Trey has an iPhone that he keeps switched off ever since a call, and Flos insisted he and Teres could keep their phones.
Trey had been in this world little more than a month at the time of the Emperor of Sands' war.
Trey and Teres openly refuse Flos's order, and Flos thanks them for the truth and apologizes.
Trey wakes at dawn when Teres takes his pillow, trains with Flos and Mars in slow-motion sword swings, then hits a cloth dummy.
Orthenon doubts a [Warrior] is the class for Trey, and trains Teres instead.
Flos tells Trey to call him Flos rather than "my King".
Trey takes a [Geomancer]'s staff after the battle at the hill, and his badly cut arm is closed by a potion from Mars.
Trey realizes that Chandrar's kingdoms keep or sell slaves, and sells captives to slave traders to feed Flos's poor kingdom.
Trey and Teres fight bitterly over Flos selling slaves, with Trey throwing a chair at a wall and calling Teres a monster.
Teres argues Flos must be changed gradually and draws her sword, and Trey runs.
Trey and Teres had not spoken for over a month after the fight.
Trey tells Flos that Flos is not his king and that he still has a Queen, and stops speaking to him.
Orthenon refuses to speak to Trey unless he apologizes, and Trey feels a pulling to give in that he compares to addiction.
Trey is alone, eating and sleeping apart from Teres and no longer training with Mars.
Months later, Trey's rift with Flos and Teres persists, and Gazi is his only friend because he objected to slavery.
Trey is a [Mage] who casts [Flash], [Sand Arrow] and [Sand Veil] under Gazi's instruction.
Trey is unsure how he feels about being a [Mage] or about his sister becoming a warrior.
Trey catches Nawal as she faints on realising Flos is the King of Destruction.
Trey practices magic because Gazi expects it, and casts [Lightsand Arrow] by combining [Light] and [Sand Arrow].
Trey casts [Sand Sprite], which creates toy-like golems with big eyes and spears modeled on Earth figurines, which Gazi calls the ugliest creations in history.
Ulyse tells Trey the staff taken from the [Geomancer] is useful but needs spells and experience to control.
Gazi tells Trey she will find him tomorrow to practice and he will learn [Featherfall] with the staff.
Trey and Teres feel like friends or siblings but not like twins, and have not yet figured out how to come back together.
Teres tells Trey that Gazi was a slave whom Flos found and raised, and Trey says he knew.
Flos sends Trey with the Quarass to meet Fetohep, since Trey has a talent as a [Diplomat] and has the phone.
Trey orders a shepherd's pie, then orange juice, at Fetohep's table, and Fetohep disapproves of the low-born dish.
Trey later asks for bubble and squeak, a fried egg, strong tea with no sugar and a treacle tart, and Khelt's [Chefs] reproduce them exactly by a Skill.
Trey tells Fetohep he comes from England, a country in the United Kingdom, and Fetohep says no such country exists.
The Quarass tells Fetohep that Trey and his sister come from another world.
Trey tells Fetohep about Egypt, pharaohs, pyramids and mummification.
Trey gives Fetohep his iPhone to keep overnight and tells him the passcode, 4467.
Trey has all of Series 1 and two episodes of Series 2 of Sherlock on his iPhone, and Fetohep watches through the night.
Trey proposes a selfie, and Trey and Fetohep take the first royal selfie in this world.
Trey is Level 16 thanks to Gazi's relentless tutoring, while Teres is Level 19.
Later, Trey reaches [Sand Mage] Level 18 and obtains [Skill - Create Lifesand Golems].
Trey curls up in the blood, clutching his throat, remembering dying, saying he hates the Quarass and wants to leave.
Trey disobeys Flos's orders, leaving Reim but not riding north, and reaches Khelt quickly with a movement Skill.
Trey refuses the Reim [Captain]'s demand that he come to Sadomere, saying he will stay with King Fetohep.
Trey carries a grimy backpack holding a camera he repaired with [Repair] and recharged, belonging to the person who became a pakheil.
Trey tells Fetohep he went to Tombhome with Gazi and the Quarass for a peace conference, was offered the meat, and had his throat cut.
Trey tells Fetohep a pakheil attacked him and turned out to be someone from Earth who had been tricked.
Trey tells Fetohep he tried to confront and kill Baosar, Gazi got her eye back, and the dead city's eyes turned toward them as they fled on the carpet.
Trey vows never to forgive A'ctelios and to bury Tombhome again someday, saying the city has to be erased.
Trey refuses Fetohep's offer of every comfort and treasure, bows, and rides back south to serve Flos, who would go to war for a single child.
Trey rides through Chandrar with two Parasol Stroll [Mages], Mirin and Fellif, on a mission incognito while learning magic.
Fellif says the Quarass taught Trey more than they have, and Trey carries a mini-Gazi golem made of the Quarass's red lifeblood sand.
Trey stands nervous at a green-watered harbor in Nerrhavia's Fallen, where String People avoid water since it rots or shrinks their cloth.
Trey was escorted south from Reim by Mirin and Palke, and Mirin, second-in-command of Parasol Stroll, casts a cooling spell on him.
Trey had not seen the Quarass since they parted after A'ctelios, and misses Nawal.
Teres tells Fetohep that Gazi is gone and Trey is heading with two Parasol Stroll [Mages] to a harbor in Nerrhavia's Fallen.
Trey boards the Emerald Signet as Troy Atlas, saying he is seventeen from Hellios, and swears under a truth spell that he is bound for Wistram Academy.
Trey asks the Australian Flynn Patel when his family moved to Australia, and Flynn realizes Trey is also from Earth.
A Drake [Mage] excitedly sends a [Message] to Wistram about another person from Earth and warns the two to be careful what they say.
Trey tells Flynn he is from England and appeared suddenly with no sign, and claims to have landed in Hellios, north of Reim.
During a storm on the ship, Trey fingers the scar on his throat, holds his camera, and vows to burn their city to the ground.
At Wistram, Trey makes a [Lifesand Golem] modeled on Gazi, Mini-Gazi, using the Quarass's gift, and fights her against dozens of sand golems.
Trey notes Mini-Gazi is faster, stronger, tougher and smarter than other golems, and he made her with his blood.
Mini-Gazi needs a little blood every day and absorbs mana from the atmosphere, which Wistram has plenty of.
Trey decides not to tell his teachers or the other Earth-people that he can make Mini-Gazi.
Trey keeps Mini-Gazi in his pack for company, finding her good at keeping magical rats out of his room.
Tritel is a Courier known as the Moonlight Rider, a short man who looks more like a horse jockey and is confident and grinning.
Ci is Tritel's beautiful silver mare, whom he insists goes everywhere with him, and who is perfectly behaved in the inn.
Tyrion Veltras tells Ullim to hire the Moonlight Rider, Tritel, as a Courier if needed to fetch gelato ingredients.
Ryoka vaguely recognises Tritel as the Moonlight Rider when she sees him, and he rides with his horse.
Ci blows tobacco smoke back at Tritel and is called a tyrant by him.
Tritel asks Erin what she wants and says the Yellow Rivers cure must be kept out of bags of holding because the mold is alive.
Tritel says a sea-Courier could get the cure to the port city of Talenqual fast but that it is not cheap.
Tritel says he has been begged thousands of times for free deliveries and now needs compensation.
Erin offers Tritel and the sea-Courier exclusive seats in the Solstice Booth, with a dedicated performance by the Players of Celum for a month.
Tritel agrees to carry the cure for free in return for the booth seats, after Erin adds a place for Ci.
Tritel and Ci send a message that no Couriers at the port city of Altvil will take the delivery, and that three samples were entrusted to three [Captains].
Tritel's message says two vessels were impounded and that the Waverider's Wake was heading for the nearest Balerosian harbour after passing Wistram.
Tritel's message says worsening weather threatens delivery and the [Harbormaster] fears a magical storm.
Tritel reports that the Waverider's Wake went down with all hands, and that Wistram saw the ship's demise on a scrying.
Troy is a young Earther from Greece who planned to study engineering after high school and is a video gamer.
Troy is one of the seven Earthers who stay at The Wandering Inn for about a week after arriving.
Troy and Leon do their own thing as a team, according to the narration.
Kevin says Leon and Troy wanted a [Gamer] class, but he told them it would only make them better at playing on his laptop.
Troy complains that Joseph has football and Galina loves the actors, asking what he and Leon get.
Troy and Leon walk Invrisil with only five silver and two silver between them, and neither complains aloud about their pay.
Troy and Leon discuss making a tabletop or card game, wondering how to design miniatures and whether they could draw cards.
Troy gulps when Grimalkin points out that he and Leon came from Magnolia Reinhart's estates.
Troy nods emphatically when Leon says there are things they cannot talk to Grimalkin about.
Troy and Leon agree to sell information to Grimalkin, secretly from Erin Solstice, starting with their reaction to Master Felkhr.
Tulm the Mithril is a Dullahan, second-in-command of the Iron Vanguard, a Great Company, and Niers' former student.
Tulm's entire body is mithril, brighter and deeper than silver, and he carries his head under one arm.
Tulm commands the whole Great Company as a [Strategist] answerable only to the Seer of Steel.
Tulm won Niers' game in years past, and he agreed to seek this time.
Tulm does not hide his presence, and Dullahans and others kneel as he appears.
Tulm's aura presses on the teachers and Perorn until Niers tells his [Strategists] not to kneel, lifting the weight.
Tulm's class is [Dragonslayer Strategist], known only to Tulm, the Seer of Steel and Niers.
Tulm's appraisal Skill let him read the rough levels and Skills of all the students and several Forgotten Wing officers.
Tulm says Niers called him by a letter sent into the Iron Vanguard's mightiest stronghold, carried over two thousand miles by one of the best Couriers in the world.
Perorn says Tulm took her leg in a past battle, and she hates him.
Tulm orders his chief [Mage] to activate the Screamer Dust.
Tulm uses [Battlefield - The Cold Iron Mists] and [Legions of Steel], whose mist hampers enemies and makes his soldiers' skin steel.
Tulm dons his helmet for the first time and uses [The Twice-Born Warlord], matching Xol's strength.
Tulm catches Venaz's fist, and Venaz lands behind Marian with torn armour.
Tulm leaps eight feet into the air to catch Cameral's head, and Niers rules "Out!"
Tulm goes white with fury when Umina surfaces from her tunnel through the privy.
Tulm says "I concede" to Niers and orders the Iron Vanguard back to its warships, leaving the injured.
Tulm asks the name of the student who beat him, and Niers answers Umina Caxical.
Tulm tells Xol he would have paid four of six warships, and even Xol, for victory.
Tulm recalls Niers once saying he would burn down a forest to win a card game if stakes were high.
Niers says Tulm once misheard a beach, marched north and was lost three hundred miles away for two weeks.
Niers says Tulm was hopelessly enamoured with a Selphid teacher and handed in a love letter with his homework.
Later, Tulm survives a battle in Baleros and saves the majority of his army, apparently using his warlord skill.
Twin Stripes is a new Antinium Soldier with a pink stripe on either side of his face.
Twin Stripes spars with Yellow Splatters and goes above ground to patrol with the other Soldiers.
Twin Stripes becomes an Aberration after a long day, to Yellow Splatters' surprise since Soldiers almost never become one.
Twin Stripes lunges at Yellow Splatters and fights off over a hundred Soldiers in the barracks with possessed strength.
Twin Stripes is restrained with bent iron bars and taken to a holding cell while glaring at Yellow Splatters with hate.
Pawn's blessing returns Twin Stripes from Aberration to a Soldier, and Yellow Splatters frees him.
The Twisted Queen is missing one large mandible, parts of her body and one eye, as if something had eaten away at her.
The Twisted Queen speaks haltingly and jerkily with her mouth, but her mental sending is far more eloquent, showing an intact mind.
The Twisted Queen is described as having endured the privations of the body, unlike the Armored Queen's broken spirit.
The Twisted Queen tells Klbkch that Wrymvr is waiting for him.
The Twisted Queen apologises to Klbkch for not recognising him and says Wrymvr greeted him with their welcomes.
The Twisted Queen lifts Anand and lowers him toward an empty Birther sac to see what his mind has changed.
Klbkch says Anand is the highest-levelled individual he has brought and that his death is unacceptable.
Klbkch draws his swords and puts the tip of one in the Twisted Queen's side, ordering her to put Anand down.
The Twisted Queen asks what Klbkch is doing, saying she is a Queen, and then puts Anand down.
Klbkch's sword only enters the outer layer of the Twisted Queen without drawing blood.
The Twisted Queen says the flaw of the Hives is Queens, and says to remove the Queens.
The Twisted Queen sends that her project is complete and that the Antinium are trapped here, with Wrymvr concurring.
The Twisted Queen says the Queens are too large to move and too dangerous, and tells Klbkch that he does not need her anymore.
Klbkch asks Wrymvr whether he could kill the Illusionist, and Wrymvr answers yes through their shared link.
The Twisted Queen says her attempts to create water-capable Antinium have all failed.
The Twisted Queen sends that the Antinium lack a way to cross the sea, being landlocked among unassailable Walled Cities.
Klbkch says the Illuminary could destroy any vessel the Antinium seize, and suggests hiring a [Pirate] of Rasea's caliber or obtaining Greater Teleportation scrolls.
Typhenous is an old [Mage] who carries a wand and a glowing staff.
Typhenous is a Gold-rank adventurer and a member of Griffon Hunt, alongside Revi.
Typhenous has a white beard and a glowing staff, and Griffon Hunt's [Mage] specialises in defence and wards.
Typhenous says he was educated for twelve years at the college of magic in the capital city of Pheron.
Halrac and Ulrien contracted Typhenous and Revi for their expertise in Griffin hunting.
Halrac says he and Ulrien wanted to hire Typhenous so badly because of his best spell, [Valmira's Comet Storm].
Typhenous tries to cast [Eltraz's Bin—] on Moore, and Moore kicks him before he finishes.
Typhenous spins sticky enchanted webbing from his staff, which lasts only a few minutes.
Typhenous casts [Platform of Air] in the corridor fight.
Typhenous casts [Sticky Webs] and [Barrier of Air] against Regrika's attackers.
Typhenous calls down comet after comet with [Valmira's Comet Storm], which wipes out groups of Shield Spiders.
Halrac says [Valmira's Comet Storm] is Typhenous's trump card, a Tier 5 spell that Griffon Hunt used against Griffin flights.
Typhenous casts [Black Burst] against the Raskghar.
Typhenous throws a [Wind Blast] from his finger that knocks Revi backwards.
Typhenous uses [Mites of Slumber], a higher-Tier [Sleep] variation with living mites as the vector, which he says works even on Gold-rank adventurers.
Typhenous fed Relc the mites in his food instead of getting them into his skin.
Eltistiman calls Typhenous "the Plague Mage".
Typhenous casts [Valmira's Comets] from Liscor's walls onto Reiss's army.
Typhenous names a yellow sludge Numbtongue found as magicore and his voice shakes.
Typhenous orders specialised lodestones, saying the door cannot be linked to many places without magical beacons.
Typhenous says the lodestones should arrive in Celum within the week and refuses to pay a Courier for them.
Typhenous has attuned one stone already and says the hard part is delivering each stone to its destination.
Typhenous says each extra destination is exponentially harder, so he advises three or four set anchors at most.
Typhenous suggests hiring a City Runner to carry a stone to its destination.
Typhenous and Pisces agreed that maintaining the portal effect was better than an involuntary translocation, and that testing showed a sudden mana failure did not harm travellers.
Pisces works a long time with Moore and Typhenous so that Erin can switch the door by tapping a mana stone against it.
Typhenous knows Moore from before, and warns him that he is not half the mage Typhenous is.
Typhenous asks to buy Pisces's ring at more than its worth, over Ulrien's disapproval.
Seborn asks to buy the dagger while Typhenous and Revi argue over the ring, and Ceria says they will sell nothing yet.
Typhenous calls Pisces and Falene insufferable students and finds Ceria and Moore more pleasant company, though they are only practitioners.
Typhenous secretly sends a [Message] to Lord Tyrion Veltras after the Christmas party, paying for priority delivery.
Halrac wants to ask his contacts about Erin, because he feels there is something about her.
Typhenous admits he was caught off-guard by Regrika Blackpaw and underestimated her and her companion badly.
Typhenous tells Eltistiman that the Smiling Man hired him.
Typhenous pockets the mana stone attuned to Pallass in a room of rogues and thugs.
Typhenous mutters that he was hired by Lord Veltras and by Pallassian [Senators] to ensure no aid reached Liscor, and by an unknown third party to keep the door inoperable.
Typhenous tells the Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings how to reach the inn and what obstacles they will meet.
Typhenous says there are several hundred Goblins camped in a cave on the northern road, none of them Hobs, but the Goblins on the slopes are far more numerous.
Typhenous says his team poisoned the Griffins' nests and killed hundreds of Griffins, but the plague got out of control and killed almost every livestock animal and sickening three cities.
Typhenous says Gold-rank status was almost lost over the Griffin plague.
Griffon Hunt and the Halfseekers swap groups every few hours in the dungeon, with Typhenous planning to impart tactics to the other teams.
In Invrisil, Typhenous grabs a gang leader and holds a dagger to his ear, and says he has run with more gangs than the boy has seen.
Typhenous tells the gang that people call him the Plague Mage, and the gang's members repeat the name with awe.
Typhenous tells Halrac the theatrics were an introduction and that the gang respects only a display.
Typhenous says he was in a gang once, and that most people who grow up without a proper job or class are.
Gang bosses treat Typhenous as a celebrity, and one says his father knew him from the days of running tricks.
Halrac says Typhenous is "a face" in the city's underworld.
Typhenous tells Halrac that the door theft was going to happen with or without his interference, and that he mitigated the damage.
Typhenous tells a Drake and a Human that he cannot lie and that his deed helped save a young woman from a theft.
Tyrion Veltras is the scion of the Veltras family, one of the Five Families of Izril, and technically as powerful as Magnolia Reinhart.
Tyrion commands one of the most powerful private armies on the continent, and some see him as a legend embodying the pride of Izril.
He has defended Izril from every threat on its soil for decades and protects Humans, his subjects, first and foremost.
Admirers do not love him, and others call him the closest thing Izril has to a tyrant.
Tyrion is a war hawk as pro-Human as the worst of the Drakes are pro-Drake, and he sees diplomacy as a weaker alternative to war.
Tyrion has a sense of honour: he does not use [Assassins] as Magnolia does, and he keeps his word.
Tyrion fought against Velan the Kind and the Antinium and is known as the most powerful martial [Lord] in existence.
Ullim reflects that only Lord Hayvon, Lord Belchaus and Lord Seagrass might rival Tyrion as a martial [Lord].
Tyrion says the Goblin King was a threat that could be dealt with, and he had a plan to bleed him by killing his Goblin Lords.
Tyrion is tall, with black hair, a trimmed goatee, a clean-shaven upper lip and cold dark blue eyes.
Tyrion holds himself strictly upright on his horse, and wears armor that glows slightly.
Tyrion dresses in black, and the artifacts he carries could lay waste to a whole room.
Tyrion wears rings that turn rain and arrows aside, though he dislikes rain as too nostalgic.
Tyrion's longsword, shield and armor are Veltras heirlooms infused with ancient magic.
Tyrion's Skills give him incredible acceleration on horseback, and he rides at a bobbing ring with a lance.
Tyrion rides faster than a horse and rider should be able to move, using the Skill [Lightning Hooves].
Tyrion uses [Repel Point] to thrust back an opponent's mount instead of the opponent.
Tyrion has the Skill [Barrier of Pride].
Tyrion has the Skill [Peilspear Formation].
Tyrion has the Skill [Lancing Hydrastrike].
Tyrion's [Knights] ride with him at the same speed, propelled by the same Skill.
Tyrion's war horse Gelden dies by Book 19, and he breaks in a new one.
Tyrion has Gelden butchered and the meat given to the dogs, and buries the bones himself.
Tyrion's private aide is the grey-haired [Mage] Jericha, who deflects a fiery arrow with a wave of her hand.
Tyrion's [Majordomo] is Ullim, who cares for his sons while he is away.
Tyrion has two sons: Sammial, a sickly boy of nine or ten with dark brown hair, and the thin, nervous Hethon, about fourteen.
Tyrion's late wife's death has driven a rift between him and his sons, and he is not an intimate father.
Tyrion orders Ullim to keep his sons entertained, and sits by their beds sharpening a dagger.
Sammial wants to be called Sammy, but Tyrion insists the name is inappropriate for a [Lord].
Magnolia offers condolences for the death of Tyrion's wife four years earlier and hopes his two young sons are in good hands.
Tyrion stiffens at Magnolia's condolences and the metal cup in his hand bends.
Later, the text gives Sammial's age as eight and says Hethon will be thirteen two weeks after his birthday.
Tyrion's father died when he was young, a casualty of the plots of the Reinharts.
Tyrion's wife was named Salva, and he wishes she were there to advise him.
Tyrion believes the Walled City of Manus plotted Salva's murder, though he says Liscor's people had no part.
Tyrion tells Hethon the Drakes killed his mother, and for that alone he should drown Izril in Drake blood.
Tyrion admits he would have spared Liscor's civilians if they surrendered, but says a [Lord] is seldom kind.
The narration calls Magnolia Reinhart Tyrion's hated nemesis.
Tyrion approves gelato for Sammial and Hethon despite Magnolia's trade war, and hires the Moonlight Rider Tritel.
Tyrion rides out that night to hunt an overactive Mothbear clan sixty miles south along the Vail Forest.
Tyrion downplays his battle with the [Assassins] to Hethon, who is agog at the story.
Tyrion has Ullim look after Sammial, who has a summer cold, and says his lungs were always weak.

section: Early appearances: Book 2 and the Antinium Wars
text: Lady Magnolia's briefing notes that only Lord Tyron's spies have realised the northern Goblin tribes are moving.

section: Early appearances: Book 2 and the Antinium Wars
text: Tyron's army has just smashed two other armies with very few losses, and is splendidly equipped.

section: Early appearances: Book 2 and the Antinium Wars
text: Magnolia says his soldiers are peerless in the north, though she wishes the same of their lord.

section: Early appearances: Book 2 and the Antinium Wars
text: Tyron Veltras, young Magnolia Reinhart and General Sserys knew of the Antinium's arrival early, perhaps through powerful spells.

section: Early appearances: Book 2 and the Antinium Wars
text: Lord Tyron took the view that the war would weaken both Antinium and Drakes and Gnolls, so Human cities could crush all sides.

section: Early appearances: Book 2 and the Antinium Wars
text: Magnolia, by contrast, took the Antinium most seriously and began contacting leaders of the Human city-states.
At a gathering of nobles, Tyrion argues to let the Drakes deal with the Goblin Lord, unless he comes north.
Tyrion says that if the north beats the Drakes at the Blood Fields, it will take Liscor, and the Goblin Lord is its chance.
Tyrion swats a thrown dagger away from Magnolia, interposing himself between her and an [Assassin].
Tyrion picks up a severed head by the hair and checks it with a flashing ring.
Mayor Wullst of Leadenfurt reports a request from Lord Veltras for twice the number of men Magnolia had levied.
Magnolia settles for two hundred cavalry, with free mages on horseback.
Tyrion is gathering a far larger army than Magnolia, including six thousand horse from the Terland family, at least a quarter [Knights].
Tyrion says his alliance with Magnolia in the Antinium War was one of necessity and that they separated their forces.
Tyrion rages when he learns Magnolia has allied with Zel Shivertail, destroying his parlor and two suits of armor.
Tyrion tells his sons he could most likely not beat the Goblin King without the ancestral relics, and that the war was won by numbers.
Tyrion rejects the account of a Drake historian that the Humans struggled to defeat the Goblin King's armies.
Tyrion tells his sons that if a foe is too strong from the front, one should bleed him to death.
Zel Shivertail tells Pawn to go to Niers Astoragon or Lord Tyrion Veltras for leadership training.
Magnolia says she would like to see Tyrion's face when he hears of Zel's rousing speech to her officers.
Tyrion sits in his war camp in the rain, and spares a thought for his sons.
Tyrion calls Zel Shivertail's death an unexpected boon, since he had hoped Zel would lose and be forced to defend Invrisil.
Tyrion plans to move part of his horse and some [Mages] ahead of the main army, which waits.
Tyrion tells Yitton he is waiting for a single precise moment, and for the rain to stop.
Tyrion hears that a new [Emperor] has appeared southwest of Invrisil, and suspects Magnolia plans to use him as an ally.
Lord Tyrion's army has a reputation as the superior one, and some think he falls little behind Shivertail in level.
The Veltras family has a conventional army, and Tyrion himself lacks siege weapons.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion plots a route south-west past the city of Filk, orders the camp struck, and plans to cover fifty miles on the first day.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion waits for a specialised group of reinforcements travelling south down Almest Road after a sea voyage.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion rides into a village with a lance faster than an arrow, and strikes Redscar through the shoulder.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion removes his helmet, bows slightly to Laken, introduces himself, and says they could be of mutual benefit.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion sends a passphrase [Message] naming Benivald Veltras, the 52nd second-son of House Veltras, to his aide Telmia, then orders "Mark".

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion says Goblins do not matter, only people, humanity, and responsibility to one's lands.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion offers Laken his hand and asks his help in uniting against a common foe.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion says he acts according to necessity, not compassion, and that he could not act without understanding the truth about Goblins.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion takes reports as the Goblins retreat back into the city, while Laken sits with his knees gone.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion stands in Riverfarm while his knights chase the last Redfang Warriors, and a mage reports four casualties.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion offers to lend Laken [Mages] for truth spells, and swears on his house's honour that he took no part in the Goblin attack.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion admits he received [Messages] from Lady Bevia and others about the Goblins, and a [Knight] of Lady Bethal found his camp.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion rides at double speed, ordering reinforcements for Lord Byres, who fights thousands of undead.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion blocks Redscar's [Flurry Strikes] while riding, and calls him "Not bad. For a Goblin."

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion has about five thousand cavalry, and a [Siege Fireball] cast by twenty mages and Jericha breaks the city's walls and gates.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion says Goblins are predictable, a manipulable tool, and ultimately expendable.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion cuts Redscar open across four ribs in a duel.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion blocks Rags's fire and sword, smiles coldly, and tells her to run quickly because she has an hour.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion bets Lord Pellmia two thousand gold and a warhorse that Pellmia cannot corner the Goblins in two hours.

section: Book 8: Laken and the Redfang Goblins
text: Tyrion tells Pellmia his schedule allows fourteen days.
Tyrion wants live Goblins driven south, and offers Pellmia three casks of his personal stock if he makes the meeting spot on time.
Tyrion tells Pellmia he has won their second bet, and thanks Arcsinger's Skills and the [Mages] for forcing the Goblins to march.
Tyrion messages Laken to ask whether he can fulfill his side of the bargain on time.
Tyrion says the chieftains' tribes are no longer needed, since only the Goblin Lord is required.
Tyrion refuses to split the Goblin tribes and decides to send the Goblins and watchers a message.
Tyrion kills the Great Chieftain Tremborag in single combat with a lance after Tremborag taunts him about his dead wife.
Tyrion tells his nobles that Liscor has been his target from the beginning, and that the army marches to take it.
Tyrion intends to offer Liscor to the Goblin Lord as a prize, by making it a target easy to take.
Tyrion says the trebuchets will "misfire" until Liscor's walls are breached, so the Goblins sack the city and the army retakes it.
Tyrion insists it is not an act of war but an unfortunate accident, and that no Drake will be killed.
Tyrion says Magnolia has warned the Drakes, and that he has already made a move concerning the magical door.
Tyrion says the door cannot carry legions, but wants Liscor for the strategic value of a doorway.
Tyrion announces that in four days Liscor will fall.
Tyrion pursues the Chieftain Garen Redfang with three thousand [Knights], but halts when tens of thousands of Eater Goats come from the High Passes.
Tyrion's informant reports that the portal door is now in Liscor's possession, which frustrates him.
Tyrion had allowed a covert operation by Lord Erill and Lady Ieka against his better judgment.
Magnolia sends Tyrion messages nonstop urging him to halt, and warns Jericha she will take steps.
Tyrion tells Jericha to double the night sentries and watch the food, expecting assassins.
Ullim reports the boys are growing restless and miss their father, and Tyrion says he may make time to return.
Tyrion's army sends a false apology to Liscor, promising to engage the Goblins at a distance with new weapons.
Ilvriss and Zevara refuse trebuchets near Liscor for fear of incidental fire.
Tyrion has Laken oversee the Riverfarm [Engineers] and the trebuchets, with Lady Ieka's enchantments.
Tyrion orders "Fire" and the first stones miss or land at the base of Liscor's walls.
The enchanted stones explode on the walls and dent the eastern gates.
The Humans claim a misfire and tell the Drakes to watch for stray missiles.
After the Goblin Lord dies, Tyrion challenges the Drakes to meet him at the Blood Fields in six days.
Tyrion leaves the trebuchets and half the foot behind, and the nobility who do not wish to fight leave.
A [Crier] reports that over forty thousand Drakes died at the Blood Fields and Lord Tyrion is returning north with most of his army.
Tyrion's grand scheme to take Liscor falls apart, and he returns home.
Tyrion orders a scroll to remove the rain and complains about the cost, at least two thousand gold.
Tyrion tells Ullim to search the cellars and storerooms for rats.
Drakes in the clouds strike Tyrion's keep with lightning, and he sends his sons to the safe rooms.
Tyrion calls for the Banner of House Veltras to shield him from lightning, and finds the Drake Oldbloods have already moved on.
Hethon asks why Liscor had to fall, and Tyrion says because they stand with his enemies.
Tyrion says duty to family, house and people informs each decision, and the Drakes sent saboteurs against his house.
Tyrion is irked by the Ailendamus war on the Dawn Concordat, and thinks of consulting Jericha, Ullim or Pellmia, but not his sons.
A messenger from the Circle of Thorns tells Tyrion Magnolia will be attacked, and Tyrion kills him before riding out.
Tyrion rides to the road, strikes the [Trapmaster], and breaks up the three [Assassins] around Ressa.
Tyrion blocks the Faces' attack and takes down Mire with [Lancing Hydrastrike], costing her arm and shoulder.
Tyrion says he is not Magnolia Reinhart's ally and detests how she rules.
Tyrion declares that he will not let a lord of the Five Families be slain by cowardice, as it would end House Veltras.
The Circle of Thorns' watchers decide Izril cannot lose its most powerful [Lord], and the [Assassins] leave.
A Circle voice calls Tyrion a feral hound, not an ally, who will be brought to heel.
Tyrion tells Jericha he saved Magnolia for Hethon and Sammial's integrity.
Hethon falls ill, and a masked Circle of Thorns [Assassin] tells Tyrion she has poisoned both his sons.
She says she does not have the cure, and that the sons will die without it in a week or at most a month.
The [Assassin] offers a Blood Oath Contract that would heal them in exchange for his cooperation.
Tyrion refuses, saying he does not deal with traitors of Izril and cowards.
The [Assassin] leaves the blood-contract behind with a warning.
Tyrion's sons are sick, and twenty-six [Alchemists] and [Healers] send only heads while the rest answer with silence.
On the fifth day Tyrion rides out with two hundred riders toward the highest-level [Alchemist] near Keriwrel.
Tyrion turns back after sixteen miles when Jericha calls him back and he sees the keep burning.
Tyrion receives a [Witch]'s recipe to neutralise a five-poison blend, needing rare ingredients such as mithril dust.
Tyrion sends a public [Message] for the cure, and First Landing accepts the delivery with Couriers outbound.
Ulinde is a Selphid [Spellslinger] of Wistram who fights with two dueling wands.
Ulinde is a dangerous duelist, regarded by Palt as good as Isceil.
Ulinde's gender follows the Selphid's body, so Ulinde is female when wearing a female Drake's body and male in a male one.
Ulinde's Selphid faction is tied to the Revivalists.
Ulinde grows up on tales of the Halfseekers in Selphid communities and admires them.
Ulinde guesses that Palt learned the spliff from the guests.
Ulinde pushes her body to move faster than all but Seborn when she Rampages, and she survives Seborn's flaming dagger stabs, which perforate her chest.
Ulinde uses her second dueling wand on Seborn's chest with [Reduced Fireball] while Rampaging.
Ulinde, in a rotting heavyset male body, is banned from Erin's inn and weeps, wanting to be friends with Ivirith.
Moore pats Ulinde on the back and says he forgave her, and Jelaqua may forgive her too.
Moore offers to ask Jelaqua to lend Ulinde one of her spare bodies.
Ulinde tells Seborn and Moore she is a fan of the Halfseekers, and cites his slaying of the Cyclops.
Seborn says Ulinde's body is disgusting and that she can borrow one of Jelaqua's.
Later, Ulinde wears a female Drake's body and speaks with Moore and Seborn.
Ulinde refuses to take part in kidnapping Erin, saying the Halfseekers would never forgive her again.
Ulinde agrees to ask her Revivalist-tied Selphid faction about allying with Palt's faction.
Ulinde links with Palt in the battle against the insects.
Ulinde is held at Ksmvr's bowpoint during Montressa's duel, along with Palt.
Ulinde loses her left shoulder and arm, and Crelers eat part of her face and torso; poison stops potions from healing her.
Ulinde quits Montressa's team to join the Halfseekers, and Moore confirms she is a member on trial.
Ulinde now wears a female Drake's body, sharing a pool of corpses with Jelaqua, and Jelaqua is Maughin's partner.
Ulinde is terrified of angering Jelaqua again, because she once confronted another Selphid.
Ulinde remains a member of Wistram though now a Halfseeker, and has not told Jelaqua about Montressa's mission.
Ullim is the [Majordomo] of House Veltras and serves Lord Tyrion Veltras.
Ullim has a high-class servant's demeanor, dress and manners, and he tells a [Messenger] that Tyrion is riding and a missive can be left.
Jericha is Tyrion's personal [Mage] and first assistant, who rushes in when he calls for her and Ullim.
Ullim reports that villages recall the passing of a [Witch], Eloise, the Tea Witch, around the time the rains began, and many believe she cursed the region.
Ullim discovers by discreet inquiry that the Tea Witch is Lady Eloise of House Havin, a Terandrian [Lady] considered dead to her family for over three decades.
Ullim and Tyrion both think of Magnolia Reinhart, who loves tea and is fond of using agents, as the possible hand behind the Tea Witch.
Ullim notes that Lords Erill, Pellmia and Lady Ieka suffer weather disturbances while Invrisil does not.
Ullim reports that Lord Pellmia's [Manservant] Kilmet saw another [Witch], Hedag or Hedag the [Executioner], pass through his lands.
Tyrion orders Ullim to send word to Pellmia and the villages the [Witch] passed through, and to check whether Bethal, Pryde and Wuvren are affected.
Tyrion says that if Bethal, Pryde and Wuvren are unaffected, he will treat Reinhart's interference at Liscor and this rain as an insult.
Ulrien is the Captain of Griffon Hunt and a Gold-rank adventurer.
Ulrien wields an enchanted greatsword, and several enchanted rings take the force of blows when he fights without armor.
Ulrien is incredibly strong, strong enough to swing his greatsword around like it was nothing.
Halrac once saw Ulrien beat a Minotaur in arm-wrestling.
Ulrien's enchanted greatsword can be swung all day without chipping the blade or hilt.
Ulrien keeps a calm, dependable manner and never seems to get worried, and Erin thinks of him as being like a rock.
Ulrien tells Yvlon that her gear alone could make her Gold-rank and suggests that the Guild may recertify the Horns of Hammerad.
Ulrien nudges Typhenous with disapproval when the mage asks to buy Pisces's ring.
Ulrien uses Mordhau, a technique not meant for repeated strikes, to break the stone floor in the dungeon trap room, taking breaks to massage his hands.
Ulrien offers to discuss helping the Halfseekers deal with Garen after the dungeon, saying justice should be done for their fallen.
Ulrien was the first to agree to help Erin set her trap, after she accused a Named Adventurer, though Revi threw a fit and Typhenous worried about their reputation.
Ulrien looked Erin in the eye for a few moments before nodding and trusting her.
Ulrien's [Devastating Slash] bends mid-swing but cuts only two inches into Regrika Blackpaw's leg.
Regrika's first sword stroke sets off an amulet on Ulrien's chest that protects him from one blow.
Regrika takes off Ulrien's head with her second sword stroke.
Ulrien is dead, headless, with his greatsword still embedded in Regrika's leg.
Erin cannot believe Ulrien died so easily, since he was a Gold-rank adventurer.
Later, Erin stands in the inn and stares at the spot where Ulrien died.
Later, Halrac remembers Ulrien dying weeks earlier in an inn, battling the traitorous Named Adventurer Regrika Blackpaw.
After Ulrien's death, Halrac thinks his team broke.
Ulseil Greenscale is an olive-green Drake [Merchant], unmarried, middle-aged and wealthy by Liscor standards.
Ulseil is the head of Liscor's Merchant's Guild and a member of Liscor's Council.
Ulseil is not Oldblood, though his great-great-aunt had vestigial wings, a source of pride for the Greenscale family.
Ulseil is content to earn and save money rather than risk much, and his goal is to find a Miss Greenscale.
In the Liscor Council, an unnamed Drake who heads the Merchant's Guild blames the dungeon and the Antinium after another attack.
Ulseil shudders to think of the Council's recent meetings and wants out of the job after helping Liscor survive possible war with Humans.
Ulseil plans to appoint his deputy Stale of the Merchant's Guild, a young Drake in his thirties, as his successor.
Cornered by a crowd, Ulseil blurts that he would support Gnolls on the Council and elections, and the crowd spreads it as a vote.
Ulseil faints after realising he will be accountable for his words before the whole crowd.
Ulseil is one of eight rich Drakes of the old Council who sit scowling at each other in the meeting room.
Ulvama is a female Hob, the chief [Shaman] of Tremborag's tribe, nearly naked with chalky body paint in exotic patterns.
Ulvama tells Rags that five other [Shamans] are in the tribe but she is strongest by far.
Ulvama's magic is basic but strong with numbers; she casts lightning, fire and shields, and heals by closing flesh and restoring blood but cannot fix a missing arm.
Ulvama is a Goblin whose mother was a Goblin, and who says she is both Human and Goblin.
Ulvama has crimson eyes and wears the markings of her class, colorful paint worn from long days.
Ulvama casts a [Bloodfury] spell on young Goblins that makes the red lights in their eyes brighten and their bodies grow before the attack.
Ulvama shoots masses of fire from her staff onto the Goblin Lord's grouped army.
Ulvama marches in the center of Tremborag's tribe beside his Hob lieutenants, her skin painted with symbols.
Ulvama casts a hazy illusion that makes Tremborag and nearby Goblins flicker, snapping an arrow aimed at Tremborag's face.
Ulvama screeches and throws herself down as Noears's lightning bolt earths just past her.
Ulvama tells Rags that her people were happy in Tremborag's mountain with sex, food and what they wanted, and that Tremborag was a great Chieftain.
Ulvama tries to seduce Pyrite as a second for Chieftain Rags, kicking Hammersteel aside.
Pyrite tells Ulvama he knew her as a small Goblin, an apprentice to the Chief Shaman, remembered for getting in trouble over paints.
Pyrite turns Ulvama down because he is busy and does not like her.
Ulvama leads Hobs and Mountain City Goblins who bow low to Rags and ask what now.
Ulvama is among the Goblin prisoners after the battle, injured and staring hatred at Laken and every Human.
Ulvama is a captive in Pebblesnatch's wagon, one of three Hobs captured by the Humans, and the chief [Shaman] of the Mountain City tribe.
Ulvama pats Pebblesnatch on the head, then flicks her and tells her to shush.
Ulvama strides into a fight with a crude wooden staff as a symbol of her authority and breaks it up with blows and shouts.
Ulvama gives herself and those who obey a large portion of meat and the rest scraps, the way the Mountain City tribe does.
Ulvama strikes a deal under which the Redfangs hunt for the camp in return for three huts, ejecting the Mountain City Goblins.
Ulvama raises a pillar of fire from a campfire to show that [Shamans] have magic.
Ulvama smears ash and dirt on a Redfang [Scout] and says she will hide the Goblins sent to search.
Ulvama grinds marrowless bone with rust to make a dye, and makes Pebblesnatch's dough rise out of its bowl.
Ulvama smacks Pebblesnatch on the head, then uses [Silenced Agony] to take away the pain.
Ulvama says she will give Pebblesnatch and two other Goblins proper names so they are remembered through memory when they die.
Ulvama tells Pebblesnatch that power is strength, sex and food, and that she can be second-strongest by taking power any way.
Ulvama says Tremborag was Great Chieftain, bigger than Rags and older than Garen Redfang, and that Humans always kill Goblins.
