Ulvama finds Pebblesnatch's hollow tree empty except for a glowing red stone and a crude bark door, and fits the stone into the door.
Ulvama inspects the stone, stares south and says it is too far, very far and too weak.
Ulvama uses sex as influence and currency, an essential part of her class and position as [Shaman].
Ulvama takes Raidpear, the strongest Hobgoblin of the Solstice Goblins, as her partner, judging males easier than the female Hob Leafarmor.
Ulvama blows soil at about ten young Goblins from the Mountain City and Flooded Plains tribes who spy on her and Raidpear.
Ulvama counts little magic-charged gems that the Goblins dug up beside a crude door in her hut.
Ulvama watches a glowing crimson stone set in the door, which has grown a stronger connection, and sees the door is open.
Ulvama tells Pebblesnatch to say that other Goblins come because they hear the Goblinlands are safe.
Ulvama casts a flea hex at Halrac during a parley, and Typhenous's [Hex Eater] and Revi's [Wind Orb] react, and Typhenous identifies it as a minor flea hex.
Ulvama calls the hex a little prank, and the Goblins relax once Halrac lowers his bow.
Ulyse is the middle-aged leader of the [Mage] group Parasol Stroll, who has distant eyes, greying hair and a vacant gaze.
Ulyse carries a bright yellow silk parasol embroidered with silver moons, and each member of Parasol Stroll carries an enchanted parasol.
Parasol Stroll is busy with the work of the Mage's Guild and coordinating the rest of Reim's magical needs.
Orthenon asks Ulyse whether Parasol Stroll has an [Enchanter] who can enchant blades for Jelaim's warriors.
Ulyse says the quality of metal is not good, and Daiton's blades are beautiful but flawed and cannot hold enchantments.
Ulyse is one of the [Mages] who recently came to Reim, and he fixes Trey's iPhone with a [Repair] spell.
Ulyse takes Flos' iPhone, levitates it and taps it with his parasol while casting [Repair].
Ulyse dies in the fight with Medain's army, stabbed through the throat by Rasea as he raises his staff.
Umina Caxical is a Lizardgirl from Baleros with yellow scales patterned pink and violet frills around her neck.
Umina is a nervous Lizardgirl and a student of Niers Astoragon, the Titan.
Umina is a Level 27 [Strategist], with a dozen Skills, at nineteen years old, one of the youngest students in Niers' advanced class.
Umina has beaten every classmate in practice war games and is especially good at taking down Venaz.
Umina got into the class on pure talent in the one-year program, while the other students paid more.
Umina has beaten Venaz three times in practice, which no one else has done, while Marian's best is two wins in a row.
Umina is the only Lizardfolk in Niers' current class, and some of her family's friends helped pay for her to attend.
Umina has barely twenty silver coins and two gold coins reserved for rent and food, so she cannot afford preparations for the game.
Umina prefers listening and understanding before acting, which has earned her a reputation for timidity in class.
Umina summarises the Goblin Lord news to Foliana, saying the Goblin Lord is on the run after losing a battle to a Human [Lord].
Umina argues to Niers that Tyrion Veltras prepared the attack on Liscor and that the Drakes will send elites into a trap.
Umina says she would want the Drakes to attack first and fill Liscor with soldiers who cannot retreat.
Umina resolves to try seriously to win the game for the first time, and teams up with Marian.
The class agrees to a truce unless their plans collide, but Umina and Marian work together as a team.
Umina talks a Lizardfolk-crewed ship into hiding her and Marian from the Iron Vanguard, since the crew are Lizardfolk.
Marian is seasick on the ship, since Centaurs do not like being at sea, boats or small spaces.
Umina and Luan meet a Dullahan [Mage] who traps Luan in a [Water Wall], and Umina defeats her by hurling flour and grit at her face and kicking her in the head.
Umina pops up from a tunnel inside the rope circle, covered in filth, and tells Niers that [Nightmen] make excellent sappers.
Umina wins the game by tunneling beneath a sewage depot to surface in the plaza, unnoticed by the [Mages] and Tulm the Mithril.
Tulm asks the name of the student who won, and Niers answers Umina Caxical.
Umina's prize is an item from Niers' vaults and a question of her choice, to be set when they return to Elvallian.
Umina and Wil have not been called to ask their question for over a month, to the class's surprise.
Niers congratulates Umina on passing a test and tells her to put her name on her report next time.
Wil demands the earned question on Umina's behalf at the end of term, and Niers admits he and Perorn had bet on it.
Niers praises Umina's tunneling through a septic tank but says she lacks the daring Venaz and Marian show, acting as a [Tactician] among [Strategists].
Umina asks Niers whether she is unique, and he answers no: he sees a brilliant young [Strategist], not something he has not seen before.
Umina asks as her second question for the identity of Niers' chess opponent, and her third for Tulm's would-be question, so that Niers must choose.
Umina says she chose the two questions she thought would bother Niers most because they are the most valuable to her.
Drunk in bed, Umina deduces that Tulm's question concerned Dragons.
Umina takes a Belt of Acrobats from the armory as the winner of the Titan's Games.
The Belt of Acrobats makes Umina nimbler, though she was never exactly agile, and lets her do backflips.
Umina moves out of her dorm room into Wil's larger quarters in Elvallian while he is away.
Umina turned down Wil's invitation to sea, wanting to keep taking classes and having things to do in Baleros.
Umina tracks Geneva in Talenqual over a speaking stone, calling herself Dancing Serpent and Marian Fast Hooves.
Umina works undercover in Geneva's clinic during the Yellow Rivers outbreak.
Umina thinks Geneva has more to hide than even Niers knows, including possible ties to the Selphids.
Umina notes that Cameral and Kissilt train with Daly's Bushrangers while she and Marian tail Geneva.
Umina takes notes near the back as Geneva operates, fascinated, and thinks Niers is right that Geneva is exceptional.
Umina slips away to find Marian, deciding to learn more about Geneva before the summer ends.
Urksh is the Chieftain of the Stone Spears tribe of Gnolls.
Urksh helps dig Ryoka out of the snow and offers her food and shelter in the Stone Spears camp.
Urksh treats Ryoka's arm with healing ointment, which he says is not a potion but works well and avoids wasting one.
Urksh grips Ryoka's arm as lightly as he can while he applies the ointment, and the swelling begins to recede.
Urksh apologises to Ryoka that Mrsha is young and does not yet know boundaries.
Urksh tells Ryoka that Mrsha found her by smell, since young Gnolls have the best noses.
Urksh scowls at the laughing adults and chases after Mrsha when she flees from Ryoka's tent.
Urksh tells Ryoka that there is no debt for the joy she has given the tribe, and that she is welcome to stay.
Urksh says the tribe knows of one Necromancer but he is dead, and that following only a stone toward a necromancer is dangerous.
Urksh tells Ryoka that Mrsha has gone missing after wandering away from a gatherer in the morning.
Urksh says that Mrsha does not speak although her throat is undamaged, so her silence worries the tribe.
Urksh and the Gnolls accept that Mrsha will probably be dead if she is not found by the next day.
Urksh gives Ryoka healing potions, a magical rope that stretches a long way, and a child-sized fur coat.
Urksh's hunter Hekra reports that thirteen adults are missing across three patrols sent to look for Mrsha, and that none came back.
Urksh worries that those who vanished left no trace and no howls, meaning that whatever took them acted swiftly and by surprise.
Urksh orders every warrior ready and packed in case the tribe has to flee.
Urksh catches a faint, twisted scent of his enemy on the air, with death in it.
Urksh clutches his stomach as he holds in his wounds, joins Ryoka in offering everything to the faeries, and falls when a Goblin stabs him from behind.
Urksh had been teaching Mrsha in the tribe to walk on two legs.
Mrsha remembers Urksh among the dead Stone Spears and thinks of herself as the lone survivor.
Urksh exiled Mrsha's hunter parents after they tried to abandon her for being mute, saying that being unable to speak was not a crime worthy of death.
Urksh raised Mrsha like a father until Goblins slew him.
Urksh taught Mrsha to read basic things and do numbers only sparingly.
Urksh was older than the old Liscor Gnoll who shares Mrsha's captivity, who is described as not as old as Urksh had been.
Vaitsha Zectiou is a Highborn of Germina, a woman in her thirties and clearly noble, who has pledged to be the Quarass's companion.
Vaitsha is one of the three protectors sworn by blood to serve the Quarass.
Vaitsha is a beautiful woman of Germina who is white as a sheet and wobbles a little when she greets Trey.
Vaitsha's class is [Highborn of Coin], which the Quarass calls weak and tells her how to change into a rare and deadly class.
Vaitsha wears gloves and sips from a vial, looking paler than the boy beside her.
The Quarass tells Trey that Vaitsha ingests poison and antidote daily, in growing quantities, so that her blood becomes poison.
Later, the Quarass says Vaitsha will become a [Viperborn], a [Serpent Lady], or another class depending on factors outside her control.
Vaitsha must take another poison as a numbing medicine to stay sane, and will soon be bedridden and hand-fed.
The Quarass says Vaitsha chose the risk herself, and her chance of death is one in sixty.
Khalid, a boy of Ger and a [Street Tough] who is the Quarass's protector, trains with tinctures and baths to gain twice a normal man's strength.
Valceif Godfrey is a Courier from First Landing, a tall and tanned Human with black hair and a crooked nose that was never set properly.
Valceif, who goes by Val, is a confident man whose presence sets him apart from other Runners.
Valceif says he earns forty gold coins per delivery, and up to one or two hundred for danger or speed.
Valceif introduces himself to the Runner's Guild in Celum as a Courier from First Landing on a delivery to Liscor.
Valceif says he has not stopped running since passing Invrisil.
Valceif killed the bandits who attacked Garia and reported the incident to the local Watch.
Valceif uses [Double Step] to run at twice Ryoka's pace and is a hundred meters ahead in seconds.
Valceif says he needs to reach Liscor by that night and wants to meet the Drake [Tactician] said to be the best chess player in Liscor.
Valceif delivers a package to Olesm, the best chess player in Liscor, as a Courier from First Landing.
Valceif gives Ryoka a small metal dreamcatcher charm, which he says dispels magic, worth several thousand gold, to free her from a spell.
Valceif says he paid over a thousand gold coins for the charm, which Ryoka's use destroyed.
Valceif waives repayment and asks Ryoka, from one Runner to another, whether it was worth it.
Valceif was brought in because Hawk, the usual Courier near Liscor, was busy with the undead.
Valceif avoids Skills when he can, because [Double Step] and [Quick Movement] tire him too much for everyday use.
Valceif says the last Runner who helped him took two arrows pulling him to safety after a [Bandit Lord] jumped him.
Valceif dislikes Crelers.
Valceif says he has met other people who choose not to level and compensate with magic.
Valceif carries a stone inscribed with glowing runes and calls Hawk to join the run.
Valceif knows Lady Magnolia Reinhart, who greets him warmly as Valceif and has not seen him in two months.
Valceif delivers Ryoka's folded letter to Magnolia in Invrisil, wondering what she will make of it.
A Celum receptionist tells Ryoka that Valceif is dead, killed two weeks earlier on a delivery.
Surviving bandits say they used a [Sleep] spell on the road to take him unawares, which is rare for a Courier who normally has wards.
Ryoka admits that Valceif's dreamcatcher could have shielded him from spells, and that she broke it.
Mihaela Godfrey says Val is buried on the Courier's Road, and that he will be there forever.
Valeterisa is the Archmage of Izril, an old-looking Human woman in her sixties who seems surprisingly normal and distracted.
Valeterisa has no grand otherworldly features like Az'kerash, though a faint tinge of magic hangs about her.
As a girl, Valeterisa wanted to be an [Archmage], and she kept that dream as she aged.
Valeterisa reached Feor's level of spellcraft within her short Human lifespan, though the half-Elf Feor is nearly four times her age.
Valeterisa stole away from the politicking of Wistram Academy to pursue her goal, though she survived Wistram to become Archmage.
Valeterisa achieved one great technique of old but dived too far into the heart of magic without a guide to pull her back.
Valeterisa claims she is bad with money and takes jobs, and says people lie to her.
Valeterisa no longer dreams or sleeps, and uses the Skill [Parallel Thoughts] to split her mind into over forty selves.
Valeterisa has forgotten her own name, and a singular part of her remembers it for her.
One of Valeterisa's selves keeps her body alive, another looks for danger, and most pursue magic.
Another of Valeterisa's selves screams, is angry and breaks things when the stress gets too much.
The narration says Archmage Chandler used the same Skill but would never have gone this far, and Az'kerash can sustain about fourteen thoughts.
Valeterisa has pursued one grand theory for over ten years, and few of her selves have time for anything else.
Valeterisa's fortress of a home holds a captive Courier, whom she knows of only dimly.
Valeterisa has spent ten years in the fortress, and countless Couriers, [Knights] and adventurers have failed to rouse her.
One of Valeterisa's fractured mental processes tracks intruders, and her shadow familiars carry them into holding cells that she has not investigated for six years.
Valeterisa believed no one would reach her and filed Ryoka's team as statistically high but not at the top.
Valeterisa calls the team's message that they are Runners ridiculous.
Valeterisa appears over Ryoka, Fierre and Salamani with nearly a hundred shadow familiars, a Golem army and a giant maw of shadows.
Valeterisa counts 4,388 [Messages] triggered by the fire on her isle and demands to know who the intruders are.
Valeterisa's fragmented selves reunite when Ryoka says they are Runners with a message for her, and she realises how much she has lost.
Valeterisa looks at her burning isle, with summoned monsters still dueling her defensive spells.
Valeterisa panics on learning prisoners starved in her cells, calling it an error that she forgot to monitor them.
Valeterisa's reaction is more like forgetting to feed housesat pets than moral anguish, according to Ryoka's view.
Valeterisa calms, blames a mental paradox and says the team's arrival was beneficial and they will be rewarded.
Ieka Imarris learns that Valeterisa is out of seclusion and calls the news fantastic.
Valeterisa sends Ieka a [Message] saying she is not pleased because the Runners burned her isle, and asks if it was intentional.
Valeterisa dismisses glowing [Messages] and Merchant Guild reports while multitasking, and says many people wanted her over the last decade.
Valeterisa says she made explicit that she was not to be disturbed, and offers to donate money to families of the dead.
Valeterisa admits she forgot to tell the familiars to feed the prisoners.
Valeterisa serves Ryoka stale tea and raw carrots from her shadow familiar and finds them disgusting after [Recall Memories].
Valeterisa says she was working on automated spellcasting, a lost magic, and that assembling the spell matrices took four years.
Valeterisa says she was trying to protect her work after a [Rogue] stole her research, and cries, calling the dead poor people.
Valeterisa says she tracked down a [Merchant] who tricked her and made an example of him, a death she thinks involved worms.
Valeterisa says she will contact Ieka Imarris, whom she calls her niece.
Valeterisa agrees to ship the team's scrolls and potions to Reizmelt and takes strands of Ryoka's hair with a shadow familiar.
Valeterisa privately notes that neither Ryoka nor Fierre has levels, and that Fierre does not show in mirrors.
Valeterisa adds Ryoka to her priority memos and finds her bag of holding, origin and bare feet interesting.
Valeterisa has only two great loves, Archmage Zelkyr and Archmage Chandler, and pursues their shades.
Valeterisa has helped her niece Ieka with secrets held over Ieka's head, while Ieka handles messy politics for her.
Velan the Kind became a Goblin King, and Rags speaks of the Goblin King of long ago as the last one.
The Gold Stone Chieftain tells Rags and Garen that the old Goblin King had a tribe larger than any other, was largely peaceful, and traded with Humans.
The Gold Stone Chieftain says the Goblin King was a Chieftain first, then a Goblin Lord, and then others called him Goblin King.
The Gold Stone Chieftain claims the Goblin King was beloved by Goblins, and that something bad later happened and there was terrible war.

Greybeard tells Rags that the Goblin King ruled peacefully for six years, that Goblins made peace with Humans, Gnolls and Drakes on this continent and forged alliances on Baleros, and that Goblins were hunted in only a few places while he lived.
A historian writes that Goblin Kings emerge every few centuries at most, each time heralding destruction and death.
Almost every nation has signed a treaty requiring aid in destroying a Goblin King, and Goblin Lords are actively hunted to prevent them from becoming Kings.

In the year 14 A.F., Velan the Kind was a Goblin Lord who lived in a peaceful relationship with the nations of Baleros, and his company of Goblins was rumored to be the fifth Great Company of Baleros.
Velan led the Clean Grass tribe on Baleros, learned to make medicines from the plants and animals, and began making poisons when adventurers and mercenary companies came to slaughter his tribe.
Velan led Hobs to shatter the Screaming Vine company, but after four companies were sent he lost his tribe and fled.
Velan flung himself into the ocean and swam for days, weeks and months without dying.
Before he became a Goblin Lord, Velan was a [Healer] and an [Alchemist], strong enough to forage alone in the jungle, and his tribe used draughts that let a Goblin run for three days straight.
Rags learns that Velan used crude funnels to pour blood into other Goblins.

In the waning months of spring, Velan fulfilled an unknown criterion and became a Goblin King, then appeared with his tribe in the Balerosian city of Zexil and razed it in a single day, breaking eighteen treaties of nonaggression.
His only message to the leaders of Baleros was one word brought by a half-dead Courier: "Vengeance".

Every company on Baleros agreed to a truce, but Velan was joined by many Goblin Lords and their tribes, seized and leveled the eastern port cities, built thousands of ships and sailed at the start of summer.
The historian says his seizing of the ports was a plan to flee across the sea to an easier target while the Four Great Companies advanced slowly.
Nine Goblin Lords sailed with him, including Greydath of Blades and his right hand, the Goblin Lord [Shaman] Tallis the Stormbreaker.
His armies won two sea battles, one against a Minotaur fleet and one at Wistram, where Tallis the Stormbreaker killed the Archmage Balkizat after a nine-hour magical duel.

The Goblin King landed at Cape Heathshell, and within about ten minutes his soldiers routed an army of about a hundred thousand led by Fulviolo El and the twins Petria and Ulva Terland, and he beheaded Fulviolo and Petria personally while Ulva escaped.
He vanished for eight days in the High Passes and reappeared south of them, opening a gateway between north and south Izril that bypassed Liscor.
Reiss tells Rags that Velan did not clear the High Passes but hid his treasure there, locked away with a key.
Reiss says that he and Garen belonged to the Ghostly Hand tribe, whose Chieftain remembered Velan's last months.
Velan led five thousand Goblin elite Hobs, as strong as Gold-rank adventurers and some as tall as half-Giants, against Terandrian ships landing over two hundred thousand troops.
Velan surrounded an Antinium Hive, wiped out the surface Antinium and killed its Queen himself, after which the Antinium stopped attacking his armies and pulled back to defend their remaining Hives.
In Tremborag's throne room Velan asks Tremborag to join him, accepts his refusal, and tells him the war has no purpose but vengeance against everything.
In that scene Velan shows Tremborag two ordinary-looking steel keys and says there will one day be a King again who follows in his footsteps.
Velan tells Tremborag to live.

Velan charged alone at the Archmages' mage detachment through the spells of three Archmages until a Silver-rank half-Elf adventurer, Elia Arcsinger, loosed an arrow with [Piercing Shot] through his eye and killed him instantly.
Vell is a sharp-tongued, yellow-scaled female Drake [Captain] in 4th Company under Wing Commander Embria.
Vell's squad includes Lieutenant Kesa, a Gnoll who is her subordinate.
Embria threatens to feed unprepared soldiers to Captain Vell for breakfast.
Vell carries a pouch of fried green beans that she uses as a natural wake-up supplement when the tea runs out.
Vell says she bought the beans in the other Oteslia, not the Walled City, and fried them to get rid of mold spots as they began to rot.
Vell says only her own squad gets to share her belongings and tells Pielt he should have bought his at Oteslia.
Vell mocks Pielt's romantic attempts and laughs at Wikir's jokes about spiders.
Vell tells Embria that her squad fears being stuck in Liscor for another month with no action.
Vell openly nods in agreement when Embria says Lism is not the right candidate.
Vell mutters "Yet" when Embria insists that the Antinium have no magic or Skills, which frightens Embria more than anything else.
Venaz is a Minotaur [Strategist] who studies at the Titan of Baleros' school, in the Titan's private class.
Venaz is the tallest member of his class, and only Marian comes close to his height.
Venaz says he is no [Warrior] but a [Strategist], and a [Strategist] to the core with only a few levels in anything else.
Venaz says he won the competition among everyone in the House of Minos under thirty years old for the honor of learning from the Titan.
Venaz says he beat a Level 28 [Armored Veteran] in a duel with bared swords to win that place.
Venaz says that he beat the [Prince] to earn a place with the mercenary forces of Minos.
Venaz says Minos was too safe for him, and that being a [Strategist] is his ticket to joining the mercenary forces.
Venaz speaks for Hammerad, and charges into battle shouting for the honor of Hammerad.
Venaz offers the Runner Luan a job in a tattooist's shop, saying he used an artifact so that no one noticed him come in.
Venaz says those watching him will not report the meeting, and that Luan will go out the back after they are done.
Venaz offers twenty gold to deliver a small object to him alone in a port city north of the city, and warns Luan may be roughed up if caught.
Luan raises the price to sixty gold after Venaz insults him, and Venaz agrees to ten up front and fifty on delivery.
Venaz shrugs off Luan's punch, which feels like hitting a mildly rubbery rock, and grins.
Niers says Venaz has not read the signs and thinks the coming game will be a little event.
Luan tells the Bushrangers that Venaz hired him for a delivery three weeks away and that the worst case is being lightly beaten and held for a day.
Luan says he checked and learned Venaz is a student of the Titan of Baleros.
Venaz shows a Mossbear pelt to a teacher and says his team eliminated it and two others.
Venaz says he contracted the Silver-rank team Thunri Dwarves to deal with a trio of Mossbears.
Venaz argues that his strategy was sound and says he could block one volley with his [Arrowguard Formation] Skill.
Venaz favours a lead-from-the-front philosophy and argues with the Professor about it.
The Professor forbids Venaz from fighting in training matches, and Venaz says he crushes opponents with his mind.
Venaz tosses Luan over his shoulder and flees dock soldiers, and Luan and Venaz end up in a communal septic tank.
Venaz is found wearing armor, and gives Umina anti-scrying and confusion ward talismans of Drath make.
Venaz casts painted paper beasts against Dullahans, saying the House of Minos and the Drath Archipelago fight with more than spells.
Venaz uses [Unit: Enhanced Strength] and [Unit: Unstoppable Advance] in the final battle, with a dozen Knights of the Summer behind him.
Venaz claims he found his own way to the end and will be the one to finish the game, which Feshi mocks.
Niers praises Venaz for reaching the end of the game unscathed, and gives him a reward.
Venaz credits what he learned to the City Runner he hired and listening to sound advice from anywhere.
Niers assigns Venaz to accompany General Felk, an expert in urban warfare, when Felk returns to duty in a month.
Venaz asks whether Armor Captain Shailt is recovering.
Niers tells Venaz he paid a [Swindler] and that his company marched out with nothing, and his soldiers deserted.
Venaz says he thought he was buying directly from the source, and that the certificate tested positive at the Merchant's Guild.
Niers tells Venaz the certificate was fake, and that the guild's [Receptionist] was either blindsided or bought off.
Venaz proposes a treasure hunt, saying three ships that sank in the last millennium bore relic-class artifacts that were never recovered.
Venaz says Peki speaks of Pomle, while Peki says Pomle has no [Kings].
Wil tosses Venaz a green diamond greatsword, and Venaz fights as fast as if under a [Haste] spell.
Fetohep names that sword the Windblade of Serpisel.
Fetohep says Wil and his comrades shall possess the blades until they die, and wants the rest of his swords returned.
Venaz and Peki volunteer to stall pursuers while fog and Gnoll horsemen arrive, nearly two thousand strong.
Venaz tells Wil he is doing calculated stupidity, and says he will meet him at the City of Growth.
Venaz watches a scrying orb of Minotaurs invading and says he knew about it, though he did not expect them yet.
Venaz tells Peki and Feshi that Minotaurs attacked Flos first, saying their King decreed it.
A cure for Yerra needs an alchemist such as Xif the Multicolored or Saliss of Lights.
Venaz receives a letter from a member of the House of Minos and calls himself needed as a representative of Hammerad and an arbiter.
Venaz says the letter from Calruz of Hammerad means he may need to go to Pallass, and that Calruz wants him to help him die.
Venaz ran three laps around Oteslia, shouting and challenging people to spars, after the battle.
Venim is a Drake Watch Captain of Pallass's City Watch.
Venim is Erin's appointed liaison, as is Sergeant Kel, and is assigned to the 8th floor every day.
Venim has two days off a week, one of which is spent with his daughter, who is allergic to grapes.
Venim tends to have a bad day whenever he meets Erin.
Venim and Zevara say the three Watch Captains of Pallass agree that a trade war or war with Liscor is unacceptable.
Watch Captains of the two cities keep in touch and sometimes bypass the chain of command, and they will deny meeting Erin.
Venim says a war with Liscor is not in Pallass's interests and that the door could be more dangerous to hold than not.
Venim says Erin's earlier paperwork authorises her portal and inn as a legal residence in Pallass, and that clerks signed approvals by accident.
Venim says the permit fees are twenty gold for both leases and six gold for inspecting a premise with monsters and magical artifacts.
Venim expects a [Message] spell from Erin by way of Liscor within the week.
Venim says he can tell the Assembly of Crafts that a Gold-rank team present most of the time will deter anyone from taking the door.
Venim stands at the Pallass end of the door, which now opens onto a side street instead of an alleyway.
Venim sits in his office with Selys and takes her statement after the thugs who kidnapped her are captured.
Venim tells Selys that Zevara has requested her immediate return to Liscor.
Venim tells Erin that any Goblin entering Pallass will be killed under standing Pallassian law.
Venim says the law must be incorruptible but thanks Erin for her part in keeping Liscor standing.
Venim tells Nevvim and Kel to leave Erin alone, since Pallass and Liscor owe her a debt.
Venim threatens to close the door over the Antinium, and Erin shames him by calling him a scaredy cat.
Erin grabs Venim's armor collar through the door and tells him Antinium are Liscor citizens until they break the law.
Venim tells Erin that Skill-forced sales are legal in Pallass, since the buyer cannot be forced to name a price.
Venim objects that Erin cannot change the checkpoint without permission because it is sovereign Pallassian territory.
Venim says he would have granted Erin's request by day's end had it come through Sergeant Kel the next day.
Venith Crusland is a [Lord] and a vassal of Flos who once rode with him as a companion.
Venith wears light silver chainmail and carries a shield on his back and a sword at his side.
Venith has dark, brownish hair and a stern, set face.
Venith's wife Maresar is a former [Bandit Lord], and his only son is Calac.
Venith's Skill [Flawless Defence] makes him nearly invincible when defending, as Flos acknowledges.
Venith fights with a shield and a sword kept close to his body, making quick, precise cuts.
Venith says he has not put down his sword for twenty years, unlike Flos.
Venith is so high-level that civilians armed with knives, clubs or stones cannot harm him.
Venith says he was a [Warrior] before becoming a [Lord], and that he is now a [Lord of Battle], which he calls hardly a unique class.
Venith says he could barely hold back Flos when Flos held a poor steel sword, and would last under half a dozen blows against Orthenon, Mars or Gazi.
In a flashback, a young Venith attacks Flos, who has eight thousand gold on his head dead and twice that alive, and lies beaten after five minutes.
Flos lets Venith take his mare and leave, telling him to come back when he has a better reason for fighting.
Venith wrote to Flos the day Calac was born, and Flos drank to the boy's health.
In another flashback, Venith strikes the slumped Flos in the throne room when Flos says he is finished as King after Queravia and Tottenval die.
Venith swore an oath to take arms against Flos should he ever wake from his slumber.
Venith says he swore an oath to save and protect his people, because Flos abandoned his kingdom while every army cut them down.
Venith claims Flos broke his own oath long ago, and says he owes him nothing.
Calac says Venith told him all his life that Flos was a fool, an oathbreaker and a coward who abandoned his kingdom.
Venith rides into the village of Manimar with an army and tells Flos he has come for his head.
Venith has ruled the villagers of Manimar as their [Lord] for twenty years, and angrily insists they are his subjects, not Flos's.
Venith duels Flos and is forced to rely on his shield as Flos proves stronger.
Venith strikes Flos in the face when Flos offers him a hand, saying he has not forgotten the day Flos turned his back on him.
Venith's wife Maresar tells him she is taking half their retainers to serve Flos, since Flos is her King too.
Venith rides away from Manimar after the duel, every inch of his body hurting.
A messenger from Hellios tells Venith the coalition plans to ambush Flos, and that his oath only requires him to stand aside.
Venith calls the ambush plan dishonorable and the act of a coward, saying Hellios should besiege Flos's capital instead.
The messenger says the coalition would crush Flos and burn Reim if the ambush fails, and that killing Flos first would save lives.
Venith knows the ambush force waits in the foothills west of Reim for Flos to ride out to save refugees attacked by raiders.
Venith's own patrols had clashed with the Hellios party, which had not covered its tracks well.
Venith lets the Hellios party of eighteen go, bound by his oath and the hurt of his wife leaving.
Calac confronts Venith for hiding behind oaths, and Venith concedes dishonorable acts have no excuse yet cannot say why he does not stop the Hellios men.
Calac leaves Venith's keep to ride to Flos, and Venith rides after him with his retainers.
Venith charges the army pursuing Orthenon's forces four miles from Reim, shouting in Flos's name and laughing as he fights.
Venith returns to Flos's side: at the gates Flos embraces him and calls him his vassal.
Venith stands with Maresar beside him, shield and sword raised, after Flos embraces him.
Venith and Maresar are assigned to Ger by Orthenon a month earlier, when its citizens would not tolerate Flos's armies.
Venith keeps order in Ger with Maresar's bow covering half the city from the Seat of Ger.
Venith dislikes Orthenon, though the King's Steward has his grudging respect.
Calac stays in Reim with Orthenon, because Venith refused to let him come after his previous failure.
Later, Flos leaves Venith in charge of managing Hellios, Reim and Germina in his absence, taking Orthenon and Mars with him.
Trey judges Venith unflappably loyal once he returned to his King, and not like the formal Orthenon.
Venith says Orthenon dislikes Maresar because she was a [Bandit Lord] and Orthenon hates criminals.
Venith brings five thousand of Reim's soldiers to Khelt's border and tries to cross it in search of Trey.
Venitra is a servant of the Necromancer Az'kerash, a woman with pale skin and green eyes who reports to him in his castle.
Venitra feels fulfilled whenever she speaks to her creator and feels his attention on her, and she dreads failing him.
Venitra was taught to mimic the gestures of the living, though she was never alive.
Venitra was designed by Az'kerash personally and created from nothing by his mind, unlike Kerash and Bea, who were not made that way.
Venitra is unique among Az'kerash's servants because she serves him and receives his commands in person.
Venitra is the first-born of Az'kerash's creations and his loyal servant.
Venitra is an undead knight whose skin, face and armor are all white bone, with a great sword of bone.
When Ryoka first meets her, Venitra's eyes glow silver with rage.
Venitra's body is an armored frame of bone that any Dullahan would envy, woven with spells crafted by her master.
Venitra's face is a perfect carved face of white bone, and when she is unmasked her eyes burn green.
Seen up close in the alley, Venitra's eyes are burning yellow flames set in her sockets, and she is as perfect as a sculpture.
Venitra's voice is deep and beautiful, and Ryoka judges that she was manufactured to be perfect both as a weapon and as a work of art.
Venitra can cast the spell [Mists of Madness], an enchantment her master built into her, which makes those caught in the cloud go insane.
Venitra's sword and shield are enchanted bone, and her body is warded against lesser spells and attacks.
In battle Venitra's mind is cool and calculating, and she thinks with perfect clarity amid spells and arrows.
Venitra believes she was enchanted to withstand spells from Named Adventurers, and that Halrac's arrows cannot injure her bone body.
Venitra reports to Az'kerash that another being has breached the outer web of his castle.
Venitra describes the intruder to Az'kerash as a human female, six feet tall, with black hair, an athletic build and highly magical equipment.
Venitra does not mention the Frost Sprites her watchers saw around Ryoka, because her master long ago insisted they were unimportant.
Venitra blocks Ryoka in a dark corridor of the castle, with a group of altered skeletons behind her.
Venitra's skeleton troops have far too many ribs and redesigned frames that make them look like walking tanks.
Ryoka's flour dust explosion goes off around Venitra, who strides out of the smoke unharmed.
After Az'kerash lets Ryoka go, voices identifiable as Venitra, Kerash and Bea discuss it; one says his decision may be in error, and another says he never errs.
The same three agree they should hold Ryoka until their master is finished.
Venitra stands in the castle watching as Az'kerash's great flesh-and-bone creation finishes forming overhead.

section: Book 3 to 5: the hunt for Ryoka
text: Venitra and her companion Ijvani, sent by Az'kerash, walk through the snow for three days to find the Courier, the Runner.

section: Book 3 to 5: the hunt for Ryoka
text: Venitra and Ijvani are roughly seventy miles off course and heading the wrong way toward Liscor.

section: Book 3 to 5: the hunt for Ryoka
text: Goblins of the Goblin Lord's army ambush Venitra and Ijvani when they ask to speak with him, and Venitra butchers them.

section: Book 3 to 5: the hunt for Ryoka
text: Venitra will not attack Goblins who do not attack her, because it would run counter to her master's plans.

section: Book 3 to 5: the hunt for Ryoka
text: Venitra regards the Goblin Lord as an ally of sorts, and his eyes comfort her because they remind her of Az'kerash.

section: Book 3 to 5: the hunt for Ryoka
text: Venitra tells the Goblin Lord that she and Ijvani are headed toward Liscor.

section: Book 3 to 5: the hunt for Ryoka
text: Venitra warns the Goblin Lord that two Drake armies, each about ten thousand strong, are closing in on his position.

section: Book 3 to 5: the hunt for Ryoka
text: Venitra had seen the two armies as she and Ijvani passed them undetected.

section: Book 3 to 5: the hunt for Ryoka
text: Venitra and Ijvani set off for Liscor to find the accursed Human named Ryoka Griffin.

section: Book 3 to 5: the hunt for Ryoka
text: Ijvani tells Venitra "I told you we were going the wrong way," and Venitra tells her to be silent.

section: Book 3 to 5: the hunt for Ryoka
text: Venitra and Ijvani reach the walls of a city wearing a travelling cloak that hides Venitra's bone body.

section: Book 3 to 5: the hunt for Ryoka
text: Using a bloody map taken from a corpse they slaughtered on the road, Ijvani works out that the city is Esthelm, not Liscor.

section: Book 3 to 5: the hunt for Ryoka
text: Ijvani says the mountain they climbed was a mistake, and Venitra sighs when she points the way to Liscor.
The Gnoll Regrika Blackpaw, a Named Adventurer and [Champion] in golden plate with a black-furred body, arrives in Liscor to fanfare from the city's Gnolls.
Regrika arrives with a slight young Drake [Mage] with dark purple scales.
Regrika asks the Liscor Council for a scout to learn about the Goblin Lord's army, and Olesm tells her about Erin's door to Celum.
Olesm recommends Ryoka Griffin to Regrika as a Runner who ran the High Passes alone, and Regrika says she would like to meet her.
Adventurers in Liscor say Regrika is nicknamed "Fortress Blackpaw" because no one can lay a scratch on her.
Regrika's presence crushes the spirits of the non-Gnoll adventurers in Liscor just by walking down the street.
In an alley Regrika twists a ring on her paw and the Gnoll form vanishes, revealing Venitra's bone body and burning green eyes.
Venitra seizes Ryoka by the throat, lifts her, says she has searched long for her, and promises that Ryoka will die.
Venitra tells Ryoka that she has trespassed and that she and everyone she loves will pay the price.
Venitra, speaking as Regrika, reminds Ryoka that she delivered a letter to the Necromancer a month earlier, running through a battlefield and his castle.
Venitra tears Ryoka's belt pouch away and drops it while choking her.
Venitra snaps Ryoka's left pinkie and later breaks the same finger a second time in a different place.
Ijvani silences Ryoka with a spell while Venitra breaks her finger.
Venitra tells Ijvani she was told to pick her tracker, and that Ijvani came because she chose her.
Ijvani says she and Oom are the eldest of Az'kerash's creations and that Venitra is the youngest.
Ijvani adds that Venitra lacks experience, and Venitra answers that she is his favorite.
Venitra throws Ryoka into a wall.
When Relc shouts from the alley, Venitra and Ijvani instantly shift into Regrika Blackpaw and the Drake [Mage] Imenet Southwing.
Regrika tells Relc she was seeking Ryoka's aid and introduces her companion as Imenet Southwing.
Venitra's illusion is sophisticated enough to fool a Gnoll's nose, though she hates having to laugh, speak and eat while wearing it.
Venitra can hear and see everything Ryoka says and does at the Gnoll party, through a spell cast by Ijvani.
Az'kerash loses two games of chess to Erin Solstice, and Venitra, shaken that her master lost, breaks inside.
Venitra drops the Regrika form in an alley, breaks Brunkr's neck, and kills him, then beats his body in a silent rage.
Venitra tells Ijvani that no one disgraces their master, and Ijvani offers to clean up the body.
Ijvani complains that Venitra has a temper and wonders why she is the master's favorite.
Az'kerash scolds Venitra for ignoring his order not to harm Ryoka, though he forgives it because the failure gave him useful information.
Az'kerash orders Venitra and Ijvani to observe, keep their identities hidden, not harm Ryoka, and learn about the inn and its door.
Venitra, still disguised as Regrika, tells Az'kerash that Ryoka has delivered to the High Passes and to Magnolia Reinhart.
Venitra reports that Ryoka recently travelled to Invrisil in a magical carriage sent by the Reinhart family.
Venitra relays rumours about Erin: a magical chessboard, the best chess player, a magical door, and a victory over the Flesh Worm Skinner.
Venitra adds rumours that the Antinium call Erin a friend, her dishes grant temporary enchantments, she once had a skeleton servant and she makes wondrous music.
Venitra also repeats a crude false rumour about Erin that makes Az'kerash react in confusion.
Regrika fights the Gold-rank adventurers in The Wandering Inn, and Seborn's knives, Jelaqua's flail, Halrac's arrows and Typhenous's spells all fail to hurt her.
Halrac's [Piercing Shot] pierces Regrika's armor and buries itself halfway into her chest, leaving a bloodless wound.
Halrac's second, explosive arrow cracks Regrika's armor.
Regrika tells Erin she was sent by her master for one reason, to kill Ryoka Griffin.
Regrika shoves Erin aside, pries her hand from her leg, and steps through the door to Celum.
Venitra smashes through the window of Octavia's alchemy shop in Celum, and bystanders raise the alarm at her bloody sword.
Venitra finds Ryoka at the Frenzied Hare in Celum with the Horns of Hammerad.
Venitra casts [Mists of Madness], which engulfs the inn and spills into the street, driving the people there and arriving [Guardsmen] insane.
Venitra bends back and tears off a pinkie from Ryoka's right hand, but Ryoka laughs and the figure vanishes into something blue and indistinct.
Az'kerash tells Venitra there is nothing in her grip, and he loses his temper.
The Ryoka Venitra seized in Celum was a decoy, and Az'kerash's scrying spell, which pointed to the Winter Sprite, was misled.
Venitra enters a cave in pursuit of Ryoka and meets a Dragon, who throws her against a mountain, cracking her body.
The Dragon's fire blackens and cracks Venitra's bone, and she screams for her master.
Az'kerash tells the burnt, damaged Venitra that she has failed him and lost his favor, and is no longer first among his servants.
Az'kerash gives his authority to Kerash in front of the assembled servants.
Az'kerash names Teriarch's fury as the cause of his lost resources.
After the murders, people in Liscor call Regrika Blackpaw a traitor who killed Brunkr and then a Gold-rank adventurer in Erin's inn.
Zel Shivertail finds, through a [Message] spell, no record of Regrika Blackpaw ever being born to the Blackpaw tribe.
Zel notices a pattern of deaths or accidents following Regrika's travels.
An investigation traces Regrika's visits across six years and finds that half the cities she visited lost a notable person under dubious circumstances.
Ilvriss learns that the fake Named Adventurer Regrika Blackpaw, whom Erin revealed as the murderer of Brunkr and then Ulrien of Griffon Hunt, is an undead servant of Az'kerash.
Venitra asks Az'kerash whether he gathered his servants to teach them about sex, because Bea asked him about it the day before.
Az'kerash replies that the gathering is not for that purpose, and Venitra bows her head and apologises.
Viceria Strongheart is Garia's mother and Wailant's wife, a slim, elegant [Mage] with a light brown braid.
Viceria looks about ten years younger than her real age, which Garia says is in her thirties.
Viceria is a Wistram graduate and a [Green Mage], an expert in plant magic, not a [Geomancer] or [Druid].
Viceria chose farming over competing at Wistram, where disciplines involving growing earned little respect.
Viceria's spells grow crops faster than normal, as well as a Skill would, according to Wailant.
Viceria says classes change appearance: [Mages] tend to be thin and look young, while [Farmers] grow larger.
Viceria says Garia inherited her father's build and that Garia's first class was [Farmer], not [Mage].
Viceria met Wailant when he saved her from Carn Wolves in the Blood Fields, killing two after her escort died.
Viceria says the second monster she met outside Wistram nearly killed her, and that she is far better at combat now.
Viceria questions Ryoka about her Frost Faerie friend and how she gets contracts for hundreds of gold.
Viceria says Ryoka looks like the girls who bullied Garia, and that Wailant fears Ryoka is taking advantage of Garia.
Viceria tells Wailant that people are right about Rhir being the Blighted Kingdom.
Viceria is affiliated, at a distance, with Palt's Ullsinoi faction, supplying what they need as a [Green Mage].
Viceria grows dreamleaf and offers to sell Erin some as a gift for her husband's behavior.
Viceria plants Sage's Grass in Erin's garden while Wailant works too.
Viceria and Wailant give Erin an old bag of holding and a basket of about a dozen huge Bullhen eggs.
Viltach is a Human Archmage of Wistram, described as the Archmage of nobility in Terandria.
Viltach is described as one of two of the five Archmages currently controlling Wistram, and is Human.
Viltach visits Amerys with Feor and Nailihuaile, and Amerys greets the three Archmages as having come back.
Viltach lacks Amerys's intensity in his gaze, as the three Archmages stop before her magical barrier.
Viltach is delighted when A'ctelios claims its leader was assassinated by Gazi Pathseeker and the Quarass of Germina, since he had always known Flos could not keep his oath.
Viltach tells Mage Rievan Forstrom to send a [Message] to the Drake commentators, and summons Feor and Nailihuaile to meet him at once.
Viltach expects that once Flos is forsworn, Reim will die, and that this moment will be broadcast worldwide by Wistram Academy.
Viltach reports that Niers Astoragon, the heads of the Four Great Companies and others have found out Wistram is watching, with word spreading from ruler to ruler.
Viltach says Wistram is denying the allegations but paying a political cost, and that he has been smoothing feathers in Terandria.
Viltach consults the numbers of how many people are watching a broadcast and dislikes Elena's uppity tone.
Viltach murmurs that perhaps Wistram wants the people pacified and that they do not need to know the truth.
Viltach's murmur is a bit too loud: the crowd of Earthers quiets, Elena looks appalled and Feor scowls at him.
Viltach and Nailihuaile, ordered by Feor to be silent, analyze the Sword Prognugators' combat as ranking them high-silver on talent and Gold with artifacts.
Viltach joins Feor and Nailihuaile on a high balcony as the Emerald Signet struggles toward the Isle of Mages through a magical typhoon.
Viltach, Feor and Nailihuaile link their wand and relic to stretch the Weatherward south, because the ship carries two children from another world.
Viltach howls at Feor to stop pulling the Weatherward in too close, as the protection spell retreats toward the isle.
The linked Archmages extend the Weatherward into a corridor of safety nearly three miles southwards, and the Emerald Signet sails in.
Viri is a small, multicoloured Lizardman of Commander Uxel's company, armed only with a staff strapped to his back.
Viri's class is [Longstick Jumper], and he vaults along the ground and walls with his pole.
Viri calls himself one of the best [Scouts] and offers to jump ahead of the army to the 5th Wall.
Viri has an ingratiating way about him.
Viri greets Cirille's Drakes cheerfully as fellow scale-folk and is surprised that Izrilian Drakes hate Lizardfolk.
Viri explains that he is not the commander, who is napping, and demonstrates a pole vault of about twenty feet.
Viri invites Cirille to meet Uxel and says she will get to play cards that night.
Viri talks his way into the nightly officers' card games even though he is not really an officer, and drinks only goat's milk.
Viri leads a wing of Uxel's Lizardfolk skirmishers who catch Merish's group and wipe it out in a practice exercise.
Uxel offers Cirille Viri and a [Mage] division, saying he wants to see what Drake spears do.
Cirille patrols with Viri and other [Scouts] hunting for Demons.
Viri leaps onto the wall to tell the officers that Delezza is dying.
Viri acts as a messenger to Cirille during the Demon assault, hopping across the wall with his staff.
Viri warns Cirille from the walls of a second wave of Demon soldiers.
Viri flies high into the Harpies, using a Demon as a foothold and lashing out with his staff.
Uxel fights towards where Viri has fallen.
Viri is found alive with one leg severed, among the survivors lying on the ground.
Viri hops after the ghost of Uxel using his staff as a cane, and Uxel tells him to stay there.
Visma is a young Drake girl with pearly-white scales speckled with greens, the daughter of the [Painter] Selena.
Visma is shy and timid, and likes copying her mother by making sculptures out of mud or things she finds.
Visma became friends with Mrsha when she asked to paint Mrsha, whose lovely fur she likened to a canvas.
Visma is in her hoarding year, according to Selena.
Visma has an older brother, Feiss, a young Drake of around fourteen who is a [Fletcher]'s apprentice.
Visma grabs Ekirra's new ball, declares it hers, and punches him in the nose when he demands it back, then runs off with it.
Selena shouts at her daughter, and Visma realizes she is in trouble and flees.
Visma grabs one of Selys's silk dresses and puts a scrying orb in it, hugging it to her, so that her brother tries to scold her.
Mrsha knows Visma is getting better about hoarding.
Visma, Ekirra and Mrsha overhear Erin cursing mildly, and Visma covers her ears with her claws while Mrsha covers Ekirra's.
Visma shouts that she hates Mrsha and arrives with a bloody nostril after Mrsha hits her for pulling Apista's wings.
Visma refuses Mrsha's apology until she sees how sad Mrsha is, then cries, and the two make up with a nuzzle and chocolate.
Visma comes to breakfast at the inn with Ekirra, brought by her older brother, and meets Ryoka.
Visma says oh when Erin introduces Ryoka as Mrsha's Aunt, ignorant of the consternation she causes among the adults.
Wailant Strongheart is Garia's father, a [Farmer] near Celum and a retired [Pirate], married to Viceria.
Wailant has black hair, green eyes, stubble and a circular scar on his jaw.
Wailant has scarred, tattooed arms, including a tentacle gripping a ship and a fanged fish that seems to swim.
Wailant wears a sleeveless light blue shirt gilded with a golden wave edge.
Wailant carries an enchanted cutlass looted from plunder, with a wand in his off-hand.
Garia says Wailant coats his cutlass with a paralysis poison.
Wailant first claims to have been a [Sailor], then admits to Garia and Viceria that he was a [Pirate].
Wailant was a Level 27 [Pirate] from a Baleros family and sailed to all five continents.
Wailant's father died at sea before he was born, and his mother died in a battle when he was five.
Wailant retired as wealthy as a Gold-rank adventurer, and spent most of it clearing the bounty on his head.
Wailant bought a farm far inland, tired of water and wary of enemies, and struggled for the first years.
Wailant got a savage scar from killing a Creler.
Wailant claims he could have become a [Storm Sailor] or [Captain], and Garia and Viceria roll their eyes at the embellished story.
Wailant calls Winter Sprites devils and recalls a farmer who lost his harvest under eight feet of snow.
Wailant approves only of Mrsha and Garia and gives Ryoka and Fals the third degree.
Wailant and Ryoka spar after dinner, and Ryoka's kick sobers him up.
Wailant farms Sage's Grass and says he rotates other crops when bored.
Wailant shoves a nervous [Trader] who refuses his Sage's Grass during the trade war and vows never to deal with him again.
Wailant kicks Numbtongue after a [Dirty Feint], slaps Merchant Geala and knocks out a [Lieutenant].
Wailant hides Numbtongue in his wagon, shares his flask and learns his name.
Wailant tells Numbtongue that Garia is his daughter.
Wailant is banned from Celum for a year.
Wailant explains he slapped a [Merchant] who hired mercenaries to threaten him, and Viceria worries about losing clients.
Wailant says he has met Goblins at sea and that Demons of Rhir are just a folk, though Viceria disagrees.
Wailant says Wistram set up the A'ctelios people to trap the King of Destruction and calls Drowned Men not proper [Pirates].
Wailant proposes planting Sage's Grass around the inn to generate mana, which Palt and the Wistram mages had not thought of.
Wailant offers to sell Erin a field of Sage's Grass at a small discount if he may sell to Invrisil direct.
Wailant replants Sage's Grass in Erin's garden, uprooting part of the meadow.
Wailant gets drunk and tries to fight Seborn over a jest about [Pirates], and Moore, Halrac and Yvlon hold him back.
Wailant and Teliv each push offers to Erin for Celum's farms, and Erin writes "no thanks" on Liscor's contract.
Wailant and Seborn call the [Clear Skies] casters idiots because suppressing storms makes them worse later.
Wailant's Sage's Grass is almost ready after eight months, and he grows a Goudolep and invisible pumpkins.
Wailant says Imani's trauma is best treated by distance from Crelers, [Thought Healers], or a [Mage] or [Shaman].
Wailant says he met Crelers at sea twice and would like to forget it.
Wall Lord Zail is Ilvriss' father; he is a very old Drake, eighty-three years of age.
Zail Gemscale is the father of Ilvriss and the husband of Helessia Gemscale, and the family of four is split between father and son on one side and mother and daughter Navine on the other.
Zail is retired and bored; he complains that a Gnoll is managing everything now and that he never should have quit managing the mines.
Zail drifts between sharp attention and confusion, though an old Drake still keeps all his levels and Skills.
Zail has a scar on his chest where lightning struck him and a slight indentation along his skull where the scales are almost gone, and the text says he sacrificed much for the city he loved.
Zail keeps his quarters at the peak of the tower, right above Ilvriss' quarters, and has slipped his attendants to visit his son.
Zail dislikes the diet his [Healers] prescribe and says they want him to live forever.
Zail's wife Helessia lives in a separate tower, which spares her from constantly running into him.

section: Book 13: the ring and the oath
text: Zail asks whether his new tower is finished, and Ilvriss walks him to a window to see it, a tower that Gemscale funds helped build.

section: Book 13: the ring and the oath
text: Zail says that when he dies his ashes should be scattered from the tower, and Ilvriss answers that he knows.

section: Book 13: the ring and the oath
text: Zail notices that Ilvriss no longer wears the ring Zail gave him, and demands to know whom he is marrying.

section: Book 13: the ring and the oath
text: Zail says he knows exactly what the ring means, since he gave it to Ilvriss, and that it stands for trust.

section: Book 13: the ring and the oath
text: Zail repeats rumours that Ilvriss left his duty to play in a border city, lost his head, or fled the Goblin Lord out of cowardice, and asks where Ilvriss was when General Shivertail died.

section: Book 13: the ring and the oath
text: Zail twists a ring that casts a truth spell and makes Ilvriss swear his loyalty to Salazsar.

section: Book 13: the ring and the oath
text: The truth stone glows blue at Ilvriss' oath, and Zail relaxes and repeats the oath's final line.

section: Book 13: the ring and the oath
text: Zail later asks when Ilvriss will bring home a wife worthy of their line, and while the truth stone still shines on Zail's claw Ilvriss answers that there was one but he could not even bury her.
Zail wears his sword in its scabbard and watches a scrying orb replay the Wyvern attack on Pallass; he is paler than usual and his claws shake.
Zail had fought in wars before and commanded during the two Antinium Wars, though his health is gone.
Zail recoils from the sight of Bird on the scrying orb and asks what madness lets an Antinium stand on a wall, even in Pallass.
Zail says that Drakes killed an Antinium called the Slayer and others, and Ilvriss supplies the name Devrkr the Glowing.
Zail says he saw Devrkr die and that they had to kill it again and again because it kept coming back.
Zail counts three of the Antinium already and now four, and warns Ilvriss not to underestimate Bird.
Zail wears a ring that casts a more powerful [Truth] spell, and Ilvriss speaks carefully near him.
Ilvriss asks Zail for permission to withdraw heirlooms from Salazsar's treasuries; Zail hesitates over the artifacts, then agrees and says he will get the key.
Zail's family holds the mining company run by Alrric, and Alrric tells him it makes excellent profits, better since Ilvriss' return.
Zail answers that the company had better be profitable since his son has placed trust in Alrric, and by 'you' he means Gnolls, glaring as if Ilvriss had been overly generous.
Zail comes to inspect the company leaning on a cane after sneaking out without his minders, whom Alrric had already alerted.
Zail is escorted back by two Drakes sent by Ilvriss, and immediately demands to see the new task force.
Winta is a River Warden of Jecrass, one of the nobles who control the rivers that make the kingdom rich in horses.
Winta is a woman who fights with a wand and leads elite troops for King Raelt.
Winta dabs at her forehead in the court as Geril reads Flos's letter demanding that his people be released.
Winta argues that the King of Destruction's oath means nothing needs to be feared, since all of Chandrar would fall on him if he invaded.
Winta suggests that Jecrass's fast cavalry could harass Reim's armies by raiding their supply lines.
Winta squeaks and turns dead white when Raelt receives a missive that Flos is flying his banner at the border.
Winta starts as the army of Reim approaches and the rumble of its footsteps carries a layer of sound.
Winta tells Raelt that no one would begrudge him bringing poison or any weapon to his duel with the King of Destruction, and Raelt answers that he would begrudge it.
Winta bows to Raelt as he leaves his tent for the battle, with worry in her eyes, and tells him Jecaina is in the capital tending to the people.
Raelt tells Winta she does not have to ride into battle, and she answers that she knows.
Winta leads elite troops on the right with Sekirst, while Emile leads on the left.
Winta uses [Step of Light] with her wand to clear the way for the Trick Riders.
Winta blasts a Death Soldier off his horse and knocks back Flos's bodyguards with another spell from her wand.
Winta shouts that the King of Destruction is dead after Raelt's rapier pierces Flos's heart, and orders a Trick Rider to pull Raelt back.
Winta rides at Flos's body and is run through with Raelt's rapier when Flos pulls it from his heart.
Raelt later counts Winta among the dead, and thinks of her death when he decides to sue for peace.
Welca Caveis is a young Knight of the Petal with black hair, and a junior [Knight].
Welca comes from a larger noble house than Sir Kerrig, though he is her senior in the order.
The Knights of the Petal admit no one below Level 20, the prerequisite for the [Knight] class.
Welca had been dueled by Pyrite and nearly drowned in battle before her capture.
Welca and Sir Kerrig are captured by the Flooded Waters tribe after trees are dropped on them.
Welca rages at her Goblin guards, fears for her chastity and honor, and demands to be killed.
Rags forbids any abuse of her prisoners, and the Goblins only want to give Welca food and clothing.
Welca tries to flee after Pyrite nods her back to her wagon, and he knocks her out gently.
Welca insists the Goblins are monsters who will always be Humanity's enemy, even if they can speak.
Welca escapes the Goblin camp on a horse at Sir Kerrig's order, promising to return.
Lady Bethal believes Welca and Sir Kerrig perished until Rags says both are prisoners.
Welca rides with Lord Pellmia's cavalry and tells him she cannot see Sir Kerrig among the Goblin army.
Lord Pellmia leads a charge using [Second Wind] alongside Welca.
Welca had informed Lord Veltras of the Goblin tribe.
Welca has been searching for her missing companion Sir Kerrig, and Tyrion tells her he was safe in Riverfarm.
Welca is assigned to Lord Pellmia's command to help locate the Goblins.
Welca reports to Lady Bethal that the Runner's Guild confirmed the roses were all genuine.
Welsca Crimsonscale is an older red-scaled female Drake with a scar down one arm who serves Wall Lord Ilvriss.
Welsca is one of Ilvriss's personal adjutants and his best staff member for coordination.
Welsca enters Erin and Ryoka's private bath on orders from Ilvriss, despite their hostile faces.
Ryoka kicks Welsca, who slips on a wet tile, into a pool filled with Gnolls.
Welsca is a former field officer in Eartiv's army, recruited by Ilvriss twelve years earlier, and now a [Veteran Adjutant] above her old [Strategist] class.
Ilvriss gives Welsca work on Olesm's chess magazine copies, and she corrects Olesm's mistakes in a game.
Ilvriss says Welsca is a fan of the magazine though she would hardly admit it.
Welsca remarks on the commentary about the new game of Go that first appeared in Olesm's last issue.
Wesle Salkis was a competent, slightly resigned low-level [Guardsman] in Celum before becoming a confident [Actor] who leads the troupe of Celum's actors with his co-star Jasi.
Erin learns that Wesle's last name is Salkis, and everyone seems too shy to call him by his first name.
Wesle signs people's arms with a sticky, oil-based marker like charcoal that an [Alchemist] in the city made for the troupe.
He tells Erin that the Players of Celum, as they call themselves for now, owe her a huge debt and have taken on many new [Actors] and a warehouse to practise in.
Erin nicknames a Celum gate [Guardsman] "Fuzzylips", and his real name is Wesle.
He leads Erin through Celum's streets to Stitchworks, an [Alchemist]'s shop, after the earlier ambush.
Wesle is terrified of bugs, and he says merchants rarely travel far south because dealing with non-humans is unprofitable.
Wesle dates the loss of trade with the south to before the Second Antinium War, which he links to the Necromancer.
Wesle has a deep hatred of the Antinium, shared by most Humans.
Agnes says Erin visits Wesle practically every day.
Wesle says every city's [Guardsmen] have been working around the clock since Esthelm, trying to learn when and where the Goblins will attack.
A large map pinned to the City Watch barracks wall is dotted with colored pins centered on a red cross over Esthelm.
Wesle says he wanted to be an adventurer but is not a born fighter and is not brave enough to go searching for evil.
He says he would have liked to be a [Knight] who fought monsters and wielded a flaming sword, or one that cuts through steel.
Wesle and Jasi both insist that Celum is a good city, and Wesle looks upset when Erin doubts it.
Wesle plays Romeo opposite Jasi's Juliet in Erin's staged Romeo and Juliet, and their stage kiss looks close to genuine.
Erin thinks that, in the roles, Wesle the low-level [Guardsman] and Jasi the [Washer] become something larger than themselves.
Wesle and Jasi are the [Actors] with the highest levels, and they already have a handful of Skills.
A [Guardsman] with a fuzzy mustache plays Hamlet at the Frenzied Hare each night and is nearly dead on his feet afterward.
Other troupes imitate Romeo and Juliet and perform it in other cities, while Wesle's troupe stays at the Frenzied Hare.
Wesle and Jasi are the stars of the troupe, many of whose other members are from the Watch.
Wesle strokes his non-existent mustache when excited.
Wesle quits his job as a [Guardsman], saying he earns far more as an actor and likes it better.
He wants to form a troupe that goes from city to city to perform.
Wesle says the troupe's fame began about a month earlier, with requests to perform in other cities for the [Mayor].
He says it all started with a [Washer] and a [Guardsman] in an inn, and says the story could be a play.
For The Battle of Liscor, Wesle plays the Drake Wall Lord Ilvriss, who roars at the audience and the moths.
In the same play, Jasi plays Watch Captain Zevara, and Humans wear fake tails and painted scales to play Drakes.
Wesle has acquired an actor's mask.
Wesle returns to Erin's inn, hears of the battle against the Raskghar, and the Players decide to make it into a play.
Wesle is the lead [Actor] of the Players of Celum and one of the two original performers.
Erin nicknamed him 'Fuzzylips' for the thin mustache he has since shaved off.
He is a Level 26 [Method Actor], and he is a former [Watch Captain] of Celum.
Later, Wesle has passed Level 30, and his class is now [Famed Method Actor], a rare class; his Skill [Everyday Prop] lets him produce any everyday prop that vanishes after use.
Wesle has the Skill [Method Acting], which lets him copy a person's talent at a level a number of levels below his own.
He copies ten levels below himself for a familiar activity and fifteen or twenty levels below for magic.
He shadows high-level [Servers] to copy their talent for serving.
Wesle flicks his fingers and shoots about eight stinging sparks across a table, but gains no new spells.
He cannot copy a very high-level person unless he stays in character, and he says he can copy a Level 16 [Bladesman].
Wesle still wears the sword from his days in Celum's City Watch.
Wesle is among the Players of Celum who come to The Wandering Inn when riots cancel the evening's play.
Wikir is a Gnoll [Captain] of 4th Company, called First Captain and second-in-command to Wing Commander Embria.
Wikir is twenty years older than Embria and has dozens of scars hidden under his fur, and one of his ears is tattered.
Wikir fights with a mace, and the narration compares his turning head to the slow wrath of the mace, which is not slow in battle.
Wikir leads 1st Squad and is described as the oldest [Captain] in 4th Company.
Wikir served with Relc in 4th Company, according to Captain Pielt.
Embria spars with Wikir first each morning and then with two more of his [Captains] while the others practise.
Embria orders Wikir to take the squads out to practise and later leaves him in charge of parade marches on her day off.
Wikir commands the [Lieutenants] and [Sergeants] under his direct command and grins when Embria announces the Shield Spider culling.
Wikir tells Pielt his group will be picking baby spiders out of its ears unless it has a strong [Mage] like Wikir's own.
Wikir tells Embria that he does not run with the civilian Gnoll crowd and that they do not trust him.
Wikir says he knows Krshia, that she is smart and has authority, and that many Gnolls will follow when she howls.
Wikir asks a Sergeant whether having more Gnolls than Drakes on Liscor's Council would be a bad thing.
Wikir smashes a Shield Spider's head with his mace as 1st Squad drops into a nest while seven more members wait above.
Wikir orders the squad to kill the adult spiders and use torches, and the nest burns with its egg sacks.
Sergeant Gna helps Wikir out of the pit, and tiny Shield Spiders scuttle from his paw to her fur.
Wikir stomps back to the pit to shake off the baby spiders, as the squad's [Mage] adds to the flames.
Wikir says he went in himself so that Pielt could not call him a coward, and that other nests are burned from above as planned.
Wil Kallinad is a Terandrian [Lord] and student [Strategist] at Niers Astoragon's academy, one of two Humans in his group of friends.
Wil is a second son of the high nobility in Terandria, not as important as his older brother, and his family paid a fortune for him to study.
Wil admits that Terandrian nobility, himself included, are the kind of Humans others blame for things.
Wil is a coastal swimmer who has experience on ships and dives into the sea to rescue Peki.
House Kallinad is a coastal duchy, and Pheislant is a coastal nation known for its lighthouses and a weaker land army.
Wil's sister Talia Kallinad is a Knight of the Summer in the Order of Seasons, and Wil has watched her spar her peers.
Wil has an Aunt Delicha, his father's sister, who is married to a [Baron] of Ailendamus.
Wil's cousin Girent is engaged to Lady Cassicel Havrington, aged thirteen, as his father wants peace with the Havringtons.
Wil explains that Terandrian nobles use inheritance Skills like [Adroit Progeny] that pass on a parent's talents, which disturbs the other species.
Wil's hired Gold-rank team was wiped out hunting a Cyclops, after a Silver-rank team on a different contract for the same monster arrived.
Wil tells Niers he knew where the Cyclops den was but not that another team pursued it.
Wil privately decides on a big risky plan that affects his family, telling friends there is no turning back.
Wil says his family has invested a lot in him and he fears embarrassing them with everyone watching.
Wil arrives at the harbour of Daquin with Feshi, and four warships carry the Order of Seasons, the Kallinad army and a dozen noble houses.
Lady Talia Kallinad asks for Wil's command as Sir [Strategist], and Wil orders "Charge" with the padded-spear [Knights] raised.
Wil plotted a sea route that took the warships to Daquin's harbour unseen.
Wil's retreat signal is three horn calls, and he tells Sir Kelm so.
Wil offers a Gnoll [Captain] thirty gold pieces for every officer knocked out.
A Gnoll [Captain] calls Wil the Human who sailed them through the Kraken's Gulch.
Wil rides at the Knights of Summer's head, orders swords in place of lances and cuts through a Dullahan shield line with [Ram's Charge].
Wil calls for [Healers] for the wounded Dullahans as his [Knights] ride on.
Niers tells Wil he brought four warships from Kallinad's harbours, predicted the Iron Vanguard's arrival and challenged Tulm.
Wil loses to Tulm's guile and tells Niers that he would have won.
Niers says Wil surprised Tulm the Mithril, which not every Level 40 [Strategist] can claim.
Niers says that in this moment Wil Kallinad is his best student, as Wil's ships arrive.
Niers tells Wil no gift because he lost, but he and Umina should each have a question ready.
Wil and Umina have won the right to ask Niers one question he will answer truthfully, but he has not called them in for over a month.
Wil got the third-highest marks in the class, losing points only because a pickpocket took a fourth of his gold.
Wil demands the question that day because the summer break is near, and Niers admits Perorn had bet he would do it within a month.
Niers praises Wil's logistics in moving a strike force from Terandria to Daquin by sea, unseen, with the Order of Seasons' help.
Niers says Wil's command was too straightforward and needs work on larger forces.
Wil first asks Niers what information would most aid House Kallinad at this moment.
Wil's real question is about the greatest undiscovered treasure or mystery that Niers knows of, how to find it and its dangers.
Wil attends Niers' lectures with Venaz, Yerranola and others, including Merrik, Peki, Kissilt, Cameral, Marian and Umina.
Wil leads a trip with five [Strategists], Feshi, Venaz, Yerranola, Merrik and Peki, who came on his offer and under his command.
Wil chose Captain Lasc, a [Storm Captain] who has traded with Kallinad, because trust matters at sea.
Wil holds a list of nine shipwreck sites in Niers' own handwriting, and the scroll is coded to Wil's touch against theft.
Niers' first entry on the list is anonymous cargo for Archmage Zelkyr, from a trade ship ambushed by Reefeyes.
Niers' list gives a possible resting place of the Diamond Swords of Serept, a Kheltian treasure stolen two thousand years ago, and warns Wil not to take them.
Wil finds the Diamond Swords of Serept in an ancient casket, and Fetohep of Khelt appears and offers him half.
Wil plans to give one sword to the King of Pheislant, one to Foliana for Niers to trade for artifacts, and one to Talia.
Wil says he will share anything he gets from the trade with his friends.
Wil and Venaz shout Skills they already spent, such as [Ram's Charge], and scare two Drowned captains into retreating.
Wil takes a clear diamond sword with three reflective leaves on its hilt, the Threefold Mirrorblade, which creates two copies of him.
Fetohep tells Wil and his comrades they will possess the swords until they die, and that Wil must return the rest.
Fetohep says Wil proved worthy of the blades for now and tells him to bring the rest quickly.
Wilen is a boy in the village where Tom's group stops. He is too young for a job beyond helping his parents but a bit too old to play with the other kids.
Wilen asks Tom whether he plans to leave, and Tom says not unless the King sends for them.
Wilen asks how [Clowns] level up, wondering whether juggling pins for long enough does it, and notes that [Tumblers] level up if they get a large crowd.
Wilen is native to this world and seems perfectly at ease in talking to Tom.
Badly wounded, Wilen tells Tom that he is going to die and that Tom should run because a Troll is coming.
Wilen holds out a kitchen knife that he must have used to defend himself, and it falls from his fingers.
Wilen asks Tom for a joke, and Tom tells him one about a fat [Clown] sitting in front of a Troll, with the punchline "the main course".
Wilen giggles at the joke, saying it is good, and then dies in Tom's arms mid-sentence.
Wilen is dead.
Later, Tom says he had enough of fighting after the night Wilen died.
Wilovan is a burly Gnoll with a nearly-top hat and a polished club at his side, who works with Ratici as one of the Gentlemen Callers.
Wilovan is a [Thug] and describes himself as a humble fellow with a club who taps folks and absconds with coin.
Wilovan is a member of the Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings, which Palt calls a smaller but elite gang with big players in northern Izril.
Wilovan speaks with a polite, posh manner and plays cards by memorising his hand at a glance and laying it face down.
Wilovan keeps a pipe, and smokes at the inn beside an open window.
Wilovan agrees with Ratici about taking the contract, citing the proximity to home, the pay and the distinction.
Wilovan says he would like to visit home even if they accept the contract.
Wilovan confronts a gang of eleven planning to kidnap little Gnolls, introducing himself as a representative of the Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings.
Wilovan leads the gang into an alley and walks out alone ten minutes later, humming a children's song about wet bodies.
Wilovan says Mrsha is not his priority but is a child, and calls kidnapping a child bad business.
Wilovan tells Ratici the Tall Man is paying too well for them to pursue their other activities.
Wilovan and Ratici are paid by the Tallman and worry the inn is fattening them up.
Wilovan relays to Ratici that Lyonette has a [Boon] Skill after overhearing Octavia.
Wilovan says untoward actions do not befit a member of the Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings.
Wilovan and Ratici were invited by the Tallman of Baleros to guard the inn and have grown bored after sitting and eating.
Wilovan and Ratici say a proper security operation would let them leave a Brother, or five, at the inn.
Wilovan tells Ratici they should eat before deciding whether to cancel the contract.
Reiss tells Numbtongue that the hats of Wilovan and Ratici are the same as those of the hat-men from Celum, friends of the [Enforcer].
Wilovan says they did not hold the fellow who ran afoul of their group accountable.
Wilovan tells Numbtongue that Goblins in a bustling city are not the sort one would want to befriend.
Wilovan says Goblins can be found everywhere, and that everywhere means everywhere.
Wilovan and Ratici discuss a hallway door that was there two days ago and now is gone, with Wilovan teasing about spaces one cannot see.
Wilovan tells Erin he and Ratici were hired to look out for her, and that they are criminals of the Brothers.
Wilovan and Ratici say they will not reveal their client, and Erin guesses Ilvriss, perhaps Magnolia, or others.
Wilovan and Ratici say they are not there to risk their lives.
Fierre says the Gentlemen Callers are two of the Brothers' best and will kill an enemy of the Brothers.
Wirclaw is a Gnoll [Farmer] with dirty blonde fur who lives in a small village near Liscor.
Wirclaw keeps many cows and sells milk, which Krshia buys from him.
Wirclaw has a son, a small Gnoll with light blonde fur.
Wirclaw says Gnolls settle near cities after learning farming from the Drakes, and that Liscor would starve without farmers.
Wirclaw says the village's defenses are a ten-foot wall, his bow and its villagers, and the Watch patrols nearby.
Wirclaw says Rock Crabs do not attack walled settlements, and that Shield Spiders can be heard when they tunnel.
Wirclaw already knows of Mrsha when Erin mentions the little Gnoll she is looking after.
Wirclaw recommends goat milk for a young Gnoll, and sells Erin milk.
Wirclaw owns a pair of Fischer Cows, which like meat and whose rich milk comes from cows that bite.
Wirclaw shoots an arrow into a charging goat as the villagers barricade themselves in their houses.
Wirclaw catches the goat as it leaps for Erin and hurls it aside, and he and Erin kick and stomp it to death.
Wirclaw leads the villagers after the fight, holding bloody weapons, and none of them is hurt.
Wirclaw half-raises his bow when he spots Bird, then glances toward the Hobs in the distance.
Wiskeria is a young [Witch] with spectacles and a pointed hat, which she wears even indoors.
Wiskeria is a few years older than Durene and wears a long dark-blue robe, a hat and spectacles.
Wiskeria tugs her pointed hat lower when she is thinking.
Wiskeria brews very strong, minty tea and carries it in canteens at her saddlebags.
Wiskeria's dark-blue hat has grown with her since she was six, and her mother sewed a charm into it.
Wiskeria is a [Witch], a specialised type of [Mage] who hinders opponents with spells, brews potions and assists friends.
Wiskeria is subordinate to Odveig in the Celestial Trackers but seems to be the brains behind the group.
Wiskeria is the only truly specialised spellcaster in either hired adventuring group, and she cannot throw fireballs.
