Zassil jokes that wars are bad for the economy and looks hurt when Issa snaps at him.
Zassil snaps at an adventurer captain who complains about keeping two miles away from the Bloodfields.
Zassil suggests that the team rent the Heartflame Breastplate after its current wearers, and Bevussa asks if he wants them to become a land-bound team.
Zassil takes the rear of the Wings of Pallass behind Issa as they enter the dungeon.
Zassil joins Issa in cutting the Frost Wyvern's neck and wings during the attack on Pallass.
Zassil starts when Bevussa orders him and Issa to leave a downed Wyvern, giving orders to her 'Captain' in front of onlookers.
Zassil leaps with Issa and Kin through the magic door to Pallass after Bevussa calls the Wings of Pallass to arms.
Onlookers at the Wandering Inn identify Zassil as the team captain of Pallass's Gold-rank Wings of Pallass.
Zassil is praised as Captain by a Pallassian Drake for taking on the Wyverns, and he answers that they did their duty as Gold-ranks.
Zassil had served in Pallass's army, and his smile looks strained as the Drake fawns over Bevussa.
Zel Shivertail is a Drake known as the legendary General of the Line and the famous Tidebreaker, though few call him by his first name.
Zel wishes at times that people believed in him less, because one day he will lose a battle and his life.
Zel is widely regarded as the greatest defensive general on the continent.
Zel is a hero of both Antinium Wars, and Drake children all know his name.
The Drakes of Liscor remember Zel just as often because General Sserys, whom they do not forget, came from their city.
Zel tells young Selys that fame is a one-way street, and once you go down it you cannot go back.
Zel tells Selys he does not like being famous and finds having everyone's eyes on him a heavy responsibility.
Zel tells Selys he takes command because there is no one else, because it is his duty, and because it must be done.
In his letter from besieged Geir, Zel describes himself as a Level 15 [Lieutenant] commanding the city's remaining forces.
Later, after his battles in the war, Zel grew from a Level 15 [Lieutenant] to a Level 39 [General], one of the most remarkable recorded rises.
Zel has ranks in the [Commander] class and no [Tactician] or [Strategist] training.
Zel considers himself a [General] who leads from the front and fights best when he trusts his gut.
Zel says [Generals] like him see opportunities and act on instinct, unlike [Strategists], who plan for every eventuality.
Zel has a [Dangersense] Skill, which goes off nonstop when he faces the Goblin Lord's army.
Zel's armor and Skills keep him alive when an undead Goblin explodes beside him.
Zel has a Skill that lets him run, as Ilvriss points out.
Zel has an offensive Skill, [Glorious Charge], which few people know he has.
[Glorious Charge] makes Zel's body lighter and sends his soldiers rushing forward like a wall of flesh and steel.
Zel fights without a weapon, and his claws cut steel.
Zel's claws slash through armor and flesh, and he blocks a spear point with one hand.
Zel survives a fall from rooftop height in armor and a [Grand Fireball] because he has Skills.
Zel's [Dangersense] tells him that Regrika Blackpaw is too strong for Gold-rank adventurers.
Zel is a [General of the Line], whom the Goblins know as the Tidebreaker and hero of two Antinium Wars.
Zel needs no Skills or spells to address a large crowd of soldiers.
Zel calls himself a defensive [General] who holds the line, and who only occasionally charges into the enemy and redefines the line.
Zel's Skills mainly revolve around defensive formations and holding the line, unlike the offensive General Sserys.
Zel uses [Rapid Maneuvering], [Hold the Line] and [Vanguard of Steel] from Reynold's flying carriage to reshape the Human army.
[Vanguard of Steel] makes the front-line Humans' bodies steel-like, so that sword strikes bounce off them for a short time.
Zel uses [Antimagic Slash] to cut through magical barriers and protections.
Zel uses [Titan's Cut] to carve four claw marks through the air and across the Shield Spider.
The Goblin Lord's [Deathbolt] pierces Zel at point-blank range, and he stumbles but does not fall.
At Geir, Zel rallies the few soldiers, guardsmen and civilians he can and retreats into the keep when a vast Antinium army overwhelms the walls.
General Sserys leads a mounted rescue of Geir's survivors, and Zel is honoured as the leader of the defenders.
Zel is immediately given a command of his own after Geir and assembles an army around its survivors.
Zel's army wins several victories, including the second defense of Shivering Falls and the retaking of Geir.
Zel's defensive skill, born of the siege, lets his army fight off far larger forces and push back the Antinium at key battles.
He is hailed as Tidebreaker because the Black Tide kept failing to overwhelm his army.
Sserys writes that Zel refused armor he commissioned, saying it suited someone of lesser level, and also forwent magical weapons.
Sserys writes that Zel's Skills let him fight with his claws more efficiently than experienced warriors.
Sserys admires Zel's humility, calls him an icon among the soldiers, and does not want to lose such a valuable young [General].
After Sserys's First Unified Army is lost, the second, larger army sent to investigate the Hive is entrusted to Zel.
The city-states instruct Zel's army not to attack the Hive, but only to gather information and retreat.
Zel routs Klbkch the Slayer's army in a pitched battle during the Second Antinium War.
Zel abandons his battles against the Antinium to march north when Liscor is attacked, as the former student and friend of Sserys of Liscor.
Three other Drake [Generals] join Zel with their armies, and they cut a path to the Necromancer's army at Liscor.
Az'kerash kills [General] Hekiss on the first day of the battle at Liscor, [General] Vusso on the second, and [General] Misa two hours later.
Only Zel remains of the four [Generals] as the Necromancer's forces threaten Liscor and the attacking army.
Zel stays on the battlefield despite Az'kerash's repeated assaults on him, and his rallying presence and Skills keep the Drake armies from folding.
Zel charges Az'kerash's position again and again but cannot corner him, because the Necromancer screens himself with undead or disappears.
Zel's only reply from Drake High Command to his countless requests for assistance is the line: "Prepare for irregular reinforcements."
At Liscor Zel strikes Az'kerash with [Antimagic Slash], tears his chest open, and throws both halves to the ground.
When Az'kerash falls in two, his undead stumble and a Bone Giant begins to crumble.
Zel charges Klbkch the Slayer right after the victory, and the two fight in the center of the battlefield.
Klbkch says he and Zel had clashed on numerous occasions before and that their animosity persists to this day.
Klbkch believes he stabbed Zel in the chest, and says Zel survived and tore off his arm.
Zel remembers Klbkch the Slayer from a battlefield in the war, where Klbkch tells him he has come to kill him.
Zel remembers the Antinium fighting mindlessly and killing anything that moved while the Drakes organized and slaughtered them.
Xrn says that Zel himself named the three original Prognugators who survived the war, Klbkch, Xrn and the last.
During the last Antinium War Zel held the front line against the Goblin King's regular army and saw the Goblin King charging minutes before his death.
Zel thought the Goblin King looked sad, as if he knew what would happen next.
Zel says the Goblins nearly beat everyone in the Second Antinium War, when the Goblin King began kicking everyone's collective tail.
Zel says the Goblin King was killed only by many armies uniting, and that they got lucky.
Zel says the Goblin King before the last brought down eight kingdoms on Terandria and ended at least two bloodlines thousands of years old.
Zel tells Liscor's Council he refuses to sleep under the same roof as Goblins, having fought them in the Second Antinium War and countless times since.
Zel argues before the Drake city rulers that the Goblin Lord, the Antinium and Flos are all real threats, as he does every year.
Zel thinks the Drake lords do not understand, and he has precious few allies and more than a few enemies.
Zel attacks Ilvriss's camp on a Gnoll scout's report of chaos in the camp, and sees a tall Human woman sprinting out of the smoke.
He uses [Glorious Charge] on the enemy line, and later wants to thank the girl for the chaos.
Zel meets Ryoka in the magical forest maze, covered in blood and lost, and introduces himself only as Zel.
Zel tells Ryoka he owes her a debt for causing the chaos in the camp, and does not threaten her.
Zel pushes the Drake army against Ilvriss's side, tired from many cuts from Ilvriss's sword.
Zel notices a blur crossing the battlefield and asks what it is.
Zel marches with Wall Lord Ilvriss as his prisoner, whose army surrendered fast once Zel had charged their lines and captured their leader.
Zel trusts Ilvriss to keep to the laws of war and his own honour.
Zel fears an unauthorised Antinium Hive, since only six Hives are allowed on the continent, and expects another Antinium War if so.
Zel marches his army through the blizzard toward the bonfires of the Gnoll tribe, ignoring the sense to make camp.
Zel leads his army and Ilvriss's remnants against the Goblin horde, fighting without a weapon.
Zel orders Ilvriss to retreat to protect the defenseless Gnoll tribe, and an undead Goblin explodes beside them.
Zel covers a few Gnoll cubs with his soldiers as the army retreats.
Zel salutes Ryoka with one claw as she runs past carrying a Gnoll.
Zel retreats defeated, and the Goblin Lord smiles as he watches Zel's back.
Magnolia Reinhart expects Zel to fall into disgrace after the defeat and plans to persuade him to come north.
Magnolia intends to send Zel a [Message] spell rather than a [Courier].
Zel travels north through the snow with Ilvriss, who has brought attendants, to find the Human Runner in Liscor.
Zel and Ilvriss dislike each other's presence but tolerate it out of respect.
Ilvriss refuses to stay at the same inn as Zel and takes the Tailless Thief, the best inn in Liscor.
Zel, Ilvriss, Klbkch and Xrn nearly fight in a Liscor street, and Pawn with twenty Soldiers bars Klbkch's way.
Watch Captain Zevara forms a line of Guardsmen to block Zel and Ilvriss, and Relc greets Zel as old man Zel.
The City Watch and Zel let the Antinium go.
Zel finds all the inns full and takes a room at The Wandering Inn, which he thinks he remembers from long ago.
Lyonette welcomes Zel to the inn and tells him it was rebuilt.
Zel expected a male [Innkeeper] and is puzzled to hear of Erin.
Zel is up early at the inn the morning after, says he has never had children, and mentions his companion is hungover.
Zel joins the rescue of Mrsha in the dungeon and accepts the aid of the azure Antinium "just this once".
After the rescue the townspeople recognise Zel and exclaim.
Zel stays at the inn receiving [Message] spells from the cities, and talks with Zevara and the local guild heads.
Zel says the cities are arguing and it is getting political with Ilvriss around.
Zel meets to discuss the Goblin Lord and the dungeon, and says he feels responsible for Liscor.
Zel tells Lyonette that Erin resembles distracted geniuses who win spectacularly but fail at skirmishes.
Zel says he tries not to put such people in command because they are unreliable in a pinch.
Zel remarks that Erin has a very scattered personality after her door mishap.
When Erin asks if he is related to Selys, Zel answers by asking if she knows his niece.
Zel scolds Erin for dismissing Lyonette, listing that Lyonette cooked, stole honey from Ashfire bees and rescued Mrsha.
Relc calls Zel the Tidebreaker and old man Zel, eating at the inn.
Zel reconsiders his judgement of Erin, who seems extremely off in a way he can attribute to only one other Human.
Zel refuses to talk to the Antinium Pawn, saying he fought in both Antinium Wars and saw their Soldiers slaughter thousands.
Pawn asks Zel for leadership advice, and Zel tells him to find Niers Astoragon or Lord Tyrion Veltras instead.
Zel agrees to answer one question and walks with Pawn to tell him what to say to a dying soldier.
Zel's advice is to tell them they did well, and sometimes only to hold their claw and say goodbye.
Zel argues with Ilvriss at Liscor's gates, who will not sit in a room with Ants, and Zel says he will keep an ear open.
Xrn tells Zel that one of three surviving original Prognugators killed Sserys, naming Wrymvr the Deathless as the last of them.
Xrn says Zel can ask Wrymvr what became of Sserys.
Zel leaves into the snowstorm, hearing the name Wrymvr the Deathless in his mind.
Zel sits in the Tailless Thief, which is all Drakes, and feels out of place.
Zel prefers The Wandering Inn and likes pancakes.
Zel likes the Gnoll cub Mrsha, who begs for scraps and sits on his lap as Selys used to.
Zel argues with Ilvriss until their unconscious intimidation Skills empty the inn around them.
Zel warns that the Goblin Lord, who easily beat back the army he and Ilvriss led together, is a real threat.
Zel says Erin has [Advanced Cooking] and that her food is new.
Zel talks with Ryoka in The Wandering Inn, thanks her for the chaos in the camp, and says his side held ground against a coalition.
Zel says he saw her scatter Ilvriss's camp and later saw her flee through the Goblin Lord's army.
Zel says Ilvriss wants to know what happened to his lieutenant Periss, who ran after Ryoka in the forest.
Ryoka refuses to explain, says Zel would be in danger if she did, and swears she did not kill Periss.
Zel tells Ryoka his reputation is overinflated by stories, but he has faced assassins for over a decade.
Zel believes Ilvriss and Periss were a couple.
Zel uses a spiral-shaped truth detector with green gems and finds that Ryoka told the truth.
Zel eats breakfast at the inn and enjoys the food and Mrsha's game of stealing from his plate.
Zel tells Pawn that Sserys told him to watch his officers for a spark and nurture it until they surpass him.
At a Liscor council meeting it is said that the exploding undead were not briefed to either general, and that Zel mutters in reply.
Zel nods when Olesm tells Regrika Blackpaw about Erin's magical door, and says it could sustain them in a siege.
In the night attack on Liscor, Zel dives from red lightning and later fights a Golem conjured by Imenet Southwing.
Ryoka tells Zel in a warded room of the Tailless Thief that the Necromancer killed Periss and sent Regrika and Imenet.
Zel had suspected illusions and had seen Erin feed them mana potions, bones and blood.
Zel learns from Ryoka that Regrika and Imenet are Az'kerash's servants, and he says he thought he killed the Necromancer in the last Antinium War.
Zel tells Ryoka that Sserys was a brilliant [General] whom people obeyed even when they hated him.
Zel reveals that Sserys held the unique class [Spear of the Drakes], which could command any Drake army.
Zel says Sserys died before gaining a single Skill in that class, having leveled once when the Antinium destroyed his army.
Zel cannot speak to all the city rulers and Lords of the Wall the way Sserys could.
After the night of the attack Zel sits with Liscor's Council, reassures people, and plans a new army with the Walled Cities.
Zel pays Erin gold for the wall and damaged furniture and apologises, saying the battle was his to lose.
Zel calls himself the highest-level warrior on the field that night, and he was not there.
Zel orders Watch Captain Zevara to stand down over the Redfang Goblins and says he will not stay at the inn if Goblins shelter there.
Zel says he backs Erin's judgement because she picked out Regrika Blackpaw's treachery, and admits he has ulterior motives he cannot state.
Zel leaves the Wandering Inn and sleeps at Peslas's inn, missing the pancakes and Mrsha.
Zel's mentor Sserys was a former [General] of Liscor and leader of its mercenary army, and Zel was a close friend and student of his.
Ilvriss points out that no Drake [General] has gone past Liscor since the last Antinium War.
Zel finds no record of Regrika Blackpaw's birth in the Blackpaw tribe and notices deaths following her travels.
Zel tells Ilvriss he has received a letter through Celum and is leaving to meet someone further north.
Zel shakes hands with Magnolia Reinhart and says "Let's save the world then."
Zel sees in Magnolia the light and certainty that Sserys had decades ago.
Zel is the famous Lineholder, hero of two Antinium Wars, and a feeder of hungry Gnoll cubs.
Zel eyes Magnolia sourly, and says he would rather have half again as many soldiers than her forty thousand.
Zel is the first Drake [General] in a Human [Lady]'s mansion, four hundred miles over the border marked by Liscor.
Zel does not trust Magnolia Reinhart because she speaks of peace but would see it through war.
Magnolia tells Zel he would be the first to accept her alliance and that she had hounded him with letters for years.
Zel says Magnolia has too many secrets and that he does not trust her at all.
Zel agrees to help against the Goblin Lord in exchange for Magnolia's help against the Necromancer.
Zel might come back with the Titan and trusted people to hear Magnolia's plan, but he refuses to ally blindly.
Zel and Magnolia become allies of convenience, with her army for his help against the Goblin Lord.
Zel receives enchanted armor from Magnolia and feels warm and conflicted.
Zel tells Magnolia that she has a shield and he holds the line, so she should ask the Titan for offense.
Magnolia presents Zel to the assembled officers as the commander who will lead them against the Goblin Lord.
Zel wears the Heartflame Breastplate, a relic of the Drakes, which makes him feel warm.
Zel becomes commander of Magnolia's Human army and tells the officers he is here at her request.
Zel tells the officers he fought in both Antinium Wars and battled the Goblin King's armies.
Zel tells the officers that he slew the Necromancer at Liscor, which he believes he did.
The officers gasp at his name, and the crowd recognises the Tidebreaker.
Zel tells the officers this is Human land but also his continent, and that he is no [Lord] but a soldier.
Zel recalls Drakes do not run, a saying of a friend of his, and says Humans did not run when the Goblin King landed.
[Lieutenant] Gershal of Vaunt and several officers pledge to follow Zel, and the crowd shouts his name and "Izril!"
Zel tells the army it will be the Goblin Lord's end, and he will stay in the camp to lead it.
Zel says he did not use a Skill to impress the crowd and needs an army willing to fight.
Zel and the Goblin Lord feel each other's presence across miles, and both whisper "Death."
Zel sits in his tent near Invrisil with Magnolia and Ressa, who give him a history book.
Zel expects the Goblin Lord's army in two days and intends to force a day battle.
Zel wonders whether the Goblin Lord is allied with the Necromancer as an equal or as a servant.
Zel orders Magnolia's secret weapons held until the Goblin Lord makes his move.
Zel refuses to use her grandfather's tube artifact unless the battle turns badly.
Zel wears two rings and a pendant from Magnolia against teleportation, curses and mental attack, though he dislikes the rings.
Zel says he was never supported by the Walled Cities and returned any artifacts he used.
Zel stands with arms folded in front of his army as the Goblins chant, and their voices falter.
The Goblin Lord had studied Zel's stories, so the Goblins all know him as a legend.
Zel tears open a black-armored Hob and catches a female Hob's axe blade bare-handed near Gershal.
Zel kicks a Goblin into eight others and clears a space with his claws.
Zel tears off Illbreath's head, holds up Noface's head, and says "Ow" when Snapjaw bites his hand before he throws her.
Zel revives Reynold with a potion and rides away from the battlefield with him.
Zel tells Magnolia to call him Zel in the field and praises Reynold for saving the horses.
Zel asks Magnolia to lend him Reynold for a dangerous strategy and to drop him at Thomast's position.
Zel hands the left flank to Thomast, who accepts without question.
Zel cuts the Shield Spider's legs with [Titan's Cut] and tears open the Goblin Lord's stomach with [Antimagic Slash], leaving him saying only "Oh".
Zel crushes Oom's mana stone, killing him, and says "That's one. Who's next?"
Zel rides Reynold's flying carriage over the Goblin Lord's army and drops from it onto the Goblins, surviving the fall.
Bea touches Zel's arm, and when he pours a healing potion on the spot the burning spreads, because the potion amplifies a magical plague.
Zel throws away his belt and healing potions and charges Venitra first.
Zel, burned and diseased, fights Venitra, Kerash, Bea and Ijvani while the Goblin Lord watches.
He proclaims himself the shield of the Drakes and says a general does not fall.
Zel cuts Bea in two and counts "Three!"
Zel kicks the wounded Goblin Lord when he creeps up with Venitra's bone sword.
Zel fights with a last [Antimagic Slash] that opens Az'kerash's throat, but he collapses.
Az'kerash grabs a scroll and vanishes, and his undead flee.
Zel talks with the Goblin Lord, names him Reiss, a Drake name Sserys wanted for a son, and dies.
Zel calls Sserys his mentor, friend and "wings of my heart" as he asks whether he did a good job.
Zel says he will let Sserys tell him in person, and the Goblin Lord vows to avenge him.
The Goblin Lord tells the dying Zel that he did a good job protecting his people.
The Human army weeps when it learns that Zel Shivertail, the Tidebreaker, is dead.
The news spreads across Izril and every continent that a Goblin Lord killed the legendary Drake hero.
Zel's family symbol is a sprig of blue flowers curled like a tail, and Liscor fills with blue flowers.
Drakes carry an empty coffin with a blue wreath, shouting Zel's name, and an announcer claims the Humans abandoned him.
Zel's body is delivered in a black wood casket by Magnolia Reinhart's coach, preserved by runes.
The body has half the head gone, torn limbs, discoloured scales, and one unbroken piece of armor on the chest.
Selys, Tekshia and Zevara see the body.
The [Healer] who removed the armor falls ill and dies, so Zel's body is cremated; Magnolia's people say only those who touch it are at risk.
Magnolia kept the Heartflame Breastplate in the Reinhart armory for two hundred years.
Ilvriss says the armor did not save Shivertail, who must have been truly cornered.
Zel's funeral is held in Liscor with a delegation from Pallass, seen by all the Drake cities.
Tekshia, Zevara and Embria light the pyre in the rain.
Zel's ashes are to be sent to his home for burial.
Chaldion finds it strange that a single Goblin Lord spellcaster beat the Tidebreaker in single combat out of sight of everyone.
Zel is Selys's uncle, and Tekshia is his aunt.
Zel visited Liscor when Selys was a child and let her sit on his lap.
Zel has visited Selys rarely, perhaps four years apart, due to duties.
Zel fought a trade dispute with Salazsar over a gemstone monopoly, which he won.
Zel tells Selys she is the only relative who does not treat him as a hero or symbol.
Selys tells Zel he has no subordinates and moves between cities.
Zel knocked out Ilvriss and tells Selys of it.
Zel hides his meeting with Ryoka and the dark news she gave him from Selys.
Zel drinks Erin's Faerie Flower drink and says he has never been better.
Zel leaves three days later, and Selys hears of his alliance with Magnolia two days after that.
In a flashback young Selys asks Zel what being a [General] is like, and he says it is not like being a hero.
Zel had led an army against the Vaskia Skyhunter Tribe the previous month.
Zel gave Selys practice claws and teaches her tricks, telling her to stay out of trouble.
Zel calls Selys his favorite niece, then maybe his second favorite.
Zel's will asked to be buried with his love, which Selys honoured by pouring his ashes in Sserys's grave.
Selys confirms to Pisces, who guesses the meaning of Turnscale, that her uncle was one.
Selys believes Sserys was a Turnscale too, because Zel would not have written his will otherwise, and she later says it was true.
Onieva says Zel was a Turnscale she met a few times, never in secret.
Zevara is the Drake Captain of the Watch of Liscor, a tall Drake.
The Captain of the Watch of Liscor, later named Zevara, is a female Drake with light-blue scales, yellow eyes and a scar on the left side of her face.
Zevara breathes fire, blasting a zombie off its feet.
Later, Erin sees that Zevara's eyes are a light purple, and Selys has told her that Zevara can breathe fire.
Zevara has a [Dangersense] that rings in the back of her head before danger.
Zevara breathes fire at adventurers until the world darkens and she gasps for air, as it always does after she uses her birthright; a mage's [Barrier of Air] disperses the flames.
Zevara has a great set of lungs, perhaps the Skill [Loud Voice], and is loud when she shouts.
Zevara is a Drake whom Selys privately thinks of as a throwback with old blood, a dragon's child, and a hero for holding back the undead with fire.

At the start of the story Zevara tells Erin that Klbkch, the fourth-strongest Guardsman in the city, died because he wasted his emergency healing potion on her, and that the Watch will stop patrolling her area.
Zevara tells Erin that Klbkch was one of her best Senior Guardsmen and that without him there is no one to control the Antinium.
Zevara tells Erin that the Guardsmen should never have interfered in the affairs of outsiders, and orders her out of her city.
Zevara leads the Watch shoulder to shoulder against the undead, firing arrows into the crowd and cutting down a zombie herself.
Zevara tells Tkrn that the attack cannot be the Necromancer's, since he would have brought giants, wights, ghosts and other horrors.
The Watch has over four hundred guardsmen in a city that holds over ten thousand civilians, and was never meant to protect the city from siege.
Zevara demands that the humans responsible for unleashing the undead be held accountable, her voice raw and coughing.
Someone refers to Erin as the one who got Klbkch killed.
Zevara has served as Captain for six years and notices that Klbkch looks different after nearly ten years, with two arms and a slimmer body.
Zevara visits Erin's inn with Klbkch, Relc, Pawn and Ksmvr, saying she wants to see the human who killed that freak and the inn Relc keeps talking about.
Zevara refuses to send Relc and Klbkch to rescue the adventurers in the ruins, since they owe nothing to non-citizens, and she will not risk losing Klbkch again.
Zevara forbids Relc and Klbkch from helping Erin, calling them valuable assets to the city.
Zevara arrives at the ruins with guardsmen to confiscate the treasure, saying she did not risk good warriors in case the ruins were infested.
Zevara is surprised to see Olesm, shoves Relc aside to check him over, and says she would have sent help had she known their [Tactician] was down there.
Zevara loves Olesm, and thinks she may die without telling him.
Olesm says Zevara is worried that the ruins are a magical dungeon rather than an old one.
Zevara shouts up at Erin during her singing that people are trying to sleep.

section: Books 3-6: Antinium reports and the Goblins
text: Under the treaty, Antinium Soldiers may leave the Hive only in times of war or at the Watch Captain's request, and six hundred Soldiers are permitted to Klbkch's Hive.

section: Books 3-6: Antinium reports and the Goblins
text: Zevara grants Klbkch's request to take Soldiers out of the Hive, authorising twenty for patrols for now.

section: Books 3-6: Antinium reports and the Goblins
text: Zevara writes a report of every encounter with Klbkch to send to every Walled City via the Mage's Guild; she has only questions about the Antinium's movements.

section: Books 3-6: Antinium reports and the Goblins
text: Zevara wonders whether the Antinium in Liscor are really enemies, and what could be done about them if they were.

section: Books 3-6: Antinium reports and the Goblins
text: Zevara, with a group of guardsmen, steps between Wall Lord Ilvriss and Ryoka, telling him he cannot bear arms in the city or abduct a Human without causing an incident with the Human cities.

section: Books 3-6: Antinium reports and the Goblins
text: Zevara fines Erin four gold coins for striking Ilvriss, payable to Klbkch, and stomps away with smoke leaking from her mouth.

section: Books 3-6: Antinium reports and the Goblins
text: A Drake Watch Captain is second to none in her own city on law and order and can be overruled in military matters only by a rank equal to or above [Colonel], not by a foreign lord.

section: Books 3-6: Antinium reports and the Goblins
text: Zevara arrives with Klbkch, Relc and sixty guardsmen after Imenet's attack, where Zel tells her that Imenet and Regrika are murderers who killed Brunkr.

section: Books 3-6: Antinium reports and the Goblins
text: Zevara storms into Erin's inn with Relc and armed guardsmen, furious that she harbors five Redfang Hobgoblins while the Goblin Lord marches on the cities.

section: Books 3-6: Antinium reports and the Goblins
text: Zevara says five Hobs would be more than a Silver-rank team could handle and suggests they may be spies, saboteurs or a Goblin ploy.

section: Books 3-6: Antinium reports and the Goblins
text: Zevara says she would rather force the Goblins to leave the area than risk any deaths.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara is a hardworking Captain of Liscor's City Watch, who stares in disbelief at the report of Erin's portal to Pallass.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara meets Erin secretly with Watch Captain Venim, saying the three Watch Captains of Pallass agree that a trade war, and possible war, between Liscor and Pallass is unacceptable.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara says the Watch Captains keep in touch by their own means and bypass the chain of command when they think it right; both will deny the meeting.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara says Erin's inn is technically an autonomous holding within Liscor's radius of authority, which Liscor is not pressing.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara tells Erin to keep her Goblins in the basement out of sight, since no one wants to see Goblins after General Shivertail and she wants to avoid a mob.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara blows smoke when angered, with some escaping in the rain at Erin.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara has lost sleep worrying about the dungeon, has called for aid against the Goblin Lord and has Liscor's army guarding the city.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara privately hoped that making peace with Pallass would win a Walled City's help against the dungeon, though she did not tell Erin; she does not know of the Antinium's decade-long silent war beneath the city.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara still carries a small candle for Olesm and hopes they could be more than fellow civil servants.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara breathes huge gouts of fire to cut down Face-Eater Moths on the wall, going dark and gasping each time while Olesm steadies her and uses command scrolls.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara barely sleeps after the battle on the walls, but levels up twice without gaining a Skill.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara learns from Klbkch that Pawn is an Individual and that there are few of them, and she says the Walled Cities will not like it; Klbkch knows she reports on the Antinium to the other cities.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara Sunderscale is an Oldblood Drake capable of using breath attacks, and smoke trickles from her mouth when annoyed.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara argues with Commander Embria that the Antinium honored their contract by dying to hold the walls and that the treaty has held; she says she commands all military matters in her city as second only to a [General].

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara tells Erin that the city needs to reserve her magic door to bring General Shivertail's body from the battlefield, which Magnolia Reinhart had preserved and transported.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara tells Selys, whose spines are dark purple against pale blue scales, that if Zel left her the possessions on his body she inherits the Heartflame Breastplate and his other artifacts.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara tells Selys that Venim says the thugs were hired to kidnap Selys and make her sign a waiver for the breastplate, for forty thousand gold pieces, and calls the plan shoddy and panicked.

section: Book 7: Pallass, the dungeon and the moths
text: Zevara advises Selys to sell the breastplate to Wistram or the army, not Ilvriss, since there is some question of Ilvriss, a member of Salazsar, influencing her.
Zevara pays Erin for damaged furniture, says the play is not offensive, and warns Erin to stay out of the city for a day or two.
Zevara tells the adventurers that a Silver-rank team caused the moth attack on Liscor, and demands a [Message] to the Mage's Guild if they find anything dangerous in the dungeon.
Klbkch's Queen noted Zevara's commendation after the siege of Face-Eater Moths.
Zevara stands with Olesm on the wall under [Illumination] lights, and when he spots Antinium Workers with bows entering the inn she tells him to put it in his report for the Walled Cities.
Zevara tells Erin of a battle at Dwarfhalls Rest, where a Human army under Lord Tyrion Veltras pursues the Goblin Lord's forces and has hired Ellia Arcsinger, the Kingslayer.
Zevara says she will not risk a single [Guardsman] in the dungeon, and thanks Erin because her alarm saved dozens of guardsmen and many civilians.
Zevara tells Olesm that officially the Antinium have three hundred Soldiers for Liscor's defense, but unofficially the walls could hold off a hundred thousand Goblins.
Zevara tells Olesm she is certain the Goblins cannot take Liscor even if the Goblin Lord brings his entire force, though they will pass through with fewer casualties.

Zevara orders Olesm to take the Celum mana stone to the armory, puts Wing Commander Embria's best men on watch, and says no one goes in or out of Celum by her order, confiscating the stone over the objection of Revi.
Zevara tells the Gnoll Beilmark, after a spell on the wall, that if he casts again without telling her first she will throw him off the wall.
Zevara reads the Cave Goblins' chant of the Redfang name as a request for a parley and proposes releasing the four Hobs in lockup in exchange for the Goblins retreating south toward the Blood Fields.
Zevara orders a scroll of [Fireball] and temporary barricades at Erin's magic door in case a Goblin comes through.
Zevara orders the adventurers to defend Liscor under Drake military law, tells the Pallass teams to remain, and has the magic door confiscated.
In Zevara's view the city of Liscor sees the siege as a victory but waits, with the inn closed and Erin unseen for a week.
Zevara suppresses the urge to whistle, jealous, when Erin turns out to be able to pay nearly fifty gold coins.
Selys admires Zevara as an Oldblood who is a female Watch Captain, a rare thing.

Zevara says she is halfway towards agreeing to Krshia and Selys's plan for an election, and that she has been petitioning the Council for more money without success to fully upgrade the Watch's weapons, armor and magic.
Zevara exhales a plume of smoke and says an election would open every Council seat, including her own post.
Zevara, Krshia and Selys decide Klbkch's Hive could be a source of funds, and Zevara says she must ask him, warning that the army and Council might interfere or replace her.
Zevara, Krshia and Selys form an alliance to force an election for Liscor's Council.
Zevara has known Drassi since Drassi was a hatchling, from patrols before she was Watch Captain, and describes her as one of Liscor's finest [Gossips].
Zevara pitches Klbkch the plan for one Council member per district.
Zevara tells the Watch at the barracks that she acts as a private individual, not as part of a coup, and that the City Council has refused her proposals for funds three times.
Zevara tells Olesm that she trusts Klbkch, who has been honorable and hard-working, and that one Hive making peace would remove one-sixth of the Grand Queen's armies.
When asked about Lism's promise to triple the Watch's budget, Zevara wavers and says she could not categorically denounce his proposals.
Zevara tests Calruz with a truth stone that stays blue, then rolls the bottle of spirits from Lism into his cell, asking if she is wrong to trust Klbkch.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara tells Calruz she will get a Wistram-certified [Mage], or a [Healer] who knows such things, to examine him, giving herself less than a week.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara tells the crowd that Calruz has not been held to justice because they are not certain he was in control of himself, and that his fate is within her jurisdiction as Watch Captain, not the Council's.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara arrests Guardsman Ulkel and everyone present for assaulting a prisoner, uses [Lawbreaker's Enemy] on them, and says no justice was done though there will be law.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara tells the new Council that it may oversee the Watch and replace its Captain, but that the Senior Guards can oppose that and nominate a candidate; the Council may overrule her only by choosing a new Captain.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara briefs the Council that Liscor's Hive can bring at least nine thousand Soldiers and twenty four thousand Workers to bear, about thirty thousand fighters, and that one of the six Hives produces Silent Antinium spy-assassins.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara tells Olesm that Klbkch frightens her and might kill them all, but traitors are defined by the one time they disobey, and she is willing to bet on that one time.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara wins nearly her full budget from the new Council, exhaling smoke in triumph, and tells Olesm she plans to put the prisoner to use, needing only to notify the Council.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara keeps in her desk a pig-faced enchanted charm which she dislikes and which turns into a horror-mask of fury when a spell is cast on her.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara resists Palt's calming charm by biting her tongue until it bleeds and kicking her toe against the desk.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara carries a tin whistle that makes no sound when she blows it, as she follows Palt downstairs.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara fires a comet from the city wall's inbuilt spells with a command scroll at Montressa's hill; Montressa's barriers hold and Zevara regrets not hitting her directly.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara puts the five Wistram [Mages] under arrest, and tells Wistram's [Scribe] that Pisces has no record of murder and paid his bounty.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara tells the Wistram team they will obey Liscor's laws, that she does not accept Wistram's bounty on Pisces Jealnet or its allegations against the Horns of Hammerad, and that The Wandering Inn counts as part of Liscor.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara breathes fire at the floor when Isceil insults her as a failure of an Oldblood who cannot breathe fire.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara tells Yvlon, Ksmvr and Selys they are entitled to part of the fine, but cannot be allowed to seek vengeance.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara invites Lyonette into her office, accepts three gold on her artifact fine, which stands at nineteen gold, and has a civil relationship with her.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara refuses a bag of cookies from Lyonette as a bribe, then keeps it and pays four silver in exchange.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara visits Calruz in jail each day, eating her lunch with him and sharing cookies, as he warns that she should not be overly familiar with a prisoner accused of murder and treachery.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara tells Calruz an [Enchanter] is due to visit and that she does not see in him the monster she witnessed in the dungeon.

section: Books 11-14: Calruz, the Council and Wistram
text: Zevara unlocks Calruz's chains and hands him a battleaxe so he can draw the Crelers in Erin's inn, telling him she will not force him to go; he charges in alone shouting "Death before dishonor!"
Zevara has held Liscor through the undead boss Skinner, the Raskghar, Face-Eater Moths, a near-siege and a Goblin Lord's army, but the weyr of Wyverns above chills her.
Zevara drinks heavily and tells Lyonette that two Senior Guards, Sheikhe and Laven, were found dead in a Shield Spider nest after a second pair put on Bearclaw vanished within two hours.
Zevara says Bearclaw evaded the Watch's truth spells and lied to their faces, and that she knows it was her, but the law lets her do nothing but investigate and Bearclaw is protected.
Zevara says Mr. Soot, who was at the same place as Bearclaw, has gone missing and does not want to be brought in.
Zevara worries that the dead Gnolls and Gnoll criminals may confirm other Watch Captains' claims that Gnolls turn to crime more than Drakes, though she says she has kept Liscor fair.
Zevara tells Lyonette the official story is that the Senior Guards met three Hollowstone Deceivers and could not run.
Zevara hunches her shoulders and orders a double drink after Grimalkin says Magnolia Reinhart analyzed the Hive and found a number far higher than any reading of the treaty allows.
Zevara screams Erin's name along with Olesm and half the Council over the broadcast, and keeps screaming for twenty minutes, a record for her.
Zevara keeps a hand-written calendar reading "Days Since Crazy Human Incident", which she resets to zero.
Zevara listens to the Archmages' broadcast at her desk as panic sets in, curses Wistram for unveiling the plot so, and calls for Senior Guardsman Relc.
Zevara tells Relc that he signed over eight hundred people into The Golden Triangle and she has fifty petitions to strip his rank, then strips him of his Senior Guardsman rank.

Zevara applies for Relc's transfer to Cellidel for several months, with his rank still counting as Senior Guardsman there if he goes, and puts him on unpaid leave; she thinks of Relc and Klbkch as her invincible Senior Guardsmen, both now gone.
Zevara commands a hundred [Guards] against an armed mob outside the Mage's Guild, forbidding return fire, then finds the riot has moved to Market Street, where Golden Triangle members' homes burn.
Zevara takes forty high-level [Guards] to place Golden Triangle members in protective custody, and finds a Worker beaten by a mob with his antennae torn off.
Zevara tells Selys that Liscor's economy was never huge and was based on its army, and urges her to think beyond Liscor to Pallass, Esthelm and Celum.
The Watch needs an upgrade to its jail, which Zevara decides not to press Selys about.
Zevara strides out to Erin, who has set off a chant, and uses [Freeze, Criminal] on her in the street.
Zevara plays chess with Calruz at the barrier of his cell, where his rats Rhata and Haldagaz sit, a custom of theirs; his imprisonment now includes fighting monsters.
Zevara keeps tabs on who visits Calruz, which includes Erin, Olesm and, twice, Bezale; Bezale brings a scrying orb showing the House of Minos marching to war.
Zevara has requested six hundred Antinium Soldiers to patrol every inch of Liscor and hold the walls.

Zevara tells the Council she has moved Raskghar only to cells sure to hold them since none can use Skills, on the advice of the prisoner Calruz, the only known expert on their capabilities, who judged that they could bend some of the iron bars.
Zevara, on a speaking-stone call, tells the Watch to let Erin go when she walks into Liscor, thanks her under her breath and would deny it.
Laken obtains [Skill - Empire: Blessing of the Hearth] when he reaches Emperor Level 9.
After the night he receives the Skill, Laken wakes rested despite sleeping far less than six hours.
The grieving villagers who slept nearby slept like logs, woke refreshed, and found that minor cuts had scabbed over and healed almost overnight.
Durene tells Ryoka that Laken's Skill makes beds soft, so that one sleeps like a baby even on hay.
A mage tells Ryoka Griffin that she needs a high-level [Healer], or better yet a [Cleric], to heal her leg, since [Healers] use only herbs and minor spells.
Ceria says treatment of that kind would cost at least a few hundred gold coins, and high-level healers are very rare.
Pisces says that once upon a time a [Cleric] in their earliest levels could do what an [Archmage] could not, because faith warped the bounds of reality.
Pisces says the gods are dead and so are the ancient ways of faith and miracle.
Pisces says [Clerics] are now simply [Healers] who are able to cast spells, the definition of the class having changed along with the skills and spells learnt.
The Fearless are a type of Demon who carry a class that is more an addition to their normal class, such as [Fearless Warrior] or [Fearless Mage], and the class means they cannot feel fear at all.

The Fearless are used as shock troopers: each is a dangerous fighter who will charge through killing grounds and is willing to die to take you with him, and the Demon King uses them when he wants to win.
A captured Fearless sits unmoving in a cage while a crowd throws stones at him, and his body is scarred from earlier stonings.
The Fearless feel unease and disturbance, though not fear, when the laughing [Clown] strolls towards them, and they loose arrows and magic at him as he vanishes and reappears.
The Fearless break and run from an enemy they cannot kill, because without fear they also cannot understand it.
Goblin [Shamans] serve in the Goblin Lord's army, and one blasts the Stone Spears tribe's Gnoll [Shaman] apart with magic, after which the dead Gnoll's body rises.
The Goblin Lord's army includes Goblin [Necromancers] and [Shamans] who chant to move undead.
An old Goblin [Shaman] with a twisted staff of ivory bones and darker crimson eyes speaks a word in the Goblin tongue that commands Toren to come to him.
Toren finds the [Shaman]'s spoken words weaker than Erin's orders, does not struggle against the command, and marches straight up to him.
Toren runs the [Shaman] through with his sword while the [Shaman] keeps trying to recast the spell.
Runners, also called Messengers, are people who deliver letters and goods for pay.
Other names for Runners include Travelers, Sealers (after the Seals they use) and Carriers, plus a host of rude words.
Krshia says Runners are quick people who run long distances to earn money, delivering letters, valuable goods, magical items and messages meant to be spoken to one person only.
Krshia says the expensive requests such as magical items or spoken messages go only to the best Runners, while most simply deliver goods cheaply.
Ryoka Griffin, a City Runner herself, divides Runners into three rough categories: Street Runners, City Runners and Couriers.
According to Ryoka, Street Runners stay within one city, take the safest and easiest jobs for the least money, and rank low in the Runner's Guild.
According to Ryoka, City Runners run from city to city in a general area, take more dangerous jobs, and mainly run away from trouble rather than fight it.
Ryoka writes that Couriers are long-distance Runners who can cross the continent or even the sea, are quick and efficient, and cost incredible amounts of money.
Ryoka reports that Garia told her each Courier is at least Level 30 and has levels in other classes as well, so they are not easy to ambush.
Ryoka also observes that each Runner's Guild is a mess of politics, friendships and infighting over territory.
Fals tells Garia that there are few experienced Runners because no one who does the job lives very long, and most people change classes after earning enough.

A Runner tells Ryoka that most City Runners in the region make short runs between Celers, Remendia, Ocres, Celum and Esthelm, almost never to Liscor, while the best Runners travel across the continent.
Val tells Ryoka that Runners level up based on how far they have run and how challenging the run is, and doubts she would reach Level 10 by the end of the year.
A Runner's reputation for honesty matters as much as speed in winning contracts, because messengers who take goods and give false Seals appear every year.
An Aberration is an Antinium Worker that has become an individual and rejects the Queen's will; Workers say those who are Aberration kill, reject the Hive and destroy.
A Worker tells Erin that no Worker who has become individual has ever failed to become an Aberration.
Klbkch finds a Worker sawing at another Worker's body, who says he corrects the fault in the others, who play games against the will of the Hive and deserve death.
The Worker refuses to serve, claiming "I am", calling the Queen's words madness and heresy, and refuses a name, saying the Experiment is a failure; Klbkch kills him.
The Free Queen tells Erin that three Workers have already become Aberration from gaining useless levels, and calls the experiment wasted.
The Queen orders her Prognugator to investigate an aberration on the surface and speak with him if he is truly free, and the Prognugator says he will dispose of any Aberrations he finds.
In the Antinium Hive, an Aberration is a Worker who has become an individual and turned violent against the Hive, and the Hive treats such a Worker as a failure to be destroyed.
Antinium speakers say that those who are Aberration kill, reject the Hive and destroy.

After Workers brought home the game of chess from Erin's inn, other Workers first wondered whether the new game was itself an Aberration, but concluded it was not because Klbkch had not eliminated the twelve who played it.
During the fifth round of chess, one Worker fetched a butcher's knife and stabbed his opponent to death, and six more Workers were killed before the Propugnator was summoned.
Klbkch found the killing Aberration sawing at another Worker's body, and the Aberration told him he had not failed, that he refused to serve the Queen, and that he refused to take a name.
The Aberration stabbed Klbkch twice before Klbkch cut him to pieces and burned the remains.
Afterwards only a quarter of the Workers were allowed to play chess at once, in case of further Aberrations.
The Queen complained that three Workers had already become Aberration from the experiment and called it a waste.
An Antinium Worker told Erin that no Worker who has become individual has ever not been Aberration, and that Pawn would be executed if he proved to be one.
Ksmvr reported that of twenty-five Workers tested, four became Individuals and the rest all became Aberration.
Ksmvr reported that among those who did not meet Erin Solstice the rate of becoming Individual was one in one hundred and sixty-three, and few Soldiers became Aberration.
Klbkch told Erin that asking a Worker its name was dangerous because most Workers become Aberration when it happens.
Bronze-rank adventurers appear alongside Silver-ranks and Gold-ranks in the Invrisil Adventurer's Guild, where Bronze-ranks are described as doing errand-work.
Ryoka Griffin was said to be far stronger than the average Bronze-rank adventurer in hand-to-hand combat.
Countless Bronze-rank adventurers crowd the Liscor Adventurer's Guild to turn in bounties or take the few requests on the board.
In Invrisil's guild, Bronze-ranks come in covered in muck from killing rats in sewers or gathering [Alchemist] ingredients, which is typical errand-work to make ends meet.
Ulrien said that Bronze-rank adventurers who die do so because they overestimate their abilities or underestimate their opponents.
The narration says each Goblin in an elite band matched any Bronze-rank adventurer by levels, and exceeded one in experience.
Prost told Laken that a pooled village purse could hire only a few Bronze-rank adventurers for a few weeks.
Over forty Bronze-rank adventurers and six Silver-rank adventurers attacked the Furgather Tribe's camp at midday and killed its Chieftain.
Halrac told Erin that beating a Gnoll warrior barehanded was as good as any Bronze-rank adventurer.
The chat is a magical group chat that connects people from Earth across the world through their phones, with a floating screen showing a list of connected users.
A user, [Level 12 Warrior], says a floating screen popped up after answering the phone.
BlackMage says he cannot send anyone home and does not even know what sent them to this world.
BlackMage says the system is not built to kick or mute a user, and that splitting the chat is not possible and this is the best he can do.
[strider_479] suggests that levelling in this world is based on adversity rather than repetition, and [America Group] confirms that the bigger the challenge the faster they levelled.

[Level 12 Warrior] claims the way to game the system is to take multiple classes because more classes give more skills, while Loran Grimnar says new classes are hard to acquire and he has no more than three.
The first chat ends with a user named 伶央 joining, writing two lines in Japanese asking whether anyone is there, and disconnecting alone.

In a later private chat the participants are Loran Grimnar (a [Warrior] in Baleros), [Humble Actor] (a [Pop Star] and [Actor] in Terandria), [strider_479] (a [Ranger] in Terandria), and BlackMage (a [Mage] at Wistram).
[strider_479] says she was adopted and that her birth name is a mystery even to her, and BlackMage says mages tried to scry her and could not.
BlackMage says he has called [batman] five times without an answer, and [strider_479] says [batman] was smarter than they thought and warned them in secret about a spy in the group.
BlackMage says the mages with him are not sure the arrival was a spell for everyone, and that reversing a spell is apparently harder than bringing people over.
[strider_479] says they can find the "Kyle imposter" or at least protect themselves from him.
BlackMage tells the others that the King of Destruction is moving and that there are a few wars going on in Terandria.
Olesm tells Erin that chess was invented in this world just a year earlier.
Erin proposes playing Klbkch and Olesm at once with only five, or rather ten, seconds per move, and calls the style Lightning Chess.
Erin explains that tournament chess can give anywhere from an hour's total thinking time to three minutes; she says that without a clock she will explain as they play.
Erin wins the first two rounds of the Lightning Chess games handily, but in the third game Olesm scores a draw.
Couriers are special long-distance Runners, and Ryoka thinks of the job as roughly the Runner equivalent of a Gold-rank adventurer.
Fals tells Ryoka there is a highest-priority special request coming all the way from First Landing and that a Courier is delivering it.
Val tells Ryoka that Couriers do not answer to Guilds in the way small Guilds expect, that they back each other up in danger but no one bosses anyone else around.
Val says "We're a community, not a cult."

Val says not all Couriers are fast, that some run slower than Ryoka but cannot be stopped, and that one Courier is a [Marksman] who rides a horse and snipes anyone in her way from two hundred feet away.
Three Couriers, Tritel, Salamani and Hawk, are ambushed on the road north by [Assassins] in enchanted coaches and on horseback.
Tritel's horse Ci and Tritel use [Flicker Dodge] and [Blinding Flash] to blind the Assassins, and Tritel later uses [Rope Trick] to drag an Assassin off her horse.
Salamani, a [Mage Runner], uses a spell to summon hundreds of [Light Arrows] that destroy a coach.
Hawk, a Beastkin Rabbit Courier, uses [Physical Overdrive] to run twice as fast, crashes through a coach and escapes the box-in.
Hemp is a plant fiber used for ropes and bags in the world, including a hemp rope that lit lanterns in a cavern and sacks that adventurers and goblins carry.
Among String-people, Hemp is also the name of a caste, the rough-skinned warriors of Nerrhavia's society.
Femithain understood the Hemp warriors to be made from the strongest materials, which gives them a rough, callused appearance closer to hide than skin.
Nerrhavia's society is caste-based, and Nerrhavia's silk-skinned officers shout insults at the Hemp foot-soldiers marching in the chariots' dust.
General Thelican's Hemp [Soldiers] formed his pike lines and foot, and he planned to send them first at the walls.
Thelican felt nothing for a fallen Hemp warrior, even though beheading is death for a String-person unless they are saved immediately.
String-people fear fire, and Tiqr's mages tried to burn the Hemp warriors, who have thick skins that make this difficult but possible.
Alked Fellbow, a Stitch-person with rough, plant-fiber skin who is not quite Hemp, is treated as an outcast in Thelican's tent.
The Liscor Watch cannot arrest someone for an attack unless the victim gives testimony, and Klbkch confirms that when Erin withdraws hers, the Watch cannot arrest Pisces.
Relc argues that being a [Necromancer] is a crime no matter what the person does, but cannot name any way to check a person's class on the spot.
Klbkch states that under Liscorian law, Goblins are considered monsters and bandits for the purposes of determining crime.
Named-rank is a level of adventurer above Gold-rank; Named-rank individuals and teams are described as another level, even compared to Gold-ranks.
A Gold-rank adventurer is described as someone who might be close to Named-rank, with only one thing, or recognition, holding them back.
Even Named Adventurers might walk into the large Adventurer's Guild at Invrisil, and its Guildmaster was part of a Named-rank team without being a Named individual himself.
Named-rank teams could be as powerful as a Named-rank person, though their individual members might not be as formidable.
Saliss of Lights is a Named Adventurer and is Pallass's only permanent resident Named-rank adventurer.
Eighty thousand gold pieces were said to be enough that one might think about becoming a Named-rank adventurer by outfitting oneself with it.
A bounty notice rated Belavierr a Named-rank threat and compared her kill of elite [Hunters] and a [Knight] to a Named Adventurer and a Named-rank team.
Selys thought a particular artifact looked worthy of a Gold-rank adventurer, maybe even a Named-rank one, before she knew what it really was.
Farmer Lupp told Ryoka that a former [Farmer] became a famous adventurer who fought in the Second Antinium Wars against the Goblins and ended up in a Named-Rank team.
Sharphorns are the new, untested young [Warriors] of the House of Minos, in contrast with the veterans whose horns are decorated.
Of the House of Minos's army, four thousand [Warriors] were new and two thousand were complete veterans.
The Sharphorns' horns are plain white ivory, and they are green [Warriors] who have seen few battles but are at least Level 16.
The Sharphorns trained for the battle against the King of Destruction and were sent to win the King of Minotaurs' victory alongside the veterans.
General Ozem called the veteran Minotaurs the House of Minos's failures who could not live in peace, and told the young Sharphorns to look at the King of Destruction and not scorn him.
When Ozem advanced the Sharphorns alongside the Axebearers, who were all Level 30 or higher, Reim's momentum stopped.
A quarter of the Sharphorns had fallen by the time Ozem ordered the retreat to the ships.
Ozem ordered the Sharphorns to drop armor, secondary weapons and shields so they could outrun horses, valuing them for their future.
The Black Tide is the name used for the Antinium swarming forward in force; guardsmen in Liscor shouted that the black tide marched when Antinium appeared in the streets.
In the history of the Antinium Wars, the Black Tide is the Antinium army, which swept across Izril as it had across Rhir and which put cities under siege.
Zel Shivertail was hailed as 'Tidebreaker' because his army repeatedly withstood the Black Tide.
Klbkch ordered his Hive to call the Black Tide when he learned a Goblin and Human force was marching on Liscor.
The Antinium are called the Black Tide of Izril, and they are seen politely eating ice cream at the gathering in Erin's inn.
A Reinhart house head watching a vast horde of Antinium thinks the Black Tide is reforming.
Tiered Magic organizes spells by tier, in contrast to the undisciplined magics.
A spell that a mage below Level 16 can cast is generally called 1st Tier or 0 Tier Magic, one up to about Level 24 is 2nd Tier, and up to Level 32 is generally the bar for 3rd Tier.
Ryoka is told of a friend of the speaker who can cast [Restoration] and other 4th Tier spells.
Ceria says she cannot cast [Fireball] and uses a wand for it, but knows [Ice Spike], which is Tier 3.
Ceria says [Detect Magic] is Tier 3 as well, and the [Haste] spell Ryoka wants is Tier 4, or perhaps Tier 5.
Ceria says she can cast Tier 3 magic at best, and that Tier 4 would need a spellbook and weeks or months of study.
Ceria says Tier 3 magic is good for fighting, [Ice Shard] is Tier 2, and she would call [Light] Tier 0 and [Spark] another example of it.
Ceria says Pisces knows one Tier 4 spell, [Invisibility], which took him at least two hours of study every night for a month.
Xrn thinks of the Antinium of the present Hives as poor copies of true Antinium who will never know the grandeur of the true Hives.
The Free Queen judged Garry, Anand, Belgrade, Pawn and the fifth Individual to be not true Antinium, because they failed her test.
Klbkch thought of the Individuals as strange new Antinium who were not True Antinium but more than the half-made Soldiers and Workers the world knows.
The Free Queen said she would rather have created True Antinium than Individuals, because Individuals shape the Hive but True Antinium are all Antinium.
True Antinium were linked, both broadcasters and receivers, unlike the tenuously held half-Antinium drones the Queens make now.
An army of True Antinium Soldiers moved as one being, thought with a thousand minds, and could outmaneuver armies of Soldiers by coordinating over long distances.
The Free Queen said True Antinium could work through a Unitasis Network, which the few remaining Queens formed again during the First and Second Antinium Wars.
Klbkch told Soldiers that in the past, a dying Antinium was remembered by all, and that he is one of the last True Antinium, remembering all of them.
In ages past Klbkch could communicate with another True Antinium a hundred miles away with ease.
Klbkch remembered that the Free Queen argued against making new forms and called only for rediscovering how to make True Antinium and for creating Queens.
The Free Queen said that Xrn, Klbkch, Wrymvr and the remaining Queens remember the True Antinium, from Rhir.
Calvaron tells new students that Wistram is not one unified place but divided into factions, and that mages either band together or go it alone depending on their personalities.
There is no formal ceremony for choosing a faction, and Calvaron advises students to tell no one if they join one.
Calvaron says most mages do not care about new students, and only the Expansionists and Revivalists are interested in ensuring there is a system.
Calvaron points out a small group of Isolationists, who would prefer that Wistram stop accepting new mages and let aspiring mages find their own way there.
Beatrice is a Revivalist, part of the faction that thinks Wistram should throw open its doors and usher in a new era of magic like centuries past.
Calvaron says he himself is undeclared, at least for now.
Almost any powerful mage belongs to one of the major factions that control Wistram's Council or is allied to one of the big players.
Feor belongs to the Centrists, and also keeps a personal group of half-Elf mages he trusts.
Welaiat is a Libertarian, and Failess is a Preservationist.
Montressa du Valeros says she is a Revivalist too, and Beatrice is also called a Revivalist.
Yellow Rivers is a new disease that Quallet reports to Geneva as one of the new ones, which he thinks is called Yellow Rivers.
Two Human men in Quallet's care caught a severe infection at a brothel in the last town, and one used a healing potion on it, after which it hurt much more.
The infection is on the men's genitals, Quallet calls it the worst case of it he has seen, and he has kept the men isolated as Geneva advised.
Niers Astoragon reads a report that the Last Light of Baleros is treating Yellow Rivers victims, and concludes that it spreads through brothels and armies in major cities.
Niers suspects the sickness has multiple ways of being contracted, because two children are being treated for it, and fears a magical plague like the Sporepits Plague, in which millions died.
A broadcast reports six cases in Pallass and over a thousand in Zeres, mainly from ships, and says the illness is not spread solely by intercourse.

Geneva says the disease is bacterial, not viral, and that the mortality rate if treated is not high, but it provokes fevers and diarrhea, which are killers where clean water and medical treatment are lacking.
Geneva calls it airborne and mutated.
Geneva would hold a quarantine without a cure and would advise city leaders to expect a 20% mortality rate.
Quallet says that anyone who comes down with the sickness cannot use healing potions, which just make the rash worse very quickly.

Geneva considers it a distinct possibility that the infection is partly magical, in which case she could not stop it, and she treats her two patients by cleaning the infections, bandaging them and giving them an antibiotic treatment based on the [Healers]' recipes.
Paige says that the Yellow Rivers patients are growing in number, that Geneva fears an epidemic, and that the bacteria have mutated across all of them, so it is not just spread by sex now.
Geneva shows Paige a petri dish of the Yellow River strain that she cultured from her own infection, which proves it is bacterial because a virus would not survive in dead matter.
Geneva needs a broad-spectrum anti-bacterial agent, with penicillin as one example.
Geneva drops a single drop of a weak healing potion onto the culture, and the bacteria instantly cover the whole dish.
She explains that using a healing potion turns a small infection into an open sore and a preventable illness into full-blown fever, diarrhea and pus that infects anyone who does not wash their hands.
Within three more days the disease lands in First Landing, Lailight Scintillation and two Terandrian ports, and it becomes a true pandemic spreading by sea and land.
Demon soldiers are fighters of the Demons, and one wears leather armor and has a strange, half-melted-looking face.
A Demon soldier has a face like leather, two horns curving downwards and bright green eyes.
A Demon soldier has no whites in his eyes, only green sclera with yellow diamond-shaped pupils, and cloven feet.
The narrator finds himself standing in a ring of dead Demon soldiers, and the last one flinches when the narrator turns to him, and he dies with the word "Monster".
A Demon soldier with a bloody sword slashes the Fool's belly open, picks up a key near a second gutted body in armor, unlocks the door the Fool was guarding and rushes in at Princess Erille.
A second Demon soldier with two knives attacks the narrator, and they fight on the floor of the room.
Gargoyles are stone monsters that hide among rocks in the High Passes and were named as the most prevalent type of monster there.
A gargoyle looks vaguely like a bird crossed with an ogre, with a curved beak-mouth and skin that looks like stone but moves like flesh.
Gargoyles unfurl massive stone wings; they cannot really fly, being heavy, but they can angle a leap from a cliff to land like bombs.
Gargoyles spit stone fragments that cut like shotgun fire, and their roar makes rocks tumble down.
Ryoka ran into a nest of gargoyles in the High Passes while wolves and goats chased her, and the gargoyles tore the goats apart and ate them.
Gargoyles have a sense of smell: they retreated from Ryoka after she covered herself in a terrible stench.
The Redfang Goblins lure Gargoyles by tying an Eater Goat to a pole, and they fight Gargoyles in the passes.
The Redfangs plan to push Gargoyles out of territory in the High Passes as part of their expansion.
A man named Ambriel said Gargoyles followed Eater Goats and troubled his sister's village near Orefell, eating half a flock, and Ylawes said the Adventurer's Guild had a bounty on them.
Six Gargoyles attacked Falene, Dawil and Ylawes; they were huge, as tall as small trees, with sensitive eyes and orange-red blood.
Hobgoblins are Goblins that enter a sudden growth spurt, begin eating twice their weight each day, and grow constantly until they are as tall as Humans and in some cases twice as wide.
The Goblins who become Hobgoblins are Chieftains or Goblins stronger, faster or tougher than normal.
Hobgoblins are the leaders of tribes, the shock troopers of a Goblin group and the only way Goblins can take on deadly monsters.
Most Goblin tribes have around one Hobgoblin, and the Flooded Waters tribe's single Hob was their Chief until Erin killed him.
Rags has leveled as much as any Hob but has not grown bigger, which sometimes happens.
In the attack on Durene's village a Hobgoblin, round and made of muscle and taller than anyone but Durene, smashes the wooden barricades with brute strength and cuts down a Celestial Tracker.
The Hobgoblin fights Durene with a sword and a shield and moves with trained grace, and he wounds her deeply on the side and along one breast.
Durene lets his sword bite into her left arm and shatters his shield, arm and head with her club, killing him.
Klbkch says Listeners are a specialized breed of Antinium developed within the Hive that can listen to movements and sounds at extreme range and, given instructions and time, monitor individuals.
Klbkch says a few Listeners were allocated to his Hive, that their existence is not a secret, and that they were revealed during the Second Antinium War along with a few other types.
Klbkch says only Soldiers and Workers are allowed within the Hive in Liscor.
Klbkch tells the Queen that Listeners to the south report a group of Gnoll warriors of the Silverfang Tribe heading toward Liscor, led by a high-level warrior.
An Antinium Listener is a rare subtype of Antinium used by the Hive, built only to listen to sounds, and can pick up a conversation five miles away in a quiet room.
Listeners have short lives because their sensory organs overload and they die, quickly even for Antinium.
The Listeners' scrawls record conversations in full, along with marching feet, animals, magic and underground water, and Klbkch scans them each day.
Manticores are monsters grouped with Goblins, Trolls and Dragons as mindless, vicious killers, in a description of how monsters differ from Demons.
Manticores are part lion, part scorpion and part bat, can fly despite being five times as large as lions or larger, and have a stinger with lethal venom.
Manticores are named as the typical monster of Chandrar, as Wyverns are for Izril and Griffins for Terandria.
Teres judged Manticores to be above her level, and she was kept out of the fight with them.
A pack of Manticores had been troubling Belchan and Jecrass for months, and a Gold-rank team slaying a Manticore was the kind of thing Terandrians discussed.
Flos Reimarch, the King of Destruction, fought a hundred or more Manticores with his army's elites, who blasted them from the sky with magic and held the line.
Flos stopped a Manticore's charge on his shield, shoved it back and killed it with a blow to the head.
Zamea, a half-Giant thirty feet tall, punched one Manticore in the battle and the rest fled her.
Lyfelt said Flos might take the Manticores' hides and parts and leave the meat to feed his army, and Flos spoke of a feast of Manticores for the Nomads.
On Day 59 the bear that the Celestial Trackers found wakes up and charges into Laken's village at incredible speed, and the adventurers recognise it as a Mossbear.
Arrows bounce off the Mossbear's fur, and Wiskeria's fire spell and thrown stone shards fail to stop it because of the thick, wet fur.
The Mossbear is easily three times as large as the biggest warrior in the village.
A patch of the Mossbear's fur near the nape of its neck is missing, and Durene and Laken judge from the lack of blood and the neatness of the cut that it was no accident.
Later, Wiskeria's emergency spell calls the Mossbear from its cave, which is the reason she had wanted its fur.
The Mossbear charges the Goblins from behind, smashes one flat and bites another.
The Mossbear leaves after eating some of the dead Goblins, possibly wounded but not deeply.
Rock-crabs are giant land crustaceans that hide under a rock-like shell, shuffle at prey, and make loud clicking sounds; the name Hollowstone Deceiver is what local people call them.
Rock-crabs have two enormous claws and a pair of dark antennae that may be their eyes, and are longer and more elongated at the back than a round crab.
Rock Crabs are immune to most acid, according to Erin's reckoning, and she thought one could level her inn.
Erin threw a seed core at a rock-crab's antennae, and it panicked, scraped at its antennae and made a loud cricket-like noise while Erin retreated.
Erin later pasted two rock-crabs with the slimy seed cores, and they retreated with loud clicks.
A rock crab at her inn swiped at Erin and tried to grab her head, and she smashed it with a chair; Goblins hunted and ate one, ripping the shell apart for its entrails.
Selys warned that a Hollowstone Deceiver sneaks up on adventurers outside, is silent in the rain, and hunts aggressively in spring.
A baby Rock Crab uncovered by Relc outside Liscor was twice Mrsha's size when newly born and had no rock shell yet; the rainy season let Rock Crabs spawn a brood.
Six rocks stood up and stalked seven Earthers in the Floodplains, while Gnoll [Hunters] normally avoid the telltale rocks; the Earthers did not know they were Rock Crabs.
Erin drove the crabs back with seed cores, but they turned on her when she ran out of cores, and her aura failed to keep a crab away.
Bird shot a [Ricochet Arrow] from the tower through a crab's exposed antennae, and Halrac's glowing arrow detonated under another crab's shell, killing it.
Ceria raised ice walls, a [Shatterbolt] broke a shell, Ksmvr fired crossbow bolts, and Grimalkin punched a third crab; Typhenous's orb finished it.
The three remaining Rock Crabs fled from the inn's defenders.
Jelaqua says Selphids are a species that find dead bodies and inhabit them, a kind of parasite or body thief, which is the only way they can live.
Ceria explains to Erin that Selphids could rudely be called parasites.
Jelaqua is a Selphid inhabiting a nearly albino dead body, and she shows Erin the writhing dark green and yellow creatures with thin tendrils inside her chest.
Jelaqua says Selphids do not inhabit living people as a rule, take on the attributes of their host, and can change bodies if one gets damaged.
Jelaqua says healing potions do not work on dead flesh.
Geneva Scale finds a Selphid stretched through a dead man's nervous system, a green wriggling mass of tendrils wrapped around his organs.
The Selphid is semi-fluid, so stitches would be as useless as trying to block water with a net, and it bleeds a viscous orange liquid.
Geneva cauterizes the Selphid with hot metal, which makes it shriek, and the bleeding stops.
A soldier tells Geneva that Selphids are body-snatchers and parasites that live in corpses and move them about, and that "Selphids aren't people".
After Geneva puts the Selphid into a dead woman's body, the woman's skin turns totally white and the right half of her body sags as if from a stroke.
The Selphid names herself Okasha, a Level 23 [Rogue] of the Burning March 6th Division, and says it takes Selphids time to assume control of a new form.
Jelaqua slithers out of Moore's open wound into a Raskghar's body, begging the others to say they saw nothing, and Bevussa promises that no one will tell.
Pisces understands that invading a living host, willing or not, is the height of Selphid sin.

The Antinium Wars, also called the Incursion Wars, were two wars between the Antinium and the Drakes, Gnolls and Humans of Izril; Ceria recalls hearing frightening stories of them even though she was not on the continent.
Krsysl Wordsmith wrote the history of the First Antinium Wars, saying Izril survived two wars with the Antinium and that the peace had lasted nearly a decade when he wrote.
Before the war, the Antinium were driven out of Rhir in the year 5 B.F. after the Blighted King's armies shattered; only four ships of some two hundred greatships reached the south-west of Izril.
Krsysl Wordsmith calls the Antinium's underestimation of the sea their one real mistake, because it cost them nearly their whole fleet.
The Antinium hid for months, attacked patrols around the port city of Nasserous and the highlands, and were first identified when a Gold-rank [Ranger] brought four corpses to a guild.
Leaders of the Walled Cities argued for nearly a month over whether the Antinium were in Izril, and only a few notables such as Lady Magnolia Reinhart, Lord Tyron Veltras and General Sserys knew.
About six and a half months after the landing, fifteen villages and a small town were destroyed in a single night.
In less than two hours the Antinium killed or maimed over 80% of the population of each of three attacked cities, and the Drake cities then fell to raising separate armies instead of one.
Drake armies adopted a standing policy of never putting more than one Level 30+ soldier in a squad, because Antinium tunnelling raids targeted concentrated high-level units.
The Antinium besieged the Walled City of Zeres after taking nearly thirty percent of the southern half of Izril, and were rebuffed with heavy casualties.
Sserys unified the Drake cities and secured a non-aggression pact with the Gnoll Tribes, and was named High General of the war.
Magnolia Reinhart worked as a diplomat holding the Human allies together; her sword from the fight at the Liscor pass is displayed in her mansion.
The Drakes, Humans and Gnolls formed the Southern Alliance, which pushed the Antinium back until the Queens answered with a second offensive that used the Prognugators.
