Nine months into the war, the allies discovered that the Antinium cannot swim and drown, after Antinium were drowned in a valley by a [Rain] spell.
Sserys led the First Unified Army against the main Hive nearly a year after the war began, despite Zel Shivertail's objection, and the army vanished overnight.
Sserys died in the attack; his diary and corpse were found in the encampment, and the diary said a new breed of Antinium was hunting his army.
The First Antinium Wars ended with an accord signed by the Walled Cities, the Antinium Grand Queen and the Human coalition led by Magnolia Reinhart.
Klbkch said the Antinium Wars were setbacks, and that the true disaster for the Antinium was losing their people on the oceans.
Klbkch explained that the Antinium types other than Soldiers and Workers were revealed during the Second Antinium War, but that only Soldiers and Workers are allowed inside the Hive in Liscor.

The Second Antinium War overlapped with the war against a Goblin King and the Necromancer, and began with a Drake army besieging an Antinium Hive at the Jessal Highlands; Krsysl Wordsmith's history of it opens in the year 13 A.F.
Klbkch and Xrn recall that the Drakes flooded the besieged Hive with rain, and the history says the Antinium freed the youngest Queen, who later led the Hive in Liscor.
Wrymvr the Deathless, the Flying Antinium and the Silent Antinium were deployed against the Drakes in the Second Antinium War.
Xrn said the historian exaggerates but does not invent events, and that the Goblin King's forces under Tallis Stormbreaker destroyed her army.
The war ended in a peace treaty with the Grand Queen after Klbkch's Antinium helped Zel Shivertail kill the Necromancer at Liscor; Zel and Klbkch then fought each other.
Five adventuring teams assemble before the dark doors at the head of the expedition: the Horns of Hammerad, the Flawless Flight, Kyrial's Pride, the Circle of Reneë and the Silver Spears.
Every adventurer in the crowd is Silver-rank.
Cervial says that, counting the extras, the five teams are over forty people strong and all Silver-rank.
Gerial says the expedition has enough supplies for at least four days and that he doubts they will be down there that long unless they need to do excavation.
Deep underground the expedition is ambushed when the walls slide open and the dead pour out.
Calruz kills a Crypt Lord with his [Hammer Blow] skill, after which the undead lose their controlling intelligence and the adventurers press them back until they are ground into paste against a wall.
After the battle Ceria says the adventurers will now get the treasure.
Every few years, sometimes once a decade and once for eight years straight, the Titan of Baleros announces a hide-and-seek game with his students, which never happens during war or unrest.
He takes his students to a location, whether a city, a patch of jungle or an artificial maze, and gives them a day to hide while an entire army searches for them.
Over a hundred students nearing graduation and some recent graduates hide, while the seekers are Niers's older [Strategists], his first students, who are veterans of dozens of wars.
The hiders try to fulfil a criterion that changes every year, and the seekers must capture them by whatever means necessary short of permanent bodily harm.
Students may fight back, set traps and form alliances, and some of Niers's soldiers carry clubs and nets.
Umina suspects the game is meant to teach students what it is like to be cut off from their forces and hunted, and that in practice it is also the Titan's way of having fun.
Wil Kallinad brought four warships from another continent to challenge the Iron Vanguard and held his own against Tulm the Mithril.
The Lizardgirl technically won, but the Titan of Baleros acknowledged Wil's feat and granted him the victor's prize along with her, the right to ask any one question.
Liscor's election replaces the current Council with a democratically elected group of eight for the next two years, with votes verified by magical spell.
Voters answer under a truth spell before voting, and the City Watch guards the ballot boxes in the streets.
Each district has at least two candidates, sometimes three or four, and the hottest debate is a split between Lism and Krshia, with almost all Drake and Gnoll candidates on each side.

Ulseil announces that the new Council by popular vote is Raekea Silversmith, Elirr Fultpar, Krshia Silverfang, Lism Swifttail, Alonna Swiftwing, Jeiss Sielmark, Tismel Lischscale and Zalaiss Holmfyre.
The Gnolls leap for joy and Lism's camp shouts, but the crowd goes still when they realise the seats were not allotted by district.
Ulseil explains that the Council chose the most popular candidates because no official backing was ever given to the proposed districts, and calls it the fairest distribution of seats.
Erin calls it cheating, and Lyonette answers that it is clever and the only move the Council could make.
The Sacrifice of Roses is the name for the slaughter of Izril's noble [Ladies] during the Second Antinium War, after they joined the front lines.

Until then the [Ladies] of the realm had refrained from fighting, but two weeks into the slaughter Magnolia Reinhart and every [Lady] in the city appeared on the front lines to lend their Skills against the Goblin King.
The [Ladies] went into combat with their personal escorts, and their combined low-level Skills let the Humans push back the surprised Goblins.
The Goblin King ordered his vassals to target the relatively undefended [Ladies], and the Goblin Lords led charges in person against them.
The Humans refused to run when death was imminent, and held their ground long enough for their soldiers to take vengeance on the Goblins.
One of the lesser Goblin Lords, Murmar, was confirmed slain as a result of the defence.
Over 60% of the [Ladies] who took to the front lines perished along with their escorts.
The Sacrifice of Roses became a rallying cry across Izril and is lauded as a defining moment of courage.
The Goblin King withdrew his forces after the loss of the first Goblin Lord, and the Goblin advance stalled for the first time.
Erin Solstice eats the blue fruit and makes blue juice from it.
Erin's guest tells Erin that the core of the Amentus fruit causes a painful death within hours if eaten, that the outer rind is safe to eat, and that the inner seeds are toxic.
Ceria identifies a blue fruit with a hollow seed pod as the core of the Amentus fruit and calls it highly poisonous.
Ceria says the seed cores are fine if unbroken but that the liquid should not touch skin, since even touching it could poison a person mildly.
Ceria says that eating enough of the liquid or the seeds would kill a person within the day, though not instantly.
Erin says she once got sick after accidentally squishing a seed pod while making blue juice, and insists the juice uses only the outer part.
Bags of holding have limits on what they can store, can break or malfunction, and cannot contain living things.
It is dangerous to carry multiple bags of holding on the same person.
A bag of holding delivers a dead Antinium drone made in the shape of a Queen, preserved in thick mucus, to the Free Queen.
Selys is warned to keep three bags of holding out of proximity and to finish quickly, because the stronger the enchantment, the sooner something happens when they are close.
Lesser bags of holding can be kept close together for a while.

After a Soldier dies, Pawn kneels by the paint he bought, dips a finger in bright green paint and draws on the hard-packed dirt wall of the Soldiers' barracks the star that was on the dead Soldier's chest.
Pawn resolves to repaint the star elsewhere if the wall is damaged, because he will remember it for the rest of his life.
The other Soldiers then paint their own marks without speaking, one for each of the twenty-five Soldiers who died.

The marks on the wall include a green star, a clumsy turquoise 7, a speckled egg, a snowflake, a black cat with orange eyes, the five numbers 46252, a smiley face, a stick-person with four arms, the word "Winter", a paw print, and a blade of grass.

By the time Pawn's barracks is changed, space has been cleared on one wall for a mural of the marks of fallen Soldiers, including a white paw print, eight lines and a curvy wave, and a golden quartet of stars.
Yellow Splatters recognises the patterns and feels that the wall is right, because it reminds the Soldiers who they lost.
A Soldier adds a white circle with a question mark to the wall by dipping a finger in white paint.
Erin receives a chessboard of gloriously smooth wood, with no pieces, that looks worth thousands of dollars in her world.
Erin says she sent out a hard chess puzzle and that whoever sent the puzzle in the first place sent her this expensive board in return.
Erin finds the board with ghostly, transparent pieces in their starting positions, wisps rising from them, except that a white pawn has moved up to e4.
Pisces guesses that the board is a duplication spell and a magically connected board.
The ghostly wisps follow the pieces as Olesm moves them, and the pieces are cool to the touch.
When Mrsha scatters the ghostly pieces, Lyonette resets the board and a piece on the other side moves, because the unseen player thinks she is Erin.
Lyonette plays on, loses a knight and a bishop, and the unseen player then eases off and plays more gently, and she wins the third game.
After the third game the pieces rearrange themselves, the white side is on the far end of the board, and no further move comes.

Niers Astoragon, the Titan, is shown sitting in front of a very small chessboard far across the world, musing that the mystery player is gone and that someone who knows chess but has barely played it has found the board.
The Diamond Swords of Serept are six blades, each forged by Serept of Khelt, and each shaped of a different coloured diamond.
Fetohep of Khelt calls them one of the true relics of this world and a great treasure of Khelt, each fit for a [General] or [King] of the old world.
One blade is a short curved sword, a mix of dagger and sword, made of black diamond that is transparent and lustrous.
Serept reigned for three thousand years before time consumed him, according to Fetohep, and no foe less than time humbled him.
Serept was a Smithing-King who forged crystalline artifacts as a motif, taken to extremes with the Diamond Swords, quartz armor and battleaxes forged from a single ruby.

Titan Niers Astoragon's list calls the swords a Kheltian treasure stolen from Khelt around two thousand years ago, and warns Wil not to take them but to message King Fetohep, since the curse may still be extant.
Fetohep says the chest and the artifacts are cursed, and that the curse consumed the thieves at sea so completely that they never uttered a word of distress.
Fetohep says his predecessor's fleets searched for the swords for hundreds of years without finding them.
When the students recover the casket, Fetohep appears as an apparition of sand above the ship, and offers them half of the six swords until their deaths, or else the curse of Khelt would engulf them.
Fetohep says that the blades shall return to him upon the holders' death, since in the sun they cannot escape his gaze, and any attempt to hide them meets the curse of Khelt.

Fetohep restates the bargain for the third time as three swords, which Wil may pick and share, and as Wil alone is granted the right to touch the blades, which otherwise carry a curse that seizes whoever touches them.
Fetohep tells Wil that he has the right of choosing, that each sword is different, and that he will return in a day for the answer.
Word spreads that the students have found the Diamond Swords of Serept, and soon everyone is aware of it.
Wil picks up a green diamond greatsword in the final battle, throws it to Venaz, and Fetohep names it the Windblade of Serpisel as Venaz clears the deck with it.
Rasea Zecrew reaches for a glowing blue blade among the swords, but Fetohep rises again out of the magical sand.

Fetohep later tells Trey Atwood that the swords were found by a group of students after a battle at sea and that he took a role in it as an apparition, since the ruler of Khelt can manifest through the swords' enchantment.
Fetohep says that each of the six swords has an unparalleled magical enchantment and that he granted half of them to the treasure seekers.
Fetohep says that he would have given the Pact of Temius, a blue blade, to the Gnoll and the Unfilled Cup of Cexila, a red blade, to the Minotaur.
Fetohep says that the Pact of Temius calls on the powers of nature and animals, while the Cup of Cexila drinks the blood of those it slays and heals the wielder.
Fetohep says the three remaining blades will return to him in time, though the carriers have been forced to take shelter at Zeres.
House Kallinad would pay for a relic-class artifact, one of the Diamond Swords, enough to buy a fleet of ships, and Captain Lasc and the surviving [Storm Sailors] were compensated royally.
Drowned Folk and [Mercenaries] hired by someone else try twice to take the swords from the three [Strategists] who carry them, and fail.
Feshi says that she holds a Diamond Sword of Serept, and her Gnoll tribe has come because of it.
Erin Solstice's magic door can teleport a person across a long distance, and the Horns of Hammerad gave it to Erin as thanks for funding their group.
After Ryoka's testing, the mages Typhenous and Moore calculated that the door could carry a person of roughly Ryoka's weight 536 miles, given minimal change in altitude or magical ambience.
The door exhausts its magic after such a teleport and needs roughly 8.2 hours to recharge fully.
Hawk the Courier sets up a second door in Pallass using an attuned stone from Pisces, and Erin's door opens onto the Walled City of Pallass for the first time.
Pallass tracks unauthorised teleports, and a [Commander] of Pallass arrests Jelaqua's party for entering by unauthorised spell.
Moore pries loose the coloured mana stone that Typhenous and Pisces attuned to the door, and the mages in Pallass report that the link between the doors is broken.
Later, Zevara tells Erin that Pallass is ready to open the door again after the Assembly of Crafts dropped its sanctions against Liscor.
Without recharging, the door has enough mana to send only two people through, so Zevara sets up a request form at the Watch barracks and clears travellers with Pallass by [Message].
Watch Captain Venim waits on the Pallass side of the door when it reopens, and the Pallass sky shows through the doorway.
A plain door set into Liscor's western wall opens onto Erin's inn; Klbkch opens it on patrol, calling for Miss Erin.
Lyonette must keep changing the door between Celum and Liscor by placing the matching mana stone on it, and a green stone selects Liscor.
Erin has to change the door every five minutes or less to let people in and out to Celum and Liscor.
Erin's door has a dial that selects its destination, and during the Creler crisis Zevara switches it between Pallass and the Bloodfields.
Pisces tells Erin the door cannot be made to move like a moving castle.
During the Creler fight at the Bloodfields, the door is still not open eight minutes in; when it opens, the workers, Palt and fleeing adventurers pour through while Crelers follow them into the inn.
Wailant proposes planting Sage's Grass in the middle of the Garden of Sanctuary to generate mana for the door, saying more grass means faster recharging.
The Emerald Signet is a galleon commanded by Captain Lasc, a [Storm Captain], and crewed by [Storm Sailors].
The Emerald Signet carries a crew of over three hundred hands, and the six students are passengers kept apart from the [Sailors].
The Emerald Signet was hired to help Wil investigate Niers' list and is specialized in recovering shipwrecks, among other things.
The ship is a good one with magical amenities to make a sea voyage more tolerable, though its hull is not ironwood and has only a few basic enchantments.

Wil Kallinad chose Lasc and the Emerald Signet because Lasc has traded with House Kallinad and Wil trusts him, and Lasc and the students are the only ones on the ship who know the voyage's true purpose of finding shipwrecks.
Captain Lasc is a tall man with a long cutlass, two ruby teeth and a tattoo like a magical rune on the back of his left hand.
Lasc often works for the Kallinad family, and is lean and young for a [Storm Captain].
Lasc's skill [Wavebreaker's Advance] drives the ship forwards so that its bow splits a colossal wave in two.
Lasc has a ship-speed Skill, and he can cast a [Ship Spell: Depth Explosion].
Lasc fights with a shortsword in his right hand and a metal gauntlet on his left, and with the gauntlet he knocks Venaz unconscious in a duel.
Delivan, the ship's First Mate, carries a sword and a miniature crossbow, and later swaps the crossbow for a wand.
Delivan has a [Dangersense], and Lasc asks him about it before approaching a wreck.
Delivan tells Wil that a [Storm Captain] on the sea has no use for armor, which would only make him sink faster.
The ship carries [Divers] with Amulets of Waterbreathing and nearly forty diving at a time, and uses a diving bell to lower men to the wrecks.
A Drowned Ship follows the Emerald Signet because, its captain says, everyone has heard the rumour that it carries a map of sunken treasure.
The Emerald Signet is attacked by slugs that prove to be parts of one giant jellyfish; Lasc steers toward its brain and the crew fights it off.
The ship flees a giant crab and a war golem guarding the wrecks, the golem firing a magical beam at it, and Lasc and Delivan steer it away from the isle.
Over two thirds of the crew draw blades in a mutiny, saying that they have been keeping their real employers updated, and fewer than a hundred loyalists, including Inky, stand with Lasc.
Lasc orders the mutineers put over the plank or shot, and tells Wil they must move because the ship is being scried.
The Errant Traveller is a tall, two-masted ship berthed at South Harbor in the city of Belan, a southern port-city of Terandria, that carries would-be students to Wistram.
The ship's [Captain] checks passengers against a paper bearing a lifelike printed portrait of each person's face.
Below decks the ship has portholes and, instead of hammocks, small cots with pillows and blankets.
The Captain announces that the trip will take two days if the weather holds, with three meals a day, and that passengers who go above must stay out of the sailors' way.
The Captain forbids any magic on his ship and threatens to throw offenders overboard or cut down anyone who draws a blade, lords or not.
A Selphid guard warns that an Evercut Arrow cannot be removed without opening the patient up, and that shaking the wounded person will make it cut through his insides.

The Roving Arrow company began using Evercut arrows a few days before Geneva meets the wounded man, and the arrows lodge inside and keep moving, slowly digging through organs and preventing healing until the patient dies.
The Evercut arrowhead Geneva finds inside the wounded man is a tiny piece of moving orange metal.
Talia recognises an Evercut Arrow in a triangular shard of an Ogre Chief's club that has broken off and lodged in Ser Eldein's chest, a weapon that healing potions cannot fix.
Eldein declares himself mortally cut and asks to die standing, and an Ogre's mace crushes his helmet and shoulder.
Faerie flowers are small yellow flowers, much like short dandelions with more exotic petals, that Erin Solstice received from faeries in place of gold.
Erin realizes that the faeries tricked her with flowers instead of gold, as faeries do in the stories.
The flowers are golden and soft to touch, and Ceria expected gold before realizing it was a trick.
Erin tastes the nectar gathered where the petals meet, which is tasteless but fizzes on her tongue, and she shrinks until the room towers above her.
Erin calls the flowers Alice Flowers after the drink in Alice in Wonderland, and she is shrunk for the better part of an hour.
Ceria senses the same tingling in her mind from the flowers that she gets from the Frost Faeries.
Selys confirms that Erin thought the faeries had paid her in golden coins, and the narrator explains that faeries trick people into accepting gold that turns to flowers or disappears the next day.
Lyonette knows the flowers can be made into a drink, and the adventurer Halrac paid gold for it.
Erin has worried about the Faerie Flower drink's power after seeing its effect on Halrac and Ilvriss.
While Erin is away, her potted golden flowers wilt, and Lyonette throws a dead flower into the fireplace and wakes on her back after coughing on its acrid smoke.
Later, yellow Faerie Flowers grow in boxes along the inn's windowsills, which Mrsha waters every morning with one cup, and Lyonette uses a few each week to gather honey.
Apista the Ashfire Bee seems addicted to the tiny flowers and laps at them with her tongue.
Over the months since winter the flowers have multiplied and now fill eight planter boxes.
Xif the [Alchemist] examines the flowers, says they all lack the characteristics of full-grown plants such as reproductive elements, and that he believes they are not fully grown.
Erin realizes that the flowers are just stalks with blooms on the end, with no root system and no ovules.
Firebreath Whiskey is a strong spirit imported from Izril, and the Drakes' signature drink.
Olesm considered Firebreath Whiskey offensive, hard to tolerate in large doses, and usually the prelude to a fight if drunk too heavily.
Erin described the taste as like habaneros poured into a sock and mixed with mouthwash, and said it was the only strong drink she had in stock at the time.
The Drakes treat it as a proper Drake drink, and Ilvriss demanded it at Erin's inn, drinking shots of it.
Erin cut Ilvriss off from Firebreath Whiskey after he arrived drunk and drank a full mug.
Erin kept a whole keg of Firebreath Whiskey at her inn and called it nasty.
Venaz drank Firebreath Whiskey by the mug, which Umina noted was a Drake favourite and expensive.
Drassi told Kevin that Firebreath Whiskey was the cheapest strong drink on offer, and Maviola grabbed a pitcher of it as the most potent drink at a table.
A cocktail called Chaldion's Eye mixes Firebreath Whiskey with an Ultasian bitter made from the Ultasa flower and lime.
Erin Solstice makes the first hamburgers in Liscor, frying patties of Krshia's ground beef with pepper and egg, and serving them with a bun, lettuce, tomato, cheese, mayonnaise and ketchup.
Erin makes the ketchup from tomatoes and the mayonnaise from egg yolk, mustard, lemon juice and vinegar, using recipes Ryoka gave her before she left.
After the burgers run out, Erin makes french fries, and Relc declares he will eat at her inn every night if she keeps making the food.
Olesm tells Erin that shopkeepers and vendors in Liscor are already selling hamburgers the morning after, and that the only part they have not figured out is how to make the red and white sauces.
Healing potions are bottled green liquids that close wounds by speeding up the body's natural healing.
Healing potions are expensive; the Liscor Watch carries them for injured members, who are not supposed to use them unless someone is badly hurt.

Ryoka Griffin delivers fifteen healing potions and five mana potions in heavily wrapped bottles to the Hammers of Hammerad, and their leader Calruz downs a thick, syrupy green liquid from one of the bottles.
Klbkch's low-grade healing potion is a shimmering, emerald-green liquid in a corked bottle.
A healing potion tastes bitter and foul.
Poured over Erin Solstice's cut hand, the low-grade potion closes the wound in an instant without hurting.
After the potion, Erin's right palm is clean and unscarred.
Klbkch tells Erin that after drinking a healing potion she will be weak for at least a day but will recover in full.
A mage says healing potions suit only quick fixes and can leave bones fused the wrong way round or off-center.
Ceria says healing potions just accelerate the body's natural healing and cannot fix a break as complicated as Ryoka's leg, where only time or magic will do.
Ryoka reports being told that a stronger healing potion would grow each bone fragment out of her skin and destroy her leg beyond any healing.
A healing potion heals all of Ryoka's and Yvlon's injuries.
Selys says the potions are very expensive, and that the stronger potions carried by Senior Guardsmen heal most big injuries in a moment, short of losing an arm or other body part.
Klbkch calls the potion he gives Erin low-grade, and when Relc calls it a lesser potion of no worth, Klbkch asks whether he would have had him tell her the true value, which Relc accepts.
In Book 3 a young man named Thriss calls his potion weak and says the better type of healing potion gets rid of poison and other problems, but they have only cheap stuff.
Poured on a swollen shoulder, a cheap potion makes the swelling recede, though Geneva needs to add more before the flesh looks normal.
Geneva concludes from watching the potion that it accelerates the body's natural processes, closing existing tissue rather than creating new skin.

Geneva reasons that potions would probably do nothing for advanced breaks unless the bones were set properly, and that they cannot heal severed limbs and would inhibit reattachment if used incorrectly.
A first-person narrator in Book 6 says a wound can be healed in seconds in this world, but the pain means few can fight afterwards, and all but the best potions leave a drinker tired or nauseous.
The agony of healing can kill some people and the shock can stop a heart; the Fool's severed innards grow together and have to be pushed into his stomach before being healed.
Geneva states that potions do not cure diseases and instead accelerate a body's natural functions, which makes a disease worse.
Geneva claims that either a [Healer] finds a cure or the potions make a disease worse until it kills everyone it infects, so plagues are far deadlier in this world.
The Heartflame Breastplate is a national artifact and a symbol of the Drake people, mentioned in several stories and older myths.
It was thought lost two centuries ago, when General Ironscales, who held it, was slaughtered and her corpse disappeared.
Legends say the breastplate can stop an enchanted lance thrust to the heart and has never been broken.
Magnolia Reinhart gives Zel the breastplate, and her maid Ressa says the Reinharts did not know Regis Reinhart had acquired it until they asked.
Zel recognises the golden-red armor at once and learns that the Reinharts had it.
Zel unbuckles his own breastplate to wear it, and it burns on his chest and makes him feel warm and stronger.
Zel is wearing the Heartflame Breastplate, shining gold and red, in his casket when he lies dead.
Tekshia identifies the armor as the Heartflame Breastplate, and Zevara says the Reinharts had it and Magnolia gave it to Zel.
The breastplate is kept on a stand in a windowless meeting room, guarded by Relc and a mage, and Selys finds the warm metal gaudy.
Pisces notes that it is a breastplate that covers only the front, and theorises that this is because a fiery ward from the armor protected the wearer's back.
Selys remarks that "Drakes do not run", a saying coined by General Sserys.
Wall Lord Ilvriss returns the breastplate to Selys, and it is stored in the Watch Barracks until she finds a renter.
Zevara explains that Zel's will makes Selys the inheritor of the Heartflame Breastplate.
Erin wears a ring that Ilvriss gave her, which bears the single word "Salazsar" in golden letters.
The ring looks gold to Erin, but Lyonette says it is not gold, and Mrsha, Teliv and Pisces agree that it looks like copper, which Pisces calls polished.
Lyonette says she has never seen Erin wear the ring in her life, though Erin insists she wore it the day before.
Erin puts the ring back on before anyone can see the faint indentation of flesh it leaves, and later she notes that no one remembers her wearing it.

A Wall Lady tells the Administrator Alrric that one of the family rings broadcast an emergency signal from Invrisil, and as it was Ilvriss's ring, all his family and the Holders of the Wall were alerted.
Salazsar nearly sent a force out before learning the ring had activated in Invrisil.
Ilvriss admits privately to Alrric that he gave the ring to a woman because he thought she needed it, and says it is a mark of respect as well as nuptials.
Alrric understands that the rings have powers beyond sending an alarm, and Ilvriss says that the ring activating in Pallass could cause a massive incident.
Lady Magnolia Reinhart's carriage first appears as a dark green coach edged with gold, with black-painted wheels, pulled by two ghostly golden horses that shimmer with magical energy.
Later the carriage is large, ornamented with gold and old carved woodwork but painted eye-searing pink, and is pulled by four misty, semi-translucent horses that run faster than any living horse.
The carriage is almost soundless thanks to the heavy magic enchanting it, which lets it survive its speed and turn nimbly.
The driver Reynold can activate [Flying Wheels], which lifts the wheels off the ground and sends the carriage over obstacles.
Reynold uses [Featherfall] to land after the pink coach flies over a hilltop, and [Grounded Wheels] to give the wheels traction again.
Ressa tells Reynold that [Flying Wheels] wastes magical energy and that recharging the mana stones costs time.
The carriage runs on mana stones, which Reynold replaces from a pillow.
When a servant asks Reynold whether an Archmage invented the carriage, he answers "Apparently" and says the workings are all runes and spellcraft to him.
The two nearly spent mana stones he removes are a ruby and a perfectly cut emerald, among the most expensive objects in the world, and the Mage's Guild can recharge them in a week or more.
The pink carriage plows into the Goblins' ranks at hundreds of miles per hour, and its collision with Eggsnatcher's mount is tremendous.

Erin's magic door is an ordinary wooden door set into the wall of Octavia's shop in Celum, linked to a door lying on the back of a wagon, so that stepping through takes Erin from one place to the other.

Pisces affixed the anchoring spell to an actual door and harnessed the teleportation spell to create a portal, and Ceria says the door in Octavia's shop is only the anchor point while the real artifact is elsewhere.
The door drinks more mana than a sponge, can teleport people back and forth many times, and takes a long time to recharge once it runs out.
Pisces and Ceria could only recharge it enough for the Horns of Hammerad to make a one-way trip to the wagon, and they still needed a few mana potions.

Erin tells Ilvriss that her door can only go as far as Invrisil, around four hundred miles, and transport one person at a time with a day to recharge, as Typhenous and Pisces did not think the enchantment could be improved.
Erin says she needs to place an anchor at a place before the door can connect to it, so someone must run to Pallass or Invrisil first.
A speaker at the inn says the inn does not have enough mana to let the door transport more than one person at a time, and that those who come through must wait twenty-four hours.
Later, the door's destinations are Liscor, Celum, Pallass, Esthelm, and, on request, the Bloodfields, with the staff turning a magic dial every ten minutes to check it.
The door also has a setting for a red gemstone leading to the Goblin cave.
Erin says the door cannot send many people to Pallass, only two or four per day.
Hawk says that Erin added a Sage's Grass field so that the door can ferry as many as twenty people quickly and recharge fast, and that this could hurt Runners across Izril.
The link between the door and Pallass is damaged, and Pisces and Typhenous say they cannot restore the connection safely without sending a Runner to form another link.
Numbtongue finds Erin's magic door propped up beside the oars by the boats outside Liscor.
Numbtongue swaps Celum's mana stone for Liscor's to use the door, which links Celum and Liscor.
A work crew moves the door along the new road so workers can use it, and Eigusha goes through to fetch workers from Liscor; Erin says the city pays her, in reduced taxes, and the crews do not.
Invrisil's The Players' Retreat is linked to the inn's door, and about four hundred people with the six-silver passage fee queue to enter Liscor while a [Bouncer], Redit, holds them back.
Messenger Seals are proof of delivery for Runners.
When Ryoka delivers potions to the Hammers of Hammerad, she asks for their seal, a silver and copper token with a hammer on a mountain embossed on one side.
Krshia shows Erin a bowl of wooden triangles with red and gold patterns, saying she keeps the twin of each seal she gives out so she knows when a Runner has delivered.
A messenger must deposit seals to receive their reward, so a delivery without one is suspect.
Magnolia's seal is a token half gleaming silver and half semi-translucent cerulean, which the narration calls silver-and-sapphire.
Wealthier patrons treat seals as a sign of status; merchants and bankers use lesser gemstones, and the most elite have their own unique form of seal.
People without such means use simple cut stone provided by their cities at nominal prices, which is cheap but can be used to prove false deliveries.
Messengers who take goods and give false seals are not unknown; cases happen every year, so a Runner's reputation for honesty matters as much as speed.
A nali-stick is a concentrated version of sugarcane sold as a snack, made of many fibres, which gives a wave of sweetness after chewing.
Sugar is one of Baleros's chief moneymakers, and sugarcane grows on the continent above all else.
Fresh nali-sticks growing in Erin's jungle biome are hard to find, thin brown tubes with a terribly sweet white interior.
Erin finds a fresh nali-stick so sweet it nearly numbs her mouth and fears it could be addictive.
Palt says there are people who cannot live without a nali-stick a day, and that fresh ones are far sweeter than dry ones.
Embria says it is a pity they grow only in Baleros, as she could see using them in field rations.
After the door to Pallass reopens, crowds of Drakes pass through the inn, waiting for Erin to switch the connection between Liscor and Pallass.
Erin says the door will stay open to Pallass for the next six hours, held by [Mages] who rotate in shifts on both sides.
Erin is hiding Hobgoblins in her basement that day, right after Zel Shivertail's funeral.

A weary [Mage] on the Pallass side announces that they will not recharge the door again, and that tomorrow access will be cut to two visitors per day, with no [Mages] available unless the [Innkeeper] or guests pay for them.
During the Creler crisis the door flickers open to Pallass about forty-seven minutes in, and Grimalkin steps through to the inn after Zevara switches the dial.
Grimalkin leads an advance party of Gold-ranks and Wing Commander Embria's best through the door to the Bloodfields on his mark, at about fifty-nine minutes.

Later, the Pallass end of the door has been moved into a chamber with a miniature steel portcullis and eight [Guards], half of them with bows, and the [Guards] call out "Two to Liscor" before raising it.
The [Guards] say the security is mandated by the Assembly of Crafts, and a Drake apologises that the portcullis stays.
The Bloodfields setting of the door is now on a hill far from the Bloodfields, and Lyonette has ruled that the door is not to be opened unless people with combat Skills are present.
A Potion of Youth can make even the oldest of people young for a short time, and a vial shone with pure magic.
Saliss of Lights makes the Potion of Youth and Onieva delivers it; Chaldion said Saliss often fails at making it, and the world was abuzz with people ready to pay far too much for one.
Saliss reckoned a Potion of Youth could earn him hundreds of thousands of gold coins, or tens of thousands at least, depending on the market.
Maviola El said Saliss can restore even someone as old as her to a young body for a while.
A contested Potion of Youthfulness, certified authentic by Xif of Pallass, was sold at an auction for about eighteen point four thousand.
At an auction in Pallass, the Potion of Youth drew everyone's attention, and the bidding was fierce.
Rie Valerund did not bid for the Potion of Youth, and on learning who bought it asked what Reinhart needed with another potion.
Maviola El held three vials of Potion of Youth that she bought with her own money, each lasting a week.
Saliss made a different Potion of Youth with Octavia's help, which cost a fraction of the usual ingredients, differed in colour, and gave Maviola El true youth; he gave it to her for free.

Lady Magnolia's food shelves carry tiny etched runes on every cupboard, which Ryoka Griffin identifies as preservation runes; Magnolia says she paid for the best preservation spells and has an [Enchanter] check that the runes are holding every year or so.
Mages charge very affordable prices for such runes, and most inns and some larger shops use them quite often.
Erin Solstice wishes she had preservation runes, and Pisces told her fancy runes would cost twenty to sixty gold coins and require replacing her cabinets so the runes stay intact.
Erin cannot afford the runes on her limited funds of just under ten gold pieces.
In Book 7 preservation runes on a lid keep a body from decomposing.
In Book 10 a Drake shows Erin glowing preservation runes on the floor of a meat store.

Octavia says that ten thousand years ago Sage's Grass did not exist, because a really powerful [Sage] bred the plant, and that after he died [Alchemists] all over the world rejoiced because it is cheap, magical and a strong ingredient.
Octavia notes that Sage's Grass water is cheap around Celum because a man named Wailant grows it, and that it is harder to get elsewhere.
Sage's Grass glows red when planted in the meadow, and Wailant and Viceria have planted it.
Montressa and Wailant note the ambient mana of a Sage's Grass field, which Wailant says will do more than fill the door, even if most of it goes there.
Viceria uses the field's mana to float Mrsha through the air with a spell, over the Sage's Grass.
Wailant says Sage's Grass dies if uprooted and that planting a field in the Garden of Sanctuary will generate mana to recharge the door for about six hundred gold.
A Silent Box is a perfectly black cube with a single door etched in pale silver on one side.
The Silent Box is a mage-prison developed by Wistram, a contained space like a very old and much more advanced Bag of Holding.
In Liscor a Minotauress among the Wistram group draws the Silent Box and tells Pisces to put his hands up and get in.
After beating Pisces down, Montressa draws the Silent Box and bends over him with it, and later a Minotauress tells Ceria's team that they put him in a Silent Box.
When Montressa lifts the box, the captured half-Elf turns into motes of black light that flow into the box and its silver doorway.
Beza passes the box to Montressa, and Montressa refuses to give it up, insisting that she keeps it.
Ulinde tells the onlookers it is just a prison and that the capture is legal.
Grimalkin explains that the box is like a Bag of Holding and not an actual dimension a person can walk into, so he only has to release the captives.
Grimalkin touches the door and it shines; he reaches in, or the box expands to fit his hands, and four figures lie on the ground, among them Ceria.
Grimalkin states that Silent Boxes preserve captives as they were, with time passing very slowly, so Pisces' injuries are fresh.
Night has fallen by the time the Horns of Hammerad are freed from the Silent Box, and their wounds have been healed.
Ceria Springwalker says a single spell book costs several hundred gold coins or even a thousand, even for low-Tier spells.
Ceria is saving up gold to buy a spell book that holds a few Tier 4 spells, since she has more or less mastered all the books she owns.
Klbkch states that most spell books are immune to conventional harm but that sufficiently powerful magic destroys them.
Teriarch says that not all spellbooks are simple repositories of spells and that some are written as instructional tomes to teach magic to those who struggle.
Teriarch says his own books contain many lower-class spells but are of higher quality in content and accessibility for those studying them.

Teriarch reasons that if the Silverfang tribe truly bought over forty spellbooks, they would have been redundant given how common low-level spells are, and that books cheap enough for one spell to destroy were probably personal references rather than proper instructional tomes.
When Mrsha opens a spell tome to a random page, the symbols shine into her head and speak there, instantly comprehensible rather than read as language.

Understanding the page gives Mrsha a migraine, and the first page she opens teaches her how to conjure a sword of stone out of the ground, a spell she thinks of as [Stone Sword] or [Blade of the Earth].
A second page teaches Mrsha the spell [Grow Grass], which makes magical grass last for minutes or possibly hours, and the spell burns itself into her thoughts.
Mrsha realizes the tome is far lighter than it looks and worth infinitely more than a mundane book, and that it is what the Silverfang tribe meant to offer at the Meeting of Tribes.
Laken's villagers build trebuchets from designs that Ryoka gave him, which he cannot read himself, and Prost says the design is simple and the size is the problem.
Laken says Ryoka could not remember how torsion siege weapons are made, so trebuchets, which are easier, are the choice.
The first trial broke the fulcrum.
On Day 80 a trebuchet arm breaks, though the shot knocks down a tree, and Laken recalls that Ryoka said the arm needed a ratio of 1:3.75, which is hard to put into practice.
Tessia fires a tiny prototype that sends a rock flying across the village.
On Day 98 a full-size trebuchet throws a stone of over a hundred pounds at least seven hundred feet.
Laken says a trebuchet is a piece of technology that needs no magic or class to operate, so anyone who understands how it works can fire it.
Tessia, one of the village's two [Engineers] and the highest-leveled, pulls the rope.
A trebuchet can be loaded with hand-sized stones that spray like a volley, and Laken tells Lord Tourant that enough trebuchets firing at once could take down a charging army.
The same trebuchet can be loaded with a heavy stone to knock down a wall.
Laken's two trebuchets bombard a Goblin city, firing a stone every ten minutes at most because the crews must pull back the arm, drag over a boulder and adjust the aim each time.
Rags observes that the Humans have bad aim, but the trebuchet that a Human female seems to aim hits the walls more often than the other one.
Yellats are orange, stringy and spicy vegetables that taste a bit like sweet potatoes when made spicy, and they are a staple of the Chandrarian diet.

Flos called Yellats a poor man's food, filling and easier to grow in Chandrar than any other plant, because they survive extended dry spells that would kill potatoes; other nations see them as a symbol of poverty.
Reim and Germina are described as hard lands in which to grow anything but the tough Yellats.
Yellats are cooked with grain in a simmering soup, fried, or served as pizza toppings, and are eaten with meat or bread.
Erin bought Yellats in Celum rather than Liscor because it was quicker.
Yellats are known as spicy red things in Baleros cuisine, served alongside blue tubers and other plants.
Prost asked Califor whether she was the woman who ran Yellats the length and breadth of the north after the 2nd Antinium War, and Califor did not deny it.
Flos pulled a large, fat Yellat from a pot, curled because it had no room to grow, and was highly amused.
Zel Shivertail personally dictated his will about eight years before his death, and it remains valid.
Zel divides his monetary wealth and lands among relatives, and his father is named first.
Tekshia and Selys are not named in the division of money and lands, as they are distant relatives.
Zel leaves his Aunt Tekshia the spears in his armory and any monetary investments or holdings he placed in Liscor.
Zel leaves whatever personal effects were on his corpse to his niece Selys Shivertail in hopes she will one day become an adventurer.
If those artifacts are lost to war or the circumstances of his death, Zel gives Selys a blade of her choosing from his armory and a sum of coins.
Zevara realises that this makes Selys the inheritor of the Heartflame Breastplate and any other artifacts he owned.
The words "Bury me with my love" in Zel's will are taboo among Drakes, and Selys thinks they were meant for General Sserys.
Selys and Pisces dig by night at General Sserys's grave, where she pours Zel's ashes beside his coffin and fills the hole in again.
Pisces does not know the word "Turnscale", and Selys confirms his guess about the meaning, saying no one knew about it and that she thinks Zel and Sserys were that.
pirateaba is the name under which the author signs the Author's Notes of the e-books.
pirateaba is described as an anonymous writer who has written ten million words in the ongoing web serial The Wandering Inn.
Less flattering rumors say pirateaba is three Goblins in a trench coat, a stupid artificial intelligence, or a creature with too many hands.
pirateaba likes to write, plays video games, eats popcorn with nutritional yeast and compares the readerbase to the endless quacking of ducks.
pirateaba's identity is anonymous at the time of the Book 11 note, and pirateaba has not attended any conventions.
In Book 2, Erin and Ryoka joke that "pirateaba" is obviously a fake name while drafting a petition.
In the same scene Erin and Ryoka argue over whether the author is a she, a he or an it, and settle on writing "pirateaba".
pirateaba says the author is better at writing new chapters than at revising, fixing typos and releasing the old volumes as e-books.
pirateaba says e-books also allow the audiobooks to be made.
pirateaba writes most days of the week, treating the story as something of a live production.
pirateaba says Book 7 was written without any support group beyond online typo-finders.
pirateaba says a team of beta-readers and editors has since developed to catch spelling mistakes and wrong names and to help with revisions.
pirateaba says finding people to help with the writing is the biggest change in the writing process over time.
pirateaba jokes about not having any handy Skills to level up as a writer.
pirateaba says that Volume 8 is over a million words long and could become eight books.
pirateaba notes that the narrator Andrea Parsneau does not want to record a single million-word audiobook.
pirateaba says nine books of The Wandering Inn correspond exactly to five volumes, split because a million words cannot be offloaded into one e-book.
pirateaba says Andrea Parsneau could not be made to read a million words in one go.
pirateaba is rewriting Volume 1 and writing Gravesong, whose audiobook should come out soon, alongside the serial.
pirateaba plans to rest for a month after the year ends, then come back to write more.
pirateaba says Book 12 was revised extensively to fix characterization and add gravitas, and the revisions took one month because of a scheduling mistake.
pirateaba thanks Diana Gill especially for helping to improve the story.
pirateaba likes [Witches] as a class and says the originals of the revised Book 12 chapters may go on the author's website.
pirateaba says the first week of a less writing-intensive schedule began in April 2024, meant to give more energy to write better.
pirateaba likes the cover of Book 13.

The company crossing the flooded plains toward Liscor is a hundred and twenty odd Drakes and Gnolls, all armed, armored and carrying their gear.
Wing Commander Embria Grasstongue leads it, with Captain Halliss.
All ninety-seven of the 4th Company are quartered in Liscor's barracks and use the Adventurer's Guild's practice area.
Four [Captains] are left in the 4th Company since the battle at Liscor.
A speaker told Ryoka that the Adventurer's Guild offers a copper piece for every four pairs of Goblin ears.

The Adventurer's Guild lets people report dangerous monsters in their area, post quests and offer rewards, while adventurers look at assignments on a large wooden board and collect their reward there.
The Liscor branch is a large hall that Erin first mistook for an inn or a bar.
The Liscor branch's patrons include grizzled Drake warriors, inhumanly tall Gnolls and several Antinium, with a few robed Drake and Antinium mages carrying staves or daggers.
Most Drake and Gnoll adventurers wear armour of varying quality, and one Gnoll wears real plate armour.
Relc said the Liscor Adventurer's Guild does not have many members, because few locals bother becoming adventurers when there is little to do around the city and fighters join the army or the Watch.
The guildmaster of the Liscor Adventurer's Guild is an elderly Drake with dusky purple scales, who is also Selys's grandmother.

When Erin asked for help for the adventurers trapped in the Ruins, Selys said no one in the Guild would go in after what had come out, and a Drake adventurer replied that the trapped should have saved themselves.
Selys offered Erin four silver for each Corusdeer antler and said the Adventurer's Guild sells them to [Alchemists] and [Blacksmiths].

The Adventurer's Guild demands a ten percent cut of the spoils from a dungeon raid or a particularly lucrative assignment; the Horns of Hammerad were surprised by it and paid rather than report the artifacts' value.
The Guild also takes a chunk out of every assignment it offers and earns money from referrals and its own products, but membership is free.
Adventurers are subject to the Guild's authority, and rules vary between Guilds, though a few are common to all of them.

According to Selys, any city with an Adventurer's Guild can demand adventurers' help in its defence in a crisis; an adventurer who refuses without good reason can lose rank or be expelled, and the city must compensate them.
Selys said a city collects a fee on artifacts recovered within its jurisdiction, and the Adventurer's Guild does as well.

Selys said the Guild pays bounties on monsters and parts, including unbroken Shield Spider shells, Raskghar, Lurkersnatch Fish, enchanted armour, slime cores, Dropbat teeth and Corusdeer horns, and that the city had put a bounty on the Raskghar.
Ceria says the Adventurer's Guild forbids using people's bones for undead, and Yvlon recalls Selys giving a list of species whose bones may not be used.
A Horns of Hammerad member complained that most Runners do not deliver to battlefields, some deliver only after the fighting ends, and those who do charge triple.
Ryoka heard adventurers whisper that a person with no levels might be a demi-human, a monster, a fool or cursed.
Erin objected that hiring adventurers to guard her inn would cost eight silver coins a day each, even for the lowest-level ones.
When Erin's Goblin guests were seen by three human adventurers, one grabbed his sword and a huge one said the Goblins were monsters and that he had lost good friends to them.
Selys said the Watch hired adventurers to clear giant rats from the sewers, a job that pays well but that no one liked.
One of the Horns told Erin that one of the rules all adventurers learn is not to touch magical objects unless you know what they are, since they might be trapped or warded.
A team member said that, with no truth crystals to prove what adventurers kill, they take proof such as a head, and that Liscor was not yet offering a bounty for monsters killed in the dungeon.

Older adventurers tried the team Vuliel Drae over a mistake in the dungeon that they had not reported, and Jelaqua and Ylawes offered to try to keep it from Liscor's citizens if the team told them everything.
Jelaqua said Gold-rank adventurers are tested regularly for corruption by the Adventurer's Guild and questioned under truth spells.
Snapjaw told Reiss that fewer than thirty Humans were in Tremborag's mountain, and Reiss asked if they were Gold-rank.
Adventurers set fire to a network of rope bridges and shot lava at another, sending hundreds of Goblins falling to their deaths.
Gold-rank teams hunting in the mountain left Goblins in black armour alone unless attacked, while killing other Goblins.
One of the adventurers recognised Garen Redfang and called him the team killer of the Halfseekers.
After the great spell faded, Jelaqua, Ylawes and Halrac chose to stay at The Wandering Inn a few more days.
The Horns, Griffon Hunt, the Silver Swords and teams like Bevussa's Wings of Pallass gathered at Erin's inn, and Jelaqua's team went first in a relay carrying a door north.
Posting in the chat as America Group, a speaker said they were a Level 26 [Knight] with companions including an [Assassin], [Pyromancer], [Beast Tamer], [Tactician], [Fist Fighter] and one [Clown].

The America Group said their summoning spell blessed them: all gained the [Hero] class on being summoned, and none had progressed it past Level 1 that they knew of, which seemed to make them level up faster.
The America Group said their group was in Karaz, a city on the Blighted Continent, where there were extremely dangerous monsters.
The America Group said they were a group of Americans from all over the continent.
This entry covers two separate bodies of people from Earth that the books call Americans: the group summoned to Rhir and the mostly-American Earth people serving in Gravetender's Fist.

The narrator says that around fifty people his age, about twenty, appeared in this world through a summoning spell in front of an old man on a throne, and everyone screamed that they were the "prophesied heroes".

Just over twenty of them are left, and instead of being the heroes of the Blighted Lands they are disgraces sent to garrison a village on the outskirts, barely acknowledged by the throne or the people.
When they first came to Rhir the king and court welcomed them with celebrations, feasts and parades until they realized the newcomers were not actual heroes, and then shipped them out to die.
They were brought back because some of them proved they could fight.
The narrator says over two thirds of their groups died in one night when they were sent to the front lines.
The twenty or so Americans summoned to this world ride together between the narrator and their escort.
The group has few electronics: Emily keeps a laptop that belonged to Reyanne, who died, Eddy has an Android phone, and Richard carries an iPhone.
They did not realize at first that they could [Repair] their electronics, and now they share them, except that Emily keeps the laptop.
Richard says he wants to talk to the others again but has not had another call from [BlackMage] and has no idea how to call him back.
Most of the people from Ken's world in Gravetender's Fist are American, Australian and European, and the Americans are the largest group.
Luan tells Aiko that the Americans say the job is bad and want to abandon the company, desert, head back to a city and sell their swords and armor.
Johanas and seven other Americans are caught sneaking through the forest and are made to kneel before a Dullahan with an axe in front of the two armies.
The eight kneeling Americans are executed, and Ken sees headless bodies and a red axe being wiped clean by a Dullahan.
Ken realizes in that moment that he can never go back.
Magnolia holds an [Assassin] named Theofore captive, and notes that the Guild's magical wards prevent him from speaking about it.
Magnolia says her contract with the Assassin's Guild had not expired when two of its [Assassins] lay dead in her room.
The Assassin's Guild in Izril is described as quite competent, and a man posing as a Guardsman warns Ryoka that a word to a Lord or Lady of the Wall might set it on Erin.
Lady Zekyria says Rhir has no Assassin's Guild of its own because infighting of that sort is too harmful, and Lord Yebior suggests contracting the Assassin's Guild on another continent.

A history of the Second Antinium War says the Assassin's Guild in the south of Izril treated the Silent Antinium as a threat to its way of life and put a universal contract on the Antinium's assassination insects, starting a quiet war in the shadows.

The same history says Magnolia Reinhart negotiated with the Assassin's Guild during the war so that her life and the Crown of Flowers would not be targeted, her first deal with the Guild, and that she employed [Assassins] widely afterwards.
Rookie recruits are the lowest rank of the Assassin's Guild, which numbers in the thousands, and possibly tens of thousands if it still has bases in southern Izril as rumoured.
A [Chevalier] judges the first assassins to attack Bethal's party as the first tier of Guild recruits, well armed because they were paid in advance.
The Assassin's Guild is expensive even for the richest [Merchants], and Ressa guesses the Ladies' attackers cost tens of thousands of gold.
At one attack on Couriers, the Guild sends its Faces rather than Ranks or expendable [Assassins], five in all.
The Assassin's Guild sends nearly a hundred of its weakest recruits against the Ladies as a message, and they die to guards and the Ladies' perfume and fans.
Magnolia says she does not have the Assassin's Guild at her back, and that if she moved openly to destroy a Guild free to choose its targets she would have to kill them all.
Magnolia reads the attack as the Guild's message that assassinations are open game and that it is not under her control, and she says Izril is now officially divided into sides.
An [Assassin] disguised as the inn's bartender breaks Lacel the Leaper's legs with a hammer, saying the Guild has a contract on him and that Magnolia Reinhart holds no sway over the Guild any longer.
The [Assassin] traces a sigil of the Guild in the air, and Typhenous and Eltistiman recognise it and lower their weapons.
The [Assassin] says this is a public statement and that the Guild is not abiding by Reinhart's laws.

Typhenous says the Guild accepted the bounty on Lacel to prove it will take contracts on Runners and operate in Invrisil, and that it used to be under Magnolia's control or at least she dictated whom it avoided.
Hawk learns that the Guild accepting contracts on Runners, in Magnolia Reinhart's own city, is known across Izril.
The Couriers reason that the Guild will leave them alone once they deliver the amulet, but that making the matter personal would be war.
In Lady Ieka's view, the Circle of Thorns stole the Assassin's Guild back from Magnolia and used it to murder some of Magnolia's fellow Ladies.
Tyrion Veltras knows Magnolia has lost control of the Assassin's Guild.
An [Assassin] tells Tyrion that the Assassin's Guild belongs to the Circle of Thorns and is only one part of it.
The Courier incident makes people aware that the Assassin's Guild is no longer Magnolia's.
A Guild [Assassin] with a mask threatens Tyrion Veltras, saying the Guild will burn down a city if it must, since his sons are already poisoned.
Five undead step out of shadow before Zel Shivertail and give their names: Venitra, Ijvani, Bea with Oom, and Kerash.
Venitra is a giant woman made of bone, in bone armor with a sword and shield and burning green eyes.
Ijvani is a skeleton of black bone in a [Mage]'s robes, with golden flames in her eyes and a staff.
Bea is a rotting female corpse, and Oom is a faceless humanoid figure in a trench coat and hat who stands beside her; Bea speaks for both.
Kerash is an undead Gnoll in armor with glowing blue eyes, taller than Zel, with a magic sword.
Zel recognises Ijvani's staff from Imenet, and the Necromancer says Zel encountered Venitra and Ijvani before.
Ijvani casts a [Blackfire Fireball].
Az'kerash treats the Chosen as his children and creations, and four of them are learning to fight, all below Level 10.
The Chosen have been granted the ability to level, which Az'kerash counts as true sapience.
The Bloodfeast Raiders are Izril's most feared [Raider] group; they strike north and south with no discernible pattern, have sacked Drake cities and turned whole Human towns to ash.
Nobody knows who the members are and no Bloodfeast Raider has ever been caught alive.
The members are all high-level and armed with powerful artifacts, and the bounties on them total hundreds of thousands of gold pieces without any of them being caught.
The group is described as new, and the Bloodtear Pirates have a standing objection to it taking their name.
The Bloodfeast Raiders have connections to Roshal, so that no one would catch a member, and they have an hour to wreak havoc.
A Runner's Guild notice warns that the Bloodfeast Raiders were reported operating out of the Gilliel Swamplands area two months earlier, though they had moved on.
Seeing a burnt village, a traveller asks whether the Bloodfeast Raiders hit another place.
Local bandits copying notorious groups do not dare call themselves the Bloodfeast Raiders, since the real groups are nasty to imitators.

One of the Horns recalls the bounty on the Bloodfeast Raiders as four hundred thousand gold pieces if the whole group or most of it is destroyed, eighty thousand for credible information on members or methods, and twenty thousand per head on top.
Masked marauders with a bloody mark on their masks burn a carriage with a [Fireball] near Celum and surround Ryoka Griffin, who recognises the Bloodfeast Raiders.
The Raiders wear dark clothing and masks with a bloody sigil, and some ride horses, one runs as fast as a Courier, and two ride a carpet.
Ryoka cannot hold on to how many Raiders there are or who they are, because each piece of knowledge about their identities fades from her mind as she looks.
The carpet-rider with a [Fireball] wand is the person Ryoka saw in a scrying orb and Fierre had pointed out.
A Raider plucks Ryoka's iPhone from her belt, and the Raiders find it expensive-looking but not magical.
The Raiders' leader gives Ryoka a head start of five minutes to warn Celum, and a Raider reads a scroll to remove the rain.
The Raiders use [Fireball] wands, a flying carpet, a bow, daggers and a spear, and a Raider's scroll of [Clear Weather] is said to be hard to get in pairs.
The Raiders hold a contest for the most kills, with the iPhone as the prize, and agree that kills count if they all see them or if heads are taken.
The Raiders destroy Celum for nearly an hour and leave, and reinforcements from other cities arrive only after they are convinced the Raiders have gone.
The Raiders ransack the Runner's Guild in Celum, taking packages and strolling out.
The Raiders celebrate afterward with captives and loot, and the Raider who killed the most people wins the iPhone.
The Raiders had always planned to meet at Celum and sack it, and the iPhone only attracted their attention to Ryoka.
Watch Captain Zevara of Liscor says Liscor's Council will support Celum and investigate claims that a Drake was among the Bloodfeast Raiders.
Eleven Raiders gather twenty miles outside Reizmelt, with two of them the same as last time, and are told to take Ryoka alive because two members are interested in her.
The oldest Raider receives a [Message] that Mihaela Godfrey is in Reizmelt, cancels the Bloodfeast, and puts a knife to the angry carpet-rider's throat when he objects.
The Raiders avoid people such as Tyrion Veltras or a Named Rank team or adventurer, and leave Reizmelt without killing anyone.
The Bloodtear Pirates are described as one of the most feared and dangerous [Pirate] navies in the world.
Five Bloodtear ships pursued Captain Gallheart's Waveblade through a storm for five days because it carried a treasure they sought, and three of their ships were lost to the waves.
The Bloodtear Pirates are cited among groups feared on the seas, alongside Midnight's Laughter, Wrymvr the Deathless and the Army of Texical.
A sailor said some pirate armadas kill every person they raid, like the Bloodtear Pirates, a savage armada, while others such as the Illuminary kill only those who fight back.
Seborn described the Bloodtear Pirates as marauders who keep their word but give no quarter, with a number of ships spread out in their armada, three being just an attack force.
A briefing held that The Gold of Paxil was probably sunk by the Bloodtear Pirates on an intercept course, and a captain's scroll reported an ambush by them in pursuit of The Emerald Signet.
A Screaming Sails sailor called the Bloodtears enemies of their crew.
The Bloodtear ships had sails filled with magical wind and were as fast as The Emerald Signet, perhaps faster, and they hailed no one.
The Bloodtear Pirates fought the Drowned Crews and each other's prey over the casket, and chased The Emerald Signet as it got away.
The Bodies of Fellden is the Selphid-only company and is called the largest Selphid company in Baleros.
Calectus, an [Honor Guard] whom Geneva and Okasha had parted ways with earlier, leads over two hundred Selphids who arrive to give Geneva aid.
Many of the Selphids wear fresh bodies, and some are members of the company while many are young Selphids who will become [Doctors] if Geneva teaches them.
Calectus says the Selphids will help manage the plague, since Selphids do not grow ill from most disease, and that they hope Geneva will help them in turn.
Fezimet worries when the company arrives, even though it is only a hundred and most are aspiring apprentice [Doctors] and aid workers.
The Bodies of Fellden, a small but elite company of Selphids, enter Talenqual to help Geneva and learn from her.
The Selphids also safeguard Geneva so that she can help them, and no one knows that.
There are over two hundred Selphids in Talenqual, all powerful, and Geneva thinks they are better allies than not.
Idis reports to Calectus and the other senior Selphids, and Geneva takes no part in their debate.
Marian and Umina learn that the Bodies of Fellden came to help Geneva and conclude from this that she has ties to the Selphids, calling the company serious strength.
In a private inn room, Calectus tells Okasha that she has gone too far, and that the Selphids see her.
Calectus says Okasha has committed the sin for which the Selphids were destroyed, that the Minds will sentence her, and he confines her in a holding-jar.
Calectus introduces Idis as Okasha's replacement, who says she is from the Minds, the Selphids' leaders, and offers to help Geneva move and to protect her.
Calectus tells Geneva that the company wants to learn from her, and that Idis will be their link and protector.
Idis overrides Geneva's voice to cover for Geneva, because Calectus said word about Geneva must not get out.
The Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings and the Sisters of Chell are underworld groups, the two largest local players in the region, and the Brothers have a reputation for being polite.
Four of the Brothers, dressed smartly and wearing rings that make people forget their faces, come to the inn, all [Thugs], and take part in the theft of the magic door alongside the Sisters of Chell.
The Brothers' leader says an intermediary of Erill gave them the job, whereas the Sisters say "Lady Spellcraft" gave them theirs.
A few months before, the Brotherhood's best Brothers in the region were contracted for a very expensive, sudden mission and died, and the Brotherhood wants to know what happened.
The Brotherhood also has a highly lucrative offer from the Tallman of Baleros, and has Brothers in Remendia.
An [Enforcer] says that if Numbtongue's actions were chance, the Brothers will not hold much of a grudge, though debts may remain.
The Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings are an underworld organisation of Izril with a reputation for being polite.
The Brothers and the Sisters of Chell were not the biggest underworld groups in Izril, but the two largest local players in the region by far.
A thug of the Brothers presented the group's regards, saying he was choosing his moment to help.
The Brothers' and Sisters' boats, driven by Skills, fled across the water past Liscor's walls, but a bolt of lightning exploded the Sisters' boat and threw the Brothers forward.
Niers Astoragon ordered a message sent to the Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings, offering a proposition and a gift of fine wine.
The Brothers wanted to know what happened to their group as badly as the Sisters of Chell did, and had a second motive in a very lucrative offer from the Tallman of Baleros.
A man in an alleyway said he represented the Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings and proposed an arrangement.
Wilovan is a member of the Brothers, and his untoward actions would not befit him.
Palt explained to Erin that the Gentlemen Callers are two big Faces who are part of the Brothers, a smaller but elite gang that are big players in northern Izril.
Wilovan said that as members of the Brothers they follow a code: if they prey on those with coin, it is never those down on their luck, never children, never decent sorts.
The Gentlemen Callers, as representatives of the Brothers, inspected two rooms at Erin's inn, and Erin thought they might not be good guys but were trustworthy to a certain degree.
The Bushrangers are the Silver-rank adventuring team of the United Nations company, led by Captain Daly, who chose the name so that anyone from home who knew basic history would recognise it.
They are Silver-rank through hard work rather than gear or levels; they all carry crossbows, mostly hunt, work in stealth and avoid melee.
Daly applies to become an adventurer because the company is not earning enough money, and signs for the Bushrangers.
They are the only active fighters among the Earthworlders, six of them, all adventurers.
Daly hands out two silver coins to each as spending money.
Dawson is a friend of Daly's from home, Ald (Aldenon) seeks Daly out in camp, and Kami is their best shot.
Kami is an Australian girl, and Tofte is a young man from Norway, while Siri and Tofte both speak Swedish.
Siri, Dawson, Kami, Aldenon, Tofte and Tobi are named among the team in the hunt for giant snakes.
The Bushrangers hunt sleeping Stelbore, nine of them: two very big, three more adults and four piglets, though Daly says only five were adults.
Daly tells Italians Lorenzo and Diana, and Blake, a New Zealander, that the Australians are friends and part of the United Nations company.
Daly has the Bushrangers learn Swedish words and hand signals from Siri and Tofte as a secret code, preparing for the day they run up against hostile people from Earth.
Their tactics are ambush from trees, traps, nets, and bombs, and they have partnered with the Rustless Vanguard, making them one of the best non-Gold teams around.
The Bushrangers are the division of the United Nations company that goes into combat, and few of the company volunteered for it.
A speaker advertised that hiring the Celestial Trackers would find a quarry or the coin back.
Odveig, a [Macewoman], calls herself the leader of the Celestial Trackers, while Wiskeria, a [Witch], is her subordinate and in Laken's view the brains of the group.
The Celestial Trackers are experienced at ambushes, tracking prey and finding hidden monsters, the opposites of the Windfrozen Riders in many ways.
Wiskeria is the only truly specialised spellcaster in either group.
The Celestial Trackers found the Mossbear's cave, and the bear woke up and attacked after an avalanche.
Laken hired the Celestial Trackers and Windfrozen Riders through the Merchant's Guild.
Wiskeria tended Beniar's poisoned arrow wound while the Trackers patrolled with the Riders against Goblin harassing attacks.
Laken suspected Wiskeria of snooping in his cottage, and when he shouted that Odveig was the spy, Odveig ran.
In the Goblin assault, Wiskeria threw glowing blue fire and led the Trackers forward; one Tracker lost a hand to a Hob.
Four of twelve Celestial Trackers survived the battle, and Wiskeria said she could not go back to Invrisil.
Celum's Adventurer's Guild is bigger than Liscor's, with room for up to six receptionists at once, against the single desk for two in Liscor's guild.
The Guild is a two-story building nearly twice the size of Liscor's, worn, with a faded sign and open shutters instead of glass.
It could hold close to eighty people before feeling cramped, with only about three dozen present including staff.
Its board holds open assignments, and exclusive contracts that only one team can take, such as escorting a [Trader]; harder and riskier ones sit near the top.
A squad of Celum guardsmen took in three muggers Erin had subdued, one of them a former Bronze-rank adventurer, and the Watch gave her two silver coins, four copper coins and three healing potions.
Celum's City Watch was bored on an uneventful day, then watched from the walls as Gold-rank adventurers carried the magic door through the city, and then the Goblins appeared.
Dozens of guardsmen on duty climbed the walls, and people on the streets crowded up to see the crowd in the distance.
Celum's City Watch stormed Celum's Adventurer's Guild, ordering Pisces and the others to put their weapons down and holding half the Watch outside, and arrested the adventurers.
Dozens of guardsmen converged on Octavia's shop, and the Watch Captain announced by order of the [Mayor] that the door to Liscor was confiscated and Celum would no longer do business with the inn.
The Watch Captain seized only the portal stone, not the magic door itself, and Numbtongue escaped through a back window.
Two adventurers at Celum's guild said four adventuring teams died at the Liscor ruins thanks to incompetent Captains, with only a handful surviving, and mocked the Horns of Hammerad's name.
One of them guessed the half-Elf had run and was a coward, saying Calruz was the only real fighter in the Horns.

Celum's adventurers told Yvlon they could not prove her team had fought, and suggested she and Ceria ran or got lucky, questioning where the Albez treasure came from and whether it was kept from survivors and the dead.
A Wistram student explained that the Centrists want every mage in the world to be part of Wistram and the academy to declare itself a nation, and that they are always fighting with the Isolationists.
Archmage Feor, an old half-Elf, leads the Centrists, who are one of the largest factions in Wistram.

The Revivalists, Centrists and Libertarians are the big three factions of Wistram, with thousands of members in the academy and across the world, the most voting power in the Council and the most active Archmages, so they are more akin to political parties.
Feor belongs to the Centrists but also keeps a personal group of half-Elf mages he trusts, including Teura, one of his best.
Feor brought six experienced Centrist [Mages] from the Council to cast a spell on Blackmage, and they stepped back and left when four hundred [Mages] watched.
A Revivalist said the Revivalists have the numbers to resist any faction, including Feor and the Centrists.
Feor told Ylawes that the Revivalists back Montressa du Valeross's team and are at odds with his own faction, the Centrists.
Elena, an Earther, belongs to Archmage Feor's Centrists faction, and the Centrists would loan her to the Revivalists if they needed to collaborate on something enriching both groups.

Feor tried to use the Centrists to persuade Wistram to go beyond a letter of condemnation and unite coastal nations against Ailendamus's blockade, but lost the Council vote when Viltach's Libertarians sided with the Revivalists.
Teura, a half-Elf [Mage] on Wistram's Council, belongs to the Centrists under Archmage Feor.
Most of the trusted mages allowed to attend Elena's Earth lectures were Centrists.
Magnolia wonders whether an attack on her mansion is the Circle of Thorns again, and says that the Circle's nightmare took her great grandmother's whole life to sort out.
A robed mage who blows out a wall tells Magnolia Reinhart that the Circle of Thorns seeks her life.
Regis, the Reinhart ancestor who guards the family armory, tells Magnolia that the Circle of Thorns haunted her grandmother and that she died with their curse still over the family.
Eloise says the Circle of Thorns may endanger [Witches] again, and that [Witches] are fewer and weaker than in the past.
The Circle of Thorns is as old as the Five Families and began as a reaction to their power.
Few members of the Five Families join the Circle, yet individuals are invited, and it has been known to move on behalf of the Five Families.
The Circle is made of the 'lesser' nobility, meaning anyone not of the original Five Families, and Lady Ieka understands it as meant to censure those with too much power.
In the past the Circle was more public, a symbol of opposition and even a political group, and only in the last few hundred years has it become more secretive.

Ieka recalls that an invitation to the Circle six years earlier was to a small social group of nobles that reminded the Five Families they were not unopposed, but the new Circle is different and more like the old times.
Most nobles get an invitation from someone connected to the Circle, and being publicly known as a member is dangerous.
The Circle asks only loyalty from members and does not care what they do in private so long as it is not public.
Lady Ieka says the Circle is meant to defend Izril from within as much as from outside, but in practice moves out of self-interest, and she thinks it rivals one of the Five Families in scope.
Tyrion Veltras knows the Circle as an old group that most nobles know of, and had assumed it extinct.
Lady Rie says the Reinharts drove the Circle into hiding, that Lady Suvelta Reinhart battled it and lost, and that later Reinharts also fought and lost.
Lady Rie says the Circle killed Lady Suvelta Reinhart, a Vampire, and Ieka recalls that she died screaming in sunlight after sixteen days and nights of torture.
Ieka knows that past Circles fought off invasions from Chandrar and Baleros, humbled Khelt when it invaded, and threw back the Six Great Companies of Baleros two thousand years back.
Lady Rie Valerund is higher in rank than Lady Ieka Imarris in the Circle, though both are members.
The inner council of the Circle is called the Petals of Death, and a ranking agent group is the Roots of Contempt, of which Rie is a part.
Rie is second only to the Petals of Death as one of their agents, and Ieka is a member of the Thorns of Contempt, two ranks up from a newly introduced member.
Lady Rie uses a glass rose called the Thorn of Speaking, activated with blood, to contact the Petals of Death by voice alone.
The voices of the Petals of Death are scrambled to be flat, and only six or seven of them speak.
Membership of the Petals of Death depends on loyalty and commitment, not on power.
An [Assassin] says the Circle has many ranks and offers Tyrion the title First of Thorns as commander of the Circle's assets.

Magnolia believes the Circle of Thorns sent the assassins who attacked the Ladies, while those who sent black roses are openly expressing contempt, and that at least one noble in Tyrion Veltras's camp is in the Circle.
Magnolia says she does not have the Assassin's Guild at her back and that the Circle of Thorns is one thing, but she does not want a political war.
