Lord Erill, a [Merchant Lord] who had backed Tyrion, leaves a bag of holding with two hundred thousand gold pieces' worth of goods with Lady Ieka as a donation, wanting no part of her organization, and Ieka says the Circle of Thorns will remember this.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the witches
text: Mavika says the people who killed the Marshlands Coven called themselves the Circle of Thorns, a secret name the witches had heard before.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the witches
text: Mavika says the killers demanded a curse upon Magnolia Reinhart and her kin, so powerful that she would die screaming and boiled by her own skin.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the witches
text: Califor thinks those who slaughtered the Marshlands Coven died painfully, after Mavika repaid blood with blood.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the witches
text: Mavika says she remembers the Circle once, two generations ago, when it slew members of the Five Families.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the witches
text: Belavierr says she remembers the Circle of Thorns thrice, that it comes again and again, and that twice it culled more than its enemies, with witches dying and war coming to Izril from north and south.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the witches
text: Belavierr says the war lasted thirty-four years and killed three thousand, three hundred and twelve Witches.
Lady Rie is told by the Petals of Death that Magnolia has betrayed the North by going to the Drakes and must be removed.
The Petals decide, five votes to two, to approach Tyrion Veltras to kill Reinhart, and say that if he refuses they may raise one of their own.
The Petals ask Rie whether Emperor Godart is an ally and order her to make him an offer, or settle it herself if he refuses.
A [Messenger] of the Circle approaches Tyrion Veltras with an invitation, and Tyrion calls him an [Assassin].
The [Assassin] is blond and sable-eyed, and he says the Assassin's Guild belongs to the Circle and offers Tyrion the title First of Thorns.
The [Assassin] claims that the Circle backed Tyrion's call for aid and that so many flocked to his banner because the Circle believed in his cause.
The [Assassin] says Magnolia is one of Izril's greatest traitors who will suffer today for her transgressions.
The Circle decides to kill Magnolia Reinhart, and countless nobles are told to watch the attack.
After Tyrion saves Magnolia, the Circle meets in fury at his act and swears he will be brought to heel and made to swear himself to the Circle as a servant and not an ally.
The Circle has failed to kill Magnolia and considers its dealings with Tyrion its one mistake.
A masked [Assassin] tells Tyrion that the Circle of Thorns is displeased and later offers an exchange for his sons' lives and his family's safety for his cooperation.
The Circle has killed over two dozen local [Healers] and [Alchemists] in Veltras's region and delivered their heads to House Veltras's door.
The contract the [Assassin] offered Tyrion is a fully binding magical contract with few avenues for escape.
A volley of spells hits Tyrion's keep and city as a warning, and a masked [Assassin] says if he leaves his estates she cannot guarantee his sons will be there when he returns.
Magnolia is on the Reinhart flagship, chased from her home, and people no longer take the Circle of Thorns as lightly as before.
Nawalishifra Tannousin sells ingots of Naq-Alrama steel forged in her clan's forges, which she insists are magic and enchantable.
She says the metal must be smithed under the moonlight until quenching, and must be struck precisely while hot.
She says the steel is kept from any sunlight, and quenching it in sun-filled waters lets it endure any pressure.
Silmak of Clan Tannousin presents himself to Lord Orthenon of Reim, travelling with thirty-two kin, to honor the oath that Nawalishifra made to the King of Destruction.

Silmak names Hesseif, who is tasked with the caravan's defence, his aunt second-removed Bezhavil, who oversees the womenfolk and the caravan, and Nawalishifra, who will forge the Naq-Alrama steel as [Blacksmith].
The men guarding the huge, covered wagon that holds the clan's treasure of Naq-Alrama metal stay standing while the rest kneel.
Hesseif vows to guard the metal day and night and let in no one of other blood and no ray of sunlight.
Silmak's tattooed hands sparkle and light up, and he later speaks as a [Shaman] to Orthenon about the sword that must be sharpened three more times.
This entry covers two separate bodies called the Council: the governing council of Wistram Academy and the ruling Council of the city of Liscor.
A student relays that the Council, made up of the leaders of all the mage factions in Wistram, scolded the mage in charge of a class and told them to start teaching right away.
Pisces argues his case for necromancy before the Council, and mages around the room shout furiously against him.

After a debate in which the opinion swings against Pisces, Archmage Feor announces that necromancy is not taught in Wistram and that the Council revokes Pisces's scholarship, so that he must pay the full dues or leave.
Pisces offers his silver-belled rapier to Calvaron to be sold to cover the academy's fees, and Calvaron says it should be enough.
The Liscor Council votes to hold an election, which is described as a referendum on the current Council, and one listener thinks the wording lets them avoid counting the votes.
The Council is offering a headhunter fee for every team that Ceria's group can recruit in Celum to build a safe trade route around the Bloodfields, and Yvlon has signed the Horns of Hammerad up.
At a Council meeting, Krshia proposes sending the [Negotiator] Teliv with wine and a puppy or two from Elirr's litter to placate Selys's grandmother.
Liscor's Council has allocated funds for all the teams who stood and fought, and will pay a pension to the dead, though it had to go to the Antinium to pay it and keep on budget.
The Council of Liscor is the governing body of Liscor and is described as a body of the heads of the guilds and so on; it normally met in the quiet City Hall.
In the attack of the undead, only two of the Antinium Hive's three entrances were known to the Council of Liscor.
The Council of Liscor was said to be putting out word of Erin's plan, with Antinium, adventurers, the Watch and Goblins all helping.
After an election that won four districts for Gnolls, the old Council led by the Merchant's Guild head Ulseil schemed to seat only three Gnolls instead of four.
The old Council cast its last vote unanimously.
Krshia Silverfang won the election handily.
The new Council includes Krshia, Elirr and Raekea on the Gnoll side and Lism, Jeiss and Alonna as firmly allied Drakes, alongside Tismel and Zalaiss, who side with the old Council.
The new Council argued all at once, with Krshia, Lism, Jeiss, Alonna, Raekea and Elirr bringing in differing ideas to a room that had only known Drakes.
The former Councilmembers convened at City Hall twenty minutes later with last year's Council and earlier Councils, twenty-two people in all, and tried to storm the new Council's room.
The Council of Liscor exploded out of their seats when Erin adjusted the door's dial to Invrisil, wanting the insane Human stopped and regulated.
The Council of Liscor hired Hexel Quithail, who asked Erin if he and three apprentices could stay at her inn.
The Council of Liscor stood on the other side of the door when Pelt announced he was moving to another city.
A negotiator says they have come to negotiate on behalf of the Council of Liscor with the Free Antinium.
Wiskeria says a coven is a group of [Witches] that meets every few months, and that it is part of the [Witch] class even though most classes have nothing like it.
Wiskeria says a [Witch] generally pursues her own craft and meets her coven a few times a month at most to trade news, warnings and goods.
Wiskeria says Humans make up most [Witch] covens.
Wiskeria says covens can be very large and that Mavika's coven covers all the [Witches] within about three hundred miles, the Marshlands Coven.
Wiskeria says the Marshlands Coven is old, with members coming and going, and has been in Izril since Humans first came or earlier.
The [Witches] meet when the two moons are full, which is not every month, and Wiskeria says the next meeting is in six days.
Wiskeria tells Durene that Mavika is insisting that she join the coven, though Wiskeria says she does not have to.
Wiskeria says Mavika will not force her again, now that Mavika has lost two of her crows.
Wiskeria refuses a City Runner's demand for a yes, telling him to tell Witch Oliyaya she will not attend her coven's meeting and that she has told Mavika the same.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the new coven
text: Califor says the Marshlands Coven was called upon by strangers a fortnight earlier, met them without Mavika, refused an offer, and died.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the new coven
text: Califor says Mavika took vengeance on those who bloodied their blades but not on those who made the offer.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the new coven
text: Califor says a ritual was cast on the dead coven's hats, and a hat was sent to each of six [Witches] to form a new coven in Riverfarm.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the new coven
text: When the coven arrives in Riverfarm, Mavika tells Wiskeria it is not her coven, that there are six, and that the seventh is coming.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the new coven
text: Mavika later says a coven was convened as seven, with Nanette as the apprentice and Wiskeria as the last.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the new coven
text: The coven calls on Wiskeria to join it, claiming the rights of travellers and sanctuary in Riverfarm until Emperor Laken can meet them over an offer and a bargain.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the new coven
text: Wiskeria accepts the coven after receiving a hat.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the new coven
text: At the coven's first meeting in Riverfarm, six Witches besides Wiskeria are in the room, with Nanette already in bed; they sit in Califor's home with tea and biscuits.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the new coven
text: Alevica is Oliyaya's representative and apprentice in the coven.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the new coven
text: Califor leads the coven for now.

section: The Marshlands Coven and the new coven
text: Prost gives the Witches newer houses without payment, and they take lodgings in Riverfarm before talking.
Belavierr says the coven is united in purpose, namely sanctuary for [Witches].
Califor says the coven wants sanctuary for all [Witches] on Laken's lands and an alliance, because it represents the interest of all Izril's covens and the decision is not just some [Witches]'.
Eloise says that if Laken needs them and a deal is struck, he would be the first noble or city in an age to openly ally with their kind.
Wiskeria asks why all of them came when a letter would do, and Califor answers that they represent what Laken stands to gain and must prove their value.
Fierre's notes list the visiting coven as Mavika, Eloise, Wiskeria, Hedag, Alevica, Nanette and Califor.
On Day 76 the six remaining [Witches] meet outside the throne room, with Califor gone and Belavierr absent.
Eloise, speaking for all Izril's [Witches], asks Laken to let [Witches] practice free of persecution in his lands and to void bounties on [Witches] unless there is ample reason.
Laken says [Witches] may roam Riverfarm, practice their craft and come there safe from unwarranted persecution if they keep the basic rules of hospitality, in the name of Califor who saved Riverfarm.
Esthelm's ruling body of Master Crafters replaced the military leader Erin had helped remove.
In Illivere, Crafters are the elite who manufacture or manage Golems, voted into positions of authority by each state, and they elect the Magus-Crafter.
Crafters are in charge, lay out plans and 'make' the Golems, with dozens or hundreds of workers helping; making Golems is an industry there and Crafters are often businesspeople.
Magus-Crafter Femithain is of the state of Dellva, whose capital is Demarsel, so the head of Illivere shifts when the next Magus-Crafter is elected.
Femithain resolved discipline among the Crafters, and young Crafters dedicated Golems to the former Empress Nsiia.
No one in Illivere can craft Sentient-class Golems.
Crafters looked down on the [Armsmaster] Dellic as an elevated [Guard].
First Crafters of each state debated declaring war on Reim, with Femithain promising to speak against.
The Dawn Concordat is the traditional bulwark of Calanfer, Kaliv and Gaiil-Drome in Terandria, known for having broken many nations sent against it.

A predictor expected Taimaguros, which has a defensive alliance with Ailendamus, to side with Ailendamus, so that two major powers and their allies would fight the traditional Dawn Concordat plus Pheislant.
Ailendamus had swelled in recent years and its ruler, King Itorin II, was looking for easy victories.
Ailendamus warships clashed twice with Pheislant vessels and blockaded trade to the Dawn Concordat, intercepting goods bound there.
Wistram's Council argued three days over the blockade and did nothing, and Feor did not rank the Dawn Concordat's fate highly, thinking he could interfere when the war began.
A general planned to land at Nadel with Lord Belchaus's permission and flank the Dawn Concordat when the war began in six days.
The Elusive Lot was on the side of the Dawn Concordat.
Anyone watching continental politics knew the Ailendamus war threatened the Dawn Concordat of three kingdoms.

Ailendamus had swallowed other nations' territory and won several wars in the two decades since King Itorin II came to power, and was set to roll over the Dawn Concordat unless Pheislant, Noelictus or another nation helped.
Lord Tyrion judged that the Dawn Concordat's best outcome was a defensive victory with significant casualties and loss of territory.
Calanfer, the most political of the three members, and Ailendamus each asked Tyrion Veltras for aid when war began.
Ailendamus declared war on the Dawn Concordat as its armies crossed the border of Kaliv and its ships began blockading nations such as Pheislant.
Abebi took her band north to avoid the war between Ailendamus and the Dawn Concordat, since Pheislant could be drawn in.
A speaker said a new [Emperor] had emerged who absorbed many of the nations in Flos's empire, created a vast army, and was sweeping across the continent with strong soldiers.

In Chandrar, military men know war is war, and Takhatres, Lord of the Skies, a vassal of the King of Destruction, was a sworn enemy of the Empire of Sands, which had declared war on Flos Reimarch not four months earlier.

Selys told Erin that the Reinharts, Veltras, Terland, Wellfar and El families were the first humans to settle on Izril, that they were aristocrats related to the kings of Terandria, and that they are still very rich and influential.
Fals said all the really powerful nobles and the Five Families live closer to the north.

The houses of Veltras, El, Reinhart, Terland and Wellfar settled Izril, taking it from the Drakes and Gnolls thousands of years ago, though they were not the only noble houses to sail from Terandria; those that fell were forgotten.

In Ullim's view, El had fallen far from its past heights, Wellfar and Terland kept much of their strength though the Antinium Wars killed some of their scions, Veltras had military might but not huge stockpiles of magical goods, and Reinhart kept most of its artifacts and grew richer.
Maviola El told young nobles that each of the Five Families has its own curse, and that all are in decline.
Maviola said the Wellfar family is rich with coastal holdings and control of trade, led the navies to Izril and still rules the seas, but is infertile and shrinking and never expanded far inland.
Maviola said the Terlands were victims of their success, keeping to mage-towns and spell-castles and looking outward little.

Maviola said the Veltras family never settled the untamed wilderness such as the Forest of Vail, and that its scions learn to fight and make excellent [Generals] and [Warmasters] but poor leaders of men.
Maviola called the Reinharts the richest and most powerful of the families, and said their only curse was Regis Reinhart, who preserved them but took from each generation.
Maviola said the House of El are great crafters of magic whose curse is that they are out of money, having lost almost all their old artifacts and investments.
Maviola said the Five Families are allies but not friends, and that they are shadows of what they were, with the nobility of Izril lacking leaders and fewer in number than anyone remembers.
The Flamewardens are a Gold-rank team of Oldblood Drakes from Pallass, led by Keldrass, a huge Drake in plate armor who coughs smoke or blue flames when he speaks.
Keldrass states they will enter the dungeon at daybreak, because if the Raskghar are strongest at night, adventurers must move by day.
Four Flamewardens, Keldrass and Nautia among them, line up and breathe fire together, melting the front row of charging armor into black slag.
Bevussa says the Flamewardens have firepower but no stamina, and after the breath they are unable to breathe for a while, which is why they are not a Named team.
Keldrass insists they can rest half an hour and burn another tunnel.
At the door, Keldrass and his Flamewardens take aim to burn Garen, but a crossbow bolt strikes Keldrass' helmet and the others have to shield themselves, unable to use their breath.
During the same fight, Keldrass carries a wounded teammate back to the door as Halrac orders a fall back.
Keldrass pays to rent the Heartflame Breastplate from Miss Shivertail, so the Flamewardens do not need Scale Soup.
Keldrass has an armor classified as Siegespell Armor, close to Named-rank gear.
Keldrass holds a corridor against the undead, with his second-in-command wearing the Heartflame Breastplate, and the Gold-ranks send a distress call.
Before a Rock Crab hunt, Rags had about sixty Goblins in her tribe, and afterward she had closer to forty, possibly forty-five, since Goblins came and died quickly.
The Flooded Waters tribe's single Hob had been its Chief until Erin killed him.
Rags considered Erin terrifying for killing a Hob by herself, something even Silver-rank adventurers struggle with.
In less than a week the Flooded Waters Tribe overran the Jawbreaker, Sword Taker and Bloody Hand Tribes, slaying or defeating their Chieftains and absorbing their Goblins.
Rags had defeated a tribe of over two hundred Goblins with virtually no casualties and led over eight hundred Goblins, having absorbed three, and now four, tribes in a week.
Rags's Flooded Waters tribe was the largest and strongest tribe in a coalition of fifteen or so tribes.
Later, it had nearly eight hundred warriors, several thousand Goblins in total and over ten Hobs, the most of any tribe, though Rags did not count the Redfang tribe as part of it.
Rags introduced herself to Humans as Chieftain of the Flooded Waters tribe.
The Flooded Waters Goblins camped for a long while in a forest by a lake near several small cities and towns, which served as their semi-permanent home.
From there they raided caravans and farms nonviolently, aiming crossbows and chasing Humans away without killing unless attacked, and grew rich on the spoils.

The tribe was originally small and barely surviving around Liscor, and was thousands strong with many Hobs and a mounted force of Carn Wolves, caught between the Goblin Lord and Tremborag's Mountain City Tribe.
Rags's tribe is organised, with tents, cook stations, food supplies and latrines, which is Rags's most important innovation, and it fought off Lady Bethal and her Rose Knights in the forest.
After Humans hunted down the Frostfeeder Tribe for a week and killed over half of it, the remainder became part of Rags's tribe.
Two Hobs, a male and a female, led Goblins guarding Lady Bethal's party, and the female spoke the common tongue, surprising Bethal.
Thousands of Goblins with crossbows and pikes and hundreds of Hobs fled in a stream across the grassland.
The tribe's Goblins communicate through sign language and posture, not talk, and a few Goblins who had known Erin and been in her inn told the others about her.
After Tremborag's fall, the tribe had grown elevenfold, with thousands of Hobs and Goblin warriors who had served Tremborag, along with Ulvama and a few [Shamans].
Fighting began between the Flooded Waters tribe and the Goblin Lord's army.
The Redfangs and the Cave Goblins had supplies of food while fleeing Reiss's army.

The Free Antinium's Workers could construct and deconstruct buildings overnight, yet they regularly under-produced when providing services, since taking over Liscor's industry would cause economic disaster and the Hive was meant to work with other species.
The Free Antinium bought food, crafted items and clothing despite having little need for them.

After a decade of suffering in neglect, the other Hives were sitting up and looking at the Free Antinium, some warily and some approvingly, and the Free Queen understood the other Queens were waiting to talk to her.
In the Grand Hive the Free Antinium could not sleep in their cubicles, which reminded them of the Free Hive, and Anand told Klbkch he recalled it.
Klbkch told the Antinium more about how the Hives had been organised by geniuses so that an Antinium took one less step to reach its destination.

The Armored Queen told Anand the statue he resembled was Galuc the Builder, in whose image the Free Antinium were made; Galuc died before coming to Izril, and the Shaper Queen Bessachidia saved his form.
Workers carried a mirror out of the Grand Hive that Anand had built as a link, and Wistram's Archmages were seriously considering sabotaging the connection because of what it meant.
Erin ran up to the mirror at the inn and asked where Anand had gone, then Grand Strategist Chaldion arrived with Grimalkin and Pallass officers while Olesm and Selys looked at the waving Antinium.
Gemhammer is a Silver-rank team led by Earlia, a Human with a warhammer.
The members were all [Miners] before discovering they could kill monsters with hammers and pickaxes, and have mining-related Skills.
Gemhammer has a [Gem Mage].
Timgal, Fea and Blaik are among Earlia's team.
Ceria, hearing a claim that Gemhammer killed a dozen Raskghar, is shocked at how hard six of them are to fight.
The claim attributed to Gemhammer and the Pride of Kelia is two dozen Raskghar, which one of the Horns scoffs at after six Raskghar nearly overcame their team and three Hobs.
Earlia announces her name and her Silver-rank team to the worldwide broadcast, and Niers calls it a smart move since the name was spread across the world in a moment.
With Nailren's team, Earlia's team of former [Miners] kills a Raskghar team in the dungeon.
Earlia cuts a gold-and-sapphire ring from a diseased Raskghar's finger; the team also finds a bag of gemstones and an enchanted-looking knife.
The teams meet Facestealer, who peeks around a corner with a Goblin's head on a stick, and its notes say it paralyzes everything in range.
The Gentlemen Callers are Wilovan, a Gnoll [Thug], and Ratici, a Drake [Thief], who belong to the Brotherhood of Serendipitous Meetings.
Palt explains that the Gentlemen Callers are two big Faces of the Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings, a smaller but elite gang with big players in northern Izril.
Fierre tells Ryoka that the Callers are two of the Brothers' best and that they will kill an enemy of the Brothers.
The Brothers of Serendipitous Meetings have built a reputation on politeness, and are one of the two largest local underworld groups along with the Sisters of Chell.
Fierre lists the Gentlemen Callers among the gangs that would take a request to kill someone, none of them based around Filk.
Fierre tells Ryoka that the Brothers are all-male, do not do kidnapping or racketeering, and keep a code of honor, and that if they take off their hats one should run.
Wilovan is a [Thug] who is also a [Reader] able to memorize a book in an hour, and he says he reads during the rest he takes with the women he romances.
Ratici is a [Thief] who can produce small objects such as a ketchup cup from nowhere and handle spells such as butterfly illusions.
Both were born in Invrisil, which is rare for a Drake and Gnoll among Humans.
Wilovan speaks in measured formal tones while Ratici speaks faster and uses fanciful words.
They wear hats, a floppy one for Ratici's neck-spines and a tall one for Wilovan.
Wilovan says the Brothers follow a code in which they prey on those with coin, never on those down on their luck, children or decent sorts.
Ratici warns Typhenous not to make them take off their hats, especially not with innocent children about.
Ratici says the Brothers do not stand for kidnapping or anything that would hurt a child.
Wilovan tells Typhenous that calling in a debt in the most final way is not their style and that repayment takes many forms.
A Brother of Serendipitous Meetings who has just faced the Goblins says that if the Gentlemen Callers had taken the case it would not have ended as it did.
In the inn, Wilovan and Ratici confront Typhenous, saying a debt is owed to the Brothers and that their Nose had learned he might have the answers.

Typhenous says he acted to prevent an inn and city from being sacked and to let a young innkeeper, her child and her friends escape, and that he gave their friends fair warning though Goblins were a threat.
Wilovan says the Brothers might accept that, but Ratici says a debt remains, and they lean forward to collect.
Wilovan and Ratici discuss taking a contract from the Tall Man, who pays well and is near their home, and they came north by Pallass's door.
The Titan of Baleros receives a note that the Gentlemen Callers are in Liscor and awaiting further instructions.
Niers, the Titan, complains that the Gentleman Callers are not being cooperative, when Foliana suggests paying the Brothers to find out more.
The Gentlemen Callers accepted the Tallman of Baleros' invitation to guard the inn, and learned the problem was Erin Solstice herself.
The two Gentlemen Callers spend their days in the inn, where they are taken with the new games Erin introduces and earn a reputation as two of the best dart-board champions.
Wilovan and Ratici tell Erin they were hired to look out for her, call themselves a [Thug] and a [Thief], and do not name their client.
The Callers also admit they were in Invrisil when the mob came, and Erin realizes they protected her.
The Callers say they stopped unscrupulous sorts from kidnapping a little Gnoll child after Bearclaw's gang was found unconscious.
The Callers say they were not able to stop the beating of Relc.
The Gentlemen Callers took off their hats while listening to Erin tell Numbtongue why she sought mercy for the Raskghar, then replaced them and bowed.
The Gnoll tribes of the plains and swamps reacted to the Antinium threat faster than the Drake city-states, and over a hundred tribes sent warriors to form a massive army.
In its first major engagement an army of twenty thousand Gnolls routed a force of nearly eighty thousand Antinium in a battle lasting a day.
The Antinium never penetrated further than fifty miles into Gnoll lands.
Teriarch said the Gnoll tribes used to meet only once every hundred years, then every fifty, then every twenty, to stay connected.
After Zel Shivertail's death most Gnoll tribes withdrew from sight and mourned with massed howls across the plains.
Elirr said the Woven Bladegrass tribe, whose new Chieftain is young and has fought Drakes before, was behind the Gnoll-Drake incidents.

A much larger force of over a hundred thousand Gnolls assembled within a week of that battle, and with hunting packs of tens of thousands it fought off every Antinium advance, though the Gnolls never sent armies out to attack the Antinium in retaliation.
The Goblin Lord's army pours into Esthelm to the sound of countless drums, some Goblins riding Shield Spiders and others horses.
Goblin [Shamans] control the undead at the head of the army, which Ylawes judges to be barely a hundred.
A Goblin riding a massive Shield Spider hacks through Humans with a halberd that cuts through armor, and Ylawes challenges him.
The Goblin Lord's army sweeps across the land like a horde of green locusts, burning and destroying anything without walls.
Reynold estimates the advance force, which fills the horizon heading north, at tens of thousands of Goblins.
Goblins riding Shield Spiders charge a column of fleeing villagers, with a whooping mass of Goblins behind them.
A Goblin with black eyes and white pupils raises a hand as black magic swirls around him.
The Goblin Lord rides a massive Shield Spider larger than a warhorse at the head of the army, and many ordinary Goblins ride large Shield Spiders too.
The army has taken every horse, pony, mule and donkey it could grab, and excess wagons and carts are pulled by teams of six Hobs.
The Goblin Lord has thousands of Hobs in the best armor looted from other soldiers, forming a disciplined core, plus regular Goblins in black armor.
Osthia judges that a regular Drake army with a competent [General] would beat the army were it not for the undead, which double its size.
The undead can dig themselves into the ground to ambush and can send exploding Goblin corpses to tear holes in an enemy line.
Eater of Spears throws Pyrite, and both the Flooded Waters tribe and the Goblin Lord's army break ranks and begin to fight in chaos.
The Goblin Lord's lieutenants are all former Chieftains who once led thousands of their kin into battle.
Osthia notes the lieutenants as they file out of the Goblin Lord's tent: Snapjaw, two Goblin [Necromancers], Eggsnatcher on a huge Shield Spider, and a Goblin with no face.
Snapjaw is a short Hobgoblin with an unnaturally large head and steel-armor, whose teeth are a fusion of enamel and steel produced by her class.
Snapjaw has a [Dangersense] that warns her of imminent death.
Eater of Spears is a seven-foot Hob whose body looks like a solid wall of muscle, and Osthia has never heard him speak.
Eater of Spears' tough skin breaks a group of seasoned [Lancers]' weapons.
Eggsnatcher is a [Beastmaster] Goblin who rides a Shield Spider as large as the Goblin Lord's mount and commands a horde of spiders.
A Goblin called Noface has no face because of an encounter with a Human [Pyromancer], and he blasts Human ranks with fire.
Illbreath leads a unit pursuing fleeing Humans.
Zel Shivertail holds up Noface's severed head to show the Goblins their dead officer, and they hold their ground.
A pink carriage with a Human [Butler] charges Eggsnatcher's Shield Spider and the two trade blows.
Hundreds, or thousands, of Goblins streamed across the plains against fleeing Gnolls and the few Gnolls holding them off, with a main host like a black tide and Hobs firing arrows among it.
Ryoka saw over a hundred Hobs advancing among the Goblin host.
The Goblin host marched past Liscor's walls in one mass, loosing arrows at the [Guardsmen] on the battlements, and a glowing ward deterrent on the wall kept it from retaliating.
Hundreds of enemy Goblins gathered around campfires outside the city, boxing the Redfang Goblins in.
The Goblin army was thousands strong, with black-armoured warriors marching alongside undead, and it ran into a snowstorm in winter without finding easy prey.
Over a hundred thousand Goblins, in black armour and without, with thousands of Hobs, wagons, pack animals, mounted Goblins and large Shield Spiders, ran south.
Lady Bethal Walchaís had never seen a Goblin child before meeting a toddler-sized Goblin girl in Book 8.

section: Book 1: the child at the grave
text: While Erin Solstice buries slain Goblins, a small ragged Goblin in a grey stained loincloth and rags, holding a small knife, rushes her from the long grass.

section: Book 1: the child at the grave
text: Erin slaps the Goblin to the ground and kicks it in the stomach, realising it is a child with murder in its eyes.

section: Book 1: the child at the grave
text: Erin sees tears running from the Goblin's red eyes, tells it she does not want to kill it, and weighs killing it for the level; she buries the last head instead and the Goblin is gone when she turns.
Lady Bethal sees a tiny, lost-looking Goblin girl no bigger than a toddler wandering among the Goblin dead, shouting a single word and crying as she searches the bodies.
Bethal learns that Goblins can weep tears just like any other species.
When Bethal asks why only the child is crying, a Hob answers that tears are a waste of water.
The girl clings to a body until the Hob pulls her away; she wails once, beats him, and bites his hand as he carries her off without looking back.
A narrator in Book 13 says a Goblin child could learn to control an iPhone with motion commands in thirty minutes, even using a feature, shake-to-shuffle, that its owner Laken Godart never used.
A Goblin tribe of perhaps forty armed Goblins by Erin's guess, smaller than the tribe Erin fled on her first day, stood watching her silently on a hill and did not charge.
The Goblins followed Erin swiftly without screaming or trying to cut her off, and let her go when she ran for her inn.
Relc called forty Goblins just the local tribe and said he could take out half of them without breaking a sweat.

Klbkch said a Goblin tribe is no threat to any but lone stragglers despite its competence, and that a small raiding party usually has at least three hundred Goblins and larger groups have exceeded a thousand.
Gold-rank adventurers who die are stripped of their equipment and cremated, so that thieves cannot despoil their corpses.
Jelaqua says Gold-rank adventurers swear an oath to fight and do not run when a city is at stake.
After the failed rescue in the dungeon, the adventurers retreat battered and exhausted, stalemated rather than beaten, while the Antinium survivors return to their Hive.
Gravetender's Fist is a suppression company: a night-duty force of "corpse battlers" that does not fight veterans.
The company's work is to clean a battlefield of corpses after each day of combat so that undead do not spawn.
Quallet offers a silver piece for every night spent fighting and four copper for nights off, and supplies swords, armor and healing potions to those without.
Quallet claims that eight out of every ten raw recruits survive their first month and promises first ten combat levels.
The company arrives at the battlefield, a wide valley where two armies meet from hilltop camps, and moves out for its first night duty.
The company's job is to find the dead, pile them and burn them so undead do not spawn, killing any already risen, then leave before fighting resumes.
On Ken's third night, the work is better than the first because the shock is gone, though the fear remains.
Ken and others were part of Quallet's company before leaving it.
The revitalised Gravetender's Fist is still burgeoning but has earned enough for a holiday in town.
The company is still small but gaining respect under Quallet Marshhand, and every soldier is armed with a crossbow they usually fire before switching to other weapons.
Quallet and Quexa, the [Mercenary Captain] who is his second-in-command, meet Daly just outside Talenqual.
Griffon Hunt is a Gold-rank team that rode through the snow to Liscor after Revi received a [Message] about the dungeon, travelling day and night to arrive before other teams.

Halrac was the team's lead [Scout] and [Marksman], Ulric (Ulrien) led the team with a greatsword and magical armour, Typhenous was one of its two mages, and Revi, a mage with stitch marks, was the newest addition.
Fighting Gnolls, Halrac loosed blunt arrows meant to break bones without killing, and Revi summoned three armed phantoms.
Griffon Hunt stayed in an expensive side room of an inn, as a mark of respect for their rank and the gold they paid, and Halrac complained the team was idle while others could get the drop on them.
Ulrien, the Captain, told Revi to put her strongest summons out at the first sign of danger and Typhenous to hang back with his best spells, then forced open the rusted dungeon doors.
Halrac, Ulrien, Revi and Typhenous quarrelled over rooms at Erin's inn, saying they had paid good coin.
Halrac explained that the name means a breed of dog used for hunting, which is what the team specialises in, and not the beast Griffin.
Halrac and Ulrien used to hunt actual Griffins, and the name is a pun on that which another member of the group, now dead, came up with.
Halrac told a Watch [Sergeant] that the name is spelled with an 'o', as in the dog.

Lord Radivaek recalled selling dogs to Griffon Hunt, and Halrac said the team let them go to a [Hunter]'s team after the incident in the north; they had used them to ambush Griffins by baiting the flying monster.
Griffon Hunt and the Halfseekers had agreed to join forces on the dungeon.
Jelaqua told Ulrien and Revi the Halfseekers' former companion was a Hobgoblin named Garen Redfang, who betrayed the team after a treasure find; Ulrien suggested justice be done after the dungeon.
Ulrien died in Liscor at Erin's inn, and Halrac, Typhenous and Revi left the inn but stayed in the city, unable to stay where he fell.
Typhenous told Revi that Halrac and Ulrien had been comrades for decades, while they had joined the party not two years earlier.
Griffon Hunt and the Halfseekers went into the dungeon by the trapped main entrance, with Jelaqua in the Heartflame Breastplate.
Halrac pushed cursed ornaments into his bag of holding after Typhenous and Moore judged they would not explode.
Typhenous proposed taking the Silver Swords, the Halfseekers and the Horns of Hammerad in turn and switching groups after a few hours.
Revi told the Horns they fought like Silver-rank because Gold-ranks are experts in a field, and said Pisces lacked a signature style.
Revi said the team's formation was weaker without Ulrien, their front-line fighter, and the team wanted to work with the Horns.

About three years earlier Halrac and Ulrien contracted Typhenous and Revi to deal with a Griffin colony in the Nameless Heights; they poisoned nests and killed hundreds of Griffins, but Typhenous used the wrong spells and the plague killed most livestock and sickened three cities, and the team was lucky to keep its Gold-rank status.
Erin thought of how the Halfseekers and Griffon Hunt had sacrificed a lot and lost Ulrien.

Halrac, Revi and Typhenous agreed to pay eighteen thousand gold pieces, six thousand per former teammate, to square their former members' losses, after Typhenous quietly added nearly seven thousand gold to the bag of holding.
Revi, a Stitch-Woman and [Summoner], said her home nation in Chandrar is now part of the Empire of Sands and that Chandrar deserves respect.
Halrac became Captain of Griffon Hunt after Ulrien was killed in a fight in Liscor's inn by Regrika Blackpaw, a Named Adventurer.
Halrac told Briganda that the team wanted to make things right, offering recompense of 6,000 gold pieces to each former member, with Elm able to claim his share if he asked, and Briganda accepted.
Halrac found a request from Emperor Laken Godart of the Unseen Empire seeking a Gold-rank team at Riverfarm for very low pay.
Halrac, Revi, Typhenous and Briganda breakfasted with friends at Erin's inn and planned to go to Hedault's with the Horns to appraise treasure.
Griffon Hunt's members are Halrac Everam, Revi Cotton, Typhenous and Briganda Rishaw, and Briganda's son Cade travels with them but would be left behind from real danger.
Typhenous cast [Valmira's Comet] and Halrac fired enchanted arrows, and with Revi's Stitch-Warriors the team destroyed a Creler nest at range.
Laken Godart asked Halrac to stay a week and destroy a nest of Crelers, and Halrac accepted, saying the team would have destroyed the nest even without pay.
Griffon Hunt's members decided to go tell Emperor Laken Godart about the Goblins in his lands but to say nothing about Erin Solstice to him, and not to tell Erin either.
The loot from the escape room included a Belt of Strength for Briganda and Boots of Stability for Halrac.
The Halfseekers are a Gold-rank adventuring team whose present core is Jelaqua Ivirith, a Selphid, Moore, a half-Giant, and Seborn, a Drowned Man.
Moore has a quarter of a Giant's blood, and Seborn smells like fish; Jelaqua says Selphids are unpopular on Izril.
The Halfseekers use a private team vote on big decisions.
Typhenous recalls hearing the Halfseekers came from Baleros as Silver-rank and were once among the best Gold-rank teams on the continent; Jelaqua corrects his count of seven to eight members.
Jelaqua says they had hoped to become a Named team.
After the Sepicus Delve, one of their own turned on them, slaughtered four of the team and fled with everything they had found; they never found him.
The survivors think he killed to hide what was stolen, perhaps an artifact or a secret, and Seborn remembers a key, a magical orb, spell scrolls and a few magical weapons.
Jelaqua names the traitor as a Hobgoblin companion, Garen Redfang, who is still alive and has his own tribe.
Griffon Hunt tells them that justice should be done for the fallen, to be discussed after the dungeon.
Halassia Evergleam, a Scorchling, was once in their ranks; the Halfseekers buried her themselves because her family did not want her remains.
Ilvriss says Halassia was born in Salazsar and that the Halfseekers took her in when many shunned Scorchlings.
Jelaqua says they lost half their members to a Goblin, and Seborn recalls Ukrina's saying that giving other species no chance leaves the world no hope.
In Garen's memory, the earlier Halfseekers ride to a city: Jelaqua in a Gnoll body, Seborn, Moore, Halassia Evergleam, the outcast full Drake Ukrina, Keilam, Thornst and the Hobgoblin Garen.
Keilam is the group's third [Mage] if Moore is counted, and is half-Gnoll, half Cat-tribe Beastkin; Thornst is a half-Elf from Terandria and the newest member.
The group has just been certified as a Gold-rank team.

In Garen's memory, he kills Keilam, Thornst, Ukrina and Halassia in the private room where they divide their loot, holding the key; Halassia calls him a traitor before he kills her with his blade Redfang.

Jelaqua, Moore and Seborn debate afterward; Seborn thinks Ukrina and Halassia were right about the Goblin King but that Garen attacked them, while Jelaqua says they should have waited for the rest of the team.

section: At the inn and the dungeon
text: Jelaqua, Moore and Seborn propose teaming up on the dungeon with Griffon Hunt, saying it is too dangerous alone, and Ulrien proposes splitting the spoils evenly.

section: At the inn and the dungeon
text: They have just been kicked out of their own inn.

section: At the inn and the dungeon
text: Griffon Hunt and the Halfseekers have agreed to join forces on the dungeon.

section: At the inn and the dungeon
text: Jelaqua notes the Halfseekers are the only Gold-rank team in the inn until the Horns are certified, and the three test the inn's window for durability.

section: At the inn and the dungeon
text: Jelaqua is a Selphid with a dead body, and Seborn has a claw-hand.

section: At the inn and the dungeon
text: Jelaqua says the Halfseekers want the city to build the official dungeon entrance higher, but the Antinium refuse to work in the downpour.

section: At the inn and the dungeon
text: Jelaqua now wears a Drake body, and Selys leases the team the Heartflame Breastplate to test.

section: At the inn and the dungeon
text: Jelaqua wears the Heartflame Breastplate as the Halfseekers and Griffon Hunt go into the dungeon, and Zevara notes Selys really leased it.

section: At the inn and the dungeon
text: Halrac nudges the cursed ornaments into his bag of holding once Typhenous and Moore judge they will not explode.

section: At the inn and the dungeon
text: Erin trusts the Halfseekers, the Horns and Griffon Hunt with the news of the axe, and notes the Halfseekers and Griffon Hunt sacrificed a lot, including Ulrien.
Seborn says the Halfseekers were never at full strength, wants to recruit teammates, and wants to go to First Landing to settle things with his old crew, who owe him.
Jelaqua's spare bodies are stored in Erin's inn.
Passing two children in a village, the three raise their fists and shout "Halfseekers!", and Moore leaves a trail of blooming and wilting flowers.
The Halfseekers stall on the way to Invrisil because Seborn objects to Jelaqua's relationship with Maughin.
Seborn gives Jelaqua an ultimatum, she sobs, and he agrees to work around Pallass with steady jobs and to recruit Ulinde.
Ulinde becomes a Halfseeker.
Erin hosts a celebration of the Halfseekers' work in Pallass, and Ulinde is the newest member.
Moore, Seborn and Ulinde arrive in Invrisil, and Jelaqua says Maughin is coming too.
Jelaqua insists on telling Seborn and Moore about the Minds' secret request over Ulinde's objection, and they vote to tell Erin.
Jelaqua and Ulinde tell Erin they know she is from Earth.
Relc says High Command has it wrong about how Liscor was saved, since the Antinium saved the city; his daughter answers that they did it to trick the Drakes.
High Command, through Wing Commander Embria, orders Zevara to release Wistram's [Mages] and return their belongings.
High Command tells Zevara that Liscor's walls are enchanted and that the city and army rely on services from [Mages].
Wistram threatens to cut off services, including maintaining the walls against the spring rains.
Ceria is Captain of the Horns of Hammerad, elected in an instant, after the team's earlier leader Calruz.
Ceria Springwalker introduces herself in Invrisil as Captain of the Horns of Hammerad, a Gold-rank team.
Ceria pictures the earlier Horns of Hammerad, Gerial, Calruz, Sostrom, Hunt and Marian, marching beside the present team in a parade.
The Horns hold a magically sealed letter of accreditation that lets them draw coin from the Merchant's Guild.
After clearing the dungeon, the Horns plan to give shares of their treasure to the families of those who died in Liscor, as far as the relationships can be confirmed.
The Horns pulled in nearly a hundred pounds of gold and gems, and forty gold coins are waiting for Erin.
Erin trusts the Halfseekers, the Horns of Hammerad and Griffon Hunt with news of the enchanted axe, and calls them up to a third-floor room to see it.
After a quarrel, Pisces and the other Horns apologise and pledge to stay together; Ceria, Yvlon and Pisces stack their hands and Ksmvr joins.
On the road crew, the Horns travel in a chariot of bone and ice pulled by two undead horses.
Ceria says Hissle can ride along with the Horns in the chariot, and Reikhle accepts that they cover a mounted team's share of the work.
In the Gold-rank bar in Invrisil, Captain Todi of Todi's Elites tells Ceria and Pisces to fetch their teammates and buy everyone a round.
Pisces mocks Todi's seniority, and the room goes quiet.
Elia Arcsinger, a half-Elf Captain with a silver bow and a Named Adventurer, invites Ceria and Pisces to her table and introduces herself as Captain of Arcsinger's Bows.
The Horns of Hammerad were formed two years before the Liscor expedition; Ceria, Gerial, Calruz, Sostrom and Hunt are five members who had worked up through the ranks for years and would never quit.
All ten members of the Horns of Hammerad were sitting in the room together in one early scene, with Calruz and Gerial discussing the plan.
Ryoka described the Horns as a twelve-member party, most above level 20, led by the Minotaur [Fighter] Calruz with an enormous battleaxe.
The Horns received official permission to search a set of ruins for a week, during which other adventuring groups could not interfere or look for treasure.
Gerial, a tall mustached human warrior, is Calruz's second-in-command.
Gerial said the Horns specialise in monster slaying as a close-combat group, closing in to smash the enemy while their mages provide backup.
Gerial described the Horns' code as not breaking promises and not retreating, and repaying everything taken in advance if a job is abandoned; he murmured "Death before dishonor."
Gerial said the Horns were a Silver-rank team and not the only one in the north, and that coastal cities had Gold-rank teams they could hardly compare with.

A week before meeting Ryoka in an inn, the Horns were pinned down by a Lich at the Ruins; Ryoka ran past it and dropped off potions in the middle of the battlefield, drawing its fire, and the Horns killed the Lich and recovered many artifacts.
Ceria wears a set of dark blue robes with golden sigils that she owes to that delivery, and liquid runs off the cloth.
The Horns moved fast, hiring a carriage and horses within an hour of Ceria receiving a reply from a necromancer she knew, and paid for Ryoka's healing potions and the carriage.
Calruz said the Horns were not yet Gold-ranked, and that they would not explore Liscor's new ruins without a full fighting party.
With Calruz away and the Horns understrength and without contracts, Ceria and Gerial lent Ryoka healing potions and dry rations, and offered to guard her belongings at the Adventurer's Guild.
A speaker told Ryoka that the Horns were all out of the city, gathered by Calruz and heading for Esthelm to prepare to enter the ruins in Liscor.
The Horns arrived at Erin's inn at night, attacked her Goblin guests, and agreed to stay only after Erin stopped them; Calruz promised on his honour not to attack her guests unless provoked.
The Horns said they needed a place to stay because every tavern, inn and home in Liscor was full of adventurers.
The Horns paid in advance, and handsomely, for their first night at Erin's inn.
Before the dungeon descent Ceria handed out rations, water, four healing and four mana potions each, and explained that too many healing potions make the body quit.
After the others died, Ceria, Yvlon, Pisces and Ksmvr joined hands at Erin's inn, and Ceria declared that the Horns of Hammerad live again.

Ceria said she was in the Horns for years and had formed it with Gerial and Calruz, that they were dead, and that all fought to the end except one who ran because her friends sacrificed themselves for her.
Pisces noted that the name came from the Minotaur, and Ceria kept it.
The new Horns, Ceria, Pisces, Yvlon Byres and Ksmvr (a former Prognugator), were on their eighth night, hungry, when Ceria recalled that Calruz had kept his old group well fed and outfitted.
The new Horns had one gold coin left, having spent nearly all they had to get food quickly.
In a dungeon the new team was teleported into a pit and Ceria looked at a flickering magical rune on the wall, after which she and Ksmvr began to misidentify one another.
They left the dungeon alive with a burned spellbook, damaged artifacts and nearly eighty pounds of gold and fused gemstones, though they were not yet a proper Silver-rank team.
In Remendia a man took the Horns to be dead, and a crowd cheered the party's name when they left their inn.
The crowd in Remendia saw the Horns off with fanfare, but they were broke enough that they guarded a wagon in exchange for transport.
The Adventurer's Guild's ten percent cut of their spoils left the Horns broke again.
Ceria, Pisces, Yvlon and Ksmvr guarded Termin's wagon, drawn by the horses Erma and Fox, and Ceria told Gold-rank teams they were a Silver-rank team.
Yvlon told the Horns that she used to get sweets at the winter solstice growing up.
Newly equipped with items from a haul, the Horns of Hammerad approached the next tier of adventuring, and Ulrien suggested the Guild might recertify them as Gold-rank.
Ceria, Pisces, Yvlon and Ksmvr agreed to take contracts in Esthelm, which Yvlon said was close by and likely short of adventurers.
In a bear cave the Horns found Crelers eating the third bear; Ksmvr named them, and Yvlon's arm was broken in the fight.
Because the Adventurer's Guild banned Pisces from using people's corpses and said nothing of bears, Ceria and the others pulled a sled of undead bears into Liscor.
The Horns took a contract to hunt a large Shield Spider nest in Liscor's sewers.
After a cave of cockroaches, Yvlon said she had swallowed some, and Ceria's poisoned snow spell only agitated the insects.
In a quiet period at Erin's inn the Horns kept busy with small hunts and extermination of small monster nests.
The Horns were hired to provide meat for Esthelm's low food supplies and were away four to five days, returning on a wagon pulled by undead bears.
Erin hugged Ceria and the others goodbye, and the Horns left by boat toward the dungeon rift.
Ceria and her team agreed that more adventurers should search for Calruz, since they could not search the dungeon alone.
The Horns rowed to the rift with dozens of others in the rain, with Ceria holding about eight silver pieces.

At Celum's Adventurer's Guild, Ceria took a bounty on [Bandits] for the team, and Caddin told her they would get no help from the guild and accused them of not sharing treasure from Albez with families who lost people.
The City Watch escorted Ceria, Pisces and Yvlon to Celum's jail, taking Ceria's wand, Yvlon's Sword of Weight and Pisces' rapier.
Pisces argued that guarding contracts paid worse per hour than monster hunting and did not level their classes, while Ceria said they were wiping out local jobs.
Grimalkin used [Dispel Magic] on Pisces' Bone Horror, and Ceria's growing [Ice Wall] was punched through.
Two days after the Wistram fight, Ceria told Liscor's Adventurer's Guild that Pisces was her teammate and she would find out what they taste like if anyone claimed Wistram's bounty on Pisces.
The Horns worked for Liscor for a week, standing guard and helping build the road two miles from the Bloodfields' corruption, scouting with the Drake [Scout] Hissle.
After an Adult Creler fight, Walt and Liscor's Watch cheered the Horns as Crelerbane, and Grimalkin nodded approvingly.
After their combined spell, Ceria and her team could not cast spells for a few days, and Wishdrinks hosted them as a courtesy as Hell's Wardens.
Guildmistress Tekshia promoted the Horns to Gold-rank, since no Silver-rank team can slay an Adult Creler.
The author's note says the Horns have always been among the author's favourite characters to write.
The Horns took one of Erin's door-portals north to Invrisil about a week and a half before the scene in which Fals asks after them.
The Horns killed a Stone Golem infestation in a village's mines on the road north and planned to reach Invrisil, then The Wandering Inn, then Ryoka.
The Horns arrived at Invrisil with a magic door on a wagon, and then burned the wagon for firewood, since the door would not open unless Erin set its stone.
Ksmvr hung tripwire bells around the Horns' camp on the road north.
Gold-rank Ceria, Pisces, Yvlon and Ksmvr joined a Face-Eater Moth raid in a chariot drawn by undead horses.
Yvlon's steel-and-silver alloy armour, sword and shield are a Byres specialty, with enough silver to ward off some monsters and aid beneficial magics.
Yvlon said House Byres has always supported the Reinharts, and she calls Magnolia Reinhart "Aunt Magnolia," a close friend of her mother's.

Ylawes told Yvlon that House Byres sent reinforcements to Lord Tyrion's levy and a smaller group to Lady Reinhart, since several assassinations of [Ladies] tied to Magnolia had called her authority into question.
Fierre said the Byres family are famous vampire slayers, as are the Veltras and Terland families.
Yvlon said House Byres used to slay Vampires and, since they are dead, that she and a few other houses only keep up the traditions.
Those pledged to House Byres traditionally tithed some of their earnings at a pedestal beneath a mural of battle between silver-tipped figures and beasts.

Yvlon said the offering of silver nuggets is for the Silver Dragon Yderigrisel, whom House Byres befriended long ago; it returned during the Creler wars to fight them and died, the greatest tragedy of House Byres.

Members of House Byres drop a tiny amount of silver dust into each well they pass, as a tradition for good luck, warding the land and scaring away some monsters; too much causes silver poisoning that turns the skin blue-grey.
Wil Kallinad, one of two Humans in the Titan's class, is a Lord of House Kallinad and was miserable when asked to present something.
Niers Astoragon said the Kallinad family possesses a steel and unyielding spine, and that Wil, though he doubts himself, shows it on the field and is his best student in logistics.
Niers identified Wil's sister as Lady Talia Kallinad, a [Summer Knight] of the Order of Seasons.
The Kallinads have a personal army, and Lady Talia arrived with that army, her order and the banners of a dozen other noble families.
Warships in the harbour and the arrival of the army Wil Kallinad led threw the Iron Vanguard into confusion, with soldiers shouting for Kallinad and the Order of Seasons.
Sir Kelm, a Knight of Autumn and representative of the Order of Seasons, said he and a hundred and twenty-six peers had joined Lady Knight Talia, equipped for a non-lethal confrontation.
Lance-Commander Wylint of House Teoring brought two hundred men to Wil Kallinad for orders.
Niers said anyone with the might of a Terandrian house could have pulled off such a tactic, and asked how others could compete if Wil Kallinad could pull an army out of his pocket.
Wil challenged Tulm the Mithril to a battle in the streets, a name known around the world in a moment.

When the Gnoll Feshi asked Wil for a deal, a present for her tribe's Meeting of Tribes in exchange for leading, his older sister Talia offered two trading caravans from the Kallinad harbours through the Gnoll Plains over six years.
At the post-battle rewards, Niers called Wil Kallinad forward.
A speaker told Ryoka they were distantly related to the Reinharts.
Selys said the Reinharts were among the first humans to settle Izril, and have so many connections that half a dozen cities would march their armies if they declared war.
Lady Magnolia Reinhart is the head of the Reinhart family, heroine of the First Antinium Wars, and one of the richest on the continent.
No one made an enemy of the Reinharts without paying for it.
The Reinhart household employs a [Butler] and has an estate in Invrisil.
Maviola El called the Reinharts the richest and most powerful family, always snakes, loyal to each other, their only curse being Regis Reinhart.
Wellfar alone refused to send aid to House Reinhart.
Fierre tells Ryoka that the Veltras family, along with the Byres and Terland families, are famous vampire slayers.
House Veltras sends another request for assistance with the poisoning of its two children, this time calling on the Five Families rather than local [Alchemists] and [Healers].
Calling on the Five Families is a sign of weakness that Lord Veltras must be reluctant to show his political rivals.
The Five Families get a fuller picture that the children are sick, not yet poisoned, and Tyrion needs a cure.
The other families agree to help after an hour of reflection, since they were children, and Magnolia Reinhart is absent from Izril.
House Walchaís is one of the larger houses in Izril and not one of the Five Families; it came soon after the original noble families and traces its roots to Terandria.
Lyonette calls the house mad as loons, fond of quests, training [Knights] and duelling over insults.
Lady Bethal Walchaís is the current scion; she eloped with and married a famous [Duelist], then returned to establish her own branch of [Knights] and take control of her family.
Lyonette says Bethal's husband has killed twelve people in honour duels.

The people of Bethal's lands love her: a [Shepherd] says House Walchaís has always been good to them, paid for medicine in the Redvein Plague two decades back, and fought for them during the Sacrifice of Roses.
Ryoka's dust storm damaged farms on those lands, and she apologised and offered payment; the people accepted once they learned it was for Bethal.
The Knights of the Petal went to war for their Lady's honour, and Bethal's people refused to do business with anyone who had sent her a rose.
General Lael is the high commander of Jecrass's armies, which are known for emphasis on cavalry and speed meant to guard the wide, open realm.
Lael is a Level 27 [General], one of the highest-leveled assets of Jecrass, and young, in her early thirties.
Raelt promoted Lael because his daughter Jecaina suggested her, hiring her for loyalty over levels, and he thinks she is a decent [General] but not brilliant.
Lael had served in Belchan with distinction until she was disciplined for striking a [Politician].
Raelt's oldest retainer, Geril, is an old man who rides with the army in a hauberk, mail armor and a conical helmet, carrying a spear he can use from horseback.
When asked how she would respond to an invasion by Reim, Lael says she would negotiate a favorable surrender of Jecrass's forces.
Raelt orders the army to muster, and an army of tens of thousands, all mounted for speed, waits at the border within five hours.
Lael has confided in Raelt that the army is all mounted so that it can fall back if worse comes to worst.
At the border Jecrass's army musters nearly a hundred and seventy thousand [Soldiers], nearly half of them mounted, and a huge portion of its military might.
The River Wardens come to the border, some with their entire armies.
Jecrass's army cheers and blows horns as Reim's smaller army approaches, then falls silent under Flos's aura.
General Lael watches the Rustängmarder uneasily, and later bellows as she rides down her ranks urging her forces back to their feet.
Raelt takes all the forces he can spare across Belchan's border as soon as he has declared war, three days earlier, mostly horses, over a hundred thousand of them.
The foot soldiers barely keep pace even with Skills boosting their movement.
Jecrass's army storms through Belchan's capital and occupies it in the hour before Flos's army can get there.
Jecrass's army is a substantial force, larger than the army that Flos Reimarch destroyed.
Jecrass's army is led by General Lael and Raelt himself, and has not fought many battles, only a few skirmishes on the first day.
Raelt uses [Flicker Charge] and his army flickers, with Riders appearing among the Serpent Hunters.
In a later battle Raelt's rapier goes through Flos's chest, and Jecrass's forces advance as Reim's army freezes.
Jecrass's tired army has raced across its nation and the border of Medain for nearly a day, using every movement Skill and potions to keep riders and mounts alive.
Medain's heavy cavalry is fresh, having ridden from the capital for less than four hours.
Jecrass's army is still riding toward its Princess, staggered, as Medain's army led by its High King marches at the conflict where Raelt is fighting.
The surprise Minotaur attack kept Medain from taking Princess Jecaina away before the forces met, and Jecrass's riders are exhausted.

Flos calls Khelt a terrible nation to fight, because its armies are insanely difficult to beat on or near its own lands, cannot be demoralized and do not tire, and Fetohep can bring back more and more.
The Khelt army is made up of undead who sprint instead of shuffling or groaning, carrying ancient rusted weapons.
The Quarass says Khelt's armies are endless and undying, made of every one of Khelt's own that has ever died.
The Quarass says the Khelt army poses little threat to men in armor, and an army of that kind is only a nuisance before Reim's might.
The undead of Khelt lie beneath the soil of the barren land around Khelt, ready to fight and be destroyed again and again.
Kheltian undead rise from the ground to form a barricade protecting Trey Atwood.
A [Rider] reports an army of twenty thousand to the west that has crossed Reim's borders at a sprint, armored and without bows.
Flos says King Fetohep is sending him a message, with a knack for bad timing, and, on learning it is armored and has no bows, says that is typical.

Flos orders a [Messenger] to tell Mars to intercept the army and hold the western border with Khelt, and tells Gazi to join Mars with soldiers, the Serpent Hunters and Parasol Stroll, with no casualties.
Flos says the twenty thousand are fully expendable because they are just zombies, and that Gazi and Mars can hack them apart with minimal effort if they stay careful.
Flos tells Trey he wants to show him Khelt's armies before the trip into Khelt and says they are undead but well in hand.
Reim's army, led by Mars and Gazi, fights Khelt's soldiers in a dried valley on Reim's border while Parasol Stroll holds the high ground.
Flos says that Fetohep can make zombies run, and that Khelt's only message is this sprint.
Mars uses [Grand Slash] repeatedly to cut through Khelt's soldiers and Flos fights on foot with a mace and shield.
The wave is crushed without a single casualty on Reim's side as far as Trey can tell, and then a second army of twenty thousand sprints out of the ground toward the border.
The Quarass says four such armies have already fallen to Flos's vassals.
In Pallass, big Drakes follow Selys, and one with dark orange scales and a scarred snout confirms her name and orders his men to take her; she is knocked out and carried away.
Selys wakes bound to a chair in a dimly lit room with about eight Drake [Thugs], one a dark-orange, knife-wielding Drake who threatens her.
The kidnappers demand that she sign a contract authorizing Watch Captain Zevara to relinquish the artifact in her possession, and promise to let her go once they have it.
Selys is relieved, having feared something worse, and tells them to untie her hands so she can sign.

A female Lancrel [Builder] tells Durene that Elmmet is a good [Councilman] and that people are saying there might have been a mix-up, since the [Thief] could change faces and might have set Elmmet up.
Durene answers that she saw the thief change his face and that Beniar caught him.
After Hedag's axe kills Councilman Elmmet in front of everyone, a woman from Lancrel shouts that she killed him.
A Lancrel man shouts that the Witch murdered Elmmet, who was only accused of theft and had not been proven guilty.

A Wistram student said the Libertarians want Wistram to start taking sides with different nations and throwing its influence around, and that many of them are from Terandria and take a deep interest in its politics.
Archmage Viltach, a Human, heads the Libertarians, a mostly Human faction, and spends as much time in Terandria as in Wistram.
Viltach and his Libertarians are known for their links to Terandria, and Viltach is especially political in that sense.
The Libertarians are one of the big three Wistram factions with thousands of members and the most voting power in the Council.
Rievan belongs to the Libertarian group, and Charles was expected to join, since his family's deep pockets and influence would be welcome and the faction might help his family in political battles.
Pisces told Ceria that Timor invited him to join Charles and himself in the Libertarians with incentives, and that Pisces refused outright, saying the faction wants every new student it can get.
After Ceria was struck from behind during a test, Calvaron blamed Charles and said the Libertarians had really done it now, and her friends vowed against Charles and the Libertarian party.

Welaiat, a Libertarian, gambled and spent freely, and a Preservationist accused the Libertarians of dragging Wistram into continental affairs and always needing deeper pockets to finance their spending.
Rievan and the other Libertarians did not agree with Archmage Feor's faction or with non-Humans, but sat down when Teura stared at them.
Montressa told Isceil that at least he was not a Libertarian, and joked about having one on their team.
Viltach threw his Libertarians in beside the Revivalists, usually enemies, in exchange for votes on a referendum inviting Chandrarian bazaars to Wistram; Feor lost.
After Wistram's team rescued Eun and George from a pirate ship, the factions fought over them: the Libertarians claimed Eun and the Sedoli group claimed George.
Charles and a group of Libertarians stomped out of a simulation covered in welts, and Rievan of the Libertarians sneered at Elena and scowled at Beatrice.
Liscor's 4th Company is part of Liscor's army, a group of hardened elites, and is made up of Liscor's sons and daughters.
Commander Grasstongue, a female Drake, returns home with the company, arriving a day or two late because of the rising water, and camps at the flooded plains.
She orders word sent to Liscor's High Command that the 4th Company is back and ready to reinforce the city against monster, Goblin or Antinium threats.
The company marched day and night without resting in the Drake cities on the way.
4th Company squads, with the City Watch, hunt Shield Spider nests on the Floodplains in a cull of nearly a thousand Drakes and Gnolls in total.
The cull is a tradition of Liscor's City Watch, a gesture of goodwill.
Selys told Ceria and Gerial that the Guild had already approved their request, so they needed no seals, letters or proof to enter Liscor's ruins.

Liscor's Adventurer's Guild gets a budget, and its cut goes to Liscor's treasury rather than Guild vaults, which it does not have; Selys expected dungeon money to go to repairing gates and walls and paying hurt soldiers.
Selys had worked nine hours since before dawn, since a [Receptionist] must be on call at all hours.
Maviss said the Guild had barely enough staff to cover shifts since two new [Receptionists] quit, and Selys said Tekshia was looking but needed more budget.
Olesm sees the Council as only a nominal ruling body handling bureaucratic measures, not leaders.
At that time the Council is all Drakes, with an appointed Head Merchant rather than Krshia.
The people who seem in control at a Council meeting about the Goblin Lord are Watch Captain Zevara, Wall Lord Ilvriss, General Zel Shivertail and the Named Adventurer Regrika Blackpaw.
Jelaqua and Ulrien, as Gold-rank adventurers, are awarded a place at that meeting due to their experience.
Zel says Liscor's army is a mercenary one, far away and preoccupied, that has agreed to send a unit to defend the city.
In this scene the working Council is Elirr, Raekea and Krshia on the Gnoll side and Lism, Jeiss and Alonna on the Drake side, with Tismel and Zalaiss also representing Drakes.
Tismel and Zalaiss rarely show up, since they lack the votes to sway all but contentious issues.
Tismel and Zalaiss are traditionalists who tend to be overridden in most majority votes.
Lism is Olesm's uncle.
The Council is eight in total and needs a majority of five votes; official ratification of unofficial promises requires a vote.
Krshia leads the Gnolls and Lism the Drakes, and the two now work together against incompetence.
Zevara, Olesm, Lism and Krshia debate the Bloodfields road; Olesm announces no team may go within four miles of the Bloodfields, and Reikhle agrees to adjust the route, with a wall possible.
The Council votes against cancelling the agreement with Architect Hexel for being a Lizardperson, and six hands then rise in a joking vote to throw Tismel out of the window.
With Tismel and Zalaiss not notified of the meeting, the Council plans football and baseball teams, Krshia proposes ticket sales, and they agree to pay the Human in charge a salary.
The Liscor Watch is the city watch of Liscor, whose guardsmen are not mercenaries or bodyguards but are voted in by the citizens.
A Liscor guardsman needs at least fifty ordinary citizens to vouch for them before being sworn in, and a Senior Guardsman needs at least four hundred.
The Watch badge is crimson edged in gold and striped twice with purple.
Guardsmen must carry their badge at all times and pay a fine if they lose it; Relc keeps his on his belt because it does not stick to his scales.
From Rags's point of view, Liscor's Watch numbers nearly a hundred guardsmen, though some are always on the walls and many stay inside the city.
Rags judges that the Watch's patrols are stronger than Goblins, and that the Watch fights together with discipline and can defend easily and sally out in force.
Olesm reflects that a thousand members of Liscor's Watch and part of Liscor's army had shown in the dungeon against the Raskghar that low-level recruits could take on threats far above their level.
Watch Captain Zevara leads the Watch.
A speaker said that Relc, a former soldier turned guardsman, was the reason Liscor had had no monster attacks for the last four years.
Relc told Erin that no magic had been detected at the places the thief stole from, so the Watch thought the thief was probably just a human.
A speaker told Erin and Pisces that the Watch would no longer patrol around the inn, because the Captain refused to patrol that area after what happened with Klbkch.

When a crowd of Gnolls and Drakes gathered in front of the Watch barracks, Captain Zevara, Relc and Klbkch stood at the entrance and refused entry, saying they were holding a Human until a trial could be set up the next day.
Culling Shield Spider nests on the Floodplains is a yearly tradition of Liscor's City Watch, and 4th Company took part in it with nearly a thousand Drakes and Gnolls in total.
Guardsman Beilmark and Senior Guardsman Jeiss spotted a huge Wyvern flight over Liscor, and Beilmark ordered a runner sent to Watch Captain Zevara rather than sound the alarm.
Zevara came at a run with Wing Commander Embria and watched the Wyverns pass, then ordered priority messages sent to every city south of Liscor and to [Strategist] Olesm.
Drakes in the Watch mess hall gossip that humans smell and do not wash, wonder why Relc is interested in one, and decide he is weird.

On patrol near Erin's inn in Book 6, Drake and Gnoll [Guardspeople] say, among themselves, that the innkeeper was always crazy, that it is a shame she has all those Goblins there, and that the Goblins are "damn lucky".

Relc said the Liscorian army fights battles for other nations for pay, fielding two thousand Drakes and a few hundred Gnolls at any given moment with an average Level of 16, against 8 in other armies.
Klbkch cautioned that Levels cannot replace tactics, numbers or equipment, but said the army's strength deters larger forces and lets it fight as a mercenary force without prolonged engagements.
Relc said the army is almost always out on some campaign, and thought it had last been in the east near the Walled City.
Liscor's army has never had a good relationship with the city; it brings chaos but does not stay long, so the citizens regard it as a nuisance.

Selys said the army is the strictest group Liscor has, hating monsters and the Antinium, and that it refused to go near the city for four years after the treaty with the Antinium following the second Antinium War, returning only twice since.
Liscor's army has an officer for every five soldiers, which makes the rank of [Sergeant] worthless compared with other armies.

Liscor fields a very small force, generally two or three thousand and up to six thousand when actively conscripting, whose strength lies in its officers, who buff the army enough to fight larger forces.
Every citizen of Liscor is formally conscripted into the army at birth in a small ceremony mandated by law, though no one has to serve.

Because every citizen is technically a soldier, the army can promote many [Sergeants], [Captains], [Lieutenants] and [Wing Commanders] over a few thousand regulars, turning low-level [Soldiers] into a force fighting under many Skills at once.
General Sserys held the Antinium at Shivering Falls Pass in the first Antinium War using this approach.
Olesm reflects that the army is not invincible: it has suffered defeats, and the Second Antinium War and Az'kerash's assault showed how weak it was against an enemy with powerful magical support.

A local Centaur clan allied with the Magehammer Company, which sent two battalions and hired a few mercenary groups, and the speaker's company was fighting them in support of the Burning March Company.

Thriss told recruits that a local Centaur clan had allied with the Magehammer Company, that the allies had sent two battalions and hired a few mercenary groups, and that his force was fighting them in support of the Burning March Company.
Okasha said the Magehammer Company had taken heavy losses after three battalions flanked one of its divisions and got its lead [Strategist], leaving it to pull back.
The Magehammer Company retreated and ceded the rights to the mine to the Burning March Company.
Nerrhavia's Fallen is one of the largest nations of Chandrar, a kingdom of String People made of silk, and the most powerful, wealthiest and most populated nation at the summit in Pomle.
Queen Yisame rules Nerrhavia.
Flos says Nerrhavia is not weak but that its ruler is not prone to war, lazy as rulers go or not as hateful of him as some nations.

Flos says the land was once smaller String People states that unified about six thousand years earlier into an empire that ruled for thousands of years until it was overthrown into the Kingdom of Nerrhavia's Fall.
Silk is manufactured only in nations like Nerrhavia and is an expensive fabric, and all of Yisame's escort is made of it.
Nerrhavia is described as among the great String-folk powers, ahead of the newer Empire of Sands.
The Nerrhavian army arrives in the war on Tiqr with thousands of chariots driven by Stitch-warriors of silk, and Hemp foot-soldiers marching behind who have rough skin.
Silk officers shout insults at the Hemp soldiers, and Femithain explains that String-people society is caste-based.
The army that Nerrhavia sends into Tiqr is two hundred thousand strong, and the army is led by General Thelican.
General Thelican's forces include dreaded chariots, Hemp foot-soldiers and Stitch-mages who do not use fire, and String-people fear fire.
Octavia, who studied in Nerrhavia, says that learning there can involve sexual exchanges with masters and that it is mostly Silk-castes who get offered them.
Saliss recalls honor-duels between [Alchemists] in the streets of Nerrhavia, and [Alchemists] there usually steal each other's work.
Queen Yisame says Nerrhavia sent no army against Reim with the coalition because she did not care to, and that Nerrhavia does not fear the King of Destruction.
Yisame says Nerrhavia is an enemy of Reim, or at least no friend.
Yisame says the only thing that has roused her ire is Flos's demands of her nation, in which he provoked her response.
At the summit, after Nsiia walks away from the other monarchs, a String-person in Nerrhavia's delegation draws his sword, calls to arms for Yisame's honor and charges Nsiia.
Twice, forces of Reim clash with Nerrhavia on its border in accidental skirmishes, and the kingdom repulses Flos both times even though it got the worst of them.
Nerrhavia's Fallen, the Illivere League, Savere and six other nations declare war on Tiqr.
On the twenty-seventh day of the war, Pisces calls it a Nerrhavian-led Coalition, with Nerrhavia the largest power by far.
A report lists standing forces of at least twelve thousand on Nerrhavia's border, and Nerrhavia reinforces its lines twice until it has over ten times Mars's number of about a thousand.
Nerrhavia and Savere lead a joint army that meets Tiqr at the Reen Plains.
Thelican says Nerrhavia was a slave-state, in a conversation about turning Tiqr into one.
Queen Yisame sends a gift of around three hundred thousand gold and mercenaries, perhaps forty thousand strong, to Raelt of Jecrass.
