Yisame declares war again on Belchan, and she and Nerrhavia are horrified by Belchan's atrocities.
Nerrhavia is described as having armies beyond compare, and as marching on Belchan from the south for a piece of the nation.
Nerrhavia's Fallen declares war on Reim, as do the Claiven Earth, Savere and a dozen other nations.
The Order of Seasons is one of the most iconic [Knight] orders of Terandria, made of four factions, one for each season, with vast ranks and famous deeds.
Lady Talia Kallinad is a [Summer Knight] of the Order of Seasons, and the Titan is told that her order arrives at Daquin harbor along with the Kallinad army and banners of a dozen other noble houses.
The Order's long-time allies include a number of nations and noble houses, and over a hundred of its Knights answered House Kallinad's call for aid.
Four Seasons operate from the Order's headquarters in Terandria, near Kallinad lands, in the southeast on a coastal area famed for shipping wealth.
The headquarters is a fortress-keep of four quarters, one for each season, with neutral ground at the center.
The Order built its home in a forest where a half-Elven empire once stood, and noble houses and even royalty send aspiring [Knights] or children to join it.
At least two thousand Seasonal [Knights] are in the headquarters at any time, and far more are abroad fighting in armies, crusading or serving elsewhere.
Each Season has its own Grandmaster, and a Knight answers to her own Season's Grandmaster but may be commanded by senior members of other Seasons.
Knight-Commander Calirn can command even the Grandmasters in the stronghold as first among equals.
Calirn is a [Winter Knight], and the Grandmasters are Fall's Sentinel, the Summer's Champion Ser Greysten, the Spring's Warden and the Winter's Watcher.
By protocol, the Winter's Watcher stays elsewhere when the other Grandmasters meet in the war room, so that one remains should they all fall.

Knights of Spring are the most plentiful and mostly new [Knights] who fight en masse in wars, and Summer Knights are the pinnacle of martial might who crusade to other continents or slay terrible monsters.
Autumn Knights are scholars or [Knights] who take to magic more than most, and the younger members joke about them as 'Fall Knights' for their weaker combat.
Sir Kelm, an Autumn Knight, was the highest-level and most senior [Knight] to lead the Order at Daquin.
Sir Kelm says the Order underestimated the games at Daquin and could claim a victory, though Calirn might object to the perceived failings of the Order.

Talia says House Kallinad paid all the costs of the Order's hundred Knights at Daquin, that Kallinad generously supports the Order, and that recordings show the Order facing the Iron Vanguard in a victory.
Belavierr is one of the few named enemies of the Order, and the Stitch Witch has killed many of its Knights.
The Order of Seasons and the Guild of Hunters are listed as pursuing Belavierr, who is wanted in Terandria.
A [Broker] tells the Order, under a truth spell, that he has credible knowledge of where the Stitch Witch is, and Calirn summons the Grandmasters.
Calirn says a ship could not catch the Stitch Witch, and that he would not pit a lance of Knights of Spring or Summer against her.
Fierre learns that the Order has raised its bounty twice, offering four hundred gold coins for someone to verify Belavierr is at the place named.
Fierre learns that three people who tried to inform the Order of Seasons died.
Calirn orders the Fall's Sentinel to prepare his Season for a grand ritual spell and tells Ser Raim to return in haste, requesting the Hunter's Guild's best experts to go with him.
Talia sees black-clad Hunters of Noelictus with crossbows and swords racing toward the Order's keep around a single man in the colors of summer, and she meets Ser Raim.
The Autumn Knights call on the grand ritual, and a rift opens above Riverfarm.
Through the rift Ryoka sees ranks of Knights in the colors of the seasons, with Calirn bellowing to Belavierr and Ser Raim and six Witch Hunters stepping into Riverfarm.
Ser Raim declares that the Hunter's Guild of Noelictus and the Order of Seasons ordain Belavierr's death.
A Witch Hunter fires crossbow bolts tipped with silver.
Calirn tells Ser Raim that reinforcements are coming, that he has three days to claim the Stitch Witch's head, and that the Order is about to be assailed by Kaliv.
Calirn orders the Fall's Sentinel to send reinforcements through the ritual, and Dame Talia then leads Knights dressed in spring and summer colors in a charge at Riverfarm.
Thirty-two of the Order line up in the stronghold to be armed with plain steel and silver.
Belavierr threatens the Order of Seasons with ruin if it harms her daughter, and says she has never considered the Order her foes.
The Order's forces are attacked by Kaliv's Griffin Queen, and the Winter's Watcher stands against the Griffins.
After Belavierr survives, Calirn lowers his head and turns away.
Dame Talia leads the surviving Spring and Summer Knights, most of them younger than Ryoka, after her seniors fell, and her orders are that the Order will not make the Stitch Witch an enemy.
Nineteen Knights, thirteen of Spring and six of Summer, ride in retreat across Izril after the Hunters were betrayed and Ser Raim died.
The Knights have been ordered to avoid pursuing Belavierr and to return home.
Ser Lorell names the fallen Dame Essa, Ser Valliad, Ser Zahil and Ser Pitres, and Dame Ingrela says she would resign her arms if the Spring's Warden demanded.
Painted Soldiers is an informal phrase for Antinium Soldiers with unique markings, which are meant to foster trust.
Pawn takes over relieving Liscor's [Guardsmen] with the Painted Soldiers on the walls.
Yellow Splatters is a [Sergeant] on command duty with Purple Smile while Pawn watches a play.
On seeing the Drakes' light-ramp spell, the Soldiers ring a bell and form up shoulder to shoulder at the top of the ramp in under two seconds.
Zevara recognises Yellow Splatters as a [Sergeant], a class she notes for her report.
Marching against Reiss' army in ranks of five, about a hundred Painted Soldiers carry unique paint: a flower, raindrops, numbers, and words.
Though arrows fall among them, the Soldiers keep running and none fall, and the arrows seem to miss.
The Painted Soldiers stand around Yellow Splatters' body and make their own decision.
The Painted Antinium number nearly seven hundred, with a cafeteria and sermon hall in their barracks.
Yellow Splatters, a giant among the Soldiers, has returned from death and seen heaven.
Chesacre and Thaina chose their own names and are Soldiers who became Autonomous, perhaps Individual, and are already Pawn's [Acolytes].
Parasol Stroll is a band of robed [Mages] who each hold an enchanted parasol.
Gazi says they are mercenaries now but served her King before, and that each [Mage] is above Level 20 at the very least.
Each member's parasol is enchanted to enhance their magic and can cast spells on its own like a staff or wand.
Ulyse, a middle-aged man, and Mirin, a younger woman, speak for the group.
Parasol Stroll is busy performing the work of the Mage's Guild and coordinating Reim's magical needs.
Ulyse says they could fight an army many times larger but that being His Majesty's sole [Mages] is a weakness.
At a banquet, Ulyse presents a performance of light butterflies and birds for the King of Destruction, and Mirin raises a real wave of water.
Ulyse names Mirin, Palke and Asimi in the performance; one of the [Mages] then casts sparks that turn out real and set fire to the hall.
Ulyse leads a group of about four dozen [Mages] with parasols as foci who cancel Esiela's spells together.
Their parasols form a mass-shield against [Arc Lightning].
Parasol Stroll answers with thousands of [Arrows of Sand] on the enemy [Archers] and [Mages].
Ulyse and a dozen [Mages] cast with Grand Mage Esiela as the focal point of a link, and Minotaur [Elite Bodyguards] catch the first spells with [Spellbreaker Guard].
A [Shieldtaunt] pulls Esiela's aim back onto the Minotaurs striking their shields.
Rasea Zecrew stabs Ulyse through the throat.
The Pithfire Hounds are a six-member adventuring team led by the [Pyromancer] Levil.
The team includes the [Mages] Levil and Ullica, the [Beast Tamer] Bram with his dogs Makki and Dassa, and the [Warrior] Lamont.
Tally is the team's [Ranger], and Keima is another member; in a later scene the same third woman is named Keida.
The six are fighting in the grasslands when a group of huge shapes attacks, and two carry a downed teammate with crushed armor and bones through his chest.
After the fight, Dassa is gone and Bram wipes away tears as Makki follows him.
Their Captain, a [Fire Mage], takes gold from a black-clad stranger, and Tally hisses that it crosses a line.
Levil refuses to kill an innocent City Runner, saying the Pithfire Hounds are not mercenaries or murderers, even if Lady Bethal Walchaís is behind the message.
The team turns on the [Mercenary Captain] and the hooded [Assassin]; Levil blasts them with fire, Tally's arrow hits the Assassin, and Levil says the favor was repaid but mostly profit.
Lamont, freshly healed from smashed ribs caused by Wailer Frogs, thanks Ryoka for saving his life.
Makki is a wolfhound, smaller than Ryoka's Mousey.
Bram says Dassa was the only dog they ever lost, when the team was on the verge of being wiped.
The Players of Celum are a troupe of [Actors] that practices daily in Erin's inn, with ten or so veteran Human actors and a new cast of Drakes, Gnolls and Humans.
A Gnoll actor addresses Temile as Director Temile while worrying about the lines of a Gnollish Macbeth.
A casting call for the Players at the inn attracted nearly a hundred applicants.
Temile becomes a [Producer], a low-level one, and takes charge of the Players of Celum in Liscor with a new cast of Drakes, Gnolls and Humans.
Erin has used up all the plays she knew from home.
The original Players of Celum travel north, earning money by performing in every place they come to.
Wesle Salkis is the lead [Actor] and one of the two original performers, and he was a [Guardsman] before acting.
Jasi Redigal is an [Actress], older sister of Grev Redigal, and Emme, a short part-Dwarf woman, manages the Players.
Grev is the only child among the Players, and he is Emme's left hand, managing and assisting the [Actors].
By the time it reaches Sovvex the troupe is over forty strong, including two teams of [Actors], people for dresses, props, makeup and stage setup, and Grev.
Acting drew crowds in Celum for months and stole Wesle, a former [Guardsman], Kilkran, Pralcem, Rima and others from their jobs, becoming an obsession and a calling.
Pralcem, a former [Huntsman], objects to the Players rewriting the Bard's original text.
Emme demands the Mayor of Sovvex let the Players rent the town square for an outdoor play, and sets up barricades for a large crowd.
The Players of Celum meet the Players of Liscor in Liscor, a name chosen to avoid confusion, with over two dozen Gnolls, Drakes and a Garuda as new [Actors].
Temile says the new [Lead Actors] are already over Level 15 and everyone else is leveling fast.
Wesle, Jasi, Kilkran, Yimur and Pralcem shine with higher levels than the newer [Actors].
Grev, who knows Griffon Hunt from the inn and was with the Players, says the cast must wear illusion spells to go out and that he wears a hood because of the autographs.
Griffon Hunt sees posters of the Players of Celum in the commercial districts advertising plays such as Elisial at the Season Theatre and Macbeth.
Grev tells Griffon Hunt that the Players are now in Liscor with Drake and Gnoll [Actors], that Erin was kicked out of Celum and the Players went with her.
Grev tells Griffon Hunt about the Horns bringing down an Adult Creler, the Wyvern attack on Pallass, Erin's magic fire and her garden; he learned of them by [Message] from Temile.
Wesle tells Griffon Hunt that the Players are holding a Solstice Booth for Erin and performing Lady Macbeth with Jasi as lead.
The Players of Liscor appear on television, and Temile signs autographs with the breakfast crowd at the inn.
Jasi says the Singer herself sent the Players a [Message] saying she is a huge fan and asking for copies of all their plays.
Emme had the Mage's Guild send the entire play, which cost a bit, in return for a shipment of song-crystals.
The Players of Celum are an acting troupe that calls itself by that name for now and owes Erin a debt as its patron and muse.
Before performing at the inn they put on plays in Ocre, Remendia and Wales and were thinking of travelling further once they had enough [Actors] for two groups.
Kilkran is one of their newer [Actors], a former [Blacksmith] with a booming voice.
Pralcem plays Sir Macduff, and a fan praises a performance of Hamlet.
The troupe left Miss Agnes' inn on bad terms.
The Players of Celum announce they will perform exclusively at The Wandering Inn, guarded by Hobgoblins and an Antinium.
The [Actors] sell autographs, and Emme, a half-Dwarf woman, is among them.
The troupe performs Romeo and Juliet as Juliet and Romeo with Wesle and Jasi, and Wall Lord Ilvriss' outrage at a Drake marrying a Human sparks a riot between Drakes and Humans.
Wesle's class gives him a Skill, [Method Acting], that makes him become the person he plays, about as good as someone with ten levels.
Wesle, Emme and Kilkran, the former [Blacksmith], are among the Players at a baseball game with Erin's guests.
The Players say they have not performed for a week because other inns are smearing Erin's name.
Lellisdam's Mayor offers gold and an escort, and the troupe, now over sixty, leaves for the city eighty miles north; Temile, Damius and Rima stay with new recruits.
Jasi leaves a letter for Erin explaining the departure.
The Players perform Romeo and Juliet through the door, with Temile as Benvolio, and later Hamlet.
The troupe is over forty strong, with two teams of [Actors], and is travelling north performing in every town.
The Players discover that another group in Invrisil is performing their plays, including Hamlet, Othello and Macbeth.
Relc has seen Macbeth about thirty times and is on a backup list for the troupe.
Hearing the Wandering Inn is open again, Temile pulls the Players out of Blazehound to rejoin their Liscor [Actors]; he is their [Stage Manager].
Jasi and Wesle are the two star [Actors] at the Season Theatre in Invrisil, where tickets are near impossible to get.
Emme manages the tickets, and the troupe has a [Magician], Eltistiman, and a reserved Solstice Booth for Erin.
Jasi plays Lady Macbeth, and Revi watches from the Solstice Booth.
Wesle, Jasi, Kilkran, Yimur, Pralcem, Emme and Grev meet the Horns in the street, and Elia's team, who have tickets for the Players, are star-struck.
The Players perform an encore through the door on Erin's stage, starting with Juliet and Romeo, with Wesle as Romeo and Jasi as Juliet, and then Elisial.
Temile dines at the Djinni's Spoon, a high-class restaurant in the City of Adventurers.
Emme protests that the Players paid over two thousand gold for a broadcast slot that was not guaranteed.
The Players perform Hamlet with Jasi as Gertrude, Wesle as Hamlet and Kilkran as Claudius, dedicating the proceeds of the next ten plays to rebuilding Celum.
Temile signs autographs with the breakfast crowd, and Jasi says the Singer sent a [Message] asking for copies of all their plays.
At Erin's request, Emme, Temile, Wesle and Jasi call off negotiations with Pallass, in exchange for her promise to try to find them other major cities to perform in.
The Pride of Kelia and Gemhammer are credited with having killed two dozen Raskghar, which one of the Horns doubts.
Nailren leads the Pride of Kelia, a Silver-rank team whose members include Gnolls.
Nailren's team joins Earlia's Gemhammer for the dungeon explorations, and the two teams find a ring, gems and a knife on dead Raskghar.
Nailren has Earlia's team be quiet and takes point to lead them back.
The teams freeze when they see a Goblin's head on a stick, the sign of Facestealer, who paralyzes everything in range.
Rags's lieutenants are the Goblins who think about the future of the tribe, among them Noears, Poisonbite, Redscar, the Rockfall Chieftain and Hobs of Tremborag's mountain.
Pyrite is her second-in-command, and the Goldstone Chieftain is staunchly loyal to her.
Poisonbite says that Rags does not know what to do, and Noears answers that she is aimless but not lost and is waiting for the right chance because the Goblin Lord is dangerous.
Noears is very intelligent and dangerous, and he plays with a spark of electricity that crawls over his hands.
Redscar, who is not talkative, wants to return to the High Passes.
Poisonbite wants to build a base and raid harder, since she dislikes only robbing travelers on the road.
A Hob says the Chieftain needs to fight the Goblin Lord, but Noears says they should talk first.
The officers agree that Rags is young and smart but not strong, and some say she needs an advisor, not another Chieftain like Garen Redfang.
The Rockfall Chieftain, a supporter of Rags, says it would be good for Rags to have a mate, and the others suggest Pyrite, who is capable, solid and calm but not aggressive.
Noears and Redscar are the other likely choices, but neither is interested in the idea, and Noears closes the talk by saying that the Chieftain must do something.

Sir Kerrig sees Rags's chief officers following behind her, and they are Redscar, who rides a Carn Wolf, Noears, a powerful [Mage], Poisonbite, who carries a pair of poisoned daggers, the Rockfall Chieftain, a female Hob who once commanded a fairly strong tribe, and Quietstab, a Hob from Tremborag's tribe and a seasoned raid leader who represents the Mountain City Goblins.
Redscar leads the former warriors of Garen's tribe and is the strongest of the group aside from Pyrite.
When Erin told Rags and her tribe they were going to help, Rags's posse backed away from her and the area emptied as the Goblins ran away.
Rags's tribe has a group of Goblins with classes [Tinkerer], [Builder], [Hammerer], [Armorer] and [Scavenger], over two thirds of them without weapons, who are unique to her tribe.
Every Goblin tribe has someone who repairs armour or makes crude spears, but Rags's tribe has learned to make crossbows and built crude armour thanks to her [Scavenger Armor] Skill.
The Raverian Fighters are a mercenary company that recruits through enlisters in a lakeside city.
The Raverian Fighters are one of the hired forces, like the larger Burning March company, that push into the jungle to attack the Centaur tribe's goldmine in Baleros.
The [Sergeant] Thriss of the 4th Battalion of the Raverian Fighter's Company offers recruits eight silver coins for each day they see combat and one for each day they do not.
Thriss also promises a hot meal each night, trustworthy comrades and all the loot a recruit can carry off.
A night raid by hoofed attackers, which a soldier guesses are the Centaurs hitting them again, smashes the potion chest in the supply wagon.
Out of more than a hundred potions, the battalion keeps fewer than twenty bottles' worth after the raid.
With the potions gone, the veterans and officers look to Geneva, a [Doctor], as the only help left.
Thriss says half-shares of the remaining twenty potions went to officers and veterans, and that the regular soldiers will have Geneva until a new shipment arrives.
The 4th Battalion has over six hundred soldiers.
The Magehammer Company retreats and cedes the mine rights to the Burning March company, and the Ravarian Fighters reform their shattered battalions.
Among mercenaries, rumours spread of a red cross and a healer-class woman who saves lives and takes no side, and soldiers cling to them as legends.
The Razorshard Armor company is a Dullahan-led mercenary company that fought the Centaur Roving Arrow company, over land or possibly an old feud, in Baleros.
Gravetender's Fist, a suppression company, was hired to dispose of undead and corpses from the fighting between the Razorshard Armor company and the Roving Arrow company.
Each day both companies lined up their forces and sent them into the valley, keeping other forces hidden in the trees or flanking.
A War Walker was described as an advancement of the [Juggernaut] class, and the Razorshard Armor company sending them out meant it was determined to win at any cost.
Geneva saved a War Walker of the Razorshard Armor company, preserving part of its strength, and a commander of the company came in person to thank her and ask help with other wounded soldiers.
Both companies began to ignore the rules of war and target third parties; the Razorshard Armor company was comprised mainly of Dullahans and the Roving Arrow company was a Centaur group.

The Razorshard Armor company won and drove the Roving Arrow forces away, though both were reduced to a fraction of their force, and it secured the area for four days before Steliers' Ring forced it to retreat.
Rags judged the Red Fang tribe the strongest tribe by pure power, spread around the entrance to the High Passes with six Hobs, dominating the other grassland tribes.
Rags thought the Red Fang Tribe numbered nearly a thousand, not counting smaller tribes that paid it tribute.

Sixty Goblins on Carn Wolves, led by a Hob with a red sword, scouted Rags's tribe, with the Red Fang Tribe's main host of over a thousand Goblins, perhaps many thousands, marching after them according to a scout.
The Red Fang Chieftain submitted to Rags, telling both sides to stop fighting because the Flooded Waters tribe was strongest, and Rags became Chieftain over the whole Red Fang tribe.
On meeting them, Rags counted about three hundred Goblins, nearly forty wolves and six Hobs with good armour and weapons.
The Red Fang tribe's non-warriors were thin and scrawny and the tribe did not seem to carry much food.

Garen Redfang took the biggest tribe around by challenging its Chieftain, a Hobgoblin who fled, and as Rags had observed he was a terrible Chieftain, so the tribe did not expand and instead established local superiority, rivalled only by the Broken Spear and Ghostly Hand Tribes to the south.
Garen Redfang secretly sent thirteen Goblins, twelve and a Hobgoblin, each over Level 10 in a combat class, to kill the [Innkeeper] without telling the Chieftain.
Six Redfang Hobs, with no arrows left and no tribe, charge the twenty Eater Goats that remain, laughing.
The Redfang Hobs have limited medical knowledge, mostly stitching bad cuts and keeping wounds clean, but far ahead of Cave Goblin medicine.
Hundreds of Cave Goblins are crammed into the cave.
The Hobs lead five mini-tribes of Cave Goblins and none has the [Chieftain] class; they all still consider themselves part of Garen's tribe.
Olesm confiscates Erin's door under military law, and a Gnoll of the Watch puts manacles on Numbtongue, arresting the five Redfang Goblins.
Laken hears that two Hobs of the Redfang tribe travel in the caravan, famed for their skill in battle, and only one is male.
In the same report, a Redfang Goblin killed the Goblin Lord, Garen Redfang is their Chieftain, and another Redfang slew the [Knight] Sir Vumat.
The Redfang tribe, once invincible in the region around the High Passes that it claimed, becomes subservient to Rags, whose tribe had been little more than a group of weaklings.
Garen Redfang threw his battle with Rags: he took only part of his forces to fight her, raided with quick attacks, and gave her the position of Chieftain over all the tribes, as all the Goblins knew.
Rags is technically a Chieftain directing other smaller Chieftains, not a Goblin Lord, and the other Chieftains follow her in a coalition.
Yvlon reports that the Redfang tribe is a notorious Goblin tribe of the High Passes, active for years, that no one has defeated or tracked to its lair.
By Yvlon's account the Redfang tribe is rated as a threat no single Gold-rank team should handle alone, some of its members ride Carn Wolves, and it has done away with several Gold-rank teams.
The Redfang Warriors are mounted on the fierce Carn Wolves of the High Passes, and their name inspires fear among Humans.
About eighty regular Goblins, not Hobs, ride Carn Wolves out of the forest shouting "Redfang!", and the Human riders retreat.
The Redfang wolves are lower to the ground and scare horses, which makes them a good counter to mounted brigades.
The Redfang Warriors ride rust-red wolves thrice as large as normal.
In revenge for their fallen, the Redfang Warriors ride in small groups to Human villages and farms with torches and crossbows and set buildings alight.
Of the four hundred Redfang Warriors sent out, fewer than two hundred and forty return.
Redscar replaced Garen as the Redfangs' chief, and according to Poisonbite changed nothing about the tribe's habits.
According to Poisonbite, the Redfang elites accept any Goblin who can fight regardless of gender, but under a quarter of the warriors are female and none lead.
The Redfang tribe numbers nearly four thousand riders, who now ride horses, after taking casualties; some of the old guard who left for Rags have returned.
The Redfang tribe is unique in being mainly male, and it accepts only the best warriors, Hobs included; Hobs are rarer because they must be able to ride.
Since the split, Garen made the tribe a fully mounted force that can fight on foot but prioritises movement.
The Redfangs mourn their dead without tears and accept deaths as expected.

From a Redfang viewpoint, the Mountain City tribe, the Goblin Lord's army and the Flooded Waters tribe would probably loot the dead and kill a [Knight], while the Redfangs have honor and respect their opponents.
Redfang warriors bring down the half-Giant Moore with ropes, saying they have fought Gargoyles in the passes and know how to topple giants.
The Redfangs snare a three-headed Bone Horror with ropes and hooks while two Hobs on warhorses smash it with a warhammer and a mace.
Eater Goats see the Redfangs' red war paint and the Carn Wolves they ride and grudgingly avoid them.
The Redfang band that Garen Redfang sends after Erin is thirteen elite Goblin warriors, each over Level 10 in a combat class and led by a Hobgoblin.
The Hobgoblin leader is called Grunter.
The band includes Badarrow, Headscratcher, Bugear and Rocksoup.
Garen Redfang himself gave the band its task: to kill a Human, whom they come to suspect is the [Innkeeper] who is friends with Rags.
The Redfang tribe knew that Rags was friendly with at least one Human and often stayed at an inn.
The band decides that Garen is a poor Chieftain outside battle and that Rags is the Chieftain, and resolves to go back and tell her what Garen ordered.
Lost in the snow, the band heads toward Liscor, not knowing that Rags, Garen and the tribes have already gone far north toward Invrisil.
Pursued by the Goblin Lord's army, all thirteen flee up the road and find the ruined city of Esthelm.
Leftstep and Rabbiteater are set by Grunter to watch the rooftop, and Badarrow and Numbtongue are their quietest trackers.
Badarrow shoots a Human man who is attacking a boy, killing him.
Grunter proposes using the ruins to ambush the army in the chaos, and the band agrees.
Watching a feral girl fight a skeleton, Grunter mutters "Ghoul" and the others agree she looks like one.
Headscratcher works out that the skeleton and the young Human woman may be the sleigh-pulling skeleton Garen described and the [Innkeeper] they were sent to kill.
Headscratcher reasons that, having decided not to obey Garen, they should protect the girl; he leaps from the roof and twelve Goblins follow.
The band cleans a burned-out building, sets up a fire pit and cooks meat that had been part of Humans and Goblins into a soup seasoned with spices and flour.
The Goblins offer the girl a bowl of soup, and when a pebble she throws lands in a Hob's bowl they all laugh.
The band catches a first group of the Goblin Lord's Goblins by surprise and kills over half with arrows, then thirteen face twenty-five more Goblin Lord warriors.
A healing potion closes a wound in Grunter's stomach, and the girl ties a splint on his broken arm.
The band, narrated as no heroes and unwilling to die, will not go down against the army, even though the girl pleads with them with her eyes.
Six Redfang warriors survive: Rabbiteater, Bugear, Numbtongue, Shorthilt, Badarrow and Headscratcher, who are Hobgoblins.
Each survivor has grown abnormally over a week, nearly doubling in height, and they think losing Grunter and the ferocity of the battle triggered the change.
Their dead companions are Grunter, Rocksoup, Leftstep, Bitefly, Orangepoo, Patchhelm and Justrust.
The warriors think Garen Redfang is wrong and an idiot, and that Rags is their rightful Chieftain.
Redfang warriors do not weep for the fallen because Garen Redfang does not believe in it.
The Redfang Warriors live in the inn's basement, and Headscratcher and Shorthilt take trays down to them, staying out of sight of guests.
Erin says the Goblins are innocent, harm no one and saved her from Eater Goats.
Erin moves the Redfang Goblins up to rooms on the third floor.
The Hobs wear white armbands marked "Security" as the inn's guards.
The Goblins walk about openly in the inn, which Erin counts as an important first step.

Tekshia Shivertail receives an application to form an authorised Bronze-rank team, the Redfang Goblins: Headscratcher, Badarrow, Rabbiteater, Numbtongue and Shorthilt, four [Warriors] and an [Archer].
Five Hobgoblins spar at dawn on the grass outside the inn.
Five Redfang Warriors hold the third-floor corridor against the Face-Eater Moths, and Numbtongue loses a chunk of flesh to a moth bite.
Headscratcher recognises a potion Erin throws and hurls it, setting the corridor ablaze.
Headscratcher pounds the basement walls in grief and anger over the tribe, and Rabbiteater takes a punch to calm him.
The eight who died on the mission are Bugear, Justrust, Orangepoo, Bitefly, Leftstep, Patchhelm, Rocksoup and Grunter, leaving five of thirteen.
Numbtongue considers killing Erin a mistake and says Garen should never have ordered it.
The five resolve to return to their chieftain Rags; Grunter had been their leader, and Redscar was Garen Redfang's second-in-command.
The five swim to the dungeon rift and sink into it carrying rocks, hoping to win treasure and strength.
The Goblins carry healing potions and alchemical weapons stolen from Octavia's shop, three hemp bags and a bed sheet.
One of the items is a smoke bag from Ryoka's range.
They stole two healing potions per Hob.
None of them has passed Level 20, and Garen created warriors who train hard and rely on their skill as much as Skills.
After the trap breaks, Numbtongue stores the cloth, necklace and bell in separate hemp bags.
The Goblins fear the head-collecting creature they met may still be alive.
Selys proposes making the Redfang Goblins adventurers, Erin's idea, and all five nod eagerly; they become a Bronze-rank team.
The team Selys addresses includes Numbtongue, Headscratcher and Rabbiteater.

The Goblins decide that the captured Cave Goblin must be killed, because Goblins keep no prisoners and letting her go would tell others too much; Badarrow would shoot her, though none of them want to.
Goblins do not betray their tribe, but the Raskghar rule the Cave Goblins, so theirs is the one tribe a Goblin would betray.
On the same day as the adventurers' assault, the Redfang Warriors descend into the dungeon.
Shorthilt alone still has an iron sword, because he is possessive of good blades.

Ilvriss tells Erin the Redfang Goblins saved thirty-three Gnolls before the final raid, worth two thousand gold each, but their paperwork will appear to date from several days after the Raskghar were defeated, voiding the claim.
Offered Erin's share of money, the Hobs care little for it until she says she can buy weapons, armour or food, and Shorthilt lists an armoury's worth of items.
Two Pallass Watch Drakes charge through the door into the inn, and the portal goes dead behind them; the five Redfang Warriors surround them and the Drake [Captain] surrenders.
Numbtongue tells Erin the Redfangs can find the Cave Goblins' camp again before tonight with help from many Cave Goblins who know many spots.
The army of Reim that marches with Flos Reimarch to Jecrass's border is about sixty thousand strong, mostly infantry.
Jecrass musters nearly a hundred and seventy thousand [Soldiers] at the border, nearly half of them mounted.
Flos chose to bring a small army because it consumes fewer supplies on the march and is not threatening enough to provoke a huge response or make other rulers paranoid.
Reim's army is led by Flos, his Steward Orthenon, and Mars the Illusionist as [Vanguard].
Half-Giants, the Nomads of the Sky, march ahead of the infantry carrying long axes and staves and shed the illusion that made them look like a normal army.
Some half-Giants are only nine or ten feet tall and most are no taller than sixteen or twenty feet, though a few carry the old Giant blood strongly.
Behind the half-Giants walk a few dozen Parasol Stroll [Mages] twirling their colored parasols.
The Parasol Stroll [Mages] are followed by the Serpent Hunters, a laughing army of String-folk with serpents etched on their armor and skin.
A few hundred Rustängmarder, soldiers in dark armor with visors that hide their faces, flank the King and are called the army that doesn't die or retreat.
Reim's army does not shine with magical armor as in legend, and its silent march at first looks small to Jecrass's host.
Reim's army halts on Jecrass's border a few hundred paces from Jecrass's army, with the Nomads of the Sky leaning on their weapons and the Rustängmarder in front.
Flos tells Raelt it is a show of force.
Sixty thousand [Soldiers] disassemble the camp the day after Flos slays a pack of Manticores, and Teres is struck by the camp's tidiness and efficiency.
Orthenon and Flos have lived at least half their lives on campaign and could set up a defensible camp in their sleep.
A Stitch-Woman cook of the Hemp class, who came from Nerrhavia's Fallen, serves Manticore meat to Teres and Flos with a smile.
The cook distrusts the Gnolls and Lizardfolk in camp, calling Lizardfolk light-fingered and Gnolls half-wild savages.
Belchan shadows Flos's camp with a small force of about six thousand, while a much larger part of its army does war exercises about twenty miles away.

Jecrass's King Raelt is cheered by Belchan's citizens and his own army after the army of Reim retreats from a battle outside Belchan's walls, with Raelt believing Flos refused to use his [Army of the King].
Rain batters Jecrass's flatlands and stops Reim's army in its tracks, and four days later it is still admiring the weather, with helmets collecting rainwater.
Reim's army moves out at twice the normal speed through [Rapid March].
Reiss' Goblins march in ranks in silence in armor tarred black with resin, which Pebblesnatch finds as unnatural as monsters.
Thousands of undead, fallen Goblins and reanimated Eater Goats, move in a separate column from the living.
In battle the dead on both sides rise, and for every warrior killed an undead is spawned.
Goblins in robes with wands and staffs stand behind Reiss' troops reanimating the dead, as does Reiss himself, with his [Necromancers] and [Shamans].
Reiss' army marches on Tremborag's mountain, and Tremborag's tribe rushes to its traps and defences and fights back.
Reiss' army fights on sixteen different fronts, with camps set about each entrance to the mountain.
Reiss has an army of over a hundred thousand, though a good third are Goblins who will not fight unless cornered, such as children and heavily pregnant Goblins.
Snapjaw, the Goblin Lord Reiss's fierce lieutenant, is a Hobgoblin with metallic teeth and too large a head who rides a horse beside him.
Eater of Spears, a Hob nearly as tall as Tremborag, is all muscle and fearlessly meets Tremborag's eyes.
Snapjaw orders Tremborag to show respect to the Goblin Lord, who is not a Chieftain.
Reiss's best officers, the ones who inspired and defined his army, were slain by Zel Shivertail.
In the later battle, only Snapjaw and Eater of Spears remain, and Snapjaw leads at least fifteen thousand Goblins on horseback against the Redfangs.
The Order of the Petal is an order of [Knights] that obeys Lady Bethal, and Sir Kerrig reports being a member who was captured while attacking the Goblin tribe; no member has been known to lie.
Their armor is pink.
The Rose Knights wear enchanted armor that glances off pike strikes; the impact shock travels back down the pike instead of denting the armor.
Hundreds of Goblin crossbows loosing together do not harm the Rose Knights, who stride out unscathed.
The knights' enchanted weapons split steel shields, emit jets of fire, or leave cutting after-trails of light and freezing cold.
One knight's roar makes him seem a towering monster to the Goblins, and another hammers his shield with a Skill that creates a target for them.
A Knight of the Petal casts [Grand Fireball] with a staff, and a voice states that [Knights] can be [Mage Knights] too.
At Lady Bethal's call to shield her husband, the Rose Knights retreat from the forest; two of their comrades lie unconscious or dead after toppled trees.
A Rose Knight with a flaming halberd stands at the front of the battle against the Goblin Lord's army and holds the line with other Rose Knights.
Sir Nil Moxae and Dame Truvia Cartiil ride with Lady Bethal through the forest as her Rose Knights.
The Order of the Petal locks down House Walchaís's border and sends eighteen to escort Lady Walchaís and Sir Thomast home.
Runner's Guilds post delivery requests on a bulletin board and hand them out first-come, first-served, like the Adventurer's Guilds.
A Runner logs the seals she delivered with her name and their composition, and a receptionist witnesses the claim and signs the log.
Runners can collect their pay whenever, but most take it in one lump sum at the end of the week, signing for it so the receptionist can validate it.

Garia says Guild requests are a mix of fast, safe and heavy deliveries; fast ones go over long distances, safe ones suit messages no one should read, and heavy ones are small enough to beat a cart or wagon.

Ryoka understands that the guildmasters of local Runner's Guilds are retired Runners, as in the Adventurer's Guilds, and that the staff are hired help or people too injured or old to do the jobs themselves.
Garia says some Street Runners and City Runners belong to a group that enforces the Guild's rules, which are not real written rules but ones everyone obeys.
Runners from three nearby cities' Guilds withheld requests from Ryoka and covered them with other Runners, according to Ryoka.
Fals judges an unmarked request offering twenty gold for a delivery to the High Passes to be a death trap for any Runner, and it sits unclaimed.

Rule 21 of the Runner's Guild states that a Runner affected by spell or Skill may refuse to provide services and cancel any request, and that anyone who attacks, hinders or alters a Runner on duty can be banned from receiving or requesting deliveries.
Runner's confidentiality, an unspoken code, requires a Runner to keep client names and the nature of a delivery secret even from [Guardsmen], unless testifying about a crime.
Each Guild has private rooms shielded against eavesdropping where clients can talk to Runners about personal deliveries.
Fals said business was slow in early winter because the frozen roads made carts and wagons go slowly until they were sharp shod.
Few City Runners were working because of the Goblins, and the City Runners kept in the city took the deliveries that normally went to the Street Runners, who sat idle at the Guild's tables.
Laken met Ryoka at a Runner's Guild when heavy snow threatened the roads, saying the Merchant's Guild could not deliver food for at least a week, and asked her to carry supplies in a bag of holding.
The Runner's Guild in Celum has still not forgotten Ryoka's incident with the Frost Faeries, and its [Receptionist] frowns when Erin mentions Ryoka.
The Celum guild's Runners are out on deliveries in other cities, and the [Receptionist] offers to ask Fals and Garia to call on Erin.
The Runner's Guild stands intact but ransacked after the Bloodfeast Raiders walked in, took all the packages, and left; that is the only reason it still stands.
The guild shelters many homeless people while the woman at the desk writes letters asking for [Healers] and builders.
The [Receptionist] sends a Street Runner with a sealed request for help to every village, starting with Cimin.
The Raiders took some of the guild's people, and a list is being made of the missing.
A Rustängmarder is a soldier who ferries Flos' orders to the rest of the company.
A Rustängmarder soldier stands at attention beside the throne as Flos' words are heard when he ends his reign.
The Rustängmarder are Flos' vanguard and hammer.
After the battle, the Rustängmarder are down to twelve; Ulyse is dead, two half-Giants have fallen and Zamea's leg is broken.
The Rustless Guard is a Silver-rank team of Dullahans in good iron armor carrying shields, maces and axes, led by Captain Eldima.
Eldima complains that her team requested the Stelbore assignment first and that Daly's team took their quarry.
Eldima tells Daly about a new dungeon entrance cleared by rainfall three miles south, which her team intends to inspect first.
Eldima says she would like to join Daly's company, after hearing that the company forms alliances, not enemies.
The Rustless Guard is a group of Dullahans in armor who snare a giant snake with ropes and a net, and Eldima kills one with a [Razor Slash].
Eldima's [Razor Cut] Skill makes precise cuts easier.
Later the Bushrangers have partnered with the Rustless Vanguard, one of the best non-Gold teams in their area.
The Serpent Hunters of Clais are a band of String People mercenaries in Flos's army, noted for envenomed blades.
Gazi names the Serpent Hunters and Parasol Stroll as part of the army that is ready when she says Flos will go to war.
The Serpent Hunters, a band of Stringfolk warrior-mercenaries, and Parasol Stroll joined Flos's kingdom during the winter and were chosen to follow him wherever he went.
Jelaim leads the Serpent Hunters.
Jelaim says he is a [Serpent Hunter], a class that puts poison on weapons, and that the group was built from that class.
Jelaim says he is a mercenary captain but has none of the soldier classes that go with the title, so he asks to be called Serpent Hunter Jelaim or Hunter Jelaim.
Jelaim says the Serpent Hunters carry enchanted blades that are poisoned in their sheaths.
The Serpent Hunters have been in Reim for months by the time of Flos's banquet.
Jelaim says Flos wants them to take any of the String Folk into their ranks and teach them, so dozens of recruits have already joined.
Jelaim expects hundreds or thousands of recruits if Flos claims a land filled with String Folk.
Jelaim says they train only String People out of practicality and not malice, because String People can remove a limb before poison spreads and cloth cannot be hurt by it.
At Flos's banquet, eight Serpent Hunters with curved black-venom daggers juggle their blades across the hall in patterns.
Jelaim walks down the hall while his eight warriors throw daggers past him, then duels two of them on a table with real envenomed blades.
Flos orders Gazi to take the Serpent Hunters and Parasol Stroll, with as many soldiers as she needs, to join Mars against the Khelt army on the western border.
In the fight against Khelt's zombies, the Serpent Hunters slash and whirl with poison-coated blades while Parasol Stroll holds the high ground.

Raelt of Jecrass recognises the Serpent Hunters among Reim's army as a company famed for its use of venom, a laughing army of String-folk with serpents and bright poison colours etched on their armour and skin.
Jelaim is among the vassals who follow Flos in his camp.
Flos counts the Serpent Hunters and Parasol Stroll as two of four divisions of elites in his army.
Jecrass's army sees the laughing Serpent Hunters, armed with poison blades, on one flank of Reim's army.
In the battle with Jecrass, the Serpent Hunters cover the Parasol Stroll Mages with bows, blowpipes and blades that kill anything they cut within seconds.
The Serpent Hunters fall back carrying comrades whose string bodies were severed and field-stitch them.
Zamea and four half-Giants wait with the Rustängmarder, the Serpent Hunters and Mars on the plains.
In the battle with Ozem and the House of Minos, Flos's Rustängmarder vanguard and the Serpent Hunters hit the House of Minos.
The Serpent Hunters take fierce casualties in that battle, and five of Parasol Stroll die.
The Silver Swords are Ylawes' team and include a Gold-rank Dwarf and a half-Elf [Mage].
The three Silver Swords are known for championing just causes and protecting those in need, and have grown famous in the north, recognisable in most Adventurer's Guilds across the continent.
The three have worked together for six years and are known for arguing, as each hails from a different race.
The members are Ylawes Byres, a Human [Knight]; Falene Skystrall, a half-Elf [Battlemage] who graduated from Wistram; and Dawil, a Dwarf [Axe Champion] in full plate.
Dawil states his age as thirty eight and Ylawes states his as twenty seven.
At Esthelm the Dwarf, five foot two with a hammer, leads over twenty Silver-rank adventurers into the flank of the Goblin host.
The half-Elf [Mage], with a blue crystal staff, casts [Windward], [Flashfire], [Lesser Twister], [Water Arrow], [Silent Sickle] and [Muddy Ground].
Ylawes names the Dwarf and the half-Elf as his team, the Silver Swords.
Ceria calls the Silver Swords a new Gold-rank team in comparison to experienced teams.
The Silver Swords commit to searching Liscor's dungeon for Calruz; Ylawes says they do not need payment and champion causes regardless of reward.
Ylawes does not want to sleep under the same roof as Goblins and asks to use the door to find lodgings in Celum.
Ylawes tells Yvlon's team to hold the inn while the Silver Swords go out to distract the moths.
Ylawes uses [Shield of Valor] against the moths and later calls "Silver Swords, on me!" with [Knight's Challenge].
Dawil is an [Axe Champion] who prefers a hammer; he won his class by winning a throwing competition while drunk and has one good throwing Skill.
Dawil learns from Numbtongue that the Goblins gave the windfall to the other teams, which Falene had resented; he had bought Numbtongue two drinks.
Ylawes accepts a request to kill Gargoyles near Orefell, saying the Adventurer's Guild has a bounty on them.
Dawil kills a Gargoyle by throwing a small axe with [Champion's Throw].
Dawil tells the story of winning a Dwarven competition while drunk.
The Silver Swords have been fighting Metalbite Slimes multiplying in an iron ore mine so a village's [Miners] can return to work.
Falene takes a call while riding with Ylawes and Dawil, who she calls ill-mannered.
After monsters that explode into viscera and spores, the Silver Swords lose their horses and say they are short of coin; recent villages have paid them in heirlooms.
Ylawes introduces himself as Ylawes of House Byres, with Falene Skystrall and Dawil Ironbreaker, Gold-rank adventurers; he calls Yvlon his younger sister.
The Silver Swords ride Termin's wagon toward Invrisil, to see a famous Dwarf-smith Dawil hopes to get in with and to meet an old friend of Ylawes.
Five masked Sisters of Chell slip into the inn behind the Brothers, armed with bows and daggers, to take the door.
The leader of the Sisters says "Lady Spellcraft" gave them their job.
One Sister mumbles a curse at the mention of a Gold-rank Garuda, and some Sisters furtively search the sleeping victims for valuables until the Brother chides them.
A scarred [Nightstalker], whose first class was [Nightwalker], travels with thin blades in her sleeves and a bandaged [Blackguard] as extra muscle.
She says she was sent from the north to find out what happened with a job that went bad right before the battle at Liscor, where her people all died.
She says an entire hand of her sisters died through the door.
Numbtongue says he killed Humans he saw stealing the door when Liscor was on alert, and the [Enforcer] judges his story consistent.

The [Nightstalker] jabs a stiletto at Numbtongue and Yellow Splatters grabs her hand and she stabs him with her other stiletto, while the [Blackguard] swings a shortsword at Numbtongue and the [Enforcer] intercepts; Yellow Splatters says poison is useless against the Antinium.
She leaves, declaring that Numbtongue is marked.
The Stone Spears Tribe was not the largest, wealthiest or most powerful Gnoll tribe in southern Izril, and occupied the northernmost lands below the Blood Fields, roaming the rocky slopes.
The tribe lived and even prospered by prospecting for gemstones and valuable minerals in caves and on the slopes of the Grisrith range, which the Gnolls revere.
Much of the tribe had to spend its time digging or prospecting away from the main camp, because it was too dangerous for the young and elderly to venture up the slopes.
A Gnoll said that when Mrsha was lost the miners had not returned and were a few days' journey away, and the tribe lacked the numbers for a search.
A Gnoll said the tribe's [Shaman] knows no spells that would help, only healing and fighting.
The Stone Spears camp lies at the foot of one of the mountains surrounding Liscor.
A report said the Stone Spears tribe was wintering in the region, with half of it camped while warriors and miners went higher for ores and gems.

The same report said an [Assassin] who slipped past the Goblin Lord's army found no survivors at the mining site, and that the Gnolls had apparently been ambushed and slew over a hundred Goblins before being overwhelmed.
Garia Strongheart is a City Runner who introduced herself cheerfully to Ryoka.
Wailant and Viceria Strongheart are the married couple who raised Garia.
The Strongheart family home near a farm looked well made and expensive for a medieval setting, with a bookshelf full of books.
Wailant Strongheart gave Ryoka a hard look and met her eyes without backing down; he has green eyes.
Ryoka taught Garia to stand and punch on a snowy hilltop near the Strongheart farm.
A speaker recalled that Wailant Strongheart runs a really productive farm around Celum.
Wailant is a [Farmer] and one of the higher-level [Farmers] around Celum, whose farm is known for a specialty crop.
Wailant has many colourful tattoos, including a sea monster and a fish that seems to swim when his muscles move, and is a former [Pirate], though he is usually on the right side of the law.
Wailant shoulder-charged past a trader's cart and attacked the Hobgoblin Numbtongue in Celum, and the Watch banned him from the city for a month, then for a year.
Wailant's cutlass seldom sees use and is mostly a prop for negotiations with [Traders].
Palt asked Erin whether she knew Viceria Strongheart, whose daughter was in the city, and Garia came forward.
Garia lost weight and gained a class as a [Martial Artist], and Ceria was surprised how attractive she had become.
Wailant calls Garia his daughter.
The Ullsinoi faction is a small Wistram faction, a little under a hundred members, more like a school of magic than an ideology such as the Revivalists, but with clout where it matters.
Palt belongs to the Ullsinoi faction, and was reminded of his duties to it after the events involving Montressa.
Everyone in the faction is full of tricks, and a candidate cannot join without working out the joke in the faction's name within the first ten minutes of hearing it.
The Ullsinoi faction wanted an Earther, hoping to learn things such as electricity, harnessing lightning and flying into space.

Palt told Erin that Ullsinoi is quite flexible and small but has some influence, that Montressa is of a major faction, the Revivalists, and asked her to be an ally to the faction by giving information.

Palt negotiated through the night with the Ullsinoi faction in heated conference and then told Erin it had convinced the Revivalists not to interfere with her inn in exchange for a few concessions, such as plays and use of her door as a hub.
Montressa du Valeross's mission to pursue Pisces would be rescinded and his bounty mitigated, though not erased, thanks to communications within the Ullsinoi faction and a larger debate in Wistram.

The Ullsinoi faction does not deal with criminals, explicitly, but welcomes anyone who can read the sign, and compensates Erin for help it asks of her; Erin may refuse to shelter people with trouble on their heels.
A [Green Mage] farmer said not everyone affiliated with the Ullsinoi faction is an [Illusionist], and that it is a practical group to associate with.
The Siren's Depths are part of the Undersea Crews.
Only Drowned Folk join the Undersea Crews, becoming [Depth Sailors] rather than [Storm Sailors], and the Crews are loyal only to Drowned Folk.
Undersea Crews often came to blows but preferred submission to slaughter of their own kind.
Depth Captain Therrium Sailwinds of the Undersea Crews commands The Passing Shadow, a ship feared above and under the sea.
Captain Rasea, a half-angler who took the Sea's Bargain, joined the Undersea Crews and later left them to be a [Pirate]; even the Crews thought her mad.
The Undersea Crews' ships were unaffected by fog because they travel underwater.
Therrium demanded the treasure of The Emerald Signet in the name of the Undersea Crews, with The Sinking Light beside him.
Dozens of Drowned Ships rose around Therrium, all the Undersea Crews in the area, and later pushed back the Storm Sailors.
Pirates and Undersea Crews ships numbering thirty did not fight each other at one point.
Some nations pay Pirates or Undersea Crews to acquire medicine.
Niers notices a newly declared company in Baleros with a few sub-companies of under a hundred members each, whose striking name is the United Nations.
The United Nations company formed right after the bloody battle between the Razorshard Armor Company and the Roving Arrow Company.
It is far smaller than other companies and devoted only to finding more people from Earth and sheltering them.
Daly and others had been part of Quallet's Gravetender's Fist before.
Ken proposes that Quallet's company and the United Nations company split, as they are not working toward the same goals, and Quallet agrees and says most of his people will go with him.
Ken says the United Nations company must earn a living without fighting, with Luan as a Runner and Geneva as a [Doctor], while the two companies remain allies.
The company rents two apartments that hold at least thirty people, and over forty when the Bushrangers, Luan, Ken and Geneva's team are back.
Later, the company has a headquarters of a pair of double-story buildings from the Centauress landlady Miss Hastel.
Paige says a third building is unaffordable, since rent and other commitments weigh on the funds.

Notable members are Geneva Scala, a [Doctor] with a legend from the bloodiest battlefields; Kenjiro Murata, a [Diplomat]; Luan Khumalo, an [Expert Rower] known as the Rower of Talenqual; and Daly Sullivan with his Bushrangers, a Silver-rank team.
Ken proposes The List: a definitive record of everyone from Earth, living and dead, with ages, names, homes and next of kin.
The company's income comes from Paige's crossbows, Luan's deliveries, the Bushrangers' missions, working jobs, and mainly Geneva's condom manufacture, with her clinic also earning well.
Geneva, Paige and Idis argue about a pandemic cure while Aiko, a [Nurse] working under Geneva, is quarantined in a dedicated wing of the company building.
Paige, Kirana, Daly, Luan, Ken and Siri are among the company's leaders at its headquarters when Joseph is contacted.
In Baleros, the company tracks the progress of the penicillin, which is being grown on pumpkins, and the treatment is working.

The Unseen Empire is small, with only a few thousand people, mostly villagers from Riverfarm, Windrest and other villages raided by Goblins, and housing, feeding and protecting them is a heavy burden.
The town of Trottvisk declares itself part of the Unseen Empire.
[Witches] come to Riverfarm to make a deal with the [Emperor], among them Agratha, whose coven is large and who arrives with nearly a dozen [Witches].
[Witches] in the Empire are protected by the [Emperor]'s laws: they are punished for committing a crime, not for existing.
Eleven nobles have replied after Lady Imarris, none of them from the Five Families yet.
Vuliel Drae is a Silver-rank adventuring team that has adventured together for two years.

The members are Anith, a Jackal leader and [Mage]; Dasha, a Human [Warrior] with Dwarven ancestry and a chestnut beard; Insill, a black-scaled Drake [Rogue]; Larr, an [Archer]; and Pekona, a [Blade Dancer] with a curved sword.
Larr is a Gnoll.
Insill says the magical food the [Innkeeper] fed them lets them use only one enchantment at a time, and that it set them for the next eight hours.
The team ties itself to ropes to climb out of the hole in the ceiling, being the first to explore the dungeon by this shortcut.
The team comes out with a rough map of a new section of dungeon, a monster's head and an enchanted mace, proof that the dungeon has treasure.
The Mace of Howling, a weapon worthy of a Gold-rank adventurer, sold for thousands of gold, and the team's success reignited fervour for the dungeon.
The team says a mysterious masked swordswoman saved them, and swore to it with truth spells.
Revi calls them the stupid team that got lucky and says eight other parties have gone in and been slaughtered since.
The team supposes the masked swordswoman may be a loner or a [Doomseeker].
Vuliel Drae is revealed to have been exploring the dungeon the day the Face-Eater Moths attacked and to have smashed a bunch of eggs.
Dasha says the masked woman smashed eggs first; Pekona says the team hid in a tunnel with the masked adventurer for a day and a half, killing the small moths that came through.
Pekona says they had no idea the moths came out of the dungeon.
Dasha argues that the Goblins' treasures noticed by Vuliel Drae belong to them, and Ylawes grants that a cut is a fair point.
Tekshia says the Horns and other teams took responsibility and forfeited their possessions, whereas Vuliel Drae hid from the moths they provoked and lied afterward.
Tekshia says running away and even incompetence are acceptable, but failing to take responsibility and lying to fellow adventurers and the Guild is the one sin not tolerated.
On the Silver Swords' orders, Vuliel Drae blocks Pisces' way as the Horns try to leave to rescue their Captain.
Earlia looks away, Nailren shakes his head, and a Pallass Drake says they sometimes have hearing problems about orders, so no one backs Vuliel Drae.
The Walled Cities are not all ruled by the same method: some elect an official, others are managed by a body of powerful individuals, and some have a hereditary leader.
Pisces claimed the Walled Cities are built with Dragon bones, the skeletons of the Drakes' ancestors placed in the walls, and that this is why the Necromancer marched south.
The Walled Cities were highly suspicious of a package being sent by Courier, and would have blocked it, but let it pass under the peace treaty so as not to reveal to the Antinium what they knew.
Over the Drake attacks, the Walled Cities rejected an accusation and claimed ignorance, and Manus suggested unusual Wyvern migrations combined with freak weather.

After the Wyvern attack, Manus ordered an investigation and wall drills for Pallass, Oteslia asked for a hunting force from the other cities, and Manus needed support for secret operations, likely a strike against the Antinium.
Ilvriss reflected that Bird the Hunter's name was spreading through security briefings and [Strategist]'s notes as a new Prognugator, as dangerous as Xrn, Klbkch or Wrymvr the Deathless.
The Wellfar family is one of the Five Families who first settled Izril from Terandria.
The Wellfar family kept much of its strength, though the Antinium Wars killed some scions.
Maviola El said the Wellfars have coastal holdings, control trade, are rich, led the first navies to Izril, and are infertile and shrinking.
The Wellfar family earns money in ships and trade, and Lady Hetessana Wellfar, a wealthy widowed [Dowager], inherited much from her husband, a [Ship Lord].
Lady Hetessana had a two-year relationship with Lord Bein Terland before he fell for Lady Dealia.
Zedalien named Lady Hetessana Wellfar's claim as part of the scandal with Lady Dealia and Lord Bein that Wellfar pressed on the El family.
A speaker said Ailendamus had been approaching the Wellfar family for naval aid and might offer a cousin's hand in marriage.
Lady Gresaria of House Wellfar is the [Harbormistress] of First Landing and a [Sea Lady] over a century old.
Only Wellfar refused to send aid to House Reinhart.
Maviola told Erin that Hetessana Wellfar is a good person, kindly though lonely, despite her failed romances.
Geram said the witch Califor broke the Wellfar dam at Lake Roisemead, and Rie said Wellfar is still hunting the perpetrator.
Windrest is a village about fourteen miles east of Riverfarm, near a big prairie.
A group of around sixty Goblins hits Windrest, slaughters a dozen people and torches buildings, and a man from the village asks Laken for adventurers to guard them.
Laken promises to send an escort to Windrest.
The entire village's worth of people arrives at Riverfarm with donkey-drawn wagons and overloaded carts, doubling its population.
The Windrest folk bring their tools, including good [Carpenters] and [Builders], and one man among them is a [Blacksmith] with his anvil.
The Wings of Pallass is led by Bevussa, a feathered Garuda and Gold-rank Captain, with Zassil, Issa and Kin.
Zassil is a winged Oldblood Drake and a [Battle Flier], and Kin is the team's [Mage].
Bevussa asks that in public Issa be called the Captain, though she is the one actually leading.
After Xess leaves, Zassil blames the Scalers' botched ambush, and Bevussa slaps him on the back of the head, forgetting she is not to act as captain in public.
Bevussa shouts "Wings of Pallass! On me!" and three others fly through the door above the ground and dive on the Redfang tribe, striking four Goblins from behind.
Redfang riders on Carn Wolves leap at the diving fliers, and a Goblin seizes onto Zassil until Bevussa hurls him off.
Bevussa says the team is sticking with the dungeon rather than taking the Council's new missions, because the real gold is there.
Liscor's bounties pay two gold coins for an adult Blankipillar's venom sac.
The Wings drink Erin's foul Scale Soup, which toughens skin like leather, and Bevussa notes it costs a fraction of a Stoneskin Scroll like the one they bought from a Minotauress.
Bevussa refuses to pay for the Heartflame Breastplate, which Keldrass is renting from Miss Shivertail for the Flamewardens.
Bevussa, Zassil, Issa and Kin rescue a young child from a frost Wyvern in the street in front of the inn: Issa pulls the child clear while Kin raises a section of street with [Pillar of Earth].
Bevussa uses [Mach Wings], [Instantaneous Redirection] and [Sundering Slash] in the fight.
The Wistram team is a group of five full [Mages] from Wistram Academy led by Montressa du Valeross, made up of Palt, Ulinde, Beza and Isceil; all are top of their years.
Montressa is an [Aegiscaster] and an expert in wards and protective spells, which gives her a steady, low income.
Isceil is an [Oldblood Magus] born with a frost breath from his Dragon heritage, and he treats Oldblood ailments in Liscor.
Bezale of Maweil is a Minotauress [Spellscribe] and a graduate of Wistram who sells scrolls.
Palt is a Centaur [Illusionist] who is also a [Smoker].
Ulinde is a Selphid in a Gnoll body.
Palt says the Revivalists, a Wistram faction, put Montressa in charge of the team.
Montressa and Beatrice form a secret-broker duo, and Montressa is fairly high-placed in the Revivalists.
The five Mages come into a Liscor tavern looking for Ceria Springwalker, and Ulinde points her out to Montressa.
The Mages beat Pisces in the street until he stops moving, and Montressa draws the Silent Box over him; the box later holds the Horns of Hammerad.
Isceil tells the others that Ceria and her companion are criminals who impersonated real Wistram Mages, and Montressa captures Ceria into the black box.
Montressa says they are within their rights to hunt fugitives from Wistram, though Isceil says they should have talked to the Watch Captain.
Palt left Selys Shivertail under a [Mind Blank] with a veil, and it wears off in an hour.
Zevara declares all five Mages under arrest, calling what they did an attack.
The Liscor Watch brings down Palt with batons and clubs before he can utter a spell.
Zevara orders the prisoners released as an order straight from the High Command, with their belongings returned.
Zevara tells the Council that Liscor's High Command, through Wing Commander Embria, instructed her about the treatment of Wistram's team because Liscor's walls and army depend on Mages.
Zevara says the Wistram team may stay in Liscor under strict surveillance and will be instantly expelled if they cast an illicit spell or threaten a citizen.
Selys says she does not want them in Liscor.
Falene says Wistram gave a blanket ban on information about the team, and her friend Bashea assured her they were acting in Wistram's best interests.
Dawil tells Ylawes that Miss Springwalker informed them the trouble with the Wistram Mages is dealt with and that Yvlon is fine, while Ylawes says her arms are still damaged.
The Revivalists' strict orders to Montressa are to make a good impression and charge low fees, since the team is in trouble at the academy.
The team does consulting work in Liscor, with Montressa inspecting and repairing wards and Isceil treating Oldbloods.
Palt warns Erin that Isceil, Beza and Montressa should not be underestimated, and that Isceil can do more damage than a [Siege Fireball].
Palt says Beza can use six enchantments at once, and Montressa's orb artifact can cast [Chain Lightning] on command.

section: The insect swarm and the Crelers
text: The Wistram [Mages] link their magic, with Isceil taking the lead, and blast a swarm of insects with Frostspark Galebreath and then [Valmira's Comets], saving the Horns and two Ensoldier Shields.

section: The insect swarm and the Crelers
text: Isceil says they saved the adventurers because they were not monsters, and Montressa says they did it because they owe Liscor and not Ceria.

section: The insect swarm and the Crelers
text: Isceil dies fighting an adult Creler.

section: The insect swarm and the Crelers
text: After the Creler fight the team buries Isceil.

section: The insect swarm and the Crelers
text: Montressa says she is done and Palt stays in Liscor because of his deal, while Beza says they must deliver Isceil's remains to his home.

section: The insect swarm and the Crelers
text: Ulinde says she will quit and join the Halfseekers.

Zel Shivertail's family speaks to Liscor over a scrying orb: an elderly male Drake at the head of a crowd of green-scaled Drakes, a younger woman and others, some richly dressed, one armored and one a [Soldier] off duty.
A Drake woman says they came to read her brother's will and to see his body.
Zel's father demands to be shown the body in the open casket; some relatives gasp, stumble or scream, and the children go pale.
He orders the relatives to stand up straight and not turn away, then tells Zevara to close the casket, saying his son is dead.
Only the military Drakes among the family can look, and some have never seen a dead body.
Relatives are outraged at Zel's final request in the will, calling it a scandal and in poor taste.
A relative begins to say that they have "a, a Turnscale" in the family before being silenced.
Xalia, Zel's sister-in-law, claims the will cannot apply to the armor, and she fights her father-in-law for the scrying orb when he orders Zevara to hold the armor.
Zevara reports a compromise: the funeral will be held in Liscor, with a delegation from Pallass attending, and Zel's ashes will be sent home for burial.
A speaker reports to the Blighted King that the 5th Wall is being built.
The 5th Wall that stands is thirty feet tall and not nearly as wide as the 4th Wall, a temporary deception put up by the Blighted Kingdom in a month.
Commander Uxel tells Cirille that the 5th Wall they march beside is not the real wall, and the narration says the real one is set nearly two miles back and deeply under construction.
The narration says that [Miners] tunnel down to create a moat of moats with a thousand feet of drop before the top, and that Wistram has sent master [Enchanters] but work is slow.
The 5th Wall disappears from the war-map, turning into fragmented pieces, as Demon units flood past.
Ailendamus is a Terandrian kingdom with an army equipped with armor and blades, ruled by His Glorious Majesty Itorin II, who has ambitious plans and is laying the groundwork for aggression.
The narration says Ailendamus has swelled in recent years while facing the Dawn Concordat of Calanfer, Kaliv and Gaiil-Drome, known for breaking nations sent against it.
Ailendamus warships clash twice with Pheislant vessels and blockade trade to the Dawn Concordat, intercepting ships and confiscating or losing goods in 'routine searches'.
Wistram's Council settles only for a letter of condemnation after Viltach trades his Libertarians' votes for a referendum inviting Chandrarian bazaars to a Wistram fair, defeating Feor.
Mercenaries led by an Ailendamus [Sword Captain] raze a farm on the Tergil River in Kaliv, declaring the land forfeit by order of Itorin II.
The Kaliv [Farmer] says the land was taken in a war about two hundred years earlier and ratified by the Treaty of Everdel, and the [Sword Captain] says Ailendamus no longer recognizes that treaty.
Ailendamus suffered a bloody nose in the Lord of the Dance incident, losing an entire fleet and suffering diplomatically, though it screamed it had been a trick.
Ailendamus offered Hethon, Lord Veltras' older son, the hand of a [Baroness], or an arranged marriage with a noble of similar rank, for Tyrion's noninterference.

Tyrion refused instantly, as insulted, and asked for Princess Ozena, who was a decade older than Hethon, and an emissary replied that King Itorin would never marry his daughter to a distant noble house.
Ailendamus declares war on the Dawn Concordat, marching its armies over Kaliv's border and blockading nations such as Pheislant.
Ailendamus seized a cargo of the cure for Yellow Rivers to deny it to Pheislant and other coastal nations.
A report says Ailendamus' blockade continues while the cure appears on black markets.
Albez is a ruined city with a dungeon beneath it.
The Horns of Hammerad find treasure in the dungeon below Albez, and when they climb out into a light snow shower they realize it is the middle of winter.
Ceria and the others celebrate that they found treasure in ruined Albez against the odds.
Stan says he has been to Albez many times, probably before Yvlon was born, and never found more than a few trinkets.
Yvlon tells Stan the Horns' treasure map came from a Drake they met in Liscor who had been part of the dungeon raid.
The Antinium Hive beneath Liscor has three entrances, only two known to Liscor's Council; the third lies buried outside the city under several tons of dirt.
The Antinium plan to build a tunnel with multiple branching sections to the main dungeon's entrance and unearth it in three days.
Lady Magnolia estimates that the smallest Antinium Hive, the one in Liscor, holds at least three thousand Antinium, with two thousand Workers and a thousand Soldiers ready for war at any moment.
The Hive holds thousands, even tens of thousands, of gold coins from over ten years of hard work and little spending, in one of several treasury rooms.
The Queen of the Free Antinium calls Klbkch her "Slayer" and Revalantor, and fears that the Grand Queen will take him from her.
Xrn is present at the Hive.

A speaker tells Klbkch that the Caverns of Consumption parasites infected over forty percent of the Silent Antinium's Hive before being eradicated, and that Antinium aided the Armored Antinium against Giant Moles.
Klbkch says the monsters' attacks on the Hive have doubled or tripled as adventurers entered the dungeon, so that for the first time the Hive is losing more Workers and Soldiers than it produces.
Sixteen regular Soldiers step out of hidden alcoves to guard the tunnel when Erin enters, then stand down when one of them nods at her.

Hundreds of Antinium move through the main corridors without lanes or pause, and when Erin sneezes they all stop and look at her; asked for Pawn, Anand, Belgrade or Klbkch, they point her down a tunnel.
The Hive has no torches or fire, only a glowing mold cultivated along the walls.
A barracks hollowed out in the Hive carries painted symbols on its wall, which Lyonette understands to be a memorial to fallen Painted Soldiers.
The mansion belongs to the Archmage of Izril, who has been a recluse for a decade.
The visible mansion is surrounded by a barren circle of about two hundred feet where no grass grows and no rats forage.
A thrown rock sets off nothing, but stepping onto the ground makes it explode, and life-sensing spells in the ground trigger artillery bolts from the mansion.
The real mansion is invisible and rests on a cliff away from the death-trapped minefield, and the illusion fooled market-grade artifacts.
Ryoka notes that a bare patch of land surrounds the mansion on the rat-infested, grassy isle.
Fierre steps onto the first magical landmine and explodes.
The Archmage watches a homing [Spear of Light] enhanced to nearly triple its yield and an artillery spell go off at the intruders.
Fierre says she thinks the spell was Tier 4, since Tier 5 can vaporize and [Fireball] is Tier 3.
The invisible mansion rests on the cliff's edge, and Ryoka only knew it was there, until a door appears.
Baleros is a continent where, despite nations and kingdoms, much of the fighting is done by mercenary groups ranging from small troops to huge Companies of multiple regiments.
Clara tells Geneva that countless Companies in Baleros have their own cities and towns as bases and earn income from contracts protecting places.
Clara says the Companies send out their own armies, and the big ones have influence and representatives in other nations.
The narration calls Baleros a continent of war and death, where the warring species are Dullahan, Gazers, Lizardfolk, Centaurs and Humans.
The warring species have no time for Goblins in the undergrowth until Goblins cause trouble, when adventurers or hired mercenary companies hunt them.
Rhir is home to the Blighted Kingdoms, described as dying lands locked in eternal conflict.

Ryoka learns that the Demons and monsters from the corrupted part of the continent are so dangerous that four walls were built to hold them back, and that the Blighted Kingdom receives aid from the rest of the world, including soldiers.
The Blighted Kingdom is the first and only defense against the Demons of Rhir.
Ships carrying supplies, food, magical weapons and soldiers come from around the world to Rhir to help hold back the Demons.

The Antinium's first attacks on Drake lands matched those the Blighted Kingdom suffered in Rhir, and the Antinium bypassed four of the Walls built by the Blighted Kingdom before they met the Walled Cities.
Unlike the Blighted Kingdom, Drakes and Gnolls had no great enemy such as the Demon King to fight against when the Black Tide arrived.
A speaker claims the Antinium overpowered the Blighted Kingdom, which survived only because the Antinium wanted to leave Rhir.
Another kingdom filled with people twisted by corruption, the Demons, fought the Blighted Kingdom and proved too powerful to destroy, which led the two nations into a deadlock.
The Blighted Kingdom has built four massive walls across Rhir to make safe zones and is working on a fifth, hoping one day to wipe out the Demons.
The capital of Rhir and the first wall date to the founding of the Blighted Kingdom, and each later wall is larger than the last but not necessarily more powerful.
Lord Hayvon says that four walls shelter the Blighted Kingdom from invasion and a fifth is being built, and that few enemies have ever crossed the second wall.
Cirille hears that the Blighted Kingdom put up a stretch of wall in a month, and Commander Uxel says it shows the Kingdom has power but is not the real wall.
Rhir pays a bounty on all Crelers the world over, on top of local bounties, and the Blighted Kingdom sends a commendation and reward to the slayer of an Adult Creler.
The Blighted King has allowed some of Wistram's [Mages] to tour the walls and cities of the Blighted Kingdom.
A grand ritual unearthed from an ancient hiding place is found by the Blighted Kingdom to summon heroes in its darkest hour.
Ryoka concludes from her books that the human nations send armies to fight and die in the Blood Fields each year against the non-humans of the south.

Relc describes the Blood Fields as a battlefield where armies still fight, so soaked with blood that the entire area is full of Blood Grass, which drinks blood and eats people if one is careless; he says he fought there twice.
Relc claims that the Blood Fields guard Liscor's southern border, one of only two ways into the valley.

Ryoka reads that the Blood Fields are an empty wasteland designated for battle and one of two gateways linking the northern and southern parts of the continent, where Drake and Human armies collide when one invades the other.
Ryoka half-remembers reading that the dead do not rise, or disappear, in the Blood Fields, which would make it safe from risings.
On her walk through, Ryoka finds the soil turning crimson and learns that the color comes from a moss-like, rooted plant that drinks blood, not from blood itself.
Nearer the center, red grass and stalks grow, and the end-stage plants are tall, twisted, barkless structures like sentinels; Ryoka's skin test on one of the plants gives no reaction.

The Bloodfields lie south of Liscor in flatland that slopes away from the High Passes, where Humans and Drakes traditionally fought by mutual consent until the grass mutated red and a blood-craving biome emerged.
Beyond the pastures in the valley leading out of the High Passes, a crimson stain cuts off the easy route south.
The red grass is razor sharp, large bulbous plants with spore-like protrusions and thorny vines dominate the landscape, and sacs on those plants are filled with insects.
Watchertrees, pale trees sixty feet or taller, stand in vast circular dead zones, and Erin sees a rabbit with teeth that seems more like a predator.

Bevussa, teaching Silver-rank adventurers, calls the Bloodfields a Gold-rank threat, meaning Gold-rank teams can and have died there, and says the only safe time is after an army has burned everything away, with the plants back within the month.
To demonstrate, Bevussa shoots a pillow-like bulb with a crossbow, and it bursts to release a mass of insects that spread across the ground.
Bevussa explains that Watchertrees sense anything moving on the soil for hundreds of feet, and that their roots kill everything in the bare ground around them and can spear through unenchanted armor.
Bevussa adds that blood slimes and vampiric spiders live there, that most animals are dangerous, even the rabbits, and orders the adventurers to stay at least two miles from the visible edge.
