A Watchertree spears a fox through the abdomen with a root tendril when the fox goes for a bird lying bare of grass, then absorbs the blood.
After the Horns' encounter, Reikhle tells Erin that pollen and pulling roots seen there are new and that the Bloodfields are evolving.
The barren ground at the foot of a Watchertree stump drinks up Yvlon's blood, the Bloodfields go silent, the red grass sways, and something wakes up.
Celum is a Human city with many inns, one of which Ryoka sits in.
Celum's walls are low, only about twenty feet tall, and a steady flow of traffic passes its gates, with everyone Erin sees being Human and fair-skinned.
In Human settlements, high-level people become mercenaries or adventurers rather than [Guardsmen], so the gate guards lack the competence and pay of Drake guards.
A guard says Liscor is over forty miles south of Celum.
A friend tells Erin soon after that it is over a hundred miles from Celum to Liscor, which Toren covered in one day.
Later narration places Celum a hundred miles north of Liscor, with the High Passes and darker skies visible from the city but not Liscor's weather.
Guards at the gate are sleep-deprived, one muttering Hamlet, and no one pays notice to the Horns of Hammerad when they arrive.
Erin's reunion with the Horns in an inn full of guests draws attention, and people recognise them as the Conquerors of Albez.
When aid is sent to Esthelm, wagons stream into Octavia's shop, someone knocks the wall through, [Actors] rush to the shop, and Miss Agnes offers free drinks at her inn.
Celum hears about Erin's Hobgoblins and boycotts her inn.
Quelm's Bazaar of Alchemies sells new matches, striking on a box, at six silvers for twenty; Quelm is a moderately successful [Alchemist] of Level 20 to 25 who backs a new street gang of about forty.
A new Watch Captain does not want to risk blood and is being bribed with potions, since the last one left to become an [Actor].
By order of the [Mayor], the Watch confiscates the door to Liscor and announces that Celum will no longer do business with the inn; the Watch Captain only seizes the portal stone.
The Watch surrounds Octavia's shop, then learns that the confiscated door is only a receptacle for the real magic.
The door at Octavia's shop has been gone for weeks, with a sign saying it is closed permanently and moved to Liscor, and a [Mayor] says Celum got rid of The Wandering Inn.
Bloodfeast Raiders sack Celum: the northern gates are torn open, the walls collapse in seven places, [Fireballs] wipe out a third of the city and flames almost half.
The raiders destroy the city for nearly an hour and then leave, and reinforcements from Remendia, Wales and Ocre arrive after being convinced they have gone.
Mayor Cetris Duiland, wounded and sooty, blames Erin for taking her door, shouting that the city had bets and was supposed to be safe once she was gone.
Chandrar is the continent on which Trey and Flos' court stand, a hot, dry place that Trey likens to Egypt or a Middle-Eastern country.
Flos says that his kingdom is wasted and its walls crumble while food is scarce.
Chandrar has two moons, one pale and yellowish like the one back home but tinged slightly blue, and one purple.
Outside the city the ground is dry and dusty with shrubs of tough greenery growing from arid earth.
Flos says that Claiven Earth is the name its people give themselves, that it hates him, and that it is one of the few nations he could not conquer outright before his slumber.
The Claiven Earth is a small, reclusive but incredibly dangerous nation settled long ago by half-Elves who came from Terandria and grew a forest along the coast.
During his first rise to power, even the King of Destruction chose to make peace rather than fight the Claiven Earth to the last.
Claiven Earth is named, with the Thalassocracy of Medain, as one of two major powers neighbouring a realm that is also adjacent to the Helliosians and Germina.
A character says that the Claiven Earth and Medain would declare war before letting Flos cross their borders to the north.
Merreid is described as lying far to the north, west of the Claiven Earth, almost halfway across the continent.
After A'ctelios declares war, Nerrhavia, the Claiven Earth and Oteslia declare war too.
Armies including the Claiven Earth march on Belchan for a piece of the nation.
The Claiven Earth sends troops to support Jecrass as "mercenaries", among them half-Elf [Archers], and its Mages include thirty-plus high-level ones.

After Mars kills many of its half-Elven [Archers], the Claiven Earth writes to the King of Duels that the loss is too high a toll and that it will send scrolls of enchanted munitions instead of lives.
The Claiven Earth is represented in a mirror conference of rulers by a half-Elf, the Speaker of the Trees, a position that is not permanent.
A character says the Claiven Earth does not like to die on foreign soil.
Daquin is a Balerosian port city, large though not quite a metropolis, whose harbor can hold as many as eight warships and whose buildings are mostly stone from a nearby quarry.
Daquin lies over a hundred and fourteen miles from Elvallian, the capital of the Forgotten Wing company and training school.
The harbor has a bowl-shaped opening with external watch towers and a sea gate that can be closed.
Niers tells his students that they will gather in Daquin for a competition with the rule of no deaths, no blades and no dangerous magic.
Niers describes Daquin as having sea and surf and some very fine prawns.
A student notes from supply reports that provisions at Daquin have greatly increased, to at least enough for a thousand soldiers and maybe two thousand.
Ships in Daquin's harbor bear the Forgotten Wing company colors, as if Niers has taken over the harbor for his games.
During the first Antinium war the Drake city-states declared a state of emergency, but each city preferred to raise its own army and keep its former alliances rather than join together.
The Drake cities' separate armies let the Antinium attack with local superiority and overrun many cities around their Hives.
Before the war the cities lived in enduring war and skirmishes with each other, and the time needed to breach walls and magical defenses before reinforcements arrived kept most from being conquered.
The Antinium's style of attack overwhelmed walls by sheer numbers and speed, so relief armies found cities already full of dead or the Antinium gone.
In less than a week eight cities fell, and although all agreed a coalition army was needed, no city would send its army past its walls for fear of being attacked while undefended.

A speaker reports that the Goblin Lord crushed both armies sent against him, that Garusa Weatherfur is dead, and that Thrissiam Blackwing ordered both armies to buy time for word to reach the other cities.

The news reached Liscor and then the rest of the Drake cities almost instantly through [Message] spells sent by Zel Shivertail and Ilvriss, while Human cities heard only in the morning because [Mages] in the Mage's Guild were monopolized by Drakes.
The people of the Drath Archipelago speak a different language from the rest of the world, which leaves Pekona's command of the common tongue weak.
A Gnoll speaker says that, as far as she knows, only two groups have a completely different language from everyone else: Goblins and the people of Drath.
Drath is also called the Empire of Drath, and its tutelage is described as proud and formal.
Venaz says that the House of Minos trades with the Drathians for useful tools such as charms and anti-scrying wards, which most species have few counters against.
The people of Drath are said to be experts at refining the body, mind and flow of mana, producing pills, liquids and other methods of cultivation.
The people of Drath hunt creatures from the world's end, according to a character who has seen others, and this one was the largest.
Porcelain from the Empire of Drath is delicate and treasured.
Orthenon was raised in the Empire of Drath.

Odveig repeats a rumor that a huge Goblin tribe lives in a nearby mountain called Dwarfhalls Rest, which no one had thought occupied, under a Great Goblin Chieftain, or so women the tribe rescued claim.
Magnolia says a Great Goblin Chieftain appeared in Dwarfhalls Rest and has apparently lived there since the last Goblin King fell.
Dwarfhalls Rest is the former home of Dwarves in another age, now a Goblin bastion housing the largest tribe in the north under the self-styled Great Goblin Chieftain Tremborag.
As mountains go Dwarfhalls Rest is not large, a foothill among giants compared to the High Passes.
When the Goblin Lord's troops in black armor entered a tunnel mined out of stone, Tremborag's Goblins ambushed them from the shadows and above.
Goblin archers crouch on hidden ledges in the tunnel, and the Goblin Lord's soldiers cannot advance a step because the fight is on the Mountain City tribe's terms.
Reiss loses Tremborag's fortress to the Gold-rank teams and the Kingslayer, and Tremborag cries that his mountain is lost and his tribe flees.
Rags notes that Dwarfhalls Rest is a lot smaller than the mountains of the High Passes, barely more than a giant hill.
The narration calls the Goblins that Tyrion Veltras marched south the Goblins of the Great Chieftain of the Mountain's tribe, from Dwarfhalls Rest.
Ryoka reflects that there must be more people from Earth than just her in this world, interdimensional travelers like her.
Ryoka tells Erin that they both come from Earth and that she has learned other people from there are scattered around this world.
Ryoka concludes that the system of leveling in this world was not created by someone from Earth.
Erin remembers that on Earth, her home, she needed alarm clocks to get up and had a phone to check the moment she woke.
Trey and Teres, twins from Earth, are served dishes from their home by Flos's kitchen staff, who try to create something from Earth each day with mixed results.
Two Humans from Earth appeared in Flos's throne room after he had slumbered for over a decade.
Elbe is the capital of one of the neighbouring city-states of Dellva within the nation of Illivere, whose own capital moves with the elected Magus-Crafter.
Elbe is a splendid old capital, flatter than Dellva's, with worn stone buildings, an ancient palace and the coliseum where the Testing is held.
Elbe is about six hours' travel from Dellva.
Elbe's academy and the Purifier are stops on Nsiia's tour of the state.
Elbe holds one of the last relics of the Golem Empires of old, which was not lost so much as willfully discarded.
A guide says that Elbe believes it is the true capital of Illivere, while another replies that each state has its own wonders.
Elvallian is one of the foremost trading hubs in Baleros, once an obscure city marooned in the jungle.
Elvallian is the headquarters of the Forgotten Wing Company, one of the Four Great Companies of Baleros, when it is not on campaign.
Aspiring [Strategists] come to Elvallian to learn from Niers Astoragon, whom many claim is the highest-level [Strategist] in the world.
The city is large, built up around the front of the citadel, and one of Baleros' trading hubs, with bustling streets.
Garia places Esthelm down south, about sixty miles away, near the road that goes to Liscor.
Esthelm is the furthest Human city south and supplies itself mainly by mining, with few visitors except for trade.

section: The Goblin attack and its aftermath
text: A Goblin army attacks Esthelm in the evening, overruns the gates and slaughters people; another Goblin army arrives and fights the first, and in the confusion many citizens escape, while the city burns.

section: The Goblin attack and its aftermath
text: The Goblins loot the city's valuables and stolen food, and over half the remaining survivors begin to tear at each other over scraps.

section: The Goblin attack and its aftermath
text: Hundreds of the dead rise, including ghouls, and the refugees cannot defend themselves; a Goblin army camped outside shoots at anyone who tries to leave, and a score of people die that way.

section: The Goblin attack and its aftermath
text: Survivors form camps and gangs in the ruins and fight and kill over blankets, food and weapons, with the strongest leading the others.

section: The Goblin attack and its aftermath
text: Goblins watching the ruined city feel uneasy at how much the Humans' warring over territory resembles Goblin tribes.

section: The Goblin attack and its aftermath
text: Umbral recounts that Ylawes Byres rallied the people after the chaos, and with a timely rescue by the other two members of his Gold-rank team, the Silver Swords, drove off the second Goblin army and began rebuilding the city.

section: The Goblin attack and its aftermath
text: A plaque in the city honours Ylawes and his party, and a statue is planned.

section: The Goblin attack and its aftermath
text: Ylawes left to look for his sister Yvlon after hearing she was wounded.

section: The Goblin attack and its aftermath
text: A grave in the city center, covered in flowers and unmarked, honours a young woman who fought the Goblins and is buried with the Goblins who fought for her; Umbral credits those Goblins with killing the skeleton with purple eyes.
Erin and the Horns find Esthelm's wall patched up and manned by archers, and the city vigilant after two Goblin attacks.
Umbral, a former [Soldier], says the city is surviving but needs supplies, because Celum, Wales and Remendia claim the roads are unsafe for aid.
Erin arrives with a relief convoy of supplies, a relief force and Antinium from Celum and Liscor, and the people of Esthelm cheer that aid has come.
After a day, most wagons, the Gold-rank adventurers and many Antinium return south, while hired adventurers, extra [Guardsmen], [Healers] and a group of Antinium under Anand stay to finish the walls.

Esthelm repels an attack by part of the Goblin Lord's army as it marches by, with a quarter of its people dead and over half wounded; its citizens now nearly all have combat classes and the Antinium repaired its walls.
A Redfang tribe approaching Esthelm sees repaired walls with many Human [Archers], who fire arrows that fall short.

Esthelm goes on high alert after seeing the Redfang tribe, and alarm spreads when the fleeing Flooded Waters tribe, led by Redscar, Poisonbite and Noears, races south past the city in front of the Goblin Lord's army.
Esthelm was sacked once, and survivors rebuilt it stronger and higher after fending off Goblins and undead; its guards keep longbows at hand.
Fals describes First Landing as the biggest city, found by going north to the ocean, over three thousand miles north of Liscor, perhaps closer to four thousand.
Its watchful towers keep vigil over the north sea, built long ago by Human nobles who fled Terandria in fear that others would follow.
It is called the first and grandest of the Human cities built on Izril, and the ancient seats of power were established there, including the Reinhart mansion, which is taller than some palaces.
In the war against the Goblin King, the Humans' oldest and grandest city on the continent was the Goblin armies' target and was regarded as the metaphorical heart of the Human people.
A history notes that the Walled Cities predate the construction of First Landing by at least six thousand years.
Eight Goblin Lords besieged First Landing for three weeks, and the Five Families gathered their forces for a stand at its walls.
Lord Tyrion Veltras took command of the city's defense while Lady Magnolia Reinhart marshaled the rest of the nobility.
The Floodplains of Liscor are a valley formed between the High Passes, one of the two routes between northern and southern Izril.
For two months of every twelve, the spring rains fill the floodplains with water that engulfs all but the highest hills until it drains, an annual and well-known process.
Klbkch says that at the time of Erin's first weeks the Floodplains hold few creatures besides Goblins, aside from grazing herds.

Relc says giant spiders hide in tunnels there soon, that the quietest time of year gives way to a ton of weird creatures once the rains start, that travelling animals come to graze when the rains stop, and that winter gets really dangerous.
Quillfish, octopus-fish with teeth and Rock Crabs creeping underwater are among the dangers in the floodwaters.
In the spring rains, barely a week after they begin, the waters engulf the Floodplains and only a few of the tallest hills and the city stand above the waterline.
From her hill, Erin sees the inn's hilltop surrounded by water a few feet deep, with Liscor in the distance also surrounded by water, and the water still rising.
Later, the eternal rain around Liscor has ended, but the Floodplains are still mostly brown mud, while the hill the inn stands on is lush.
The Frenzied Hare is an inn run by Agnes, who tells Ryoka she stayed there when she began as a City Runner.
Agnes was a [Tailor] by trade before she became an [Innkeeper] with her husband, who has been ill in bed with a fever for two weeks.
The barmaids at the Frenzied Hare are Maran and Safry.
A patron says Agnes' husband Jerom is a good cook, though Agnes, who runs the inn in his absence, is not.
While Erin stays there, the inn is packed each day with customers drawn by her cooking, and Agnes acts as barmaid while Erin flips crepes in the kitchen.
Agnes is the actual owner of the Frenzied Hare, and she and Erin split the profits.
Agnes hopes Erin will become the real manager of the inn even once Jerom recovers from his sickness.
The inn serves a strong local drink called a Firebird.
A speaker says Erin usually eats at the Frenzied Hare, more often now that the inn has a new cook.
Jerom is still feverish and sleeps too much, but Agnes hopes a new alchemist's potion bought with Erin's help will cure him.
Safry serves tables and cooks whatever is needed in the kitchen.
The [Garden of Sanctuary] is a Skill of Erin's, and Mrsha is the first to find the door into it.
The garden is a domed, circular room of dark brown wood covered with vines, reached through a door that vanishes behind the visitor.
The door to the garden can appear anywhere in the inn, and Mrsha sees it near the kitchen's door.
Erin can enter the garden by stepping backward toward any wall, and can exit through any door she names, such as the kitchen.
Erin says the Skill is based on her magic door, and she would never have gotten it without that door.
Palt tells Erin that the Skill is an Inheritance Skill that only one or a few people get at a time, and that an [Empress] first owned it.
Palt says the garden was a secluded refuge for those of royal classes and the most secure place he can name.
A circular opening in the dome lets bright light fall into the garden, and Mrsha sees blue sky and clouds that look like the sky above Liscor and a mountain of the High Passes.
Soft grass covers the ground, and the garden is large enough to hold a small hill and is divided into different spots.
A shaded part has loamy soil, a stone with huge mushrooms and a ring of small purple mushrooms in the grass.
A meadow of every flower color except black, with wheat and full-grown grass, lies on a plateau in the middle.
A clear pond with smooth stones and sand at its base sits against the wall, and Mrsha guesses it is fed by rainwater.
A moving fog wets a dense jungle zone at the base of the hill with sycamores, fronds and burr-bushes.
The other side of the hill is arid, with yellow grass and an acacia tree with small thorns.
Mrsha concludes that the garden has zones of marsh, arid, tropical and temperate.
There are no bugs, fish or other living things in the garden except plants and the visitor.
Klbkch reports that the tropical area has a number of plants indigenous to Baleros but nothing harmful, only some thorns.
Saliss finds many mundane plants in the garden.
Mrsha's [Druid] class tells her she is safe in the garden.
Moore raises an [Earthen Spire] under Zevara and Olesm, who climb through the opening in the dome and appear on the inn's roof.
A speaker concludes from this that the garden is a secret room, letting in sunlight and probably rain but not enterable any other way.
Numbtongue is led by Mrsha up a foggy hill to see Goblins Erin had known, including Bugear, Headscratcher and Shorthilt.
Spiderslicer, Noears and Eater of Spears are also among the Goblins on the hill, together with Garen Redfang on a Carn Wolf.
Reiss sits at a stone table with a hole in his chest, as he looked when Erin saw him die.
Erin, Numbtongue, Lyonette, Mrsha and Bird plant seed cores in each biome and plant cocoa, carrots, cucumbers, potatoes and wheat.
Mrsha uses her wand to make the garden's plants grow.
Erin hopes the garden will provide free blue fruits, chocolate, faerie flowers and apple trees.
When Erin offers the garden for the night, it holds Mrsha, Lyonette, Pawn with Antinium, Ekirra and other Gnoll families, Visma, Kevin, Rose, Joseph, Imani, Troy, Leon and Galina.
Bezale and Montressa ward their rooms in the inn instead, and half the Players of Liscor sleep in the garden with friends or family.
Bird refuses to leave his tower because he does not need to sleep.
Erin tells Palt the garden cannot support everyone because it is too small, and that if the inn goes, so does it.
Ger is the capital of Germina, a city built around an oasis from which the kingdom was founded.
The oasis is a vast reservoir of water that has sustained Germina for thousands of years, and the first Quarass claimed the land there.
The palace of the Quarass, known as the Seat of Ger, is the tallest building in the city, standing on a slope atop the city and directly over the reservoir that feeds the wells.
The King of Destruction personally leads his armies into Ger, cuts down everyone in his way, climbs to the Palace of the Quarass, and beheads her.
Nearly a month after the Quarass's passing, Flos's armies still occupy much of Ger and the country to keep order.
Germina is a Shield Kingdom, one of four remaining, ancient and sometimes waning but never erased.
Rags sees a former city of stone inside a mountain that, after centuries of neglect and Goblin habitation, still shows traces of what it had been.
Rags thinks Dwarves perhaps carved the place and built its monuments, while Goblins broke down windows and walls and strung bridges and rope across it.
Huge furnaces expel black smoke upward, their embers never die, and Goblin [Blacksmiths], whom Rags has never seen before, hammer and reforge metal there.
Guards in the stronghold wear steel armor that makes even some Hobs look on in jealousy.
Goblins in the hall wear steel or iron arms, some complete plate armor scavenged from adventurer corpses, and others hold glowing magical swords.
Rags counts over thirty Hobs in one room, with far more present.
The mountain is hollowed out as a dwelling for tens of thousands of Goblins, and the narration says it was built under Tremborag or perhaps stolen and claimed by him.
The Goblins took what was apparently an abandoned Dwarf city and chipped away rock walls and ceilings, and the space inside feels vast.
Tremborag's tribe is the only tribe there before Rags arrives, but sub-Chieftains who manage parts of it or lead warbands fight each other for influence.
Goblins mark factions with ragged armbands or tattoos, and all the [Blacksmiths] wear a chain bracelet or necklace.
When Elia Arcsinger appears, Tremborag leaps into a lower tunnel and Tremborag's Goblins and the Goblin Lord's forces throw down weapons and flee in panic.
The narration says Tremborag's mountain is lost as both the Mountain City tribe and the Goblin Lord's army flee the Human army and the memory of her.

Goblinhome is the name of the fortress Rags built in the mountains with the remnants of every tribe, including the Flooded Waters Tribe, the Mountain City Tribe, the Redfangs, the Cave Goblins and a few survivors among Reiss' subjects.
The Mountain City Tribe dug out the fortress, which is a copy of Tremborag's mountain.
Part of the fortress is a huge wall of wood built into the stone on one side of a valley.
Arrow slits dug into the rock and camouflaged let Goblins shoot crossbow bolts from the darkness.
A dozen hidden passages lead to the roof, each trapped with a fire-trap hatch that explodes in the face of anyone following.
Goblinhome uses its limited bags of holding, relics of tribes or stolen from the Liscor battlefield, to drop boulders from walkways, including an eighty-pound boulder from a hundred feet up.
Wolf Riders on Carn Wolves use bolas tied to bags of holding to snag Wyverns, so that boulders of about four hundred pounds suddenly appear and drag the Wyverns down; there are four such bags.
Goblins fire a ballista of Wyvern hide, sinew and bone at the Wyvern Lord, and the force of the shot tears it free of its mounting.
The last defense against adventurers is a trap-hill with crossbow Cave Goblins and a single Hobgoblin [Greatbow Sniper] on the cliffs behind a Thunderbow, who has killed exactly three adventurers.
Montressa says Wistram wants her and Beza to investigate the Golden Triangle in Pallass on orders from Naili.
Beza says some [Lords] and nations have joined the movement, and thousands of gold are being turned into profits.
Montressa and Bezale discover how much gold is going to the Golden Triangle and file worried reports.
Yerzhen says that everyone knows it is a pyramid scheme.
Yerzhen says he heard a rumor that Viltach and Feor both want the scheme to continue, because large groups going into debt helps Wistram.
Yerzhen says the Walled Cities are at the center of the scheme and over a hundred thousand gold pieces are in circulation through it.
The Elusive Lot decide to warn friends and gangs, expecting Wistram to move once word spreads.
Hectval is a small city closest to Liscor, part of the Hectval-Drisshia-Luldem Alliance, a defensive pact between nearby cities and towns.
Hectval is the nearest city past the Bloodfields.
The Three Cities Alliance is known for crossbows, strong bows and arrow fletching, with hilly terrain that makes fighting its [Archer] battalions a pain.
Hectval sends Liscor a letter, exceptionally formal, asking for an exchange of goods, ideas and visitors and for a meeting, as Liscor's new road nears completion under Master Builder Reikhle.
Hectval sends a delegation of some of its city leaders to Liscor, the first guests, and Liscor's Council debates a soccer game to show off.
A delegation of three dozen well-dressed Drakes with packhorses arrives in Liscor during the chaos, saying it is the delegation from Hectval.
The Hectval guests arrived unannounced and are placed at the Tailless Thief.
Hellios is a kingdom in Chandrar to the northeast of Germina, a sometimes friendly neighbor ruled by Queen Calliope.
Hellios has no [King]: Treland of Hellios died decades earlier at Flos' hands in his first wars of expansion, and Calliope rules alone, followed by her son Prince Siyal.
The narration says the capital of Hellios is a mountain-fortress, like the other cities that use geography to their advantage.
Before winter, Flos' armies marched north at speed with Orthenon, Mars and Gazi, and the conquest of Hellios took less than two weeks.
Hellios surrendered unconditionally as Flos' armies crossed its borders and crushed its army.
Queen Calliope and her son Prince Siyal became captives in their own castle, because Flos made it clear he would behead both royals if the army resisted.
Hellios' army laid down arms almost to a man rather than keep fighting, because the royals' deaths would have sparked an uprising.
Both Calliope and Siyal had been spared death, for the moment.
Later, Flos calls Calliope the former Queen because she abdicated, and says she is complying, if unhappy, while Hellios supplies resources.

Flos says Orthenon is free to leave for other work soon, perhaps leaving the upstart [Prince] to manage his own kingdom, and that he would rather have Hellios supply resources and soldiers than be a thorn in his side.
Flos requests more [Builders] from Hellios and Germina to colonize old villages and rich farmland.
Runners call the High Passes a very nasty place, where more Runners have died than in most places and where tons of monsters live.
Fals says that surviving the High Passes would take fighting skills or insanely high levels, probably above Level 30, to get out unscathed.
The High Passes are the tallest mountains in the world, estimated by Archmage Chaiemegia at over seventy thousand feet, perhaps higher.

Two known routes lead through the mountains: one by a basin, the Floodplains and Liscor, which is mostly safe, and one straight through the High Passes past a Dragon's cave, known as the route of death.
Ryoka sees rust-colored rock mountains looming, which together form an impenetrable barricade except for a small gap winding through them.
The gap is a road as wide as two football fields, strewn with boulders taller than fully grown oak trees.
Ryoka, wearing a foul-smelling potion by Octavia, is shunned by a Goblin tribe, Carn Wolves, evil toothed goats and gargoyles, all of which flee her smell.
A naked, human-shaped creature with twisted eyes and a stretching clawed arm stalks Ryoka in the pass.
Teriarch scares the creature away with fire and tells Ryoka that darker things lurk in the High Passes that either do not smell or have different opinions about smells.
Halrac warns other adventurers that the High Passes hold Eater Goats, Gargoyles and worse monsters, and that Eater Goats can sneak up on even Named Rank adventurers at night.
Halrac says a Weyr lies in the High Passes, where one wrong move means facing a Greater Wyvern and a few hundred Wyverns.
Illivere is a mage-state that produces Golems, and its leader is the Magus-Crafter Femithain.
Pisces says Femithain is a cautious and pragmatic ruler who may have been reluctant to declare war on Tiqr.
The Illivere Federation is a group of smaller states with several thousand years of unity and roots in Golem crafting even earlier.
Illivere borders Nerrhavia's Fallen and is a small fish in a large pond, with its might resting in Golems.
Each Illivere state votes for a smaller group of Crafters, the elite who manufacture or manage Golems, who in turn vote in the Magus-Crafter.
The nation's capital is Demarsel, for now, because Femithain belongs to the state of Dellva, so the head of Illivere shifts when the next Magus-Crafter is elected.
Ressa reports that the Illivere League launched an immediate assault into Tiqr.
Illivere sends only eight thousand soldiers and four hundred Golems against Tiqr.
The narration says Illivere's eight thousand are experienced [Soldiers] but its strength lies in the Golems.
Tiqr surrenders to Illivere rather than to the coalition, and Femithain keeps Nsiia as a political prisoner of Illivere.
Invrisil is called the city of adventurers, named for having the largest population of adventurers.
Durene says Invrisil has Gold-rank teams, sometimes Named Adventurers passing through, and markets full of magical items, monster parts, rare gems and artifacts.
The narration calls Invrisil the heart of the northern half of Izril, a place that would appear on any map of the world.
Reynold says the [Guardsmen] at the gates check all visitors, even Runners, because Invrisil sees far more magical artifacts and dangerous items than most places.
The narration says its streets hold String People, Drakes, Minotaurs, Gnolls and Humans, so it is more varied than a Human city like New York.
Many buildings are painted or given artistic fronts by [Painters] and [Muralists], and hanging orbs of crystal give light even by day, some enchanted to change color.
Reynold points out that the city guards are fine warriors, some of them retired adventurers.
Invrisil has a separate route for vehicles so wagons do not mix with pedestrians.
Later narration says Invrisil is guarded by low ten-foot walls that seem to expand each year, and that it is one of the largest cities on the continent and a hub connecting the northern Human lands.
The Gold-ranks have their own section of the adventurers' guild, reached through an ordinary door.
Invrisil is owned, at least in part, by Magnolia Reinhart.
A gate [Guard] tells the Players that Lady Reinhart encourages the arts and that every inn and tavern in Invrisil has something special.
The narration describes Invrisil as a trading hub that dwarfs Celum and Liscor.
A merchant selling balms says Invrisil is the last major city going south and gets trade from all over.
A performer says a Level 40 [Troubadour] in the city steals audiences from other musicians.
The Goblin Lord tells Osthia that the Origin of Seeking Death is the Goblin name for Invrisil and asks if the City of Adventurers can be taken.
The Goblin Lord decides to go around Invrisil to a lone mountain northeast of it, saying he needs more Goblins and tribes, and that there are more past the city.
The narration says Invrisil had not come under attack since the Second Antinium Wars and, with the Goblin Lord's armies near, its adventurers are in hiding.
Later, the gates are closed at night by the Mayor's orders because a decomposing flesh giant was sent at the walls less than a week earlier.
Izril is the continent of Drakes and Gnolls and a few humans, which the Drakes call Issrysil; Ryoka will only pronounce Izril.
Izril is vast, and Humans have lived on it for millennia without settling or intruding into some parts, where monsters, disease or bad luck erased earlier structures.
A Gnoll says it was said long ago that Izril was known not as the home of Drakes and Gnolls but as the home of Dragons.
The High Passes mountains separate northern and southern Izril, with one route through the Floodplains of Liscor.
Zel Shivertail grew up in the south of Izril, where even the smallest Drake city-states have a clear chain of command, open lines of communication and order.
The Antinium have six Hives and a foothold in southern Izril, and the Hives and nearby foothills are forbidden zones that Drake cities patrol.
The Assassin's Guild in southern Izril never recovered from its war with the Silent Antinium, unlike the flourishing Human guilds in the north.
Politics in Izril is a game of connections and intrigue, of strategy and alliances.
In the Antinium Wars the Antinium barely slowed as they rampaged across Izril, and later the Humans, Drakes and others of the continent united against the Goblin King's armies.
News of Zel Shivertail's death spreads across Izril and then to every continent at the speed of magic, with riots in the first day in southern Izril followed by silence and tears.
Jecrass is a kingdom whose nobility are called River Wardens because they control the rivers that make Jecrass rich in horses.
Jecrass is known across the continent, and perhaps the world, as a place to buy good horses.
Raelt privately calls the River Wardens River Robbers, because anyone who owns even a stream can build farmlands, raise animals and dole out the precious water.
Jecrass is famed for the speed of its riders.
Jecrass borders the Republic of Belchan, a democracy known for its mage-schools and gold mines, whose ruler is Prime Minister Lyfelt.
Jecrass has more water than the southern nations such as Hellios or Reim thanks to its rivers, and sells some water each month to Khelt.
At Raelt's court, the River Wardens Warden Winta, Dulfe, Cerani and the twenty-seven-year-old Emile discuss a paper read out by Geril.
Warden Dulfe is frog-like, and Raelt notes that he put a copper tax on every bucket of water drawn from his wells.
Raelt orders Dulfe to announce and count the citizens claiming the King of Destruction's protection or intending to leave.
Dulfe suggests in reply that the Wardens contribute less gold to the royal coffers if Raelt fails to protect the borders against Reim, perhaps through a vote.
Jecrass' fast raiding parties attack held settlements, overrun garrisons and threaten Reim's supply lines, so Flos' armies cannot advance too far.
A speaker notes that Silver-rank adventurers, a Gold-rank team Orthenon hacked up and Stitch-Soldiers from Nerrhavia appear on Jecrass' side.
Other nations back Jecrass unofficially, sending gold, soldiers and even artifacts to Raelt to push back Reim.
A speaker, consulting a [Strategist], says Jecrass just lost twenty percent of the entire nation by retreating to fight closer to its main cities.
Jecrass' army falls back, General Lael abandons her front, and Reim's armies advance unimpeded, stopping only for the King of Destruction's wounds and to fortify.
Raelt writes a two-line letter to every nation that has contacted him, saying he intends to sue for peace at any cost by nightfall.
A breakaway wing of about four hundred Jecrass heavy riders with long-handled axes and shields on bicorns crashes into an equal number of Medain [Lancers] and downs them.
A history book calls the Clash on the Jessal Highlands the event that began the Second Antinium War in earnest.

Five days after the start of summer, a Drake army formed by three of the Walled Cities and a number of lesser city-states marched past the Antinium's border and laid siege to one of their Hives by surprise, meaning to exterminate the Antinium.
The Drake army laid waste to the Hive, killing Workers and Soldiers, and used rain-based tactics to flood its tunnels.

section: The battle as Klbkch tells it
text: Klbkch says that he and Xrn were the only two Prognugators close enough to respond, and that they found the Drake army dug in with a kill zone of [Mages], [Archers] and a wall of [Spearmen].

section: The battle as Klbkch tells it
text: Klbkch says the Antinium had only seven Queens left, so the Drakes' strike on the Hive forced them either to attack or to lose a Queen.

section: The battle as Klbkch tells it
text: Klbkch charges with the Soldiers while Xrn fights the Drake [Mages], and the Antinium break the Drake lines only when Wrymvr arrives with the Flying Antinium.

section: The battle as Klbkch tells it
text: On that day the Antinium freed the besieged Hive and its youngest Queen, whom Klbkch personally rescued from drowning and who later led the Hive in Liscor.
The history book says the battle on the Jessal Highlands ended in disaster for the Drakes, leaving recriminations among city-states that had not known of the surprise attack.
The history book says the Antinium launched a counterattack at once, and their armies were marching again within a day of the battle.
The Quarass tells Trey that Khelt is a necrocracy, one of two remaining in the world, and an ancient kingdom whose borders are seldom questioned.
The Quarass says Khelt is not a Shield Kingdom, since Germina is older, and that Fetohep is the latest of its rulers and is six hundred years old.
Jecrass sells some water to Khelt each month, and Fetohep pays dearly for water Jecrass can spare.
Khelt is a green forest in the desert, with plants and trees blooming across its land.
Its villages are built of carved stone, painted without wear, with fully maintained paved streets and roads even outside the capital.
The people are well dressed, look healthy, and some are pudgy.
Hundreds of skeletons harvest, sow and water the fields, and a skeletal horse pulls a plough.
The Quarass says that undead crave death, that Khelt's undead are held by their [King], and that other undead might seize control of them.
Khelt has a playground with a wooden fortress, rope bridges, a slide and swings, because children there are not apprenticed or put to work.
The Quarass says Khelt's children are safer than anyone because Fetohep's reach touches all his land and his people are buried everywhere.
The capital has walls only to block sand and no fortifications like Reim or other cities.
Fetohep says slavery is banned within Khelt and outsiders are banned, as they spread diseases and violence.
Fetohep says his people work four of seven days and give three of the rest to pleasures, working less than laborers elsewhere.
Fetohep says his people are sterile without his blessing.
Fetohep says his people may leave Khelt at any time with his blessing, coin and provisions, and no child may be taken, but those who leave may not return.

Fetohep says his fifteenth predecessor, King Thekheldan, observed his subjects grown apathetic and quarrelsome, and the reforms since have kept Khelt's people working so that few take to pure indulgence.
In the same line, Fetohep calls Thekheldan the third of Khelt's rulers, which contradicts calling him the fifteenth predecessor.
Fetohep says Khelt uses artifacts such as Oasis Tears, gems that produce limited water, of which he has enough for a few barrels an hour.
Fetohep says [Hydromancers] drawing water from the air take from an already dry land, so it is better to have them remove salt from seawater, and Khelt imports water when necessary.
Fetohep says every drop of rain and the oceans imported over centuries are stored beneath Khelt, enough for a year or a decade.
Khelt pays lavishly for [Mages] to carry water from the sea and bring rains each year.
A pass leads out of the Order of Seasons' territory and down into the Kingdom of Pheislant.
House Kallinad is under the domain of the Kingdom of Pheislant and owes it loyalty.
Wil Kallinad says Pheislant is a coastal nation, known for its lighthouses, which is not as big as some of Terandria's larger kingdoms and has a weaker land army.
Wil adds that Pheislant would probably act if Ailendamus pushed at Calanfer and the other nations, because they cannot be allowed to keep expanding.
Pheislant's largest port-city is Phel's Light, with harbors on the southwestern edge of Terandria that give easier access to Baleros, Chandrar and Izril than Lord Bel's harbors further east.
The Order of Seasons is headquartered in Pheislant on its own lands, allied with the kingdom, and is one of the largest orders in Terandria and part of Pheislant's might.
Relations between Pheislant and the vast kingdom of Ailendamus, which threatens war, are strained.
The 3rd Prince of Pheislant, Tellsiv, is a devoted fan of a travelling [Singer] who performs her way south to Pheislant.
A knight says Pheislant has no reason to support Ailendamus and many to oppose it, and that it will decide where it stands if Ailendamus pushes.
Levrhine is the capital city of Belchan and the home of Grand Mage Esiela.
Levrhine has its own garrisons and defenders, probably tens of thousands, to prevent a surprise raid.
Raelt of Jecrass takes three days to reach Levrhine, slowed by his battles and the prisoner trains he takes.
Esiela is forced by contract to march with the other [Mages] against Levrhine, her home, to be attacked before nightfall.

Orthenon reaches the capital with six thousand cavalry, intending to prevent the Prime Minister from fleeing, and finds a massive army already encircling Levrhine with its gates open and horses pouring in.
A speaker proposes to take Levrhine first, to claim it before it is destroyed and its people slaughtered.
Liscor is a walled city of Drakes, built with the help of the industrious Antinium, that is also home to Gnolls and the occasional Beastkin and is visited by many races.
Ryoka is told, before she reaches it, that Liscor is a city far to the south with no humans, only Drakes and Gnolls.
From the inn, Liscor looks like a black spot in the distance; Relc and Klbkch say it is about ten minutes' run away, while Relc says it is only an hour's walk with few monsters on the way.
Erin cannot make out the city from the window, and Klbkch says he believes humans have more limited eyesight than Drakes or Antinium.
Relc says the area within a few miles of the city is regularly patrolled.
Klbkch says that only those with a past record of crime are unwelcome in Liscor.
Liscor's wall is nearly forty feet tall, and its gate is two solid metal doors instead of a portcullis.
The city's buildings are of stone and wood with a lot of roundness, gently sloping roofs and open rooftops; the streets are hard dirt, in places paved with cobblestones.
Most of the people Erin sees in the streets are Drakes, with the occasional Gnoll and only rarely an Antinium.
Drakes stare at Erin in the street while Gnolls and other furry people keep as far from her as they can.
Dress in the city varies: some male Drakes wear only loincloths and perhaps a light cloak, many female Drakes wear little more, and only the Gnolls follow a human-style dress code.
Liscor's bathrooms are marked with tails instead of stick figures: a long straight tail for male, a curly tail for female.
Klbkch says herds are usually confined in villages north of Liscor, while the city itself hosts pigs, sheep and horses.
Relc claims there are only two ways into the valley, north and south, that the mountains are practically impassable and that the Blood Fields guard the southern border.
Klbkch replies that the north is still relatively unguarded and worries that the human nations might unite.
Relc says the human nations lie to the north and that Drakes have an okay relationship with them.

Selys explains that Liscor sits near the centre of the continent where it is narrowest, and that it is the only way through the mountain range apart from the High Passes and the coastal routes to east and west.
Selys adds that without Liscor, goods must travel around the continent by land or sea or brave the High Passes.
A Necromancer nearly destroyed the city about ten years before Erin's arrival, according to Relc.
Klbkch says the three most dangerous things to Liscor are said to be rain, the undead and war.
Relc says Liscor is home to a Colony of the peaceful Antinium, one of five in the world (he corrects himself from six).
Klbkch says the Antinium have a standing contract with the people of Liscor, providing services and goods in exchange for their presence.
Relc explains that the Antinium defend the city if it is attacked, help with construction and other jobs, and send some of their people to work jobs like Klbkch's; in return nobody kills them.

A merchant tells Erin that prices have risen since the humans' caravans arrived, that the Watch has been picking fights with adventurers, and that a human thief is said to have come with a caravan, so Humans get the blame.
A Drake says there have been a number of petty thefts across the city, and that Shopkeeper Lism was the latest victim.
Ryoka thinks that the closest city to the High Passes is Liscor, though a runner has to go around the mountain range to reach it.
Someone tells Erin that the road south of the city was destroyed ten years earlier and that no one has lived south of Liscor since, apart from her.
Erin judges Liscor bigger than Celum or Esthelm, and a footnote says its walls are second only to those of the Walled Cities, as all Drake cities have gigantic walls.
The Antinium dug the tunnels of Liscor's sewers but are not obliged to clean them or clear out the monsters.
Liscor has no hospital: people heal at home, hire a [Healer], or rely on organizations, and the Adventurer's Guild and the Watch each keep a few beds.
A speaker tells Erin that Liscor has just over ten thousand souls.
The center of the city holds a large park with a playground of towers, slides and rope bridges, where a Wistram [Mage]'s spells, checked each year, slow children who fall.
Liscor is Sserys's home city; in the Antinium Wars it was besieged by a huge Antinium army but repelled it countless times thanks to above-average magical wall defenses.
The city was attacked a few weeks before Erin's walk through it with Klbkch in the snow.
Klbkch tells Erin that over eighty guardsmen and nearly two hundred civilians died before the Hive was mobilized, and that the Antinium lost sixty-five Workers and forty-seven Soldiers.
Two Gold-rank teams enter Liscor that evening.
Residents have gradually grown used to Pawn's daily patrols, and his Soldiers bring back Shield Spider and Corusdeer carcasses that are turned into meat for the city.
Hawk reports to the crowd that the Goblin Lord has crushed both armies sent against him, that Garusa Weatherfur is dead and that Thrissiam Blackwing had ordered the armies to buy time.
The news reaches Liscor and the other Drake cities almost instantly through [Message] spells from Zel Shivertail and Ilvriss, while Human cities hear in the morning.
A Drake says that Liscor does not let undead into the city for any reason.
The Siege of Liscor in the Antinium Wars lasted three months by the time it reached breaking point, with every adult taking to the walls.
News of Zel Shivertail's death strikes the city like a wave, and Drakes stand weeping in the streets while horns blow.
Klbkch carries the news to the Queen of the Free Antinium and then, through a black mirror, to the Grand Queen.
Three days after the news, black banners fly at half-mast on the battlements, Drakes weep openly, and more than half the usually open shops are shuttered.
Zevara has the Watch check all four walls for cracks before the rains, because she knows enchantments can fray like stone.
Selys explains that every year, after winter, hard rain falls for about two months, the city is practically closed off, and Liscor floods.
Zevara recalls that Carn Wolves prowled the Floodplains three years earlier and that everyone's [Dangersenses] warned them to stay indoors.
During the Face-Eater Moth attack, Zevara orders the wall command spells prepared and the Antinium summoned, siege alarms sound, and a glowing field of energy springs up around the city.
After the battle, Liscor's dead have been recovered and cremated, buried or otherwise laid to rest, and only moth corpses remain on the walls.
Embria declares that her 4th Company will henceforth dedicate itself to defending the city against Goblins, dungeon monsters and other threats.
Floodwaters rise halfway up Liscor's walls; Drakes and Gnolls leave on rope ladders and a ramp to a floating dock, where a small fleet of boats waits.
When the rains stop, a rainbow appears over Liscor.

Messages arrive that other Drake cities are sending aid to Liscor: Oteslia's Winged Riders can arrive in six days, Zeres pledges eighty thousand soldiers and five thousand Saltscale Wardens, and Manus pledges an army.

Zevara confiscates the inn's magic door and orders the Pallass Gold-rank teams to stay in Liscor, and Ilvriss demands they fight until the walls fall, with the door staying in the heart of the city as an escape route.

Eight days after the Goblin Lord's death, the city is short of wood for cremations, and Zevara notes that the eastern gate is still destroyed and cracks in the wall must be repaired before the next spring rains.
Zevara says the trial of the Minotaur prisoner will begin soon.
Liscor mainly imports goods, helped by the army's mercenary work and some natural resources, and its shops with preservation runes serve as its grocery stores.
In Liscor, artisans do not sell personally as in Celum and the north but go through [Shopkeepers] as middlemen, and some [Shopkeepers] run warehouses for others.
The Council is usually made up of Guildmasters and other prominent citizens who rotate every two years, with eight Councilmembers; Ilvriss stepped in to aid it after the disasters.
Krshia tells a crowd that rent has doubled in some parts of the city without the Council acting and that Zevara handled most of the work during the Raskghar attack and the siege.
Krshia says Liscor can hold less than a hundred thousand souls at full capacity and cannot grow larger than its walls.

Numbtongue is barred from Liscor: the gates slam shut on him three days running, the Watch tells him the Council voted that no Goblins may enter, and Zevara's signed paper naming him an adventurer does not change the orders.
Erin backs Zevara, who warns that the inn's magic door to Liscor would be removed if Numbtongue used it.

Ulseil Greenscale announces the results of an election that replaces the Council with a democratically elected group of eight for two years: Raekea Silversmith, Elirr Fultpar, Krshia Silverfang, Lism Swifttail, Alonna Swiftwing, Jeiss Sielmark, Tismel Lischscale and Zalaiss Holmfyre.
A new residential district is being built west of the western gate, with new apartments, Antinium Workers hauling stone, and plans for the city to grow a third larger.
The expansion's plans come from an [Architect] travelling from Baleros, and the Antinium raised a ten-foot temporary outer wall of stone and dirt in a single day.
Liscor has public bathhouses with hot, scented water that cost five coppers to enter, which Erin pays at the same rate as Drakes.
Gnolls and other Beastkin pay twice as much as Drakes because of their fur.
The bathhouses are of high quality, like Roman ones in Ryoka's eyes, and rent private bathing spots for a small fee.
Bathers need not wash before entering, since purification spells are used.
Drakes and Gnolls bathe in separate rooms, and the baths are also gender-specific.
Erin says Gnolls are touchy-feely while Drakes are not, and that Selys told her she once went to the bathhouse with Krshia, so the separation is not a strict rule.
Klbkch confirms that a dungeon lies under Liscor and says his Hive has fought monsters emerging from it for many years.
Klbkch says that some monsters are drawn to the location, many seem to have nests inside, and the dungeon has traps and many magical defenses.
Klbkch says the Antinium Queen once wanted to secure the dungeon herself but found that unfeasible, so she chose to open an entrance in the hope adventurers would eliminate some traps.
A speaker says none of the adventurers want to go in, that Griffon Hunt has not yet gone through the entrance, and that the dungeon is another threat for the city besides the Goblins.
The official entrance is guarded by sixteen city guardsmen with bows, spears and one apparent [Mage], watching from behind a small wooden rampart.
Adventurers also go toward a second entrance, and Halrac and another speaker discuss a set of ropes stretching over a hundred feet down.
Later the second entrance is the rift in the ground, a chasm leading to the surface, and Halrac prefers it though the escape route is a long perilous climb.
The official entrance leads through a maze of trapped rooms that has not been cleared.
Reports of the dungeon's monsters include Shield Spiders, Crypt Worms, various undead, enchanted suits of armor, Bog Wraiths, a trap full of Face-Eater Moths, giant infested slugs and the Children.
Teams in the dungeon have also met groups of Goblins and strange Gnoll-like monsters who use weapons and fight efficiently.
The first group to meet them and survive, Vuliel Drae, brought back several heads that resembled a Gnoll's but were far larger with vicious canines.
The narration says a nation long forgotten by the living once built a city far underground, and the dungeon was built out of its ruins.
Toren notices that trap-filled corridors are not populated by most monsters, while others lead into nests holding tens of thousands, such as the massive Shield Spider infestation.
Toren concludes the monsters are deliberately organized so they do not crowd each other.
Rainwater pouring down the chasm does not enter the dungeon but pools a few meters overhead as a wall of water suspended in midair.
Halrac notes that the layer of water between sky and dungeon has grown.
Liscor's market is a wide, cobblestoned street lined with wooden stalls, and Erin first reaches its food section after what she thinks is an hour or two of wandering.
Drake shopkeepers there sell goods such as weird blue-leaved plants that look like oversized white carrots, and meat cut to order.
During the first game of chess in the street, most customers stop haggling to watch, and a Gnoll sells them food as they watch.
Manus is a Walled City on the border zone next to the five Antinium Hives, on land claimed by the Antinium during the First Antinium War.
Manus is called the City of War because it exports military might, not goods, with the largest army and training schools that produced legends such as General Sserys and Dalthson Forwing.
Manus is the bastion of Drake might against the numberless Antinium and bordered their Hives in both wars, which is one reason the Antinium failed to expand.

The narration says Manus is fairly poor as Walled Cities go, second-poorest after Oteslia, since its military industries and imports of Pallassian steel, Oteslian food and Fissival magics make it weak to economic pressure.
Manus is designed as a many-sided star whose walls overlap and hit any threat.
The outer wall slants outward a few degrees, so ladders fall on attackers, and it has machicolations that let defenders pour oil, spells and arrows on those below.
Beyond the first wall lie a glacis and an inner wall on the incline, so attackers who take the outer wall find themselves exposed.
The outer wall protects the lowest layer of the city, mostly residential, which can be sacrificed in an attack, while valuables lie past the second wall.
The city is full of slanted walkways, choke points, portcullises and plazas that let defenders block an army's advance in three or four ways.
The narration says Manus is unassailable by ground and almost so by air, with towers, narrow passages against flyers and sacrificial heights that can be evacuated in case of aerial spells.
The officer's academy in the inner city is to Izril what Wistram is to [Mages], and Drakes and Gnolls from every city come to learn war there.
Manus' Lords and Ladies of the Wall add to their ranks every decade by merit rather than heritage, and include [Generals], [Captains], [Commanders] and [Strategists].
Manus is an elective monarchy whose leader rules for two years per election, and may be re-elected without limit if they do the job well.
Manus' war council runs to a room with a scrying orb and learns that Pallass is under attack by Wyverns.
The people gathered include Dragonspeaker Luciva Skybreath, [Hunt Commander] Makhir, General Milka, Wall Lord Kishield and Wall Lady Rafaema.
Rafaema says she ordered four full wings to alert and that they are already heading toward Pallass.
Rafaema looks no older than twenty-three yet commands deference beyond her apparent age, and she is a Dragon.
Market Street is a street of closely packed wooden stalls in Liscor, meant as temporary structures that can be taken down for the next shopkeeper.
A fire sweeps through the street and destroys nearly half of it, even cracking the paving stones from the heat.
Relc says the fire was started by the mystery thief, caught the night before, who used a fire spell to escape.
Not long after the fire, the unburnt half of the street has resumed business as usual and Workers have already replaced a large part of the burnt half.
A Guardsman now walks the street every few minutes, and Humans who enter get unfriendly looks, though shopkeepers who know Erin do not mutter insults at her.
In winter the street has braziers, iron poles and basins of burning coal that warm the air, and some shopkeepers cook food over them for passers-by; Erin buys roasted meat from a Gnoll.
Erin is told that cooking on the street is free except for a fee of five silver coins if she makes over four gold coins' worth of profit.
After Erin's example, every Gnoll and Drake food vendor on the street sells hamburger variants, with cheeses, spice blends or different meats, and one Drake sells a quadruple-patty version.
A Gnoll traveler recalls that Medain's [King] did not want them there long, and that they had a difficult time gathering supplies there, unlike in Jecrass.
Flos says he knows Medain's [King] but must ask Orthenon his name.
A group of Medain [Lancers] shouts a battle cry naming High King Perric, the Golden Ranks and the Kingdom of Adventurers.
A speaker infers from the Silver-rank and Gold-rank adventurers fighting beside Jecrass' army that Medain is supporting Jecrass.
Raelt's peace letter reaches King Perric among other monarchs.
A Medain Knight-Captain sends about four hundred [Lancers] against a breakaway Jecrass wing, which smashes them.
Medain's ruler seized a cargo of the cure for Yellow Rivers out of desperation, because Yellow Rivers ran in its ports.
Merreid is a Shield Kingdom, a single city in the desert of Zeikhal, far north and west of the Claiven Earth, near the top edge of the Great Desert, where it sits on a trading route.
Merreid is called the Labyrinth City, the Bazaar of Fables, and the city that thinks.
Merreid is a safe haven whose bazaars are truly neutral, and no one may break its laws, not even its rulers.
Its builders trusted to craft and law to make something larger than any person, and dragons and ancient Drake fortress-cities never took it.
Djinn serve as Merreid's defenders, bound by an order given before the first Quarass was born to maintain and defend the city, and no ruler of Merreid can command them to battle.
Merreid was founded when Djinni and Jinn were both plentiful, and the Jinn have died while the Djinni are slaves.
Merreid's rulers control the people and manage trade, but not the djinn, so they are less influential than other Shield Kingdom rulers.
Noelictus is a Terandrian nation, inland, and inconsequential to Manus's politics.
Aldonss authenticates reports from Noelictus about one of Manus's Grade 9 threats.
News of Noelictus has not spread openly, since the Court of Dusks and Landsreight seem to have tamped rumors down, while the [Witches] of the north are apparently gathering.
A speaker says ghosts returned to walk Noelictus.
A Knight asks about the Stitch Witch Belavierr, whom they said was in Noelictus.
A knight says that Noelictus's armies, Ailendamus's forces, the entire Hunter's Guild and [Knights] far and wide have a right to her.
Hunters of Noelictus travel with Ser Raim.
Oteslia is a Walled City, known as the City of Growth, that grows cash crops and exports produce cheap as Izril's agricultural giant.

The narration says Oteslia is the poorest of all the Walled Cities by a lot, though poorest of them is still richer than most, because a Level 30 [Farmer] harvests six times more than someone from Erin's world.
Oteslia grows coffee beans, actually red berries, which it is trialing as an expensive additive in stamina potions.
Oteslia has saved more than one city from starvation with free food shipments, so smaller cities consider it a hero, but a quarrel with it would only make enemies buy food elsewhere.
Oteslia contends year by year with ensuring harvests and fighting monsters such as locusts, Crelers and hungry birds, employing [Druids] and [Gardeners].
Oteslia has the largest Pegasus population in the world and the largest Gnoll-to-Drake population of any Walled City.
The city is built upward around a vast central tree, the Heart of Oteslia, and is surrounded by a vast lake that serves as defense, water source and entertainment.
The First Gardener has a balcony built into the wood of the Heart of Oteslia and looks over terraced rice paddies and arid zones where every plant is grown.
The narration says the Walled Cities were designed for roles: Manus to train, Zeres to hold the seas, Pallass to create, Salazsar to mine, Fissival to connect and Oteslia to provide.
Fissival's teleportation network would have connected all the Walled Cities so that none would starve under siege, thanks to Oteslia's foodstuffs.
Oteslia's great secret is known to Manus alone among the other Walled Cities.
The Drake Cire, ward of the First Gardener Shaerrha, is a Dragon over ninety years old who is in the middle of his adolescence.
The First Gardener forbids Cire to date Plains Gnolls, fearing he will let something slip.
During the Second Antinium War, at a private meeting in Oteslia, the Lords and Ladies of the Wall found six Silent Antinium and four [Assassins] dead under the tablecloths after ten minutes.
Ilvriss tells Erin that Pallass is a Walled City and about three hundred and eighty miles from Liscor, roughly the distance to Invrisil.
Ilvriss says a veteran [Courier] such as Hawk can travel over a hundred miles in a day, far more than a mounted rider can manage without Skills.
Nelliam welcomes Erin to Pallass as the north-most of the Walled Cities.
The narration calls Pallass one of the six Walled Cities of Izril.
Pallass is known as the City of Invention, and one of its guides boasts that it manufactures more arms and potions than any other city on the continent.
The narration says each Walled City specializes in a trade, so that Pallass forges weapons and does alchemy while Oteslia is an agricultural giant and Salazsar rules the gem trade.
The narration says inventors in Pallass can be granted a stipend depending on what they do.
The walls, streets and buildings of Pallass are made of a sandy cream-colored stone.
Pallass has four walls, one in each cardinal direction, towering in the sky.
The city's urban center sits at the lowest level, and four massive staircases rise toward the walls to reach higher floors of buildings.
Each level going down is progressively smaller and circles the interior of the walls, so the city looks like an inverted pyramid or a bowl.
Houses sit on ledges that protrude from the walls, water is pumped up to hanging gardens, and the four stairwells descend into the center.
The highest residential level is too high to see the walls from.
Erin's door is set up in a high residential spot chosen as the first empty space.
A guide says any new construction must be approved by an [Architect] and an official who knows the city's layout.
The Blacksmith's Quarters were built two years before and occupy the second-highest level, in response to complaints about smoke and noise.
A guide says that one of Pallass' [Craftswomen] invented the smock mill the month before, a lighter version of the tower mill that can be built from wood and metal.
Nelliam shows Erin an elevator worked by a hand crank and gears that descends slowly without magic.
Nelliam says larger lifts powered by mana stones are expensive, but the city has several to move people from the bottom floors to the top.
Street Runners and City Runners run or slide down the middle ramp of the stairs because it is faster and does not run people over.
The city's walls are so wide that they hold emplacements for trebuchets and catapults, room for [Guardsmen] to patrol and walkways for citizens.
A guide says visitors on the walls can pay to rent enchanted spyglasses to watch the High Passes and roads.
Erin sees the street floors as smooth squares of light beige stone, and four walls filling part of the sky, with other floors built into the walls.
Pallass fuels its elevators with mana stones, which is partly the reason for its nickname.
Erin has heard that Pallass holds over a million souls, and finds a city ten times Liscor believable.
A guide describes the city as floor upon floor, each floor the size of a smaller Drake city or larger, in a city of millions.
A guide says the library of Pallass has tens of thousands of books.
A guide says the main cargo lifts carry goods across the city, forges are on the ninth floor, and an irrigation system of canals and water wheels runs a river up the walls from level to level.
A guide says Pallass has five bathhouses, each able to hold thousands at once, fed by the river.
On the ninth floor the [Smiths] of Pallass work day and night so that the forges never stop, which gives the city its reputation for quality steel.
Pallass is described as spontaneity and change, where [Alchemists] devise new potions and [Engineers] built the elevators that carry goods from floor to floor.
Erin's magic door is on the eighth floor, below the ninth, and higher floors partly shade lower ones, with magical lights as a second daylight.
Youths of all species, including Dullahans who control their bodies remotely, draw graffiti on the ceilings under the floors above.
Pallass is ruled by the Assembly of Crafts, whose members are elected representatives of the major Guilds, and the speaker compares it to Liscor's Council.
Ilvriss says a democracy rules Pallass and mocks the city's shamelessness.
A speaker says only Pallass elects its Assembly of Crafts.
A speaker says the Assembly must reach consensus, which makes Pallass historically the slowest of the Walled Cities to react to incidents.
Senator Errif, a Gnoll of the Scalethrift party, tells Olesm and Embria in public that the Assembly will not act until a vote is called and asks for a day or two to verify Liscor's report.
The narration says the Assembly of Crafts works alongside an inner group of a few [Senators], the Grand Strategist and [Generals] who do what needs doing.
Pallass has multiple armies, each with a specialty, a [General] and a goal, and 1st Army is always stationed in the city.
2nd Army handles foreign affairs and campaigns abroad, and the former 3rd Army, monster slayers, was destroyed under Thrissiam Blackwing.
4th Army under Edellein Blackwing handles resource-acquisition and ambushes and is unofficially called "Pallass' Bandits" by other cities.
The Dullahan Duln is 1st Army's [General] and is always in the city, and Edellein is the fourth most trusted and highly-levelled [General] of eight armies.
The narration says there should be nine armies to match the floors, but the ninth has been hypothetical for decades.
General Shirka is the newly-minted [General] of 3rd Army, chosen by High Command because it wanted another Drake.
7th and 8th Army are the only armies led by Gnoll [Generals].

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Pallassians mock Liscor as the home of rain, the Antinium and boredom, and a Pallass citizen boasts that Pallass has three dungeons in the area and is six times larger.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Liscor's Zevara says Pallass exports weaponry and alchemical goods and that over half the arms of Liscor's City Watch come from Pallass, while Liscor has only one or two low-level [Alchemists].

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Liscor is told that Pallass will impose a trade embargo until Erin's door is returned, and Zevara fears a blockade of the northern trade route.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Pallass has strict laws on bringing monsters into the city, so Erin's Goblins are a complication.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Pallass' Assembly of Crafts drops all sanctions against Liscor and prepares to open the door to Erin's inn.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Zevara says Ilvriss has been in communication with his Walled City for days, that a political struggle between Pallass and Salazsar has been going on, and that Salazsar appears to have won.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Erin's door can only send two people through without recharging, so Liscor requires request forms at the Watch barracks and Pallass confirms by [Message].

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Pallass' Belldrakes spread word of the door, and Liscor's army has already sent a detachment north.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: The Assembly of Crafts does not take Liscor's report on dungeon raids too seriously, since monster raids from dungeons are not uncommon.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: A speaker complains that Pallass thinks the Liscor dungeon is like its three Bronze and Silver-rank dungeons, which have been cleared.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Venim's company waits at Pallass' end of the door with no Assembly authorization to send troops through while Liscor is attacked.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: A speaker says Pallass makes siege weapons and keeps their secrets zealously guarded, refusing to sell to Humans.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Venim sends Liscor a daily list of travelers through the door, which is normally empty.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Pallass conscripts over a hundred adventurers under Drake law, together with the Assembly's motion to aid Liscor, and sends them through the door.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Teams that march through include the Gold-rank Flamewardens and Wings of Pallass, the Silver-rank Scaleshard Mages, Tempest Singers, The Tail of Xil and Meliem, and the Bronze-rank Rhine of Blades.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Krshia notes that Pallassian soldiers in yellow armor had marched into Liscor the day before.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: A Pallass parade honors the 3rd Infantry, called the Linebreakers, who served at the Vellir Fields outside Rheist, and the 4th Cavalry, of whom Erin sees only eleven pass.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: A Pallass guard stops Erin with a spear at the door because her arrival was not cleared against the daily list of allowed visitors.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Venim says he will have a list of approved names worked out with Liscor by [Message].

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: The door checkpoint is now on the eighth floor near the Watch House, behind a gate with stricter guards.

section: Relations with Liscor and Erin's door
text: Sergeant Kel inspects Erin at the gate and sends a note to the Watch Captain that she is in Pallass.
Erin is on holiday in Pallass, lying on grass outside the walls beside a stream.
A speaker says Erin's [Grand Theatre] Skill began working two days ago while she is still away.
Wyverns attack Pallass, Chaldion announces it across the city, and the news spreads to the Walled Cities and around the world.
Pallass sends a notice that the Antinium were repatriated to Liscor without incident under Pallassian authority, that damage assessments are underway and that the war is off.
Dead are estimated at around five thousand six hundred, mostly civilians killed by the Frost Wyvern's first breath.
Many citizens tie red cloth to their bodies to show they lost someone.
Later the city is restored to how Erin remembered it before the Wyvern attack, and a poster seeks assistants for the [Commentators] Noass and Sir Relz.
The narration says the Dragonthrower Project is a trebuchet to be mounted in Pallass with a sixteen-mile range, approved for funding the previous week.
The narration says Salazsar is forming a new army in secret.
Palt estimates that if the Golden Triangle scheme has taken hold across all nine floors, Pallass may have at least 50,000 people involved and at least 25,000 gold in the fraud.
Riders try the new skateboards down the staircases, including a Garuda who wipes out after two floors and Hedault, who goes down all nine floors with [Sticky Web] on his feet.
Chaldion comes to Erin's inn, tells her Pallass owes her an apology and offers her a game of chess.
Pomle is a small, almost completely circular nation lying at the intersection of four nations, smaller even than Reim had been, and known as neutral territory.
Pomle has no government or rulers, and those who come are free to do as they please, including outcasts, refugees and criminals.
Most residents train for combat as [Martial Artists] or hermits practicing weapon styles, in Pomle's single oasis or on the plateaus.
Troublemakers, murder and crime are not tolerated, and Pomle's warriors deal with them themselves.
Only two things hold sway over Pomle: the tradition of the Strongest and Salii.
Whoever beats the current leader of Pomle becomes the Strongest, and Orjin won the position eight years earlier and has defeated all challengers.
Salii appeared about five years earlier, started ordering people about, and was mostly obeyed because she had good ideas, such as settling quarrels over bathing.
The warriors gather by the oasis seldom, only when the Strongest calls them for war or for momentous occasions.
The [Martial Artist] community shelters people who have committed murder, so long as they do not break the peace in Pomle, and the Strongest enforces that rule.
The Strongest makes the rules until someone challenges him, and Orjin currently holds the position.
Orjin has allowed many outsiders in, including refugees fleeing the war in Tiqr, many of whom stayed and made a small settlement that the [Martial Artists] dislike but tolerate.
Near the oasis, the only body of water in Pomle, refugees and visitors have built houses, agriculture and a vineyard, and keep golden-furred sheep that crackle with static electricity.
The narration says a herd of Shockwoolies can generate enough electricity to stop the heart of anything that attacks them, and their fur is good insulation.
Salii says she charged fees to the refugees who stayed and used the coin, with loans from [Merchants], to buy animals and crops, so that Pomle now has a budget.
Pomle expands for the first time since its inception when Salii buys part of Tiqr's former land from the king of Lamullt, cheaply.
Salii plans to hire [Geomancers] to alter the ground into natural defenses, and to use caves in the new territory for training.
Salii has an underground chamber with a ring set up to make money from the [Martial Artists].
Reim is the home kingdom of the King of Destruction, shown as a small dot in the northeast of Chandrar, closer to the border than to the center.
Desert and arid land surround Reim, and the map marks a small green patch for the deep underground streams from which it draws its water.
Servants and workers in the palace walk on the right side of corridors, those going the other way on the left, with the center left for people in a hurry or carrying bulky things.
Trey sees almost no young people in Reim and fears that, if Flos goes to war, there would be nobody left to come back.
A speaker says Drevish spent the least time on Reim of all his projects and that its walls are merely thirty feet high without added fortifications.
Flos says Reim has never been besieged, since he was always on the offensive and Reim sat at the heart of his empire.
Reim has sixteen towers, and a rune diagram on a tower wall forms a map of the city.
Gazi says the enchantment [Storm Keep] was made by Amerys and Drevish to destroy entire armies, and that it was never used.
When Gazi presses her hand to the diagram and traces a line toward the city's center, lightning from the sixteen towers gathers into a ball above the city.
Flos orders his storehouses opened for frightened, homeless people fleeing to Reim.
Teres notes that hundreds of caravans came to Reim in one month, many numbering in the thousands, carrying Flos' subjects who still think well of him and are sheltered by his proclamation of peace.
It has rained for days, which a speaker calls unheard of out of season.
Flos says he issued an [Edict of Bloom], and Teres's Yellat plant grew in seven days instead of the seventy it usually takes.
A speaker says refugees were safe in Jecrass, where King Raelt gave free passage and let them barter for supplies, but many have become targets.
Flos orders potions split and given to anyone in need, and requests more [Builders] from Hellios and Germina for old villages and rich farmlands.
The King of Destruction orders a retreat and Orthenon to strike Jecrass' army, and Reim's army withdraws in orderly fashion while Raelt wonders why.
Jecrass and Belchan are now at war with Reim, with King Raelt in control of both nations.
Nerrhavia's Fallen, the Claiven Earth, Savere and a dozen other nations declare war on Reim.
Hellios and Germina, lands Reim seized, now neighbor nations that have declared war.
Reynold names the building ahead as the manor of Magnolia Reinhart, and Ryoka sees it as a mansion guarded by high walls and a single gate.
