Reynold drives through gates that swing open at once with no gatekeeper in sight, and Ryoka wonders if they are automatic magical gates.
A whale swims across the stone front of the house as if it were a sea.
A line of metal giants, suits of armor with empty visors, stands at attention flanking the entrance.
The air around the mansion is warmer than the winter outside, so that Ryoka feels as though it is spring again.
A cloud circles Magnolia's garden and, overhead, opens up to rain on Ryoka alone.
The [Assassins] and Nemor attack Magnolia in her home, striking the servants first.
After the battle the courtyard is left with burning ground and fallen bodies, and Nemor is reduced to a crater of black ash.
One wounded manservant has his leg burnt away, though Ressa and Magnolia see that the wound is healed.
Reizmelt is a small city that lies between many cities, so Runners passing through often find deliveries there.
Reizmelt is further north than Invrisil.
It has paved streets of smooth brickwork and a Runner's Guild, where Ryoka is a regular.
A speaker tells Magnolia that no Couriers are based in Reizmelt, though some pass through.
Mad Madain runs the inn the Huntress' Haven in Reizmelt, and the narration calls him its most infamous [Innkeeper].
Madain is a retired adventurer from a Gold-rank team who wakes his guests at his own hours, so his inn is very empty of regular overnight guests.
Alber the [Fist Fighter] is one of the inn's three regulars and earns his coin challenging visitors and citizens of Reizmelt to fights in the square.
Later the inn is empty as usual, and Alber is eating there.
Guards at the gates and children call Ryoka the Wind Runner and ask for breezes, because her runs bring cooling winds.
Rhir is a continent whose Blighted King rules it as sole ruler and is at war with the Demon King, who leads Demons and monsters.
Tom is told that Rhir has been at war for thousands of years, and its citizens cry out "The Walls stand!" and "Rhir! The last war! The endless war!"
The narration calls Rhir the smallest and most cursed continent, and says the blight that corrupts it is endemic only to Rhir.
Ryoka reads that Rhir is always at war with some threat, and that huge armies from every corner of the world have come to take it back.
Ryoka reads that the Demons emerged five thousand years back, catching a prosperous set of kingdoms off-guard after several hundred years of peace.
Ryoka reads that a record claims the last Crelers were purged, yet in the book's account a black slime then appears and mutates everything around it.
Ryoka concludes that something in Rhir, a dead God as Klbkch said, keeps creating new things to destroy it.

Ryoka reads that a huge army from three continents went underground searching for the root of the problem, none came back, and a year later abominations made from parts of people slaughtered everyone.
Lord Hayvon says Rhir has been settled, lost and retaken many times, and that the last time it was lost, about seven thousand years ago, the world chose to abandon it to the blight.
The narration says the Creler Wars ravaged the world six thousand years ago, after which the first Blighted King established his kingdom as a safeguard, fortified with help from around the world.

The narration says people had avoided living on Rhir because it was inhospitable and filled with corruption that twisted the form, until the Demons arrived and fought the Blighted Kingdom to a deadlock.
Tom is told that beyond Rhir there is no world, only a few islands and unexplored depths and then an abyss, and that the world is flat.
Tom's procession passes six successive outer walls of the city and a seventh being built, each taller than the last, with new housing added with each wall.
Lord Hayvon says one of Rhir's walls, the second, lies in the distance, that four walls shelter the Blighted Kingdom and that a fifth is being built.
The narration says the Blighted Kingdom has built four, soon five, massive walls across Rhir to hold back the Demons and create safe zones, with the fifth still incomplete.
A speaker reports to the king that the 5th Wall is being built and that the Deathless have not emerged since their defeat.
A soldier tells Tom that every nation has to send an army to support Rhir under the old treaties, and that two Drake armies would be there if it were all-out war.
A foreign company says it was sent to assist the Blighted King and escorts lesser dignitaries around.
The people of Rhir know their steel is made of metal mined on other continents and shipped by other nations' fleets, and that Drakes die on Rhir's soil to fulfill ancient oaths.
King Othius the Fourth holds court with his steward Nereshal, a [Chronomancer], and watches events through a scrying orb.
The Blighted King's champions at one banquet include a black-furred Minotaur, a half-Elf with a self-standing staff, a pale Selphid with two greatswords and many [Knights].
A court speaker says that Richard has reached Level 30 and so is considered a peer of the realm, and that those above Level 30 are honored by the crown.
An old woman with a spear defeats Richard in a spar, and he is applauded and led to the table of champions.
When news that Zel Shivertail allied with Lady Magnolia reaches the Blighted King's court, Drake [Soldiers] in the banquet hall brawl over whether he is a traitor.
Cirille covers her face with her claws during the Drake brawl, while Richard and the other summoned Humans watch from a table with Rhir nobles.
Riverfarm is a farming village on farming land fed by a river, which Durene says gives the village its name.
Durene describes Riverfarm as a village of around sixty souls with a blacksmith and a dedicated trader who goes to a town to buy and sell for the village.
Later, the narration says the villagers of Riverfarm numbered little over a hundred.
Riverfarm lies south of Walta and Bethal's lands and southwest of Invrisil, in the shadow of a small mountain, on land no noble house claims.
The Valerund family, whose [Lady] is apparently in Riverfarm, has a small area of influence but is a day's journey from Riverfarm.
In Durene's account, children often go to learn jobs in other towns as they grow, and new faces are rare except for the occasional adventurers or Runners.
Durene says the nearest major city is Invrisil, the city of adventurers, and that Riverfarm is not far north but decently far from the High Passes.
Laken's narration says all the villagers, Durene included, are poor, earning a few gold coins a year when weather and crops are good and subsisting at the worst of times.
Durene says Goblins are the only real nuisance, that the village sends for adventurers if any are spotted, that everyone pays into a bounty, and that adventurers take weeks to arrive.
Durene says every family might have one gold coin in savings, and Gamel says the [Merchant] who visited had three gold coins, the most he had seen at once.
Durene realizes the village lay directly in the path of the avalanche, and Laken fears the buildings could not withstand thousands of tons of snow.
Within an hour of Laken's guidance, all the villagers are found, and the living outnumber the dead.
Laken, taking charge, styles himself Emperor of the Unseen, Protector of Durene's Cottage and Ruler of Riverfarm Village.
Laken notes that since he took charge he has heard no bad word about Durene from the villagers.
The avalanche killed all the village's animals, so the villagers are eating a meaty broth.
The dead chickens, pigs and cows were what Riverfarm depended on for food and coin, but their frozen bodies let the villagers eat them one by one to stretch their food.
Foxes or similar animals gnaw at a buried cow, and Laken suggests storing the dead animals in the barn to keep animals away.
Laken says the avalanche hit the village a few days earlier, killing many and wiping out a lot of their provisions.
On the night before Christmas, Runner Ryoka reaches Riverfarm and tells sentries and Prost she has a delivery from [Emperor] Laken.
The villagers shelter in the renovated barn, and Prost finds food in the bag of holding Ryoka delivers.
Laken senses that eight buildings in Riverfarm have been dug out of the snow, three more than when he left, and nearly thirty are still buried.
The barn is the main hub of the new village, with beds, recovered goods and cooking fires outside.
Odveig tells Laken of a Goblin Lord to the south and a Great Chieftain nearby, and Laken and Prost note that Riverfarm never had walls of any sort.
Laken proposes a palisade using the back of the barn as a wall, and Prost says it will be slow without a sawmill or more hands.
The population of Riverfarm doubles in a moment when the people from Windrest arrive.
After the Windrest arrival, Prost calculates that supplies will last for a month but no longer through to spring.
Laken senses at least sixty-four Goblins and two Hobs on his land, while the defenders include twelve Celestial Trackers and seven of Beniar's riders.
Prost says over a hundred and fifty people are at Riverfarm but many are children, old or injured and most have never fought.
Odveig flees after Laken's confrontation with Wiskeria, and Laken says he is left with one less warrior to defend the village.
A speaker tallies twenty-three acceptances from nobles, almost all those attending.
Wiskeria tells Durene that the army from Riverfarm was routed by the Goblins and that Lord Pellmia's cavalry then broke the Goblins in turn.
Lord Tyrion Veltras himself rode to rescue Riverfarm.
When Durene went to war, Riverfarm was a collection of nearly six hundred people, the remnants of a few villages banding together, and it later holds over two thousand.
Row after row of identical stone and wood houses without glass go up on the new streets, each able to fit a large family.
Prost says Riverfarm's [Builders] can put up a house in less than a day, or two or three houses in a day, by dividing the work among teams.
Beycalt Newman is [Forewoman] of one of the building crews.
Chimmy says Riverfarm has a pillory for anyone who argues with Lady Rie, that Mister Helm makes lots of metal but wants their own mines, and that buying ore is costly.
Chimmy says some of the village's [Farmers] have [Fast Growth] and one has [One Day Bloom], so Riverfarm does not need to buy food.
Chimmy says her father Prost has Mister Tepple sow the seeds and the other [Farmers] till and water, so those with growth Skills make the seeds come up.
Lady Rie says the fields have been harvested once and she wants to double them to feed Riverfarm, sell and stockpile.
The residential district is already nearly four hundred houses, and massive warehouses hold food in another district.
Of the over two thousand people in Riverfarm, six hundred are original people loyal to their [Emperor], and the group from Lancrel outnumbers the villagers two to one.
Riverfarm's outhouses are small and open, and its toilet paper is a corn cob, so Ryoka uses paper she bought in Walta.

Ryoka reports to Gralton that hundreds and possibly thousands of refugees are coming to Riverfarm, that Yitton Byres will leave within the week, and that the Goblins are kept separate in their own area.
As summer begins, Riverfarm is the first settlement to claim allegiance to the Unseen Empire, and it begins to export its goods.
Riverfarm produces far more crops than ever because [Farmers] pool their Skills over vast fields.
Riverfarm has a large waterwheel for making flour, and its [Engineers] offer to build windmills, which outrages [Millers].
Rumors say Riverfarm's lands are protected, that [Bandits] avoid it, that [Witches] are treated with respect there, and that its [Emperor] is a blind ancient-blooded man called the Unseen Emperor.
The narration says Riverfarm is laid out perfectly, no longer a village but a small town, with an assembly-line trial and [Engineers] designing wells and cranes.
Humans of Riverfarm build a wall of up to ten feet around the Goblin territory in their free time, since their [Emperor] forbids killing the Goblins.
Laken has a letter from Ryoka carried by Dustrider Charlay, takes thirty minutes to get through it, and begins to incorporate her plans.
Laken has the first bumpy stone roads torn up and replaced with flat brick roads after about four weeks of work.
The Ruins of Albez sit at the heart of what was once a magical kingdom, a community of mages or an ancient citadel, and the whole area is saturated in magic.
The ruins attract both monsters, who nest among the ruined buildings and endless underground tunnels, and adventurers seeking lost treasure.
Adventuring groups get official permission to search the ruins for a set period, which lets the nearby cities profit by charging access and keeps adventurers from conflict.
Garia notes that it is a long way from the Ruins of Albez to Celum for someone who is not a Runner.
Ceria says the Horns' last mission before Liscor's ruins was digging through the Ruins of Albez, near Celum.
Yvlon says that the Ruins of Albez are up north.
The Horns of Hammerad occupy the ruins during Ryoka's first view of them.
Ceria gets a few enchanted items there, including spelled cooking equipment, an old recipe book and a few expensive plates, enough to cover healing costs.
Yvlon says the ruins are famous for treasure but mostly cleaned out decades ago, and that adventuring teams find something extremely valuable only now and then.
Ceria says that Albez was unearthed during an earthquake, and that most of the traps and all the big monsters and guardians of the dungeon are gone.
The city has sunk into the earth, leaving a basin of half-buried walls and pitfalls, with shifted passages that do not match the maps.
The Horns under Calruz went into Albez four times, as did other Silver-rank teams; surviving Albez is practically a rite of passage before harder requests.
The ruins near Liscor lie about ten miles out of the city according to one account, with so much traffic to and from them that Erin and Selys hitch a ride on a cart.

At the ruins, a tent city of makeshift shelters surrounds an excavation pit three times the size of a football stadium, which has unearthed a dark stone opening that Erin and Selys are told is a doorway into a crypt.
More than a hundred, mostly human, adventurers are in the city and the tent city.
A Drake shepherd found the ruins a few months earlier when he tripped on a rock that proved to be part of a building; the Antinium were called, and the hill turned out to be the whole structure.

The ruins are half-uncovered against a large hill, with a black stone entrance and carved doorway; the roof and lower half have not been excavated, and an Antinium dug down over a hundred feet without reaching the bottom.
The doors are big enough for two creatures twice Calruz's height or two wagons at once.
The ruins are still filled with dirt and dried mud from years of burial, and adventurers dig while fending off giant burrowing rats, various undead, spiders and other low to mid-level monsters.
Several teams find small caskets of silver and jewels, suggesting an old crypt, but the more adventurous teams that went further in never come back, and some return as shuffling undead.

Around fifteen armed warriors, mainly Drakes and a few Gnolls, guard the doors; Bronze-rank teams and members of the Watch are on permanent guard duty because the place disgorges monsters, such as a mob of zombies, every few days.
Yvlon proposes a six-team raid, claiming the ruins are practically untouched beyond the first level and that Liscor leaves the investigation to adventurers.
Calruz says the ruins are less than an hour from the city.
Another account says the ruins are several miles from the city.
A scout reports empty rooms, urns of dust and old non-magical scrolls, and a few undead.
Deeper, the adventurers find an open room of stone altars and slabs long enough for a body, which Ceria realises is a crypt where bodies are placed to be cleansed before burial.
A member of the Watch reports squiggly white tentacled things in the ruins and the suspicion of a brood monster, with the other teams clearing rooms one at a time.
Sadomere is a city of Reim's border war that Flos' army took three days before, with simple short walls and standard battlements.
Teres sees that Sadomere is not Reim, is not built as strongly, has no secret weapons and has exposed walls the [Builders] made without an eye for sieges.
Only one of the King's Seven, Mars, is there to defend it.
Sadomere is rechristened Drevish's Madness and becomes a linchpin of the King of Destruction's defensive line as Raelt's armies fall back.
Newly reinforced, the city withstands a full-scale assault by General Lael's forces, and Lael refuses to retreat despite the Skill-enhanced fortifications.
Magical statues of Orthenon attract arrow fire, and the inner city is designed to stymie assaults and favor defenders.
Later the city is no longer under siege.
Salazsar is the second-largest of the Walled Cities and is built into the side of a mountain as a mountain-fortress, and out of it.
The narration says Salazsar is defined by tradition, the lineage of Wall Lords and Wall Ladies, and by mining and gem cutting.
Salazsar is called the City of Gems and rules the gem trade.
Ever-burning flames warm only the highest floors of the city, where only the richest denizens can afford to live.
A Drake crosses crisscrossing bridges in the sky between the highest towers, and the narration says each Walled City has its own personality.
Wall Lords control holdings such as mining areas or enough wealth to finance sectors, and each employed person owes allegiance to a particular Wall Lord, or house of Salazsar.
Salazsar is not ruled by democracy like Pallass but by the Wall Lords and Ladies.
A speaker says it is impossible to teleport into Salazsar because it has more ward-stones and counter spells than anyone can count.
A speaker says Ilvriss and Salazsar have made it clear that war will follow if Pallass takes Erin's door.
The same speaker suspects that more Drake cities and other Walled Cities might take Salazsar's side.
The narration says Salazsar is forming a new army in secret.
Flos says Savere is prosperous, dangerous and seafaring, and that its ruler hates him.
Flos names Savere, with Pomle and Illivere, among the nations that are neither Tiqr nor Nerrhavia and are all dangerous.
Savere's ruler is the Siren of Savere, Revine.
In character Savere falls between Tiqr and Illivere: its people are wild, ride forward without order, laughing, and some look like folk from the waters.
Revine arrives at a gathering of monarchs walking along a path that the waters form for her in the sands.
Revine, the Siren of Savere, is open about her hatred for Flos, saying his armies looted Savere's lands and treasuries.
Savere is one of four major nations, with Tiqr, Nerrhavia and Illivere, that send leaders to the meeting.
Stitchworks is Octavia's boarded-up store down a side street in Celum, and a sign on it says potions are half-off and that matches are no longer sold there, with inquiries to Alchemist Quelm.
The access point of the magic door is inside Stitchworks, though the real door is still in Liscor.
A new sign on Stitchworks says it is under the protection of the Redfang Goblins, a Bronze-rank team.
The sign's note says that if you attack the Goblin, he may hit back, and that he can talk, listen and see.
The stream runs down a hill a few miles from the inn, and Erin judges it a good spot to gather water or wash.
Erin, fleeing the Goblins, clears the stream in a single leap.
Erin bathes in the cold water with soap bought from Krshia and is startled by a fish in the water that shoots at her like a torpedo.
Erin fills her bucket from the stream and splashes water over acid flies feeding on the dead fish, which makes them fall onto their backs.
The Tailless Thief is an inn in the north side of Liscor that Selys calls the most famous and most expensive inn in the city.
The Tailless Thief is run by the Drake [Innkeeper] Peslas.
When Erin first visits, the Tailless Thief is nearly full before midday, with retired and well-off Drake customers and Drake barmaids, and Erin sees no Gnoll there.
The inn has no broken chairs, no holes in the walls, bright lamps and a bustling staff, and Erin judges it a proper inn without flaws.
Its clientele is entirely Drake, with no Gnoll or Human present.
The narration calls the Tailless Thief the most famous and well-reputed inn in Liscor.

Even after Erin's Skills make her inn about three times as attractive as other inns, the Tailless Thief remains a byword for Drakes in Liscor, though it is specialized while Erin's inn accepts everyone.
Olesm considers the Tailless Thief the best inn in Liscor, because of its food from a [Cook] with [Advanced Cooking], its high-level [Innkeeper] and its advantageous placement.
After Ilvriss levels up Swifttail's class, he tells Weille to run to the Tailless Thief and have its [Innkeeper] prepare a celebratory feast and says he will buy out the inn for the day.
Later, characters talk about the innkeeper's new dish of hamburgers and say the recipe came from Erin.
Later, the guests from Hectval, who arrived unannounced, are placed at the Tailless Thief.
Tails and Scales is a bar in Pallass that a character calls the best bar in all of Pallass.
Tails and Scales is very bar-focused but has a number of tables.
Rufelt and Lasica own the bar, and Rufelt serves drinks as its [Barkeep] with an apprentice named Usshi.
A speaker says it is one of the most famous bars in Pallass, where you normally have to be invited by a regular.
A table in the center of the room is a solid flat black block with a furnace below it, which Lasica cooks on as a hot plate table.
Lasica cooks appetizers or an early dinner at the table while a [Line Cook] learns from her.
Rufelt serves flaming drinks and a drink that turns the whole glass invisible.
A Dullahan [Cellist] in white and green ceramic armor plays in the bar at night.
Its customers include Drakes, Gnolls, Dullahans and a Garuda couple, [Smiths] such as Maughin, and many other tradespeople.
During the Wyvern attack, Rufelt waves people inside, slams the door and bars it, and the Wyvern's impact only rattles the door while the bar itself does not shake.
Lasica says the owners paid for the door to be practically indestructible, so it should stay safe from the Wyverns.
The bar shelters Erin, Rufelt, Lasica, the Gnoll Felkhr, a Dullahan family, two Drake [Warriors] and a young jet-black-scaled Drake called Lady Salkis.
Viss, an injured Drake [Bodyguard], is next to Lady Salkis, the highborn Drake.
Talenqual is a port city on Baleros, big enough to employ all the Humans looking for a job and to appear on a continental map though not a capital.
It is claimed by the Featherfolk Brigade, which is not engaged in major conflicts, and has no vastly rich resources that would tempt others to fight over it.
The streets are dominated by Lizardfolk, with Dullahans and Centaurs seen daily, and buildings rarely over three stories, made of wood or Lizardfolk mud brick.
Centaurs tend to move in the center lanes of the traffic in Talenqual.
A member of the company says they must stop and earn money or it will never get to Talenqual.
The company's house is two apartments bought and converted into one, on the outer edges of the city near the rice fields.
Talenqual is a port city, small to medium-sized, ruled by the Featherfolk Brigade, a mercenary company that seized the city and area and keeps control to this day.
The United Nations Company now has four large, adjoining houses leased for the next four months.
The landlady, Miss Hastel, allowed the company to install connecting doors between the houses.
The Wandering Inn is an inn on a long slope of grassland near Liscor, an old wooden building that Erin Solstice finds abandoned and reopens as her own.
The inn is a wooden building on a stone foundation, made of oak boards that have weathered the years well, and it is four times the size of a normal house, built to hold crowds.
When Erin first arrives its signboard is faded and the paint long worn away.
The common room is dusty and long deserted, and water drips down through cracks from somewhere upstairs when it rains.
The inn is built almost entirely of wood, with wooden walls, ceiling beams and floor.
A long counter stands at the end of the common room, made of high-quality wood and long enough for at least twenty people, or fifteen if they want elbow room.
A door behind the bar opens into the kitchen, which holds old rusty pans and pots and a bucket.
The second floor is reached by a staircase of which nearly every second stair creaks loudly.
The first room Erin enters upstairs has a curtain hanging at its window.
The downstairs windows have no glass or curtains; they are square holes in the wall with shutters.
The door has a metal bar that can be slid across to keep it shut, and the common room has many windows with wooden shutters and cheap metal latches.
Upstairs, some window mantles have rotted but the shutters are mostly intact.
A skeleton lies in the last bed, in the room at the end of the upstairs corridor.
Goblins break shutters on the way in during their first attack, but the door holds.
The kitchen has a window facing the mountains, through which cool air comes down from them.
Erin complains that the stream she fetches water from lies a long walk across the grasslands from the inn.
Klbkch says the inn's site was once a small community whose people all died of a plague, and that the inn was abandoned nearly three years earlier, so there is no law against occupying the area.
The inn stands on a long, gradual incline; Liscor is visible from it. Relc and Klbkch call the walk to the city about ten minutes, but Erin judges it nearer an hour.
Ceria, discussing the inn with Gerial, says it is odd to see Erin living so far out from the city; Gerial answers that it was barely an hour's walk even with them getting lost.
Erin paints a new name on the old plaque above the inn, The Wandering Inn, and plants a sign beside it reading "No Killing Goblins."
Erin sleeps at her favourite table, the second one near the bar, because she cannot afford mattresses; Klbkch has helped her install a new door.

Later, a second inn is built for Erin: as large as the first but of mostly new wood, coated with the Antinium's varnish, nailed with copper, fairy approved, and fitted with glass windows with shutters, a redone kitchen, an outhouse and a well.
Selys's [Receptionist] Skills organise Erin's possessions in the new inn, and a bright gold sign now hangs over it.
Erin says the Antinium built everything in her inn and that she has glass windows, which even Peslas's inn lacks.

In a Goblin's-eye view, a black carriage drawn by ghostly horses brings Erin back through the snow to the inn, after which a Drake, an Antinium, a Drake [Receptionist], a Human [Scout], a [Princess] and a skeleton enter, and a fight follows.
Lyonette and Zel find a trapdoor in a small closet leading down to a large, empty stone basement with grain storage and shelves; Lyonette had not known it existed.

After a shaking of the inn stops, Lyonette senses a charged atmosphere in the walls and ground that Zel cannot feel, and her [Light] spell produces oversized glowing orbs; she identifies what she feels as magic.
Erin later tells the Players of Celum that her inn is charged with mana, so that spells cast there come out brighter and bigger.
Erin's inn gains a reputation as a hangout for adventurers and as the only place for good, cheap honey apart from one Gnoll.

The inn is full because of its cooking, fast service, magical food and the magic door to Celum, and Erin's current Skills make it three times as attractive as other inns; only Peslas's Tailless Thief stays a byword for Drakes.

The Antinium rebuild the inn: the ground floor is a third larger, there are two new second-floor rooms, an entire third floor, two new outhouses, and a watchtower for Bird that sits against the back wall and makes the inn look lopsided.

Goblin archers of the Goblin Lord's army fire flaming arrows at the inn on its hill near Liscor; the arrows fail to ignite it and some bounce off the glass windows, and the army marches on, judging it too close to the city to loot.
The inn is emptier than ever in the days after Erin takes in Goblins; Lyonette notes that only two adventuring groups are staying and that Ishkr has not returned since Brunkr's death.

Erin holds a party with music and dancing at the inn, attended by Goblins, Antinium, Bird, Jelaqua, Ceria, Yvlon, Pisces and others; Octavia looks in at the noise, and passing [Guardspeople] hear the music from outside.

During the Face-Eater Moth attack, Erin insists her inn will survive because she has a Skill, though the moths hurl themselves at the windows; afterwards the inn stands, scarred, with every window broken and Bird's watchtower smashed.

After the moth attack, the common room is wrecked with moth blood on the floor and moth corpses piled inside, both outhouses are wrecked and the watchtower is reduced to smithereens, while the windowless kitchen and basement are untouched and the second and third floors are mainly intact.

When Goblins gather in the inn, Olesm and others suspect Erin's aura Skill keeps people out; only Bevussa, Mrsha and Krshia of the Liscor group can open the door, and Embria opens it only with effort.
Wall Lord Ilvriss enters unimpeded, says he could repel the aura if he chose, and decides against interfering.
Lyonette says no one from Liscor can enter the inn except the Horns of Hammerad, the Halfseekers, herself and Mrsha, and that Olesm failed to get up the hill after three hours of trying.
Later, Erin tells Lyonette that the inn is open again.
The magic door has five rotating mana stones: Celum, Liscor, Numbtongue's purple one, an orange one for a door Griffon Hunt and the Halfseekers use, and Pallass.
The inn is a thousand gold coins richer from the Redfang Goblins' gift, but the third floor and Bird's tower are still gone.

The inn is still partly destroyed from the Goblin Lord's attack on Liscor, with the third floor and tower gone but the first and second floors repaired; the hilltop has room for a few outhouses and a sign.
Erin says the Antinium will expand the hill the inn stands on.
The Pallass door is thronged with people on both sides, and Erin checks the Celum side at thirty-minute intervals; Grimalkin, Moore and other [Mages] help supply mana to the door.
The Halfseekers are stuck in the inn for two days on their way to Invrisil, and Jelaqua spends the time glued to the Dullahan Maughin.
Temile, the [Stage Manager] of the Players of Celum, puts new casts through their paces on the inn's stage, while Grimalkin, Relc and Wing Commander Embria devise workouts with Erin's new weights.
The inn now has five outhouses, two of them newly dug, and one is built to fit a half-Giant.
The third floor is being rebuilt: its frame and floor are done and a Worker, assigned by Belgrade, lays roof tiles with copper nails.
A single Ashfire Bee is living in the inn, pollinating flowers inside.
The inn is crowded for days with guests from Liscor and Pallass watching a play in the background while staff serve them.
The expanded common room can hold hundreds of people, and the [Grand Theatre] stands at its far end, where [Actors] perform.
Only about forty guests are in the inn one evening.
Lyonette and Ishkr start a meal-order system so patrons can request a dish for a given night, which frees Erin from being in the kitchen all the time; Erin is still the inn's only [Cook].
A "No Killing Goblins" sign hangs over the bar.
Lyonette tells visitors that the inn is staging a horror-themed play lineup including Psycho and The Shining, and that few rooms are open because the Antinium are building.

Erin mixes soap and water on the common-room floor and slides down it with Mrsha, Relc and others following, while the Horns of Hammerad patch up their quarrel; the Wistram team watching through the door leave, and Montressa swears they will capture both Erin and Pisces.

The Watch assaults the inn during the Creler infestation: spells blow down the walls, Antinium Soldiers come up into the basement to fight the Crelers that fell through the floor, and floors begin to collapse into the basement.
When the magic door is blank after the fight, Erin switches the dial and the Watch Captain Zevara opens it to Pallass.
The inn is left badly broken, with caved-in walls and crumbling floors, and nowhere for the Horns of Hammerad to stay.
Erin finds the inn too wrecked to repair; her [Grand Theater] Skill no longer works, and her [Partial Reconstruction] Skill reassembles chairs and tables but not the broken floor or sagging ceiling.
Later, the remaining structure collapses entirely into rubble on the hill, and rescuers find Erin kneeling, protected by a beam that caught the weight of the inn.
The Antinium rebuild the inn with money granted by the city for its part in subduing the Crelers, private donations and a small cost to the Antinium.
Klbkch says that the Worker Belgrade designed the rebuilt inn together with Lyonette, and that Belgrade is adept at making traps.
The inn reopens under Lyonette's management two weeks after its destruction, while Erin is still away; her [Grand Theatre] Skill began working two days before.

At the reopening, people in the inn see through a scrying orb and the open magic door that Pallass is under attack by Wyverns, with the Drake [Commentator] Noass and Sir Relz appearing in a mirror held up at the door.
Relc drags the door into the common room during the attack on Pallass, and Olesm leaves to fetch Guildmistress Alonna and [Mages].
Klbkch forbids the Antinium to go through to Pallass, saying it would be an act of war.

The new entry hallway has arrow slits, murder holes, walls three times as thick and two tough sliding doors, and a hidden trapdoor Belgrade installed; elsewhere the walls are twice as thick as before and the foundations are stone.
Lyonette says she told Belgrade not to build an escape trapdoor, but he wanted to make part of the inn collapse over a pit of blades or water.
Erin feels that her inn has become a fortress.
The new inn has two stairwells at opposite ends, but only a third of the second floor is finished, so one stairwell is blocked.
Lyonette plans guest rooms, stables and a proper road, and says the new door to Liscor will go next to the Adventurer's Guild and the Mage's Guild.
Guests and staff, led by Relc and Lyonette, shout "No killing Goblins!" at a gathering in the inn; Erin drinks to it.
The second floor is finished with many rooms open, and the third floor is under renovation with Bird's tower set on it; Lyonette wants larger, more luxurious rooms there.

The inn works partly as a warehouse: Bird's crew of eighteen Workers roll barrels of preserved fish into the basement, Lyonette signs receipts, and the door is moved to the basement to ship about two thousand two hundred pounds of fish to House Sanito.
Erin installs a television-like display in the common room: a six-foot mirror enchanted with [Scrying] by Palt, showing the war in Ailendamus.
Erin has the mirror moved to a spare room, labelled the Viewing Room, so the Players of Celum can perform in the common room.
The kitchen of The Wandering Inn holds several knives, from a cleaver down to one the size of a finger, and a frying pan.
The kitchen has many cupboards and drawers, which hold basic utensils such as spatulas, tarnished silverware and plates.
One cupboard still holds a bag of flour and a golden block of butter that are fresh despite the thick dust in the room.
That cupboard is edged with faintly glowing silver runes, and Erin concludes they are magic.
The other cupboards carry the same small runes around their edges, but these are not glowing.
Erin scrapes the runes in the good cupboard and splinters the wood so that the line of runes is cut, and the glow at once fades.
The kitchen has an old oven, which Erin's instincts tell her she can use for baking bread.
Among the kitchen's odds and ends are a hammer, a rock and a fire striker, which Erin identifies as flint and steel.
Tiqr is a prosperous empire of savannas and oases that is renowned for its [Beastmasters], and its [Empress] is known as the Empress of Beasts, Nsiia.
Pisces says Tiqr is among the few nations openly sympathetic to, or at least not opposed to, the King of Destruction.
Tiqr is allied with the Garuda-led nation of Kilalle to the west, which is militarily inferior.
Ressa reports that after Jecrass, Belchan and Nerrhavia's Fall affirmed the King of Destruction's claim, Tiqr was already on the defensive.
Ressa says the Illivere League and Savere launched immediate assaults and Nerrhavia moved in, and that war golems and Savere's [Raiders] forced Tiqr's forces to retreat.
Pisces says that on the twenty-seventh day of the conflict, a coalition of about ten or eleven nations led by Nerrhavia is attacking Tiqr, with Nerrhavia's Fallen the largest power.
Vasraf is told that Kilalle is not coming, as their flocks send only regrets.
Savere and Nerrhavia offered Tiqr surrender terms, and Nsiia says surrender would be absolute and give her people to slavery.
Nsiia leaves the surrender letters from Savere's Siren and Nerrhavia's Queen Yisame unopened.
Tiqr's army, nearly eighty thousand strong, breaks the encirclement toward the Kilalle Steppes while Nsiia delays by surrendering.
Later, General Vasraf swears to liberate Tiqr and flees to the Kilalle Steppes with the rest of the army and nearly a hundred thousand citizens.
Tiqr surrenders to Illivere and not to the coalition, and Nsiia says Tiqr is no more and she is no longer an [Empress].
Femithain makes Nsiia a political prisoner of Illivere, whose army guards her, while Nerrhavia garrisons Oliphant.
Tiqr's lands were seized by other nations, which must garrison them, while its army still attacks from the Kilalle Steppes.
Refugees fleeing the war in Tiqr have settled in Pomle.
In Liscor, the Watch House is where the City Watch is based and where guards can borrow weapons, and news of Erin's play spreads from it.
Embria leaves the Watch House with the 4th Company waiting in lines outside.
Palt weaves a calming spell for the entire Watch House.
Zevara strides out of the Watch House with Selys and the Watch following.
Jerci and Tkrn march a thief to the Watch house.
Pallass operates many City Watch stations, with almost every floor having a Watch House so patrols are never far from trouble, except the 9th floor.
The 8th floor's Watch House in the eastern section is generally quiet, run by a Desk Sergeant when Watch Captains are away.
Pallass's Watch House is like the one in Liscor, but different enough to feel odd to Erin.
Windrest is a village that suffered a Goblin raid in which about sixty Goblins killed a dozen people and torched a few buildings.
The Goblins took the village's animals and winter stores, making off with two thirds of its goods and two young women.
The narration says Halrac returns to find Windrest ash, having been too late, and that sickness, war and monster attacks had long hurt his home.
Briganda tells Halrac that Windrest is gone, destroyed by raids from the mountain during the Goblin Lord's attacks, and that fires were part of it.
Briganda says the rumor is that Drakes started the fires.
Briganda says Windrest was Halrac's childhood home, where a small village could not hire enough adventurers to fight raiders off.
Briganda says most of Windrest's survivors are at Riverfarm, having joined the Unseen Empire.
A speaker says most of Windrest had gone to Riverfarm, which is still standing.
Wishdrinks is a very expensive pub in Liscor, which is to a bar what the Tailless Thief is to an inn, where attractive younger Drakes and Gnolls entertain guests.
A troupe plays at Wishdrinks and people dance there.
Embria rewards the squad that gathers the most Shield Spider nests with a night at Wishdrinks, which she calls one of the best taverns in the city.
Wishdrinks is out of the budget of a Senior Guardsman most of the time.
A speaker lists Wishdrinks among the great things to see in Liscor, along with Market Street.
Teliv Witherscale works part-time as a [Host] at Wishdrinks.
Yvlon finds Wishdrinks the most popular bar in Liscor, with a waiting list.
Wishdrinks has private rooms, plush and comfortable, with friendly staff and food Erin admits is delicate and spiced.
Ceria says that Wistram accepts necromancers, and that Pisces was expelled for what he wanted to do with necromancy.
Ceria adds that every time the Academy learns where Pisces is staying, it sends a team to capture him.
Krshia says Wistram is a place of magic where mages go to learn, nationless and a nation unto itself, which has never bowed to any ruler.
Krshia says that, since a past grievance, [Mages] from Wistram are not welcome among the Gnoll tribes and the tribes do not trade with their island.
Krshia warns that the seas around the college are calm at times but at others devour ships and sink fleets, especially in winter.
A speaker tells Pisces that the academy has existed for thousands of years, founded when many nations were at war and mages wanted a place to learn and teach in peace.
The same speaker says Wistram is independent, with an army of its own, and that only a grand fleet could reach its shores with weather spells raised against it.
Wistram sells enchantments and analysis to adventurers, doing a booming trade in better gear.
Wistram is an island inside a magical bubble where the weather ceases, reached by sailing through a storm.
Its castle is a citadel built into the island's cliffs, a few interconnected buildings with impossibly tall spires and domes, glowing runes in the air, and a tower that looks engulfed in fire.
Inside, Wistram is far larger than it appears from outside; mages have built high into the air and far beneath the isle, and newcomers get lost.
Over thousands of years so many mages have built onto the academy that one can run for hours without crossing it, and a straight line is rare.
Magical barriers, locked doors and Golem guards near stairwells stop new students from going too high or too low, where dangerous experiments run wild.
The top three floors are off limits to new mages, and above them a door is guarded by Cognita and many Golems; mages here can cast Tier 5 or even Tier 6 spells.
The catacombs hold many stored bones that sometimes reanimate people who are killed down there.
Wistram accepts new students on only one day of the year, when the isle opens.
Twenty gold pieces buys a month of study, after which a student must prove their worth by an exam or be sent home.
Living in Wistram without a scholarship costs hundreds of gold, so most hope to pass the exam, which rewards a high level or a unique spell or Skill.
Ghouls burst into the dining hall during Ceria's first meal; she and many mages kill them with spells.
New students take mandatory basic courses, and the academy has no signs or maps, so they must find classrooms and rules themselves.
Ceria and Pisces never find the illusion class, and Pisces suspects it is a prank on newcomers.
Combat mages train in the early morning on the rocks, and duels over wands or other matters, fought with spells or debate, are common and bet on.
After the yearly exams, [Captains] chartered from around the world come to take away the failed students; of the hundreds who come, less than a tenth pass.
Thirty-four students pass in Ceria's year.
The mages on Wistram's isle link scrying orbs, a service offered beyond Drake cities, such as a Titan's mock battle in Baleros watched by kings and lords.
Pallass sells expensive playbacks of the Liscor battle made by minor Wistram artifacts that replay it, which they call movies.
When Earth humans arrive among the students, the Revivalists shelter them and give them autonomy, to Archmage Feor's displeasure.
It is rumored that Wistram watches everything through scrying orbs and the Mage's Guilds' [Messages], though this has never been proven.

Archmages Feor, Viltach and Nailihuaile watch Empress Nsiia by hijacking her scrying spell: Feor is a half-Elf and leader of the most powerful Centrist faction, Nailihuaile is a Star Lamia enchanter and Revivalist leader, and Viltach is a Human and head of the Libertarians.

Wistram sends a highest-priority [Message] through every Mage's Guild that the King of Destruction has allied with Tiqr, then retracts it about ten minutes later as an error made without verification.
A speaker calls the false announcement beyond scandalous and says Wistram's credibility is ruined.
Wistram puts a bounty of two thousand gold on Pisces Jealnet as a Level 26 [Necromancer], sent to Mage's Guilds across Izril.
The bounty text calls Pisces a common-born Terandrian whose family serves House Dultel, accused of petty thievery and necrophilia.
Later, Cognita is said to have granted Pisces and Ceria the authority to call themselves graduates, and Grimalkin notes Wistram has amended the false-claim charge.
Wistram's single "channel" of magic-vision can show only one event at a time, and it receives requests from over forty nations, so it declines to choose between them.
Wistram apologises for broadcasting scenes of dead children and blood, and says it will need policies such as delays.
Archmages Feor, Nailihuaile and Viltach expose the Golden Triangle as a fraudulent scheme in a broadcast as the scheme collapses and investors lose hundreds of thousands of gold.
New students arriving later include Flynn Patel, two apparent Earthers from Baleros, Terandrian nobles with a crying child, a Gorgon, Oldblood Drakes, Stitchfolk and a swordsman.
Zeikhal is a massive desert on Chandrar, which Teres says is probably twice the size of the Sahara.
A speaker in Flos's court says that marching an army across Zeikhal is dangerous and is the one thing that has stopped the Emperor of Sands's expansion.
Zeikhal is called the Great Desert of Chandrar, larger than entire continents of Trey's world, and it has apparently engulfed countless kingdoms and empires that turned to dust.
It is said that rain falls seldom so far inland, and in Zeikhal not at all.
Zeikhal has not always been there.
The city of Merreid lies in the desert of Zeikhal.
Zeres is a Walled City that the Antinium encircled and besieged during the first Antinium war.
After a week of day-and-night warfare the Antinium were rebuffed from Zeres with extreme casualties and virtually no losses among the defenders.
The Walled Cities' three-hundred-foot walls are held up by magic that hardens the stone and lets it repair itself given time, and no army has ever taken a Walled City by siege.
The Antinium's living ladders were too short to reach the battlements, and defending archers and mages rained down fire while Antinium arrows could not reach the defenders.
The ground around the Walled Cities was impenetrable to conventional tools because of enchantments radiating from the walls, so Antinium Workers dug until their limbs broke.
Zeres stood, and the Antinium could not abandon the siege without the army being attacked from behind, which slowed their advance along with the sieges of other Walled Cities.

Later, Zeres lodges a formal complaint about the Yellow Rivers illness in the city, where [Healers] are fighting it, and its High Command orders any vessel with Yellow Rivers refused entrance to the harbor.
The awakened Raskghar are Raskghar who underwent a ritual and call themselves awakened.
In the ritual, twenty Gnolls are killed on a stone altar, and the chosen Raskghar tear open their chests, eat their hearts, and change, leaving twenty-one Raskghar standing together.
Calruz inspects the twenty-one and approves.
A large female awakened Raskghar who performed the ritual claims to be stronger, smarter and faster than before, hungry for battle, and able to speak language.
She brings Calruz the head of a giant Face-Eater Moth mother, killed with sixteen others, and says she has found a treasure site that may be opened.
She says more rituals will mean more awakened Raskghar.
Nokha, a female awakened Raskghar, says "We are whole" to the captive Gnolls.
The lesser Raskghar give way to the awakened, and the Raskghar then mate in a frenzy that fills the night.
Gorgons are one of the main evolutions of Lizardfolk, alongside Nagas, Lamias and Medusae; general Lizardfolk-evolution facts are held in the species file.
A Medusa says Medusae are not as strong and tough as Gorgons or even Nagas.
Commander Uxel is a Gorgon who commands a mixed army of Nagas, Gorgons, Lamias and Lizardfolk at the Walls of Rhir.
Gorgons and Nagas act as the heavy punch of the Lizardfolk forces, while Lamias and other spellcasters batter the enemy with magic.
Gorgons are individually strong and tough, more than Gnolls or the average Drake.
Uxel has venom fangs, enhanced scales, great height and brawn, and infrared vision with which he sees the heat of a nervous horse.
Gorgons and Medusae share sight-attacks, though a Gorgon's only makes the enemy's muscles lock for a second or two, which Uxel used to break Drake formations.
Five Redfang Hobs form a strike team with the mission to track down the Raskghar, get Mrsha and Ceria, and escape the dungeon.
The Hobs take Badarrow's cursed bell of pain but leave the cursed necklace for fear of what it might do.
The Hobs once belonged to the Redfang Tribe in the High Passes, which fought dangerous monsters at the base of the mountain range.
The Hobs ambush a four-Raskghar patrol that is moving behind Cave Goblin scouts, kill them, and persuade the freed Cave Goblins that the Hobs are Goblins too.
The Hobs then find a Raskghar camp of two dozen Raskghar with at least fifty Goblin slaves, whom the Raskghar torment and eat.
Badarrow ties the cursed bell to an arrow, and its clang drops the Cave Goblins in pain and cripples the Raskghar before the Hobs charge shouting "Redfang!" against twenty-six of them.
The Raskghar all fall to the Hobs, with Badarrow picking off enemies with arrows from behind.
An old Hob who is offered garlic bread hopes that the Chieftain needs old Hobs, and Headscratcher answers that the group has no Chieftain.
The Redfangs wonder whether Erin might be the Chieftain.
Zevara agrees to let the other Redfang Hobs out of Liscor's prison as a sign of goodwill, and they climb down from the wall to meet the Cave Goblins.
[Illumination] is an advanced version of the [Light] spell: officially Tier-2 magic, but with complexity closer to Tier-3.
[Illumination] lights over a hundred meters around the caster by shedding orbs of light, which makes it perfect for dungeons.
Ceria is having trouble mastering the spell she is learning.
In the crypt, light suddenly fills the long corridor as bright white orbs fly up from the ground, spaced ten feet apart, turning the dark into day.

Ryoka Griffin, running toward the High Passes, is followed by animated sparks of light like fireflies carrying flashing symbols and a garbled sound, which she guesses may be a curse; she speeds up and loses them whenever they try to lock on.
A red and gold firefly of light appears at Erin's inn, and Pisces says it is a messaging spell but he has not seen one like that before.
The light resolves into flickering runes that are painful to look at for Erin and Rags, while only Pisces can look at them without pain, and he leaves to read it.
A mage service sends a single [Message] for a couple of gold coins, and Ryoka relays from Ceria that the spell is not easy to cast and needs Level 15 or so.
The service holds any reply for one week before disposing of it.
Krshia tells Erin that archmages are the rarest of spellcasters, and that she knows of only a few and none on this continent.
Krshia says there are several archmages: one in the Human lands to the north, two on other continents, and at least three with homes in Wistram, the Isle of Mages.
Pisces recalls the saying that a [Cleric] in the earliest levels could do what an [Archmage] could not.
By Book 17, Wistram counts six great [Mages] of Archmage rank: Terandria has two, Izril one, Chandrar one and Baleros three living Archmages, with none from Rhir.
Archmage Amerys is no longer numbered among them.
Izril's sole Archmagus lives on an island and seldom interferes in her home's affairs.
Archmagus Verdan Blackwood, a Human raised by Dullahans, is old and effectively retired from Wistram politics.
Feor is a white-bearded half-Elf Archmage, head of the Centrists; Viltach is a Human Archmage who leads the Libertarians; and Nailihuaile is an Archmage with a staff.
When the three confronted Amerys, she reportedly called down a storm of lightning bolts over Wistram's exterior.

Feor, Viltach and Naili show Aaron Vanwell paintings of the interiors of the Antinium Hives and vote not to send the images to the Drakes, preferring to keep observing until they have something worth more.
The Archmages say Wistram's access to the Hives runs both ways and that they have limited their observation after rumors began to spread.
Wistram's higher floors are sealed behind the Truestone Golem Cognita's test, and she has killed every [Mage] who attempted to challenge her.
Bastion-General is the rank of the officer who commands one of the Walls of Rhir; Bastion-General Quiteil is described as the person in charge of the entire 4th Wall.
Subordinate commanders such as Cirille address a Bastion-General by that title and authenticate with codes over a speaking stone.
Bastion-General Zavarial commands 5th Wall, and Bastion-General Quiteil can place divisions under him.
Zavarial and Quiteil each report to the Blighted King's command and use speaking stones and authentication codes.
Chief Warrior is the title by which Cirille addresses Merish, a Plains Gnoll who commands a Gnoll contingent sent to Rhir under the pact.
Merish's contingent counts two thousand one hundred and three Gnolls, and he personally brought sixty heavy-infantry warriors.
Chief Warrior Merish is a [Shamanic Warrior] of the Plain's Eye tribe, a class he described as a magic warrior suited to heavy fighting.
Merish is over seven feet tall with dyed fur, carries a bone axe, and his Gnolls show little interest in Drake military discipline.
Depth Captain is the title of a Drowned Folk ship [Captain] in the Undersea Crews who sails an underwater ship; a Drowned Ship's [First Mate] addresses its captain as "Depth Captain".
Depth Captain Therrium Sailwinds is a half-Eel Drowned Man who commands The Passing Shadow, a ship feared above and under the sea.
Crews under the waves follow the precept to make no sound, lest they attract what draws to it.
A second Depth Captain, a half-Shrimp Drowned Woman, followed the same treasure rumour about The Emerald Signet and argued with Therrium across the barrier of their ships.
When the two crews fought, the rival Depth Captain surrendered her blade, and Therrium made her sign a document placing her ship under his command.
A Desk Sergeant is a position, not a rank, in a Watch House, and it is temporary; a Senior Guard can fill the role and often does.
The Desk Sergeant manages the Watch House and the patrols coming in when the Watch Captains on duty are not present.
At Pallass's 8th floor Watch House, the Desk Sergeant on duty was Kel, to whom Patrol Leader Tanic reported.
Desk Sergeant Kel said it was within his authority as Desk Sergeant to let Erin walk free for her accident, and was enjoying the moment.
During the Wyvern attack, Desk Sergeant Kel led the 8th Floor's defenders and saluted Olesm when Olesm assumed command of the sector.
A Drake Desk Sergeant waved Lyonette up to see the Watch Captain after she slipped him a tart.
Dragonspeaker is a title in Manus, held by Luciva Skybreath as Dragonspeaker of Manus.
The Dragonspeaker carries the glaive known in Manus as the Fang of Manus, whose old first name is Parentkiller, and those who wield it hold it as a symbol of authority.
The Dragonspeaker presides over a council of Wall Lords and Ladies of Manus, where she hears opinions, asks the youngest member Rafaema for her thoughts, and signs and stamps decisions with her ring.
Luciva is a blue-scaled Drake with white and yellow in her scales, and her heritage is among the purest of all Drakes.
Ilvriss named the Dragonspeaker of Manus among the big names he wished to alert about the Necromancer once he was sure she was not under his control.
The Dragonspeaker sat down with the Lords and Ladies of the Wall to discuss the Siege of Liscor, the battle at the Bloodfields and the ambitions of Tyrion Veltras.
Luciva wore white in mourning, as the reinforcements from Manus in the battle had cost her everything.
When Wyverns attacked Pallass, Dragonspeaker Luciva watched the scrying orb in Manus's inner keep and led the war room's response.
Knight-Commander is the title of the head of the Order of Seasons, a major Terandrian knighthood; Knight-Commander Calirn holds it.
The Order of Seasons has four Seasons, each with its own Grandmaster, and at least two thousand Seasonal [Knights] in its headquarters at any time.
Even so, no [Knight] in the Order is beyond any other full member, even the Knight-Commander, so Talia spoke up to Calirn when she asked leave to hunt Belavierr.
Calirn is a Knight of the Winter with pale grey eyes, and the room around him grows freezing when he is troubled, though he can warm the air again.

Calirn rules from the Order's keep, whose cathedral is the domain of the Knight-Commander, and he leads the Order in command duties such as speaking with monarchs and settling arguments among the Seasons.
When Belavierr was reported to be in Filk, Calirn said the Order could slay her, but that it was one of many orders and tempered its strength with humility.
It is said that Calirn uses nothing but ordinary steel at times to challenge himself into levelling up.
The Order of Seasons is headquartered in Pheislant, on its own lands but allied with the Terandrian Kingdom.
Calirn personally attended a vigil on the docks for Ser Raim's funeral barge, blaming himself for leading the Order to war, and had white hair as white as the snow he could call.
Prime Minister is the elected ruler of the Republic of Belchan, a parliamentary government north of Germina.
Lyfelt was elected [Prime Minister] by Belchan's people, which makes Belchan a democracy and rare among nations; he is a career politician who consolidated a [Politician] class into [Minister].
Lyfelt rose to rule purely by political skill, not by birth, unlike the River Wardens of Jecrass.
Lyfelt was new to his position though he had served six years as [Prime Minister], and had held it less than a decade.
Lyfelt speaks with King Raelt of Jecrass through a pair of magical marble statues, and Raelt considers him a friend who sometimes thinks too much like a [Politician].
Lyfelt uses a Skill with a soothing voice to calm Raelt, and Raelt dislikes how he can play with lives like numbers.
Lyfelt recommended that Flos Reimarch hunt Manticores in Belchan, and invited Reim to dine and cross Belchan's borders.
Flos Reimarch accused Lyfelt of letting the Saltstone Tribe be slaughtered inside Belchan, and declared war on Belchan and on Lyfelt personally.
The Quarass is the ruler of Germina, a position revered and acknowledged across Chandrar, and one of four leaders counted among the Shield Kingdoms of eastern Chandrar.
Bethal explains that the Quarass and the other Shield Kingdoms were each once powerful empires, capable of challenging Dragons.
[Quarass] is a unique class, and the first Skill its holder obtains is [Memory of the Quarass].
A pale-yellow-eyed girl of no more than ten is presented to the crowd as the Quarass; the [Councilor] doubts she can be the ruler until she wakes from a collapse with the old presence in her gaze.
The crowd, including sixteen men, kneels and proclaims that the Quarass lives, and the girl is accepted as the Quarass of Germina.
The previous Quarass remembers her own death as a woman who feared the King of Destruction enough to risk everything to kill him, and the face of her death was Flos with red-gold hair and a sword.
The previous Quarass was a foolish, vain woman bitter at kneeling to Flos Reimarch, who had poisoned her mother to take the throne and then learned her mother's contempt for her.
The current Quarass calls her predecessor a fool and a matricide who was forced to live through slaying herself, and she says she herself will be one of the greatest Quarasses.
Meeting other rulers, the Quarass admits her predecessor was a fool, says she is not that woman, and says it was good she died before more could be ruined.
The other rulers are reserved with the Quarass, and Baosar says a kinkiller and matricide was a poor Quarass.
The current Quarass is a girl barely thirteen who nevertheless counts as a ruler beside Flos.
She can recall being a man in a number of her lives.
Flos tells her that Trey and Teres come from another world, and she says she has never heard of such a thing in all her lifetimes.
She examines Trey's iPhone and accepts it as proof that the twins come from another world.
She says plastic has never been made in any of her lifetimes and judges it weaker than metal.
She cannot cast the Tier 5 spell [Pestilence's Touch] in her young body, since she has little magic now.
She remembers fighting monsters but says her body cannot lift a sword properly or kill a single adult, because the knowledge of her body is gone.
She says undead are not farmed elsewhere because the undead crave death, and necromancers could lose control of them to other undead.
She says the Siren of Savere may be a sign of the resurgence of an old breed of [Bandit Lady], which she has seen rule many kingdoms in times past.
The Quarass has dined with Fetohep across eight lifetimes and orders the same first dish each visit: roasted eels, white grape juice, and eight glossberries sprinkled with nali powder on crushed ice.
She says eels and glossberries were her favourite dishes in past lives and her happiest meals, so the memory makes her seek them out each time.
She bets Fetohep that the Antinium will lead an attack within six years, expecting the Drakes to hold back after losing the Tidebreaker.

Fetohep bets that the Antinium will be attacked within six years by Drakes or another side; they settle on four hundred pounds of Khelt's gold against sixteen assassinations by Germina's highest-leveled [Assassins], Level 30 at minimum.
Fetohep notes that the previous Quarass lost two bets to him across two incarnations.
She tells Trey that she failed to convince Fetohep to offer Flos something of value, since he would rather use force than seem Reim's ally, and she plans to use Trey's device to sway his vanity.
The Quarass gets back a flying carpet from Germina's treasury, which Flos's armies looted when they took Ger and which he returned in exchange for her aid.
She has not flown in forty-two years and is still adjusting to the carpet.
She keeps a double, a little girl with yellow eyes, to show her face once a day in Ger or Reim in her absence.
Trey shows her [Light Arrow], taught to him by Gazi, [Sand Wall] and [Featherfall]; she corrects his mana control twice and says King Reimarch intends her to help shape his class.
She asks to see his Skill [Basic Golem Shaping] and watches his sand golems, noting his [Magical Specialization: Sand].

As training, the Quarass cuts Trey's throat with a ring-blade of the kind used by Germinan [Assassins], then forces him to move a golem covered in his own blood and sand, calling the result lifesand and the foundation for his golems.
She heals Trey with a potion afterwards, and he shouts that he hates her and wants to leave.
Revalantor is an Antinium rank that stands a step above Prognugator; Klbkch is the Revalantor of the Free Antinium in Liscor's Hive.
The Revalantor is technically above Prognugator and could ignore even the Queen's instructions, such was the nature of his duties.
Within his Hive, a Revalantor walks in a bubble of his own, and no one would get in his way.
Klbkch had become Revalantor only a few weeks earlier, and was expected to report less to his Queen and work more with Pawn and the new Individuals.
Ksmvr became the new Prognugator in the position Klbkch once held, and Klbkch as Revalantor is famous among the Antinium.
Pawn noted that the Hive now had a Revalantor who also acted as a Prognugator in the form of Klbkch.
The Revalantor monitors the new Individuals, and Pawn was told to report changes in his level or class to Klbkch.
The Revalantor Klbkch instructed the Antinium to rebuild Erin's inn, in return for letting Antinium visit the inn to learn chess.
Revalantor Pivr of the Flying Antinium visited Liscor's Hive with the leaders of other Hives and questioned the Individuals, speaking in his role as Revalantor for his own Queen.
River Warden is the name for the nobility of Jecrass, who control the water in the kingdom's sprawling plains and pastures.
The River Wardens are heirs to land that holds water, and anyone who owns a stream can build farmland, raise animals and dole out the resource.
King Raelt privately calls them River Robbers, because it is hard to tell a [Lord] from a [Bandit Leader].
The River Wardens are peers of the realm, below only Raelt in stature, and they can hold votes and drag their feet or oppose his decisions even though he is a [King].
Raelt hates his River Wardens, oranges and horses, even though Jecrass has all three in profusion.
Lyfelt remarked that the River Wardens could be shortsighted, and that half of the minor parties in his own parliament were the same.

The River Wardens argue over their horse breeds versus Terandrian ones but cannot consider the King of Destruction for ten minutes without gossiping; when asked what happens if he wins, they fall silent.
Raelt told Warden Dulfe that his people might leave his duchy to join Flos's empire because he had ignored Raelt's demand to improve living and working conditions.
The River Wardens were annoyed by the caravans of Flos's people passing through their borders and forgot Raelt's decree to aid them.

General Lael, who is not a River Warden, told them that Jecrass's armies could not triumph over Reim's, and Raelt told her to let the Wardens stew on the thought of an invasion for another week while she prepared.
Senior Guardsman is a rank in Liscor's City Watch, and Relc insists it is an important and highly prestigious rank.
A Senior Guard is a rank, whereas a Desk Sergeant is a temporary position that a Senior Guard can fill.
Relc and Klbkch are the best-known Senior Guardsmen of the Liscor Watch; Zevara called Klbkch one of her best Senior Guardsmen.
The Watch sends out Senior Guardsmen against Goblins and posts bounties to keep their numbers down.
Relc and Klbkch were not the only pair of Senior Guardsmen in the city, but between them they were the Watch's greatest fighting strength.
Klbkch, as a Senior Guardsman, could take Erin up onto the battlements where citizens are not allowed.
Klbkch told Zevara he was visiting not as a Senior Guardsman but as Prognugator of his Hive.
In the fight against the Raskghar, the Senior Guardsmen moved independently while the rest of the Watch fought shoulder to shoulder.
Senior Guardsmen include Gnolls, such as a Gnoll in his mid-forties with black and grey fur.
Siren is the title of the ruler of Savere, a nation of Drowned People and chaotic warriors, which Raelt thinks of as a unique country with a long history and culture.
Revine is the Siren of Savere; she calls water and rain with her hands, and the waters formed a path in the sands as she walked.
Revine is also known as the Siren of Tides or, unofficially, one of the [Bandit Queens] that plague the world.
Savere is described as home to ships and theft from every part of the world.
Revine is open about her hatred for Flos, and she attended the monarchs' gathering at the watering hole to speak of the King of Destruction.
At the gathering the Siren glared at Empress Nsiia and then pointed jets of water at her, which Orjin and a blast of air stopped.
The Siren of Savere offered the leader of Tiqr torture and her citizens as slaves, according to the leader of Tiqr, who would prefer death.
Revine's full name is Revine Zecrew.
The Baroness of the Beats is also called the Siren of Songs, a nickname for a [Singer] of Terandria.

Ilvriss says that a Wall Lord's lineage extends back to the age of Ancestors and Dragons, that they built the Walled Cities with the Dragons' help, and that their role is to lead and inspire Drakes and defend their home.
Magnolia says Zel deserves as many artifacts as a Lord of the Wall, and Zel scoffs at wearing a hundred rings and amulets at all times.

section: The Holders of the Wall of Salazsar
text: The Holders of the Wall of Salazsar gather in a room that only those whose hearts belong to Salazsar can stand in, and they present rings of copper and brass that turn gold and glow.

section: The Holders of the Wall of Salazsar
text: Wall Lady Calistoca, the oldest of those gathered, presides and opens by naming complacency, noting that an Antinium called Bird the Hunter appeared on the walls of Pallass.

section: The Holders of the Wall of Salazsar
text: The room is divided into camps: Ilvriss, a traditionalist, sits opposite his sister Navine Gemscale.

section: The Holders of the Wall of Salazsar
text: Wall Lord Brilm, a continual drinker and collector of what is new and trending, offers Ilvriss support for his plan.

section: The Holders of the Wall of Salazsar
text: Wall Lord Tasilt, who married a Gnoll, reads the plan, doubts it at first, and then agrees to talk with Ilvriss over a drink.

section: The Holders of the Wall of Salazsar
text: Ilvriss tells Tasilt his plan is the chance to create a unified force of all the Walled Cities, to replace what Zel Shivertail was.

section: The Holders of the Wall of Salazsar
text: Brilm tells Alrric that the other Children of the Walls wonder what activated Ilvriss's rings, and guesses the recipient is a Gnoll, a Human or a Selphid, and that Ilvriss will marry.
Hamlet is a play from Erin's world that she taught to the Players of Celum, the [Actors] who perform at her inn and in Celum.
The audience at the Frenzied Hare cheered the performance of Hamlet, including the Watch [Guardsman] with the fuzzy mustache who played Hamlet.
Erin taught Hamlet after Romeo and Juliet, and the Players performed it each night to great success.
Erin and the Players finished learning Hamlet and kept it for occasional performance, and then looked for another play.
Colina told Wesle she loved his Hamlet calling his uncle a false [King].
A Dullahan watched Hamlet being shown on stage at the inn.
Grev listed Hamlet among the plays the Players of Celum have done.
The Players put on Hamlet as a classic, with Jasi as Queen Gertrude, Wesle as Hamlet and Kilkran as Claudius.
Macbeth is a play from Erin's world, and Erin shuddered at the idea of performing it when choosing her next play for the Players of Celum.
Erin explained Macbeth to a customer by saying that a line was from Macbeth, a play, before explaining what a play is.
A Gnoll [Actor], Yimur, played the lead in a Gnollish Macbeth with 'hand' changed to 'paw', and Director Temile told him the dagger is a vision in Macbeth's mind.
The Players of Celum ran through Macbeth and then put on a full performance for an audience that was not heckling them.
Relc delivered Macbeth's dagger soliloquy without a flaw.
In Sovvex, the Players of Celum led with a comedy of a [Jester] and then performed Macbeth as the second play of the night, with Wesle as Macbeth.
The Players' Macbeth later used props, armor, blood, costumes, a stage and sets, with revised, modern scripts instead of the original, though Erin had first taught it in Celum.
